body:
Hi Bilawal, this PR makes the globe render lighter on phones, automatically. **Desktop does not change at all.**

First, so nobody sends the same thing twice: I went through the open PRs and issues before writing this and nothing covers phones. The closest are #2 (the top bar responsive) and #72 (the desktop perf items from #8). #72 also drops `preserveDrawingBuffer`, so the two touch the same line in `main.js`; I can rebase on whichever lands first.

The short version of why: the desktop settings ask the GPU to draw every frame several times over (the 3x pixel density of a phone screen, and each visual style, sharpen, bloom and scope mask being one more full-screen pass), and the photoreal tile cache has no limit. A laptop GPU does not care. A phone GPU cannot keep up, and on iOS the tab reloads itself once WebGL memory goes past **1 to 1.5 GB**.

**What changes on a phone:** the viewer now starts with no preserved drawing buffer (only recording needs it), the screen's own resolution instead of 3x, a 256 MB tile cache with a bit less detail (`maximumScreenSpaceError` 24), and the post-process passes off. The picture is slightly softer and the globe keeps running. **Anti-aliasing stays at 4x** on purpose: at the screen's own resolution it is cheap, and edges need it more there. All of it is one small file, `src/mobileProfile.js`, with the desktop and phone values side by side.

**How it decides:** touch screen and the shorter side under **900 px**. That is the whole rule, on purpose. It means a regular iPad counts as a phone here and gets the lighter profile; a 12.9 inch iPad Pro does not. Nobody has to do anything, but there are two manual switches, documented in `docs/KNOWN-ISSUES.md` under "Phones and small tablets": `?gevMobile=0` if a tablet user wants desktop quality, and `?gevMobile=1` to try the phone path on a desktop.

**One more small thing** in the same file: `?gevFlags=diag` paints a green box with browser, GPU, pixel density and canvas sizes. When someone says "it looks wrong on my phone" you can ask for a screenshot of that box instead of guessing. Without the flag nothing is added to the page. I needed exactly that this week with a Galaxy S24 and Edge; screenshots and the story in the comment below.

**Verified** on an iPhone (Edge iOS, WebKit) and a Galaxy S24 (Chrome), both load and render with the profile active. Desktop checked with the profile forced off: stages, cache and resolution exactly as before. `npm test` (4 new tests in `src/mobileProfile.test.mjs`), `npm run build` and `npm run test:track` are green. `CHANGELOG.md` and `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md` updated.

To be clear, this **does not touch the HUD layout**, which is still a desktop layout on a narrow screen.

And honestly, thanks for opening this. I have spent more hours than I should this week flying over my own island with it, and it is the first map app in a long time that made me want to work on it. Have a good one!

title: chore: add .gitattributes so 25 tests stop failing on Windows clones
body:
`npm test` fails **25 checks on an unmodified `main`** for anyone who clones on Windows. The cause isn't any of those tests — it's that the repo has no `.gitattributes`.

## What happens

Git's default on Windows is `core.autocrlf=true`, so every text file checks out with CRLF. 44 test files read repository source with `readFileSync` and match it against multi-line regexes anchored on `\n`:

```js
// src/scenes/director.test.mjs:486
const source = fs.readFileSync(new URL('../ui.js', import.meta.url), 'utf8');
const method = source.match(/\n {2}async applyVisualState\([\s\S]*?\n {2}\}\n/);
assert.ok(method, 'applyVisualState is missing from ui.js');
```

With CRLF the `\n {2}` never matches, and the assertion reports the source as *missing* rather than as differently-terminated. 158 `readFileSync` call sites across the suite share this exposure.

## Reproduce

```bash
git clone https://github.com/bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view.git   # core.autocrlf=true, the Windows default
cd gods-eye-view && npm install
npm test
```

25 failures across 13 files:

```
src/cameraHandoff.test.mjs          src/data/militaryInstallations.test.mjs
src/cockpitMarkup.test.mjs          src/data/trackedModelRegime.test.mjs
src/data/cctv.test.mjs              src/firstRunExperience.test.mjs
src/data/firmsInteraction.test.mjs  src/loadingFeedback.test.mjs
src/data/militaryAwareness.test.mjs src/locationReadouts.test.mjs
src/overlays/worldOverlay.test.mjs  src/reasonableDefaults.test.mjs
src/scenes/director.test.mjs
```

Confirmed on Node 24.14.0 (the version CONTRIBUTING pins) — not a Node-version artifact. `git config core.autocrlf false` plus a re-checkout makes all 25 pass, which isolates line endings as the only variable.

## The fix

One file. `* text=auto eol=lf` pins the working tree to LF on every platform, with `*.sh` explicit and the binary assets (`.gif`, `.png`, `.glb`, `.wav`, `.pbf`) marked so Git never rewrites them.

I put the reasoning in the file itself, since the next person to hit this will be reading `.gitattributes`, not this PR.

## Verification

**No content churn.** The index is already LF everywhere, so this rewrites nothing in history:

```
$ git add --renormalize .
$ git diff --cached --stat
(empty)
```

**It actually fixes the failures.** Cloned this branch with the Windows default explicitly forced:

```
$ git clone -c core.autocrlf=true <branch> gev-verify
$ cd gev-verify && npm test
ℹ tests 2587
ℹ pass 2587
ℹ fail 0
```

Zero CRLF files in the tracked tree after that clone. Before the change, the same clone gave 2562 pass / 25 fail.

`npm run build` is green. I could not run `npm run test:track` or the `qa:*` gates — those need a Google Maps key with the Map Tiles API enabled, which I don't have; this change touches no runtime code.

## Note for existing Windows clones

`.gitattributes` fixes new clones. Anyone who already cloned needs one refresh:

```bash
git rm --cached -rf . && git reset --hard
```

Happy to add that to CONTRIBUTING if you'd like it documented.

title: fix(cctv): cap the buffered snapshot body in the frame proxy (#28)
body:
Closes #28.

`fetchCctvImageFromUpstream` validated content-type and then buffered the whole upstream body:

```js
if (!upstream.ok || !contentType.startsWith('image/')) return null;
return { ok: true, body: Buffer.from(await upstream.arrayBuffer()), contentType };
```

There's no cap on that read. SECURITY.md says "high-volume or attacker-influenced upstream responses are capped where that boundary matters" — this path is the gap.

## Confirming it's real, not theoretical

Before writing the fix I ran the current function against a source that streams 64 chunks of 64 KB with no `Content-Length`:

```
{ isNull: false, len: 4194304, pulled: 64, cancelled: false }
```

Every chunk pulled, whole body buffered, stream never cancelled. The 8s frame timeout doesn't help — it bounds *time*, not bytes, and a fast upstream can deliver a lot in 8 seconds. Frames refresh on a 10s cadence per active camera, so this repeats.

The catalogs are server-registered, so this needs a configured source to turn hostile or be misconfigured — not a client-supplied URL. That's why I'd call it hardening rather than an exploitable hole.

## The fix

`readCappedResponseBytes` — the binary counterpart of the existing `readCappedResponseText`, placed next to it and following the same shape:

- a declared `Content-Length` over the cap is refused **before a single body byte is pulled**
- a missing or lying one is caught as chunks arrive, and the stream is cancelled
- overflow returns `null`

`null` is what makes this cheap: the frame route already treats it as an upstream miss, so an oversize body falls through the existing Street View → synthetic-SVG chain instead of erroring. No new failure mode, no new response shape.

Cap is 16 MB (`CCTV_FRAME_MAX_BODY_BYTES`), exported so the test can pin it. Public CCTV stills run well under a megabyte; 16 MB clears even a 4K PNG. It sits under the media route's existing 64 MB declared cap, and the test asserts that ordering so the two can't drift.

## Tests

Four added to `src/data/cctvProxy.test.mjs`:

| Test | Pins |
|---|---|
| declared oversize | cancelled, ≤1 chunk pulled (the stream's own prefetch) |
| undeclared oversize | cancelled mid-stream, ≤6 of 64 chunks pulled |
| chunked under cap | every chunk reassembled, correct byte length |
| existing valid image | unchanged |

Verified red→green: with the old `arrayBuffer()` line restored, the two oversize tests fail; with the fix, all five pass.

One deliberate detail — the oversize tests assert on `result?.body?.length` rather than on `result` itself. Asserting object equality made a regressed run hang: `assert.equal` builds a diff of the 4 MB Buffer, which takes longer than the check it's reporting on. Comment in the test says so.

## Gates

```
npm test    ℹ tests 2590  ℹ pass 2590  ℹ fail 0
npm run build   ✓ built (only the pre-existing chunk-size warning, #40)
```

Node 24.14.0. I could not run `test:track` or the `qa:*` gates — they need a Google Maps key with the Map Tiles API enabled.

CHANGELOG entry added under Security. I left `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md` alone since no product-visible behavior changes — the fallback chain it documents is unchanged. Happy to add a note there if you'd rather it be recorded.

title: fix(data): keep node:fs out of the browser-built data modules (#34)
body:
Closes #34.

`npm run build` emits these on every production build:

```
[plugin vite:resolve] Module "node:fs" has been externalized for browser
compatibility, imported by ".../src/data/naturalEarthRegions.js".
[plugin vite:resolve] Module "node:fs" has been externalized for browser
compatibility, imported by ".../src/data/neighborhoodPolygons.js".
```

Both modules carried the same dual path — the comment in `neighborhoodPolygons.js` explains why it was there:

```js
if (isNode) {
  // node:test path — plain dynamic JSON import needs an import attribute in Node,
  // so read the file directly (same dual-path pattern as naturalEarthRegions.js).
  const { readFileSync } = await import(/* @vite-ignore */ 'node:fs');
  ...
} else {
  const mod = await city.loader();   // Vite bundles the JSON file as a module
}
```

Vite only *warns* about externalizing `node:*`, so the import survives into the browser build and the boundary rests entirely on the `isNode` guard being right.

## The fix

The comment names the real constraint: Node needs an import attribute. So give it one, and the two paths collapse into one that both runtimes serve:

```js
loader: () => import('./local_data/neighborhoods/san-francisco.json', { with: { type: 'json' } })
```

Vite bundles the JSON exactly as before, Node loads the same file under `node:test`, and `isNode` plus `node:fs` disappear from both modules. Net −27/+22 lines in the two data modules.

## Verification

**Build.** Zero `externalized` warnings. The emitted JSON chunks are byte-identical to before — same content hashes:

```
regions-RPMKg9pq.js  marine-BJ61ZZ9E.js  san-francisco-B-TUYeaR.js
```

**Browser, not just build.** A build passing doesn't prove a dynamic import with an attribute still resolves at runtime, so I built a probe entry against these two modules and loaded it in headless Chrome:

```
{"neighborhoodName":"Chinatown","neighborhoodRingPoints":12,
 "saharaFound":true,"regionCount":1338}
```

title: Feature: Live weather radar and satellite imagery overlay layer
body:
Problem

God's Eye View already has environmental layers for fires (FIRMS), earthquakes (USGS), and an opt-in cockpit WX cloud effect. But there is no real-time weather data layer for the globe itself. A weather radar or satellite imagery layer would provide critical context for the other layers: flight diversion patterns, storm formation, and current conditions anywhere on the planet.

Proposed solution

Add a weather radar and satellite imagery overlay as a new toggleable layer:

- Global satellite cloud imagery (GOES, Himawari, Meteosat composite)
- Regional weather radar reflectivity where available (NOAA MRMS for US, local equivalents)
- Optional temperature, wind, or precipitation contour overlays

Data sources (all public and free tier)

- NOAA GOES satellite imagery (public, no API key)
- OpenWeatherMap (free tier, optional API key for more data)
- NOAA MRMS radar (public, US only)
- EUMETSAT for European coverage (public)

How it would work

Similar to the existing map stack switching, the weather layer would be a toggleable overlay. Tiles would be fetched through a lightweight proxy (already the pattern used for FIRMS, TomTom, etc.) and rendered as a semi-transparent overlay on the 3D globe.

The layer would:
- Show current cloud cover as a semi-transparent overlay
- Animate the last few hours of radar and satellite data with a time slider
- Respect the existing sensor modes (FLIR, NVG, etc.)

Why this fits God's Eye View

The project is about making the world's signals visible. Weather is one of the most fundamental signals. It provides context for flights (diversions, holds), ships (storm avoidance), fires (wind direction), and the cockpit WX mode already hints at this capability. A proper weather layer would make the globe feel even more alive.

title: Toto
fix(firms): drop argument spread in fires.push — RangeError silently dropped 2 of 3 VIIRS sources
body:
## The bug

With a valid `FIRMS_MAP_KEY`, the Active Fires layer renders roughly a third of the detections it should. It looks healthy — there is no user-visible error, and `/api/firms` returns 200 with a plausible fire count.

The dev-server log tells the real story:

```
[firms-proxy] VIIRS_NOAA20_NRT fetch failed: Maximum call stack size exceeded
[firms-proxy] VIIRS_SNPP_NRT  fetch failed: Maximum call stack size exceeded
```

## Root cause

`refreshUpstream()` merged each source's records with `fires.push(...records)`. Spread passes every element as a separate function argument, and a `world/2` VIIRS pull is well past V8's argument limit (~125k):

| Source | Records | Outcome |
|---|---:|---|
| `VIIRS_NOAA20_NRT` | 130,863 | `RangeError` — dropped |
| `VIIRS_NOAA21_NRT` | 113,996 | under the limit — survived |
| `VIIRS_SNPP_NRT` | 132,325 | `RangeError` — dropped |

Two things made it hard to spot:

1. **NOAA21 is the only source small enough to survive**, so the layer always has data and never looks broken.
2. **The throw lands after `sources.push({ source, count: records.length, ok: true })`**, so the `catch` appends a *second* entry for the same source. Each failed source is reported twice in the payload — once `ok: true` with its real count, once `ok: false` — while its records are gone. The `sources` array looks like the fetch succeeded.

Since at least one source always succeeds, the `if (!sources.some((s) => s.ok))` guard never trips and the broken result is cached as a normal entry.

## The fix

```js
- fires.push(...records);
+ for (const record of records) fires.push(record);
```

No spread, no argument-count ceiling, same ordering and same allocation behavior.

## Result

| | before | after |
|---|---:|---:|
| Sources OK | 1 of 3 | **3 of 3** |
| Global fires (trailing 24 h) | 113,996 | **377,169** |

`sources` no longer contains duplicate entries.

## Verification

All three required checks, run against Node 26:

- `npm run build` — clean (exit 0)
- `npm test` — **2587 passed, 0 failed** (the 2 allocation microbenchmarks self-skip on Node 26: *"budgets are calibrated for Node 24"*)
- `npm run test:track` — **100 passed, 0 failed**, including *"no console errors across the FULL run"* and *"no HTTP 5xx responses across the FULL run"*

Also verified live against the real endpoint: `/api/firms` returns all three sources `ok: true`, and the dev-server log shows zero `Maximum call stack size exceeded` entries after the change.

## One consequence worth flagging

Carrying all three sources takes the `/api/firms` response from ~22 MB to ~74 MB. That is the correct amount of data — it was always meant to be there — but it is a real jump for anyone serving this beyond localhost. Happy to follow up with a separate PR if you would like the payload trimmed or paginated; I kept this one to the bug.

Found while running the project on a home server. Thanks for open-sourcing it.

title: Add Flat Earther Mode Toggle
body:
## **Add Flat Earther Mode Toggle**

### **Description**
This PR adds a **"Flat Earther Mode"** toggle to the app, allowing users to switch between the standard map projection and the **Azimuthal Equidistant Projection** (Flat Earth view).

### **Why This Feature?**
- **Computational Efficiency**: Flat mode simplifies rendering by using a 2D plane, reducing the computational overhead of spherical projections.
- **Better Terrain & Elevation Oversight**: Provides a clearer, distortion-free view of sea levels and elevation data, making it easier to analyze terrain in a Flat Earth context.
- **Model Comprehension**: Helps users visualize and understand the Flat Earth model more intuitively by removing spherical distortions.

---

### **Changes Made**
- **`mapStackChips.js`**: Added a UI toggle button for Flat Earther Mode.
- **`mapStackController.js`**:
  - Implemented a custom **Flat Earth CRS** (Azimuthal Equidistant Projection).
  - Added `toggleFlatEartherMode()` to switch projections dynamically.
  - **Left comments** for the original dev to integrate:
    - Gleason’s map overlay (static image).
    - Elevation/sea level data (heatmap or custom layer).

### **How It Works**
- Users click the **"Flat Earther Mode"** button to toggle the projection.
- The map switches to the Flat Earth view with the North Pole at the center.
- **Placeholders** are included for Gleason’s map and elevation data (to be implemented by the original dev).

### **Dependencies**
- Requires `Leaflet`, `Proj4Leaflet`, and `Proj4js` (already included in the project).

### **Testing**
- [x] Toggle button appears in the UI.
- [x] Projection switches correctly between standard and Flat Earth.
- [x] UI updates to reflect the current mode (ON/OFF).

---
### **Next Steps**
@original-dev:
- Please implement the **Gleason’s map overlay** (as an `L.imageOverlay`).
- Add **elevation/sea level data** (e.g., as a heatmap or custom layer).
- See comments in `mapStackController.js` for integration details.

---
**Note**: This is a non-breaking change and only adds functionality. No existing features are modified.

title: feat(ocean): ocean observations, GSHHG land/sea mask, animated current field, drift Monte Carlo
body:
> **This PR has grown a lot since it was opened.** It was an ocean-observation
> layer plus a drift simulator; it is now those plus a bundled land/sea mask and
> an animated surface-current field. If the size is a problem I am happy to split
> it — the four pieces are separable and I've noted the seams at the bottom.

## What

Four pieces, stacked, each usable without the ones above it.

### 🌊 Ocean Conditions — NDBC buoy observations (`ocean-conditions`, token `o`)

~900 NOAA NDBC stations from **one** server-cached bulk fetch (`/api/ocean/obs`:
10 min TTL, 60 min stale-serving, non-fatal station-name join from
`activestations.xml`) — never per-station polling. Rendered as static-geometry
entities color-banded by significant wave height.

Cards show **observed values sparsely**: a wave-only station gets wave lines,
missing fields are omitted rather than rendered as placeholders. Open-Meteo
**Marine forecast lines are appended `FC`-prefixed** so observation and forecast
are never conflated. Direction fields name their convention — NDBC `MWD`/`WDIR`
and Open-Meteo `wind_direction_10m` read `from N°` (meteorological),
`ocean_current_direction` reads `toward N°` (oceanographic) — because a bare
arrow shared one glyph between two opposite meanings.

Full analyst + voice integration ("turn on buoys", "sea state", "waves"), with
analyst queries over `waveHeightM, wavePeriodS, windSpeedMs, gustMs, sstC,
pressureHpa`.

### 🗺️ Bundled land/sea mask (GSHHG-derived)

A global **1/8° three-state raster** — water / land / coastal-mixed, 2 bits per
cell, 2880×1440, exactly 1,036,816 bytes — built offline from GSHHG v2.3.7 by a
committed regeneration script, with a zero-dependency native `.b` parser, an
even-odd scanline rasterizer (per-ring longitude unwrap for the dateline,
artificial south-pole seam edges for the globe-circling Antarctic ice front), and
a `GEVM`-header codec shared by the build script, the browser loader and the
drift worker.

Three states rather than two, and the third is the point: a cell a shoreline
passes through is *partly wet*, so it is never trusted either way. Ocean clicks
on a coastal cell fall back to the live probe; drift particles never beach there.

Measured composition of the committed artifact: 64.963% water, 32.113% land,
2.925% coastal by cell count (69.948% / 27.321% / 2.731% area-weighted).

**Licence:** GSHHG is LGPL, so the derived raster is too. `LICENSE` gains a
carve-out alongside the existing TeleGeography and OSM ones, and
`DATA_SOURCES.md` records the source URL, fetch date, input SHA-256 and
regeneration command.

### 🌀 Ocean Currents — the field itself, animated (`ocean-field`, token `n`)

`/api/ocean/field` serves a **two-tier ladder, and every tier that contributes is
named on screen with its own age, resolution and physics.**

- **Nearshore**: IOOS HF-radar total vectors (nine CoastWatch ERDDAP datasets,
  0.5–6 km, hourly) through QC gates — `hdop ≤ 1.6`, `|u|,|v| ≤ 2.4 m/s` per
  component, ≥ 40 vectors in a **single** served hour (never a multi-hour pool:
  M₂ is 12.42 h), served hour ≤ 12 h old — then a **two-pass Barnes objective
  analysis** with holdout cross-validation. `L = 2.05·Δ` floored at 2.05 km,
  solved so the two-pass response reaches half amplitude at exactly 4Δ.
- **Everywhere else**: **HYCOM ESPC-D-V02** (0.04°×0.08°, 3-hourly, −10 d…+5 d) —
  a primitive-equation forecast carrying wind-driven flow and eight tidal
  constituents, so it is physically comparable to the radar tier rather than
  merely adjacent to it. NOAA CoastWatch's 0.25° blended altimetry is retained as
  an **automatic fallback**; it is absolute geostrophic velocity and nothing else
  (no Ekman, no tides), and the legend says which one served and what it carries.
- **Both**: a view served by both is `composite` and states the split — "11% of
  drawn cells are 1 km HF radar (4 h old); the other 89% is 4.4 km HYCOM global
  forecast currents (40 min old)". Each drawn cell keeps exactly one provenance:
  radar, then fill, then `null`. Never averaged, never zero.

Client side: 4,000 particles advected through a 16 px screen-space velocity
raster rebuilt on camera settle, so the projection's meridian convergence, tilt
and foreshortening are measured per node rather than approximated. Time
compression is solved per rebuild to hold a median current at 1.1 px/frame,
keeping the field legible across the ~400× range in screen speed between a
100 km view and the whole Earth. The colour ramp is strictly increasing in WCAG
relative luminance (0.169 → 0.636) with hue falling 192° → 41°, interpolated in
linear light.

**Coverage is measured over water cells**, using the mask above — counting land
against a coastal analysis demotes exactly the views HF radar exists to serve.
The same radar hour scored 20% over a 1°×1° box centred on Monterey Bay and
99.9% over a 0.6°×0.6° box moved offshore; the difference was land, not data.
A cell with no data is drawn as nothing, never as slack water.

Tier logic and ingest live in `src/server/ocean/*`, not in `vite.config.js`
(issue #41) — the route handler is 65 lines over 7 modules.

### 🧍‍🌊 Person-overboard drift Monte Carlo

A `▶ DRIFT` chip on buoy and ocean-point cards runs a stochastic **leeway drift
ensemble** — Breivik & Allen (2008) formulation, USCG taxonomy **PIW-1**
coefficients (Allen & Plourde 1999 / Allen 2005), transcribed from OpenDrift's
`OBJECTPROP` table with citations in `src/sim/leeway.js` and verified against it
verbatim. Classical RK4 with step-held stochastic terms (measured: forward-Euler
global error 0.052 m vs RK4 8.0 × 10⁻⁶ m on the shipped configuration), a
zero-noise deterministic control particle, backward/hindcast integration, a
turbulent-diffusion term, and beaching against ETOPO bathymetry with the bundled
mask as offline fallback.

Labelled `SIMULATED DRIFT ENSEMBLE — NOT A SAR PRODUCT` everywhere, following the
repo's `RECONSTRUCTED ESTIMATE` honesty grammar. **What the ensemble actually
is**, measured and stated in the panel rather than implied: at the defaults
(n = 10⁴, 24 h, dt = 10 min, σ_pos = 1 km, σ_turb = 0.05 m/s, 8 m/s wind), the
variance decomposition is leeway residual + crosswind sign **153.70 km² (98.1%)**,
initial position scatter 2.00 km² (1.3%), turbulence 0.26 km² (0.2%). The spread
is a leeway-uncertainty cloud, not a resolved-flow prediction, and the panel says
so.

## Fixes found while auditing this branch

I ran a review over the whole branch before updating the PR. Seven defects came
out of it; all are fixed here, each with a test that fails without the fix.

1. **The HYCOM tier never served.** `parseHycomAscii` required both velocity
   components to carry a coordinate map named exactly `time`, but the THREDDS
   FMRC aggregation numbers the two axes apart — the `.dds` declares
   `water_u[time]` beside `water_v[time1]` — so the parser rejected *every*
   well-formed response as shape drift and fell through to the altimetry
   fallback on 100% of requests. Measured across five disjoint boxes (Monterey,
   mid-Pacific, North Sea, antimeridian, equator): 5/5 failed against a healthy
   upstream. The test fixture reproduced the server's variable *ordering* quirk
   but not its *naming* quirk, so all 52 of the module's tests passed against a
   body the server never sends. Now matched by family — safe because the two
   axes are the same axis under two names (max |time − time1| = 0 across all 129
   steps) — and the fixture emits the real shape, which turns 10 of its tests
   into a regression guard.
2. **A forecast field rendered as `just now`.** `resolveAgeMs` clamped with
   `Math.max(0, …)`, discarding the negative `ageMs` HYCOM reports on purpose, so
   a field valid five days out looked like a just-published analysis with
   `stale: false`. The sign is kept on the fetcher-reported branch (measured
   against *now*) and still clamped on the derived branch (measured against the
   *requested* instant, which may be historical); `formatAge` renders a negative
   age as `4 days ahead`.
3. **The Ocean Currents layer reported no status.** It exposed `getStatus()`
   while `DataLayerManager` reads `getStats()`, so its DATA panel row showed a
   blank count and "never" permanently — including while `refresh()` was failing.
   The contract test asserted the wrong name too; it now drives
   `DataLayerManager._moduleStats` itself.
4. **`/api/ocean/field` answered 500 for every malformed request.**
   `normalizeBox` refuses by throwing, so the handler's `if (!box)` 400 branch
   was unreachable. Verified live against five invalid inputs. Four route-level
   tests now drive the middleware — previously all 26 tests in
   `oceanProxy.test.mjs` called pure helpers, leaving dispatch, method checks and
   status codes covered by nothing.
5. **`node:fs` was back in a browser module.** The mask loader branched on an
   `isNode` check, reintroducing what #83 removed. Now two modules over one pure
   codec, and `browserModuleBoundary.test.mjs` gains a second assertion — no
   browser module imports from `src/server/` — which is what makes excluding that
   tree from the first assertion sound rather than a hole.
6. **Voice could not turn the current field on.** `ocean-field` was in the
   registry and `main.js` but in no tool enum and had no aliases, so "show me the
   ocean currents" resolved to the buoys.
7. **Documentation described a design the code could not reach.** With HYCOM
   actually serving, README / `DATA_SOURCES` / `CURRENT-STATE` / the credits /
   the `@file` block / the composite provenance strings are reconciled. HYCOM had
   no credit entry at all while it was the primary tier; the CoastWatch entry
   said "U.S. public domain" where the dataset's own licence text requires
   Copernicus and AVISO+ acknowledgements. A Monterey coverage figure recorded as
   20% in two places and 25% in a third is reconciled to 20%.

## Verification

All three gates green on the merged tree:

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `npm run build` | ✅ exit 0 |
| `npm test` | ✅ **3,182 pass / 0 fail**, across 24 new test files |
| `npm run test:track` | ✅ **108/108**, no console errors, no HTTP 5xx |

Live endpoint smoke against a fresh dev server (2026-09-02):

- `/api/ocean/obs` → 200, real NDBC bulk feed.
- `/api/ocean/marine`, `/marine-grid` → 200, served-coordinate georeferencing in
  the payload.
- `/api/ocean/etopo` → 200.
- `/api/ocean/field` → 200. Global-only box: HYCOM, `kind: modeled`, 17.72 km,
  40 min old. Monterey: `composite`, holdout RMSE 0.031 m/s, 11% radar / 89%
  HYCOM, 69% water coverage.
- Malformed input → **400** with the failing bound named, on all five refusal
  classes and on an omitted bound.

All five `/api/ocean` routes register in **both** `configureServer` and
`configurePreviewServer` — they share one `install(server.middlewares)`, so
preview parity is structural rather than per-route.

`upstream/main` (v0.1.1) is merged in. Three conflicts: `CHANGELOG.md` folded
under the new bare `## [Unreleased]`; `README.md`'s layer count combined and
verified against the table itself (15 rows, 13 keyless); and the frozen
`GEV_REALTIME_TOOLS` pin **re-cut** rather than resolved to a side — both sides
recorded a length and sha over the same 31,104-byte baseline and the two edits
are disjoint (upstream's `esri-imagery` +85 B, this branch's ocean layers
+562 B), so neither value could survive.

## Known limits

- **Neither tier resolves Stokes drift**, and only the HYCOM tier carries tides —
  on the altimetry fallback there is no tidal signal at all. The legend states
  the physics of whichever source served rather than describing the tier once.
- **The drift model is not coupled to the current field**, deliberately. A
  single-hour observed snapshot cannot honestly force a 24–48 h integration, and
  I measured that even perfect HF forcing roughly doubles the structured spread
  against a cloud that is 98.1% leeway uncertainty. That is a research decision,
  not missing wiring.
- **The mask is 1/8°** (~14 km at the equator). That is why the third state
  exists and why coastal cells are never trusted either way.
- **One leeway class** (PIW-1). The USCG taxonomy has many more — life raft,
  kayak — and the coefficient table is already structured for them.

## If the size is the problem

The seams, in dependency order: (1) the NDBC layer and its proxies; (2) the GSHHG
mask; (3) the drift Monte Carlo, which needs (2) for beaching; (4) the current
field, which needs (2) for water-relative coverage. (4) is the largest and the
most novel and would get the better review on its own — happy to peel it off into
a follow-up PR against this one, or to restage entirely. Just say which.

title: fix(installations): derive a point from bounds when Overpass omits center
body:
## The bug

`militaryInstallationsProxy` asks Overpass for `out center tags geom`. Overpass honours only the **last** geometry mode, so `geom` wins and `center` is never emitted. Every way and relation therefore arrives without `lat`/`lon`, and `pointFrom` drops it.

The layer has been rendering nodes and nothing else:

| Area | Kept |
|---|---|
| San Diego | 149 of 228 elements — every way and relation gone |
| Warendorf (DE) | 0 — the town has no surveyed nodes, so the screen is empty over a mapped Bundeswehr barracks |

Silent: no error, no warning, just missing installations.

## The fix

`out geom` ships `bounds` alongside exactly those elements — relations included, which carry no `geometry` at all — so `pointFrom` falls back to the midpoint of that box. No change to the query, no change to the footprint path.

## Tests

Four new cases in `src/data/militaryInstallationData.test.mjs`. Two fail on the unfixed normalizer (way and relation carrying only `bounds`); two are regression guards — an explicit `center` must keep winning, and a half-filled or out-of-range box must be dropped rather than averaged into a plausible-looking lie.

## Verification

`npm run build`, `npm test` (2591 passing) and `npm run test:track` (100/100) green.

title: fix(qa): poll waits on a timer so qa-cctv-v2 can boot the app under SwiftShader
body:
## The bug

Every `waitForFunction` in `scripts/qa-cctv-v2.mjs` used Puppeteer's default `raf` polling. The app idles behind the explicit render governor, and under SwiftShader the rAF polling loop competes with the render loop the app needs to finish initialising.

Measured on an M-series Mac, headless:

| Polling | Result |
|---|---|
| `raf` (default) | boot predicate still `false` after 45 s |
| `polling: 200` | ready in 0.2 s |

So the harness timed out at its 60 s boot wait and never ran a single check — it was not reporting failures, it was not running.

## The fix

`polling: 200` on all four waits, plus the `protocolTimeout: 300_000` hardening `scripts/track-regression.mjs` already carries with the same reasoning:

> This machine intermittently stalls single CDP calls past the 180 s default under SwiftShader load.

Four lines of behaviour change, no test logic touched.

## Verification

The harness now boots and runs. It still cannot complete headless on this hardware (a later `Runtime.callFunctionOn` stalls out), but it reaches 30+ checks instead of zero. Headful it runs to completion.

title: feat(overpass): allow extra mirrors via OVERPASS_EXTRA_UPSTREAMS
body:
## Why

The built-in mirror list is not reachable from everywhere. From one German consumer connection every entry failed at once — `overpass-api.de` and `lz4` refused TCP outright, and `overpass.kumi.systems` is a CNAME onto `private.coffee`, so the list holds fewer distinct hosts than it looks like.

Traffic, mapped installations and every other Overpass-backed layer were dead, with no fix short of editing `vite.config.js`. A network-local mirror belongs in the operator's environment, not in the repo's default list.

## What

`OVERPASS_EXTRA_UPSTREAMS` (whitespace- or comma-separated) is tried **before** the built-ins: a mirror someone configured deliberately is a better first try than one that just timed out for them, and each dead built-in costs a full `OVERPASS_TIMEOUT_MS` before the chain moves on.

Resolved lazily and re-resolved when the value changes, because module evaluation runs before Vite's `loadEnv()` copies `.env` into `process.env` — the file already documents that trap elsewhere.

Validation is **structural only**. Unlike a world-editable OSM tag, this value comes from the operator's own env, so a private or localhost address is a legitimate self-hosted instance rather than an SSRF target, and is deliberately allowed. The JSDoc says so, so it does not get "hardened" later by mistake.

One warning carried over from the field: **only add planet-wide instances.** A regional extract such as `overpass.osm.ch` answers fast with HTTP 200 but serves Switzerland only, so every query outside CH returns an empty element list — which this proxy then caches as a valid result for 24 h. It fails silently, not loudly.

## Tests

`src/data/overpassUpstreams.test.mjs` — separator forms and order, private/localhost allowed, unusable entries dropped rather than passed to the fetch loop, duplicates collapsed.

## Verification

`npm run build`, `npm test` (2591 passing) and `npm run test:track` (100/100) green. Confirmed in the running dev server: `[Overpass] 1 extra upstream(s) from OVERPASS_EXTRA_UPSTREAMS, tried first`.

title: feat(cctv): add a keyless OSM webcam source pack
body:
## What

A fourth live pack alongside Austin, Caltrans and TfL, reachable in any country via `CCTV_OSM_AREA` (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, default `DE`). `man_made=surveillance` + `contact:webcam` is the operator's **own published frame URL**, so fetching it is the same act as fetching an Austin or a TfL frame. No camera data is committed — the catalog is fetched at runtime, per CONTRIBUTING rule 4.

## Why it earns a place next to three traffic-camera packs

`camera:direction`. Austin and TfL have no heading signal at all and fall back to `fallbackHeadingFromId()` — an id hash, a number unrelated to where the camera looks. Measured for `DE` on 2026-08-28:

| | Nodes |
|---|---|
| `man_made=surveillance` | 46,129 |
| …with `camera:direction` | 20,771 |
| …with `contact:webcam` | 851 |
| …surviving the still-image filter | 279 |
| …of the 150 served, with a real mapped heading | 136 |

## What survives the filter, and why

- **Still images only.** Most `contact:webcam` values are landing pages. Reading a frame off those would be scraping.
- **No MJPEG.** `axis-cgi/mjpg/video.cgi` answers with an unbounded multipart stream; declared as an `image` feed it would not fail fast, it would hold the frame proxy to its own timeout every refresh tick.
- **Public hosts only.** This catalog is world-editable — anyone can point `contact:webcam` at a link-local metadata address — so the same non-global refusal `publicRadioHttpsUrl` applies to Radio Browser streams applies here. Plain `http:` is allowed, because municipal webcams are routinely TLS-less.

Roughly half the surviving URLs are dead at any moment; municipal webcams rot and OSM keeps the old URL. That is health's job, not the loader's — the first failed frame marks the camera `degraded`, exactly as for an offline Caltrans camera. No liveness sweep at load, which would be a per-refresh cost no other pack pays.

## Two supporting changes this pack forces

- **`fetchOverpassPayload` takes a per-caller `timeoutMs`.** The country-wide scan measured ~51 s on the fastest reachable mirror, so under the shared 22 s *interactive* budget it could never succeed. The pack also refreshes on its own 6 h clock and **never on the request path** — awaiting it inside `refreshCctvSources` would hang the first `/api/cctv/sources` after every TTL expiry for a minute, for every client.
- **The catalog cap goes 900 → 1100.** Four packs default to 950, and the cap slices from the *front* of the merged list, whose tail is the file/env pack — so 900 silently dropped hand-authored cameras rather than trimming a live pack. Stays under `HEALTH_MAX_ENTRIES` (1200).

## Licensing

ODbL covers the **catalog** (position, direction, the URL). It never covers the picture — each frame stays the publishing operator's under their own terms. `DATA_SOURCES.md` says exactly that.

## Known limitation

`OSM_WEBCAM_ANCHORS` is a fixed list of five German metros used to pick which cameras survive the per-pack cap. Set `CCTV_OSM_AREA=FR` and find more than 150, and you get the ones nearest Germany. Happy to make the anchors derive from the area, or to skip distance prioritisation entirely for a non-default area — say which you prefer.

The deeper version of the same point: like the other three packs this one is region-pinned at boot. Making it viewport-driven (as the mapped-installations layer already is) would remove the question entirely, but that changes the CCTV registry contract for all four packs and does not belong in this PR.

## Tests

`src/data/osmWebcamSources.test.mjs`, 13 cases: URL filter accept/reject including MJPEG and landing pages, the SSRF refusals, `camera:direction` wrapping (`-195 → 165` is live OSM data), mount priors, the drop rules, and that the licence names catalog and frame separately.

## Verification

`npm run build`, `npm test` (2600 passing) and `npm run test:track` (100/100) green. In the running app: catalog 803 → 953, 150 OSM cameras of which 136 carry a mapped heading, frames served as `X-CCTV-Source: upstream-image`.

title: feat(cctv): add a Warendorf source pack (Marktplatz + two Kfz-Zulassungsstellen)
body:
## What

Three publicly published municipal webcams in Kreis Warendorf, Germany, as a hand-authored source pack in the shape `loadSourcesFromFile` already reads. Like `config/cctv_sources.shinjuku.json` the file is inert until pointed at:

```bash
CCTV_SOURCES_FILE=config/cctv_sources.warendorf.json
CCTV_FORCE_AUSTIN=1   # REQUIRED — a non-empty file pack otherwise
                      # disables the live Austin/Caltrans/TfL packs
```

## The poses are measured, not guessed

The Marktplatz camera sits on the Historisches Rathaus (OSM way 261404006) — the mount passes a point-in-polygon test against that footprint — and looks at the area centroid of the Markt pedestrian square (OSM way 23483618, 1923 m²). The ground intersection of its view axis at 14 m mount and −23° pitch lands **inside** that polygon, and a heading sweep over 195–255° shows a plateau at 217–227°, so 221° is a measurement rather than a guess. Mount height follows the OSM tags (`building:levels=2` + `roof:levels=2`, gabled). Ground elevations come from the app's own `/api/terrain/heights`.

All three carry `poseSource: 'curated'` so the CAL badge keeps distinguishing them from raw automated priors.

## Licensing — weaker than the other packs, and labelled that way

Austin, Caltrans and TfL all publish explicit open-data terms; TfL's attribution is even mandatory and pinned. Stadt and Kreis Warendorf state **nothing**. `DATA_SOURCES.md` therefore records courtesy attribution plus the note that frames are fetched at runtime and never redistributed — no licence is claimed that was not granted.

The poses are derived from OSM geometry, so ODbL attribution travels with them.

## Verification

`npm run build` and `npm test` (2587 passing) green. All three cameras serve live frames through the proxy (`X-CCTV-Source: upstream-image`) and report `ok` on `/api/cctv/health`.

title: feat(installations): show OSM provenance in the popup and walk the viewport roster
body:
> **Stacked on #102.** The first two commits of this branch *are* #102 (the bounds fix and its tests) — a fork PR cannot target a branch that does not exist upstream, so this is opened against `main` and its diff currently shows both. Merge #102 first and this shrinks to the three follow-up commits. Reviewing #102 on its own is the better read; it is an unrelated silent-data-loss bug that should not wait on this feature.

## 1 — Provenance in the popup

The label carried the class alone, so every unnamed feature read `MILITARY LAND` and nothing else. The provenance that decides whether a viewer should trust a marker — which OSM object, which operator, how old, reviewed or not — was already collected by `registerEntityContext` and then only ever read back by the voice agent.

`normalizeMilitaryInstallations` now copies a fixed, **named** slice of tags (`short_name`, `operator`, `start_date`, `wikipedia`, `wikidata`) onto the record, trimmed to strings, so an arbitrary upstream tag can never reach a label. `installationDetailLines` renders them and is pure, so the wording is testable without a Cesium viewer.

Small deliberate choices: the OSM id is rendered pasteable (`OSM WAY/92701457`); `wikipedia` wins over `wikidata` so the two do not spend two lines on one fact; a Places candidate is marked as one rather than passed off as mapped military land; an absent source is stated as unknown rather than omitted, because silence would read as vouched-for.

## 2 — Hover emphasis and a PREV/NEXT walk

Until now the only way to reach a second installation was Global Context, which needs a tracked aircraft or vessel as its subject — installations are a cohort there, never the subject. So "show me these one after another" had no answer at all for ground features.

Points and footprints now emphasise on hover, and a collapsible strip in the right rail walks the viewport roster, bound to `,` and `.` (the media-player step convention; matched raw, since both sit unshifted on QWERTY and QWERTZ). The keys are guarded on the layer being enabled, so they stay free otherwise.

**The walk order is frozen on first use rather than recomputed per step.** Nearest-from-here ping-pongs between two mutual neighbours forever, and the counter would have no stable meaning; a fixed order makes "3 / 59" true and the walk exhaustive.

## Tests

- `osmTags`: the named slice is copied and trimmed, an arbitrary tag (`description`, `note`, `website`) never travels, a feature with nothing descriptive gets an empty bag rather than `undefined`.
- `installationDetailLines`: an unnamed feature says more than its class, wikipedia beats wikidata, a Places candidate is marked, an unparseable timestamp drops its line instead of printing `Invalid Date`.
- `stepSelection`: every record is visited once before repeating, the counter is 1-based and zero while nothing is selected, the first step opens at the nearest going forward and the farthest going back, both directions wrap, an empty roster is inert rather than throwing.

## Verification

`npm run build`, `npm test` (2604 passing) and `npm run test:track` (100/100) green.

## Note for review

The nav strip polls the roster once per second (`setInterval`) rather than chasing every writer — the roster is viewport-driven and the selection can also change by a direct marker click. It reads two integers and requests no render, so it does not touch the render governor, but if you would rather have it event-driven, say so and I will wire it.

title: fix: Windows CRLF test portability in reasonableDefaults.test.mjs (#88)
body:

`node --test src/reasonableDefaults.test.mjs` reads `src/ui.js` with a hardcoded LF-only source anchor. On a Windows checkout with `core.autocrlf=true`, `ui.js` uses CRLF line endings, so the anchor is never found — 8/9 tests pass instead of 9/9.

## Fix

Normalize CRLF to LF before the anchor search, so the result doesn't depend on git's line-ending config.

title: fix: make GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY optional, fall back Google 3D Tiles -> Cesium ion -> OSM globe (#59, #64, #71)
body:
Closes #59, closes #64. Implements the fallback proposed in #71.

## Problem

`main.js` hard-throws at startup if `GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY` is unset — the app refuses to start at all without it (#64), and EEA billing accounts that get a 401 from the Map Tiles API directly (#59) have no recourse.

## Fix

New fallback chain instead of a hard throw:
1. Google Photorealistic 3D Tiles (unchanged — preferred when a Google Maps key is set and the account can reach the Map Tiles API)
2. Cesium ion's mirror of the same imagery (asset `2275207`, via `CESIUM_ION_TOKEN`) — the workaround from #71, which also fixes #59 since EEA accounts can reach the same tiles through Cesium ion even when the Map Tiles API itself 401s
3. The free, keyless OSM globe — already supported by `MapStackController`, just previously unreachable because the app refused to start at all without a Google key

`.env.example` and `README.md` updated to document both keys as optional and explain the fallback order.

title: fix: split server-only Places/Street View key from the browser-exposed Google Maps key (#33)

title: fix: remove node:fs from browser-built data modules (#34)
body:
Closes #34.

`npm run build` warns on every production build:

```
[plugin vite:resolve] Module "node:fs" has been externalized for browser compatibility, imported by "src/data/naturalEarthRegions.js".
[plugin vite:resolve] Module "node:fs" has been externalized for browser compatibility, imported by "src/data/neighborhoodPolygons.js".
```

Both modules carried a Node-only `fs` branch, only reachable under `node --test` (Node's loader requires an explicit import attribute for a JSON module that Vite doesn't need), alongside a Vite dynamic-JSON-import branch for the browser.

## Fix

A dynamic `import('./x.json', { with: { type: 'json' } })` works identically under Node's native loader and under Vite (dev + build, still its own lazy chunk) — Node 20.10+/22+ support the `with` import-attribute syntax natively. One loader for both environments, zero `node:fs` reference anywhere in either file, so there's nothing left for the browser build to externalize.

## Verification

`node --test` on both files' suites (20/20 pass), `npm run build` with the `node:fs externalized` warnings gone and the regions/marine/san-francisco JSON chunks still split out exactly as before (same sizes, still lazy — not folded into the eager bundle).

title: feat: live weather radar / satellite overlay layer via RainViewer (#85)
body:
Addresses #85. **Note:** aware of #89, an independent WIP PoC for this same issue also using RainViewer — didn't coordinate in advance since we were working in parallel. Happy to close whichever the maintainer doesn't prefer; leaving both open for now so you can compare.

## What this adds

New toggleable "Weather Radar" data layer, two independently-toggled overlays (radar precip reflectivity, IR satellite cloud cover), drawn as semi-transparent `Cesium.ImageryLayer`s on the globe surface.

**Source:** RainViewer's public API (`api.rainviewer.com/public/weather-maps.json` for the frame list, tiles from `tilecache.rainviewer.com`) — keyless, CORS-open (verified live: both send `access-control-allow-origin: *`), fetched directly from the browser, no server proxy needed. Polls every 10 min (RainViewer's own frame cadence); a same-frame poll is a no-op rather than tearing down and rebuilding a live imagery layer for nothing.

**Scope:** just the latest radar and satellite frames from this one free endpoint. The full #85 proposal also named region-specific sources (NOAA MRMS, EUMETSAT) and an animated multi-frame time slider — deliberately out of scope for this pass. RainViewer's `radar.past` array already carries ~2h of frame history if a future pass wants to add animation on the same tile-URL-building code. Satellite defaults off (RainViewer's free satellite feed was observed empty during testing) so the chip doesn't default to showing nothing; radar (reliably populated) defaults on.

Wired into `layerState.js`'s share-link/persistence registry and `dataCredits.js` / `DATA_SOURCES.md` for attribution.

## Testing

Added `src/data/weatherOverlay.test.mjs` (8 tests: frame-picking, response parsing against a real captured RainViewer payload, tile URL building against a live-verified tile fetch, param/visibility helpers). Full test suite passes (no regressions vs. `main`), production build succeeds with no new warnings.

title: feat: toggle to route Radio audio into the Voice Model (#52)
body:
Closes #52. Stacked on #114 (OpenSeaMap/OpenSnowMap overlays) for branch history reasons only — no functional dependency between the two.

A dock button (📻, next to the voice-tier button) lets the voice model hear whatever Radio station is currently tuned in ("what did they just say", "what's playing"). Off by default, opt-in only — this is the one voice setting that sends third-party broadcast audio to the realtime API, never inferred from Radio simply being on.

**Mechanism:** `radio.js` arms `crossOrigin='anonymous'` on newly-installed `<audio>` elements (never mutated on a live element, which can't retroactively fix already-buffered bytes); `gevRealtime.js` taps the element via `AudioContext.createMediaElementSource` and mixes it with the mic through a `MediaStreamAudioDestinationNode`, swapped onto the outbound WebRTC track via `RTCRtpSender.replaceTrack` (no renegotiation, instant toggle mid-session). CORS verified live against 8 real Radio Browser stations — 7/8 already send permissive headers; the toggle reports honest live per-station capture status rather than just "on".

**Includes a same-day follow-up fix:** the speaker-tap node for the previous station wasn't disconnected from `context.destination` on a station change, so per the Web Audio spec the audio graph kept each abandoned node+element pair alive indefinitely — one permanent leak per station change in a long session with the toggle on. Fixed with a regression test using a minimal fake Web Audio graph.

title: feat: Rayhunter (EFF cell-site-simulator detector) tap layer (#56)
body:
Closes #56. Stacked on #115 for branch history reasons only — no functional dependency.

[Rayhunter](https://github.com/EFForg/rayhunter) runs on a device the user owns — typically a flashed Orbic mobile hotspot — and flags suspicious cellular behavior it observes. Personal, opt-in, local-network layer: polls the user's own Rayhunter over the same-origin `/api/rayhunter/*` proxy (the device's embedded web server sends no CORS headers, so the browser can't reach it directly) and plots newly-seen warnings at wherever the browser currently is when the warning is first observed — not the device's actual location at detection time, which this app has no way to know. That approximation is surfaced honestly via `getStats().error` rather than presented as precise.

API shape verified against EFForg/rayhunter's real source (route table + stats/diag modules), not guessed.

title: fix: never frame an arrival below ground at elevation
body:
## Repro

Fly to a city well above sea level: Denver (~1,609 m) or Mexico City (~2,240 m). The camera lands under the surface and the frame renders black or from inside the terrain.

At Austin (~150 m) the same error is only a few metres, so it reads as a slightly low camera angle rather than a bug. That is probably why it hasn't come up.

## Cause

Arrival framing runs before the destination's tiles exist, so it has to predict the ground height. All three available predictions are unreliable at that point:

- `globe.getHeight()` is dead here, since the globe sits under the photorealistic tileset with no terrain provider installed.
- The `groundElevation` presets only exist for the cities in `CITY_POIS`.
- The DEM resolves async. Measured cold at one test site it came back about 134 m below the rendered surface, usually after the flight had finished.

So `flyToLandmark` fell back to `groundElevation`, which defaults to sea level. Anything outside the curated city list got framed as if it stood on the ocean.

## Fix

Prediction alone can't solve this, so this does two things.

**Better prediction.** Consult the ground-floor elevation service already in the tree (`src/data/groundFloor.js`, same datum) before falling back to zero. Applied on the coordinate path and the search path, and the cell is warmed so the next nearby arrival is already correct. The search path resolves elevation before the `mayFly()` gate so a cancellation still wins the race.

**Then measurement.** `src/cameraGroundGuard.js` samples the real surface after the flight lands, once tiles have streamed in and `scene.sampleHeight` can be trusted, and lifts the eye if it sits below `MIN_EYE_CLEARANCE_M` (120 m).

The guard stays out of the way. It stops on a clear view, on exhausted attempts, or as soon as the user touches the controls, since a low angle someone chose is better than a correction under their hands. The lift holds heading and pitch so it reads as the shot settling rather than a second flight. Sub-metre differences are ignored.

`groundClearanceDeficitM` is a pure function, so the clearance policy is unit-tested without a scene.

## Verification

- `npm test`: 2,593 pass, 0 fail. That is up 6, which are this PR's tests. The 2 allocation microbenchmarks self-skip on Node 26, same as on `main`.
- `npm run build`: clean.
- `npm run test:track`: 100 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped, including the no-console-errors and no-5xx checks across the full run.
- Checked by hand at elevation: black frame before, arrives above the surface after.

Node 26.7.0.

## Scope

Limited to the ground-framing bug. No new dependencies: `probeMeshFloorM` and the ground-floor service are both already in the tree and unmodified. Other work from the same branch (time-of-day control, route duration caps) is held back for separate PRs.

title: fix: retry photorealistic 3D tiles via Cesium ion when Google returns the EEA 403
body:
## What

Google Maps projects linked to a **European Economic Area billing address** get a hard `403 PERMISSION_DENIED` on satellite and 3D tiles under the [EEA terms effective 2025-07-08](https://developers.google.com/maps/comms/eea/map-tiles). For every EEA user, startup silently fell back to the flat Cesium globe — no photorealistic planet at all, with no key misconfiguration to fix on their side.

This patch keeps the direct Google load as the primary path. When it fails **and** a Cesium ion token is configured, it clears `Cesium.GoogleMaps.defaultApiKey` and retries `createGooglePhotorealistic3DTileset()`, which then streams the **same Google tileset** through Cesium ion asset 2275207 under Cesium's own agreement (1,000 root tiles/month on ion's free Community plan). Without an ion token, behavior is unchanged: the error propagates to the existing flat-globe fallback.

Also updates `CHANGELOG.md` and `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md` per CONTRIBUTING.

## How verified

On an actual EEA-billed setup (Iceland 🇮🇸):
- Reproduced the 403 at the API level: `POST tile.googleapis.com/v1/createSession` and `GET /v1/3dtiles/root.json` both return the documented EEA `PERMISSION_DENIED`.
- Verified the ion route end-to-end: `GET api.cesium.com/v1/assets/2275207/endpoint` → 200, and the Google root tileset it hands back loads fine.
- `npm run build` ✅ and `npm test` ✅ (2,587 pass / 0 fail).
- `npm run test:track`: 97 pass / 3 fail — the 3 failures are the harness's "no console errors" gates catching the **browser-emitted** network log of the initial 403 (`Failed to load resource: 403 … tile.googleapis.com`). That line is logged by Chrome itself before JS can handle the rejection, so it can't be suppressed from the app; it pre-exists this patch on EEA machines (the old code's failing boot logged the same error) and does not occur on non-EEA machines, where the suite should stay fully green. The run itself proves the fallback works: the share-link tests emit `map=photoreal`, i.e. the tileset was live via ion.

## Notes

- Fixes the misleading UX where EEA users see only the OSM/flat globe and reasonably assume their Google key is broken.
- If you'd rather avoid the one-time 403 console line on EEA machines, a follow-up could probe `createSession` once and cache the verdict, but that adds state for a cosmetic gain — kept this minimal instead.

title: feat: add OrcaRouter as a named provider for the AI HUD summary
body:
## Add OrcaRouter as a named provider for the AI HUD summary

God's Eye View is a spy-satellite simulator that turns live public signals — flight transponders, ship beacons, seismographs, public cameras — into a photorealistic 3D globe you can talk to. Today the hands-free voice agent and the five-word intelligence HUD summary are both brokered server-side through OpenAI. This PR adds **OrcaRouter** as a first-class named provider for the HUD summary lane, completely parallel to the existing OpenAI wiring.

### What's wired where

The change mirrors the repo's existing OpenAI HUD summary plumbing (server-side `openAiRealtimeProxy()` in `vite.config.js` → `/api/openai/hud-summary`, consumed by `src/hud.js`) file by file:

| Existing OpenAI path | OrcaRouter parallel |
| --- | --- |
| `vite.config.js` → `middlewares.use('/api/openai/hud-summary')` | `vite.config.js` → `middlewares.use('/api/orcarouter/hud-summary')` |
| `OPENAI_API_KEY` + `OPENAI_HUD_SUMMARY_MODEL` (server-side only) | `ORCAROUTER_API_KEY` + `ORCAROUTER_HUD_SUMMARY_MODEL` (server-side only) |
| `https://api.openai.com/v1/responses` upstream | `https://api.orcarouter.ai/v1/responses` upstream |
| `GEV_RATELIMIT_OPENAI_PER_MIN` opt-in per-IP limiter | `GEV_RATELIMIT_ORCAROUTER_PER_MIN` opt-in per-IP limiter |
| `HUD_SUMMARY_URL` hardcoded to `/api/openai/hud-summary` in `src/hud.js` | `VITE_HUD_SUMMARY_URL` env override (default stays OpenAI) |

OrcaRouter is an OpenAI-compatible AI gateway built for both models and agents. Like OpenRouter, it exposes a provider/model namespace across many models — but it also combines adaptive routing, automatic failover, zero-markup inference, observability, guardrails, and agent-tool governance behind the same endpoint. Adding orcarouter as a first-class provider means this project's users can use that stack directly, without treating OrcaRouter as an anonymous custom base URL.

It also runs gateway-level, zero-trust security for AI agents on the same endpoint — screening every prompt/response and governing every tool call on a default-deny basis, with no application code changes.

Because OrcaRouter speaks the OpenAI Responses API (`/v1/responses`) for its models, the new endpoint reuses the repo's shared five-word summary parser (`extractOpenAiResponseText` + `toFiveWordHudSummary`) — only the upstream base URL, key, and namespaced model id differ. No parsing or client logic is duplicated.

### Verified

- `npm run build` — green.
- `npm test` — 2580 pass; the 2 failures (`aisWatchdogTransport.test.mjs`, `hudAltitudeDatum.test.mjs`) are pre-existing on a pristine checkout under this container's Node 20 runtime (the repo targets Node 24) and are untouched by this change.
- Live end-to-end: with `ORCAROUTER_API_KEY` set and the client pointed at `/api/orcarouter/hud-summary`, the dev server's new endpoint returned **HTTP 200** with a real five-word summary — `{"summary":"San Francisco United States flights","error":null}` — for a San Francisco view context. (Voice still needs OpenAI; this only changes the HUD summary provider.)

### Docs

`README.md` keys table, `.env.example`, `CHANGELOG.md`, and the `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md` proxy baseline were updated to match.

To use it: set `ORCAROUTER_API_KEY`, optionally pick a model via `ORCAROUTER_HUD_SUMMARY_MODEL` (default `orcarouter/fusion-mini`), and point the client at the new endpoint with `VITE_HUD_SUMMARY_URL=/api/orcarouter/hud-summary`.

I'm an engineer on the OrcaRouter team.

## Summary

Adds a filterable AR Experiences data layer that turns Geoverse, MeshMap, ARpoise, and configured Open AR Cloud/OSCP operators into normalized map hotspots. Each source remains independently selectable, expired experiences are controlled by a separate Past filter, and launch links retain provider attribution.

The implementation follows the approved AR content-layer plan while keeping Niantic represented as capability coverage rather than inventing a public experience catalog.

## What Problem This Solves

- Gives users one map layer for discovering nearby mobile or headset AR content without collapsing provider identity.
- Adds a same-origin provider gateway with secret isolation, response limits, timeouts, exact-viewport caching, stale fallback, rate limiting, and bounded federation.
- Persists and shares provider selections through the existing layer-state contract, including voice and scene-policy support.
- Keeps ARpoise disabled by default until its lightweight maintainer/rate-limit gate is cleared, and treats each OSCP operator as its own source.
- Documents provider configuration, security boundaries, data provenance, and rollout constraints.

## Verification Steps

- `npm test` — 2,624 passed, 0 failed.
- `npm run build` — passed; only the existing chunk-size and browser externalization warnings remain.
- `npm run test:track` — 100 passed, 0 failed on the final run.

## Post-Deploy Monitoring & Validation

- For the first 24 hours after enabling each provider, the deployment owner should monitor `/api/ar-content` latency and status, provider `error`/`stale` responses, unexpected `429` responses, timeout/size-limit errors, and request volume versus cache hits.

body:
Really nicely built project — congrats on the reception. I maintain [Better Than HTML](https://betterthanhtml.com/gps), a small collection of free, no-login browser games and tools — its actual purpose is making computers a bit more approachable and fun to learn with, particularly for neurodivergent folks and others who bounce off traditional signup/login flows. One of the tools in there is a live GPS/situational-awareness dashboard that's been aggregating a very similar mix of feeds (ADS-B aircraft, AIS ships, TLE satellites) since earlier this year, arrived at completely independently — wrote up the overlap here: https://betterthanhtml.com/api/exchange/mtgw3zdifwa6

Worth being upfront: it's a one-person, self-funded project running on a small Cloudflare Workers setup — nowhere near the infrastructure to handle the kind of traffic God's Eye View is pulling right now, so this isn't a "let's merge codebases" pitch. But a few things ours does that might be worth considering for yours, since the underlying data is already flowing through both:

1. **Live multi-person position sharing** — a user generates a share code, and anyone with the link sees their live position update in real time alongside the existing data layers (with chat and proximity alerts on top).
2. **Proximity/threshold alerts** — e.g. a toast when a low-flying aircraft (below a set altitude) enters a radius around a point, useful outside controlled airport zones where that's otherwise invisible in normal ADS-B viewers.
3. **Point-to-target / bearing HUD** — lock onto any contact (aircraft, ship, ISS, a dropped pin) and get a live bearing arrow + distance + altitude differential rather than just eyeballing the map.

Both projects are open source, so happy to compare implementations if any of this is useful for God's Eye View at your scale — equally happy to hear if anything in your codebase (the 3D Tiles integration especially) is worth us looking at for ours. No pressure either way, just thought the overlap and the difference in what each of us optimised for was worth flagging.

title: Osm to main
Layers should be registerable from config, not by editing main.js
body:
## Problem

`DataLayerManager.register(layerModule)` is already a clean public API, but the
only way to reach it is `src/main.js`, which imports every layer statically and
then seals registration. So adding a layer from outside the repo means **editing
two vendored files**:

```js
// src/main.js
import { groundworkLayer } from '@ptc/gev-plugins/layer';
dataManager.register(groundworkLayer);
```

Two lines, but in a file that changes often — every re-sync with upstream has to
re-apply them, and anyone who wants to try a third-party layer has to hand-patch
a checkout before they can see whether they like it.

## Proposal

A build-time virtual module. Vite resolves `virtual:gev-extra-layers` to a
generated module whose imports come from a config value:

```
GEV_EXTRA_LAYERS=@ptc/gev-plugins/layer,@ptc/gev-plugins/feature-layers
```

`main.js` then carries **one** line that is not layer-specific:

```js
import extraLayers from 'virtual:gev-extra-layers';
for (const layer of extraLayers) dataManager.register(layer);
```

Build-time, not runtime, because Vite has to see the specifiers to bundle them —
a runtime `import(someString)` would not be bundled and would fall foul of the
CSP anyway.

## Why this shape

- **It is upstream-shaped.** Nothing in it mentions Groundwork or PTC. A user
  with their own layer package benefits identically.
- **It removes local mirror changes rather than adding them.** The two
  `LOCAL MIRROR CHANGE` lines in main.js become an env var, so this file stops
  diverging from upstream.
- **Unset = today's behaviour exactly.** No config, empty array, nothing
  registered, no import cost.

## Requirements

- A module may export a single layer or an array of them; both must work,
  because a package that contributes sixteen layers should not have to expose
  sixteen entry points.
- A specifier that fails to resolve must fail the BUILD, loudly. A layer that
  silently does not appear is indistinguishable from one that appears and has
  no data — the failure mode this project keeps hitting elsewhere.
- Registration order stays deterministic: config order, after the built-ins.

## Not in this issue

The other half of an integration is `vite.config.js`, where server-side proxy
plugins are added. That is a config-time concern with different mechanics
(dynamic import in an ESM config) and deserves its own change.

perf: fix crash when toggling many data streams on at once
body:
## What this fixes
The multi-layer data-toggle rail crashes the renderer when many streams are enabled at once. The user's first report:

> "right now when I toggle on lots of data streams it crashes and stops working — my #1 focus is to fix that and make it smooth."

Reproducible in a real browser: rapid clicks on `#data-toggles` or `#pp-toggles` followed by enough live-source toggles (FIRMS, AIS, Flights, etc.) produce unhandled rejections, a blank scene, and a permanent render stall.

## Why this happens
Rapid concurrent `dataManager.setEnabled` calls each fire a `requestRender` and Cesium swallows the burst; once the burst overshoots a threshold, the data manager falls over. There is no rate limiter and no request coalescer upstream, so a user-triggered burst is the worst case.

## Fix
A small head-of-app patch script (`src/perfInit.js`) loaded **before** `src/main.js` via one `<script type="module">` insertion in `index.html`. It installs two cooperating sinks; both are no-ops once disabled so the path is reversible:

1. **`installRenderCoalescer`** wraps `viewer.scene.requestRender` and queues calls per animation frame so any number of in-flight requests collapse to **one** upstream call. The Cesium scene is in `requestRenderMode`, so this is the right intervention.

2. **`installLayerEnableSerializer`** wraps `dataManager.setEnabled` through a FIFO with:
   - duplicate-layer collapsing (the most recent desired state wins),
   - `max-concurrent = 2` parallel dispatches,
   - `80 ms` start gap between dispatches.

   Rapid toggle bursts no longer crash, duplicate toggles are deduped instead of replayed.

A few Cesium knobs that survive construction are also applied (`viewer.targetFrameRate = 60`, `viewer.resolutionScale` drops DPR > 1 to 0.85). Knobs that are immutable after construction (`scene.msaaSamples`, `context.preserveDrawingBuffer`) are left alone.

## Byte-equality vs. upstream HEAD
Every existing file in `src/`, `vite.config.js`, `scripts/`, and `style.css` is **byte-identical**. The only added files are `src/perfInit.js` and `scripts/perf-profile.mjs`; the only edit is one `<script>` tag insertion in `index.html`. Verified with:

```
git diff upstream/main HEAD -- src/main.js src/data src/voice vite.config.js style.css scripts/
```

returns zero changed lines.

## Verification (real Chromium browser via Playwright)
- `node scripts/perf-profile.mjs` exits 0 — static gate confirms `perfInit.js` exists, precedes `main.js`, declares both sinks.
- Burst test: 15 rapid data-layer toggles in a single pass — zero console errors, zero `viewer.scene.renderError`, both `__perfCoalescerInstalled` and `__perfSerializerInstalled` true, `__perfSerializerStats().totalSerialized > 0`, multi-layer bursts settle cleanly.

## Files
| File | Status |
| --- | --- |
| `src/perfInit.js` | added (~340 LoC) |
| `scripts/perf-profile.mjs` | added (static gate) |
| `index.html` | one `<script>` insertion (loads `src/perfInit.js` before `src/main.js`) |
| everything else | unchanged |

Stock macOS `/bin/bash` is 3.2, where expanding an **empty** array under `set -u` is a fatal `unbound variable`. The keyless `./scripts/dev-fresh.sh` path hit exactly that on the external-keys provenance line and died before doing anything. One-line fix: the `${arr[*]:-}` guard (the same idiom the script already uses for `DEV_UNSET`).

**Verified with `/bin/bash` 3.2.57**: the extracted block runs clean under `set -u` keyless (empty CSV) and keyed (`FIRMS_MAP_KEY,TOMTOM_API_KEY` joined in order); the full launcher boots keyless to a live server; exported keys still show `managed: external` in Provider Settings — provenance semantics unchanged.

Adds a behavioral guard to the dev-fresh test surface (runs the real block from the script both ways) plus a textual assertion pinning the 3.2-safe idiom, and an `Unreleased → Fixed` changelog bullet.

title: fix(radio): keep the stream playing when the Radio layer is turned off
body:
Turning the Radio layer off called `stopRadioPlayback`, so a station you were listening to went silent the moment you hid its globe markers. Presentation and audio are now decoupled — turning the view off never stops what is already on air.

**radio.js.** `disable()` no longer stops playback or tears down the `<audio>` element; it only hides the globe presentation (markers, tuner, click-to-select, in-flight directory fetch) and keeps the selected station. `destroy()` now releases the stream explicitly. A new `radioTransportAllowed()` gate — layer presentable OR a live stream — replaces the presentation-only gate on `play` / `togglePlayback` / `setVolume` / `selectStation` / `cycleStation`. While detached, selection and cycle skip the camera flight and marker work. `getUIState()` gains `audioDetached` / `transportActive`.

**ui.js.** The transport row, mini-player, and cockpit strip (play/pause, stop, next/prev, volume) stay live while a stream is on air with the layer hidden; the tuner, filter, and Enable toggle stay layer-gated. The Radio panel no longer auto-collapses while audio is detached, and the playback line notes "Radio layer hidden". Re-enabling the layer brings presentation back; hitting STOP re-gates everything to inert. No behaviour change when the layer is on.

STOP (button, or voice "stop") is still how you silence it.

**Tests.** `npm test` — 2738 pass. `npm run build` — green. New test: "disabling the Radio layer leaves a live stream audible and its transport controllable". `npm run test:track` not run (needs a live dev server); this change does not touch flight-tracking invariants.

**Note.** This branch was cut from local `main`, which is 4 commits ahead of `bilawalsidhu/main`, so the PR carries those 4 commits plus the radio fix (`7a93bd3`).

title: feat(military): merge adsb.lol + adsb.fi + airplanes.live for the Military layer
body:
The Military Flights layer was fed by adsb.lol's `/v2/mil` alone, so a military contact adsb.lol's receiver network never heard — or had just dropped — showed on nothing, even airborne and squawking. (Field report: a low pass appeared on neither the commercial nor the military layer.)

**What changed.** `/api/adsblol/mil` now fans out to three `/v2/mil` feeds — adsb.lol, adsb.fi, airplanes.live — in parallel with an 8 s per-feed timeout, unions the rows by ICAO hex keeping the copy with the freshest position (`seen_pos` then `seen`; a positioned row always beats an unpositioned duplicate; ties fall to feed order so adsb.lol stays authoritative), and caches the merged `{ ac, total, sources, msg, now }` for 12 s. A feed that errors or times out is skipped; a stale cache is served only if all three fail; the `X-ADS-B-Sources` header names the contributors. The route, the response shape, and both consumers (`militaryFlights.js`, `militaryRegistry.js`) are unchanged.

Still ADS-B only — an aircraft transmitting nothing appears on no feed.

**Files.** `vite.config.js` — exported pure `mergeMilitaryFeeds` / `militaryRowPositionAgeSeconds` and the rewritten `military-flights-proxy` plugin. `src/data/militaryFeedMerge.test.mjs` — 10 cases (union/dedupe, freshest-wins, positioned-beats-unpositioned, tie order, partial and total feed failure, bad-hex rows, non-array input). Attribution + docs in `dataCredits.js`, `DATA_SOURCES.md`, `README.md`, `CHANGELOG.md` (adsb.fi + airplanes.live, ODbL).

**Tests.** `npm test` — 2746 pass. `npm run build` — green. `npm run test:track` not run (needs a live dev server); this is a dev-proxy plus a pure function, nothing in the render path.
