title: docs(cctv): state the project's position on camera frame content
body:
**Intent:** record, in the file that documents every camera source's terms, what the project does with the *content* of the frames those sources serve. Documentation only — no code, and no change to the existing "The line" commitment in the README.

Refs #269.

## What changed

One entry in `DATA_SOURCES.md`'s live-source notes. The file documented licence and attribution for Austin, Caltrans, TfL and community packs but never what a frame may contain, and the README's "The line" paragraph covers *features* — named-person search, face recognition, tracking individuals — rather than relayed imagery. For a project positioned around public spatial intelligence, that gap is easier to close than to keep answering.

The note records what the code actually does: frames are piped through untouched, nothing is blurred or detected, the server never holds a frame, `.gev-cache/` holds feed JSON rather than imagery, and only server-registered URLs are fetched.

## How it was verified

Every claim was checked against the source before it was written, and two came out weaker than #269 assumes. Both are stated precisely in the note rather than flatteringly:

- **Retention.** `proxyMediaResponse` relays the *upstream's* own `Cache-Control` and only substitutes `no-store` when the upstream sends none (`server/providers/local.js:2344`). So "frames are served `no-store`" would have been false; browser-side retention follows the provider's policy, not this app's. The note says that.
- **No processing.** `sharp` is a devDependency and appears in `local.js` only as the word "sharpen" (a post-process toggle). The library is imported solely by `scripts/qa-flyroute-cinema.mjs` and `tools/`, never in the live frame path.
- **Not persisted.** `.gev-cache/` writers are adsbdb, firms, overpass, military-installations and celestrak. No camera imagery.
- **Registered URLs only.** Matches `SECURITY.md:63`.

Gates on `docs/cctv-frame-content-policy`, Node 26.5.0 / Windows 11:

- `npm test` → `tests 2953 · pass 2947 · fail 0 · skipped 6`
- `npm run format:check` → `Checked 71 adopted files.`
- `npm run build` → `✓ built in 3.17s`

## Notes for reviewers

This is a policy statement in your voice, not mine, so treat the wording as a proposal — particularly the last sentence ("a source pack that needs frames altered before they can be shown is a source pack that shouldn't be added"), which sets contribution policy and may be further than you want to go in a data file. Happy to cut it or soften it.

#269 itself rates confidence as "Suspected" and allows that you may consider the existing README language sufficient. If that's your read, closing it is a legitimate outcome and this PR should just be dropped.

## Out of scope / follow-up

- No pointer added from `CONTRIBUTING.md`'s source-pack section, though #269 notes that gap too. `DATA_SOURCES.md` is what its acceptance criteria asks for, and `CONTRIBUTING.md` has had several recent maintainer edits; a one-line pointer is an easy follow-up if you want one.

> 🤖 Claude Code helped

title: Search box advertises "or coordinates" but has no coordinate parser; keyless users get "Search failed" for every query
body:
The location search input is labelled:

```html
aria-label="Search location by name or coordinates"
```

but no coordinate-string parser exists anywhere in `src/`. `searchAndFlyTo`
refuses everything before parsing anything:

```js
// src/locations.js:349-351
export async function searchAndFlyTo(viewer, query, options = {}) {
  const apiKey = window.__GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY__ || import.meta.env.GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY;
  if (!apiKey) throw new Error('No Google Maps API key available for geocoding');
```

so on a keyless install the search box cannot service any input at all.

**Repro** (fresh clone, no `.env` keys, `npm run dev`):

1. Click LOCATION in the dock, then the search icon
2. Type any of the following and press Enter

| Input | Expected | Actual |
|---|---|---|
| `Lewiston, NY` | geocode, or a clear "needs a Google key" message | `Search failed` toast |
| `43.1731, -79.0384` | fly to those coordinates (per the aria-label) | `Search failed` toast |
| `London` | fly to the bundled `CITY_POIS.london` preset | `Search failed` toast |

Console for all three:

```
[Search] Geocoding failed: Error: No Google Maps API key available for geocoding
```

**Why it reads as broken rather than as a missing key:** the toast says
"Search failed", and the same box is the only obvious way to navigate. A new
keyless user concludes search is broken. The 8 `CITY_POIS` entries are already
client-side and need no network, and coordinate parsing needs no provider either.

**Suggested fix**, roughly in order of value:

1. Parse a coordinate pair before the key check and fly directly. Honours the
   existing aria-label and works fully keyless.
2. Match `CITY_POIS` names before geocoding, so `London` works keyless.
3. When no key is configured, make the toast say so ("Add a Google Maps key in
   POWER UP to search by place name") instead of "Search failed".
4. Optionally an OSM/Nominatim keyless geocoder fallback, respecting their
   usage policy.

Happy to send a PR for 1 to 3 if the approach sounds right.

title: `npm run doctor` reports "OpenSky OAuth credentials not configured" even when keyless anonymous flights work, and ignores OPENSKY_AUTH_MODE
body:
The capability line is derived only from the presence of two credentials:

```js
// scripts/setup-doctor.mjs:142
flights: configured('OPENSKY_CLIENT_ID') && configured('OPENSKY_CLIENT_SECRET')
```

It never consults `OPENSKY_AUTH_MODE`, so an install that is working perfectly
is reported as unconfigured.

**Repro:**

1. Fresh clone, no OpenSky credentials
2. Optionally set `OPENSKY_AUTH_MODE=anon` in `.env` (makes no difference)
3. `npm run doctor` prints:

```
Flights: OpenSky OAuth credentials not configured
```

4. But the proxy returns a full feed:

```
$ curl -s 'http://localhost:4173/api/opensky?lamin=25&lomin=-125&lamax=50&lomax=-66' \
  | head -c 80
{"time":1789220864,"states":[["39de4e","TVF15FY ","France",...
```

That response was 1.59 MB, 12,011 aircraft. The browser layer also reports
`[Data:Flights] Updated: 12020 aircraft`.

Verified the doctor does read `.env` (adding `LL2_API_TOKEN` flips the Launch
Library line to `[OK] ... (dotenv files)`), so this is the flights branch
specifically, not env loading.

**Suggested fix:** factor in `OPENSKY_AUTH_MODE` and report the mode that will
actually be used, e.g.

- `anon` (or no credentials): `Flights: keyless anonymous access (rate-limited)`
- credentials present with `oauth`/`basic`/`auto`: current wording

The README already documents flights as a keyless layer, so the doctor is the
only thing suggesting otherwise.

title: Browser geocoding cannot work with a referrer-restricted key, so SECURITY.md's guidance forces an unrestricted key in the page bundle
body:
This is the most consequential of the three, because following the documented
security guidance breaks search, and making search work requires ignoring it.

`SECURITY.md` says of `GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY`:

> **Restrict it** (HTTP referrer + API restriction to the required Google APIs)

But the geocoder calls the Maps **web service** endpoint directly from the browser:

```js
// src/locations.js:359
let url = `https://maps.googleapis.com/maps/api/geocode/json?address=${encodeURIComponent(query)}&key=${apiKey}`;
```

and Google refuses referrer-restricted keys on that endpoint. Verbatim response:

```json
{ "status": "REQUEST_DENIED",
  "error_message": "API keys with referer restrictions cannot be used with this API." }
```

HTTP referrer restrictions apply to the Maps JavaScript API and the client SDKs,
not the web service endpoints. So the browser-exposed key must be either:

- **referrer-restricted**, and search is permanently broken, or
- **unrestricted by referrer**, in which case a key that is visible in devtools
  by design (via the `define` block in `build/vite.js`) can be lifted and spent
  by anyone who loads the page.

Neither is acceptable, and the docs currently recommend the first while the code
requires the second.

**Suggested fixes**, any one of which resolves it:

1. Move geocoding to a server-side proxy (`/api/google/geocode`) using
   `GOOGLE_MAPS_SERVER_API_KEY`, consistent with how Places and Street View are
   already handled. The key then takes an IP restriction, which the web service
   does honour, and it stops being browser-visible at all.
2. Use the Maps JavaScript API Geocoder client-side instead of the web service,
   which does honour referrer restrictions.
3. At minimum, correct `SECURITY.md` to state that the browser key cannot carry
   Geocoding API under a referrer restriction, and scope the documented browser
   restriction to Map Tiles API only.

Option 1 also fixes issue 1's root cause for keyed users.

**Related note on the IP restriction:** when configuring
`GOOGLE_MAPS_SERVER_API_KEY` by IP, both IPv4 and IPv6 need listing. A dual-stack
host egressed over IPv6 and got `API_KEY_IP_ADDRESS_BLOCKED` with an IPv4-only
restriction in place, which is easy to misread as a key problem. Worth a line in
SECURITY.md.

title: `vite build` + `vite preview` drops most provider proxies; missing routes return index.html with HTTP 200 instead of failing
body:
Most provider middleware registers only `configureServer`, not
`configurePreviewServer`, so a built app loses those routes. Because the SPA
fallback answers anything unmatched, the client receives `text/html` with a
**200** where it expects JSON, so nothing surfaces as an error. The app looks
healthy and has no live data.

**Repro:**

```bash
npm ci && npm run build
npx vite preview --port 4174 &          # built app
npm run dev &                            # dev server, for comparison
curl -s 'http://localhost:4174/api/opensky?lamin=40&lomin=-80&lamax=44&lomax=-76' | head -c 40
# => <!DOCTYPE html><html lang="en"><head>
curl -s 'http://localhost:4173/api/opensky?lamin=40&lomin=-80&lamax=44&lomax=-76' | head -c 40
# => {"time":1789220864,"states":[["39de4e",...
```

Comparing all routes across both servers (HTML body ⇒ route absent):

| Lost in a production build | Still present |
|---|---|
| `/api/opensky` (live flights) | `/api/opensky-track` |
| `/api/adsblol/mil` (military) | `/api/ais-live` |
| `/api/adsbdb/*` (aircraft metadata) | `/api/radio/*` |
| `/api/firms` (active fires) | `/api/military-installations` |
| `/api/terrain/heights` (HUD elevation) | `/api/weather-effects` |
| `/api/overpass` | `/api/regional-brief` |
| `/api/cctv/health` | |
| `/api/gbfs` (bikeshare) | |
| `/api/tomtom/*` (traffic) | |
| `/api/setup/status` (**Provider Settings panel**) | |

Losing `/api/setup/status` is particularly awkward: the POWER UP panel is how
the README tells users to add keys, and it is unavailable in the only build
mode a self-hoster would reasonably leave running long-term.

**Impact.** `npm run dev` becomes the only way to run the app with its full
feature set, which conflicts with SECURITY.md describing the Vite server as a
development/preview server not intended for exposure. Anyone self-hosting
(behind their own auth, a tunnel, or a tailnet) is pushed onto the dev server.

**Suggested fixes:**

1. Register every provider plugin under both `configureServer` and
   `configurePreviewServer`. Several already do this (`local.js:1103-1104`
   pairs them), so it looks like an oversight rather than a design decision.
2. Make an unmatched `/api/*` path return a JSON 404 rather than falling through
   to the SPA fallback, so this class of bug fails loudly. Worth doing
   regardless of fix 1.
3. If some proxies genuinely cannot work in preview, have `npm run build` warn
   and document which layers a built app cannot serve.

**Environment:** aacfa06, Node 24.21.0, npm 11.19.0, Ubuntu 24.04.

title: Global status chip reads LOAD FAILED on a relayed adsb.lol 429 and on the installations zoom-in prompt
body:
## Summary

While tracking a grounded aircraft at JFK and pressing NEXT in Cockpit, the global status chip repeatedly reads **LOAD FAILED** even though every layer is still populated and the new target loads a few seconds later. Reproduced on `main` @ aacfa06 with the chip and the data manager instrumented; two independent triggers, both false alarms.

## What the chip is

`#global-loading-status` is driven by `src/loadingFeedback.js`. It aggregates every registered layer; when a loading/refresh batch settles, the terminal label is LOAD FAILED if **any participating layer carries an `error` string at that instant** (`terminalFromParticipantStats`) or a `refresh-failed` manager event landed during the batch. The manager itself derives `refresh-failed` from the same field (`refreshFailureFromStats` reads `stats.error`).

## Trigger 1: a relayed adsb.lol 429 becomes a 45 s failure loop

- `server/providers/aircraft/adsb-lol.js` is documented as "on upstream failure, serves a stale cached response", but only the `catch` path does that. A non-OK status is relayed verbatim, so an upstream **429 is forwarded to the browser** even when a 12 s-old cache is sitting right there.
- `src/data/militaryFlights.js` treats a 429 as a 45 s cooldown (`BACKOFF_INTERVAL`). Every `update()` inside that window returns early with `_lastError = 'adsb.lol rate limited'`, so every refresh — the 15 s poll, and any tracking resolve — is reported as `refresh-failed` **without a network call**.
- Captured timeline (ms since page load), military layer only:

```
155042 refresh-transition
155208 refresh-failed  Error: adsb.lol rate limited   <- real upstream 429 relayed by the proxy
170060 refresh-transition
170062 refresh-failed  Error: adsb.lol rate limited   <- 2 ms: cooldown, no fetch
185049 refresh-transition
185049 refresh-failed  Error: adsb.lol rate limited   <- 0 ms: cooldown, no fetch
200047 refresh-transition
200242 refresh                                        <- cooldown over, recovered
```

Each `refresh-failed` flipped the chip to LOAD FAILED while the layer still held 140 aircraft. Cockpit NEXT is just when the operator is looking at the chip.

## Trigger 2: the installations "zoom in" prompt is stored as an error

- In Cockpit the camera looks at the horizon, so `viewer.camera.computeViewRectangle()` cannot bound the view and `militaryInstallations.js` sets `status: 'zoom-in'` **with the prompt text in `state.error`**.
- `layerFeedState` and the layer row already treat `zoom-in` as guidance (nominal), but `normalizeLayerLoading` and `refreshFailureFromStats` do not: any batch the installations layer participates in ends LOAD FAILED. Two of the six captured flips had only this layer in "error":

```
125084  military-installations st=zoom-in err="Zoom in to load mapped installation context" n=0
200312  military-installations st=zoom-in err="Zoom in to load mapped installation context" n=0
```

The layer never called Overpass in this state; nothing actually failed.

## Fix (PR to follow)

1. **Proxy**: on an upstream 429/5xx serve the cached body as `X-ADS-B-Cache: STALE` (200) and back off from upstream for `Retry-After` (bounded 5–120 s, default 30 s for 429 / 15 s for 5xx), mirroring the OpenSky proxy's cooldown. A 429 with nothing cached is still relayed.
2. **Installations**: `zoom-in` is set without an error string; the row and toast read the prompt from `statusMessage` (already produced by `installationFeedback`).
3. **Chip**: `normalizeLayerLoading` ignores `error` for guidance statuses (`zoom-in`, `empty`, `idle`), the same carve-out `layerFeedState` already has.

Follow-up worth its own issue: a refresh that fails while the layer still has data probably deserves a STALE terminal state rather than LOAD FAILED. The first-run code already ledgers the same aggregation gap for the keyless FIRMS "KEY REQUIRED" case.

## Environment

macOS, Node 26.3.0, `main` @ aacfa06, keyed install (OpenSky OAuth, all providers configured), Chrome.

title: fix(status): stop false LOAD FAILED from a relayed adsb.lol 429 and the installations zoom prompt
body:
Fixes #370.

Military aircraft remain available during an adsb.lol 429/5xx when the proxy holds a cached response. Retry-After is bounded to 5–120 seconds, with defaults of 30 seconds for 429 and 15 seconds for server errors. Cold-cache failures remain errors and carry a retry delay. Cached fallback cancels the failing body immediately, and cooldown starts when the response arrives.

Cached responses expose their age. The browser retains the original observation times, labels fallback data STALE, and resumes fresh updates after recovery. Installation zoom guidance stays in the layer row without turning a successful load into LOAD FAILED; independent feed and manager errors still count as failures.

Bilawal’s original commit is retained, with a follow-up fixing cached timestamps and adding regression checks. The browser’s cold-cache retry behavior and broader global loading-state design are unchanged.

Validation:

- 194 focused tests passed, including cached position replay, slow/stalled 5xx responses, Retry-After dates/bounds, recovery, and independent errors during guidance.
- Full unit/allocation suite passed (one platform skip); doctor, build, format and package boundaries passed.
- All 108 tracking/browser regression checks passed, with no console errors or HTTP 5xx across the run.
- Chromium inspection at global and oblique views confirmed the STALE aircraft row and installation zoom guidance. The first QA attempt encountered stale Vite optimized dependencies; rebuilding those in the temporary checkout resolved startup, and the final run exited successfully.

title: feat: ham radio layers — DX spots, activations, DXpeditions, beacons, propagation, repeaters, stations (HamRig)
body:
## Summary

Seven new data layers bring the amateur-radio "DX Workbench" onto the globe, fed through a same-origin proxy (`/api/hamrig/*`, `src/hamrig/`) that talks to [HamRig](https://hamrig.com) (the maintainer's own project, API use granted), POTA, SOTA, KC2G and AD1C's cty.dat.

| Layer (id · token) | What it draws | Sources |
|---|---|---|
| DX Spots (`dx-spots` · j) | live DX-cluster spots coloured by band, ageing out over 60 min, great-circle arcs DX↔spotter (dashed when a position is only an entity/call-area centroid) | HamRig live WebSocket + REST seed, cty.dat, HamRig callsign DB on demand |
| Activations (`ham-activations` · n) | POTA / WWFF / BOTA spots (SOTA opt-in, see below) | api.pota.app, HamRig (WWFF, WWBOTA) |
| DXpeditions (`dxpeditions` · p) | NG3K announced operations sized by Club Log most-wanted rank | HamRig |
| Beacons (`ham-beacons` · o) | the 18 NCDXF/IBP beacons with the live 10-second schedule; VHF beacons after login | static table, HamRig |
| Propagation (`ham-propagation` · v) | grayline + twilight rings, NOAA OVATION aurora, GIRO ionosondes with MUF(3000), VOACAP area coverage from a home grid | HamRig, prop.kc2g.com |
| Repeaters (`ham-repeaters` · l) | FM and D-STAR repeaters around the view | HamRig curated table |
| Ham Stations (`ham-stations` · y) | callsign lookups with QRZ-derived positions; worked DXCC, worked grids and rotator beam after login | HamRig, cty.dat |

Plus a HAM RADIO companion panel (share token `h`) with seven tabs and eight voice tools (`lookup_ham_station`, `show_dx_spots`, `tune_to_dx_spot`, `show_ham_activations`, `show_dxpeditions`, `show_ham_propagation`, `show_ham_beacons`, `show_ham_repeaters`) with English and German cue words.

## Design points

- **Tune to a spot picks a receiver near the spotter, never near the DX.** The area around a transmitting station is skip zone; the spotter proves a path exists. The chooser prefers a PSKReporter station that heard the DX on that band in the last 45 min, otherwise the spotter (precise position when known, else call-area/entity centroid, stated in the result), and then opens the Web Receivers dock. The browser QA proves it: receiver 101 km from the spotter, 11 247 km from the DX.
- **Callsigns resolve locally** through cty.dat (exact → designators → call-area centroids → longest prefix, WAE-aware), so bulk placement never hits HamRig; precise positions come from HamRig's callsign database only for selected stations.
- **Privacy:** station records are scrubbed of e-mail, postal address, ZIP, county and biography before serialization; rotator rows lose their gateway key; a HamRig login is optional and its token never leaves the server.
- **SOTA is off by default** (`HAMRIG_SOTA_ENABLED=0`): the SOTA API terms require prior approval for AI-written clients, so a deployment enables it only once it holds that approval.
- **Context-mode companions unchanged:** the ham layers switch off on Context entry and restore on exit.

## Verification

- Unit tests for every pure module and the proxy against fixtures captured from the live feeds (3087 pass).
- `scripts/qa-ham-radio.mjs`: 29 browser checks (all seven layers draw, all eight voice tools, the spotter-side rule, dock focus).
- `npm run build` succeeds.
- An adversarial review pass (six lenses, one skeptic per finding) confirmed 27 findings; all are fixed in the second commit.

This branch is stacked on `feat/web-receivers` (#279) because spot tuning reuses the web-receiver ranking; the diff will shrink to the ham commits once #279 merges.

title: feat(taps): shared address contract for receiver taps
body:
First PR in the receiver-taps lane, per your sequencing note on #171 — the shared contract the rest stack on, kept to one thing.

## What this is

Receiver taps (#57 RTL-SDR/dump1090, #56 Rayhunter, #7 TAK, #6 Meshtastic) differ from every other provider in this tree in one way that matters: **the upstream address comes from the user at runtime**, not from a fixed constant. That makes each tap route an SSRF surface unless the address is constrained. Right now each tap would answer that question for itself, and they would disagree — my own Rayhunter branch currently accepts any host and blocks only the cloud metadata address, which is not a rule I want four layers each reinventing.

`parseTapAddress()` is the single place the rule lives:

> A tap may address loopback or an RFC1918 private network, plus the `localhost` and `*.local` (mDNS) names. Nothing else.

That is what a tap *is* — reading your own device on your own network. A tap pointed at a public address is either a mistake or the proxy being used as a confused deputy, and both get the same answer. Link-local (169.254/16) is excluded wholesale, so the metadata address is unreachable by construction rather than by blocklist.

## The one subtle bit

I deliberately did **not** reuse `isNonGlobalIpv4()` from `radio/stations.js`, even though it looks like exactly the right function. It reports malformed input like `999.1.1.1` as non-global — the safe direction for the radio proxy's *"is this public enough to fetch?"* test, but it **inverts** into *allowing* garbage under a tap's *"is this local enough to fetch?"* test. A positive allowlist can't invert that way. There's a test pinning that case so nobody later "simplifies" it back into a negation.

## Documented non-goals

Written into the module header so they don't read as oversights:

1. **No general hostname resolution.** A name other than `localhost`/`*.local` is rejected outright rather than resolved-and-pinned. Local devices are reachable by IP or mDNS, so arbitrary names buy nothing and would drag in DNS-rebinding defence that `radio/transport.js` already shows is not small.
2. **No IPv6.** Zone-index handling (`%eth0`) is platform-specific and no tap has needed it. Rejected explicitly rather than half-supported.

## Scope

Address rule only. **The recorded-fixture harness is not here** — you asked for a fixture per tap so CI can run without hardware, and I'd rather design that against a real recorded response than guess at an API with no consumer. It lands with the first tap. Say the word if you'd rather see both together.

Nothing is wired to this yet; it's the base the tap PRs rebase onto. I'll port Rayhunter/TAK/WiGLE/Meshtastic onto it one at a time as you asked, each rewritten as a `server/providers/*` plugin since `vite.config.js` is now 3 lines.

## Verification

`npm test` 2984 pass / 0 fail (with `GEV_REQUIRE_ALLOCATION_GATE=1` on Node 24.19.0), `npm run build` clean, `npm run test:track` 108 passed / 0 failed, `format:check` and `check:boundaries` clean.

12 contract tests cover each allowed range and its boundaries, public addresses, link-local, malformed dotted-quads, URL-shaped input, port validation, IPv6, and non-string input.

Formatting adoption is a separate mechanical commit per CONTRIBUTING — the six sibling modules in `server/providers/common/` are already adopted, so this one matches them.

﻿Resolves #361

### Description
The search input in placeSearch advertised "Search cities or coordinates...", but:
1. Entering raw coordinates (43.1731, -79.0384, 40° 42' 46" N, 74° 00' 21" W, or MGRS) went straight to external geocoders (Google / Photon), which often failed or returned "Search failed".

title: fix: handle antimeridian crossing in clampBoundsAroundCenter
body:
## Summary

Fixes #352.

`clampBoundsAroundCenter()` computed the longitude span as a plain `bounds.east - bounds.west`, which assumes longitude is linear. It isn't: a small viewport crossing the antimeridian can be represented as `west = 179.98, east = -179.98`, and the plain subtraction gives `-359.96` instead of the actual ~0.04° span. The clamped output then also drifted outside the normal `[-180, 180)` range.

- Added `longitudeSpanDeg(west, east)`: wraps the span through 360° when `east < west`.
- Added `normalizeLonDeg(lon)`: normalizes a longitude back into `[-180, 180)`, reusing the same wrap idiom already used by `destinationPoint()` in this file.
- `clampBoundsAroundCenter()` now uses both, so the returned `west`/`east` stay in range and the span stays correct near the date line.

Non-antimeridian behavior is unchanged: `longitudeSpanDeg` reduces to a plain subtraction when `east >= west`, and `normalizeLonDeg` is a no-op for longitudes already in range — verified by the pre-existing span-clamp tests still passing unmodified.

## Test plan
- [x] Added the antimeridian regression case to `trafficBounds.test.mjs` (from the issue's repro)
- [x] `node --test src/data/trafficBounds.test.mjs` — 10/10 pass
- [x] `npm test` (full suite) — 3085 pass, 0 fail, 6 skipped (Node-24-calibrated allocation microbenchmarks, expected on Node 22)
- [x] `npm run build` — clean
- [x] `node scripts/format.mjs --check` — clean
- [ ] `npm run test:track` — not run. This harness drives the flight-tracking camera/3D regression suite via headless Chromium against a running preview server; it doesn't touch traffic bounds or this code path, and my local Node version (22) is below the project's required 24-26, so I didn't want to report a false pass/fail on an unrelated harness. Happy to run it if you'd like before merge.

title: fix(qa): safely resolve puppeteer.executablePath across QA harnesses
body:
### Summary
In modern Puppeteer runtime environments, calling `.catch()` directly on `puppeteer.executablePath()` can throw `TypeError: puppeteer.executablePath(...).catch is not a function` when `executablePath()` returns a synchronous string or throws synchronously during module evaluation.

This specifically caused issues when running test suites such as `src/qaVesselCardsHarness.test.mjs`, which imports `scripts/qa-vessel-cards.mjs` where top-level candidate evaluation occurs.

### Changes
Wrapped `puppeteer.executablePath()` evaluation in `Promise.resolve().then(...)` across all 28 QA scripts and regression runners:
```javascript
// Before
await puppeteer.executablePath().catch(() => null)

// After
await Promise.resolve()
  .then(() => puppeteer.executablePath())
  .catch(() => null)
```

title: feat(cctv): add Finland — Fintraffic road weather cameras as a fourth source pack
body:
Austin, Caltrans and TfL cover two countries. This adds a fourth keyless pack: Fintraffic's road weather cameras, covering all of Finland, via Digitraffic's open API. Related to #209 (open camera integrations).

### What changed

- **New source pack** (`server/providers/cctv/sources.js`). One keyless GeoJSON request to `tie.digitraffic.fi/api/weathercam/v1/stations` — ~810 stations, of which ~808 are `GATHERING` and carry ~2,260 in-collection presets (measured 2026-09-13; the catalog grows). A station's *presets* are its fixed views and share its position, so one preset is one camera; 300 are kept, prioritized against seven anchors along Finland's main road spine so the cap keeps national coverage rather than just Helsinki. Stations that aren't `GATHERING` and presets that aren't `inCollection` are dropped, so the mesh carries no dead cameras.
- **Frame URLs are built, not read.** `FINTRAFFIC_IMAGE_ORIGIN + presetId + '.jpg'`, with the preset id gated on `/^C\d{7}$/` and required to start with its station id. No upstream field can steer the proxy off-host or escape the path. The catalog fetch refuses redirects and sends the `Digitraffic-User` header the service asks clients to identify themselves with, plus gzip.
- **No heading exists in this dataset**, so presets take the id-hash fallback and the low-confidence pose personality, exactly like headingless Austin and TfL cameras. (The per-preset `direction` on Digitraffic's detail endpoint is road-register relative — `INCREASING_DIRECTION` means "towards higher road addresses" — not a bearing, and it isn't in the bulk list anyway.) Because the hash keys on the preset id, a station's co-located presets fan apart instead of stacking on one bearing.
- **Road-surface views get a steep pose.** About a quarter of Finnish presets are "Tienpinta" views: a camera a metre or two up staring at the asphalt. Given the road pose they aim at the horizon. They now get pitch -55° / range 220 m / mount 6 m — each value the boundary `src/data/cctv.js` already clamps registered poses to, so the prior is as close to a downward-staring camera as the renderer represents and nothing is silently rewritten. Identifying them from the preset id is an **observed convention, not a documented contract**, and the constant says so with the evidence: 575/575 presets over a systematic 202-station national sample have `directionCode` equal to their id suffix, and 140/140 suffix-09 presets are named "Tienpinta" — but a separate sample found one counterexample (`C1853409`), so it's ~99%. It steers a draggable pose prior, never which cameras exist, so a rare miss costs one gizmo nudge.
- **10-minute frame cadence** (`cctvLod.js`). Digitraffic publishes one JPEG per station collection interval — 600 s on every station sampled, borne out by the images' `Last-Modified` headers. The default 5-minute cadence would fetch each image twice per update.
- **Attribution.** CC BY 4.0, attribution required: registered in `DATA_CREDITS` so it surfaces in the Data attribution popover, plus the `DATA_SOURCES.md` licence row and source note.
- **Docs.** `CHANGELOG.md`, `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md`, `README.md` (which said Austin/California/London and "~800 cameras"), and `.env.example` for the two new env vars — both of which are actually read, `CCTV_FINTRAFFIC_ENABLED` in `catalog.js` and `CCTV_FINTRAFFIC_MAX_SOURCES` in `sources.js` (cf. #270). `CCTV_FINTRAFFIC_ENABLED=0` is the kill switch; the pack fails independently of the other three.

### One trade-off to decide on: the default source cap (`87d6ae8`)

That commit raises `DEFAULT_CCTV_MAX_SOURCES` 900 → 1,200, and it's isolated so you can drop it on its own.

The merge truncates by position (`mergedSources.slice(0, maxCount)`). Austin + Caltrans + TfL already fill 800 at their default caps, so a fourth pack appended after them is cut to 100 — and to nothing the moment an earlier pack's cap is raised. 1,200 isn't a new ceiling: it's the hard bound `getCctvSources` already clamps `CCTV_MAX_SOURCES` to, and the size `HEALTH_MAX_ENTRIES` was chosen to cover. It holds all four packs at their defaults (250+300+250+300 = 1,100) with headroom for file/env entries.

This is the only change here that shifts a runtime default for every user rather than just for the new pack. Drop the commit and everything still works — Finland is just truncated. Happy to go the other way instead (a smaller Fintraffic cap that fits under 900) if you'd rather not move the default.

### On #269 (face/plate content)

These are road **weather** cameras: highway and trunk-road views published by the national traffic agency under CC BY 4.0, refreshed on a 10-minute cadence, with a quarter of them pointed at the road surface. Nothing is cached or rehosted — frames are proxied live from `weathercam.digitraffic.fi`, same as the existing packs. A 10-minute stills cadence is a poor instrument for following anyone, and the pack adds no identity surface. It doesn't resolve #269, which asks for a stated policy rather than a per-pack judgement, but it doesn't add to the gap either.

### How I verified it

- `npm ci`, `npm run doctor -- --json`, `npm run format:check` (257 files), `npm run check:boundaries`, `npm test` (**3191 tests, 3190 pass, 0 fail**, 1 pre-existing runtime-gated skip), `npm run build` — all green on Node 26.8.2, on the branch rebased onto `cf149ec`. `package-lock.json` untouched.
- **`npm run test:track` I could not run** — my machine has no browser-capable environment (Chrome installs but is missing 20 system libraries). Flagging it honestly rather than claiming it; happy to act on anything it reports.
- 9 new unit tests (`src/data/cctvFintraffic.test.mjs`) covering preset→camera mapping, the official-origin frame URL, filtering of dead stations / uncollected presets / malformed ids, elevation handling, the Digitraffic header and redirect refusal, the cap and fail-soft paths, and the two poses.
- Live against a dev server: `/api/cctv/sources` returns 1,100 cameras (250/300/250/300), `/api/cctv/frame/…` returns `image/jpeg` with `X-CCTV-Source: upstream-image`, surface presets carry exactly one pose and road presets another, and `CCTV_FINTRAFFIC_ENABLED=0` drops the total back to 800.
- Station/preset counts, the 600 s cadence, the elevation semantics and the preset-id convention were all measured against the live API on 2026-09-13, not taken from docs.

A screenshot of Finland in the mesh follows in a comment.

title: feat: add Mesh Network layer (MeshCore public node map)
body:
## What

Adds a new **Mesh Network** data layer showing the public [MeshCore](https://meshcore.dev) LoRa mesh network worldwide — ~60,000 community-reported nodes (Clients, Repeaters, Room Servers, Sensors). This is the same open data that backs community deployments like [cascadiamesh.org/map](https://cascadiamesh.org/map/): both this app and cascadiamesh.org's map ultimately read from the public `map.meshcore.io/api/v1/nodes` feed.

- 🟢 Keyless, no signup — matches GEV's "start without API keys" philosophy.
- Nodes render as points, color-coded by last-heard freshness (recent/stale/old/extinct/manually-added — the same buckets the official MeshCore map uses) and sized by node type (Repeater/Room Server infrastructure a bit larger than Client/Sensor).
- Click-to-inspect: name, type, radio parameters (frequency/bandwidth/spreading factor/coding rate), last-seen time, public key.
- Status legend in the layer toggle row.

## How it's built (mirrors existing layer conventions)

- `server/providers/meshcore.js` — proxy for the upstream feed: memory + disk cache, 10 min TTL, single-flight refresh, serve-stale-on-failure. Same shape as `firmsProxy`; chosen because the upstream has no bounding-box query support, so a full refetch (~60k nodes, tens of MB) is the only option and minimizing how often that happens matters.
- `src/data/meshcoreNodes.js` — pure record-trim/normalize logic (drops the embedded `meshcore://` deep link and inserted/updated-by keys, the biggest contributors to the raw feed's size), shared by the proxy and unit-tested independently of any network call.
- `src/data/meshcore.js` — the Cesium layer itself, following the same lifecycle contract (`init/enable/disable/update/getStats/getRowControls/destroy`) and click-to-inspect pattern (`src/overlays/worldOverlay.js`) as `bikeshare.js`.
- Wired into the layer registry, toggle panel, and share-link state (`src/standalone/data.js`, `src/data/layerState.js`) the same way every other layer is.
- Documented in `README.md`, `DATA_SOURCES.md`, `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md`, and `CHANGELOG.md`; credited in `src/data/dataCredits.js`.

**Out of scope for this PR (by design):** voice-agent integration (`src/voice/gevActions.js` / `server/providers/openai/tools.js`). The layer is fully usable via the UI toggle but not yet voice-controllable — happy to follow up with that separately if there's interest.

## How I verified it

- `npm run build` — clean.
- `npm test` — 3185/3185 passing (14 new tests covering node normalization/filtering and the layer's freshness-status, color, and click-selection logic).
- `npm run test:track` — 109/109 passing (full regression harness, unrelated to this layer but required by the PR checklist and confirmed green).
- `npm run format:check` / `npm run check:boundaries` — clean.
- Manually verified the live proxy end-to-end against a local dev server: cold fetch ~27s (trims the ~50MB upstream payload down to ~15MB, 61,800 nodes), cached response ~60ms.

title: Fix Mapped Installations: permanent "unavailable" and silently dropped features
body:
Mapped Installations never loaded for me, and it turned out to be three independent defects. Any one of them alone was enough to hide most or all of the layer, which is why it never recovered on its own.

Each is fixed separately below, with the evidence that identified it.

## 1. A 4xx from one mirror ended the whole mirror chain

`fetchOverpassPayload` fell through to the next mirror only on rate-limits, runtime errors, and 5xx. A **4xx was treated as an authoritative answer and returned**, so the first mirror spoke for every mirror below it.

Since `/api/military-installations` treats any `status >= 400` as a failure, that surfaced as a 503 → `"temporarily unavailable"`, and the 30s→240s retry re-hit the same dead mirror forever.

4xx is now a skip. The most informative refusal is still remembered, so if *every* mirror declines (e.g. a genuinely malformed query 400ing everywhere) the error text survives rather than being flattened into "all upstreams failed". The decision is extracted as a pure exported `overpassMirrorDisposition`, so the policy is testable without a server — matching the existing `resolveOverpassPreflight` convention.

## 2. The project's User-Agent is blocklisted by overpass-api.de

This is the part worth a maintainer's attention.

| User-Agent sent | `GET /api/status` |
|---|---|
| `gods-eye-view-overpass-proxy/1.0` (current) | **406** |
| `gods-eye-view-overpass-proxy/9.9` | **406** |
| `overpass-proxy/1.0` | 200 |
| `foo-overpass-proxy/1.0`, `myapp-overpass-proxy/2.3` | 200 |
| `curl/8.4.0`, browser UA | 200 |

Generic `overpass-proxy` strings pass from the same IP, so this is a **targeted rule against this project's exact string**, not a pattern filter or an IP ban. It 406s every request including `/api/status` with no query at all.

Combined with defect 1, that single 406 from the first mirror took the feed down permanently for anyone running this.

Replaced with a string that identifies the app and carries a contact route, which is what the [OSM API usage policy](https://operations.osmfoundation.org/policies/api/) asks for:

```
gods-eye-view/0.1 (+https://github.com/bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view)
```

I've left a comment noting that if this is ever blocked again, the signal is to cut query volume — not to rename the client. **Happy to drop this commit if you'd rather contact the operator about the existing string**; the other two fixes stand on their own.

Also added one verified full-planet fallback mirror. A health sweep found the list had no fast survivor when the `.de` cluster is unhappy: kumi failed the real installation query in every measurement (504 at 55s, then a 22s abort) and private.coffee did not answer inside 180s. Cold latency went ~35s → ~6s.

## 3. Ways and relations were dropped for having no location

The query asked for `out center tags geom`, but **Overpass geometry modes are exclusive and `geom` wins**, so `center` was never in the reply. Every way and relation arrived carrying `bounds`/`geometry` and no centre point, and the normalizer discarded all of them.

Austin mapped **six** features and drew **one** — the lone tagged node. Camp Mabry, Texas Guard Armory, and the Texas National Guard sites were invisible.

Features are now placed from `bounds` (the same box `out center` derives from), falling back to `geometry` and to relation member geometry. The query no longer asks for a mode it cannot receive.

Worth noting: every existing normalizer fixture used `center:`, which real payloads never contain — which is why this never showed up in tests. The new cases use the verified live shape.

## Verification

Against live upstreams, not mocks:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| Endpoint | 503 `unavailable` | 200 `ready` |
| Austin | 1 record | **6 records** |
| Tokyo | — | **10 records** |
| Cold latency | never succeeded | ~6s |
| Warm (cache hit) | — | 3ms |

Test suite: **2567 pass**. There are 25 failures on this branch, but they are **pre-existing on `main`** — `applyVisualState is missing from ui.js` and related cockpit tests — and I confirmed that by stashing: `main` alone gives the identical 25. None touch installations or Overpass. This branch adds 5 tests, all passing, and changes no other behaviour.

title: CCTV: add Finland, Ontario, British Columbia (keyless) + Washington, NSW, Singapore (opt-in) — 800 to 1556 cameras
body:
Takes the CCTV catalog from **800 cameras in 3 regions to 1556 in 8**, across six new sources. Three need no key or signup at all.

> **Stacks on #420.** The first commit here is that PR's — these loaders use the `OVERPASS_USER_AGENT` constant it introduces. Review #420 first; if it merges, this rebases to four commits. Happy to split further if you'd rather take these one source at a time.

## What's added

| Source | Available upstream | Loaded | Key |
|---|---|---|---|
| 🇫🇮 Fintraffic Digitraffic | 811 stations / **2277 presets** | 150 | **none** |
| 🇨🇦 Ontario 511 | 944 | 150 | **none** |
| 🇨🇦 DriveBC | 1062 | 150 | **none** |
| 🇺🇸 WSDOT | 1705 | 150 | free, opt-in |
| 🇦🇺 Live Traffic NSW | 217 | 150 | free, opt-in |
| 🇸🇬 LTA DataMall | 8 | 8 | free, opt-in |

Every pack is switchable (`CCTV_<PACK>_ENABLED=0`) and sized (`CCTV_<PACK>_MAX_SOURCES`, where `0` also disables). **The keyed ones return `[]` before any network call when their key is absent**, so a keyless clone is byte-for-byte what it is today — verified: 1250 keyless, 1556 with all three keys, and none of the keyed providers present in the keyless run.

Heading quality across the catalog improves from 273 high / 157 medium to **273 high / 317 medium / 966 low**, because DriveBC, WSDOT and NSW all publish real bearings.

## Findings worth a maintainer's attention

Each of these would have shipped a silently broken pack. They're recorded as comments at the code, not just here.

**NSW's CDN fakes success.** It serves frames only to browser-shaped clients; to anything else — including this repo's own `gods-eye-view-cctv-proxy/1.0` — it returns **HTTP 200 with a 307-byte HTML "Page not found" body**. `resp.ok` alone would accept that. The existing `content-type.startsWith('image/')` guard in `fetchCctvImageFromUpstream` already converts it to an honest miss, but the outcome would have been every NSW camera quietly falling through to Street View with nothing logged. That function now takes an optional per-source `userAgent`, declared by the pack as `imageUserAgent` and deliberately **not** exposed through `/api/cctv/sources`.

**WSDOT's `Direction` is mostly not a bearing.** Of 1705 cameras, **1182 are `"B"`** (both directions) and 13 are `"O"`. Mapping those through a compass table would have aimed two-thirds of Washington due north *with `medium` confidence attached*. Only N/S/E/W are trusted.

**Digitraffic 406s without `Accept-Encoding: gzip`.** It's mandatory on their JSON interfaces. A 406 here is indistinguishable at a glance from a User-Agent block (cf. #420), so it's called out in a comment. The requested `Digitraffic-User` header is also sent — it raises the rate limit.

**Digitraffic's bulk list omits `imageUrl`.** Presets arrive as `{id, inCollection}`; `imageUrl` and `direction` exist only on the per-station detail endpoint, and 811 of those against 60 req/min is ~14 minutes — not viable at startup. The loader uses the documented URL pattern and one call, accepting id-hash headings as the cost.

**Two opposite elevation semantics, one line apart.** Digitraffic's third GeoJSON coordinate is a placeholder `0.000000` on every station, so `|| 30` is correct there — `0` means "not published". DriveBC publishes real elevations, so `??` must keep a genuine `0`. Both directions are pinned by tests so the next reader doesn't "fix" one into the other.

**Ontario describes views in prose.** `"Toronto Bound"` says where the *road* goes, not where the camera looks, so only unambiguous compass words are promoted to a heading; everything else stays `low`. Longest-first matching keeps `"northeast"` from degrading to `"north"`. Its frames are PNG, not JPEG — handled by the existing pass-through content-type.

**NSW uses hyphenated codes** (`"N-E"`), de-hyphenated before lookup; otherwise 60 diagonal cameras degrade silently.

**WSDOT documents `http://` endpoints.** The loader forces `https`, verified to serve the full catalog, so the proxy never makes a cleartext upstream call on the operator's behalf.

## Global cap

Raised 900 → 1700. At 900 the three existing packs already fill 800, and since new packs are appended last, the global `slice()` would have truncated **them** rather than Austin or TfL — per-pack caps would have looked respected while the new cameras quietly vanished. Lower it or any `CCTV_*_MAX_SOURCES` if the catalog size isn't worth it on your hardware.

## Also included

A **Kuala Lumpur pilot pack** (`config/cctv_sources.kualalumpur.json`) plus `config/README.md`, documenting the previously-undocumented source-pack mechanism — including that `CCTV_SOURCES_FILE` silently disables the live packs unless `CCTV_FORCE_AUSTIN=1` is set. It's explicitly **not** a live feed (`sourceKind: "pilot"`); KL's operators publish no coordinates, so there is nothing to connect. Its positions are real OSM traffic-signal nodes and its elevations come from this repo's own terrain proxy. **Drop this commit if you'd rather not carry a demo pack** — the live sources don't depend on it.

## Verification

Live, not mocked. Every pack serves `X-CCTV-Source=upstream-image` with health `ok`/`snapshot`: Digitraffic Helsinki Ruoholahti, Ontario Lake Shore Blvd at Yonge, DriveBC Georgia St Vancouver, WSDOT I-5 at 5th Ave/Columbia Seattle, NSW Erskine St Sydney, LTA Tuas Checkpoint.

**29 new tests** pinning each upstream's field contract, so a rename fails loudly rather than yielding an empty pack — the exact failure mode #420 exists to fix.

Suite **2591 pass**. The 24–25 failures are pre-existing `ui.js` cockpit tests (`applyVisualState is missing from ui.js`); I diffed the failing set against a stash of these changes and it is **identical**, so nothing here regressed. One of them is flaky, hence the 24/25 wobble.

title: fix(traffic): recover loading after city navigation
body:

title: fix(layers): release bundled GeoJSON entities on toggle-off instead of hiding them
body:
## Problem

Owner field test (2026-09-13, main @ 3143d00): turn on **Data Centers + Submarine Cables + Dams**, turn them all off again, go back to flights/military/satellites. Everything is noticeably more sluggish for the rest of the session even though the three layers are "off".

Root cause: the three bundled layers (`localGeojsonCore.js` for datacenters/dams, `telegeographySubmarineCables.js`) implement `disable()` as `dataSource.show = false`. Cesium's `DataSourceDisplay.update` still walks every visualizer of a *hidden* data source on every frame, and the ~11.5k entities (polylines, billboards, stems, pick records) stay resident. The per-frame walk plus the GC pressure from hundreds of MB of parked entities inflates every frame's cost, not just the geojson share.

## Fix

- `disable()` now **removes the data sources from the viewer** and drops the built records (stems, pick maps, entity contexts, sweep gate state) instead of hiding them.
- The **parsed dataset is cached** (NDJSON features for datacenters/dams; cable + landing-point JSON for cables), so a re-enable rebuilds the entities without a refetch or re-parse. `destroy()` clears the cache.
- A `disable()` that lands while a load is still in flight releases the finished build instead of parking it hidden (the existing generation/ownership pattern in the cables layer is untouched; the stale generation still removes exactly what it added).
- Cables: `_markerBlendDone` resets on release so the rebuilt marker collections get their own translucent-blend pass.

No API or UI changes. `getStats().count` still reports the dataset size while off, as before.

## Measurements

Headful Chrome (real GPU) driven by Puppeteer against the dev server; flights + military + satellites on, camera rotating continuously so the render governor is out of idle; each row is a 250-frame window. Per-frame timings are wrapped `scene.render` / `dataSourceDisplay.update`.

**Before (main), toggling the three layers on then off:**

| window | DataSourceDisplay.update | scene.render | resident entities | JS heap |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| fresh | 0.02 ms | 10.0 ms | 0 | 144 MB |
| geojson ON | 2.75 ms | 14.2 ms | 11,537 | 578 MB |
| geojson OFF (hidden) | 1.09 ms | 13.9 ms | 11,537 | 857 MB |
| OFF +30 s | 0.99 ms | 11.4 ms | 11,537 | 1,603 MB |
| manual `entities.removeAll()` | 0.03 ms | 9.3 ms | 0 | 699 MB |

Control run (same elapsed time, never touching geojson): 5.6 → 6.6 → 5.8 ms render, heap flat at ~150-180 MB. So after OFF the scene is roughly 2× the control's cost, and the `removeAll()` row is what pointed at hidden entities as the cause.

**After (this branch), same script:**

| window | DataSourceDisplay.update | scene.render | resident entities | JS heap |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| fresh | 0.02 ms | 5.0 ms | 0 | 128 MB |
| geojson ON | 1.85 ms | 6.1 ms | 11,537 | 492 MB |
| geojson OFF | 0.02 ms | 5.2 ms | 0 | 740 MB (pre-GC) |
| OFF +30 s | 0.02 ms | 4.8 ms | 0 | 342 MB |

Entities go to zero on OFF, the data-source walk disappears, render returns to the fresh baseline, and the heap comes back down once GC runs. (Absolute render numbers differ between the two sessions by machine load; the within-run deltas are the signal.)

Re-enable after OFF rebuilds from the cache: no network request, no re-parse.

## Tests

- `src/data/localGeojsonLifecycle.test.mjs`: disable now asserts zero data sources and zero entity contexts; the disable-during-load case asserts the completed build is released and re-enable rebuilds with `fetch` called once; new test for the toggle-off/toggle-on cycle (sources 0 → 1, fetch once, count stable).
- `src/data/telegeographySubmarineCables.test.mjs`: the post-cable-GeoJson abort race updated for the cached-JSON path (load B skips the fetch, its own cable build is the only new GeoJson call, stale A still never builds landings); new test asserting a toggle-off removes all three sources and a toggle-on rebuilds them with `fetch` stubbed to throw.

Gates on the branch: `npm test` 3235/3237 (the two failures are the pre-existing macOS tmpdir cases in `devCctv.test.mjs` and `previewServing.test.mjs`, which also fail on untouched main), `npm run format:check` clean, `npm run build` clean, `npm run check:boundaries` clean.

## Reviewer notes

- The cables layer's `releaseDataSources()` is also what `destroy()` now uses, so the three-remove block there collapsed into one call.
- Re-enable does rebuild ~11.5k entities each time (a few hundred ms of `GeoJsonDataSource.load` on this machine) rather than being instant. That is the trade: a toggle-off that actually frees the scene versus a toggle-on that is slightly slower than the old un-hide. Happy to gate the rebuild behind a short grace timer if you'd rather keep quick flips cheap.

title: Expand public cameras with opt-in video and live-layer reliability improvements
body:
## Summary

This draft collects improvements developed from the original August 24 open-source release. It is a broad integration proposal, not a merge-ready replacement for newer upstream work.

- Expand official US and international public camera catalogs, with bounded map markers and searchable directories.
- Add opt-in HLS playback for the selected camera only, plus independent Video cameras / Snapshot cameras switches. Switching cameras, hiding the active group, stopping, closing, or hiding the tab disconnects playback.
- Refresh aircraft for the settled viewport, improve scroll/zoom behavior, and harden layer activation, rendering budgets, and stale-contact cleanup.
- Add country-based submarine-cable ownership colors with multinational/unknown cases preserved.
- Improve public AIS fallback coverage, source/freshness reporting, vessel silhouettes, incident/NOTAM support, and documented administrative Ukraine and mapped-installation context.
- Extract shared API adapters and add a Cloudflare Worker build. Private deployment identifiers and deployment-specific social assets are excluded; Sites remains opt-in via an operator's own ignored hosting manifest.

## Source and privacy boundaries

The September 4 US camera snapshot contains 29,763 published views, including 6,615 admitted public video links. Catalog membership is not an online-feed guarantee. Playback is not recording, and provider terms and delay still apply. Video connects the viewer directly to the provider.

Source attribution, data-license boundaries, incomplete coverage, and fallback freshness are documented in DATA_SOURCES.md and the relevant source directories. The site's private hosting settings, credentials, and local deployment history are not included in this branch.

## Validation

- Production build: passed using the project's Vite CLI on Node 24.
- Full unit/performance suite: passed, 2,865 tests.
- Camera lifecycle, independent group filtering, directory, navigation, viewport refresh, and allocation regressions are included.
- Browser tracking harness: **not passing**. It timed out at the initial application-ready wait after 60 seconds, before tracking assertions ran. The environment lacked the expected pinned Chrome build, so this attempt used installed Microsoft Edge.
- Formatting check passes outside the fixed-width CelesTrak snapshots, whose source padding is intentionally retained.

## Before this is ready for merge

- Reconcile/split this broad contribution against current upstream main. Its single contribution commit is based on release 880a672b5e16ad3e41d318801d3a5203f9201923; newer upstream changes have not been rebased into it.
- Resolve the browser-harness startup issue and rerun the required tracking checks in the supported environment.
- Review the new provider integrations, attribution/licensing notes, and snapshot maintenance cadence.

CHANGELOG.md, docs/CURRENT-STATE.md, and the camera instructions have been updated to describe both the features and these integration limitations.

title: feat(cctv): consolidate seven contributed camera packs on a fair catalog cap
body:
## What this is

Seven contributed CCTV camera packs consolidated onto one branch so they can be tested and merged together, on top of one fix that every pack was working around. Each pack is its own commit under the contributor's authorship (cherry-picked or re-ported onto the current `server/providers/cctv` layout, with a `(cherry picked from PR #N)` note).

| Commit | Pack | Author (source PR) | Terms | Cameras served |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| e737ccf | Fair catalog cap + `LIVE_PACKS` table | Bilawal | | |
| 9bf838f | Ontario 511 | sendmebits (#376) | Open Government Licence – Ontario | 944 |
| c6a7869 | Fintraffic, Finland | avocadoAgent (#415) | CC BY 4.0 | 300 |
| 436e21c | DriveBC, British Columbia | Alex Harvey / infamy (#399) | OGL-BC (DataBC highway-cam dataset) | 250 |
| 946b41b | DriveBC partner credits carried per camera | Bilawal | | |
| 646acd3 | TxDOT San Antonio | Jason Meredith (#423) | Public TxDOT traffic camera data | |
| 0d48fa4 | TxDOT district-configurable (AUS,SAT default) | Daniel Smith (#280), co-author Jason Meredith | Public TxDOT traffic camera data | 500 |
| 0f1b2e1 | Estonia: Tallinn curated + Tarktee DATEX2 | Vladimir Sobolev (#47) | Public City of Tallinn / Transpordiamet data | 255 + 179 |
| f8e09c9 | Warendorf municipal webcams | Matthias Schneider (#106) | Public municipal webcam data | 3 |
| 8c7f827 | Live Traffic NSW | Cyber Knight (#425), co-author NovaSoft (#222) | CC BY 4.0 (Transport for NSW) | 217 |
| 0c5149e, fa41d52, 8b8a2fe | Ceiling, review fixes | Bilawal | | |
| ee5ed56, 4b0294a | Only the outdoor Warendorf camera; semantic unselected labels for every pack | Bilawal | | |
| 223cfd7, b6daeb1, cb96642, fe21efb | Monitor-plane clearance, shipped ground heights, review fixes, docs | Bilawal | | |

Default catalog: **3,446 cameras** across 11 packs (was 800). Every default pack loads whole; the ceiling is 4,000.

## The cap fix (first commit)

The catalog merged all packs into one list and kept the first `CCTV_MAX_SOURCES` entries, so whichever pack was appended last was silently dropped first. Every camera PR had been "fixing" that by raising the global number. `cap.js` now fills the cap round-robin across packs, each contributing its own nearest-to-anchor cameras in turn, so a lowered cap thins every region a little instead of deleting one. Packs register in a `LIVE_PACKS` table; adding a region is one entry plus its loader. `DEFAULT_CCTV_MAX_SOURCES` is a 4,000 safety ceiling (hard bound 5,000, which also sizes the health map).

## Verification

- **Live catalog** from a dev server on this branch: all 11 loaders report success; 3,448 cameras served; no cap trim logged.
- **One frame per pack fetched through the proxy**, each a real `image/jpeg` with a valid JPEG header (Austin, Caltrans, TfL, Ontario, Fintraffic, DriveBC, TxDOT, Tallinn, Tarktee, Warendorf, NSW).
- **Perf**, headful Chrome, CCTV layer on, camera rotating, 40 samples per region, seven regions (Austin, Toronto, Helsinki, Vancouver, Tallinn, Sydney, London):

| | cameras | `scene.render` per frame | JS heap |
|---|---|---|---|
| main | 800 | 1.5 – 2.1 ms | 171 – 290 MB |
| this branch | 3,448 | 1.06 – 1.18 ms | 126 – 153 MB |

  No regression from the larger catalog (one primitive per catalogued camera; the per-frame cost did not scale with it).
- **Gates**: `npm test` 3,283 / 3,285 (the two failures are the known macOS tmpdir cases that also fail on untouched main), `npm run build`, `npm run format:check`, `npm run check:boundaries` all clean.
- **Codex review (gpt-6-astra, read-only, two passes)**: first pass found nine issues (redirect following could carry a host-pinned fetch off-host; TxDOT decoded before size-checking; a duplicate inside one pack took two cap slots; a synchronous throw in a file-based loader could sink a refresh; out-of-range coordinates accepted; ceiling vs docs; per-pack ordering not guaranteed nearest-first; TxDOT id hash collisions; cadence wording). All fixed in fa41d52 and 8b8a2fe; the second pass confirmed them and found three residuals (origin vs hostname pin, reversible TxDOT ids, base64 padding), fixed in 8b8a2fe with tests.

## Things worth your eye

- **Frame fetches now follow redirects only within the original origin** (two hops max) and the TxDOT snapshot path follows none. Two pre-existing gaps are **not** touched here: the `/media/` live-stream route still follows unrestricted redirects, and `/media` stores raw upstream exception text in the health map that `/health` exposes (`server/providers/cctv.js` around line 290). Both predate this branch.
- **Packs are now always distance-sorted** even under their own cap, so the catalog-wide cap thins from the far end. Side effect: NEXT/PREV and auto-hop order changes for packs that previously fit their cap unsorted.
- **NSW**: the image host serves frames only to browser-identified clients, so `media.js` sends a browser User-Agent for that exact hostname and the proxy's own identity everywhere else. Disclosed in DATA_SOURCES.md.
- **DriveBC**: about 25 cameras in the feed are partner-supplied (TransLink, City of Vancouver, City of Surrey, Parks Canada). The feed's per-camera credit is carried onto the record and shown beside the provider in the CCTV panel.
- **Warendorf**: two of the three cameras are the Kreis's registration-office waiting rooms, published by the Kreis itself for queue length. Kept as contributed; easy to drop the two rows if you'd rather not.
- `src/locations.js` gains a Tallinn city preset (from #47).

## After merge

Each source PR (#376, #415, #399, #423, #280, #47, #106, #425, #222) gets closed with a link to its commit here; the authors were told this in advance.


## Monitor planes no longer clip the terrain (added after the owner field test)

**Diagnosis.** The plane's bottom edge was buried by design: the ground clamp lifted only the plane's center to ground + 2 m and derived the corners rigidly below it, and the client inflated every pack range to 220 m. At the nominal pitches the bottom edge sat 45–60 m underground in every region, including the 2D view.

**What ships.**
- `src/data/cctvFootprint.js` (pure, shared): plane dimensions, a 3×3 grid of support points on the plane, the rigid lift, a pose hash.
- `geometry.js`: one rigid lift for the whole rectangle, sized by the largest clearance deficit over the supports against the ground under each (mount ground where nothing finer is known), capped at 60 m above the mount-based lift so a tall building under a far edge can't launch the plane. Range floor 220 → 120 m so pack ranges are honoured; saved calibrations re-base their `rangeScale` once.
- `src/data/local_data/cctv_ground_heights/`: precomputed ground heights under every camera's mount and its nine plane supports for the pose as served (3,445 of 3,446 cameras), joined into the served catalog as `groundHeights`. A camera whose rendered pose still hashes to its entry is placed from the file with zero runtime sampling; verified live on 21 of 22 sampled cameras (the 22nd hit the obstruction probe and correctly took the fallback). Everything else resolves the ground under its footprint from the terrain proxy on activation, calibration commit, gizmo release and regime switch, nine cached points for the one camera being looked at.

**Clearance across the catalog:** every camera's plane clears the ground under all nine supports except 35 cameras (1%) that hit the lift cap because their plane crosses a tall building.

**Reviews.** Three review passes on the terrain commit; all findings fixed, the final pass confirmed the shipped branch runs with zero sampler calls through the real catalog factory. Full suite 3,328 / 3,330 (the two known macOS tmpdir cases).

title: feat(cctv): add the Open Calgary camera pack
body:
## What

Adds Calgary as a fourth CCTV city pack alongside Austin, Caltrans and TfL — about 214 public
traffic cameras from Open Calgary, keyless, served through the existing frame proxy. This is the
"add a CCTV source pack" invitation in CONTRIBUTING.

I live in Calgary, which is mostly why I picked it: it's the city I can actually sanity-check
camera by camera, and it turned out to matter for the heading problem below.

## The one thing worth reviewing carefully

Calgary's dataset looks like it tells you which way each camera points. It doesn't.

Every record has a `quadrant` field (`NE`/`NW`/`SE`/`SW`), and `camera_location` ends in the same
token — "9 Avenue / 3 Street SE". If you live here you read that immediately as the address grid:
the city is split into four quadrants and nearly every street name carries one. It says nothing
about where the camera is aimed.

The trap is that `directionToHeading()` parses it quite happily. Feed it "9 Avenue / 3 Street SE"
and you get 135°, confidently, for all 214 cameras — and all 214 are wrong. That's the same
failure `src/data/directionText.js` already documents for Austin street names containing cardinal
words (59 of ~1000 there). Calgary just hits it on every single row instead of a few.

So this pack derives no heading at all. Cameras get the shared id-hash fallback at
`headingConfidence: 'low'`, same as TfL JamCams, and you correct them by dragging the gizmo.
There's a test pinning that behaviour so nobody "fixes" it later by wiring up the quadrant.

## Smaller details

- **Frame URLs.** The catalog publishes `http://trafficcam.calgary.ca/...`, but the host serves
  HTTPS and 301s to it, so I upgrade the scheme before registering and pin to that exact origin.
  Same idea as the Caltrans and TfL host pins.
- **Dataset id** came from the Socrata catalog API rather than being hardcoded from somewhere —
  `k7p9-kppz`, "Traffic Cameras".
- **Parsing** lives in `src/data/calgaryCameras.js` with 12 unit tests, following how
  `firmsCsv.js` and `directionText.js` keep server-side parsing testable outside Vite.
- Gated behind `CCTV_CALGARY_ENABLED` (default on) with `CCTV_CALGARY_MAX_SOURCES` to cap it.

## One change outside the pack, which I'd rather flag than bury

I raised `DEFAULT_CCTV_MAX_SOURCES` from 900 to 1100.

Four packs at their default caps come to 1014 (250 + 300 + 250 + 214). The global cap keeps the
first N after the merge and Calgary merges last, so at 900 it registered 100 of 214 and logged the
"exceeds cap" warning. Raising the ceiling looked like the smaller change — capping Calgary at
under half seemed worse than growing the catalog by about 11% — but it does affect everyone, not
just people looking at Alberta. If you'd rather hold 900 and cap Calgary instead, say so and I'll
switch it.

## Licensing

Open Government Licence – City of Calgary, which requires attribution. Registered in
`src/data/dataCredits.js` and documented in `DATA_SOURCES.md`:
"Contains information licensed under the Open Government Licence – City of Calgary."
No city logo is used.

## How I verified

On Node 24.14.0 and 26.8.2:

- `npm ci` clean
- `npm test` green on both (allocation gate enforced on 24.14.0 via `GEV_REQUIRE_ALLOCATION_GATE=1`)
- `npm run build` green
- `npm run test:track` 108 passed, 0 failed
- Live against the dev server: 1015 cameras registered across the four packs, no cap warning, and
  `/api/cctv/frame/calgary-86` and `calgary-142` both return `image/jpeg`

Happy to add screenshots of the mesh over Calgary with a live frame in the monitor panel if
that's useful for review.

title: fix bikeshare layer: address the GBFS proxy by path, not query string
body:
## Summary

The bikeshare layer currently fails for every city on `main`. Every station request answers `400 Bad Request` and the layer reports `UNAVAILABLE — GBFS fetch error`.

The extracted station source asks the proxy for `/api/gbfs?url=<encoded-upstream>`, but the proxy reads its upstream target from the **path**, not the query string:

- `server/providers/gbfs.js` — `url.pathname.replace(/^\/+/, '')`
- `src/layers/bikeshare/ingestion.js:17` — builds `/api/gbfs/${encodeURIComponent(upstreamUrl)}`
- `src/layers/bikeshare/source.js:12` — builds `/api/gbfs?url=${...}` ← the outlier

Two of the three already agree on the path shape. This changes `source.js` to match, and updates its unit test, which asserted the query-string shape against a mocked `fetch`, which is why the suite stayed green while the layer was dark.

Reproduced against the running dev server:

```
GET /api/gbfs?url=https%3A%2F%2Faustin.publicbikesystem.net%2F...  → 400
GET /api/gbfs/https%3A%2F%2Faustin.publicbikesystem.net%2F...      → 200
```

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run build` — green
- [x] `npm test` — 3265 tests, 0 failures
- [x] `npm run test:track` — 109 passed, 0 failed
- [x] `npm run format:check` and `npm run check:boundaries` — green
- [x] Before: enabling Bikeshare over Austin shows `UNAVAILABLE — GBFS fetch error`
- [x] After: the same toggle loads and renders stations (W 11th/Congress [7/11], E 11th/San Jacinto [8/11])

Found while working on #359. The two changes are independent. This one is branched from `main` and touches no registry data.

title: Add Québec 511 traffic camera source pack
body:
## Proposal

Add an official Québec 511 / MTMD traffic-camera source pack to the existing CCTV system, using the same bounded live-source pattern as Ontario 511 / Caltrans / TfL.

This looks like a good fit for the repository's preferred first-contribution lane in `CONTRIBUTING.md`: a public camera catalog with coordinates, attribution, and server-registered frame/view URLs.

## Official source

**Publisher:** Ministère des Transports et de la Mobilité durable (MTMD), Gouvernement du Québec

**Dataset:** Caméra de circulation / Traffic camera

**Catalog:**
https://www.donneesquebec.ca/recherche/dataset/camera-de-circulation

**GeoJSON/WFS resource:**
https://ws.mapserver.transports.gouv.qc.ca/swtq?service=wfs&version=2.0.0&request=getfeature&typename=ms:infos_cameras&outfile=Camera&srsname=EPSG:4326&outputformat=geojson

The dataset description states that these are the cameras shown on the Québec 511 interactive map and that each camera has a URL for viewing its image/video stream.

## Licensing / provenance

- Licence: **CC BY 4.0**
- Projection: **EPSG:4326 / WGS84**
- Update frequency: **daily**
- Geographic coverage: **Québec-wide**, including Montréal, Laval and Montérégie
- Publisher contact listed by Données Québec: `geomatique@transports.gouv.qc.ca`

The implementation should fetch the official catalog at runtime and preserve MTMD / Québec 511 attribution rather than vendoring or redistributing the source dataset.

## Proposed first scope

Keep this intentionally small:

- Add a Québec 511 live source loader under the existing `server/providers/cctv/` architecture.
- Normalize stable camera ID, latitude/longitude, location description, source/view URL, source kind, and licence/attribution.
- Register only URLs derived from the official catalog; no client-supplied upstream URLs.
- Add `CCTV_QUEBEC_ENABLED` and `CCTV_QUEBEC_MAX_SOURCES` style controls consistent with the existing Ontario/Fintraffic packs.
- Use a bounded camera count and deterministic ordering rather than loading an unbounded feed.
- Update `DATA_SOURCES.md`, `.env.example`, `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md`, and `CHANGELOG.md` as required by the contribution guide.
- Add focused parser/normalization tests and run the normal build/unit/track gates.

I would prefer not to invent camera pose/orientation where the official feed does not provide it; those cameras can remain raw/un-calibrated just like other non-curated sources.

## Why this source

Besides filling a Canadian coverage gap between the existing Ontario pack and the rest of the CCTV mesh, it is a useful real-world test of the source-pack abstraction: official public catalog, explicit open-data licence, stable coordinates, multilingual location metadata, and live viewing URLs.

If this direction looks good, I'm happy to implement it as a narrow follow-up PR.

title: feat(cctv): add Perth & Kinross and Scottish mountain webcam packs
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #207 with the Traffic Scotland part removed, rebuilt on the current `server/providers/cctv` layout as two curated catalog packs on the Warendorf pattern.

- **Perth & Kinross Council** (`config/cctv_sources.pkc.json`, `CCTV_PKC_ENABLED`): 23 road cameras at 14 sites on the M90, A9, A90, A93, A94, A822, A977, A827, Kinloch Rannoch, Muirend Road in Perth, and A90 Forfar. The council publishes 15-minute JPEG stills but no catalog, so positions are hand-placed: trunk-road sites take Traffic Scotland's published site coordinates, the rest come from OpenStreetMap features matching the council's own descriptions ("north of Balbeggie", "east of Crook of Devon"). Directional cameras take their heading from the caption burned into each frame ("Looking East"), so 20 of 23 carry a CURATED pose; the three with no stated facing keep an id-hash prior at low confidence.
- **Scottish mountain and ski webcams** (`config/cctv_sources.scotland_webcams.json`, `CCTV_SCOTLAND_WEBCAMS_ENABLED`): 22 public webcams — Cairngorm Mountain (5), Glencoe Mountain Resort via Winterhighland (11; three stale views left out), Glenshee via webcam-hd.com (3, daylight only), Deeside Gliding Club at Aboyne airfield, About Fort William's Ben Nevis camera, and Winterhighland's Leadhills camera. Headings are curated only where the view direction is documented (base stations, Loch Morlich, Ben Nevis); on-slope cameras stay RAW PRIOR.
- One shared curated-catalog reader in `sources.js` (`loadCuratedStillCatalog`) backs both loaders: only registered image origins are accepted per pack (`PKC_IMAGE_ORIGINS`, `SCOTLAND_WEBCAM_IMAGE_ORIGINS`), coordinates must be plausible, duplicate ids are dropped, a missing heading gets `fallbackHeadingFromId`. Two `LIVE_PACKS` entries; no change to the catalog cap.
- Operator cadences join `PROVIDER_STATIC_REFRESH_MS` (council 15 min, Cairngorm 2 min, the rest 5 min). Shipped ground heights precomputed for all 45 cameras with `scripts/precompute-cctv-heights.mjs --kinds council-road-camera,mountain-webcam` (45 ok, 0 miss). Two credit entries, DATA_SOURCES rows and notes, CURRENT-STATE, CHANGELOG, launcher and `.env.example` updated.

**Traffic Scotland is deliberately not included.** Its copyright page states the Scottish Government retains full copyright of the camera images and that users may not hyperlink directly to them; the documented route is a registered FTP service with per-user credentials, which does not fit a default pack. The rejection is recorded in CURRENT-STATE so nobody re-proposes it.

## Data sources and terms

- Perth & Kinross Council and the mountain operators publish plain still URLs with no stated reuse licence, the same footing as the Warendorf pack. Frames are proxied live from the registered hosts only, never stored or redistributed, polled at each operator's stated cadence, and every operator is credited by name and link in the Data attribution popover. `DATA_SOURCES.md` says to remove an entry if an operator objects.
- Positions for the council cameras are ±100 m priors and are labelled as such. The Ben Nevis frame is ~1.6 MB per fetch and is the heaviest camera in the catalog.

## Validation

- Node 26.8.1: `npm test` — 3,398 passed, 2 failed, 1 skip. The two failures (`src/devCctv.test.mjs` "CCTV preset starts keyless on localhost", `src/tooling/previewServing.test.mjs` "real dev and built-preview servers serve provider JSON") fail identically on unchanged `main` in this environment: both are macOS `/var` vs `/private/var` temp-path mismatches, not related to this change. The one skip is the Node 24 allocation-benchmark gate.
- `npm run format:check` — clean (new test added to `scripts/format-scope.json`).
- `npm run build` — passed; existing chunk-size warning only.
- `npm run test:track -- --url http://localhost:4199` — 109 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped.
- Live dev server: `/api/cctv/sources` served 3,491 cameras including 23 `council-road-camera` and 22 `mountain-webcam`; frames for both Forfar views, A90 Starr Farm, Cairngorm base, Glencoe Main Basin, Glenshee, Aboyne, Ben Nevis, and Leadhills all returned `image/jpeg` with `X-CCTV-Source: upstream-image`.

title: feat(satellites): precise pass times and naked-eye visibility
body:
The voice tool says it gives the next visible ISS pass, but it returns any pass, even in daytime, and doesn't check whether the sky at the location is dark. The rise and set times were also off by up to 5 seconds, and it was only exposed for the ISS.

This PR makes the rise and set times 30 to 50 times more accurate, adds `getNextSatellitePass` so it works for any satellite in the loaded catalog (not just the ISS), and makes the voice tool pick a pass you can actually see, or say `visible: false` if there isn't one.

Visibility is a separate commit. Happy to drop it if the tool is meant to report any pass.

### Changes

- `src/data/satellitePass.js` (new): 20 s coarse scan, 7-step bisection for rise/set (~0.2 s), parabolic peak fit from the transit samples.
- Visibility: USNO low-precision Sun position and a cylindrical Earth shadow. A pass is `visible` when part of it is sunlit while the observer's Sun is at or below −6°.
- `getNextSatellitePass` is exposed from the satellites layer and `src/data/satellites.js`; it accepts numeric or string NORAD IDs (not wired to voice yet, since that needs a tool schema change).
- `findNextIssPass` keeps its signature and defaults as a wrapper.
- `next_iss_pass` falls back to the next pass with `visible: false` when no visible pass occurs in 24 h. Tool schema unchanged.
- The existing "ISS voice lookup uses the registered satellite instance" test now expects the visible-first call before the fallback.

### Behaviour change

title: feat(cctv): enrich identified cameras with datasheet FOV + specs
body:
## What

When a CCTV source pack (or a seed) names its hardware `model`, resolve it against a camera-model spec table:
- the coverage **frustum uses the manufacturer's horizontal FOV** instead of the pose estimate, and
- the **HUD meta line gains the model's specs** (resolution, night-vision range, PTZ).

Cameras with no identified model are unchanged — unknown never implies anything (matches the layer's existing honesty about `RAW PRIOR` poses). This is a small enabler for the "add a CCTV source pack" contribution lane in CONTRIBUTING.md: a pack that publishes its hardware models gets accurate cones + specs for free. No existing camera's behavior changes (Austin Open Data doesn't publish per-camera models, so nothing lights up until a pack opts in).

## Data source

Spec records are vendored verbatim from the [CCTV Camera Database](https://github.com/ch-bas/cctv-camera-database) — an open, **CC0-1.0** dataset of 28,000+ camera models transcribed from manufacturer datasheets (84% carry FOV). This PR lands a small starter table (4 models) plus the join/parsing helpers; packs or a future full-extract vendor can grow it. Records describe camera **products** (optics, resolution, night vision) — no endpoints, stream paths, or access data.

## Changes

- `src/data/cctvModelSpecs.js` — spec table, case-insensitive + alias lookup, wide-end FOV parser, HUD summary formatter
- `src/data/cctvModelSpecs.test.mjs` — lookup / alias / unknown-null, FOV parsing across the real `fov_deg` string shapes, summary rendering
- `src/data/cctv.js` — apply enrichment in both catalog builders; pass `fovSource` + `spec` through the public camera state
- `src/ui.js` — label a datasheet-driven FOV and append the spec summary

## Checks

`npm test` (2713 pass / 0 fail) and `npm run build` green on Node 24. New behavior is inert until a source declares `model`.

Happy to grow the spec table (or wire the full CC0 extract) if this direction is useful.
