title: fix: prevent Nepal media from opening external browsers in Pinokio
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to [#590](https://github.com/bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view/pull/590).

Fix Nepal scene playback in the Pinokio shell: avoid automatic external-browser launches and let source-only timed shots advance after their authored dwell. Also require an explicit Play Scene or Play Shot action before scene media can autoplay.

## Issue and reproduction

1. Open God's Eye View inside Pinokio and play the Nepal Flood Incident scene.
2. Provider iframe navigation, including hidden preloads, can open an external browser without clicking Open Original.
3. Suppressing those providers alone leaves a trimmed shot such as Mailung Bazzar, Dandaguan waiting for playback completion from a player that was never created.

Separately, loading or restoring scene parameters could authorize autoplay without a playback action.

## Changes

- Detect the Pinokio shell before allocating provider frames, SDKs, or hidden preloads. Keep source-linked evidence cards and explicit Open Original actions.
- Distinguish deliberately disabled playback from a supported player that is still loading. With no local clip, the Mailung source card uses its authored 7.65-second dwell and then advances.
- Preserve ordinary-browser embeds and the supported Mailung player's seven-second source-time trim plus 0.65-second exit.
- Give scene media transient, cancellable playback ownership from Play Scene or Play Shot. LOAD, restoration, and seek remain passive; Stop, replacement, failed loads, and layer disable revoke ownership.
- Grant cross-scene replay ownership only after the previous scene releases its layers, so cleanup cannot silence the new shot.
- Add unit regressions and a composed browser playback check covering fallback progression, trim timing, passive loading, explicit replay, and cancellation.

This is a Pinokio compatibility fallback, not a repair to the shell's navigation handler. Provider-hosted inline playback remains disabled inside Pinokio; source links and optional approved local clips retain their existing behavior. No media assets, credentials, dependencies, or launcher changes are included.

## Validation

- `npm run build` — passed.
- `npm test` — passed.
- `npm run format:check` — passed.
- `npm run check:boundaries` — passed.
- Tracking harness — 109 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped.
- Composed Nepal playback check in headed, GPU-backed Chrome — 17 assertions passed. Timing assertions use a controlled provider clock, and the Pinokio policy check uses an emulated user agent.
- Director timing check — 11 assertions passed.
- Separate live-provider Chrome check — the Upper Valley Collapse YouTube embed rendered and played after explicit replay.
- Manual native Pinokio test — Mailung shot behavior and absence of automatic external media launches confirmed.

title: i18n foundation: locale core, parity gates, English-only string extraction
body:
## Summary

Foundation PR for interface localization, per the discussion on #312: the locale subsystem, parity gates, and a complete **English-only extraction** of all application-owned presentation strings. This PR changes no user-visible behavior — English output is byte-identical to `main`, enforced by tests. Locales ship as stacked follow-ups (#-es is the first, built on this branch); nothing here depends on them.

Following the #412 notes: there is **no automatic DOM translator**. Keys are static and semantic (`cockpit.readout.groundSpeed`), lookups are deterministic, and locale switching (when a locale ships) is a full reload — so first-observed-text caching and stale-async-translation states cannot occur by construction.

## What changes

- **`src/i18n/` core** — `locale.js` (normalization, `?lang=` → stored preference (`gev:locale:v1`) → browser language → default; guarded storage; `<html lang/dir>`), `index.js` (`t()` with `{named}` interpolation and `Intl.PluralRules` selection, Intl formatters, `applyDocumentTranslations()` for static markup, hash-preserving reload). Zero new dependencies.
- **English catalogs** — 912 keys across four append-only namespaces (`shell`/`cockpit`/`layers`/`setup`), semantically keyed, never renamed.
- **Extraction** — every user-facing English string at its final presentation boundary: `t()` call sites across the UI/layer/voice modules plus `data-i18n*` attributes across the HTML templates. Machine contracts (layer IDs, enums, share-link/hash parameters, API fields, voice tool schemas, provider names, attribution) are untouched by design; the keep-English boundary is documented in `docs/TRANSLATORS.md`.
- **Gates** — `catalog.test.mjs` (strict key/placeholder/plural-variant parity, generalized to any shipped locale set; CI fails on a missing translation), `markupCoverage.test.mjs` (every `data-i18n*` attribute resolves), `i18n.test.mjs` (resolution precedence, guards, fallback, interpolation, plurals, DOM application), `repairPass.test.mjs` (English byte-identity anchors).
- **Selector machinery** — the dock renders one button per *shipped* locale; with only English shipped this is a single EN button. Configurable via `GEV_DEFAULT_LOCALE`/`GEV_SECONDARY_LOCALE` (validated against shipped catalogs; unshipped values degenerate safely).
- **Docs** — `docs/TRANSLATORS.md` is the deliberate-design artifact: glossary conventions, keep-English boundary, and the add-a-locale recipe each follow-up PR executes.

Also fixes one latent markup bug found during extraction: duplicate `data-i18n` attributes on the first-run choice tiles wiped the sub-copy markup in **every** locale including English.

## How to test

```sh
node --test src/i18n/   # 40/40
npm test                # 5 known environmental failures + 1 Windows skip (all reproduce on pristine main)
npm run build           # green
```

Behavioral check: run the app — everything renders exactly as on `main` (the extraction is a pure refactor of string sourcing). `?lang=xx` for unshipped codes is ignored; stored preferences outside the shipped set fall through to English.

## Reviewer notes

- One sanctioned test-form change family: source-reading tests that pinned English literals in place now pin the `t()` call form — same strings, same surfaces, source-shape updated to the extraction.
- Commit structure: `core → extraction → docs` — three commits, squash-friendly.
- Non-goals: locales (stacked PRs), RTL (the `dir` machinery exists), locale-aware number formatting (`toLocaleString` sites documented as deferred).

Stacked follow-up: **#-es** (Spanish) is open against this branch — its diff is exactly the four `es` catalogs, the es plural test pins, and one measured es-scoped CSS wrap rule.

title: i18n: interface localization with Spanish and Russian (English-text keys)
body: ## Summary Interface localization for God's Eye View, shipping **Spanish** and **Russian**. This PR now carries the i18n foundation from #601 (closed in favour of this one; all of @meirm's commits are kept in the history), reworked so that the English text itself is the message key, plus the two locales. ```js t('Save keys') // translate now t('Saved to {store}', { store }) // named placeholders tn(count, '{count} camera', '{count} cameras') // plural by Intl.PluralRules msg('Live Flights') // mark text kept in data; t() it later ``` ```html Normal ``` English needs no catalog: the code is the source. Every other language is one flat JSON file, `src/i18n/locales/.json`, keyed by the English text. A missing entry falls back to English. ## What changes - **Foundation (#601, @meirm):** extraction of the application's UI strings to `t()` call sites and `data-i18n*` markup, the locale core, Intl formatters, reload-on-switch. - **English-text keys:** a codemod replaced the ~930 semantic keys (`setup.firstRun.title`) with their English text (`'Choose your first view'`), so code reads like the UI and English has no catalog to keep in sync. Namespaces, the configurable locale pair (`GEV_DEFAULT_LOCALE` / `GEV_SECONDARY_LOCALE`) and its build defines are gone. The language comes from `?lang=` (one-shot), the stored choice from the EN | ES | RU dock switch, then `navigator.languages`, then English. - **`npm run i18n`** (`scripts/i18n.mjs`): extracts all 833 messages from `t`/`tn`/`msg` literals and markup, and fails on missing, unused, placeholder-mismatched or wrongly-shaped plural entries. `npm test` runs it through `src/i18n/catalog.test.mjs`. `--missing ` prints what a language lacks as JSON; `--prune` drops unused entries. - **Spanish** (`es.json`, 833/833): @meirm's translation from this PR, converted unchanged in its own commit, then completed against the current English (13 new messages, the `many` plural form for exact millions, fixes where the English had changed) with consistent terminology. Keeps the es-only CCTV row-wrap rule. - **Russian** (`ru.json`, 833/833): started from @meirm's Russian catalog in #312, reviewed and completed. - **Fixes found on the way:** `data-i18n` on parents would have wiped the cockpit LEVEL line, the local-weather cells (TEMP/WIND/SKY/PRECIP) and the first-run EXPLORE MANUALLY tile; a doubled degree sign in the TRACK ACQUIRED signal; doc sections an earlier merge had resurrected in `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md`. - **Docs:** `docs/I18N.md` (how to mark UI text: `t` vs `tn` vs `msg`, markup, rules), `docs/TRANSLATORS.md` (workflow, adding a language), `docs/translations/{es,ru}.md` (per-language style, plurals, glossary). `CONTRIBUTING.md` points to them. ## How to test ```sh npm run i18n # es: 833 messages, complete / ru: 833 messages, complete npm test npm run build ``` Open the app with `?lang=es`, `?lang=ru` or `?lang=en`, or use the EN | ES | RU switch in the Visual Presets dock. English renders as before. ## Known gaps - Strings added after #601's extraction (for example the Street Level panel, "GET KEY ↗") are still English, and there is no lint yet for unmarked UI text. - The other community locales (#907 fr, #908 de, #909 pt, #912 it, #913 ja, #914 zh-CN, #915 ar) cover 830/833 of the current messages and convert the same way; they follow as separate PRs, credited to their authors. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: fix(transit): keep parked vehicles pointed along their course while the camera orbits
body:
## Changes

Follow-up to #596 from the owner's look: a parked transit vehicle turned with the camera. Moving vehicles project their world course into screen space on every camera change, but a vehicle that had never moved on screen could have no display course and was skipped by that pass, leaving its billboard at a screen-anchored angle; rotation invalidation also relied on camera events that a pose change without a revision could miss. Now every visible vehicle with any usable course (derived, held, or the feed's reported bearing) is re-projected at the existing 5 Hz cadence on camera pose changes. Moving playback and the 120°/s course limiter are unchanged.

## How it was verified

- `npm run format:check` (861 files), `npm run check:boundaries` (109 groups), `npm test` (4,068 passing), `npm run build` clean; tracking regression 109/109 in a real browser on Google 3D tiles.
- Node tests: a stationary vehicle with a held course, and one with only a reported bearing, under a camera at heading 0° then 90° yield screen rotations 90° apart.
- Browser harness (`scripts/qa-transit.mjs`, keyed on Google 3D tiles): a parked scripted vehicle orbited by 90° rotates 90.000° on screen; a moving vehicle's rotation still matches its rendered travel; both checks fail on main and pass here. Full keyed run: 201 pass; the nine failures are the per-frame allocation gate already recorded as a follow-up and threshold-edge readability lines on the Boston matrix, both unchanged from #596.

title: refactor(voice): separate Realtime session ownership
body:
The Realtime controller mixed connection setup, turn processing, Radio handoff, input/audio analysis, cost state, viewport context and diagnostics. It now composes focused owners with explicit dependencies; the existing controller API delegates to their single source of state. Voice controls, backend/session contracts, response policy and model preferences remain compatible.

The extraction also closes lifetime gaps: stale offers and peer callbacks cannot affect a replacement connection, delayed action/capture continuations cannot resume a closed conversation, and failed or stopped audio meters release their resources. Seven regression tests cover these boundaries, including action success/rejection and viewport completion after Stop and restart. Existing protocol assertions are preserved. Ownership is documented in `docs/VOICE-OWNERSHIP.md`.

Verification on the current main baseline, including #596 and #603:

- 4,089 passing unit/allocation checks and one existing skip; formatting, import/package boundaries, setup doctor and production build.
- Native click and hold-Space recorded-microphone acceptance: globe reset, microphone release, confirmed Radio playback and voice shutdown, with no browser errors.
- 109 tracking checks, scene and location control acceptance; desktop/narrow browser screenshots inspected.
- The five transit-heading browser checks pass after adopting #603; the shell/voice source is identical across that baseline update.
- Resolve the Cesium terrain test fixture through package lookup so the same assertions work with hoisted dependencies.
- The stale-offer and late-continuation tests were observed failing before their fixes.

Live Radio acceptance depends on the selected broadcaster: exploratory runs on another station failed playback, while the pre-refactor baseline and candidate passed with the same working station. No fixture or protocol policy was changed to force that result.

title: feat(cctv): FL511 Florida statewide camera pack (stills)
body:
## What this is

FL511 (Florida DOT) traffic cameras as a CCTV source pack: about 4,000 statewide stills from FL511's public camera catalog, capped to 500 by default. It is off by default. FL511's terms limit its content to individual, non-commercial use, so an operator turns it on with `CCTV_FLORIDA_ENABLED=1` after reading those terms.

## How it works

The loader reads FL511's ArcGIS FeatureServer layer a page at a time, the same shape as the other ArcGIS-backed packs. Each page is read under a byte cap and redirects are refused, so a misbehaving host cannot hand back an unbounded body or steer the request somewhere else.

- Frames are pinned to FL511's two image hosts (`images-dis.divas.cloud`, `snapshots.divas.cloud`) over HTTPS. A row whose image points anywhere else is dropped.
- Coordinates go through a Florida bounds check (`isLikelyFloridaCoordinate` in `normalize.js`), so a bad row cannot place a camera outside the state.
- Headings come from the catalog's direction codes through `directionToHeading`. FL511's direction field is a real compass direction, not an address grid, so it is used as the pose prior. `NOT DIRECTIONAL` rows take the shared id-hash fallback at low confidence.
- Camera ids come from the image channel. The catalog's ID column repeats across regions, so keying on it would collapse distinct cameras into one.
- `prioritizeSources` against eight anchors (Miami, Fort Lauderdale, West Palm Beach, Orlando, Tampa, Jacksonville, Tallahassee, Pensacola) picks the 500. `CCTV_FLORIDA_MAX_SOURCES` changes the cap, clamped to 8 through 4,200.
- Registration uses `envOptIn('CCTV_FLORIDA_ENABLED')`, the same switch the NYC and Lithuania packs use, so only `1` turns it on.

## Data source and terms

- Catalog: `services.arcgis.com/3wFbqsFPLeKqOlIK/.../FL511_Traffic_Cameras/FeatureServer/0`. It is published from a Florida Division of Emergency Management account rather than by FL511 directly, and the service carries no licence text of its own.
- Frames: `images-dis.divas.cloud` and `snapshots.divas.cloud`, fetched at runtime through the existing frame proxy. Nothing is bundled or redistributed.
- Terms: FL511's site terms limit its content to individual, non-commercial use. That is why the pack is opt-in. The DATA_SOURCES row says so, and the note covers the FDEM publisher and the missing licence text.
- Attribution: DATA_SOURCES.md row and note, and a `dataCredits.js` entry.

## Security

Untrusted input is the catalog response and the image URLs inside it.

- Catalog reads are capped per page (`FLORIDA_MAX_CATALOG_BYTES`, 2 MiB, against about 650 KiB measured for a 2,000-row page) and use `redirect: 'manual'`.
- Image URLs must be HTTPS on one of the two pinned hosts.
- Coordinates must fall inside Florida.

`src/data/cctvFlorida.test.mjs` covers each of these: an oversized page is refused, a redirect on any page drops the whole pack, and off-host frames and rows outside Florida are dropped.

## Docs

- `changelog.d/605-fl511-florida-cameras.md`: the changelog fragment, per `changelog.d/README.md`.
- `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md`: Florida (FL511, opt-in) added to the CCTV row.
- `DATA_SOURCES.md`: row (off by default, `CCTV_FLORIDA_ENABLED=1` to enable) and note (terms, FDEM publisher, no licence text).
- `README.md`: Florida (FL511) added to the CCTV Mesh row.
- `.env.example`: `CCTV_FLORIDA_ENABLED` and `CCTV_FLORIDA_MAX_SOURCES`.

## Validation

Environment: native on Arch Linux, Node 24.21.0, system Chromium headless. Branch rebased onto `73aec2e`.

| Check | Result |
| ----- | ------ |
| `npm run doctor -- --json` | ready |
| `npm run format:check` | pass, 1,424 files |
| `npm run check:boundaries` | pass |
| `npm test` | 7,717 tests, 0 failed, 1 skipped |
| `npm run build` | pass |
| `npm run test:track` | 109 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped |
| `node scripts/qa-cctv-v2.mjs` | 52 passed, 0 failed, 1 inconclusive (the headless geometry-load drain, which the harness itself says needs a headful run) |
| New tests | `src/data/cctvFlorida.test.mjs`: 11 cases. Feature mapping onto a pinned host, the `NOT DIRECTIONAL` fallback, dropped rows, ids from the image channel, the bounds check, paging and de-duplication, redirect refusal, a failed later page keeping earlier pages, the byte cap, catalog wiring with `CCTV_FLORIDA_ENABLED=1`, and the lane staying off without it. |

## Changes since the last review

- Squashed to one commit and rebased once onto current main.
- Made the pack opt-in with `envOptIn`, matching NYC and Lithuania.
- Added the FDEM publisher note to DATA_SOURCES.
- Moved the changelog entry to a `changelog.d` fragment.

## Not in this PR

- Live video. Florida's cameras are stills here.

title: feat(cctv): add Lithuania Eismoinfo road cameras
body:
## Summary

Enable Lithuania's public Via Lietuva / Eismoinfo road cameras in the existing CCTV layer without an API key. A live check returned 296 cameras, and the Vilnius A1 camera rendered through the registered-image proxy.

- Join the public snapshot catalog to the map catalog by camera ID. Use the map's WGS84 latitude/longitude, not the snapshot table's LKS-94 metre coordinates.
- Accept only the official HTTPS image endpoint with matching IDs; reject redirects, invalid coordinates and oversized catalogs. Reuse the shared catalog cache, fair allocation and image proxy.
- Add attribution, documentation, a disable switch and a configurable cap (400 by default). Images remain periodically refreshed stills, with low-confidence camera-pose estimates.
- Add tests for catalog joining, malformed data, destination validation, deduplication, registration and failure handling.

Provider: https://eismoinfo.lt/
Open-data statement: https://eismoinfo.lt/eismoinfo-backend/content?id=44

## Validation

Windows, Node 24.21.0, based on upstream main at 5728dec.

- Passed: `npm run format`, `npm run format:check`, `npm run check:boundaries`, `npm run build`.
- Passed: `npm test`, including both serialized allocation gates (4085 passed, 10 skipped in total).
- Passed live check: 296 Lithuania records; `/api/cctv/frame/lithuania-72` returned HTTP 200, `image/jpeg`, `X-CCTV-Source: upstream-image`. The installed app also displayed a Lithuania camera with `SNAPSHOT · OK`.

All three failed checks concern console errors / HTTP 5xx responses from the existing `/api/terrain/heights` service. A separate request for `points=-97.74400,30.26800` reproduced HTTP 502. title: feat: Expand cctv layer globally using free/open-source webcam APIs
body:
### Problem

To this date i can notice there are too much less cameras in the rest of the world besides the US then there are in other apis

### Proposal

Integrate a static JSON dump from OpenWebcamDB into the project as a new global CCTV layer. For the first small version, we can parse a curated subset (e.g., 500–1,000 top global cameras) and project them onto the CesiumJS globe using their latitude/longitude coordinates. The UI would simply display the camera's static snapshot or live stream when clicked, proving the concept before scaling to a live API or a larger dataset. 


### Data source, license, and attribution

Source: OpenWebcamDB Directory (https://openwebcamdb.com)
License:Open / Public Domain Data (Crowdsourced and community-vetted public feeds)
It doesnt need a key. By using a downloaded JSON dump or their public endpoint, anyone can run this locally with zero API keys required.


### Will you build it?

Yes, I will build it.

title: feat: Historic Fires layer — archived FIRMS detections with spread replay, NIFC perimeters, context panel and voice control
body:
## Historic Fires: replay past wildfires from the NASA FIRMS archive

Adds a **Historic Fires** data layer (Events group) that replays archived NASA FIRMS detections for registered past wildfires, with a spread replay clock, the official NIFC perimeter, a Context-panel section and voice control. Ships with three events: Camp Fire 2018, Lahaina 2023, Park Fire 2024.

This is the archived counterpart of Active Fires: same `FIRMS_MAP_KEY`, same acknowledgement, no bundled data. Everything is fetched at runtime through the local proxy and cached under `.gev-cache/`.

### Why

Active Fires shows the last 24 h. A past fire is a spatial story with a timeline, and FIRMS has kept every detection since 2000. The Space Missions layer already proved the pattern of "layer + dedicated tooling + replay in event time"; this applies it to wildfires while staying inside the project's public-data, verifiable-only posture: what is drawn is either a satellite detection or an agency-mapped perimeter, labeled as such.

### What changed

**Server** — `server/providers/fire-history.js`
- `GET /api/fire-history` lists events registered in `config/fire_events.json` (works keyless).
- `GET /api/fire-history/<id>` fetches the FIRMS standard-processing archive in ≤5-day windows per source (the dated area API rejects longer ranges), sequentially for quota courtesy, filtered to the event's box and days. Complete events are cached permanently; partial results are served and only failed windows are retried.
- `GET /api/fire-history/<id>/perimeter` builds an ArcGIS query against one of two whitelisted NIFC Open Data layers from structured, character-restricted filters, keeps the largest matching polygon, simplifies to ~50 m and caches permanently. No key needed.
- Only registered events are ever requested (no client-supplied dates, boxes or URLs). Upstream bodies go through the shared capped readers (16 MB window / 4 MB perimeter) with 60 s timeouts.

**Layer** — `src/layers/fireHistory/`
- Depth-test-free points colored by event progress (yellow → ember), sized by FRP; ambient label; camera framing via the navigation-authority seam; analyst records; per-day timeline.
- Replay clock as pure functions (`replay.js`): 6 event-hours per real second × 0.5–4×; pending detections hide, fresh ones flare for 12 event-hours, older ones cool into the scar. `requestAnimationFrame` under a continuous-render hold released on pause/end/reset/disable/destroy.
- Row chips: one per event (settling through layer params), ▶ REPLAY / ❚❚ PAUSE, ↺ ALL, speed. Row subtitle reads the event clock; count reads `shown / total`.
- Official perimeter drawn as ground-clamped outlines after the detections load (best effort, superseded by a newer selection).

**Panel** — `panel.js`, `src/ui/styles/fire-history.css`
- A layer-owned `HISTORIC FIRES` section mounted in the Context panel above Radio while the layer is enabled: event roster, event card, detections-per-day chart carrying the replay cursor, seek and speed sliders, FOCUS / REPLAY SPREAD / ALL, and https references from the config. All config/feed text is HTML-escaped.
- Deliberately **not** a third context mode: Contacts/Space Missions carry dependency, restoration and exclusivity semantics that this feature does not need, so it follows the Bhote Koshi precedent of a layer-owned rail section instead of touching that state machine.

**Voice** — `control_fire_history`
- list / select / replay / pause / reset / speed / seek / focus / status. Every action except status enables the layer itself and waits (bounded, 8 s) for the archive; failures are stated plainly. Results carry the event, detection count, replay clock and peak day so confirmations come from evidence.
- The three Realtime tool-inventory pins were re-derived with dated notes (28 → 29 tools); pre-existing tool definitions are byte-identical (the "unchanged" digest still guards them).

**Share links**
- The selected event is a layer param (`eventId`; token `y`, option `e`). Chips, panel roster and voice all route through `dataManager.setLayerParams`, so a shared link restores the layer and its event.

**Docs / attribution**
- `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `DATA_SOURCES.md` (FIRMS archive + NIFC section), `README.md` layer table, `.env.example`, `src/data/dataCredits.js` (two new credits), `scripts/package-boundaries.json`, `scripts/format-scope.json` (separate mechanical commit).

### Adding an event

One entry in `config/fire_events.json`: id, name, region, inclusive UTC day range, bbox, archive sources, summary, https references and an optional NIFC perimeter reference. Invalid entries are dropped and logged, never fatal. No code change needed.

`scripts/fire-event-scaffold.mjs --name Dixie --year 2021 --state US-CA [--write]` does the lookup for you: it searches NIFC (WFIGS for 2020+, the perimeter history before), lists candidates, takes the largest, pads the record's extent into a bbox, derives the window from the published discovery/containment dates, picks the archive sources that existed that year and prints a validated entry — flagging anything it had to estimate. Pure helpers in `src/data/fireEventScaffold.js` with tests; verified live on Dixie 2021, Camp 2018 and Lahaina 2023.

### How it was verified

| Gate | Result |
|---|---|
| `npm test` | 4073 passed, 0 failed (new: event/window helpers, replay clock, model, panel builders, provider fixtures, voice handler, scaffold helpers) |
| `npm run test:track` | 109 / 109, no console errors, no 5xx |
| `npm run build`, `npm run format:check`, `npm run check:boundaries` | green |
| `node scripts/qa-fire-history.mjs` (headless Chromium against the dev server, real FIRMS key) | exit 0, no page errors |

The QA script covers: enable + first load frames the event; chips switch events through params; the Context section (roster, card, chart, seek, speed, reset); NIFC perimeter (5 rings for Camp Fire, panel text `62,053 HA · NIFC Interagency Fire Perimeter History`); replay with visible points equal to the clock's `shown` count (2,193 at 2018-11-09 23:47Z, 2×); disable clears the scene. Share-link restore was verified in a fresh page (`l=y&lo=y.e.lahaina-2023` → layer on, Lahaina, 151 detections).

Live archive loads used during development: Camp Fire 5,490 detections over 14 days (8 windows), Lahaina 151 (3 windows), Park Fire 15,919 (39 windows), all complete. Perimeters: 62,053 ha / 859 ha / 173,854 ha.

### Screenshots

<!-- attach from qa-shots/fire-history/ -->
- `fire-history-camp.png` — Camp Fire, static progress ramp (yellow = 8 Nov, red = last days)
- `fire-history-replay.png` — replay paused mid-event: cooled scar vs. bright active fronts
- `fire-history-panel.png` / `fire-history-panel-chart.png` — Context section with roster, card, daily chart + cursor, transport, NIFC outline on the map
- `fire-history-lahaina.png` — Lahaina, west Maui

### Notes for review

- FIRMS dated archive requests cap at 5 days (`"Invalid day range. Expects [1..5]"`), unlike the live `world/2` pull; the constant and its comment record this.
- NIFC publishes final perimeters for these incidents, not daily progression, so the replay remains detection-driven and the outline is a static reference labeled "final mapped perimeter".
- Both new data sources are U.S. public domain (FIRMS CC0 / NIFC government work); attribution text follows DATA_SOURCES.md and surfaces in the credit popover.
- Scope is larger than a typical PR; happy to split into layer → replay/panel → voice/share → perimeters if that reviews better (the commits are already cut that way).

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: Separate Director timing, clocks and scene-pack presentation
body:
Scene playback currently keeps authored-time calculations, timer handles and pack-specific presentation rules in the editor/controller. This change gives timing/seek calculations, playback clocks and scene-pack presentation their own owners while preserving existing controls and saved projects.

Stop settles pending holds and clears playback timers immediately. Replaced, destroyed or synchronously stopped clocks cannot publish through stale callbacks or acquire a timer after cancellation. Trusted scene-pack adapters supply hold requirements, map fallback and motion cleanup without editing the controller. Existing Nepal scenes, assets, IDs, attribution and contributor history are preserved.

Validation: 4,098 unit/allocation tests pass (one existing skip), formatting/import/package gates and build pass. Existing scene controls, 109 tracking checks, recorded voice and two-angle Nepal inspection pass. A focused browser harness exercises direct load, forward/backward seek, replay, completion and Stop during a long hold. Final browser verification and all three CI jobs passed on the reviewed candidate.

The four locator test fixtures now construct the extracted owners; their cancellation assertions are unchanged. Nine new focused tests cover the clock, timing and alternate pack composition. No dependency or scene-document format change.

title: Validate scene documents and preserve saved edits
body:
Scene imports previously normalized malformed files into default content and could discard saved visual edits. This separates authored-project migration from playback and validates files before replacing the current project. Version 3 stays the write format; legacy imports keep their IDs, camera edits, pack bindings and bloom migration.

- Add bounded renderer-independent document validation, field-path errors and a documented format.
- Preserve zero pitch, low camera heights, scope and extended detection settings. Protect unreadable browser saves and reject invalid writes without replacing saved bytes.
- Cancel and settle playback before a valid import, reject stale file reads, and retain empty projects.
- Preserve all scene assets, source links and existing contributor credit, including the Nepal sequence from @manjunath22466.

Validation: 4,111 unit/allocation tests pass (one existing skip), format/import/package checks, doctor and build pass. Browser checks pass 23 scene-control cases, 11 timing/seek/Stop cases and 109 tracking cases, with Nepal inspected from two angles. The final save-path browser recheck and recorded real voice also pass with zero uncaught browser/voice console errors. Thirteen new focused tests cover migration, bounds, preservation, cancellation and disposal.

title: Add Director camera anchors and authored moves
body:
Scene files can now name geographic anchors and define a camera move from an authored start to the shot's destination, with easing, duration and a hold. Playback and seek use the same coordinate sampler, including shortest-arc longitude crossings. Existing shots retain their ordinary flights.

- Version 4 preserves older projects, IDs, visual edits and pack bindings. Version-3 bloom keeps its existing scale.
- Validate anchor references, explicit ellipsoidal heights, easing and timing before replacing a project. Terrain-relative heights are rejected instead of guessed.
- Give authored animation frames their own owner. Stop, replacement, disposal, navigation handoff and manual input revoke the move; navigation during a hold prevents the next shot reclaiming the camera.
- Keep Update Shot's destination separate from shared anchors. Camera directions are currently authored in JSON; visual authoring remains a later step.

All existing scenes, assets, notices and contributor credit are preserved, including @manjunath22466's Nepal sequence.

Validation: 4,121 tests pass (one existing skip), including camera/migration/cancellation and allocation checks; format, boundary, doctor and build checks pass. Browser acceptance passes 12 new camera-direction checks, 23 existing scene-control checks and 11 timing/seek/Stop checks. Tracking passes all 109 checks; recorded real voice passes with no console errors. Austin was inspected at two local angles and the existing 25-shot Nepal scene still passes timing/content checks. All three CI jobs pass.

The first tracking attempt had three corridor-floor failures while the server reported an incomplete live terrain refresh. The unchanged rerun passed 109/109; no terrain code, test assertion or threshold changed.

title: Director: add bounded scene data packs and geographic placement
body:
## What changed

Scene documents can now declare versioned data-pack manifests and choose packs per shot. Import validates without acquiring assets; LOAD, seek and playback use registered sources with byte/time limits and optional size/hash verification. GeoJSON geometry, geographically placed PNGs and manually played media have separate storage and placement declarations, visible attribution, and owned cleanup on Stop/replacement/disposal.

The standalone `assets` registration resolves paths under `/scene-assets/`. Scene files cannot supply endpoints, headers, credentials or executable modules. Requests omit credentials, reject redirects and cannot escape the registered directory. The format remains extensible through trusted source/format adapters.

Existing version-1–4 projects migrate to version 5 without changing their authored camera behavior. Existing scene assets, links, licenses and contributor attribution remain intact. No new third-party assets or dependencies are introduced; browser QA uses self-authored synthetic fixtures.

## Verification

- Full unit/allocation suite: 4,134 passed, one existing skip; 13 new pack tests cover validation, path confinement, streaming limits, integrity, rollback and cancellation races.
- Boundaries, doctor, formatting and production build passed. After the final image-disposal fix, all 62 focused pack/presentation/Director tests and the build passed again.
- Pack browser QA passed all 15 checks: import/no-fetch, GeoJSON/image/media placement, ready geometry, attribution, manual media, seek, Stop, replacement, missing files and late responses. Cleanup asserts image material destruction and object-URL revocation. Final screenshots show all geometry and image placement at two angles after photoreal tiles settled.
- Visual review caught initially unready asynchronous entity geometry; bounded owned primitive batches now render correctly and are removed on cleanup. A focused regression reproduced and fixed image URLs surviving until a cancelled decode settled; image materials also receive explicit destruction.

- Existing camera directions: 12 browser checks; scene controls: 23; timing: 11; tracking: 109; recorded real voice passed with no console errors.
- The complete suite was rerun successfully on the final candidate. Final review also adds a passing source regression for releasing failed response bodies and refusing requests whose signal is already aborted. All final-head CI jobs passed in run 35042435012: Node 24.14.0, Node 26.x and Windows onboarding. Final diff and human author/committer metadata reviewed; no outstanding findings.

## Scope

JSON authoring, ellipsoid heights, non-dateline image rectangles, Point/LineString/Polygon GeoJSON, PNG images and native browser media. Terrain following, bundles, custom transforms, interactive actions and visual authoring remain separate stages. There is no persistent pack cache or offline fallback; missing assets fail explicitly.

title: feat: add declarative Director feature actions
body:
Scene files can now attach explicit actions to stable GeoJSON feature IDs. After a shot loads or a seek settles, clicking a feature selects its actions; native buttons provide the same actions with Tab and Enter/Space. Supported actions show a plain-text/source card, focus an anchor, seek another shot, or request an explicitly declared layer state.

Version-6 validation bounds action counts and transition chains, validates scene references and layer reset baselines, and rejects executable content and unsafe links. The portable session owns cancellation; the scene controller owns accessible controls and picking. Drawing/camera ownership and ordinary layer admission still apply. Stop, replacement and teardown remove handlers and cancel pending work. Same-shot seeks restore pack geometry released by Stop. Detached controls cannot invoke replacement actions.

Existing scenes, assets, licenses and contributor attribution are preserved. No dependencies or endpoints are added. Actions are authored in JSON and inactive during automatic playback; visual authoring and share previews remain follow-up work.

Validation: format, boundaries, doctor, full unit/allocation suite and production build; 14 interaction browser checks, 15 data-pack checks, 12 camera checks, 23 scene-control checks, 11 timing checks, all 109 tracking checks, and recorded voice with no console errors. Synthetic fixtures exercise real globe picking, accessible selection/cards, camera focus, pointer priority, cancellation, seek/reset and teardown. Controls and pack geometry were inspected over settled photoreal tiles at multiple views.

title: feat(voice): add Google Gemini Live voice model support
body:
## Summary
Adds Google Gemini 3.8 Live as a 3rd voice model tier alongside OpenAI (`standard`, `mini`, and `gemini`).

- **UI:** The voice dock model selector now cycles `STD` (GPT-4o) ➔ `MINI` (GPT-4o Mini) ➔ `GEM 3.8` (Gemini 3.8 Live).

## Verification
