- Boundary and formatting checks pass.

title: Add Director authoring, import previews and scene bundles
body:
Scene imports now open a preview before replacing the project. The preview reports pack attribution and source/layer availability without fetching assets; Cancel leaves the current project intact. EDIT DETAILS provides validated camera/anchor, timing, pack and action drafts, and SHARE SCENE exports the selected scene as JSON or a bounded bundle of explicitly selected files.

Portable bundle validation and byte ownership, dialog controls and scene composition have separate owners. Bundles verify confined paths, exact sizes and SHA-256; no remote files are fetched for export. Existing scene content, source links, licenses and contributor credit are preserved. No dependency or third-party asset is added.

Bundled bytes last for the current session: Stop releases rendered resources, replacement/teardown releases bytes, and a reload requires reimport. The preview explains this. Registered recipe media, live data and map tiles are not included. The detail editor is a basic validated draft interface, not a node graph.

Validation: boundary, doctor, formatting and build gates pass; 4,150 unit/allocation tests pass (one existing skip). Browser acceptance passes 21 sharing, 14 interaction, 15 pack, 12 camera, 24 scene-control, 11 timing and 109 tracking checks, plus recorded real voice with no console errors. Controls and overlays were inspected over settled 3D tiles and at a narrow viewport. Sharing acceptance covers canceled Apply during cleanup, stale drafts, removed-pack byte cleanup and teardown. Final diff and human commit metadata were reviewed.

title: feat(weather): add globe wind, observed weather and cyclone context
body:
## Round 7 — fourth owner field test

The flicker is gone on Google 3D. Three items remained.

- **Lightning coarser on Google 3D than on the globe.** The shell drew one 2048×1024 image over lightning's 250° extent (about 13 km per pixel) while the globe host tiles the same product at about 1 km per pixel. Each shell now also fetches a 4096×2048 image of a 2:1 window around the view (max(2 × the view's longitude span, 6°) wide, edges on a 0.5° grid inside the product bounds) and samples it on the same surface: the material carries the full-extent image and the window image with a window rectangle in texture coordinates, so there is no second mesh, no seam and no double blend. The window follows the camera on move end with hysteresis (it moves when the view centre leaves its inner half or the wanted width changes by more than half), stages invisibly until its image has drawn, keeps the previous window image through a time change until the next is decoded, and an older window image never stays over more than one newer frame. `/api/weather/image` accepts `bbox=west,south,east,north` (rounded to 0.25°, 2:1 within 1 %, inside the product bounds; cached by product, time, size and bbox); lightning's full-extent image is 4096×2048; global infrared keeps one image because its contrast depends on the requested extent. Decoded images are held up to 128 MiB per product: the shown frame and the warmed next frame, each full-extent and window.
- **Cyclone names as Cesium entity labels.** Storm cards (name and classification) and the selected storm's lead-hour labels now go through the app's shared label system (`src/layers/cyclones/labels.js` publishes to the world overlay host in the ambient-card group, with the same anchors, horizon test, collision handling and fades as fire and vessel cards); a card click selects its storm. The entity labels are gone.
- **The WEATHER accordion jumped to the top when another card opened.** Opening a card now makes one scroll write on the panel body: the smallest move that shows the whole card, or its header at the top when the card is taller than the body; refreshes never scroll. The rail's measuring pass lifted the body's `max-height`, which reset its scroll, so the rail now restores the scroll offset of any body marked `data-rail-scroller` (documented under "Adding a right-rail readout panel").

Verification, round 7: `npm test` 4598/4599 (1 platform skip), build, format, boundaries. Browser, Google 3D at the field-test pose (30.69N 108.65W, 771 km): window images ready for radar, satellite and lightning (20°×10° at 771 km, 7°×3.5° at 271 km); 0 entity labels, 3 storm cards published and 11 entries with a tracked storm selected; opening Lightning from the bottom of a scrolled body kept the card in view. The same label and scroll checks pass on the keyless server. A last read-only review of the window change found one edge case, now fixed: the surface counted hidden frames towards a drawn image, so hiding and resuming during a window change could apply the window a frame early. Main (#699) is merged into the branch. Final head c1447d5d: `npm test` 4600/4601 (1 platform skip), build, format, boundaries; shell probe on Google 3D (every product on the shell host, 0 imagery layers on the tileset, 0 tiles over the draped-texture budget, 0 coverage rebuilds in 6 s of playback, primitives back to baseline after the layers are turned off); flicker probe 50 samples, 0 over-budget tiles, modification counter 0 → 0; swap harness 0/26 black frames; panel probe passes; journeys 19/19 on both servers; teardown probe clean apart from the known init-time listeners; `test:track` 109/109 on both servers. Detail probe on Google 3D: one primitive per product with the window sampled on it; after a camera move the window stays empty until its image has drawn and was current within about a second; through 12 s of history playback the window image was current whenever radar was shown and for about half of the lightning samples, with the full-extent image showing otherwise, and an older window image never stayed over a newer frame for more than one step; decoded images held at most 128 MiB per product.

## Round 6 — draping replaced by raised shells on 3D Tiles

Lightning still popped in and out at some zooms on Google 3D after round 5. Both remaining mechanisms are inherent to draping imagery on 3D Tiles in Cesium 1.138: each tile primitive keeps at most 10 draped textures and needs 4–9 per product at the level Cesium picks, so the last products are truncated on whichever tiles refine into that state; and every change to the draped layer set rebuilds every tile's coverage, during which the tile draws no weather (the tileset's modification counter jumped 4 → 19 when a zoom ended).

On the tileset host the observed products and the wind colour field now render as raised, translucent, textured shells instead: one `Primitive` per product with a `RectangleGeometry` over the product bounds at 5.0–6.6 km (wind 5,000 · global infrared 5,500 · regional infrared 5,800 · radar 6,200 · lightning 6,600), a flat-shaded image material with an alpha uniform and a blank-texture guard, drawn in the opaque pass in primitive order with alpha blending and no depth writes so the stack order holds and nothing is picked through a shell; one full-extent image per frame from `/api/weather/image`, which now serves every product (4096×2048 for radar and regional infrared, 2048×1024 for lightning and the global mosaic; `size=WxH` up to the product's maximum; 24-hour cache by product, time and size; 16 MiB cap). The previous image stays until the next is decoded; decoded images are cached by bytes (48 MiB per renderer); the next frame is warmed during playback as before. There are no imagery layers on the tileset any more and no 60 km gate: the products stay visible down to street level, overhead. The globe host (Esri, Bing, keyless) is unchanged.

Verification, round 6: `npm test` 4575/4576 (1 platform skip), build, format, boundaries; a real-Cesium test builds the material, appearance and primitive in Node. Browser: shell probe on Google 3D — all four products report the shell host, 0 imagery layers on the tileset, 0 tiles over the draped-texture budget through a continuous zoom from 3 Mm to 40 km (below the old gate), 0 coverage rebuilds during 6 s of playback, primitives back to baseline after the layers are turned off; flicker probe 50 samples, 0 over-budget tiles, modification counter 0 → 0; swap harness 0/26 black frames; panel probe passes; journeys 19/19 on both servers; teardown probe clean (only the known init listeners) with non-weather layers at 56–60 fps versus 57–60 in the control page; `test:track` 109/109 on both servers.

## Round 5 — third owner field test (the draped tile profile below was replaced by shells in round 6)

- **Draped weather dropping out on 3D Tiles.** Lightning (and, per tile, any product) disappeared at some altitudes on Google 3D only. Cesium drapes imagery per tile primitive and keeps at most 10 draped textures per primitive (`ImageryPipelineStage` truncates the rest); it chooses, per layer, the imagery level where one tile is about the primitive's size, so a Google tile often straddles 2×2 or 3×3 imagery tiles per layer: measured 4–9 textures for one product, 27 for three and 29 for four, with 17 of 28 tiles over the cap at 1.6 Mm. On the tileset host the tiled products now use an altitude-banded draping profile (`src/layers/weather/drapingProfile.js`): 1024-px tiles with maximum level 5 below 400 km, 4 up to 1.5 Mm and 3 above (10% hysteresis on move-end; a band change re-stages the current frame through the same smooth swap as history), so each layer needs about one texture per tile at the same ground resolution as before; the global mosaic and the wind colour field drape as 512-px crops at levels 3 and 2. The tile proxy accepts `size=256|512|1024` (WMS dimensions and cache keys follow; the immutable header and the 8-request upstream limit are unchanged). The globe host keeps 256-px level-6 tiles, so Esri and Bing are untouched. Google tiles over the 10-texture budget at 1.60 Mm: three products 17/28 → 2/28, four products 20/28 → 5/28; at 1.28 Mm 13/24 → 3/24 and 16/24 → 6/24; at 600 km 15/24 → 3/24. A few large tiles at the edge of the view can still exceed the budget (they need up to nine tiles for one layer on their own); the products are whole across the view.
- **Card polish.** Layer icons on the card titles; the open card carries the CONTEXT panel's cyan stroke and wash; the wind action reads `Read wind at map center` and its result is a boxed reading with the value bright on its own line, the model and valid time beneath, and an `×` that clears the reading and the marker; compact readouts sit on the primary text colour for contrast over bright imagery.

Verification, round 5: `npm test` 4575/4576 (1 platform skip), build, format, boundaries; `test:track` 109/109 on both servers; altitude probe on Google with four products: Google tiles over the 10-texture budget at 1.60 Mm: three products 17/28 → 2/28, four products 20/28 → 5/28; at 1.28 Mm 13/24 → 3/24 and 16/24 → 6/24; at 600 km 15/24 → 3/24. A few large tiles at the edge of the view can still exceed the budget (they need up to nine tiles for one layer on their own); the products are whole across the view.; swap harness 0/26 black frames on Google; journeys on both servers; panel probe after the polish on Google.

## Round 4 — panel information hierarchy

- **Order and grouping.** Cyclone advisories first, then Wind (forecast), then an explicit OBSERVED HISTORY group whose heading, scope line and timeline sit above the three products the timeline drives: Rain radar, Satellite clouds, Lightning density.
- **One open card at a time.** The open card shows the full anatomy; the others are one line each (title, coverage, observation time or a status such as `Map center outside coverage`; cyclones show `3 active storms · Fay selected`). A header click or a layer the user just enabled chooses the open card; feed refreshes and clock ticks never change it; disabling the open layer opens the first remaining card; the choice lasts for the page session. Headers are buttons with `aria-expanded`.
- **Labelled setting rows instead of chip clouds.** `MODEL`, `FIELD`, `UNITS` (whenever a speed value is visible), `MOTION` for wind; `REGION`, `IMAGE`, `OPACITY` for satellite clouds; `OPACITY` for radar and lightning. Verbs live in the card footer: `View US radar`, `View coverage`, `View Americas & Pacific`, `Official advisory ↗`, and `Read wind here` (at map center), whose result appears as a `WIND AT SAMPLED LOCATION · lat lon` block with speed and direction, model and valid time, and an `×` that clears the reading and the marker. The sampled location stays fixed until the next read; a model change re-samples it.
- **Cyclones card leads with the list** (name · category · wind; the selected row highlighted; click selects and flies), then the selected advisory's details, legend and the official link. Opening or collapsing the card never changes the selected storm.
- The card building blocks (`src/ui/railCardBlocks.js`: summary line, selectable list, detail lines, labelled setting rows, legend, footer actions, result block) are documented in `docs/CODE-BOUNDARIES.md` for the sibling satellite-scene panel.

Verification, round 4: `npm test` 4542/4543 (1 platform skip), build, format, boundaries; `test:track` 109/109 on both servers; panel v3 probe on both servers (order, single open card, header buttons with `aria-expanded`, labelled rows, footer verbs, sampled-wind block and clear, storm list and fly, fallback when the open layer is disabled, 720 px); panel content 594 px in the 370 px allocation with the cyclones card open (was 1,261 px).

## Round 3 — second owner field test (the v2 panel below was reorganised in round 4)

- **Right rail stability.** Expanding CCTV next to the docked WEATHER panel made the rail flip between focus and normal layout on every pass (about 200 flips in three seconds), because the focus decision measured panel heights that change with the mode it had just chosen. The rail now measures every panel's intrinsic need under a synchronous CSS override that removes live allocations and hides nothing, enters focus when the need exceeds the available height, leaves only when it drops below that by 48 px or 6% of the viewport, and an auto-collapse can schedule one follow-up pass. Probe: 0 flips, 7 attribute mutations in 3.2 s (was 615).
- **WEATHER panel v2.** The left DATA LAYERS rows for the five weather layers are toggles only (icon, name, source line, ON/OFF). Every setting lives in that product's card in the WEATHER panel as a collapsible Settings section (model, field, units, Inspect; N. America/Global, Clouds only/Full image, Soft/Vivid, coverage navigation; the storm list and the advisory link for cyclones). The wind reading appears as a section inside the wind card with unit chips and a Clear action instead of a floating box. Cards use the row typography tokens (names, mono meta, panel-title section labels). The pattern is built from `src/ui/railCards.js`, `railSections.js`, `railTimeline.js`, `chipGroup.js` and `rowList.js`; `docs/CODE-BOUNDARIES.md` describes how another feature adds a right-rail readout panel with them.
- **Session caching.** Time-keyed tiles and the global image are served `immutable` for a day so the browser cache answers revisited frames; the satellite renderer keeps the last six decoded global mosaics in memory (cleared when the layer is disabled or the product changes); while playback runs, the next frame is warmed with at most eight cancellable requests.

Verification, round 3: `npm test` 4540/4541 (1 platform skip), build, format, boundaries; `test:track` 109/109 on the keyless server and 109/109 on the Google 3D server; panel v2 probe on both servers (card sections, chips inside cards drive the layers, storm list flies, wind reading section with unit chips and Clear, typography parity with the rows, 720 px); journeys on both servers; CCTV thrash probe 0 flips on both; scrub-latency probe before/after (global revisit 280 → 263 ms with a cached mosaic; regional revisit unchanged at ~330 ms, which is the frame-admission settle, not network).

## Round 2 — owner field test follow-ups

Field test on Google Photorealistic 3D Tiles and on the keyless globe raised nine items; all are addressed on this head.

- **Black globe during history swaps on 3D Tiles.** Cesium withholds a tile's draw commands while its draped imagery is not ready unless the tileset was created with `asynchronouslyLoadImagery: true`; every history swap adds a staging layer, so every loaded tile stopped drawing until its new texture arrived. Both Google tileset routes now load draped imagery asynchronously, the replacement layer becomes visible before the outgoing one retires (one rendered frame later), and imagery ordering skips layers already in order. Swap harness (`scripts/qa-weather-swap.mjs`, 26 captures over Earlier + 10 s of Play at the Earth view): 3 black frames with up to 80% of the globe disc black → 0.
- **Seamed, slow global frames.** The global satellite product is now fetched once per frame as the bounded 2048×1024 mosaic, decoded and cropped locally into tiles on both hosts, so there are no per-request contrast seams and a swap costs one request (frame load ~0.3 s on this connection instead of ~37 tile requests).
- **Hard cloud edges; no way to see the whole image.** The satellite layer (GOES-19/18 longwave infrared Band 14 regional; NESDIS global longwave mosaic) is filtered by a soft alpha ramp in linear brightness applied once per decoded image instead of a hard `colorToAlpha` cut, and a `Clouds only / Full image` choice on the row is kept in share links. A same-camera probe confirms the filter leaves open water untouched.
- **History is one moment in time.** One observed-weather clock (`src/layers/weather/clock.js`) drives radar, satellite and lightning: a union timeline, per-product nearest-at-or-before selection within a bounded gap (30 min; 3 h for the hourly global product), Latest = newest per product, playback that waits for every product to settle, and a product with no frame in its gap hides and says so rather than showing a stale image as if it were synchronised. The wind row states that the forecast does not follow history.
- **WEATHER panel = readout, rows = configuration** (round 3 moved the configuration into the cards as well; see above). The right-rail WEATHER panel now shows one card per active product (name, coverage badge, that product's own observation time and age, a reserved status line, colour ramp; the selected storm's advisory details and official link on the cyclones card) above ONE history timeline for radar, satellite and lightning (native range slider with `‹ ›`, Latest, Play/Pause and a UTC readout). The left DATA LAYERS rows keep configuration only: on/off, model and field, N. America/Global, Clouds only/Full image, Soft/Vivid, coverage navigation and the storm list (a click selects and flies); the per-row transport chips, duplicated legends and info blocks are gone, leaving one status line. The panel is built from two generic modules, `src/ui/railCards.js` and `src/ui/railTimeline.js`, composed by `src/ui/weatherPanel.js`; `docs/CODE-BOUNDARIES.md` documents how another feature adds a right-rail readout panel with them.
- **Cyclones on the surface; select, focus, clear.** Tracks and cone fills are ground-classified on terrain and 3D Tiles (cone outlines as clamped polylines), markers and labels never depth-fail, lead-hour labels appear within 4,000 km. Clicking a storm in the list selects it and flies the camera; clicking empty map clears; a refresh never undoes an explicit clear; on 3D Tiles a pick that resolves to the tileset surface counts as empty map.
- **Wind units, coverage.** The km/h · m/s · mph chips render only when a speed legend is visible, and the same units sit inside the inspection card, where changing them re-formats the open reading without closing it. Coverage is a badge on every card: CONUS, North America, Global · 60°S–60°N, Americas + Pacific, Global · 1° grid, Atlantic + E/C Pacific.

## Verification (round 2)

Gates on the final head: `npm test` 4525/4526 (1 platform skip), `npm run build`, `npm run format:check`, `npm run check:boundaries`; `npm run test:track` 109/109 against the Google 3D server and 109/109 against the keyless server.

Browser evidence (Apple M4 Max, Chrome 153), each run on both map sources:

| probe | Google 3D | keyless globe |
|---|---|---|
| history-swap harness (26 captures, Earlier + 10 s Play, global satellite) | 3/26 black frames, max 80% of the disc → **0/26, 0.0%** | 0/26 before and after |
| shared clock (step from any row, play, pause, latest, deep history) | same targets and per-product selections on both hosts; products with no frame in their gap hide and say so | same |
| cyclones (auto → user → cleared intents, row click flies, empty-map click clears, refresh keeps a clear) | all cases pass, including the 3D Tiles surface pick | all cases pass |
| WEATHER panel (5 cards, one timeline, scrub/play/latest, Controls opens the row, wind units gated and live in the inspection card, 720 px) | pass | pass |
| scripted user journey (Earth view → every wind field and model → radar, satellite, lightning, cyclones → 600 km … 350 m → history playback → drag/wheel) | 19 steps, no page errors | 19 steps, no page errors |

Not changed on purpose: the union timeline is the union of every product's advertised frames, so playback can reach a time where only lightning (3 h of history) has a frame; the other products then hide and state the gap rather than showing a stale image. A reload of a URL that carries a share hash applies the shared view and not the stored collapse choice, which is the existing rule for every rail panel.

## Round 1 — performance report follow-ups

The candidate was refreshed onto current `main` and field-tested on both map sources — Google Photorealistic 3D Tiles (keyed) and the keyless Esri globe — with a scripted user journey (Earth view → every wind field and model → radar, satellite, lightning, cyclones → storm and radar views → 600 km, 120 km, 12 km, 1.2 km, 350 m → history playback → drag/wheel) and a matched-route benchmark. Findings and fixes:

- **Weather imagery on Google 3D Tiles.** Radar, satellite infrared, lightning and the wind colour field were imagery layers on the Cesium globe, which the photorealistic stack hides, so nothing drew there while history playback kept advancing. The products now resolve an imagery host per map stack: the globe when it is shown, otherwise the shown tileset's `imageryLayers` (Cesium 3D Tiles imagery draping), re-homing on stack switches; with no host, playback pauses and the row says so. Level-zero providers (the global infrared mosaic and the wind field) are tiled on the tileset host because Cesium 1.138's draping clamps coverage to `maximumLevel − 1`.
- **Street-level cost on 3D Tiles.** Cesium re-maps every loaded tile when a draped layer is added, removed or re-alpha'd, which made history playback at 1.2 km over dense Google tiles drop to 18–27 fps. Below 60 km camera height on a tileset host the observed products now hide their layer, stage nothing and pause playback (the row says so), resuming above; the products are level-6 rasters (~2.4 km per pixel) with nothing to show at that scale.
- **Infrared display filter** (superseded in round 2 by the soft ramp and the Clouds only / Full image choice): pixels below a brightness threshold were drawn transparent so bright (cold) areas stood out instead of a grey rectangle over the basemap.
- **Wind streamline culling.** The 7,200 curves were one primitive Cesium could not cull; they are now batched in 30° cells, horizon- and frustum-culled per frame, faded out below 60 km camera height, and the animation loop parks when no curve is visible.
- **Wind colour-field fade.** The ~1° scalar field fades out between 1,200 km and 200 km camera height instead of washing out city views (0.1-step move-end updates on 3D Tiles to avoid draw-command rebuilds).
- **Cyclones beyond the horizon** (markers, labels, tracks, cones) are hidden on every map source.
- **Weather summary panel** reserves its status line so it no longer jumps during playback; layer-panel refreshes are coalesced per frame and DOM writes are change-gated.
- **Weather summary panel** now lives in the right rail between CCTV and CONTEXT with the standard chrome (drag, collapse, remembered state, hidden in clean view) instead of floating over the map; it appears while a weather layer is on and expands itself the first time (round 2 turned it into the readout panel described above).
- **Throttled tiles** (HTTP 429/503) retry up to three times per tile before a frame is failed; proxy queue bounds raised from 32/40 to 96/120 (upstream concurrency unchanged at 8).

New QA tooling: `scripts/qa-weather-perf.mjs` (matched-route throughput and idle-work harness with DOM/height instrumentation) and `scripts/qa-weather-journey.mjs` (user-journey screenshot capture with per-step layer diagnostics). Both need a running dev server.

## Verification, round 1 (Apple M4 Max, Chrome 153, 1200×886 @ DPR 2)

Gates on the final head: `npm test` 4477/4478 (1 platform skip), `npm run build`, `npm run format:check`, `npm run check:boundaries`; `npm run test:track` 109/109 against the Google 3D server and 109/109 against the keyless server with bundled imagery.

Idle test, camera parked at 1.2 km over Austin, normal render governor, pre-fix vs fixed build on the same machine:

| state | redraws / s | DOM mutations / 8 s | summary height jumps / 8 s |
|---|---|---|---|
| history playing (radar + infrared + lightning), Google 3D | 3.0 → 0 (products parked below 60 km) | 488 → 36 | 12–13 → 0 |
| history playing, keyless globe | 3.1 → 2.9–4.7 (frames keep swapping; the imagery is visible there) | 420 → 30–33 | 7 → 0 |
| wind on (either map source) | 29.4 → 0 | 0 → 0 | 0 → 0 |

Wind visibility on the fixed build (keyless journey diagnostics): 53 of 72 cells at the Earth view, 37 at 5,300 km, 12 at 600 km, 7 at 120 km, 0 below 15 km with the scene idling. Route throughput on this GPU is 60 fps before and after at native resolution and at `resolutionScale` 2; the M5 laptop numbers in the earlier report were GPU-bound and could not be reproduced here, so the idle-work and vertex-count evidence above is what changed.

Google 3D with the imagery host: the US radar view loads real tiles on the tileset (radar 42, infrared 61 in the final journey, versus 0 on the draft), the wind colour field drapes, and at the 1.2 km pose the scene idles with wind on and the observed products parked below 60 km. Street-level orbit/zoom windows are back at the all-off numbers (matched-route harness: history playing at 1.2 km went from 18–27 fps with draping to 60 fps with the 60 km gate).

Not reproduced: the 20–22 s keyless frame loads (NOAA answers in 0.2–0.4 s from here) and the 300 ms hitches beyond the wind zoom-out long tasks, which the culling removes. The 429s seen during zoom bursts on the keyless globe are terrain tiles from the terrain proxy, not weather; that is pre-existing `main` behavior and is being handled separately.

## Community prior art

Unchanged from the draft (#459/#464 wind foundation retained with author history; design input from #588, #457, #458, #414, discussion #85). Two later PRs informed this refresh: #618 (@monwiss) for treating a hidden globe as an explicit product state rather than a silently healthy toggle, and #680 (@GGPOShadows) for the render-count and canvas-size discipline used in the benchmark harness. No code was imported from either.

## Remaining acceptance

- [x] Owner field tests on both map sources — rounds 2 to 7 above; the eighth test approved the head for merge.
- [ ] Squash-merge with `Co-authored-by` trailers for the retained community commits.

title: feat(weather): thirty selectable layers on one globe, metered on purpose
body:
Adds an optional **Weather** layer drawing Vaisala Xweather raster tiles, and a
`WEATHER` panel in the right rail that decides which of them draw and when they
are allowed to cost anything.

The globe gains observed radar, lightning, severe-weather warnings, tropical
cyclones, storm cells, surface analysis and a dozen analysis fields. Radar alone
is on by default, so the globe is unchanged until someone asks for more.

Branched from and merged up to `main` at `a65d9d8`.

## Why Xweather, and not NOAA / ECCC

**On the key first, because it is easy to mis-read.** Xweather is BYOK freemium:
15,000 accesses a month free, no credit card to obtain one. That is the same
shape as keys this project already carries — Live Vessels and Active Fires both
need one and have no keyless path either, and the flagship photorealistic globe
through the direct Google route needs *billing enabled*, which this README
already says. Against that, a free-tier key with no card is not the heaviest ask
here. What is genuinely new is the metering past the allowance, which is exactly
what the WEATHER panel exists to keep deliberate.

The free stack was not skipped, either — it was **built first, shipped in
sixteen commits on this branch, and then deleted**. The history is in this PR;
what follows is what measuring it showed.

### One free source could not do it

No single free source is global, observed and current at once, so the free
design was a ladder, each rung covering the one below:

| source | grid | runs | observed? | reaches |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ECCC GDPS | 15 km | 2×/day | no | the globe |
| ECCC RDPS | 10 km | 4×/day | no | North America, north Atlantic, Scandinavia, Arctic |
| NOAA/NWS MRMS → IEM NEXRAD | ~1 km | 5 min | **yes** | United States |

Radar is the only honest one and covers a few percent of the planet. The models
fill the rest, and RDPS existed only because it is both finer *and* fresher than
GDPS where it reaches — a +3 h forecast from the 18Z run instead of +9 h from
12Z.

### Stitching them produced one incoherent globe

Three sources on one sphere meant three of everything, and they disagreed:

- **Coverage never closed.** RDPS advertises the whole northern hemisphere,
  which is the *envelope of a rotated grid* rather than its domain — believing
  it would have put empty tiles over most of the planet. Its real footprint had
  to be mapped by probing a field that is never blank where the model runs.
- **Different gradients per zone.** GeoMet's default style buckets the field
  into eight classes: measured over one 5,000 km extent, 8 distinct colours and
  a 42 km mean colour run, so 15 km cells merged into flat plateaus. Forcing
  `PRECIPPRTMMH-LINEAR` gave 714 colours and an 18 km run — the native grid —
  but that is one source tuned to match another, per source, forever.
- **Visible seams.** The CONUS cutout that stopped modelled rain reading as
  observed ran its southern edge at 24 N, just below Miami, so zoomed-in views
  there showed the model resume along a straight line, with holes wherever radar
  was silent inside the box.
- **Different refresh moments.** Radar inherited the model's hourly tick, so a
  five-minute product sat up to an hour stale; each tier ended up with its own
  cadence, which means adjacent regions of the same globe show different
  moments. Each also needed its own alpha to sit consistently over the basemap.

Every one of those was fixable, and each was fixed. The result was still a globe
assembled from parts that did not agree.

### And the parts themselves were forecasts

The defect that ended it was not rendering. GDPS runs twice a day and takes
about five hours to publish, so **the field valid *now* is a +3 h to +15 h
forecast — measured at +15 h**; RDPS is +3 h to +9 h. Both already pinned the
newest run available, so no layer work could close it: a forecast half a day old
and a live radar sweep disagree about where the rain is, which is exactly what
showed on zooming in.

The obvious escape was checked rather than assumed. **NASA IMERG** is global
*and* observed, but 7 h 20 m stale — rain travels 300–500 km in that time, so it
places worse than the model it would replace.

### Even as a precipitation source alone, it is the better one

Set aside the other twenty-nine layers and compare like with like. Against the
ECCC ladder, `radar-global` is finer (~1 km observed against a 15 km and a 10 km
model grid), global at that detail rather than only where a regional model
reaches, and coherent across zoom — one source, one palette, one moment, no
seams and no cutouts.

Its one real drawback is ours rather than the vendor's: upstream refreshes every
two minutes, but the default refresh is once a day to stay inside the free
allowance, so what you see is an observation from the last refresh. Even then it
compares well — a day-old *observation* of where rain was is a different and
smaller error than a *forecast* of where rain will be in three to fifteen hours,
and the panel's Refresh button closes it on demand for the cost of one tile set.

### What one observed source bought

Xweather `radar-global` is observed, global (ground radar with satellite fill
between networks) and refreshed upstream every two minutes. It replaced all four
placements, and took the stitching machinery with it: the rectangle covers, the
complementary-cover arithmetic, the cutouts, the zoom bands, the partition rule,
a layer-scoped WMS capabilities parser (the unfiltered GeoMet document is
~39 MB) and the concurrent multi-source reads. One palette, one refresh moment,
no seams.

Scope note: the layer is optional and off by default, the key is BYOK with a
free 15,000 accesses a month, and without one the row says so rather than
degrading quietly. Nothing else in the app changes behaviour because of it. If a
mandatory-key layer is outside what this project wants to carry, that is a
reasonable call and better made now than after review — the reasoning above is
offered so it can be made on the evidence.

## Why the panel exists

Every tile is billed against a monthly allowance, and the bill scales with **how
many layers are enabled, not how often they refresh** — each enabled layer
re-fetches on every camera move. One exploratory session of a single layer
fetched 405 tiles, about 2.7% of a month.

So the feature is a control surface, not a layer list:

- Layers are opted into one at a time; offering one is free, enabling one spends.
- Refresh is a button. A timer is available and off until chosen.
- The running monthly total sits beside the controls that move it.
- The layer set was chosen so that a daily refresh of everything enabled, for a
  whole month, fits inside the free 15,000.

Every layer offered bills at the base rate. The vendor also sells lightning and
air-quality products at five and ten times that; each has a base-rate equivalent
that is as good or better, so the surcharged variants are excluded and a test
names them.

## Notable decisions

**The proxy is mandatory, not an optimisation.** Xweather authenticates by
putting *both* halves of the credential in the tile URL path, so the browser can
never be allowed to build that URL. It fetches same-origin
`/api/xweather/tile/{layer}/{z}/{x}/{y}.png`. The layer name arrives from the
browser, so it is checked against the catalogue before the key is read —
forwarded on trust this would be an open proxy to every product on the account.
Log lines from that proxy are masked, because an upstream failure quoting the
request it attempted would otherwise write the secret to disk.

**One catalogue, three consumers.** `src/data/xweatherCatalogue.js` is the only
list of drawable layers. The Node provider derives its allowlist and each
layer's zoom ceiling from it; the browser layer derives its spec table; the
panel derives its labels and grouping. They cannot disagree.

**Fields are single-select.** Continuous fields paint every pixel (24–160 KB a
tile against an overlay's 116 bytes), so two would bill for one visible layer.
Sparse overlays stack freely above them, held there by paint rungs rather than
by refresh order.

**Zoom ceiling is a property of the layer.** Radar and the continuous fields are
sampled rasters and stop at level 9, where the service starts upsampling. The
symbol layers — lightning, warning polygons, storm cells, cyclone tracks — are
redrawn at each level at constant screen size and run to 12, because magnifying
a symbol scales the symbol rather than blurring a field.

**Coverage is on the row.** A layer drawing nothing over Europe because its
source stops at a border is indistinguishable, on screen, from a broken one.
Each such layer carries its coverage on the chip, checked against the coverage
Vaisala publishes, and forecasts are labelled as forecasts.

**Refresh means refresh.** Tiles carry a freshness floor — the moment new data
was last asked for — so a cached tile older than that is refetched. The cache
TTL is tuned for spend and is far longer than the weather stays still; without
the floor the button would re-request every tile and be served the same bytes.

**The panel follows its layer.** It is the layer's control surface, so it is
absent while the layer is off and opens with it when switched on, and the layer
stays *on* in the two states it is designed to explain — no key, and a photoreal
stack hiding the globe — rather than failing to enable and taking the
explanation with it.

**It does not draw in 3D, and that was a decision.** A photorealistic stack
hides the globe and every imagery layer with it. Draping the tiles on the 3D
tileset instead was built and measured before being withdrawn: Cesium picks the
draped level per model primitive rather than from the camera, so sharpness
oscillates as you descend and magnification turns lightning glyphs into blobs.
`docs/KNOWN-ISSUES.md` records the measurements, so the next person to notice
finds the answer rather than rebuilding it.

## Security notes for review

- **No credential reaches the client.** Neither half appears anywhere in `dist/`
  after a build; the browser only ever sees the relative `/api/xweather/*` route.
  Pinned by a test on the tile template.
- **One new outbound host**, `https://maps.api.xweather.com`, fixed in the
  provider — not composed from any client input. The layer segment is validated
  against the catalogue allowlist *before* the credential is read, so a probe
  for an unlisted product is a 400 and never a billable fetch.
- **Logs are scrubbed.** The credential sits in the URL path, so an upstream
  error quoting its own request would otherwise write the secret to disk. A test
  asserts the mask holds while keeping the message useful.
- **Supply chain shrinks**: one devDependency swapped (`vite-plugin-cesium` →
  `rollup-plugin-external-globals`), 3 packages added, 31 removed, net **−28**.

## Also in this PR

Two changes that are not the Weather layer, called out so they can be judged
separately:

- **`vite-plugin-cesium` replaced with an in-repo plugin** (`build/cesium.js`),
  dropping the deprecated `sourcemap-codec` chain while producing byte-identical
  build output. The upstream plugin is unmaintained and the layer needed a
  working Cesium build to land on. Happy to split this out if preferred.
- **The provider disk cache and the voice debug log are excluded from the dev
  server's file watcher.** The tile proxies write a file per tile; watching that
  directory costs a cold tile 3–9 s instead of ~150 ms, because the watcher's
  stat calls take the libuv threads `getaddrinfo` needs. Development only —
  there is no watcher in preview or production — but it affected every
  disk-cached provider.

## Without a key

There is no keyless mode for this layer, unlike every other source here. The row
reports `UNAVAILABLE · ADD XWEATHER KEY` and draws nothing, rather than showing
an empty globe that reads as "no weather anywhere".

## Verification

Run on the merged tree, at `main` `a65d9d8`:

| Gate | Result |
|---|---|
| `npm test` | 4217 tests, 4207 pass, 0 fail |
| `npm run test:track` | 109 pass, 0 fail — no console errors, no 5xx |
| `npm run build` | clean |
| `npm run format:check` | 936 source files clean |
| `npm run check:boundaries` | clean |
| `scripts/qa-l9-matrix.mjs` | B10b/B10c/B11b cover tiles, accounting, the allowlist refusal and the keyless path |

Exercised against the live API: layer selection and single-select fields; share
links round-tripping a multi-layer selection; the budget counter moving only
when a fetch actually happens; refresh refetching (23 requests, 23 `MISS`, +23)
where a cached pass is 23 `HIT`, +0; two dev servers on one checkout summing
their spend rather than overwriting it; the panel appearing and disappearing
with its layer row; `UNAVAILABLE · GLOBE HIDDEN IN 3D` under a photoreal stack.

Zoom ceilings were measured rather than assumed, by comparing the same ground at
levels 9 and 12 for both a sampled raster and a symbol layer.

## Merge notes

One collision with upstream: share-link token `n` is now the Directions layer,
so Weather takes `k`. Nothing had shipped with `n`. The registry holds 22 layers
on 22 distinct tokens.

Three pinned Realtime tool digests are re-derived, deliberately — `weather`
joins the two layer menus in `actionSchemas.js` and the common-name mapping in
`toolDescriptions.js`. The serialized schema length is unchanged at 26,257.

## Docs

`CHANGELOG.md`, `README.md`, `DATA_SOURCES.md` (license and attribution),
`docs/CURRENT-STATE.md`, `docs/CODE-BOUNDARIES.md` (new package exports),
`SECURITY.md` (allowlist, credential scrubbing, the LAN quota list) and
`.env.example`.

The shared catalog cap round-robins across packs; `CCTV_VANCOUVER_MAX_SOURCES` sets the pack cap (600 by default, nearest downtown first, ceiling 1000). - **Opt-in gate:** the open-data licence (Open Government Licence – Vancouver) covers only the link/location list, and the City's Terms of Use don't confirm redistribution of the frame JPEGs — so, like NYC and Lithuania, the pack is **off unless `CCTV_VANCOUVER_ENABLED=1`**. - **Catalog data:** intersection-level coordinates (the city publishes one point per intersection), headings derived from the city's own N/E/S/W designations (`headingConfidence: 'medium'`), frame URLs pinned to `https://trafficcams.vancouver.ca/` and enforced on every row by the loader. - **Refresh:** explicit 5-minute ambient refresh entry in the CCTV LOD table (`city of vancouver traffic cams`) — the city's stills regenerate on a 300 s page cycle. - **Attribution:** new `vancouver-cctv` credit in the data-attribution popover and a `DATA_SOURCES.md` row (licence nuance included). - **Curated location:** Vancouver joins `CITY_POIS` with five fly-to POIs (Canada Place, Vancouver Lookout, City Hall, BC Place, Science World) and is registered in the place-name localizations (en/es/ru). - **Docs:** `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md` and `DATA_SOURCES.md` updated in the same PR; the changelog entry lives in `changelog.d/620-vancouver-cctv-pack.md`. ## Screenshots _Coverage overview — 834 cameras clustered across 219 intersections with live label frames and panel state._ _Canada Place / downtown waterfront — labeled cameras over photoreal tiles._ _Full-screen projected live frame (Alma St & Point Grey Rd) with raw-prior monitor feed in the CCTV panel._ ## Verification - All 834 frame URLs return `image/jpeg` from `trafficcams.vancouver.ca`; the loader enforces the origin prefix on every row. The merged catalog serves 600 of 834 with `CCTV_VANCOUVER_ENABLED=1` (default cap, `CCTV_VANCOUVER_MAX_SOURCES`), 0 without, peer packs unaffected. - `npm test`, `npm run build`, `format:check`, `check:boundaries`, `i18n` and `changelog:check` all green at the head.

title: feat(voice): add ChatGPT OAuth for Realtime voice
body:
Adds an explicit ChatGPT/Codex OAuth option for Realtime voice in Provider Settings. API-key voice remains the default, and the existing mic flow and API-key spend controls remain available. The OAuth choice reuses a local sign-in or starts `codex login` and waits for it to complete.

The local credential reader now accepts only ChatGPT token-mode credentials with an access and refresh token, checks JWT expiry with a 60-second margin, and bounds tokens without an `exp` claim using the auth file's modification time. It reads the Codex file without changing it. Status, login readiness, and token minting share this validation. The optional `GEV_PREFER_CODEX_OAUTH=true` setting blocks API-key minting and tells the user to select OAuth; it never switches auth modes silently. OAuth access and login launch remain local-only, with a same-origin check on the login POST. The token response identifies the selected auth source in `X-GEV-Voice-Auth`.

OAuth sessions now retain reported response and token counts and show **COST UNKNOWN** instead of hiding the readout or implying zero spend. An interrupted response is marked incomplete. The API-key dollar estimate, warning, and hard cap are unchanged.

Validation: `npm test` (all groups passed, including 13 performance-budget checks; one platform skip), `npm run build`, `npm run format:check`, `npm run check:boundaries`, and `git diff --check`.

title: feat: add DeepSeek AI chat + HUD summary (multi-provider)
body:
## Summary

Adds **DeepSeek V4.1-Flash** as an alternative AI provider so the app works without an OpenAI key.

- **DeepSeek AI Chat panel** - a floating chat terminal that drives the map through the existing 28 voice/action tools. Dictation and text-to-speech use the browser-native Web Speech API / `speechSynthesis` (zero-cost STT/TTS).
- **HUD summary fallback** - when `OPENAI_API_KEY` is absent but `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` is set, the 5-word tactical HUD summary routes to DeepSeek.
- **Server-side key isolation** - `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` never leaves the server; a new provider plugin exposes `/api/deepseek/chat` and `/api/deepseek/status`.
- **Opt-in rate limiting** - `GEV_RATELIMIT_DEEPSEEK_PER_MIN` (default unlimited), mirroring the existing OpenAI limiter.

## Why

OpenAI Realtime voice runs roughly $5-$18 per active hour; DeepSeek's cached tool-calling plus small HUD summaries cost a fraction of a cent per session. This makes AI map control usable for people without OpenAI access or on a tight budget.

## Changes

- New `server/providers/deepseek.js` plugin (chat + status + HUD summary), registered in `server/providers/local.js`.
- `server/providers/openai/hud-summary.js` now delegates to DeepSeek when no OpenAI key is configured.
- New client modules `src/ai/deepseekChat.js` + `src/ai/deepseekController.js`, wired in `src/app/tools.js` alongside voice.
- Styles in `src/ui/styles/deepseek-chat.css`; obstacle selectors updated in `panelLayoutController.js` / `worldOverlay.js`.
- `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` added to key setup, Pinokio environment, and setup-doctor; tests updated.

title: Add nine Ontario transit feeds, with per-feed mode and route naming
body:
Adds nine Ontario transit feeds and two small mechanisms that let a feed speak
its riders' vocabulary. References #70.

Toronto is the largest metro in North America with no coverage here, and the
surrounding region publishes open realtime data of unusually good quality. This
is a completed regional survey rather than a selection: every Ontario feed that
clears the bar is included, and every one that doesn't is listed below with the
reason.

### The bar

A feed ships only if it is **public** (no key, no registration), served over
**HTTPS**, carries **real per-vehicle coordinates** (not positions inferred from
arrival predictions), reports **per-vehicle timestamps** so staleness is
honest, and is under a licence that **permits redistribution with attribution**.

### Feeds added

| Feed | Region | Licence |
|---|---|---|
| TTC | Toronto | Open Government Licence – Toronto |
| MiWay | Mississauga | City of Mississauga Open Data Terms of Use |
| Hamilton HSR | Hamilton | City of Hamilton Open Data Licence |
| Durham Region Transit | Durham Region | Region of Durham Open Data Licence v.1.0 |
| YRT/Viva | York Region | YRT Open Data Licence v2.0 (UK OGL-derived) |
| Guelph Transit | Guelph | Open Government Licence – City of Guelph (v2.0) |
| Burlington Transit | Burlington | City of Burlington Open Data Terms of Use |
| Barrie Transit | Barrie | Barrie Transit Data licence |
| Kingston Transit | Kingston | City of Kingston Open Data Licence 1.0 |

Each entry quotes its licence grant verbatim with a working URL in its `terms`
field. `DATA_SOURCES.md` is updated for all nine.

### Excluded, and why

| System | Reason |
|---|---|
| OC Transpo (Ottawa) | requires an API key |
| GO Transit / Metrolinx | realtime API needs a manually-approved key (~10 business days); its static download is keyless but carries no vehicle positions |
| Grand River (Waterloo) | feed header 211 days stale, zero per-vehicle timestamps — would draw dead buses as live |
| London Transit, Thunder Bay | HTTP only, no HTTPS endpoint |
| Brampton, Oakville, Niagara, Milton, Windsor, Greater Sudbury, UP Express, +12 smaller | static GTFS only, no realtime positions |

Between the nine included and these exclusions, every Ontario realtime
vehicle-position feed catalogued in the Mobility Database is accounted for.

TTC subway is deliberately absent: BusTime is surface-only, and no public
subway vehicle positions exist. Inferring them from arrival predictions would
break the "real coordinates" rule (cf. withdrawn PR #338).

### Two mechanisms

Both exist because a feed's internal vocabulary isn't always the rider's, and
both are opt-in per feed — unset, nothing changes for existing feeds.

1. **`modeWords`** — a feed may rename a shared mode. TTC's `tram` reads
   "Streetcar"; Helsinki's still reads "Tram".
2. **`routeLabel`** — a feed whose `route_id` is an internal key can translate
   it. Needed by Hamilton (80 ids), Guelph (33), Burlington (16) and YRT (Viva
   colours plus branch suffixes). Unknown ids pass through unchanged, and no
   label is ever invented: YRT's `9101` runs live but is absent from the
   published `routes.txt`, so it stays opaque.

Two tables can't be shortcut. Burlington's `351` is route 1 while `3510` is
route 10, so it's a real join rather than a trimmed prefix. Hamilton runs two
generations of id at once — `5688` and `5780` are both the 2 BARTON — so 80 ids
collapse to 46 routes and both generations must be listed. Every table is
derived from the operator's own published GTFS `routes.txt`, under the same
licence as the realtime feed.

### Verification

All nine sampled live against real upstreams during afternoon revenue service:

| Feed | vehicles | usable position | with route |
|---|---|---|---|
| TTC | 1837 | 100% | 88% |
| MiWay | 357 | 100% | 100% |
| Hamilton HSR | 228 | 100% | 100% |
| YRT/Viva | 314 | 100% | 100% |
| Durham | 132 | 100% | 100% |
| Kingston | 137 | 97% | 46% raw / 70% drawn |
| Guelph | 52 | 100% | 100% |
| Burlington | 49 | 100% | 100% |
| Barrie | 32 | 100% | 100% |

Kingston publishes out-of-service vehicles with no trip assignment at all; the
existing 10-minute `VEHICLE_MAX_FIX_AGE_MS` gate drops the stale ones before
drawing, and the rest correctly fall back to fleet numbers.

Every `routeLabel` table was checked against the live feed's actual route ids —
no id in service renders as an untranslated internal key.

Full CI matrix green: `npm run build`, `npm test` (4169 pass / 0 fail),
`npm run doctor`, `npm run format:check` and `npm run check:boundaries`.

title: ALPR analyst queries, cordon analysis, and a Live Trains layer
body:
## What this adds

Three additions to the surveillance-awareness and movement layers, each its own commit and independently revertable. Happy to split into separate PRs if you'd prefer to review them individually — say the word.

### 1. ALPR: analyst queries + corrections loop (`81a4447`)
- `alpr-cameras` joins `ANALYST_LAYERS` and the `analyst_query` layers enum, so voice can answer "how many plate readers within 5 km?" / "show the Flock cameras in view" (filter hint: `manufacturer contains flock`). Counts announce the viewport-loaded caveat via the existing coverage-note path (`VIEWPORT_LOADED_LAYERS` generalized past flights).
- New **FIX ON OSM** row chip opens the selected camera's OSM node, so corrections flow back to the shared dataset instead of a private copy.
- Camera cards surface mapped `surveillance:zone`, `ref`, and `check_date`/`survey:date`.

### 2. ALPR: cordon analysis (`76ccffb`)
A **CORDON** row chip measures what share of the roads entering the town at view center pass a mapped reader, and shows where the gaps are. The admin boundary (`is_in` → area pivot, your proxy's 30-day boundary cache class) induces a cut of the road graph: every drivable way crossing the ring is an entry gate; split carriageways merge; a gate is covered when a mapped camera sits within 100 m of its road polyline. Gates render on the globe (coral = unmonitored, labeled), and the legend reports covered/total + majors — always with the mapped-cameras-are-a-floor caveat and a truncation warning when either fetch hits its cap. Crossing detection intersects segments with the ring directly, so a long sparse segment passing clear through a small town still counts. Pure math in `cordon.js` (Cesium-free, pinned in Node tests); fetch adapter and overlay renderer separated per the layer's owner split. No `poly:`/area-scans — bbox + `is_in`/pivot only, per the proxy validator.

### 3. Live Trains layer (`f9344cc`, motion in `fa80360`)
Keyless, CORS-open Amtrak GPS via the Amtraker community API, polled once a minute. Trains dead-reckon every frame along the line their last two *real* fixes define (no compass guessing), with carry-forward clamped to two minutes so quiet GPS leaves a dot resting near where the train was genuinely last seen. Holds the continuous render loop while enabled (aircraft-layer pattern), entities persist across polls, lateness uses the operator's own color (validated hex only), Predeparture trains are dropped so origin stations never paint phantom positions, and a malformed payload is a failure — never an authoritative empty map. Registered across catalog, panel, share-state registry (token `l`), credits, `DATA_SOURCES.md`, package boundaries, and both voice layer enums with spoken aliases.

## Validation
- Full suite: **4,161 tests, 0 failures** (25 new tests across `alprCordon.test.mjs`, `alprCameras.test.mjs`, `liveTrains.test.mjs`)
- `npm run check:boundaries` and `npm run format:check` clean; new modules registered in `scripts/package-boundaries.json`
- Voice schema pins re-derived per the in-test procedure for the deliberate enum/wording changes (`firstRunExperience`, `actionSchemas`, `radioMarkup` pins), with the changed tools named in the pin comments

title: feat: ship a web app manifest and home-screen icons
body:
## What this changes

Adding the app to a phone home screen produces a blank tile today. `index.html`
links only an SVG favicon, and Safari ignores SVG for `apple-touch-icon` —
it substitutes a screenshot of the page instead. There is no web app manifest
at all, so Android and desktop Chrome have nothing to install against either.

This adds the manifest and the raster icons, generated from the existing
`public/logo.svg`.

- `public/manifest.webmanifest` — standalone display, `#0a0a0f` background and
  theme (taken from `--bg-dark` in `src/ui/styles/foundation.css`, so the splash
  matches the app), 192/512 icons plus a 512 maskable variant.
- `index.html` — manifest link, a 180px `apple-touch-icon`, a 32px PNG favicon
  and the `apple-mobile-web-app-*` meta. **The existing SVG favicon is
  unchanged** and still serves the browser tab.
- `scripts/generate-icons.mjs` — renders every raster with `sharp`, which is
  already a devDependency. Re-run it after changing the logo.

Two decisions worth calling out:

**The PNGs are committed.** They could be generated during `vite build`, but
committing them keeps the build free of an image toolchain and means the icons
are reviewable in the diff. The script is the reproducible path, not a hidden
build step.

**The mark is inset, not stretched.** The logo's viewBox (`180 120 775 520`) is
wider than it is tall, so each icon centres it on a square canvas — inset to 78%
normally, and to 54% for the maskable variant so it stays inside the circle
Android may crop to.

## Verification

Run at `ff6b64a` on Node 26.8.2:

| Gate | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `npm run format:check` | pass (918 files) |
| `npm run check:boundaries` | pass |
| `npm test` | pass — 4148 passed, 0 failed, 1 skipped |
| `npm run build` | pass; `dist/icons/` and `dist/manifest.webmanifest` emitted, links intact in built HTML |

`src/tooling/webAppIcons.test.mjs` is new and covers the regression directly: it
asserts the links exist, the manifest declares a standalone app with the sizes
Android's install prompt requires and a maskable icon, and that every committed
PNG is genuinely square at the size the manifest claims. A manifest that
overstates a size is worse than a missing one, since the platform trusts the
declaration and scales whatever it finds.

Two caveats, stated plainly:

- `npm run test:track` was not run. It is not part of the CI workflow, and it
  had pre-existing display-floor failures on my machine unrelated to this change.
- The 2 allocation microbenchmarks skipped locally because their budgets are
  calibrated for Node 24. This PR touches no runtime JavaScript, so it cannot
  move an allocation budget.

Also deployed and checked on a live HTTPS host, since a manifest does nothing
over plain HTTP: the manifest and all five icons serve 200 as `image/png`, and
the `rel="manifest"`, `apple-touch-icon` and `theme-color` tags are present in
the served HTML.

## Notes

No runtime JavaScript changes, so no behavioural surface moves. `CHANGELOG.md`
and `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md` are updated per CONTRIBUTING. There is no existing
issue for this — I searched issues and PRs for manifest/favicon/PWA/home-screen
and found none; the "install" issues are all about installing the repository
(Pinokio, npm, the Windows installer), not installing the web app.

title: Pattern Watch: circling-aircraft detection
body:
## Pattern Watch — circling-aircraft detection

Adds a derived layer (no new network source) that reads records already held by Live Flights and Military Aircraft. It keeps a rolling 12-minute track per airborne aircraft and flags sustained same-direction circling: at least two revolutions over four minutes, with the track inside an 8 km circle. Short displacements carry no bearing, preventing GPS jitter from creating false turns; spherical geometry handles tracks across the antimeridian, and stable ICAO24 identity preserves history when a callsign changes. Flags render as a coral ground ring with a shared-overlay label. The legend states the limitation where flags appear: a flag describes a flight path, never the mission — training, traffic watch, survey work, and airport holding stacks all circle.

### Scope
Rebased directly onto current `main` (`7be5937`); this PR branch contains one commit with only Pattern Watch. ALPR/cordon and Live Trains changes are not included.

### Validation
- Latest targeted integration run: 106 passed, 0 failed, covering Pattern Watch, layer-state/token ledger, catalog/source composition, i18n, and the world-overlay label guard.

title: Foot Traffic (Melbourne): open pedestrian counters (stacked on #635, #637)
body:
## Foot Traffic (Melbourne) — open pedestrian counters

Adds a layer for the City of Melbourne **Pedestrian Counting System** — fixed directional street counters, published open (CC BY) through the council's Opendatasoft portal, keyless and CORS-open like the earthquakes layer. Sensors render as graduated intensity discs (cyan quiet → coral crowded) showing pedestrians tallied in the last 15 minutes. These are **foot-traffic tallies from council sensors — never devices or people**, central Melbourne only, and a floor; the legend says so.

Two honesty choices verified against the live API:
- **Window anchored to the feed's own latest reading, not wall clock.** The "past hour" feed publishes in bursts and ran ~60 min behind during testing — a now-anchored window returned an *empty map*. The layer instead shows the most recent real snapshot and surfaces its age ("Feed ~N min behind").
- **Stale ≠ zero.** A genuine 0 reads as 0; a sensor with no reading in the window reads "NO RECENT COUNT", never a fake zero.

### ⚠️ Stacked on #635 and #637
Based on `feat/pattern-watch-gps-trains` (#637), itself based on #635, so this PR's diff includes both. The commit unique to this PR is **"Add Melbourne foot-traffic layer (open pedestrian counters)"** (`b8a92eb`); the rest drop out as the base PRs merge. Merge order: #635 → #637 → this.

### Validation
Full suite green; 8 new tests (feed-anchored window, stale-vs-zero, malformed-payload-is-a-failure, live source join) plus end-to-end verification against the real endpoint. Boundaries + format clean; no voice enums, so no schema re-pin.

title: bug: heading confidence is discarded, so guessed camera bearings are indistinguishable from surveyed ones
body:
### What happened

Every CCTV pack sets `headingConfidence` on each camera. Nothing reads it.

```
$ grep -rn "headingConfidence" src/ --include="*.js" | grep -v catalog.js | grep -v test
(no output)
```

The only references are in `src/layers/cctv/catalog.js`, where the value is assigned. There are no consumers.

Cameras whose feed publishes no facing are given a synthetic bearing by `fallbackHeadingFromId` — `(hashSeed(id) % 16) * 22.5`, a function of the id **string** alone, with no geographic input — and are marked `headingConfidence: 'low'`. Because nothing consumes that flag, the guessed bearing draws the same projection plane and gizmo as a surveyed one. Nothing on screen distinguishes a measured facing from a hash.

This is **2,827 of 3,997 cameras (71%)** in a default catalog:

| Provider | low-confidence cameras |
|---|---|
| Ontario 511 | 551 |
| TxDOT | 474 |
| Fintraffic | 300 |
| Transport for London | 250 |
| Austin | 241 |
| Calgary | 216 |
| Transpordiamet (Tarktee) | 179 |

Expected: a low-confidence bearing is visibly provisional. Actual: it renders as authoritative.

Worth noting the defect holds either way for pan-capable cameras. If a camera's facing is fixed, we render an invented value for a knowable quantity. If it varies, we render a precise static projection for a quantity that has no single value. In both cases the app has no way to express "this bearing is a guess."

### Steps to reproduce

1. Fresh clone, `npm ci`, `npm run dev`
2. Confirm nothing reads the flag:
   `grep -rn "headingConfidence" src/ --include="*.js" | grep -v catalog.js | grep -v test` → no output
3. Confirm the scale:
   `curl -s localhost:4173/api/cctv/sources | python3 -c "import json,sys,collections;print(collections.Counter(c.get('headingConfidence') for c in json.load(sys.stdin)['sources']))"`
   → `Counter({'low': 2827, 'high': 1170})`
4. Open the app, enable CCTV, select any Calgary, TfL or Austin camera and turn PROJECTION on
5. Compare the projection direction with what the frame shows. The plane points somewhere unrelated, with no indication the bearing was synthesized

A compact demonstration that the value carries no geographic information — consecutive ids, which belong to unrelated locations, and neighbouring values that are unrelated to each other:

```
fallbackHeadingFromId('calgary-142') -> 225
fallbackHeadingFromId('calgary-143') -> 292.5
fallbackHeadingFromId('calgary-86')  -> 157.5
```

The only input is the id string, so the bearing changes if a feed ever renumbers a camera, and two cameras metres apart receive unrelated values.

### How you installed

Terminal (git clone + npm)

### OS, Node version, browser

macOS 15.6 (Darwin 24.6.0), Node 26.8.2, Chrome 141

### Version or commit

`0d41b6b`

### Output of `npm run doctor`

```
[OK] Node 26.8.2: supported runtime
[OK] npm 11.19.1
[OK] dependencies installed

Map:     Esri World Imagery (keyless satellite basemap) with keyless terrain
Traffic: built-in traffic simulation

(No provider keys configured in this checkout. The CCTV packs involved are
all keyless, so this does not affect the report.)
```

### Server log and browser console

```
No errors in either. This is a correctness and presentation defect rather
than a failure: the evidence is the absent consumer in step 2 and the
counts in step 3.
```

---

Raising this rather than working around it because `CONTRIBUTING.md` asks contributors not to misrepresent public-data inference as authoritative. A hash-derived bearing drawn as a precise 3D projection seems to sit close to that line, and the metadata needed to fix it is already plumbed through to every camera.

Happy to send a PR if you have a preferred treatment — dashed or translucent projection, a badge on the card, or suppressing the plane entirely below a confidence threshold.

title: feat(cctv): add the City of Toronto RESCU camera pack
body:
Toronto has two camera networks and God's Eye View carries one. The Ontario 511 pack covers the province's highways; this adds the municipal network underneath it — **336 cameras** on downtown arterials plus the Gardiner, DVP, Allen and Lake Shore, from the City's own open data.

Follows the pattern `catalog.js` documents: one loader in `sources.js`, one entry in `LIVE_PACKS`.

## Source

City of Toronto Open Data, dataset **Traffic Cameras** (Transportation Services), keyless. The list is `tmcearthcameras.json`, served as JSONP and refreshed within two minutes of any change. Groups: Arterial 253, Lake Shore 37, Gardiner 22, DVP 16, Allen 8.

Licensed **Open Government Licence – Toronto**, which requires an attribution statement; registered in `dataCredits.js` and documented in `DATA_SOURCES.md`. Frames are fetched per request, never stored or redistributed.

## Frame URLs are built, not read

The list publishes an `IMAGEURL`, but this loader ignores it and constructs the URL from the documented `CameraImages/loc####.jpg` convention plus a camera number validated as `/^\d{1,6}$/`. That pins the frame proxy to the portal origin by construction rather than by trusting a field — the approach the Fintraffic pack uses. A test plants hostile `url`/`snapshotUrl` keys on a row and asserts they stay inert, and that traversal-shaped numbers are refused.

The list fetch refuses redirects (`redirect: 'manual'`), caps the body it buffers, and cancels the response body on every rejection path.

## No heading exists in this dataset

The rows carry `D1`–`D4`, and the portal's GeoJSON spells them `DIRECTION1`–`4` as `North`/`East`/`South`/`West`. **They are not a camera facing.** Across all 336 records, every non-empty direction value pairs with a `ComparisonImages/` URL — static reference stills, last modified 2016. No bearing, azimuth or angle field exists anywhere in the schema.

So every camera takes the shared id-hash fallback at low confidence, as the headingless Austin, TfL, Fintraffic and Calgary cameras do. A test asserts no direction combination changes the heading, so the letters aren't wired up later by someone who spots them.

Duplicate names are real: 8047 and 8048 are both `BATHURST ST & BLOOR ST W`, five metres apart, as at Bay & Queen and Yonge & King. Distinct units, so both ship. Names stay verbatim — the feed's labels are upper-case, and title-casing would mangle `MCCOWAN RD` and `ST HELEN'S AVE`.

## Verification

`npm run build`, `npm test` (4,159 pass / 0 fail / 1 skip — a Node 26 allocation benchmark) and `npm run test:track` (109 pass / 0 fail) are green, plus `format:check` and `check:boundaries`. The track run asserts no console errors and no 5xx.

15 new tests in `src/data/cctvToronto.test.mjs` cover JSONP unwrapping (foreign callbacks, truncated bodies), URL construction against hostile input, the coordinate gate, dedupe, redirect and oversize refusal with body release, registration through the served catalog, the `CCTV_TORONTO_ENABLED=0` kill switch, and round-robin cap fairness.

Beyond the suite I ran the loader against the live endpoint (336 cameras, all URLs on the pinned origin) and pulled frames through `/api/cctv/frame/` on a running instance — Bathurst & Bloor and Dundas E & DVP North both returned current, timestamped frames.

## Two known gaps

**Headings are synthesized.** As above, the dataset has no facing, so these 336 cameras get a hash-derived bearing at `low` confidence. In practice that bearing is unrelated to what the camera shows. That is the existing convention for headingless packs rather than anything new here, but it is also the subject of #639 — `headingConfidence` is set by every pack and read by nothing, so a guessed bearing renders identically to a surveyed one. If you'd prefer this pack wait on that, or land with `CCTV_TORONTO_ENABLED` defaulting off, I'm happy either way.

**No precomputed ground heights.** `ground.js` names this case as a designed fallback ("a new pack"), so cameras resolve placement from the DEM on activation rather than being pre-seated. The ground prior is set to 116 m, the measured mean across the 336 sites — Toronto runs 76 m at the lake to 209 m at Steeles, so no constant fits well. I can generate the sidecar with `scripts/precompute-cctv-heights.mjs --kinds toronto-rescu-open-data` (336 cameras, 92 cells) and push it to this branch if you want it before merge. `groundElevationM` isn't part of the served pose, so it changes no pose hash and invalidates no existing entry.

Disable with `CCTV_TORONTO_ENABLED=0`.

title: feat(bikeshare): add Bike Share Toronto, and fix the layer-wide failure it exposes
body:
Adds Bike Share Toronto, and fixes the layer-wide failure that adding it exposed. Two commits, readable independently.

## 1. Bike Share Toronto

Toronto runs the same PBSC platform as the Austin, Honolulu and Chattanooga systems already in the registry, and publishes the identical GBFS v2 endpoint pair under `toronto.publicbikesystem.net`. The proxy allowlist already admits the host through its `*.publicbikesystem.net` wildcard and the paths end in the expected `station_information.json` / `station_status.json`, so it needs no new plumbing — only the registry entry.

Verified against the live feeds: 1,069 stations in both documents, all 1,069 joining on `station_id`. It would be the largest system in the registry.

The layer reads `num_bikes_available`, which Toronto populates normally. It does not populate the standard `num_bikes_available_types`, reporting per-type counts under PBSC ids (`ICONIC`/`BOOST`/`EFIT`/`ASTRO`) instead. Nothing reads that field today, so this deliberately does not translate it rather than adding a mapping with no consumer. Worth knowing if per-type counts are ever surfaced: the system genuinely runs 2,813 e-bikes alongside 8,451 mechanical.

Credited to Bike Share Toronto (Toronto Parking Authority). The City's open-data package declares no licence and the feed publishes no `license_url`, so it is treated as attribution-only like the other GBFS operators, rather than claiming a licence that was never granted.

`registry.test.mjs` is new: it holds every city's feed URLs against the same host and path predicates the proxy enforces, so a city the proxy would silently refuse fails the suite instead of rendering an empty layer.

## 2. The failure it exposed

`getStats()` surfaces one layer-wide error string:

```js
// src/layers/bikeshare/controls.js:40
if (layerState._error) stats.error = layerState._error;
```

City feeds are fetched independently, but any one of them can set that flag:

```js
// src/layers/bikeshare/viewport.js:175  (activateCity)
layerState._error = 'GBFS fetch error';

// src/layers/bikeshare/ingestion.js:191  (update)
layerState._error = 'GBFS status update failed';
```

The only code that clears it is a *successful activation*:

```js
// src/layers/bikeshare/viewport.js:171
layerState._error = null;
```

…which a city that is already loaded never reaches, because `runProximityCheck` only activates cities with no rendered points:

```js
// src/layers/bikeshare/viewport.js:221
if (!layerState._cityRuntime.has(cityId)) toActivate.push(cityId);
```

So a dead feed inside the activation radius re-activates on every camera move, fails, sets the flag — and nothing ever clears it, because the healthy city alongside it is never re-activated. The panel shows `LOAD FAILED` permanently over a map drawing every other city's stations. `_lastUpdate` stays `null` for the same reason.

Buffalo's Reddy Bikeshare sits 95 km from Toronto, inside the 100 km activation radius, and its registered feed had 404'd since the operator left BCycle. Panning around Toronto:

```
AFTER INITIAL LOAD:     {"count":1069, ..., "error":"GBFS fetch error"}
AFTER PAN -79.40,43.65: {"count":1069,"loading":false,"error":"GBFS fetch error"}
AFTER PAN -79.36,43.66: {"count":1069,"loading":false,"error":"GBFS fetch error"}
[Data:Bikeshare] buffalo-reddy activate error: Error: GBFS HTTP 404
```

1,069 stations rendering correctly the whole time.

### The fix

Track failure per city (`_failedCityIds`) instead of in one shared string, and report it only when it cost the layer everything it had to draw:

```js
if (
  layerState._failedCityIds.size > 0 &&
  layerState._stationRenderMap.size === 0
) {
  stats.error = 'GBFS fetch error';
}
```

A city that recovers deletes its own entry, on both the activation path and the status poll, rather than depending on a neighbour succeeding. An empty layer with nothing failed stays non-error — out of range is empty, not broken.

After, same reproduction:

```
AFTER PAN -79.40,43.65: {"count":1069,"lastUpdate":1789606694804,"loading":false}
AFTER PAN -79.36,43.66: {"count":1069,"lastUpdate":1789606694804,"loading":false}
[Data:Bikeshare] Initialized with 31 cities
```

## 3. Feed audit

Finding one dead feed prompted probing all 33. Five served nothing. Three had moved operators and are repointed; two have wound down and are removed:

| System | Status on `main` | Action |
|---|---|---|
| Reddy Bikeshare — Buffalo, NY | `gbfs.bcycle.com/bcycle_reddy` 404 | → `reddybikeshare.socialbicycles.com` (143 stations) |
| Tugo — Tucson, AZ | `bcycle_tugo` 404 | → `tucson.publicbikesystem.net` (41 stations) |
| Trinity Metro — Fort Worth, TX | `bcycle_fortworth` 404 | → `fortworth.publicbikesystem.net` (57 stations) |
| CoGo — Columbus, OH | `gbfs.cogobikeshare.com` does not resolve | **removed** |
| Broward B-cycle — Fort Lauderdale, FL | 404 at every documented endpoint | **removed** |

Replacement endpoints are the ones listed in MobilityData's GBFS registry (`systems.csv`).

The two removals are the only judgement calls here, and I'm happy to revert either. CoGo's registry entry points at a host that no longer resolves, and its Lyft-hosted replacement (`gbfs.lyft.com/gbfs/2.3/cmh`) publishes zero stations with `station_status` last reported in March 2025 — the system appears wound down rather than moved. Broward's system has shut down. Both are removed outright rather than left commented, so the registry stays a list of systems that exist; the reasoning lives here and in the commit message. `gbfs.cogobikeshare.com` is dropped from the proxy allowlist with them, and `reddybikeshare.socialbicycles.com` added.

All 31 remaining systems were verified serving stations, and every registry URL was checked against the proxy host and path allowlists.

## Why these travel together

The dependency runs one way. The fix stands alone — five dead feeds are broken for users on `main` today, wherever their camera sits over Tucson, Fort Worth, Columbus, Fort Lauderdale or Buffalo.

Toronto does not stand alone. Merged by itself it renders all 1,069 stations correctly but reports `LOAD FAILED` permanently, because Buffalo is the one dead system in the registry with a healthy neighbour inside the activation radius — and Toronto is that neighbour. That pairing is also what makes the defect reproducible at all: on `main` today each dead system fails alone, where `LOAD FAILED` over an empty map reads as correct, which is why the latch went unnoticed.

Splitting them risks the feature landing without the fix. They are separate commits, so they can still be reviewed — or reverted — independently.

## Testing

- `src/layers/bikeshare/registry.test.mjs` — new; every city's feed URLs against the proxy allowlists, plus the Toronto entry and its service area.
- `src/layers/bikeshare/failureReporting.test.mjs` — new; a failed city does not fail a layer that is drawing stations, failure is reported when nothing is drawn, an empty layer with nothing failed is not an error, and a recovered city clears its own failure.
- `src/layers/transit/lifecycle.test.mjs` — its hand-built bikeshare state stub gains `_failedCityIds`.
- Full suite: **4,151 passing, 0 failing**. `format:check`, `check:boundaries` and `vite build` clean.
- Both commits verified running against the live feeds through the real proxy, not just in unit tests.
