title: fix(cctv): surface heading confidence — estimated bearings are now visible
body:
Fixes #639.

## What

Every pack sets `headingConfidence` on each camera, but nothing consumed it: a bearing synthesized by `fallbackHeadingFromId` (a hash of the id string, no geographic input) rendered exactly like a surveyed one — 2,827 of 3,997 cameras in a default catalog, per the issue.

This adds the two missing consumers, plus a passthrough:

- **HUD**: the heading token is tagged when the bearing is synthetic — `HDG 194° (ESTIMATED)` — so a hash never reads as a measured facing.
- **Wireframe**: a low-confidence camera draws its coverage frustum with **dashed** polylines instead of solid. Colors, widths, and the active/idle emphasis are unchanged in both the cyan/green scheme and viewshed hue mode — the dash is the only signal, so it composes with everything else the wireframe already communicates.
- **Public camera state** gains `headingConfidence` (raw pack flag) and `headingEstimated` (derived bit) so UI consumers never have to re-derive it.

## Calibration interplay

A human-vouched pose always wins over the pack flag: a manually saved calibration (`calSource:'manual'`) or a curated catalog entry (`poseSource:'curated'`) is never presented as estimated — mirroring the CAL badge states in `calibration.js`. Covered by tests.

## Notes

- `src/layers/cctv/headingConfidence.js` — pure helpers (`isHeadingEstimated`, `headingHudToken`), JSDoc'd
- `src/layers/cctv/headingConfidence.test.mjs` — confidence normalization (trim/case), calibration/curation overrides, HUD token formatting
- The dash material is constructed in the existing styling pass (not per-frame), same allocation pattern as the pass's current `withAlpha` calls
- `npm test` 4151 pass / 0 fail · `npm run build` green · Prettier clean

Related: #452 applies the same provenance principle to the FOV axis (`fovSource: 'datasheet'` when a camera's hardware model is identified) — together they cover the two pose quantities the issue calls out as rendering more authoritatively than they're known.

title: feat(cctv): WSDOT highway camera source pack (Washington State)
body:
Closes #624.

## What

Washington State's highway cameras as a keyless source pack — the Esri JSON layer WSDOT's own Travel Center map consumes (`data.wsdot.wa.gov/travelcenter/Cameras.json`, ~1,700 point features). **1,630 cameras** survive the filters against the live feed; by default the 250 nearest Seattle and Spokane load (`CCTV_WSDOT_MAX_SOURCES` / `CCTV_WSDOT_ENABLED=0` as usual).

## Data diligence

- **License**: WSDOT's layer metadata marks the feed for *"low volume"* use; the [travel information disclaimer](https://wsdot.wa.gov/about/policies/travel-information-disclaimer) asserts no redistribution prohibition. The 15-minute catalog cache and per-request frame fetches respect the low-volume clause; frames are never stored or redistributed; the WSDOT credit is registered in the attribution popover and documented in DATA_SOURCES.md.
- **Partner cameras skipped**: only frames on WSDOT's own `images.wsdot.wa.gov` host are registered. The catalog also lists ~70 partner cameras (Oregon DOT/tripcheck, City of Seattle, lodges, airports) whose own terms apply — skipped rather than proxied.
- A **keyed WSDOT Traveler Information API** serves the same population for higher-volume use; deliberately not required so the pack stays keyless like the others.

## Mechanics

- Geometry arrives in EPSG:3857 → converted to WGS84 on load, bounded to a WA box.
- `CompassDirection` N/E/S/W → high-confidence heading; the majority `B` ("both directions") rows carry no single facing → shared id-hash fallback at low confidence, usual two pose personalities.
- The body carries Windows-1252 bytes (en-dashes in titles) with no charset declaration → decoded explicitly before parsing.

## Tests

Mercator conversion checked against a real layer feature, official-host + malformed-row filtering, compass mapping and both pose personalities, cp1252 decoding, env cap, upstream-failure fallback. `npm test` 4148 pass / 0 fail · `npm run build` green · Prettier clean.

title: feat(cctv): King County road camera source pack (Washington State)
body:
## What

King County DOT Road Services' cameras as a keyless source pack — one public ArcGIS FeatureServer GeoJSON query. **59 live cameras** against the current feed, covering the unincorporated county road network around Seattle (Redmond, Federal Way, Renton, Novelty Hill…). `CCTV_KINGCOUNTY_MAX_SOURCES` / `CCTV_KINGCOUNTY_ENABLED=0` as usual.

## Why this pack is special

The county publishes **each camera's hardware `Manufacturer`/`Model`** in the layer — Cohu 3950/3965, Bosch AUTODOME IP 5000i, Axis Q6135-LE, Siqura PD910. All 59 live cameras carry a model value. The pack carries it through as the source's `model` (whitespace-collapsed — the feed has stray newlines), with an additive passthrough in `normalizeSourceItem` mirroring the `poseSource` pattern. On current `main` the field is inert metadata; #452 consumes it to render datasheet-accurate FOV cones and hardware specs for identified cameras — this is the first feed that would light that up with county-published data, zero guessing.

## Data diligence

- **Explicit `outFields`** on purpose: the layer also carries asset-administration columns (including staff names in `ModifiedBy`) that are never fetched.
- **WSDOT-owned rows skipped** — the layer is titled "King County *and WSDOT* Traffic Cameras"; a statewide WSDOT pack (#644) is those cameras' home, so nothing renders twice.
- Only frames on the county's own `info.kingcounty.gov` handler are registered (feed writes `http://`; the handler serves HTTPS — upgraded and pinned, Calgary-style). City-owned cameras the county hosts keep their owner as the per-camera credit, DriveBC-style.
- **License**: [KCGIS Center terms](https://kingcounty.gov/en/dept/kcit/data-information-services/gis-center/about/terms-conditions-copyrights), attribution registered in the popover + DATA_SOURCES.md.
- No facing published → id-hash fallback at low confidence.

## Tests

Owner/live/status/host/geometry/bbox filtering, HTTPS upgrade, model whitespace-collapse + `normalizeSourceItem` passthrough semantics, partner-city credit, env cap, upstream-failure fallback. `npm test` 4148 pass / 0 fail · `npm run build` green · Prettier clean.

title: feat(voice): local Ollama voice assistant with watchkeeping, incidents, radio, camera sweeps and federation
body:
## Summary

Adds a fully local voice assistant behind `AI_PROVIDER=ollama`: nothing leaves the machine and nothing is billed. The browser runs Silero VAD, the dev server runs faster-whisper (CUDA/CPU) and Piper, and Ollama serves the tool model (`qwen3:8b`) and a vision model (`qwen3-vl:4b`). The 28 upstream voice tools work unchanged; the local path adds 42 more in eight registered tool packs.

**What the assistant can do beyond the shared tools**

- **Vision and memory:** ask about the current view, remember places, standing alerts, data reports, multi-language replies, optional Porcupine wake word.
- **Time travel:** rewind and scrub the last 15 minutes of live contacts (`docs/TIME-TRAVEL.md`).
- **Watchkeeping:** scheduled patrols with spoken briefings, a rule-based anomaly engine (stopped vessels, rapid descents, orbiting aircraft, impossible jumps, went-dark), named geofences with entry alerts, dead-reckoned prediction ("who will be near X in 10 minutes").
- **Incidents:** `export_incident` freezes the current view into one self-contained HTML evidence bundle with a track replay (`docs/INCIDENTS.md`).
- **Radio in the loop:** ffmpeg + faster-whisper transcribe the station playing in the Radio layer so you can ask what they just said (`docs/RADIO-LISTEN.md`).
- **Camera sweeps:** fetch one frame from each nearby CCTV camera and ask the vision model for a verdict per camera, pinned on the map (`docs/CAMERA-SWEEP.md`).
- **Speaker identity:** enrol a voice and address people by name (`docs/SPEAKER-ID.md`).
- **Federation:** peer globes share spoken alerts and saved places (`docs/FEDERATION.md`).
- **Auto-Director:** narrated tours built from live records (`docs/AUTO-DIRECTOR.md`).
- **Phone companion:** `remote.html` mirrors the transcript and mic control (`docs/REMOTE.md`).

Entry point and architecture diagram: `docs/LOCAL-VOICE.md`.

**Things worth a close look**

- `config/cctv_sources.world.json` (100k lines) is a generated world CCTV catalog produced by `scripts/export-world-cctv.mjs`, and the CCTV source ceiling is raised to 10,000 to load it. Happy to split this into its own PR if you'd rather review it separately.
- New browser dependencies: `@ricky0123/vad-web`, `@picovoice/porcupine-web`, `@picovoice/web-voice-processor` (wake word is optional and needs `PICOVOICE_ACCESS_KEY`).
- Server-side Python worker (`scripts/local_audio.py`) for Whisper and Piper; launchers in `scripts/dev-local.ps1` / `scripts/dev-local.sh`.
- Provider registries: `src/voice/tools/` and `server/providers/ollama/routes/` let feature packs register tools and routes without touching the adapter.

## Test plan

All run on the head commit:

- [x] `npm run build`
- [x] `npm test` (4,335 tests, 0 failures)
- [x] `npm run test:track` against the dev server (109 passed, 0 failed)
- [x] `npm run format:check` and `npm run check:boundaries`
- [x] `npm run qa:local-voice` end-to-end ("Fly to Paris" -> `fly_to_location`, first audio at 362 ms)
- [x] `node scripts/qa-tool-calls.mjs --models qwen3:8b` (11/12; the "track it" miss is expected with no prior selection)

Runtime changes are documented in `CHANGELOG.md`, `DATA_SOURCES.md` (world CCTV pack licences and provenance), `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md` (added in the follow-up docs commit) and the per-feature docs above.

title: feat: get OpenStreetMap data from planet dumps not Overpass
body:
### Problem

This application is massively overusing overpass-api.de to download OpenStreetMap data. By our accounts you have used up around 20k CPU seconds in the last 24h. Given the resources we have have and the numbers of users, your fair share would be at around 300 CPU seconds. In addition, [changing the user agent after being UA blocked](https://github.com/bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view/pull/420) has now resulted in a [very annoyed sysadmin](https://www.redbubble.com/i/t-shirt/Don-t-Mess-With-System-Administrators-We-Have-Admin-Rights-by-jaygo/38981176/z5wf).

So this is to let you know that you have been blocked again.

### Proposal

Please find a solution where you process OpenStreetMap data yourself and deliver them to your users in form of vector tiles or similar. Or you can run your own Overpass server. There are also [commercial offers](https://wiki.openstreetmap.org/wiki/Overpass_API#Public_Overpass_API_instances) to help you do that.

Simply dropping overpass-api.de and switching to another "free" Overpass server is not going to be a solution either. These other services have even less computing resources available than the main instance. So this inevitably leads to even more annoyed sysadmins.

### Data source, license, and attribution

OpenStreetMap data should be usually consumed from [the planet dump](https://planet.osm.org/pbf/) and, if frequently updated data is required, from [diffs](https://planet.osm.org/replication/). License is ODbL, attribution "OpenStreetMap".

### Will you build it?

No, this is a request for someone else

title: fix: treat AIS "not available" speed and course as unknown
body:
## What

AIS encodes speed over ground in 0.1-knot units and course over ground in 0.1-degree units, reserving the top code of each field for "not available" (ITU-R M.1371). SOG 1023 arrives from AISStream as `102.3` and COG 3600 as `360`. Both are finite numbers, so `numberValue` stored them as ordinary readings and every consumer — vessel cards, the HUD, voice analyst queries — treated a missing measurement as a real one.

`normalizedHeading` already does exactly this for true heading's own sentinel (511). This applies the same treatment to SOG and COG, in the same place, so the sentinels never enter the cache.

## Evidence

On a live AISStream feed of 3,062 vessels:

- exactly **3** records at `102.3` knots, and **no reading anywhere between 40 and 102.3**
- **404** records at exactly `360` degrees
- one Dutch rescue boat moored at its station (`KNRM ARBOR VITAE`, MMSI 244060365) carried both sentinels at once

An analyst summary over that snapshot reported a maximum speed of 102.3 knots — faster than any vessel afloat. After the change, on a live feed of 2,088 vessels: 0 sentinels, max speed 66.4 kn, max course 359.9°.

## How verified

- `npm test` — 4,150 passing, 0 failing, including 5 new tests in `src/data/aisStreamSentinels.test.mjs`
- `npm run build` — clean
- `npm run format:check` and `npm run check:boundaries` — clean
- a live AISStream feed, before and after

The new tests cover both sentinels plus three guards that fail if the filter is too aggressive: a stopped vessel's `0`, and the highest values the fields can actually encode (102.2 kn and 359.9°). The tests were written first and observed failing against the old behaviour.

The test file lives under `src/` rather than next to the module, because `scripts/run-unit-tests.mjs` only discovers tests under `src/`; a test placed in `server/` is never executed by `npm test`.

## On `npm run test:track`

I could not establish a reliable baseline with this harness on my machine, so I am reporting what I saw rather than claiming a pass.

Three of six runs on this branch, and **two of three runs on unmodified `main`**, ended in a puppeteer harness error (`TargetCloseError`, `Execution context was destroyed`) before completing. Of the runs that finished: `main` gave 109/0 once; this branch gave 107/2 and 105/4.

Every failure on this branch was the same frame-capture gate — `frames=27/30` and `frames=22/30` with `timedOut=true` — plus the assertion derived from it (`trackedReadyFramesComplete && …`), whose own measured value was the correct `0`. No value, height or sampling-count assertion failed in any run.

The changed code path is the server's AIS websocket ingest, which this harness bypasses by stubbing `/api/ais-live` to a zero-row snapshot. I am running under software rendering (`--use-gl=angle --use-angle=swiftshader`) on a laptop, and a `test:track` result from a machine with hardware GL would be welcome.

title: Geofence tool: draw/edit/clear a polygon on the globe, with live breach monitoring and webhook alerts
body:
Adds a geofence capability to the globe: draw a closed polygon by clicking, edit or clear it, and get alerted when a live entity crosses into it.

![Geofence tool](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kevinsalerno/gods-eye-view/geofence-arm1/docs/images/geofence-tool.png)

## What it does

**DISPLAY ▸ Geofence** adds a tool alongside the existing Draw tool:

- **Draw** — click vertices on the globe; double-click, Enter, or **Finish** closes the ring. Minimum 3 points, collinear/degenerate rings rejected, duplicate points within 0.5 m filtered, 512-point cap.
- **Render** — a dedicated `gev-geofence` `CustomDataSource` draws an interior fill (`ClassificationType.BOTH`, so it drapes on the photoreal surface) plus a glowing clamped boundary polyline, a dashed draft preview while drawing, and vertex handles.
- **Edit** — toggle **Edit** and drag a handle; grab tolerance scales with camera height, and camera rotation is suspended during a drag.
- **Clear** — removes the draft and the finished fence.
- **Live monitoring** — on every position update, entity coordinates are tested against the active polygon. Crossing in fires an internal event, shows an on-screen banner, and POSTs a JSON payload to a configured webhook.

The tool claims the pointer through the existing `inputOwnership` lease (`src/data/inputOwnership.js`) with its own `geofence` owner, the same way `drawTool` does, so ambient selection handlers yield while a session is open and the stock viewer click actions are borrowed and restored.

## Layout

| Module | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `geofenceModel.js` | Pure polygon session — add/move/remove/insert vertex, close validation, `toClosedLonLat`, GeoJSON round-trip, ring area |
| `geofenceRenderer.js` | Cesium entities: fill, boundary, draft preview, edit handles |
| `geofenceTool.js` | Pointer ownership, draw/edit/clear state machine, DOM wiring |
| `geofenceIntersection.js` | Ray-cast point-in-polygon with antimeridian unwrapping; boundary counts as inside |
| `geofenceStateTracker.js` | In-memory inside/outside map; reports a transition only when it actually changes |
| `geofenceMonitor.js` | Pulls `getAnalystRecords()` from each enabled layer on `data-updated`, evaluates, dispatches |
| `geofenceWebhook.js` | URL validation, payload shape, POST |
| `geofenceAlert.js` | Breach banner |

The model, intersection, tracker, webhook and alert modules are free of Cesium and DOM imports, so they run directly under `node --test`.

## Alerting

Alerts are deduplicated by design: the internal event fires only on the initial outside-to-inside transition. An entity that stays inside does not re-alert; leaving and re-entering does. Clearing the fence resets tracker state so a redrawn fence cannot replay stale entries.

The breach payload:

```json
{
  "entityId": "a1b2c3",
  "timestamp": "2026-09-17T22:54:35.000Z",
  "coordinates": { "lon": -97.7341, "lat": 30.2841 },
  "speed": 231.4,
  "layer": "flights"
}
```

**Test Webhook** POSTs a mock payload (`entityId: TEST-123`, `test: true`) so connectivity can be checked without waiting for a real crossing.

## Verification

- `npm test` — 4197 pass, 0 fail
- `npm run format:check` — clean
- `npm run check:boundaries` — clean; the new modules are registered in `scripts/package-boundaries.json`, and the new files are added to `scripts/format-scope.json`
- 39 new unit tests across the model, intersection, tracker, webhook and alert, covering draw validation, duplicate-point filtering, antimeridian crossings, boundary-as-inside, dedup on re-entry, payload shape and URL validation

## Known limitation

The breach POST sends `Content-Type: application/json`, which is not CORS-safelisted, so the browser issues an `OPTIONS` preflight first. Endpoints that answer preflight (Slack, Zapier, webhook.site, and most hosted receivers) work; a plain endpoint that returns 501 to `OPTIONS` will fail with `Failed to fetch`.

Routing the POST through the existing `server/` provider layer would remove the constraint entirely, and I'm happy to follow up with that if you'd prefer it in-tree rather than leaving the caveat to the operator.

title: feat(cellular): add cellular network infrastructure layer
body: ## Summary Adds a cellular network infrastructure layer with physical site data from OpenStreetMap and logical cell observations from OpenCellID. The layer supports: - mapped cellular sites and towers from OpenStreetMap - logical GSM / UMTS / LTE / NR cells from OpenCellID - technology filtering - mapped sector directions where available - estimated OpenCellID range visualization - click details for sites and cells - independent progressive loading of sites and cells - server-side OpenCellID credentials - bounded viewport tiling, caching, request concurrency, and rate-limit handling - partial-coverage and API-limit status reporting ## OpenCellID API handling OpenCellID requests are made server-side so the API key is not exposed to the browser. The implementation uses canonical bounded tiles, deduplication, caching, conservative concurrency, and separate close-view / overview request budgets to avoid treating the OpenCellID API as an unlimited map-tile service. Rate-limited and unavailable responses are reported explicitly instead of being presented as zero cells. ## Data semantics OpenStreetMap entries represent mapped physical cellular infrastructure. OpenCellID entries represent logical observed cells and should not be interpreted as one physical tower per record. OpenCellID `range` values are displayed as estimates rather than authoritative RF coverage boundaries. ## Documentation Updated: - `CHANGELOG.md` - `DATA_SOURCES.md` - `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md` - provider/setup documentation and configuration where applicable ## Verification - `npm run format:check` - `npm run build` - `npm test` - `npm run test:track` - focused cellular provider/source tests - manual testing of site/cell loading, technology filters, selection, range display, zoom behavior, caching, and OpenCellID rate-limit handling ## Screenshots

This PR introduces four cohesive enhancements to God's Eye View:
1. **Traditional Chinese (`zh-TW`) Localization**: Full UI localization and runtime language switching across all panels, tools, HUD overlays, and voice prompts.
2. **OpenAI-Compatible LLM Endpoints & Voice Synthesis**: Custom base URLs (`OPENAI_BASE_URL`), summary model overrides (`OPENAI_HUD_SUMMARY_MODEL`), and text-to-speech audio synthesis (`TTS_BASE_URL`) with quick-fill presets for **ChatGPT**, **Groq**, **Grok (xAI)**, **Ollama**, and **DeepSeek**, plus optional private LAN administration (`GEV_ALLOW_LAN_SETUP=1`).
3. **Taiwan CCTV Camera Pack & Taipei POI Destination**: 25 curated public cameras across Taiwan Freeway 1, 3, 5, and Taipei 101, along with a Taipei destination POI preset.

![Taiwan Freeway CCTV Live Stream on 3D Globe](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tbdavid2019/gods-eye-view/feat/i18n-zh-tw-custom-llm-taiwan-cctv/docs/media/taiwan-cctv-live-streaming.png)

title: feat: voice auth falls back to Codex CLI login (ChatGPT subscription)
body:
## What

When `OPENAI_API_KEY` is unset, `/api/realtime/token` now resolves the operator's local **Codex CLI login** (`$CODEX_HOME/auth.json` or `~/.codex/auth.json`, ChatGPT token mode) and mints the same ephemeral Realtime client secret on the ChatGPT subscription instead of a metered API key. Voice works keyless for anyone already signed into the Codex CLI.

The README already invites this (*"Want Gemini or another provider behind the mic? PRs welcome"*) — this is the same-provider lane: identical mint endpoint, identical session config, only the bearer token source changes.

## Auth resolution (fail-closed)

1. `GEV_PREFER_CODEX_OAUTH=true` → Codex lane only; refuses metered fallback when the login is missing/expired.
2. `OPENAI_API_KEY` — a blank value falls through (both lanes mint the same secret for the same provider, so no billing ambiguity).
3. Codex OAuth: requires ChatGPT token mode + well-formed JWT, checks `exp` with a 60s margin, anchors a missing `exp` on the auth.json mtime (+1h). **Read-only** — the vendor file is never refreshed or rewritten; an expired token 503s with a `codex login` hint.

Out of scope on purpose: the HUD summary still requires `OPENAI_API_KEY` (Codex OAuth is only proven against the Realtime mint, not the chat endpoints).

## Receipts

- New `server/providers/openai/codex-auth.js` + 12 unit tests (one per resolution path, plus handler-level 503/mint/legacy-string tests).
- The mint lane is echoed in a new `X-GEV-Voice-Auth` response header (`env` / `codex-oauth`); the 503 body keeps the `OPENAI_API_KEY is not set` prefix existing QA greps rely on.
- `setup-doctor` reports `available via Codex login (ChatGPT subscription)` when the key is absent but the lane is valid.
- **Live verification**: dev server with no `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `GET /api/realtime/token` → `200` with a real `ek_` client secret and `X-GEV-Voice-Auth: codex-oauth`.
- `npm run build`, `npm test`, `npm run test:track` (109 passed / 0 failed), `format:check`, `check:boundaries` all green.
- One existing test updated: the HUD-quota test now also blanks `CODEX_HOME` so both voice lanes are absent (it asserted the exact 503 body).

Ported from [hermes-talk](https://github.com/TheSmokeDev/hermes-talk)'s `talk_auth.py` — itself a port of OpenClaw PR #100671, "Reuse Codex OAuth for OpenAI Realtime voice".

title: feat: HUD summary rides the Codex CLI login too
body:
Builds on #653 (voice Codex OAuth lane) — stacks on that branch; only the second commit is new.

## What

Extends the Codex OAuth lane to `/api/openai/hud-summary`. When `OPENAI_API_KEY` is unset (or `GEV_PREFER_CODEX_OAUTH=true`), the five-word HUD summary is generated on the **ChatGPT backend** — `chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/responses`, the Codex CLI's own endpoint (same routing OpenClaw uses for Codex OAuth) — instead of the metered platform Responses API. With this + #653, **voice and the HUD summary both work with zero API key** for anyone signed into the Codex CLI.

## What the backend demands (all probed live)

- `ChatGPT-Account-Id` header, decoded from the JWT's `https://api.openai.com/auth` → `chatgpt_account_id` claim
- `store: false`, `stream: true` (SSE; parsed for `response.completed` / `output_text.done`), list-form `input`, no `max_output_tokens`
- Codex-supported model ids only — the account's catalog is discoverable at `GET /backend-api/codex/models?client_version=…`. Default `gpt-5.6-luna`, overridable via `OPENAI_HUD_SUMMARY_CODEX_MODEL`.

## Degradation

A 429 `usage_limit_reached` (subscription quota) or any upstream error keeps the existing free deterministic telemetry summary — same fallback the keyless mode already uses. The lane is echoed in `X-GEV-Hud-Auth`. Key-lane behavior is byte-identical to before.

## Receipts

- 7 new handler/wire tests (key shape unchanged, strict Codex shape, 429 passthrough, SSE parsing, env model override) + the 12 from #653 — all green.
- Live on this machine (env-key lane): `POST /api/openai/hud-summary` → `{"summary":"God s Eye View Austin"}`.
- Live Codex-lane 200 pending the author's ChatGPT quota reset (request shape verified to pass backend validation; blocked only at quota). Will confirm and post.
- `npm run build`, `npm test`, `npm run test:track` (109/0), `format:check`, `check:boundaries` all green.

title: fix(traffic): prioritize on-screen roads in the dot budget
body:
Closes the first "next iteration candidate" under *Street traffic can be slow/uneven when panning across dense city blocks* in `docs/KNOWN-ISSUES.md`: prioritize currently visible road segments inside the active viewport before off-center segments.

## Changes

`MAX_DOTS` is a hard cap and every dot costs the same per-frame animation work whether or not it is on screen, but allocation spread that cap evenly across the whole fetched tile. Roads are fetched in a box centered on the look-at ground point (the C4 fix) while the frame the user sees is the camera rectangle, and at an oblique pitch the two are offset: measured on the running app at 650 m / −30° over midtown, 47 % of the fetched roads lay outside the camera rectangle with the cap already exhausted, and only 36.8 % of the dots landed on canvas. `allocateRoadDotBudgets` now takes the live camera rectangle — the one from `getViewBounds()` at render time, not the one the fetch was centered on, since a render can follow a cached tile or a late flow response. Roads whose bounding box meets that rectangle, grown by a margin ring, reach their ideal dot count first; the rest take every dot the visible tier leaves. Passes 2 and 3 are unchanged in kind and simply run per tier.

The ring is floored at `MIN_CENTER_SHIFT_KM`: `onCameraChanged` skips reloading — and therefore re-allocating — for any pan shorter than that, and a purely proportional ring is narrower than that pan on a small rectangle, which is exactly where the cap binds hardest. `VIEWPORT_PRIORITY_MARGIN` has to stay well under 0.5 for the same reason in reverse; at 0.4 the ring swallowed the whole tile in that measurement and the pass became a no-op.

The fairness *seed* does change, and I would rather state it than let it be found later: under a cap too small to give every road one dot, the visible roads are seeded first, so a road outside the frame can drop from one dot to none where it previously kept one. That is the intended trade, `docs/KNOWN-ISSUES.md` records it, and `model.test.mjs` pins it rather than hiding it. With no viewer, or a rectangle that cannot be used — a zero span, or the wrapped form Cesium reports across the antimeridian — allocation falls back to the previous demand-only order, byte for byte.

## How it was verified

- Gates, on the pinned CI matrix rather than only my machine: Node 24.14.0 and 26.x are both green. `doctor -- --json` reports `"ready": true`, `format:check` covers 918 files, `check:boundaries` and `build` pass, and `npm test` is 4170 tests / 0 failing / 1 pre-existing skip — under `GEV_REQUIRE_ALLOCATION_GATE=1`, so the Node-24-calibrated allocation probes ran as hard failures instead of being skipped. `npm run test:track` is 109 passed, 0 failed locally; it needs a browser, so CI does not run it.
- New `src/layers/traffic/model.test.mjs`, 11 tests, including one that runs the real Overpass parse rather than hand-built roads. Every one of the 11 is proven able to fail — I ran 12 mutations against the real source; 11 were killed by the specific test that claims to guard them, and the twelfth is recorded as an equivalent mutant with the argument for why nothing can kill it.
- Randomized property check, 50 000 allocations (48 251 with the cap binding): never exceeds the cap or a road's ideal; an uncapped budget reaches every road exactly; the total is conserved; the visible tier never comes away with fewer dots than before; and **with no rectangle the output is byte-identical to the previous algorithm**. The largest per-road difference inside a tier is 1 dot, from largest-remainder rounding.
- Cost is +1.5–2.3 ms per allocation at 2520 roads × 80 coordinates. There is one call site and it sits on the load path, not in the `preRender` loop.
- `scripts/qa-traffic-viewport-budget.mjs` drives the running app against a deterministic road fixture, reads every rendered dot back through the layer's own `getDetectableObjects()`, and classifies it against the live camera. It exits non-zero when its own preconditions fail — most importantly when no camera reached the cap, since allocation order cannot change such a capture. That is not hypothetical: the first reading I took was exactly that mistake, and it measured this change as a no-op.

| camera | at cap | on canvas before | after |
|---|---|---|---|
| **650 m, −30°, midtown** | **yes** | 36.8 % | **43.8 %** |
| 650 m, −35°, London | no | 40.0 % | 40.2 % |
| 1500 m, −55° | no | 55.1 % | 55.2 % |
| 1500 m, −78° | no | 74.1 % | 74.0 % |

Same 6000 dots, 419 more of them on canvas, and dots behind the camera fall 608 → 257. The three cameras below the cap move by at most 0.2 points against a measured re-run spread of 0.36 — unchanged, as intended.

Two bounds on that number, both stated in the harness header: occlusion is not tested, so the percentage is an upper bound on what is really visible; and the fixture grid is axis-aligned, where the allocator's bounding-box reachability test is very nearly exact, so real curving ways will land in the visible tier more often and the measured *gain* is an upper bound too. `--real-overpass` swaps in live road data at the cost of run-to-run comparability.

What I have not done is a human visual pass on a real GPU. Worth one before merge — and note that #656 makes that pass harder than it should be at exactly the 650 m oblique camera this change targets.

## Unrelated bug found while measuring (not fixed here)

`parseRoads` places an entire road from a single `scene.sampleHeight()` probe taken at its start, guarded only by `Number.isFinite`. When that probe lands before the tiles under it are loaded it returns a finite but absurd value, which passes the guard and plants every dot on that road kilometers underground.

This is not an artifact of my harness. On plain `main` (0d41b6b), with real Google 3D tiles and a real GPU (`ANGLE (NVIDIA Corporation, NVIDIA GB10/PCIe, OpenGL 4.5.0)`, `softwareRenderer: false`), arriving at midtown 650 m / −30° from above the activation ceiling:

```
midtown 650 m / -30:  layer reports 6000 dots | height min -16851 median -16829 max -16805 m | 6000 of 6000 below -1000 m
midtown 1500 m / -55: layer reports 2680 dots | height min   -31 median    -19 max     51 m |    0 of 2680 below -1000 m
```

The HUD says 6000 dots and the screen has none. `policy.js` already documents a milder form of the same single-sample root cause in `JAM_DOT_DEPTH_PUNCH` ("396 jam dots, zero visible"). The QA harness in this PR works around it by re-projecting each dot at ellipsoid height 0 and reporting `meanRenderedHeightM` so the contamination stays visible instead of being folded silently into the numbers.

I left it alone deliberately — `docs/MAINTAINER_WORKFLOW.md` asks contributions to avoid unrelated changes — and filed it separately as #656, with the console repro and the contrast case. Nothing in this PR depends on it, and nothing in this PR fixes it.


---

**Re-validated after updating the branch.** Merged `main` (`81eb443`) in at `1de988ad` — clean, nothing to hand-resolve. The validation above predates that merge, so on the merged tree (Node 24.20.0, Linux aarch64): `doctor` · `format:check` · `check:boundaries` · `build` all exit 0 · `npm test` with `GEV_REQUIRE_ALLOCATION_GATE=1` **5,086 pass / 1 skipped / 0 fail** of 5,087, and the 1 and 13 allocation budgets green.

`npm run layer-token:check -- --base-ref main` → `28 published, 0 new`. That one is new: #744 added it to CI after the checks recorded above this line, so this is the first time the branch has been measured against it. The branch shares no source file with #744 — the overlap is documentation and `scripts/format-scope.json`, which merged cleanly.

Browser-driven gates were not re-run for the merge itself, since what the merge brings in is confined to the share-link token ledger.

title: feat: assign share-link layer tokens explicitly — 34 open PRs are competing for 5 free letters
body:
### Problem

Every layer carries a one-character share-link token in `LAYER_STATE_REGISTRY`, and `validateLayerStateRegistry` requires them to be unique (`src/data/layerState.js:450`). `main` has 21 layers, so five letters are left: `k l o v y`.

I scanned the open pull requests against `main` at `0d41b6b` on 18 September. **34 of them add at least one registry entry, proposing 55 new layers between them.** They are competing for those five letters:

| token | claimed by |
|---|---|
| `k` | 9 — #651 cellular-networks · #638 melbourne-pedestrians · #618 weather · #606 tectonic-plates · #584 message-signs · #464 wind · #459 wind · #58 slf-alpine-stations · #11 wigle-networks |
| `y` | 9 — #638 flight-patterns · #637 flight-patterns · #633 meshtastic · #617 weather-cyclones · #609 fire-history · #414 fire-weather · #374 ham-stations · #277 mapillary · #116 rayhunter-tap |
| `l` | 7 — #638 live-trains · #637 live-trains · #635 live-trains · #617 weather-lightning · #458 glm-lightning · #414 floods · #374 ham-repeaters |
| `v` | 5 — #617 weather-radar · #588 weather-radar · #414 high-wind · #374 ham-propagation · #13 nifc-wildfires |
| `o` | 5 — #617 weather-satellite · #414 winter-weather · #374 ham-beacons · #205 warscope-events · #100 ocean-conditions |

Five more tokens are claimed by PRs that have simply been overtaken — the letter was free when they were opened and is not free now:

| token | now held on `main` by | still claimed by |
|---|---|---|
| `h` | `bhote-koshi-2026` (merged 15 Sep, #590) | #586 #568 #457 #414 #374 #279 #129 #12 |
| `z` | `bhote-koshi-locator` (merged 15 Sep, #590) | #414 |
| `n` | `directions` | #419 #414 #374 #307 #100 #15 |
| `j` | `transit` | #374 #115 #114 |
| `p` | `alpr-cameras` | #414 #374 |

Twenty-three of the 34 already show a merge conflict, so a good part of this queue has rotted in place. The conflict marker only says the registry file changed — it does not say the token is gone, and an author who resolves it by keeping both sides ends up with a duplicate that nothing catches until `validateLayerStateRegistry` throws in CI.

Restricting the count to the eleven that are still clean (#584 #588 #606 #609 #617 #618 #633 #635 #637 #638 #651) shows the competition is live rather than historical: five of them want `k`, five want `y`, four want `l`.

The same shape shows up in the pinned layer count. **33 of those 34 PRs rewrite `assert.equal(REGISTERED_LAYER_IDS.length, N)` in `src/data/layerState.test.mjs`, and they pin it to seven different values**: `17` (14 PRs), `19` (3), `20` (5), `22` (6), `23` (1), `24` (3), `26` (1). `main` is at 21, so the fourteen pinned at `17` sit four below it.

The net effect is that whichever layer PR merges next puts the other 33 in line for a red build on their next rebase — duplicate token, stale count, or both.

Two things I don't want to overstate:

- **Nothing breaks silently.** `Duplicate layer-state token` throws and CI fails, so no published share link has ever been corrupted by this. The cost is rework and review time, not user-visible breakage.
- **The pinned count is not the bug.** It is a deliberate tripwire that makes a registry change visible in review, and it is doing its job. The conflicts are a symptom of queue depth.

Counts include stacked PRs (#635 → #637 → #638 are one line of work), and #617 is your own draft — it claims `o`, `l`, `v` and `y`, so the in-flight weather work is competing with the queue too.

To re-derive any of the above:

```bash
REPO=bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view
gh api "repos/$REPO/contents/src/data/layerState.js" -H 'Accept: application/vnd.github.raw' \
  | grep -oP "id: '\K[a-z0-9-]+" | sort -u > /tmp/gev-main-ids.txt

gh pr list --repo "$REPO" --state open --limit 300 --json number -q '.[].number' |
while read -r n; do
  gh api "repos/$REPO/pulls/$n/files" --paginate \
      -q '.[]|select(.filename=="src/data/layerState.js")|.patch' 2>/dev/null \
    | grep '^+' | sed 's/^+//' | tr '\n' ' ' \
    | grep -oP "id: '\K[a-z0-9-]+'[^}]{0,120}?token: '[a-z0-9]'" \
    | sed -E "s/',[[:space:]]*token: '/ /; s/'$//" \
    | while read -r id token; do
        grep -qx "$id" /tmp/gev-main-ids.txt || echo "#$n $id $token"
      done
done
```

It prints 55 lines across 34 PRs, and `awk '{print $3}' | sort | uniq -c` gives the tables above.

Two details in that script matter, and both of them caught me out on the first pass. Added lines have to be joined before matching, because a registry entry spans several lines and a line-by-line grep quietly finds only the few that happen to be written on one. And ids already on `main` have to be dropped, because a whole-file Prettier reformat — #457 is one — re-adds every existing `token:` line as a `+` line, which reads as 21 fresh claims if you let it. My first numbers were wrong in both directions before I fixed that.

### Proposal

Smallest thing that helps, in the order I'd do it:

1. **Write the rule down in CONTRIBUTING.md.** One paragraph: the share token is assigned when a layer PR merges, not when it is opened, and a rebase may require picking a new one. No code changes. Most of the cost here is the surprise, and a paragraph takes that away.

2. **Start using digits.** `validateLayerStateRegistry` accepts `^[a-z0-9]$` and no layer uses a digit yet, so `0`–`9` are ten slots available today with no format change and no migration.

   I verified the whole path rather than trusting the regex. With `civic-offices` on token `1`:

   ```
   encodeLayerStateParams → v=2&l=c.1.t&lo=f.e.1
   decodeLayerStateParams → ["cctv", "civic-offices", "traffic"]
   npm test → 4170 tests, 0 failures
   ```

   Tokens are joined with `.`, and layer tokens live in `l` while option tokens live in `lo`, so a digit is never ambiguous with an option value.

3. Going past 36 layers is a share-link format question — two-character tokens behind the existing `v=2` gate — and deserves its own issue rather than being decided here.

I'm deliberately not suggesting you derive the pinned count automatically. It's there on purpose so a registry change can't pass review unnoticed, and that's worth more than the conflicts it causes.

### Data source, license, and attribution

None — contributor workflow and share-link namespace, no data.

### Will you build it?

Yes, I plan to open a PR — for (1) and (2), if you want them. I'm already running (2) on a branch here. Equally happy to leave this as a report if you'd rather settle the allocation rule yourself first.

title: bug: Street Traffic reports road data unavailable even with working TomTom access
body: ### What happened The Street Traffic layer consistently ends in: `UNAVAILABLE · OpenStreetMap · Road data temporarily unavailable` This happens even when the camera is left completely still. It is reproducible in a city-level view, so it is not caused by panning or a city jump. ### What I verified - The running app reports the TomTom provider as configured (`GET /api/tomtom/status` returns HTTP 200 with `hasKey: true`). - A real TomTom traffic-flow tile request through the app returns HTTP 200 with data. - The OpenStreetMap/Overpass road request fails independently in this environment: - `overpass-api.de` returns HTTP 406. - `lz4.overpass-api.de` returns HTTP 406. - `overpass.kumi.systems` and `overpass.private.coffee` time out. - The local Overpass cache is empty, so there is no road snapshot available for fallback. This indicates the TomTom credential is not the cause. Street Traffic needs OSM road geometry before it can match TomTom flow data to roads. When the Overpass mirrors refuse or time out, the layer becomes unavailable even though TomTom is responding. The repository already documents slow or uneven street-traffic loading while panning in `docs/KNOWN-ISSUES.md`; **this report is more specific because the same failure occurs while stationary and the road-data dependency is independently failing.** ### Expected behavior The layer should either recover through a healthy road-data source, clearly identify the Overpass provider failure and retry, or use a cached/local road snapshot so valid TomTom flow data can still be used. The current UI makes this look like a general Street Traffic or API-key failure and gives no actionable indication that the failing dependency is the public Overpass road-data service. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Start the local development server and open `http://localhost:4173`. 2. Zoom to a city-level view. 3. Enable the Street Traffic layer. 4. Leave the camera completely still and wait for loading to settle. 5. Observe `UNAVAILABLE · OpenStreetMap · Road data temporarily unavailable`. 6. Separately verify that `GET /api/tomtom/status` returns `hasKey: true` and that a TomTom flow tile request returns HTTP 200. ### How you installed Terminal (git clone + npm) ### OS, Node version, browser Windows; Node 24.19.0; Chrome (version unknown) ### Version or commit 0d41b6b ### Output of `npm run doctor` ```text `npm run doctor` could not be invoked in the current PowerShell session because `npm` is not on PATH. Running the equivalent `node scripts/setup-doctor.mjs` reported: - Node 24.19.0: supported LTS - npm was not found - dependencies installed - the doctor summary showed built-in traffic simulation The running app's TomTom status endpoint independently reports `hasKey: true`, and the TomTom flow tile request returns HTTP 200. ``` ### Server log and browser console ```text The visible UI error is: `UNAVAILABLE · OpenStreetMap · Road data temporarily unavailable` Local provider checks from the same app instance: - `GET /api/tomtom/status` -> HTTP 200, `hasKey: true` - TomTom flow tile request -> HTTP 200 with traffic data - Overpass mirror `overpass-api.de` -> HTTP 406 - Overpass mirror `lz4.overpass-api.de` -> HTTP 406 - Overpass mirrors `overpass.kumi.systems` and `overpass.private.coffee` -> timeout No API keys, tokens, or personal information are included here. ```
