title: feat(data): add a single audio claim so one producer plays at a time
body:
Part 3 of 4 for #715. Independent of #718 and #719.

## The sentence in the issue that has nothing behind it

> "Plays through the Radio transport, one audio source at a time."

That guarantee does not exist yet. Radio's single-source property is the incidental consequence of there being exactly one `HTMLAudioElement`, owned privately by one layer (`layerState._audio = new Audio()`, `src/layers/radio/playback.js:36`). Nothing outside Radio can ask whether audio is free or who holds it.

Meanwhile `src/` already has **eight** independent audio producers:

`voice/realtimeInput.js` · `voice/realtimeFacade.js` · `layers/radio/playback.js` · `layers/radio/tuningNoise.js` · `layers/cctv/videoPlayback.js` · `layers/cctv/projection.js` · `layers/weather/clock.js` · `data/bhoteKoshiEvent.js`

The only arbitration between any of them is Radio's one-way voice duck. CCTV audio, the Bhote Koshi clip and a radio stream can all sound at once today. ATC would be the ninth, and "one at a time" would be a comment rather than a mechanism.

## What this adds

`src/data/audioOwnership.js`, shaped after the house precedent one layer up (`src/data/inputOwnership.js`):

```js
const lease = claimAudio('atc', { onRevoked: () => stopAtc() });
releaseAudio(lease);
audioOwner(); isAudioFree(); isAudioOwnedBy('radio'); isAudioLeaseCurrent(lease);
```

## Why it preempts where the pointer claim refuses

This is the one place it deliberately diverges from `inputOwnership`, so it is worth stating plainly: a click that does two things is worse than a click that does nothing, so `claimPointer` is **refused** while another tool holds it. Audio is the other way round — if the user opens a CCTV stream while the radio plays, silence from the camera is a bug and two soundtracks at once is a worse one. The last thing the user asked for is the thing that should be audible, so a claim **always succeeds** and the incumbent's `onRevoked` tells it to stop.

**Ducking stays out of this module.** The voice assistant lowering the radio for the length of an utterance is a volume policy between two sources that are both meant to be live (`layerState._voiceDucked`, `src/layers/radio/volume.js:41-113`). This is about which source is playing at all. ATC will need both; they are not the same mechanism.

## The ordering is the substance

A lease module is three lines of state and a pile of ordering decisions, so each one is pinned:

- The new owner is installed **before** the old one is told. A revoked producer whose teardown runs a beat later calls `releaseAudio` with the lease it still holds — with a revoke-then-install order that frees its successor's brand-new claim, and the next thing to ask "is anyone playing?" is told no while ATC is audible.
- `onRevoked` runs **at most once**, and never on a voluntary release — a producer that stopped itself does not need to be told to stop.
- `claimAudio` returns the lease **that call issued**, not whatever the module holds afterwards. A revocation callback may claim for itself (a producer told to stop deciding to restart); returning the live lease would hand the caller someone else's token and let it release a claim it never held.
- A callback that throws is reported and swallowed. A broken incumbent must not prevent the new sound from starting.
- `resetAudioOwnership()` drops the claim **without** revoking, because application teardown reaches a half-disposed producer and calling its stop path there is how an error gets thrown out of shutdown.

### The footgun the review pass caught

A producer that already holds the audio and changes what it plays — Radio on station A, user picks station B — would claim again and **revoke itself**: its own `onRevoked` fires and stops the playback it is starting. That is not something a caller should be expected to notice.

So a holder passes its live lease as `renew`, which suppresses the revocation but still issues a fresh lease, so a queued teardown from the previous attempt cannot free the new claim. A **stale** lease cannot renew past a takeover — that is a takeover, and the current owner is properly revoked. The same holds for a *live lease that belongs to another owner*: `renew` is only honoured when the lease is current **and** was issued to the owner that is claiming.

## Nothing is wired to it yet

Deliberate. Each producer's "am I audible right now" rule is its own question, and Radio's is not trivial: `playPreparedRadioForVoice` starts a stream at volume 0 to verify it, so a naive claim there would take the audio away from whatever is actually audible in order to play silence. That belongs in a change that can be reviewed on its own, not folded into the primitive. The ATC panel (part 4) is the first consumer.

## Testing

15 tests, every one mutation-verified:

| mutation | result |
|---|---|
| refuse to preempt (copy `inputOwnership`) | 7 fail |
| revoke before installing the new owner | 2 fail |
| drop the lease identity check in `releaseAudio` | 4 fail |
| revoke on voluntary release too | 1 fail |
| remove the `try`/`catch` around the callback | 1 fail |
| return `currentLease` instead of the issued one | 1 fail |
| ignore `renew` | 1 fail |
| accept any lease as a renewal | 1 fail |
| accept another owner's live lease as a renewal | 1 fail |
| reuse the old lease id when renewing | 1 fail |
| restored | 15 pass / 0 fail |

## Gates, re-measured after a rebase

This branch was `BEHIND`. Rebased onto `main` at `b210ab0`; head is now `b6d41d2`, content unchanged.

| gate | result on `b6d41d2`, Node 24.20.0 |
|---|---|
| `doctor` · `format:check` · `check:boundaries` | clean |
| `build` | clean |
| `npm test`, `GEV_REQUIRE_ALLOCATION_GATE=1` | **5,092 pass · 1 skipped · 0 fail** of 5,093 |
| `test:track` | **109 passed · 0 failed** |
| `node scripts/qa-radio.mjs` | 105 passed · 1 failed, same single failure as `main` |

On the feature gate, plainly: no `scripts/qa-*.mjs` exercises this module, because nothing imports it yet. Of the 70 gates, four touch audio at all — `qa-radio`, `qa-voice-routing`, `qa-voice-wav`, `qa-director-packs` — and none names a claim, a lease or an owner. The regression surface for the module is `src/data/audioOwnership.test.mjs`.

So I ran `qa-radio` as the nearest live audio surface, the producer ATC will contend with, and compared failing checks by name rather than by count — five runs, three on this branch and two on `main` at `b210ab0`:

| failing check | this branch | `main` |
|---|---|---|
| `runtime console remains clean` | 3 of 3 | 2 of 2 |
| a panel-lane check | 1 of 3 | 1 of 2 |

`runtime console remains clean` fails on both trees for the same reason: a 404 on `https://tile.googleapis.com/v1/3dtiles/root.json` and a 403 on `/api/google/nearby-places`, because the local Maps key is not enabled for those APIs.

The panel-lane failure is intermittent and hit a *different* check each time — `HUD-off to Tactical preserves the latest-opened Scenes panel` on this branch, `closing Tactical lane owners restores eligible temporary siblings` on `main`. Since it appears on the unchanged tree too, it is not from this PR; I mention it only because a single run would otherwise look like a regression. Payloads are in both logs if they are useful to you.

Two notes for anyone reproducing. Comparing by name matters — `grep '[FAIL]'` reads as zero failures because the harness colours the word, so the brackets are not adjacent. And on ARM Linux the browser gates need `PUPPETEER_EXECUTABLE_PATH`: Chrome for Testing publishes no linux-arm64 build, so the cached binary is x86-64 and `existsSync()` accepts it anyway.

The phrase "13 allocation budgets" counted tests inside one probe file — `ALLOCATION_TEST_FILES` holds two files, run serialized under `--expose-gc`, for 1 + 13 = 14 budget tests.

---

The validation above predates that merge, so on the merged tree (Node 24.20.0, Linux aarch64): `doctor` · `format:check` · `check:boundaries` · `build` all exit 0 · `npm test` with `GEV_REQUIRE_ALLOCATION_GATE=1` **5,089 pass / 1 skipped / 0 fail** of 5,090, and the 1 and 13 allocation budgets green.

`npm run layer-token:check -- --base-ref main` → `28 published, 0 new`. That one is new: #744 added it to CI after the checks recorded above this line, so this is the first time the branch has been measured against it. The branch shares no source file with #744 — the overlap is documentation and `scripts/format-scope.json`, which merged cleanly.

Browser-driven gates were not re-run for the merge itself, since what the merge brings in is confined to the share-link token ledger.

## Follow-up (review)

- `claimAudio('cctv', { renew: radioLease })` used to count as a continuation because the radio's lease was current, so the radio was never told to stop. It now revokes it; covered by a new test and verified by removing the owner check (1 fail).
- Note for #255: it also adds `src/data/audioOwnership.js`, exporting `claimAudio(owner, { preempt = true })`. The two signatures differ (`preempt` there, `onRevoked`/`renew` here), so whichever merges second has to reconcile them.

title: fix(live): return 502 and prevent caching on oversized track responses (fixes #720)
body:
Fixes #720

### Problem

When querying historical aircraft tracks via `/api/opensky-track` or `/api/adsblol/trace`, `readCappedResponseText(upstream, RESPONSE_CAP_BYTES)` guards against memory exhaustion by aborting responses that exceed the 5 MB threshold (`tooLarge = true`). 

However:
1. **Wrong HTTP Status:** `res.statusCode` was unconditionally assigned `upstream.status`, which was `200 OK` (the upstream started streaming with a 200 header before the body exceeded the cap). As a result, the proxy returned an HTTP 200 response with an error body: `{"error":"Upstream track response too large"}`.
2. **Silent Failure in Client:** In `src/sources/live/standalone.js` (`getTrack()`), the client checks `if (!response.ok) throw httpError(response, 'OpenSky')`. Because `response.ok` is `true`, no error was thrown, and `normalizeAircraftTrack(payload?.path)` received `undefined`, silently treating the failure as an empty track (`{ records: [], complete: false }`) and bypassing fallback error handling.
3. **Cache Poisoning:** The aborted failure payload was saved to `cachePut` with `status: 200`, causing repeated requests within `TRACK_CACHE_MS` (60s) to be served the cached 200 error string.

### Solution

- **Accurate Error Semantics:** In `server/providers/aircraft/tracks.js`, assign `status = 502` (Bad Gateway) when `tooLarge` is true so that downstream clients and proxies recognize this as an upstream transport failure.
- **Cache Isolation:** Bypass `cachePut` when `tooLarge` is true, ensuring transient oversized stream failures are not cached.
- **Regression Test:** Added an automated unit test in `src/tooling/liveProviders.test.mjs` verifying that:
  - An oversized stream returns HTTP 502 with `{"error":"Upstream track response too large"}`.
  - The failure is not cached, allowing subsequent requests for the same ICAO to reach upstream and succeed.

### Verification

All checks recommended by `CONTRIBUTING.md` pass locally:

- **Targeted Unit Tests:** `node --test src/tooling/liveProviders.test.mjs` (9/9 pass)
- **Production Build:** `npm run build` (Clean exit 0)
- **Package Boundaries:** `npm run check:boundaries` (Clean exit 0)
- **Code Formatting:** `npm run format:check` (Clean exit 0, 1021 source files checked)

title: feat(data): an ATC decision layer — phase, airport, frequency, audio
body:
Closes part of #715.

**Stacked.** This branch sits on top of #718, #719 and #721 and its diff contains
their commits. Only the last commit is new here — `8f22841`, four modules and their
tests, plus `CHANGELOG.md` and `scripts/format-scope.json`. Merge order:
718 → 719 → 721 → this. I kept them apart on purpose — each stands on its own and
each is reviewable without the others.

Rebuilt on `main` at `b210ab0`, and rebuilt rather than rebased: the copies it carried
of the other three predated their current heads — #718 has since gained a
`docs/CURRENT-STATE.md` paragraph — so a plain rebase would have kept stale copies and
could have dropped that paragraph on merge. The copies here are re-taken from the three
branches as they now stand; nothing else changed.

## What this adds

Four leaf modules in `src/data/` that answer "which controller is the aircraft I am
tracking talking to, and can I hear them". No app code imports them yet, so this
adds **zero bytes to the shipped bundle** (checked: none of the four appear in
`dist/assets/*.js`).

| Module | Answers |
|---|---|
| `flightPhase.js` | taxi / runway / takeoff / climb / cruise / descent / approach — or refuses |
| `atcTuning.js` | which airport, which position, or why there is none |
| `atcStreamPreference.js` | the viewer's own stream URL, validated and remembered |
| `atcAudio.js` | plays it through the shared claim from #721 |

## The design argument

**The phase→frequency mapping in the issue is a fiction at most airports.** Of the
9,562 airports in the pack, 443 publish all four of TWR/GND/APP/ATIS and **6,036
publish none of them**. So a phase produces a *preference order* that degrades
against what an airport actually publishes, not a lookup. An uncontrolled field is
reported as uncontrolled — its CTAF comes back with `matchedPhase: false` and a
reason attached, so a panel cannot caption it "Ground 122.8" and invent a
controller. ATIS is tagged `broadcast` for the same reason: it is a recorded loop,
not someone talking to this aircraft.

**Two things the classifier refuses to guess**, because guessing produces confident
wrong answers instead of visible gaps:

- *Height above the field.* `altitudeM` is barometric MSL. 900 m MSL is short final
  on the coast and below the runway at Denver (field 1,655 m). No field elevation →
  `airborne`, not a phase computed against sea level. This is why #719's pack
  carries `elevationM`.
- *Climb versus descent.* Level at 3,000 ft and descending through 3,000 ft are the
  same row without a rate, and they are different controllers. No rate → `airborne`.

Both name the missing input in `missing[]` rather than leaving the caller guessing.

`flightDirection()` is separate because the dependency would otherwise be circular:
the phase needs the reference airport's elevation, and choosing that airport needs
to know climbing from descending. `flightDirection` needs neither.

## No panel

The presentation is deliberately not here. Radio builds its UI from 6 files in
`src/ui/` on top of a 20-file layer, and guessing at that convention blind is not
something I can QA to a standard worth reviewing. Everything a panel needs is one
`await resolveAtcTuning(info)` away. Happy to build it once the shape is agreed —
I would rather ask than guess.

## What an audit of the branch turned up

I ran the call graph over this before opening it, and it found one thing worth
stating rather than leaving for review to catch:

**`routePlausible.js` already asks the same climbing-or-descending question, at a
different threshold.** It uses `VERT_TREND_MPS = 2 m/s` (~400 ft/min) to decide
*departing → origin should be local, arriving → destination should be local* —
which is the same mapping `chooseReferenceAirport` uses. This classifier uses
`LEVEL_RATE_MPS = 1.524` (300 ft/min). Between those two figures the modules
disagree.

I left both constants alone and documented the divergence at the definition site.
The jobs carry different costs for being wrong: `routePlausible` decides whether to
*hide a route label*, so it should only act on a trend pronounced enough to call a
filed route wrong; this one picks *which controller to show*, where reading level on
a shallow descent puts the wrong frequency on screen. If you would rather they
shared one constant, say so and I will unify them in a follow-up rather than widen
this PR.

Two smaller notes from the same pass: `ourAirportsAtc.js` reuses `greatCircleKm`
from `routePlausible.js` rather than adding a 17th private distance helper to the
16 already in the tree (15 under `src/`, one under `server/`); and
`atcStreamPreference.js` keeps its own `safeStorage` guard, matching what the other
14 files touching `localStorage` under `src/` do, though mine also survives the
property *access* throwing (the trap `src/layers/cctv/model.js` documents).

## Testing

62 tests, **mutation-verified** — 19 mutations run, 16 turned a test red
on the first pass. Two survivors were real gaps and are now closed:

1. A missing vertical rate silently read as **cruise** high above the field, because
   `null > 1.524` and `null < -1.524` are both false and it fell through to the
   level branch. A confident answer built on a datum nobody reported.
2. A self-revoking re-claim was invisible in the reported state — the assignments
   after the claim overwrite what the callback cleared — while it tore the audio
   element down (pause, drop src, load) on **every station change**. Only an
   assertion on the element's call sequence catches it.

The third survivor is an equivalent mutant: releasing inside `onRevoked` is already
a no-op, because the claim installs the new lease before revoking, so the old one is
stale by then.

## Gates, re-measured after the rebuild

| gate | result on `8f22841`, Node 24.20.0 |
|---|---|
| `doctor` · `format:check` · `check:boundaries` | clean |
| `build` | clean |
| `npm test`, `GEV_REQUIRE_ALLOCATION_GATE=1` | **5,161 pass · 1 skipped · 0 fail** of 5,162 |
| `test:track` | **109 passed · 0 failed** |
| `node scripts/qa-cockpit-utility.mjs` | 2 failures, `main` has 3 — read on |
| `node scripts/qa-attribution-b12.mjs` | 23 passed · 1 failed, same as `main` |

Two feature gates, because the branch carries two areas that have one. `qa-cockpit-utility` covers the tracked-aircraft descriptor #718 extends; `qa-attribution-b12` covers the credits surface #719 adds to. The four modules this PR's own commit adds have no gate, because nothing imports them yet — the regression surface for them is the four colocated `*.test.mjs` files, 55 tests.

Both gates fail the same way on `main` at `b210ab0`, compared by failing check name rather than by count:

| failing check | `8f22841` | `main` |
|---|---|---|
| `runtime console remains clean` / `no console errors during QA` | yes | yes |
| `Cyber collapsed Live Signals … resize to 720px` | yes | yes |
| `Cyber collapsed Live Signals … resize to 640px` | no | yes |

The console failures are a 404 on `https://tile.googleapis.com/v1/3dtiles/root.json` and 403s on `/api/google/nearby-places`, because the local Maps key is not enabled for those APIs. The Cyber Live Signals check fails on the unchanged tree too, and its 640px sibling failed there and not here, so that one is intermittent. Nothing here is attributable to this PR.

Two notes for anyone reproducing. `qa-attribution-b12` defaults to `--url http://localhost:4300` and does not read `PORT`. And on ARM Linux the browser gates need `PUPPETEER_EXECUTABLE_PATH`: Chrome for Testing publishes no linux-arm64 build, so the cached binary is x86-64 and `existsSync()` accepts it anyway.

Correcting numbers this description carried earlier: they were measured on `1263536` over `513dc87`, before the rebuild, where `npm test` read 5,119. The phrase "13 allocation budgets" counted tests inside one probe file — `ALLOCATION_TEST_FILES` holds two files, run serialized under `--expose-gc`, for 1 + 13 = 14 budget tests. `test:track` and the two feature gates were missing from that list; they are above.

---

**Re-validated after updating the branch.** Merged `main` (`81eb443`) in at `c08058d0` — clean, nothing to hand-resolve. The validation above predates that merge, so on the merged tree (Node 24.20.0, Linux aarch64): `doctor` · `format:check` · `check:boundaries` · `build` all exit 0 · `npm test` with `GEV_REQUIRE_ALLOCATION_GATE=1` **5,158 pass / 1 skipped / 0 fail** of 5,159, and the 1 and 13 allocation budgets green.

`npm run layer-token:check -- --base-ref main` → `28 published, 0 new`. That one is new: #744 added it to CI after the checks recorded above this line, so this is the first time the branch has been measured against it. The branch shares no source file with #744 — the overlap is documentation and `scripts/format-scope.json`, which merged cleanly.

Browser-driven gates were not re-run for the merge itself, since what the merge brings in is confined to the share-link token ledger.

## Follow-up (review)

- **Route airport by coordinates.** `chooseReferenceAirport` looked a route end's `code` up as an OurAirports ident, but adsbdb publishes the IATA code where there is one (`AUS`, not `KAUS`), so most routes silently fell through to proximity. It now resolves by the route end's `lat`/`lon` (nearest packed airport within 5 km), uses a four-character code as an ident only when there are no coordinates, and believes the route only while the airport is within `maxKm` of the aircraft — previously a route end of any distance won.
- **Claim after the stream starts.** `atcAudio.play()` claimed the audio before `audio.play()`, so a stream that never started (blocked autoplay, dead URL) still stopped the radio, and a failed station change left a lease on a silent element. It now claims when playback has started and releases on failure. The previous source keeps sounding for the moment the stream takes to start.
- `controlled` is documented as a property of the airport, not the frequency (a cruising aircraft is rightly offered a `CNTR` frequency at an airport with no tower). The `onGround`-absent branch of `classifyFlightPhase` is documented as reachable only from a hand-built descriptor, since the flights layer always sets a boolean.
- Phase labels, tuning reasons and the audio and stream-URL errors are marked with `msg()` and translated for all 11 locales (consumers render them through `t()`). Translations other than es, ru and zh-CN are machine-assisted and would benefit from a native-speaker pass.
- Includes the #719 (`CNTR`) and #721 (`renew` owner) fixes. New tests: route by IATA code with coordinates, far route airport, tight radius, unmatched coordinates, `CNTR`-only cruise, claim not taken on failure or while loading, lease released after a failed station change; each verified by mutation (4 of 4 killed).
- Re-measured on `f801a3f` after merging `main`: all gates clean, `npm test` 11,598 pass · 0 fail of 11,602 (4 skipped). The gate table above predates the merge.

title: Add live Taiwan CCTV coverage with Traditional Chinese localization
body:
## Summary
- Adds Taiwan camera catalogs from the Freeway Bureau (keyless XML) and TDX (provincial highway + city). Their live MJPEG streams are proxied through the existing CCTV pipeline. Neither source publishes camera bearings, so headings are derived from road geometry.

title: fix(aircraft): return 502 on oversized track response and avoid caching failure
body:
## What

When an upstream aircraft track payload (OpenSky or adsb.lol) exceeds the 5 MB buffer ceiling (`RESPONSE_CAP_BYTES`), `readCappedResponseText` aborts the stream and returns `tooLarge = true`.

Previously:
- The proxy still assigned `res.statusCode = upstream.status` (which is HTTP 200 OK) alongside the `{"error":"Upstream track response too large"}` body.
- The failure payload was cached with status 200 in `cachePut` for 60 seconds.
- Consequently, client-side callers (`src/sources/live/standalone.js:90`) checked `response.ok`, found it to be true, and called `normalizeAircraftTrack(undefined)` which returned an empty array instead of triggering error handling and fallback paths.

This PR:
1. Returns HTTP `502 Bad Gateway` when `tooLarge` is true.
2. Bypasses `cachePut` on oversized responses so failed responses are not cached as valid responses.
3. Adds automated unit tests in `src/tooling/liveProviders.test.mjs` asserting the 502 status, error response, and cache-bypass behavior.

Closes #720

- `npm run check:boundaries` (clean)

title: feat(ui): portable, resizable rail panels (CCTV opts in)
body:
## Portable, resizable rail panels

Rail panels can opt into a portable mode: drag the panel by its header to lift it out of `#right-context-rail`, resize it from any of the four edges or corners, and double-click the header to snap it back. CCTV opts in here; other panels can follow with one `dragSpecs` entry (`{ id, panel, handle, portable: true, min: { width, height } }`).

### Why

The right rail lays panels out adaptively and pins them in place, so today nothing in the rail can be moved or sized. Users working with the CCTV frame (and, in a follow-up, the street-level viewer) want more room than the rail column gives them without leaving the map view.

### How

- `src/ui/panelResize.js`: pure `resizeBox(box, dir, dx, dy, limits)` geometry — the edge under the pointer moves, the opposite edge stays pinned, minimums and the viewport margin win. Unit-tested.
- `PanelPositionControls`: portable specs get a 4 px drag threshold; the first movement adds `panel-floating`, freezes the current width, promotes z within the [100, 139] ladder and reflows the rail. Eight resize handles (seven invisible strips plus the visible south-east grip). Position and explicit size persist under the existing `godsEyeView.v8.panelPos.<id>` key with a `floating` flag; a viewport reclamp only moves, never re-measures. First lift-out shows a one-time toast about snapping back.
- `rightPanelRail.js` skips `.panel-floating` panels when measuring and allocating.
- CSS in `controls.css` with no `!important`; rail rules in `layers.css` / `responsive.css` are guarded with `:not(.panel-floating)`.
- `onPanelResized(panelId)` hook threaded through `PanelChrome` to `ApplicationShell` for panels that need to refit content.

### Verified before merge

- `npm run format:check`, `npm run check:boundaries`, `npm run build`; unit suite 4,168 passing, 0 failing (1 pre-existing skip).
- New tests: `panelResize.test.mjs` (4), rail exclusion case in `panelRails.test.mjs`, `panelResizeQa.test.mjs` (5); `scripts/qa-panel-resize.mjs` (`npm run qa:panel-resize`) drives a browser through lift-out, all eight handles, minimum sizes, reload persistence and snap-back.

title: feat(mapillary): Street Level layer — coverage, sequences, embedded viewer, optional plain-English query
body:
## Street Level (Mapillary): coverage, sequences, embedded viewer, optional plain-English query

Adds Mapillary as a street-level data source. Mapillary is the largest open street-level imagery platform (CC BY-SA 4.0 imagery, MIT tooling), and its detected map features and traffic signs are a natural fit for a globe that already shows CCTV and ALPR cameras. The layer lives as an ordinary collapsible panel in the right context rail next to CCTV, starts collapsed, and stays useful without any key beyond the free client token.

### What the user gets

- **Coverage on the globe**: z0–5 overview points from orbit, ground-clamped sequence lines below 60 km (drawn on terrain and Google 3D tiles), a colour legend (recent / older / 360° / selected) and 360°-only and capture-date filters.
- **Photos**: click a green line to see its image cones, click a cone (or OPEN NEAREST PHOTO) to open an embedded MapillaryJS viewer with FIT/FILL, an EXPAND mode that is a focus-trapped dialog, a CAMERA FOLLOWS VIEW mode that drives the Cesium camera from the panorama, and a deep link to mapillary.com.
- **Ask in plain English** (only with `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, server-side): "show me all fire hydrants in Sacramento" becomes a plan (feature class, place, date filters) that is streamed from Mapillary's z14 map-feature tiles and drawn with Mapillary's own sprite icons; clicking a result opens the detecting photo with the detection outlined. ASK becomes STOP while running; results summarise as "834 fire hydrants · seen 2017–2021".
- **Keyless behaviour**: without `MAPILLARY_CLIENT_TOKEN` the panel shows a gated empty state naming the variable with a POWER UP link; without an Anthropic key the query box explains itself and stays disabled while everything else works.

### Keys

- `MAPILLARY_CLIENT_TOKEN` (free): a public client token by design, injected into the browser like the Google and Cesium keys (SECURITY.md updated to "three deliberately client-side keys"). The dev server uses the same token to fetch tiles.
- `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` (optional): never reaches the browser; the page posts the sentence to `/api/mapillary/plan`. Opt-in per-IP rate limit `GEV_RATELIMIT_ANTHROPIC_PER_MIN` mirrors the OpenAI provider.

### Architecture

- `src/layers/mapillary/` — layer factory (`init/enable/disable/update/destroy/getStats`), coverage, sequences, features, viewer bridge, query engine; boundary package `mapillary-layer`.
- `server/providers/mapillary/` — status, tiles (memory + disk cache; the 12 MB z14 `image` point layer is stripped in transit at the protobuf level, 12 MB → ~80 KB), NDJSON feature stream capped at 600 tiles, grammar-guarded sprite proxy, structured-output planner; boundary package `mapillary-provider`.
- `src/ui/mapillaryControls.js` + `src/ui/mapillaryPresentation.js` — panel body; every string and flag comes from the pure presentation module.
- Panel markup lives in `layer-panels.html` and is moved into `#right-context-rail` by `PanelLayoutController` exactly like CCTV; registered in `panelChrome` share-state, cockpit-entry and right-rail lists.

### Attribution and licensing

- On-globe Cesium credit "Street Level: imagery © Mapillary contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0" while the layer is enabled; MapillaryJS's own attribution component inside the viewer.
- MapillaryJS 4.1.2 (MIT) as a dependency; its stylesheet vendored with a header (loaded eagerly so the first image has styled controls). Sprite icons from `mapillary/mapillary_sprite_source` (MIT), fetched on demand and cached.
- Mapillary blurs faces and licence plates before publishing imagery.
- New runtime dependencies: `mapillary-js`, `@anthropic-ai/sdk`, `zod` (the last two server-only, used by the optional planner).

### Not in this PR

Procedural 3D objects for results, a Google 3D map-stack shortcut, portable/resizable rail panels (separate PR: #727), and a voice-UI toggle stay on the showcase fork. A shared PBF decode helper with the traffic layer is noted as a follow-up in `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md`.

### Verified before merge

- `npm run format:check`, `npm run check:boundaries` (new `mapillary-layer` / `mapillary-provider` packages), `npm run build`, `npm run doctor -- --json` clean.
- Unit suite: 4,217 tests, 4,216 passing, 0 failing (1 pre-existing skip), Node 24.19. New tests: provider routes/tiles/sprite guard/query caps/planner/trim (`src/tooling/mapillaryProvider.test.mjs`), source, presentation, markup, query summaries.
- `scripts/qa-mapillary.mjs` (`npm run qa:mapillary`): keyed run 9/9 (rail placement at 1440×900 and 1280×800, coverage + credit, streamed plan, viewer, expanded dialog focus/Esc, close/deselect, no page errors); keyless run 4/4 (collapsed strip, legend, gated empty state naming `MAPILLARY_CLIENT_TOKEN`).
- Browser tracking suite (`npm run test:track`): 89 passed, 0 failed, 1 skipped (run on the fork's main, which is this branch plus #727 and the showcase-only extras).

title: feat(local-aircraft): draw your own ADS-B receiver beside public Flights
body:
**Intent:** draw aircraft from the user's own dump1090 / readsb / tar1090 receiver beside public Flights, in their own colour, as decided on #57. It deliberately leaves Flights untouched: nothing under `src/layers/flights/` changes, and public marks are not hidden where the receiver has the plane (deferred on #57 as "later, if cheap").

Closes #57 · part of #714 · first consumer of the tap contract from #382.

## What changed

**Server route** — `GET /api/local-aircraft?base=host:port` (`server/providers/localAircraft.js`). The browser can't read a receiver directly because it sends no CORS headers, so the address makes a round trip. That round trip is what makes this an SSRF surface, and why the checks run in this order:

1. `GET` only → 405.
2. **Cross-site gate** → 403. Refuses `Sec-Fetch-Site` other than `same-origin`/`none`, and any foreign or opaque `Origin`. Without it, any website open in the user's browser could fire a simple GET here. It couldn't read the answer, but the status codes and timing would still let it map the user's LAN. This is the rule #242 proposes as shared; this route should switch to that helper when #242 lands.
3. Always-on rate limit, 120/min per client, 400 global → 429. It sits after the gate so a hostile page can't spend the user's budget.
4. `parseTapAddress` → 400, **never a fallback host**.

Then it reads the fixed path `/data/aircraft.json`. Redirects are refused, not followed. The 4 s timeout covers the body read as well as the headers, the body is capped at 2 MB, and the response is relayed unmodified with `no-store`. An unreachable receiver gets a generic 502, and neither the response nor the log names the host.

**Model** — `src/layers/localAircraft/model.js` turns one `aircraft.json` snapshot into contacts. It **delegates** per-aircraft parsing to `normalizeAdsbLolAircraftState` instead of writing a second parser, because adsb.lol v2 rows are readsb rows. A test pins both paths to the same answer for the same airframe. The module owns only three things: the envelope, the `rssi`/`messages` fields that normalizer drops, and the heard-vs-drawn split. Positions older than 30 s are dropped, the figure #134 settled on.

**Layer** — My Receiver (ADS-B), `local-aircraft`, in the Movement group after Military:
- Each poll is a level-triggered reconcile keyed by ICAO: surviving contacts are moved in place (same entity, no flicker), new ones added, missing ones removed. A restarted receiver, a lost response or a toggle all converge on the next poll.
- It reads any source with `getSnapshot()`. The receiver tap is the first; #134's browser-USB decoder is meant to be the second, and needs no address.
- An unset or rejected address is guidance (`idle`), a receiver hearing nothing is `empty`, and only a failed read is an `error`.
- Magenta, the colour #134 chose, in a shade (`#ff3ec8`) distinct from the weather radar's `#ff00ff`. Marks use Flights' own distance scale and class sizes, so the same airframe differs only in colour.
- The receiver mark **leads** the public one. That's expected, since Flights renders about one poll behind. It's documented, not corrected.
- The address is set from a row chip and kept in `localStorage`, never in layer-state params: in a share link it would publish a host on the user's network to every recipient.

**Registration** — layer-state token `2` (`enabled-only`), catalog, panel group, its own `./layers/local-aircraft` boundary group and `package.json` export. `src/data/tapAddress.js` had no owning boundary group yet; this is its first browser-side importer, so the groups that now reach it claim it. Three existing tests that pin the exact layer list and count are **updated to include the layer, not loosened**.

**Docs** — `DATA_SOURCES.md` (source row + note), `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md` (section), `CHANGELOG.md`, and `SECURITY.md`. The last one was required: it said every proxy but CCTV "targets fixed upstream hosts", which this route makes false.

## How it was verified

Node 24.21.0, WSL2 Ubuntu, at the pushed head:

- `npm test` → `tests 4781 · fail 0` (+44 new; the Node-24 allocation benchmarks ran too)
- `npm run check:boundaries` → exit 0, 111 groups, including `Checked local-aircraft: 1 exports, 8 owned modules`
- `npm run format:check` → `Checked 1033 source files.`
- `npm run build` → `✓ built in 5.10s`
- `npm run test:track` → **not run.** It needs a Google Maps key, which I don't have here. It exercises flight tracking, which this change doesn't touch.

**Every new test was confirmed to fail on a real defect.** 14 mutations, each reintroducing one bug, each caught by the test written for it. They include falling back to `localhost` on a bad address, following redirects, letting the client choose the path, dropping the signal from the body read, putting the cross-site gate after the limiter, rebuilding entities instead of moving them, and losing the address when storage is blocked. Commit `3c86292` also passes on its own, so the series bisects.

**End to end, with no mocks.** A fake dump1090 serving `aircraft.json`, through the real Vite dev server, into the client source. This run caught a bug the unit tests had missed: HTTP 200 with an empty body. Cause: the docstring in `server/providers/common/http.js` says `readResponseTextCapped` returns `{tooLarge, text}`, but it returns a string (see follow-ups).

**In a browser.** Headless Chrome (the official Puppeteer image under Podman, SwiftShader WebGL) against the same fake receiver: boot → open DATA LAYERS → the row's own toggle → five contacts drawn, zero page or console errors. The fake receiver puts four aircraft on the four cardinal tracks around Austin, and a north-up view shows every nose pointing along its track. This run found two defects the tests couldn't, both fixed in `9714e35`: marks drew at a fraction of Flights' size, and the heard/drawn sentence in the count column wrapped the row into four lines. I have screenshots of the cross and the row and can add them here.

Not verified against a real receiver, only the fake one.

## Notes for reviewers

- **The address is entered through a `prompt()` chip.** Row controls only render chips and lists, not a text input. A proper `host:port` input belongs in the shared panel, since Rayhunter #116 needs the same thing, so I didn't add one to the panel in a one-layer PR. This is the part I'd most like an opinion on.
- The numbers most worth a look: the 2 s poll, 120/min, the 30 s expiry, the 4 s timeout.
- One environment note, in case it looks like a bug: on WSL2 a connection to a closed loopback port hangs instead of being refused, so a missing receiver shows as a `504` after 4 s here. On a normal host it's an immediate `502 Receiver unreachable`. Both paths are tested.

## Out of scope / follow-up

- A shared `host:port` input in row controls, for this layer and Rayhunter #116.
- Hiding the public mark where the receiver has the plane (deferred on #57).
- The stale `readResponseTextCapped` docstring in `server/providers/common/http.js`. It misled me into the empty-body bug, but it's outside this layer.
- Moving the cross-site gate onto #242's shared helper once that lands.

## Delivery readiness

- **Rollback:** revertible as a unit; no migration, no persisted server state.
- **Config:** no environment variables. The layer does nothing until it's switched on and given an address.
- **Exposure:** on the default loopback server only the user reaches the route. Under `HOST=0.0.0.0` other LAN devices can make it read `/data/aircraft.json` from private addresses, which the LAN opt-in note in SECURITY.md now says.
- **Breaking change:** none. One new layer, route and package export.

> 🤖 Claude Code helped

title: fix(weather): upright N. America cloud tiles; lift shells over coarse 3D tiles
body:
Two fixes for satellite clouds.

**N. America clouds on globe basemaps (Esri, Bing, OSM).** Cesium decodes imagery tiles as `ImageBitmap`s that are already flipped, because WebGL ignores `UNPACK_FLIP_Y` for them. The regional infrared transfer redrew each tile onto a canvas, and the canvas upload flipped it again, so every tile drew upside down in its slot. The clouds jumped between zoom levels and left a blank band near the southern edge of the data. Tiles are now drawn upright before the transfer. Radar, lightning, global clouds and the 3D Tiles shell were not affected.

**Terrain showing through the shells on Google 3D Tiles.** From far away, Google's coarse tiles rise tens of kilometres above the ground and hid the shells at 5.8 km. Shells now rise with the camera, 4 m per km of camera height up to 60 km, in 500 m steps. The lift is a uniform scale about the Earth's centre, so the shells keep their order. City-level heights are unchanged.

Verification: zoom sweep from 15,000 km to 1,500 km over Mexico on Esri and Bing labels; Google 3D top-down at 3,000, 8,000 and 18,500 km; unit tests; weather journeys, swap and tracking harnesses.

title: fix(ui): keep panel scroll position through rail layout passes
body:
The right-rail layout pass lifts the Context, CCTV, Weather and Recent Imagery panel scrollers to their natural height to measure them, which clamps their scroll offset to zero. It only restored scrollers tagged `data-rail-scroller`, so a layer that refreshes its Layers-panel row every second snapped the Context panel back to the top while you scrolled.

- Tag every scroller the measuring pass lifts.
- Add `src/ui/railScrollers.test.mjs`, which reads the measuring CSS and fails if a lifted scroller is untagged.

Verified: `npm test` 4,740 pass / 0 fail, `format:check`, `check:boundaries`, `build`. Reproduced before the fix with real wheel input in Chrome (scroll reset every ~1 s); after the fix the panel scrolls to the bottom and stays.

title: feat(sdr): local receivers — browser RTL-SDR, Local ADS-B layer and decoder feeds
body:
Puts what *your own* antenna hears on the globe.

Builds on @samehkhamis's SDR prototype and the initial GEV port by @mazy1998 (#134). The decoder-feed design follows @Lob26's notes on #57. On top of that, this PR adds 1090 MHz and 978 MHz UAT decoder feeds, the Live Flights treatment for local aircraft, dual-channel receiver support, surface-position decoding, and the hardening from five review rounds.

Closes #57.

**Browser SDR.** A Local RTL-SDR card in the Radio panel opens a USB RTL-SDR in desktop Chrome or Edge through WebUSB and decodes in the page: broadcast FM (tune, seek, volume) or 1090 MHz ADS-B. Gain is AUTO or a manual R820T step per mode (ADS-B defaults to 28 dB). Local FM and internet radio never play together. Dual-channel boards such as the Nooelec FlyCatcher pick their 1090 MHz channel automatically.

**Decoder feeds.** The same layer reads the `aircraft.json` from decoders you run — dump1090-fa, readsb or tar1090 (1090 MHz), dump978-fa + skyaware978 (978 MHz UAT) — configured server-side with `LOCAL_RECEIVER_FEEDS`. Addresses are restricted to loopback and private networks by the shared tap address rule from #382; names are resolved, every address checked and the connection pinned. See `docs/LOCAL-RECEIVERS.md`.

**Local ADS-B layer** (`local-adsb`, off by default, never in share links). Aircraft heard by your receivers draw in magenta beside the public Flights layer, with the Flights treatment: class from the ADS-B emitter category and type, per-class silhouettes, 3D models with the 3D toggle, path-derived heading and smooth motion, trails from the positions your antenna actually heard, and a position sanity filter. The click card names the band and input that heard it ("Heard by your receiver · 978 MHz UAT · decoder feed"). Local markers usually lead their public twins because the public Flights layer renders about one poll interval behind for smooth interpolation; both are drawn on purpose.

**Verified**
- `npm test` 4,875 pass / 0 fail; `build`; `format:check`; `check:boundaries`; `test:track` 109/109 against a keyed dev server; clean cold start on a fresh `npm ci`.
- Decoder checked against dump1090-fa on real frames captured over Austin (positions match to 0.000 nm, categories match); on the same 30 s of recorded IQ it decoded 27 DF17/18 frames to dump1090-fa's 20, same aircraft. Surface decoding checked against the published 1090 MHz Riddle vectors.
- Headful on real hardware (Nooelec FlyCatcher, macOS, Chrome): browser SDR connect and reconnect; decoder feeds from dump1090-fa and dump978-fa (first UAT aircraft decoded); keyed Google 3D run with click cards, enrichment (e.g. 145TX → Eurocopter EC145, category A7), 3D models and trails.
- Five independent review rounds; every finding fixed with a regression test that fails before the fix.

Follow-ups are tracked in #714.

title: feat(transit): MBTA route lines, service alerts and stop alerts
body:
Adds MBTA route geometry and service alerts to the Transit layer — keyless, from the same operator and licence as the existing MBTA vehicle feed.

## What it does
- **Route lines.** Every MBTA route in its official colour, drawn as batched ground polylines (rapid transit bold, commuter rail and ferries medium, buses thin/translucent). Geometry is the operator's *typical* pattern per route and direction (V3 `route_patterns`, typicality 1), so diversions and the rail-replacement shuttle catalog are never drawn as permanent routes. Card and docs say detours are not drawn.
- **Disruptions.** Routes with a delay, detour, suspension, shuttle, cancellation or service change in force get magenta dashes (a colour no MBTA line uses). Closed, moved or bypassed stops are ringed magenta markers at the stop instead of outlining whole routes (one closed busway stop otherwise flags 14 bus routes).
- **Cards.** Vehicle cards name the route the way riders do ("Red Line", not "Route Red"; buses keep their number and gain their destinations) and list alerts in force. Clicking a route line or a stop marker opens its own card; one card at a time.
- **Row.** "MBTA 738 · 43 routes disrupted", plus "Bus lines" / "Stop alerts" chips (ordinary layer params) and a legend with counts.

## Server
Two new resources on the existing portable transit service:
- `GET /api/transit/routes/<feedId>` — one V3 request (~2.4 MB decoded → ~410 KB normalized, encoded polylines kept on the wire), 12 h fresh, a week of serve-stale.
- `GET /api/transit/alerts/<feedId>` — `Alerts_enhanced.json` normalized to bounded text (no links passed to the browser), 60 s fresh, 30 min serve-stale; stop positions for stop-level alerts are looked up from V3 `/stops` for the ids MBTA's own alert feed names (never browser-supplied), cached a day, alerts served unplaced if the lookup fails.

Both resolve only for feeds whose registry entry carries the resource, fetch only registered URLs, follow redirects hop by hop on the same https origin, are byte-capped, coalesced, admission-limited and backed off like the vehicle feeds, and set `nosniff`. Keyless V3 allowance is 20 req/min; this uses roughly one catalog request per 12 h plus occasional stop lookups.

## Validation
- `npm test` — 4,903 tests, all pass (on current `main`, 1fc7955) (new: `src/data/transitNetwork.test.mjs`, `src/tooling/transitNetworkService.test.mjs`, layer tests in `src/layers/transit/lifecycle.test.mjs`)
- `npm run format:check`, `npm run check:boundaries`, `npm run build` — green
- `npm run test:track` — 109 passed, 0 failed
- `scripts/qa-transit.mjs` (headless Chrome, SwiftShader software rendering) — the same small set of frame-budget and thermal-preset contrast checks fails on unmodified `main` in this environment (6 named failures on `main`, 5 on this branch, flipping between runs); no check fails only because of this change. It would be worth re-running on real GPU hardware.
- Live against MBTA: 182 routes / 357 shapes, ~135 alerts, ~19 stop markers; real mouse clicks on a route line and a stop marker in headless Chrome open the expected cards; the "Bus lines" chip hides bus lines and their outlines.

title: feat(fires): MODIS in Active Fires and a Fire Perimeters layer
body:
Brings two community fire PRs onto current main, with fixes from review.

**Active Fires adds MODIS** (from #455 by @beneduzi). FIRMS now merges MODIS NRT (Terra + Aqua) with the three VIIRS sources: one more request per 30-minute refresh against the same key.

**Fire Perimeters** (from #684 by @Frankenleg). A keyless layer in Events with current NIFC WFIGS interagency perimeters, coloured by reported containment, with an incident card and a link to the incident's InciWeb page when one matches. Changes from the original PR:
- WFIGS and InciWeb go through `/api/fire-perimeters`: fixed upstreams, capped reads, timeouts, 5-minute cache with stale-on-error, and a per-client limit. The browser no longer calls ArcGIS or InciWeb directly.
- InciWeb retired the publication endpoint the link check used, so links never appeared. The check now reads the origin and update times from the incident page, pinned to InciWeb's host and capped at 2 MiB.
- Refreshes that don't change anything keep the existing geometry; link checks cancel on disable or a new selection.
- Row legend for containment.
- Share token `2` (every letter is in use, #658).

Verification: `npm test` 4942/0, format, boundaries and build clean; `test:track` 109/109, `qa-layer-panel` and `qa-ui-disposal` pass against a keyed dev server; headed Chrome on Google 3D and Esri shows 147 live perimeters, the legend, the incident card and the InciWeb link, with no direct upstream requests from the browser.

Closes #455. Closes #684.

title: Other worlds: Moon and Mars as alternate globes
body:
Several requests ask for objects beyond Earth orbit: Mars rovers (#627), lunar orbiters (#630), Mars orbiters (#631) and solar probes (#632). The satellites layer places Earth-orbiting objects from TLEs, so these don't fit it as-is.

CesiumJS can render other bodies (Moon and Mars ellipsoids and tilesets), but switching the globe touches most layers, the camera and the share-link state. Opening this to see if anyone wants to explore what an "other worlds" mode would take: data sources (e.g. NASA/JPL ephemerides, rover positions), what Cesium provides, and what the rest of the app would need.

Not a near-term priority for the maintainers, but proposals are welcome here.

title: feat(geo): add Cesium-free spatial query primitives
body:
## Summary

Adds a small, reusable, Cesium-free spatial query primitive for point-based geographic data.

The utility is independent of Cesium and any specific entity shape. Callers provide a position accessor, allowing the same spatial logic to be reused across different datasets without coupling it to aircraft, transit, vessels, or other domain-specific objects.

### Included

* great-circle distance in metres using the haversine formulation
* radius queries returning matches nearest-first
* nearest-entity lookup
* deterministic handling of equal-distance results
* finite coordinate and argument validation
* support for both `lon` and `lng`
* invalid entity positions skipped during collection queries
* caller-supplied position accessors receiving the entity and index
* source collections are not mutated

### Current consumer

The shared primitive is also used by `transitFeedsInRange()` in `src/data/transitFeeds.js`.

This keeps the spatial-query implementation independently reusable while replacing the feed-range distance calculation with the shared great-circle primitive and query operation.

### Tests

Coverage includes:

* identical and coincident points
* one-degree latitude calibration
* antipodal points
* dateline crossing
* `{ lon }` / `{ lng }` coordinate compatibility
* zero-radius queries
* inclusive radius boundaries
* nearest-first ordering
* deterministic distance ties
* invalid coordinates
* index-aware position accessors
* invalid entity positions
* empty / no-valid-result inputs
* source-array non-mutation
* invalid query arguments

### Local verification

```text
node --test src/spatialQuery.test.mjs
18 tests
18 passing
0 failures

node --test src/spatialQuery.js
1 test
1 passing

node --check src/spatialQuery.js
passed
```

The full repository dependency installation was not completed locally because `npm ci` did not finish, so the repository-wide test and formatting commands were not used as evidence here. The focused spatial-query suite is fully passing.

### Scope

This change deliberately does not perform the broader distance-formula refactor associated with #274.

The goal is to establish the reusable spatial-query API and demonstrate adoption in one existing consumer while keeping the primitive independent of Cesium and domain-specific data models.

Closes #188

title: feat(weather): global rain radar from RainViewer
body:
Adds a **Global (RainViewer)** option to Rain radar, next to the existing US MRMS radar. It builds on the idea in #713 by @sandivd.

**What you get**
- Region chips on the Rain radar card: `US (NOAA)` (unchanged default) and `Global (RainViewer)`. The choice is kept in share links on the existing `v` token; old links open on US.
- Past 2 hours at 10-minute steps on the shared weather timeline, with RainViewer's Universal Blue legend (10–65 dBZ) and a "Global · where radars exist" coverage label.
- Globe basemaps draw RainViewer's Web Mercator tiles. On Google 3D the shell stitches those tiles in the browser into one image per frame and detail window.

**Proxy**
- No existing check was removed or loosened; all 35 weather proxy tests are unchanged and pass.
- The tile host is pinned to `tilecache.rainviewer.com` (the manifest's `host` is ignored), frame paths are validated, and Web Mercator z/x/y are bounds-checked. `/image` is refused for this product.
- Upstream is limited to 80 tile requests a minute, under RainViewer's 100 per IP. Requests over that wait up to 20 s in a bounded FIFO queue instead of failing.

**Known limits — please look at these when testing**
1. **Zoomed-out views look wetter than they are.** RainViewer's low-zoom tiles spread rain outward. Measured over central Germany on the same frame, rain covers 77% of the area at zoom 2, 50% at zoom 4 and 24% at zoom 6. The Google 3D shell composes continental views from lower zooms than the Esri globe uses at the same height, to stay within the request budget. Raising the shell's tile budget sharpens this but costs about twice the requests.
2. **Cold start can leave a few blank tiles.** The first look at a new area can need more tiles than 100 a minute plus the 20 s queue allows. The gaps fill on later frames and on revisits, since tiles are cached.
3. The free API is past radar only (no nowcast) at zoom ≤ 7, and RainViewer's terms are free for personal or educational use.

**Verification**
- `npm test` 4964/0, format, boundaries and build all clean.
- `qa-weather-journey` 19/19, `qa-weather-swap` 0/26 black frames, `qa-weather-teardown` clean.
- `test:track` 109/109 on the third run. Two earlier runs failed 4 and 1 different frame-timing checks, which moved between runs.
- Headed Chrome on Google 3D and Esri at global, Europe and regional heights, on a warm cache: 163 tile responses with 0 rate-limited and no console errors.

The `DATA_SOURCES.md` row for RainViewer needs owner approval of its wording.

Co-authored with @sandivd (#713).

title: fix(cyclones): accept advisories NHC publishes before their nominal time
body:
The Cyclones layer shows "Cyclone data unavailable" for about half an hour in every NHC advisory cycle.

NHC stamps each advisory with its nominal time (for example 03:00Z) but publishes it early; tonight's 03:00Z advisories were written at 02:34–02:50Z. The status parser rejected any time more than 5 minutes ahead of the server clock, and one rejected storm invalidates the whole feed. So from publication until the nominal time, no storms showed. Four were active when this was found (Fay, Odalys, Polo at 140 kt, Nolo).

The fix accepts advisory and position times up to 90 minutes ahead, with a comment explaining why. Far-future and expired times are still rejected, and the existing test for that is unchanged.

Verification:
- `npm test` 4943/0, format and boundaries clean.
- The live `CurrentStorms.json` captured at 02:53Z, which failed before, now parses all four storms.
- Against a keyed dev server, `/api/cyclones` returns the four storms with current geometry. Headed Chrome on Google 3D shows their tracks, cones, labels and the WEATHER card list, with no page errors.

title: fix: stop using public Overpass by default
body:
Fixes #648. Public Overpass is no longer used by default; nothing hits Overpass unless an operator sets `OVERPASS_UPSTREAMS`.

## What changed

| Area | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|
| Traffic roads | Overpass per camera move | OpenFreeMap vector tiles; TomTom flow tiles with a key (Road source chip: TomTom / OSM / Hybrid, Hybrid default when keyed) |
| Mapped Installations | Overpass, ≤10° views | OpenFreeMap military polygons + bundled worldwide name index (36,466 OSM names, 1.7 MB gzip, lazy); named points at continent zoom |
| ALPR | Overpass | Hourly OSM extract as vector tiles (US/Canada) |
| Cockpit place context | Nominatim reverse | Bundled Natural Earth |
| Voice outlines | Overpass | Bundled countries, states/provinces (Natural Earth) and US counties (Census) |
| Credits | Per-layer OSM lines | One OpenStreetMap credit, shown on the map briefly when an OSM layer first appears |

Also: arrivals never land below ground (from #118, Milan Khanal), keyless terrain retries on 429, configured Overpass gets bounded relation geometry (#667, theGaryLarson), installation names draw through the world overlay, and a unit test now bans new Cesium text labels (three older uses are allowlisted).

## Traffic performance (@samehkhamis — see if you can push this further)

- First dots: 7.6–11 s → ~0.3–0.5 s warm, ~2–3 s first city of a session; revisits make zero requests.
- Coverage = ground footprint of the reticle square (5×5 `pickEllipsoid` samples), so tilted views fill to the horizon. z14 near / z12 far, nearest first; only missing tiles are fetched.
- Tiles stream in and paint per tile; stable dot identities (rebuilds while still: 265 → 0); drivable roads only.
- Heights sampled per vertex against the rendered mesh; off-screen points don't hold the loading state; each road pass has a deadline.
- Where it still lags: new areas fill ~1–1.5 s after the camera stops because fetching waits for settle (320 ms debounce). Prefetching along camera velocity during motion, or decoding MVT in a worker, are the obvious next steps, as long as panning stays smooth.

Journeys we test with (keyed server URL as the argument):
- `scripts/qa-traffic-motion.mjs` — 18 holds across TomTom/OSM/Hybrid; late rebuilds, jumps, settle time.
- `scripts/qa-overpass-offload.mjs --pan` (20 moves, no duplicate tiles), `--tour` (six cities), `--compare`.
- `scripts/qa-traffic-oblique.mjs` — tilted Dubai/Austin/London; compares against a fresh layer toggle.
- `scripts/qa-journey-recorder.mjs` — 24 fps clip + per-frame metrics of a neighborhood → pan → zoom-out journey.
- Also `qa-alpr-journey.mjs`, `qa-military-names.mjs`, `qa-context-arrivals.mjs`, `qa-admin-outlines.mjs`, `npm run test:track`.

## Hosted — main ask

Please check hosted works as well with this. Public tests all pass inside hosted; 3 of 348 private tests fail at this commit:
- Traffic and ALPR sources now take `tileFetchImpl` (public tiles) separately from `fetchImpl` (`/api/*`). `createOverpassAlprSource` is the Overpass implementation again.
- `mobilitySources.test.mjs` (2): hosted's traffic adapter now receives the tile-backed graph. If hosted keeps its own Overpass, implement `traffic.requestRoads` over the scoped `/api/overpass` transport with `normalizeOverpassRoads`.
- `layerSources.test.mjs` (1): expects `/denied/`; the source now throws `Installation context unavailable` with status 403.

## Verification

`npm test` (5,336), format, boundaries, build, `test:track`, and every script above against a keyed server. Zero Overpass/Nominatim requests in every browser run.

title: fix(data): load bundled region packs in the browser; bound region lookups
body:
Region scopes in voice analyst queries were failing in the dev server. The Natural Earth and neighborhood packs were loaded with a JSON-attributed `import()`, which Vite dev answers with a JavaScript module that the browser rejects. Every region scope then fell through to the geocode + admin-boundary lookup, which could take 12–28 s.

- `src/data/bundledJson.js` fetches the pack from a `new URL(..., import.meta.url)` asset in the browser; under Node the caller's attributed import runs.
- When a region is not in the bundled packs, the geocode + admin-boundary fallback answers `region-timeout` after 3 s; the lookup keeps running and fills the cache.
- The production build also emits JS chunks for the Node-only import path (about 2.8 MB in `dist`, never fetched by the browser).

Verified: `npm test`, `format:check`, `check:boundaries`, `build`; `node scripts/qa-voice-routing.mjs --layer behavior` 37 passed, 0 failed (Gulf of Mexico resolves from the bundled pack in 5 ms; before this change it failed).

title: feat(layers): Repeaters — FM and D-STAR amateur radio repeaters around the view
body:
Closes part of #374 — this is the first of the per-layer splits @bilawalsidhu asked for. One layer, one PR: **Repeaters**.

## What this adds

A `ham-repeaters` layer that plots amateur-radio **FM and D-STAR repeaters** around the view. Fly below 1,500 km and it loads what is around you; press **LOAD HERE** in the panel to load at any altitude with your own radius. Markers are coloured by mode, the panel lists them nearest-first, and band (6m / 2m / 1.25m / 70cm / 23cm) and mode chips filter what you see.

Each row shows output and input frequency, the offset, CTCSS tone or the 1750 Hz tone-burst, the D-STAR module, EchoLink / AllStar / IRLP / WIRES node ids, the place, and a muted provenance line.

Voice: *"show me the 70 cm repeaters around Munich"*, *"which 2 metre repeaters are near me"*, *"Relais / Umsetzer um München"*. The tool switches the layer on itself and is explicitly **not** Internet Radio (`control_radio` still owns that).

## It is a directory, not a coverage map

This is the thing the layer says out loud, in the panel, on the marker and in the voice answer: distance is **ground distance from the search centre**, never a reachability claim. Nothing here models terrain, antennas, power or whether a repeater is actually on the air. A status is rendered as the directory last recorded it, not as a live check.

## The adapter seam (#380)

The visual layer (`src/layers/hamRepeaters/`) depends only on a source object:

```js
getRepeaters({ lat, lon, radiusKm, band, kind, limit }, { signal }) -> rows
```

Rows are one provider-neutral schema (`src/sources/hamRepeaters.js`, `REPEATER_ROW_KEYS`), and every row carries `source`, `sourceLabel`, `confidence`, `recordUpdatedAt` and `sourceUrl`. HamRig is the first adapter (`server/providers/ham-repeaters/hamrig.js` behind `/api/ham-repeaters/nearby`).

A **RepeaterBook adapter** (the operator's own approved app token, server-side only, "Data courtesy of RepeaterBook.com") or an **OpenStreetMap adapter** (Overpass on `communication:amateur_radio:repeater=*`, ODbL credit) drops in as another provider module plus a `sourceLabel`, without touching the layer, the panel or the voice tool. No repeater directory is bundled in this repository.

@pbloss001 — this is the seam for your licensed-adapter idea from #380. Happy to take a RepeaterBook or OSM provider module against `REPEATER_ROW_KEYS`, and the per-row provenance display you asked for is already there rather than bolted on later.

## Provenance of the HamRig rows, said plainly

HamRig's **FM table is a historic import** (last refreshed 2026-01, six countries) from RepeaterBook, whose API application HamRig was later **denied** (2026-07-28) and whose current terms forbid mirroring and redistribution. HamRig's owner grants this project use of HamRig's own tables, but that cannot clear the upstream provenance — so:

- FM rows are marked `confidence: unverified` and say so in the UI.
- The former upstream record ids are never relayed.
- `HAM_REPEATERS_HAMRIG_FM=0` drops the FM table entirely and serves D-STAR only.
- `DATA_SOURCES.md` records the whole lineage rather than hiding it.

**D-STAR rows** are HamRig's scrape of dstarinfo.com / ircddb.net (neither publishes a licence) and are marked `reported`, with `statusKnown: false` because the gateway status is whatever the directory last listed.

Deployments that want cleaner provenance disable the HamRig provider and run their own adapter. **Maintainer's call:** if the FM lineage is not acceptable for this repo even with the marking, say so and I will ship D-STAR only and leave FM to a licensed adapter — the switch already exists.

## Not using the DL3EL route

HamRig also holds Thomas DL3EL's relaislisten.darc.de lists behind its **login-only** `/api/repeaters/for-location`. That data was granted to HamRig alone under a per-location, weekly-cached, request-marker usage model, and expressly **not** for bulk lists or third-party repeater sites. This PR never calls that route — there is no code path for it, and GEV holds no HamRig credentials. Using it here would need DL3EL's own permission for GEV and its own credit line; the adapter seam is where that would go.

## Server

`GET /api/ham-repeaters/nearby` is the only path the browser talks to.

- Validates every parameter with its own message (`radiusKm must be <= 500`, `band must be one of all, 6m, 2m, 1.25m, 70cm, 23cm`, …).
- Rounds the search to a 0.1° cell for the cache key, coalesces in-flight requests, keeps 256 cells for 10 minutes and serves a stale cell for up to ten times that when upstream fails.
- Answers `Cache-Control: no-store` with `updatedAt`, `sources`, `partial` and per-feed `errors`.
- Merges the two feeds first-wins by id; **PARTIAL** when only one answers, **STALE** when a cached cell is served after a failure.
- Filters 23cm locally, because the upstream FM table has no such band filter.
- Drops the D-STAR directory's sponsor e-mail and other contact fields server-side; they are never serialised.
- `HAMRIG_BASE_URL` is operator configuration, never user input, and must be https outside loopback.

`HAMRIG_ENABLED=0` makes the route answer 503 with `enabled: false`, and the layer says so instead of erroring.

## No camera polling

`updateInterval: 0` — there is no poll. The layer watches `camera.moveEnd`, debounces 1,500 ms, and only fetches below the 1,500 km height gate; above it the panel reads `Fly below 1500 km or press LOAD HERE`. The radius follows the view span clamped to 15–300 km, and a fetch whose centre and radius are close enough to the last one is skipped, so panning inside a loaded area costs no requests.

## Tests and gates

All gates green on `feat/ham-repeaters` (commit `eef1e49`, rebased onto `ce671ce`):

| Gate | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `npm run format:check` | 1,109 files clean |
| `npm run check:boundaries` | pass |
| `npm test` | 5,092 pass, 0 fail |
| `npm run build` | pass |
| `node scripts/qa-ham-repeaters.mjs --fixtures` | 40 of 41 checks pass |

New tests: `src/sources/hamRepeaters.test.mjs` (rules and both normalisers against captured fixtures), `src/data/hamRepeatersProxy.test.mjs` (routing, the validation table, caching, stale and partial, the env and base-URL hardening), `src/layers/hamRepeaters/index.test.mjs` (lifecycle, the height gate, selection, teardown), `src/ui/hamRepeatersControls.test.mjs` (panel wiring), `src/voice/hamRepeaterActions.test.mjs` (the voice action), plus a credit case and the live gate `scripts/qa-ham-repeaters.mjs`.

**The one QA failure is this machine, not the branch.** The Google 3D Tiles key in the repo answers 403 from here, which the harness counts as a console error. `curl` against the same URL confirms it independently. Everything the script checks about the Repeaters layer passes: the height gate loads nothing and explains itself, LOAD HERE overrides it, dropping below the gate auto-loads, the filters partition the set without refetching, a list row selects its repeater with its provenance line, and the HamRig credit appears in the Data attribution popover.

The proxy was also exercised end to end against the live HamRig routes: real Cologne repeaters with correct band classification, tones and provenance, the validation messages as specified, and no contact field from the D-STAR directory anywhere in the response.

## Configuration

```
HAMRIG_ENABLED=1               # 0 makes the route answer 503 and the layer say so
HAMRIG_BASE_URL=https://hamrig.com
HAM_REPEATERS_HAMRIG_FM=1      # 0 drops the FM table and serves D-STAR only
```

**Share-link token.** This layer takes `4`. `2` went to Fire Perimeters in #737 and `3` to Web Receivers in #279 while this branch was being written, which is exactly what @daikaginza describes in #658: the letters are gone and the digits are going the same way. Happy to take whichever token you want to assign.

Refs #374, #380, #658, #714.

title: AI ASSISTANT INTEGRATION
Provider: PDOK Dutch building and area data
body:
### Problem

National and regional governments publish valuable geospatial data that can enrich the existing global basemaps. PDOK provides keyless Dutch 3D buildings and terrain, high-resolution aerial imagery, cadastral parcels, buildings, addresses and BGT surface information.
Adding every dataset from every country as a permanent top-level map-source button would not scale. The current map-source row would become crowded, provider-specific and difficult to understand.
Users should be able to add relevant regional public data without replacing the global map model or expanding the primary map-source UI indefinitely.

### Proposal

Introduce a scalable pattern for regional public-data providers, using the Netherlands’ PDOK service as the first implementation.
For the first version:
1. Keep the primary map-source row limited to the existing global/general basemaps.
2. Register PDOK as a regional provider available when the view is over the Netherlands.
3. Make PDOK datasets optional layers that can be used over compatible basemaps, including Google Photorealistic 3D:
   - cadastral parcels;
   - BAG buildings and addresses;
   - BGT surface objects.
4. Show useful PDOK metadata when a user selects an object, using the existing anchored map information-card interaction.
5. Close or clear selected-object information when map navigation begins.
6. Add PDOK high-resolution RGB and infrared aerial imagery through the same regional-provider model, rather than permanent top-level buttons.
7. Keep the architecture reusable for future regional providers without adding country-specific logic to the core UI.
PDOK 3D terrain/buildings may require a dedicated scene configuration rather than behaving like an ordinary overlay. Before implementation is split into PRs, maintainer guidance is requested on whether that source should appear in a regional source picker, as a provider preset, or in another existing interaction.
Suggested implementation sequence:
- PR 1: provider registration and PDOK map/imagery integration;
- PR 2: reusable cadastral, BAG and BGT overlays;
- PR 3: selected-object metadata and lifecycle behavior.
Each PR should remain independently reviewable and use the existing map, layer, selection, attribution and share-state contracts.
Data source, license, and attribution
Provider: [PDOK](https://www.pdok.nl/), the Dutch government platform for geospatial datasets.
Candidate datasets include:
- 3D Basisvoorziening;
- aerial RGB and infrared imagery from Beeldmateriaal Nederland;
- BAG buildings and addresses;
- BRK cadastral parcels;
- BGT large-scale topography.
The services are public and keyless. Exact licensing, required attribution and reuse terms will be recorded separately for each included PDOK dataset in DATA_SOURCES.md and the in-app attribution surface. The implementation will fetch live data at runtime and will not redistribute datasets unless their published terms explicitly permit that.

title: feat(build): serve the app under a configurable base path (GEV_BASE_PATH)
body:
## Problem

Deployments that serve the app under a sub-path break in three places: Vite's `base` is hard-coded to `/`, every client `/api/...` fetch is root-absolute, and the provider middlewares mount at `/api/...`, which a browser under a base never reaches.

This is the shape of a real deployment: a self-hosted platform embeds the built app same-origin behind its own login gate at `/gods-eye/` (reverse proxy to the container's `vite preview`). On that path every live-data route silently answered the SPA document — a 200 that looks healthy — so the whole live-data surface was dead behind it.

## Change

- `build/vite.js`: a `base` parameter (default `/`) plus a `__GEV_BASE__` define; the standalone wiring reads `GEV_BASE_PATH` (default `/`).
- `src/services/apiBase.js` (`withBase()`): every root-absolute client API path is prefixed with the runtime base at its call site.
- `server/standalone/base-api-strip.js`: strips the base for `<base>/api/...` before the provider middlewares, leaving documents and assets to Vite.
- Runtime-built asset references (`data-logo-src`, the mic-orbit markup, the logoGaze fallback) resolve against the document instead of the origin root.
- Framing headers stay same-origin-only: `X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN` and `frame-ancestors 'self'` (same-origin embedding allowed, third-party framing not).

## Tests

- `src/services/apiBaseSweep.test.mjs` is the contract: it fails when a client file carries an unwrapped root-absolute `/api/` literal, or a root-absolute asset reference in runtime-built markup or a `data-*` attribute (Vite rewrites only the attributes it knows and CSS `url()`). Two explicitly allowed exceptions document the server-side transit path checks.
- `src/tooling/baseApiStrip.test.mjs` covers the strip: provider routes lose the base, documents and assets keep it, and `/` needs no plugin.

## Verification

- `npm run build` at the default base (assets under `/assets/...`) and under `GEV_BASE_PATH=/gods-eye/` (assets under the base, Cesium included).
- `npm test`: 5036 tests, 0 failures. `npm run test:track`: 109 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped (headless Chromium against the dev server).
- `npm run check:boundaries` and `npm run format:check` green.
- Live in the sub-path deployment: provider routes answer JSON (`/gods-eye/api/cctv/sources`, `…/weather/manifest`, `…/fire-perimeters`), the document keeps `SAMEORIGIN`, and the app renders with no console errors.

`docs/CURRENT-STATE.md` and `CHANGELOG.md` are updated in this PR.

title: fix(data): normalize haversineKm argument order in naturalEarthRegions (#274)
body:
## Problem

`src/data/naturalEarthRegions.js` defined its internal `haversineKm` using `(lon1, lat1, lon2, lat2)` order:

```javascript
function haversineKm(lon1, lat1, lon2, lat2) {
```

Every other `haversineKm` implementation across `src/` (`analystEngine.js`, `transitFeeds.js`, `bikeshare/model.js`, `cctv/model.js`, `voice/gevActions.js`) takes arguments in `(lat1, lon1, lat2, lon2)` order.

Having one file quietly swap the coordinate order under the identical name creates a latent bug landmine (#274) for callers and future refactors.

## Fix

- Reorder `haversineKm` parameters in `src/data/naturalEarthRegions.js` to `(lat1, lon1, lat2, lon2)`.
- Update the single internal callsite in `buildEntries`:
  ```javascript
  bboxDiagonalKm: haversineKm(minLat, minLon, maxLat, maxLon),
  ```
- Export `haversineKm` and add a unit test in `src/data/naturalEarthRegions.test.mjs` verifying standard `(lat, lon)` order calculation.

## Verification

```bash
$ node --test src/data/naturalEarthRegions.test.mjs

...
```

title: Satellites with Alpha-5 catalog numbers collapse onto one `NaN` key and all but the first are dropped
body:
### What happened

The satellites layer handles today's CelesTrak data well. Fed 604 current element sets through `parseTLE` and the real `update()` path (with Cesium stubbed), every satellite got the right five-digit NORAD id, including the 8xxxx analyst block and objects with blank designators; a 1998 epoch pivoted correctly; and every element satellite.js parses came back exactly as printed. The dedupe-by-id and the partial-group handling ran as designed. [tested]

One case breaks identity. The catalog passed 99999 in July 2026, and in a TLE those numbers are written in Alpha-5: a letter A-Z, skipping I and O, stands for 10-33 in the ten-thousands place, so 100000 is `A0000`. satellite.js keeps that field as the string `"A0000"`, and the three places that build the catalog convert it with `Number(satrec.satnum)` (`src/layers/satellites/ingestion.js:111`, `catalog.js:116`, `orbits.js:303`; the same three lines in v0.1.1's `src/data/satellites.js`), which gives `NaN`. The `Set` used to deduplicate and the `Map` used to store treat `NaN` as equal to `NaN`, so the first Alpha-5 satellite is stored under key `NaN` and every later one is skipped as a duplicate. With a 256-satellite file of such numbers, the catalog ends with one entry; with 346, one entry. [tested]

Today a running instance does not see this, because the proxy requests `FORMAT=tle` and CelesTrak omits objects above 99999 from that format, so those satellites (new Starlink shells included) are simply absent from the globe rather than collapsed. The collapse happens on the first Alpha-5 line from any source, and the absence itself may be worth knowing about. [tested against CelesTrak's TLE output for a group with only six-digit objects]

The fix is a small decoder (`noradIdFromSatnum`: a first character A to Z, skipping I and O, stands for 10 to 33 in the ten-thousands place; a five-digit field is unchanged; anything else goes through `Number` as before) used at the three catalog-builder sites, with boundary tests for `A0000`, `Z9999`, the I and O skips and a five-digit field. With it the 256 satellites above get ids 100404 to 100789 and their own catalog entries, and the unit suite passes before and after (5,030 tests then 5,033 with the three added, 0 failed, on Node 26). I am happy to open a pull request with it. [tested]


### Steps to reproduce

Without the corpus, two Alpha-5 element sets through satellite.js and the `Number` plus `Set` path the catalog builders use:

```js
import { twoline2satrec } from 'satellite.js';
const l1 = '1 A0000U 26067CY  26195.90649229  .00004770  00000+0  22159-3 0  9994';
const l2 = '2 A0000  97.4593 154.0970 0005590 270.5113  89.5482 15.20467281 15911';
const seen = new Set();
for (const id of [Number(twoline2satrec(l1, l2).satnum), Number(twoline2satrec(l1.replace('A0000', 'A0001'), l2.replace('A0000', 'A0001')).satnum)]) {
  console.log(id, seen.has(id) ? 'dropped as duplicate' : 'kept'); seen.add(id);   // NaN kept, NaN dropped as duplicate
}
```

With the corpus (https://github.com/hneogy/gp-omm-conformance): drive `src/layers/satellites/ingestion.js` on main with a local TLE file in place of the CelesTrak group and Cesium stubbed; the 256-satellite file `derived/alpha5-tle/alpha5-A-last-30-days-snapshot.tle` leaves one catalog entry, keyed `NaN`. [tested]


### How you installed

Terminal (git clone + npm)

### OS, Node version, browser

macOS 26.7, Node 26.5.0, no browser (the ingestion module was driven headless with Cesium stubbed)

### Version or commit

main ce671ce (2026-09-24); the same three conversion lines are in v0.1.1's src/data/satellites.js

### Output of `npm run doctor`

```text
Not run: no provider is involved. The satellites ingestion module was driven directly by a Node harness with the CelesTrak fetch replaced by a local file, so provider configuration does not enter into it.
```

### Server log and browser console

```text
None: no server or browser was started. The harness prints the catalog after update(); with the 256-satellite Alpha-5 file it holds one entry keyed NaN, and with the decoder in place it holds 256 entries with ids 100404 to 100789.
```
