title: Add Cyber Intelligence Layer
body:
## Summary

This pull request adds a first-class, provider-neutral Cyber Activity layer to God's Eye View.

- **Cloudflare Radar and DShield:** show country-level Radar origin/target aggregates and reported country-pair flows on the globe, with selectable symbols, directional red-to-blue arcs, map popups, and a separate DShield threat summary for non-geographic source IPs and targeted ports.
- **Shodan and GreyNoise:** add optional, operator-triggered IP enrichment. Shodan area searches combine the current map area with an optional query, map up to 100 unique returned devices individually when locations are available, and provide device popups. Missing Shodan coordinates can use cached, approximate IP network geolocation. GreyNoise lookups are on demand.
- **CISA KEV and AlienVault OTX:** add searchable vulnerability intelligence, explicit-CVE Shodan matches, and indicator lookups for IPs, domains, URLs, hashes, and CVEs. These records remain non-geographic.
- **IODA:** add keyless country-scoped connectivity events with country reference markers and map popups.
- Add Cyber panel/legend interactions, provider controls and attribution, and document sources, limitations, and the focused browser QA gate.

Cyber is off by default. Provider credentials are managed through the existing Provider Settings flow and remain server-side. Providers fail independently. The map avoids invented geography: Radar markers represent country aggregates, IP-derived locations are approximate network locations, KEV records are not mapped, and IODA markers indicate country scope rather than outage location or cause.

title: feat(layers): World News — place-tagged headlines on the globe, and news for the view in focus
body: ## What this adds An optional, bring-your-own-key **World News** layer: the newest place-tagged headlines from the World News API, pinned at the place each headline names and coloured by the provider's tone score. This is the focused resubmission you invited in #317 — "the news layer alone, against `server/providers`". Nothing is bundled or redistributed: headlines are fetched at runtime through a server-side proxy, and `DATA_SOURCES.md` carries the licence, the one-hour caching limit and the required backlink. Keyless installs are unaffected: the proxy answers `503 {error:'no_key'}`, the row reads KEY REQUIRED, and no upstream request is ever made. **Disclosure:** I run World News API, the provider this layer uses. The layer is opt-in and bring-your-own-key like the other keyed feeds, and the screenshots below are hosted on its site. ## Screenshots Captured on this branch against the live provider. ![The worldwide feed over Europe](https://worldnewsapi.com/img/gods-eye-view/01-worldwide-feed.jpg) *The worldwide feed over Europe: one pin per place a headline names, coloured by tone (rose negative, indigo neutral, seafoam positive), with a story count where a place carries more than one (Cork · 2).* ![A London pin and its readout card after NEWS IN VIEW](https://worldnewsapi.com/img/gods-eye-view/02-story-card.jpg) *London after NEWS IN VIEW. The pin holds 20 stories; clicking it again steps to the next one, here 9/20. Clicking the card opens the article at the publisher.* *The layer row after two NEWS IN VIEW circles (London, Paris) on top of the worldwide feed: 107 headlines, every chip, and the tone legend. LOAD MORE is off because the refresh now follows a view, and a view is a single page.* ### Server — `server/providers/world-news.js` - `/api/world-news`, `/api/world-news/more`, `/api/world-news/status`. The key stays server-side in the `x-api-key` header; the browser polls same-origin. - Only contract fields reach the browser: title, link, domain, publish time, tone, category, language, source country and the coordinates of the place the headline names. No article text, summaries, authors, or person/organization entities. Publisher thumbnail URLs are opt-in (`WORLD_NEWS_THUMBNAILS`) and are links the browser resolves — this server never fetches or re-serves them. - 30-minute TTL with a hard 60-minute retention cap, because the provider's terms allow caching user-requested data for at most an hour. A batch older than that is deleted rather than served stale. - A persistent UTC-day point governor (`WORLD_NEWS_DAILY_POINT_BUDGET`) counted from the provider's `X-API-Quota-Request` header, or from the documented estimate when a response carries none. 402/429/401 surface as distinct, named row states rather than a generic failure. ### Viewport fetching — "NEWS IN VIEW" `region=view&lat&lon&radius` fetches one page filtered to the circle the camera frames, cached under its own key so the global feed is untouched. Measured against the live provider before building on it: - `location-filter` is hard-capped at 100 km (500 returns `400 "Distance must be between 1 and 100 kilometers"`). A wider view therefore resolves to the global band rather than a clamped circle that would not cover what the operator is looking at. - Points are charged on results **returned**, not requested: 25 requested over a sparse region returned 1 and cost 1.11, while a full page cost 3.75. A generous region page is cheap exactly where news is thin. - The provider **ignores** unknown parameters and answers 200 with the whole 50,163-article global feed, so a malformed region is rejected with `400 {error:'bad_region'}` and never falls back to global — which would otherwise be cached and shown as regional news. A region batch pins each headline on the location entity that **matched** the circle, reporting `placeFoundIn: 'content'` when the title did not name it. Insisting on a title place put 13 of 14 pins outside the circle that had matched them (a headline titled "Russia" geocodes to the country centroid in Siberia, 3,601 km away). After the change, measured on the live endpoint: 25 of 25 pins inside a 50 km Moscow circle. The global feed stays title-only, so a passing mention still cannot drag a story to a city it is not about. **Syndicated copies collapse into one story.** The provider gives every outlet's copy its own id, so de-duplicating by id alone left them all on the map: across the worldwide feed and two views on 2026-09-24, 113 articles held 4 stories carried 10 times — one Australian feature three times on the London pin, and a restaurant review three times at Kyiv. Copies are matched on the normalized headline *at the same place* after the batches merge (a copy often arrives in a different fetch from the one it duplicates), ignoring case, punctuation, typographic quotes and HTML entities. The earliest copy represents the story and the card names the rest ("+2 outlets"). Headlines under four words, and identical headlines in different places, are left alone. Measured after the change: 107 stories, and the London pin went from 22 to 20. **Known limitation: a pin says where a story matched, not what it is about.** The provider matches an article by *any* location entity, including a single mention in the body, so of the 20 stories on the London pin only a few are clearly about London — the council-tax story in the screenshot is one. Others are UN General Assembly coverage and a Nigerian governor on UK fuel prices. The records carry no mention-strength signal to rank by (`placeMentions` is zero for every content match). Title matching has misses of its own: the Kyiv pin in the worldwide feed is a restaurant review of chicken Kyiv. Preferring articles whose title names the place would be a natural follow-up; this PR ships the behaviour as measured. ### Browser layer — `src/layers/worldNews/` Headlines aggregate per place, pins size by story count and colour by tone band. Fetches **add** to the map — asking about a second city keeps the first, and GLOBAL FEED joins the worldwide feed to whatever circles are pinned. Only CLEAR PINS removes anything; batches otherwise age out under the same one-hour window the proxy enforces, de-duplicated by article id and with syndicated copies collapsed (above). The ten-minute refresh re-asks for the last feed fetched and does **not** follow the camera, so a drifting view cannot spend budget nobody asked to spend. Clicking an already-selected pin steps to the next story there, since the card counts "1/8 stories here" directly under the cursor. Row chips: OPEN ARTICLE, LOAD MORE, NEWS IN VIEW, GLOBAL FEED, CLEAR PINS, and PREV/NEXT STORY while a multi-story place is selected. ## Registration `WORLD_NEWS_API_KEY` across the key registries and setup doctor, share token `3` (`y` went to Cyclones while this was in progress, so it follows your digit sequence after Recent Imagery `1` and Fire Perimeters `2`), voice aliases, the layer catalog and credits, `scripts/format-scope.json` and `scripts/package-boundaries.json`. ## Docs `CHANGELOG.md`, `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md`, `DATA_SOURCES.md` (licence, attribution, and exactly what leaves the browser), and `.env.example` for every new setting. ## Verification Run on this branch, rebased onto `main` at ce671ce (the 30 commits merged since then merge with it cleanly): | gate | result | | --- | --- | | `npm run build` | green | | `npm test` | green — 5124 pass, 0 fail | | `npm run format:check` / `npm run check:boundaries` | green | | `npm run test:track` | green — 109 passed, 0 failed | | `scripts/qa-layer-panel.mjs` (the feature gate for the layer row) | green — 11 passed | Beyond the gates, the chips were exercised in a real browser against the live provider: two NEWS IN VIEW circles and the worldwide feed held together on the map (64 → 74 → 95 headlines, "from the worldwide feed and 2 views"), GLOBAL FEED merged without removing a circle, and CLEAR PINS emptied the map and disabled itself. Local Node is 22.23.x rather than the required 24.14/26, which skips 2 allocation-budget microbenchmarks in the unit suite. Worth a run on a correctly provisioned environment before merge. Happy to split this into provider / layer / viewport-fetching PRs if that reviews more easily.

title: feat(alerts): add CAP alert ingestion
body:
## What is CAP?

CAP (Common Alerting Protocol) is an open XML standard from OASIS for exchanging emergency alerts between different systems.

It provides a common structure for warnings from weather services, civil-defense agencies, disaster-response organizations and other authorities. A single CAP message can contain the event type, severity, urgency, certainty, affected areas, descriptions, instructions, validity periods and links to related updates or cancellations.

Because the format is standardized, the same alert can be consumed by multiple channels, without each system requiring a custom parser for every provider.

CAP also supports the lifecycle of an alert:
- Alert creates a new warning.
- Update changes an existing warning.
- Cancel withdraws a previous warning.

## Summary
- add secure CAP 1.2 XML parsing and alert lifecycle state
- add server-side `/api/cap` ingestion with bounded CAP/RSS/Atom sources
- catalog requested regional and public alert feeds with opt-in controls and attribution
- register the CAP provider in development and built-preview servers

## Data path

```text
registered CAP/RSS/Atom sources
        │
        ▼
server/providers/cap.js
  fetch → size/timeout/redirect checks
        │
        ├── direct CAP XML
        └── RSS/Atom → whitelisted CAP links
        ▼
src/data/cap.js
  secure CAP parsing and normalization
        ▼
GET /api/cap
```

## Sources

Includes the requested public sources across Brazil, Latin America, North America, Europe and Oceania. Direct CAP and confirmed RSS/Atom feeds are enabled by default. Uncertain entries are opt-in through `CAP_OPT_IN_SOURCES`; IFRC, WMO/SWIC and KDE remain disabled until a direct feed contract is confirmed.

## Safety

- DTD/external entity, HTML and malformed XML rejection
- bounded response size, document count, concurrency and timeout
- redirects rejected
- RSS/Atom links restricted to registered host/path
- arbitrary XML links and GeoJSON rejected
- CAP `Alert`, `Update`, `Cancel`, expiry and references supported

## Verification

- `node --test src/data/cap.test.mjs src/tooling/previewServing.test.mjs` — 17 passing
- `npm run check:boundaries` — passed
- `npm run format:check` — passed
- `npm run build` — passed

## Limitations

- No dedicated visual alert layer is included; alerts are exposed through `/api/cap`.
- Live feed availability and contents can change independently of the application.
- Attribution and redistribution terms remain those of each publisher.
- CAP lifecycle state is in-memory and is not persisted across process restarts.

title: feat(layers): discover user layers without editing tracked files
body:
Closes #138. Addresses the structural half of #658.

## Problem

Adding a layer from outside the project means editing two vendored files — a registry entry in `src/data/layerState.js` and a registration in the catalog. Two small edits, but in files that change often: every upstream sync has to re-apply them, and anyone who wants to *try* a third-party layer has to hand-patch a checkout first. #138 described exactly this and was closed only because it was filed against the wrong repository, not on merit.

**This got materially worse while this PR was being prepared.** When it was first written `main` had four free letters (`k l o y`). One day later, after #617, #382 and #716 merged, the registry is at 27 layers and **every one of the 26 letters is taken** — and #716 had to fall back to the digit `1`, the first digit token in the project. A layer added from outside now has nothing to take that will not be taken from under it.

There is a second, sharper problem. Every built-in layer owns a one-character share token (`^[a-z0-9]$`) — 36 slots for the whole project. #658 inventoried the open queue and found **34 PRs proposing 55 new layers competing for five free letters**. A locally added layer that takes one collides with whatever upstream assigns next, and the author only finds out on their next rebase.

## What this adds

A module dropped in `src/userLayers/` as `<name>.layer.js` is discovered at build time and registered automatically:

```js
export default {
  id: 'my-thing',
  label: 'My Thing',
  createLayer: () => ({ id: 'my-thing', name: 'My Thing', icon: '*', enable, disable, update }),
};
```

`.gitignore` covers `src/userLayers/*.layer.js`, so local layers never appear in a diff or a pull request, and an upstream sync cannot conflict with them. The directory ships with a README, a copyable example, and no layers — which is exactly the state CI sees.

Discovery is build-time rather than runtime because the bundler has to see the specifiers; a runtime `import(someString)` would be neither bundled nor allowed by the app's CSP. This is the shape #138 proposed, via `import.meta.glob` rather than a virtual module and an env var, which avoids adding a build plugin.

## User layers spend no share token

This is the part that closes #658's structural half. Rather than competing for a letter, user layers are addressed **by id in their own `ul` field**:

```
?v=2&l=c.t&ul=my-thing.my-other-thing
```

Nothing here consumes the token namespace, so upstream can keep assigning letters freely and a local layer can never collide. Capped at 16 layers / 256 characters.

This PR is itself the evidence: it survived the registry growing from 21 layers to 27 and the letter space going from four free to zero, with no change to its own share-link behaviour and no conflict in `layerState.js` on rebase.

**One deliberate asymmetry:** an unknown id in `ul` is *skipped*, while an unknown token in `l` still fails the whole payload closed. An unknown token means a corrupt or future link; an unknown user-layer id just means the sender's install has different local layers, and their built-in selections should still restore. `src/data/userLayerState.test.mjs` pins both halves, including a guard that the leniency does not leak across to `l`.

Local storage is id-keyed already, so persistence needed nothing.

## Notes for review

- **The registry lives in `layerState.js` rather than a sibling module on purpose.** Eight package boundaries already own that file, so a new sibling would have to be declared in all eight — churn on a file the PR queue already contends over. Inlining it makes this change zero boundary edits for the feature itself; the only `package-boundaries.json` edit is declaring the loader for the two boundaries that own `constructCatalog.js`.
- **The pinned `REGISTERED_LAYER_IDS.length` tripwire is untouched.** #658 makes the case that it is deliberate and worth its conflicts, and this change does not add built-in layers, so the count does not move.
- Layers are sorted by id before registration so discovery order cannot leak into the encoded link — the same selection always produces the same URL.
- Panel visibility defaults to on for user layers (explicit `false` honoured). `layerPanel` skips rows whose `showInTogglePanel` is falsy; a layer that registers correctly and then silently never appears is a miserable first experience.
- Registration throws at startup on a bad descriptor rather than dropping it quietly, for the same reason.
- User layers land under the panel's trailing "Other layers" heading, since `PANEL_ORDER` names only built-in ids.

`docs/USER-LAYERS.md` documents the descriptor and layer contracts, share-link behaviour, in-app management, live-data-source guidance (including that a new third-party upstream still needs a proxy in `vite.config.js`, which is tracked — the honest boundary of this feature), and a troubleshooting table.

## Validation

- `npm run format:check` — clean
- `npm run check:boundaries` — clean
- `npm test` — **4769 tests, 4768 pass, 0 fail, 1 skipped** (32 new), rebased onto `082074a`
- `npm run build` — clean
- `npm run test:track` — **109 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped**
- **Feature gate: `scripts/qa-application.mjs`** — both checks PASS (startup and data registration, terminal teardown). Chosen because this changes how the catalog is assembled at startup.
- **Verified on a physical iPad** against a live deployment carrying two real user layers: both appear in the layer panel, enable, and are interactive.
- Real-browser boot of a running app **with two local layers actually present**: 18 layers registered including both, no page errors, normal startup. `npm run build` confirmed to bundle gitignored layers rather than merely compile.

> A user layer contributes an `enabled-only` serialization disposition, which the catalog pairs with its instance and `finalizeRegistrations` seals against. Registering in the state codec alone is not enough — startup fails with `Layer serialization registry mismatch`. `src/app/userLayerCatalog.test.mjs` pins both directions of that pairing, and the empty case, because the shipped loader has no layers and every other gate therefore exercises only that path.

> **Note on `scripts/qa-layer-panel.mjs`:** it times out waiting for `window.__godsEyeView` in my environment. I ran it against pristine `main` as a control and it fails identically there, so it is an environment issue on my side, not a regression from this change.

title: feat(share): allow two-character layer share tokens
body:
Addresses the capacity question deferred in #658.

## Problem

The built-in layer registry now has 28 layers. Every one of the 26 letters is
taken, leaving only the ten digits in the one-character share-token namespace.
#658 called out this exact limit, deferred the question of widening tokens, and
was never followed by the promised capacity change. The remaining slots postpone
exhaustion; they do not remove it.

## Fix

Allow built-in layer tokens to contain one or two lowercase alphanumeric
characters instead of exactly one. This changes only the validator regex. The
codec already splits the `l` field on `.` and resolves each complete piece through
a token map, so token width was never load-bearing in the encode/decode format.

All published links keep decoding and retain the same meaning, so there is no
share-state version bump. One- and two-character tokens can coexist in the same
registry.

The enabled-layer payload cap moves from 64 to 256 characters at the same time.
At two characters per token, `N` enabled layers encode as `3N-1` characters; the
old cap would fail before the widened namespace was useful. Past the cap the
decoder returns `null`, and restoration silently drops the whole layer payload —
it does not salvage a prefix or surface an error. The new bound clears about 85
two-character tokens while remaining deliberately finite.

This fixes **capacity**, not **contention**. Built-in additions still edit the
central registry and can conflict with other queued layer work. That remains open.

## Validation

- `npm run format:check` — clean
- `npm run check:boundaries` — clean
- `npm test` — **5074 tests, 5073 pass, 0 fail, 1 skipped**
- `npm run build` — clean
- `npm run test:track` — **109 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped**
- **Feature gate: `scripts/qa-application.mjs`** — both checks PASS (startup and
  data registration; terminal teardown without late browser errors). Chosen
  because share-state restoration runs during application startup.

`src/data/layerTokenWidth.test.mjs` (9 tests) pins acceptance of mixed one- and
two-character tokens, rejection beyond two characters, unchanged duplicate and
character validation, every shipped token against the widened grammar, an
all-layers-enabled link inside the raised cap, and fail-closed behaviour above
it.

The compatibility claim was checked directly rather than argued: a legacy

change, and a mixed-width link (`v=2&l=c.1.aa`) round-trips correctly on a scratch
registry entry. An all-layers-enabled link is 55 characters against the new
256 cap.

title: fix(dev): stop the dev server watching .gev-cache and .gev-logs
body:
Disk-cached providers write a file per response into `.gev-cache`, and the voice debug log appends to `.gev-logs`. Vite's dev watcher had both directories in scope; chokidar's stat calls hold the libuv threads that `getaddrinfo` needs, so each cold upstream fetch queued behind a DNS lookup.

- `server/standalone/unwatched-cache.js`: a config-only plugin (`apply: 'serve'`) adding `**/.gev-cache/**` and `**/.gev-logs/**` to `server.watch.ignored`. Vite prepends its own defaults, so nothing else changes.
- `server/standalone/vite.config.js`: registered after `api-not-found`.

Ten cold tiles through the dev server, TomTom traffic (`/api/tomtom/flow/{z}/{x}/{y}.pbf`, z=12, adjacent tiles over New York City), Windows 11, Node v24.14.0:

| | tile times (s) |
|---|---|
| watched | 0.272, 0.068, 0.074, 0.074, 0.077, 0.069, 0.082, 0.089, 0.086, 0.085 |
| not watched | 0.304, 0.075, 0.066, 0.068, 0.065, 0.063, 0.065, 0.067, 0.087, 0.082 |

No measurable difference on this checkout: both runs land in the same ~0.06-0.3 s band (first tile in each run a little higher, likely connection warm-up, not the watcher). The 3-9 s stall the 2026-09 Xweather-branch measurement recorded did not reproduce here. Plausible reason: that measurement's contention came from a specific interaction between chokidar's stat calls and the platform DNS-thread pool under a workload this checkout doesn't currently reproduce (different OS scheduling / concurrent write volume / antivirus-scanned filesystem, etc.) — the mechanism described in the code comment (chokidar watching a directory the app writes into, holding libuv threads) is real and worth guarding against regardless of whether it's currently costing this checkout anything measurable. Recorded as measured on this checkout, not reused from the Xweather-branch figures.

`docs/CURRENT-STATE.md` is not touched — this is dev tooling only (the watcher config), not a runtime behaviour change to the app itself.

Not in this PR: moving the `.gev-cache` name into one shared helper and migrating the eight providers that spell it out, so a future provider cannot cache outside the ignored directory. Happy to send it separately if you want the guard.

title: build: replace vite-plugin-cesium with an in-repo Cesium plugin
body:
`vite-plugin-cesium` is unmaintained (last release 1.2.23) and pulls a nested `rollup@2.80.0` and the deprecated `sourcemap-codec@1.4.8`. `build/cesium.js` replaces it with the same three jobs: serve Cesium's unminified build in development, externalise `cesium` and load the prebuilt global in builds, and copy `Assets`, `ThirdParty`, `Workers` and `Widgets` into the output.

- `dist/` is byte-identical before and after (SHA-256 over sorted paths and contents: `b27966df37147ca8ca5afec366ced12edd019f46427dd5fb4927c09ed895a004`, both runs).
- `package.json`: `vite-plugin-cesium` removed, `rollup-plugin-external-globals@^0.13.0` added (the plugin already depended on an older, nested `0.6.1` copy of it); 35 packages removed from the lockfile by `npm uninstall vite-plugin-cesium`, 7 added back by `npm install -D rollup-plugin-external-globals@^0.13.0` (net 28 fewer packages).
- Behaviour differences, all stricter: a failed asset copy fails the build instead of `console.error`; `outDir` comes from `configResolved`; the dev middleware serves GET/HEAD files only and rejects traversal, NUL and bad percent-encoding (tests in `src/tooling/cesiumAssets.test.mjs`).
- `docs/CODE-BOUNDARIES.md` and `scripts/package-boundaries.json` (`vite-build`) updated. No runtime change, so no CHANGELOG / CURRENT-STATE entry.

One disclosed note: `GET /cesium/../package.json` returns HTTP 200 against the dev server, but this is Vite's own project-root static file server answering `/package.json` (identical behaviour with or without this plugin — Vite serves the whole project directory by default in dev, gated only by `server.fs.deny`). It is not traversal into the Cesium plugin's own directory: `resolveAssetPath` folds every traversal, `%2e%2e`, double-encoded and NUL payload tested in `cesiumAssets.test.mjs` back inside the Cesium build root before this plugin's middleware ever calls `next()`, and a request that Vite's own `fs.deny` blocks (e.g. `/cesium/../.env`) still correctly 403s.

title: feat(weather): add Xweather as an optional keyed radar and lightning source
body:
With `XWEATHER_CLIENT_ID` and `XWEATHER_CLIENT_SECRET` set, the Rain radar and Lightning cards get a SOURCE setting: `NOAA` (the default, keyless) or `Global (Xweather)`. The Xweather choice draws Vaisala Xweather `radar-global` and `lightning-flash` through the existing weather renderer. On globe map sources it drapes as geographic tiles; on Google 3D it uses the #617 shells (one whole-extent image plus a detail window). A new `/api/xweather` proxy does the work: it lists frames through Xweather's time redirect (no map units), fetches Web Mercator tiles, reprojects them to the geographic grid the renderer reads, and counts each billed tile against the free month. The card shows that count as a line. Without a key nothing changes: SOURCE stays hidden, and a share link that asks for Xweather falls back to NOAA.

- `server/providers/xweather.js`: the `/api/xweather` plugin. `/status` → `{hasKey, month, used, allowance, over, upstreamError}`. `/manifest?product=`. `/tile?product&time&z&x&y` serves geographic z ≤ 6 for the globe. `/image?product&time[&size][&bbox]` serves whole-extent images and detail windows for the shells. Validation is the same as `/api/weather`. Without a key it makes no upstream call: `/tile` and `/image` answer 503 `no_key`.
- `server/providers/xweather/png.js`: a small `node:zlib` PNG decoder and encoder for the subset Xweather serves (RGBA radar; indexed 1/4/8-bit lightning with `tRNS`). Compositions use `encodePngAsync`, which deflates on the thread pool; its bytes equal `encodePng`'s. No new dependency; `sharp` is not used.
- `server/providers/xweather/mercator.js`: Mercator tile ranges, zoom choice under a tile cap, and bilinear reprojection to equirectangular RGBA, with each column's source index and fraction computed once (a test checks it byte for byte against the per-pixel version).
- `server/providers/xweather/frames.js`: resolves `current` or a UTC `YYYYMMDDhhmmss` stamp through the 302 to the canonical `{valid}_{run}.png`, then walks back to a list of up to 13 frames. Each step asks for 1.5 × the product's cadence before the previous frame (3 min for radar, 7.5 min for lightning; `cadenceMs` on each product), which takes the previous frame while frames are ~0.75–1.5 × the cadence apart; a single missing frame makes the walk skip the one beyond it. A lookup that is not earlier (a gap) is retried once twice as far back, so a frame costs at most two lookups. Lookups cost no map units; whether they count toward the account's billing-period allowance is unknown. So only a cold start walks the whole list (13–14 lookups): a refresh passes the previous list as `known`, walks back only until it meets a frame it already lists, and merges, so one new frame costs two lookups and none costs one.
- Refreshes are single-flight per product and belong to no client. A stale list keeps serving while one runs (stale-while-revalidate): `/manifest` returns it at once, and a `/tile` or `/image` at a time it already names never waits, cache hits included. Only a cold start, a list older than an hour, or an unknown time waits for the walk. Before this, every refresh (radar 2 min, lightning 5 min) re-walked 13–14 lookups and held every tile request behind it for 2–4 s. Because `/manifest` no longer waits for a refresh, an idle card sees each new frame up to one poll late — about 2 min for radar and about 10 min for lightning.
- `server/providers/xweather/budget.js`: counts `x-cost-tokens` per UTC month in `.gev-cache/xweather/budget.json`. Flushes are serialized and merged with the file, so two processes sharing it add up, except that two flushes overlapping exactly can lose one delta (read-modify-write without a lock). It warns and never blocks.
- `server/providers/xweather/limit.js`: `makeUnitLimiter`, the `makeRateLimiter` shape with weighted admissions. A composition that misses the output cache is charged the source tiles it would fetch that are not already decoded (a request joining one in flight is charged too, erring towards refusal).
- `server/providers/xweather/gate.js`: single-flight upstream work with a concurrency cap (8), a queue limit (96) and a deadline (12 s). **This is a near-copy of `weather.js`'s `pump()`/`shared()`**. I kept it separate rather than refactoring your provider in a feature PR; happy to consolidate both into one helper here or as a follow-up.
- A second gate for compositions, an addition: at most 4 run at once, each with ≤ 8 source tiles in flight. Without it, a 192-tile image would overflow the 96-entry upstream queue, and one composition would hold the slots its own tiles need.
- `server/providers/local.js`: registers `xweatherProxy()` after `weatherProxy()`.
- `src/layers/weather/source.js`, `index.js`, `rendering.js`, `shellRendering.js`: the `xweather-radar` / `xweather-lightning` products, a per-product API base, `getXweatherStatus()`, the SOURCE chips, per-product copy, the budget line, and the shell heights (same as NOAA: radar 6.2 km, lightning 6.6 km).
- `src/data/layerState.js`: share option `s` (`n` NOAA, omitted by default / `x` Xweather) on the existing radar (`v`) and lightning (`l`) tokens. It is an option code inside existing tokens, not a new layer token, so #658 is not affected.
- `src/data/tileBudget.js`: adds `utcMonthKey`.
- `src/data/dataCredits.js`: a dynamic "Powered by Vaisala Xweather" credit linked to https://www.xweather.com/, as Xweather's attribution guide asks. It is registered once an Xweather frame is shown, like TomTom.
- `src/keySetupCore.mjs` and the env ladder: an `XWEATHER` Provider Settings entry. `npm run doctor` prints a `Weather:` line.
- Docs: `DATA_SOURCES.md`, `.env.example`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md`, `docs/KNOWN-ISSUES.md`, the `README.md` keys tables, `SECURITY.md`.

Stacked on the tile-budget refactor PR #762, `refactor/tile-budget`, which moves `utcDayKey` / `normalizeBudget` / `isOverBudget` into `src/data/tileBudget.js`. Until that merges, this diff includes that commit.

## Findings

- **Mercator only.** Xweather serves Web Mercator tiles, with no EPSG:4326 option and no WMS. Static maps are Mercator too and cannot crop to an exact bbox. The proxy stitches and reprojects, and coverage ends at ±85.05°. Polar geographic tiles get a transparent PNG with no upstream call.
- **The time lookup costs no map units.** Both `current` and an absolute stamp answer `302` to the canonical frame with `x-cost-tokens: 0`. Only the canonical `200` is billed (`x-cost-tokens: 1`, `Cache-Control: public,max-age=259200`). Whether lookups count toward the account's billing-period allowance is unknown, which is why a refresh makes only one or two.
- **Absolute stamps resolve forward, not back** (measured 2026-09-25). A stamp resolves to the first frame at or after it: `051100 → 051239`, `045959 → 050039`, `052237 → 052238`; `lightning-flash` the same (`052459 → 052500`). I first assumed a snap down, and the first walk ("one second before each frame") got the same frame back and stopped, so every manifest had one time. The walk now steps back 1.5 × the product's cadence per frame (see `frames.js` above). Its tests use ceiling fakes built from these measured, irregular times, including a 6 min gap; a real-key re-check awaits the allowance resetting.
- **Frame times are irregular** (`05:10:40`, `05:12:39`, `05:20:39`, `05:22:38`), so a fixed grid would not give exact observation times.
- **Upstream PNGs:** `radar-global` is 8-bit RGBA (colour type 6). `lightning-flash` is indexed (colour type 3) at 1, 4 and 8 bits, with `PLTE` + `tRNS`. All are non-interlaced.
- **Measured costs** (units = billed 256² tiles):
  - Whole-extent frame: 64 (zoom 3).
  - Google 3D detail windows, capped at 192: radar at 3,000 km 128, 800 km 120, 250 km 108. At 80 km the 250 km window was reused (0). Lightning at 3,000 km and 250 km: 180 each.
  - A full radar descent (3,000 → 80 km) was 484 including two whole-extent frames. Before the cap, one descent was ~1,000 per product.
  - Globe: 57 units at 8,000 km and 54 at 800 km. Each output tile read 2–3 Mercator tiles (cap 9).
- **Opening a globe share link also fetches one whole-extent `/image` (64 units)** before the tiles. It looks like a shell is staged on the initial photoreal host before `map=esri-imagery` applies. NOAA pays the same, but for free.
- **A free-plan account that exhausts its billing-period allowance gets refused, not just warned.** After ~1,370 units in one session (plus the account's other use), Xweather answered `403 authorization_error`: first "Invalid client credentials" for a few minutes, then "This client does not have access to the Aeris Maps Platform: Maximum number of daily accesses reached." That wording is Xweather's 403 body — Xweather documents only per-minute and per-billing-period limits, nothing separately keyed to the day. The proxy counts monthly units only and cannot predict this cutoff; Xweather's pricing page states no number. While it lasts, the card shows `Xweather refused the request · see Provider Settings`. Past the free 15,000 the card only warns, not blocks, so an account on a paid Xweather plan keeps working — `XWEATHER_MONTHLY_FREE_UNITS` only moves that warning threshold. The docs now say so (`DATA_SOURCES.md`, `KNOWN-ISSUES.md`, `CURRENT-STATE.md`, `README.md`, `SECURITY.md`).

## Google 3D and globe

Screenshots (attached):

- `s3-globe-8000km.png`, `s3-globe-800km.png`: globe (Esri imagery), radar drapes, no seams.
- `s3-globe-250km.png`: globe magnified past level 6; faint one-pixel lines at tile edges (noted in `KNOWN-ISSUES.md`).
- `s3-colour-proxy-z5-12-13.png` next to `s3-colour-direct-z6-12-28.png` / `-29.png`: proxy output against Xweather's own tiles for the same frame.
- `s4-radar-3000km.png`, `s4-radar-800km.png`, `s4-radar-250km.png`, `s4-radar-80km.png`: shells on Google 3D, sharpness steady.
- `s4-lightning-3000km.png`: flashes as separate symbols.
- `s6b-s6-40s-after-restart.png`: `Xweather key removed · showing NOAA` after the key was removed live.
- `s7-over-allowance.png`: the past-allowance budget line.

- **Google 3D:** sharpness stays steady from 3,000 to 80 km. The detail window covered the whole view at every altitude I shot, so the known window/whole-extent seam was not in frame. Lightning flashes at 3,000 km stay separate dots. I have no close-up of lightning glyphs this time: at 250 and 80 km over the cyclone core there were no flashes in view.
- **Globe:**
  - Imagery drapes, and `/api/xweather/tile` requests stayed at geographic z 0–6 (8,000 km: z0–3; 800 and 250 km: up to z6).
  - Per output tile, 75 compositions read 2 source tiles and 12 read 3 (cap 9). Measured with a temporary log line that is not committed.
  - Colours against Xweather's own tiles for the same frame (geographic z5 x12 y13 vs Mercator z6 x12 y28–29): mean |ΔRGB| 3.4 (sum of channels, of 765), 51% of opaque pixels identical, 0.01% off by more than 60, 1.1% alpha mismatch along edges. That is bilinear resampling.
  - At 250 km, where level-6 tiles are magnified, faint one-pixel lines show along geographic tile edges: a step of ~15/765 summed RGB against a ~4–8 background gradient. I could not yet compare NOAA at the same zoom (no rain in view), so this is noted in `KNOWN-ISSUES.md` as not yet ruled out.

## Cost

- One image never fetches more than 192 source tiles: a detail window costs at most 192 units, a whole-extent frame 64, and an output tile at most 9. Each tile body is capped at 1 MiB (`readResponseBytesCapped`).
- You asked to keep the budget governor; past the free 15,000 the card warns but doesn't block, so an account on a paid Xweather plan keeps working — `XWEATHER_MONTHLY_FREE_UNITS` only moves that warning threshold — and spend is bounded instead by a per-client cap of 600 source tiles (units) per minute and 3,000 overall. Worst case per minute: 600 units from one client and 3,000 from all clients together (the old request-count limit, 120 requests of up to 192 tiles, allowed about 23,000 per client). Over the cap a composition gets 429 `xweather_rate_limited` before any upstream work. Cache hits and compositions over already-decoded tiles are not charged. Frame walks keep a request count (120 a minute per client, 1,200 overall).
- Only a real refusal shows as one: 401, 403, or a 200 with a JSON body, from a tile or a frame lookup, sets `upstreamError`; a 404, 429 or 5xx is reported as unavailable. A successful frame redirect or tile clears it.
- The budget line reads `Xweather · 1,370 / 15,000 free this month`. Past the allowance it becomes `Xweather · past the free 15,000 this month · requests may fail`, not muted, and fetching continues — the card warns but doesn't block, so a paid Xweather plan keeps working. A free-plan account is different: once its shared allowance for the billing period runs out, Xweather refuses every request (a 403 that reads "Maximum number of daily accesses reached") until the allowance resets.
- The free 15,000 are shared across every Xweather service on the account, so the card's count (this app only) can be lower than Xweather's dashboard.
- Composition deadline: 48 s (4 × the 12 s upstream deadline), and it includes queue time. A composition that fails, including one that timed out in the queue without starting, waits out a 30 s cooldown. `weather.js` does the same.
- Memory: decoded source tiles are an LRU of 512 (~128 MiB). Encoded outputs are 128 entries / 64 MiB for 24 h. Four compositions in flight hold ~160 MiB each (192 decoded tiles 48 + mosaic 48 + output 32 + encode buffer 32), so the worst case is ≈ 830 MiB. The only file written is `.gev-cache/xweather/budget.json`.
- Credentials appear only in upstream URL paths. Errors to the browser are bare codes, logs go through a redactor, and redirect `Location` headers never reach the browser.

## Fixed after the real-key run

- **History was one frame.** Fixed by the cadence-based walk above. Stepping back had given `No frame within 30 min of …` (`s5-history-earlier3.png`).
- **A keyless `s.x` share link left the layer off.** The key fallback returned `false` from the first `update()`, which the lifecycle reads as a rejection. It now switches to NOAA and fetches it in the same update. The new test restores the layer through `LayerLifecycle`, and a headless keyless run of a `lo=v.s.x` link ends with Rain radar enabled on NOAA, the `Xweather key removed · showing NOAA` notice, and no `LifecycleRejectedError`.
- **The refused status was unreachable.** It now comes ahead of the frame error a refusal causes (after the missing-data and imagery-host lines).
- **The OBSERVED HISTORY header said "Lightning density" on Xweather flashes.** It now takes the head of each card's label (`Lightning` on Xweather).

## Not in this PR

- The Xweather warnings card (next PR).
- A disk cache for past frames. Caches are memory-only, so a restart pays for frames again.
- Consolidating `gate.js` with `weather.js` `pump()`/`shared()` (see above).
- Opening a globe share link fetches one whole-extent `/image` (64 units) before `map=esri-imagery` applies (a shell staged on the initial photoreal host). This is upstream renderer behaviour, not specific to Xweather.
- Faint lines along geographic z6 tile edges at 250 km on the globe are not ruled out (a `KNOWN-ISSUES.md` bullet).

Refs #617.
Refs #618.

Commits:
1. feat(weather): decode and encode the PNG subset Xweather serves
2. feat(weather): reproject Xweather Mercator tiles to the weather grid
3. feat(weather): take Xweather frame times from its free redirect
4. feat(weather): count Xweather spend from x-cost-tokens against the free month
5. feat(weather): bound Xweather upstream work with a gate and a tile budget
6. feat(weather): serve Xweather radar and lightning through /api/xweather
7. feat(weather): route Xweather products to their proxy in the weather client
8. feat(weather): offer Global (Xweather) on the rain radar and lightning cards
9. feat(weather): add Xweather to Provider Settings and the setup doctor
10. docs(weather): document the Xweather source, its cost and its limits

title: feat(weather): add an Xweather warnings card for official weather alerts
body:
This adds a Warnings card to the WEATHER panel. It shows official warning, watch and advisory areas from national weather agencies, taken from Xweather's `alerts` layer. The card is Xweather only and needs the key from #764. On the server it is one more product in the `/api/xweather` table (`xweather-alerts`), so it uses the same frame walk, Mercator reprojection, 192-tile cap, rate limit and budget as radar and lightning. In the browser it is a fourth `createWeatherLayer` card. It sits after Lightning in the observed-history group and follows the shared history clock. It has the Xweather budget line, the refusal status and the Xweather credit. It has only an OPACITY setting: there is no NOAA product, so there is no SOURCE row. There is no colour ramp either, because Xweather colours alerts by type, so the info panel links Xweather's alert-type reference. There is no `View coverage` action, because flying to the global bounds would imply global coverage. Without a key the card stays in the panel and asks `/api/xweather/status` and nothing else. Its one-line status then reads `Needs an Xweather key · see Provider Settings`. The detail line above it (which wraps) and the toggle give the full `Needs XWEATHER_CLIENT_ID + XWEATHER_CLIENT_SECRET — add it in Provider Settings`.

- `server/providers/xweather.js`: `'xweather-alerts': { layer: 'alerts', cadenceMs: 180_000, maxZoom: 8, metadataTtlMs: 180_000, … }`, with the same title, coverage and description fields as the other products. The 3-minute cadence comes from Xweather's documented 2–3 minute updates; I have not measured it against a live key (there is a code comment saying so). Warning areas need less detail than radar, so tiles stop at zoom 8, and the 192-tile cap still applies.
- `src/layers/weather/index.js`: an `alerts` flag (`id === 'weather-alerts'`), fixed to the `xweather-alerts` product. It sets `requiresKeyId: 'xweather'` on the layer and reports `getStats().keyRequired` (row meta `KEY REQUIRED`). Until `/status` reports `hasKey: true` it never requests a manifest or a frame. A key removed at runtime takes the last frame off the map, and the radar/lightning NOAA fallback is skipped for this card. The copy is `Warnings · Xweather`, coverage `US · Canada · Europe · Australia · Japan · Korea`, and the muted caveat `Official warnings where issued · no global coverage`. While the key is missing, the status is the short form, the summary carries `keyRequired`, and history mode never reports a missing frame. The info panel links https://www.xweather.com/docs/maps/reference/alert-types.
- `src/ui/layerPanel.js`: when a card's key is missing, its detail line gets the `layerKeyRequirementTooltip` text, the same key guidance the toggle row already uses. The card's own short status stays. `weather-alerts` is added to both weather id lists.
- `src/layers/weather/source.js`, `rendering.js`, `shellRendering.js`: the product and its 4096×2048 image size. On the globe it is drawn on top at priority 4 (lightning is 3), with the Xweather credit. On Google 3D it gets a 6.9 km shell, above lightning's 6.6 km. It takes the non-infrared path.
- `src/ui/weatherPanel.js`: `ORDER` puts warnings after lightning, and `names['weather-alerts'] = 'Warnings'`. A summary with `keyRequired` keeps its own detail in history mode. `src/ui/layerBindings.js`: the id is added to the shell list. `src/app/constructCatalog.js`: the fourth `createWeatherLayer`.
- `src/data/layerState.js`: a `weather-alerts` registry entry (`enabled+options`) and an `OPTION_GROUPS` entry with opacity only (`o`, `l`/`s`).
- `src/keySetupCore.mjs` and `.env.example`: the XWEATHER entry now also lists the warnings.
- Docs: `CHANGELOG.md`, `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md` (a paragraph in the Xweather section), `DATA_SOURCES.md` (the live-sources row, the notes bullet and an `alerts` product bullet with coverage), `docs/KNOWN-ISSUES.md` (three bullets in the Xweather entry), `README.md` (the key row and the weather paragraph) and `docs/CODE-BOUNDARIES.md` (the observed-history card list).

Token: the share-link token is the placeholder `9`, with a code comment. It was unused on this base. Please reassign it when you allocate tokens (#658 / #744). Opacity is option `o` on that token. A test pins `9`, and the registry-size assertion goes from 28 to 29.

Stacked on #764 (`feat/xweather-weather-source`, Xweather as an optional keyed radar and lightning source). Until #764 merges, this diff includes its commits.

Commits:
1. feat(weather): serve Xweather alerts through /api/xweather
2. feat(weather): add an Xweather warnings card
3. docs(weather): document the Xweather warnings card
4. fix(weather): keep the warnings key notice readable and scoped

Verified: Windows 11, Node v24.14.0, at the head of this branch, rebased on b210ab0. I checked keyless only: the test account has still exhausted its Xweather billing-period allowance (403), so no real Xweather request was made.
- `npm test`: 5,169 pass / 0 fail / 10 skipped on Windows. That is 5,179 tests: the main suite 5,155/5,165 plus the two serialized allocation probes, 1/1 and 13/13. CI on Linux runs the 10 skipped.
- New tests, each failing first: the server manifest for `xweather-alerts` validates through `validateWeatherSnapshot`, and `/image` fetches layer `alerts` (64 whole-extent tiles; a detail window stays ≤ 192). Keyless: the card is enabled through `LayerLifecycle`, makes no manifest or frame request, and `layerKeyRequirementTooltip` gives the Provider Settings line. With a key: it joins the observed clock on `xweather-alerts` and shows the label, coverage, caveat, budget line, credit and refusal status. A removed key clears its frame. Keyless in history mode it shows the key, not a missing frame. Its settings are `['OPACITY']`, it has no actions and no legend. It draws above lightning on the globe. The share link round-trips under `9`. The panel order is `cyclones, wind, radar, satellite, lightning, warnings`. With a missing key, the weather card shows the short status and the full requirement on its detail line.
- `npm run format:check` ✓ (1,101 files), `npm run check:boundaries` ✓, `npm run build` ✓ (the usual chunk-size warning).
- `npm run test:track`: 109 pass / 0 fail / 0 skipped against a keyless dev server.
- `node scripts/qa-weather-journey.mjs` (keyless): exit 0, 19 steps. It logs 12 `chip … missing or disabled` notes, the same count #764 reported.
- `node scripts/qa-weather-swap.mjs` (keyless): `frames=26 black(>15%)=0 max=0.0% distinctTimes=4`.
- `node scripts/qa-weather-teardown.mjs` (keyless): exit 0. `DIFFERENCES after teardown: {"listeners.moveEnd":[5,8],"windCells":[null,0]}`, which #764 found on its parent commit too. Both the weather run and the control run logged a 403 and some upstream 502s.

- These gates enable radar, satellite and lightning only. They do not list weather cards, so the new card changes none of their results.

Its status is `Needs an Xweather key · see Provider Settings`, and the detail line reads `Needs XWEATHER_CLIENT_ID + XWEATHER_CLIENT_SECRET — add it in Provider Settings` in full. title: fix(ci): run allocation gates on Node 26
body:
## Summary

Node 26 is advertised as a supported runtime, but the unit runner treated only Node 24 as calibrated for the GC-bracketed allocation budgets. As a result, `npm test` on Node 26 could be green while omitting the focus and world-overlay allocation regression gates.

This change calibrates the existing budgets for both supported Node majors (24 and 26) and updates the L9 gate/docs accordingly. The byte ceilings are unchanged.

Fixes #39.

## Verification (rebased on upstream `main` `2dca762e4ad514ed2a1337a925592adcbc7ef1c9`)

- Regression: current upstream skips supported Node 26 in `isCalibratedAllocationRuntime`; the updated runner accepts both Node 24 and 26 without changing allocation byte budgets.
- Node 24.15.0: `GEV_REQUIRE_ALLOCATION_GATE=1 npm test` completed with 8,524 passed, 0 failed, 1 skipped in the ordinary suite, then 1/1 focus and 14/14 world-overlay allocation checks passed.
- Node 26.12.0: 33/33 focused runner/L9 tests passed; actual GC-bracketed allocation checks passed (1/1 focus and 14/14 world overlay). The full ordinary suite was not rerun under Node 26 after rebase.
- `npm run format:check`, `npm run check:boundaries`, `npm run changelog:check`, `npm run build`, and `git diff --check` passed. Build has the existing large-chunk warning.
- Browser track regression on the rebased head: 108 passed and 1 timing failure (military arrival `moveEnd` measured 510.4 ms against a 500 ms threshold); no console errors or HTTP 5xx. This latency check is separate from the allocation runner change and has not been treated as passing.

The changelog entry is now in `changelog.d/766-node26-allocation-gates.md` rather than the shared `CHANGELOG.md`, and the calibration tests preserve the newer test discovery coverage from `main`.

title: fix(satellites): decode Alpha-5 catalog numbers in the layer and the satellite tools
body:
Reported in #751 and confirmed independently there by @SM-26. Rebased onto v0.2.1 (aa16b7c) and moved into the layout v0.2.0 introduced.

Catalog numbers above 99999 arrive in a TLE as Alpha-5, a letter A–Z (I and O skipped) standing for 10–33 in the ten-thousands place, so 100000 is `A0000`. satellite.js keeps that field as the string `satrec.satnum`, and the three places that build the catalog converted it with `Number()`, which gives `NaN`; the `Set` and `Map` used to deduplicate and store treat `NaN` as equal to `NaN`, so the first such satellite was stored under key `NaN` and every later one dropped as a duplicate. The satellite tools added in v0.2.0 read the same field with `parseInt` and get no number, so `next_satellite_pass` cannot find such a satellite by it.

The decoder now lives in `src/sources/tle.js`, which the layer and the tools both import already, so no package boundary changes: `noradIdFromSatnum` for `ingestion.js`, `catalog.js` and `orbits.js`, and `tleCatalogNumber` decodes through the same function. A five-digit field reads as before, and anything else still goes through `Number()` in the layer and `parseInt` in the tools. The tests sit with the module's existing ones in `src/tools/queries/space.test.mjs`; two of the three fail on the old conversions. `CHANGELOG.md` and `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md` each gain a line.

Validation on aa16b7c, Node 26.5.0: `npm test` 5,601 → 5,604 passing, three tests added, none failing; `npm run build`, `npm run format:check` and `npm run check:boundaries` green; `npm run test:track` against the dev server, 109 passed, 0 failed, no console errors. The gates that fetch CelesTrak live (`qa-l9-matrix` B4 and C5, the `qa-overlay-baseline` detection scenes) were not run. The harness behind #751 drove the same ingestion module with a local 256-satellite Alpha-5 file: one catalog entry before this change, 256 after.

title: feat(street-level): provider-neutral street-level imagery, Mapillary first
body: ## Street Level: provider-neutral street-level imagery (Mapillary first) ### What and why GEV shows the world from orbit and from traffic cameras, but not from the street. This PR adds a **Street Level** layer, modelled on the iD editor's photo overlay: one panel for street-level imagery from any provider, drawn on the globe and viewable in place. Mapillary is the first provider (public, CC BY-SA 4.0, free client token). The provider contract is built so Google Street View, KartaView and Panoramax can follow without touching the core. The branch also carries the portable, resizable rail-panel work (CCTV and Street Level can float as windows), plus fixes to that work found while verifying this PR. Supersedes #727 (portable rail panels) and #728 (the earlier Mapillary layer with a plain-English query, which this PR drops). ### What users get - **STREET LEVEL panel** in the right rail next to CCTV. The header **ON/OFF** pill switches the layer; the **PROVIDERS** row has one chip per registered provider, and a chip is lit only while the layer is on. - **Coverage on the globe**, from orbit (z0–5 points) down to single streets (z11–14 ground-clamped sequence lines). Click a line for its image cones, a cone for the photo. - **One colour per source.** Every source draws in its own colour everywhere it appears: its PROVIDERS chip (a swatch dot, and the whole chip while on), coverage lines, overview points, image cones and a single legend swatch. Mapillary is green; Panoramax will be purple and Google Street View blue (`PROVIDER_COLORS` in `src/layers/streetLevel/policy.js`). 360° cones are rings, the 360°/FLAT filter separates panoramas, and the selected sequence is cyan. - **On the ground on Google 3D.** At street zoom on the Google 3D map, lines, cones and the position marker sit on the bare earth, so trees, bridges and buildings hide what is behind them. Draped lines landed on the top of the photoreal mesh and seemed to float over trees and overpasses. Other maps and higher views keep draped lines. - **Shared filters** for every provider: **ALL / 360° / FLAT** and a **SINCE** slider (any date → last month) whose readout names the cut-off date. - **Photo first.** The viewer opens at the top of the panel, visible without scrolling, including on phones. Its bar has EXPAND, FIT (whole photo) / FILL (cropped to the frame), FOLLOW (the globe camera follows the street view; Google 3D map only) and close. The caption credits the author and links to the image on the provider's site. - **Movable window.** Drag the header to float the panel and resize it from any edge; the photo takes the extra room. A header double-click, collapsing it, or SHRINK after EXPAND docks it at its default size, so it never stays parked over the globe. - **Attribution and sharing.** One on-globe credit per active provider ("Street Level: imagery © Mapillary contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0"). Share links carry the layer, provider switches and filter (token `0`; options `m`, `p`, `s`). ### How it is built - `src/layers/streetLevel/` is the provider-neutral core: enable state, filter, one click router by pick prefix, one viewer host that mounts the open image's provider adapter, marker, camera follow, credits and share params. - `src/layers/streetLevel/registry.js` documents the provider contract (definition, instance, viewer adapter, common pose). `providers/mapillary/` implements it: coverage tiles, Graph API sequences and nearest image, MapillaryJS viewer adapter. - `src/layers/streetLevel/groundCast.js` places overlays on the bare earth in the core's `terrain` surface mode: Google 3D and a camera below 1,400 m, back to `draped` above 1,800 m. Heights come from the existing terrain service (`/api/terrain/heights`) on the ground-floor grid (0.001°, shared cache), interpolated bilinearly, plus 2 m. A z14 tile costs at most a few hundred lookups, once per tile, and they are aborted when the tile is dropped. A tile draws draped first and swaps to its cast lines when the heights arrive, with no blink. A geoid fallback (terrain proxy down) counts as unknown, so those lines stay draped. Providers get `getSurface()` and `groundCaster` in their context and an optional `setSurface(mode)`. - `server/providers/mapillary/` proxies coverage tiles with the token added server-side, caches them for 24 h, and strips the unused z14 `image` layer in transit (≈12 MB → ≈80 KB per tile). `/api/mapillary/status` reports only whether a token exists. Only `coverage` tiles are proxied; the path is validated and the upstream host is fixed. - `MAPILLARY_CLIENT_TOKEN` is client-exposed by design (MapillaryJS needs it in the browser), documented in `SECURITY.md` and `.env.example`, and registered in Provider Settings. Without it the panel reads KEY REQUIRED and its controls stay disabled. - Dependencies: adds `mapillary-js` (MIT). No other new runtime dependency. ### Fixes to portable rail panels - **Reload restore.** A window restored as floating after a reload fell back into the rail, because the rail's startup move cleared every panel's inline position. Floating panels now keep theirs. - **Double-click.** A real header double-click never snapped a floating panel back: the drag handler's `pointerdown` `preventDefault()` suppresses the mouse events a native `dblclick` is built from. Double presses are now detected in `pointerdown`. - **Stacking.** A restored floating window had no z-index, and the z ladder renumbered from 101, so the docked DISPLAY panel (z 110) painted over it. The ladder now starts at 111 and restored windows are promoted. - **Docking on collapse.** `dockOnCollapse` is opt-in per panel (Street Level uses it). Only a user's own collapse docks a window; cockpit entry, restores and the Cyber accordion never move or forget it. - **Harness.** `qa-panel-resize` fixes: s/e handle points were NaN, it now counts only visible rail panels, it parks the window clear of the voice dock, and it names the element under the pointer on failure. ### Share-link token (merged #744) The branch now includes upstream `main` with #744's token ledger. Following CONTRIBUTING, Street Level's provisional token `3` was replaced by what `npm run layer-token:next -- street-level` assigns: `0`, the first free digit. It is in the registry and in `src/data/layerStateTokenReservations.json`, and `npm run layer-token:check -- --base-ref origin/main` passes (28 published, 1 new). No link with `3` was ever published. The pinned token tests move with the ledger, as CONTRIBUTING asks: 29 reservations, next free digit `3`. The competing-PR and retired-digit scenarios move up one free digit (`0`→`3`, `3`→`4`), so they still test the same rules. ### Test strategy | Layer | What it guards | | --- | --- | | Unit, pure modules | filter, params, registry, tile maths, UI state, ground casting and mesh refinement | | Unit, fake scene | `coverage.test.mjs`: the superseded-tile race (review P0 #2), the draped-to-cast swap, no pointless rebuilds. `cameraFollow.test.mjs`: the underground-camera fix. All of these fail on the pre-fix code. | | Contract | `streetLevelControls.test.mjs`: a 360° click and a SINCE release reach the durable layer state and the share link through the real `DataLayerManager` and `LayerStateCoordinator`; also the chip rule, legend rebuilds and resize-on-open | | Browser, hermetic (CI) | `qa:street-level:fixtures`: generated coverage tiles, no token; 14 steps including stricter filter checks, plus the panel gate | | Browser, live (manual) | `qa:street-level` with a token: adds the six photo steps | ### Fix: shared tile fetches no longer die with their first caller Thanks @kvnloo. `fetchTile` coalesced concurrent requests for a tile onto one upstream fetch that ran on the first caller's abort signal. An abandoned older pan could therefore cancel a tile that a newer request still needed. A flight now owns its `AbortController` and counts waiters, the pattern the weather and wind providers use: - a caller's own abort rejects that caller at once; - the upstream fetch is cancelled only when its last waiter leaves; - a later request after that starts a fresh fetch. ### Fix: share links now keep the filter and provider switches The panel changed the filter and provider switches by calling the layer directly. That skipped the data manager's params request, the only path saved state and share links record. A link copied after picking 360° or a SINCE window came back with the defaults. The controls now go through `dataManager.setLayerParams('street-level', …, { origin: 'user' })`, as the CCTV panel does, and the gate's 360° step asserts the share hash carries `0.p.p`. ### Mesh-refined ground casting The bare-earth grid (~111 m) cannot see a freeway in a trench, a steep street between its corners, or the road under a tree. Near the camera, `meshSampler.js` samples the rendered Google 3D surface with `scene.sampleHeight`, overlays excluded: - once per ~11 m cell within 900 m, nearest first; - in idle time, within a 6 ms budget; - misses are retried, not latched. `refineHeights` then blends it in, point by point along each line: - **mesh up to 3 m above bare earth is the road:** follow it, 1 m above; - **higher mesh (canopy, deck, roof):** carry the road's offset across from the road on both sides; - **otherwise:** bare earth + 2 m, as before. Lines, cones and the marker all use it. Tiles touched by new samples are redrawn one per idle slice, without blinking. Measured with a raycast challenge: rendered line pixels are picked on screen and cast down to the most-detailed mesh. Before → after, on the surface / floating more than 4 m: | Site | On the surface | Floating | | --- | --- | --- | | Austin (trees, I-35 cut) | 90.0 → 95.3% | 8.5 → 0.7% | | San Francisco (steep) | 69.0 → 86.4% | 27.1 → 9.1% | | LA four-level interchange | 52.3 → 91.0% | 43.8 → 4.0% | | Innsbruck (alpine) | 95.0 → 95.7% | 0.2 → 0.2% | | Sacramento (flat) | 80.7 → 79.3% | 3.8 → 2.7% | Buried lines stay under 1%. The only extra main-thread long tasks are on the densest tile: at most 134 ms, in Austin. **Known limitation:** roads on elevated decks are still drawn at ground level under the deck, since from heights alone a deck looks like a canopy. | LA, bare earth only | LA, mesh-refined | | --- | --- | | | | ### CI and review round (after merging `main`) - **CI was red because of the `main` merge, not the feature.** The merge appended main's entries straight after ours, without commas, in `scripts/format-scope.json` and two groups of `scripts/package-boundaries.json`. Both stopped parsing, so every job failed at its first step. The commas are back. - **High cities on Google 3D.** `cameraHeightAboveGround` read `globe.getHeight`, but Google 3D hides the globe, so coverage chose its zoom from the ellipsoidal height. Over Denver, a camera 500 m up read 2,100 m: coverage stayed at z12/z13, whose tiles are too big to cast, and lines stayed on the roofs. It now uses the bare-earth height. Verified in Denver: terrain mode, z14, lines on the ground. - **No pointless rebuilds.** A tile with nothing castable (terrain proxy down, tile too big) is no longer rebuilt. - **Gate.** The share-link step reads Street Level's token from the registry instead of a literal `0`. ### Fix: framing a photo could fly the camera underground Opening a photo frames it from 140 m behind, using `scene.sampleHeight` for the ground. Before the Google tiles under the photo have loaded, that sample can be kilometres wrong: one Austin 360° photo sampled −14,886 m and the camera ended at −14,811 m. The sample now counts only when it is a plausible surface height and, once the bare-earth height is known, within −15/+80 m of it. Otherwise the bare-earth height is used. FOLLOW's eye height goes through the same check. ### Docs `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md` (runtime reference, provider contract, how to add a provider), `CHANGELOG.md`, `DATA_SOURCES.md` (Mapillary: CC BY-SA 4.0, attribution), `README.md` (Street Level section and keys table), `SECURITY.md`, `docs/KNOWN-ISSUES.md`, `.env.example`. ### Validation Node 24.19.0, macOS, candidate `284cd0a` on base `aa16b7c` (v0.2.1) (upstream `main`, 0 commits behind). The run mirrors CI's steps in order: doctor, format:check, check:boundaries, layer-token:check, npm test, build, and the Windows job's focused onboarding tests. | Check | Command | Result | | --- | --- | --- | | Setup policy | `npm run doctor -- --json` | ready | | Formatting | `npm run format:check` | pass | | Package boundaries | `npm run check:boundaries` | pass | | Layer tokens | `npm run layer-token:check -- --base-ref origin/main` | 28 published, 1 new (`street-level`: `0`) | | Unit tests | `npm test` | 5740 pass, 0 fail | | Windows job, focused tests | `node --test src/setupDoctor.test.mjs …hudSummaryResponse.test.mjs` | 70 pass | | Production build | `npm run build` | pass | | Tracking regression | `npm run dev`, then `npm run test:track` | 109 passed, 0 failed | | Feature gate, keyless | `node scripts/qa-street-level.mjs --url http://localhost:4174` (server started with empty `MAPILLARY_CLIENT_TOKEN`) | 4/4 | | Feature gate, keyed | `npm run qa:street-level -- --url http://localhost:4173` | 20/20 (step 3: one legend swatch per source and the chip in `#05cb63`; step 8: share hash carries `0.p.p`; step 12: draped on Esri, `terrain` on Google 3D) | | Feature gate, fixtures (CI) | `npm run qa:street-level:fixtures -- --url …` against a dev server with every key blank | 14/14 on three consecutive runs (photo steps skipped); new CI job "Street Level browser gate" runs it with `qa:panel-resize` | | Panel gate | `npm run qa:panel-resize -- --url http://localhost:4173` | lift, 8 handles, minimum size, reload restore, double-click: all pass | | Built app | `npm run build && npm run preview -- --port 4176`, then the keyed gate against it | 20/20 | | Ground placement | Scripted, Austin on Google 3D (headless Chrome, GPU) | `surface: terrain`; 31–65 terrain requests for 9 z14 tiles, cast within ~7 s; a click on a cast line selects its sequence; no page errors | | Raycast challenge | `.gev-cache` harness: rendered line pixels picked on an oblique view and cast down to the most-detailed Google 3D mesh, six sites | lines on the surface / floating > 4 m: Austin 95.3% / 0.7%, San Francisco 86.4% / 9.1%, LA interchange 91.0% / 4.0%, Innsbruck 95.7% / 0.2%, Sacramento 79.3% / 2.7%; buried < 1% everywhere (see below) | | Console errors | Scripted session (enable, filters, SINCE, open photo, FIT/FILL, FOLLOW, EXPAND/Esc, close, offline tiles, disable) vs the same page idle | none from Street Level (see below; run on `c7dc314`, and gate step 20 checks page errors on `d77dccb`) | **Regression tests that fail on the old implementation:** - `src/ui/panelDock.test.mjs`: double press, restored-window z-order, z-ladder renumbering, dock on collapse. All 5 fail on the pre-fix `panelPositionControls.js` (768f256) and pass on the fix. - `scripts/qa-street-level.mjs` step 8: the share-hash assertion times out on the previous `streetLevelControls.js` (`d7d5bec`) and passes on the fix. - `src/tooling/mapillaryProvider.test.mjs`: the three in-flight tile tests (a joined request survives the first caller aborting; a joined caller that aborts leaves at once; the last waiter cancels the fetch) all fail on the previous `tiles.js` (`d77dccb`) and pass on the fix. - `src/layers/streetLevel/viewerHost.test.mjs`: "a failed mount is retried" fails on the pre-review viewer host (5877f24) and passes on the fix. The concurrent-mount and cancel-mid-mount tests are guards that pass on both. **Console, failure and teardown evidence (scripted, headless Chrome):** - Console errors during the session are all `403` from `/api/google/nearby-places`, the upstream Places supplement, which needs a Google server key not configured here. The same 403 appears with the layer off. Street Level adds none. - Offline tiles: going offline and panning shows the panel alert ("Failed to fetch") instead of failing silently; back online, coverage reloads (44 sequences) and the alert clears. - Teardown: turning the layer off removes the credit, all coverage and the viewer. **Removed tests belong to removed code only.** An earlier draft of this layer had a plain-English map-feature query (Claude planner, map features, traffic signs, sprites). It is not in this PR, and neither are its tests (`query`, `values`, `ndjson`, planner and sprite tests). No other test was removed, skipped or relaxed. Two upstream tests were updated only for the new rail panel and layer count (`catalog.test.mjs`, `layerState.test.mjs`). **Keyed paths.** Tested with a Mapillary client token. A reviewer without one can run the keyless gate and the unit suite; coverage, viewer and filter behaviour then need a free token (see README → Street Level). ### Test cases for reviewers Setup: `npm run dev`. For the keyed cases, put `MAPILLARY_CLIENT_TOKEN` in `.env`. Expand the STREET LEVEL strip. Turn the layer on from DATA LAYERS → Cameras. | Header reads KEY REQUIRED; controls are greyed out; the MAPILLARY chip is amber, and its tooltip names the env var.
