title: feat(ui): S-key Street View — click the globe, walk the street
body:
## What

Press **S**, click a street, and a Google Street View panel opens at the nearest outdoor panorama (within 50 m, then 250 m). A globe marker follows the panorama as you move; **S** or **Esc** closes it; ⤢ enlarges the panel.

## How it fits

- Arming claims the globe pointer as `street-view` via `src/data/inputOwnership.js`, so the placing click never also selects an entity underneath, and an active tool (e.g. Directions) blocks arming with a toast instead of being displaced.
- Uses the existing browser `GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY`; the Maps JavaScript API must be enabled on it. Loaded lazily on first use. Without a key, arming is refused with a toast; a rejected key (`gm_authFailure`) closes the panel with a toast.
- **Daily cost cap.** Google bills every `StreetViewPanorama` created (Dynamic Street View, 5,000 free/month) and the Maps JavaScript API has no quota row to cap it, so the tool caps itself at 150 new panoramas per Pacific-time day (`STREET_VIEW_DAILY_LIMIT`; 150 × 31 stays inside the free tier). Count kept in `localStorage` (`godsEyeView.streetView.dailyLoads`) with an in-page fallback. Moving an open panel, panning and walking don't count.
- Only a bare S triggers it — Cmd/Ctrl/Alt+S keep their browser meaning.
- New: `src/ui/streetView.js`, `src/ui/styles/street-view.css`, `src/ui/streetView.test.mjs`. Wired through `applicationShortcuts.js` → `displayBindings.js` → `applicationShell.js`; registered in `scripts/package-boundaries.json`; documented in `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md`.

## Validation

- `npm test` — 5,088 pass / 0 fail (includes new `streetView.test.mjs`: arm, cancel via S/Esc, no-key refusal, pointer-blocked, destroy, daily limit incl. day rollover, one count per new panorama, storage failure; and S-key cases in `visualInput.test.mjs`)
- `npm run build` ✓ · `npm run check:boundaries` ✓ · `npm run format:check` ✓
- `npm run test:track` — 106 pass / 3 fail. All three are the "no console errors" checks tripping on a 403 from `tile.googleapis.com/v1/3dtiles/root.json` — my local key isn't authorised for Map Tiles in the headless run. Unrelated to this change; every tracking invariant passed.
- Manually tested in Chrome on macOS: London, pan/zoom/walk, marker follow, expand, Esc close.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: qa:transit cannot start off macOS: the transit gate family pins the system Chrome path
body:
`npm run qa:transit` cannot start on Linux or Windows. It exits at the first `puppeteer.launch`, before a single check runs:

```
Error: Browser was not found at the configured executablePath
(/Applications/Google Chrome.app/Contents/MacOS/Google Chrome)
    at scripts/qa-transit-heading.mjs:5
    ← scripts/qa-transit.mjs:93
```

Three files in the transit gate family set that path as their **only** `executablePath` candidate:

- `scripts/qa-transit.mjs:265`
- `scripts/qa-transit-heading.mjs:7`
- `scripts/qa-transit-recovery.mjs:11`

## Why this one matters

`CONTRIBUTING.md` asks contributors to run the gate covering whatever they touched, notes that CI does not cover it, and asks for the applicable local run as the PR's validation evidence. `qa:transit` is one of only two gates with an `npm run` alias, and `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md` calls this pair the Transit layer's acceptance harness. CI runs on `ubuntu-latest` and `windows-latest` (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:18,59`). So a contributor working on either of the platforms the project builds and tests on cannot produce the evidence the guide asks for.

It is also being worked around rather than fixed. Two open PRs each carry part of this:

- #402 rewrites the resolution expression across the 28 harnesses that already have one.
- #753 ("Add Cyber Intelligence Layer") carries a two-line fix for `scripts/qa-transit-heading.mjs` inside an otherwise unrelated 52-file feature change.

Two people needed the same thing within two weeks, in two unrelated PRs. That is the argument for fixing it once, in one place.

## Scope, measured at `b210ab0`

Of the 64 files under `scripts/` that call `puppeteer.launch`:

| shape | count |
|---|---|
| macOS system Chrome as the sole candidate | **8** |
| `PUPPETEER_EXECUTABLE_PATH` only, no resolver | 5 |
| env var + `puppeteer.executablePath()`, macOS paths as fallback | 31 |
| no `executablePath` at all | 20 |

The eight: `precompute-cctv-heights`, `qa-directions`, `qa-draw-tool`, `qa-overlay-baseline`, `qa-recent-imagery`, `qa-transit`, `qa-transit-heading`, `qa-transit-recovery`.

## The fix already exists in the repository

`scripts/qa-firms.mjs:50-62` resolves the browser as environment variable → pinned Chrome-for-Testing → the `/Applications` paths, with a comment explaining why the pinned browser is preferred (a system Chrome major bump produced six false-negative `qa-cctv-v2` runs against a healthy build on 2026-07-30). That shape has been in the tree since the initial open-source commit `880a672`; these eight files were simply written without it.

I would like to propagate that existing pattern to the transit family first, since it is the one with an `npm run` alias, keeping `/Applications` as the last resort so a macOS checkout without the pinned browser cache behaves exactly as it does today. Happy to follow up for the other five if that is welcome, and happy to defer entirely if you would rather this land through #402.

title: fix(qa): resolve the browser in the transit gates instead of pinning the macOS path
body:
Fixes #770.

`npm run qa:transit` exited at the first `puppeteer.launch` on any non-macOS machine, before a single check ran. This adopts the resolution order already used in `scripts/qa-firms.mjs:50-62` for the three transit entry points:

1. `PUPPETEER_EXECUTABLE_PATH`
2. `puppeteer.executablePath()` — the pinned Chrome-for-Testing
3. `/Applications/Google Chrome.app/Contents/MacOS/Google Chrome`

The macOS path is kept as the last resort, so a macOS checkout without the pinned browser cache behaves exactly as it does today. `headless`, launch `args`, viewport and every assertion are untouched. No signature changed and no shared helper was introduced — the resolution expression is duplicated the way the sibling gates duplicate it.

**Gate covering the change, per CONTRIBUTING.md:** `npm run qa:transit`.

## Relationship to the two open PRs in this area

- **#402** rewrites `await puppeteer.executablePath().catch(...)` across the 28 harnesses that already have a resolver. Its file list and mine do not overlap at all — these three files have no resolver to rewrite. I have written the new lines in the form #402 proposes, so whichever order the two land in, nothing is left behind for someone to clean up.
- **#753** carries a two-line version of this fix for `scripts/qa-transit-heading.mjs`. That is one file and one hunk of overlap, so whichever of us lands first, the other gets a one-minute conflict. This PR covers all three files, keeps the `/Applications` fallback, and adds the existence check the sibling gates use. I am happy to rebase, to narrow this, or to drop it entirely if you would rather it ride along with #753 or #402 — just say which.

## Validation, on Linux aarch64 (Ubuntu 6.17, snap Chromium 152.0.7977.82, Node 24.20.0)

- `npm run build` — pass
- `npm test` — 5120 tests, 5119 pass, 0 fail, 1 skipped (a Windows-only DACL test), run with `GEV_REQUIRE_ALLOCATION_GATE=1` so the allocation microbenchmarks cannot silently skip
- `npm run test:track` — 109 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped
- `npm run format:check`, `npm run check:boundaries` — pass
- `npm run qa:transit` — **before:** none of the harness's checks execute; the process exits at the first launch. **After:** the harness runs to completion.

### The gate is not green on this machine, and this change does not make it green

One run with `PUPPETEER_EXECUTABLE_PATH=/snap/bin/chromium` gave **202 pass, 5 fail, 17 unexercised**. Four of the five failures are the 800- and 3000-vehicle CPU, frame-interval and allocation budgets; the fifth is a silhouette pixel read. The WebGL renderer here reports `ANGLE (Google, Vulkan 1.3.0 (SwiftShader Device), SwiftShader driver)` — software rasterisation, which is not a fair substrate for a frame-interval budget.

Two further sources of variance I measured on this box: the `capmetro-austin` upstream answers HTTP 403 from this address, and `page.goto` intermittently exceeds its 30 s bound. Three runs gave three different counts, so I am reporting one run with its conditions rather than a number.

### Evidence that the residual failures are not from this change

I ran the **unmodified** gate at `b210ab0` on this same machine, with only the browser binary overridden at launch time (a small loader that patches `puppeteer.launch`; no source change). The current code produced the same `mouse click selects the displayed sprite` failure in all five style presets — five occurrences, against three in one of my runs and zero in another. That failure class exists without this change.

### One honest limit

On this ARM64 box the resolver returns a cached `linux_arm-152.0.7977.75/chrome-linux64/chrome` whose binary is ELF x86-64, and `existsSync` is not an architecture check — so step 2 resolves to something that cannot execute here and step 1 is required. This change fixes ordinary Linux and Windows checkouts and gives everyone the environment-variable path; it does not rescue this particular machine on its own.

### Note for reviewers

`src/tooling/transitQa.test.mjs:205-224` asserts on the **source text** of `scripts/qa-transit.mjs` — the ordering of several statements. It still passes, but it is worth knowing that this file has a source-scanning test attached to it.


---

**Re-validated after updating the branch.** Merged `main` (`81eb443`) in at `30c8a604` — clean, nothing to hand-resolve. The validation above predates that merge, so on the merged tree (Node 24.20.0, Linux aarch64): `doctor` · `format:check` · `check:boundaries` · `build` all exit 0 · `npm test` with `GEV_REQUIRE_ALLOCATION_GATE=1` **5,075 pass / 1 skipped / 0 fail** of 5,076, and the 1 and 13 allocation budgets green.

`npm run layer-token:check -- --base-ref main` → `28 published, 0 new`. That one is new: #744 added it to CI after the checks recorded above this line, so this is the first time the branch has been measured against it. The branch shares no source file with #744 — the overlap is documentation and `scripts/format-scope.json`, which merged cleanly.

Browser-driven gates were not re-run for the merge itself, since what the merge brings in is confined to the share-link token ledger.

title: docs: add the realtime backend to the voice ownership table
body:
`docs/VOICE-OWNERSHIP.md` opens by saying the backend interfaces remain unchanged, then lists every owner except the backend. `realtimeBackend.js` has no row, though it owns state the other rows point at: the two requests, their separate transports, the abort/timeout scope around both, and client-secret expiry.

The method signatures are already documented with application construction (`docs/APPLICATION.md` under "Voice connections and controls"), so this does not repeat them. It adds the row, links there for the signatures, and states only the ownership facts that are written nowhere:

- the connection is the backend's only consumer in the application;
- the resolved credential is opaque to the connection and is handed to `negotiate` whole;
- client-secret expiry is refused inside the backend, not by the connection;
- `realtimeOwners.test.mjs` already drives whole sessions through a substitute that implements only those two methods.

Five contributions have had to work this seam out from the source: #42 (closed with "the LiveKit overlay is a separate decision; open it on its own once the Docker base lands"), #51, #236 (for #212), #275, #621. #275 adds a `realtimeProvider.js` row to this same table and still leaves the backend without one.

### How each added line was measured

| Line | Ruler |
| --- | --- |
| The controller accepts `backend` and falls back to `createRealtimeBackend()` | `realtimeController.js:62,71` |
| The connection is the only consumer in the application | grep `.backend` across `src/`: 4 hits — two calls in `realtimeConnection.js`, one assignment and one `readBackend` in the controller. `realtimeFacade.js` delegates method by method, with no Proxy and no property loop, and contains 0 occurrences of `backend` |
| Two methods, no more | grep for definitions and dot-calls of `requestToken`/`negotiate` across `src/`, `server/` and `scripts/`: defined at `realtimeBackend.js:18,62`, called at `realtimeConnection.js:90,224` |
| The credential is opaque and passed whole | `realtimeConnection.js:90` mints it, reads only `.token`, `.model` and `.tier`, and passes `credential: minted` at `:224` |
| Expiry lives inside the backend | `expiresAt` appears in exactly one file under `src/`: `realtimeBackend.js` (`:44-51`, `:65-71`). `realtimeConnection.js` has no matches |
| The test substitute drives whole sessions | `realtimeOwners.test.mjs:58-61`, `:104-107`, `:234-237`; each awaits `controller.start()` and reaches `status === 'listening'` |

Documentation only, no source change, so no CHANGELOG entry — every existing entry records a behaviour change.

### Validation

Run on the exact bytes in this PR:

```
npm run build              rc=0
npm test                   5079 tests, 5078 pass, 0 fail, 1 skipped (GEV_REQUIRE_ALLOCATION_GATE=1)
npm run test:track         109 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped
npm run doctor             rc=0

```

The voice-area gate `scripts/qa-voice-wav.mjs` is credentialed acceptance and needs a real OpenAI Realtime key, which I do not have, so it was not run. Nothing in this change is reachable from it: no test or build input reads this file, and its only inbound reference anywhere is a link from `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md:282`.

### Overlap with open PRs

- #275 edits this same table, inserting `realtimeProvider.js` after `realtimeCost.js`; this inserts `realtimeBackend.js` after `realtimeConnection.js`. Different anchors, so both rows can stand together. #275 already conflicts with main independently of this.
- #746 reformats the whole table to padded pipes, so it will conflict textually with the added row.

Happy to rebase behind either, or to drop this if you would rather the table wait for those.

title: feat: APRS-IS layer (amateur radio stations + weather), working in a fork
body: ### Problem APRS (Automatic Packet Reporting System) is a real-time amateur radio network used for weather reporting, emergency communications (ARES/RACES), high-altitude balloon tracking, and mapping the digipeater/iGate infrastructure that relays it. There's no way to see that traffic in God's Eye View today, and it fits naturally alongside the ADS-B, AIS, and radio layers. Amateur radio operators, emergency-comms volunteers, and weather watchers would all use it. Various public maps are already available at aprs.fi and other locations. ### Proposal I've built and am running this on a local fork, and it works well. Small v1: - Server: one read-only APRS-IS connection (passcode -1, nothing is ever transmitted) through a Vite provider plugin, with a server-side range filter (mine is 150 km around my QTH). It connects only while the layer is on and closes after 5 minutes idle, to be polite to the volunteer-run APRS-IS servers. Packets are parsed with js-aprs-fap. - Client: a layer following the existing factory pattern. Colored points (weather / fixed / moving), callsign labels at close range, short trails for moving stations, and a click card with symbol type, RF vs Internet, age, speed/course/altitude, and full weather readouts for WX stations. - Scope: position reports and weather only. Objects, items, messages, and telemetry are ignored. On the "no tracking individuals" rule, I want to raise it up front: every APRS station is an FCC-licensed operator who deliberately broadcasts their position to a public network, and aprs.fi already shows all of it worldwide. Even so, the layer has no callsign search or voice lookup, is registered local-only (never serialized into share links), and only shows what the user's own range filter pulls in. I'd be glad to adjust defaults if you prefer, for example weather and fixed infrastructure on by default and mobile trails opt-in. Verified: npm test all passing (one layer-count assertion updated from 29 to 30), npm run build, check:boundaries, and format:check clean. Tested live with real stations around central South Carolina. I'll open the PR IF YOU ARE INTERESTED. Happy to adjust scope or defaults first based on your feedback. Next up, add my open source project [https://github.com/taco40sauce/kcgr-resource-feed] to disseminate collected data via APRS, Winlink, and many amateur radio sources in case of an emergency. Developed because the normal route is to send collected data to state and county agencies and the regular folks don't see it. see qsl..net/kc4rc/kcgr 73's, Dave AA4TE ### Data source, license, and attribution APRS-IS (aprs2.net tier-2 network), fetched live at runtime and not redistributed or bundled. APRS packets are public amateur radio transmissions with no formal data license; attribution would be "APRS-IS / aprs2.net". It does not work fully keyless: APRS-IS expects a callsign at login (some servers reject the N0CALL placeholder), so the user sets APRS_CALLSIGN in .env. The login is receive-only (passcode -1). Parser: js-aprs-fap (ISC license, npm). ### Will you build it? Yes, I plan to open a PR

title: HUD summary labels a nautical zone as `UTC±N`
body:
**The arithmetic is right, so this is not a math report.** `Math.round(lonDeg / 15)` at `src/hud.js:646` computes a correct *nautical* time zone. Measured exhaustively at 0.01° across the whole meridian range — 36,001 samples — every result falls inside its own nautical band `[15N − 7.5°, 15N + 7.5°)`, with **0 exceptions**, and the domain is exactly `[−12, +12]`, so no clamp is missing either.

What does not match the arithmetic is what it is called:

- `src/hud.js:632` (JSDoc): "… sun elevation, ONA, and **local timezone**."
- `src/hud.js:645` (comment): "**Rough local timezone** from longitude (15 deg per hour)"
- `src/hud.js:647`: the token is `` `UTC${sign}${offset}` `` — `UTC+7` is the notation for a civil offset, not for a nautical zone.

### Where the token is actually seen

Your comment at `:427-430` is explicit that the deterministic line is a pre-network placeholder and "the AI summary upgrades this within a second", so with a key configured the token is short-lived. It is not short-lived in two measurable cases:

- **No `OPENAI_API_KEY`.** `keylessHudSummaryResponse()` in `src/hudSummaryResponse.js` answers `200` with `configured: false, summary: null`, and `hud.js:744-747` sets the deterministic line and returns. For a keyless deployment this line *is* the summary readout, permanently.
- Every summary failure or rejection path: `:700`, `:720`, `:731`, `:745`, `:765` all fall back to it, and `:433`/`:448` repaint it directly on first telemetry and when the geoid correction flips.

Either way it reaches `#hud-summary` through `_setSummaryText()`, at `:777-778` directly or via `_typeSummary()` at `:675`.

### How far label and civil time diverge

Nine cities, the label against the offset each place actually keeps, via `Intl.DateTimeFormat` `longOffset` at two fixed instants (2026-01-15, 2026-07-15):

| Place | Label | Civil Jan | Civil Jul | Error Jan | Error Jul |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Hanoi | `UTC+7` | +7 | +7 | 0 | 0 |
| Madrid | `UTC+0` | +1 | +2 | −1 h | −2 h |
| Anchorage | `UTC-10` | −9 | −8 | −1 h | −2 h |
| Reykjavík | `UTC-1` | 0 | 0 | −1 h | −1 h |
| Buenos Aires | `UTC-4` | −3 | −3 | −1 h | −1 h |
| Delhi | `UTC+5` | +5:30 | +5:30 | −0.5 h | −0.5 h |
| Adelaide | `UTC+9` | +10:30 | +9:30 | −1.5 h | −0.5 h |
| Kathmandu | `UTC+6` | +5:45 | +5:45 | +0.25 h | +0.25 h |
| Chatham Islands | `UTC-12` | +13:45 | +12:45 | −25.75 h | −24.75 h |

Eight of the nine differ; the table comes from a short throwaway script over `Intl`, which I can paste if it is worth checking. Chatham is the clearest case: the islands sit at 176.55° W but keep +12:45, so a longitude formula puts the label on the wrong side of the date line by about a day.

The structural point is smaller than the table and harder to argue with: **4 of these 10 zones change offset between January and July**, so no function of longitude alone can agree with civil time year-round. That is a property of civil timekeeping, not a defect in the formula.

### Why I am not proposing a timezone lookup

The project has no timezone infrastructure and, from the outside, that looks deliberate: `Intl.DateTimeFormat` and `getTimezoneOffset` appear **0** times in shipped code under `src/` and `server/`, there is no timezone API call anywhere, and the three `maps.googleapis.com` calls are geocode ×2 (`search/defaults.js:49`, `search/http.js:56`) and Street View ×1 (`server/providers/cctv.js:96`) — no `maps/api/timezone`. Bundling a lat/lon→IANA dataset would be a bundle-size decision that is yours, not mine, and I am not asking for it.

### The small change instead

Nautical zones already have a notation, and this HUD already speaks it: `_formatUTC()` at `:290-299` calls it "a UTC Zulu string" and emits `…:SSZ`, and the cockpit readouts append `Z` the same way (`ui/cockpitInstruments.js:118`, `ui/cockpitSignals.js:56`, `ui/cockpitContext.js:148`). `Z` is the zone letter for zone 0; the same series covers the rest — `A`…`M` east (skipping `J`), `N`…`Y` west — so `round(lon / 15)` maps onto it exactly, with no new concept and no lookup. Hanoi would read `G` instead of `UTC+7`.

Other options, all one line at `:647`, if the letter is too terse for the readout:

- `ZONE+7` / `ZONE-4`
- `NAUT+7`
- `SOLAR UTC+7`
- keep `UTC+7` and change only the two comments

The comments at `:632` and `:645` are wrong whichever token you choose, since they claim the local timezone rather than a nautical zone — that part is a taste-free correction.

The wording is a taste call on your own HUD, so I would rather you pick it than have me pick it. Happy to send the one-line PR with whichever you prefer, or to drop this if the current reading is intended.

Note on overlap: #601 and #602 both touch `_composeSummary`, but at `:637` (`'Awaiting telemetry...'` → `t(...)`), eight lines above the timezone block, so a change here is independent of them.

title: `layerStateInvalid` is computed and never read: a rejected layer token set restores defaults silently
body:
This is the separate issue I offered to open in my review on #744 and in my comment on #658. **Nothing here asks #744 to change**, and nothing here touches the fail-closed decision — I think both are right.

### The fail-closed rejection is correct

`src/data/layerState.js:767-769` states the reason in the code:

> `l=` is the one valid explicit-empty representation. Any non-empty token set containing an unknown member rejects the complete layer payload so a typo or future token cannot silently become an authoritative empty set.

Agreed, and that is not what this issue is about. Running the real `decodeLayerStateParams` over `v=2` links:

| `l` | decodes to | `layerStateInvalid` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `f` | `["flights"]` | false |
| *(empty)* | `[]` — the valid explicit-empty set | false |
| `f.v.a` | three layers | false |
| `f.v.Q` — two known, one unknown | `null` | **true** |
| `Q` — one unknown | `null` | **true** |
| 68 chars, over `MAX_ENABLED_LAYERS_CHARS` | `null` | **true** |

So the rejection works, and `src/sharelink.js:247-250` already records that it happened:

```js
layerStateInvalid:
  params.get('v') === '2' &&
  params.has('l') &&
  decodedLayerState === null,
```

### The signal is computed, tested, and read by nothing

Across `src/`, `server/` and `scripts/` on current `main`:

- **written once**, at `sharelink.js:247`
- **read by no shipped code** — zero consumers
- read only by three assertions in `sharelink.celestial.test.mjs:73`, `:77`, `:84`

#744 adds two more assertions on it (`sharelink.celestial.test.mjs`) and still no consumer, which is exactly right for that PR's scope.

The restore path never looks at it: `src/ui/shareRestoration.js:147-149` passes `this._initialShareState?.layerState` and `?.sharedAtMs` into the coordinator and reads nothing else from the parsed state.

### What that leaves the user with

`src/app/controls.js:47` sets the loader to `Restoring shared view...`. When the token set is rejected, the layer payload is discarded, the default layers come up instead, and nothing corrects the statement the app just made. The link opens, looks like it worked, and the shared layer selection is gone.

### Why this looks cheap rather than like new plumbing

The class that would consume the flag already surfaces this exact category of message. `shareRestoration.js:218-223` chooses between three, for the narrower case of a shared *tracking subject* that cannot be found:

```
Shared ${subject} follow expired
Shared ${subject} could not be restored — feed unavailable
Shared ${subject} is unavailable
```

and `:214-255` already solves the hard part — deferring the notice until the startup cover clears, with a generation counter so a stale verdict cannot replace a newer one (`canPresentDeferredStatusNotice`). A fourth message of the same shape, for the whole-payload case, needs a consumer rather than new machinery. `layerState.js:1246-1256` shows the same care about wording, distinguishing `expired` from `unavailable` by the share's own age.

### Scope, measured against the PRs in flight

- #744 raises `MAX_ENABLED_LAYERS_CHARS` from 64 to 4096 and widens tokens to `/^[a-z0-9]{1,2}$/`. That **removes the over-cap row** of the table above for any realistic layer count.
- The unknown-token rows are unaffected by it: a typo, a URL truncated by a chat client, or a link minted by a newer build and opened by an older one all still land on the same silent path. The code comment quoted above names two of those three itself.
- #760 was closed by its author in favour of #744.
- #658 is about allocation and contention; this is neither.

Credit where it is due: @KnottyDyes described this same silent drop independently, in the #658 thread and again in the note closing #760 — "restoration drops the whole layer payload rather than salvaging a prefix, with nothing surfaced to the user."

### What I would send

A consumer for the existing flag plus one message in the existing shape, routed through the notice path that is already there. Wording is yours to pick — I would rather match your three than invent a fourth style.

@bilawalsidhu @manjunath22466 — I offered this on #744 and nobody has had a chance to answer yet, so I have opened it rather than let it sit in a review thread. If you would rather fold it into #744 or drop it, close this and I will follow that instead.

`audio.input.transcription` is never configured, so the adapter's user-transcript branch cannot fire
body:
The Realtime session the server mints never configures input audio transcription, so one branch of the event adapter cannot be reached. Turning it on is not a one-line change, which is why I am asking rather than sending a PR.

### Measured

`server/providers/openai/realtime.js:91` builds `sessionConfig`. Its `audio` block (`:103-114`) gives `input` exactly two keys:

```js
audio: {
  input: {
    noise_reduction: { type: 'near_field' },
    turn_detection: { … },
  },
  output: { voice },
},
```

There is no `transcription` key, and OpenAI's documentation states that "configuration for input audio transcription defaults to off and can be set to null to turn off once on."

`src/voice/realtimeEvents.js:6-13` is the only place a user-role transcript is produced:

```js
if (type === 'conversation.item.input_audio_transcription.completed')
  return { type: 'transcript', role: 'user', text: payload.transcript || '', final: true, itemId: … };
```

That event only arrives when transcription is configured, so with the session above the branch never runs. Assistant transcripts are unaffected — they come from the `response.output_audio_transcript.*` family a few lines below.

Two supporting counts, so the scope is not overstated:

- `transcription` appears **twice** in `src/` and `server/`: that adapter line and one test. It is listened for, never configured.
- `\blanguage\b` appears **twice** across `src/voice/` and `server/`, both `'accept-language': 'en'` in `server/providers/regional/place.js:127,177`. No language hint is sent to the model on any path.

### What is *not* broken

Nothing visible today. The only production subscriber, `src/voice/sessionCommands.js:44-45`, returns unless `event.type === 'state'`, so no transcript of either role reaches the UI. This is about the documented session contract — `src/voice/session.js:5` lists `transcript` among the events an alternate adapter can rely on — rather than a user-facing defect. I would rather say that plainly than dress it up.

### The part that needs your decision, not mine

Enabling `audio.input.transcription` requires naming a transcription **model** (`gpt-live-transcribe`, `gpt-transcribe`). That is a second billed model in the session, and the spend guard does not know it exists:

- `src/voice/voiceCost.js` meters exactly two ids — `gpt-realtime-2` and `gpt-realtime-2.1-mini` — with rates marked verified on 2026-08-18.
- Zero transcription model ids appear anywhere in `src/voice/` or `server/`.
- The meter is deliberately conservative: *"An unrecognised id bills at the most expensive known rates rather than guessing cheap — under-metering is what lets a cap be overrun"* (`voiceCost.js:137-138`).

Whether a transcription model's tokens land in the same session `usage` payload that meter reads, I could not verify: I have no Realtime key, so I cannot run `scripts/qa-voice-wav.mjs` or inspect a live session. That seems like the thing worth knowing before switching it on, and it is your call rather than mine.

One more wrinkle if you do want it: the field name depends on the model. `gpt-live-transcribe` takes `languages` as an array of codes; the other transcription models take a single `language` in ISO-639-1. So a passthrough has to know which model it is configuring.

### If you want it, the shape already exists

Six environment variables already follow one pattern — read in `realtime.js` at `:63`, `:69`, `:71`, `:78`, `:87` against a `*_DEFAULT` in `server/providers/openai/constants.js` at `:5`, `:7`, `:9`, `:11`, `:13`, `:15`. An `OPENAI_REALTIME_LANGUAGE` would sit in that row, and omitting the `transcription` key entirely when the variable is unset keeps the minted request byte-identical to today's.

### What I am not claiming, including the part that argues against me

I have not measured any accuracy change. OpenAI's documentation says a language hint "will improve accuracy and latency" — their claim, not a number I produced, and I would not put it in a PR description as if it were mine.

More to the point, the same documentation limits what a language hint could buy here: "input audio transcription is not native to the model, since the model consumes audio directly. Transcription runs asynchronously through the `/audio/transcriptions` endpoint and should be treated as guidance of input audio content rather than precisely what the model heard."

So a language hint would improve the *displayed transcript*, not the model's understanding of a spoken command. If the value of this is better recognition of place names in voice commands, that reasoning does not survive that paragraph, and I would rather say so here than have it found in review. It also explains the cost point above: the transcription runs as a separate asynchronous call, not as part of the audio the realtime model already consumed.

### Three ways this could go

1. Configure transcription behind an environment variable, accepting the second model's cost and metering it.
2. Leave the session as it is and treat `realtimeEvents.js:6-13` as reserved for an alternate adapter that does enable transcription — in which case a one-line comment saying so would have saved me this issue.
3. Remove the branch as dead code.

I am happy to send whichever you prefer, but I cannot pick between them from the outside — 1 costs money, 2 and 3 disagree about whether the session contract means to include user transcripts at all.

title: CHANGELOG.md is the most frequent merge conflict across open PRs — 40 of 82, and the only conflict in 6
body:
`CONTRIBUTING.md` asks, for any runtime-behaviour change: *"update `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md` and
`CHANGELOG.md` in the same PR."* New entries go at the top of `CHANGELOG.md`, so two PRs in flight
write into the same few lines and git has nothing to merge on.

Measured rather than guessed, against `main` at `b210ab0`. For each of the 82 open PRs GitHub
reports as `CONFLICTING` that aren't mine, `git merge-tree --write-tree main <pr head>`:

- `CHANGELOG.md` is in the conflict set of **40** — more than any other path in the repo
- for **6** it is the *only* conflict: #741, #740, #733, #693, #634, #607

Two of those are yours: #741, whose three checks are green, and #740 as a draft.

#607 shows the shape. Git merges seven files without help and stops on one:

```
$ git merge-tree --write-tree main <#607 head>
Auto-merging .env.example
Auto-merging CHANGELOG.md
CONFLICT (content): Merge conflict in CHANGELOG.md
Auto-merging DATA_SOURCES.md
Auto-merging docs/CURRENT-STATE.md
Auto-merging scripts/format-scope.json
Auto-merging scripts/package-boundaries.json
Auto-merging server/providers/cctv/catalog.js
Auto-merging src/data/dataCredits.js
```

`DATA_SOURCES.md`, `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md` and the camera catalog all merge cleanly. The one file
that doesn't is the flat list.

Between 10 and 24 September `CHANGELOG.md` took 164 non-merge commits on `main`, 70 of which begin
their first hunk inside the first six lines — roughly five a day writing into the same window.
`README.md` took 12 commits over the same period. The median gap between two such top-of-file
inserts landing on `main` is 42 minutes (mean 7.8 hours, 2.8 a day over the last 26 days — they
arrive in bursts), so rebasing past one of these conflicts buys a mergeable state the next entry can
take back the same afternoon.

**One file per entry** removes it:

- a PR adds `changelog.d/<pr-number>-<slug>.md` instead of editing `CHANGELOG.md`
- a release concatenates that directory into `CHANGELOG.md` and empties it

Distinct filenames never conflict, and the PR number makes them distinct for free. The trade-off is
that between releases the pending entries live in a directory rather than at the top of the file,
and the release step is what puts them back.

Narrower than it may look: this unblocks the 6 outright and removes one conflict from the other 34.
The next-largest cluster — `src/data/layerState.test.mjs` (24) and `src/data/layerState.js` (20) —
is the share-link token contention I filed separately as #658, and it needs a different fix.

Disclosure: I have open PRs in this state, so I'm not a disinterested party; the 82 above exclude
mine. If you want the change I'll send `changelog.d/`, the assembly script and the
`CONTRIBUTING.md` edit as one PR.

title: fix(styles): keep Snow wind sway bounded over time
body:
## Problem

In the Snow style, the flakes speed up sideways the longer the app stays open.

`snowLayer` in `src/styles/snow.js` does:

```glsl
float windForce = sin(time * 0.5 + layer * 3.14) * (0.05 + wind * 0.2);
snowUV.x += time * windForce;
```

That makes the offset `time · sin(0.5·time + φ) · k`, so its rate of change, `k·sin(…) + 0.5·k·time·cos(…)`, grows linearly with `time`. `time` is seconds since `VisualEffectsController` was created (`startTime = wallNow()` in `src/ui/visualEffects.js`), not since Snow was selected. So how the effect looks depends on how long the session has been running:

| session age | peak sideways speed at default Wind (0.5) | at Wind 1.0 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 10 s | 0.76 cells/s | 1.3 cells/s |
| 1 min | 4.5 cells/s | 7.5 cells/s |
| 5 min | 22.5 cells/s | 37.5 cells/s |
| 30 min | 135 cells/s | 225 cells/s |

A layer spans 4–8 cells across the screen. After a few minutes the snow is thrashing several screen widths per second and reversing every ~6 s.

## Change

Keep the swaying velocity the code meant to have (`sin(0.5·time + φ) · k`), and apply its integral as the offset:

```glsl
float windForce = 0.05 + wind * 0.2;
snowUV.x -= 2.0 * cos(time * 0.5 + layer * 3.14) * windForce;
```

The peak sideways speed is now `k` (0.15 cells/s at default Wind, 0.25 at max) at every session age, and the offset stays within ±2k. The Wind slider still scales the sway, and the vertical fall and per-flake jitter are unchanged.

## Validation

Run locally on Node 24.21.0, macOS (Metal ANGLE):

- `npm run build`: passes.
- `npm test`: 5065 tests, 0 failures.
- `npm run format:check`: clean.
- `npm run test:track` against the dev server: 109 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped.
- `node scripts/qa-visual-effects.mjs` (the gate covering `src/styles/`): 23/23 PASS, including `snow: only the selected style remains visible` and `snow: the animation clock follows visible animated stages`, with no uncaught browser errors.

title: feat: add Vigo (Galicia) traffic camera pack
body:
## Summary
Adds a new CCTV source pack for **Concello de Vigo** (Galicia, Spain) traffic cameras, following the same pattern as the Calgary/DriveBC packs.

- Camera list: public, keyless ArcGIS FeatureServer (`camaras-trafico`) on `datos.vigo.org` — ~59 cameras citywide, also mirrored on the [CKAN open-data portal](https://datos-ckan.vigo.org/dataset/t-camaras).
- Frames: stills on `camaras.vigo.org`, updated roughly every minute.
- License: CC BY 4.0, attribution required ("Fuente de los datos: Ayuntamiento de Vigo") — added to DATA_SOURCES.md.
- Disable independently with `CCTV_VIGO_ENABLED=0`.

## A shared fix along the way
The Vigo host has two quirks discovered while wiring this up:
1. The dataset publishes `http://` frame URLs, but the host only answers on HTTPS (plain HTTP fails outright, no redirect). Fixed by upgrading + pinning to `https://camaras.vigo.org/` before registration, same as the Calgary pack does for its own HTTP→HTTPS quirk.
2. The host serves a valid JPEG with **no `Content-Type` header at all**. Rather than special-case Vigo, I added a magic-byte sniff fallback (`sniffImageContentType` in `server/providers/cctv/media.js`) that only kicks in when the header is missing/wrong, and only ever accepts real image signatures (JPEG/PNG/GIF/WEBP) — never a way to relax what gets proxied. This should help any other misconfigured city host in the future.

## Testing
- Verified locally: `npm run dev`, CCTV layer on, cameras render over Vigo and frames load.
- `npm run build`, `npm test`, `npm run format:check` all green.
- The `npm test` run has 6 pre-existing failures unrelated to this change (reproduced identically on a clean `main` via `git stash`), so not introduced by this PR.
- Didn't run `scripts/qa-cctv-v2.mjs` (Windows dev environment); happy to run it if requested.

title: fix(ui): re-solve the Cockpit utility strip on a window resize
body:
Shrinking the browser window in Cyber HUD can leave the collapsed **Live Signals** launcher off-screen and unclickable, until something unrelated happens to move it.

## What is wrong

`CockpitView` owns the utility strip's anchor and republishes it on a layout tick. A window resize was not one of those ticks: `applicationShell`'s resize handler scheduled the two panel rails and the CCTV viewport, and nothing else reaches `scheduleContextLayout()` except a cockpit disclosure change and the Radio row refresh (`radioBindings` → `layoutCockpit`).

So after a resize the strip keeps the *previous* height's anchor. Below roughly 830px of browser height — the threshold `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md` already names — the collapsed Live Signals launcher stays at its old offset, past the bottom of the viewport, and `elementFromPoint` on its centre lands on something else. It comes back only when a radio refresh happens to tick the layout.

Measured at 1440 wide, Cyber HUD, Display expanded, Live Signals collapsed:

| viewport | `signal.bottom` | on screen | hittable |
|---|---|---|---|
| 987px | 809 | yes | yes |
| 720px | 809 — unchanged | **no** | **no** |
| 640px | 809 — unchanged | **no** | **no** |

The intent is already written down. `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md`: *"Cockpit owns the strip's anchor and republishes it on every layout tick"*. This restores that for resizes; the doc now names the resize alongside the HUD-transition and map-swap settling passes.

## The change

`_handleWindowResize()` runs `_scheduleAdaptivePanelLayout({ settle: true })` instead of scheduling the two rails by hand. That pass already exists and already covers both rails **and** Cockpit — it is what `visualSettings` uses — and its settle pass re-solves once a drag stops. The CCTV viewport sync is unchanged.

Net: two lines of behaviour, plus the handler moved out of the constructor into a method so it can be tested.

## Why the gate was flaky, and that it now is not

`scripts/qa-cockpit-utility.mjs` already asserts this ("Cyber collapsed Live Signals remains visible and reachable after resize to Npx"). It was intermittent because the Radio row refresh sometimes ticked the layout before the check read the rect — the bug hid itself.

Six runs of that gate before and after, on the same machine and server, counting failures by check name:

| | runs with a stale-geometry failure |
|---|---|
| `main` at `b210ab0` | **4 of 6** — 720px five times, 640px once |
| this branch | **0 of 6** |

I first assumed a harness race and tried waiting for the geometry to settle, up to 2.4s. Two of six runs still failed with the rect frozen at the old value for the whole wait, which is what ruled the race out and pointed at the missing tick.

The gate still reports one failure on both trees — `runtime console remains clean`, a 404 on `tile.googleapis.com` and 403s on `/api/google/nearby-places` from a local key that is not enabled for those APIs. Unrelated to this change.

## Tests

`src/ui/shellLifecycle.test.mjs` gains one: a resize schedules the CCTV viewport sync, the adaptive pass, and the Cockpit anchor, and arms the settle pass. It fails against the previous handler and passes against this one — checked by reverting the handler and re-running.

## Gates

Node 24.20.0, on `cbda1de`: `doctor` · `format:check` · `check:boundaries` · `build` all clean · `npm test` **5,079 pass / 1 skipped / 0 fail** of 5,080 with `GEV_REQUIRE_ALLOCATION_GATE=1` · `test:track` **109 passed / 0 failed** · `scripts/qa-cockpit-utility.mjs`, the feature gate for this area, as above.

On ARM Linux the browser gates need `PUPPETEER_EXECUTABLE_PATH`: Chrome for Testing publishes no linux-arm64 build, so the cached binary is x86-64 and `existsSync()` accepts it anyway.

title: feat(tooling): one changelog file per pull request
body:
Implements #781. A pull request adds `changelog.d/<pull request>-<slug>.md` instead of editing the top of `CHANGELOG.md`; a release concatenates the directory into it.

| `CHANGELOG.md` | **41** of 85 | **6** — #741, #733, #693, #634, #625, #607 |
| `src/data/layerState.test.mjs` | 25 | 0 |
| `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md` | 23 | 1 — #780 |
| `DATA_SOURCES.md` | 22 | 0 |
| `src/data/layerState.js` | 20 | 0 |

Median conflict paths per pull request: 4.

Rule 3 names two files, and they behave differently. `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md` merges cleanly for 23 of the 41 that conflict on `CHANGELOG.md` — its edits land in the section for the area you touched, so two pull requests collide only when the areas do. New `CHANGELOG.md` entries all go to the same few lines at the top, whatever the change was about. That is the whole of the difference, and it is why this PR touches one of the two.

The layer-state pair is the share-link token contention I filed separately as #658; it needs a different fix.

Disclosure: #781 measured 82 / 40 / 6 at `b210ab0`. The set of only-`CHANGELOG.md` pull requests has churned since — #740 left, #625 arrived — while the count held. The numbers above are the fresh ones.

## What changes

For a contributor, rule 3 becomes: update `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md` as before, and put the changelog entry in `changelog.d/<pull request>-<slug>.md` rather than in `CHANGELOG.md`. Nobody edits both — that would recreate the conflict.

For a release:

```
npm run changelog:check   # list the batch and the order it would take
npm run changelog         # splice it into CHANGELOG.md and empty the directory
```

Newest pull request number first, filename as the tie-break. An empty directory is a no-op, so the step is safe to run unconditionally.

## Fragment text is copied through unchanged

Apart from trailing whitespace. `src/annotations/drawTool.test.mjs` reads `CHANGELOG.md` as prose: it finds `DISPLAY ▸ **Draw**`, takes the next 1200 characters and asserts that window never says GeoJSON. An assembler that reflowed an entry could push text across that window. So fragments are also deliberately outside `scripts/format-scope.json` — `npm run format` never touches one.

The same constraint has a contributor-facing consequence, now written down in `CONTRIBUTING.md` and `changelog.d/README.md`: a documentation claim that needs a regression test should assert against `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md` or `README.md`, which a pull request still edits directly. A fragment is not in `CHANGELOG.md` until release, so a test of that shape cannot see it.

## How a bad fragment gets caught

The assembler validates the whole batch before writing anything, and refuses rather than guessing: a filename that is not `<pull request>-<slug>.md`, or two fragments claiming one pull request number, stops the run and names the files.

Two of the tests run that check over the *real* `changelog.d/`, so a fragment the release could not assemble fails `npm test` — which CI runs — in the pull request that adds it, rather than at release time when its author has moved on. Verified by mutation: dropping `changelog.d/notes.md` into the tree fails the suite, and so does a second fragment claiming a number another already has.

The other mutations the tests were checked against: sorting ascending instead of descending (2 fail), removing the duplicate-number guard (2 fail), `--check` writing to disk (1 fail), and an assembler that reflows a fragment instead of only trimming its trailing whitespace (1 fail — the verbatim test uses a wrapped, indented, two-paragraph entry precisely so that mutation cannot survive it).

## What this does not do

It does not retroactively unblock the 41. Each still needs its entry moved into a fragment once — a three-line change their authors or an integrator can make while resolving anything else. What it removes is the recurrence. Ruler: `git log main --no-merges --since=2026-09-10 --until=2026-09-25 -- CHANGELOG.md`, 158 commits, of which 60 have their first hunk beginning at or before line 6 — about four a day writing into the same window, so rebasing past one of these conflicts today buys a mergeable state that the next entry can take back the same afternoon.

Disclosure on that pair: #781 published 164 and 70 for the same window. I cannot reproduce those figures under the ruler above, or under three variants of it (with merges: 179; `--until=2026-09-24`: 154; `--first-parent`: 37). 158 and 60 are what I measure today and what I stand behind; I'll correct #781 rather than leave the older pair standing.

## Dogfood

This pull request carries its own entry as `changelog.d/787-changelog-fragments.md` and does not touch `CHANGELOG.md`. Adding it needs the number, which only exists once the pull request is open, so the fragment arrives in a second commit — a small, honest cost of numbering by pull request, and the reason `changelog.d/README.md` says to push first and add the fragment after.

Checked against the consumer above rather than asserted: assembling this fragment moves the `DISPLAY ▸ Draw` marker in `CHANGELOG.md` by 533 bytes, exactly the length of the spliced entry, and the 1200-character window `drawTool.test.mjs` slices after that marker comes out byte-identical.

## Gates

Node 24.20.0, Linux aarch64. `doctor` · `format:check` · `check:boundaries` · `build` all exit 0. `npm test` with `GEV_REQUIRE_ALLOCATION_GATE=1`: **5,088 pass / 1 skipped / 0 fail** of 5,089, plus the 1 + 13 allocation budgets green. `npm run test:track`: **109 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped**.

No feature gate owns this area, so the nearest one: `node scripts/qa-l9-matrix.mjs --only A` — the release-candidate repo group, which contains the only QA coupling to this file (**A7**, public-facing files present, checks `CHANGELOG.md` exists) — **9 of 9 PASS**, A7 and the private-name scan A6 included.

## Credit

@kvnloo audited the consumers on #781 and set the shape this implements: fragments are pull-request input, the flat file is release output, nobody edits both, numeric-prefix sort with a filename tie-break, loud failure on duplicates. The `drawTool.test.mjs` constraint above is the one consumer that audit and mine between them turned up that changes the design rather than the count.

We both said on #781 that we'd wait for maintainer direction rather than open a competing implementation. I'm opening this because a concrete diff is easier to say no to than a proposal, not to pre-empt that call — it is seven files and reversible, and I'll close it without argument if you'd rather not take the workflow change, or rework it if you want a different shape.

title: feat(i18n): add French, Spanish, German, Portuguese localization
body:
## Summary

- Adds a complete i18n framework (`src/i18n/index.js`) with `t()`, `setLocale()`, `initI18n()` supporting dynamic locale switching and localStorage persistence
- Creates 5 locale dictionaries (en, fr, es, de, pt) with **411 translation keys each** ( all 409 common keys plus 2 new voice-control keys )
- Converts **9 HTML templates** to use `data-i18n` / `data-i18n-aria` attributes for static UI text
- Converts **20+ JS files** to use `t()` calls replacing hardcoded English strings
- Covers all UI surfaces: welcome, provider settings, command dock, context, display controls, layer panels, scene chrome, cockpit, HUD, voice controls, replay, CCTV, and more

## Locale coverage

| Locale | Keys | Status |
|--------|------|--------|
| English (base) | 411 | Complete |
| Français | 411 | Complete |
| Español | 411 | Complete |
| Deutsch | 411 | Complete |
| Português | 411 | Complete |

## Files changed

- **New:** `src/i18n/index.js`, `src/i18n/locales/{en,fr,es,de,pt}.json`

title: docs(pinokio): distinguish embedded-browser stutter from hardware limits
body:
Refs #365.

A Pinokio 8.2.0 Linux user reported severe stutter in Pinokio's embedded app view, then opened the exact same running local server URL in their normal browser and found the rendering smooth.

This documents that troubleshooting split without inventing a minimum hardware requirement:

- Quick Start tells a choppy Pinokio user to open the launcher-provided local URL in a normal hardware-accelerated browser before concluding the GPU is unsupported.
- `docs/PERFORMANCE.md` now asks future measurements to record embedded Pinokio vs external-browser execution as part of the test context.
- The existing M5/Chrome baseline remains explicitly a baseline, not a minimum specification.

Docs only; no runtime behavior or provider contract changes.

## Credit / provenance

- @BennyBread reported #365 and supplied the key observation that the same running GEV instance stuttered in Pinokio's embedded view but ran smoothly in a normal browser. This docs change preserves that distinction rather than inferring a hardware minimum.

title: feat(layers): add QLD road events layer (QLDTraffic)
body:
Adds a keyless **QLD Road Events** layer (Events group, off by default) that shows live QLDTraffic incidents across Queensland: crashes, hazards, flooding, congestion, special events and roadworks.

No other open PR covers road events. #752 adds QLDTraffic *cameras*; this is the incidents feed and doesn't touch the CCTV code.

### Server: `server/providers/qldRoadEvents.js` → `/api/qld-road-events`
- Reads the fixed upstream `api.qldtraffic.qld.gov.au/v2/events`. The default key is the **public shared key published in the QLDTraffic API specification** for developers without their own key (limit is 100 req/min across all its users). `QLDTRAFFIC_API_KEY` overrides it. #752 uses the same env name.
- Normalizes on the server into compact records. Every GeoJSON geometry type is flattened to markers and polylines (the live feed today has MultiLineString 341, MultiPoint 152 and GeometryCollection 6). Lines are Douglas–Peucker simplified (~11 m) and capped at 200 vertices per line, 600 per event and 60k per snapshot. Today's 2.1 MB feed comes out at ~530 KB.
- One 2-minute snapshot is shared by all clients, with request coalescing. A failed read backs off for 60 s, and the last good snapshot is served as stale for up to 6 h. 12 MB body cap, 30 req/min per client.

### Client: `src/layers/qldRoadEvents/` (records / cards / source / index) + `src/app/layers/qldRoadEvents.js`
- Markers are coloured and glyphed by type. Roadworks are small, faded diamonds with dashed lines so ~340 long-running works don't bury the incidents.
- Markers beyond the horizon are hidden, and event lines drape on terrain and 3D tiles.
- Clicking a marker or line opens a card with type/subtype, road, locality, impact, advice and update age. Clicking the card opens qldtraffic.qld.gov.au. Card lines wrap at 64 characters because the overlay host draws one line per entry; unwrapped street lists made the card wide enough to slide under the left rail.
- The panel row shows a per-type legend with counts.
- Registered in the catalog, layer panel, data credits and share-link state.

### Share-link token and the ledger tests (separate commit)
Following CONTRIBUTING after rebasing on #744, this takes the next free token, **`0`**, and reserves it in `layerStateTokenReservations.json`. `npm run layer-token:check -- --base-ref origin/main` passes (28 published, 1 new).

Taking `0` breaks seven #744 scenario tests that aren't about this layer. They claim literal `'0'`/`'3'` and pin the ledger size (28) and the full-registry `l` length (67), which only holds while `0` is unreserved. The first commit, `test(layer-state): derive scenario tokens from the live ledger`, makes them take tokens from the ledger's free digits, compare the ledger size to the JSON rows, keep every legacy token pinned, and compute the `l` length from the registry. The rules they test are unchanged, and on today's ledger they claim the same tokens as before. That commit passes on its own against current `main`. Without it, every future layer PR would hit the same seven failures. I'm happy to split it into its own PR if you'd prefer.

Also, `npm run layer-token:next` can't run while the new registry entry is still unreserved, because importing `layerState.js` throws `Unreserved layer-state token` first. So the documented step "run the helper, then add the reservation" only works if you run the helper before adding the registry entry. That might be worth a line in CONTRIBUTING.

### Not included
Voice and analyst integration. Adding them means changing the voice schema enums (and the test pinning their hash), the tool descriptions and the analyst layer list, so they're better as a follow-up.

### Validation
- New unit tests for records (every geometry type, simplification, caps, malformed input), cards (styles, wrapping), the source, the layer lifecycle, and the proxy (caching, coalescing, stale serving, backoff, limits, body cap).
- `npm run format:check`, `npm run check:boundaries`, `npm run layer-token:check -- --base-ref origin/main`, `npm test` (5,095 pass, 0 fail) and `npm run build` are all green.
- Checked in a running dev server over Brisbane on Windows/Chrome: 496 live events loaded with the per-type legend, markers sat on the ground, clicking the Suncorp Stadium special event opened the correct card (after the wrap fix it stays clear of both rails), and there were no console errors.
- **Not run:** `npm run test:track` and the `qa-*` gates, and I didn't check the Google 3D tiles view (no Google key on the test machine).

Data: QLDTraffic, Queensland Government, CC BY 4.0. Added to DATA_SOURCES.md, data credits and docs/CURRENT-STATE.md.

title: feat(a11y): UI text size setting (#659)
body:
Adds a **Text size** setting to the Display panel: Default (100%), Large (115%) and Larger (130%).

This follows the plan @abdulwaarith0 set out in the #659 thread: the setting lives in Display, it persists under `gev:text-scale:v1`, it scales through one `--gev-text-scale` root property, and it covers panels first, with globe labels as a follow-up. @abdulwaarith0, you offered to take this on 25 Sep. If you already have work in progress, I'm happy to close this in favour of yours or fold anything useful from here into it.

### What changes
- Every stylesheet font size is `calc(<size> * var(--gev-text-scale))`, with `--gev-text-scale: 1` on `:root`, so 100% renders exactly as before. Icon glyphs and `#cesium-credits` aren't scaled (the attribution keep-out test pins the credit line's measured height). Spacing and panel widths aren't scaled either.
- `src/uiTextScale.js` owns the steps, normalization (ids, factors or percentages, clamped and snapped) and best-effort `localStorage` persistence. If storage is blocked or throws, it falls back to 100%. The setting is per viewer and isn't part of share links.
- The layout floors that stand in for unmeasured text now scale with the chosen step: the 96 px usable panel floor in both rails, and the Cyber Cockpit footer fallbacks (60/44/64 px). Measured heights still take precedence, and nothing changes at 100%.
- Globe labels (world overlay, detection, Cesium labels) are drawn on canvas and keep their size. Scaling them needs the overlay allocator's metrics to follow the font, so they're left for a follow-up.
- 130% is the top step because the fixed-width panels (272 px Display, 312 px Cyber rail) don't scale; beyond that, their mono labels stop fitting.

### Reviewing
There are two commits:
- `style(ui)`: the mechanical CSS rewrite only. A postcss script wrapped each font size, and every added line carries `var(--gev-text-scale)`. The only other change in it is `src/radioMarkup.test.mjs`, which pinned `font-size: 9px` literally.
- `feat(a11y)`: the setting, persistence and layout floors.

A unit test fails if a future stylesheet font size skips the scale.

### Validation
- 13 new tests in `src/uiTextScale.test.mjs` (normalization, persistence failure paths, root application, the stylesheet guard, scaled layout floors), plus the existing layout, display and markup tests.
- `npm run format:check`, `npm run check:boundaries` and `npm run build` are green. `npm test`: 5,078 pass. The one failure was the timing-sensitive `cctvMediaRange` test "a live feed that keeps producing is not cut off by the idle deadline", which passed 3/3 when rerun alone. It isn't touched by this PR.
- Checked in a running dev server (Windows/Chrome, desktop width) at 130%: the header, HUD, left Data Layers rail and right Display rail all scaled with no overlap or clipping. Switching back to Default restored 100%.
- **Not checked:** narrow (≤720 px) layouts, the cockpit views, the Cyber theme, and the first-run / Provider Settings dialogs at 115% and 130%. `npm run test:track` and the `qa-*` gates weren't run either.

Closes #659
