title: fix(build): discover unit tests under server/, not only src/
body:
## Summary

- `npm test` is the only suite CI runs, and `discoverUnitTestFiles` walked `src/` alone. `server/providers/transitHistory.test.mjs` has therefore never executed, in CI or locally, since it was added.
- Its 8 tests pass, so this was silent coverage loss rather than a hidden failure: in review the file reads like covered code, and it never ran anywhere.
- Add `server/` to a named `UNIT_TEST_ROOTS` list, and pin the property with a test that walks the repository itself and compares the two sets, so a tree added later without updating the roots fails loudly instead of going quiet.

## Problem

`discoverUnitTestFiles` built its file list from one directory:

```js
const sourceRoot = path.join(root, 'src');
…
visit(sourceRoot);
```

Measured on `main`: 415 `*.test.mjs` files exist in the repository, and the runner returns 414. The missing one is `server/providers/transitHistory.test.mjs`.

## Solution

- `UNIT_TEST_ROOTS = ['src', 'server']`, iterated in stable order; discovery is otherwise unchanged.
- A new case in `src/unitTestRunner.test.mjs` walks the repository (skipping `node_modules`, `dist`, `build`, `public` and dot-directories) and asserts every file it finds is one the runner returns. It compares sets, so a failure names the file rather than disagreeing about a count.

## Validation

- Unit tests: 5,090 before, 5,099 after; 0 failures, 1 skipped. The difference is the 8 tests in that file plus the regression test added here.
- The newly discovered file passes on its own: 8 tests, 0 failures.
- Mutation checks, both caught: restoring the roots to `['src']` fails the new test; adding a stray `*.test.mjs` outside the roots fails it too.
- `npm run doctor -- --json`, `npm run format:check`, `npm run check:boundaries`, `npm run layer-token:check -- --base-ref origin/main` and `npm run build` all pass.
- Node 24.20.0, Linux.

## Remaining limitation

`discoverUnitTestFiles` reads each root directly, so a caller invoking it from a root without a `server/` directory would throw rather than skip. Nothing in the repository does that: `npm test` and `scripts/qa-l9-matrix.mjs` both run it from the repository root.

title: feat(server): describe the /api mount table as data, and pin it with a test
body:
## Summary

- Answering "what does this server expose, and in what order?" meant reading 29 provider files, and the answer moved whenever one of them did. `server/apiRoutes.js` records the `/api` mounts in install order with the plugin that installs each.
- The test does not read that table back. It installs the real plugin chain against a recording stub, honouring each plugin's `apply`, and asserts the sequences match — so the table describes the server rather than an intention.
- Three properties nothing currently protects are pinned by it: install order, prefix-boundary matching, and the fact that dev and preview are different surfaces.

## Problem

Three behaviours are load-bearing and undocumented, all verified against running servers rather than read off the source:

1. **Install order.** Connect runs the FIRST middleware whose prefix matches. `/api` — the catch-all that answers `Unknown API route` — behaves as a fallback only because `server/standalone/vite.config.js` installs it last. Moved earlier it swallows every route below it, while each individual handler still looks correct in isolation.
2. **Prefix matching ends at a segment boundary, and a dot counts as one.** On a running dev server: `/api/gbfs.json` reaches the GBFS handler (400 `Invalid GBFS upstream URL`), while `/api/gbfsXYZ` does not and falls through (404 `Unknown API route`).
3. **Dev and preview are not the same surface.** 34 mounts under `npm run dev`, 32 under `npm run preview`. On a running preview server, `/api/setup/status` answers 404 `Unknown API route` while `/api/opensky` answers 200. `gev-key-setup` excludes itself from preview twice over, deliberately: it declares `apply: command === 'serve' && !isPreview`, and it also defines only `configureServer`, because — as its own note records — a bare `apply: 'serve'` would still configure under preview.

## Solution

- `server/apiRoutes.js`: the mounts as data, in install order, with `serveOnly` on the two dev-only rows, plus `matchApiRoute`, which encodes the boundary rule the tests pin.
- `src/tooling/apiRoutes.test.mjs`: builds both chains from the real plugins and compares sequences; checks the fallback is last and unique, that no mount is duplicated, and that every `/api` path the browser bundle references resolves to a provider rather than the fallback.
- Because either of key setup's two exclusions alone yields the same 32 mounts, the chain comparison cannot see one of them disappear. A separate case asserts both, so neither can be dropped silently.

One thing the table corrects: `/api/route` is mounted by `overpass-proxy`, though its handler lives in `places/routes.js`.

## Validation

- Unit tests: 5,090 before, 5,097 after; 0 failures, 1 skipped.
- Mutation checks, all caught: moving the catch-all to the front (4 cases fail), a wrong plugin attribution, dropping `.` from the boundary rule, deleting a row, dropping `serveOnly`, removing `apply` from the key-setup plugin, and giving that plugin a `configurePreviewServer`.
- Boundary and surface claims re-measured against running `npm run dev` and `npm run preview` servers immediately before this was written, not taken from source reading.
- `npm run doctor -- --json`, `npm run format:check`, `npm run check:boundaries`, `npm run layer-token:check -- --base-ref origin/main` and `npm run build` all pass.
- Node 24.20.0, Linux.

## Remaining limitation

The table lists **mounts**, not every addressable path: several handlers route internally on a sub-path (`/health`, `/image`, `/manifest`, `/sources`, `/stations`, `/status`, `/tile`, `/track`), so the set of URLs that answer is larger than 34 and is not described here. `matchApiRoute` is used by the tests and is otherwise not yet called from runtime code; it exists so the matching rule is written down in one place instead of being rediscovered.

title: fix(server): declare the method contract on the three read-only query proxies
body:
## Summary

- `/api/opensky`, `/api/adsblol/mil` and `/api/route` answered any verb with the same body while ignoring the request entirely. Their siblings do not.
- All three are read-only query proxies, so they now answer `405 Method Not Allowed` to anything but `GET`, using the wording and shape `/api/geocode` already uses.
- The refusal comes first, before rate limiting and before any upstream call, which the tests assert by stubbing `fetch` to throw.

## Problem

Measured against a running dev server on `main`, before the change:

| route | GET | POST | POST body |
|---|---|---|---|
| `/api/opensky` | 200 | **200** | 833,759 bytes of live state vectors |
| `/api/adsblol/mil` | 200 | **200** | 47,372 bytes |
| `/api/route` | 200 | **200** | full JSON answer |
| `/api/geocode` | 400 | 405 | — |
| `/api/weather` | 404 | 405 | — |
| `/api/transit` | 404 | 405 | — |

Nothing in the endpoint said whether a body was read or ignored, and a reader could not tell whether POST support was deliberate.

## Solution

A `req.method !== 'GET'` guard at the top of each of the three handlers, matching `server/providers/regional/place.js` in both wording and response shape. `/api/overpass` is deliberately POST-only and is untouched.

One existing fixture in `src/search/geospatial.test.mjs` built a request object without a `method`, which a real Node request always has; it now sets `GET`.

## Scope, stated plainly

This is a consistency and intent fix, not a security one. **No rate limiter was being bypassed.** `/api/route` already limits every request regardless of verb, and the two aircraft routes have no limiter at all — only 9s and 12s server-side caches, which bound upstream cost for any method.

No client is affected: every `method: 'POST'` call site in `src/` was resolved, and they target `/api/overpass`, `/api/openai/hud-summary`, `/api/realtime/debug-log`, `/api/setup/keys`, `/api/radio/click/`, or an external host. None targets these three routes.

## Validation

- Unit tests: 5,090 before, 5,092 after; 0 failures, 1 skipped.
- New cases assert 405 for POST, PUT, DELETE and PATCH on all three routes, with `fetch` stubbed to throw so the refusal is proven to precede any upstream work.
- Mutation checks, all caught: removing each of the three guards individually turns its test red.
- Re-measured on a running dev server after the change: GET still 200 on all three, POST 405 on all three, and `/api/overpass` (GET 405 / POST 400), `/api/geocode` and `/api/weather` unchanged.
- `npm run doctor -- --json`, `npm run format:check`, `npm run check:boundaries`, `npm run layer-token:check -- --base-ref origin/main` and `npm run build` all pass.
- Node 24.20.0, Linux.

## Remaining limitation

`HEAD` is refused along with the other verbs, because the guard copies the existing `req.method !== 'GET'` form used by the sibling proxies rather than introducing a second convention. If `HEAD` should be allowed, it should be allowed across all of them in one change.

title: feat(server): compress the cached OpenSky snapshot for clients that accept gzip
body:
## Summary

- `/api/opensky` now answers `Content-Encoding: gzip` to clients that offer gzip, and `Vary: Accept-Encoding` to every client. Measured on a live anonymous snapshot: **874,002 B to 258,012 B (3.39x)**.
- The frame is built once per upstream refresh, beside the cached body, not once per request, and off the event loop.
- A new `server/providers/common/compress.js` returns the body and the header that names it as one value, so an encoding header can never describe bytes other than the ones being sent.

## Problem

The OpenSky proxy holds its global snapshot for an adaptive 9-300 s TTL and served it uncompressed to every request. Browsers send `Accept-Encoding: gzip, deflate, br` on every one of those requests. No response anywhere in `server/` set `Content-Encoding` or `Vary`, so roughly 610 KB per response crossed the wire that did not have to.

## Solution

Compression is opt-in at the call site rather than a middleware. Two response paths in this tree must not be wrapped: `cctv/media.js` pipes a body and answers byte ranges with 206, and `wind/gfs.js` serves ranges too; seven providers additionally forward an upstream `content-type` verbatim, including already compressed binary. A general wrapper would have to special-case all of them. Compressing a body the proxy already holds and already caches has none of that risk, and the failure mode of missing a call site is a response that is merely uncompressed.

`encodedBody(req, identity, compressed)` returns `{ body, headers }` together, and every call site writes both in the same `writeHead`/`end` pair. All five bodies this route can answer with are covered: the fresh snapshot, the fresh-enough cache, the stale-during-cooldown cache, the error-path cache, and the regional adsb.lol fallback. Bodies that are *not* cached (auth failures, cooldown notices) are identified by comparing identity against the cached body, so an error can never be sent under the previous snapshot's frame.

`Accept-Encoding` is parsed against the `qvalue` grammar of RFC 9110 section 12.4.2 rather than with a numeric parse, so `q=0` refuses gzip and anything outside the grammar — `q=2`, `q=1oops`, four decimal places — is unreadable rather than rounded into acceptance. Unreadable means identity, which every client can decode.

Compression runs off the event loop. On this snapshot the synchronous call stalls every other in-flight request by **11.0 ms**; the asynchronous one stalls them by **0.9 ms** against a 0.3 ms quiet baseline, and costs the request that triggered the refresh about 5 ms it was already spending on the upstream fetch. The frame and the body it encodes are assigned in the same synchronous step after that await, so a request arriving mid-refresh reads the previous body with the previous body's frame and never a mismatched pair.

A frame is only kept when it is smaller than the body it encodes, so each cache grows by less than it already holds: about 250 KB beside the 860 KB snapshot, and the same bound applied per entry to the 80-entry regional LRU.

`Vary: Accept-Encoding` is sent on the identity branch as well as the compressed one. This route already answers `Cache-Control: no-store`, so no conformant shared cache stores either body today; the header is the correct negotiation signal regardless, and it is what keeps the two bodies distinguishable if that policy is ever relaxed.

## Validation

Rebased on `e7707d9a`; every number below was measured there, and the baselines were re-measured on an unmodified checkout of that same commit in the same environment.

- Live dev server, real anonymous OpenSky snapshot: `874,002 B` identity, `258,012 B` gzipped, **3.39x**, and `gunzip` of the compressed response is byte-identical (`cmp`) to the identity response.
- Same under `npm run preview`: a single gzip layer decoding to JSON in one pass, so Vite's own compression middleware correctly leaves an already-encoded response alone.
- 4 new tests (3 unit, 1 end-to-end through the route on its own module instance); suite 5384 to 5388, 0 failures.
- 13 mutations of the new code. 12 fail at least one test: dropping `Vary` from either branch, ignoring `Accept-Encoding`, ignoring `q=0`, matching `gzip` as a substring, reading a `q` value as a numeric prefix, letting an error body inherit the cached frame, dropping the size threshold, emitting a frame larger than the body, forgetting either cache fill, and sending the identity body under the compressed header. The 13th — replacing the asynchronous gzip with the synchronous one — survives, and cannot do otherwise: the two are indistinguishable at the behaviour layer, which is why the case for the asynchronous call is the event-loop measurement above and not a test.
- `npm run doctor`, `format:check`, `check:boundaries`, `layer-token:check`, `npm test`, `npm run build` pass on Node 24.20.0.
- Feature gates, per CONTRIBUTING: `npm run test:track` passes, 109 of 109. The two flights-layer gates that drive the OpenSky payload path behave identically with and without this change: `qa-sprites-b5` 8 passed / 1 failed and `qa-enrich-ambient` 7 passed / 4 failed on this branch, with the identical failure set (E5, E8, E10, E12) on the untouched base. Those failures are pre-existing and are the console-error assertions counting cross-origin 403s for imagery I hold no key for; the local server logged no 403 in either run.
- Worth saying plainly: all three harnesses install a `fetch` shim for `/api/opensky` inside the page, by design, so they show the flights layer is undisturbed but they do not exercise the transport. The transport evidence is the live run above.

## Remaining limitation

Only `/api/opensky` is covered. The same shape fits any proxy that caches a serialized body it owns, but each one needs its own call sites and its own tests, and the endpoints that pipe, serve ranges, or forward an upstream content-type are deliberately out of scope.

Brotli is not offered here. On this payload it is a real but modest further win and not a free one: quality 5 gives 239,360 B against gzip's 251,823 B on a snapshot of the same size at the same ~12 ms, and quality 11 reaches 194,241 B but costs 747 ms per refresh. Taking it means caching a second frame per body and a second negotiation branch, which deserves its own change measured on its own.

title: fix: fall back when photoreal tiles cannot draw
body:
## What this fixes

`loadPhotorealisticTileset` tries direct Google access, then Cesium ion, then
reports the keyless OSM route. The chain was already there, but its success test
was too loose: any tileset the provider resolved counted as a win.

Cesium can resolve a `Cesium3DTileset` whose root never arrived. `src/app/scene.js`
then sets `globe.show = false` on the strength of the object existing, so the
result is a hidden globe, no tiles, a loader line reporting success, and the ion
route never tried — a black screen with nothing said about it.

A rootless tileset is now a failed attempt: it is released, the reason is pushed
onto `errors`, and the loop moves to the next route. When no route can draw, the
existing keyless-globe branch runs and puts the last upstream error on the loader
line.

`root` is the check because Cesium populates it from the tileset JSON. With no
root there is nothing to traverse, so no tile is ever requested or drawn.

The change is contained to `loadPhotorealisticTileset`; no caller needed editing.

## Verification

Checked against real Cesium rather than only the test doubles. Driving actual
`createGooglePhotorealistic3DTileset` objects in the running app, a working
photoreal tileset has a populated `root` and reads as drawable, so a healthy
setup is never rejected by the new check.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `npm run doctor -- --json` | pass |
| `npm run format:check` | pass |
| `npm run check:boundaries` | pass |
| `npm run layer-token:check -- --base-ref origin/main` | 28 published, 0 new |
| `npm test` | 5374 passing, 0 failing |
| `npm run build` | pass |
| `npm run test:track` | 109 passed, 0 failed |
| `npm run qa:map-source-tray` | 82 passed, 0 failed |

Feature gate run: **`npm run qa:map-source-tray`**, the gate `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md`
names for map stack and photoreal fallback behaviour.

Five tests added to `src/mapStartup.test.mjs`: the drawability predicate,
fall-through to ion on a rootless direct tileset, the keyless route preserved
when every route is rootless, release of the rejected tileset, and no double
destroy on one already disposed. Existing fixtures gained a `root`, which is what
they were already asserting.

### Flake seen while verifying

`qa-map-source-tray` intermittently fails its final "no new page or console
errors" check on `net::ERR_FAILED` for `api.cesium.com/v1/assets/<n>/endpoint`,
with a different asset id each time. It reproduced on an unmodified `origin/main`
(81eb443) at about the same rate, and those endpoints answer HTTP 200 to `curl`,
so it looks like an in-flight ion request being aborted during rapid stack
switching rather than anything in this change. Flagging it rather than leaving it
as a surprise; happy to open a separate issue if that is useful.

## Notes

- Rebased onto `origin/main` e7707d9 on 2026-09-29 to clear a `CHANGELOG.md`
  conflict with the Overpass change. Both entries are kept; nothing upstream was
  dropped. All checks above were re-run on that base.

- Runtime behaviour changed, so `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md` and `CHANGELOG.md` are
  updated here.
- No data source added or changed, so `DATA_SOURCES.md` is untouched.
- Node 26.x was not run locally, as there is no toolchain for it on this machine.
  CI covers it, and the change adds no syntax the file did not already use.
- Nothing visual to screenshot: the change is only visible when photoreal fails,
  where it replaces a black screen with the keyless globe.

title: feat: hand selected hazards to Recent Imagery and nearby cameras
body:
## Problem

GEV already has the pieces for a useful crisis-evidence workflow, but they currently stop at layer selection:

- FIRMS fires can be selected with stable source-owned coordinates;
- Recent Imagery can open a validated 10 km box around a point;
- CCTV can select/focus cameras, but its existing nearest-camera path is viewer-relative.

For fire/crisis inspection, the useful next step is a small handoff from the selected hazard into those existing evidence views rather than a new humanitarian subsystem.

## Proposed interaction

On a supported hazard selection, offer:

- `RECENT IMAGERY`
- `NEARBY CAMERAS`

First implementation can stay conservative: remember only explicit successful choices locally and rank the usual action first next time. Do not auto-run anything yet.

## Reuse existing owners

- FIRMS keeps publishing the selected record / provenance.
- Recent Imagery keeps its own `boxFromPinAt(lon, lat)` 10 km policy.
- CCTV navigation owns nearest-camera math.
- DataLayerManager owns enables/persistence.
- existing panels own presentation.

One small CCTV generalization makes the camera handoff correct for any feature, not just hazards:

```js
nearestCameraIdToPoint(lat, lon)
focusNearestToPoint(lat, lon, options)
```

`nearestCameraIdToViewer()` can delegate to the same point owner, so there is no second distance implementation.

## Downstream evidence

I prototyped this on the fork in draft PR https://github.com/kvnloo/gods-eye-view/pull/16.

The downstream experiment currently covers:

- selected FIRMS fire -> Recent Imagery around the fire coordinate;
- selected FIRMS fire -> CCTV nearest the fire coordinate;
- local explicit-choice ranking (`imagery` / `cameras`);
- blocked/malformed storage fallback;
- invalid WGS84 target rejection;
- listener teardown;
- no new provider/feed/model/polling loop.

## Follow-up coverage

If this interaction is useful, fire-perimeter and earthquake selections can publish through the same neutral selected-entity lane instead of adding per-layer special cases.

## Scope

This is intended as a small product handoff between existing GEV features, not a new humanitarian mode or agent framework.

title: Scrollable location pills + a full pin/landmark editor
body:
## Summary

The location pill row overflows on most screens once a few cities are pinned — the bar caps at 720px — with no discoverable way to reach the rest. This adds:

- **Horizontal scroll**: a wheel gesture over the row, plus two always-visible arrow buttons (mask-gradient edge fade as a visual hint there's more).
- **A full editor for the row**, not just new pins:
  - `+` saves the current camera view as a new named pin.
  - Every pill — bundled city or custom pin — gets hover-revealed **rename** and **hide/delete** controls. Renaming or editing a *bundled* city writes a local override; the shipped entry in `locations.js` is never touched.
  - A hidden bundled city can be brought back via a "N hidden – restore" control next to `+`; an overridden (renamed/edited) bundled city gets a `↺` reset to discard the override and restore the shipped default.
  - The expanded landmark (POI) row gets its own add/rename/remove controls. A city always keeps at least one landmark, so the last one has no remove control.
- **Accurate pin capture**: a saved pin's lat/lon comes from `readCameraTargetFrame()` (already used by the orbit controller) — a ray-pick against the real terrain/3D-tile surface under the viewport center — rather than the camera's own ground projection, so it reproduces the exact view even at a steep tilt, not just the neighborhood.

## Design

All edits funnel through the existing `CITY_POIS` registry via two new tiny mutators in `locations.js` (`registerLocation`/`unregisterLocation`), so a new or edited entry is flyable, searchable and voice-addressable with **zero changes** to `flyToPresetLocation`/`flyToPOI`/search/voice paths — they already resolve against that registry. The new `src/services/customLocations.js` owns persistence: one `localStorage` key (`gev.customLocations.v1`) holding either a new pin or a bundled-city override, hydrated into the registry once at `_initLocationBar()`. A pristine snapshot of the bundled defaults is captured once at import time (before anything can mutate the live registry), which is what makes "reset to default" always possible. A missing/throwing `localStorage` (private browsing, storage full) is a silent no-op — edits still work for the rest of the session via the in-memory registry, they just don't persist.

Threaded through the existing `services` DI pattern (matching how `CITY_POIS`/`flyToPresetLocation` etc. already reach `LocationNavigation`) rather than a direct import, to respect the `application-components` package boundary — `customLocations.js` is added there alongside the other `src/services/*.js` entries it sits next to.

All new UI actions (add-pin, rename, add-landmark, rename-landmark) share one inline text input rather than one per action, since they're mutually exclusive — `LocationControls` tracks which is pending and dispatches on Enter/Escape.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run build`
- [x] `npm test` — 5107 tests passing (34 new: `locationControls.test.mjs`, `customLocations.test.mjs`, `locations.test.mjs`)
- [x] `npm run test:track` — 109/109 passing
- [x] `npm run format` / `npm run format:check`
- [x] `npm run check:boundaries`
- [x] `node scripts/qa-location-controls.mjs` — 12/12 passing (the feature-specific gate)
- [x] Manual verification in a live session: add/rename/hide/restore/reset on both bundled cities and custom pins, add/rename/remove landmarks, and a round-trip check (fly to a tilted view → save pin → fly elsewhere → fly back) confirming the resulting camera state matches exactly (`lat`/`lon`/`alt`/`heading`/`pitch` all identical)

`docs/CURRENT-STATE.md` and `CHANGELOG.md` updated in the same PR per the contributing guide.

title: fix(local-adsb): hold an altitude no aircraft could have reached
body:
Refs #714 (the altitude plausibility filter under "Next").

**Intent.** Stop Local ADS-B from drawing or reporting an altitude that no aircraft could have reached, whichever input it came from. The position check, the decoder, the feed route and the display motion are unchanged.

## Where the check goes, and why there

The DC-9 at 108,800 ft could not have come from the browser decoder. `decodeAltitude` handles only 25 ft (Q=1) altitudes, and those stop at 50,175 ft. UAT stops at 101,350 ft. A value of 108,800 ft is a multiple of 100, so it is a Gillham altitude relayed by a 1090 decoder feed.

That puts the check in the layer's per-aircraft ingest (`upsertMarker`), where the browser SDR and the feeds already meet. `LocalAdsbMotion` re-runs the position speed check for feed records in the same place.

## What it does

- **`localAdsbAltitudeIsPlausible(previous, next)`** in `src/sources/adsbRecords.js`, next to `localAdsbFixIsPlausible` and built the same way.
  - The allowance is 300 ft plus the climb covered over the elapsed time + 1 s.
  - The vertical-rate limit is 1.5 × the larger reported rate + 2,000 ft/min, or 12,500 ft/min when neither report has a rate.
- **`gateLocalAdsbAltitude(record, gate)`** keeps per-aircraft state, which the caller owns and drops with the marker.
  - **A refused report holds the last accepted altitude on the record itself.** The marker height, the card, the 3D-model ceiling and route plausibility therefore agree. Holding it only in the motion model would have put the marker at the right height while the card still said 108,800 ft.
  - **Only a newer `lastMessageAt` is judged.** The layer re-syncs the same record several times a second. Without this, one spike re-read three times would re-anchor onto the bad value.
  - **Three refusals in a row re-anchor**, using `LOCAL_ADSB_REANCHOR_AFTER` as positions do. A bad *first* altitude therefore clears itself within about 1.5 s.
  - **Surface reports pass unjudged.** A feed's `alt_baro: "ground"` is 0, not a barometric reading, and a landing at Denver is not a 5,600 ft drop.
- `getStats()` gains `rejectedAltitudes` next to `rejectedPositions`.

There is no absolute ceiling, because balloons do fly above 100,000 ft. The rate check catches the spike without hiding them.

## Verification

- **`npm test`:** 5,081 tests, 5,080 pass, 0 fail, 1 skipped (the existing Windows-only DACL test).
- **`npm run format:check`:** 1,090 files checked, exit 0.
- **`npm run check:boundaries`:** exit 0.
- **`npm run build`:** ✓.
- **New tests** (5): the vertical-rate allowance at its exact boundaries, the logged spike held and counted once across re-reads, a bad first altitude re-anchoring, the Denver landing, and the layer end to end (marker height, card line and stats).
- **Mutations:** each new test fails on the defect it guards. I applied 10 mutations and all 10 were caught:
  - gate bypassed in the layer
  - re-reads judged again
  - no re-anchor
  - next report's rate ignored
  - no +1 s
  - no margin
  - held value not substituted
  - stats count dropped
  - surface reports judged
  - out-of-order gap not clamped

  Two earlier survivors were dead code (a reference reset on landing, and a 10-minute reference cutoff that the marker's 60 s expiry makes unreachable), so I removed that code rather than write tests for it.
- **End to end through a decoder feed.** I ran a fake dump1090 with one DC-9 at 35,000 ft whose `alt_baro` read 108,800 ft for 1 s in every 10 s. The real dev server read it via `LOCAL_RECEIVER_FEEDS`, and headless Chrome (SwiftShader) sampled the marker 100 times.
  - Without the fix, the marker was drawn at 108,712 ft and the card read `ALT 108,800 FT`.
  - With the fix, the marker never went above 34,912 ft (35,000 ft baro plus the geoid offset), the card read only `ALT 35,000 FT`, `rejectedAltitudes` was 1, and there were no page errors.

Not run: `test:track` (no Google Maps key here), and no real receiver. The spike is synthetic, built to the shape of the logged value.

## Out of scope / follow-ups (stacked on this PR)

- **#802**: the browser decoder ignored Gillham (Q=0) altitudes entirely, so those aircraft showed no altitude over WebUSB. Stacked on this PR.
- **#803**: a 60,000 ft ceiling for the fixed-wing weight categories A1–A5. It closes the two gaps this check leaves: a corrupt first frame is drawn for about 1.5 s, and a feed stuck on one corrupt value is adopted on the third refusal. Stacked on #802.

## Delivery readiness

- **Client-only.** No server, route, config, or share-link change, so rollback is a revert.
- **The worst case of a false refusal** is an altitude lagging about 1.5 s behind before the re-anchor. It can't hide an aircraft.
- **Old and new code never run side by side.** It's a page reload.

> 🤖 Claude Code helped

title: fix(sdr): decode 100 ft Gillham altitudes in the browser decoder
body:
> **Stacked on #801.** GitHub can't base a PR on a fork branch, so this targets `main` and also shows #801's two commits. **Review only the top two commits**, `beab516` (the fix) and the CHANGELOG credit ([diff](https://github.com/bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view/pull/802/files/2be50ae..HEAD)). Once #801 merges, this diff shrinks to those commits. Refs #714.

**Intent.** The browser SDR decodes 100 ft (Gillham, Q=0) altitudes instead of dropping them. Nothing else in the decoder changes: CPR, CRC, the speed check and the frame extraction are untouched.

## Why

`decodeAltitude` returned `null` whenever the Q bit was clear. Two kinds of aircraft send Q=0:
- those whose transponder encodes altitude in 100 ft steps;
- anything above 50,175 ft, which Q=1 can't express.

Either way the aircraft showed **no altitude over WebUSB**, while a dump1090 feed of the same antenna showed one. #801 lists this as found but not fixed.

It stacks on #801 because it widens what the browser path can produce, up to 126,700 ft. That range is exactly what #801's vertical-rate check filters, so this should not land without it. It also makes #801's CURRENT-STATE sentence "the browser decoder cannot produce that value" untrue, and this PR corrects it.

## What

With Q=0 the 12-bit field `C1 A1 C2 A2 C4 A4 B1 Q B2 D2 B4 D4` is a Gillham code:
- a Gray-coded 500 ft count, `D2 D4 A1 A2 A4 B1 B2 B4`;
- a five-step 100 ft digit, `C1 C2 C4`, which runs backwards in odd 500 ft bands.

The result is -1,200 to 126,700 ft in 100 ft steps. The three digits no altitude uses (`000`, `101`, `111`) leave the altitude unknown rather than guessed. I implemented it from the code tables, not ported from another decoder (dump1090 is GPL; this repo is MIT).

## Verification

- **Oracle:** all 2,048 Q=0 codes, each in a CRC-valid DF17 frame, decoded by this decoder and by **pyModeS 2.x** (`adsb.altitude`).
  - Result: **0 mismatches** (1,280 altitudes, 768 unknown). pyModeS's own CRC check passes on every frame.
  - Sensitivity control: removing the odd-band reflection produces **512 mismatches**, so the comparison can fail.
- **Tests** (2 new):
  - Nine frames pinned to pyModeS's values: both ends of the range, a band boundary where the digit reverses, 108,800 ft, and each of the three non-altitude digits.
  - A round trip over every altitude from -1,200 to 126,700 ft, using an encoder written from the tables in the test.
  - The existing Austin real-frame tests (all Q=1) still match dump1090.
- **Mutations:** 7 applied, all caught:
  - Q=0 still null
  - no odd-band reflection
  - no 7→5 remap
  - non-altitude digits accepted
  - only `000` refused
  - D2/D4 swapped
  - wrong offset
- **Gates:**
  - `npm test`: 5,083 tests, 5,082 pass, 0 fail, 1 skipped (the existing Windows-only DACL test).
  - `format:check`: exit 0, 1,090 files.
  - `check:boundaries`: exit 0.
  - `build`: ✓.

Not run: a real Q=0 transmission. The Austin capture has none (25 of 25 airborne positions are Q=1). `test:track` also needs a Maps key I don't have.

## Out of scope

- Altitude from DF4/DF20 surveillance replies, and GNSS height (TC 20–22). The decoder handles only DF17/18 airborne positions (TC 9–18), and that doesn't change here.

## Delivery readiness

- **Client-only** decoder change: no config, server or share-link change. Rollback is a revert.
- **The worst case of a wrong decode** is an implausible altitude, which #801's check refuses.

> 🤖 Claude Code helped

title: fix(local-adsb): refuse fixed-wing altitudes above 60,000 ft outright
body:
> **Stacked on #802, which is stacked on #801.** GitHub can't base a PR on a fork branch, so this targets `main` and also shows their commits. **Review only the top two commits**, `ed2111a` (the fix) and its CHANGELOG credit, ([diff](https://github.com/bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view/pull/803/files/134cad4..HEAD)). The rest shrinks away as #801 and #802 merge. Refs #714.

**Intent.** Local ADS-B never shows an altitude above 60,000 ft for a fixed-wing weight category (A1–A5), closing the two gaps the vertical-rate check from #801 leaves. Categories without a ceiling, and the rate check itself, are unchanged.

## Why: the two gaps

1. **A corrupt first frame has no reference.** #801 draws it until three refusals re-anchor, about 1.5 s.
2. **A feed stuck on one corrupt value gets it adopted.** On the third refusal it becomes the reference.

   I measured this end to end: a fake dump1090 relayed 108,800 ft for 5 s straight, with #801 and #802 in place and no ceiling. The marker was drawn at **108,712 ft** and the card read `ALT 108,800 FT`.

#801 lists this as found but not fixed. It stacks on #802 because Gillham decoding lets the browser SDR produce these values too, up to 126,700 ft.

## What

`localAdsbAltitudeCeilingFt(category)` returns **60,000 ft for A1–A5**, and null for everything else, including an unknown category. The number: nothing certified in those categories flies above 51,000 ft (G650, Citation X), and Concorde, the one that did at 60,000 ft, retired in 2003.

In `gateLocalAdsbAltitude`:
- **A report above the ceiling is refused outright and never counts toward the re-anchor**, however often a feed repeats it.
- **A reference accepted before the category was known is dropped once it is.** The identification message often arrives seconds after the first altitude.
- **With nothing to hold, the altitude is returned as `null`.** That's the layer's existing "unknown": the card shows a dash and the marker sits at the geoid, as it already does for a Gillham code with no altitude. Showing an impossible number is worse.

**No ceiling** for A6 (high performance), A7 (rotorcraft) or any B category: gliders have soared to 76,000 ft, and balloons and UAVs fly far above 60,000 ft.

## Verification

- **End to end:** the same fake-feed plus headless-Chrome harness as #801, with a 5 s stuck spike and 100 samples each.
  - Without the ceiling (the control): marker up to 108,712 ft, card showed `ALT 108,800 FT`.
  - With the ceiling: marker never above 34,912 ft, card only showed `ALT 35,000 FT`, 5 refusals counted, no page errors.
- **Tests** (5 new):
  - the category table;
  - a bad first frame shown as unknown;
  - a stuck feed never re-anchoring;
  - a reference dropped when the category arrives;
  - no-ceiling categories kept, with the exact boundary (60,000 ft kept, 60,025 ft refused).
- **Mutations:** 9 applied, all caught:
  - no ceiling
  - ceiling counting toward the re-anchor
  - reference not dropped
  - impossible value shown instead of null
  - A6 given a ceiling
  - 50,000 ft
  - `>=`
  - `> +25`

  An earlier `>=` mutation survived, which is why the boundary assertions were added.
- **Gates:**
  - `npm test`: 5,088 tests, 5,087 pass, 0 fail, 1 skipped (the existing Windows-only DACL test).
  - `format:check`: exit 0.
  - `check:boundaries`: exit 0.
  - `build`: ✓.

Not run: `test:track` (no Maps key), and no real receiver.

## Delivery readiness

- **Client-only:** no config, server or share-link change. Rollback is a revert.
- **The worst case of a wrong ceiling** is a real A1–A5 altitude above 60,000 ft showing as unknown. No such aircraft is in service. It can't hide the aircraft itself.

> 🤖 Claude Code helped

title: feat(perimeters): publish selected wildfire incidents to shared context
body:
Refs #797.

This keeps wildfire-perimeter selection source-owned while publishing the selected incident through the existing shared selected-entity context lane.

- registers one `fire-perimeters` context record with NIFC/WFIGS provenance and the card anchor coordinates;
- announces only explicit user selection;

title: feat(cctv): focus nearest camera to an explicit point
server: make 405 responses declare the allowed methods
body:
## Problem

GEV has many explicit `405 Method Not Allowed` guards, but their response contract is inconsistent. `server/providers/radio/catalog.js` already sends an `Allow` header; many sibling providers do not.

This surfaced while reviewing #794, which is adding explicit method guards to `/api/opensky`, `/api/adsblol/mil`, and `/api/route`.

Examples on current `main` without an `Allow` declaration include handlers in:

- Weather / Wind / Cyclones / Fire Perimeters
- Overpass and GBFS
- geocode / regional brief / weather effects
- military installations
- launch-library
- Google Places
- local receivers
- several OpenAI routes

The exact method set differs (`GET`, `POST`, `GET, HEAD`, or `GET, POST`), so this should be a method-contract cleanup rather than a blanket header string.

## Direction

Use one small server-side owner for `405` responses, or otherwise pin the same invariant across provider handlers:

- every `405` response includes `Allow` with the methods that route actually accepts;
- rejection happens before upstream work / rate-limit spend where that is already the route contract;
- existing response bodies/status semantics stay unchanged unless deliberately normalized;
- tests cover representative `GET`, `POST`, `GET + HEAD`, and multi-method routes.

`server/providers/radio/catalog.js` is an existing in-tree example of the desired header behavior.

## Scope

This is separate from deciding whether a route *should* support `HEAD`; #794 correctly notes that question. First make each current method contract self-describing, then any repo-wide `HEAD` policy can be changed intentionally.

title: fix(ui): close stale compact Radio when Context is open
body:
Fixes #804.

The compact Radio disclosure is an absolute-positioned child of the Global Context header, so the right-rail allocator cannot reserve separate space for it. The normal Radio header-click path already avoids this overlap when Context is expanded; the remaining hole was a stale disclosure surviving a no-op Context-open transition.

`PanelChrome.setPanelCollapsed('global-context-panel', false)` enforced the compact-Radio cleanup only after its no-op return. This moves that invariant before the return, so any request to leave Context expanded closes a stale compact disclosure before Contacts/Space Missions content can coexist with it.

Changes:
- enforce compact-Radio cleanup even when Global Context is already expanded;
- add a regression for the stale `disclosure-open` state;
- document the ownership invariant in `CURRENT-STATE.md` and `CHANGELOG.md`.

No rail sizing, z-index, Radio playback, or Context-mode behavior changes.

body:
## Problem

GEV already exposes a rich semantic action vocabulary through voice, but keyboard users often have to find the matching visible panel/control first.

A command palette could make common actions fast without introducing DOM-click automation or a second execution layer.

## Proposal

Add a `Cmd/Ctrl+K` palette that searches actions such as:

- Go to
- Track/select
- Layers
- Panels
- Context modes
- HUD/styles
- Evidence actions
- Scene controls

The important constraint: palette results call the **same typed owners/services** used by voice and normal UI. The palette should not query selectors and click arbitrary buttons.

Example:

```
> radar
  Show Weather panel
  Enable Rain radar
  Switch HUD to Tactical
```

## Keyboard ownership

GEV already has focused surface keyboard handling. The global shortcut should yield when:

- an input/editor owns the keystroke;
- an active surface has claimed keyboard handling;
- the event was already prevented.

Escape closes the palette and restores prior focus.

## First slice

Keep v1 deliberately small:

- static catalog of existing actions;
- fuzzy search over label/keywords;
- execute 5–10 existing action owners;
- no AI required;
- no background suggestion popups.

## Acceptance

- same result semantics as voice/direct UI;
- no focus theft;
- full keyboard navigation;
- reduced-motion compatible;
- invalid/unavailable actions explain why instead of silently failing.

Downstream design reference: https://github.com/kvnloo/gods-eye-view/pull/24

### Will you build it?

Yes, as a small action-adapter experiment first.

title: RFC: change-first “What Changed” ribbon for live world-state deltas
RFC: semantic zoom / attention states for dense HUD panels
body:
## Problem

GEV is intentionally information-dense, but panel density currently tends to be binary: collapsed header vs expanded full surface.

That makes users choose between too little context and multiple competing full panels.

## Proposal

Prototype a shared presentation grammar with four attention states:

- `background` — no persistent chrome;
- `ambient` — identity + health + newest material change;
- `focus` — top facts/actions for the current task;
- `critical` — bounded exception requiring awareness.

This is presentation metadata only. It must not enable/disable data, change source truth, or overwrite share-authored state.

Example Weather projection:

```
ambient:  RADAR · LIVE · 4m
focus:    3 cells nearby · +1 strengthening
detail:   timeline / provider / controls / provenance
```

## First experiment

Apply the same helper to **two unrelated panels** (for example Weather + Context) and measure:

- visible lines/area;
- clicks to a common action;
- stale/error/source visibility;
- panel switching;
- clipping at constrained viewport heights.

## Attention ownership

Automatic refresh may update content but should never steal keyboard focus or become the preferred rail owner. Explicit user expansion remains authoritative.

This would complement, not replace, the current rail allocation/collapse logic.

Downstream RFC: https://github.com/kvnloo/gods-eye-view/pull/24

### Will you build it?

Yes, if a two-panel proof can stay small and generic.

body:

**Exact head:** [`c1dd417`](https://github.com/kvnloo/gods-eye-view/commit/c1dd4171dbb2dcc98c427b5338bcdb5f256018ac), merged non-force with origin `main@1df2a27`, zero behind at comparison, GitHub mergeable. It preserves current main's i18n wiring and avoids obsolete top-of-CHANGELOG conflict.

Following the independent Windows analysis from **quanticsoul4772** and **asturksever's P1 review**, a new regression constructs **real PanelChrome** and then drives its actual right-rail controller; this tests the constructor-injected callback rather than a manually wired fake. It verifies an auto-collapsed Context restoring to open dismisses compact Radio before layout. This complements the existing rail-method and repeated-owner tests. Original issue report credit: **raysung-2026**.

[Exact-head CI #39023019504](https://github.com/bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view/actions/runs/39023019504): **SUCCESS** on `c1dd417`: Node 24.14.0 full suite/build, Node 26.x full suite/build, Windows onboarding, and generic Street Level browser/panel gate all passed. This includes the new real-PanelChrome-constructor regression. The generic browser gate is not the requested before/after Radio screenshot. This source-level real-owner regression **does not replace** the specifically requested before/after live-browser screenshots for issue #804, which remain unverified. Normal maintainer review and merge required.

---

Fixes #804.

## Reachable path on current `main`

The compact Radio mini is allowed while Context is collapsed. The normal Radio-header click *already* routes to the nested full Radio controls when Context is open (`radioBindings.js`); it is not the source of the stale state.

The alternate path bypasses the panel owner:

1. Tactical's right rail temporarily auto-collapses `global-context-panel` (`layout-auto-collapsed`). A user opens the compact Radio disclosure from its collapsed header.
2. The responsive rail later reconsiders automatic collapse (e.g. a resize/HUD layout change): `PanelLayoutController._scheduleRightPanelLayout({ reconsiderAutoCollapse: true })` removes `collapsed` and `layout-auto-collapsed` **directly**, calling only `_syncPanelCollapseButton`.
3. Because that path does **not** call `PanelChrome.setPanelCollapsed()`, the Radio mini can remain visible above the newly expanded Context/Space Missions body. The mini is absolutely positioned outside the rail's measured content.

## Fix

- Inject `PanelChrome._syncRailPanelCollapseButton` into the right-rail controller, so direct rail restores dismiss compact Radio before Context is laid out. This also covers `layoutRightPanelRail` restoring auto-collapsed panels on HUD variant changes.
- Preserve the original fix moving `setPanelCollapsed('global-context-panel', false)` cleanup before its no-op return.
- Add two focused regressions, the first for an already-open Context owner call, the second exercising the **real rail reconsideration method** from a valid `collapsed + layout-auto-collapsed + compact Radio open` state. This is a behavior fix, not a z-index exception.
- Update `CHANGELOG.md` and `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md`.

## Validation / limits

- Isolated JavaScript source-level regression check (actual class methods, simplified DOM): **both tests fail on upstream `main@8b8ccc9`; both pass on the prior PR implementation `19372875`**. The tested runtime module and regressions are carried unchanged into the current head, but the exact merged head has not run the full suite.

The earlier CI at `b22e6d5` predates the rail-restoration addition and is not signoff for this branch.
- Reporter screenshots of the overlapping UI are in #804; an actual before/after Chrome capture of this path is still needed for maintainer P1.

- **@raysung-2026** reported #804, including English/Chinese UI screenshots and reproduction.
- **@asturksever** identified the needed current-main path validation, changelog requirement, and the direct right-rail restoration seam; the updated regression covers that seam.

title: feat: accept a ChatGPT OAuth session for Realtime voice
body:
## Problem

Voice cannot be turned on with a ChatGPT subscription login. The app only reads `OPENAI_API_KEY` and sends that string as the bearer for `POST /v1/realtime/client_secrets`. The README points at platform.openai.com. There is no OpenAI OAuth login, and the OAuth already in the repo is OpenSky's.

Someone who already has a ChatGPT / Codex session still has to create a separate metered API key before the mic works.

## Proposal

Keep `OPENAI_API_KEY` as the preferred credential. It remains the only credential that covers both Realtime and the AI HUD summary.

Add a first version that also accepts a God's Eye View-owned ChatGPT OAuth session for Realtime only:

- `node scripts/openai-oauth-login.mjs` runs a device-code login and writes `.gev/openai-oauth.json` (mode 600, gitignored).
- The login creates its own session. It does not read or refresh `~/.codex` or `~/.hermes` auth files, because those refresh tokens are single-use and rotating one signs the other app out.
- `/api/realtime/token` uses the OAuth access token only when `OPENAI_API_KEY` is unset.
- `/api/openai/hud-summary` keeps requiring `OPENAI_API_KEY`. The same OAuth token was rejected by `POST /v1/responses` with HTTP 401 in a local check, so the HUD path should stay on the existing keyless response instead of forwarding that token.

This is not Sign in with ChatGPT. That product shares identity, not an API credential. OpenAI does not publish a third-party OAuth client that mints API keys for this app. The login has to reuse the public Codex CLI client id (`app_EMoamEEZ73f0CkXaXp7hrann`) so a ChatGPT subscription can authorize the Realtime client-secret endpoint. That client is not registered to God's Eye View.

## Data source, license, and attribution

none

Yes, I plan to open a PR

title: RFC: minimum-sufficient perception ladder for voice/agents
body:
## TL;DR

Before an agent asks for a full viewport image or stronger multimodal reasoning, let it try the cheapest structured evidence GEV already owns.

```
typed app state
  -> bounded world/view packet
  -> selected/source record
  -> scoped spatial query
  -> referent-centered crop
  -> fresh viewport frame
  -> stronger multimodal reasoning
```

Stop as soon as the decision is supported.

This is primarily a latency/reliability contract, not a new model/provider.

## Why this fits current GEV

GEV already has most of the lower rungs:

- `get_current_view_state`;
- `get_entity_context`;
- normalized layer/feed snapshots with freshness/source;
- selected/tracked context;
- Realtime viewport capture when visual context is actually needed.

Today each consumer can independently decide how much state to inspect. A small shared escalation policy would keep simple control/query work off the expensive visual path while preserving vision for genuinely visual questions.

Related:
- #812 — bounded local/JEV-style intent router;
- #815 — semantic zoom / attention states;
- #466 — deterministic Spatial Context Builder.

## Smallest useful slices

### Slice 1 — pure policy helper

Add a Cesium-free resolver such as:

```js
resolvePerceptionTier({
  questionKind,
  hasSelectedRecord,
  hasStructuredAnswer,
  requiresVisualEvidence,
  maxLatencyMs
})
```

Return one bounded tier:
`state | selected | query | crop | viewport | multimodal`.

Unit tests only. No behavior change.

### Slice 2 — instrument existing Realtime viewport sends

Record why a viewport image was requested:
- structured evidence insufficient;
- visual verification requested;
- unknown/other.

This gives us a baseline before changing routing.

### Slice 3 — one consumer

Apply the ladder to one read-only voice/query path. If structured state answers it, skip the image. If not, preserve the existing visual path.

### Slice 4 — JEV integration

Let #812 request an escalation tier rather than guessing from incomplete state.

## Metrics

Track both failure directions:

- **missed perception** — a lower tier lacked evidence that a higher tier needed;
- **wasted perception** — a higher tier was invoked although lower-tier state was already sufficient.

Also measure:
- p50/p95 decision latency;
- image bytes/tokens;
- escalation rate;
- action/query accuracy.

## Guardrails

- never infer visual facts from structured state that does not contain them;
- preserve freshness/provenance/unknowns;
- viewport images remain fresh when visual timing matters;
- this policy has no execution authority;
- stop if two consumers cannot share the same escalation vocabulary.

Downstream RFC/prototype planning:

title: feat(voice): add minimum-sufficient perception tier policy
body:
Refs #822.

This is Slice 1 from the Minimum-Sufficient Perception Ladder RFC: a small Cesium-free policy module with no production routing change.

It defines the escalation order:

`state -> selected -> query -> crop -> viewport -> multimodal -> abstain`

Callers still own the actual sufficiency check. The helper never infers missing visual facts or decides that structured state is sufficient on its own.

It also adds a receipt classifier for:
- `matched` — chosen tier equals minimum sufficient tier;
- `missed` — chosen tier was too weak;
- `wasted` — a more expensive tier was used unnecessarily;
- `unknown` — unrecognized input.

This gives #822 a testable vocabulary before any existing Realtime viewport behavior changes.

title: feat(cctv): expose camera suitability for machine vision
body:
## Proposal

Add an optional, provider-neutral **vision suitability** record to CCTV cameras so the UI can distinguish cameras that are merely live from cameras that are actually useful for downstream measurement.

This is deliberately metadata only. It does **not** put a CV model, Torch, or OpenCV in the browser.

## Motivation

A live 1080p camera can still be a poor measurement source if the roadway is too distant, while a lower-resolution camera can be much more useful when vehicles occupy more pixels.

That suggests a small new CCTV capability:

- `ready` — framing/scale looks suitable for measurement
- `marginal` — usable with caveats
- `unsuitable` — live, but framing/scale fails the measurement gate
- `unknown` — no qualification data

The existing CCTV health and calibration surfaces already have most of the UI/ownership seams needed to present this cleanly.

## Possible record

```js
{
  cameraId,
  status: 'ready' | 'marginal' | 'unsuitable' | 'unknown',
  medianObjectPx,
  usableShare,
  reason,
  measuredAt,
  provenance
}
```

The exact fields should stay small and generic. A backend or external measurement service could produce them; GEV should only normalize and present them.

## First slice

- Add an optional normalized qualification record keyed by CCTV camera ID.
- Keep it independent from ordinary stream health: `live` does not imply `vision-ready`.
- Surface a small badge/state in the existing CCTV panel/card.
- Fail soft when no qualification source is configured.
- Preserve provenance/timestamp so inferred quality is not presented as authoritative fact.
- Add focused presentation/normalization tests.

## Non-goals

- No bundled detection model.
- No browser-side video inference.
- No person/identity recognition.
- No automatic claim that a camera is accurate enough for engineering use.
- No hard-coded pixel threshold in the core contract.

## Why this fits GEV

GEV already owns the camera catalog, health state, viewshed/calibration UI and public-source provenance. This would let downstream spatial-intelligence systems describe **what a camera can reliably observe** without coupling GEV to a particular CV stack.

If this direction makes sense, I can implement it as a small fail-soft metadata/presentation PR first.

title: feat(cctv): surface optional traffic observations in camera cards
body:
## Proposal

Let a CCTV camera card display **optional, recent traffic observations** produced by an external measurement source.

This builds on #828 but keeps the first implementation intentionally presentation-only: GEV consumes compact observations and does not own the detector/tracker.

## Example observations

A camera could expose a small summary such as:

- observed flow: `18 veh/min`
- class mix: `86% car · 11% heavy vehicle · 3% other`
- observation window: `last 5 min`
- quality/provenance: measured timestamp + source
- optional turning movements when the source can resolve them

A compact normalized record might look like:

```js
{
  cameraId,
  windowStart,
  windowEnd,
  vehicleRatePerMin,
  counts: {
    car: 0,
    heavyVehicle: 0,
    motorbike: 0
  },
  movements: [],
  quality,
  provenance
}
```

The exact taxonomy should remain generic enough that other public camera-analysis sources can plug in later.

## First slice

- Add an optional observation-summary record keyed by CCTV camera ID.
- Render it inside the existing camera detail/card rather than adding a new global panel.
- Clearly distinguish `live camera` from `recent measured observation`.
- Show timestamp/provenance and stale/unknown state.
- Fail soft when no observation service is configured.
- Keep raw video, models and heavy dependencies outside the frontend.
- Add focused UI/presentation tests.

## UX direction

The card should answer, at a glance:

> Is this camera measurable, and what has it observed recently?

Potential compact presentation:

```
VISION READY
18 veh/min · last 5m
86% car · 11% HV · 3% other
measured 32s ago
```

The existing CCTV health/calibration states should remain visually primary when observation data is absent or stale.

## Non-goals

- No identity, plate or person recognition.
- No claim that estimated counts are ground truth.
- No persistent video archive.
- No CV runtime bundled into GEV.
- No coupling to one traffic-analysis implementation.

## Follow-up

A provider-neutral traffic-layer observation source can then consume the same data spatially instead of limiting it to the camera card (see follow-up issue once opened).

Blocked by / complements #828.

title: feat(traffic): add a provider-neutral observed-flow source contract
body:
## Proposal

Add an optional **observed traffic source contract** alongside the existing traffic data path so GEV can render externally measured road/intersection activity without coupling the traffic layer to a particular computer-vision stack.

This is the bridge between CCTV-derived observations and the existing traffic visualization.

Related: #828, #829.

## Motivation

GEV already has a traffic layer and a separate CCTV subsystem. What is missing is a narrow contract for measured observations such as:

- vehicle counts/rates
- coarse vehicle class
- turning movement
- approach/road-segment association
- observation time window
- quality/provenance

The CV stack should remain external. GEV only needs enough normalized data to place an observation in the world and render it honestly.

## Possible record

```js
{
  id,
  sourceId,
  observedAt,
  windowStart,
  windowEnd,

  cameraId,

  geometry: {
    type: 'road-segment' | 'approach' | 'intersection',
    coordinates
  },

  flow: {
    vehiclesPerMin,
    counts
  },

  movements: [],
  quality,
  provenance
}
```

This is illustrative, not a proposed frozen schema.

## First slice

- Define a small portable source interface for observed traffic records.
- Normalize timestamps, provenance and geometry association.
- Keep observed data distinct from simulated/predicted traffic state.
- Add stale/partial/error presentation semantics.
- Allow the source to be absent with zero behavior change.
- Avoid introducing any CV/runtime dependency.
- Add fixtures/tests for malformed, stale and partial records.

## Rendering direction

Initially, observed traffic could reuse existing traffic-layer visual primitives:

- road/approach intensity
- directional flow
- small measured-state badges

The renderer should make it possible to tell `observed` from `simulated` or provider-estimated flow.

## Constraints

- Public-data model only.
- No identity/person/plate data in the contract.
- No raw video transport through the traffic layer.
- No requirement that one camera resolve every movement.
- No assumption that every observation is ground truth.
- Preserve source/timestamp/quality so the UI can communicate uncertainty.

## Why a separate contract

This keeps the architecture reusable. CCTV-derived measurements are one producer, but future public sensors or municipal count feeds could implement the same interface without depending on CCTV internals.

A later corridor demo can exercise the contract end-to-end with a small set of public traffic cameras.

title: feat(traffic): prototype a camera-observed corridor mode
body:
## Proposal

Prototype an end-to-end **camera-observed traffic corridor** using a small public-camera corridor as a proving ground for #828, #829 and #830.

The goal is not to add a traffic-analysis product to GEV. The goal is to prove that GEV can consume externally measured observations and turn them into a useful live spatial view.

## Candidate corridor

A useful first target is the SR-90 / Imperial Highway corridor in Orange County, California.

The public Caltrans camera catalog includes a sequence of signalized-intersection cameras along this corridor, making it possible to test several adjacent observation points instead of one isolated camera.

The exact cameras should remain configurable and should only be enabled after source/licensing/terms checks are complete.

## User experience

A user could enable an `Observed traffic` mode and see:

- qualified cameras along the corridor
- recent measured flow at each camera/intersection
- directional/approach state where available
- coarse vehicle mix
- observation age and quality
- explicit gaps where a camera is unavailable or unsuitable

Selecting a camera would continue to use the existing CCTV card, augmented by #829.

## First slice

Keep the demo intentionally bounded:

- a small configured set of cameras/intersections
- externally supplied synthetic or recorded observation fixtures first
- render observations through the provider-neutral contract from #830
- show observed vs simulated/provider-estimated traffic distinctly
- show stale/missing camera periods instead of silently interpolating them
- add a focused browser/QA path for the corridor mode
- document provenance and limitations

Only after the GEV-side contract works should a live external measurement service be connected.

## Architecture

```
public camera feed
      ↓
external measurement service
detect → track → calibrate → aggregate
      ↓
compact observation records
      ↓
GEV observed-flow source (#830)
      ↓
traffic layer + CCTV card (#829)
```

The heavy CV runtime remains outside GEV.

## Success criteria

The prototype should make these states visually distinguishable:

1. camera live + qualified + recent observation
2. camera live + qualified + stale observation
3. camera live + unsuitable/unknown
4. camera unavailable
5. road segment with only simulated/provider-estimated traffic

No state should imply more measurement certainty than the source provides.

## Non-goals

- No face/person/plate recognition.
- No raw-video archive in GEV.
- No requirement for all 12 turning movements.
- No bundled Torch/OpenCV/YOLO dependency.
- No extrapolation across missing observations presented as measured fact.
- No claim of validated traffic-count accuracy until independent ground truth exists.

## Dependencies

- #828 — camera suitability metadata
- #829 — observation summary in CCTV cards
- #830 — provider-neutral observed-flow source

This should stay a follow-up until the generic contracts are small and reviewable.

title: feat(actions): add verified action episode policy
body:
## Current-main reviewer repair — October 16, 2026

Current head [`b7cf845e`](https://github.com/kvnloo/gods-eye-view/commit/b7cf845e11a393c181d97deb5e438a9814efdf6e) incorporates [quanticsoul4772's independent Windows findings](https://github.com/bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view/pull/836#issuecomment-6223714526), without a new origin PR:

- Reject prototype-sensitive `__proto__` / `constructor` / `prototype` argument keys, rather than normalizing different actions to the same identity.
- Enforce bounded argument depth (8), container width (64), total nodes (256), value length (2,048), and serialized argument length (8,192); reject >32 actions before mapping.
- A repeated receipt with the same context/sequence/start time counts once; conflicting duplicate outcomes conservatively prevent verified success.
- Reject invalid `minOccurrences` explicitly rather than silently clamping it; add five targeted regression cases.

Non-force merge with [origin `main@1df2a27`](https://github.com/bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view/commit/1df2a272cf7cfbb2f1a4c637c897e90719b0af95) preserves the upstream voice-layer manifest owner. Current diff is exactly four intended files; GitHub reports mergeable without conflicts. The pinned Prettier 3.9.6 formatter was applied via hosted CI, and temporary formatting instrumentation was removed.

**Evidence:** eight independent isolated assertions passed against the byte-identical pre-formatting module on Node 22.16.0 (not the supported production Node). [Exact-head hosted CI #39001916095](https://github.com/bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view/actions/runs/39001916095) is **SUCCESS** at this exact head: [CI #39001916095](https://github.com/bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view/actions/runs/39001916095) completed with all four jobs green — Node 24.14.0 and Node 26.x full suites/builds, Windows onboarding, and the generic Street Level browser gate. The browser gate does **not** exercise a dedicated action-episode UI (this remains a data-only unused module); maintainer acceptance and any real usage remain separate. This kernel is **not consumed by the app**, does not execute macros or grant authority, and has no demonstrated production behavior yet. Maintainer review/merge remains external. Thank you to the independent reviewer and the original GEV contributors.

---

Refs #824.

This is Slice 1 only: a bounded, deterministic receipt format for repeated **typed GEV actions**, plus exact candidate detection.

The receipt is versioned and each step carries:

- action `name`
- `schemaFingerprint`
- `capabilityFingerprint`
- normalized plain-data `args`
- observed `success | failed | cancelled` outcome

Episode identity also includes a bounded `contextFingerprint`. Correction/undo prevents a verified success.

The detector:
- groups only exact semantic sequences;
- normalizes object-key ordering;
- defaults to 3 occurrences and 100% verified success;
- keeps schema/capability drift in separate candidate identities;
- rejects unknown/future receipt versions;
- uses no model/fuzzy matching.

This incorporates the drift concern raised in #824: the same action name/args under changed schema or capability semantics cannot silently compile into the same candidate.

Deliberately **not included**:
- suggestion UI;
- macro execution;
- stored authority;
- full result/capability payloads;
- model calls.

A future replay path would still need to revalidate current action schema/capabilities immediately before each step and append a fresh owner result.

body:
# feat(voice): voice core — honest layer reach, spoken summary with on-screen card, narration, point-and-ask

## Why

Voice had three problems:

- **Confident wrong answers.** `analyst_query` counted only the first 2,000 records, answered zero when a layer was off or still loading, and quietly widened unknown scopes or fields.
- **Limited reach.** Many shipped layers (transit, cyclones, wind, weather, Recent Imagery, mapped installations and others) could not be turned on or queried by voice, and common names like "buses" or "hurricanes" didn't resolve.
- **Dead air and long answers.** Slow tools ran in silence, then the assistant read out every caveat and source.

## What changed

**Reach and honest answers**
- `src/voice/layerManifest.js` declares each layer's spoken names, voice verbs and queryable fields. The layer enums in the tool schema, the alias table and the analyst field hints are generated from it. `layerManifest.test.mjs` fails when a new layer has no entry.
- `src/data/analystEngine.js` refuses unknown fields, operators, units, value types, scopes and centres, and returns the allowed values. It counts up to 250,000 loaded records per layer (`complete: false` past that), marks partly answered queries as `partial` with `unanswered` layers, keeps "layer off", "still loading" and "feed unavailable" separate from a real zero, and refuses a follow-up that names different layers than the last answer. A superseded query is cancelled and never replaces follow-up memory.
- Seven more layers expose analyst records: bikeshare, transit, launches, cyclones, ALPR, mapped installations and local ADS-B. Fire records carry their sensor.

**Speech, card and narration**
- `src/voice/speech.js`: results carry a code-built `say` line and a `display` object. The model speaks the line. Sources and notes stay on screen, and "at least" and partial answers are always spoken.
- Voice card inside the mic control (`src/voice/voiceCard.js`, `voiceCardPresentation.js`, `src/ui/styles/voice-card.css`): captions, plan steps and the result. `src/voice/resultDisplay.js` is the single adapter from a tool result to the card, and the numbered-referent list reads from it too.
- `src/voice/narration.js`: a tool still running after 1.5 s speaks its current step once (out of band, never after the result); others get one "still working" line at 8 s; a soft earcon in push-to-talk only.
- Space barge-in: holding Space while the assistant talks cancels the reply and clears its audio (`realtimeTurns.js`), but not while Radio holds the speaker.
- Turn spans (`src/voice/turnMetrics.js`, `scripts/voice-turn-spans.mjs`) write latency and word counts to the debug log. Caption transcription is metered into the session cost and cap (`OPENAI_REALTIME_TRANSCRIBE_MODEL`, `off` disables it). The debug log omits transcripts and typed text unless `GEV_VOICE_LOG_CONTENT=1`.

**Point and ask**
- `src/voice/pointerContext.js`, `pointerPick.js`, `pointerReticle.js`: the cursor target is captured when Space goes down and sent as an inert `pointer_context` item. A reticle marks the point during the turn.
- `src/voice/deixis.js` resolves `"pointer"` in `get_entity_context`, `track_entity`, `fly_to_location`, `analyst_query` (scope kind) and `annotate_map`, plus `referent:n` from the last numbered list (`src/voice/referents.js`). `src/data/pickedContext.js` describes what was picked.
- Bare ground up close sends a 512 px crop around the point (`realtimeViewport.js`).
- Pointer, referents and follow-up memory end with the voice session (`runner.resetConversation()` on stop, `dispose()` on removal).

**Prompt**
- `server/providers/openai/instructions.js` and `toolDescriptions.js` now state each policy once (place precedence, counting, caveats, preambles). Instructions + tools go from 48,457 to 46,747 characters (−3.5%) with the same 30 tools.

**Harness**
- `scripts/voice-bench/` holds the phrase table and grading, shared by `scripts/qa-voice-routing.mjs` and the new provider-neutral benchmark `scripts/qa-voice-bench.mjs` (OpenAI Realtime, Gemini Live, OpenAI-compatible local servers).
- The behavior layer now fails if any Overpass request is made during the run.

Schema pins in `src/voice/actionSchemas.test.mjs` and `src/firstRunExperience.test.mjs` were re-derived for the generated layer enums, the pointer/referent arguments and the shorter wording.

## How to run

```sh
npm install
PORT=4173 ./scripts/dev-fresh.sh      # keys from env, .env or the macOS Keychain
```

- `OPENAI_API_KEY` is needed for live voice and for the routing/deixis harness layers.
- No model turns and no key needed: `npm test`, and `node scripts/qa-voice-routing.mjs --layer behavior --url http://localhost:4173` (drives the action runner directly in a headless page).

## Try these

Type them into the voice text box, or hold Space and speak.

Reach
- [ ] "Turn on the buses" / "Show hurricanes" / "Open the weather panel"
- [ ] "Turn on mapped military bases"

Honesty
- [ ] With flights on: "How many flights are over Texas?" (count plus scope, e.g. "378 loaded flights over Texas")
- [ ] With flights off: "How many flights are in view?" (says the layer is off and offers to turn it on; no zero)
- [ ] "How many flights and earthquakes are there?" with earthquakes off (a partial answer that names what it couldn't read)
- [ ] "Which of those is highest?" right after a count (follow-up); then "which of those earthquakes…" (refused: the last answer was flights)
- [ ] "Count the fires inside the area I drew" (says there is no drawn-area scope yet instead of answering for the view)

Terse speech + card
- [ ] "What's the biggest fire near Los Angeles?" (one spoken line; card shows scope, window and caveats under NOTES & SOURCES)

Narration on slow tools
- [ ] "Turn on flights and select the closest aircraft to Dallas" (one short plan line, then a step line if it takes more than 1.5 s; the card shows the steps)

Space barge-in
- [ ] Ask something long ("Tell me about the history of Austin"), then hold Space while it talks: the reply stops

Point and ask (hold Space with the cursor on the map)
- [ ] Cursor on an aircraft: "Tell me about this" (reticle; card shows THIS)
- [ ] Cursor on an aircraft: "Track that one"
- [ ] Cursor on the ground: "How many flights are around here?"
- [ ] "How many flights are in view?" then "Track the second one"

## Gates and harness results

On this branch (squashed on `public/main` e7707d9a):

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `npm test` | 5,526 tests, 0 failed |
| `npm run format:check` | clean |
| `npm run check:boundaries` | clean |
| `npm run build` | ok |
| `qa-voice-routing.mjs --layer behavior` | 50/50, including "no Overpass request during the run". One earlier run failed `fly_route` once; it passed in isolation and on the rerun |
| `qa-voice-routing.mjs --layer routing` (budget 120) | 62/62 |
| `--layer deixis` | 13/13 |
| `--layer deixis-live` | 3/3 |
| `--layer behavior --deixis-only` | 17/17 |

## Benchmark summary

`scripts/qa-voice-bench.mjs` sends text turns with the production instructions and tools, and stubs the tool results. It measures tool choice, not spoken accuracy or audio latency. These numbers come from a wider branch that also had the area and on-device tools, so treat them as indicative:

| Model | Core full-call | Median send → tool call |
| --- | --- | --- |
| gpt-realtime-2 | 99.2% | 869 ms |
| gpt-realtime-2.1 | 98.4% | 964 ms |
| gpt-realtime-2.1-mini | 93.5% | 782 ms |
| gemini-3.8-live | 97.6% | 649 ms (about 4x the cost) |

`gpt-realtime-2` stays the default. 2.1 showed no gain on these phrases and was slightly slower. A spoken test would be the next check.

## Known limitations

- "In view" is still a radius around the view centre, not the visible footprint.
- Region scopes count inside the largest part of a boundary (islands dropped). Region lookups beyond the bundled packs answer `region-timeout` after 3 s.
- There is no drawn-area scope yet. The prompt tells the model to say so.
- In open mic, pointing counts only if the cursor moved on the map in the last 5 s.
- Some models pass raw coordinates instead of the `pointer` target. The benchmark tracks this.
- The routing harness pins tool names, not wording.

## Not in this PR

- Area geometry (named boundaries as reusable areas, area/drawn scopes, recent imagery and OpenStreetMap search by voice). This follows in a separate PR.
- The on-device voice tier. This also follows separately.

title: feat(layers): add real-time GDELT & NASA EONET OSINT global events layer
body: ## Summary Adds a new global spatial intelligence layer (`gdelt-events`) that visualizes real-time geopolitical news, unrest, and severe environmental crisis telemetry on the 3D globe. ## Motivation While existing layers focus on physical telemetry (ADS-B/AIS) and natural hazards (FIRMS/USGS), this layer bridges the gap with real-time geopolitical and breaking event intelligence, providing the situational context for *why* aircraft, vessels, and assets are moving across the globe. ## Features - **Live Ingestion**: Dual-stream telemetry fetching from GDELT Project DOC 2.0 API and NASA EONET active event feeds. - **Sentiment & Severity Styling**: Tactical color classification (Crimson for crisis sectors, Amber for developing situations, Cyan for diplomatic stability). - **Dynamic Observation Volume**: Scales event disks and telemetry counts based on actual reporting density and satellite observation passes. - **Interactive Dispatch Card**: Native glassmorphic UI card with real-time headline snippet, source link, and a 3D camera "Fly to Sector" action. - **Analyst Engine & Voice Support**: Implements `getAnalystRecords()` conforming to the analyst engine schema (mirrored after the earthquakes/FIRMS layers). ## Validation Evidence - [x] Verified live data ingestion (GDELT & NASA EONET) and 3D globe rendering - [x] Verified interactive UI card interactions ("Fly to Sector" and source link navigation) - [x] `npm run format:check` passed - [x] `npm run check:boundaries` passed (all groups verified) - [x] `npm test` passed (70/70 unit tests green) - [x] `npm run build` passed (production bundle compiled) - [x] `node scripts/check-layer-state-tokens.mjs --base-ref main` verified (28 published, 1 new) - [ ] *Note: Live voice agent interaction was not tested directly due to lack of an OpenAI API key, but `getAnalystRecords()` adheres to the standard analyst record schema.*

restore sourced city, neighbourhood, street, building, campus and grounds outlines without enabling public Overpass or Nominatim by default

this continues the outline work in #842 using bundled Natural Earth, Census, DataSF and reviewed Who's On First boundaries, suitable OpenFreeMap geometry and guarded opt-in Nominatim

traffic and outlines share decoded tiles while keeping mutable results and cancellation ownership separate
multipart shapes and holes stay intact, annotations remain pending until owned installation settles, and credits stay with committed geometry

named-building fallback requires the resolved anchor inside the selected filled footprint, so a nearby anonymous building or courtyard hole cannot supply its outline
pointed-at buildings keep nearby selection within 40 metres

review follow-up (Sameh's 19-point review, re-checked against the current head)

- Google 3D server-token wiring in the standalone app is restored and covered by a test that runs the real assembly
- public Nominatim stays off unless `NOMINATIM_URL` is set; the 1.1 s spacing is measured at the transport call, under a shared lock across processes, and the unused reservation path is removed
- `GET /api/geocode/status` reports whether Nominatim is configured, like `/api/overpass/status`; when it is not, the place search and voice outline clients send no lookup the server would refuse, and an ask cancelled while that check is pending starts no request
- building outlines use only the selected component and its holes; a cut or malformed sibling no longer refuses the building
- outline extraction runs only when an outline is asked for; shared OpenFreeMap consumers are charged their own slice, and the charged cache budget stays at the 64 MiB of the single source traffic and installations shared before (estimates, not a measured heap bound)

offline validation on the merge of main `43a67f9` into `d9a4606`, using Node 24.19.0 locally; the four CI checks that ran on `d9a4606` passed in [run 41398181163](https://github.com/bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view/actions/runs/41398181163), and main's newly required Node 24.22.2 check runs once this merge is pushed
