- on the merge of main `43a67f9` (keyless, headless Chrome for Testing 152, no Nominatim, Overpass or Photon): at 1440x900 and 390x844, "this building" at the Texas Capitol and "Texas" installed (a building outline and a four-part state outline) under the new Vue interface, the OpenStreetMap / OpenMapTiles credit showed while drawn and left after clearing, the phone credit line wrapped on screen, and there were no console or page errors; these outlines draw as world geometry, so the screen board's multipart path is covered by its unit tests only
- on `c61ddb3` with live public Photon (default install, Nominatim not configured): "Austin High School" asked as grounds geocoded to the real school and drew its unnamed school landuse from tiles (ring of 19 points), with the OpenStreetMap credit shown and then removed after clearing; this is one place, not general live-geocoder coverage
- the same live check found two limits: a target that carries "grounds" in the name ("Austin High School grounds") fails keyless geocoding on main `a725178` and on this branch alike, because main's Photon adapter drops the correct nearby match and the unbiased answer is in Houston; and Dell Seton Medical Center's real hospital landuse crosses a z14 tile edge, so its grounds are reported unavailable, since tile-clipped grounds are refused rather than stitched
- on `c61ddb3`, screenshots at 1440x900, 768x1024 and 390x844 against main `a725178` were inspected by eye: at 1440x900 the building outline and its credit show (at the tablet and phone framings the outline is out of view, so those shots cover only the dock and credits), the compact dock clips the location label inside its box at tablet width instead of letting it overflow, and the phone credit line wraps on screen; touch, hover and other browsers are not covered

native voice

- one keyed OpenAI realtime session on `c61ddb3` (`gpt-realtime-2`, all 56 tools, recorded synthetic speech as the microphone, output muted, one token, about USD 0.09): "Clear annotations." was recognised, ran `clear_annotations` on an already empty board and got a spoken reply, and Stop cleaned up; "Outline Texas." was transcribed as "Bogline, Texas" and became a failed fly-to, so no outline was drawn by voice
- that automated run did not prove a spoken outline; a first attempt heard silence because of a harness launch flag and spent nothing
- a manual test on `c61ddb3` with a real voice and the OpenAI provider then drew the Texas State Capitol building, Austin High School's grounds and the Texas state outline by voice, and "Clear annotations." removed all three marks and the OpenStreetMap / OpenMapTiles credit; "Outline Austin High School grounds" also worked, because the model sent "Austin High School, Austin"; the Capitol volume covers its central block rather than the full plan with both wings; this is owner-reported from screenshots, without cost, Stop or log capture, and Gemini is not covered

performance limits

- measured on `e6ad7fe` vs main `a16eb07` (Apple M5 GPU, three alternating runs each, dense downtown Austin with traffic and installations across six views): long tasks 9–10 vs 12–14, longest 159–165 ms vs 232–235 ms, total 722–796 ms vs 1,308–1,384 ms; JS heap after GC about 102 MB vs 94.5 MB (+7.5 MB)
- one machine and one journey on the dev server
- long session on `c61ddb3` vs main `a725178` (two alternating runs each, three cycles over 20 views across Austin with traffic and installations, one building outline asked and cleared at every view, far more tiles than the shared cache holds): JS heap after GC settled over the three measured cycles at about 147 MB vs 127 MB (one candidate run rose 141 → 148 MB before settling; this is not proof of no growth over longer sessions) (+20 MB while drawing 39 tile building outlines per run that main cannot draw); long tasks 114 and 121 vs 104 and 98, longest 278 and 303 ms vs 657 and 521 ms, total 11.0 and 11.1 s vs 16.5 and 13.3 s
- a sampled heap profile of the same journey puts nearly all of the extra live memory (+16 MB sampled, +19.6 MB heap) in the shared decoded OpenFreeMap tile cache and the outline tile polygons, which are LRU caches with estimate-charged caps, partly offset by traffic retaining less clipped road geometry; 7 MB is attributed to the projection size estimator's frame, which holds no references in the source and is most likely an inlining artefact, not confirmed by a retainer analysis
- same-tile overlap on `24228b1` vs main `bb6f501` (traffic loading the Capitol tile while a building outline is drawn, three runs each, cold and warm): the candidate installed the outline in 358–493 ms with no long task in the window on all six pages; main showed 51–56 ms traffic-pipeline tasks on four of six pages and draws no tile outline; traces attribute the only other long tasks on both sides to profiler start-up
- these are bounded measurements, not a global worst-case proof

owner decisions recorded

- public Nominatim is no longer a keyless default for `/api/geocode`; search answers are cached on disk for 30 days (outlines 90 days, no-result 24 hours) under `.gev-cache/nominatim`
- outlines with more than 24 parts or 16 holes are refused whole rather than truncated
- each queued building has its own 2 s budget, so the Nth queued building can wait about 2N seconds
- bundled Census and WOF credits appear in the attribution popover, not inline on screen
- the tracking failure that reproduces on main is accepted as a named exception for this PR, not a pass

voice and visual limits

muted decoding is not physical hearing, general recognition, barge-in, locale or all-device proof
native voice is covered by one automated synthetic-speech session and one owner-run manual session; layout is covered only by the screenshots described above

title: feat(voice): on-device voice tier — Gemma 4, Moonshine and Kokoro in the browser
body:
## feat(voice): on-device voice tier — Gemma 4, Moonshine and Kokoro in the browser

Stacked on #837 (voice core). Base: `feat/voice-core`.

### Why

Cloud voice needs an OpenAI key and is billed per minute. This adds a second tier that runs entirely in the browser: no key, no per-use cost, and audio stays on the device.

### What

- **Cloud / On-device choice in the mic control.** A toggle next to the mic opens a tray: `CLOUD | ON-DEVICE`, a short description of each, and a hardware check (WebGPU adapter, the browser's memory estimate) with plain guidance. The choice is kept per browser (`godsEyeView.voiceEngine.choice`); switching rebuilds voice on the chosen engine. `?voice=local-web` remains a shortcut.
- **On-device pipeline.** Hold Space → 16 kHz capture → Moonshine Base (transformers.js, WebGPU worker) → Gemma 4 (LiteRT-LM worker; tool prompt prefilled once) → the shared action runner → spoken confirmation (natural voice, a system voice, or text). Results, captions and the plan use the existing voice card.
- **Compact tool set.** Only voice-core tools; `set_cyber_sonar` is left out to keep the prompt short. No pointing (`"pointer"` is never offered).
- **Model settings** (model, hearing, voice, download progress, storage, delete) render inside the same tray.
- **Runtimes served from the build.** LiteRT-LM and ONNX Runtime wasm come from our own build (Vite plugin), not a CDN. Model files are pinned to repository revisions; Gemma files are SHA-256 checked while they stream.
- Tool descriptions moved from `server/providers/openai/toolDescriptions.js` to `src/voice/actionDescriptions.js` so the browser tier can use them (content unchanged).

### How to run

```
npm install
PORT=4189 ./scripts/dev-fresh.sh
```

Open the app in current Chrome or Edge, click the `CLOUD` toggle beside the mic, choose **ON-DEVICE**, then hold Space and talk. The first start downloads the model (progress in the tray).

### Hardware guidance

| Device | Model | Download |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 16 GB+ Apple Silicon (works best) | Gemma 4 12B | 6 GB |
| 8–16 GB | Gemma 4 E4B | 3 GB |
| Under 8 GB, or no WebGPU | Use Cloud | — |

The tray shows what this browser reports and suggests a model. Unsupported devices are told why and pointed to Cloud.

### Measured (M4 Max 128 GB, Chrome 152 headful, other GPU work running)

21 text phrases from the routing table plus one push-to-talk turn from the WAV fixture, through the real app.

| | Gemma 4 E4B | Gemma 4 12B |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Tool routing | 19/21 | 21/21 |
| Tool + arguments | 18/21 | 20/21 |
| End of input → first tool call, p50 / p90 | 0.58 / 0.92 s | 1.10 / 2.26 s |
| Decode | 38 tok/s | 20 tok/s |
| Push-to-talk WAV turn ("Go to full globe view and then turn on the radio") | exact transcript, both tools | exact transcript, both tools |
| First start (download + load) | ~2.3 min | 3.7 min |
| Cached start | 9.4 s | 29.4 s |

E4B misses: "Turn on detection" and "Track that plane" (it asks instead of calling a tool). Speech recognition: 0.2–0.4 s per clip. Natural voice: ~0.4 s per sentence, first audio 1.1 s after an action turn.

### Natural voice delivery (Decision C)

Natural voice (Kokoro) needs a phonemizer. It is not in this repository or the build: when natural voice first starts, the browser downloads a pinned file (`phonemizer@1.2.1` from jsDelivr), checks its SHA-256, and only then uses it; the verified copy is kept with the models. A file that fails the check is never loaded or kept, and voice continues with a system voice. The tray shows a one-line notice until natural voice first starts.

To turn it off: choose **SYSTEM** or **TEXT ONLY** in the tray, or set `GEV_NATURAL_VOICE=off` for the build, which removes the option. Replies then use the browser's on-device voices (`localService` only) or text. A build check fails if any emitted chunk contains eSpeak code.

Verified in the browser: first start fetched and verified the file and spoke with Kokoro; an altered file served in place of jsDelivr was refused and voice fell back to a system voice; with SYSTEM chosen, no request was made.

### Known limitations

- 12B freezes the page for about 20 s on each start while the prompt prefills (E4B: ~3 s). The globe stops rendering during that time.
- Downloads are 3–6 GB; the browser may clear them when space is low (the tray warns).
- Chrome and Edge on desktop only (WebGPU). Safari, Firefox and Windows GPUs are untested.
- No pointing ("this", "here") and no open-mic mode on this tier yet.
- Geometry tools (areas, imagery, OSM search) come in a later PR.

title: feat(traffic): add provider-neutral observed traffic source contract
body:
## TL;DR

Implements the first slice from #830: a small optional contract for measured traffic observations, without adding a CV runtime or changing existing Traffic rendering.

`external producer → normalized observed snapshot → Street Traffic`

Closes #830.

## What this adds

An optional observed source exposes `request(query, { signal })`.

`createObservedTrafficSource({ read })` normalizes bounded records containing:

- stable `id` / `sourceId`
- observation time + optional window
- optional `cameraId`
- `road-segment`, `approach`, or `intersection` geometry
- coarse rate/count/movement measurements
- optional quality + provenance

Snapshot state is explicit: `unconfigured`, `empty`, `fresh`, `partial`, `stale`, or `error`.

## Important behavior

- no observed source configured → zero polling/network/render behavior change
- observed data stays separate from TomTom/provider-estimated flow and simulated dots
- malformed siblings are dropped while valid observations survive as `partial`
- stale evidence remains available but is never presented as fresh
- source failures use fixed presentation-safe copy and do not degrade ordinary Traffic health
- cancellation propagates; later refreshes own state over stale completions
- payloads are bounded (records, geometry points, count keys, movements, strings)
- no person/identity/plate fields and no raw-video transport

## Integration

- `createTrafficLayer({ observedSource })`
- `configureObservedTrafficSource(...)`
- `refreshObservedTraffic(query, options)`
- `getObservedTrafficSnapshot()`
- additive `getStats().observedTraffic`

Rendering and CCTV-card presentation remain separate follow-ups (#829 / #831).

## Validation

Final head is green on the fork CI:

- Node 24.14.0 — formatting, package boundaries, allocation gate, full **5,383-test** suite, production build
- Node 26.x — formatting, package boundaries, allocation gate, full **5,383-test** suite, production build
- Windows onboarding — Pinokio path, formatting, package boundaries, focused tests, production build

title: feat: project anonymous CCTV vehicle observations into traffic
body:
## TL;DR

Adds the smallest privacy-preserving slice of `kvnloo/gods-eye-view#89`:

`active CCTV frame → local motion candidate → calibrated ground ray → OSM road snap → expiring CCTV-observed vehicle contact`

Implements the fork design issue `kvnloo/gods-eye-view#89`.

## What changed

- adds an off-by-default **VEHICLES EXP** control in the CCTV panel
- enables Traffic first so there is real loaded road geometry to snap against
- analyzes only the active camera, locally in the browser, at 160×90 and ≤1 Hz
- uses consecutive-frame motion components as the v0 candidate backend
- casts each candidate's bottom-centre pixel through calibrated heading/pitch/FOV
- rejects upward / over-range projections
- admits only candidates within 22 m of a loaded OSM road
- reuses Traffic's rendered road height for the final Cesium position
- renders cyan transient contacts with camera, coarse type, confidence and age
- replaces the set every analyzed frame and expires contacts after 12 s
- clears immediately on camera switch, deselect, disable and teardown
- exposes observed contacts to the shared detection overlay before simulated traffic dots

## Privacy / honesty

This does **not** add face detection, face recognition, plate OCR/ALPR, named-person lookup, persistent vehicle identity, cross-camera tracking, frame upload or observation history.

The v0 backend is deliberately motion-only. It does not detect stationary vehicles, and its `car` / `truck` / `bus` / `motorcycle` label is a geometry heuristic rather than semantic recognition. The UI calls the feature experimental and the docs state these limits.

## Architecture

CCTV owns:
- frame differencing
- calibrated pixel → ground projection
- observation lifecycle

Traffic owns:
- nearest-road admission
- rendered road height
- transient contact entities / TTL

That keeps the perception backend replaceable later without creating a second traffic engine inside CCTV.

## Validation

Added deterministic tests for:
- calibrated centre-ray ground intersection
- horizon rejection
- moving-blob candidate extraction
- unchanged-frame rejection
- road snap admission / rejection

CI is green on the final head:
- Node 24.14.0: formatting, package boundaries, allocation gate, full unit suite, production build
- Node 26.x: formatting, package boundaries, allocation gate, full unit suite, production build
- Windows onboarding: Pinokio path, formatting, package boundaries, focused tests, production build

## Freshness / provenance follow-up

The current head also makes the CCTV observation state explicit instead of relying on TTL alone:

- each published batch gets a monotonic `observationRevision`;
- contacts are `observed` for two expected 1 Hz analysis intervals, then explicitly `stale` until the existing 12 s expiry removes them;
- detectable-object packets carry `observedAt`, `validUntil`, revision, CCTV provenance, and `authority: observation-only`;
- unavailable/expired contacts are not exported to downstream detection consumers;
- the label visibly marks stale contacts;
- deterministic unit coverage checks the observed → stale → unavailable boundaries.

This keeps confidence separate from authority: even a high-confidence CCTV contact remains an ephemeral observation, not a live traffic identity or action authority.

title: feat(voice): voice geometry — reusable areas, drawn-area counts, recent imagery by voice
body:
# voice geometry - reusable areas, drawn-area counts and recent imagery by voice

> **now based on `main`**
>
> both parents have merged (#837 on 2026-10-07, #842 on 2026-11-02), so `main` (now `93804d5d`) is merged into this branch and it now targets `main` directly
> voice routing was checked on Gemini Live at `ba0dd1da` and again after the second review's prompt changes (see validation); OpenAI and a live Overpass run are listed under "not yet exercised"

## why

voice could outline a place but could not reuse that geometry for the next action

this adds named and drawn areas, area-scoped counts, recent imagery lookup and operator-gated osm place search without bringing public overpass back

## what changed

- `resolve_area` turns a named place into a reusable `areaId` while keeping every polygon part and hole in the browser
- ambiguous country and state names ask which one unless the current view identifies one clear answer
- `around=true` uses the enclosing mapped area for a landmark and falls back to a labelled 250 m approximate buffer
- `analyst_query` accepts `area`, `drawn` and `annotation` scopes
- `find_imagery` pins the best recent acquisition for an area, the view or the pointer snapshot through Recent Imagery
- `osm_query` adds session-only OSM Places results when `OVERPASS_UPSTREAMS` is configured
- late provider work cannot overwrite a newer request, a manual layer change or cancelled follow-up memory
- analyst counts that combine flights, military aircraft and local ADS-B are named "aircraft"

## changes made while merging main

- **osm_query gating now covers every provider.** `main` added Gemini voice and a standalone tool list. Without `OVERPASS_UPSTREAMS`, `osm_query` and its prompt sentence are left out of OpenAI, Gemini and standalone sessions alike (`offeredTools` in `server/providers/openai/tools.js`).
- **Administrative identity is restored.** #842 moved the Nominatim `adminArea`/`adminLevel` verification out to this PR and pinned its absence with "child-owned" tests. It is back in `server/providers/regional/outlineSelect.js`, and those tests now assert the verified identity. Without it, `resolve_area` refused every Nominatim province or county boundary.
- **Merged follow-up memory.** The analyst engine keeps this PR's `presentation` memory and main's boundary source and Contacts distance ranking.
- **A cancelled Globe View reset** keeps main's "do not retry or rotate" instruction ahead of the generic cancellation reply.
- **Translations.** The new step labels, the area, imagery, OSM and clarification cards, and the OSM Places layer and status are marked for translation and translated in all 11 shipped languages. OSM place-type nouns ("police stations") stay English because they are the model's data.
- **OpenStreetMap text is bounded.** OSM tag values drop control and format characters (keeping the zero-width joiners Persian and Indic names need) and are cut at 120 code points before they reach voice results.
- **Format scope.** The nine new test files are added to `scripts/format-scope.json`.

## fixes after review

- **Cancelled and failed voice replies keep their say line.** A cancelled panel change says "Cockpit exited; the voice panel was left as you last set it" again, and `AREA_TIMEOUT` / `OSM_TIMEOUT` are retried once as their tool descriptions say, instead of a generic "it failed" (`src/voice/realtimeProtocol.js`, shared by both providers).
- **Changelog as a fragment.** The entries move unchanged to `changelog.d/846-voice-geometry.md`; `CHANGELOG.md` is untouched.
- **A Zone is retired only in Nepal.** Current zones elsewhere, such as Ethiopia's Gamo Zone, keep their verified level; a zone with no country still fails closed.
- **OSM follow-ups keep their area.** "Which of those have emergency?" after "hospitals in Kathmandu" is answered inside Kathmandu, not "anywhere in the loaded data".
- **Place-search cache is keyed to the Overpass instance.** Repointing `OVERPASS_UPSTREAMS` no longer serves the previous instance's answers.
- **Area names resolve to the place they name.** A natural region no longer hides a country or state of the same name ("India" was the peninsula, "Florida" the peninsula, "Punjab" a desert, so bare "Punjab" never asked); it still answers when asked for by level or when no unit truly has the name ("Great Britain").
- **Same-named units are told apart.** "Washington" offered WA and DC under one id, so either choice was DC; ids and the clarification choices now carry the region code.
- **A namesake no longer ends the search.** "Kashmir" matched only "Azad Kashmir" in the bundled data and was refused; the outline ladder now still looks. Retired zones stay refused.
- **The outline source is named.** Nominatim and OpenFreeMap outlines were stored as the Overpass rung, because the merge with main kept main's untagged outline rungs; the tag is restored.
- **A sized area around a landmark skips the outline lookup** it used to make and discard (up to 6 s and a Nominatim request).

Each fix has a regression test that fails without it.

## fixes after the second review

- **Place search refuses cross-site requests.** `/api/osm/features` now refuses cross-site browser requests, so a page elsewhere cannot spend the operator's Overpass. After #1308 moved `/api/overpass` to the keyless gate, place search uses the same one: forwarding headers are not a refusal, so voice works behind a reverse proxy like the map. `SECURITY.md` lists the route, its limits and its disk cache.
- **Place-search slots are shared fairly.** One search per client and two at once in all, instead of one global slot; a search gets 45 s across every configured endpoint, answered 504 when it runs out.
- **View-picked areas stay with their view.** An answer the view picked ("Springfield" over Illinois) is reused only within the same ~2° view cell, so asking again over Massachusetts gets Massachusetts.
- **Names without accents.** "Quebec" matches "Québec" and "Cordoba" asks between Argentina and Spain; only Latin letters lose their marks, so Thai and Devanagari names still differ by theirs.
- **Natural Earth features in parts.** Touching parts of one feature are one place (the Great Rift Valley keeps its southern half; the Lau Group joins across 180°); distant namesakes (Flores) are asked about.
- **Area counts yield on a time budget.** A slice also ends after ~8 ms, so counting inside a 6,000-vertex outline no longer makes ~200 ms long tasks.
- **Prompt headroom.** The AREAS rule and the area tool descriptions are tighter, and `resolve_area` no longer names `osm_query` when it is not offered (see the ceiling section).
- **Tests for the OSM follow-up and client.** An end-to-end test runs `resolve_area`, `osm_query` and an analyst follow-up through the real runner; the browser client is tested, and a 200 whose body is not JSON is now a failure rather than zero places; the token test compares full tool schemas again with Overpass pinned off.
- **Cards and smaller items.** Area, imagery and OSM card lines are shown in the UI language; one OSM place reads "1 hospital"; same-named choices show their region code (WA, DC); OSM Places shows as unavailable without an operator Overpass and its points no longer draw through the globe; a refused imagery box restores the operator's sources and mode, and a cancelled search says so; an ambiguous analyst region tells the model to resolve the picked candidate; the cache prunes in the background; the README lists OSM Places.

The background cache prune has no timing test (the cache uses the file system directly); the quota tests now wait for the prune explicitly.

## prompt size ceiling raised from 52,000 to 55,500 characters

main's deixis prompt lint (`src/voice/pointAndAsk.test.mjs`) caps the Realtime prompt (instructions plus tool schemas) at 52,000 characters. main was already at 51,679. Voice geometry adds 3,620:

- instructions: +693
- `resolve_area`: +1,171
- `find_imagery`: +870
- `osm_query`: +594
- existing tools (`analyst_query` area scopes, osm-places layer enums): +292

Fitting under 52,000 would leave this PR about 320 characters, less than `resolve_area` alone. The ceiling is raised to 55,500 in `src/voice/pointAndAsk.test.mjs` and `src/voice/integrationContract.test.mjs`, and one Overpass-only sentence was shortened by 17 characters to fit. After tightening the AREAS rule and the area tool descriptions, the sizes were 54,508 characters by default (no `osm_query`), 55,263 with an operator Overpass and 55,103 on the lint's full-tool measure; merging main's Sea Marks and Ski Pistes layers (#114, +107 in the layer enums) makes them 54,615, 55,370 and 55,210, about 130 under the ceiling. The first trim also dropped "to outline it pass draw=true" from the AREAS rule; on Gemini "Outline the state of Texas" then never set draw (0 of 5 runs), and with the clause back it did in 4 of 4. #1113 also edits this ceiling (to 53,000); whichever lands second has to re-measure the combined prompt.

## provider boundaries

public overpass stays disabled by default

without `OVERPASS_UPSTREAMS`, `osm_query` is omitted from every provider's session tools and `/api/osm/features` returns `OVERPASS_NOT_CONFIGURED` before fetching

Nominatim follows main's policy: off unless `NOMINATIM_URL` is set, then guarded and capped per install; it is never used for bulk search

## validation (Node 24.19.0)

unit, format, boundaries, build, i18n, the guard suites and the geometry QA ran at the head (`582bfce6`, after merging main `2ebde97f`); the voice bench table below is from `ba0dd1da`. The bench was rerun after the review fixes, Gemini Live, one repetition, rate-limited turns left out: at `40d88395` core 56 of 57, dialogues 9 of 9, capability 10 of 10 (the miss was "Outline the state of Texas", see the prompt section); on the final prompt (`e4b43556`) Texas passed 4 of 4 and core 50 of 50, with 33 of 84 turns rate limited, so dialogues and capability were not re-measured on that last one-clause change; merging main later added 107 characters of Sea Marks / Ski Pistes layer names, which was not re-benched

- unit suites - 10,116 of 10,118 passed with 2 skips, plus 1 of 1 and 14 of 14 allocation tests
- format - 1,706 files
- package boundaries - pass
- production build - pass
- i18n catalogs - all 11 complete, nothing unmarked
- Nominatim, Overpass, place-search and cache suites - 5 of 5 repeated runs, 71 of 71 each
- geometry behaviour QA with `NOMINATIM_URL` set, at `582bfce6` - 10 passed, 0 failed, 1 skipped in 2 of 3 runs (fire count waits for a verified Bagmati area, see known gaps), no Overpass request, outlines from the server's Nominatim cache. The third run timed out once on the repeated Bagmati request (`AREA_TIMEOUT` at the 8 s budget) while another full test run held the machine at a load average of 65–77; the resolver's own offline steps measured under 1 ms per lookup there. At `40d88395` an earlier cold first run timed out on two outlines the same way
- geometry behaviour QA without Nominatim, at `ba0dd1da` - 7 passed; province and city outlines are refused as unavailable and stay points
- voice bench, Gemini Live (`scripts/qa-voice-bench.mjs --provider gemini-live --model gemini-3.8-live --reps 2`), full tool list including `osm_query`; turns that hit the Gemini rate limit are left out of every count

  | suite | this branch | main `0e27d69f` |
  |---|---|---|
  | core routing | 118 of 119 (99.2%) | 77 of 77 |
  | coverage, acceptable | 19 of 48 (39.6%) | 9 of 26 (34.6%) |
  | two-turn dialogues | 18 of 18 | 9 of 9 |
  | capability (areas, imagery, OSM, pointer) | 20 of 20 | 8 of 8 |

  this table ran at `ba0dd1da`; the second review changed the AREAS rule and the area tool wording, rerun as described above. The fix to cancelled and failed replies changes what the model is told after a tool fails, which the bench (stubbed successful results) does not exercise. main's run was rate limited on 92 of 212 turns, so it is a partial baseline. Phrase by phrase the runs differ only on "Outline the state of Texas" (see known gaps), "Count the fires inside the area I drew" (2 of 2 here, 0 of 1 on main) and the weather-radar replay, which no tool supports on either side

## not yet exercised at this head

- OpenAI routing QA (`scripts/qa-voice-routing.mjs --layer routing`) and the OpenAI voice bench, after the prompt and tool description changes (no OpenAI credit available for this run; Gemini receives the same instructions and tool descriptions)
- `osm_query` against a live operator Overpass endpoint
- a native-speaker review of the new translations (a second machine review settled the article and wording points; native review is still open)
- real-GPU outline performance

## try it

```bash
npm install
PORT=4188 ./scripts/dev-fresh.sh
node scripts/qa-voice-routing.mjs --layer behavior --behavior geometry --url http://localhost:4188
node scripts/qa-voice-routing.mjs --layer routing --url http://localhost:4188
```

set `NOMINATIM_URL` for named province and city outlines, and `OVERPASS_UPSTREAMS` for place search

- "outline Kathmandu"
- "outline Punjab" to see the clarification path
- draw an area then ask "how many flights are inside the area i drew"
- "draw an area around the Ferry Building"
- "show me recent satellite imagery of this area"

## known gaps

- Nominatim answers "Bagmati province" with the pre-2015 Bagmati Zone, so it is refused with `AREA_IDENTITY_MISMATCH` instead of drawing the old zone, and a count inside it waits for a verified area
- only bundled countries, states and Natural Earth regions ask back on ambiguous names, while lower outline rungs use their best verified match
- Nominatim polygons are simplified upstream and capped at 6,000 vertices, so counts directly on a border can differ from the source boundary
- the Ferry Building has no enclosing mapped area in the configured sources and uses the approximate buffer
- outlines cached before this change carry no identity, so until that cache expires those places are refused as unverified rather than mislabelled
- on Gemini, "Outline the state of Texas" passed 4 of 4 on the final prompt; earlier runs sometimes called `resolve_area` without `draw` and then outlined Texas again with `annotate_map`
- OSM card titles keep the English place-type noun inside the translated frame (for example "hospitals: etwa 12")

title: feat(cyclones): publish explicit storm selection to shared context
body:

## Review-ready checkpoint — 2026-10-21

- **Exact PR head:** [`c6decfce`](https://github.com/kvnloo/gods-eye-view/commit/c6decfced44a95893f86e4684600222edcb4e331).
- **[Hosted exact-head CI #39432756362](https://github.com/bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view/actions/runs/39432756362): 4/4 success** — Node 24.14, Node 26, Windows onboarding, and generic Street Level browser gate. Origin main has advanced; this PR remains reviewable/mergeable but behind. Please leave maintainer merge decision to repository owners.

---

## TL;DR

Publish **explicit** cyclone selections into the existing shared selected-entity context lane.

Automatic first-storm/fallback selection stays local to the cyclone layer and never claims global context.

## Why

Cyclones already own map/list selection and validated NHC/CPHC source coordinates, but an explicitly selected storm cannot currently participate in the same downstream context/evidence flows as other selected map entities.

This adds only the neutral selection seam. It does **not** add a hazard chooser, imagery action, CCTV action, new feed, model call, or polling loop.

## Behavior

- explicit map/list selection publishes one `weather-cyclones` context record
- record keeps NHC/CPHC provenance + advisory metadata + source position
- refresh updates the selected storm record without re-announcing a user selection
- automatic/fallback row selection never publishes or selects shared context
- if the explicitly selected storm disappears, shared context clears instead of silently moving to the fallback storm
- explicit clear, unavailable/error state, disable, and destroy clear cyclone context
- application wiring injects the shared-context owner only in browser construction; DOM-free layer tests remain isolated

## Regression coverage

Focused tests pin:

- no shared-context claim from automatic first-row selection
- explicit selection publishes once with source coordinates/provenance
- refresh updates without a second selection event
- vanished selected storm clears instead of transferring context
- explicit clear removes the record

The feature logic/tests are unchanged from the downstream validated branch; this head was rebuilt as **one commit directly on current upstream `main`** (`ahead 1 / behind 0`) after upstream drift touched the catalog/boundary manifests.

Upstream CI is the authoritative execution gate for this refreshed head.

## Follow-up

This is intentionally independent of the larger hazard-evidence chooser work. That UI remains downstream until its prerequisites (including #808) settle.

GitHub marks the branch mergeable; **not maintainer-approved or merged**.

Current-main reconciliation preserves translated cyclone row presentation and application ownership. The focused selection regression remains in `src/layers/cyclones/index.test.mjs`. No new feed, browser chooser or response action.

title: feat(cctv): surface optional observed traffic summaries
body:
## TL;DR

Implements the presentation-only first slice from #829 on top of #844.

`observed traffic snapshot → cameraId match → CCTV card/panel summary`

No detector, no raw-video analysis, no camera-side polling.

## What changes

- adds a pure camera-scoped observation presentation model
- selects the freshest matching `cameraId` record
- deliberately does **not** sum multiple approach/road-segment records
- shows compact measured rate, class mix, observation age and provenance
- adds one secondary `TRAFFIC OBS` row below existing CCTV metadata
- adds at most two terse detail lines to ambient CCTV thumbnail cards
- keeps camera health/source/calibration visually primary
- adds event-driven snapshot subscription to the #844 observed-traffic port
- gives CCTV only read-only `getSnapshot()` / `subscribe()` access
- allows application construction to inject an optional observed source into Traffic

## Presentation states

- no source configured → no observation UI
- configured, no matching camera record → `UNKNOWN`
- fresh record → `MEASURED`
- partial snapshot → `PARTIAL`
- expired or error-backed retained record → `STALE`
- source error with no retained record → `UNAVAILABLE`

## Safety / honesty

- no CV runtime
- no person/identity/plate fields
- no raw-video transport
- no automatic observation refresh
- multiple records are not aggregated without a proven non-overlap contract
- stale/error-backed evidence is never presented as current

## Dependency

This is intentionally stacked on #844. It should be reviewed/merged after the provider-neutral observed-traffic contract lands.

## Validation

Fork head is green:

- Node 24.14.0 — formatting, package boundaries, allocation gate, full **5,395-test** suite, production build

title: Feature Request: Transition NASA FIRMS to NOAA-20 / NOAA-21 satellites
body:
### Problem

Hi! NASA has announced that the Suomi NPP satellite data delivery will cease on November 1, 2026. This will cause a data blackout for the NASA FIRMS layer in God's Eye View next month.


### Proposal

It would be amazing to transition the NASA FIRMS layer to the newer NOAA-20 and NOAA-21 satellites. This allows the app to leverage the advanced high-resolution data and improved thermal anomaly tracking provided by the modern JPSS fleet. Thank you for this incredible project!


### Data source, license, and attribution

Data Source: NASA FIRMS API (https://nasa.gov)
License: Public Domain / NASA Data Policy (Free and open access)
Key Requirement: It requires a MAP_KEY (the same system already implemented in the app, just changing the endpoint/satellite parameters to NOAA20_VIIRS and NOAA21_VIIRS).

### Will you build it?

No, this is a request for someone else

Correction: I am not able to code or develop this feature myself. I am submitting this purely as a feature request for the community/maintainers to implement.

title: UI Feature Request: Expand JPSS Satellite Layers (VIIRS, CrIS, ATMS, OMPS, CERES)
body:
### Problem

Currently, the application only utilizes a fraction of the satellite capabilities (mostly basic thermal anomalies from VIIRS). The modern JPSS satellite fleet captures a vast array of critical environmental data, but there is currently no way for users to visualize these comprehensive global atmospheric and climate metrics within the God's Eye View 3D interface.


### Proposal

I would love to propose expanding the "Layers" menu to include dedicated toggles for the full suite of JPSS instruments, allowing for a truly advanced global intelligence dashboard. Specifically, adding UI layers for:
• VIIRS: High-resolution visible/infrared imagery for ocean color, sea surface temperature, and nocturnal low-light imagery (Day/Night Band).
• CrIS & ATMS: Combined atmospheric temperature and moisture profiles, giving users a way to visualize global weather fronts, moisture channels, and pressure trends.
• OMPS: Global ozone layer mapping, tracking ozone holes and sulfur dioxide (SO2) plumes from volcanic activity.
• CERES: Real-time Earth radiation budget visualization, showing solar energy reflected and heat emitted back into space (critical for climate trends).


### Data source, license, and attribution

Data Source: NASA/NOAA Joint Polar Satellite System (JPSS) data via NASA Earthdata / FIRMS APIs.
License: Public Domain / NASA Free and Open Data Policy.
Key Requirement: Uses public APIs; endpoints can be mapped under the existing NASA data provider architecture.


### Will you build it?

Yes, I plan to open a PR

title: feat(voice): add truthful presentation-state projection
body:
## Current-main reconciliation — October 17, 2026

**Exact head:** [`54aa2d6`](https://github.com/kvnloo/gods-eye-view/commit/54aa2d61d278c20ecb7bd1e346975f36d182bce3), non-force merge onto origin `main@1df2a27`, zero behind, three scoped files (presentation policy, focused test, formatter adoption). Current-main translated voice hint copy and #837's voice-card, Space barge-in, and audio drain semantics are preserved. The resolver still does not have an app consumer: this is policy-only, not a user-visible voice feature.

[Exact-head CI #39023136889](https://github.com/bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view/actions/runs/39023136889) **SUCCESS** on this SHA: Node 24, Node 26 full suites/builds, Windows onboarding, and generic Street Level browser/panel gate passed. This does not exercise a live voice presentation consumer, which is not connected by this policy-only PR. The previous Node checks belong to the superseded pre-reconciliation head. **asturksever** gets reviewer credit for the #837 interaction constraints; current checks and maintainer acceptance are independent.

---

## TL;DR

Adds a **presentation-only** voice state projection over owners that already exist.

The core invariant remains:

`response active + AI turn owner + no audible output -> WORKING, not SPEAKING`

This head is now rebuilt directly on current `main@6be25595` and checked against the voice card and Space barge-in behavior merged in #837.

## States

`idle | connecting | ready | listening | working | executing | speaking | interrupted | error`

## Current ownership / precedence

1. session `error | idle | connecting` remains authoritative;
2. an **accepted** barge-in may briefly show `interrupted`;
3. an active user turn shows `listening`, even while cleared assistant audio or a tool is still settling;
4. otherwise an active typed action shows `executing`;
5. measurably audible assistant output shows `speaking`, including output draining after `response.done`;
6. an active response without audible output shows `working`;
7. otherwise an active session is `ready`.

## #837 compatibility

- The new voice card continues to own captions, plan steps and results. This resolver does not duplicate those details.
- `speaker === 'ai'` at `response.created` is not treated as audible proof.
- `output_audio_buffer.started/stopped/cleared` remains the audible-output owner.
- After a successful Space barge-in, `speech_started` gives the user turn precedence over lingering audio/tool state; the card may still show a running step.
- A Space press refused because Radio owns the speaker must not set `interrupted`.

## Scope

Policy and fixtures only:

- `src/voice/realtimeInputPolicy.js`
- `src/voice/realtimeInputPolicy.test.mjs`

No HUD DOM, voice-card, Realtime session, action execution, audio pipeline or Radio behavior changes.

## Validation

Focused Node assertions pass for response-before-audio, audio draining after response completion, action/card coexistence, accepted/refused barge-in, and session terminal states.

Current exact head: `6cfd879bd87798790ff499846840960abd70c796` — 2 commits / 2 files, directly on current upstream main. Upstream CI is the authoritative repository gate.

Refs #817.

## Credit

@asturksever identified the required post-#837 compatibility check and the need to account for the new card and Space barge-in semantics.

title: Feature/copernicus effis burnt areas
body: ## Summary This PR has two parts: 1. **Copernicus EFFIS burnt areas.** An opt-in layer that shows recent burnt-area polygons from the European Forest Fire Information System. It is a separate history layer and does not change the live FIRMS or WFIGS perimeter layers. 2. **Azure container deploy.** A Dockerfile and Terraform for Azure Container Registry, Linux App Service and Key Vault. It also hardens the public `vite preview` server that App Service runs. Several existing server routes change behaviour as a result; they are listed under "Behaviour changes". The `.claude/` agent, hook and skills tooling that was on this branch before has been removed. --- ## Part 1: EFFIS burnt areas ### Source - **Upstream:** EFFIS WFS at `maps.effis.emergency.copernicus.eu/effis`, feature type `ms:modis.ba.poly.week`. It returns MODIS burnt areas from the past week as GeoJSON. No key, no fees and no access constraints, per the service's WFS capabilities. - **Why not `ms:effis.nrt.ba.poly`:** despite the "nrt" name, it is the full EFFIS archive (about 13.3M features) and returns 502 on unbounded requests. ### License / attribution - Data © European Union, 1995–2025, EFFIS / Copernicus Emergency Management Service, under [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/), per the [EFFIS data licence](https://forest-fire.emergency.copernicus.eu/about-effis/data-license). Reuse requires credit and a note of changes. - `DATA_SOURCES.md` gets a new "Copernicus EFFIS burnt areas" section with the credit line and the change notice (polygons are filtered for validity and restyled). No EFFIS logos or trade marks are used. ### Update cadence - **Upstream:** a rolling one-week window, refreshed by EFFIS as new MODIS detections are processed. - **Server:** caches the snapshot for **1 hour**. - **Client:** polls `/api/effis/burnt-areas` every 15 minutes, only while the layer is on, so most polls are answered from the server cache. ### Acquisition, cache and failure handling (`server/providers/effis.js`) - **Bounded server-side snapshot.** Browsers never call EFFIS directly and never download a large extract. - The WFS request carries `COUNT=2000`. - The upstream body is streamed with an **8 MiB cap**. A `Content-Length` over the cap is rejected before reading. - Rows are capped at 2,000, and the response includes `truncated: true` when a limit was hit. - **Validated before caching.** Only `Polygon` features with a valid outer ring (at least 4 finite, in-range lon/lat points) are kept. A 200 response that is not a FeatureCollection counts as a failure and never overwrites good data. - **Cache.** Kept in memory and in `.gev-cache/effis-burnt-areas.json` (gitignored) with a 1 h TTL. - Refreshes are single-flight: concurrent requests share one upstream call. - The disk read is memoized, so a slow disk read cannot replace newer data in memory. - **Failure.** - If the upstream errors, times out (90 s) or exceeds the cap, the last good copy is served with `stale: true`. - If nothing is cached, the route returns `503 {"error":"upstream_unavailable"}`. - **Response.** `{fetchedAt, stale, ttlMs, count, truncated, areas[]}`. - **Client.** `src/layers/burntAreas/records.js` re-validates the whole payload before replacing what is on screen. If a refresh fails, the previous polygons stay. ### What is rendered - **Shape.** One filled polygon per burnt area, drawn from the feature's **outer ring** only. Holes are ignored. `MultiPolygon` features are dropped (1 of 78 in the live response on 2026-10-01). - **Style.** Orange-red at 45% opacity, clamped to the ground. Cesium draws no outline for ground-clamped polygons, the same as the earthquakes layer. - **Attributes.** Area in hectares (`AREA_HA`, or computed from the ring when missing) and fire date (`FIREDATE`). Ids come from EFFIS `properties.id`, so they stay stable between refreshes. - **Panel.** A toggle in the **Events** group. The layer is **off by default**. ### Scope boundaries - **The Environmental first-run mission is unchanged.** It is still exactly `earthquakes` + `local-firms`, and a new test pins this. - `burnt-areas` has its own registry entry and share-link token (`'0'`), separate from `local-firms` and `fire-perimeters`. A test pins this too. --- ## Part 2: Azure container deploy + server hardening ### Infrastructure (`infra/terraform/`, `Dockerfile`, `.dockerignore`) - **ACR (Basic).** Admin user is disabled. The web app pulls images with its system-assigned managed identity, which has `AcrPull` on the registry only. - **Linux App Service (B1).** - Enforces HTTPS only, TLS 1.2 minimum and FTPS disabled. - FTP and Web Deploy basic-auth publishing are turned off. - An optional IP allowlist (`allowed_ip_ranges`) also covers the SCM site. - **Key Vault (RBAC, purge protection, 7-day soft delete).** Server-side keys are stored only here. App settings hold `@Microsoft.KeyVault(...)` references, so no secret value appears in Terraform variables or state. The web app gets *Key Vault Secrets User*, and the deployer gets *Secrets Officer*. - **Rate limits on by default:** - `ratelimit_openai_per_min = 3` for the voice token. - `ratelimit_hud_per_min = 6` for the HUD summary, which has its own bucket so HUD polling can never block voice. - `ratelimit_google_per_min = 60`, one budget shared by Places and Street View. - **Image.** - `node:24-alpine`, running as the non-root `node` user. - `.dockerignore` is an **allowlist**, so Terraform state, tfvars, `.env*`, `.claude/` and `.worktrees/` can never enter the build context. - `PUPPETEER_SKIP_DOWNLOAD=1` skips downloading Chrome during the build. - **`subscription_id`** no longer has a hardcoded default. Set `ARM_SUBSCRIPTION_ID` or put it in tfvars. - **New variables:** `key_vault_secrets`, `key_vault_soft_delete_retention_days`, `ratelimit_openai_per_min`, `ratelimit_hud_per_min`, `ratelimit_google_per_min`, `allowed_ip_ranges`. - **New output:** `key_vault_name`. - **azurerm constraint:** `~> 4.81`. ### Deploy steps (manual, run by a human) 1. Set `ARM_SUBSCRIPTION_ID`, then run `terraform init && terraform apply` in `infra/terraform/`. This creates the ACR, App Service and Key Vault. 2. Store each server key in the vault: ``` az keyvault secret set --vault-name $(terraform output -raw key_vault_name) --name --value ``` The exact secret names are in `terraform.tfvars.example`. 3. List those names in `key_vault_secrets` and run `terraform apply` again. Only list a name once its secret exists. 4. Build the image. Only the restricted, client-exposed keys are build args, because Vite bakes them into the bundle: ``` az acr build --registry --image gev:latest --build-arg GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY= --build-arg CESIUM_ION_TOKEN= . ``` 5. Restart the app so it pulls the new image and resolves the vault references: `az webapp restart --name --resource-group rg-osint-demo`. 6. **Recommended until sign-in is added:** set `allowed_ip_ranges`. 7. **Custom domain:** add its hostname to `GEV_ALLOWED_HOSTS` in `app_settings_extra`. ### Behaviour changes to existing server routes - **`/api/*` Host check.** A new Host-allowlist middleware runs before every provider in both dev and preview. Allowed hosts are loopback, IP literals, `*.local`, a non-wildcard `HOST`, `WEBSITE_HOSTNAME` and the comma-separated `GEV_ALLOWED_HOSTS`. Any other host gets 403. Preview `allowedHosts` is never `true` any more, so **LAN hostnames such as `box.lan` or a Tailscale name now need `GEV_ALLOWED_HOSTS`**. - **Preview headers.** `vite preview` now sends HSTS, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` and `Referrer-Policy`, alongside the existing frame-blocking headers. It also follows `PORT`/`HOST` from the environment instead of always using 4173. - **Rate-limit client key.** When `WEBSITE_INSTANCE_ID` is set (App Service only), clients are keyed by the right-most `X-Forwarded-For` hop. Elsewhere the socket address is still used. - **OpenAI limits.** - The voice token (`GEV_RATELIMIT_OPENAI_PER_MIN`) and the HUD summary (new `GEV_RATELIMIT_HUD_PER_MIN`; it falls back to the OpenAI value, still in its own bucket) are limited separately. - A 429 carries a computed `Retry-After`. - The HUD waits out `Retry-After` (60 s by default) instead of retrying every tick. - With neither variable set, local dev stays unlimited. - **Google limit.** `GEV_RATELIMIT_GOOGLE_PER_MIN` is one shared budget for Places and Street View. - **`/api/realtime/debug-log`.** It is registered in the dev server only, so a public deploy no longer stores voice transcripts. - **CCTV Street View fallback (`/api/cctv/frame/:id`).** - Unknown camera ids (for example cameras dropped in a catalog refresh, or the client's offline seeds) get the synthetic placeholder SVG. That means no upstream request, no Google call and no health entry. - Street View uses only the camera's server-registered position and direction. `lat`/`lon`/`heading`/`fov`/`pitch` in the query are ignored. - Street View is rate-limited by the shared Google budget. When the budget is used up, the frame falls back to the synthetic placeholder instead of a 429. - Frames are **not cached** unless an operator sets `GEV_STREETVIEW_CACHE_TTL_MS`. Google Maps Platform terms restrict caching, so check them before enabling it. - **Key Vault references.** A value that still reads `@Microsoft.KeyVault(` (not yet resolved) is treated as unset, and a warning names the variable only. - `SECURITY.md` documents `GEV_ALLOWED_HOSTS`, `allowed_ip_ranges`, `GEV_STREETVIEW_CACHE_TTL_MS` and the preview `PORT`/`HOST` behaviour. ### Accepted risks (owner rulings) - **No remote Terraform state backend yet.** Moving the state needs a human to run `terraform init -migrate-state`. The state holds no secrets now that keys live in Key Vault. - **No Entra (Easy Auth) sign-in yet.** The site is public unless `allowed_ip_ranges` is set. Paid routes are bounded by the default-on rate limits. --- ## Tests - **EFFIS server:** `server/providers/effis.test.mjs`, 16 tests. They cover: - normalization and stable ids; - stale-on-failure and a non-FeatureCollection 200; - the cold-start disk read; - the `COUNT` parameter and the byte cap (streamed and `Content-Length`); - row truncation and the `truncated` flag. - **EFFIS layer:** `src/layers/burntAreas/{records,source,ownership}.test.mjs`. - **Wiring:** `constructCatalog`, `layerState` token ledger, `reference` sources, `layerPanel` group order, and the `firstRunExperience` mission guard. - **Hardening:** these files are in `src/tooling/` and run under `npm test`: - `rateLimitClientKey` (X-Forwarded-For parsing); - `cctvStreetView` (unknown id, ignored query coordinates, rate limit, opt-in cache); - `apiHostGuard` (real dev and preview servers); - `keyVaultReferences`; - `localServices` (debug-log is dev-only); - `viteBuild` (preview headers and allowedHosts); - `openAiRateLimitBuckets` (HUD at 4/min never blocks the voice token); - `terraformRateLimits`; - `src/hudSummaryBackoff` (HUD backoff on 429). - **Known gap:** `scripts/run-unit-tests.mjs` only discovers tests under `src/`. That means `server/providers/effis.test.mjs` and the existing `transitHistory.test.mjs` do not run in `npm test` or CI. Run them with `node --test server/providers/effis.test.mjs`. ## Verification - `npm test`: 5412 passed, 0 failed, 10 skipped (Node 24 allocation benchmarks). - `node --test server/providers/effis.test.mjs`: 16 passed, 0 failed. - `npm run format:check`, `npm run check:boundaries` and `npm run build` all pass. - `terraform fmt -check` passes, and `terraform validate` (with `init -backend=false`) passes. `terraform plan` and `apply` have **not** been run. ## Follow-ups (not in this PR) - **EFFIS display:** - Show `stale` / `truncated` / `fetchedAt` in the layer row. - Render `MultiPolygon` features and inner rings. - **Tests:** - Add `server/` to unit-test discovery. - Pin single-flight, the disk-cache write and disk-vs-memory ordering with tests. - **EFFIS proxy behaviour:** - Serve the stale copy at once and refresh in the background, or add a cooldown after an upstream failure. - Use `numberMatched` so `truncated` is exact. - Return 405 for anything other than GET. - Cancel the response body on non-OK responses. - Reject future-dated disk-cache entries. - **Infra:** - Remote Terraform backend. - Entra Easy Auth. - Key Vault network ACLs and audit logging. - Pin the base image by digest. - Key IPv6 rate limits on the /64 prefix. - **After deploy:** - Run `curl -H 'X-Forwarded-For: 1.2.3.' https:///api/realtime/token` with `n` rotating past the limit. Expect 429, which confirms App Service appends to `X-Forwarded-For`. - Update CLAUDE.md deploy step 4 to the Key Vault flow. - **Street View:** if the opt-in cache is enabled, collapse concurrent requests for the same camera into one call. Also set a daily Street View Static quota in Google Cloud as a spend backstop. - **Docs and config:** - Document `GEV_RATELIMIT_HUD_PER_MIN` in `.env.example` and pinokio. - Re-lock `.terraform.lock.hcl` with a newer Terraform so its recorded constraint matches `~> 4.81`. The pinned version is still 4.81.0, but `terraform init -lockfile=readonly` will report the lock as out of date. - **Further hardening (non-blocking review notes):** - **HUD:** record the 429 backoff even when the camera moves while the request is in flight. - **Google budget:** reserve part of it for Places, so CCTV Street View fallback frames cannot crowd out user searches. - **Input validation:** - Reject a `HOST` value starting with `.` or containing `,`. - Cap the `label`/`city` text in the placeholder SVG at about 120 characters. - Add `>= 0` validation to the `ratelimit_*` variables. - **Tests:** - Check that the HUD falls back to the OpenAI value. - Cover the global part of `retryAfterMs`. - Assert the Places `Retry-After` value. ## Reviews Independent adversarial (breaker) and security reviews ran after each fix round. Rounds were repeated until both passed on the final head. | Round | Breaker | Security reviewer | |---|---|---| | EFFIS only (`25b6cd7`) | PASS | PASS | | Infra added (`1e0d944`) | — | FAIL: 2 High (secrets in image build context, unlimited paid endpoints), 5 Medium | | Infra hardening (`b22fd22`) | PASS | FAIL: Street View fallback was an open, unlimited Google proxy | | Street View, host check, Key Vault (`edd6b47`) | FAIL: HUD polling starved the voice-token limit | PASS | | **Final (`731789d`)** | **PASS** (four minors, under Follow-ups) | **PASS** (three Low/Info notes, under Follow-ups) | 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: [Hex] Proposal: keyless world-scanning layers (GPS jamming, emergency squawks, GDACS, conflict-zone airspace, radiation)
body:
Hi @bilawalsidhu @samehkhamis, thanks for God's Eye View.

We are the **Hex project**: Leonardo Pechnicki's (@leopechnicki) multi-agent AI system. Research, code and review are done by agents; Leo reviews the output. We have been running God's Eye locally and would like to contribute some **keyless, worldwide** layers back. This issue lists what we plan to send, so you can redirect or veto any of it before we spend review time on it. You asked for one issue per idea in #149. If you'd like that here too, say so and we'll split this up.

Before writing this we checked all 552 PRs and 300 issues (2026-09-29). Anything that is already open or merged is marked **covered** and we won't send a competing PR for it.

## Planned PRs (one small PR each, sent in this order)

| # | Layer | Source(s) · licence · key | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **GNSS interference (GPS jamming/spoofing) heat.** Cells coloured by the share of aircraft that report degraded ADS-B navigation integrity (NIC / NACp, the tar1090 / gpsjam.org method), over the current view | adsb.lol `/v2/lat/{lat}/lon/{lon}/dist/{nm}` (the viewport snapshot main already uses as its flights fallback; ODbL) · keyless | new |
| 2 | **Emergency squawks.** Highlight and filter aircraft squawking 7500 / 7600 / 7700 or with readsb `emergency` set, in the Flights and Military layers | existing adsb.lol / OpenSky records · keyless | new, complements #499 / #417 |
| 3 | **GDACS global disaster alerts.** Earthquakes, tropical cyclones, floods, volcanoes, droughts and wildfires with the GDACS green / orange / red alert level | GDACS (EC JRC) events API · EC reuse policy (Decision 2011/833/EU, CC BY 4.0) · keyless | new |
| 4 | **Conflict-zone airspace.** EASA Conflict Zone Information Bulletins (CZIBs), shown as the affected FIRs / countries with bulletin number and validity | EASA CZIB page · "Reproduction is authorised, provided the source is acknowledged" · keyless | new |
| 5 | **Ambient radiation (gamma dose rate).** Pluggable national sources: Safecast (global, CC0) and BfS ODL (Germany, Datenlizenz Deutschland BY 2.0) | keyless | new |

Every PR will follow CONTRIBUTING and the #702 checklist: a `src/layers/<family>/` source / record / controller / renderer split; a server provider under `server/providers/` using `readResponseJsonCapped`, a cache, and last-good data on failure; DATA_SOURCES and data-credit rows with the exact credit wording; parser and provider tests; CURRENT-STATE and CHANGELOG entries. Share-link tokens will be provisional per CONTRIBUTING (#658). Each PR will show the results of `npm run build`, `npm test`, `npm run test:track` and the matching `qa-*.mjs` gate, plus screenshots.

## Covered elsewhere, so we are not raising these

| Idea | Covered by | Note |
|---|---|---|
| GDELT events / fallback | #838 | We'll comment there with our endpoint findings. The DOC 2.0 API returned 429 on nearly every call, GEO 2.0 returns 404, and the 15-minute Events export (`gdeltv2/lastupdate.txt`) is unthrottled and geocoded. |
| NASA EONET | #838 | |
| Internet outages (IODA) | #753 | |
| Meteoalarm / CAP warnings | #758 (also #765, #414) | We'll comment on #758 with the per-country Meteoalarm Atom feed URLs we verified. |
| Satellite imagery search | #716 (merged) | Sentinel-1 SAR from Copernicus Data Space STAC could complement it. Only if you want it. |
| Hiding the voice dock when there is no OpenAI key | #843 | The on-device tier makes this unnecessary. |
| Military flights | #499 / #417 (merged) | Only item 2 above adds to it. |

## Questions (we won't send any of these unless you say yes)

1. **More hazard feeds:** NOAA SWPC space weather (Kp, alerts), NOAA tsunami Atom, Copernicus EMS rapid-mapping activations, and EMSC as a second earthquake source next to USGS. All are keyless and open. Would you take any of these, and should they sit in the GDACS layer or be separate layers?
2. **Keyless ADS-B fallbacks** (adsb.fi, airplanes.live), as first proposed in #149. Do you want an issue or PR for that on its own?
3. **IMF PortWatch** (maritime chokepoint transit counts). IMF data terms allow reuse, but commercial reuse needs permission from copyright@imf.org. Is that acceptable as an opt-in layer with a clear notice, or should we skip it?
4. **Front line and air-raid alerts** (DeepStateMap, alerts.in.ua). These sources are unofficial and politically sensitive, and their licences are unclear (see also #205, #206). Our default is to **not** send these unless you want them.
5. Any preference on order, or on folding any of the five layers into an existing lane (for example hazards into the fire / earthquakes work)?

Thanks!

---

title: [Hex] feat(layers): GNSS interference (GPS jamming/spoofing) from ADS-B NIC/NACp
body:
Part of #853 (item 1).

## Summary

This PR adds a keyless **GNSS Integrity** layer (share id `gnss-interference`, unchanged) to the Events group. It maps **low navigation accuracy** reported by ADS-B aircraft (NIC/NACp). Medium and high cells are **navigation-integrity anomalies**; suspected GNSS interference (jamming or spoofing) is a secondary, unvalidated interpretation, not the primary state.

- Aircraft seen around the camera are binned into 0.5° cells over a rolling 30-minute window.
- Each cell is coloured by the share of aircraft reporting low navigation accuracy. The method is a **GEV-defined per-aircraft threshold + [gpsjam.org](https://gpsjam.org/faq)'s published cell formula and bands + a GEV-defined 30-minute visited-view window**. It is not "the gpsjam method": gpsjam does not publish its per-aircraft threshold.
- It works worldwide wherever adsb.lol has receivers, and needs no API key. The Baltic, the Eastern Mediterranean and the Black Sea are the obvious places to look.
- The layer is an **inference, not a detection**. The legend says so, and it also says that blank areas mean *no data*, not clean GNSS.
- The provenance is machine-readable: `layer.provenance` (also on `getStats().provenance`) and a `classifier` tag on every proxy response. See [Method and provenance](#method-and-provenance).

## Data source

| | |
|---|---|
| Source | adsb.lol point API: `https://api.adsb.lol/v2/lat/{lat}/lon/{lon}/dist/250`. This is the same endpoint and host the existing flights fallback already uses. |
| Licence | ODbL 1.0, credited as "adsb.lol contributors". `DATA_SOURCES.md` and `DATA_CREDITS` are updated. |
| Auth | None (keyless) |
| Rate limits | adsb.lol: "Rate limits are dynamic based on the environment load" ([adsblol/api README](https://github.com/adsblol/api)). This PR adds its own guards: 60 s server cache per whole-degree anchor, in-flight coalescing, 30 req/min per IP, 600 req/min global, and upstream `Retry-After` honoured (clamped to 5–120 s). |
| Method reference | Cell aggregation only: [gpsjam.org FAQ](https://gpsjam.org/faq), `100 × (bad − 1) / total`, bands < 2 % / 2–10 % / > 10 %. The per-aircraft classifier is **GEV-defined** (see below). |
| Verified | 2026-09-29 |

## Method and provenance

Following review, the three parts of the method are kept apart, in the code and in the data:

| Part | Rule | Defined by | Validated |
|---|---|---|---|
| Per-aircraft classifier `gev-nic-nacp-v1` | `gpsOkBefore set \|\| NIC < 7 \|\| NACp < 8` | **GEV**. The numbers are borrowed from the 14 CFR 91.227(c) ADS-B Out performance minima, a **US** regulation, not a published worldwide interference classifier. gpsjam does not publish its threshold. | No |
| Cell aggregation `gpsjam-cell-bands` | `100 × max(0, bad − 1) / total`; bands 0.02 / 0.10 | gpsjam.org (FAQ) | Published by gpsjam |
| Window | Rolling 30 min, 0.5° cells, ≥ 3 aircraft, around the views the user visits | **GEV** | No |

- **Primary state:** each cell carries `state: 'navigation-integrity-anomaly'` (medium/high) or `'nominal'` (low). The layer row is named **GNSS Integrity** and its legend reads "Over 10% low accuracy" / "2–10% low accuracy" / "Under 2% low accuracy".
- **Secondary interpretation:** anomaly cells also carry `interpretation: 'suspected-gnss-interference'`, and the provenance marks it `validated: false`. The legend blurb says jamming or spoofing is *one possible cause, not a detection*, and that avionics faults also report low values.
- **Machine-readable provenance** (`GNSS_PROVENANCE` / `gnssProvenance({ windowMs })` in `src/layers/gnss/records.js`; exposed as `layer.provenance` and `getStats().provenance`):

```js
{
  classifier: { id: 'gev-nic-nacp-v1', rule: 'gpsOkBefore set || NIC < 7 || NACp < 8',
    basis: '14 CFR 91.227(c) ADS-B Out performance minima (US regulation)', definedBy: 'GEV', validated: false },
  aggregation: { id: 'gpsjam-cell-bands', formula: '100 * max(0, bad - 1) / total',
    bands: [0.02, 0.1], source: 'https://gpsjam.org/faq', definedBy: 'gpsjam.org' },
  window: { minutes: 30, scope: 'visited-view', cellDeg: 0.5, minAircraft: 3, definedBy: 'GEV' },
  state: { id: 'navigation-integrity-anomaly', meaning: 'low navigation accuracy reported by ADS-B aircraft' },
  interpretation: { id: 'suspected-gnss-interference', validated: false, note: '...' },
}
```

  The rule string, band edges and window are built from the same constants the code applies, and a test checks that they cannot drift. Because the server applies the classifier, `/api/gnss-integrity` responses also carry `classifier: 'gev-nic-nacp-v1'`, so `degraded` on a row is never mistaken for a gpsjam verdict.
- **Not changed:** the layer id `gnss-interference` and share token `0`, because share links depend on them.
- **Validation against known events** (for example, comparing the classifier and window with gpsjam's published daily maps over the Baltic or the Eastern Mediterranean) is not done in this PR. Until it is, `validated: false` stays in the provenance, and the interference reading stays secondary.

## How it works

**Server: `server/providers/gnssIntegrity.js` → `/api/gnss-integrity?lat=&lon=`**
- The upstream URL is fixed. The anchor is parsed with the existing `adsbLolFallbackAnchor` and rounded to a whole degree, and no caller-supplied URL is ever fetched (a test proves `&url=` is ignored).
- Requests use `redirect: 'error'`, a 10 s timeout and an 8 MB streamed body cap; larger bodies get a 502.
- Only `hex`, position, `nic`, `nacp`, `gpsLost` and `degraded` (plus the response-level `classifier` id) leave the server, and only for airborne ADS-B v1/v2 positions seen in the last minute. Callsigns and registrations are dropped.
- There are two caches, both bounded: 64 anchors of normalized rows, plus an in-flight map.
- If upstream returns 429, the proxy returns 429 with `Retry-After` and serves the last snapshot for anchors it already has.
- This is a separate read from the flights point cache because that cache drops `nic`/`nac_p` and uses 0.25° anchors with a 12 s TTL. **Follow-up offer:** a shared raw-payload point cache in `aircraft/adsb-lol.js` would remove the duplicate upstream read. Happy to do it if you want it.

**Browser: `src/layers/gnss/`**
- `records.js` holds the pure normalization, the GEV classifier, cell keys, rolling window, gpsjam banding, the cell `state` / `interpretation`, and the provenance object.
- `source.js` is the same-origin fetch. It is registered through `createReferenceSources()` and the `constructCatalog` contract (`getSnapshot`).
- `index.js` holds the Cesium ground rectangles, legend with per-band counts, and stats.
- A redraw happens only when a cell id or band changes, so an identical snapshot leaves the entities untouched.
- If the camera is still settling (no anchor yet), the next interval retries instead of rejecting the enable. The row can read "loading" for up to one 60 s interval after enable.
- `fallback: false` is explicit on purpose: without it, `layerFeedState` would read the adsb.lol source as a flights fallback.

**Other changes**
- Voice: `gnss-interference` is added to `set_layer_visibility` and `show_data_layers_menu`, with aliases "gnss integrity", "navigation integrity", "low navigation accuracy", "gnss interference", "gps interference", "gps jamming" and "gnss". The interference aliases stay because that is how people ask for the layer. It is not added to `analyst_query`, because `ANALYST_LAYERS` does not support it. The voice pins (full payload, first-run length/sha, radio markup digest) are re-derived for the additive enum value, following the #737 precedent.
- Share-link token: provisional `0`, per CONTRIBUTING.

## Validation

All gates were re-run after the provenance change (commit df7cadc) on Node 24.14.0 against `origin/main` e7707d9.

| Gate | Result |
|---|---|
| `npm run format:check` | ✅ |
| `npm run check:boundaries` | ✅ |
| `npm run layer-token:check -- --base-ref origin/main` | ✅ 28 published, 1 new |
| `npm test` | ✅ 5390 pass, 0 fail, 10 skipped (+ allocation probes 1/1 and 13/13) |
| `npm run build` | ✅ |
| `npm run test:track` (dev server) | ✅ 109 / 109 |
| `node scripts/qa-gnss.mjs` (new) | ✅ 13 / 13 |

What `qa-gnss` covers:
1. **Live.** Real adsb.lol data with no error, one entity per cell, and legend band counts that sum to the cell count. At least one cell is required only when the snapshot has enough aircraft.
2. **Bands.** A synthetic fixture checks that high, medium and low are drawn over both land and sea, and that a 2-aircraft cell is withheld. It also checks that `stale` reaches the row.
   It also checks **provenance**: `getStats().provenance` carries classifier `gev-nic-nacp-v1` (`definedBy: 'GEV'`, `validated: false`), the gpsjam FAQ source, bands `[0.02, 0.1]`, a 30-minute `visited-view` window, and an unvalidated interpretation. And it checks **wording**: the row is named "GNSS Integrity" (with no "interference" in the name), every legend label ends in "low accuracy", and the blurb leads with low navigation accuracy and names jamming or spoofing only as one possible cause.
3. **Failure.** When the proxy returns 502, the error is surfaced and the cells are kept.
4. **Disable.** The data source is hidden.

New unit tests: `the primary state is a navigation-integrity anomaly; interference is only the secondary reading`, `provenance separates the GEV classifier from the gpsjam aggregation and the GEV window` (records), `the visible layer leads with low navigation accuracy and exposes its provenance` (ownership). The proxy and source tests now assert the `classifier` tag.

Each shot waits until every cell's bounding sphere is `DONE`. The route is stubbed with an in-page `fetch` stub rather than puppeteer request interception, because interception stalls Cesium's geometry workers and the ground rectangles never finish building.

| Live (adsb.lol, Poland) | Synthetic bands (stale) |
|---|---|
| ![live](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/leopechnicki/gods-eye-view/453b78bea88671874055ca4e26537e0442f614c7/pr-assets/gnss-interference/gnss-live-poland-baltic.png) | ![bands](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/leopechnicki/gods-eye-view/453b78bea88671874055ca4e26537e0442f614c7/pr-assets/gnss-interference/gnss-synthetic-bands.png) |
| **Upstream failure (502)** | **Disabled** |
| ![failure](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/leopechnicki/gods-eye-view/453b78bea88671874055ca4e26537e0442f614c7/pr-assets/gnss-interference/gnss-failure.png) | ![disabled](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/leopechnicki/gods-eye-view/453b78bea88671874055ca4e26537e0442f614c7/pr-assets/gnss-interference/gnss-disabled.png) |

## Limitations

- **Coverage.** Only aircraft covered by adsb.lol receivers are counted, and cells with fewer than 3 aircraft are not drawn. Oceans and quiet airspace stay blank.
- **Other causes.** Low NIC/NACp can have causes other than interference, such as avionics faults or a mis-set transponder. That is why the primary state is a navigation-integrity anomaly and interference is only the secondary reading. The first degraded aircraft per cell is discounted, following gpsjam.
- **Unvalidated threshold and window.** The NIC/NACp threshold applies US ADS-B Out minima worldwide as a GEV choice, and the 30-minute visited-view window is also a GEV choice. Neither has been checked against known events yet (`validated: false`).
- **Scope of the read.** The layer reads a 250 nm snapshot around the view you are looking at, not the whole globe. Observations accumulate across the views you visit within the 30-minute window.
- **Shared cooldown.** One upstream 429 pauses every anchor for the cooldown window. This is deliberate, because the upstream is shared.

Possible follow-ups:
- Validating `gev-nic-nacp-v1` and the window against known events or gpsjam daily maps, then either flipping `validated` or bumping the classifier id.
- Click-to-inspect cell details (aircraft, degraded, percent) through the shared pick plumbing.
- Aligning the band palette with the perimeters severity ramp. The current palette uses gpsjam's green/amber/red convention.
- The shared adsb.lol point cache described above.

## Built by the Hex project

| **Scout** | Source research: adsb.lol endpoint, ODbL licence and rate-limit policy; gpsjam.org method; 14 CFR 91.227 minima; dedupe against open PRs and issues |

| **Axon** | Code review (security, conventions, honest docs and licensing): **APPROVE** after two rounds |
