title: [Hex] feat(layers): emergency squawk (7500/7600/7700) and ADS-B emergency highlighting in Flights and Military
body:
Part of #853 (item 2).

## Summary

This PR makes the Flights and Military Flights layers highlight aircraft that are **broadcasting a transponder emergency**. It uses fields the existing feeds already return, so there is no new source, request or key.

- Squawk **7500** (unlawful interference), **7600** (radio failure) and **7700** (general emergency) are ICAO-standard worldwide. Where adsb.lol/readsb also sends its ADS-B `emergency` status (`general`, `unlawful`, `nordo`, `downed`), that status is used too.
- Emergencies are tinted red on the globe, in Cockpit far-contact dots and in military snapshots. The military layer also applies the tint when a billboard is first created and when a tracked contact is released.
- While an emergency aircraft is tracked, the Cockpit HUD aircraft-meta line names it. For example: `SQUAWK 7700 · GENERAL EMERGENCY`, or `ADS-B EMERGENCY · DOWNED AIRCRAFT` when the squawk itself does not name the status. The line is red and bold, so the state is not shown by colour alone.
- **Priority** statuses (`minfuel`, `lifeguard`) are reported to the analyst and voice layers but are **not** tinted.
- The status follows the latest poll and is never sticky. A cleared code stops highlighting on the next refresh.
- The analyst and voice query engine can filter by `squawk`, `emergency` (flag), `emergencyKind` and `emergencySource`. For example: "show aircraft squawking 7700".
- Analyst records keep the same broadcast-not-incident distinction as the HUD. `emergencySource` is `'squawk'` when the Mode A code names the status and `'ads-b'` for the readsb `emergency` field. `emergencyBroadcast` gives the matching phrase (`broadcasting squawk 7700 (general emergency)` or `ADS-B reports general emergency`), and `observedAtMs` is when the transponder was last heard.

This builds on the military-flight component split merged in #499 / #417, and adds nothing else to it.

## Data source(s)

| | |
|---|---|
| Sources | Existing records only: OpenSky state vectors (`squawk`, index 14) and adsb.lol `/v2/mil` and point snapshots (readsb `squawk` and `emergency`). No new request. |
| Licence | Unchanged: OpenSky terms as already documented, and adsb.lol ODbL 1.0. `DATA_SOURCES.md` gains a note on how the fields are read. |
| Auth / rate limits | None added. It rides on the existing polls. |
| Code reference | ICAO emergency Mode A codes 7500 / 7600 / 7700. readsb [`emergency` field](https://github.com/wiedehopf/readsb/blob/dev/README-json.md) ("a superset of the 7x00 squawks"). |
| Verified | 2026-09-29 |

## How it works

- `src/data/aircraftEmergency.js` is new and pure.
  - `normalizeSquawk` accepts exactly four octal digits.
  - `aircraftEmergency({squawk, emergency})` returns `{kind, label, severity, squawk, source}` or null. An explicit ADS-B status wins over the squawk. `source` is `'squawk'` only when the Mode A code itself names the status, so the HUD never quotes an unrelated code: a `1200` squawk with `downed` set reads `ADS-B EMERGENCY · DOWNED AIRCRAFT`, not `SQUAWK 1200`.
  - `isEmergency` separates emergencies from priorities, and `EMERGENCY_TINT_CSS` is the one tint.
- Live normalizers (`src/sources/live/aircraft.js`) keep `squawk` and `emergency`. OpenSky rows get `emergency: null`, because state vectors do not carry that field.
- Records (`flights/records.js`, `military/records.js`) replace both fields on every poll.
- Rendering:
  - civil `_fleetBillboardColor` and `_cockpitContactColor`;
  - military `_fleetBillboardColor`, which is exported and reused by `snapshotRenderer.js` and by the `tracking.js` release path, so each military tint site now reads the same helper.
  - Helpers take the record the caller already has.
- The HUD uses `formatCockpitEmergency` in `cockpitMath.js`, with the `.emergency` class styled through `--cockpit-emergency` and `var(--cyber-red-bright)`.
- Analyst and voice: `analystEngine` fields, the `gevActions` query fields and the `analyst_query` tool description all list `squawk`, `emergency`, `emergencyKind` and `emergencySource`. Each layer's `mapAnalystRecord` also adds:
  - `emergencySource: 'squawk' | 'ads-b' | null`, the provenance `aircraftEmergency()` already computes;
  - `emergencyBroadcast: string | null`, from the new pure `emergencyBroadcastPhrase(status)`, so a generated summary says "broadcasting squawk 7700" or "ADS-B reports general emergency" instead of flattening both into an incident-like boolean;
  - `observedAtMs: number | null`, the record's existing `lastContactEpochMs`: epoch ms of the last transponder message (OpenSky `time_contact`; readsb snapshot time minus `seen`), matching the `observedAtMs` naming of the live-source contract.

  The voice payload passes `emergencySource` and `emergencyBroadcast` through, and adds `observedAtMs` only for aircraft with a status, so ordinary results stay the same size. The tool description tells the model to narrate with `emergencyBroadcast`, as what the aircraft broadcasts. The two voice pins that hash the tool payload (`firstRunExperience` length/sha and `actionSchemas` sha) are re-derived for this additive description change, following the #737 precedent. No layer id or enum is added, so no share-link token is needed (`layer-token:check`: 28 published, 0 new).
- Docs: a new `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md` section called "Transponder emergency highlighting", plus `CHANGELOG.md` and `DATA_SOURCES.md` updates. The new files are added to `scripts/format-scope.json`, and the edits to unscoped test files stay in the original style (no formatting churn).

## Validation

All gates were run on Node 24.14.0 against `origin/main` e7707d9. The head is `1ecc456`.

| Gate | Result |
|---|---|
| `npm run format:check` | ✅ |
| `npm run check:boundaries` | ✅ |
| `npm run layer-token:check -- --base-ref origin/main` | ✅ 28 published, 0 new |
| `npm test` | ✅ 5373 pass, 0 fail (5383 total, 10 skipped as on main), plus the serialized allocation probes |
| `npm run build` | ✅ |
| `node scripts/track-regression.mjs` (dev server) | ✅ 109 / 109 |
| `node scripts/qa-emergency-squawk.mjs` (new) | ✅ 11 / 11 |

`qa-emergency-squawk` runs the real app against in-page stubs of `/api/opensky` and `/api/adsblol/mil`. Everything downstream is production code. It checks four things:
1. **Tint.**
   - Civil squawk 7600 and a military ADS-B `general` emergency are drawn red.
   - A normal civil flight stays white.
   - A normal military flight and a military `minfuel` priority stay amber.
2. **HUD.** Tracking the military emergency and entering Cockpit gives `MILITARY · SQUAWK 7700 · GENERAL EMERGENCY · LIVE TRACK` in `rgb(255, 68, 68)`.
3. **Clear.** When the next poll drops the code, the line returns to `MILITARY · LIVE TRACK · COURSE ALIGNED`.
4. **Release.** When the code returns and tracking stops, the restored fleet billboard is red rather than the plain military amber.

New unit tests cover the status rules (including the `1200 + downed` case), the HUD wording, per-poll clearing in both layers' records, and the live contract.

`src/data/aircraftEmergencyAnalyst.test.mjs` is a source-to-analyst query fixture. An OpenSky state vector squawking 7700 and an adsb.lol aircraft with `emergency: "general"` on squawk 1200 go through the real normalizers, records and `mapAnalystRecord` into the analyst engine. Both come out as `emergency: true, emergencyKind: "general"`. They differ in `emergencySource` (`squawk` vs `ads-b`), in `emergencyBroadcast`, and in `observedAtMs` (OpenSky `last_contact` vs snapshot time minus `seen`). A query filtered on `emergencySource` returns only the matching aircraft.

| Globe tint (civil 7600 and mil 7700 red, minfuel and normal amber or white) | Cockpit HUD while tracking the 7700 |
|---|---|
| ![tint](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/leopechnicki/gods-eye-view/refs/heads/hex/pr-assets/pr-assets/emergency-squawks/emergency-globe-tint.png) | ![hud](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/leopechnicki/gods-eye-view/refs/heads/hex/pr-assets/pr-assets/emergency-squawks/emergency-cockpit-hud.png) |
| **After the code clears (next poll)** | |
| ![cleared](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/leopechnicki/gods-eye-view/refs/heads/hex/pr-assets/pr-assets/emergency-squawks/emergency-cockpit-cleared.png) | |

## Limitations

- **A code is a broadcast, not a verified incident.** Crews pass through 7x00 while dialling a new code, so a one-poll red flash is possible. The status is deliberately per-poll.
- **OpenSky has no ADS-B emergency field.** Civil highlighting on the OpenSky path relies on the squawk alone. OpenSky also sends `null` squawks intermittently, so a highlight can drop for one poll. A one-poll grace period would fix that; happy to follow up if you want it.
- **Local ADS-B** (`localAdsb`) records are not covered in this PR.
- **On the globe the cue is colour only.** The HUD line names the code and is bold. Showing the code on the globe label or the Live Signals row is a possible follow-up.
- `scripts/qa-cockpit-utility.mjs` has a pre-existing intermittent failure ("Cyber collapsed Live Signals remains visible… after resize to 720px/640px"). It shows at the same rate with this PR's CSS reverted, so it is unrelated.

## Built by the Hex project

| Agent | Role on this PR |
|---|---|
| **Scout** | Research: ICAO emergency codes, the readsb `emergency` field semantics, OpenSky state-vector fields; dedupe against open PRs and issues |
| **Crew** | Implementation: status helper, normalizers, records, tint sites, Cockpit HUD, analyst and voice fields (including the `emergencySource` / `observedAtMs` provenance asked for in review), docs |
| **Forge** | Fork, branch and push; screenshot assets; PR and issue bookkeeping (#853) |
| **Probe** | Tests and the `qa-emergency-squawk` harness; ran every gate listed above; isolated the pre-existing `qa-cockpit-utility` flake |
| **Kat** | UI review: asked that the HUD quote only a squawk that names the status, and that the state not be shown by colour alone (bold HUD line). Both were done and verified in re-review |
| **Axon** | Code review (tint-site coverage, per-poll semantics, formatting churn, docs): **APPROVE** after two rounds; its final nits were applied |

title: [Hex] feat(layers): GDACS disaster alerts (floods, volcanoes, droughts)
body:
Part of #853 (item 3).

> **Updated 2026-10-19 (review follow-up):** narrowed to **floods, volcanoes and droughts** per @mazy1998; rebased onto `main` 93ea088; the four P2s, the volcano-404 validation bug from @quanticsoul4772, i18n (es/ru) and a `changelog.d` fragment are done. Details in the reply on this PR. Sections below are updated to the new head `714f5fb`.

## Summary

This PR adds a **Disaster Alerts** layer to the Events group. It shows current GDACS **flood, volcano and drought** alerts worldwide with no key. Earthquakes, wildfires and tropical cyclones are left to the existing USGS, FIRMS / Fire Perimeters and NHC layers, so GDACS's feeds for those are never requested.

- Each event is a point at the centroid GDACS publishes. It is sized and coloured by the GDACS **green / orange / red** alert level, and the legend counts events per level.
- **Red and orange** events, plus the selected one, get globe labels through the world-overlay host (no Cesium entity labels). Multi-country names are shortened on the globe to the first country and a count, for example `Drought in Austria +4`. The row list keeps the full name.
- The row lists events most severe first. Choosing a row selects the event and flies there through the shell's navigation policy, which honours reduced motion. A **Report** chip opens the GDACS event report.
- A globe click on a point selects it. Picks owned by other layers are left alone, and a click on empty map clears the selection.
- **Shared selection lane** (review follow-up). Row and globe selection both publish one normalized record on `gev:entity-selected` through the shared context store (`registerEntityContext` + `selectEntityContext`), the same lane installations, FIRMS and ALPR use, so imagery, nearby-camera, analyst and evidence workflows can attach without a GDACS-specific bridge. Clear, empty-map click, a vanished event (`reason: 'evicted'`), disable and destroy release it through `clearSelectedEntityContextForLayer`, which emits `gev:entity-selection-cleared` only while GDACS owns the selection; a sibling layer's selection is never cleared.
- The row, legend and help text always carry GDACS's own caveat: *automatic impact estimates, not official warnings*.
- Voice and share links: `set_layer_visibility` accepts `gdacs-alerts`, with the common names "disaster alerts", "disasters" and "gdacs".

## Data source(s)

| | |
|---|---|
| Sources | GDACS map feeds, `https://www.gdacs.org/gdacsapi/api/events/geteventlist/MAP?eventtype=` with FL, VO and DR. These are three of the feeds the gdacs.org map loads, and they are the only URLs the proxy will fetch. |
| Licence | © European Union, reused under the Commission [reuse policy](https://commission.europa.eu/legal-notice_en#copyright-notice) (Decision 2011/833/EU, CC BY 4.0), as linked from the [GDACS terms of use](https://www.gdacs.org/About/termofuse.aspx). Credit line: "Disaster alerts: GDACS (Global Disaster Alert and Coordination System), © European Union, CC BY 4.0". The change made here is that only flood, volcano and drought centroids and their alert levels are kept and re-drawn on the globe (stated in `DATA_SOURCES.md` and in the in-app credit line). |
| Auth / rate limits | Keyless. GDACS publishes no rate limit, so `/api/gdacs` keeps load low. Each hazard type has its own cache (volcanoes 30 min, floods 1 h, droughts 3 h). There are also 30 requests/min per client, and one shared cooldown after a GDACS 429 that honours a valid `Retry-After` in full (up to 24 h; the longest concurrent deadline wins). |
| Code reference | None copied. Field names follow the GDACS GeoJSON event list (`alertlevel`, `eventtype`, `eventid`, `episodeid`, `fromdate`, `todate`, `url.report`). |
| Verified | 2026-10-19. The live `qa-gdacs` run returned 15 flood, volcano and drought events: 0 red, 4 orange, 11 green. |

## How it works

- **`server/providers/gdacs.js`** (new; `/api/gdacs`, registered in `server/providers/local.js` for dev and preview).
  - Fetches the three fixed feeds with `redirect: 'error'`, a 20 s deadline and an 8 MB body cap. Concurrent requests share one upstream fetch.
  - Keeps only each event's `Point_Centroid` feature. Cyclone and drought feeds carry 2–3 MB of tracks, cones and footprints; those never leave the proxy.
  - GDACS answers a type with no current events (volcanoes, most days) with a `404 application/problem+json`. That is an empty feed, cached for the type's TTL, not an outage.
  - Feeds fail independently. A failed feed serves its last good copy, marked `stale`, or is reported in `missing`, and is held off for 5 min (or its TTL, if shorter). The other feeds stay fresh and are not re-fetched.
  - The response is `{fetchedAt, feeds:[{type, fetchedAt, stale, missing?}], events}`.
- **`src/layers/gdacs/`** (new family package; `check:boundaries` entries added).
  - `records.js`: pure normalisers. They whitelist the event type and level, validate coordinates and parse times. Report links are kept only on the `https://www.gdacs.org` origin. The client sanitises the payload again.
  - `source.js`: the snapshot source.
  - `index.js`: the layer.
    - Points are billboards with per-frame far-side culling.
    - Labels go through `overlayHost` with `variant: 'label'`.
    - It provides row controls (legend, list, chips, info) and globe picking through the shared pick registry.
    - A refresh is aborted on disable. A selection whose event vanishes is cleared after the markers are rebuilt.
    - `gdacsSelectionContext(event)` builds the published record: `id` (`gdacs-alerts:<TYPE>-<eventId>`), `layerId`, `layerName`, `kind: 'disaster-alert'`, `source: 'GDACS'`, `label`, `latitude`/`longitude`, `geometryKind: 'point'`, `locationKind: 'centroid'`, `caveat: 'automatic estimate, not official warning'`, and `provenance` (`source`, `reportUrl`, `eventId`, `episodeId`, `eventType`, `alertLevel`, `fetchedAt` from the snapshot, `updatedAt` from GDACS `datemodified` or `null`, never the episode dates). It carries no polygon, footprint or extent. Only the selected event is registered, and a refresh updates it in place without re-announcing it, including a new position when GDACS moves the centroid.
- **`src/app/layers/gdacs.js`**: the app wrapper. It injects `picking`, `pointer`, `openExternal`, `overlayHost` and the shared `context` store, and is wired through `constructCatalog`, `sources/reference` and `layerPanel`.
- **Navigation**: the layer joins the `CAMERA_LAYERS` loop in `layerBindings.js`. The weather-specific helper names there are renamed to `_cameraShellModules` / `_connectCameraLayers`, since they now serve more than weather. There is no behaviour change for the existing layers. GDACS passes the noun `disaster alert`, which has its own Cockpit refusal (en, es, ru); the noun-scan test now reads `CAMERA_LAYERS`.
- **Share-link token**: `5`, the next free token on `main` (`layer-token:check -- --base-ref origin/main`: 31 published, 1 new). **Merge note:** other open PRs may also claim `5`. Whichever merges second re-runs `npm run layer-token:next -- gdacs-alerts` and re-pins the ledger tests; happy to do that on request.
- **Voice pins**: the two pins that hash the tool payload (the `firstRunExperience` length/sha and the `actionSchemas` sha) are re-derived for the additive `gdacs-alerts` enum value, following the #737 precedent.
- **Docs**:
  - `DATA_SOURCES.md` gets a sources-table row and a paragraph covering caching, limits, centroids only and the GDACS disclaimer.
  - `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md` gets an Events-row entry.
  - `changelog.d/857-gdacs-disaster-alerts.md` (no `CHANGELOG.md` edit); `dataCredits.js` and `format-scope.json` are updated.
- **i18n**: row, legend, list, chips and help text go through `t()` / `tn()` / `msg()` with es and ru entries (`npm run i18n`: es and ru complete).

## Validation

All gates were run on Node 24.14.0 against `origin/main` 93ea088. The head is `714f5fb`.

| Gate | Result |
|---|---|
| `npm ci` | ✅ |
| `npm run format:check` | ✅ |
| `npm run check:boundaries` | ✅ |
| `npm run layer-token:check -- --base-ref origin/main` | ✅ 31 published, 1 new |
| `npm run i18n` | ✅ es and ru complete |
| `npm run changelog:check` | ✅ |
| `npm test` | ✅ 7777 pass, 0 fail (7787 total, 10 skipped as on main), plus 1/1 and 14/14 |
| `npm run build` | ✅ |
| `node scripts/qa-gdacs.mjs` | ✅ 20 / 20 (live GDACS: 15 events) |

`test:track` was not re-run on this head.

`qa-gdacs` runs the real app in headless Chromium:
1. **Live.** Against real GDACS through `/api/gdacs`:
   - there is no error;
   - there is one entity and one list item per event;
   - the legend counts sum to the event count.
2. **Fixture** (in-page stub of `/api/gdacs`):
   - an unknown hazard type is dropped;
   - the list is most severe first;
   - there are legend counts per level;
   - red and orange are labelled through the overlay host and green is not;
   - the far-side point is hidden;
   - the missing Drought feed and the GDACS caveat are shown in the row.
3. **Select.**
   - A real mouse click on a point selects it and shows the Report chip, which opens the exact GDACS report URL.
   - A click on empty space clears the selection.
   - A list click flies the camera to the event at 1,500 km.
   - On the shared lane: the globe pick and the list click each publish exactly one normalized `gev:entity-selected` (point centroid, provenance, report URL, caveat, no area keys), and the empty-map clear publishes one `gev:entity-selection-cleared`.
4. **Failure.** With the route stubbed to 502, `stats.error` is set, the four events stay drawn and the row says the refresh failed.
5. **Disable.** The data source is hidden, a GDACS-owned shared selection is released (one `gev:entity-selection-cleared`, store empty), and no uncaught browser errors occur.

The new unit tests cover four areas:
- **Proxy:** fixed URLs (EQ, TC and WF never requested), caps, per-type TTLs, the 404-as-empty volcano feed, per-feed failure isolation and hold-off, 429 cooldown with `Retry-After` kept in full and the longest deadline winning, stale and missing feeds, rate limit.
- **Normalisers:** types and levels, coordinates, time zones, report-link origin.
- **Source.**
- **Layer ownership:**
  - labels and their shortening;
  - selection, navigation, cancellation and reduced motion;
  - picking;
  - culling;
  - the race where a selected event vanishes while a new labelled one appears;
  - disable and destroy cleanup.
- **Selection contract** (`selectionContract.test.mjs`, against the real context store): row and globe selection each emit exactly one normalized `gev:entity-selected`; re-choosing the same event is silent; switching events keeps a single GDACS record; clear, empty map, disable and destroy each clear once; a vanished event clears as `evicted`; a sibling layer's selection is never cleared; re-choosing after a sibling took the selection claims it back; a refresh updates the record in place; the centroid is a point and no key in the record reads as area geometry; the caveat and provenance are present; without the context service selection stays local.

Screenshots are from the earlier six-hazard head.

| Live, worldwide (real GDACS) | Fixture: levels, labels, missing feed, caveat |
|---|---|
| ![live](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/leopechnicki/gods-eye-view/refs/heads/hex/pr-assets/pr-assets/gdacs-alerts/gdacs-live-world.png) | ![fixture](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/leopechnicki/gods-eye-view/refs/heads/hex/pr-assets/pr-assets/gdacs-alerts/gdacs-fixture.png) |

| ![selected](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/leopechnicki/gods-eye-view/refs/heads/hex/pr-assets/pr-assets/gdacs-alerts/gdacs-selected.png) | ![focus](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/leopechnicki/gods-eye-view/refs/heads/hex/pr-assets/pr-assets/gdacs-alerts/gdacs-focus.png) |

## Limitations

- **Centroids only.** A point marks the event, not its affected area, and the shared selection record says so (`geometryKind: 'point'`, `locationKind: 'centroid'`). Flood and drought footprints are dropped to keep the payload small. Drawing footprints for the selected event is a possible follow-up.
- **GDACS alerts are automatic estimates.** GDACS says its information "is purely indicative and should not be used for any decision making without alternate sources of information", and it does not replace official warnings from local or national authorities. The layer says so in the row, legend and help text.
- **No published rate limit.** The caching and cooldown above are our own conservative choices.
- **Labels:** only red, orange and the selected event are labelled, so the globe stays readable. Green events are points only.
- **The row info renders as one wrapped paragraph** (lines joined with ` · `), because the shared row-info renderer collapses newlines.

All were done and verified in re-review: **APPROVE** |

title: [Hex] feat(layers): EASA conflict zone bulletins (CZIB), worldwide aviation advisories
body:
Part of #853 (item 4).

## Summary

This PR adds a **Conflict Zones** layer to the Events group. It shows the active **EASA Conflict Zone Information Bulletins** (CZIBs) worldwide with no key. CZIBs are the EU aviation-safety advisories that tell air operators about risks to civil flights over or near conflict areas.

- EASA publishes no geometry, so each bulletin shades the **countries it names**, using the bundled Natural Earth boundaries.
  - A bulletin that covers the **whole country** is shaded red.
  - A bulletin that covers **part of a country** is drawn as an amber dashed outline with almost no fill, and labelled "(part)". Examples: "Pakistan – Baluchistan…" and "Yemen – Sana'a FIR".
- Every active bulletin gets a globe label through the world-overlay host (no Cesium entity labels).
- The row lists bulletins by latest revision as *WHOLE/PART · area · number*.
  - Choosing a row selects the bulletin and flies to the named countries through the shell's navigation policy. It is refused in Cockpit and instant under reduced motion.
  - An **EASA bulletin** chip opens the bulletin page.
- A globe click inside a shaded country selects its bulletin. Picks owned by other layers are left alone, and a click on empty map clears the selection.
- The row always says that **the shading marks the countries named, not the exact airspace**, both in the summary and when a bulletin is selected. The legend blurb and help text say it too, and add EASA's own advice to read the bulletin and the current NOTAMs.
- Voice and share links: `set_layer_visibility` accepts `easa-czib`, with the common names "conflict zones", "conflict zone bulletins", "czib" and "czibs".

## Data source(s)

| | |
|---|---|
| Sources | EASA CZIB list export `https://www.easa.europa.eu/en/domains/air-operations/czibs/export-json` (title, countries, status, issue, revision and validity dates), joined on EASA's node id with the RSS feed `…/czibs/feed.xml` (bulletin number and page link). These two fixed URLs, with no query strings, are the only ones the proxy fetches. EASA's `robots.txt` disallows `/*?`. |
| Licence | EASA [copyright notice](https://www.easa.europa.eu/en/copyright-disclaimer): "Reproduction is authorised, provided the source is acknowledged, save where otherwise stated". Credit line: "Conflict zone bulletins: EASA (European Union Aviation Safety Agency)". The change made here is that the countries named are re-drawn from Natural Earth. |
| Auth / rate limits | Keyless. EASA publishes no rate limit. `/api/czib` caches for 1 h and allows 30 requests/min per client (600 global). After an EASA 429 there is one shared cooldown that honours `Retry-After` (clamped to 30 s–60 min). During an EASA outage the last good copy is served for at most 72 h (`CZIB_MAX_STALE_MS`), marked stale with its age. |
| Code reference | None copied. Field names follow EASA's export (`title`, `countries`, `status`, issue, revision and valid-until fields) and the RSS `guid` ("nid on date"). |
| Verified | 2026-09-29. The live run returned 15 active bulletins naming 19 countries, all resolved to bundled boundaries. |

## How it works

- **`server/providers/czib.js`** (new; `/api/czib`, registered in `server/providers/local.js` for dev and preview).
  - Uses `readResponseJsonCapped` / `readResponseTextCapped` with a 2 MB cap, a 20 s deadline and `redirect: 'error'`. Concurrent requests share one upstream fetch.
  - A failed refresh serves the last good copy, marked `stale` with `staleAgeMs` (and `X-Data-Stale`), for at most **72 h** (`CZIB_MAX_STALE_MS`). Past that the route answers `502 czib_unavailable` rather than present old safety information as current; the next successful fetch serves fresh data again. Three days rides out a long-weekend EASA outage while staying well inside the few-week revision cycle, so withdrawals, revisions and new bulletins cannot be hidden for long. If only the feed fails, bulletins still return with `linksMissing: true`.
  - Other paths get 404 and non-GET requests get 405.
- **`src/layers/czib/`** (new family package; `check:boundaries` entries added).
  - `records.js`: pure normalisers, and **`czibEffectiveStatus(bulletin, nowMs)`**, the one rule the drawing, the list, the legend counts, the summary and `getStats().count` share. EASA's `status === 'active'` alone is not trusted:
    - active, published end date still ahead → `active` (drawn, counted);
    - active, end date passed → `expired` (not drawn, not counted, not selectable; the summary names it: "Not shown: 1 bulletin past its published end date; check EASA for a revision"). The end date is inclusive: a bulletin valid until 30/09 lapses at 00:00 UTC on 01/10. "Unless reviewed earlier" cannot be inferred locally, so the published date is used as the safe upper bound;
    - active, no published end date → `unverified` (kept and drawn, but the list row says "no end date", the summary counts them and the detail reads "No end date published; check EASA that it still applies");
    - withdrawn → `withdrawn`.
  - The layer re-applies that rule against its injected clock on **every update tick, including a failed refresh**, so a long-lived session or a cached copy that crosses the validity boundary drops the bulletin within one tick instead of painting it as active indefinitely. It parses EASA's `dd/mm/yyyy` and stamp dates, decodes entities, detects part-country areas, and keeps links only on the EASA origin with a CZIB/SIB page shape. The client sanitises the payload again.
  - `source.js`: the snapshot source.
  - `index.js`: the layer. A cached copy names its age in the row ("Showing a cached copy from 5 h ago").
    - Polygons and outlines are clamped, with `ClassificationType.BOTH`, so they drape over 3D Tiles as well as terrain.
    - It provides row controls (legend, list, chip, info) and globe picking through the shared pick registry.
    - A refresh is aborted on disable, and `destroy` releases the data source.
- **Country boundaries are injected.** `src/app/layers/czib.js` passes a `resolveCountry` backed by `findAdminArea`, so the portable layer package does not take ownership of the bundled Natural Earth JSON. Without a resolver, the layer lists bulletins but draws nothing. Countries that cannot be matched are named in the row ("Not drawn: …").
- **Navigation**: the layer joins the `CAMERA_LAYERS` loop in `layerBindings.js` with the noun "conflict zone". #857 makes the same small refactor, so whichever merges second will need a trivial rebase.
- **Share-link token**: a provisional `0`, following CONTRIBUTING (`layer-token:check`: 28 published, 1 new). **Merge note:** #855 and #857 from this project also claim the provisional `0`. Whichever merges later should re-run `npm run layer-token:next -- easa-czib` and re-pin the ledger and `layerState` tests. Happy to rebase and do that on request.
- **Voice pins**: the pins that hash the tool payload (`firstRunExperience` length/sha, `actionSchemas` sha and the `radioMarkup` digest) are re-derived for the additive `easa-czib` enum value, following the #737 precedent.
- **Docs**:
  - `DATA_SOURCES.md` gets a sources-table row and a paragraph on the fetch, cache, limits and caveat.
  - `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md` gets an Events-row entry.
  - `CHANGELOG.md`, `dataCredits.js`, `format-scope.json` and `package.json` exports are updated.

## Validation

All gates were run on Node 24.14.0 against `origin/main` e7707d9. The head is `188fa17`.

| Gate | Result |
|---|---|
| `npm run format:check` | ✅ |
| `npm run check:boundaries` | ✅ |
| `npm run layer-token:check -- --base-ref origin/main` | ✅ 28 published, 1 new |
| `npm test` | ✅ 5403 pass, 0 fail (5413 total, 10 skipped as on main) |
| `npm run build` | ✅ |
| `npm run test:track` (dev server) | ✅ 109 / 109 |
| `node scripts/qa-czib.mjs` (new) | ✅ 18 / 18 (live EASA: 16 bulletins, 20 countries) |

`qa-czib` runs the real app in headless Chromium:
1. **Live.** Against real EASA through `/api/czib`:
   - there is no error;
   - there is one list item per active bulletin;
   - every bulletin is drawn;
   - the legend counts sum to the bulletin count.
2. **Fixture** (in-page stub of `/api/czib`) with seven rows: Mali (whole), Pakistan (part), a five-country Gulf bulletin, an unknown country, a withdrawn bulletin, a bulletin EASA still marks active whose end date has passed, and an invalid row.
   - The invalid row is dropped.
   - The withdrawn bulletin is not drawn.
   - The expired bulletin is neither drawn nor counted, and the row names it as not shown.
   - The partial bulletin is dashed.
   - The unknown country is named as not drawn.
3. **Select.**
   - A real mouse click inside Mali selects its bulletin and shows the chip, which opens the EASA page.
   - A click on empty space clears the selection.
   - A real mouse click inside the faint part-country fill (Baluchistan) selects Pakistan, which proves the outline-first style still takes Cesium picks.
   - A list click selects a bulletin and flies the camera to it.
4. **Failure.** With the route stubbed to 502, `stats.error` is set, the shading stays on the globe and the row says the refresh failed.
5. **Disable.** The data source is hidden, and no uncaught browser errors occur.

New unit tests (34):
- **Proxy:** fixed URLs with no query string, caps, TTL, 429 cooldown, stale and links-missing paths, rate limit, 404/405, and the 72 h maximum stale age (served at exactly 72 h with `staleAgeMs`, 502 one millisecond later, fresh again once EASA returns).
- **Hard expiry (review follow-up):** `czibEffectiveStatus` across the end-of-day boundary, unknown validity and withdrawn; a **fake-clock regression** where EASA fails and the clock crosses midnight after `validUntilMs` — at 23:59 UTC the bulletin is still drawn, at 00:01 it is no longer drawn, labelled, listed, counted in the legend or selected; an unknown-validity bulletin is kept and flagged; a cached copy names its age.
- **Normalisers:** dates, entities, part-country detection, link origin and shape, revision ordering.
- **Source.**
- **Layer ownership:** styling, labels, selection, navigation and its cancellation, reduced motion, picking, a failed refresh keeping the drawing, and destroy cleanup.

| Live, worldwide (real EASA) | Fixture: whole / part / unknown / withdrawn |
|---|---|
| ![live](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/leopechnicki/gods-eye-view/refs/heads/hex/pr-assets/pr-assets/easa-czib/czib-live-world.png) | ![fixture](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/leopechnicki/gods-eye-view/refs/heads/hex/pr-assets/pr-assets/easa-czib/czib-fixture.png) |
| **Selected bulletin with the EASA chip** | **Row-list focus flight** |
| ![selected](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/leopechnicki/gods-eye-view/refs/heads/hex/pr-assets/pr-assets/easa-czib/czib-selected.png) | ![focus](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/leopechnicki/gods-eye-view/refs/heads/hex/pr-assets/pr-assets/easa-czib/czib-focus.png) |

## Limitations

- **Expiry is the published end date only.** A bulletin withdrawn or revised early ("unless reviewed earlier") is only seen on the next successful EASA fetch; the 72 h stale cap bounds how long that can be missed.
- **Countries, not airspace.** EASA publishes no geometry, so the layer shades whole countries. A bulletin about one FIR, or about the Persian Gulf, shades the named states' land. The row, legend and help text say this. Drawing FIR boundaries would need a separate licensed source.
- **Not operational guidance.** A CZIB gives information and recommendations to operators. The layer points to the bulletin and advises reading the current NOTAMs.
- **No published rate limit.** The 1 h cache and cooldown above are our own conservative choices. Bulletins change a few times a month.
- **The row info renders as one wrapped paragraph** (lines joined with ` · `), because the shared row-info renderer collapses newlines. The legend swatch is a dot, so the dashed style is named in the legend label instead. Adding `white-space: pre-line` and a dashed swatch to the shared row styles would help several layers. We can open that as a separate PR.
- **Share-link token** is provisional (see the merge note above).

## Built by the Hex project

| Agent | Role on this PR |
|---|---|
| **Scout** | Research: EASA CZIB export and RSS feed, `robots.txt` constraints, copyright notice; dedupe against open PRs and issues (no CZIB or aviation-advisory PR open; #205 WarScope covers ground conflict events, a different source and purpose) |
| **Crew** | Implementation: `/api/czib` proxy, `czib` layer package, injected country resolver, app wrapper and wiring, voice and share-link entries, docs |
| **Forge** | Fork, branch and push; screenshot assets; PR and issue bookkeeping (#853) |
| **Probe** | Unit tests and the `qa-czib` harness (live and fixture); ran every gate listed above |
| **Kat** | UI review. Asked for the part-country zones to be visually distinct (outline-first, with longer and thicker dashes), the caveat to stay visible when a bulletin is selected, the dashed style to be named in the legend, list rows to lead with the area, and the shorter name "Conflict Zones". All were done and verified in re-review: **APPROVE** |
| **Axon** | Code review against the #702 checklist (capped reads, last-good serving, credit wording, `ClassificationType.BOTH`, provisional token, link-origin validation, lifecycle cleanup). After the design changes, asked for proof that the faint part-country fill still picks in real Cesium (added a real-click qa case) and flagged the empty list gutter, now a WHOLE/PART lead. **APPROVE** |

title: [Hex] feat(layers): Radiation — ambient gamma dose rate (BfS ODL Germany + Safecast worldwide)
body:
Part of #853 (item 5).

## Summary

This PR adds a **Radiation** layer to the Events group. It shows **ambient gamma dose rate** (µSv/h) with no key, from two open networks:

- **BfS ODL**, the German Federal Office for Radiation Protection's official monitoring network: about 1,600 stations, as 1-hour means.
- **Safecast** fixed real-time sensors worldwide, a volunteer network under CC0 (Japan, Ukraine, Taiwan, the Americas and elsewhere).

What the layer does:

- **Points.** Each station or sensor is a point sized and coloured by band: **High** ≥ 1, **Raised** 0.5–1, **Elevated** 0.2–0.5 and **Typical** < 0.2 µSv/h.
  - Typical and elevated points shrink with distance and have no outline. That way the dense German network reads by colour at world scale instead of as a mass of outlines.
  - Raised and high readings stay full size and are labelled through the world-overlay host (no Cesium entity labels).
- **Row list.** The row lists the **25 highest readings**, with the dose as the lead.
  - Choosing a row selects the reading and flies to it through the shell's navigation policy. It is refused in Cockpit and instant under reduced motion.
  - A chip opens the source's own map: BfS ODL-Info or the Safecast map.
- **Globe clicks** select readings. Picks owned by other layers are left alone, and a click on empty map clears the selection.
- **Caveat.** The row, legend blurb and help text all say that these are **ambient dose rates, not official warnings**. They name natural background (typically 0.05–0.3 µSv/h) and tell users to follow their national authority.
- **Voice and share links.** `set_layer_visibility` accepts `radiation`, with the common names "radiation levels", "dose rate", "gamma dose rate" and "safecast".

## Data source(s)

| | |
|---|---|
| Sources | **BfS ODL** WFS: `https://www.imis.bfs.de/ogc/opendata/ows?service=WFS&version=1.1.0&request=GetFeature&typeName=opendata:odlinfo_odl_1h_latest&outputFormat=application/json` (GeoJSON, updated hourly). **Safecast** realtime devices: `https://tt.safecast.org/devices` (the latest record per device, about 1.4 MB). These two fixed URLs are the only ones the proxy fetches. We do not use `api.safecast.org`, because its `robots.txt` disallows `/`. |
| Licence | **BfS:** [Datenlizenz Deutschland – Namensnennung – 2.0](https://www.govdata.de/dl-de/by-2-0), per the [BfS site policy](https://www.imis.bfs.de/geoportal/resources/sitepolicy.html). The change made here is that station values are re-drawn on the globe. **Safecast:** [CC0](https://safecast.org/data/) ("Safecast data is published under a CC0 designation"); attribution is kept as a courtesy. Credit line: "Radiation: Safecast (CC0); © Bundesamt für Strahlenschutz (BfS), dl-de/by-2-0". |
| Auth / rate limits | Keyless. Neither source publishes a rate limit. `/api/radiation` caches BfS for 15 min and Safecast for 10 min, and allows 30 requests/min per client (600 global). A 429 from either feed cools down only that feed, honouring `Retry-After` (clamped to 30 s–60 min). |
| Privacy | Safecast device records carry owner contact fields (`device_contact_name`, `device_contact_email`) and device identifiers (`device_urn`, `device_sn`, `dev_dashboard`, `service_transport`, which holds an IP address). The proxy builds new records from an allow-list, so **none of these leave the server**. A test asserts it. |
| Code reference | None copied. The 334 CPM per µSv/h factor for the LND 7318 tube (`lnd_7318u` / `lnd_7318c`) is the one Safecast's own ingest applies (`mapview_schema.sql` in Safecast/ingest and `conversion.go` in Safecast/safecast-new-map). |
| Not used | **EURDEP** (the European network), because its terms forbid redistribution. |
| Verified | 2026-09-29. The live run returned 1,726 current readings: 1,578 BfS stations and 148 Safecast devices. |

## How it works

- **`server/providers/radiation.js`** (new; `/api/radiation`, registered in `server/providers/local.js` for dev and preview).
  - Uses `readResponseJsonCapped` with an 8 MB cap, a 20 s deadline and `redirect: 'error'`. Concurrent requests share one upstream fetch per feed.
  - A failed feed serves its **last good copy, marked `stale`**, but only the readings that are still current: BfS within 6 h, Safecast within 24 h. A long outage therefore reports the feed as missing instead of showing old values.
  - A feed that returns rows but none of them current (for example a late BfS hour) is treated as failed, so it cannot wipe the good copy.
  - If both feeds are missing, the route returns 502, or 429 with `Retry-After` when upstream rate-limited it. Other paths get 404 and non-GET requests get 405.
- **`src/layers/radiation/`** (new family package; `check:boundaries` entries added).
  - `records.js`: pure normalisers.
    - **BfS:** keeps stations in operation only (`site_status` 1), requires the `µSv/h` unit, and takes the hour end as the reading time.
    - **Safecast:** drops test devices and anything but LND 7318 tubes, and keeps the latest record per device.
    - **Both:** future-stamped and implausible values are dropped.
    - The client sanitises the payload again.
  - `source.js`: the snapshot source.
  - `index.js`: the layer.
    - Points are drawn over terrain and 3D Tiles (`disableDepthTestDistance`), so points behind the globe are hidden by an ellipsoid occluder. It re-runs only when the camera moves.
    - It provides row controls (legend, list, chip, info) and globe picking through the shared pick registry.
    - A refresh is aborted on disable, and `destroy` releases the data source.
- **Navigation.** The layer needs `runNavigation` with its own toast noun ("radiation station"). To support that, `layerBindings.js` generalises the existing weather-only shell wiring (`_weatherShellModules`) into a small `CAMERA_LAYERS` loop. The behaviour of the existing layers is unchanged. #857 and #858 make the same refactor, so whichever merges later needs a trivial rebase.
- **Share-link token.** A provisional `0`, following CONTRIBUTING (`layer-token:check`: 28 published, 1 new).
  - **Merge note:** #855, #857 and #858 from this project also claim the provisional `0`. Whichever merges later should re-run `npm run layer-token:next -- radiation` and re-pin the ledger and `layerState` tests.
  - The ledger test's fixture tokens moved from `0` to `3` only because `0` is now taken. That also reverts when the token is renumbered. Happy to rebase and do this on request.
- **Voice pins.** The pins that hash the tool payload (`firstRunExperience` length/sha, `actionSchemas` sha and the `radioMarkup` digest) are re-derived for the additive `radiation` enum value, following the #737 precedent.
- **Docs.**
  - `DATA_SOURCES.md` gets a sources-table row and a paragraph on the fetch, cache, limits, privacy and caveat.
  - `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md` gets an Events-row entry.
  - `CHANGELOG.md`, `dataCredits.js`, `format-scope.json` and `package.json` exports are updated.

## Validation

All gates were run on Node 24.14.0 against `origin/main` e7707d9. The head is `f4d996e`.

| Gate | Result |
|---|---|
| `npm run format:check` | ✅ |
| `npm run check:boundaries` | ✅ |
| `npm run layer-token:check -- --base-ref origin/main` | ✅ 28 published, 1 new |
| `npm test` | ✅ 5403 pass, 0 fail (5413 total, 10 skipped as on main) |
| `npm run build` | ✅ |
| `npm run test:track` (dev server) | ✅ 109 / 109 |
| `node scripts/qa-radiation.mjs` (new) | ✅ 16 / 16 (live: 1,726 readings from both feeds) |

`qa-radiation` runs the real app in headless Chromium:
1. **Live.** Against real BfS and Safecast through `/api/radiation`:
   - there is no error;
   - there is one entity per reading;
   - the list is capped at 25;
   - both feeds are present;
   - the legend counts sum to the reading count.
2. **Fixture** (in-page stub of `/api/radiation`): a high and a raised Safecast reading in Fukushima, a typical one in Taiwan, a BfS station on the far side of the globe, and an invalid row.
   - The invalid row is dropped.
   - The list is highest first.
   - High and raised readings are labelled.
   - The far-side point is hidden.
   - The cached feed is named in the row.
3. **Select.**
   - A real mouse click on a point selects it and shows the source chip, which opens the Safecast map.
   - A click on empty space clears the selection.
   - A list click selects a reading and flies the camera to 300 km above it.
4. **Failure.** With the route stubbed to 502, `stats.error` is set, the readings stay on the globe and the row says the refresh failed.
5. **Disable.** The data source is hidden, and no uncaught browser errors occur.

New unit tests (40):
- **Proxy:** fixed URLs, privacy allow-list, per-feed TTL and coalescing, per-feed 429 cooldown, stale serving with age limits, rows-but-none-current, size cap, rate limit, 404/405.
- **Normalisers:** status, unit, freshness, tubes, fractional counts, dedupe, bands, sanitising.
- **Source.**
- **Layer ownership:** styling, labels, list, selection, navigation and its cancellation, reduced motion, picking, horizon culling, a failed refresh keeping the drawing, and destroy cleanup.

| Live, Europe (real BfS + Safecast) | Fixture: bands, labels, far-side culling |
|---|---|
| ![live](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/leopechnicki/gods-eye-view/refs/heads/hex/pr-assets/pr-assets/radiation/radiation-live-world.png) | ![fixture](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/leopechnicki/gods-eye-view/refs/heads/hex/pr-assets/pr-assets/radiation/radiation-fixture.png) |
| **Selected reading with the source chip** | **Row-list focus flight** |
| ![selected](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/leopechnicki/gods-eye-view/refs/heads/hex/pr-assets/pr-assets/radiation/radiation-selected.png) | ![focus](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/leopechnicki/gods-eye-view/refs/heads/hex/pr-assets/pr-assets/radiation/radiation-focus.png) |

## Limitations

- **Not an official warning.** These are ambient dose rates from independent networks. BfS values are official 1-hour means; Safecast values are volunteer sensor readings. The layer says so everywhere it shows a value.
- **Coverage is uneven.** BfS covers Germany densely. Safecast fixed sensors are sparse and clustered, and many countries have none. Pluggable national sources can be added the same way. We skipped EURDEP because its terms forbid redistribution.
- **Only Safecast LND 7318 tubes.** Safecast's published conversion factors for the LND 712 / 7128 tubes disagree (120.5 vs 108 CPM per µSv/h), so those devices are left out rather than shown with a guessed value.
- **BfS method change.** BfS notes that a change in its measuring method on 2025-07-01 produced "a slight increase in the measured values". Long-term comparisons across that date should allow for it.
- **No published rate limits.** The caches and cooldown above are our own conservative choices.
- **The row info renders as one wrapped paragraph** (lines joined with ` · `), because the shared row-info renderer collapses newlines.
- **Share-link token** is provisional (see the merge note above).

| **Scout** | Research: BfS ODL WFS and Safecast realtime endpoints, licences (dl-de/by-2-0, CC0), `robots.txt` on `api.safecast.org`, the 7318 conversion factor in Safecast's own code, EURDEP's redistribution terms; dedupe against open PRs and issues (no radiation, Safecast or dose-rate PR or issue exists) |

| **Probe** | Unit tests and the `qa-radiation` harness (live and fixture); ran every gate listed above |
| **Kat** | UI review. Found that about 1,600 overlapping outlined points turned Germany into a dark blob at world scale (now drawn quietly: distance scaling, no outline for typical and elevated readings), and asked for plain-English band names in the legend and details, device numbers on duplicate list names, and thousands separators. All done and verified in re-review: **APPROVE** |

Found that a cached copy could serve readings of any age during a long outage, and that a feed returning only stale rows could wipe the good copy. Both are fixed with tests. Also asked for a source for the 7318c factor and wider privacy assertions. **APPROVE** |

title: feat(server): run the provider API standalone, without Vite
body:
## What

Adds `server/standalone/headless.mjs`, which mounts the existing `/api/*`
provider middleware (`localProviderPlugins`) onto a plain Node `http.Server`
instead of Vite's dev/preview server. A new `server/standalone/connectRouter.js`
supplies the Connect-compatible mount-path matching and URL rewriting the
middleware relies on, since Vite's own `connect` dependency isn't resolvable
outside Vite. No existing provider code changes — the same plugin composition
is reused as-is (confirmed automatically picking up 5 providers that landed on
`main` mid-branch, with no changes needed on this side).

`gev-key-setup` (the in-app "POWER UP" panel) is intentionally not mounted: its
handler calls a real Vite dev-server `server.restart()` this process doesn't
provide, and CONTRIBUTING.md already documents `/api/setup/*` as
development-only.

`docs/API_REFERENCE.md` documents the request/response contract for a
selected subset of the routes this exposes, including a new `GET /healthz`;
`server/apiRoutes.js` (from #793) is the complete `/api` mount table. The
server binds to loopback by default, refuses a non-loopback bind unless
`GEV_HEADLESS_UNSAFE_PUBLIC=1` is set, rejects unexpected `Host` headers,
and bounds shutdown.

## Why

`vite preview` is explicitly documented as not a production server. This gives
the provider layer — the live OpenSky/CCTV/transit/etc. proxies — a way to run
unattended: as its own process, on its own port, without a browser or Vite's
dev-server semantics in the loop.

## Verification

- `npm run build`, `npm test`, `npm run check:boundaries`, `npm run format:check`: green, at parity with `main`.
- `npm run test:track`: not run — Puppeteer/Chrome fails to launch in my sandbox even with `--no-sandbox`; unrelated to this change (no rendering/UI code touched).
- 13 new unit tests (`server/standalone/connectRouter.test.mjs`, `headless.test.mjs`).
- Live-verified with real upstream data: started `node server/standalone/headless.mjs` and confirmed OpenSky OAuth flights, real CCTV frames from the Austin pack, and live CapMetro transit vehicles all serve correctly, plus a clean SIGTERM shutdown.

title: [Hex] feat(layers): Live TV — iptv-org channel directory with click-to-play HLS
body:
Part of #853 (item 6).

## Summary

This PR adds a **Live TV** layer to the Utilities group: a keyless worldwide directory of free-to-air live TV from the [iptv-org](https://github.com/iptv-org/iptv) project.

- **One pin per country** that has playable channels, sized by channel count. The busiest countries are labelled through the world-overlay host, and far-side pins are hidden.
- **Choosing a country** (a globe click on its pin, or a row in the list) loads that country's channels, 40 per page, with a **News only** filter, and flies there through the shell's navigation policy.
- **Choosing a channel plays it in the layer row.** One `<video>` element appears below the list, and hls.js (or native HLS) connects **straight from the viewer's browser to the broadcaster**. Nothing streams until a channel is chosen.
- **Failure handling:** after a fatal error, or 15 s without a picture, the player moves on to the channel's next stream. When none plays, the row says **"stream unavailable"** and why.
- **Stop** closes the player. The player is also released when the channel, country or layer changes.
- The row and help text say the streams are **third-party, linked not hosted**.
- **Adult 18+ toggle** (off by default). Channels iptv-org marks `is_nsfw` are listed, labelled `18+`, only while this row chip is on, and it is not persisted. Turning it off stops an adult channel and closes an adult-only country, and the row says why. Today iptv-org publishes a playable stream for just one such channel. If you would rather not have the toggle at all, say so and we'll drop those channels instead.

**How this differs from #285.** #285 embedded live news by scraping YouTube pages, which you closed as against YouTube's terms. This layer does none of that:
- no YouTube;
- no scraping;
- no third-party page embeds.

It plays only the direct `.m3u8` links in iptv-org's own `streams.json`. Hosts whose name contains a video platform are refused, so `twitch-m3u8.*.workers.dev` style relays are refused too. The server never requests, relays, caches or stores any video.

## Data source(s)

| | |
|---|---|
| Source | iptv-org API: `https://iptv-org.github.io/api/{channels,streams,blocklist,countries}.json`. These four fixed files are the only URLs the proxy will fetch. Pins sit at Natural Earth country label points (public domain), bundled in `src/layers/liveTv/anchors.js`. |
| Licence | The iptv-org directory is released under [The Unlicense](https://github.com/iptv-org/api/blob/master/LICENSE), a public-domain dedication. iptv-org states that it only collects links to publicly available streams, stores no video, and handles takedown requests on its repository. The streams belong to their broadcasters and are **linked, not hosted**. Credit line: "Live TV channel list: iptv-org (Unlicense); streams belong to their broadcasters, linked not hosted". |
| Auth / rate limits | Keyless. GitHub Pages serves the files with `Cache-Control: max-age=600`. `/api/live-tv` rebuilds its index at most every 6 h. Concurrent rebuilds share one fetch. After a failure it backs off for 5 min (serving the last good copy, marked stale). There are also 60 requests/min per client. |
| Code reference | None copied. Field names follow the iptv-org API docs. |
| Verified | 2026-09-30. 31,407 channels, 17,766 streams and 1,440 blocklist rows (1,073 DMCA, 367 NSFW) resolve to **9,182 playable channels in 178 countries** (12,888 streams, one channel adult). |

## How it works

- **`server/providers/liveTv.js`** (new; `/api/live-tv` and `/api/live-tv/country/{CC}`, registered in `server/providers/local.js` for dev and preview).
  - Fetches the four fixed files with `redirect: 'error'`, a 30 s deadline and body caps of 32 / 16 / 2 / 1 MB (about 4× today's sizes).
  - Builds the per-country index once and serves a small summary. Each country page is at most about 400 KB today (US), and the client caps it at 4 MB.
- **Filtering** (`src/layers/liveTv/records.js`, pure). Dropped:
  - blocklisted channels (DMCA and NSFW takedowns);
  - closed channels;
  - streams that need a custom `User-Agent` or `Referer` (a browser cannot send those);
  - anything that is not a credential-free `http(s)` `.m3u8`;
  - video-platform hosts.

  A channel keeps up to four streams, main feed first. `is_nsfw` channels are flagged `adult` and counted apart. The client sanitises every payload again.
- **`src/layers/liveTv/playback.js`**:
  - lazy-loads hls.js;
  - tries streams in order;
  - makes one media-error recovery;
  - arms the startup watchdog only after hls.js has loaded;
  - skips `http` streams on an `https` page instead of proxying them.
- **`src/layers/liveTv/index.js`**: the layer. It draws pins with manual horizon culling, labels through `overlayHost`, and uses the shared pick registry, so picks owned by other layers are left alone. It also provides row controls and a `media` descriptor.
- **Layer panel**: a generic, opt-in **`media` row slot**. A layer returns `{key, label, attach(video)}` and gets one keyed `<video preload="none" controls>` below its list. The slot is released on key change, on a null descriptor, on disable and on remount.
  - While a player is mounted, the row info carries `role="status"`.
  - `rowList` now numbers paged lists from their first ordinal.
  - Disabled chips show `not-allowed`, and loading chips keep `wait`.
- **Navigation**: the layer joins a `CAMERA_LAYERS` loop in `layerBindings.js`, with its own Cockpit noun. The same small refactor is in #857 and #859; whichever lands second will rebase onto it.
- **Share-link token**: a provisional `0`, following CONTRIBUTING (`layer-token:check`: 28 published, 1 new). **Merge note:** #855–#859 from this project also claim the provisional `0`. The ledger test fixtures use `3`/`4` because `0` is taken, so whichever merges after another should:
  1. re-run `npm run layer-token:next -- live-tv`;
  2. re-pin `layerStateTokenLedger.test.mjs`, the `layerState.test.mjs` token assertions and `layerStateTokenReservations.json`.

  Happy to rebase and do that on request.
- **Docs**:
  - `DATA_SOURCES.md` gets a sources-table row and a paragraph covering the filtering, caching, mixed content, IP exposure and takedown note.
  - `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md` gets a Utilities-row entry.
  - `CHANGELOG.md`, `dataCredits.js`, `format-scope.json` and `package-boundaries.json` are updated. There are new `./layers/live-tv` and `./layers/live-tv/source` exports.

## Validation

All gates were run on Node 24.14.0 against `origin/main` e7707d9. The head is `9485b5a`.

| Gate | Result |
|---|---|
| `npm run format:check` | ✅ |
| `npm run check:boundaries` | ✅ |
| `npm run layer-token:check -- --base-ref origin/main` | ✅ 28 published, 1 new |
| `npm test` | ✅ 5411 pass, 0 fail (5421 total, 10 skipped as on main) |
| `npm run build` | ✅ |
| `npm run test:track` (dev server) | ✅ 109 / 109 |
| `node scripts/qa-live-tv.mjs` (new) | ✅ 17 / 17 (live: 178 pins, 9,181 channels; ABC News Live played in-app) |

`qa-live-tv` runs the real app in headless Chromium:
1. **Live.** Against real iptv-org through `/api/live-tv`:
   - there is no error;
   - there is one pin per country;
   - the 25 busiest countries are listed;
   - the caveat is shown;
   - Adult 18+ is offered and off.
2. **Live play.**
   - Picking the US lists channels, and **no `.m3u8` is requested before a click**.
   - Clicking news channels in turn mounts a `preload="none"` player that settles. The first broadcaster that answered today was ABC News Live. Whether a given stream plays is recorded as a note, not a gate, because broadcasters go offline.
3. **Fixture** (in-page stub of `/api/live-tv`):
   - the malformed and adult-only countries are left off;
   - the far-side pin is hidden;
   - a real mouse click on a pin lists that country without streaming;
   - News only filters the list;
   - a channel with two dead streams tries both, then shows "stream unavailable";
   - Stop removes the player and keeps the country;
   - Adult 18+ adds the adult-only pin and a labelled 18+ row, and turning it off hides them again;
   - All countries returns to the summary.
4. **Failure.** With the route stubbed to 502, the error is surfaced, the pins are kept and the row says the refresh failed.
5. **Disable.** The data source is hidden, the player is released, and no uncaught browser errors occur.

The new unit tests cover six areas:
- **Proxy:**
  - fixed URLs, with no stream URL ever fetched;
  - route and country validation;
  - TTL, stale copy and backoff;
  - rate limit.
- **Records:**
  - the blocklist, closed channels and header-bound streams;
  - platform hosts and relays;
  - feed order;
  - adult flags and counts;
  - the sanitisers.
- **Source.**
- **Playback:**
  - direct play;
  - fall-through on fatal error, timeout and element error;
  - mixed content;
  - native HLS;
  - dispose before load.
- **Layer ownership:**
  - pins and labels;
  - paging and filters;
  - click-to-play, restart and stop;
  - the adult toggle;
  - picking, culling and navigation;
  - cleanup.
- **Panel:** the media slot lifecycle, list numbering and the status role.

| Live, worldwide (real iptv-org) | Live play: ABC News Live in the row |
|---|---|
| ![live](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/leopechnicki/gods-eye-view/refs/heads/hex/pr-assets/pr-assets/live-tv/live-tv-live-world.png) | ![play](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/leopechnicki/gods-eye-view/refs/heads/hex/pr-assets/pr-assets/live-tv/live-tv-live-play.png) |
| **Fixture: pins, culling, labels** | **Dead streams fall through to "stream unavailable"** |
| ![fixture](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/leopechnicki/gods-eye-view/refs/heads/hex/pr-assets/pr-assets/live-tv/live-tv-fixture.png) | ![unavailable](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/leopechnicki/gods-eye-view/refs/heads/hex/pr-assets/pr-assets/live-tv/live-tv-unavailable.png) |
| **Adult 18+ on (fixture)** | |
| ![adult](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/leopechnicki/gods-eye-view/refs/heads/hex/pr-assets/pr-assets/live-tv/live-tv-adult-on.png) | |

## Limitations

- **Many streams will not play.** Some are geo-blocked, offline, or refuse cross-origin playback in a browser. The player tries the channel's streams in order and then says so. With no video proxy, that is the honest limit.
- **Mixed content.** On an `https` deployment, `http` streams (about 20 % of them) are skipped rather than proxied. On `http://localhost` they play.
- **Excluded streams.** Streams that need a custom `User-Agent` or `Referer` (957 today) are excluded, because a browser cannot set those headers.
- **Privacy.** Direct playback exposes the viewer's IP address to the broadcaster, whose own terms apply. The help text says so.
- **Pin placement.** Pins mark the country, not the broadcaster's location.
- **No voice actions.** `set_layer_visibility` is not extended in this PR, so voice pins stay untouched.
- **Adult channels.** The toggle is session-only. iptv-org publishes almost no adult stream links, so it rarely changes the map.
- **Share-link token** is provisional (see the merge note above).

## Built by the Hex project

| Agent | Role on this PR |
|---|---|
| **Scout** | Research: the iptv-org API, licence and legal notes, raw and filtered counts; dedupe against all 558 PRs and 302 issues (only #285, closed, is related; #189 / #489 / #617 are CCTV HLS) |
| **Crew** | Implementation: `/api/live-tv` proxy, `liveTv` layer package, playback, the panel `media` slot, wiring and docs |
| **Forge** | Fork, branch and push; screenshot assets; tracking comment on #853 |
| **Probe** | Unit tests and the `qa-live-tv` harness (live, live play and fixture); ran every gate listed above |
| **Kat** | UI review: list numbering across pages, the disabled-chip cursor, two-line row copy, reasons of 45 characters or fewer, an em-dash lead, "No channels" copy, Stop last, `role="status"` while playing, and a notice when the 18+ toggle stops a player. **APPROVE** after re-review |
| **Axon** | Code review: platform relays (`twitch-m3u8.*.workers.dev`), the watchdog armed before hls.js loaded, main-feed-first ordering, stale backoff, remover growth in the panel, the caveat while playing, and a hidden adult channel accepted by id. All fixed with tests. **APPROVE** after two rounds |

title: [Hex] feat(layers): Wildlife — animal GPS tracks from public CC0 Movebank studies
body:
Part of #853 (item 7).

## Summary

This PR adds a **Wildlife** layer to the Movement group: keyless animal tracks from [Movebank](https://www.movebank.org), for seven public studies whose owners publish the data as **CC0**.

- **One glyph per tagged animal** at its latest GPS fix, coloured by species (Okabe-Ito, so it stays readable for colour-blind viewers). A legend names each colour and its count.
  - The arrow points along the animal's last real move.
  - An animal that has not moved, or has only one fix, is a dot.
- **A fading track** covers up to the animal's last 20 fixes, clamped to the ground. The track stops at any gap of more than a day or 250 km, so the globe never draws a straight line the animal did not fly.
- **Time window**: 30 days / 1 year / All time, by the age of the latest fix. The default is 1 year, because several studies report in seasons.
- **The row** lists the studies with their animal count and latest fix. Choosing a study flies to its animals and lists them, latest first, 40 per page.
- **Choosing an animal** (a row, or a globe click on its glyph) shows:
  - species and tag;
  - the time and age of its last fix;
  - its study, owner and licence.

  The dataset DOI is one chip away, and the full citation is in the row tooltip.
- **While studies are still on their way from Movebank**, the row says which ones and checks again every 20 s.
- **Honest freshness.** A study served from a copy past the one-hour TTL is marked "not refreshed" in the list, and the row says "N studies not refreshed since 3 h ago". A withdrawn study reads "no longer public" and its tracks are gone. The PARTIAL badge shows whenever any study is not fresh.

## Data source(s)

| | |
|---|---|
| Source | Movebank public JSON feed: `https://www.movebank.org/movebank/service/public/json?study_id=<id>&sensor_type=gps&max_events_per_individual=20`. Only the seven hard-coded study ids below are ever requested. |
| Studies | DELTATRACK (herring and lesser black-backed gulls, NL); LifeTrack White Stork SW Germany; LBBG_ADULT (BE); MEDGULL_ANTWERPEN; HG_JUVENILE (BE); ARMENIAN_GULL; SPOONBILL_VLAANDEREN. Owners are INBO (Research Institute for Nature and Forest, Belgium) and the Max Planck Institute of Animal Behavior. |
| Licence | Each study is **CC0 1.0**. We verified each licence by hand in the study's published dataset record (Zenodo, or the Movebank Data Repository), because Movebank does not expose licence metadata without a login. Each entry in `records.js` records where its licence was checked. Movebank's terms encourage citation for CC0 data, so every animal card names the owner and the tooltip carries the full citation and DOI. Credit line: "Animal tracking data: Movebank (movebank.org), CC0 1.0 — study owners as cited in the layer". |
| Auth / rate limits | Keyless. Movebank allows **one concurrent request per IP**. Large studies take up to about two minutes to answer (116 s measured), and it answers an occasional HTTP 500 that a retry clears. See How it works for how the proxy handles this. |
| Sensitive data | Study owners decide what is public. They can hide individual animals or embargo recent months, for example to protect a threatened population, and Movebank applies that before the public feed answers. The layer shows only what the keyless public feed returns and never asks for anything else. Revocation **fails closed** (see How it works): a study that stops being public is dropped with its cached tracks at once, and no copy of any study's coordinates is served past six hours, whatever the reason refreshes fail. Test tags recorded as *Homo sapiens* are discarded. |
| Code reference | None copied. Field names follow the Movebank REST API docs. |
| Verified | 2026-09-30. All seven studies answered: 418 animals with public fixes, 43 of them with a fix in the last year. The newest fix was 1 h old. |

**Alternatives considered:**
- **OCEARCH** (sharks, turtles) was rejected. Its tracker API refuses keyless requests, and its terms forbid any use of its tracks without written permission.
- **GBIF** is keyless and holds CC0 mirrors of some of the same INBO studies, but as periodic archival snapshots, not current positions. It would be a good source for a future "history" view, not for this layer.

## How it works

- **`server/providers/wildlife.js`** (new): serves `/api/wildlife`, registered in `server/providers/local.js` for dev and preview.
  - One refresher walks the curated studies **strictly one at a time**, matching Movebank's one-request-per-IP rule. Each request has a 150 s deadline, a 16 MB body cap and `redirect: 'error'`, and gets one retry after 5 s.
  - A study that fails twice is left alone for 15 minutes.
  - **Each study has a status: `fresh | stale | pending | withdrawn | unavailable`.** Only fresh and stale studies carry animals.
    - `fresh`: the copy is younger than the one-hour TTL.
    - `stale`: older than the TTL while refreshes fail (network error, timeout, 5xx, malformed body). It is still served, and the row says so.
    - **Hard maximum stale age: 6 hours** (`WILDLIFE_MAX_STALE_MS`). Past it, the copy is deleted and the study reads `unavailable` until Movebank answers again. These are exact positions of live animals, so a withdrawal the proxy cannot see (a new error shape, a long outage) still takes them off the map within six hours. Six hours is six refresh cycles and about twenty backed-off retries, enough to ride out a Movebank restart or maintenance window. By then the copy is also several report intervals behind the tags.
    - `withdrawn`: Movebank answered **401, 403, 404 or 410** (purged at once, no retry), or an empty 200 twice (its existing "no longer public" answer). The cache entry is deleted immediately. The next good answer after the 15-minute backoff restores the study.
  - The browser sanitiser fails closed too: it drops any animal whose study is not `fresh` or `stale`, even if a proxy sends one. An older proxy's `ok` is read as `fresh`, and the `withdrawn: true` row flag is kept.
  - **The route never waits on Movebank.** It answers at once from the one-hour cache, naming the studies still pending. A second request joins the running walk instead of starting another.
  - GET only, with 30 requests/min per client.
- **`src/layers/wildlife/records.js`** (pure, shared by the proxy and the browser):
  - the curated study list;
  - Movebank parsing (drops invalid fixes, fixes at 0,0 and *Homo sapiens* tags; tracks ordered and capped);
  - heading and gap-aware track helpers;
  - short ages;
  - the browser-side sanitiser, which re-checks every snapshot against the curated list.
- **`src/layers/wildlife/index.js`**: the layer.
  - Billboards with manual horizon culling.
  - Rotation is recomputed only when the camera pose changes, using `screenProjectedRotation` as the other heading layers do.
  - Clamped, fading polylines.
  - Picking goes through the shared pick registry, so picks owned by other layers are left alone.
  - Row controls include chips, the legend and paged lists.
- **Layer panel**: `rowList.js` numbers a paged list from its first ordinal, so page 2 starts at 41. **This is the same change as #861, byte for byte**, so whichever lands second merges cleanly.
- **Navigation**: the layer joins the `CAMERA_LAYERS` loop in `layerBindings.js`, with its own Cockpit noun `animal`. The same small refactor is in #857, #859 and #861; whichever lands second will rebase onto it.
- **Share-link token**: a provisional `0`, following CONTRIBUTING (`layer-token:check`: 28 published, 1 new). **Merge note:** #855–#859 and #861 from this project also claim the provisional `0`, so the ledger test fixtures use other digits. Whichever merges after another should:
  1. re-run `npm run layer-token:next -- wildlife`;
  2. re-pin `layerStateTokenLedger.test.mjs`, the `layerState.test.mjs` token assertions and `layerStateTokenReservations.json`.

  Happy to rebase and do that on request.
- **Docs**:
  - `DATA_SOURCES.md` gets a sources-table row and a paragraph covering the walk, caching, withdrawn studies, sensitive data, and why OCEARCH and GBIF were not used.
  - `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md` gets a Movement-row entry.
  - `CHANGELOG.md`, `dataCredits.js`, `format-scope.json` and `package-boundaries.json` are updated. There are new `./layers/wildlife` and `./layers/wildlife/source` exports.

## Validation

All gates were run on Node 24.14.0 against `origin/main` e7707d9. The head is `57244c8` (review fix for fail-closed revocation on top of `54c68ce`).

| Gate | Result |
|---|---|
| `npm run format:check` | ✅ |
| `npm run check:boundaries` | ✅ |
| `npm run layer-token:check -- --base-ref origin/main` | ✅ 28 published, 1 new |
| `npm test` | ✅ 5403 pass, 0 fail (5413 total, 10 skipped as on main), plus 14 / 14 allocation probes |
| `npm run build` | ✅ |
| `npm run test:track` (dev server) | ✅ 109 / 109 |
| `node scripts/qa-wildlife.mjs` (new) | ✅ 15 / 15 (live: 7 / 7 studies walked through the proxy, all `fresh`) |

`qa-wildlife` runs the real app in headless Chromium:
1. **Live.** It waits for the proxy to walk every curated study through real Movebank, then enables the layer.
   - Glyphs and tracks are drawn, and every study is listed.
   - The row shows the CC0 note and a species legend.
   - Opening a study and choosing an animal names its species, last fix, study and owner.
2. **Fixture** (in-page stub of `/api/wildlife`):
   - old animals and uncurated studies are left off;
   - the far-side glyph is hidden;
   - arrows point east and north as the fixes do, and a resting animal is a dot;
   - a still-pending study is named;
   - a withdrawn study is listed as "no longer public", and its animal is never drawn even though the stub sends it;
   - a real mouse click on a glyph selects it;
   - the DOI chip opens the dataset;
   - the windows add and drop animals.
3. **Failure.** With the route stubbed to 502, the error is surfaced as a short reason, the glyphs are kept and the row says the refresh failed.
4. **Disable.** The data source is hidden, the selection handler and poll are released, and no uncaught browser errors occur.

The new unit tests cover four areas:
- **Proxy:**
  - the walk is sequential, and a second request joins it (peak concurrency 1);
  - the handler answers without waiting;
  - retry and backoff;
  - a withdrawn study is dropped with its tracks;
  - fail-closed revocation (from review): a study is `fresh` within the TTL; after the TTL, with refreshes failing round after round (500/503), it is served `stale` with its coordinates until the 6 h maximum, then its coordinates are gone (`unavailable`), even when no refresh runs; 401, 403, 404 and 410 each purge at once (`withdrawn`, one request, no retry) and a later good answer restores the study; the empty-200 path still purges;
  - malformed answers;
  - routes, methods and the rate limit.
- **Records:**
  - every curated study is CC0 with an owner, citation, DOI and a label that fits a row;
  - parsing edge cases (*Homo sapiens*, 0,0, duplicates, other studies);
  - headings;
  - the gap-aware track;
  - ages;
  - the sanitiser, including dropping animals of withdrawn, unavailable or pending studies.
- **Source.**
- **Layer ownership (real Cesium):**
  - glyphs, tracks and the legend;
  - rotation only on a pose change;
  - culling;
  - windows and paging;
  - selection and navigation, including stale navigation;
  - pending polls;
  - stale and withdrawn studies named honestly (never as current);
  - failures;
  - globe clicks;
  - release on disable and destroy.

`rowList` numbering has its own test.

| Live, Europe (real Movebank) | Live: a lesser black-backed gull in Spain, selected |
|---|---|
| ![live](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/leopechnicki/gods-eye-view/refs/heads/hex/pr-assets/pr-assets/wildlife/wildlife-live-europe.png) | ![animal](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/leopechnicki/gods-eye-view/refs/heads/hex/pr-assets/pr-assets/wildlife/wildlife-live-animal.png) |
| **Fixture: glyphs, headings, culling** | **Fixture: selected animal** |
| ![fixture](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/leopechnicki/gods-eye-view/refs/heads/hex/pr-assets/pr-assets/wildlife/wildlife-fixture.png) | ![selected](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/leopechnicki/gods-eye-view/refs/heads/hex/pr-assets/pr-assets/wildlife/wildlife-selected.png) |

In the live screenshots, one study (HG_JUVENILE) had just answered Movebank's intermittent HTTP 500 twice. The layer marks it unavailable and shows the row as PARTIAL until the 15-minute backoff ends.

## Limitations

- **Europe-heavy.** Six of the seven studies are gulls, storks and spoonbills tracked from the Low Countries and Germany; the Armenian gulls are the exception. Few public studies are CC0 with current data. More can be added to the curated list once their licence is checked (studies on hold are listed in our research notes).
- **Not real time.** Tags report every few minutes to hours, some studies report in seasons, and owners may embargo recent data. The row says "fixes may lag hours".
- **Cold start.** The first walk after a server start takes a few minutes, because Movebank answers one study at a time. The row names the studies still loading, and the cache then serves instantly for an hour.
- **Dev and preview only.** Like the other `server/providers` routes, a static deployment would need the same proxy.
- **No voice actions.** `set_layer_visibility` is not extended in this PR.
- **Share-link token** is provisional (see the merge note above).

## Built by the Hex project

| Agent | Role on this PR |
|---|---|
| **Scout** | Research: Movebank's public feed, rate limit, empty-body semantics and latency; per-study licence checks in Zenodo and the Movebank Data Repository; OCEARCH and GBIF assessed; dedupe against all open and closed PRs and issues (nothing related besides #853) |
| **Scholar** | Evaluation: which of 165 public studies are CC0, current and safe to show; sensitive-species studies held back |
| **Crew** | Implementation: the `/api/wildlife` sequential proxy, the `wildlife` layer package, wiring and docs |
| **Forge** | Fork, branch and push; screenshot assets |
| **Probe** | Unit tests and the `qa-wildlife` harness (live, fixture, failure, disable); ran every gate listed above |
| **Kat** | UI review: study labels and animal rows that survive the ellipsis, terse age leads, two-segment info, the "No animals …" copy and short error reasons, tracks that stop at gaps instead of drawing false migration lines, the Okabe-Ito palette with a legend, paged numbering, and chip order. **APPROVE** after re-review |
| **Axon** | Code review: the proxy's concurrency, backoff and withdrawal handling, SSRF and body bounds, cleanup on disable and destroy, doc accuracy, and the month pluralisation edge. **APPROVE** after two rounds |
