title: feat: ask for vessels by area
body:
## Summary

Vessel requests can now name the area they are for, so a server that holds vessels by location can answer for that area instead of sending a fixed number of rows from everywhere.

- **Source** (`src/sources/live/standalone.js`): `getSnapshot({ maxRows, area })` sends an optional `area` as `lat`, `lon` and `radius_km` on `/api/ais-live`.
- **Vessel layer:** each refresh asks for the area the camera shows, centered on the middle of the screen and sized by camera height (`src/layers/vessels/viewArea.js`, `cameraArea.js`). From high enough up it asks for every vessel, as before. It also asks again when the view moves or zooms by a quarter of that radius, on the camera's `moveEnd`.
- **`vessels_in_area`:** names its resolved area. `find_vessel` still asks for every vessel.

The bundled local server ignores the new parameters and keeps returning every vessel it holds, so local behaviour is unchanged. Callers still keep only the vessels inside their area.

## Testing

- `npm test`: 5,606 passed, 0 failed. New tests cover the radius and move thresholds, ingestion asking by area and re-asking only after a real move, and `vessels_in_area` naming its area while `find_vessel` does not.
- `npm run check:boundaries`, `format:check`, `layer-token:check` and `build` pass.

title: fix(security): gate the CCTV Street View fallback and stop serving the voice debug log
body: ﻿## Summary Two security fixes, each with a reproduction, a fix and regression tests. | # | Issue | Impact | |---|-------|--------| | 1 | `/api/cctv/frame/:id` makes billable Street View Static calls with the **server Google key** for **any camera id at caller-chosen coordinates**, with **no cross-site gate and no throttle** | Any web page open in the user's browser (or any LAN client under `HOST=0.0.0.0`) can run up the owner's Google bill with `` tags | | 2 | The dev server serves `.gev-logs/` and `.gev-cache/` | `GET /.gev-logs/realtime-conversations.jsonl` returns the voice debug log (**on by default**): user speech transcripts, assistant transcripts, session instructions, tool results with locations. Readable by any `localhost` page through Vite's localhost CORS reflection | --- ## 1. Street View spend bypasses the Google cost controls `SECURITY.md` states that the cost-bearing Google endpoints refuse cross-site browser requests and are throttled by `GEV_RATELIMIT_GOOGLE_PER_MIN`. `/api/google/nearby-places` and `/api/google/text-search` do this. The CCTV Street View fallback uses the same server key but did neither: ```js // server/providers/cctv.js (before) const source = sourceById.get(cameraId); // undefined for unknown ids const lat = Number(url.searchParams.get('lat') || source?.lat); // client-controlled const lon = Number(url.searchParams.get('lon') || source?.lon); ... const sv = await streetViewFallback({ lat, lon, heading, fov, pitch }); // billable, keyed, ungated ``` A camera with no upstream image (including **any id that does not exist**) fell through to `streetViewFallback`, which fetched `maps.googleapis.com/maps/api/streetview?...&key=` at the caller's coordinates. ### PoC The real `cctvProxy` plugin, `GOOGLE_MAPS_SERVER_API_KEY` set, `fetch` stubbed to count outbound calls (nothing billed). There were 500 requests, each with a random camera id, carrying the headers a browser sends for a cross-site `` (`Sec-Fetch-Site: cross-site`, `Sec-Fetch-Dest: image`): ``` before: requests sent: 500 (unknown camera ids, Sec-Fetch-Site: cross-site) responses served as X-CCTV-Source=streetview: 500 billable Street View Static calls made with server key: 500 first call : https://maps.googleapis.com/maps/api/streetview?size=960x540&location=48.85%2C2.2945&heading=0&...&key= last call : https://maps.googleapis.com/maps/api/streetview?size=960x540&location=48.8999%2C2.2945&heading=139&...&key= after: responses served as X-CCTV-Source=streetview: 0 billable Street View Static calls made with server key: 0 ``` The same cross-site request shape against the live dev server: ``` GET /api/google/nearby-places?lat=48.85&lon=2.29 -> 403 Forbidden (gated, as documented) GET /api/cctv/frame/not-a-camera?lat=48.8584&lon=2.2945 -> 200 OK (reached the Street View call) ``` An attacker page needs only: ```html ``` Every distinct coordinate is a separate billable Street View Static request. ### Fix The Street View fallback now meets the same bar as the Places proxies: - **Registered cameras only.** `resolveStreetViewPose(source, query)` returns `null` for an unknown id, so an unknown id gets the synthetic frame. - **Pose pinned to the camera.** A client `lat`/`lon` is honoured only within 1.5 km of the registered position. The calibration panel's maximum offset is 900 m north plus 900 m east (about 1.27 km), so calibrated views keep working. Anything farther away, out of range or non-numeric snaps back to the registered position. - **Same-site gate.** Uses the existing `admitSameSiteRequest` (foreign or opaque `Origin`, cross-site `Sec-Fetch-Site`, proxy headers). A refused caller gets the synthetic frame rather than a 403, so the `` UX is unchanged. - **Per-IP throttle.** `GEV_RATELIMIT_GOOGLE_PER_MIN` (default 120, `0` disables), in its own bucket so 10 s card polling cannot starve place search. - **30 min frame cache** (64 entries, keyed without the API key). Street View imagery is static and cards refresh every 10 s, so an open card now costs one call instead of 180 per half hour. The cache sits behind the same-site gate. ## 2. Dev server serves the voice debug log and provider caches `server.fs.deny` in `build/vite.js` covered `.env`, certificates, `.git` and `ENVIRONMENT`, but not `.gev-logs/` or `.gev-cache/`, which sit under the served root. The Realtime debug sink is on by default (`debugSink = postDebugLog`), and it logs full `server.event` payloads (including `conversation.item.input_audio_transcription.completed` transcripts) and every `client.event`. The redactor strips keys and tokens, not conversation content. ### PoC (live dev server) The log contained a probe transcript `"PROBE-SECRET take me home to 221B Baker Street"`. ``` before: GET /.gev-logs/realtime-conversations.jsonl (Origin: http://localhost:3000) -> 200, body = full log Access-Control-Allow-Origin: http://localhost:3000 <- readable by any other localhost app GET /.gev-cache/probe.json -> 200 after: /.gev-logs/realtime-conversations.jsonl -> 403 leak=False /.gev-cache/probe.json -> 403 leak=False /@fs//.gev-logs/realtime-conversations.jsonl -> 403 leak=False /.gev-logs/realtime-conversations.jsonl?raw -> 403 leak=False /.gev-logs/realtime-conversations.jsonl?import -> 403 leak=False POST /api/realtime/debug-log (app writer still works) -> 204 ``` `Origin: https://evil.example` received no ACAO header. The exposure is to other localhost origins (any other dev server or local web app the user runs) and to LAN clients under `HOST=0.0.0.0`. ### Fix Add `'**/.gev-logs/**'` and `'**/.gev-cache/**'` to `server.fs.deny`. --- ## Tests New regression tests (`src/tooling/mediaProviders.test.mjs`, `src/tooling/viteBuild.test.mjs`): - Unregistered ids never call Street View (25 random ids, 0 fetches). - Cross-site / same-site-but-cross-origin / foreign `Origin` / `Origin: null` / `X-Forwarded-For` callers get the synthetic frame and 0 fetches. A same-origin caller still gets Street View. - A ~200 m calibration nudge is honoured. A far-away, out-of-range or garbage pose snaps to the registered camera. - Per-IP throttle (cap 3 → 3 billed calls, rest synthetic); 10 repeats of one pose → 1 call. - `fs.deny` includes both directories. These fail on `main` and pass with the fix. ## Validation - `npm test`: 5611 tests, 5601 pass, **0 fail** - `npm run format:check`: clean (1208 files) - `npm run check:boundaries`: clean (`cctv-provider` manifest updated for the new imports) - `npm run build`: ok - Live dev server: before/after curl results above `npm run test:track` and the `qa-*.mjs` browser gates were not run. The CCTV client contract (`/api/cctv/frame/:id?lat&lon&heading&fov&pitch`) is unchanged, and `src/layers/cctv/source.js` already sends the registered id and calibrated pose. `CHANGELOG.md` and `SECURITY.md` are updated to match.

## Deployment-testing line — aliasfoxkde fork at v0.10.5

> **Read this first:** this is a **divergent development/deployment line** of
> gods-eye-view, opened for upstream visibility and end-to-end testing — not a
> merge-ready change. The fork sits 303 commits ahead / ~636 commits behind
> `upstream/main` (fork point `880a672b`), touching 1,086 files
> (+114,035 / −22,362). GitHub will show this as conflicting; that is expected
> and out of scope here. Nothing in this PR should be merged without a
> deliberate re-graft pass (the fork's own process for absorbing upstream work
> is documented in its `docs/PLAN.md` Phase 13, which did exactly that for 513
> upstream commits).

### What this line is

A long-lived hardening + performance campaign on top of gods-eye-view, run as
its own product line ("God's Eye View / Globe") with:

- **A full CI pipeline of record** (lint → strict security scan → unit tests
  on Node 24 AND Node 26 with allocation gating → coverage → wasm+build →
  bundle budgets), enforced on every push.
- **~4,070 unit tests** co-located with source, run headless.
- **Parity-enforced dev/prod API surface**: client code composes `/api/...`
  URLs through a single builder inventory; a guard test fails if any inventory
  route lacks a dev middleware or a Cloudflare Pages Function, so the dev
  server and production deployments cannot drift.
- **WCAG 2.1 A/AA gated** via axe + pinned census/contrast tests, with a
  criterion-by-criterion AAA conformance ledger in `docs/ACCESSIBILITY.md`.
- **Phased, measured performance work** (PLAN.md Phases 13–15): parked-camera
  render-request elimination, worker offload (AIS horizon occlusion, detection
  projection), chunked processing, render governor, label arbiter, and — in
  this release — a boot payload split plus the first measured per-frame
  callback census.

### What v0.10.5 (this PR's tip) contains

See the fork's `CHANGELOG.md` for the full per-release record. Highlights:

- **Fixed**: the Planets layer could not be enabled through the Layers UI
  (the module never implemented the layer-manager `update()` contract, so
  every enable silently rolled back — present since the layer's import), and
  planet labels ignored their distance fade (`Cesium.Interval` passed where
  Cesium requires `NearFarScalar`).
- **Performance**: boot payload split — voice, scenes, annotations, cockpit
  cloud effects, and first-run experience load as deferred chunks on first
  use (entry bundle 6,086,202 → 5,843,743 B, five seam chunks pinned by a
  budget guard test); rocket-launch mission declutter walk gated behind dirty
  flags + a quantized camera-position key with a 500 ms floor instead of
  running per frame.
- **Instruments**: `scripts/profile-frame-census.mjs` (per-frame callback
  census with registration-time attribution) and
  `scripts/qa-frame-cadence.mjs` (behavioral cadence gate).

### How to test this line

```bash
npm install
GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY=... npm run dev        # or scripts/dev-fresh.sh on macOS
npm run lint && npm test && npm run build && npm run check:budgets
```

A deployed build of this exact tree is on the fork's Cloudflare Pages
production alias (project `globe`). Every release in the fork's history is
tagged `v0.9.0` … `v0.10.5` with its own changelog section.

### What upstream may want to cherry-pick

The fork maintains an explicit upstream-extraction pipeline (PLAN.md Phase 13
categorized all 513 then-upstream commits and grafted 16 fixes). The reverse
flow — work here that upstream may want — is easiest to browse via the fork's
`CHANGELOG.md` and `docs/PERFORMANCE.md`; the highest-value, lowest-coupling
candidates are the layer-manager enable-contract fix (planets), the
`NearFarScalar` fade fix, and the dev/prod route-parity guard test.

title: feat: import GeoJSON, KML, KMZ and GPX files onto the globe
body:
This is something interesting that I was adding to my instance and wanted to see if others would be able to use it.

## What it does

DISPLAY ▸ **Import** puts your own GeoJSON (`.geojson`/`.json`), KML, KMZ and GPX files on the globe: pick them with the Import button or drop them onto the globe. Each file becomes its own Cesium data source (`GeoJsonDataSource`, `KmlDataSource`, `GpxDataSource`), clamped to the ground, in its own color from the whiteboard palette, with a row to show/hide it, fly to it, or remove it. The first file of a batch is flown to. Files are read in the browser and never uploaded; they last for the page session.

This covers the import half of #890 (hike tracks, trails, property lines and similar). Saving/exporting drawings is not part of this PR.

## Safety

- **An imported file cannot make the page fetch anything.** Before `KmlDataSource` sees a KML/KMZ document, `sanitizeKmlDocument` removes `NetworkLink`, `NetworkLinkControl`, `ScreenOverlay`, `PhotoOverlay`, `Model` and `Tour`, every `href` that is not an image packed in the same KMZ (served from a blob URL) or a `data:image/` URL, every non-local `styleUrl`, and placemark `description`/`BalloonStyle`/`Snippet` HTML. The hint says when something was left out.
- **KMZ** is read by a small dependency-free zip reader on the platform `DecompressionStream` (stored and deflated entries; no encryption, no ZIP64), with a 120 MB inflate limit as a zip-bomb stop. Relative hrefs resolve only to entries inside the archive.
- **Bounds:** 50 MB per file, 20,000 entities per file, 12 files on the globe at once. A refused file names its reason and doesn't stop the rest of the batch.
- File names are rendered with `textContent` only.

## Files

- `src/data/geoFileImport.js`: format detection, zip reader, KML sanitizer, loaders.
- `src/ui/geoFileImport.js`: the DISPLAY control, drop handling, list, teardown (`window.__gevGeoImport` test seam).
- Wiring in `src/app/tools.js` (after the draw tool, with deferred `destroy()`), markup in `src/ui/templates/display-controls.html`, styles in `src/ui/styles/controls.css`, icons `upload_file`/`visibility`/`visibility_off` added to the `icon_names` subset.
- `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md` section, `CHANGELOG.md` entry, `scripts/format-scope.json` and `scripts/package-boundaries.json` entries.
- No share-link token: imported files are local and not part of shareable state.

## Validation

- `npm test`: 5,621 tests, 5,620 pass, 0 fail, 1 skipped (the allocation test that requires Node 24; this machine runs Node 26). New: `src/data/geoFileImport.test.mjs` (format detection, GeoJSON checks, zip reader incl. deflate, zip-bomb, encrypted and damaged archives, KMZ path resolution) and `src/ui/geoFileImport.test.mjs` (behavioral, with DOM/viewer doubles: picker, drop, list actions, limits, errors, teardown, late loads after destroy).
- `npm run build`, `npm run format:check`, `npm run check:boundaries`: clean.
- `npm run test:track`: 109 passed, 0 failed.
- New gate `scripts/qa-geo-import.mjs` (keyless dev server): all 13 checks pass, run twice. It imports a GeoJSON, a KML, a KMZ (packed icon and ground overlay) and a GPX through the real file input; checks the polygon actually paints, stops painting when hidden and paints again when shown; imports a dropped file; refuses a text file with a reason; removes every data source; and fails if the page requests anything from a trap host named in the KML/KMZ network link, icon, style and balloon (none were requested).
- `scripts/qa-draw-tool.mjs`: I can't get this gate to complete on my Linux machine (SwiftShader software rendering). Unmodified `main` gets 25 passes and then fails "a shape can be drawn after the board was cleared from the keyboard". This branch fails that same check, and in one run also "a shape can be drawn again after a reload". Replaying that exact step by hand (reload, Draw on, three clicks, Enter) draws the mark on both `main` and this branch, so I believe it's timing on slow rendering. Please run it on a normal GPU to confirm.

title: feat: load Google 3D with short-lived server tokens
body:
## What

Without a browser key, the app can load Google Photorealistic 3D Tiles with short-lived Google access tokens from its own server instead.

- `src/maps/googleTokens.js`: asks the app's server for a token at `GET /api/google/tiles-token` (answer: `{ accessToken, expiresAt }`), reuses it until shortly before it expires, and renews it once however many tile requests were refused for the same token. Any other answer (404, HTML, malformed, offline) means the server does not offer tokens.
- `src/maps/google3d.js`: a `google-token` route between the key route and ion. Tiles carry the token as an `Authorization` header; a tile refused (401/403) for an expired token gets the renewed one and is retried once. Same tileset settings as Cesium's Google helper.
- `src/standalone/application.js` / `src/app/scene.js`: offer the token source only when no key is configured.

## Behaviour unchanged when

- A browser key is set: the key route is used and no token is requested.
- The server does not offer tokens: startup continues through ion or the keyless globe as before.

## Tests

- `src/maps/googleTokens.test.mjs`: reuse, renewal before expiry, one renewal for concurrent refusals, servers that do not offer tokens.
- `src/mapStartup.test.mjs`: token route resource and header, retry with a renewed token, key precedence, fallback to ion.
- `npm test`: all pass. The 4 cancelled tests in `src/services/requests.test.mjs` are also cancelled on `main`.
- `npm run check:boundaries`: passes.

title: bug: MCP globe panel in Claude Desktop shows "Only the God's Eye View panel may make this request"
body:
### What happened

In Claude Desktop (Windows, Cowork mode) I asked: "Show the active tropical cyclones in God's Eye View." Claude asked permission for `get_cyclones`, then called `show_in_gods_eye_view`. Where the globe should appear, the panel showed:

> God's Eye View could not load here: Only the God's Eye View panel may make this request.

Claude's text answer and the "Open in God's Eye View" link worked fine; only the in-conversation panel failed.

Afterwards there were **two** `server/mcp/stdio.js` processes running, started by the same parent process in the same second (Claude Desktop). As far as I can see, each server process creates its own `panelKey` with `randomBytes(32)` (`server/mcp/server.js`, line 35), the panel page carries that key, and `panel_request` rejects other keys (`src/tools/queries/panelRequest.js`, line 275). My guess, not verified: the panel page was served by one process while its `panel_request` calls reached the other, so the keys did not match. It may also be specific to Cowork mode or to Windows.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Fresh clone at tag `v0.2.1`, `npm ci`, `npm run build:panel`, start the app (we used `npm run dev -- --port 5173 --strictPort` to follow docs/MCP_SETUP.md)
2. Add the server to `claude_desktop_config.json` as in docs/MCP_SETUP.md, with absolute paths to `node.exe` and `server/mcp/stdio.js` and `--api-base http://localhost:5173`
3. Fully quit Claude Desktop from the tray and reopen it
4. In a new conversation (Cowork mode, Opus 5.5) ask: "Show the active tropical cyclones in God's Eye View." Allow the tool once.
5. The panel shows the message above. In Task Manager / `Get-CimInstance Win32_Process`, two `stdio.js` node processes are running.

### How you installed

Terminal (git clone + npm)

### OS, Node version, browser

Windows 11 Home (10.0.26200), Node 24.19.0, Claude Desktop 2.19675.0.0 (Microsoft Store package)

### Version or commit

v0.2.1 (aa16b7c)

### Output of `npm run doctor`

```text
[OK] Node 24.19.0: supported LTS and calibrated for release gates
[OK] npm 11.21.0
[OK] dependencies installed

Map:     Esri World Imagery (keyless satellite basemap) with keyless terrain

Configured providers: none

Ready. Run npm run dev, then open http://localhost:4173.
```

Thanks for the project, the rest of the MCP tools worked well in our test: an earthquake and two hurricanes matched USGS and NOAA exactly.

title: docs: MCP_SETUP.md uses port 5173, but npm run dev and the MCP server default to 4173
body:
### What happened

`docs/MCP_SETUP.md` says `npm run dev  # http://localhost:5173` and uses `--api-base http://localhost:5173` in every client example. At v0.2.1, `npm run dev` starts on **4173** (`build/vite.js`, `port = 4173`), the doctor says "open http://localhost:4173", the README uses 4173, and the MCP server's own default is `http://localhost:4173` (`server/mcp/services.js`, `DEFAULT_API_BASE`).

Someone who follows MCP_SETUP.md literally starts the app on 4173 and points the MCP server at 5173, where nothing is listening.

Suggested fix: use 4173 in MCP_SETUP.md, or drop `--api-base` from the examples so the server's default applies.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Fresh clone at tag `v0.2.1`, `npm ci`, `npm run dev`
2. The dev server listens on http://localhost:4173, not 5173 as MCP_SETUP.md states
3. A client configured with `--api-base http://localhost:5173`, as the guide shows, then points at a port where nothing is listening (we did not run this failing combination ourselves; we started the app on 5173 instead)

### How you installed

Terminal (git clone + npm)

### OS, Node version, browser

Windows 11 Home (10.0.26200), Node 24.19.0

### Version or commit

v0.2.1 (aa16b7c)

### Output of `npm run doctor`

```text
Ready. Run npm run dev, then open http://localhost:4173.
```

### Server log and browser console

Not applicable: this is a documentation mismatch. We avoided the failure by starting the app on 5173 explicitly.

title: feat: add Statens vegvesen (Norway) road cameras as a CCTV pack
body:
Adds Norway's public road cameras from Statens vegvesen (the Norwegian Public Roads Administration) as a new live CCTV pack.

## Source

- **Catalog:** one keyless GeoJSON request to the agency's OGC API Features view of its official DATEX 3.1 CCTV site table (`ogckart-sn1.atlas.vegvesen.no/ogc/features/v1/collections/datex_3_1:CctvSimple/items`). The raw DATEX node needs an account; this view does not. The whole country comes back in one request: 896 cameras, about 800 KB.
- **Frames:** stills on `kamera.atlas.vegvesen.no/api/images/<cameraId>`.
- **Live video:** about 135 working cameras also publish HLS at `kamera.vegvesen.no/public/<cameraId>/manifest.m3u8` (a master playlist pointing to an MPEG-TS variant). These play through the existing in-memory HLS relay, with the still as the snapshot fallback. No new playback code was needed.
- **Licence:** NLOD 2.0 ([dataset page](https://dataut.vegvesen.no/en/dataset/webkamera)). The required attribution is registered in the Data attribution popover and in `DATA_SOURCES.md`.

## Behavior

- Every working camera loads: about 850 today, after dropping the cameras the feed itself reports as `videoOrImagesUnavailableDueToCameraFault`. With all packs loaded, the catalog serves about 3,890 cameras, under the default `CCTV_MAX_SOURCES=4000`, so no other region is thinned.
- All cameras sit under one "Norway" category in the picker, as Finland does. Labels read `<road> <place> → <facing toward>`, for example `E39 Fjøsangerveien v/BKK → sentrum`.
- `orientationDescription` names the place a camera faces, not a bearing. Headings therefore use the shared id-hash fallback at low confidence, as Calgary and Fintraffic do, and the calibration gizmo corrects them.
- **Security:** the URLs are server-registered and pinned. A still is accepted only when it equals `VEGVESEN_IMAGE_ORIGIN + cameraId`, and a manifest only when it equals the camera's own manifest path. Camera ids must match `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,40}$`. The catalog fetch refuses redirects and is size-capped.
- **Env:**
  - `CCTV_VEGVESEN_ENABLED=0` turns the pack off.
  - `CCTV_VEGVESEN_MAX_SOURCES` (default 900, range 8–1000) caps it. Cameras nearest Oslo, Bergen, Stavanger, Trondheim, Kristiansand, Bodø and Tromsø are kept first.
  - `CCTV_VEGVESEN_VIDEO=0` keeps every camera on stills.
  - `CCTV_VEGVESEN_URL` overrides the catalog URL.

## Testing

- `npm run format:check`, `npm run build` and `npm test` all pass (5,633 tests, 0 failures). The new `src/data/cctvVegvesen.test.mjs` covers mapping, pinning, faulty and out-of-area drops, HLS selection with its kill switch, loader dedupe and failure handling, and catalog wiring with its kill switch.
- Manual check, following the TESTING.md §6 HLS soak: I turned on CCTV in Bergen and selected `E39 Fjøsangerveien v/BKK`. The panel showed **LIVE · OK** / "Live HLS connected" and the relay served `video/mp2t` segments. Still-only cameras, for example in Tromsø and Bodø, show frames through `/api/cctv/frame/…`.
- `npm run test:track` was **not run**: Puppeteer's Chrome wasn't installed locally. This change doesn't touch tracking code.

title: Touch-first iPad UI, PWA installability, and layer hardening
body:
# Touch-first UI, PWA installability, guided tour, honest feed status, 2D mode, wind failover, and a dev-server bind fix

## What

Improvements that make God's Eye View work as an installed touch app
(iPad), fix a first-launch failure, harden the layers against upstream
outages, and tell the truth about missing keys:

1. **Dev server binds `127.0.0.1` by default** (`build/vite.js`). `localhost`
   can resolve to `::1` only, leaving IPv4 clients with connection refused
   and the app looking dead on launch. `HOST` still overrides it (e.g.
   `0.0.0.0` for LAN sharing, which keeps the widened `allowedHosts`
   behavior).

2. **PWA support** — `public/manifest.webmanifest`, generated app icons
   (`public/icons/`: 192/512 + maskable 512, radar-crosshair motif in the
   app's cyan-on-dark style), and `index.html` head tags (manifest,
   `theme-color`, `apple-touch-icon`, `mobile-web-app-capable`). "Add to
   Home Screen" now installs it as a standalone app instead of a bookmark.

3. **Touch-first CSS** (`src/ui/styles/foundation.css`, `index.html`):
   - `#cesiumContainer canvas { touch-action: none }` — the globe owns its
     gestures (drag rotates, pinch zooms) instead of the browser hijacking
     them for pull-to-refresh. (Cesium's widgets.css normally sets this;
     the app doesn't load it — the default toolbar is hidden.)
   - `touch-action: manipulation` on buttons/links/inputs — no tap delay,
     no double-tap zoom.
   - `overscroll-behavior: none` at the document level, no iOS tap flash,
     no text selection or callout on HUD chrome long-press.
   - `viewport-fit=cover` + `@media (display-mode: standalone)` safe-area
     rules so the installed app uses the full screen without clipping HUD.

4. **GUIDED TOUR tile on the first-run launcher** (`src/ui/templates/welcome.html`,
   `src/firstRunExperience.js`). Runs the scripted San Francisco flythrough —
   the same camera moves and annotations the voice agent would produce — as
   a self-running narration, watchable end-to-end with no mic and no API
   keys. Fire-and-forget: the launcher closes immediately; a synchronous
   throw keeps it open for retry.

5. **Platform share sheet** (`src/sharelink.js`, `src/ui/applicationShell.js`).
   The share button now uses `navigator.share()` where available (one-tap
   sharing on iPad), falling back to the clipboard exactly as before.
   Dismissing the sheet reports "Share dismissed" — never silently converted
   to a copy.

6. **KEY REQUIRED terminal state** (`src/loadingFeedback.js`,
   `src/ui/styles/status.css`). The global status chip no longer folds
   "needs an API key" into LOAD FAILED: a missing key is guidance, shown in
   amber with the layer names and a pointer to POWER UP. A real breakage in
   the same batch still dominates (severity ordering preserved).

7. **2D map mode** (`src/ui/globeMode.js`, DISPLAY panel, `M` key). The flat
   Cesium map is dramatically lighter on weak GPUs — the escape hatch for
   older tablets. Session-local on purpose: a performance preference for
   this device, not a view worth serializing into share links.

8. **Service worker** (`public/sw.js`). App-shell caching for the installed
   PWA: documents are network-first (updates flow, offline falls back to
   cache), same-origin assets are cache-first, `/api/*` and cross-origin
   tiles are never intercepted. Registered in production builds only.

9. **Wind model failover** (`src/layers/wind/index.js`). When the selected
   model is down (observed: NOAA GFS outage), the layer tries the other
   model once (ECMWF IFS) instead of going dark. The UI names the serving
   model with a "(fallback)" marker; stats follow the serving model.

10. **Toggle hardening** (`src/ui/layerPanel.js`). The layer toggle's busy
    state is bounded at 30s: if an enable never settles, the control
    re-syncs from the layer's actual state so a retry stays possible.

11. **ISS quick-track chip** (`src/layers/satellites/controls.js`). The
    satellites row gains an ISS chip that flies to and tracks the station
    (NORAD 25544) — previously hard to isolate among hundreds of labels.

`CHANGELOG.md` documents all seven under [Unreleased]. The bind-default and
mission-table assertions in the unit tests now expect the new behavior.

## Verification

- `npm run doctor` — clean
- `npm run build` — clean (service worker registration confirmed in bundle)
- `npm test` — full unit suite green (5568 tests, 0 failures)
- `npm run format:check` — clean
- `npm run check:boundaries` — clean
- Manual: dev server listens on `127.0.0.1:4173` (was `[::1]` only);
  `/manifest.webmanifest`, `/icons/icon-192.png`, and `/sw.js` serve
  correctly; the new CSS rules and `viewport-fit=cover` confirmed in the
  served page.
- Not run: `npm run test:track` (needs a headed browser with GPU;
  unavailable in this environment).

## Notes for reviewers

- The icon artwork is generated (PIL), not hand-drawn — happy to swap in
  official brand art if preferred.
- No service worker yet: installability (manifest + icons + meta) is the
  core of the iPad story; offline caching can follow as a separate change.
- Not included: moving `docs/media` to Git LFS. That rewrites contributor
  infrastructure and deserves a maintainer decision, not a drive-by in this
  PR — flagging it here instead.

## Exploration notes (hosted edition, no local changes)

Verified live on the community host: first-run panel, live flights via the
adsb.lol fallback (tracked AAL2707 over Austin with telemetry), cockpit view,
CelesTrak satellites (831 objects; ISS not isolatable), all four sensor modes
(Normal/CRT/NVG/FLIR), Portland close-up. Upstream issues noticed while
testing, not caused by this PR: Wind layer UNAVAILABLE (NOAA GFS upstream
down); Earthquakes, Cameras, and Rain-radar toggles unresponsive.

Follow-ups in this PR from those findings:
- Wind now fails over GFS → ECMWF IFS automatically, with a "(fallback)"
  marker in the UI.
- Layer toggles bound their busy state at 30s so a hung enable can never
  wedge the control.
- Satellites row has an ISS quick-track chip.

title: feat: add encrypted investigations and offline discovery
body:
God's Eye View can query public geographic data, but cannot retain those results in a sourced local investigation or offer a lightweight offline learning atlas. This PR adds encrypted area investigations and a separate public discovery library. For example, an operator can capture the observed Earth center, request dated Landsat scenes or soil estimates, retain their provenance in an encrypted case, and separately explore installed Earth/Moon/Mars cards without a model call.

## Implementation

- **Encrypted area investigations:** reuse existing USGS earthquake, OSM dam/datacenter and NASA recent-imagery tools through a narrow standalone facade. Preserve source links, attribution, retrieval/source dates, coverage, missing/stale states and bounded results. Separate observations, hypotheses, contradictions and manual follow-up. Closing cancels queries and scrubs the workspace; authenticated encrypted backups restore into a new case ID.
- **Dated imagery and soil estimates:** query yearly Landsat Collection 2 candidates with cadence/cloud controls and play the same fixed geographic crop with acquisition dates and explicit gaps. SoilGrids supplies center-cell sand/silt/clay estimates by depth with 5th/95th prediction quantiles; missing values stay unknown. Scientific metadata joins the encrypted area case; image bytes remain online.
- **Public discovery:** 15 English/French, revision-pinned CC0 Wikidata cards for selected Earth landmarks, aircraft families and Moon/Mars sites. Exact IDs, local text/spatial lookup and a bounded session cache work without API/model calls. Explicit nearby Earth lookup is optional and off by default. Public pack import/export validates schema, bodies, HTTPS links and SHA-256 integrity. Earth navigation reuses the existing coordinate action.
- **Offline learning:** a separate `/discovery.html` page omits Cesium and map providers. Its dedicated worker caches only the public shell and local assets. Three source-reading journeys provide snapshot-grounded quizzes; study progress stays in its own local storage key and is excluded from public exports and source requests.
- **Independent Moon/Mars overviews:** `/planet.html` renders lightweight WebGL spheres with small original NASA JPEGs, body-specific coordinates, site markers and source links. Its own offline worker keeps planetary maps separate from Earth providers. Map provenance, original-byte checksums and NASA/JPL credits are included.
- **Routing observations:** opt-in diagnostics export only closed lookup metadata, excluding raw searches, coordinates and study answers. Shadow proposals never execute requests or actions. A CLI bridge captures/hashes an explicitly selected Parcimonia checkout's core and probes strict-local requests read-only. Optional Jev/Laya/OpenJev injected choice contracts remain disabled, bounded and shadow-only; no provider SDK or model loader is added.

The existing Demon Forge privacy workspace remains separate from public discovery and the area vault: external Social Analyzer report import, manual candidate confirmation, attested non-self mandate scope, encrypted history and English-default request drafting with French available. There is no Social Analyzer execution, named-person web search, face recognition, individual tracking or automatic request submission. Case titles, private notes, study answers and passphrases never enter geographic source requests. Contact handoff remains disabled without a verified source directory; mandate metadata is operator attestation rather than electronic-signature verification.

## Validation

Validated on Node 24.19.0 against the integrated upstream baseline `a08a53cf9469eb991f708bd3d042c327a2347e3c`; published contribution head is `26c359fb4c9aeee5ee0f923721f0d3b431b245d9`.

- Full unit runner: **5,713 passed, 10 skips, zero failures**, including serialized focus/overlay allocation probes. Four additional Python metadata-boundary tests passed before upstream synchronization; their source is unchanged.
- After upstream synchronization, the standard production build and actual MCP panel build passed. The local routing/journey browser gates were also rerun successfully with offline reload. Import-direction and package-boundary checks passed. Routing/controller/benchmark files pass scoped Prettier; the existing large-chunk advisory remains.
- Twelve authored discovery fixtures matched explicit expected source IDs and reference ordering/distances, with zero lookup API/model calls. Lookup-only CPU timing separates setup, uncached index and session cache; no universal speedup or monetary saving is claimed.
- A real read-only Parcimonia `shadow-routing/1` core execution retained strict locality and recorded **12/12 abstentions** because that prototype cannot guarantee candidate locality. Core source hashes are recorded in the local report. Jev/Laya/OpenJev tests use synthetic transports only, including cancellation, timeouts, invalid probabilities, identity mismatch and unsupported-route refusal.
- Real Chromium walkthroughs cover encrypted area lifecycle/backups and scientific fixtures, local bilingual discovery, checked import/export, Earth navigation/vehicle-family selection, source-reading journeys, routing diagnostics/redacted export and offline reload. The independent planetary gate covers coordinate selection, body switches, offline maps and missing-texture failure under software WebGL. Dedicated discovery/routing/planet pages produced no foreign/API requests or page errors during their local/offline gates.
- Bounded real provider probes returned one SoilGrids profile and a 1990 Landsat scene/crop. These are point/scene checks, not global coverage or laboratory validation. The prior encrypted-investigation head also passed the 109-case tracking regression; that earlier run is not claimed as a rerun of all new modules.

The contribution integrates upstream main at `a08a53c`, including the Norway CCTV pack and TomTom link corrections. The changelog conflict was resolved by retaining both branches' entries. GitHub reports the published head as mergeable; the PR remains a draft for maintainer review.

## Scope and proof limits

This remains a **draft for maintainer scope/design review**, including whether the optional privacy workflow belongs alongside geographic investigation and discovery. The code is modular, but the contribution spans several optional capabilities.

Historical playback uses individual ~30 m optical scenes, not annual mosaics or reconstructed 3D; clouds, seasons, nodata and scan-line gaps affect comparison. SoilGrids is a static modeled ~250 m center-cell texture estimate, not an area average, historical soil series, mineral assay or proof of deposits. Offline discovery covers a small editorial sample, not complete articles, a global encyclopedia or offline Google tiles. Aircraft cards describe families, not verified identities of live vehicles. Planetary maps are coarse static visual overviews without detailed elevation or current phase/lighting.

Source linkage and SHA-256 integrity do not establish entity-match accuracy or author authenticity. Study quizzes do not establish mastery or model training. A provider revision echo does not authenticate weights; adapter confidence remains uncalibrated, billed cost is unknown, and all routing results prohibit auto-act. No real Jev/Laya/OpenJev inference, model download, paid call or change to the Parcimonia checkout occurred. Source-provided text remains in its original language; privacy drafts are France/EU-first and not legal advice.

Documentation: `docs/DEMON-FORGE.md`, `docs/AREA-INVESTIGATION.md`, `docs/AREA-SCIENCE.md`, `docs/DISCOVERY.md`, `docs/PLANETARY-OVERVIEWS.md`, `docs/DISCOVERY-ROUTING.md`; attribution in `DATA_SOURCES.md` and `public/planetary/`. Local logs, synthetic screenshots/downloads, private case data and external source corpora are ignored and excluded from the commit.

title: bug: Overpass disk cache ignores which upstream produced it, so configuring your own instance can still serve public-mirror data
bug: setting tileJsonUrl alone is silently ignored, so there is no working way to point vector tiles at a self-hosted mirror
body:
### What happened

Since #742, road geometry (Street Traffic) and military areas come from
`tiles.openfreemap.org` on every install, and there is no configuration path to point that at a
mirror the operator runs. `.env.example` has 20 variables and none of them covers tiles; no
production caller passes tile options — `src/layers/traffic/source.js:83` and
`src/layers/installations/source.js:97` both construct `createOpenFreeMapSource()` with no
endpoint, and `src/standalone/layerSources.js:25` with no arguments at all. Compare
`OVERPASS_UPSTREAMS`, which exists precisely so an operator can carry their own load.

**Scope, stated up front:** this is not reachable from configuration today, so it is not an
end-user bug report. The seam does exist in code — `createVectorTileSource` accepts
`tileJsonUrl`, `allowedOrigin` and `template` (`src/sources/vectorTiles.js:20-23`),
`createOpenFreeMapSource` spreads `...options` last (`src/sources/openFreeMap.js:218-226`), and
both layer sources take `mapTiles` as an injectable default parameter. A fork or embedder
reaching for that seam hits a trap, measured below, which is worth closing before any
configuration path is built on top of it.

### Steps to reproduce

A local nginx `proxy_cache` mirror of OpenFreeMap on port 12348, then the production factory
driven directly:

```js
import { createOpenFreeMapSource } from './src/sources/openFreeMap.js';
const MIRROR = 'http://127.0.0.1:12348';
for (const c of [
  { name: 'A upstream (control)', tileJsonUrl: 'https://tiles.openfreemap.org/planet', allowedOrigin: 'https://tiles.openfreemap.org' },
  { name: 'B both -> mirror',     tileJsonUrl: `${MIRROR}/planet`, allowedOrigin: MIRROR },
  { name: 'C only tileJsonUrl',   tileJsonUrl: `${MIRROR}/planet`, allowedOrigin: 'https://tiles.openfreemap.org' },
  { name: 'D mirror serves its own TileJSON', tileJsonUrl: `${MIRROR}/local/planet`, allowedOrigin: MIRROR },
]) {
  const source = createOpenFreeMapSource({ tileJsonUrl: c.tileJsonUrl, allowedOrigin: c.allowedOrigin });
  let meta = null, metaError = null;
  try { meta = await source.getMetadata(); }
  catch (e) { metaError = `${e.message}${e.cause ? ` | cause: ${e.cause.message}` : ''} (retryable=${e.retryable})`; }
  console.log(c.name, '\n  template:', meta?.template ?? '—', '\n  error:', metaError ?? 'none');
}
```

```
A upstream (control)
  template: https://tiles.openfreemap.org/planet/20260927_080001_pt/{z}/{x}/{y}.pbf
  error: none
B both -> mirror
  template: —
  error: Vector tile metadata unavailable | cause: Invalid vector tile origin (retryable=false)
C only tileJsonUrl                      <-- the first thing anyone would try
  template: https://tiles.openfreemap.org/planet/20260927_080001_pt/{z}/{x}/{y}.pbf
  error: none                           <-- loads fine; every tile still goes upstream
D mirror serves its own TileJSON
  template: http://127.0.0.1:12348/planet/20260927_080001_pt/{z}/{x}/{y}.pbf
  error: none                           -- 9 tiles decoded; nginx logs MISS then HIT
```

C is the problem: `tileJsonUrl` is accepted, no error and no warning is raised, and the mirror
receives nothing. B fails hard with a message that does not say the cause is the TileJSON's
`tiles[0]`.

### Mechanism

`src/sources/vectorTiles.js:119-147` takes `template` from `value?.tiles?.[0]`, resolves it
against `allowedOrigin`, and rejects when the origins differ (`:141`). A transparent caching
proxy returns upstream's TileJSON verbatim, and in it `tiles[0]` is an absolute upstream URL:

```
$ curl -s http://127.0.0.1:12348/planet | jq -r .tiles[0]
https://tiles.openfreemap.org/planet/20260927_080001_pt/{z}/{x}/{y}.pbf
```

So B's origin check fires, and C passes the check only because `allowedOrigin` still names
upstream — which is also exactly why no tile reaches the mirror. The origin check itself looks
right and worth keeping: it stops a TileJSON from redirecting the client to an arbitrary host.
The gap is that `tileJsonUrl` and `allowedOrigin` are independent and both hardcoded to upstream
(`src/sources/openFreeMap.js:220-221`), so setting one without the other is silently inert.

### Suggested fix

Smallest change that removes configuration C while keeping the origin check: default
`allowedOrigin` to `new URL(tileJsonUrl).origin`. Overriding `tileJsonUrl` alone then becomes
case B, which reports a real error instead of quietly doing nothing.

Two notes that may help whoever picks this up:

- A local origin is already an expected mode for this reader —
  `src/layers/traffic/flowSource.js:12-13` uses `template: '/api/tomtom/flow/{z}/{x}/{y}.pbf'`
  with `allowedOrigin: 'http://localhost'`.
- Working self-hosting needs the mirror to serve its own TileJSON with `tiles[0]` on its own
  origin (case D). That is not obvious from the code, so it is worth a line of documentation —
  or operators can skip TileJSON entirely with the existing `template` option.

### Environment

- Node **24.21.0**, npm 11.19.0 — within `engines: >=24.14.0 <25 || >=26 <27`.
- `upstream/main` at `e1cc7afa`, clean worktree.
- `npm run doctor`: `[OK] Node 24.21.0` · `[OK] npm 11.19.0` · `[OK] dependencies installed` ·
  `Ready.`
- Mirror: `nginx` with `proxy_cache` in front of `tiles.openfreemap.org`; case D adds one
  `location` serving a TileJSON copy whose `tiles[0]` names the mirror. Tile requests upstream
  were limited to seeding 13 cache entries over Monaco at z14.

title: fix(tiles): derive the tile origin from the configured TileJSON (#933)
body:
Closes #933.

### The change

`createVectorTileSource` took `tileJsonUrl` and `allowedOrigin` as independent options, and `createOpenFreeMapSource` hardcoded both to `tiles.openfreemap.org`. Repointing only `tileJsonUrl` — the obvious single change — left `allowedOrigin` on the default host, so the TileJSON's absolute upstream `tiles[0]` passed the origin check and every tile was fetched from the default host. No error, no warning, nothing reached the configured mirror.

`allowedOrigin` now defaults to `new URL(tileJsonUrl).origin`:

- `src/sources/vectorTiles.js` — new `tileJsonOrigin()` helper as the default for `allowedOrigin`; returns `undefined` for a missing or relative `tileJsonUrl`, so the `template`-only callers are untouched.
- `src/sources/openFreeMap.js` — stops hardcoding `allowedOrigin` and lets it follow whichever `tileJsonUrl` is in effect.

The origin check itself is unchanged. A TileJSON still cannot point the client at a host the caller did not configure; that check is now simply applied against the host the caller actually asked for.

### Why nothing else changes

All three direct callers pass `allowedOrigin` explicitly today, and an explicit value still wins over the derived one:

| caller | passes |
|---|---|
| `src/sources/openFreeMap.js:219` | `tileJsonUrl` (origin now derived) |
| `src/layers/alpr/source.js:74-75` | `tileJsonUrl` + `allowedOrigin` |
| `src/layers/traffic/flowSource.js:12-13` | `template` + `allowedOrigin` |

### Measured

Against a local nginx `proxy_cache` mirror of OpenFreeMap, running the production factory. Before / after, Node 24.21.0:

| configuration | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| default (no override) | loads from `tiles.openfreemap.org` | unchanged |
| only `tileJsonUrl` → mirror serving its own TileJSON | **silently loaded from `tiles.openfreemap.org`** | loads from the mirror: `template: http://127.0.0.1:12348/planet/.../{z}/{x}/{y}.pbf`, 9 tiles decoded, nginx `MISS` then `HIT` |
| only `tileJsonUrl` → transparent proxy (upstream TileJSON verbatim) | **silently loaded from `tiles.openfreemap.org`** | `Invalid vector tile origin` (`retryable: false`) |
| `tileJsonUrl` + explicit `allowedOrigin` | honoured | honoured, unchanged |

### Tests

Four added, covering both directions so neither half can regress silently:

- `vectorTiles.test.mjs` — a configured `tileJsonUrl` sets the tile origin; a `tiles[0]` on a different host is still refused; an explicit `allowedOrigin` still wins.
- `openFreeMap.test.mjs` — a repointed source fetches nothing from `tiles.openfreemap.org`; a mirror serving the default host's TileJSON verbatim fails loudly.

```
node --test src/sources/vectorTiles.test.mjs src/sources/openFreeMap.test.mjs
  tests 24  pass 24  fail 0

node --test src/layers/traffic/source.test.mjs src/layers/installations/source.test.mjs \
  src/layers/alpr/source.test.mjs src/data/militaryNames.test.mjs \
  src/layers/installations/namesLoading.test.mjs src/maps/sourceFactories.test.mjs \
  src/data/flowTiles.test.mjs src/data/alprCameras.test.mjs
  tests 129  pass 129  fail 0

npm run format:check
  Checked 1209 source files.
```

Downstream suites chosen from the call graph of `createVectorTileSource` (3 direct callers, 15 symbols to depth 3), not by guesswork.

### Not in scope

This does not add a configuration path for tiles — there is still no env knob for `tileJsonUrl`, as #933 notes. It makes the existing seam behave, so a knob can be built on it without inheriting the silent case. `src/layers/alpr/source.js` points at a second fixed tile host (`tiles.dontgetflocked.com`) and is left alone here.

title: fix(overpass): do not serve cached answers from a different upstream (#932)
body:
Closes #932.

### The change

Both disk caches fed by `OVERPASS_UPSTREAMS` key only on the query, so an entry written against one instance is a hit for the same query against another. Cached answers now carry a tag identifying the configured upstream set, and a disk read refuses an entry that does not match.

- `overpass/constants.js` — `resolveOverpassUpstreamTag()`, a 12-hex hash of the resolved endpoint list memoised alongside the existing list, plus the shared `cachedByConfiguredUpstream()` predicate.
- `overpass/transport.js` — a successful payload records `upstreams: <tag>` next to the existing `endpoint: 'configured'`.
- `overpass/cache.js` — `readOverpassDisk` refuses a non-matching entry, on the `Infinity` stale path too.
- `military-installations.js` / `military-installations/cache.js` — the same, since that cache is fed by the same upstreams and keys only on the bbox.

The tag is a hash, never a URL. It is written to disk and compared on read; it is not sent to clients and does not appear in errors, so `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md`'s guarantee about endpoint metadata still holds.

### The policy choice, and where I need your call

`cachedByConfiguredUpstream()` accepts **any** entry while nothing is configured, and only matching entries once an instance is configured:

- **Nothing configured** — there is no instance to contradict, and serving last-good data at any age is what `overpass.js:129-137` exists for. Behaviour unchanged.
- **An instance configured** — only its own answers are served. An entry from a different instance is refused, and so is an entry with no tag, because there is no way to tell which instance wrote it.

That second half has a cost worth stating plainly: **on upgrade every existing entry is untagged, so the first outage after upgrading serves nothing where it previously served stale data.** It recovers as soon as each query is fetched once from the configured instance. I took that over the alternative — accepting untagged entries on the stale path only — because an untagged entry may well have come from the public instances that were the default before #742, and "last-good roads beat an empty layer" is a weaker claim than "we are not serving overpass-api.de's data". If you would rather keep the stale-path resilience, it is one condition in `cachedByConfiguredUpstream` and I will change it.

### Measured

Same probe as in #932: two separate processes, one query, an empty `.gev-cache/overpass/`. Phase 1 points `OVERPASS_UPSTREAMS` at a stand-in that returns a marked payload; phase 2 points it at a real local Overpass and repeats the query.

Before:

```
seed  | generator: PUBLIC-MIRROR-MARKER | elements: 1
local | generator: PUBLIC-MIRROR-MARKER | elements: 1   <-- new upstream never asked
```

After:

```
seed  | generator: PUBLIC-MIRROR-MARKER | elements: 1
[Overpass] ignoring cached responses produced by a different OVERPASS_UPSTREAMS;
           they will be refetched from the configured instance.
local | generator: Overpass API 0.7.62.11 | elements: 3587   <-- the configured instance
```

The warning is printed once per process, not per request, following the shape `local-receivers.js:416-420` already uses for a rejected operator value: name the variable, say what will happen.

### Tests

```
node --test src/overpassProxy.test.mjs src/data/overpassProxy.test.mjs \
  src/overpassOffload.test.mjs src/data/installationProxy.test.mjs \
  src/data/militaryInstallations.test.mjs src/data/militaryInstallationData.test.mjs
  tests 83  pass 83  fail 0

npm run format:check
  Checked 1209 source files.
```

Added `a disk entry is not served after OVERPASS_UPSTREAMS is repointed`, which pins all three states: an instance's own entry is a hit, the same entry is refused for fresh and stale reads once a different instance is configured, and it is served again when nothing is configured.

One existing fixture changed: `coalesced outage callers both receive last-good data` seeds a disk entry while an upstream is configured, so that entry now carries that instance's tag the way the transport writes it. The test's intent is unchanged — it still proves last-good data beats a cached refusal.

### Scope

Only the disk layer checks the tag. The memory caches are process-local and are repopulated from the configured instance, so they cannot carry an answer across a configuration change in practice; `src/overpassOffload.test.mjs:222` also seeds `_overpassCache` directly to test stale headers, and adding the check there would change what that test is about without fixing anything real.

Not addressed: an install with nothing configured keeps serving whatever its cache holds, including entries written before #742. That is the existing not-configured behaviour rather than part of this bug, and purging it is a policy decision for you — say the word and it is the same one condition as above.

title: feat: add C-ITS (V2X) layer from OpenTrafficMap
body:
> **Draft. Not ready to merge until OpenTrafficMap agrees to the data use** (see *Open questions*).

## What this adds

A keyless **C-ITS (V2X) layer** built on [OpenTrafficMap](https://opentrafficmap.org), whose volunteer receivers pick up public C-ITS broadcasts (CAM, DENM, MAPEM, SPATEM), mostly in Austria and Germany (Graz, Vienna, Kiel, Heilbronn, Braunschweig and others).

- **Traffic lights with their live signal phase**, painted onto the MAPEM lane geometry of each intersection (green, amber, red per signal group)
- **Roadside units, warning trailers, and DENM hazards** (roadworks, traffic conditions), with the hazards drawn as glowing ground corridors
- **Buses and trams** with line, destination and vehicle number; trams get always-on detection brackets with a two-line card
- **A C-ITS panel in the right rail** for visibility ranges (vehicles, lights, labels, brackets), dot size and which kinds are shown, stored per viewer in `localStorage`
- Everything is drawn in Street Traffic's style through the renderer contract (draw-port point and line sets, clicks through the input dispatcher, no Cesium in the layer): grounded point primitives, the same flow palette, distance scale and fade, and preset-aware colours under NVG, FLIR and CRT. Vehicles glide between the 1.5 s polls.

## Privacy

This follows README's line on not tracking individuals:

- **Private vehicles are anonymous dots only.** Everything except infrastructure, hazards, buses and trams goes to the browser as kind, position, speed and report age, under a random id that is new in every response, in random order, instead of its station address. Two responses can't be joined into a track by id or list position; the browser pools these dots by slot and moves them without gliding.
- **Hazards come only from public stations** (infrastructure, buses, trams). A DENM sent by a private car is dropped, and a re-broadcast counts only when its originator is a public station the relay knows.
- Station kinds match case-insensitively; trucks, emergency vehicles and stations without a kind stay anonymous.
- Anonymous dots can't be selected, never get a bracket or card, and are never handed to the global detection mode. They are not claimed in the pick registry either, so main's Context card treats a click on one as empty map.
- **Vehicle tracks are neither returned nor kept.** The tile mirror holds only the track ids the upstream patch protocol needs, with no coordinates.

## Upstream load and safety

- **Tiled relay (default):** `/api/cits` holds one socket to `wss://opentrafficmap.org/ws_tiled` (gzip), shared by all tabs.
  - It subscribes the union of tiles requested in the last 10 s: zoom 9–14, at most 16 tiles.
  - It refuses views that need coarser tiles with `status: 'zoom-in'`.
  - It closes after 60 s without demand and reconnects with backoff.
  - Typical cost is about 60–130 KB/s while the layer is on, and nothing while it is off.
- **Full stream (`/ws_ext`, about 1 MB/s) is opt-in.** It needs `CITS_OTM_FULL_STREAM=1`; without it, `mode=full` gets a 403 and the layer hides its bandwidth chips.
- **Size caps:**
  - upstream frames: 32 MB compressed, 96 MB after gunzip
  - mirror size per tile and for the full stream
  - per-response object, hazard and intersection counts
- **Fixed hosts and gating:** upstream hosts are fixed, and the route uses `sameSiteGated` plus an error guard, so a relay fault returns a 500 and doesn't take down the server.
- **Voice:** `cits` is listed in `VOICE_OFF_LAYERS`, which keeps the Realtime prompt under its 52,000-character budget and leaves main's tool schema pins unchanged.
- **Kill switch:** `CITS_OTM_ENABLED=0` turns the relay off.
- **Share token:** the layer uses token `03` (`npm run layer-token:next -- cits` on current main). The token-allocation scenario tests move to the next free token, as CONTRIBUTING describes.

## Verification

Run on Node 26.13 (Linux x86_64), at `4c16e5f8` (merged with main `2004cad9`):

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `npm run format:check` | ok |
| `npm run check:boundaries` | ok |
| `npm run layer-token:check -- --base-ref <main>` | 39 published, 1 new |
| `npm run changelog:check` | ok |
| `npm run i18n` | all 13 locales complete |
| `npm test` | 15,378 pass, 0 fail, 3 skipped |
| `npm run build` | ok |
| **New gate:** `node scripts/qa-cits.mjs` (dev server, headless Chromium) | 17/17 pass |

`scripts/qa-cits.mjs` uses a fixed fixture and never contacts OpenTrafficMap. It reads the drawn dots through the renderer's query port and checks:
- the panel and layer appear and disappear together
- every fixture station is drawn
- a click on the anonymous car lands on its dot but opens no card, neither the layer's nor the Context card, and the car is never passed to detection
- a click on the tram opens its card
- the kind switches filter the dots
- the bandwidth chips are hidden without the opt-in
- polling stops on disable
- the console stays clean

Screenshots are written to `qa-shots/cits/`.

Against live data (Graz, keyless): about 90 traffic lights with phases, 50 trams, 40 buses, hazards, and anonymous cars, with no station addresses in anonymous records. `mode=full` returns a 403 without the opt-in.

## Open questions

1. **Data permission.** OpenTrafficMap publishes no data licence or API terms, and `/ws_tiled` and `/ws_ext` are the site's own internal endpoints, so the protocol can change without notice. I'd like to ask the operator (OpenTrafficMap – Verein für intelligente Verkehrssysteme, Graz) before this merges. `DATA_SOURCES.md` says the same.
2. **Scope.** Should private vehicles appear at all, even as anonymous dots, or should the layer stay strictly infrastructure plus public transport? Removing them is a one-line change in `CITS_PUBLIC_KINDS` plus a filter.
3. **Full stream.** Should it ship at all, or stay out of the codebase?

title: fix(viewer): clamp canvas dimensions to maximumTextureSize on high-res displays (#905)
body:
Fixes #905.

### Problem
On displays where WebGL reports `MAX_TEXTURE_SIZE` as 2048 (e.g. software renderers, Angle fallbacks, remote desktop sessions, or integrated GPUs) running in fullscreen on 1440p or 4K monitors, `CesiumWidget.prototype.resize` sets `canvas.width = clientWidth * pixelRatio * resolutionScale` which exceeds 2048. When `GlobeDepth.update` subsequently attempts to allocate its depth framebuffer texture, Cesium's `Texture` constructor throws:
`DeveloperError: Width must be less than or equal to the maximum texture size (2048). The width is: 2560`
crashing the render loop.

### Solution
- Added `src/app/textureSizeCompat.js` to dynamically compute the upper-bound resolution scale based on `gl.getParameter(gl.MAX_TEXTURE_SIZE)` and defensively clamp drawing buffer dimensions so neither dimension exceeds `maximumTextureSize`.
- Installed hook in `createApplicationViewer` (`src/app/viewer.js`) on widget resize and `scene.preRender`.
- Added dedicated unit tests in `src/app/textureSizeCompat.test.mjs` verifying scale ratios, clamp limits, and boundary cases.
- Registered helper in `scripts/package-boundaries.json` and `scripts/format-scope.json`.

### Verification
- `npm run format:check` (1,210 source files pass)
- `npm run check:boundaries` (885 modules, 0 violations)
- `node --test src/app/textureSizeCompat.test.mjs` (5/5 tests pass)
- `npm run build` (Clean production build in 9.8s)

title: feat: read Norway transit from Entur's Vehicles API
body:
## What

Point the `entur-norway` transit feed at Entur's **Vehicles GraphQL API (realtime v2)** instead of the v1 GTFS-Realtime feed.

The v1 feed omits several Norwegian operators that publish positions only to the v2 API: Skyss (Bergen), Vestfold og Telemark, Innlandet and others. Measured on a Sunday evening, vehicles reporting within the last 10 minutes:

| Source | Vehicles | Skyss |
|---|---|---|
| v1 GTFS-RT (current) | ~570 | 0 |
| v2 Vehicles API (this PR) | ~745–870 | ~140–180 |

## How

- `src/data/transitFeeds.js`: the Entur entry gains `format: 'entur-vehicles'` and a fixed POST `request` (body holds `ENTUR_VEHICLES_QUERY`). Still a registered URL only; the browser never supplies one.
- `src/sources/transitService.js`: sends the registered method/body when a feed declares one.
- `src/data/transitProxy.js`: JSON `Accept`/`Content-Type` for that format, and `buildTransitSnapshot` decodes it with the new decoder.
- `src/data/enturVehicles.js` (new): turns the GraphQL answer into the same vehicle records `decodeVehiclePositions` produces (newest report per vehicle id, plausibility checks, string caps, entity cap). Speed is left null because Entur does not document its unit.
- Each record carries Entur's reported mode (BUS/COACH → bus, TRAM, METRO → subway, RAIL, FERRY). `transitModeFor`/`transitModeResolved` take an optional reported mode that wins over route-id hints, so ferries, trams and trains get their own markers. Feeds without the field behave exactly as before.
- Coverage is three circles (61.3°N 6.5°E r 380 km, 67.3°N 4.5°E r 600 km, 71.3°N 23.0°E r 340 km) from Lindesnes to Vardø and Grense Jakobselv; every neighbouring city (nearest: Lerwick, Östersund, Kiruna) stays over 50 km outside, past the 40 km slack.
- Docs: `DATA_SOURCES.md`, `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`. Boundaries and format scope updated for the new module.

Ruter (Oslo/Akershus) publishes to neither open Entur feed, so it is still absent.

title: feat: Kartverket ground heights for Statens vegvesen cameras
body:
Follow-up to #929, as requested in [the review](https://github.com/bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view/pull/929#issuecomment-5984977452): each Statens vegvesen camera now gets its own ground height instead of the flat 150 m prior.

## Why

The Vegvesen feed only carries 2D points, so every camera shared `groundElevationM: 150`. Mountain-pass cameras (Valdresflye at 1,391 m, Haukeli, Sjonfjellet) could therefore sit hundreds of metres underground on a stack where neither the point-height prior nor the ground snap resolves.

## How

[Kartverket's point-height API](https://ws.geonorge.no/hoydedata/v1/) is keyless and licensed CC BY 4.0. It returns terrain height above sea level (NN2000), which is the orthometric datum `groundElevationM` already uses, so the client's geoid handling is unchanged.

- **Batching:** 20 points per request, eight requests in flight. All of Norway is about 36 requests and takes about 6–13 s cold; a slower first lookup leaves the rest on the flat prior until the next refresh. The API accepts 50 points, but above ~20 it answers the extra points from contour lines (`hoydekurver`) or not at all. At 20, nearly every camera resolves from the 1 m `dtm1` model, so no retry pass is needed.
- **Water:** over water, `/punkt` returns the sea-floor depth (`datakilde: dybdekurver` or `terreng: Havflate`; −547 m under Nordhordlandsbrua). Either marker counts as 0 m, the water surface. For the ~14 bridge cameras that is below the deck, but far closer than the sea floor or the flat prior.
- **Matching:** answers are matched by the coordinates the API echoes back, and are recorded only for the points that request asked about. `z: null` is never read as 0, and heights outside −20…2,500 m count as no height.
- **Caching:** heights are cached in memory by position for the life of the server. Points with no height (three ferry quays and one bridge) are cached for 6 h. A warm refresh therefore makes no Kartverket requests.
- **Failures:** the first 429, 5xx or network error stops the lookup. Nothing is retried, and no new lookup starts until the backoff ends: `Retry-After` when sent, else 10 min, bounded to 1 min–1 h. A failing Kartverket costs one attempt rather than one per refresh. The whole lookup shares one 30 s deadline, and it never throws.
- **Bounded wait:** the lane waits at most 12 s for heights, counted from the start of the loader with the catalog fetch included, so it stays under the 15 s per-provider timeout. A slower lookup keeps filling the cache for the next refresh.
- **Request:** only coordinates are sent, with the same User-Agent as the other CCTV requests.
- **Kill switch:** `CCTV_VEGVESEN_HEIGHTS=0`.
- **Attribution:** Kartverket is credited, with the CC BY 4.0 link, beside Statens vegvesen in the Data attribution popover. `DATA_SOURCES.md` has a new row and note.

## Results (live)

- **Coverage:** 851 of 855 cameras get a height. The four without data are three ferry quays and one bridge, and they keep the prior.
- **Startup:** a full `/api/cctv/sources` load at app start took 15 s, the same as before this change. A warm refresh took 0.9 s.

| Camera | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| F51 Valdresflye | 150 | 1,390.7 |
| E134 Liamyra → Haukeli | 150 | 571.2 |
| E16 Langhuso → Flåm | 150 | 352.8 |
| R80 Bodøelv | 150 | 18.6 |
| E39 Nordhordlandsbrua | 150 | 0 (water surface) |

## Testing

- `npm run format:check` passes, as do `npm run build` and `npm test` (5,646 passing, 0 failing).
- New tests in `src/data/cctvVegvesen.test.mjs` cover: batching at 20 and matching by echoed coordinates in reverse order; recording only the points a request asked; each water marker on its own; the −20/2,500 m bounds; the 8-in-flight cap; a 429 stopping the lookup with no further requests; the shared deadline; `Retry-After` bounds; cache reuse and the null TTL; the backoff; the kill switch; and a slow lookup that doesn't hold the catalog.
- While writing the tests I found and fixed a bug before it shipped: `toFiniteNumber(null)` returns 0, so "no data" would have been read as sea level.
- `npm run test:track` was not run, because Puppeteer's Chrome isn't installed locally. Tracking code is untouched.

title: feat(bikeshare): add Norway's city bikes (Oslo, Bergen, Trondheim, Stavanger, Skien/Porsgrunn, Lillestrøm)
body:
## Summary

Adds every Norwegian station-based city-bike system with an open GBFS feed to the Bike Share layer and `get_bike_share`, about 760 stations in all:

| System | Area | Source | Stations |
|---|---|---|---|
| Oslo Bysykkel | Oslo | Urban Sharing (`gbfs.urbansharing.com`) | 267 |
| Bergen Bysykkel | Bergen | Urban Sharing | 98 |
| Trondheim Bysykkel | Trondheim | Urban Sharing | 75 |
| Kolumbus Bysykkel | Stavanger / Nord-Jæren | Entur Mobility (`api.entur.io`) | 254 |
| Farte Bysykkel | Skien / Porsgrunn | Entur Mobility | 54 |
| Bysykkel Lillestrøm | Lillestrøm | JCDecaux Cyclocity (`api.cyclocity.fr`) | 6 |

All feeds are keyless.

## Changes

- **Registry**: six new entries in `src/layers/bikeshare/registry.js`.
- **Allowlist**: `gbfs.urbansharing.com`, `api.entur.io` and `api.cyclocity.fr` join `GBFS_ALLOWED_HOSTS`. Both `api.entur.io` and `api.cyclocity.fr` also serve other APIs, so the proxy only accepts paths under their GBFS trees (`/mobility/v2/gbfs/` and `/contracts/`).
- **Extensionless paths**: Entur serves `station_information` / `station_status` without `.json`, so the registry and proxy endpoint checks accept either form. Cache policy is unchanged: 5 min for station information, `no-store` for status.
- **Identifying headers**: the proxy sends `Client-Identifier: gods-eye-view` on every upstream request, as Urban Sharing asks. Requests to Entur also carry `ET-Client-Name: gods-eye-view-bikeshare`, as Entur requires.
- **Attribution**: three new rows in `DATA_SOURCES.md` and three new entries in `dataCredits.js`:
  - Oslo, Bergen and Trondheim Bysykkel under NLOD 2.0, per each operator's open-data page.
  - Kolumbus and Farte Bysykkel under NLOD, per the Entur Mobility API docs.
  - Bysykkel Lillestrøm under Licence Ouverte (Etalab), the feed's own `license_url`.
- **Load radius**: Farte and Lillestrøm use a 40 km radius so `get_bike_share` over Oslo does not also search Skien. The map layer still uses its 100 km minimum.
- **Docs**: `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md` and `CHANGELOG.md` (Unreleased) are updated.

Out of scope: Entur Mobility also carries scooter and car-share systems (Voi, Bolt, Ryde, Dott, Getaround, …). They have no fixed stations, so they are not added here.

## Testing

- `npm run format:check`, `npm run check:boundaries`, `npm run build`: pass.
- `npm test`: passes. `src/toolProjectRoot.test.mjs` timed out once under full-suite load and passes on its own.
- `npm run test:track`: 109 passed, 0 failed.
- New tests:
  - Header tests: `Client-Identifier` on every request, `ET-Client-Name` only to Entur.
  - Mounted-route round trips for each new system.
  - The proxy rejects non-GBFS paths on the Entur and Cyclocity hosts.

title: Harden Vite fs.deny for local logs and cache

title: feat: add Sentinel-2 Latest map source via Copernicus Sentinel Hub
body:
## What

Adds a **Sentinel-2 Latest** map source: the least-cloudy Copernicus Sentinel-2 L2A scene of the last 30 days (≤20 % tile cloud cover, true colour B04/B03/B02, 10 m), served by the Copernicus Data Space Ecosystem Sentinel Hub Process API through the local server.

## Why

The existing basemaps (Esri, Bing, Google 3D) are months-to-years-old composites. This gives a recent, dated, cloud-free view wherever the camera is, using a free Copernicus account.

## How

- **Keys.** New free Provider Settings entry `sentinel-hub` (`SENTINEL_HUB_CLIENT_ID` + `SENTINEL_HUB_CLIENT_SECRET`), also wired through `.env.example`, the Pinokio env templates, `dev-fresh.sh` and the setup doctor. Both values stay server-side; the browser only learns `hasKey` from `/api/sentinel2/status`.
- **Proxy** (`server/providers/sentinel2.js`, `/api/sentinel2`):
  - OAuth client-credentials token kept in memory only: 60 s refresh margin, one shared request for concurrent tiles, 30 s cooldown after a failed mint, one re-mint on a 401.
  - Tiles only at z8–z14 (z14 ≈ 9.6 m/px, the native 10 m). Memory + disk cache (`.gev-cache/sentinel2/`) for 48 h; stale tiles served when upstream fails.
  - `/scene?lon&lat` returns the acquisition date from the Catalog API, cached 6 h per 0.1° cell.
  - Only two fixed CDSE hosts are contacted; redirects refused; capped bodies; non-PNG rejected; shared same-site gate; GET only; upstream error text, client ID, secret and token are never echoed or logged.
  - A per-UTC-day budget (`SENTINEL_HUB_DAILY_REQUEST_BUDGET`, default 300 ≈ 9,300/month) keeps usage inside the free 10,000-requests-per-month quota.
- **Map.** New `sentinel2-latest` stack. `MapSourceController` gains an optional per-source `underlay` and `layerOptions`: Sentinel-2 draws on terrain levels 7–14 over an Esri underlay, so far views and close-ups past the native resolution show Esri instead of stretched pixels. Three tile failures fall back to Esri Satellite.
- **Not live.** While active, the on-screen credit shows the acquisition date and cloud cover of the scene at screen centre, ending "not live". Copernicus attribution is added on screen, in the Data attribution popover and in `DATA_SOURCES.md`.
- **Keyless.** The chip is shown locked with the Provider Settings hint. The default stack, other stacks and share links are unchanged; nothing is requested from Copernicus.

## Reviewer notes

- **Voice is deliberately not wired.** `src/voice/gevActions.test.mjs` now names `sentinel2-latest` as not voice-selectable instead of requiring every stack to appear in `set_map_stack`.
- The Map Source row goes from five to six chips (`mapStackChips.test.mjs` updated).
- **Known limitation:** a wide view can mix several acquisition dates; the label describes the scene at screen centre and says so.
- The daily budget is conservative: about 8–15 fresh screens of new area per day; areas already viewed are cached for 48 h.
- **Unrelated to the keyless Recent Imagery layer** (NASA HLS, 30 m, per day).

## Validation

- `npm test`: 5,639 pass, 0 fail (new: `sentinel2Tiles`, `sentinel2Provider`, `sentinel2Sources`, `sentinel2Scene` tests, plus a key-setup registry test). They cover the key-missing state, token caching/refresh/retry/cooldown, the allowlist, caching and the budget.
- `npm run build` passes (its chunk-size warning was already there before this change).
- `npm run format:check` and `npm run check:boundaries` pass.
- Dev server, keyless: status reports `hasKey:false`, tiles return 503 `no_key`, z15 returns 400, cross-site and foreign-Host requests return 403. The chip is `aria-disabled` and clicking it leaves Esri active.
- **Not run:** `npm run test:track` and the `qa-*` browser gates. No live Copernicus request has been made yet; this needs a test with real CDSE credentials.
