title: fix(cctv): start live HLS on plain-HTTP LAN pages
body:
## What

Live HLS cameras don't start when the app is opened over plain HTTP from another machine, which is the documented `HOST=0.0.0.0` LAN setup. `attachCctvVideo` builds the client lease with `crypto.randomUUID()`, and browsers only expose `randomUUID` in secure contexts, so on `http://<lan-ip>:4173` the call throws before playback starts. On `localhost` it works, which is probably why it hasn't come up.

## How

`createLeaseId()` uses `randomUUID` when it exists and otherwise builds a v4 UUID from `crypto.getRandomValues`, which is available in every context and passes the server's `/^[a-f0-9-]{36}$/i` lease check. `cryptoImpl` is injectable the same way `fetchImpl` is, so the test can drop `randomUUID`.

`CHANGELOG.md` and the live CCTV section of `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md` are updated.

## Verified

- Browser: app built with `npm run build` and served from a LAN box, opened in Chrome on another machine over `http://`. With v0.2.1 a DelDOT live camera doesn't start; with this change it plays.
- `node --test src/layers/cctv/videoPlayback.test.mjs`: 6 passed, 2 of them new (lease shape and uniqueness without `randomUUID`; HLS start with an insecure-context crypto).
- `npm run format:check`, `npm run check:boundaries`, `npm run build` and `npm test` on Node 24.21.0: all pass (`npm test`: 5636 passed, 1 skipped, 0 failed).
- No `qa-*.mjs` gate drives HLS playback (`qa-cctv-v2` covers geometry, calibration and stills), so the browser check above stands in for it. I didn't run `npm run test:track`; nothing here touches tracking.

title: fix: start new live aircraft at their delayed display position
body:
Live aircraft and military contacts are drawn behind real time (30 s for flights, 15 s for military). Until a contact has two fixes, its displayed position is its first fix projected back to that delayed time. But a newly seen contact's billboard was created at the raw fix, so the next fleet tick moved it back: a plane appeared at one spot and, a moment later, jumped back by roughly one render delay of travel before moving forward.

New billboards are now created at the same delayed position the per-frame update uses (`motion._deadReckon`), falling back to the raw fix when there is none.

- `src/layers/flights/snapshotRenderer.js`: create new aircraft at the delayed position.
- `src/layers/military/index.js`, `src/layers/military/snapshotRenderer.js`: give the military snapshot renderer the layer's motion and do the same.
- Regression tests in `src/data/flights.test.mjs` and `src/layers/military/ownership.test.mjs`: a contact with a 2 s old fix is created behind the fix by about one render delay of travel. Both fail without the fix.

`npm test` passes (5,623 tests); `format:check` and `check:boundaries` are clean.

title: fix: start a new grounded aircraft on the floor under its delayed position
body:
Follow-up to #951. A grounded (taxiing) contact is drawn at its delayed position lifted onto the floor under it (`_floorGroundedDisplayPosition`), but #951 created a new billboard at the delayed position without that lift. When the ground under the delayed position is higher than under the reported fix, the aircraft started low and rose on the next fleet tick (100.0 m, then 131.5 m in the regression below).

New billboards now apply the same floor the fleet pass does, with the same record and model-ownership inputs. The military fleet draws its delayed position without a floor lift, so its creation already matches and is unchanged.

- `src/layers/flights/snapshotRenderer.js`: floor the delayed position before creating the billboard.
- `src/data/flights.test.mjs`: a new taxiing contact whose fix is on a 100 m floor and whose delayed position is over 131.5 m is created at 131.5 m plus the ground lift. It fails without the fix (100.0 m).

`npm test` passes (5,624 tests); `format:check` and `check:boundaries` are clean.

title: data: refresh Norway datacenters from a Geofabrik OSM extract
body:
Refreshes the Norwegian part of the bundled datacenter layer from a current OpenStreetMap extract, and adds a script so the refresh can be reproduced or checked.

## What changes in the data

This round adds **one site**. The rest of the diff is tag updates that the app does not display.

- **Added:** Troll Housing (`w1551029155`, 62.863 N 7.108 E, underground, `operator=Troll Housing AS`). Its card shows "Troll Housing" with the operator line.
- **Tags updated, no visible change:** STACK OSL04 gained `landuse=industrial`; both Green Mountain Ytre Enebakk outlines gained a `source` tag (Kartverket orthophoto 2024); Maan Group gained `opening_hours=24/7`.
- **Unchanged:** no site moved or was removed. The largest vertex difference across the 17 existing Norwegian features is 1 cm, which is coordinate rounding.
- The layer goes from 4,351 to 4,352 features. Every line outside Norway is byte-for-byte identical.

Well-known Norwegian sites such as Green Mountain Rennesøy and Rjukan, Lefdal Mine, Bulk N01 and STACK Fetsund are still missing because they are not mapped in OSM yet. They will arrive through this script once they are mapped upstream.

## Source and provenance

- Geofabrik `norway-261005.osm.pbf` (OSM data 2026-10-05T20:21:35Z), MD5 `1d2cfdeb98980fce11b8891d0f9146c0`, checked against Geofabrik's published checksum.
- Filter: `osmium tags-filter nwr/telecom=data_center nwr/building=data_center`. Contact tags are dropped, as in the original snapshot.
- "Norway" means inside Geofabrik's `norway.poly`, which includes Svalbard.
- The dataset README records all of this and says plainly that the file now mixes two vintages: Norway as of this extract, and the original snapshot everywhere else.
- Same source and licence as before (ODbL 1.0, © OpenStreetMap contributors). `DATA_SOURCES.md` only has its count updated.

## Script

`scripts/build-datacenters-norway.py --cache <dir> [--extract <name>] [--verify]`, a maintainer-only script in the style of `build-military-names.py`. It requires `osmium-tool`.

It downloads a Geofabrik Norway extract and checks its MD5, filters it, and merges the result into `datacenters.geojsonl`:

- Norwegian features are added, updated or removed to match OSM.
- A feature is rewritten only when its tags change or a vertex moves more than 5 cm. Comparison ignores ring start point and winding.
- Existing `properties.id` values and line order are kept, and new features take the next free id.

Geofabrik keeps only its newest dated extract (`norway-261005` is already gone), so `--extract` defaults to the current one and prints the dated name it used. `--extract <dated name> --verify` rebuilds in memory and fails if the committed file differs, while that extract is still listed. It passed on this branch against `norway-261005`. Files are read and written as UTF-8 with LF line endings, so the script also runs on Windows.

## Validation

- `npm run build` ✅
- `npm test` ✅ 5,633 passed, 0 failed
- `node scripts/qa-infra-lod.mjs` ✅ 23/23
- `npm run test:track` ⚠️ 106 passed, 3 failed. All three are the same console error: Google 3D Tiles `root.json` answering `403 SERVICE_DISABLED`, because Map Tiles API is not enabled on my local key's Cloud project. This is unrelated to the change.
- `format:check`, `check:boundaries` and `layer-token:check --base-ref main` ✅
- Manually checked in the app (launched from Pinokio): Troll Housing renders and its card shows name and operator.

title: feat(installations): name Norway's unnamed military areas and add missing bases
body:
Audits Norway's military installations against the layer and fills the gaps that OpenStreetMap leaves, without touching the pinned Overture name pack.

## What the audit found

The bundled pack holds 155 named military records in Norway, and it mirrors OSM faithfully: of the 323 named military polygons in a current Geofabrik extract, the only ones missing are bunkers and small barracks the pack filters out by design. The gaps are upstream. Several active bases are mapped as **unnamed** military areas, so they render as "Military land", and others have **no military area** in OSM at all.

## What changes on the map

**Named mapped areas** (outline was already drawn, now labelled):

| Site | OSM | Wikidata | Wikidata position vs. area |
|---|---|---|---|
| Andøya flystasjon | `w162902961` | Q3271057 | 0.9 km |
| Evenes flystasjon | `w1315767988` | Q17770259 | inside |
| Gardermoen flystasjon | `w918686469` | Q3275900 | 0.6 km |
| Værnes garnison | `r10264027` | Q19398493 | inside |
| Luftkrigsskolen | `w25312357` | Q4573106 | inside |

**Point-only sites** (no military area in OSM, so they're placed at their Wikidata position):

Luftforsvarsbase Bodø (Q4380750), Banak flystasjon (Q6516685), Ramsund orlogsstasjon (Q4353910), Setermoen leir (Q19388269), Garnisonen i Sør-Varanger (Q134429601). Bodø and Banak take their bounds and area from the co-located aerodrome, so they rank sensibly in wide views.

**Deliberately left out:** Karljohansvern and Lahaugmoen, which are closed. A 466 ha area near Ramsund lies 1.8 km from the naval station and does not contain it. Two ~300 m² polygons at Høybuktmoen are single buildings, not the camp. Candidates I couldn't confirm against a source (Sortland, Sørreisa, Reitan, Mågerø) are not included.

## Code

- `militaryNames.js` merges `norway.json` after the Overture pack. The first name for a key wins, so the supplement can never rename something already named. Rows carry a Wikidata id and are attributed `OpenStreetMap + Wikidata`, or `Wikidata` alone for point-only rows.
- Close views: tile snapshots carry only mapped areas, so a point-only site used to disappear as soon as you zoomed in. `source.js` now adds standalone sites in the view box. The Overpass path gets the same names, but only on records that are still unnamed, so a name OSM has gained since wins.

## Script and provenance

`scripts/build-military-names-norway.py --cache <dir> [--verify]`, a maintainer-only script that requires `osmium-tool`. It works from the curated `scripts/military-names-norway.json` and a dated Geofabrik extract (the committed pack records `norway-261005`, MD5 `1d2cfdeb98980fce11b8891d0f9146c0`, checked). It refuses an object that has gained a name, lost its military tag, covers less than a hectare, or lies more than 4 km from its Wikidata position. `--verify` passes. The dataset README and `DATA_SOURCES.md` record ODbL geometry with CC0 Wikidata names.

## Validation

- `npm test` ✅ 5,627 passed, 0 failed (new tests: supplement integrity, OSM-name precedence, close-view standalone sites, Overpass enrichment)
- `npm run build` ✅, `format:check` ✅, `check:boundaries` ✅
- Headless Chrome QA at Bodø, Andøya, Gardermoen and Setermoen: labels and outlines render as expected and there are no page errors.

title: feat(airports): add an Airports layer for Norway with new Bodø Airport
body:
Adds an **Airports** layer, starting with Norway. It sits under Infrastructure and is built on the same bundled local-GeoJSON factory as Data Centers and Dams, so it needs no keys and no live requests.

## What you see

- **89 aerodromes.** These are all the aerodromes OSM maps in Norway with an `EN..` ICAO code: every Avinor airport, plus Torp, Rygge, Ørland, Stord, Svalbard, Jan Mayen and the club and general-aviation airfields. Each is drawn with its mapped outline.
- **136 runway surfaces**, built from each OSM runway centreline and its `width` tag (30 m when the tag is missing). They are drawn as surfaces with no stem or card of their own.
- **Cards** show the Norwegian name (`name:no`, so Bodø reads "Bodø lufthavn" rather than the truncated bilingual name), then `ICAO · IATA · operator` and the civil/military type. Scheduled airports with an IATA code outrank airfields when labels compete.
- **New Bodø Airport** is drawn in amber. OSM maps it as construction: the site (`w714425964`), the new runway (`w1019473337`) and the terminal (`w539307318`). Its card sits on the new runway, clear of today's airport, and reads *Under construction · opens 2029 · runway 2750 m*. Those facts come from Avinor's project brief: a 2,750 m runway about 900 m south-west of today's, a 24,000 m² terminal, and trial operation from the second half of 2029. OSM gives the new runway no width, so it is drawn 45 m wide like today's code-4 runway, and the dataset README says so.

## Code

- `src/data/airports.js` is the new module, registered in `constructCatalog` next to the infrastructure layers. Existing layers are unchanged.
- `localGeojsonCore` changes, all additive:
  - A feature with `properties.role` is drawn as a surface (or a light wash for `role: "site"`), with no stem, card or pick context, and it is not counted.
  - A feature may set a simplestyle `stroke`, which becomes its outline, stem and card accent.
  - There is airport card copy and a label priority for airports.
- `infrastructureData`: the dataset URL, `layerTitle` "Airport", and analyst records that skip drawn parts and add `icao`, `iata`, `kind` and `status` for airports.
- Registration:
  - layer panel (Infrastructure) and the cyber icon `✈`
  - share-link token `5`, the next free one. #1007 also claims `5`; whichever merges second takes `6`.
  - voice and analyst: `local-airports` is added to `set_layer_visibility`, `show_data_layers_menu`, `get_entity_context` and `analyst_query`, with "airports/airfields" as aliases. The pinned Realtime schema digests are re-derived for these additive values, and the legacy-arguments test filters them out the same way as `fire-perimeters`.

## Data and provenance

`scripts/build-airports-norway.py --cache <dir> [--verify]` is a maintainer-only script that requires `osmium-tool`. It reads Geofabrik's current Norway extract (the committed file is from `norway-261005`, MD5 `1d2cfdeb98980fce11b8891d0f9146c0`, checked) and keeps an allow-list of tags (`name`, `name:en`, `icao`, `iata`, `operator`, `aerodrome:type`, `ele`, `wikidata`). It fails if OSM stops mapping new Bodø as construction. `--verify` passes. The dataset is ODbL; see `src/data/local_data/airports/README.md` and `DATA_SOURCES.md`. The file is 311 KB with 229 features.

title: feat(cctv): add the Autostrada del Brennero (A22) motorway webcams
body:
Closes #155. This adds the first Italian cameras: the 13 public webcams that Autostrada del Brennero runs along the A22 from the Brenner Pass to Modena.

## Source

- **Catalog:** one keyless request to the [Open Data Hub](https://opendatahub.com/) tourism API (`tourism.api.opendatahub.com/v1/WebcamInfo?source=a22`). NOI Techpark in South Tyrol runs the API, and it republishes Autobrennero's own camera list with coordinates and kilometre markers. The whole motorway comes back in one request: 13 cameras, about 45 KB. This is the same set the operator's [webcam page](https://www.autobrennero.it/it/in-viaggio/webcam/) lists. That page gives only kilometre markers, with `Lat`/`Lng` set to null, so the Open Data Hub list is the one with usable positions.
- **Frames:** the operator's own stills at `www.autobrennero.it/WebCamImg/km<N>.jpg`, refreshed about once a minute (`Last-Modified` tracks the minute). The host answers server-side fetches without a challenge, so frames go through the existing still proxy unchanged. No new playback code was needed.
- **Terms:** the Open Data Hub marks the list as open data (`ClosedData: false`) and names Autobrennero as licence holder, but its licence field is empty. The pack therefore follows the existing "public … data (courtesy)" pattern used for Caltrans, TxDOT and Tallinn. The images are credited to the operator in the Data attribution popover and in `DATA_SOURCES.md`, fetched at request time, and never stored. If you'd rather hold this until Autobrennero publishes explicit terms, `CCTV_A22_ENABLED=0` turns the pack off.

## Behavior

- All 13 cameras sit under one **"A22 Brennero"** category, in road order from north to south. Labels read `A22 <place> (km <N>)`, for example `A22 Bolzano Nord (km 77)`.
- **Ground elevation:** the feed's coordinates are 2D, and the road climbs from about 20 m in the Po valley to about 1,370 m at the Brenner Pass. A single flat prior would bury the Alpine cameras, which is the known limitation documented for the Vegvesen and Caltrans packs. Instead, each camera's orthometric ground elevation comes from a 13-entry table keyed by motorway kilometre, sampled once from the Copernicus GLO-90 DEM through Open-Meteo's elevation API. A camera that isn't in the table falls back to a 200 m prior.
- **Headings:** the feed gives no bearing, so headings use the shared id-hash fallback at low confidence, as Calgary and Vegvesen do, and the calibration gizmo corrects them.
- **Security:** URLs are registered by the server and pinned. A frame is accepted only when the feed's `Webcamurl` equals `A22_IMAGE_ORIGIN + km<N>.jpg` for that camera's own kilometre. The kilometre must be 1–3 digits, and coordinates must fall inside the Brenner–Modena corridor. The catalog fetch refuses redirects and is size-capped at 2 MB.
- **Env:** `CCTV_A22_ENABLED=0` turns the pack off, and `CCTV_A22_URL` overrides the catalog URL. There's no max-sources knob because 13 cameras sit well under any cap.

## Testing

- `npm run format:check`, `npm run check:boundaries`, `npm run build` and `npm test` all pass: 5,629 passing, 0 failures, 1 skipped by the suite itself.
- The new `src/data/cctvA22.test.mjs` covers:
  - mapping a feed item to a source;
  - the per-kilometre elevation and its fallback;
  - dropping inactive cameras, cameras from another source, off-host frames, another kilometre's frame, a malformed kilometre and coordinates outside the corridor;
  - deduplication and north-to-south order;
  - an empty pack on 503, redirect or network error;
  - catalog wiring and the kill switch.
- `npm run test:track`: 109 passed, 0 failed.
- `node scripts/qa-cctv-v2.mjs`: 51 passed, 1 failed, 1 inconclusive. **The same result as unmodified `upstream/main` on the same machine.** The failing check (`>=1 real ground sample once tilesLoaded observed`) and the inconclusive one (headless GL geometry queue) both need 3D tiles that this keyless headless run doesn't have.
- Against the live sources, through the dev server: `/api/cctv/sources` serves all 13 A22 cameras, and `/api/cctv/frame/it-a22-km1` and `…/it-a22-km205` return `200 image/jpeg` with `X-CCTV-Source: upstream-image`, which means real operator frames rather than the Street View fallback.

Thanks to @kvnloo for the source-contract pass in #155, which confirmed that the operator's frames are direct first-party JPEGs.

title: docs: require screenshots, recording, category and data licence on new-layer PRs
body:
## What this changes

Adds a PR template and an "Adding a new layer" section to `CONTRIBUTING.md`, so PRs that add a layer come with what maintainers need to review it:

1. **Screenshots** of the layer on the globe, plus its info card or panel.
2. **A screen recording**, preferably 15 to 30 seconds (attach under GitHub's 10 MB limit for free accounts, or link a larger file).
3. **The proposed category**, one of the layer-panel groups in `PANEL_GROUPS` (`src/ui/layerPanel.js`): Movement, Cameras, Infrastructure, Events, Weather, Utilities. Or a proposed new group with a reason.
4. **The data source and licence**: provider and endpoint, licence link, in-app attribution, whether a key is needed, and runtime vs bundled. Plus checkboxes for the `DATA_SOURCES.md` row, the `dataCredits.js` credit and the share-link token.

The template also has a short general section (summary, build/test/track checks, feature gate, docs) for every PR. Contributors delete the new-layer section when it doesn't apply.

`CONTRIBUTING.md` gains step 6 in "Pull requests" and a link from the "Add or improve a data layer" bullet.

## How I verified it

title: fix(mcp): share one panel key across an install's stdio servers
body:
Fixes #927.

When a panel resource is read from one stdio process and its requests reach another, per-process panel keys reject the requests. Stdio processes from one install now share a persisted key; local two-process tests reproduce the old failure and confirm the fix. Actual Windows/Claude Desktop Cowork routing remains unverified.

### Implementation

- Store the shared key in `.gev-cache/mcp-panel-key`, independent of the client's working directory. Atomic hard-link publication selects one winner on first creation.
- Serialize malformed-file repair with a small exclusive lock and re-read the key before replacing it. Competing processes return the same winner; a busy repair waits at most two seconds before the logged per-process fallback.
- Preserve per-server keys for HTTP/in-process MCP servers, existing route restrictions, and the key's role as a panel guard rather than authentication.
- Document unwritable/busy-cache fallback, abandoned-lock handling, and process-local large-response continuations in `CURRENT-STATE.md`.

### Credit

Original implementation by @jibraaan. Thanks to @MarvinNL046 for reporting #927 and proposing the cross-process diagnosis, and @kvnloo for identifying the concurrent malformed-file repair race. Reporter and reviewer credit is also recorded in the changelog. Contributor commits and authorship are preserved; the maintainer repair is a separate commit.

### Validation

Validated the runtime candidate against main `208814a`; refreshed onto `6423d60` after #934 merged (only port documentation and contributor credit changed; the validated runtime tree is identical). Final candidate: `64a0200`. Validated in a credential-free, offline Bubblewrap environment on Node 24.14.0:

- 6,197 unit/allocation test passes, one existing skip; 28 focused MCP tests pass.
- The deterministic concurrent-repair regression fails on the original implementation and passes with the fix. Busy-lock fallback preserves the existing owner's lock and removes staging files.
- Setup doctor, formatting, package boundaries, whitespace, production build, and panel build pass.
- Two actual stdio processes reproduce the base refusal and serve the built panel successfully with the candidate. GPU-accelerated Chromium in the sandbox exercises the panel using a local MCP Apps host harness; the page comes from one process and tool calls go to another.
- Prior tracking validation produced 102 passes and seven identical offline-service failures on base and candidate. This is recorded as a limitation, not a clean tracking result. Rendering code is unchanged; no FPS equivalence claim is made.

Windows/Claude Desktop Cowork confirmation and live upstream loading remain untested. Large-response continuation calls must stay on the process holding their response. All four hosted CI jobs passed on `64a0200`: Node 24.14.0, Node 26.x, Windows onboarding, and the Street Level/portable-panel browser gate. #927 should close when this fix is merged, with the platform validation limitation retained.

title: RFC(perf): make optional refinement yield to camera motion
RFC(disaster): evaluate candidate routes against explicit access evidence
body:
## Problem

GEV's existing Directions path can produce a valid street route, but routing success is not evidence that a disaster-affected road or bridge is open.

The useful boundary is:

```text
Directions / OSRM candidate
  + explicit access observations
  -> supported | degraded | unsupported | unknown
  + reasons + evidence revision
```

Never `safe`.

This connects existing GEV work rather than creating a second routing system:

- #797 — selected hazards -> evidence views;
- #830 / #831 — observed traffic/source contracts and corridor proof;
- #882 — model-free disaster-access support kernel.

## Proposal

Keep the current Directions/OSRM owner authoritative for candidate geometry.

A separate pure adapter evaluates that candidate against **explicitly associated** access segments/evidence:

```js
evaluateRouteAccess({
  route,
  segmentRefs,
  accessPacket
})
```

The first slice must not infer closure/open state from geometry, imagery, witness text, nearby traffic, or routing success.

## Receipt

Return a deterministic receipt binding:

- route identity/fingerprint;
- access-packet revision;
- per-segment support result;
- overall `supported | degraded | unsupported | unknown`;
- explicit reason codes.

Changing either the route or the access revision makes the old receipt non-current.

## Guardrails

- OSRM success never implies road openness.
- Never label a candidate route `safe`.
- Missing access evidence is `unknown`, not open.
- Stale-open evidence is `unknown`, not current-open.
- Unmapped route segments remain explicit unknowns.
- No automatic reroute loop against public OSRM/FOSSGIS infrastructure.
- No consequential action is authorized by this evaluator.
- Source/time/provenance remain visible through the existing access owner.

## Acceptance

A deterministic fixture should prove:

1. candidate route + fresh explicit open observations -> `supported`;
2. inject one fresh blocked segment -> same route becomes `unsupported`;
3. stale-open -> `unknown`;
4. remove the access revision -> fail closed to `unknown`;
5. mutate access revision -> old receipt is non-current;
6. existing Directions behavior is unchanged when no disaster-access evaluation is requested.

## Downstream proof

This is already implemented as a downstream experiment in `kvnloo/gods-eye-view#155`, stacked on the Bhote Koshi historical replay fixture.

Exact-head CI is green on Windows, Node 24.14, and Node 26. The deterministic proof is:

```text
Bhote Koshi evidence
 -> explicit simulated access r1
 -> OSRM candidate
 -> supported receipt
 -> access r2 blocks one bridge
 -> old receipt non-current
 -> recompute
 -> unsupported
```

The OSRM route identity stays unchanged; only the versioned access evidence changes. The historical evidence adapter deliberately emits no access state from imagery/witness context unless explicit access observations are supplied.

## Promotion rule

The downstream implementation should stay downstream until #882's generic access-kernel contract settles. If this direction is accepted, re-cut the adapter on current `main` and reuse the accepted kernel rather than promoting the stacked branch wholesale.

title: perf(firms): stop re-downloading an unchanged fire snapshot every poll
body:
## Problem

Active Fires polls `/api/firms` every 10 minutes, but the proxy refreshes its cache only every 30. Every poll still transferred the whole worldwide snapshot — **~40 MB of JSON, ~200k detections** — and the layer re-parsed, re-adapted and re-sorted all of it on the main thread. Two of every three polls carried data the layer already had.

## Why not a plain content ETag

The proxy re-applies the trailing 24 h window at serve time, so the served rows change as detections age out. On a live 207k-row snapshot the served count changed on **3/3** consecutive 10-minute polls within one cache entry (−40, −784, −172). A validator over the served rows would almost never match.

## Change

- **Proxy** (`server/providers/firms.js`): `/api/firms` sends a weak `ETag` naming the cache entry and its stale flag (`W/"firms-<at>-<f|s>"`). A matching `If-None-Match` gets an empty `304`; the ~40 MB payload is never built. A stale fallback is a different validator than the fresh entry it replaces, so clients hear about it.
- **Source** (`src/layers/firms/source.js`): conditional requests are opt-in via `getSnapshot({ etag })`. A `304` returns `{ notModified: true }`, and its empty body is read so Chrome does not list every unchanged poll as `net::ERR_ABORTED`.
- **Layer** (`src/layers/firms/ingestion.js`): offers a validator only for the exact record set it arrived with (any other writer of `_fires` voids it). On `304` it keeps its records and drops detections that left the window via `expireFirmsRecords`; if none did, it does no work at all.
- **Tool callers** (`src/tools/services.js`) send no validator and always receive the full snapshot. Unchanged.

`expireFirmsRecords` restates the proxy's window bounds rather than importing `firmsCsv.js`, which would have pulled the CSV parser into three packages (`fire-layer`, `application-components`, `application-layer-construction`). A parity test pins equality with `filterTrailing24h`: same records, same indices, same FRP order, at +10/+20/+30 min. Widening the copied window to 25 h fails it.

## Measured

Chrome, through the real layer (`dataManager` → `local-firms` → `update()`), 206k detections, Apple M3:

| Poll | Time | Main-thread long tasks |
|---|---|---|
| Full refresh (before) | 258–293 ms | ~150 ms (two tasks) |
| Unchanged, nothing aged out | 4–20 ms | none |
| Unchanged, 252–1,159 rows aged out | 47–72 ms | one 70 ms task in 3 runs |

Transfer for an unchanged poll: 40.6 MB → 0 bytes. Polls where the proxy's entry actually changed cost the same as before.

## Verification

macOS, Node 26.3.0, rebased on `95fa816`.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `npm test` | 6,196 pass, 0 fail, 1 skipped (allocation benchmarks are Node 24-only) |
| `npm run build` | ok |
| `npm run test:track` | 109 passed, 0 failed |
| `npm run format:check`, `npm run check:boundaries` | ok |
| New tests | 13: 11 seen failing first, plus 2 guards that already held (a mismatched validator gets the full snapshot; a validator is only offered for its own record set). Guarded lines mutation-tested (validator scope, stale flag in the tag, 304 never sent, tag over filtered rows, no renumbering, exclusive bound, stale scene state carried over, FRP order lost, 304 restamping freshness) |
| `scripts/qa-firms.mjs` | see below |

**`qa-firms.mjs` — disclosing an unresolved result.** The `ACTION (synthetic)` check passed 4/4 on `main` and 5/8 on this branch, with all three failures in the first three runs and the last five passing. Each failure differed only in `selectedActions=0` (the card's pressed state not yet present 250 ms after the flight). That section intercepts `/api/firms` with a fixed 200 response and no validator, so this change's 304 path never runs there; I could not find a mechanism, but have not proven it unrelated either. A split this size is plausible by chance (Fisher exact p ≈ 0.5). Every other section passed on every run.

Also in this PR: the interaction test harness's stub viewer gains `scene.primitives` (`add`/`remove`/`raiseToTop`). Without it, every refresh in those tests threw inside the LOD rebuild and was recorded as "live feed unavailable", so the refresh tests were not exercising rendering.

## Not included

Response compression. gzip would cut a full response from 40.7 MB to 4.0 MB (level 6, 271 ms server CPU) or 5.2 MB (level 1, 93 ms), but on localhost the transfer is already cheap and nothing in the server compresses today, so it is a broader decision. Happy to follow up.

CHANGELOG.md and docs/CURRENT-STATE.md updated per CONTRIBUTING.

title: Street Level: Google Street View as the second imagery provider
body:
## Summary

Google Street View joins the Street Level layer as its second imagery provider, beside Mapillary (#768).

- **Viewer.** Google's own `StreetViewPanorama` (Maps JavaScript API) renders in the shared viewer host. You get dragging, zoom, the arrows to step along a street, and Google's logo and terms. The panel caption shows the address, the month the panorama was taken and a **STREET VIEW ↗** link to Google Maps. FOLLOW works as it does for Mapillary.
- **Opening a panorama.** Google offers no coverage layer for other maps, so nothing is drawn. With the **STREET VIEW** chip on, a click on the map itself opens the nearest Google-collected outdoor panorama within 50 m, and the camera stays put. The rules for what counts:
  - only at street zoom, below 3 km (higher up, the hint says to zoom in);
  - a Mapillary line under the pointer wins;
  - a click on another layer's object, or while a tool holds the pointer, does nothing.
- **OPEN STREET VIEW button.** In the PROVIDERS row, it opens the nearest panorama at the ground under the middle of the screen, also without moving the camera. Street View therefore doesn't need a pointer. The button is disabled, and says why, until the camera is at street zoom.
- **Google 3D only.** Google's Maps Platform terms (§3.2.3(e)) forbid showing Street View imagery with non-Google maps on the same screen. Off Google 3D, Street View doesn't appear at all:
  - no chip, legend swatch, globe credit, layer source text or button;
  - Google's script isn't loaded either; it loads on first use, never as a pre-warm;
  - lookups and opens skip Street View, and leaving Google 3D closes an open panorama;
  - the share link keeps the user's choice for when Google 3D comes back.
- **Off by default.** Every panorama load is billed to the Google Maps key. The share-link option is `g`, default off.
- **Key.** It uses the existing browser `GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY`, which needs the **Maps JavaScript API** enabled.
  - If Google refuses the key (`gm_authFailure`: the API is not enabled, a referrer it does not allow, or billing is off), the chip reads KEY REJECTED with the fix, and a pending open fails at once.
  - A lookup or open that Google never answers fails after 10 or 20 s, instead of loading forever.
- **CSP.** `script-src` adds `https://maps.googleapis.com`. The MCP globe panel adds Google's Street View tile, control-image and photo origins.

### Core changes, provider-neutral

- **New provider fields:** `groundClick`, `defaultOn` and `requiresMapStack`.
- **New pose fields:** `capturedAtPrecision` (`'month'`) and `title`.
- **Coverage line:** keeps every provider's hint.
- **Shared viewer host:**
  - opening one provider's photo releases another provider's pre-warmed viewer, including one that finishes loading later;
  - FIT/FILL hides for viewers without render modes, on every open.
- **Layer row:** names the key of the providers that are on.
- **Chips:** a chip without a usable key explains it instead of lighting, but it still darkens beside a lit chip, and the other chips keep switching. So a refused Street View key can't lock Mapillary out.
- **Ground picking:** `scenePick` gains `pickGroundPosition` and `isSurfacePick`. Directions now uses the shared helper instead of its own copy.

## Test plan

- [x] **Unit tests.** New coverage:
  - the provider: status, lookups, filters, timeouts, a refused key, outages, abort;
  - the viewer adapter: poses, arrows, races with close and unmount, timeouts, a substituted id, the date lookup cache;
  - the Maps loader: a single load, retry, auth handler installed once;
  - ground clicks: surface picks, the ellipsoid fallback, street zoom, the map stack;
  - the viewer host: releasing pre-warmed viewers, render modes;
  - the core with the real provider: default off, the Google 3D gate, provider-filtered lookups, no camera flight;
  - presentation, layer-state codec, CSP;
  - the app wiring: each provider's default matches its share-link default.
  - **Results:** 6,245 pass, 0 fail (one Windows-only skip).
- [x] **`npm run format:check`, `npm run check:boundaries`, `npm run build`:** pass.
- [x] **Strict fixture gate, CI mode (production build, no Google key):** 29 passed, plus 3 documented skips: two "no Google 3D" and one "no Google key". It passed twice in a row. Off Google 3D (CI's only map), nothing of Street View shows, even after a share link switches it on, and `g.1` stays in the link. The click step skips as `no Google key`, which is a documented skip.
- [x] **Panel gate:** 7/7, twice.
- [x] **Live gate (real Mapillary token and Google key):** 26 passed. The Street View click-and-button step skipped as "Google did not answer", because the key used for QA does not have the Maps JavaScript API enabled yet; that is the case this step reports instead of failing. Earlier, one live Mapillary step (step 13) failed the same way on this branch and on merged main, from live Mapillary "Failed to fetch data" errors, so it was not this change.
- [x] **Manual QA in the app:**
  - With the Maps JavaScript API answering: a click on 10th St, Sacramento opened its panorama with the caption and link, and the globe marker sat on the street.
  - With the key refused: KEY REJECTED shows on the chip and as the error line, and the open fails at once.

## Not in this PR

- **CI can't exercise the Street View viewer end to end.** It has neither a Google key nor Google 3D, and the terms rule out faking a panorama on another map. The viewer is covered by unit tests against fakes that follow Google's documented behaviour, plus the live gate.

title: fix(voice): name the missing key instead of blaming the microphone
body:
Part of #143, the "disabled controls name their key" half. This doesn't close the issue.

## Problem

Layers, map sources and street level already explain a missing key with `keySetupRequirement()`, as @kvnloo noted in #143. Voice doesn't. With no `OPENAI_API_KEY`, the mic looks fully available, and pressing it shows:

> VOICE SYSTEM ERROR
> Realtime connection: OPENAI_API_KEY is not set
> Check microphone permission and network access, then try again.

The last line sends a keyless user to check their microphone and network, when the real fix is adding a key.

## Fix

The key travels from the server to the UI, so the voice control never has to guess from the wording of the error:

- `server/providers/openai/realtime.js`: the 503 response now carries `keyId: 'openai'` alongside the existing `error` text.
- `src/voice/realtimeBackend.js`: a refused token sets `keyId` on the thrown `Error` when the server names one.
- `src/voice/realtimeDiagnostics.js`: the error record keeps `keyId` and passes it to `setStatus`.
- `src/voice/realtimeController.js`: when `keyId` is set, the error tray's hint shows `keySetupRequirement(keyId)`. For every other error, it falls back to the existing hint, now the exported `VOICE_ERROR_HINT` in `control.js`.

After the change:

> VOICE SYSTEM ERROR
> Realtime connection: OPENAI_API_KEY is not set
> Needs OPENAI_API_KEY — add it in Provider Settings

The guidance comes from the key registry, so it reads exactly like the layer and map tooltips. The `error` string is unchanged, so `qa-l9-matrix.mjs`'s `/OPENAI_API_KEY is not set/` checks still match.

## Testing

- **In the running app, with no key configured:** pressing the mic shows the tray above. I read it from the live page after clicking `#gev-voice-button`.
- New tests:
  - `realtimeOwners.test.mjs` drives the real `GevRealtimeController` and `createRealtimeBackend` against a 503 that names `openai`. It asserts that the tray shows the key guidance, and that a later non-key error restores the microphone and network hint. This test fails on `main`.
  - `realtimeBackend.test.mjs` checks that `keyId` is carried on the error when the server names one, and absent otherwise.
- I updated `hudSummaryResponse.test.mjs` for the new `keyId` field in the token response body.
- `npm run format:check`, `npm run check:boundaries`, `npm run build` and `npm test` all pass: 6,185 passing, 0 failures. `npm run test:track`: 109 passed, 0 failed.

## Not in this PR

- **Visual preset tooltips:** the other half of #143 already looks done. Every preset button in `src/ui/templates/command-dock.html` has a one-line `title`.
- **The mic before it's pressed:** it still looks available until you press it. Showing the key requirement up front would need the client to know key status before any request. That's a bigger change, and I'd rather check the approach with you first.

title: feat: allow optional local package boundary additions
body:

title: fix(recent-imagery): scroll the DETAILS card into view when it opens
body:
Opening DETAILS in the Recent Imagery panel is meant to bring its card into view when it opens below the fold. `revealCard()` (added with the layer in #716) has never done that. It ran in `renderDetails()`, which `render()` calls inside `preserveScroll()`, and `preserveScroll()` writes the saved `scrollTop` back in its `finally` block. The reveal and the restore happen in the same task, so a card that opens below the fold stays out of view. In headless Chrome with an 860 px window (panel body 80 px high, 274 px of overflow), clicking DETAILS leaves `scrollTop` at 0 and the bottom of the card 315 px below the body.

The weather panel has the same `revealCard()` and a test for it (`src/ui/weatherPanel.test.mjs`, a write spy on `scrollTop`). Its render is not wrapped in a `preserveScroll()`, so it works there. This PR does not touch it.

The reveal now runs from the card's `onOpen` handler, after `render()`, and only when the card has just opened. That keeps the rule of the old code (once per opening, never on a refresh) without the `detailsShownOpen` flag that enforced it.

- `src/ui/recentImagery.js`: call `revealCard()` after `render()` in `onOpen` when the card opened; remove `detailsShownOpen`.
- `src/ui/recentImagery.test.mjs`: opening DETAILS with the card below the fold of a scrolled body moves the body to show it (40 to 150), and closing it does not scroll. The test fails without the source change (`actual: 40, expected: 150`).
- `CHANGELOG.md` and `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md`: one entry and one sentence.

Validation, on top of `95fa8162` with `npm ci` on the lockfile (Node 26.8.2):

- `npm run format:check` and `npm run check:boundaries` are clean, and `npm run build` succeeds.
- `node --test src/ui/recentImagery.test.mjs src/layers/recentImagery/*.test.mjs src/ui/weatherPanel.test.mjs src/ui/sceneControls.test.mjs src/ui/layerPanel.test.mjs`: 120 pass.
- `npm test`: 6,185 tests: 6,183 pass, 1 skipped, 1 fails. The failure is `ranking 250k rows stays within a budget and yields to the page` (`src/data/analystEngine.test.mjs`, a time budget), which fails the same way on the unmodified `95fa8162`; the file does not touch Recent Imagery.
- Real browser (headless Chrome 147 against `npx vite`, Recent Imagery enabled from its toggle, DETAILS closed, panel body scrolled to the top, then a click on the DETAILS header): with the fix `scrollTop` goes from 0 to 308 at an 800 px window and from 0 to 272 at 860 px, and the DETAILS header is visible. Without it `scrollTop` stays 0 and the header stays out of view (the bottom of the card is 141 px and 315 px below the body). The new unit test uses the DOM stand-in of the existing tests; this browser check is a throwaway puppeteer script and is not part of this PR.
- Feature gate `scripts/qa-recent-imagery.mjs`: I ran it headless (software WebGL, a loaded machine, live NASA endpoints) twice on this branch and twice on the base. 22 and 23 of its 107 checks fail on the branch and 21 and 21 on the base. The same 19 failing checks (layout and rendering ones) are in all four runs. The rest change from run to run, including on the base, so this tells nothing for or against the change. The script sets the body scroll position itself after it opens DETAILS (`:1382-1397`), so it does not cover the reveal either way.

refactor(street-level): one provider, docked panels, memory-only proxy
body:
## Street Level, slimmed: a lean provider registry, docked panels, memory-only proxy

### What and why

#768 shipped Street Level at +22,489 lines. This PR keeps the feature and cuts the parts that were over-engineered for their value: coverage from orbit, terrain casting with a mesh sampler, floating resizable panels, a disk tile cache with sweeps, a hand-built modal EXPAND, prewarmed viewers, nearest-image lookups. Against `main` the diff is +4,911 / −16,791 (123 files); `src/layers/streetLevel` runtime code goes from 11,119 to 8,851 lines with all four providers in it.

The provider registry stays: `main` built on it after this branch started (#982–#985: injected `streetLevelProviders`, an empty composition, the `r` switch field), so it has a consumer now. Its contract is trimmed to what a provider actually implements.

Review follow-ups from @asturksever are in (see Fixes).

### Merged with `main`'s new providers (at `6390a33`)

`main` gained Google Street View, KartaView and Panoramax while this branch was open, built on shared modules that still carried what this PR removes. The merge ports them onto the slim core instead of bringing those back:

- `lineCoverage.js` is this branch's `coverage.js` made provider-neutral (draped lines near the ground, the selection drawn over them, key / rate-limit blocking); `sequenceCones.js` is `sequences.js` the same way. Mapillary, KartaView and Panoramax all use them, and Mapillary moves back to `providers/mapillary/` beside the others.
- Still gone: ground casting, mesh sampling, surface modes, FOLLOW, the legend, viewer prewarm, orbit overview points (Panoramax's density dots too: above 60 km the panel says to zoom in), stale-tile swaps, the water-filled point budget (a simple per-tile cap instead) and the sequence image cache.
- Kept from `main` because the new providers need them: one source lit at a time, `requiresMapStack` / `attachMapStackController` (Street View on Google 3D only), ground clicks and `openNearest` with an optional provider `nearestImage`, `openImage({frame})`, `reportError`, the view-cone marker (now an SVG glyph), `filters` / `coverageLabel` / `sinceBasis`, OPEN STREET VIEW, `keyAlternatives` and the translated UI (es/ru catalogs updated).
- The shared photo viewer treats EXPAND as the Fullscreen API / iPhone popover.
- User-visible beyond the list above: a KartaView filter change blanks its lines until the filtered tiles arrive (no stale lines kept meanwhile).

### What stays

- Coverage lines at street zoom (z11–14), draped on terrain and Google 3D tiles alike. Click a line for its image cones, a cone for the photo in the embedded MapillaryJS viewer, with author, date and a Mapillary link.
- The provider registry and contract (`registry.js`), a chip per provider, `streetLevelProviders` composition, the `r` custom-switch field, the ALL / 360° / FLAT and SINCE filters, the on-globe CC BY-SA credit, FIT / FILL.
- KEY REQUIRED (with the key hint) and KEY REJECTED.
- The server proxy: token added server-side, the `image` layer trimmed in transit (12 MB → ~80 KB), same-site gate, per-IP limit, size cap.
- Share links: format unchanged (layer token `0`, options `m`/`r`/`p`/`s`, panel token `t`), so links made since #768 keep working.
- The hermetic browser gate in CI (`street-level-browser` job), now 8 steps: coverage and credit, a rejected key, line → cone → photo, close, a keyless page, every request answered from fixtures, no errors, strict.

### What was removed

| Area | Gone | Why |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Rail panels | Floating, resizable CCTV and Street Level panels: drag-out, 8-way resize, snap-back, saved geometry, and the panel-drag code nothing called | Docked panels, as before #768 |
| Panel | FOLLOW, the legend, the hover cursor over lines, the modal EXPAND with `inert` and focus trapping | EXPAND is the browser's Fullscreen API; on iPhone (no element fullscreen) a top-layer popover. Esc shrinks the photo in both |
| Layer | Orbit overview points (z0–5), viewer prewarm, the nearest-image lookup, the sequence image cache; from the provider contract: `groundCaster`, `meshSampler`, surface modes, `nearestImage`, `prewarm`, `reportError`, the legend and surface fields of the UI snapshot | Mapillary is `mapillaryProvider.js` over flat `coverage.js` / `sequences.js` / `viewer.js`; the core drives providers as `main` does |
| Globe | Google 3D ground casting (`groundCast`, `meshSampler`, surface modes, cast/remesh swaps) | Lines drape and cones clamp; photo framing and the horizon cull stay |
| Proxy | Disk cache and sweeps, legacy retrim, server-side key holds, hand-followed redirects | Memory LRU of 120 tiles (≤ 4 MiB each), 24 h TTL; a 3xx is answered 502; a tile fetch every client has left is cancelled, or never started; at most six Mapillary fetches at once |
| Glyphs | Canvas-drawn billboard images | SVG data URLs with the same geometry; tests need no canvas |
| QA | `qa:panel-resize`, the panel-drag helpers, gate steps the unit tests cover (filters, pill, strip geometry, phone layout) | `qa-street-level.mjs` 1,828 → 588 lines |

### Fixes

From the review (P2s):
- After a 429 the rest of the view, and the fetches queued behind the first, still went to Mapillary. The proxy now answers 429 itself until the Retry-After is over, scoped to the token that was refused.
- A Retry-After sent as an HTTP date read as 60 s; it is now the seconds left, with the same 10-minute cap.
- A body that failed to trim (up to the 48 MiB cap) could fill the 120-entry cache; anything over 4 MiB is served but not kept.

Found while verifying:
- A key status that failed or never answered left the layer in KEY REQUIRED until reload: it is asked again on the next switch-on, and the check gives up after 10 s.
- Esc in full screen shrank the photo and collapsed the panel too; now only the photo.
- A photo that finished loading after the shell detached navigation threw instead of framing nothing.
- A new sequence load kept the previous sequence's error.
- A freed upstream slot could be taken by a newer request ahead of the waiting one; it now passes straight to the oldest waiter.
- The panel did not open on a user switch-on because its controls connected before the data manager existed.
- An empty view said nothing; it now says whether the filter emptied it.
- A click just beside a 2.5 px coverage line selected nothing (3 px pick window, no hover cue any more); clicks pick in a 9 px window.

### User-visible changes (product decisions)

- CCTV and Street Level panels no longer float or resize.
- No FOLLOW mode. Nothing is drawn from orbit: above 60 km the panel says to zoom in.
- On Google 3D, coverage lines can sit on roofs and tree tops.
- No legend, no pointer cursor over coverage lines.
- The first photo opens a little slower: the MapillaryJS viewer is no longer prewarmed.
- EXPAND is native full screen; Clean View, recording and the cockpit end it.

### Checks (at `6390a33`, `main` merged)

- `npm test`: 7,569 pass, 0 fail, 1 skipped. `doctor`, `format:check`, `check:boundaries`, `layer-token:check -- --base-ref origin/main` (31 published, 0 new), `changelog:check`, production build, `git diff --check`.
- Fixture browser gate as in CI (`vite preview`, dummy token, `--strict`): 10 / 10 — the 8 steps plus KartaView and Panoramax (chip → keyless coverage and credit → line → photo → close), every Mapillary / KartaView / Panoramax request answered from fixtures. One of four runs failed step 3 with a blank (white) globe at startup; the other three passed.
- Live run, headless Chrome (SwiftShader), real services: Mapillary over Austin (535 sequences → line → cones → photo), KartaView over Cluj-Napoca (755 streets → line → photo), Panoramax over Paris (609 sequences → line → photo with author and licence), Google Street View on Google 3D in San Francisco (nearest panorama with its address). No page errors.
- Not checked: Safari and iPhone on a device.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: fix(server): refuse cross-site requests on the terrain-heights route (stacked on #686)
feat: GEV COMMAND - a typed transport for the existing voice agent
body: ## Summary Adds **GEV COMMAND**, a typed transport for the agent voice already drives. It runs the same 30 app actions through the same action runner, over any OpenAI-compatible `/v1/chat/completions` endpoint — **OpenAI, OpenRouter, or a local Ollama**. This replaces #51, rebased onto current `main` and narrowed to the typed-agent core that @kvnloo identified as still unclaimed. Docker (#208), the Cesium ion map path and the HUD summary are left to their existing owners; nothing from those three rides along. Voice is untouched. (Open the panel using the "GEV COMMAND" button in the bottom left, and a movable command prompt UI opens that you can move around and resize) ## Why Voice is excellent and expensive. Audio tokens dominate the bill, an open mic bills for silence, and the Realtime API has no open-source equivalent speaking its WebRTC protocol with native speech-to-speech plus tool calling. Typing removes all three at once: the same agent, the same tools, roughly two orders of magnitude cheaper, and reachable by back ends that will never implement Realtime — including a model on the operator's own GPU. | | Per typed command | |---|---| | `gpt-5-nano` | ~$0.0002 | | `gpt-5-mini` | ~$0.0008 | | Ollama | free | against roughly $0.10–$0.30 per minute of open-mic voice. The console shows the estimate for the selected model before you type. ## What it does not change - **Voice is byte-identical.** `realtimeInstructions` now joins an exported directive array instead of a literal one; a test pins that the joined string is unchanged. - **The HUD summary is untouched.** Main's implementation stays exactly as it is, so `gpt-5-nano`, `max_completion_tokens` and `reasoning_effort: minimal` are not this PR's business. - **No new required configuration.** An install that sets none of the new variables offers OpenAI on the `OPENAI_API_KEY` voice already uses. - **`gevActions.js` is untouched.** The console takes `voiceCommands.runner`, the same runner `installViews` drives, so there is one action runner and one tool inventory. ## Addressing the review on #51 | Review item | How | |---|---| | Rebase onto current `main` | Branched from `main`; server code lives in `server/providers/agent/`, composed in `localProviderPlugins`. | | Shared request-admission safeguards | All three endpoints go through `sameSiteGated` and share a per-IP throttle built with `makeCostRateLimiter` (`GEV_RATELIMIT_AGENT_PER_MIN`, default 60, explicit `0` to disable). | | Server-side model-selection policy | `resolveRequestedModel` is total, like `resolveVoiceModel`: a malformed, over-long or non-allowlisted id degrades to the configured default instead of reaching the upstream. `GEV_AGENT_MODELS[_]` lets an operator pin what a visitor may spend credit on. The response echoes `X-GEV-Agent-Model` and `X-GEV-Agent-Model-Fallback`. | | HUD: preserve `gpt-5-nano` | Dropped from scope — main's HUD is retained unchanged. | | Narrow to the typed-agent core | Docker, `compose.yaml`, the ion route and `mapCredentials` are all gone. | | Build text instructions from voice's manual | `server/providers/agent/instructions.js` reads `realtimeDirectives()` and rewrites four channel lines. Each rewrite is matched by its opening words, and `adaptDirectives` reports an anchor that matched nothing or more than once, so rewording a voice directive fails a test rather than leaving "speak your confirmation" in a typed prompt. | | Derive the prefix estimate; warn, don't assert | `server/providers/agent/prefix.js` computes it from the real instruction string and the real tool schemas (currently ~12,655 tokens). Truncation and reasoning overflow are **warnings on a 200**, with their remedy, never refusals. | | Trim history client-side, keeping pairs | `fitHistoryToBytes` trims to 448 KB before each POST, below the server's 512 KB cap, and never opens a slice on a `tool` message. The console says how many messages it dropped. | | Don't cut tool results mid-JSON | `boundedResultJson` sheds the largest non-essential fields, largest first, until the result fits. `ok`, `say`, `error`, `count`, `scopeLabel` and `partial` are never shed, and the output always parses. | | Hide non-chat OpenAI models | `isOpenAiChatModel` drops speech, transcription, embedding, image, moderation and legacy completion families from the picker. | | HUD provider as an explicit setting | Moot: the HUD is out of scope. | ## Architecture ``` src/agent/ server/providers/agent/ ├── conversation.js ├── registry.js providers, model policy, gating ├── cost.js ├── instructions.js voice's manual, adapted ├── consoleBox.js ├── toolSchema.js reshape + schema validation ├── agentLoop.js ├── diagnostics.js silent-failure detection └── agentConsole.js ├── prefix.js derived prefix size ├── upstream.js provider HTTP, injectable fetch ├── rate-limit.js the per-IP cap └── routes.js the three handlers ``` Endpoints: `GET /api/agent/config`, `GET /api/agent/models`, `POST /api/agent/command`. Credentials stay server-side; the browser executes the tools because they drive its own viewer. The console is a `dialog[data-panel-surface]` per `docs/panel-surfaces.md`, so it takes the shared clean-UI, recording, Cockpit and scene concealment. It owns its own geometry and dismissal, with Escape and Tab from the existing `createSurfaceKeyboard` — which matters, because a provider with no usable model leaves the input disabled and a keydown listener on the dialog itself would then never see Escape. **The window.** Chip and console sit bottom-left; POWER UP keeps the right corner. The window drags by its header, resizes from every edge and remembers where it was left; a double press on the header forgets that. The default placement clears the left rail above it and the map attribution below it, because a credit line is a licence condition rather than a layout preference. It reuses `resizeBox` and the existing `.panel-resize-edge` / `.panel-resize-grip` handles rather than adding a second set. It is not a rail panel, so `PanelPositionControls` does not apply — that owns lifting a panel out of a rail and docking it back, and this has no rail to return to. The double press is detected from `pointerdown` rather than `dblclick`, because the drag's `preventDefault()` suppresses the native event; `PanelPositionControls` documents the same conclusion for the same reason. **Existing files touched.** Only five carry behaviour: `server/providers/openai/instructions.js` (exports the directive array; the joined string is unchanged), `server/providers/local.js` (registers the plugin), `src/app/tools.js` (mounts the console on the existing runner), `src/keySetupCore.mjs` (one registry entry, so the OpenRouter key is pasteable in Provider Settings like every other server-side credential) and `index.html` / `style.css` / `build/application-html.js` for the template registration. The rest are docs, `.env.example`, and the two tooling manifests. ## Two silent failures this preserves from #51 Both were found on real hardware, and both return **HTTP 200** with a plausible answer. 1. **Truncated tool prefix.** Ollama's stock runtime context is 4096 against a ~12,000-token prefix, which silently cuts the tool list; the model then writes a `` block as prose and picks the wrong tool. The capability gate cannot catch it — `/api/show` reports the model's *architectural* context, not the runtime window. Detected from the returned prompt token count, with the remedy named. 2. **Reasoning overflow.** A reasoning model spends its whole output budget thinking and returns empty content with `finish_reason: "length"`. Raising the ceiling does not help, so the message says to change model. Per the review, both are warnings rather than errors: the prefix size is a character heuristic compared against another provider's tokenizer. ## Testing | Gate | Result | |---|---| | `npm test` | **6431 passed**, 0 failed (+216 new) | | `npm run build` | clean | | `npm run test:track` | **109 passed**, 0 failed | | `npm run format:check` | clean | | `npm run check:boundaries` | clean | | `npm run doctor -- --json` | clean | | `npm run layer-token:check` | 29 published, 0 new | | `node scripts/qa-agent-console.mjs` | **24/24 PASSED** (live, OpenRouter) | New gate: `scripts/qa-agent-console.mjs` drives the real console in the real app. `--offline` proves the chrome and both listing endpoints without a configured provider; the full run carries one typed command through the relay and the client tool loop to a state change it reads back from the viewer. **Verified end to end** against OpenRouter on `deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash`: the gate's 24 checks include a real typed command travelling through the relay and the client tool loop to a state change read back from the viewer, plus the drag and resize gestures. Probed separately on the same model, all with zero corrections and zero warnings: | Typed | Tool calls produced | |---|---| | "turn on flights and zoom out to the whole planet" | `set_layer_visibility{flights}` **+** `zoom_to_globe{}` in one turn | | "what am I looking at?" | `get_entity_context{scope:"auto"}` | | "how many flights are over Texas right now?" | `analyst_query{layers:["flights"],scope:{kind:"region",name:"Texas"}}` | Ollama was not exercised on this machine (no daemon available); that path was verified on #51 with an RTX 3070 and `qwen3:4b`. ## Docs `docs/TEXT-AGENT.md`, with `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `.env.example` and a one-line README pointer updated in the same change set. Every environment variable the code reads is documented in `.env.example`; nothing below is required to run the feature.

title: Same-site gate refuses every browser request behind a TLS-terminating reverse proxy — opt-in trusted-proxy mode?
body:
**The situation.** We distribute God's Eye View as a [StartOS service package](https://github.com/Start9-Community/gods-eye-view-startos). StartOS terminates TLS at the OS and forwards to the container over plain HTTP through its HTTP-aware gated proxy. For `http` bindings that proxy *adds* `X-Forwarded-For` and `X-Forwarded-Proto: https` (after stripping any client-supplied `X-Forwarded-*`), and it refuses TLS connections for hostnames the operator has not enabled, so the container sees only the exact `Host` headers of addresses the user opted into.

**What breaks in v0.2.1.** Two things, both from the hardening in `src/localRequestGate.mjs` / `build/allowedHosts.js`:

1. `hasProxySignals` lists `x-forwarded-for` / `x-forwarded-proto` among the refused signals, so every same-origin browser request to `/api/realtime/token`, `/api/openai/hud-summary`, `/api/google/nearby-places`, `/api/google/text-search` and `/api/realtime/debug-log` gets `403 Proxied requests are not accepted` — the voice token, HUD summary and Google place search simply stop working.
2. `admitSameSiteRequest` computes the request's own authority from `req.socket.encrypted` + `Host`. TLS ended at the proxy, the container socket is `http:`, the browser sends `Origin: https://…`, and check (3) would refuse even if (1) passed.

(`GEV_ALLOWED_HOSTS` solves the new host allowlist cleanly — no complaint there, that's working as designed and we populate it from the interface's addresses. It's the same-site gate that has no equivalent knob.)

**What we're carrying.** Since the proxy is trusted infrastructure — it strips the client's copies of those headers before adding its own, and enforces its own hostname and auth policy before anything reaches the app — we apply a small patch: with `GEV_TRUSTED_PROXY=1`, `hasProxySignals` ignores exactly `x-forwarded-for`/`x-forwarded-proto`, and the authority check derives the scheme from `X-Forwarded-Proto`. Everything else (the rest of `PROXY_SIGNALS`, `Sec-Fetch-Site`, foreign/opaque `Origin`s) is unchanged, and unset the module is byte-for-byte upstream behavior. Cross-site and DNS-rebinding shapes still 403; we verified on a live box.

**Ask.** Would an equivalent opt-in be acceptable upstream, so LAN/proxy deployments can keep the cost-bearing endpoints working without carrying a fork patch? Happy to open a PR if the shape is welcome — the environment variable name, whether it should also honor `Forwarded`/`Via`, and whether the credential panel's loopback-only gate should get the same treatment are your call. If you'd rather not support proxied deployments at all, say so and we'll keep the patch on our side permanently and note it in our README.

title: feat(i18n): add English and Simplified Chinese localization
body: # feat(i18n): add English and Simplified Chinese localization ## What this does God's Eye View now ships two fully supported interface locales — **English** (the complete baseline and fallback) and **Simplified Chinese (`zh-CN`)** — switchable in-app, with no page reload and no loss of map, tracking, panel or form state. ## User-visible behavior - **First launch** follows the browser language (any `zh*` variant selects `zh-CN`); the loading screen is already in the detected locale before the app module evaluates (a CSP-safe external pre-paint script — the app CSP forbids inline scripts). - **Manual choice wins**: a new **Language** select at the bottom of the Display panel offers *English / 简体中文*; the choice persists under the namespaced `gods-eye-view.locale` key and beats the browser preference. Invalid values, blocked storage (privacy mode) and read failures all fall back gracefully. - **Switching is live**: open panels re-render through locale subscriptions; controls destroy their subscriptions on teardown. The Cesium viewer is never rebuilt, data is not refetched, share links keep their protocol, and a selected/tracked contact survives a switch (verified live with a tracked aircraft across zh→en→zh). - **English never regressed**: English pack values are byte-identical with the previously shipped strings; the default locale reproduces the old output exactly, which kept the entire existing test suite meaningful. ## Coverage All own-UI surfaces are localized: static templates (welcome, dock, display, context, layer panels, cockpit, provider settings), dynamic panels and cards (layers, CCTV, radio/SDR, weather rail, cockpit instruments/briefing, launches, satellites, awareness, earthquakes, weather/wind/cyclones/fires/ perimeters, flights/military/vessels/local-ADS-B, traffic/transit/bikeshare/ directions, ALPR, installations, radio layer, recent imagery, street level, draw/annotations, scene director, Bhote Koshi event, analyst answers, voice UI, HUD labels, provider settings). ~2,100 keys across 35 namespaces. The full ledger — including **deliberate exclusions and reasons** — is in `docs/I18N-COVERAGE.md`. Highlights: - Kept as matching keys / protocol: layer registration `name:`/`source:` fields (display resolves them through a keyed map), portable boundary modules (`layers/*/source|records|ingestion`, `sources/*`), server error JSON, voice tool schemas and system prompts. - Kept verbatim by design: brands, entity names, coordinates/MGRS, units (`kt`, `ft`, `dBZ`, UTC…), third-party legal/attribution lines, and the HUD's fictional `TOP SECRET // SI-TK // NOFORN` banner. - Honesty semantics are invariant: 实时/预报/模拟/估算/数据已过期/需要密钥 never translate into stronger capability claims. ## Architecture notes - `src/i18n/core.js` is a portable engine (dot-path keys, `{param}` interpolation, en fallback, `Intl.PluralRules` plurals, cached `Intl.NumberFormat/DateTimeFormat`); it never touches `window`/`document`/`localStorage`, so any module — including portable package graphs — can import it. Detection/persistence live in `entry-only` `src/i18n/browser.js`; DOM rebinding in `src/ui/staticI18n.js`. - Static templates keep their English text as the source of truth and carry `data-i18n` / `data-i18n-attr` attributes; a binder applies the active locale at boot and reapplies on switches. Elements that feature code repaints are deliberately NOT tagged — their owners translate at render time and re-render on locale change, so the binder can never clobber live state. - En/zh key + placeholder parity is enforced by a test (`src/i18n/locales/parity.test.mjs`), and a drift test keeps the pre-paint script's strings aligned with the packs. - New package-ownership registrations: the pure i18n module graph is listed in the boundary groups that now import it (mechanical addition to `scripts/package-boundaries.json`; no new dependencies — **zero new runtime or dev dependencies**). - `npm run test:track` now pins the English locale before loading the app: its visible-text assertions (e.g. the ` · STALE` cue) are English contracts, and a zh-locale machine would otherwise boot the app in Chinese. ## Docs - `README.zh-CN.md` (new): Chinese intro, install, keys, language switching, FAQ, data-capability limits. English README gains a language entry (additive only). - `docs/I18N.md`: architecture, key rules, terminology baseline, security rules, add-a-locale steps. - `docs/I18N-COVERAGE.md`: per-module coverage ledger, exclusions, known gaps. - `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md` + `CHANGELOG.md` updated per the contribution guide. ## Verification - `npm test` — 6,236 tests; the only failure (`codexOauthRealtime` executable resolution) reproduces on base `6be2559` on Windows and is untouched by this PR. - `npm run test:track` — **109/109** (dev server + headless Chrome). - `npm run format:check`, `npm run check:boundaries`, `npm run build` — green. - New i18n suites: engine behavior (13 tests), en/zh parity (3), pre-paint drift (5). - Live browser matrix (dev + production `build`/`preview`, Chrome): zh/en first paint, detection vs saved choice, persistence across reload, no-reload switching with tracked target and camera preserved, XSS-inert interpolation (`` probe renders as text), share protocol intact, 1440×900 / 1024×768 / 800×600 without clipped chrome. ## Not covered / known limits - Live third-party voice/model replies follow the model's language, not the UI locale (documented in both READMEs). - Layer registration names inside the HUD summary provenance and some producer-composed status strings remain English (matching keys / pass-through protocol) — ledgered in the coverage doc. - No real-credential integrations were exercised for Mapillary or paid voice sessions; those paths are unit-covered only. --- ## 中文摘要 God's Eye View 现在支持**简体中文**与**英文**两种界面：首次启动按浏览器语言自动选择，显示面板可手动切换（无需刷新，地图、跟踪、面板状态全部保留），手动选择会持久化。英文仍是完整基准与回退语言，英文文案逐字未动。自有界面已全量汉化（约 2,100 条文案、35 个命名空间）；协议字段、实体名称、品牌与法律署名按规范保留原文，诚实语义（实时/预报/模拟/已过期/需要密钥）不因翻译而增强。详见 `docs/I18N.md` 与 `docs/I18N-COVERAGE.md`，中文使用说明见 `README.zh-CN.md`。 --- ## Acceptance-review fixes (2026-10-10) An independent acceptance pass reported one P1 and six P2 findings; all are fixed on this branch: - **P1**: a privacy mode whose `localStorage` getter throws could block startup — storage is now resolved inside the guards, with unit tests for throwing getters/getters/setters and a real-browser verification. - Panel collapse/dock toggles compose Expand/Collapse through pack keys and re-sync on locale switches; traffic/CCTV sync chips carry localized defaults for the zh first paint. - `detectBrowserLocale` now merges `navigator.languages` with the legacy `navigator.language` (an unsupported preference list no longer hides a supported `navigator.language`). - The document title resolves through the pack at boot and on switches. - `qa-map-source-tray` / `qa-street-level` pin the English locale before load (their text assertions are English contracts); `qa:street-level:fixtures` passes 29/29 here. `qa-transit` no longer hardcodes the macOS Chrome path (12/12 heading assertions pass on Windows; its Boston section waits on a live GTFS-RT feed and times out on this network — documented in the coverage ledger). - `docs/I18N-COVERAGE.md` refreshed with real test counts (6,246; 6,235 pass; the single failure reproduces on base) and per-gate status. --- ## Branch rebuilt to i18n-only (2026-10-10) The acceptance review caught that a commit made while a parallel session shared this working tree had swept its in-progress OpenAI-compatible provider changes into this PR (19 files, 14 failing tests). The branch was rebuilt: the PR now contains ONLY the localization work — the CCTV fix was re-landed as the i18n-only commit `aec8a9e`, the archived review snapshots are out of the PR, and the ledger records the real i18n-only head numbers (6,251 tests / 6,240 pass / 1 baseline failure). The OpenAI-compatible work lives on its own branch with 4 independent commits for a separate PR.

title: docs(readme): add GitHub Codespaces setup path
body:
Adds a Path 4 to Quick Start for running the dev server in GitHub Codespaces.

Codespaces removes the local toolchain — no Node install, no `npm ci` on your machine, no Docker — but it does not move the rendering: the globe still runs in your own browser and needs the same graphics as any other path. GitHub Free includes 120 core-hours a month with no card on file (~60 hours on the default 2-core machine); Org and Enterprise plans include no free quota.

Two things the steps handle that are easy to miss:

- `GEV_ALLOWED_HOSTS` must name the forwarded host, or `build/allowedHosts.js` returns `403 Blocked request`. Leading-dot wildcards are discarded by design, so only the exact name works.
- `nvm install 24` first — `engines` is `>=24.14.0 <25 || >=26 <27`, and the default Codespaces image ships Node 20/22.

README-only, one file.
