title: Fix startup with optional Street Level providers
body:
## What changed

Application catalog startup threw `Invalid catalog source: mapillary` when a consumer omitted the optional imagery source. Street Level now registers Mapillary only when its source is supplied. Callers can replace it through `streetLevelProviders`, including an empty list; the layer remains registered so controls and share-link identities stay stable.

The existing provider registry still validates supplied definitions. Empty compositions show a no-provider message and use the existing lifecycle without acquiring imagery. There is no fallback network source or new provider implementation.

## Verification

- Focused catalog, provider registry, replacement/removal and lifecycle tests passed.
- Package-boundary and formatting checks passed.
- Full unit suite passed: 6,218 passed, one pre-existing skip; all 14 allocation checks passed. Production build passed.
- All 52 focused presentation/control tests passed after the empty-provider UI follow-up.
- Existing Windows Chrome: source-less catalog constructs all 30 layers; the empty Street Level layer initializes, enables, disables and destroys successfully; the real panel renders the no-provider message, zero provider chips and disabled filter controls.
- Tracking harness passed clean startup, synthetic feed ingestion and 3D-toggle checks, then stopped at the share-selection assertion because a previous run left `__gevWithhold=aaa001` in session storage. Clearing that test-owned flag restored all three aircraft, accepted tracking and the correct share token in the same tab. The complete tracking harness has not yet passed.
- GitHub CI, including the configured Street Level fixture browser gate, is pending.

The default standalone Mapillary registration is unchanged.


The expansion gate now asserts its bounded wait instead of ignoring a false timeout result. Optional `settle` callers retain their existing behavior. Provider precedence is documented: an explicit list bypasses the unused Mapillary source and its validation. Seven focused composition/registry tests pass. The new CI run is pending; this change makes failure reporting precise and does not claim to cure a renderer timing failure. The full tracking harness remains outstanding.


Local browser acceptance on the integrated stack passed: default Mapillary panel expanded/collapsed three times; an empty provider composition started with no provider chips, disabled filters and no Mapillary requests; two replacement providers appeared and toggled independently without fallback acquisition.

title: Make catalog feeds optional and configurable at startup
body:
Application startup previously required every catalog feed, even when a composition deliberately omitted one. Centralize the 19 acquisition contracts and their consuming layers, accept omitted/null feeds as unavailable, and keep malformed supplied implementations as configuration errors.

Standalone application/catalog constructors accept source overrides: unspecified entries retain defaults, supplied objects replace them, and null removes them. Availability is an explicit catalog lookup supplied to the existing lifecycle; layer objects are not patched. The lifecycle refuses unavailable-source enables before initialization, and the layer panel reports a reason using the layer's display name. Street Level exposes the same availability contract when its provider list is empty.

Layer identities, metadata and share tokens remain stable. Missing sources never return fabricated empty data or acquire a fallback. Source contracts remain family-specific; configuration applies at construction time, without live replacement of initialized layers.

Stacked on #982.

Validation:

- Full suite: 6,227 passed, one skipped; both allocation gates passed (1 + 13 tests).
- Production build, formatting and package boundaries passed.
- Removal matrix covers each feed individually and all 19 feeds omitted. Tests cover malformed sources, override typos, source identity, frozen layer objects, display names, unavailable UI and lifecycle refusal.
- The application assembly test verifies the catalog lookup is supplied to the lifecycle.
- Missing-military-source regression verifies no fallback acquisition, no active military duplicate suppression, and retention of explicitly supplied classification identities.
- Existing browser session on the descendant stack: missing Fire Perimeters and Military Flights show display-name reasons and refuse initialization; empty Street Level uses the same lifecycle. Layer objects have no injected availability method.
- Full tracking and complete local browser acceptance harnesses remain outstanding.


Local browser acceptance on the integrated stack passed: startup with all 21 acquisition sources omitted retained all 30 layer identities; all 24 affected layer consumers (including Street Level) refused activation before initialization. Rendered controls showed UNAVAILABLE and display-name reasons. Clicking the disabled Flights control did not activate it. Individual omission checks passed for every source contract, with no fallback feed requests.

title: Separate Directions and Recent Imagery acquisition sources
body:
Directions and Recent Imagery previously selected acquisition inside their application constructors, so replacing or removing catalog feeds did not configure those layers. Both now participate in the existing catalog source contracts. Standalone chooses the default adapters, while the application receives explicit sources.

Directions receives `getRoute`; its adapter owns HTTP acquisition and cancellation while the layer retains route normalization and presentation. Recent Imagery receives catalog search, thumbnail responses, tile templates and attribution, retaining the existing HLS/VIIRS product schema and rendering/resource owners. Both source factories have independent package exports. Missing sources preserve layer identities and share tokens and refuse activation before initialization.

Stacked on #983, which is stacked on #982. This is construction-time configuration; live provider replacement is not implemented.

Validation:

- `npm test`: 6,231 passed, one skipped; both allocation gates passed (1 + 13 tests).
- `npm run build`, `npm run format:check`, `npm run check:boundaries`, and `git diff --check` passed.
- 120 focused tests passed, covering all 21 catalog acquisition contracts, route cancellation/failures, imagery adapters and resource cleanup.
- Existing browser session: a catalog with omitted sources retained all 30 layers and refused Directions/Recent Imagery before initialization. A supplied route adapter completed successfully. A supplied imagery adapter served catalog, thumbnail and tile requests, displayed its attribution and released its imagery layer on destruction.
- Full `test:track` and the live `qa-recent-imagery.mjs` acceptance harness have not passed for this head. The browser checks above are targeted integration evidence, not substitutes for those complete gates. Keeping this PR draft pending that validation.


Local browser acceptance passed for default and replacement sources. The default routing service returned a 1.9 km route with four steps; NASA returned 45 imagery candidates, thumbnails and tiles. Image/basemap and two-date comparison modes rendered at different camera angles and zoom levels. A replacement adapter supplied imagery credit, catalog, thumbnail and tiles without default-provider requests. Disabling aborted both pending route and imagery requests and released imagery resources/leases. Injected source failures appeared without fallback acquisition.

title: Preserve custom Street Level provider switches in shared state
body:
Custom Street Level providers could be injected, but their on/off switches were discarded by share-link and stored-state serialization. Add a bounded `r` option containing switches sorted by stable provider ID, while preserving Mapillary's published `m` token and its historical default.

`example-1*panoramax-0` restores Example on and Panoramax off even when the recipient registers them in reverse order. The separators survive URLSearchParams without percent escaping. Unknown providers are ignored by the receiving layer; absent custom switches leave current defaults unchanged. Malformed or duplicate entries invalidate the complete custom-switch field. Provider registration checks the 256-character bound before constructing instances and explains that shorter IDs or fewer providers are needed when it is exceeded.

The layer-state codec and Street Level use the layer-neutral boolean-switch codec in `src/data/idSwitches.js`. Generic share serialization no longer imports a Street Level module. The existing option table owns its schema. Its packed-switch updater persists only IDs named by an explicit provider toggle, preserving unrelated durable values without adopting passive live changes. Unknown IDs are dropped when editing a receiving composition so they cannot exhaust its share bound; this does not introduce runtime codec registration. Isolated token-ledger fixtures copy the new dependency without changing their assertions.

Stacked on #984 → #983 → #982.

Validation:

- Full suite: 6,240 passed, one skipped; both allocation gates passed (1 + 13 tests).
- 234 focused tests passed, covering sharing, stored state, Mapillary compatibility, reordered/unknown providers, malformed and oversized input, hyphenated IDs, and source availability.
- Production build, formatting and package boundaries passed.
- Existing browser session: the compact switch codec round-trips without percent escaping; catalog availability refuses missing sources before initialization and does not patch layer objects.
- Full tracking and complete local browser acceptance harnesses remain outstanding. This PR remains draft pending those gates and CI.


Local browser acceptance on the integrated stack passed after fixing a coordinator integration gap: an actual provider-chip click now writes the compact custom-switch field to both the URL and local storage. A real reload with reversed registration order restores the same on/off state; a separate reload without a hash restores stored state. A Mapillary-only receiver ignores custom IDs, and a legacy Mapillary-off link preserves its meaning. Coordinator regression tests cover explicit versus passive updates and bounded restoration across different compositions.

Tracking smoke checks in the same browser also passed: 30 display/detection samples matched exactly, the tracked 3D model was ready and visible, switching aircraft stayed in the follow-height band, civil/military handoffs cleared the previous owner, and disabling released the camera. These are targeted checks; the complete standalone tracking harness remains outstanding.

title: Handle healthy empty vessel coverage without an outage
body:
A vessel source can return a successful, complete empty viewport while the feed is healthy. The layer previously treated every zero-row response as failed acquisition, retained obsolete contacts, and showed an unavailable warning.

Accept empty coverage only when the source explicitly reports current freshness, a complete snapshot, zero raw rows, a healthy transport and a positive last-message timestamp. Clear obsolete contacts and settle startup without manufacturing observation times. Stale, incomplete, malformed and unconfirmed empty responses retain their existing recovery behavior.

Validation: unit coverage exercises authoritative emptiness and the stale/incomplete/rejected-data cases; production build and package boundaries pass. Full local suite: 6,242 passed, 1 skipped, plus both allocation gates (1 and 13 tests). CI is running.

title: test(codex): match the installed-executable stub on Windows
body:
## What

`npm test` fails on Windows in `src/codexOauthRealtime.test.mjs`:

```
✖ Codex login resolves an installed executable before PATH and starts browser auth detached
  actual: 'codex'
  expected: '\home\fixture\.local\bin\codex'
```

## Why

`resolveCodexExecutable` (`server/providers/openai/codex-auth.js`) builds its candidates with `path.join`, so on Windows the `~/.local/bin/codex` candidate has backslashes. The test's `access` stub matched with `candidate.endsWith('/.local/bin/codex')`, which never hits on Windows, so the resolver fell through to `PATH` and returned `'codex'`.

The resolver is correct; only the test stub was platform-specific.

## Change

Test-only. The stub now compares against the same `path.join(...)` value the assertion already expected. No runtime behavior changes, so `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md` and `CHANGELOG.md` are untouched.

CI doesn't catch this: the unit suite runs on `ubuntu-latest`, and the `Windows onboarding` job runs a fixed list of test files that doesn't include this one.

## Verification

Windows 11, Node 24.16.0, branched from `main` at 591f299:

- `node --test src/codexOauthRealtime.test.mjs`: 8 passed, 0 failed (was 7/1 before the change)
- `npm test`: all files pass
- `npm run test:track` (dev server up): 109 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped
- `npm run build`, `npm run format:check`, `npm run check:boundaries`: pass

No feature gate applies; no runtime code changed.

body:
## Why

Rain radar is a quality-controlled precipitation mosaic, so it hides the biological echo that shows nocturnal migration. This layer drapes lowest-tilt NEXRAD reflectivity and draws a direction only where a velocity fit produced one.

## What changed

- A motion frame where only a tracked radar has a direction, and only beside its fit.
- Bird migration on the weather history slider, with a light-echo wash and one streak per tracked radar.

## Scope

Covers the continental US and the scans on the shared weather timeline. Leaves out a national velocity mosaic, any split between birds and insects, and animated streaks. A noisy fit stays unresolved.

## Tradeoffs

Scrubbing this layer also moves rain, satellite, and lightning. One timeline lets you compare rain at the same time. A separate scrubber on the bird row was the alternative, and it lost.

## Blast Radius

The layer stays off until someone turns it on. The first scan reads NWS velocity and correlation products through the local server, and that first read takes about a minute. Share links gain one new token.

## Verification

- 148 unit tests passed on this branch, including a due-east velocity sinusoid and a rejection of a tracked radar with no fit.
- In the running app, the layer reported 47 tracked radars and 9 rain discs, and the continental view showed the wash and the streaks.


Made with [Cursor](https://cursor.com)

- Report omitted invalid features as partial data and retain stale/error

boundary features, 4,976 trail segments and 83 trailheads. These are feature

and can include regional features; it does not report current access or closure.

The City catalog has no named dataset license for these three collections.
Reuse is presented under its linked portal terms and dataset notices. The

title: feat(openai): OPENAI_BASE_URL — run the existing OpenAI path through an OpenAI-compatible gateway
body:
I run GEV self-hosted, and all our OpenAI traffic goes through a LiteLLM gateway that holds the real key and enforces per-key budgets. GEV hard-codes api.openai.com in three places (Realtime client_secrets, the browser's Realtime calls endpoint, and the HUD summary's /v1/responses), so it can't use one.

This adds a single optional env var, `OPENAI_BASE_URL` (the OpenAI SDK's own name for it). It is not a new provider: same models, same Realtime protocol, same request bodies, only the host changes. Unset, nothing changes.

When it's set:

- `/api/realtime/token` mints at `${OPENAI_BASE_URL}/realtime/client_secrets`, and the HUD summary posts to `${OPENAI_BASE_URL}/responses`.
- A secret minted by a gateway is only valid at that gateway, and the gateway usually isn't reachable from browsers. So the token response carries `X-GEV-Realtime-Calls: /api/realtime/calls`, and the browser sends its SDP offer to that same-origin relay, which forwards it with the ephemeral bearer to `${OPENAI_BASE_URL}/realtime/calls`. The browser only honours a same-origin `/api/` path from that header. Media still flows directly between the browser and the provider; only signalling is relayed.
- The relay route is only installed while the variable is set. It sits behind the same `sameSiteGated` admission as the token endpoint, accepts only `application/sdp` up to 64 KiB with a bearer, adds no credential of its own, and never relays the gateway's error body.
- ChatGPT OAuth voice ignores the variable and always stays on api.openai.com, so a ChatGPT token is never sent anywhere else.
- A value that isn't a plain http(s) URL (credentials, query, fragment, garbage) falls back to the default.

This overlaps with #976 only in spirit: that adds a typed transport and leaves voice untouched, while this keeps voice as it is and only lets it go through an operator's gateway. They compose; nothing here touches the agent or the action runner.

Docs: `.env.example`, `SECURITY.md` (the relay), `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md` (voice token flow), `CHANGELOG.md`. The new module is registered in the `openai-provider` package boundary.

Verification, Node 26.10, on 591f299:

- `npm test`: 6253 pass, 0 fail, 1 skipped. New `src/openAiBaseUrl.test.mjs` (11 tests) covers URL resolution, both minting targets, OAuth staying on OpenAI, the relay's forward and refusal paths, route installation, the HUD target, and the browser rejecting a non-same-origin relay header. Each of the HUD, OAuth and header assertions was checked by mutating the code and watching it fail.
- `npm run build`, `npm run format:check`, `npm run check:boundaries`: green.
- `npm run test:track` against the dev server: 109 passed, 0 failed.
- Manually against `npm run dev` with `OPENAI_BASE_URL` pointing at an unreachable host: the relay returns 502 with the fixed error, wrong content type 415, a cross-origin `Origin` 403, a forwarded request 403, and the token response carries the relay header.
- I have not run `qa-voice-auth` end to end against a live gateway yet; I'll add that result here once I have.

title: feat: Ancient Sites layer – 4,900 curated archaeological sites (CC BY 4.0)
body:
### Problem

God's Eye View shows what is happening on the planet right now, but nothing about what was there before. Flying over the Nile valley, the Andes or Orkney, you get no hint of the archaeology underneath. Your README calls time travel an open, hard problem.

### Proposal

A toggleable, keyless **Ancient Sites** layer: **4,900 hand-curated archaeological sites** worldwide, from Neolithic stone circles to Roman forts, each with type, date and country.

- Static and bundled like Dams/Datacenters (`src/data/local_data/ancient_sites/`, GeoJSON Lines, 1.7 MB raw / ~370 KB gzipped). No proxy, no polling, no key.
- Per site: name, type, start year (BC/AD), era, country, Wikidata QID.
- Card per site with name, type, date and country, readable without a click, plus a link to the site's source page (https only, host allowlist, `noopener,noreferrer`, the Fire Perimeters pattern).
- If it fits: voice/analyst queries through the layer manifest ("show Bronze Age sites in Greece").
- Possible follow-up, as a separate PR: every site has a start year, so an era filter would be a small, concrete first step toward a time dimension.

This is the dataset on our own globe:

![Ancient Sites dataset](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/ancientnerds/e8229e43648f605eb322607b033360e0/raw/ancient-sites-dataset.png)

Before we open the PR, two questions so it fits your architecture:

1. **Bundled snapshot** (proposed) or fetched at runtime?
2. **Its own layer family** (`src/layers/ancientSites/`) or an extension of the local GeoJSON infrastructure path (`createLocalGeoJsonLayer`)?

### Data source, license, and attribution

- **Source:** the curated site database of [Ancient Nerds](https://ancientnerds.com). We built it and maintain it.
- **License:** [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/), attribution "Ancient Nerds (ancientnerds.com)". It would be recorded in `DATA_SOURCES.md`, the `LICENSE` data carve-out, `DATA_CREDITS` and a snapshot README.
- **Facts only:** no descriptions or images, so no Wikipedia/Commons content and no share-alike terms.
- **Places only:** no people, no personal data.
- **Keyless:** yes, it's a bundled file.
- **Maintenance:** we keep the snapshot current and fix data errors reported against it.

### Will you build it?

Yes, I plan to open a PR.

title: feat: drone airspace restrictions layer (no-fly zones)
body:
### Problem

The globe shows aircraft and other airspace activity, but not where drone flight is restricted or needs authorization (airports, military sites, government facilities, temporary restrictions). Anyone exploring an area, or planning a drone flight, has to switch to separate national tools. Useful for drone hobbyists, journalists and anyone curious about what is restricted near a place.

### Proposal

Add a "Drone restrictions" map layer, first version small:
- One provider under server/providers/ using a single source with a redistributable license
- Polygons colored by severity (prohibited / restricted / advisory)
- On selection: name, type, altitude limits, validity period, source link
- Freshness/state label like other layers
- UI note: informational only, not a substitute for official flight-planning tools

Later PRs: more countries via the same adapter shape, time-aware temporary restrictions (TFR/NOTAM-based).

### Data source, license, and attribution

Candidates (license and key requirements still to be verified before any PR):
- US: FAA UAS Facility Map / LAANC grid, prohibited areas, special use airspace, TFR feed (tfr.faa.gov). Public FAA data, no key expected.
- EU: under Regulation (EU) 2019/947 each member state publishes its own UAS geographical zones in a common digital format, so this needs per-country adapters. Example: Latvia (ais.lgs.lv UAS geozones).
- Bulgaria: DG CAA UAS geographical zones page (caa.bg/en/node/7062), reportedly with an official JSON file. File URL, schema and license unconfirmed.

I will not propose any source whose license does not allow redistribution. This layer maps static regulatory zones only and does not identify or track individuals.

### Will you build it?

No, this is a request for someone else

## Summary
Adds a **Weather Warnings** layer under Weather with Norway's official warnings in effect now, yellow and above:

- **MET Norway** (MetAlerts 2.0): weather warnings for land and sea areas (gale, wind, rain, snow, flooding and other MET events).
- **NVE flood and landslide warnings**, drawn over the warned municipalities.
- **Varsom avalanche danger** levels 2–5, drawn over the forecast regions.

Warning areas are coloured by level (yellow / orange / red), higher levels on top. Selecting an area opens a card with the level, area, validity, warning text and advice, linking to MET Norway or Varsom. Row chips switch Weather, Flood, Landslide and Avalanche on and off, with counts; the legend and analyst query follow the visible families. The layer is registered for share links, voice (`weather warnings`, `flood warnings`, `avalanche danger`, `farevarsel`, …), the analyst query and data attribution; DATA_SOURCES.md and CHANGELOG are updated.

## Data sources
All keyless, fetched through one same-origin `/api/weather-warnings` proxy (GET-only, rate-limited, identifying `User-Agent`):

| Feed | License | Cache |
|---|---|---|
| `api.met.no` MetAlerts 2.0 `current.json` | CC BY 4.0 | 5 min |
| `api01.nve.no` flood / landslide `Warning/All` | NLOD 2.0 | 10 min |
| `api01.nve.no` avalanche `RegionSummary/Simple` + `Region` polygons | NLOD 2.0 | 10 min / 24 h |
| Kartverket `kommuneinfo` municipality outlines | CC BY 4.0 | 7 days |

- NVE's offset-less timestamps are read as Norwegian time, DST-aware.

Uses token `5`, the next free token on `main` (`layer-token:check` passes). #955 (Airports) also claims `5`; whichever merges second takes `6`.

title: fix(recent-imagery): prefer the least cloudy day when none is clear
body:
## Problem
START HERE fell back to the **newest** day whenever no day had every granule at or under 20% scene cloud, no matter how cloudy that day was. In persistently cloudy regions that is most of the time. Over Bergen (Oct 2026) it chose an L30 day at 28–83% scene cloud while an S30 day six days earlier was 8–30%.

A second, smaller issue: CMR returns every HLS tile that *touches* the search box, so a cloudy 110 km tile clipping one edge of the box could disqualify an otherwise clear day.

## Change
- **Cloudy tier → least cloudy.** When no covering day is clear, pick the least cloudy one, preferring a newer day within 10 scene-cloud points of it, so recency is not traded for noise. Unknown cloud ranks behind any known value.
- **Weigh cloud by the box area each granule covers.** `boxCloud` is the mean, over the centres of a 9 × 9 split of the box (each standing for an equal share of its area), of the worst granule's cloud at each point, so a tile clipping the box counts for its sliver. Without footprints, the worst granule over the box.
- A footprint also overlaps when one of its edges crosses a box edge (a band across the box between the samples).
- **Cards show the cloud that ranked the day.** The catalog's `scopeToBox` sets each candidate's `cloud` range from the granules over the box only, so a day ranked clear no longer reads e.g. "5–90% cloud". Granules are kept intact for drawing.
- `rankLatest` takes an optional `box`, passed from the layer and from the imagery tool service. Without it, behaviour matches the old granule set.
- UI wording: "least cloudy day" instead of "newest day (cloudy)".

Clear, partial and overview tiers are unchanged.

## Testing
- New tests: least-cloudy selection including the Bergen case, the 10-point recency tolerance, unknown cloud, and edge-clipping tiles / tiles inside a large box.
- Recent Imagery, UI and tools suites: 158/158 pass. `npm test` (macOS, Node 24): 6244 pass, 0 fail.
- New tests also cover a band crossing the box and `scopeToBox`'s cloud range.
- `npm run format:check` and `npm run check:boundaries` pass.
- Against live CMR data for six Norwegian cities: Bergen now picks 2026-10-02 (8–30%) instead of 2026-10-08 (28–83%); Oslo, Tromsø, Trondheim, Stavanger and Bodø pick the same day as before.

## Overlap with other open PRs
Only CHANGELOG.md overlaps with my other open PRs (a one-line top-of-file entry).

title: fix(maps): allow Bing HTTP tile origins in CSP on local dev pages (#977)
body:
## Root cause

Closes #977.

In Cesium 1.124, the Bing Maps imagery provider derives its tile protocol from `document.location.protocol` when the ion asset endpoint does not specify an explicit protocol override. On the normal local `http://localhost:4173` dev/preview server, Cesium therefore requests Bing metadata with `uriScheme=http`, which returns tile URLs using:

```text
http://ecn.t[0-3].tiles.virtualearth.net/tiles/...
```

The application's Content Security Policy (`BROWSER_CSP`) allowed `https:` but not arbitrary `http:`, causing the browser to block these tile requests with CSP violations and leaving the map unrendered for users with Cesium ion keys when selecting "Bing Aerial" or "Bing Labels".

---

## Fix

Keep the CSP strict and scoped without opening bare `http:` or wildcards:
- Explicitly admit the four Bing tile origins Cesium uses in `connect-src`:
-   - `http://ecn.t0.tiles.virtualearth.net`
-   - `http://ecn.t1.tiles.virtualearth.net`
-   - `http://ecn.t2.tiles.virtualearth.net`
-   - `http://ecn.t3.tiles.virtualearth.net`
- - Preserves `https:`-only behavior for all other remote network connections.
- - HTTPS deployments continue to use HTTPS Bing tiles because Cesium inherits the page protocol there.
---

## Regression & Quality Gates

- Added regression test in `src/tooling/viteBuild.test.mjs` asserting:
-   - The four explicit Bing tile origins are present in `connect-src`.
-   - `https:` and `wss:` remain present.
-   - Bare `http:` is strictly absent.
-   - No wildcard sources were introduced.
- - `node --test src/tooling/viteBuild.test.mjs`: 7 passed, 0 failed
- - `npm run check:boundaries`: Passed (100% compliant)
- - `npm run format:check`: Passed (All 1307 source files formatted)

title: Add free Jersey data sources for all twelve parishes
body:
Adds free, keyless Jersey public data sources, with island-wide coverage and official parish notices from all twelve parishes.

### Jersey data coverage
- **Transport:** LibertyBus vehicle positions, bus stops and on-demand stop departures through Jersey Open Data.
- **Parking:** car park facilities, tracked live occupancy, accessible bays and EV charging-bay inventory.
- **Roadworks:** current and next-30-day Jersey RoadWorkx records, dates and restrictions. Geometry is converted from the service's published NewJTM grid.
- **Weather:** Jersey Met forecasts, rain probabilities, wind and UV.
- **Coastal and marine:** Ports of Jersey tide predictions, dated coastal-access information, shipping forecasts and current offshore buoy observations.
- **Public facilities:** toilets, recycling points, defibrillator locations and Eat Safe food-hygiene ratings.
- **Parish notices:** headline, publication date and official article link from each of the twelve parish RSS feeds, with unavailable feeds reported.
- **Local listings:** links to offers, events, parish services and transport notices. These are provider links, not a claimed live inventory.

### Acquisition and display
A fixed-source GET endpoint under /api/transit acquires the public feeds with capped response bodies, bounded fan-out, request coalescing and in-memory caching. Caller-supplied URLs and invalid parameters are rejected. Public data is fetched at runtime, with source attribution; article bodies and commercial listings are not bundled. Stale or flagged buoy observations are omitted.

A compact phone Nearby menu lets users choose these sources, browse their location or a chosen area, and navigate to any of the twelve parish village centres. Closing the menu retains enabled map overlays. Additional global layers remain available in an expandable section. Desktop and embedded layouts retain their existing presentation, and map labels use the existing world-overlay host.

Parish presets use village-centre radius navigation rather than administrative boundaries. Charging information describes facilities rather than live charger availability. Published coastal-access predictions link to the official source. Jersey overlays are session-local and do not add share-link tokens or voice controls.

title: feat(security): support GEV_TRUSTED_PROXY_IPS for TLS-terminating proxies (#978)
body:
Resolves #978.

### Summary
Implements opt-in trusted proxy support via `GEV_TRUSTED_PROXY_IPS` strictly following maintainer specifications on issue #978:
- Parses comma- and space-delimited IPv4, IPv6, and IPv4-mapped IPv6 proxy peer addresses.
- - When `GEV_TRUSTED_PROXY_IPS` is configured and the socket remote address matches the allowlist:
-   - Admits single-hop `X-Forwarded-For` and single-value `X-Forwarded-Proto` (`http` or `https`).
-   - Derives the request scheme from `X-Forwarded-Proto` to validate `Origin` and `Host` authority matching for TLS-terminated endpoints.
-   - Strictly rejects multi-hop/comma-separated `X-Forwarded-Proto` or other schemas.
-   - Strictly rejects any other proxy/CDN signal headers (`Forwarded`, `Via`, `X-Forwarded-Host`, `X-Forwarded-Port`, `X-Real-IP`, `CF-Connecting-IP`, `CF-Ray`).
- - When `GEV_TRUSTED_PROXY_IPS` is unset, default same-site gate behavior is 100% unchanged (refuses any proxy headers).
- - Leaves credential-panel loopback gate (`keySetupCore.mjs`) unmodified and strictly proxy-refused.

3. 3. Trusted peer + foreign Origin -> 403
4. 4. Trusted peer + `Sec-Fetch-Site=cross-site` -> 403

title: fix: guard scene director callbacks
body:
## Summary

Fix callback exception handling in the scene director and interaction session to prevent inconsistent state, duplicate scene cleanup, and unintended error masking.

Closes #972

## Root Cause Analysis & Changes

### 1. Handle immediate `clock.subscribe()` callback failures

**Root cause:** If a listener threw during its initial snapshot callback, `subscribe()` propagated the exception before returning the unsubscribe handle, leaving the listener registered.

**Fix:**
- Wrapped the initial listener invocation in `try...catch`.
- Logged failures using `console.warn('[Scenes] Scene clock listener failed:', error)`.
- Ensured `subscribe()` returns the unsubscribe function even when the initial callback throws.

### 2. Preserve playback errors when cleanup fails

**Root cause:** An exception from `adapter.releaseScene(activeScene)` inside `finally` could mask an earlier phase error, such as a travel failure.

**Fix:**
- Tracked failures occurring during playback using `runError`.
- Preserved the original run or phase error when cleanup also failed.
- Propagated the cleanup error when no earlier run error occurred.

### 3. Prevent duplicate scene releases

**Root cause:** `activeScene` was cleared only after awaiting `adapter.releaseScene()`. If release failed, the `finally` block could attempt to release the same scene again.

**Fix:**
- Captured the scene in `toRelease`.
- Set `activeScene = null` before awaiting the release operation.
- Ensured each scene is released at most once.

### 4. Isolate interaction session observer failures

**Root cause:** Exceptions thrown by `changed(state())` could leave the session permanently busy when an action started or cause `dispatch()` to reject during cleanup after successful execution.

**Fix:**
- Introduced a `notify()` helper that isolates observer exceptions.
- Logged observer failures using `console.warn('[Scenes] Interaction session observer failed:', error)`.
- Prevented observer failures from corrupting session state or unexpectedly rejecting dispatch operations.

## Tests Added

- **`src/director/clock.test.mjs`**
  - Verifies that immediate subscriber errors are caught and logged.
  - Verifies that `subscribe()` returns a functional unsubscribe handle.

- **`src/director/playback.test.mjs`**
  - Verifies that playback phase errors are preserved when scene cleanup fails.
  - Verifies that a scene is released only once during inter-scene transitions.

- **`src/director/interactions/interactions.test.mjs`**
  - Verifies observer failure handling during action start and end, activation, and clearing.
  - Verifies that dispatch completes correctly, the busy state is cleaned up, and subsequent dispatches remain possible.

## Verification

- [x] Reproduction script for the reported scenarios
- [x] `node --test src/director/*.test.mjs src/director/interactions/*.test.mjs` — 57 tests passed
- [x] `npm run check:boundaries` — Passed
- [x] `npm run format:check` — Passed

## Result

These changes make callback failures safer to handle while preserving playback error semantics, preventing duplicate cleanup, and keeping interaction sessions usable after observer exceptions.

title: fix(satellites): prevent corrupt TLE entry from dropping subsequent satellites (#906)
body:
Resolves #906.

### Problem
`parseTleText()` stepped through catalog lines in rigid increments of three lines (`i += 3`). If a single TLE set was missing line 1 or line 2 (e.g. from upstream transmission glitch or corrupt feed), every subsequent set in the catalog was thrown out of step and dropped silently without error, reporting only the satellites preceding the corrupt entry.

### Fix
- Replaced rigid 3-line step loop with pairwise scanning:
-   - Scans for valid `1 ` and `2 ` TLE pairs.
-   - Verifies catalog numbers match between line 1 and line 2 (`tleCatalogNumber`).
-   - Resolves the preceding non-TLE line as the satellite name, or falls back to `CATALOG-<noradId>` for 2-line format or missing titles.
- - When an individual TLE set is malformed or missing a line, only that individual set is dropped; all subsequent satellites in the group parse cleanly.
### Testing
- Added regression tests in `src/tools/queries/space.test.mjs` verifying:
-   - Repro case from #906: 8 satellite sets where set 1 is missing line 2 now parses 7 satellites instead of only 1.
-   - Set missing line 1 now parses 7 satellites instead of 1.
-   - Mismatched catalog numbers across line 1 and line 2 drop only the corrupt pair.
-   - Two-line TLEs without preceding name line parse with `CATALOG-<noradId>`.
- - `node --test src/tools/queries/space.test.mjs` passed (8/8 tests).
- - `npm run check:boundaries` passed.
- - `npm run format:check` passed.

title: Coordinate parser drops empty components and guesses a destination
body:
The strict coordinate parser silently removes empty components, so malformed
queries can become an exact offline coordinate and bypass the remaining geocoders.

Reproduced on `main` at `591f299d11f38a612629a274463196d57ae3862e`, Node 24.14.0 on Windows:

```powershell
node --input-type=module -e "import {parseCoordinateQuery} from './src/search/coordinateParser.js'; console.log(parseCoordinateQuery('40,,74'))"
```

Actual output:

```js
{ lat: 40, lon: 74, label: '40.0000° N, 74.0000° E' }
```

Expected: `null`, so the coordinate provider declines and the original query
continues to the next geocoder. `,40,74`, `40,74,`, `40;;74` and `40,;74` also
produce a coordinate today. A correctly formed `40,74` should continue to resolve.

In `src/search/coordinateParser.js`, `splitComponents()` calls
`parts.map((part) => part.trim()).filter(Boolean)` before checking for two
components. Removing the blank-field filter preserves the true component count;
the existing reader already refuses blank components. This follows the parser's
documented strict-input contract and avoids interpreting a malformed pasted or
typed query as an exact destination.

I prepared that one-line fix locally and verified it with the existing
malformed-input test strengthened by seven empty-component cases, plus a real
coordinate-provider/search-chain regression asserting that the next provider
receives four malformed queries unchanged. Before the fix, 2 of the 15 focused
tests failed for the incorrect coordinate result; afterward, all 15 pass.

Additional local checks on the proposed fix: production build passes; the Location
controls browser gate passes 12 checks at desktop and narrow viewports; the
tracking regression passes 109 checks with 0 failures or skips. The full unit
suite is not green in this environment: Windows executable-fixture, host-memory
allocation, signing-fixture and timing failures were observed in untouched owners
(6 failures; 6,165 passes and 10 skips). A full-suite base comparison was not run.
This report provides the reproduction and focused fix evidence without claiming
the required full PR validation is complete.

title: feat(radio): add the Reception Horizon layer (#714)
body:
## What

"What can my antenna hear from here": the **Reception horizon layer** from the up-for-grabs list in #714.

For each altitude band, the farthest position your own receiver has heard in each direction is drawn as a stepped 3D shell around the antenna. Low traffic sits inside and high traffic reaches farther. A ridge or building shadowing the antenna shows as a shorter or open side. It's built only from this page session's Local ADS-B positions, kept in memory and never shared or stored.

![Reception Horizon filling in: about 30 minutes of synthetic traffic around an Austin antenna, played back fast while the camera orbits](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b51a4a1e-100b-4fb1-be42-a2f9824ac8cc)

*About 30 minutes of traffic from the synthetic decoder (`scripts/fake-adsb-feed.mjs --speed 30`) with HEIGHT ×10 on: each band's wall steps outward as higher traffic is heard farther away.*

![The five altitude bands as stepped walls around the antenna mast, with HEIGHT ×10](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/aa9c883a-ab78-42cd-984d-643b9c12b97a)

## How it works

- **Input:** `src/layers/localAdsb` gains `subscribeHeardFixes(listener)`. It publishes only fixes that passed the existing speed check against the *same aircraft's previous accepted fix*: an aircraft's first fix, and the first after a re-anchor, are never published. One corrupt frame (CRC-valid but wrong, like the DC-9 "at 108,800 ft") therefore cannot stretch the shell. Anything over 800 km from the antenna (beyond any line of sight) is counted as implausible and never drawn.
- **Model:** `src/layers/receptionHorizon/model.js` is pure and has no Cesium.
  - Five barometric bands: <5k, 5–15k, 15–25k, 25–35k and 35k+ ft.
  - 72 directions of 5°; the farthest fix wins each direction.
  - A bounded buffer of 20,000 positions, so the horizon rebuilds when the antenna position arrives or moves.
- **Drawing:** `src/layers/receptionHorizon/rendering.js`.
  - Neighbouring directions join while ≤ 30° apart. A wider unheard sector leaves the shell open rather than bridging it with a chord.
  - Between neighbours the outline sweeps in bearing (range linear in bearing), so it reads like a coverage plot.
  - Each run is a translucent wall from the band floor to its ceiling with a rim on top, plus an antenna mast and a drop line under the farthest position.
  - Every primitive uses `allowPicking: false`, so clicks reach the aircraft inside the shell. Redraws are coalesced to at most one per second.
- **Antenna position:** SET ANTENNA then a click on the globe (memory only; AUTO clears it), then the decoder's `receiver.json`, then the Radio card's LOCATE. SET ANTENNA claims the pointer through `inputOwnership.js` exactly like Directions' SET A/B: it refuses while another tool holds the pointer and Esc cancels.
- **Row:** the count shows the farthest range. The legend shows each band's farthest range, and its tooltip the share of directions heard. The info line gives the antenna source, positions and aircraft counted, and the farthest position as km/NM, bearing and altitude. HEIGHT ×10 stretches drawn heights for display only, and the row says so while it is on.
- **Registration:** local-only, like Local ADS-B, so it never enters share links. It sits under Local ADS-B in Data Layers → Movement. Voice: "reception horizon", "my coverage", "antenna coverage" and similar map to `reception-horizon`.

## One decision worth a look: `GET /api/local-receivers/receiver`

Decoders that know where they are write it to `receiver.json` beside `aircraft.json` (dump1090-fa, readsb, tar1090, skyaware978). The new route:

- reads that file from the **same validated origin and directory** as each configured feed. Only the file name differs, and the same transport rules apply: pinned resolution, no redirects, a 64 KB cap;
- returns only `{ band, label, status, position: { lat, lon } }`, with no addresses and no upstream text;
- is wrapped in `sameSiteGated`, since it is the operator's location;
- caches for a minute, and the browser reads it only while the layer is on.

The existing aircraft route, its payload and its tests are untouched; the second route lives in the same plugin. If you'd rather keep feeds aircraft-only, dropping the route leaves the other two antenna sources working.

## Trying it without a radio

```sh
node scripts/fake-adsb-feed.mjs --speed 20
LOCAL_RECEIVER_FEEDS=1090=http://127.0.0.1:8090/data/aircraft.json npm run dev
```

`scripts/synthetic-adsb.mjs` is a deterministic sky: aircraft at every altitude inside a 4/3-Earth radio horizon, a ridge that shadows low traffic to the west-north-west, and a corrupt 1,500–1,800 km fix every 20 s. `--speed 20` plays an hour in three minutes.

## Verification

- `npm run build` ✓
- `npm test` ✓ on current main (8,203 tests; 44 new). `src/terrainHeightsBounds.test.mjs` fails only in a checkout whose dev server has already filled `.gev-cache/`; it passes with that cache moved aside, and passes on an untouched main.
- `npm run test:track` ✓
- `npm run format:check` ✓, `npm run check:boundaries` ✓
- **New gate:** `node scripts/qa-reception-horizon.mjs --url http://localhost:4173` ✓ (26 checks). It answers the two routes with the **real** route handlers over the synthetic decoder, and drives the app through the real UI (the Data Layers toggles, the row chips, a real click on the globe). It checks that:
  - the antenna comes from `receiver.json`;
  - every drawn direction lies inside the radio horizon of the altitude and bearing it was heard at;
  - all five bands fill, and higher bands reach farther;
  - the ridge shows;
  - corrupt fixes are refused upstream and never drawn;
  - neither local layer enters the share link;
  - SET ANTENNA → click → AUTO works;
  - positions keep counting while the layer is off;
  - a decoder without a location gets a prompt, with positions waiting until SET ANTENNA;
  - the console stays clean.
- Not yet run against a physical RTL-SDR or a real dump1090/readsb install: everything above used the synthetic decoder. I'd welcome a run from anyone with a feeder.

## Pins updated (and why)

- Catalog layer count 32 → 33 (`constructCatalog`, `sourceComposition` tests), and the Movement panel order.
- Voice tool schema pins (`firstRunExperience`, `actionSchemas` tests) re-derived. The serialized schema grows by exactly 89 characters: `,"reception-horizon"` in the two toggle enums plus the generated alias hint `; reception horizon/my coverage→reception-horizon`.

Translations: the layer is in `LAYER_NAME_KEYS`, every shown string goes through `t()`/`tn()`/`msg()`, and `npm run i18n` reports Spanish and Russian complete. The Spanish and Russian entries are mine, so a native speaker's pass is welcome.

Docs: `CURRENT-STATE.md` (Reception Horizon section and the new Local ADS-B hook), `LOCAL-RECEIVERS.md` (how to use it, and trying it without a radio), `DATA_SOURCES.md` (`receiver.json` handling), `changelog.d/1053-reception-horizon.md`.

title: feat(tools): count and summarize every match in the area tools
body:
## What

`aircraft_in_area` and `vessels_in_area` gain two optional arguments:

- `group_by` counts every matched record by one field: `operator`, `origin_country` or `type_code` for aircraft, and `type` or `destination` for ships. It lists the ten largest groups, plus `other_count` and `unknown_count`, and the summary names the three largest.
- `stats` returns count, min, median, mean and max for airborne altitude and speed (aircraft), or speed (ships).

Both are computed over all matches before `capRows`, so they cover every match, not just the rows returned. Without either argument, answers are unchanged.

## Why

These tools return at most 200 rows (25 by default). An MCP client asked "which countries' aircraft are over Texas?" or "what's the average altitude there?" could only estimate from a truncated sample and present it as an answer. With these arguments, the tool computes the answer itself.

## Notes

- **MCP only.** `src/tools/surfaces.js` keeps both tools off the voice surface. This doesn't change voice or `analyst_query`.
- **Feed coverage is stated, not hidden.** The default civil feed (OpenSky) reports no operator or type code, so those breakdowns say `no operator reported` / `no type reported` instead of returning an empty list silently. adsb.lol (the military feed) does report type codes.
- The helpers (`breakdown`, `numericSummary`, `breakdownPhrase`) live in `src/tools/results.js` beside `capRows`, so other list tools can reuse them.

title: fix(setup): stop Node's DEP0190 warning when npm runs on Windows
body:
## What

On Windows, every `npm run doctor` and every Pinokio install prints:

```
(node:1764) [DEP0190] DeprecationWarning: Passing args to a child process with shell option true can lead to security vulnerabilities, as the arguments are not escaped, only concatenated.
```

It's in the `Windows onboarding` job on `main`, right after the install report: [run 38022495185, job 114126300158](https://github.com/bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view/actions/runs/38022495185/job/114126300158) (Node 24.14.0).

## Why

Windows has to run `npm.cmd` through a shell. `npmProcessSpec` (`scripts/setup-doctor.mjs`) returned `shell: true`, and both callers passed an argument array alongside it (`['--version']` in the doctor, `['ci']` in `pinokio-install.mjs`). Node 24 deprecates that combination at runtime (DEP0190).

There's no real exposure, since the arguments are fixed npm subcommands. But a "security vulnerabilities" warning at the end of a one-click install reads like something went wrong.

## Change

`npmProcessSpec(args, platform)` now takes the npm arguments. On Windows it joins them into the command string (`npm.cmd ci`) with an empty argument array. Elsewhere it returns `npm` with the arguments unchanged. Both callers pass `npm.args`. Unix behavior is the same.

`CHANGELOG.md` has an entry. `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md` is untouched, because the app's runtime behavior doesn't change.

## Verification

Windows 11, Node 24.16.0, branched from `main` at 591f299:

- `npm run doctor`: the warning is gone (it appeared before the change), and it still reports `[OK] npm 11.16.0`.
- The installer's npm path, through `runChecked` with the new spec: npm runs with no warning.
- `node --test src/setupDoctor.test.mjs src/pinokioEnvironment.test.mjs src/pinokioPreflight.test.mjs src/pinokioLauncherContract.test.mjs` (the Windows onboarding job's setup files): 38 passed, 0 failed. `setupDoctor.test.mjs` now checks the Windows, macOS and Linux specs, including the empty argument array on Windows.
- `npm test`: everything passes except `src/codexOauthRealtime.test.mjs`, the Windows-only failure fixed separately in #997.
- `npm run build`, `npm run format:check`, `npm run check:boundaries`: pass.

### Problem

title: feat(earthquakes): add EMSC events the USGS feed does not report
body:
## Summary
The Earthquakes layer reads only the USGS `all_day` feed, which carries few M2.5+ events outside the United States. This adds **EMSC's SeismicPortal**, which aggregates national networks worldwide, under the layer's existing rules (last 24 hours, M2.5+).

On 2026-10-11 the 24-hour M2.5+ snapshot grew from **39 to 304 events**:

| Region | USGS | + EMSC |
|---|---|---|
| Latin America | 16 | +188 |
| Asia and the Pacific | 14 | +48 |
| Europe and the Mediterranean | 1 | +24 |
| Middle East and Central Asia | 2 | +3 |
| United States | 6 | +2 (both in Baja California, Mexico) |

Over a year, Norway with Svalbard and Jan Mayen had 285 M2.5+ events in EMSC against 32 in USGS.

## Changes
- `createEmscEarthquakeSource`: keyless and CORS-enabled, fetched from the browser like USGS; licence CC BY 4.0. Queries `format=json&minmag=2.5` for the previous 24 hours.
- `normalizeEmscSnapshot`: same row shape as USGS (`stableId` `emsc:<unid>`, `emscId`), M2.5+ only. Keeps known, suspected and induced earthquakes and drops quarry blasts and explosions (`evtype`). Region names stored in capitals are written in normal case ("NORTHERN NORWAY" → "Northern Norway"). A malformed feed is rejected as a whole, as for USGS.
- `mergeEarthquakeSnapshots`: USGS rows, then EMSC rows USGS does not report. An EMSC event within **90 s and 150 km**, or **5 minutes and 25 km**, of a USGS event is the same event. The second window comes from a live case: a West Texas event was 2 km but 235 s apart in the two catalogs.
- `createEarthquakeSource`: either catalog alone still yields a snapshot; only both failing is an error.
- The layer (source label "USGS · EMSC"), the reference sources and the `get_earthquakes` tool use the combined source. EMSC-only events get `emsc:<unid>` analyst ids.
- Attribution in Data attribution and DATA_SOURCES.md; CHANGELOG updated.

## Testing
- New `src/layers/earthquakes/emsc.test.mjs` (7 tests): normalization, event-type and magnitude filtering, region case, malformed feeds, both duplicate windows (including the 235 s case), the query URL, the source and partial failure.
- `src/tools/localServer.test.mjs` now expects the stdio server to contact USGS and EMSC.
- `npm test`: 6239/6250; the one failure (`Codex login resolves an installed executable…`) also fails on `main` on Windows. `format:check` and `check:boundaries` pass.
- Against the live feeds: 304 unique events. All 39 USGS events were matched in EMSC, and the remaining EMSC events inside the US box are two Mexican events with no USGS counterpart.

title: bug: keyless boot logs a 404 for /api/google/tiles-token on every page load
body:
### What happened

Without `GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY`, every page load logs a console error:

```
Failed to load resource: the server responded with a status of 404 (Not Found)   /api/google/tiles-token
```

Since a2f61d4 ("load Google 3D with short-lived server tokens"), `src/standalone/application.js` creates `createGoogleTokenSource()` whenever there is no browser key, and the scene requests `GET /api/google/tiles-token` at startup. Nothing in this repo serves that path, so `server/standalone/api-not-found.js` answers 404. `googleTokens.js` treats that correctly as "no tokens offered", but the browser logs the failed request as a console error anyway, and the page can't suppress it. Keyed setups never send the request, which may be why it hasn't shown up.

**Impact.** On a keyless checkout, the gates that require a clean console fail on this request alone:

- `scripts/qa-attribution-b12.mjs`: `no console errors during QA — 404 /api/google/tiles-token` (23 passed, 1 failed)
- `scripts/qa-cockpit-utility.mjs`: `runtime console remains clean — 404 /api/google/tiles-token`
- `scripts/qa-context-arrivals.mjs`: `zero failed app responses — 404 /api/google/tiles-token`

A keyless boot is the default path for new users, and CONTRIBUTING asks PRs to avoid new console errors, so contributors without a Google key start from a red baseline.

**Possible fix.** The token contract already says "any other answer means it does not [offer tokens]". The standalone server could give that answer without an error status: answer `GET /api/google/tiles-token` with `204 No Content` from `server/standalone/` (before `apiNotFoundPlugin`). `request()` gets `response.ok` with an empty body, `response.json()` throws inside its `try`, and it resolves null with nothing logged. A server that does offer tokens replaces the route as before. Happy to open a PR for this if it matches your intent.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Unset `GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY` and run `npm run dev`.
2. Open http://localhost:4173 with the console or network tab open: one 404 for `/api/google/tiles-token`, with no interaction.

### How you installed

Terminal (git clone + npm)

### OS, Node version, browser

Windows 11, Node 24.16.0, headless Chrome through Puppeteer. Nothing here is platform-specific.

### Version or commit

`main` at 591f299

### Output of `npm run doctor`

```
God's Eye View setup doctor

[OK] Node 24.16.0: supported LTS and calibrated for release gates
[OK] npm 11.16.0
[OK] dependencies installed

Map:     Esri World Imagery (keyless satellite basemap) with keyless terrain
Flights: OpenSky keyless anonymous access (rate-limited)
Voice:   available
Vessels: off until an AISStream key is added
Fires:   off until a FIRMS key is added
Traffic: built-in traffic simulation
Missions: Launch Library 2 public access

Configured providers:
  [--] Google Maps
  [--] Google Places / Street View server
  [--] Cesium ion
  [OK] OpenAI voice (environment)
  [--] AISStream vessels
  [--] NASA FIRMS fires
  [--] TomTom traffic
  [--] OpenSky client ID
  [--] OpenSky client secret
  [--] Launch Library 2
  [--] Mapillary street level

Ready. Run npm run dev, then open http://localhost:4173.
```

### Server log and browser console

Browser console on a plain load (25 s, no interaction):

```
Failed to load resource: the server responded with a status of 404 (Not Found)
```

Network: `404 http://localhost:4173/api/google/tiles-token`. The server log has nothing for this request.

title: fix(qa): return from early gate exits instead of process.exit on Windows
body:
## What

On Windows, four feature gates crash instead of exiting cleanly when the dev server is unreachable or has no provider key:

```
Server has no FIRMS key — run against the keyed dev server (:4420).
Assertion failed: !(handle->flags & UV_HANDLE_CLOSING), file src\win\async.c, line 94
```

The gate exits with 127 instead of its documented 2. The affected gates are `qa-firms`, `qa-traffic`, `qa-traffic-jamviz-ab` and `qa-traffic-preset-ab`.

## Why

Each gate's `main()` calls `process.exit(2)` right after a `fetch()`. On Windows, exiting while undici's keep-alive sockets are still closing trips the libuv assertion above, so the process aborts.

## Change

The two early exits in each gate set `process.exitCode = 2` and `return` from `main()`, and the process ends once its handles close. The final exits and the `main().catch` handler are unchanged. No runtime change, so `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md` and `CHANGELOG.md` are untouched.

## Verification

Windows 11, Node 24.16.0, branched from `main` at 591f299, dev server on :4173 with no FIRMS or TomTom key:

| Gate | Before | After (no key, 3 runs) | After (server unreachable) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `qa-firms` | exit 127 + assertion, 3/3 runs | exit 2, no assertion | exit 2 in 1 s |
| `qa-traffic` | exit 127 + assertion | exit 2, no assertion | exit 2 in 0 s |
| `qa-traffic-jamviz-ab` | exit 127 + assertion | exit 2, no assertion | exit 2 in 0 s |
| `qa-traffic-preset-ab` | exit 127 + assertion | exit 2, no assertion | exit 2 in 1 s |

Isolated outside the gates, on the same machine:

- `await fetch(app); await fetch(app + '/api/firms/status'); process.exit(2)`: assertion in 3 of 3 runs.
- `process.exit(2)` with no prior fetch: exits 2 cleanly.
- The same fetches followed by `process.exitCode = 2`: no assertion in 3 of 3 runs.

The final exits are left alone. `node scripts/qa-firms.mjs --fixtures` runs to its final `process.exit` with `RESULT: 8 passed, 0 failed` and exits 0 with no assertion (2 of 2 runs), so the full path doesn't hit this.

`npm run format:check`: pass. I didn't run the keyed paths (no FIRMS or TomTom key here); they're unchanged.

title: Add opt-in model gateway and World Monitor intelligence
body:
God's Eye View currently couples its assistant and HUD summaries to OpenAI, while country news and risk context live separately. This adds an opt-in profile that uses a loopback Bifrost/OpenAI-compatible gateway and reads an operator's World Monitor service from the globe and MCP.

- Add an Intelligence panel with country briefings, news refresh, and text chat using the existing globe tools and real tool-result continuation. Answers stream into one visible row as they arrive; tools run only after the complete response and arguments validate. Stop and stream failures label partial answers incomplete. The panel displays the model that actually answered and preserves visible throttling errors.
- Preserve existing MCP tools and image/globe resources; add three World Monitor queries with source timestamps and partial/stale/unavailable coverage.
- Keep model/feed credentials server-side, reject remote gateway URLs and redirects, and disable Realtime/cloud fallback when the gateway profile is selected. Chat takes priority over background HUD work. Optional HUD model selection and per-page minimum request spacing are server configuration, not browser-supplied model choices.
- A loopback gateway can deliberately route remotely. Document Bifrost's `openrouter/openrouter/free` route (upstream model ID `openrouter/free`), provider/virtual-key allowlists and the retained local-model option. The repository includes no OpenRouter credential or automatic cloud activation.
- Launch an isolated World Monitor sidecar with per-run transport/operator credentials, cloud service fallback disabled, and all text-model tiers pinned to the selected route. Companion backend: https://github.com/koala73/worldmonitor/pull/9101.
- Request HTTPS Bing imagery on local HTTP origins while preserving ion and Bing attribution.

World Monitor source is not copied into this repository. This is a subset of World Monitor capabilities; persistent derived-data pipelines, broader UI/MCP federation, durable investigations, scheduled alerts, embeddings, speech and image input remain separate work. Setup and boundaries are in `docs/HYBRID_LOCAL_SETUP.md`.

Validation on `c2031be`: full Node 24 suite passed 6,367 tests with one skipped, including serialized allocation checks. Production build, formatting and package boundaries passed. The Chrome tracking regression passed all 109 checks. Streaming regression coverage includes split UTF-8/SSE frames, nullable tool-call fragments, complete/EOF gating, byte caps, mid-stream failures, Stop, transport cleanup and recovery. Build retains its existing large-chunk warning.

Live `openrouter/free` streaming returned first text in 7.7 seconds and completed in 10.0 seconds (32 events, `dots-studio/dots-3-note-preview:free`). Live Chrome also verified a streamed tool conversation: `dots-studio/dots-3-note-preview:free` called `world_monitor_country_headlines`, then `nvidia/nemotron-3.5-lightning:free` answered from its unavailable-coverage result. Text was observed while generation remained active. Five live browser checks passed with no page errors or failed requests. The opportunistic HUD request was skipped with 503 while chat owned the gateway; HUD streaming is outside this change. Interceptor was unavailable, so the repository Puppeteer harness used installed Chrome.

The separate deterministic browser gate passed six checks using explicitly labeled synthetic streams to hold partial output visible, check Stop/incomplete marking and confirm mobile recovery without model requests. UI images must be attached before this draft is ready for review; local paths alone are not GitHub evidence. No merge or public deployment is requested.

Desktop partial-output and mobile incomplete/recovery screenshots were captured and visually inspected on clean `c2031be`. GitHub CLI 2.102 again rejected attachment upload with “attaching files requires write access to the repository.” The required GitHub image evidence is therefore still blocked by upstream permissions, and this PR remains draft. The separate desktop incomplete capture had clipped glyphs and is excluded; the mobile capture clearly shows that state.
