title: bug: Cesium DeveloperError (Expected width to be greater than 0) on canvas zero-dimension / tab backgrounding
body:
### Describe the Bug

When the browser window or tab is minimized, placed in the background, or experiences a transient zero-dimension layout cycle, Cesium throws an uncaught `DeveloperError` and halts rendering (`Rendering has stopped`):

```text
DeveloperError: Expected width to be greater than 0, actual value was 0

Error
    at new DeveloperError (node_modules/.vite/deps/cesium.js:8116:11)
    at Check.typeOf.number.greaterThan (node_modules/.vite/deps/cesium.js:8195:11)
    at new Texture (node_modules/.vite/deps/cesium.js:36019:31)
    at FramebufferManager.update (node_modules/.vite/deps/cesium.js:40859:34)
    at GlobeDepth.update (node_modules/.vite/deps/cesium.js:219186:29)
    at updateAndClearFramebuffers (node_modules/.vite/deps/cesium.js:239065:21)
    at Scene.updateAndExecuteCommands (node_modules/.vite/deps/cesium.js:238695:3)
    at render (node_modules/.vite/deps/cesium.js:239479:9)
    at tryAndCatchError (node_modules/.vite/deps/cesium.js:239493:5)
    at Scene.render (node_modules/.vite/deps/cesium.js:239548:5)
```

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Open God's Eye View in a browser tab.
2. Minimize the browser window, switch tabs, or trigger a layout resize where the container or canvas momentarily reports a client width or height of 0.
3. Observe the Cesium render error dialog or console error terminating the render loop.

### Cause

Cesium's internal `GlobeDepth` allocates and updates depth framebuffers matching the pixel dimensions of the viewer canvas. When `canvas.clientWidth === 0` (or `canvas.clientHeight === 0`), `Texture` construction fails Cesium's runtime assertion guard (`Expected width to be greater than 0`), which halts the entire render loop permanently.

### Suggested Fix

In `src/app/viewer.js` (inside `createApplicationViewer`), guard `viewer.scene.render` to skip execution when the canvas dimensions are zero:

```javascript
const originalRender = viewer.scene.render.bind(viewer.scene);
viewer.scene.render = function (time) {
  const canvas = viewer.canvas;
  if (
    !canvas ||
    canvas.clientWidth <= 0 ||
    canvas.clientHeight <= 0 ||
    canvas.width <= 0 ||
    canvas.height <= 0
  ) {
    return;
  }
  return originalRender(time);
};
```

title: bug: share links with heading=360 or roll=360 hang on "Restoring shared view..."
body:
## Summary

Opening a share link whose `heading` or `roll` is `360` never finishes loading: the startup cover stays on **"Restoring shared view..."** indefinitely (observed for 2+ minutes). The same link with `0` instead of `360` loads in ~5 s.

The app produces such links itself: after a camera move ending near north, the address bar showed `heading=360` and `roll=360`, so reloading or sharing that URL hangs.

## Reproduction

Unmodified `main` at 591f299, `npm run dev`, Node 24.21.0, macOS, Chromium-based browser.

| URL hash (after `http://localhost:4173/`) | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `#v=2&lat=46.6886&lon=-71.2701&alt=7111&heading=0&pitch=-35&roll=0` | loads in ~5 s |
| `#v=2&lat=46.6886&lon=-71.2701&alt=7111&heading=360&pitch=-35&roll=360` | stuck (35 s+, and 2+ min in an earlier try) |
| `#v=2&lat=46.6886&lon=-71.2701&alt=7111&heading=360&pitch=-35&roll=0` | stuck |
| `#v=2&lat=46.6886&lon=-71.2701&alt=7111&heading=0&pitch=-35&roll=360` | stuck |
| `#v=2&lat=46.6886&lon=-71.2701&alt=7111&heading=360&pitch=-90&roll=360` | stuck (tilt doesn't matter) |

"Stuck" = `#loading-screen` never gets the `hidden` class. No console errors.

## Likely cause (not fully confirmed)

- The writer rounds to whole degrees, so headings/rolls ≥ 359.5° serialize as `360`: https://github.com/bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view/blob/591f299/src/sharelink.js#L555-L565
- The reader accepts `360` as-is and restores via `flyTo` with `toRadians(360)`: https://github.com/bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view/blob/591f299/src/sharelink.js#L262-L312
- The startup cover only hides once `styleManager.initialRestorePromise` settles: https://github.com/bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view/blob/591f299/src/app/startupChrome.js#L26-L37

I haven't pinned down which step stops settling with a 2π angle. Normalizing to `[0, 360)` on write (`(Math.round(deg) % 360 + 360) % 360`) and on read would likely avoid it either way.

title: Mobile camera workflows, Street Level and local analysis tools
body:
This draft improves phone use and camera recovery, then adds explicit local observation tools: original/crop image Q&A, local enhancement, guarded optional image reconstruction, Street Level picking and public embeds, local sun/time/shadows, and a limited place-name news list. The complete contribution is presented for maintainer review; no merge or ready-for-review conversion is requested.

**Setup:** [installation and feature guide](https://github.com/DatafyingTech/gods-eye-view/blob/contrib/mobile-camera-infrastructure-20261012/docs/LOCAL-FEATURES-SETUP.md) · [camera/image workflow and explicit allowance setup](https://github.com/DatafyingTech/gods-eye-view/blob/contrib/mobile-camera-infrastructure-20261012/docs/LOCAL-IMAGE-WORKFLOW.md) · [sun and limited news](https://github.com/DatafyingTech/gods-eye-view/blob/contrib/mobile-camera-infrastructure-20261012/docs/SUN-AND-NEWS.md) · [synthetic screenshots](https://github.com/DatafyingTech/gods-eye-view/blob/contrib/mobile-camera-infrastructure-20261012/docs/media/local-features/README.md).

### Resulting behavior

- **Phone interface and Locate me:** a compact Menu/MIC/Locate/camera-return toolbar, touch sections reusing desktop controls, safe-area/attribution placement, and smaller rendering/tile/HLS budgets. Camera minimization preserves the playing surface. Locate uses one explicit browser fix, with cancellation/error feedback; successful device-derived camera positions are excluded from this page's hash and copied links. No location watch or saved device marker is added.
- **Camera viewing:** Refresh reconnects the selected source; Close releases it. Phone fullscreen uses native fullscreen where available and a modal fallback otherwise. Desktop Expand/Restore and Escape retain the existing player, attribution and focus. Retry waits for prior lease teardown. Unavailable media remains unavailable.
- **Snapshots:** preserve and separately download original/marked images, selected regions and local contrast/sharpen derivatives. Enhancement runs locally, yields for cancellation and cannot recover missing pixels. Notes remain unverified hypotheses. CORS restrictions and provider attribution remain in place; the capture timestamp is the device clock, not a verified provider frame time.
- **Optional Q&A:** an explicit send uses the original PNG, normalized marks and a server-created lossless crop for a selected region, through `gpt-6.1-sol` with high reasoning. Enhanced/generated pixels and research notes are excluded from evidence. No model fallback, automatic retry, person/plate identification or cross-camera matching is supported. Make/model/year suggestions must explain visible evidence and uncertainty. Model listing alone is not proof of inference access or quota; Q&A charges are separate from reconstruction.
- **Optional reconstruction:** an explicit whole-image or selected-original-crop send uses one low-quality 1024-square `gpt-image-2.5-flare` output. The original stays separate; selected-region exterior pixels are retained. Output is visibly labeled AI-generated reconstruction that may invent detail. Key presence alone does not enable spending. Owner approval initializes an ignored, Vite-denied `.gev-private` policy/ledger; a missing `--policy` correctly selects that private default. Fixed allocations survive restart, concurrent sends are serialized, and missing/corrupt/uncertain state fails closed. Repeat setup preserves the ledger. This is an app-side allocation estimate, not a provider invoice/account-wide ceiling; no automatic retries or key creation are added.
- **Street Level:** explicit point picking, nearest-photo and retry controls, clearer empty/unavailable feedback, mobile modal coordination, and Mapillary sequence IDs followed by bounded metadata batches. A public Mapillary link/ID can open the official provider embed with credits and an external fallback; closing releases the iframe. Google Street View retains its supported external link. Public website visibility and API access remain separate. Added controls live in scrolling settings so the existing image viewer retains its placement and resize space.
- **Sun/time/shadows:** an opt-in panel calculates locally with vendored SunCalc 2.1.1, explicit IANA wall time, DST gap/repeated-time handling, sunrise/sunset and polar conditions. The time slider follows the selected wall time. A dashed shadow sketch assumes a vertical object on level unobstructed ground; it does not model terrain, buildings, weather or actual scene occlusion, and does not change global globe lighting. Near/below-horizon sketches are withheld. Source and binary BSD notices are retained.
- **Limited news fallback:** explicit GDELT DOC2 place-name/topic text searches with bounded UTC dates, source-linked cards, seen/indexed date labels, cancellation, stale/error/empty feedback and rate-limit waits. **The rectangle is local area-of-interest context, not verified spatial filtering. No news pins are drawn, and geocoded search places are not substituted for article/event coordinates.** Geographic retrieval was unavailable: the documented GEO2 route returned HTTP 404, while DOC2 returned HTTP 429. This does not establish GEO2 retirement; no live article-retrieval success is claimed. Only search text/dates leave the PC; article bodies and publisher images are not scraped.
- **Optional data/access:** a bounded Georgia511 adapter for operator-permitted metadata; independent default-off EIA/OSM infrastructure sources with budgets, explicit technology filtering and source/date/owner/operator details; and opt-in owner-only Tailscale Serve gating through configured environment values. Missing local data and unknown attributes stay unknown. Settings, OAuth/log/MCP administration remain desktop-only. No firewall, account, credential or public-sharing setup is automated.

### Setup and data boundaries

Use Node 24.14+ within 24.x or 26.x, `npm ci`, then `npm run start:local` for loopback access. The keyless globe, local image enhancement and sun math require no paid API. Optional provider features require the operator's own keys, permitted data and model access. The launcher does not expose a public server or configure authentication.

Source adapters and invented fixtures are shipped; credentials, private host/identity configuration, camera captures, usage ledgers, generated local infrastructure/catalog datasets, browser profiles and bookmarks are excluded. Provider/data rights remain separate from the preserved upstream MIT license. See [DATA_SOURCES.md](https://github.com/DatafyingTech/gods-eye-view/blob/contrib/mobile-camera-infrastructure-20261012/DATA_SOURCES.md) and [third-party notices](https://github.com/DatafyingTech/gods-eye-view/blob/contrib/mobile-camera-infrastructure-20261012/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md).

### Validation of the reviewed contribution

Reviewed head: `f12e1e09a6a8dd8ec6918fa3ad483fd8deb4a851`, based on upstream `591f299d11f38a612629a274463196d57ae3862e`, preserving the three existing fork commits. Node 24.21.0 on Windows; the user's installed Edge was controlled through dedicated test profiles. Existing locked dependencies were reused; a fresh `npm ci` was not performed.

- Production build, formatting (1,379 adopted files), import/package boundaries and whitespace checks passed. All 29 published layer assignments were retained, with five new assignments.
- Full unit run passed: 6,380 ordinary tests, 10 platform skips, zero failures; all 14 serialized allocation probes passed. The final reviewer-requested allowance-path and related regression set passed 63/63 after the fixes, including the exact documented default setup invocation and ledger-preservation check.
- Deterministic tracking browser gate: 109/109 passed, no skips, no console errors or HTTP 5xx responses.
- Synthetic camera/mobile gate: 9/9 passed. Synthetic sun/news gate: 40/40 passed across desktop, portrait and touch landscape, with no page errors and no paid or live news queries.
- Strict Street Level fixture gate: 28 passed, two documented Google 3D skips, zero failures; every Mapillary request was answered by fixtures. Actual pointer resizing and growth assertions remain in place; the fixture places its lower grip onscreen before that gesture. Nearest/cone navigation, expansion/Escape, docking, phone fit and keyless behavior passed. **Actual Mapillary provider image rendering remains unverified.**
- Normal and filesystem routes both denied private-policy probe files with HTTP 403; the keyless candidate kept paid reconstruction disabled. Changed-file and four-commit history scans found no known secrets, private deployment identities, user-associated image/location references or usage state. Published screenshots and their provenance are synthetic. Heuristic scanning is not a guarantee about every unknown secret or data-rights issue.
- Independent review cleared the frozen head, including the two requested fixes. No additional paid OpenAI calls were made during this preparation; browser/model tests used fixtures.

Earlier `qa-cctv-v2` testing ended 52 passed / one failed because the required real 3D ground sample was unavailable in the keyless synthetic scene; the untouched upstream base reproduced the same failure. This remains a real terrain/GPU/media validation limitation, not complete live-source sign-off. Google 3D follow/drape behavior, real Georgia issuance/playback, real provider image rendering and another-device private Serve behavior need operator-specific validation. CI and any maintainer workflow-approval gates should be assessed separately on the exact pushed head.

### Publication and deployed smoke check

The fork branch and this draft PR both point to reviewed head `f12e1e09a6a8dd8ec6918fa3ad483fd8deb4a851`, published by a normal fast-forward push. The exact-head upstream [CI run](https://github.com/bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view/actions/runs/38322923328) is `action_required` with zero jobs; no GitHub CI success is claimed. Workflow approval is an upstream maintainer gate. GitHub reports the branch behind main and mergeable. The PR remains draft.

The running installation was updated with only reviewed runtime files: all 90 relevant files match the approved source, and credentials/environment metadata and existing allocation policy/ledger remained unchanged. Twelve live UI/access smoke checks passed on localhost and private Tailscale in isolated pages of the owner's installed Edge, including local sun/time synchronization, the limited-news disclosure, private settings denial and preserved allowance. Paid generation, live news and provider imagery traffic were blocked during browser tests. This confirms transport and phone emulation on the same PC; actual other-device, provider imagery and geographic news validation remains limited as described above.


### Related upstream work

There is overlap with [mobile #930](https://github.com/bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view/pull/930), [mobile #636](https://github.com/bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view/pull/636), [camera #1054](https://github.com/bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view/pull/1054), [camera #991](https://github.com/bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view/pull/991), [locate #238](https://github.com/bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view/pull/238), and [proxy #1013](https://github.com/bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view/pull/1013). Novelty/compatibility is not claimed without reconciliation; maintainers may prefer focused follow-ups or splitting this draft before acceptance.

title: feat: add Norway avalanche layer with forecast and observation playback
body: > *Work in progress* — still under active development. Any feedback is appreciated. ## Avalanches layer (Norway) Closes #1016 Adds a keyless **Avalanches** layer under Events. It shows avalanche danger and avalanches that have just happened, played over a ten-day window, much like the cyclone forecasts and the Nepal flood event. - **Danger forecasts** ([Varsom / NVE](https://www.varsom.no/en/), NLOD): each forecast region is coloured by its European danger level (1–5). Colours blend day to day, and forecast days are marked as forecasts, with ↑/↓ when danger is rising or falling. - **Observed avalanches** ([regObs](https://www.regobs.no/), NLOD): each report appears when it happened and runs from release to runout, then fades with age. - **On-map panel**: the date, an observed/forecast badge, play/pause, a clickable day scale and the danger key. - **Off-season**: forecasts run 1 Dec – 31 May. Outside that, the panel explains the empty map and replays last season, opening on its busiest week. A bar per week lets you pick another. - **Cards**: a region card shows its ratings and the forecaster's summary. An avalanche card shows time, size, trigger, release/runout heights and the observer (regObs asks for observers to be credited), with a link to the report. - Region outlines come from [EAWS](https://regions.avalanches.org/) (CC0), whose IDs match Varsom's. ### Notes - A new `/api/avalanches` proxy validates dates, limits each request to 14 days, rate-limits, caches, combines identical requests and serves the last good answer when a source is down. It trims regObs from about 1.7 MB to 73 KB a week. - Share-link token `3`, from `npm run layer-token:next`. Re-run it if another new layer merges first. - The token ledger tests now read free digits from the ledger instead of assuming they're free. The voice-tool hash pins are updated for the new layer. ### Testing `npm test`, `npm run format:check`, `npm run check:boundaries` and `npm run layer-token:check -- --base-ref origin/main` pass. The only failure is the Codex login test, which also fails on `main`.

title: feat(search): resolve two-dimensional geo URIs offline
body:
Pasting `geo:39.7392,-104.9903` into Location search currently sends it to network geocoders. This resolves it offline to the same point, decimal label and camera framing as `39.7392, -104.9903`.

The parser accepts the two-dimensional WGS84 subset of [RFC 5870](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5870.html#section-3.3), including an optional case-insensitive `;crs=wgs84`. Altitude, uncertainty, other parameters, query strings and fragments are declined and reach the remaining providers unchanged. This avoids silently stripping information from a pasted URI. Decimal parsing keeps its existing path; no dependency or provider changes are needed.

Validation on `11bc2ec`, based on upstream `591f299`:

- Focused parser/provider tests: 18 passed. The two new acceptance regressions fail against unchanged `main` and pass with this change. Coverage includes range limits, numeric syntax, unsupported fields, exact framing and bypassing network geocoders even with a Google key configured.
- `npm test`, Node 24.14.0: 6,260 passed, 0 failed, 1 existing skip, including both calibrated allocation files. An initial run hit the unchanged traffic navigation timing test; that test passed standalone on untouched `main`, and the complete rerun passed.
- `npm test`, Node 26.7.0: 6,246 passed, 0 failed, 1 existing skip. The runner skips the two allocation files on Node 26 by design; both passed on Node 24.
- `npm run build`: passed, with the existing large-chunk warning.
- `node scripts/qa-location-controls.mjs`: 15 checks passed, including native URI submission, visible decimal readout, camera arrival, no geocoder requests, desktop/narrow layouts and cancellation.
- `npm run test:track -- --offline-imagery`: 109 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped; synthetic aircraft feeds and bundled imagery, no console errors or HTTP 5xx.
- Setup doctor, formatting, package boundaries, published layer-token checks and `git diff --check`: passed.

README, CURRENT-STATE and CHANGELOG document the supported URI subset. I checked the complete open backlog and searched open/historical issues and PRs for `geo URI` and `geouri`; no matching contribution was found.

title: feat: add San Antonio-area USGS water observations
body:
## Why

San Antonio-area water measurements need their station, series, units and observation time to be useful. This adds one site-grouped USGS layer with separate readings per time-series identity, including locations whose current observations contain no numeric value.

## Changes

- Add **San Antonio USGS Water** with one ground-clamped marker per monitoring location, selected source cards, local Area/Bexar filtering, reading navigation, voice aliases and share visibility.
- Use the current Water Data OGC v1 latest-continuous, monitoring-locations and time-series-metadata collections. Query a fixed regional rectangle with a dynamic 24-hour measurement window and complete station/series joins.
- Preserve zero, negative values, original source text, observation units/time, approval status, qualifiers (including actual list responses), parameter/statistic/computation/sublocation metadata and official station links. Null, blank and nonnumeric observations remain missing numeric values.
- Bound requests, records, responses and acquisition time. Use a 15-minute observation cache and longer bounded metadata caches; honor 429 Retry-After/backoff, cancellation and stale display. Disable releases graphics, handlers, cards and pending work.
- Add portable source/layer exports, focused unit and real-browser gates, a bounded aggregate-only live check, attribution and runtime/source documentation.

Marker color indicates numeric-reading availability, not danger. Stage is not necessarily river depth; groundwater depth is not map altitude. A 24-hour query window is not a 24-hour rainfall total. Historical charts and derived flood categories are outside this PR.

## Source and live validation

Credit **U.S. Geological Survey**, with source and provisional-data links. The documented USGS policy places USGS-authored data in the U.S. public domain; third-party material retains separate rights. This adapter accepts USGS station identities/agency metadata and copies no logos, third-party imagery or downloaded observation snapshot. It is keyless; no private key enters browser code or URLs. Provisional readings can be revised. See `DATA_SOURCES.md` and `docs/SAN_ANTONIO_USGS_WATER.md`.

At **2026-10-12 04:26 UTC** (October 11 in America/Chicago), the implemented bounded live gate acquired:

| Scope | Locations | Readings/series | Numeric readings | Locations with numeric readings |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| San Antonio-area rectangle | 45 | 141 | 136 | 43 |
| Bexar subset of that rectangle | 30 | 103 | 98 | 28 |

All **45/45 station IDs** and **141/141 series IDs** joined. Both no-numeric locations remain represented. All observations were Provisional. Bexar filtering uses state `48`, county `029`; it does not claim full county coverage. These are timestamped findings, not correctness constants. Only aggregate evidence was saved in ignored QA output.

## Validation

Windows; Node 24.19.0; npm 11.6.0; full Chrome for Testing 152.0.7977.75.

- `npm ci`, `npm run doctor`, `npm run build` — passed; large-chunk build warnings remain.
- `npm run format`, `npm run format:check` — passed (1,320 files).
- `npm run check:boundaries` — passed, including independent portable source/layer graphs.
- `npm run layer-token:check -- --base-ref upstream/main` — passed: 29 published reservations preserved, one new assignment.
- `git diff --check` — passed.
- `node scripts/qa-usgs-water.mjs --headful` — **38 passed**. Actual drawing/picking, site grouping, units/time/status, safe provider text, filters, cleanup, cached re-enable, fresh share recipient and 429/retry were verified; no uncaught page or Cesium render errors.
- `node scripts/qa-usgs-water-live.mjs` — passed; complete joins and counts above.
- Final `npm run test:track -- --headful` rerun — **109 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped**, clean console and HTTP 5xx checks. Unchanged upstream comparison also passed 109/0/0.
- `npm test` — **NOT GREEN**: final main phase **6,262 passed, 1 failed, 10 skipped**. The Windows installed-executable resolution test in `src/codexOauthRealtime.test.mjs` expected `\home\fixture\.local\bin\codex`, received `codex`; a fresh targeted run on unchanged upstream reproduced it. The unchanged onboarding code is outside this source PR. The allocation phases were run separately under their required Node 24 GC flags: **14 passed**; this does not make the full required unit command green.

### Tracking intermittency retained

The first contribution tracking run had 107 passes and two M3 camera age-out failures: altitude delta 295.46 km and horizontal delta 392.01 km against 2 km limits. They did not reproduce in the unchanged-upstream comparison or contribution rerun (both deltas 0.00 km). The cause remains unproven. The USGS layer stayed disabled and this PR changes no aircraft/camera runtime or tracking assertion. Both original reveal-timing checks passed at frame 4 with zero heading error in all three runs. The failed run remains recorded in the source review document.

## Draft status and token coordination

Keep this draft pending a green required unit gate or maintainer disposition of the reproduced upstream failure. Tracking intermittency remains explicit. The unchanged lockfile reports three existing audit findings (one low, two high); no dependency upgrades are included.

Reviewed commit: `aadd853b9c3781de9f0a5be201ee289214f87ef1`.

title: feat: optional native macOS app using SwiftUI and WKWebView
body: ### Problem God's Eye View currently runs primarily as a browser application. For macOS users following the terminal installation path, launching it requires a local Node.js environment, an installed source checkout, and a manually started server before opening the application in a browser. While the browser-first approach works well, it introduces additional friction for users who prefer a conventional macOS desktop experience. In particular: - Launching the application requires managing a separate terminal process. - The frontend and local backend do not share a native application lifecycle. - Starting, stopping, and restarting the server requires external interaction. - Backend status and resource consumption are not integrated into the macOS window. - The terminal installation path does not produce a standalone `.app` that can be launched directly from Finder or Applications. I encountered these limitations while setting up God's Eye View on my Mac and started experimenting with a lightweight native wrapper. The goal is not to replace the browser experience, but to make the existing application accessible through an optional, self-contained macOS desktop package. ### Proposal I have built a working native macOS prototype, currently named **GodEye**, using SwiftUI, AppKit, and WKWebView. It preserves the existing God's Eye View frontend, CesiumJS globe, data layers, and local backend rather than introducing a separate rendering engine or rewriting the application. ### Working prototype The current implementation includes: - Native macOS window management using SwiftUI. - WKWebView rendering of the existing God's Eye View application. - Automatic discovery of compatible Node.js installations, including NVM and Homebrew. - Automatic startup of the local backend when the application launches. - Managed backend lifecycle with Start, Stop, and Restart controls. - Dynamic loopback port allocation. - Native macOS title-bar controls and backend status indication. - Live backend CPU usage, memory consumption, and uptime statistics. - Backend logging and startup diagnostics. The existing globe and keyless live-data features work inside the native window. The application loads God's Eye View as the top-level WKWebView document, so no iframe embedding exceptions or changes to the existing Content Security Policy have been necessary. ### Prototype screenshot The screenshot below shows the existing God's Eye View interface running in a native macOS window, with backend lifecycle controls and live resource statistics integrated into the title bar. ### Proposed initial contribution The first contribution would focus on packaging the existing application as an optional macOS desktop target. The intended result would be a self-contained `.app` that: 1. Launches directly from Finder or Applications. 2. Includes the required frontend assets and backend runtime. 3. Starts and manages its backend automatically. 4. Preserves the existing God's Eye View interface and functionality. 5. Provides lightweight native lifecycle controls. 6. Shuts down its managed backend when the application exits. The desktop-specific implementation would remain isolated from the existing browser application as much as practical. ### Current limitations The prototype currently relies on an external God's Eye View checkout and a locally installed Node.js runtime. Standalone packaging, bundled runtime management, security hardening, and signing/notarization are not yet complete. These would be addressed before considering the application ready for distribution. ### Scope and project direction I noticed that #574 was closed because its proposed native, local-first geospatial workstation direction was broader than the project's plans. This proposal is intentionally narrower. It does **not** propose a native globe renderer, GIS workstation functionality, new geospatial formats, offline project management, or a broader architectural transformation. The intention is simply to provide another way to run the existing application on macOS. I would be happy to contribute the implementation, documentation, and testing work. Before proceeding further, I wanted to ask whether an optional macOS desktop application would fit the project's direction. If maintaining a macOS target in the main repository is undesirable, I would also be open to maintaining it as a separate community companion project. The name "GodEye" is currently just a working name for the prototype, not a proposed official product name. The screenshot above demonstrates the current prototype, including its native macOS controls and backend resource monitoring. Thanks for building and maintaining God's Eye View! ### Data source, license, and attribution None — this proposal introduces no new data sources, feeds, or APIs. The macOS application would reuse the existing God's Eye View frontend, backend, and supported providers without changing their data licensing or attribution requirements. The native wrapper would preserve the original project's license and copyright notices, along with the attribution requirements of its existing data providers. Any redistribution would also respect the licenses of bundled runtime components and dependencies. No additional API keys would be required beyond those already supported by God's Eye View. ### Will you build it? Yes, I plan to open a PR

title: feat: optional local historical tracking database with configurable retention and timeline replay
body:
### Problem Problem God's Eye View provides an impressive real-time geospatial intelligence platform, displaying live aircraft, vessels, satellites, and other spatial data sources on a 3D globe. However, I would like to propose an optional historical data recording, storage, and playback capability that would allow users to preserve supported live tracking data locally and retrieve or replay it later. Currently, the platform primarily focuses on live situational awareness. When historical observations are not retained, users cannot easily return to a previous time to investigate the movement and activity of tracked objects. This presents limitations for users interested in: Reviewing historical aircraft, vessel, and other supported tracking activities. Replaying movements over a selected historical period. Investigating events after they have occurred. Comparing current and previously recorded tracking data. Performing historical geospatial analysis without relying on external historical data services. Maintaining a locally controlled archive of observations collected by their own God's Eye View installation. The goal is to extend God's Eye View from a primarily live-viewing platform into an optional live and historical geospatial observation system. ### Proposal

I propose introducing an optional Local Historical Data Storage and Replay Module that continuously captures supported live tracking observations and stores them in a local database.

Users should be able to configure how long historical data is retained, retrieve observations for a selected date and time, and replay recorded tracking activity directly on the existing CesiumJS 3D globe.

The feature should support customizable historical retention periods covering hours, days, weeks, and months.

Importantly, the existing real-time tracking functionality should remain unchanged.

1. Local database integration

Introduce an optional local database for storing supported geospatial tracking observations.

Suggested database options:

  • SQLite: Lightweight, embedded database suitable for individual installations.

  • PostgreSQL with PostGIS: Optional advanced backend for larger datasets and geospatial queries.

SQLite could serve as the default implementation to minimize configuration and external dependencies.

The database should store relevant available metadata, including:

  • Tracking object identifier.

  • Object category and originating data source.

  • Latitude and longitude.

  • Altitude, where applicable.

  • Speed, heading, and other available movement attributes.

  • Observation timestamp in UTC.

  • Data collection timestamp.

  • Additional source-specific metadata where permitted.

Each tracking observation should be timestamped and linked to its corresponding object identifier to reconstruct historical movement.

Database writes should be asynchronous or buffered to avoid degrading the existing live globe performance.

2. Configurable historical data retention

Users should be able to customize how long recorded observations are retained.

Suggested retention presets:

Retention period | Example configuration -- | -- Hours | 1, 6, 12, 24 hours Days | 3, 7, 14 days Weeks | 2, 4, 8 weeks Months | 1, 3, 6, 12 months Custom | User-defined duration

Additional configuration options could include:

  • Enable or disable historical recording.

  • Select which supported tracking layers are recorded.

  • Configure recording or sampling intervals.

  • Set a maximum database storage size.

  • Monitor database storage consumption.

  • Automatically delete observations older than the configured retention period.

  • Optionally retain selected events or tracks longer than the global retention period.

Retention management should operate automatically without requiring users to manually clean database records.

A configurable storage limit would also help prevent excessive disk consumption when monitoring large numbers of tracking objects.

3. Historical timeline and playback

Introduce a dedicated Historical Playback Mode within the existing God's Eye View interface.

This mode would allow users to select a previous date and time and visualize recorded tracking observations on the 3D globe.

Suggested playback controls:

  • Date and time selection.

  • Historical timeline slider.

  • Play and Pause.

  • Stop and Restart.

  • Forward and backward timeline navigation.

  • Adjustable playback speed (0.5x, 1x, 2x, 5x, 10x, 30x, 60x).

  • Jump to a specific timestamp.

  • Display the currently selected historical timestamp.

  • Filter playback by geographic region, data source, or tracking object.

The replay system should reconstruct historical object positions using recorded observations and update the existing globe as the playback timeline advances.

Where appropriate, interpolation between observations could provide smoother movement, while clearly distinguishing interpolated positions from actual recorded observations.

Historical playback should also be clearly distinguished from live tracking to avoid confusion between past and current positions.

4. Historical tracking and trajectory visualization

For individual tracked objects, users should be able to retrieve and visualize recorded movement history.

Suggested functionality:

  • Search for a recorded tracking identifier.

  • Select the start and end date/time.

  • Display the historical movement path on the globe.

  • Follow an individual object during playback.

  • Inspect available historical attributes at selected timestamps.

  • Display the first and last recorded observations.

  • Show gaps in historical observations rather than assuming continuous tracking.

For example, a user could select an aircraft identifier and replay its recorded movement over the previous six hours.

The feature should use actual locally recorded observations rather than relying on estimated or externally purchased historical tracking information.

5. Recording and playback modes

The interface could provide three operating modes:

LIVE MODE

Displays current tracking data from the existing supported providers.

RECORDING MODE

Continues displaying live tracking data while simultaneously storing supported observations in the local database.

HISTORICAL MODE

Retrieves stored observations and replays them for a selected historical date and time range.

Ideally, recording should continue in the background while the user reviews historical observations, provided the local backend remains running.

A visible recording indicator and database status would help users understand whether historical collection is active.

6. Proposed implementation architecture

The feature could be implemented as an optional module alongside the existing God's Eye View frontend and local backend.

Suggested processing architecture:

Existing Live Tracking Data Sources
                |
                v
      Existing Data Processing
                |
          +-----+------+
          |            |
          v            v
     Live Globe    Optional Recorder
          |            |
          |            v
          |       Local Database
          |            |
          |            v
          |      Historical Query API
          |            |
          |            v
          +----> Historical Playback
                     |
                     v
                CesiumJS Globe

Possible implementation components:

  1. A recording service that subscribes to supported tracking observations.

  2. A storage adapter supporting SQLite initially.

  3. A configurable retention and cleanup scheduler.

  4. Backend APIs for historical queries.

  5. A frontend timeline and playback controller.

  6. A historical track rendering adapter that reuses existing CesiumJS capabilities.

The implementation should avoid modifying individual live-data provider modules unnecessarily.

Where feasible, recording should occur after observations have been normalized into the existing application data structures.

7. Data export and portability

As an optional enhancement, users could export recorded historical tracking data.

Suggested export formats:

  • CSV for tabular analysis.

  • GeoJSON for GIS applications.

  • GPX for compatible GPS and tracking software.

  • JSON for interoperability and backup.

Exports could be filtered by time range, object identifier, geographic area, and data source.

The export functionality should preserve timestamps, coordinates, and available tracking metadata, subject to applicable provider restrictions.

8. Performance and database management

Since God's Eye View can display large numbers of tracking objects, historical recording should be designed to minimize performance overhead.

Suggested considerations:

  • Buffered or batched database inserts.

  • Indexed timestamps and tracking identifiers.

  • Efficient time-range queries.

  • Configurable sampling intervals.

  • Background database cleanup.

  • Storage usage monitoring.

  • Pagination or chunked retrieval of large historical datasets.

  • Protection against unbounded database growth.

The module should remain optional and should not negatively affect installations where historical recording is disabled.

9. Proposed initial contribution

To keep the initial implementation manageable, I suggest a phased approach.

Phase 1 — Minimum viable implementation

  • Optional SQLite database.

  • Historical recording for one supported live tracking layer, preferably aircraft.

  • Configurable recording interval.

  • Retention settings in hours, days, weeks, and months.

  • Basic date/time historical search.

  • Historical tracking path visualization.

  • Simple Play/Pause timeline controls.

Phase 2 — Enhanced replay

  • Additional supported tracking layers.

  • Multiple-object playback.

  • Adjustable playback speeds.

  • Tracking identifier search.

  • Geographic filtering.

  • Advanced database management.

Phase 3 — Optional advanced capabilities

  • PostgreSQL/PostGIS support.

  • Data export.

  • Advanced historical queries.

  • Long-duration archive management.

  • Historical and live-data comparison.

This phased implementation could reduce development complexity while providing a useful initial historical playback capability.

10. Scope and project direction

This proposal is intended as an optional extension of God's Eye View rather than a replacement for its existing architecture.

It does not require:

  • Replacing the existing CesiumJS globe.

  • Rewriting the frontend or backend.

  • Introducing a full enterprise GIS platform.

  • Requiring an external cloud database.

  • Making historical recording mandatory.

  • Changing existing live-data providers.

The intention is to allow users who run God's Eye View locally to optionally preserve and replay the tracking observations their installations already receive.

If integrating the feature into the main repository would introduce excessive complexity, it could alternatively be developed as a separate companion module that integrates with the existing local backend.

11. Current limitations and considerations

Several aspects would need to be evaluated during implementation:

  • Not all providers expose consistent tracking identifiers or timestamps.

  • Different tracking sources refresh at different intervals.

  • Some layers represent static information, derived positions, or simulated activity rather than directly observed movement.

  • Historical recording can consume significant disk space.

  • Playback accuracy depends on observation frequency and source reliability.

  • Some providers may prohibit storing, redistributing, or retaining their data beyond specified periods.

  • Recording should not be represented as continuous when observations are missing.

  • Source availability and provider outages could create gaps in recorded history.

Only data sources whose licensing and usage terms permit local historical storage should be eligible for recording.

Recording and export controls should respect those individual provider restrictions.

12. Data source, license, and attribution

This proposal does not introduce any new external tracking providers or APIs.

It would operate on observations already received by supported God's Eye View data-source integrations.

However, historical retention and redistribution rights may differ between providers.

Each source should be evaluated before enabling persistent storage, and the implementation should preserve the original project's license, source attribution, and applicable third-party data usage requirements.

13. Expected outcome

The desired result is an optional, local-first historical tracking capability allowing users to:

  1. Continue monitoring supported live geospatial tracking data.

  2. Automatically record observations into a local database.

  3. Configure historical retention in hours, days, weeks, or months.

  4. Retrieve tracking observations for a selected historical period.

  5. Replay recorded movements directly on the existing 3D globe.

  6. Analyze individual historical trajectories without depending on an external historical data service.

This would make God's Eye View more useful for historical situational awareness, research, demonstrations, and post-event geospatial analysis while preserving its original live tracking experience.

Will you build it?

I am proposing this feature for consideration by the project maintainers and community.

I would appreciate feedback on whether an optional local historical recording and replay module aligns with the project's development direction.

If appropriate, this could be implemented incrementally or maintained as a separate community extension.

Thank you for developing and maintaining God's Eye View!

### Data source, license, and attribution No new external data sources, feeds, or APIs are proposed. This feature would record and replay tracking observations already received through God's Eye View's existing supported data providers. - **Data sources:** Existing God's Eye View tracking integrations (aircraft, vessels, satellites, and other supported layers). - **License:** Existing provider-specific licenses and terms of use apply. Historical storage would only be enabled for sources that explicitly permit local recording and retention. - **API keys:** No additional API keys are required beyond those already supported by God's Eye View. Existing provider authentication requirements remain unchanged. - **Attribution:** All original provider attribution, copyright notices, and licensing requirements will be preserved. The proposed SQLite database would store observations locally, subject to each provider's retention and redistribution restrictions. No new external data service is required. ### Will you build it? No, this is a request for someone else

title: feat: draped GeoJSON/KML vector polygon layer support for municipal boundaries, parcels, and zoning
body:
### Problem

Today, users can draw ad-hoc areas manually or load point-based infrastructure markers (datacenters, dams), but there is no mechanism to import or toggle open vector polygon datasets (such as county appraisal district boundaries, municipal zoning districts, watershed conservation areas, or regional parks). While issue #890 requested KML line paths for hiking, researchers, urban planners, and GIS analysts frequently need to visualize boundary polygons draped on 3D terrain.

### Proposal

Add native support for loading GeoJSON and KML polygon FeatureCollections in the DISPLAY / Overlays drawer:
1. **File Import / URL Feed:** Allow users to drop a `.geojson` or `.kml` file into the UI or supply a public URL.
2. **Terrain Draping:** Utilize Cesium's `GeoJsonDataSource.load()` with `clampToGround: true` so polygon fills and perimeter outlines conform smoothly to Google 3D and keyless Cesium terrain.
3. **Layer Controls:** Provide standard opacity slider, fill color picker, outline toggle, and show/hide visibility switches in the layer tray.
4. **Attribute Inspection:** Clicking an imported polygon opens a HUD card displaying its GeoJSON `properties` table (e.g. Zone ID, District Name, Area in sq km).

Keep the initial version small: support drag-and-drop local GeoJSON polygons with basic styling and ground clamping.

### Data source, license, and attribution

This proposal operates on user-supplied or public open-data GIS vectors:
- **Sample Datasets:** Texas Open Data Portal (Zoning & Municipal Boundaries), US Census Bureau TIGER/Line Shapefiles/GeoJSON (Public Domain), Montgomery County Open GIS Portal (Public Domain).
- **License:** Public Domain / Open Government Data.
- **API Keys:** Zero external keys required; parses entirely within the browser via standard Cesium vector loaders.
- **Attribution:** Preserves attribution metadata embedded in the GeoJSON FeatureCollection.

title: fix(firms): retry over IPv4 when every address fails to connect
body:
Fixes #68, following @asturksever's note on #73 asking for the IPv4 fallback and `error.cause` logging in the current FIRMS provider.

## Cause

Node's network-family auto-selection gives each resolved address a short attempt timeout (250 ms on Node 24, 500 ms on Node 26), except the last. When the system lists IPv4 before IPv6, IPv6 is unreachable, and the IPv4 handshake takes longer than that timeout, Node abandons the working IPv4 attempt. The IPv6 attempt then fails at once, and fetch reports only `fetch failed`. That is exactly the reporter's error: `ETIMEDOUT 198.118.194.34:443` followed by `ENETUNREACH 2001:4d0:241a:40c0::34:443`.

## Fix (`server/providers/firms.js`)

- When every address fails to connect, retry once with a single IPv4 connection (`family: 4`, `autoSelectFamily: false`) within the same deadline. HTTP errors, timeouts, aborts and DNS failures are not retried.
- Node 26's fetch wraps the `AggregateError` in a `ConnectTimeoutError`, so both shapes are handled.
- FIRMS warnings include the per-address errors, e.g. `fetch failed (connect ETIMEDOUT 198.118.194.34:443; connect ENETUNREACH 2001:4d0:241a:40c0::34:443) — retrying over IPv4`. The keyed URL is never logged.
- The IPv4 retry does not follow redirects. FIRMS endpoints answer directly; a 3xx would surface as a logged `HTTP 3xx`.

`docs/CURRENT-STATE.md` and `CHANGELOG.md` are updated.

## Validation

### Real network with broken IPv6

Ubuntu 26.04 host, Docker 29.8. Each container was on a Docker network with an IPv6 subnet but no IPv6 route out, so the resolver returns NASA's AAAA record and IPv6 connects fail with `ENETUNREACH`. IPv4 latency was added inside the container with `tc netem`, and address order was set with `/etc/gai.conf` (`precedence ::ffff:0:0/96 100` for IPv4 first). The containers use the official `node` images, which are Debian-based; the reporter is on Linux Mint, which shares the same glibc resolver and `gai.conf` behaviour. Requests went to the live FIRMS host, using this branch's provider code against `main`'s:

| Node | Address order | Added latency | `main` | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 24.19.0 | IPv6 first | 300 ms | HTTP 200 | HTTP 200 (no retry) |
| 24.19.0 | IPv4 first | 300 ms | **`fetch failed`** | **HTTP 200** after one IPv4 retry |
| 26.11.1 | IPv6 first | 300 ms | HTTP 200 | HTTP 200 (no retry) |
| 26.11.1 | IPv4 first | 300 ms | HTTP 200 (under the 500 ms timeout) | HTTP 200 (no retry) |
| 26.11.1 | IPv4 first | 600 ms | **`fetch failed`** | **HTTP 200** after one IPv4 retry |

In the failing setup, the reporter's one-liner from #68 reproduces their `AggregateError [ETIMEDOUT]` exactly. Their `--no-network-family-autoselection` workaround succeeds with IPv4 first, but fails with `ENETUNREACH` when IPv6 is listed first, since it only tries the first address. This change handles both orders.

### Full app on the real network (Ubuntu)

I ran the whole dev server (this branch's tree, `npm ci`, live MAP_KEY, empty FIRMS cache) in the same broken-IPv6 container on Node 24.19.0, with IPv4 listed first and 300 ms of added latency. The served `server/providers/firms.js` was swapped between `main` and this PR:

| | `main` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `/api/firms` | **HTTP 502** "firms fetch failed and no cache available" | **HTTP 200** in 21 s, 138,193 detections |
| Sources | all four `fetch failed`; mapkey status `fetch failed` | all four ok |
| Server log | `[firms-proxy] VIIRS_NOAA20_NRT fetch failed: fetch failed` (×4) | `[firms-proxy] fetch failed (connect ETIMEDOUT 198.118.194.34:443; connect ENETUNREACH 2001:4d0:241a:40c0::34:443) — retrying over IPv4` (×4) |

### Full app, simulated network (macOS)

I ran the dev server with a preload that resolves the FIRMS host to [IPv4, unreachable IPv6] and lowers the attempt timeout below the real round trip, with an empty FIRMS cache:
- `main`: all four sources log `fetch failed`, and `/api/firms` returns **502** "firms fetch failed and no cache available".
- This PR: each source logs the cause and retries over IPv4, and `/api/firms` returns **200** with 143,140 detections from all four sources.

### Tests and gates (macOS, Node 26.10; FIRMS tests also on Node 24.19)

- New unit tests in `src/data/firmsProxy.test.mjs`:
  - both error shapes are retried
  - HTTP errors, single-cause DNS failures, empty aggregates, timeouts and expired deadlines are not retried
  - a failed retry reports its own error
  - logs contain the connection errors and never the key
  - a real-socket test checks that the retry connects only to IPv4 (`localhost` listening on both `::1` and `127.0.0.1`); it fails if `family: 4` is removed
- The existing `refreshUpstream` harness passes the new `describeFetchError` dependency in.
- `npm test`: 6,248 passed, 0 failed, 1 skipped.
- `npm run build`, `npm run format:check` and `npm run check:boundaries` are clean.
- `npm run test:track`: 109 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped.
- `node scripts/qa-firms.mjs` with a live MAP_KEY: 9 passed, 0 failed.

Not tested: a physical machine whose own network has broken IPv6. The containers reproduce that at the kernel level, both for the provider code and for the full app.

title: feat(drivebc): add BC road conditions overlay
body:
## Summary

Adds a keyless, BC-only DriveBC Open511 road-conditions overlay and an area-scoped `get_bc_road_conditions` query tool.

## What changed

- Adds a bounded public Open511 source for active BC events. Requests use a 12-second timeout, a 12 MiB response cap, a 500-event page cap, 60-second caching, and a short stale-cache fallback. Incomplete/capped results and stale data are reported rather than presented as complete and fresh.
- Normalizes valid point and line geometry. Renders point reports as markers and road segments as ground-clamped severity-colored polylines, with long line geometry decimated to a bounded vertex count.
- Adds the DriveBC Road Conditions toggle to the Movement layer panel. The row includes a severity key (Critical, Major, Moderate, Minor, Unspecified) and explicitly notes that color denotes event severity, not traffic speed.
- Clicking a DriveBC event opens a bounded map popup with its headline, severity/color, event type, update time, description, and official event-details link. The content is rendered as text and the link is restricted to the official Open511 host.
- Adds the `get_bc_road_conditions` tool for area-filtered event records, including source, coverage, freshness, partial-result, and truncation metadata.
- Registers the layer in application and standalone source composition, share-state token `3`, voice layer metadata, package exports/boundaries, and data-source attribution.
- Documents the source, coverage, limits, and integration in the project data-source, tools, and current-state docs.

## Scope and limitations

The source is public and requires no API key. Coverage is limited to British Columbia; this is not a pan-Canadian road feed. The overlay reads one bounded page of up to 500 events and marks the result partial if that cap is reached.

## Verification

title: feat: structured entity knowledge graph schema and authority metadata in Place cards
body:
### Problem

When searching or inspecting places (via Google Places or OpenStreetMap features), the current UI displays a basic name, address, and category. In OSINT investigations, supply chain analysis, and investigative research, analysts need to disambiguate corporate, civic, and maritime entities against authoritative open knowledge registries (such as Wikidata, OpenCorporates, and Wikipedia) to verify organizational authority and eliminate entity ambiguity.

2. **Structured Metadata Display:** Present clean badges for Entity Type (`Organization`, `CivicStructure`, `Airport`, `CommercialTerminal`), official website link, and verified coordinates.

title: feat(bikeshare): add Detroit, Pittsburgh, Aspen and Kona & Hilo
body:
Adds four live US bikeshare systems, all on Lyft's PBSC platform, which the registry already uses for Austin, Honolulu and Chattanooga:

| System | City | Stations | Feed host |
|---|---|---|---|
| MoGo | Detroit, MI | 81 | `detroit.publicbikesystem.net` |
| POGOH | Pittsburgh, PA | 60 | `pittsburgh.publicbikesystem.net` |
| WE-cycle | Aspen, CO | 101 | `aspen.publicbikesystem.net` |
| HIBike | Kona & Hilo, HI | 23 | `kona.publicbikesystem.net` |

These are the layer's first stations in Michigan. Each feed is keyless and listed in MobilityData's `systems.csv`. The proxy already admits `*.publicbikesystem.net` and the paths are the standard `station_information.json` / `station_status.json`, so there is no server change.

**HIBike centre.** HIBike runs stations in both Kailua-Kona (13) and Hilo (10), about 95 km apart. A Kona centre would leave Hilo just outside the 100 km activation radius, so the centre sits between the towns (19.68, −155.54): every station is within 54 km, and both towns are within 48 km.

**Licensing.** None of the four publishes a `license_url`, the same as the existing PBSC cities. The feed contact is Lyft's (`mobility-data-client@lyft.com`). They're treated as attribution-only, like the other GBFS operators. `DATA_SOURCES.md` and `dataCredits.js` already cover them under the GBFS row. I left those example lines unchanged because #641, #946 and #1063 all edit the same lines.

**Left out:** Beaverton's Nike Biketown (appears to be a corporate campus system), Stony Brook's Wolf Ride (campus, 14 stations), and Miami's Inter Bike (7 stations). Easy to add if wanted. Lyft's Denver scooters are dockless, which the layer doesn't model.

## Coordination with open PRs
- Entries sit after Chicago, a stretch of the registry that #641, #946 and #1063 don't touch. `git merge-tree` against each shows the registry merges cleanly; only the top `CHANGELOG.md` line overlaps.
- #641 adds a `registry.test.mjs` that checks every city against the proxy. This PR's test is in a separate `usPbscCities.test.mjs` to avoid an add/add conflict.

## Validation (macOS, Node 26.10)
- **Browser, keyless dev server:** each view enables the bikeshare layer and reads `getStats()` and the loaded records. There were no page errors in any run. The `main` columns swap `main`'s `registry.js` into the same server.

  | Camera over | `main` | this PR |
  |---|---|---|
  | Downtown Detroit | 0 stations | 81 |
  | Downtown Pittsburgh | 0 | 60 |
  | Aspen | 0 | 101 |
  | Kailua-Kona | 0 | 23 |
  | Hilo | 0 | 23 (whole system, via the shared centre) |

- **Proxy:** `/api/gbfs/…detroit…/station_information.json` and `station_status.json` both return 200 with 81 stations.
- **New test:** `src/layers/bikeshare/usPbscCities.test.mjs` checks:
  - each system is registered with the right host and provider
  - its feeds pass `isAllowedGbfsHost` / `isAllowedGbfsPath`
  - a camera over its outermost station, taken from the live feed, activates it through the production `computeInRangeCities` (for HIBike, the outermost station in both Kona and Hilo)
  - HIBike stays inactive over Honolulu

  Moving HIBike's centre to Kona makes the Hilo check fail.

  It fails on `main`.

title: feat(cctv): add NYC DOT Traffic Management Center camera pack
body:
## Summary

Add New York City traffic cameras from the NYC DOT Traffic Management Center as a live CCTV pack.

The server loads the keyless `webcams.nyctmc.org/api/cameras` catalog and keeps cameras the feed marks online. Frame URLs are synthesized from each camera UUID on that same host (`/api/cameras/<uuid>/image`); catalog fields cannot steer the proxy off-host. Offline cameras are dropped. There is no published heading, so gizmos use the shared id-hash fallback at low confidence.

By default the 250 cameras nearest the five borough cores load. `CCTV_NYC_MAX_SOURCES` sets the pack cap (8–400) and `CCTV_NYC_ENABLED=0` turns the pack off. The catalog-wide ceiling stays at 4,000 and is shared round-robin with the other packs.

## Validation

- Node 24.14.0 (`npm run doctor`)
- `npm run format:check`
- `npm run check:boundaries`
- `npm run build`
- `npm test` (6258 pass, 1 skip)
- `npm run test:track -- --url http://localhost:4173 --offline-imagery` (109 passed, 0 failed)
- **QA gate:** `node scripts/qa-cctv-v2.mjs --url http://localhost:4173` (44 passed, 3 failed, 6 inconclusive). The three failures are headless SwiftShader geometry sampling and an empty-canvas click that stayed occupied under the 4,000-camera catalog; frustum, frame URL family, viewshed, and gizmo asserts passed. Frames from the pack return `200 image/jpeg`.

`docs/CURRENT-STATE.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `DATA_SOURCES.md`, and in-app credits are updated.

## Demo

title: feat(layers): add FAA drone restrictions airspace layer
body:
Closes #1006

## Summary

Add an off-by-default **Drone Restrictions** layer (Infrastructure) for US FAA prohibited (P) and restricted (R) special-use airspace.

`/api/drone-airspace` pages the public FAA SUA FeatureServer for `TYPE_CODE IN ('P','R')`, simplifies geometry, caches for one hour, and serves the last good snapshot as stale when a refresh fails. Client-supplied URLs are rejected. Zones draw as ground polygons (red prohibited, orange restricted). Selecting a zone shows name, altitudes, times of use, and controlling agency, plus a notice that the layer is informational only and not a substitute for B4UFLY / LAANC. title: GEN-299: open a published run at its receipt's revision and show its mission effects
body:
God's Eye side of GEN-299. It's built on GEN-309/310 (receiver pass, run player).

**openRun (embedded API)**
- `app.openRun(head, { revisionId, validAt, compare: { head, revisionId } })`.
- Every row is pinned to the receipt's revision (`follow: 'pinned'`), never to whatever the head says now.
- Refused with a `RunOpenError` whose message the host can show:
  - `revision-not-on-head`
  - `no-simulated-products`, instead of the old empty globe.
- The result reports `headAdvanced` and the run's `interval`.
- A comparison that can't be opened is reported as `compareError`; the run still opens.

**Run player: mission-effects lanes**
- One lane each for communications, collection and navigation, one cell per published row, coloured by `state_code`.
- Unknown is hatched, never drawn as an outage.
- Opportunities sharing an epoch keep separate cells, stacked.
- Each cell's tooltip gives the opportunity, state, reason (from the product's `reason_codes` legend) and outcome, e.g. "50 B of 100 B delivered".
- With the nominal case, each lane has its nominal lane under it, and a "differs" row marks every epoch where a state differs.
- Under the lanes: the effects models' calibration status ("illustrative, not validated"), with the assumptions on hover, and a note when the head has a newer revision.
- A run with effects and no receiver track plays at the effects' own epochs. Every run World Model holds before DWM-218 is like that.

**Source:** `getRevision({ revisionId })` → `GET /revisions/{id}`, for the descriptors' header metadata. It's optional, shown in `sourceFeatures` as `revision`. Without it the lanes still draw and the model is described as unknown.

**Tests:** new `runEffects.test.mjs` (11), plus additions to `worldRuns`, `runPlayer`, `source` and `ownership`. The fixtures are generated from Foundation's `examples/ground-rf-mission` run, both cases (Foundation #44). `npm test` has 3450 passing; the 2 failures (`devCctv`, `previewServing`) also fail on `main`. `check:boundaries` passes.

**Checked in a browser:** the embedded QA host (`tools/embedded-qa`) now serves the pair. `__embeddedQa.openEffectsPair()` opens the contested run compared with the nominal one. At 02:00:42 the banner reads "COMMS unavailable · COLLECTION unavailable · NAVIGATION unavailable", and 4 epochs are marked as different.

Not in this PR: the client deep link passing `revisionId` and the nominal head (dataforge-client, next).
