title: feat(transit): add keyless RTD vehicles for Denver and Boulder
body:
## Draft status: full transit browser acceptance is not green

This is an intentionally **incomplete draft**, not a ready-to-merge submission. Updated RTD-specific live checks, offline tests and Tracking passed. Earlier full transit browser runs had failed and unexercised checks on both their upstream base and original candidate; the full gate has not been rerun on the updated head. Attribution under clause 4 also remains unresolved. The results and unresolved differences are disclosed below. Maintainer guidance on those shared rendering/fixture gates would be useful before marking this ready.

## Summary

Adds RTD's keyless live VehiclePositions feed to the existing **Transit / Movement** layer for Denver and Boulder.

- One `rtd-denver` feed and regional poll path, centered on Denver with a 70 km activation radius. Existing 40 km warm-feed hysteresis is unchanged; this is a polling heuristic, not a service boundary.
- Exact static-GTFS route-ID/type lookup: 120 bus, 6 tram/light-rail and 4 rail IDs. Unknown, new, unassigned and padded RTD IDs stay unclassified instead of defaulting to bus.
- The shared protobuf decoder retains its default route-ID trimming for existing providers. Only RTD opts into exact nonblank route-ID preservation at the feed-aware snapshot boundary; blank/whitespace-only values still become null. Encoded-wire regression tests cover RTD padding and existing-provider behavior, including MBTA. Other identifier/label normalization is unchanged.
- Reuses registered-feed fetching, response/redirect bounds, cache/backoff, per-vehicle freshness, renderer and lifecycle. Adds dynamic RTD attribution, tests and source/runtime/changelog documentation.

**Out of scope:** no dependencies, layer/share tokens, route geometry, arrivals, alerts, runtime static-GTFS downloads, HOP/CU feeds, RTD proxy-history retention, bundled live captures, or cockpit/follow-camera changes. Exactly 12 files change; platform-specific QA adaptations are not included.

## Data source and terms

RTD's [official realtime-feed page](https://www.rtd-denver.com/open-records/open-spatial-information/real-time-feeds) publishes the anonymous endpoint:

`https://open-data.rtd-denver.com/files/gtfs-rt/rtd/VehiclePosition.pb`

The data is subject to the [RTD GTFS Realtime License Agreement](https://www.rtd-denver.com/open-records/open-spatial-information/gtfs-realtime-license-agreement), **not CC BY or the project's MIT code license**. The agreement grants limited, non-exclusive, revocable rights subject to its full terms, including modification/discontinuance and trademark/non-endorsement provisions. This integration is unofficial and not affiliated with or endorsed by RTD. No RTD logo or map artwork is included; vehicle data is fetched at runtime.

**Attribution remains an open interpretation question:** clause 4 is broader than a logo-only prohibition. Factual text-only source credit and non-affiliation language do not themselves establish permission; clauses 8–9 do not clearly resolve that restriction. The rendered operator credit is unchanged pending guidance. No claim of RTD approval or an express credit exemption is made.

The route table was independently compared with all 130 IDs in RTD static GTFS version `Sep26-37243-12-13-20261009-141920`, checked 2026-10-12. Archive SHA-256: `c4e8dd19fb780f189c0c2b9fa20f0ceec0c1a2777263ea38f8ac1b53ca896fd6`. It needs refreshing as schedules change; new IDs remain unknown meanwhile. Regional feed totals are not Boulder-only vehicle counts or proof of passenger service.

## Updated validation — review fixes in `83f88d77`

- Integrated/tested upstream base: `ec7823daad6b83db8890e15e74a6770b60c89e27`.
- Current submitted head: `83f88d77342822e32bd49f4ea2b4642bcd6c9637`, a merge preserving the original published history.
- Reviewed upstream-to-candidate patch SHA-256: `2415375d74333d29a14a79ff9576bc35ed28e6d538d97aaab07453ec5d31ce0a`.
- Committed and remotely verified tree: `a06602bb39d1a99267b05d267b036cdada17bb4f`; all 2,049 frozen files matched after validation.
- Resolved the four review-identified conflicts, preserved Canadian feeds and NYC DOT disclaimer/tests, corrected the enabled region count to **17**, and used the current changelog-fragment policy.

| Check | Exact upstream base | Updated candidate |
|---|---:|---:|
| Focused suite | 178 passed | 207 passed |
| Full unit runner, including allocation phases | 7,640 passed / 0 failed / 10 skipped | 7,669 passed / 0 failed / 10 skipped |
| Tracking, native launch adaptations | 109 passed / 0 failed / 0 skipped | 109 passed / 0 failed / 0 skipped |
| Format, boundaries, doctor, i18n, production build | Passed | Passed |

Windows / Node 24.21.0; browser checks used Chrome 155.0.8059.40 and RTX 4070 D3D11. The previous Windows Codex fixture failure is fixed upstream by #997 (`91ac5c11`) and passes on both trees without a unit-test overlay. Independent agent review passed 238 focused tests and 578 encoded-wire snapshot cases; it is not human maintainer approval.

Live RTD dev and built-preview smoke passed over Denver and Boulder, including activation, disable/re-enable and actual rendered credit. Preview observations showed 71 Denver / 30 Boulder markers from 658 regional records; some Denver reports exceeded 90 seconds, so neither universal freshness nor passenger service is claimed. Tracking preserved original assertions, fixtures, deadlines and viewport. Initial external QA-server setup omitted required keyless terrain middleware, causing three ground-check failures on both variants; restoring the unchanged middleware produced the paired green runs. Initial failure evidence is retained. Owned test processes and profiles were removed; this round used no personal credentials.

**Full Transit: not run on the updated head.** The required visible Google photorealistic tileset was unavailable in this credential-free round. The historical failures below remain uncleared, not converted to passes by the smoke/Tracking checks.

At publication, main was `a571142d0ea1c09ceb000b26b2ecffff66df8b87`. A complete-tree three-way merge check was conflict-free; GitHub reported mergeable but behind main. These test results apply to the pinned base and reviewed candidate, not the later main.

Current-head CI: [run 38978407710](https://github.com/bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view/actions/runs/38978407710) is **action_required**, with zero jobs started. No CI pass is claimed.

## Historical validation provenance — original submission (not the updated head)

- Base: `8b8ccc9a81379e8b40d4be67610570ee5b159512`.
- Submitted head: `bf75cb011340441bca177dec157118a98ecfecd1`.
- Reviewed binary patch SHA-256: `074eebed4c19e42821e234ece1bf222e3171a82dba5e8423c2536cb3e5a6925e`.
- The committed base-to-head patch matches that reviewed/tested patch byte-for-byte. No feature edits were made to chase browser-gate failures.

| Check | Observed result |
|---|---|
| Complete restricted Linux/WSL unit runner, Node 24.21.0 | **6,275 passed, 1 skipped, 0 failed** |
| Doctor, format check, package boundaries, build, diff check | Passed |
| Independent agent review | PASS; 163 focused tests plus exact/padded-route probes |
| Live keyless RTD dev and built-preview smoke | Denver/Boulder activation, visible vehicles, RTD credit, disable/re-enable passed |
| Adapted native Tracking | Base and candidate each **109 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped** |
| Adapted native recovery | Base **649.5 ms**, candidate **573.7 ms**; both **7/8** trail samples against unchanged **>=6/8 within 2,000 ms** |
| Full adapted native transit | **Not passing**, detailed below |
| GitHub CI | [Run 38321552794](https://github.com/bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view/actions/runs/38321552794) reports **action_required**, with no jobs started; no CI pass is claimed |

The preview smoke saw one aborted request to the development-only setup-status endpoint, which production preview intentionally lacks; it is not described as zero network errors. Recovery is the existing synthetic Austin fixture, not an RTD-specific performance benchmark. A single paired recovery run does not establish statistical stability.

### Historical full native transit results — failures retained

Actual scene renderer: NVIDIA RTX 4070 / ANGLE Direct3D11, Chrome 154.0.8037.98, native browser sandbox enabled. Both full runs passed a separate preflight requiring an asset GET 200 and an active, shown photoreal tileset with ready content. All original gate assertions, fixtures, viewport sizes and inner timing budgets were retained.

| Variant | PASS | FAIL | UNEXERCISED | Total | Exit |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Unmodified base | 208 | 1 | 15 | 224 | 1 |
| RTD candidate | 206 | 4 | 14 | 224 | 1 |

**UNEXERCISED is not a pass or a skip:** the harness counts it toward failed acceptance. The original ordinary failures were:

- Base: retro bracket mode colours.
- Candidate: selected trail visibility at 900 m/45 degrees; 3,000-moving-vehicle budgets; bright white-hot matrix; dark NVG matrix.

Bounded follow-up diagnostics, not a replacement acceptance run:

- Untouched base reproduced the 3,000-vehicle budget failure: frame-interval p95 **25.7 ms > 25 ms**. Other recorded budget components passed. The original candidate's precise failed subcondition was not retained.
- Both variants reproduced the trail check with **0/8 eligible captures** because capture readiness was false, although final readiness was true. Transient readiness versus primitive-identity changes remains unresolved; this does not prove the trail pixels were invisible.
- Both reproduced dark-NVG contrast failure: **3/7 base** and **2/7 candidate** cores below the **0.593928** threshold, with zero bracket misses.
- Narrowed bright white-hot checks passed on both; the original candidate failure remains unexplained. The original retro failure was not reproduced.
- Live thermal/NVG/Noir views yielded **2/2/0** eligible samples on base and **1/1/0** on candidate, versus six required. Sensor masks and UI/label occlusion excluded most projected sprites while photoreal remained active/shown/loaded.

No RTD-specific regression was isolated, **but this is not proof that none exists** or that the remaining failures are harmless. Shared rendering/fixture issues and live-sample prerequisites require disposition before readiness. One diagnostic attempt timed out; another exported the relevant measurements but then hit a diagnostic-only null-detail exporter bug. Its fix was checked offline only; neither diagnostic is represented as complete acceptance.

<details>
<summary>Platform adaptations, earlier failures, and evidence limitations</summary>

Tracking/recovery/full-transit scripts were run from exact base and candidate copies with identical external Windows launcher/import adaptations. Installed Chrome and fresh private profiles replaced hardcoded platform paths; native D3D11 replaced explicit SwiftShader selection where present; unsafe no-sandbox/disable-web-security flags were removed. AI endpoints were denied. Original headless/headful intent, viewport, fixture bodies, reducers, assertions and deadlines remained intact. Reversing recorded adaptations reconstructed the complete original gate sources. These adaptations are outside the proposed patch.

The full gate's outer process ceiling was 1,800 seconds per variant, not an increased inner test budget; both completed rather than hitting it. Keyed raw logs/traces/screenshots were intentionally not exported. Only allowlisted result enums/numeric diagnostics were retained. Test profiles and processes were removed; known-token scans found no matches in scanned test/source/evidence files. This is not a claim of OS-wide sandboxing or exhaustive crash/pagefile secrecy.

Earlier WSL/Xvfb/SwiftShader attempts also failed and are not superseded into passes: both full runs hit an external 720-second timeout after frame/performance/live-style failures. Their aggregate failure counts were 22/26, including 13/14 unexercised checks. Required Google-3D checks were not exercised there. WSL recovery missed its unchanged deadline; later native recovery passed separately.

Windows harness issues and proposed launcher fixes were reviewed separately (#997, #865, #1061); none was folded into this feature patch. Public CI is a separate result and does not replace the local full-transit gate. No screenshots containing map credentials or raw machine-local artifacts are attached.

</details>

## AI assistance

Hermes Agent assisted with research, implementation, test execution, independent agent review and this PR description. The independent review is an **agent review**, not human maintainer approval. No human code-review or green full-browser-acceptance claim is made. This draft is submitted to make the implementation and remaining validation limits available for review, not to request bypassing them.

title: feat(layers): add SA Fire Incidents layer (CFS and MFS)
body:
Branch: `sa/fire-incidents` · New layer `sa-fire-incidents` (Events group) · Share-link token `5` (provisional: GNSS Integrity published `3` in #1108 and Air Quality published `4` in #568, so this PR moved to the next free token each time; will rerun `layer-token:next` again if another layer merges first)

## What

Live South Australian Country Fire Service and Metropolitan Fire Service incidents, plus CFS public warning areas, as a new Events layer. This picks up the regional-incidents idea from #702, with the review points from that PR addressed:

| #702 review point | How it's handled here |
|---|---|
| `ClassificationType.BOTH` | Warning polygons and their ground-clamped outlines both use `ClassificationType.BOTH` |
| `readResponseJsonCapped` | Every upstream read goes through the capped JSON reader (incidents 1 MiB, warnings 8 MiB per page) |
| Serve last good data on failure | Incidents and warnings each keep their own last good snapshot, served with `stale: true` and `X-Data-Stale`. 502 only before the first good fetch. A warnings outage never blanks incidents, and the UI says "warnings unavailable" rather than "no warnings" |
| Correct CC credit wording | Separate credits for incidents (CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, licence deed and dataset linked) and warnings (see licensing note) |
| Visible last-updated time | "Feed updated HH:MM ACDT/ACST" in the layer row and on every card |
| Parser and provider tests | 73 tests across records, cards, source, layer and proxy |

## Sources

- **Incidents:** `data.eso.sa.gov.au/feeds/prod/cfs_current_incidents.json`. The old CRIIMSON XML URLs listed on the CFS RSS page now return HTTP 200 with an HTML "File Unavailable" page. The proxy rejects any non-JSON response, so that page becomes a failure that serves last-good data, never "zero incidents".
- **Warnings:** the CFS ArcGIS `SACFS_Warnings_Public` FeatureServer, layers 0 (points) and 1 (polygons). The proxy follows `exceededTransferLimit` paging. Only warnings with `public = true` are shown, and expired ones are dropped.

## Notes for review

- **Times:** reported times arrive as `dd/mm/yyyy HH:MM` plus an IANA zone. They are converted to UTC with `Intl` in the record's own zone, never the server's. Tests cover both Adelaide daylight-saving boundaries.
- **Backoff:** a failed upstream is not retried before one TTL, doubling per consecutive failure up to 10 minutes. `Retry-After` is honoured on 429, capped at 15 minutes.
- **Card text:** the overlay cards paint text to canvas, so feed text has no HTML injection path. A warning's `message_link` is kept only if it is https on `cfs.sa.gov.au` and carries no credentials.
- **No invented join:** warnings carry an integer `incident_id`, while feed ids are strings like `F2610120119`. A warning is linked to an incident only when the digits match exactly; otherwise warnings display on their own.
- **Voice:** the layer is voice-off (`VOICE_OFF_LAYERS`), following the scope advice on #790. A manifest entry in `src/voice/layerManifest.js` is the natural follow-up.
- **Fixtures:** the test fixture is synthetic, with the feed's shape but no feed data, because the feed is CC BY-NC-ND.

## Licensing

- **Incidents:** CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 per the data.sa.gov.au dataset page. Fetched live at runtime and never bundled. `DATA_SOURCES.md` carries a NonCommercial note in the same style as the Google News and TeleGeography entries. `DATA_SOURCES.md` now states both licence terms, NonCommercial and NoDerivatives, and tells commercial deployers, or anyone redistributing a modified copy, to check the CFS terms.
- **Warnings:** the ArcGIS service publishes **no licence terms** (its `licenseInfo` is blank). It is credited to CFS, fetched live and never stored, and `DATA_SOURCES.md` says this plainly. Happy to drop the warnings half if you'd rather wait for explicit terms.

## Review follow-ups

A community review (quanticsoul4772) ran this PR live and listed what current `main` now requires. All of it is done:

- UI text goes through `t()`, `tn()` and `msg()`, with Spanish and Russian entries (34 new messages each). `npm run i18n` is clean.
- `sa-fire-incidents` is in `LAYER_NAME_KEYS` (`src/ui/layerNames.js`).
- `src/i18n/marker.js` and the other i18n modules are in the package-boundary lists, so `check:boundaries` passes.
- The changelog entry is the fragment `changelog.d/1089-sa-fire-incidents-layer.md`; `CHANGELOG.md` is untouched.
- `DATA_SOURCES.md` now names both terms of the incidents licence, NonCommercial and NoDerivatives.
- Share token: the review notes that #885, #887, #1089, #1090 and #1091 all hold token `5` provisionally. Per CONTRIBUTING a token is assigned against the merge-time base, so whichever of them merges later moves to the next free token (`npm run layer-token:next`).
- Known limit: dates on the cards keep English month abbreviations in es and ru, because the repo's date formatter would change the English output that the tests pin.

## Validation

Current head `6fee4a2`, on top of upstream `main` `1df2a272`. Run on Windows 11 with Node 24.21, inside the repo's pinned range.

- `npm test`: 7,759 pass, 0 fail of 7,769 (10 skipped).
- `npm run build`: passes.
- `npm run format:check`, `npm run check:boundaries` and `npm run i18n` (es and ru complete, no unmarked strings): pass.
- `npm run layer-token:check -- --base-ref origin/main`: 31 published, 1 new.

Evidence from the earlier round of this PR (Node 22.x, before the review follow-ups above):

- `npm run test:track`: **109 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped**, with no console errors and no HTTP 5xx across the run. This ran against a local dev server on a branch combining this PR with the other two Australian layer PRs (SA road events, BoM radar).
- Browser check on that same server, on both Google Photorealistic 3D Tiles and Esri World Imagery:
  - Live incidents render ground-clamped over Adelaide. At test time there were 9: 2 Going and 7 Controlled, including a Going MFS rubbish fire at Para Hills.
  - The row legend shows the CFS/MFS chips, counts by status, and "Feed updated 10:55 ACDT · No active public warnings".
  - The incident card shows "Going · L1 · MFS" and "Reported 13 Oct 10:34 ACDT", converted correctly from the feed's local time.
  - The share link round-trips. This was checked live while the layer held its earlier provisional token `3`; token `5` is covered by the registry and share-link unit tests.
  - The credits appear in the Data attribution popover.
- **Not verified live:** warning polygons. The CFS warnings service had 0 public warnings throughout, so the polygon path, `ClassificationType.BOTH` included, is covered by unit tests with synthetic features only.

- **Not re-run since the follow-ups:** `npm run test:track` and the browser check, and the new translations have not been viewed under `?lang=es` or `?lang=ru`. I will update this section when they have.

title: feat(layers): add Traffic SA road events layer
body:
Branch: `sa/road-events` · New layer `sa-road-events` (Movement group) · Share-link token `5` (provisional: GNSS Integrity published `3` in #1108 and Air Quality published `4` in #568, so this PR moved to the next free token each time; will rerun `layer-token:next` again if another layer merges first)

## What

Live South Australian roadworks, incidents, road closures and detours from Traffic SA (Department for Infrastructure and Transport), keyless. It has the same shape as #790 (QLD road events) and follows the review there: source geometry, type and impact text, source update time and snapshot stale state, with no voice or routing semantics.

## Source: three independent upstream groups

Traffic SA split its service, and the data.sa.gov.au dataset now lists three ArcGIS endpoints. Each is read as its own group:

| Group | Endpoint | Today |
|---|---|---|
| Roadworks | `maps.sa.gov.au/.../DPTIExtTransport/TrafficSAOpenData/MapServer/0`, with `TrafficSAOpenData2` as its only fallback | 1,422 (24-hour and long-term) |
| Incidents | `dit-cms-prod.geohub.sa.gov.au/.../TrafficSATime_OpenData/MapServer/0` | 11 (incident, collision, flooding, emergency waterworks) |
| Closures and detours | the same geohub service, `MapServer/2` | 11 (9 closures, 2 detours) |

**An earlier revision of this PR was reading a frozen layer.** It took incidents and closures from the old service's layer 1 and layer 0 incident rows. Checked directly against the live services: the old closures layer's newest start date is 4 May 2026, against 16 October for the new closures layer, and the old incident row dates from April. That revision's default view therefore showed months-old closures as current. This revision reads the live groups and never requests the frozen layers (a proxy test asserts no request is made to either layer 1).

## Notes for review

- **Independent groups.** Each has its own cache, backoff, `Retry-After` handling and last-good snapshot, so one group failing never blanks the others. The response keeps its old top-level fields and adds `sources: { roadworks, incidents, closures }`, each `live`, `stale` or `unavailable`. The route returns 502 only when all three are unavailable.
- **No fallback to stale data.** If the geohub service is unreachable and there is no last-good data inside the 6-hour stale limit, incidents and closures are omitted and the row says "Incidents and closures unavailable", rather than showing frozen closures as current. Roadworks still show.
- **Geo-block, reported but not verified.** A reviewer reports that the geohub host is blocked from outside Australia. I developed this inside Australia and could not verify that. If it is blocked for you, you get roadworks only, and the row says so.
- **Feed times are local clock times stored as UTC.** Both services' `start_date`/`end_date` hold Adelaide wall-clock time encoded as if it were UTC. Checked against the feeds' own `*_DATE_STRING` fields on the point layers: they agree once read as local Adelaide time. `records.js` converts them to real instants, with daylight-saving tests. The closures layers have no string date, so the same convention there is an assumption, stated in `DATA_SOURCES.md`.
- **Geometry admission.** A second reviewer (kvnloo) found that `normalizeLineGeometry` validated only the thinned copy of a line, so a bad vertex between the sampled points was silently dropped. It now validates every source vertex. The regression test fails on the old code.
- **Paging.** The geohub incidents layer has no `ESRI_OID`; a bad `orderByFields` answers HTTP 200 with an ArcGIS error object instead of a feature collection, which the proxy treats as a failed page. Incidents order by `incident_id`, closures by `ESRI_OID`. A failed page, or a feed still claiming `exceededTransferLimit` after 10 pages, fails that group's refresh.
- **New incident kinds.** Collision, flooding and emergency waterworks join incident as incident-class: default-visible, each with its own colour and a legend row shown only while present. Unknown types stay grey "Other". `traffic_dir` is JSON text on the new service and is parsed defensively into direction and lanes closed; plain text from the roadworks service still works.
- **Default view.** Incident-class kinds and all closures and detours show. The two roadworks kinds are hidden behind chips that show their counts, so the default view is not buried under ~1,400 amber markers.
- **Rendering.** Closures are red and detours violet and dashed, both clamped to the ground with `ClassificationType.BOTH`. Markers are ground-clamped `point` graphics, horizon-culled as in #790.
- **Text handling.** Text fields are stripped of tags, control characters and bidi characters. Lines are capped at 1,000 vertices each and 60,000 per snapshot. The stale limit is 6 hours, as in #790.
- **Voice.** The layer is voice-off (`VOICE_OFF_LAYERS`), matching #790's scope advice.

## Review follow-ups

A community review (quanticsoul4772) ran this PR live and listed what current `main` now requires; a second review (kvnloo) found the geometry issue above. All of it is done:

- UI text goes through `t()`, `tn()` and `msg()`, with Spanish and Russian entries (39 new messages each). `npm run i18n` is clean.
- `sa-road-events` is in `LAYER_NAME_KEYS` (`src/ui/layerNames.js`).
- The changelog entry is the fragment `changelog.d/1090-sa-road-events-layer.md`; `CHANGELOG.md` is untouched.
- The reviewer's question about the endpoint is answered in "Source" above: `maps.sa.gov.au` stays for roadworks, and incidents and closures moved to the geohub service.

title: feat(layers): opt-in Bureau of Meteorology rain radar for Australia
body:
Branch: `au/bom-radar` · New layer `bom-radar` (Weather group) · Share-link token `5` (provisional: GNSS Integrity published `3` in #1108 and Air Quality published `4` in #568, so this PR moved to the next free token each time; will rerun `layer-token:next` again if another layer merges first) · New runtime dependency: `basic-ftp`

## Why opt-in

The existing nowCOAST radar covers the contiguous US only. BoM radar is the only open radar source for Australia, but its anonymous-FTP products are licensed for **personal or in-organisation use only, with no redistribution** (https://www.bom.gov.au/catalogue/anon-ftp.shtml). So this layer:

- **Is off by default.** It only fetches when the server operator sets `BOM_RADAR_ENABLED=1` in their own `.env`, which `.env.example` documents with the caveat.
- **Never stores frames.** The operator's own local server fetches them live and holds them only in a bounded in-memory LRU (96 frames / 48 MB). Nothing goes to disk and nothing is bundled; tests use synthetic PNG bytes.
- **Carries the caveat in-app.** The BoM credit, including the personal-use caveat, is registered only once the layer actually draws.
- **Says it's off when it's off.** When disabled the layer exists but reads "BoM radar is off: set BOM_RADAR_ENABLED=1 (personal use only)" and makes no network requests.

It's a standalone layer rather than a source inside `weather-radar`, so it's trivially droppable if you'd rather not carry it.

## How

- **Discovery:** the server lists `ftp.bom.gov.au/anon/gen/radar/` once (cached 5 min) and finds every Australian radar in it (68 today). Georeferencing comes from BoM's own `.map` files, one per radar, cached 24 h, with a bounded warm-up. No radar coordinates are hard-coded.
- **Frame route:** `/api/bom-radar/frame/:file` accepts only names matching `^IDR(\d{2,3})([1-4])\.T\.(\d{12})\.png$` **and** present in the current listing. It checks the PNG signature before serving.
- **Product choice:** the client picks the radar nearest the view centre and a range by camera height (64 / 128 / 256 km), with hysteresis.
- **Rendering:** reuses the weather layer's imagery host, ordering and raised-shell helpers. It drapes on globe imagery and uses a raised shell on Google 3D Tiles. It loops the latest 12 frames, preloaded before playback, and pauses for reduced motion or a hidden tab.
- **Frame cleanup:** each BoM frame bakes a 16-px grey title bar and black caption text into the PNG. Those pixels (rows 0–15, plus exact header grey and pure black, neither of which is in BoM's rain palette) are made transparent once, at decode time, so both rendering hosts draw only the rain. This is display-only; the rain pixels are untouched.
- **Legend:** shows the radar name and frame time in the viewer's local time zone, e.g. "Adelaide 128 km · 02:39 ACDT · 4 min ago".
- **Dependency:** `basic-ftp` is used server-side only. `check:boundaries` passes, and `dist` contains no `basic-ftp`. It is listed in `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`.

## Known limits

- **Projection:** BoM images are gnomonic and are draped as a lat/lon rectangle from the `.map` corners. That's about 3.5 km off at the 128 km range and more at 256/512 km (documented).
- **First enable:** radar discovery can take about 20 s per server session, so the layer shows "Locating radars…" meanwhile.

## Review follow-ups

A community review (quanticsoul4772) ran this PR live and listed what current `main` now requires, plus two items of its own. All of it is done:

- UI text goes through `t()`, `tn()` and `msg()`, with Spanish and Russian entries (32 new messages each, plus the layer name). `npm run i18n` is clean.
- `bom-radar` is in `LAYER_NAME_KEYS`; the `package-boundaries.json` conflict is resolved; the changelog entry is the fragment `changelog.d/1091-bom-radar-layer.md`, which also says `basic-ftp` is a new runtime dependency, so existing checkouts need `npm install`.
- The FTP warm-up now stops when the dev or preview server closes. Before, `/products` kept reconnecting to ftp.bom.gov.au and the process lived on for about 105 s. After shutdown the proxy opens no connection, clears its idle timer and answers 502. Seven new tests fail without the fix.
- Licence: `DATA_SOURCES.md` and `.env.example` now also say that BoM's copyright page states radar imagery may be subject to a data licence agreement, which is needed to reproduce or publish it, and that nothing in the code limits use beyond the opt-in `BOM_RADAR_ENABLED` flag. Whether a public project should carry this at all, even opt-in, is a maintainer call; the layer is standalone so it is easy to drop.
- Share token: the review notes that #885, #887, #1089, #1090 and #1091 all hold token `5` provisionally. Per CONTRIBUTING a token is assigned against the merge-time base, so whichever of them merges later moves to the next free token (`npm run layer-token:next`).

## Validation

Current head `8e70877`, on top of upstream `main` `1df2a272`. Run on Windows 11 with Node 24.21, inside the repo's pinned range.

- `npm test`: 7,763 pass, 1 fail of 7,774. The one failure is "concurrent malformed-file repairs return the same persisted key" (`src/tools/mcpPanelKey.test.mjs`), a race that also fails about 1 run in 5 on its own in a file identical to upstream `main`.
- `npm run build`: passes.
- `npm run format:check`, `npm run check:boundaries` and `npm run i18n` (es and ru complete, no unmarked strings): pass.
- `npm run layer-token:check -- --base-ref origin/main`: 31 published, 1 new.

Evidence from the earlier round of this PR (Node 22.x, before the review follow-ups above):

- Live smoke test, one pass with nothing saved: 68 radars discovered, Adelaide `.map` parsed, 12 frames listed, a frame served as `image/png` in 170 ms (2 ms cached), and bogus frame/product names rejected with 404/400.
- `npm run test:track`: **109 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped**, run against a local dev server on a branch combining this PR with the two SA layer PRs (#1089, #1090).
- Browser check on that server with `BOM_RADAR_ENABLED=1`:

  - **Esri globe:** 12 frame imagery layers plus the basemap, with the legend "Adelaide 128 km · 09:59 ACDT · …".

The second has a regression test that fails without the fix.

title: fix: request HTTPS tiles for ion-backed Bing imagery
body:
On HTTP localhost, Cesium's ion-backed Bing provider inherits the page protocol, so the existing CSP blocks its HTTP tile requests. Resolve the ion endpoint using the supplied token and construct Bing Aerial and Bing Labels with `tileProtocol: 'https'` so both styles use HTTPS under the existing CSP.

The helper preserves ion attribution and Bing's per-tile credits, passes construction errors through, and keeps other ion imagery assets on the standard SDK factory. Regression coverage checks both styles, explicit token handling, attribution and error paths. The only other changes are the required changelog and runtime docs.

This is the standalone extraction of the Bing fix from draft #1065. Its local model gateway and World Monitor work is outside this PR; #1065 remains intact.

Thanks @ulihhhh for [suggesting the focused extraction and testing both Bing styles in Firefox with unchanged CSP](https://github.com/bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view/pull/1011#issuecomment-6133420524). This addresses the Bing loading issue discussed in #1011 without widening its CSP allowlist.

title: fix(cables): preserve feature ownership across multipart geometry
body:
## Summary

Cesium expands a GeoJSON `MultiLineString` into several entities. Cable ingestion previously paired entities with source features by array position, so later segments inherited the wrong styling, click destination and horizon-culling reference; entities beyond the feature count were left unassociated.

This carries a source-feature index through a copied GeoJSON collection and resolves every cable and landing entity back to its original feature. It retains one reference stem per source feature and leaves provider input objects, bundled data, dependencies and lifecycle behavior unchanged.

The bundled data contains 712 cable features, 1,913 segments, 301 multipart features and 17 duplicate source-ID groups. The fix therefore does not depend on unique IDs or guessed Cesium ID suffixes.

## Regression coverage

Five new real-Cesium regressions fail against pristine ingestion and pass with this change:
- Multipart styling, picking and horizon culling for every segment
- Missing, repeated and suffix-colliding IDs
- Multipart landing ownership and one reference stem per feature
- Ownership of every bundled cable segment
- Frozen provider collections, unchanged source properties, and a pre-existing property with the internal index name

The index remains observable in Cesium entity properties and default descriptions; the runtime documentation states this explicitly and notes that the application disables the Cesium info box.

## Current validation (2026-10-22)

Updated against upstream `7be5937fc3e3b10cdfa8d3f833536167268768ad`; final head `58a41759b52e795268e1be6cb2d1fa84547b2630`. title: fix(viewer): survive WebGL context loss with a guarded recovery
body:
Dropping or evicting the canvas' WebGL context — GPU process crash, OS backgrounding eviction, driver reset — kills the main viewer permanently. The drawing buffer collapses to 0×0 while the canvas layout size is unchanged, and the next frame dies in `FramebufferManager -> Texture` with `DeveloperError: Expected width to be greater than 0`, stranding the render loop behind Cesium's dead "Rendering has stopped" panel. A transient zero-size layout cannot reach this state (Cesium skips rendering a 0×0 canvas), which matches the issue triage. The app had no context-loss protection: `createApplicationViewer` (`src/app/viewer.js:109`) only tunes scene parameters, and the one `webglcontextlost` listener in the inline panel runtime (`src/app/globePanelRuntime.js:537-551`) neither `preventDefault()`s nor recovers. Root cause is upstream CesiumGS/cesium#5991.

The fix installs a context-loss guard (`src/app/contextLoss.js`): `webglcontextlost` is `preventDefault()`ed (without it the browser never offers the context back), the render loop stops before any frame renders into the dead context, and a render error while the context reports lost is the fallback detector for drivers that deliver the event late. Recovery lives in `createApplicationScene` (`src/app/scene.js`): the standalone page and iframe embeds reload once — the share-link hash already persists camera, layers and style — a second loss inside a 30 s cooldown (or refused web storage) degrades to a plain notice with a manual reload, and an inline panel never reloads its host page, keeping the panel runtime's notice. Cesium's error panel is dismissed when recovery takes over. The new module is registered in `package-boundaries.json`'s viewer/application-components group; `CHANGELOG.md` and `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md` document the behavior per repo convention.

Fixes #1067.

Validation:
- Red: `node scripts/qa-context-loss.mjs` at HEAD 8b8ccc9 with the fix reverted fails on its first assertion, "webglcontextlost must be preventDefault()ed" (`false !== true`, scripts/qa-context-loss.mjs:122). The pre-fix failure was reproduced in a scratch puppeteer headless + `WEBGL_lose_context` harness: `DeveloperError: Expected width to be greater than 0`, Cesium's "Rendering has stopped" panel, and a frozen render loop (postRender counter stalls). The zero-size layout route does not reproduce at HEAD (Cesium skips 0×0 canvases), matching the issue triage.
- Green, re-run on the final tree 5fa4f83:
  - `node --test src/app/contextLoss.test.mjs`: 9 passed, 0 failed.
  - `npm test`: 6,268 tests — 6,267 passed, 1 existing skip, 0 failed.
  - `npm run build`: passes on Node 24.
  - `npm run test:track`: 109 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped.
  - `node scripts/qa-context-loss.mjs`: context loss preventDefaults and stops the loop, recovers through exactly one guarded automatic reload, degrades to the cooldown notice with a manual reload, Cesium's dead panel is replaced, and a zero-size layout cycle stays healthy. The gate pins the event-first order because CDP runs showed Chrome dispatches `webglcontextlost` asynchronously; the error-first order is covered by the fallback-detection unit tests.
  - `node scripts/qa-application.mjs` and `node scripts/qa-panel-resize.mjs`: pass.
  - `npm run format:check` and `npm run check:boundaries`: pass.

title: fix(military): hold the last track and speed when a poll omits them
body:
`MilitaryFlightRecords.receive` turned a missing course into 0 (`courseDeg || 0`) and a missing speed into 0 (`speedMps ?? 0`) before calling `stickyNumber`. The hold-last-known-good branch therefore never ran.

When an adsb.lol row arrived without `track` or `gs`:
- the icon swung to north;
- the history fix got 0 kt / 0°, so dead reckoning froze the aircraft or flew it north;
- the HUD and voice context read "0°".

The civil `FlightRecords` holds the last value for the same input.

Example: poll 1 has track 270, speed 200 m/s. Poll 2 has both missing.

| | track | speed |
|---|---|---|
| Before | 0 | 0 |
| After | 270 | 200 |

0 is still the fallback until a value is known. A grounded row without a speed still reads 0, so a parked aircraft doesn't coast at its landing speed.

**Verified**
- New case in `src/layers/military/records.test.mjs`. It fails on `main`, and the ground-speed rule has its own failing mutant.
- `npm test`: 6245 pass.

- `npm run build`, `format:check` and `check:boundaries` all pass.

I updated `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md` and `CHANGELOG.md`.

title: fix(overpass): read failure phrases from the remark, not element tags
body:
`overpassLooksRuntimeError` and `overpassLooksRateLimited` searched the whole 200 body, element tags included. A valid result was refused as an upstream failure if any element's tags contained one of these phrases:
- "timed out" (e.g. a place named "Timed Out Escape Rooms")
- "runtime error"
- "out of memory"
- "too many requests"
- "rate_limited"

The refusal also put the endpoint on cooldown, 30 s to 5 min, for every other query: annotations, ALPR, installations and outlines.

Before: query A (the escape room) gets a 502 with retryAfter 30000. An unrelated query B is also refused, with no upstream call.
After: both return data.

The body is now parsed once. A data reply (one with an `elements` array) reports failure in its `remark`, so the phrase checks run on that. Any other body is matched whole as before: an HTML or plain-text error page, or JSON without elements such as `{"error":"rate_limited"}`. Rate-limited remarks still return 429 and honour `Retry-After`.

This only affects installs with `OVERPASS_UPSTREAMS` configured.

**Verified**
- New cases in `src/overpassProxy.test.mjs`. The tag-phrase case fails on `main`, and the remark and `{"error"}` cases each have a failing mutant.
- `npm test`: 6245 pass.
- `npm run test:track`: 109/109.
- `npm run build`, `format:check` and `check:boundaries` all pass.
- `qa-overpass-offload` fails here with "Sources did not settle for austin". It fails the same way on `main` (no Overpass configured, live tiles), and it makes zero `/api/overpass` requests either way.

I updated `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md` and `CHANGELOG.md`.

title: feat(infrastructure): add global power plants and renewable energy layer
body:
## What

Adds a new **Global Power & Renewable Energy Infrastructure** layer (`local-power-plants`) under the `Infrastructure` panel group.

- **Curated Dataset:** Bundles 147 major global power generation and energy storage facilities in `src/data/local_data/power_plants/power_plants.geojsonl` (derived from the World Resources Institute Global Power Plant Database and OpenStreetMap, ODbL 1.0 / CC BY 4.0). Covers Nuclear, Hydroelectric, Solar, Wind, Geothermal, Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS), and Gas/Thermal facilities.
- **Layer Presentation:** Cyber HUD aesthetics matching existing Datacenters and Dams layers, using dynamic point graphics, status badges, and cyber icon (`⚡`).
- **Analyst & Voice Integration:** Fully integrated with the analyst query engine and voice manifest (`"power plants"`, `"power station"`, `"nuclear plant"`, `"solar farm"`, `"wind farm"`, etc.).
- **URL & Share Links:** Allocated immutable layer token `'3'` in `LAYER_STATE_REGISTRY` and `src/data/layerStateTokenReservations.json`.
- **Attribution & Docs:** Updated `src/data/dataCredits.js`, `DATA_SOURCES.md`, and added provenance README in `src/data/local_data/power_plants/README.md`.

## Why

God's Eye View previously had infrastructure layers for Datacenters and Dams, but lacked power grid and generation infrastructure. Adding global renewable energy and power generation facilities gives users and analysts direct spatial visibility into global energy grids and critical energy infrastructure without requiring external API keys.

title: fix(satellites): reject TLE pairs with mismatched catalog numbers (#906, #936)
body:
Follow-up to #906 and #936 as requested by @asturksever.

### Summary
When parsing three-line TLE sets, parseTleText checks for line1.startsWith('1 ') and line2.startsWith('2 '). However, if a corrupt or spliced catalog contains mismatched lines (e.g. line 1 belonging to one satellite and line 2 belonging to another), they could be mistakenly paired.

This change:
Validates that tleCatalogNumber(line1) === tleCatalogNumber(line2) and neither is null before pairing lines into an entry.
Allows tleCatalogNumber(line) to extract the NORAD catalog number from either line 1 or line 2.
Re-synchronizes at the next valid set when mismatched pairs are encountered.
Adds unit test coverage asserting rejection of mismatched pairs and recovery on the next valid set.
Updates CHANGELOG.md referencing #906 and #936.

Ref: #906, #936

title: fix(radio): reject null-body and out-of-range mirror statuses instead of crashing
body:
A Radio Browser mirror answering 204, 205 or 304, or a status above 599, crashed the whole local dev/preview server, so every layer went down, not just radio.

`fetchPinnedRadioResponse` built the `Response` inside the raw `https.request` callback, which runs outside its promise. The `Response` constructor throws for those statuses (and for an invalid reason phrase), and that TypeError/RangeError was uncaught.

| Mirror reply | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| 204 | process exits 1 (`TypeError: Response constructor: Invalid response status code 204`) | resolves with a null body |
| 304 | process exits 1 | resolves with a null body |
| 700 | process exits 1 | rejects; the existing mirror failover tries the next mirror |

204/205/304 get a null body, and the socket is drained so keep-alive can reuse it. The callback body is in a try/catch that rejects, the same guard `local-receivers.js` already uses.

**Verified**
- New tests in `src/data/radioProxy.test.mjs` cover 204/205/304, 600/999 and an invalid reason phrase. They mock `https.request`, and each races the fetch against an uncaught exception, so the old code fails at once instead of hanging. All 6 fail on `main`.
- `npm test`: 6249 pass.
- `npm run test:track`: 109/109.
- `npm run build`, `format:check` and `check:boundaries` all pass.

I updated `CHANGELOG.md` and `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md`.

AI-assisted (Claude); I reviewed and tested the change.

title: fix(search): reject coordinate queries with empty components from consecutive delimiters (#1021)
body:
Fixes #1021

### Summary
In src/search/coordinateParser.js, splitComponents(query) used .filter(Boolean) on split parts. As a result, queries with consecutive, leading, or trailing delimiters (such as 40,,74, 40, 74,, ,40, 74, 40;;74) had empty elements silently filtered out, causing them to be incorrectly accepted as valid 2-component decimal coordinates rather than declining and falling through to subsequent geocoders.

### Changes
- In splitComponents, preserve trimmed components and ensure trimmed.length === 2 && trimmed[0] && trimmed[1].
- - Add test coverage in src/search/coordinateParser.test.mjs for queries with consecutive/leading/trailing delimiters.
- - Add CHANGELOG entry referencing #1021.

fix(satellites): decode Alpha-5 catalog numbers instead of collapsing to NaN
body:
Fixes #751.

satellite.js keeps six-digit catalog numbers as Alpha-5 strings like `A0000`, and the three catalog builders converted them with `Number(satrec.satnum)`, yielding `NaN`. Since `Set`/`Map` treat every `NaN` as the same key, the first Alpha-5 satellite was stored under `NaN` and every later one was dropped as a duplicate.

New `noradIdFromSatnum` decoder in `src/layers/satellites/policy.js` (already imported by all three sites): a leader A-Z skipping I and O stands for 10-33 in the ten-thousands place (`A0000` -> 100000, `Z9999` -> 339999); five-digit fields pass through unchanged; anything else goes through `Number` exactly as before. Used at `ingestion.js:111`, `catalog.js:116`, `orbits.js:287`.

Verification:
- new `src/layers/satellites/norad.test.mjs` (4 tests: five-digit passthrough, A0000/Z9999 + I/O-skip boundaries, Number fallback, satellite.js round trip proving two Alpha-5 sats get distinct ids)

title: feat(border-waits): add a Border Wait Times layer from U.S. CBP
body: ### What A **Border Wait Times** layer (DATA ▸ Movement), off by default. It shows the live wait to enter the U.S. at every land crossing U.S. Customs and Border Protection reports: 85 today, along both the Canadian and Mexican borders. - **Markers:** one per crossing, coloured by the passenger-vehicle wait: - green under 15 min, yellow 15–29, orange 30–59, red 60+ - grey for closed, blue for no wait reported - each has an ambient minute label - crossings with no passenger lanes, such as San Ysidro PedWest, use the pedestrian wait, then the commercial one - **Card:** selecting a marker lists each reported lane (standard, NEXUS/SENTRI, Ready, FAST, pedestrian) with minutes and lanes open, plus CBP's update time, port hours and any notice. For the 26 northern crossings the Canada Border Services Agency reports, the card also shows the wait **into Canada**, for example "Into Canada · Cars no delay · Trucks 5 min · updated 11:18 EDT". - **Legend:** the row legend counts crossings in each band. - **Voice:** "show border waits" works, and `analyst_query` can answer questions like "longest border waits". ### How - **Proxy:** `server/providers/borderWaits.js` serves `/api/border-waits`. - It reads only `https://bwt.cbp.gov/api/bwtnew`, which is one keyless document of about 135 KB for every crossing. - Reads are timed out and capped at 2 MB, and redirects are refused. Results are cached for 5 minutes, concurrent requests share one fetch, and there is a per-client limit. - If CBP is unreachable or returns something malformed, it serves the last good snapshot marked stale (`X-Data-Stale`); the card says so. With no snapshot yet, it returns a sanitized 502. - **Waits into Canada:** the same proxy also reads CBSA's current land-border CSV (`https://www.cbsa-asfc.gc.ca/bwt-taf/bwt-eng.csv`, keyless, about 3 KB). - It has its own 5-minute cache and stale fallback. - CBSA is optional: if it fails, CBP's waits are still served, with `canada: { available: false }`. - `src/layers/borderWaits/canada.js` maps each CBSA office to the CBP crossing it faces. The four offices with no CBP crossing (Lacolle Routes 221 and 223, Hemmingford, North Portal) are logged once and skipped. - **Normalization:** `src/layers/borderWaits/records.js` runs server-side. - A malformed document never replaces the last good one. - A single unplaceable crossing is listed in `unlocated` and logged once, rather than dropped silently or blanking the other 84. - **Locations:** CBP publishes no coordinates, so `src/layers/borderWaits/crossings.js` bundles a point per CBP `port_number`. - 72 come from the crossing's Wikidata item (CC0); the other 13 from the BTS *Border Crossing Entry Data* port location (public domain). Each entry names its source. - CBP lists some physical crossings more than once (Otay Mesa four times, Bridge of the Americas three times), and those entries share one point. - **Layer:** `src/layers/borderWaits/index.js` follows the Fire Perimeters lifecycle and click selection. It owns its picks, like ALPR and bikeshare. ### Data source, license, and attribution - **Wait times:** U.S. Customs and Border Protection. A work of the U.S. federal government, so U.S. public domain (17 U.S.C. §105). Credited as "Border wait times: U.S. Customs and Border Protection". - **Waits into Canada:** Canada Border Services Agency, under the [Open Government Licence – Canada](https://open.canada.ca/en/open-government-licence-canada), which requires attribution. Credited as "Waits into Canada: Canada Border Services Agency. Contains information licensed under the Open Government Licence – Canada." - **Crossing locations:** Wikidata (CC0) and U.S. DOT Bureau of Transportation Statistics (public domain). Credited in the attribution lightbox. - **Privacy:** both are aggregate per-crossing figures; nothing identifies or tracks people. - **Docs:** DATA_SOURCES.md, `dataCredits.js`, CURRENT-STATE.md and CHANGELOG.md are updated. ### Share links Layer token `3`, from `npm run layer-token:next -- border-waits`. It is reserved in the ledger and registry, and the pinned count and token tests are updated, as CONTRIBUTING describes. `layer-token:check --base-ref upstream/main` reports 29 published, 1 new. ### Testing - **New unit tests (34):** - `records.test.mjs`: - lane normalization and the pedestrian fallback - unplaceable crossings - malformed documents - values outside their contract - every crossing CBP reported on 2026-10-13 is placed - every point sits on the international boundary, checked against the bundled Natural Earth outlines with a 5 km tolerance for simplified rivers; the Point Roberts exclave is checked against Canada only, because the outlines drop it. Moving the Ambassador Bridge 12 km inland fails this test. - `cards.test.mjs`: band edges, closed and unreported crossings, card lines, the stale note and label ordering. - `layer.test.mjs`: lifecycle, click selection, a sibling layer's pick, stale refresh, failed refresh, and release on disable and destroy. - `canada.test.mjs`: CBSA value parsing, the CSV with BOM and CRLF, refusing a changed or foreign file, every office mapping to a distinct placed crossing, and attaching the waits to rows. - `borderWaitsProxy.test.mjs`: both hooks, the fixed upstream, the 5-minute cache with coalescing, stale-on-failure for network errors, HTTP errors and malformed bodies, the 502, 405 and 404 responses, and logging an unplaced crossing once; for CBSA, the join onto the right crossing, CBP being served when CBSA fails, CBSA falling back to stale on its own, and logging an unmatched office once. - **Pins re-derived for the new layer:** - catalog and registry counts, the panel order, reference sources and the token-ledger scenarios - the voice tool schema digests. I diffed the schema before and after: the only changes are the three `border-waits` enum entries, its alias hint and its field hint. - **Results:** - `npm test`: 6,278 passed, 0 failed, 1 skipped - `npm run test:track`: 109 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped - `npm run build`, `format:check`, `check:boundaries` and `layer-token:check` are clean - **New browser gate:** `npm run qa:border-waits` runs against the dev server with the live CBP feed, and all checks pass. It covers the panel row, all 85 crossings loading through the proxy, the five Michigan crossings and their waits into Canada, painted labels, clicking the Ambassador Bridge marker opening its card, a clean disable, and no page errors. ### Out of scope - Waits into Mexico - The four CBSA offices with no CBP crossing - History and trends - Ferries (CBP doesn't publish waits for them) - Predictions

title: feat(cctv): add a Maryland camera pack from MDOT SHA CHART
fix(flights): don't treat OpenSky's position-less rows as a partial snapshot
body:
OpenSky's state-vector spec allows null longitude/latitude, and every live `/states/all` has about 50 such rows. `admitRecords` rejects them, so `complete: records.length === rows.length` was false on effectively every poll. While a snapshot is incomplete, `FlightRecords.absence()` retains every aircraft seen in the last 300 s.

As a result, the stale fade, `MISSING_POLL_LIMIT` and the landed fast-cull (`LANDED_MISSING_POLL_LIMIT`) never ran in production. An aircraft that left the feed stayed on the globe at full opacity for about 5 minutes: first dead-reckoning, then frozen, including landed planes parked at airports.

Measured on two live snapshots taken 325 s apart (7,816 and 7,942 rows, 52 and 50 of them position-less), for the 696 aircraft that vanished between them:

| | retained | stale | removed |
|---|---|---|---|
| Before | 696 | 0 | 0 |
| After | 3 | 449 | 244 |

The 3 still retained are still in the feed, just without a position.

A row with a valid icao24 and null lon/lat no longer makes the snapshot partial. It is returned in `retainIds` and keeps only its own aircraft, within the same 5-min bound, unless that aircraft is likely landed. These still mark the snapshot partial:
- id-less rows
- half-null rows
- truncated rows
- out-of-range rows

A feed with no positioned rows is still malformed, as the existing `flights.test.mjs` case requires. The change is opt-in per source, so military (readsb) behaviour is unchanged.

Known limits, left as they are:
- An aircraft retained this way shows no stale cue while retained (the existing behaviour for retained contacts).
- The adsb.lol regional fallback drops position-less contacts on the server.
- Military has the same pattern (82 of 219 rows in one `/v2/mil` fetch). That's a follow-up.

**Verified**
- New `contract.test.mjs` and `records.test.mjs` cases. They fail on `main`, and every assertion was mutation-checked.
- `npm test`: 6246 pass.
- `npm run test:track`: 109/109.

title: fix(maps): retry the real imagery and terrain provider after a fallback
body:
On the keyless default (no Google key), one transient failure at boot locked in the fallback for the whole session:
- **Imagery:** `_getImageryProvider` cached the OSM construction fallback under `esri-imagery`. Re-selecting "Esri Satellite" kept showing OSM until reload.
- **Terrain:** `createKeylessTerrain` turned any Re:Earth failure into flat `EllipsoidTerrainProvider` terrain and reported it as success. The controller cached it and latched `_terrainMode`, so the globe stayed flat until reload.

Before: a network blip at boot means OSM and/or a flat globe for the session. After: the fallback still shows at once, and switches never wait on a retry. One background timer retries the real provider behind whichever fallback is on screen, starting at 30 s and doubling up to a 10 min cap.

When the real provider comes back:
- **Esri:** it is cached and switched in automatically. If a switch is in flight, that happens once the switch settles.
- **Terrain:** it is installed live with a render request, keeping the same flat instance until then. Behind a 3D tileset it is only cached, and the next globe activation installs it.

Fallbacks that aren't on screen aren't retried, and `destroy()` cancels the timer.

**Verified**
- New `controller.test.mjs` and `sourceFactories.test.mjs` cases. They cover:
  - immediate fallback;
  - backoff and the cap;
  - retry only while shown;
  - recovery during a switch;
  - live terrain swap;
  - hidden globe;
  - the stale-read race;
  - destroy.

  Each is mutation-checked.
- `npm test`: 6253 pass.
- `npm run test:track`: 109/109.
- `npm run build`, `format:check` and `check:boundaries` all pass.

Known limits:
- Each failed terrain retry still logs `createKeylessTerrain`'s warning, at most once per backoff step.
- An Esri recovery during an open imagery-comparison lease behaves like the existing tile-failure fallback: `release()` keeps the recovered stack.

I updated `CHANGELOG.md` and `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md`.

AI-assisted (Claude); I reviewed and tested the change.

title: feat(scanner): add police scanner layer with Radio Browser feeds
body:
## What

Adds a police/public-safety scanner map layer. Live audio streams are proxied through the server so stream URLs never reach the browser.

Feeds are registered in `config/scanner-feeds.json` with id/name/lat/lon/type only. The server holds a separate registry of real URLs and looks them up by feed id.

## Data source & license

Radio Browser (public API, no key). Station metadata and stream URLs are stable.

## Security

- All audio goes through the server proxy; the browser never supplies a URL
- SSRF protection via `isPublicRadioAddress` (same helper the radio layer uses)
- Concurrency capped at 8 simultaneous streams
- Feed URLs are allowlisted to http/https at load time

## No individual tracking

Layer maps radio infrastructure only — feed locations and audio. No PII, no user queries.

## Scope note

The default `config/scanner-feeds.json` ships **Radio Browser streams only** — live feeds that work out of the box.

An `openmhz` feed type is fully implemented and tested in this PR (import script, server proxy, layer playback queue), but OpenMHz's public API is best-effort with no documented contract, and its `/systems` endpoint currently returns 403 for programmatic access. It's disabled by default; users can regenerate the feed file with `scripts/import-openmhz-systems.mjs` against a saved `systems.json` if they want it.

## Tests

- `src/layers/scanner/importOpenMhz.test.mjs` — import script
- `src/layers/scanner/model.test.mjs` — feed validation, call queueing
- `src/layers/scanner/source.test.mjs` — client source
- `src/layers/scanner/proxy.test.mjs` — server proxy (SSRF, host allowlist, malformed payloads)

title: feat(street-level): "show me X on Street View" — assistant action, view field and share link
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #966. "Show me the Eiffel Tower on Street View", "street view of 10th Street in Sacramento" and "Times Square on Mapillary" now work by voice, or typed into the same session. KartaView and Panoramax work by name too. Views and share links carry the same request.

- **`show_street_level` action** (`src/voice/gevActions.js`). One call runs these stages in order, and each reports its own failure so the spoken line says which part did not happen:
  1. **Key** (`key`). Checks that the source has its key. A keyless source explains itself and changes nothing, as a chip does.
  2. **Location** (`location`). Flies to the place at street framing and waits for arrival. The place can be a name, coordinates, a pointed spot, a numbered item, or nothing for the view centre.
  3. **View** (`view`). Stops if cockpit, clean view, recording or scene playback hides the panel.
  4. **Map** (`map`). Switches to the map the source needs. Google Street View shows only on Google 3D, per Maps Platform terms §3.2.3(e).
  5. **Provider** (`provider`). Lights that source in STREET LEVEL the way a chip click does: one source at a time, kept in the share link.
  6. **Layer** (`layer`). Turns the layer on.
  7. **Imagery** (`imagery`). Opens the nearest photo. An empty result names a 360°, flat or SINCE filter that narrowed it.

  `provider` is `google` for "Street View", or `mapillary`, `kartaview` or `panoramax` by name. When none is named, the lit source is used. `"pointer"` and `referent:n` resolve as they do for `fly_to_location`.
- **Lookup radius.** `openNearest` takes `radiusM`. Google honours it up to 250 m for the action and links, since a landmark's centroid is rarely within 50 m of a street. Ground clicks and the OPEN button keep 50 m, and Mapillary's Graph API caps the radius at 50 m. Mapillary's nearest search asks for 100 photos, the API's most. The API cuts the radius's photos at the limit in no particular order, so the distance sort and the imagery filter need the whole set.
- **Views and links.**
  - A view's `street_level` names a source and a point. The point defaults to where the camera looks; `show_in_gods_eye_view` measures that from the terrain under the camera.
  - A `google` source brings `map: photoreal` and refuses any other map. `street_level` cannot be combined with `follow`.
  - Links carry it as `sl=<source>,<lat>,<lon>`. `show_in_gods_eye_view` accepts it, the globe panel applies it through the action, and a plain link runs the action once the link has restored.
- **Billing: a plain link never loads a Google panorama without a click.**
  - A link with `sl=google` flies there, switches to Google 3D, lights Street View, then arms the lookup and opens the panel. A toast points at OPEN GOOGLE STREET VIEW, and one press loads the panorama.
  - The press uses the link's point only while the view centre is within 1 km of it.
  - Posted views, and the MCP globe panel's own link for a result issued in the last five minutes, open the photo. A host that mounts the panel again later (reopening a conversation) hands back the old result, which only arms.
  - Mapillary, KartaView and Panoramax links open at once; none of them bills per image. SECURITY.md describes all of this.
- **Where the photo shows.**
  - Embed mode hides the rail that holds the panel, so an open photo moves to an overlay on the globe. Esc closes it.
  - On a phone, a photo that opens, or a link that arms, opens the Cameras tab sheet.
- **`fly_to_location` returns its coordinates** on every branch (preset, curated POI, geocode), so composite actions can use them.
- **`setMapStack` reports the controller's own reason** when a stack is unavailable. Before, Google 3D without a Maps key said "requires a Cesium ion token".

### Decisions for reviewers

- **Prompt budget raised from 55,500 to 56,500 characters** (`src/voice/pointAndAsk.test.mjs` and `src/voice/integrationContract.test.mjs`, [fed397a7](https://github.com/bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view/pull/1113/commits/fed397a764ca736f409918d982f54e506e0f2e56)). Main's voice geometry (#846) left 290 characters under 55,500. This PR adds about 940: the `show_street_level` tool (731) and its routing rule. With every tool the prompt measures 56,147, 353 under the new budget; a session without an Overpass measures 55,552, and with one, 56,307. The alternative is trimming about 650 characters from the tool and rule wording to stay under 55,500.
- **Mapillary `nearestImage` restored** ([ed2703d3](https://github.com/bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view/pull/1113/commits/ed2703d345e88f702f0d59e07f821ff82ee4b60b)). The action and `sl=mapillary` links need a nearest-image lookup, which the slim Street Level layer (#974) dropped. It is one Graph `images?lat&lng&radius` request per action or link, never per click.

## Test plan

At head [0ec57057](https://github.com/bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view/pull/1113/commits/0ec57057fa2bf6692cdbe8f608984b2729c27906). After [7703090d](https://github.com/bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view/pull/1113/commits/7703090d906f58fc53f4a7caa5d128fc1a62e1ab) and the main merge [34f694c6](https://github.com/bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view/pull/1113/commits/34f694c6) (voice geometry), at [fed397a7](https://github.com/bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view/pull/1113/commits/fed397a764ca736f409918d982f54e506e0f2e56): unit 10,249 pass, 0 fail, and format, boundaries, i18n, changelog and the keyless build pass. The browser gates below ran at 0ec57057.

title: fix(tools): identify historical camera fallback imagery
body:
When a registered camera's upstream image fails, the existing CCTV proxy can return historical Google Street View imagery with `X-CCTV-Source: streetview`. The portable frame source discarded this header, so `get_cctv_snapshot` described that image as the camera's current view and credited its transport agency.

Retain the known frame-source kind and label Street View fallbacks as historical Google imagery. Original upstream frames keep their current-view label and camera credit; placeholders are unavailable snapshots. Missing/custom unknown provenance is explicit (`current_view: null`) and preserves catalog attribution. The tool name and inputs are unchanged; its title is now "Camera snapshot". `current_view` distinguishes camera-feed origin from historical fallback, not measured capture time or image freshness.

The regression runs the actual mounted CCTV proxy through the portable source, tool catalog and MCP image response. Only registered fictional input, upstream failure/image responses and a dummy Google key are fixtures; every upstream request is intercepted. It covers restored original images, historical fallback, synthetic refusal through MCP, unknown provenance and the proxy's four known header kinds.

title: feat: support cctv caltrans video
body:
# feat: Caltrans Live HLS Video Streams (CCTV_CALTRANS_VIDEO env var)

## Summary

Enable live HLS video streams from Caltrans traffic cameras when `CCTV_CALTRANS_VIDEO=1` is set in the environment. When disabled (default), cameras still display still-image snapshots — fully backward compatible.

## Changes

### `server/providers/cctv/sources.js`
- Added `hasCaltransVideoData()` — detects `imageData.streamingVideoURL` presence in Caltrans API responses
- Added `extractCaltransVideoUrl()` / `extractCaltransSnapshotUrl()` — extracts HLS stream URL and still-image URL from the API's `imageData` field
- Modified `loadCaltransSourcesFromOpenData()` — when `CCTV_CALTRANS_VIDEO=1` and video data exists, cameras get `feedType: 'hls'`, video URL as `url`, still image as `snapshotUrl`

### `.env.example`
- Added `# CCTV_CALTRANS_VIDEO=1` — set to `1` to enable live HLS video streams from Caltrans cameras instead of still images only

### `CHANGELOG.md` + `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md`
- Documented the new opt-in feature

## How it works

The Caltrans API (`cwwp2.dot.ca.gov`) provides `imageData.streamingVideoURL` fields containing HLS playlist URLs (e.g., `https://wzmedia.dot.ca.gov/D4/W580_JWO_24_IC.stream/playlist.m3u8`). When `CCTV_CALTRANS_VIDEO=1` is set and the API returns video data, cameras register with `feedType: 'hls'` — the frontend already supports HLS playback via hls.js, so no frontend changes are needed.

## Verification

- `npm run build` and `npm run preview` pass (frontend already supports `feedType: 'hls'`)
- Follows existing patterns: same approach as DelDOT (`feedType: 'hls'`), Vegvesen, and other CCTV sources
- Default behavior (`CCTV_CALTRANS_VIDEO` absent or `0`) is identical to before — still images only, fully backward compatible

title: Street Level: KartaView as the third, keyless imagery provider
body: ## What this changes KartaView joins Street Level as its third imagery provider, beside Mapillary (#768) and Google Street View (#966). It needs no key: the browser talks to KartaView's public API directly. - **Chip and coverage.** A KARTAVIEW chip (purple) starts off; one source is lit at a time, as before. Below about 6 km the streets KartaView has photos of draw as lines, from its z14 JSON tiles below 2.5 km and z13 tiles above. Higher up the panel says to zoom in, and an empty view says there are no KartaView photos in it. The coverage line reads "N streets in view · click a line for its nearest photo". - **Opening a photo.** A click on a line opens the nearest photo within 50 m and leaves the camera where it is. The photo's drive then shows as cones; a cone opens its photo (and frames it, as for Mapillary). **‹ ›** in the viewer, or ← →, step along the drive. The panel counts the drive's photos ("2,250 images in this sequence"). - **Marker and direction.** The open photo has its own marker, a purple view cone (Street View's is blue), not the default pin Mapillary uses. - It points along the drive: the camera direction is the direction of travel to the next photo a few metres on. This direction is used for the marker, the cones, FOLLOW and a panorama's centre. - KartaView's `heading` is the device compass. Whole drives read `0` (no compass), and others sit a steady ~110° off inside a car. - The compass stands in only until the drive loads (`0` counts as unknown). - **Viewer.** - **Flat photos** show in an `` with FIT / FILL: 1,280 px first, and 2,560 px only once the viewer is expanded. - **360° photos** use a small WebGL equirectangular renderer (`panorama.js`: one full-screen triangle, no new dependency). The image is decoded off the main thread into an ImageBitmap. It loads at 1,024 px, then 2,048 px docked or 4,096 px expanded. - **Looking around:** drag, pinch, wheel, or Shift+← →, ↑ ↓ and + −. FIT / FILL hide for panoramas. - **GPU reset:** a lost WebGL context redraws the photo on a new canvas, facing the same way. - The globe marker and FOLLOW track the view direction. - **Attribution.** "Street Level: imagery © KartaView contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0" on the globe while it is lit (KartaView terms §4). - **Filters.** IMAGERY (ALL / 360° / FLAT) and SINCE apply to KartaView as to Mapillary. - **Lines.** KartaView filters coverage on its server only in its PNG tiles; its JSON tiles come back empty once a filter is asked for. So a filtered tile's PNG is a mask over the cached JSON lines: a segment stays when at least half the points along it lie on drawn pixels. On a Jakarta tile with 360° on, 332 of 1,041 segments lie on it, 676 miss it and 33 fall between. The check takes 1–5 ms a tile. - **Changing the filter** keeps the drawn lines until the filtered ones are in. Line shapes are reused, so only the masks are fetched, cached per filter and tile. - **Slow tiles.** KartaView draws a filtered tile on demand: a dense one can answer 504 after 60 s and be ready 1–3 s later. A timeout or 5xx is asked again 4 s later, four tries in all, then the panel says it could not filter the area in time. - **Photos.** The line click asks the photo search for the projection and date. The cones follow the filter as Mapillary's do. When photos are near but none pass, the panel says so. - **SINCE is the upload date** for KartaView, the only date its server filters by, applied to lines, photos and cones alike (the cut-off is its UTC day). While KartaView is lit, a note under the slider says "KartaView: by upload date". Providers declare this with a new optional, validated `sinceBasis: 'upload'` field. - **Share links.** KartaView travels in the existing provider-switch field: the app writes `0.m.0_0.r.google-0*kartaview-1`, and a hand-written `0.m.0_0.r.kartaview-1` works too. No new layer token. ### KartaView API behaviour the provider handles All verified against the live API: - **Coverage host.** The documented host `api.openstreetcam.org` answers but serves empty coverage tiles; `api.kartaview.org` serves them. - **Storage host.** Photo records' `fileurl*` always name `storage1`, but a photo stored on another host (`storage2`…) 404s there. URLs are built from `storage` + `filepath*`, and a `fileurl*` fallback must itself be an https storage host. - **Archived photos.** Many photos answer 409 for their file, while a HEAD says 200. - A line click probes the six nearest photos at once with a GET cut off at the headers, and opens the nearest one that can be shown; where all are archived the panel says so. - ‹ › skip archived photos. - Only a definite answer is remembered; a storage timeout or 5xx is asked again. - **Connections and rate limits.** `api.kartaview.org` speaks HTTP/1.1, so the browser gets six connections. - Tiles take three, photo lookups two and sequence pages one (newest first), so a click never waits behind slow tiles. - The photo API answers 429 to more than about three requests at once; a 429 is retried with backoff (capped at 10 s). - **Slow lookups.** Lookups sometimes take 11 s or more, then answer in 3 s when asked again. A lookup gets 8 s, then 15 s once more. No network, or a refused request, says so and is not retried. - **Sequence pages.** Pages follow photo ids, which only roughly follow the index. - A photo's page is found by search (halving past the end when many photos were deleted). - A neighbour page joins near an edge. - The cones re-centre whenever a photo of the selected drive opens on another page. - **Tiles.** Tiles come uncompressed and uncacheable (up to ~0.7 MB and several seconds each). - The last 24 decoded tiles are kept for 10 minutes while KartaView is lit. - Segments are chained in linear time, capped at 20,000 per tile and 5,000 points per line. - Answers are chunked without a length, so the 16 MB cap counts bytes while reading. - **Photo link.** kartaview.org's photo pages fail for signed-out visitors ("Sequence cannot be loaded"), so the **KARTAVIEW ↗** link opens the full-size photo through KartaView's image proxy. ### Core changes, provider-neutral - **Shared modules.** Mapillary's camera-driven line coverage and sequence cones move to `src/layers/streetLevel/lineCoverage.js` and `sequenceCones.js`. The tile fetch, zoom ladder, colours, pick prefixes and filter test are injected. `providers/mapillary/coverage.js` and `sequences.js` are now thin wrappers, and Mapillary's own tests pass unchanged. - **Line clicks.** `handlePick(id, {groundPoint})` hands the provider the ground under the click, measured only if it asks. - **Provider actions:** `openImage(id, {frame})` and `openNearest(point)`. - **Provider fields:** - `coverageLabel`: the coverage line's wording. - `highlightsSequence`: no "Selected" legend swatch for a source whose lines never turn cyan. - Viewer adapters may report `supportsRenderModes()`. - **Switching sources.** Lighting another source, by chip, voice or link, stops a lookup still running for the previous one and clears its spinner and error. ## How I verified it - [x] `npm run build` (production build served by `vite preview`, as CI does). - [x] `npm test` at 04b3231: 6,448 pass, 0 fail, 1 skipped (Windows-only). For the filter commits: all 452 Street Level, UI and gate-tooling tests pass, plus the GBFS tests from the `main` merge. - [x] `npm run test:track` (dev server running): 109 passed, 0 failed (run on an earlier commit of this PR). - [x] **Feature gate:** `npm run qa:street-level:fixtures -- --strict` against the production build. - **Result:** 32 ok, 3 documented skips ("no Google 3D" ×2, "no Google key"). - **What it now covers:** it answers every KartaView request from fixtures and checks: - keyless coverage with its credit, the filter controls and the "by upload date" note; - 360° and LAST YEAR thinning KartaView's lines through filtered PNG tiles (the fixture adds an older flat-only street beside the drive), and ALL / ANY DATE bringing them back; - a line click opening the nearest photo while the camera stays put, after a rate-limited (429) first lookup; - cones along the drive, with the camera looking along it while the photos' compass says 200°; - › skipping an archived photo (409 at its storage host); - a 360° photo without FIT / FILL, turned by a drag, that survives a real `WEBGL_lose_context`; - on the keyless second page, KartaView drawing with no Mapillary key. - **Flaky pick step, fixed.** Step 13 (the existing Mapillary "click a coverage line, then pick an image cone" step) sometimes timed out. Each `scene.pick` costs 0.5–2 s under SwiftShader, and the search: - picked every centre five times at radius 0; - aimed the cone pick at ground points that can sit off the drawn cones; - could spend a whole wait inside one evaluation. Now each centre is picked once, the cone pick aims at the drawn billboards, and each evaluation stops after 4 s and resumes on the next poll. One cone-pick evaluation went from 2.3–6.9 s to 10–363 ms. - **Runs on the filter code:** the gate passed in full locally on the first filter commit: 33 ok, 3 documented skips, including the new filter step. Other local runs failed only from machine load (load average 50–70 from other sessions' browsers): one on the panel-drag step, one on step 13's line pick, which now gets 60 s. CI's gate is the clean check. - `qa:panel-resize` passes. - [x] `npm run format:check`, `npm run check:boundaries`, `layer-token:check` (no new token). - [x] **Tests.** KartaView's modules have 105 unit tests. There is also a new `lineCoverage.test.mjs`, plus core tests for the new actions, fields and source switching. A mutation run on an earlier head of this PR killed 138 of 159 mutants; the tests it suggested are in. - [x] **Live API, filters.** Jakarta: 537 streets with ALL, 157 with 360° (that filtered tile took 3–4 s), 0 with LAST YEAR.
