title: feat: Energy Atlas — explore geographic energy use and the Kardashev scale
body:
### Problem

It would be useful to click a country, region, or supported local administrative area on GEV's globe and answer: **how much energy does this place use, over what period, and according to whom?** An infrastructure overlay such as [#10](https://github.com/bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view/issues/10) can show power lines, but it can't explain the area's energy consumption.

### Proposal

An **opt-in Energy Atlas** on the existing map, starting very small:

1. Select one geography with an authoritative boundary and matching energy data.
2. Highlight its polygon and show **annual TWh**, **equivalent average GW**, the **calendar year**, geographic coverage, and a visible source/uncertainty label in GEV's existing rail.
3. Change the year or select another compatible area without mixing different energy measurements. Missing data should show *unavailable*, not zero.

The year-average GW display is calculated from annual energy divided by the actual hours in that year (8760 or 8784); it's **not a live power meter**. Primary energy, final energy, and electricity demand must be separately labeled, not treated as interchangeable.

**Kardashev Explorer** could be a later educational mode that zooms back out to Earth and explains the civilization-scale Type I/II/III power milestones, with original colorful vector illustrations, restrained narrative animations, and reduced-motion support. The style could draw inspiration from Kurzgesagt's accessible science storytelling without reusing its assets. A city shouldn't receive a misleading “Type I” rating, and higher consumption shouldn't itself be a game reward.

The existing layer lifecycle, geographic boundaries, source injection, and polygon/rendering patterns seem like a good fit. [#1076](https://github.com/bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view/issues/1076) (reusable geographic polygon support) is relevant; I'd prefer reuse over another map renderer.

### Data source, license, and attribution

A concrete keyless pilot is the UK Department for Energy Security and Net Zero's [2005–2024 local-authority/regional/country **total final energy** series](https://www.gov.uk/government/statistics/total-final-energy-consumption-at-regional-and-local-authority-level-2005-to-2024), published **30 July 2026** and listed under the [UK Open Government Licence](https://www.data.gov.uk/dataset/4b7b7f64-0b97-4a6e-8e45-1218b9a81876/sub-national-total-final-energy-consumption-data). Boundaries would come from a matching version of official ONS/Open Geography data, preserving applicable ONS/Ordnance Survey/Crown attribution. The actual area-code and boundary-version join, suppressed values, and redistribution obligations need checking before bundling any records.

Global country primary-energy data (e.g., Our World in Data) could be a separate follow-up after source/licence review; it must not be combined with UK final-energy figures as though they measured the same thing. This builds on the authoritative-provider direction in [#864](https://github.com/bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view/issues/864).

### Will you build it?

**Yes, if this direction is useful here.** I'd be happy to begin with a tightly scoped, testable energy-measurement model, then a **single sourced polygon + readout** as the first visible slice—no new backend or full heatmap required. No feature PR or real-data integration has been made yet.

There is a more detailed [downstream architecture sketch](https://github.com/kvnloo/gods-eye-view/issues/233); this issue is meant to check fit and scope first.

Related first-step proposal: #1124 — a small pure annual-energy model, subject to whether that approach fits the project.

title: feat: small annual-energy measurement model for Energy Atlas (#1123)
body:
### Problem

The proposed [Energy Atlas #1123](https://github.com/bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view/issues/1123) needs one small, reliable boundary between *annual energy data* and a map's animated readout. Without it, blank values could look like zero consumption, a 2024 leap year could get the wrong power conversion, or electricity demand and primary energy could be compared as if they were identical.

### Proposal

If the feature direction is welcome, I would start with a **pure JavaScript model + tests**, tentatively in `src/layers/energyAtlas/model.js`, without touching the app catalog or Cesium.

- Validate a source-attributed observation with administrative **area code / boundary revision**, year, named metric (`final_energy`, `primary_energy`, or `electricity`), annual quantity, estimated/measured status, source licence and publication revision.
- Preserve **real zero vs. missing/suppressed/invalid**. Do not turn `null`, `''`, `NaN` or unsupported areas into zero.
- Convert annual TWh into **equivalent mean watts** using the actual year's 8,760 or 8,784 hours. Label it *annual average*, not live telemetry.
- Refuse comparisons across mismatched years/metrics/coverage or geography definitions. A code-backed area join must be explicit; do not sum overlapping scopes.
- Optionally expose the standard Sagan Kardashev logarithmic formula as an **educational, planetary-scale-only** calculation, not a rating for towns or a percentage-to-Type-I progress bar.

This is intentionally **not** a source fetcher, public data bundle, heatmap, global cache, package API, or browser visualization. A later PR could use this model for one sourced polygon + readout, using GEV's existing layer and overlay ownership.

### Data source, license, and attribution

**No external source is needed for the model's synthetic unit tests.** A future first data integration could use the Department for Energy Security and Net Zero's [UK local-authority total final energy series, 2005–2024](https://www.gov.uk/government/statistics/total-final-energy-consumption-at-regional-and-local-authority-level-2005-to-2024), licensed under the [UK Open Government Licence](https://www.data.gov.uk/dataset/4b7b7f64-0b97-4a6e-8e45-1218b9a81876/sub-national-total-final-energy-consumption-data). The actual boundary-code join, missing-data flags and attribution would need separate review first. No keys or private data for the model.

### Will you build it?

**Yes, if useful.** This is a proposed small implementation step, not a completed PR or passing test suite. If the maintainers would prefer a single end-to-end polygon/readout slice rather than a model-only PR, I'd follow that direction. [Downstream technical sketch](https://github.com/kvnloo/gods-eye-view/issues/234).

title: feat(cctv): add Houston TranStar camera pack
body:
Add Greater Houston traffic cameras from Houston TranStar as a live CCTV pack.

The server reads the keyless catalog at `traffic.houstontranstar.org/data/layers/cctvSnapshots_json.js` and keeps cameras with a numeric snapshot id inside the metro bounding box. Frame URLs are built from that id under `www.houstontranstar.org/snapshots/cctv/<id>.jpg`; catalog `url` fields are ignored so they cannot steer the proxy. Cameras whose id is `0` (a different, non-snapshot class) and cameras outside Greater Houston are dropped. Dedicated `dir` values become high-confidence headings; `None` uses the shared id-hash fallback.

By default the 250 cameras nearest downtown, Uptown, the Medical Center, IAH, and Galveston load. `CCTV_HOUSTON_MAX_SOURCES` (8–400) changes the cap and `CCTV_HOUSTON_ENABLED=0` turns the pack off. The catalog-wide ceiling stays at 4,000 and is shared round-robin.

title: feat: experimental Android app (Capacitor shell + on-device APIs)
body:
Experimental Android port of God's Eye View: launch it from the app drawer on an Android 17 device (verified on Pixel 9 Pro Fold and Pixel 10 Pro Fold) with the phone as the whole computer.

## What this adds

**Capacitor shell** (`android/`, app ID `ai.halfpixel.gev`, `compileSdk`/`targetSdk` 37, `minSdk` 24):
- `scripts/mobile/build-apk.sh` (web build + `cap sync` + `assembleDebug`), `scripts/mobile/smoke-check.mjs` (static surface + `--require-apk` gate), and `scripts/mobile/generate-icons.mjs` (adaptive + legacy launcher icons generated from `public/logo.svg` on the `#0a0a0f` dark theme background).
- No orientation/aspect locks; unfold resizes in place via `configChanges`.
- Same-origin XHR bypass for the bridge's interceptor (its XHR patch has no same-origin skip, unlike fetch): without it, bundled Cesium assets fail `CONNECTION_REFUSED` and stop rendering with an `[object Object]` panel. Self-healing across bridge re-patches.
- Never returns the raw Preferences proxy from the storage loader (awaiting it throws UNIMPLEMENTED on-device).

**On-device APIs** (no home server required): secure key vault (Keystore-backed plugin seam, canary-tested redaction) connected to catalog boot, native fetch over core `CapacitorHttp` with per-family allowlists + byte caps, source policy (direct iff Capacitor && no backend URL), and direct adapters — keyless (weather, terrain, adsbdb, geocode/route, static feeds, mapillary, local-LAN receivers), keyed realtime (OpenSky/adsb.lol flights, AISStream vessels with binary-frame decode, direct OpenAI voice token + HUD summary, TomTom/Google with persisted governors), and heavy ports (transit protobuf, wind GRIB, CCTV registries + TxDOT + HLS leases, Overpass direct, NOAA tiles) with layer-boundary shape adapters. Vessels, TomTom flow, and fire perimeters are wired into layer selection; web behavior is byte-identical off-Capacitor; OAuth voice stays desktop-only. Keys are BYOK in encrypted on-device storage, never baked into the build.

See `docs/MOBILE.md` (setup, key model, permissions, release checklist), `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md`, and `changelog.d/1127-android-capacitor-shell.md`.

## Verification

- `npm test`: 8846 pass, 0 fail (1 skipped; 2 allocation microbenchmarks skip outside Node 24).
- `npm run doctor -- --json`, `npm run format:check`, `npm run check:boundaries`, `npm run i18n` (`es`, `ru`, `zh-CN` complete at 2712 messages), `npm run changelog:check`, `npm run layer-token:check -- --base-ref upstream/main`, `npm run build`: green.
- `npm run qa:street-level:fixtures -- --strict`: 12/12 pass, 0 skipped.
- `node scripts/track-regression.mjs --offline-imagery --headful`: 109/109 pass, 0 fail.
- `smoke-check.mjs --require-apk`: PASS (APK assembles with SDK 37).
- Device-verified on Pixel 9 Pro Fold and Pixel 10 Pro Fold (Android 17): clean boot with the custom adaptive eye launcher icon and `#1325` bottom tab-shell phone layout on the cover screen, keyless globe, live flights (6300+ aircraft), watercraft populating on the map, live TomTom flow recolor, fire perimeters starting cleanly, FIRMS live, military aircraft (69–72 live), CelesTrak satellites with dense catalog, CCTV frames, ALPR markers (11 on screen over Austin), fold/unfold mid-session with camera surviving. On-device defects found and fixed here: render-stop bypass, Preferences proxy, binary AIS frame decode, FIRMS CSV cap, vault-to-boot plumbing; direct military/satellite wiring and the CCTV null-URL frame guard; secure vault round-trip on hardware (keys ciphertext in the Keystore-backed plugin store, read back at boot).
- Rebased onto `upstream/main` (`a3a19883`); all three shipped locale catalogs (`es`, `ru`, `zh-CN`) and `changelog.d/1127-android-capacitor-shell.md` are up to date.

## Known gaps (documented, not hidden)

- Four families stay proxy-routed with in-diff evidence each (voice-backend composition; places/HUD slots; local-receiver feed plumbing; overpass boundary) — see `docs/MOBILE.md` narrowing.
- No live-device proof for HLS playback or GRIB-in-WebView yet — release checklist in `docs/MOBILE.md`.
- APK sideload tested; Play Store track not started.

title: fix: answer tiles-token with 204 when no tokens are offered
body:
Without a Google browser key, the app asks GET /api/google/tiles-token once per page load, and nothing in the standalone server served it, so the request fell through to the API 404 catch-all and logged a console error on every keyless boot.

The standalone server now answers the route with 204 No Content before the catch-all. The client's token source treats any non-token answer as "no tokens offered" and resolves null without logging, and a server that does offer tokens still registers its route ahead of this middleware.

The client-contract test now covers a 204 answer, and the standalone plugin-order test asserts the new route precedes the API fallback.

Fixes #1060

title: feat(perimeters): Australian bushfire warnings — QLD QFES + NSW RFS merged into the fire perimeter snapshot
body:
## Summary

Adds Australian bushfire coverage to the Fire Perimeters layer by merging two keyless government feeds into the existing `/api/fire-perimeters` snapshot, downstream of the WFIGS rows:

- **QLD QFES bushfire alerts** — community warning areas (Advice / Watch and Act / Emergency Warning) from the Queensland Fire Department feed. Warning polygons render as perimeters; the card shows the warning title, level, call-to-action and warning area.
- **NSW RFS major incidents** (Fires Near Me) — incident alert level, size (ha → acres), status and council area. The feed emits polygons only for larger incidents; point-only features are skipped, so quiet days can contribute zero rows.

### Implementation notes

- Both feeds are fetched server-side in parallel with a per-feed 8 MiB cap and a 30 s timeout, then merged after the WFIGS rows in `firePerimetersProxy` (`server/providers/firePerimeters.js`).
- **Fail-soft by construction**: the helper catches per-feed failures and the proxy call site re-try/catches — an AU feed outage can only ever contribute zero rows, never blank or delay the US snapshot.
- The QLD feed is fetched from the WAF-free `publiccontent.gis.psba.qld.gov.au` origin (the documented `www.qfes.qld.gov.au` URL sits behind an Incapsula JS challenge that rejects non-browser clients; the PSBA host is the redirect target of that URL and serves the identical JSON). A unit test pins the URL.
- QLD timestamps read `ItemDateTimeLocal_ISO` — the `*_UTM` fields are W3C/DMTF (`20261014031508.630000`), not ISO 8601, and `Date.parse` returns NaN on them.

title: Text command bar with an OpenAI-compatible chat endpoint (no Realtime/voice required)
body:
**Problem**

The in-app agent only exists inside an OpenAI Realtime session. Typed commands (`sendTextCommand`) travel over that same connection, so without an OpenAI key there is no way to drive the globe from inside the app, not even by typing. Self-hosters using DigitalOcean Inference, OpenRouter, Ollama, vLLM etc. only have chat-completions endpoints with tool calling, no Realtime API.

**Proposal**

An optional text command bar that runs the existing tool catalog (`src/tools/functions.js` already adapts it for function-calling clients) against any OpenAI-compatible `/v1/chat/completions` endpoint:

- `GEV_LLM_BASE_URL`, `GEV_LLM_API_KEY`, `GEV_LLM_MODEL`
- the same tools and view actions the voice agent uses, with text in and text out
- voice stays on Realtime when an OpenAI key is present

**Small first step: HUD summary**

`server/providers/openai/hud-summary.js` hardcodes `https://api.openai.com/v1/responses`. Pointing it at an OpenAI-compatible `chat/completions` endpoint (tested locally with DigitalOcean Inference, `openai-gpt-5-nano`) works fine, so making the base URL configurable upstream would already help.

**Related**

#212 (local voice; MCP is the suggested route for external agents) and #812 (local intent router). This request is about an in-app text path, independent of any voice provider.

title: fix(qa-cctv-v2): keep long headful waits under puppeteer's protocolTimeout
body:
## Problem

`node scripts/qa-cctv-v2.mjs --headful` against the full catalog (N≈3,700–4,000) gives up on the geometry-load drain after about 3 minutes. The headful drain budget is `camCount * 800 + 30000` ms, about 50 min. But `page.waitForFunction` returns its result through one long CDP call, which puppeteer aborts at its default `protocolTimeout` of 180 s, and the `.catch(() => false)` then records *"timed out waiting for drain on the real-GPU sign-off path"*. `waitForFunction` also polls on `requestAnimationFrame` by default, and rAF stops in a minimised or hidden headful window while timers keep running.

## Change (one file: `scripts/qa-cctv-v2.mjs`)

- **Node-side polling:** `waitForPredicate` replaces every `waitForFunction` in the harness (the drain, the app-ready wait, tiles loaded, the first ground sample). It runs one short `page.evaluate` per tick (1 s for the drain, 250 ms elsewhere) against a monotonic `performance.now()` deadline. So no CDP call outlives `protocolTimeout`, and a hidden window can't stall the check. It retries when a navigation or Vite reload replaces the execution context. A predicate that throws now fails the run instead of silently spending the budget.
- **`protocolTimeout: 300_000`** at launch, matching the other `qa-*.mjs` harnesses, for the few long evaluates such as enabling the full catalog on a real GPU.
- **Bounded frame waits:** one in-page `window.__qaRenderFrames(count, capMs)` helper serves the gizmo-drag wait (5 s) and the sibling-owner wait (10 s, previously unbounded). The sibling record reports `frames=N/3`. A miss with 0 frames is reported as a stalled renderer: FAIL on the headful sign-off path, INCONCLUSIVE under headless GL. A miss with 1–3 frames still FAILs in both modes.
- **Screenshots** for visual review log and continue if a capture fails.
- **`pipe: true`**, so no CDP port stays open on localhost for a long headful run.

`--disable-backgrounding-occluded-windows` isn't added: puppeteer 25.10 already passes it in `ChromeLauncher.defaultArgs`, and no harness here sets `ignoreDefaultArgs`.

## Verification (macOS)

| Run | Result |
|---|---|
| `qa-cctv-v2.mjs --headful` (earlier sliced version), Chrome window covered for the whole run, `npx vite --port 4211` | `RESULT: 53 passed, 0 failed, 0 inconclusive` twice. The drain (N=3724, budget 3009 s) took over 3.5 min and passed. |
| `qa-cctv-v2.mjs` headless at this head (N=4000) | `RESULT: 52 passed, 0 failed, 1 inconclusive`. The inconclusive is the 120 s headless drain cap; sibling step `frames=3/3`. |
| Hidden-page repro (rAF 0/s), budget 3 s, condition flips at 2.3 s | Old rAF slices return `false` at 3,002 ms; `waitForPredicate` returns `true`. |
| Scaled `protocolTimeout` repro (3 s) | A single `waitForFunction` dies at 3 s with `Runtime.callFunctionOn timed out`; the Node-side poll runs the full budget. |
| Throwing predicate / reload mid-wait | Throws at once / keeps polling and returns `true` (3/3). |

`npm run format:check` and `npm run check:boundaries` are clean.

title: Street Level: Panoramax as a fourth, keyless imagery provider
body:
## Street Level: Panoramax as a fourth, keyless provider

[Panoramax](https://panoramax.fr) is the open, federated street-level commons: OpenStreetMap France, IGN, MapComplete and about 20 other instances. Its meta-catalogue, `api.panoramax.xyz`, needs no key and allows any origin, so the provider runs entirely in the browser. It adds no server route and no new dependency.

### What users get
- A **PANORAMAX** chip in orange `#ff6f00`, Panoramax's own colour. It starts off, and only one provider is lit at a time.
- **From orbit:** dots show where Panoramax has pictures. Each dot is sized by how many pictures it stands for.
- **Below 60 km:** the sequences draw as lines, the same ceiling as Mapillary.
- **Click a line:** that line's own photo nearest the click opens, and the camera stays put. Cones show along the sequence, and **‹ ›** / ← → follow the photo's own prev/next links.
- **Flat photos** support FIT/FILL. **360° photos** open on the WebGL panorama shared with KartaView: drag, pinch, wheel and keys look around.
- **Filters:** **360° / FLAT / SINCE** apply to the lines, and are sent to the API for lookups.
- **Caption:**
  - every producer: the uploading app and the photographer; accounts named by an email address are never shown
  - otherwise the instance holding the photo ("via panoramax.ign.fr")
  - the **photo's own licence** (CC BY-SA 4.0, Licence Ouverte 2.0, …)
  - a link to the photo in the Panoramax viewer
  
  The globe credit reads "© Panoramax contributors, licence per picture".
- **Share links:** `0.m.0_0.r.panoramax-1`.

### How it works
- **New provider** in `src/layers/streetLevel/providers/panoramax/`:
  - `policy` (STAC normalisation, licences)
  - `source` (tiles and STAC search; timeouts, a streamed size cap, busy/Retry-After handling)
  - `decode` (Douglas–Peucker line simplification, binned density grid, z15 pictures)
  - `index`
  - `viewer`
- **Shared code:**
  - KartaView's viewer is now `streetLevel/photoViewer.js`, which both providers drive through a per-provider `PhotoSources` table; KartaView's own tests, including the ones added upstream after #1121, pass against it.
  - `panorama.js`, `limiter.js` and `tileCache.js` move up to `streetLevel/`.
- **`lineCoverage.js` gains three opt-in options:** `keepOrder`, `overviewPointSize` and `maxPoints`. `maxPoints` is a point budget shared across the tiles in view once loading settles, so a city centre is not drawn thinner than its suburbs, and the selected line is always drawn. Mapillary and KartaView are unchanged.
- **Connections:** the API speaks HTTP/1.1 only, so the provider uses five of the browser's six connections to it: 3 for coverage tiles, 2 for searches and 1 for the cones' tiles.
- **Image sizes:** the SD (2,048 px) version shows first. The HD original loads only for the expanded viewer, once, and is aborted when the photo changes.
- **`StreetPose`** gains an optional `license` field.
- **MCP globe panel:** the CSP allows the meta-catalogue and the largest instances.

### QA and review
- **Two agentic QA rounds** against the live API:
  - **Functional, 12 findings:** the nearest-photo search missed photos facing away from the click; long lines lost to the per-tile cap; a quadratic author-name check could freeze the tab; and others.
  - **UX in the browser:** line clicks timed out behind megabyte tiles (HTTP/1.1); Paris looked empty from 30–100 km; Esc collapsed the panel; attribution.
- **IC8 review**, five lenses (correctness, security, tests with mutation testing, performance, UX), then two verification rounds. The last round's one finding is fixed in ce3f66a and checked in the browser: re-sharing the budget made the centre blink after a pan.
  - **P0, fixed:** over Paris at 12–60 km, unsimplified lines produced gigabytes of ground-polyline geometry and hung the tab.

    | 55 km over Paris | Before | After |
    |---|---|---|
    | Time to settle | 99 s | 4.4 s |
    | Longest long task | 125 s | 0.65 s |

  - **P2–P4, all fixed:** caches, HD only when expanded, the cone cache, the budget shared across tiles, Douglas–Peucker measured to the segment, Esc on the whole viewer, attribution, and the test gaps.
  - **Mutation testing:** 34 of 34 targeted mutants killed.

### Gates
- `npm run format:check` and `npm run check:boundaries` pass.
- `npm test`: 6,598 tests, 0 failures.
- **Strict hermetic browser gate** (`qa:street-level --fixtures --strict`, production build with no keys): 39 steps, 36 ok, 3 allowed skips (Google 3D and the Google key). Three new Panoramax steps run against a fixture with two sequences interleaved on one street. The gate clicks over the *other* sequence's photos, so it passes only when the click opens the line actually clicked.

### Known follow-ups (non-blocking)
- Asset hosts are not tied to the `via` instance.
- The licence name has no link to its terms.
- A ‹ › link to a hidden picture can block stepping past it. I have not reproduced this.
- The panel's sequence count can run ahead of the lines drawn while geometry builds. This affects every provider.

### Screenshots
| A flat photo, captioned with author and licence | A 360° photo; a hidden author falls back to the instance |
|---|---|
| ![flat](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/asturksever/gods-eye-view/pr-panoramax-screenshots/1-flat-photo.png) | ![360](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/asturksever/gods-eye-view/pr-panoramax-screenshots/2-360-photo.png) |
| **Paris from 55 km: the centre is the densest** | **25 km** |
| ![55 km](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/asturksever/gods-eye-view/pr-panoramax-screenshots/3-coverage-55km.png) | ![25 km](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/asturksever/gods-eye-view/pr-panoramax-screenshots/4-coverage-25km.png) |

The selected sequence draws in cyan ([close-up](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/asturksever/gods-eye-view/pr-panoramax-screenshots/5-selected-sequence.png)).

title: fix(stream, street-level): resolve AIS stream memory leak and harden KartaView viewer stability
body:
## Problem

1. **AIS vessel store memory leak & event loop starvation:** In `server/providers/vessels/ais-store.js`, while `_aisStreamVessels` and `_aisStreamTracks` are pruned when stale, `_aisStreamStatic` was never evicted or bounded. In continuous live maritime feeds, this produced an unbounded Map growth leading to server OOM crashes. Additionally, calling `pruneAisStreamCache()` synchronously on every single message packet triggered full-cache array conversions and sorting, starving Node's event loop during high-throughput bursts.
2. **KartaView concurrency limiter memory leak & pre-aborted task stall:** In `src/layers/streetLevel/providers/kartaview/source.js`, `createLimiter` attached `{ once: true }` abort listeners that were only removed if an abort event fired. For normally resolved/rejected tasks, listeners were never removed, permanently leaking closures and promise handlers on long-lived signals. Furthermore, pre-aborted signals were queued rather than rejected immediately.
3. **KartaView viewer step navigation freeze:** In `src/layers/streetLevel/providers/kartaview/viewer.js`, sequential navigation steps were chained onto `steps = steps.then(...)`. If `onStep()` threw or rejected an error, the promise transitioned into a permanent rejected state, permanently breaking all subsequent `‹`, `›`, and arrow key navigation.

## What this changes

- **`ais-store.js`:**
  - Tracks `_updatedAt` on static records and evicts stale static records during pruning passes and capacity trimming.
  - Paces cache pruning (`maybePruneAisStreamCache`) to avoid sorting 50,000 items synchronously on every single incoming packet.
- **`kartaview/source.js`:**
  - Removes the abort listener upon dequeuing in `createLimiter` so completed tasks never leak closures in memory.
  - Rejects pre-aborted signals immediately upfront without polluting the queue.
- **`kartaview/viewer.js`:**
  - Wraps `onStep` in `try / catch` to keep `openingId` aligned if stepping fails.
  - Protects the `steps` promise chain with `.catch()` to ensure user navigation controls remain responsive.
- **Tests:** Adds unit test coverage for limiter abort cleanup, pre-aborted rejection, viewer error resilience, and static data cache pruning.

## Validation

- `npm run check:boundaries`: 957 modules checked, 0 violations.
- `npm run format:check`: 1338 source files checked, clean.
- `npm run build`: built in 27.77s without errors.
- Unit tests: 6,482 passed (including 114 KartaView tests and AIS store tests).

title: Add live remote control of the open globe
body:
## Summary

A page can subscribe to a session and apply views that an authenticated caller pushes. The caller can send the share link `show_in_gods_eye_view` already returns, so a bridge that has the tool result can move the open globe without a second description of the view. Explicit camera, layers, annotations, and follow in the same payload apply on top of that link.

This is off by default. With `REMOTE_CONTROL_TOKEN` unset, push and the session list answer 503.

## API

- `GET /api/remote/stream?session=<id>` is a server-sent event stream. The page opens it for session `default`, or for `?remote=<session>`. `?remote=off` does not connect. The stream carries no bearer token. Heartbeat comments keep proxies from closing it.
- `POST /api/remote/push` requires `Authorization: Bearer <REMOTE_CONTROL_TOKEN>`. The body is `{ session?: "default" | "*", view }`. A valid view is delivered to the connected browsers of that session, or to every session when `session` is `"*"`. The response is `{ ok, delivered, sessions }` even when nobody is listening.
- `GET /api/remote/sessions` uses the same bearer token and lists connected sessions.

`view.link` may be a full share URL, its hash, or the bare parameter string. The browser parses it with the existing share-link codec (`viewFromParams`). A link that names layers replaces the enabled set; a camera-only link leaves layers alone. Omitted style and map stay as the open globe already has them.

## Security

Push and the session list compare the bearer in constant time and never log or return the token. The stream is same-origin and has no bearer, so anyone who can open the app can receive pushed views. A push moves the camera, layers, marks, and follow. It does not call provider APIs or spend keys. `.env.example` and `SECURITY.md` describe the token.

## Tests

Unit tests cover the view schema, share-link round trip, client apply and reconnect, and the bearer, fan-out, and SSE server. `npm test` and `npm run check:boundaries` passed on this branch (Node 26; the two Node-24 allocation microbenchmarks were skipped).

title: feat(street-level): Vegbilder, Statens vegvesen's road photos of Norway, as a keyless provider
body: ## What this changes Vegbilder, Statens vegvesen's road photos of Norway, joins Street Level as a fifth provider beside Mapillary, Google Street View, KartaView and Panoramax. It needs no key: the browser reads Vegvesen's public GeoServer WFS directly (CORS open); the data is NLOD, as for Vegvesen's other open data. - **Chip and coverage.** A VEGBILDER chip (pink) starts off; one source is lit at a time, as before. Over Norway, below about 1.5 km, the national and county roads Vegvesen photographed in the last three years draw as lines. Vegbilder has no line features, only a photo point every 5–10 m, so lines are built from z15 boxes of points: grouped into drives (road reference, lane, day), ordered by metre (lanes against the metering are turned round) and cut at gaps over 40 m or 10 minutes. Tiles outside mainland Norway ask nothing. - **Opening a photo.** A click on a line opens the nearest photo within 50 m, newest year first and flat before 360° within a year. The drive shows as cones; **‹ ›** or ← → step along it. The caption reads the road ("Rv. 162", "E18") and links to the photo. - **Viewer.** Flat photos in an ``. 360° photos (2021 onwards, 8,192 × 4,096) are decoded into a 4,096-wide bitmap for KartaView's WebGL panorama renderer, reused as is; their 2,520 px front view stands in if that fails. The viewer uses the shared photo-viewer styles, in Vegbilder pink. - **Filters.** IMAGERY (ALL / 360° / FLAT) picks the feature types asked for; SINCE goes by capture date and skips years before it. - **Attribution.** "Street Level: road photos © Statens vegvesen, NLOD 2.0" on the globe while it is lit. - **Share links.** Vegbilder travels in the existing provider-switch field (`…*vegbilder-1`). No new layer token. ### Vegbilder API behaviour the provider handles All verified against the live service: - One feature type per year and kind (`Vegbilder_` flat from 2014, none for 2015; `Vegbilder_360_` from 2021). A year not published yet answers "Feature type … unknown", read as empty. - Photo addresses are signed for ten hours, so coverage asks without them (`propertyName`), and a photo is asked for again by `resourceId` after an hour. - Photos live on two hosts, `s3vegbilder.atlas.vegvesen.no` and `s3-oslo.osys.vegvesen.no`; any other address is dropped. - Some listed photos have no file: many of Oslo's 360° photos answer 404, and the store takes no HEAD or range request. The nearest candidate is loaded as an `` first (the viewer then has it cached) and a missing one is skipped for the next feature type's, at most four tries; then the panel says Vegvesen has no file. - A drive around an open photo is a CQL query on road reference, lane and day within 300 m, cached per 200 m of road. - Large boxes time out (504), so only z15 boxes and 50 m search boxes are asked, four requests at a time. ## QA - `npm test`: 6,532 tests, 0 failures (25 new in `providers/vegbilder/`). - `npm run qa:street-level:fixtures -- --strict` against a production build: 33 ok, 3 documented skips; the VEGBILDER chip is in the expected chip order. - Live, in the app: Oslo (Rv. 162) draws 143–374 road stretches depending on the view; a line click skips a 2026 360° photo with a missing file and opens the 2025 flat photo; › steps from m568 to m573 along the drive (88 photos in the pass). On Fv. 61 in Vestland a 360° photo opens on the panorama facing along the road, with ring cones along the drive. - `npm run format:check` and `npm run check:boundaries` pass.

title: feat(maps): Kartverket topo and nautical charts as keyless basemaps for Norway
body:
## What this changes

Two keyless basemaps for Norway, from Kartverket's open WMTS cache (`cache.kartverket.no`, CC BY 4.0, CORS open):

- **Kartverket Topo** (`kartverket-topo`): Norway's topographic map (`topo` layer).
- **Kartverket Nautical** (`kartverket-nautical`): Norway's nautical charts (`sjokartraster` layer).

How they fit in:

- **Imagery.** `createKartverketImagery` in `src/maps/imagery.js` is a `UrlTemplateImageryProvider` on Kartverket's web-mercator `{z}/{y}/{x}` PNG tiles up to z18. Tiles are requested only inside each layer's WGS84 extent from the capabilities document. Kartverket serves empty tiles outside it, so elsewhere the bare globe shows; nothing is fetched there.
- **Fallback and credit.** After two tile failures a stack falls back to OSM, as Esri does. "© Kartverket, CC BY 4.0" is credited while either is on.
- **Surfaces.**
  - Map-source chips after OSM. `PRESENTED_MAP_STACK_IDS` is an owner-approved allowlist, so this PR is the request to add them.
  - Share links: `map=kartverket-topo`, `map=kartverket-nautical`.
  - `VIEW_MAPS`.
  - Submarine cables show on both, as on the other globe stacks.
  - Allowed origins in the MCP globe panel.
- **Voice.** Both ids are in the `set_map_stack` enum, with aliases ("kartverket", "norwegian topo", "norwegian topographic map", "norwegian nautical chart", "norwegian sea chart", "sjøkart") and one sentence each in the stack description and the disambiguation instructions. The Realtime payload and first-run schema pins are re-derived. The legacy-arguments test treats the two ids as deliberate additions.

Norge i bilder orthophoto is not included. Its WMS/WMTS services need a token issued only to Norge digitalt partners and data-agreement holders, and the open `opencache.statkart.no` WMTS is being shut down.

## QA

- `npm test`: 6,508 tests, 0 failures. A new source-factory test checks the template, tiling scheme, max level, extent (Oslo in, New York out), credit and OSM fallback.
- `npm run format:check` and `npm run check:boundaries` pass.
- Headless Chrome against a production build:

  - The chip lights and the hash carries `map=…`.

- `scripts/qa-map-source-tray.mjs` and `scripts/qa-focus-evidence.mjs` list the seven stacks.

title: feat: Local-based map layers
body:
### Problem

currently, the view of the globe/map disappears when you go offline.

### Proposal

title: fix(perimeters): handle antimeridian queries and incident card anchors
body:
Fire-perimeter containment treated longitude as a Cartesian coordinate, so an outline crossing 179°E to 179°W missed nearby enclosed areas and could match an unrelated area near Greenwich. The returned query coordinate and the incident-card anchor also averaged those longitudes across the wrong side of the globe.

The query fix unwraps each ring along short longitude edges before ray casting and projects the query center onto the same sheet. Holes use the same rule; returned query coordinates use a circular longitude mean.

## Review follow-up

Addressed the [October 16 review](https://github.com/bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view/pull/1142#issuecomment-6220428856) in this PR:

- Rebased onto upstream `e8b3a10a`. Both sides of the `CHANGELOG.md` and `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md` conflicts are preserved, including the catalog-cancellation paragraph.
- `perimeterAnchorDegrees` now uses circular longitude for the largest outer ring, still excluding the repeated closing vertex.
- The largest-ring comparison also follows short longitude edges. A small dateline-crossing part previously appeared almost 360° wide and could incorrectly win over a larger ordinary part.
- Card regressions cover closed/reversed/rotated rings, vertices at either sign of 180°, and multipart selection in both directions and orders.

## Validation

Code: `8d37661219f7fbe6592e75b16cefda9b317d0e11`.

- All three new card regressions fail before the card fix and pass afterward.
- Focused geometry/environment/card suite: **43 passed**.

- `npm run build`, `npm run format:check`, `npm run check:boundaries` and `git diff --check` pass.
- `npm run test:track -- --url http://127.0.0.1:4173 --offline-imagery`: **109 passed, zero failed, zero skipped**, with no console errors or HTTP 5xx responses across the full run (GitHub-hosted Ubuntu, Node 24.14.0). [Run and logs](https://github.com/ariannamethod/gods-eye-view/actions/runs/38948213956).

title: feat(cameras): speed camera layer from OpenStreetMap via the shared Overpass proxy
body:
## What

Adds an optional **Speed Cameras** layer mapping OpenStreetMap `highway=speed_camera` nodes worldwide — the enforcement-device counterpart to the existing ALPR layer, which only covers the US/CA hourly extract (`surveillance:type=ALPR`).

## How

- `src/layers/speedCameras/`: policy / records / source / model / index. Records parse OSM tags (`maxspeed` incl. mph, `camera:direction` bearings, operator, ref, check_date), validate snapshots strictly, and never let a malformed payload become an authoritative empty map.
- The source POSTs viewport-bounded Overpass QL through the repo's shared `/api/overpass` proxy (caching, abuse guards, rate limiting) — no new server provider, no new keys. DI-injected `fetchImpl` for tests, matching repo convention.
- Lifecycle follows the earthquakes template (CustomDataSource + overlay-host labels) with ALPR-style city-bounded viewports (3°), 0.05° query snapping so pans reuse one accepted snapshot, debounce, and in-flight move handling. Failed queries keep the last accepted records.
- UI: panel entry under Infrastructure; voice manifest entry (queryable fields: maxspeedKph, directionDeg, operator, enforcement, ref); ambient km/h labels via the shared overlay host.
- Registration touches the expected pins: layer-state registry + ledger (token `3`), package exports (`./layers/speed-cameras` + `/source`), boundary groups (mirroring earthquakes), catalog/voice schema count + digest pins.

## Data

Community-mapped device locations only — never live detections, enforcement schedules, or exhaustive coverage. Coverage mirrors OSM contributor density (AU: ~1,150 nodes; US: tens of thousands). Attribution rides the existing OpenStreetMap ODbL credit; `DATA_SOURCES.md` documents the layer's semantics next to the ALPR section.

## Validation

- `npm ci && npm test`: **6363 pass / 0 fail** (4 cancelled = known upstream flakes) on the stacked tree; clean-branch tree verified with format:check, boundaries and build on an isolated runner
- `npm run format:check` ✓ (1328 files) · `check:boundaries` ✓ · `npm run layer-token:check -- --base-ref main` ✓ ("29 published, 1 new") · `npm run build` ✓

### Activation and authorization

This PR does not establish provider authorization for a GEV deployment. Before activation, the deployment operator must establish that applicable published permissions or a separate written authorization cover the intended use, including automated server-side retrieval, temporary caching and display to the deployment's users. If that scope is unclear, request confirmation and leave the pack disabled until it is resolved. An unanswered request does not establish authorization.

[Varitech's terms §§6 and 8](https://varitech.ar/terminos) restrict reuse, unauthorized automated extraction and surveillance/tracking of people. The press page's embedding examples and publicly accessible JPEGs do not establish blanket permission for GEV. Preserve the provider/resort attribution and watermarks.

Once permission for that scope is established, configure the **GEV server's environment** (or the checkout's `.env`) and restart the server:

```dotenv
CCTV_VARITECH_ENABLED=1
```

Only `1` enables the pack; unset/empty/`0`/`true`/`yes` leave it disabled. To disable it again, remove the setting or set it to `0` in the server's effective configuration and restart. While disabled, the pack contributes no cameras and makes no Varitech image requests.

This is a deployment operator's switch. It does not grant or verify permission, and it does not enforce permitted uses after activation. Accepting GEV terms, including through a visitor checkbox, cannot supply provider authorization. See the [activation and authorization guide](https://github.com/radianx/gods-eye-view/blob/77685b6976938f08de53c8319192feb268403a8e/DATA_SOURCES.md#varitech-ski-resort-webcams-argentina).

body: Adds the Acaray and Yacyretá-Apipé dams to the existing OpenStreetMap Dams dataset (`src/data/local_data/dams/dams.geojsonl`, 704 → 706 features). No new data source: both records come from OpenStreetMap under the same ODbL 1.0 as the rest of the dataset, fetched from the public OSM API instead of the Open Infrastructure Map extract. - **Acaray** — [way 262532166](https://www.openstreetmap.org/way/262532166) v7, its closed outline stored as a polygon. - **Represa Yacyretá-Apipé** — [relation 5671745](https://www.openstreetmap.org/relation/5671745) v2, its eight outer ways joined into one closed 116-position polygon; the relation keeps the dataset's negative-ID convention (`-5671745`). Each record keeps the OSM name and tags, its source URL, object version and retrieval date (2026-10-15). No node metadata or contributor identifiers are bundled. ### What changes for users - Both dams appear in the Dams layer with a marker, label, click selection and an analyst record, and in `find_infrastructure`. - The Dams layer was credited to `USACE`, which never supplied this data. It now reads `OpenStreetMap / OpenInfraMap`, and the `find_infrastructure` attribution names both Open Infrastructure Map and OpenStreetMap. - Known limitation, unchanged by this PR: the layer places a polygon's marker at the centre of its bounding sphere, so the marker of the L-shaped Yacyretá outline sits about 1.6 km from the dam, over the reservoir. ### Before and after Same keyless build and camera on both sides: before is main at `bcc25be`, after is this PR at `fa4b4ad`. title: Add UK public data overlays, regional cameras and persistent Scope preference
body:
Adds a UK public-data panel to the standalone app and expands the published traffic-camera catalogue. A local Scope OFF choice now survives reloads and shared/scene states that request Scope ON, fixing the circular border reappearing.

### Behaviour and coverage
- Adds 370 distinct published UTMC snapshot-camera locations: Gateshead (61), northern A19 (18), and an additional regional pack (291). The refresh script reads the publisher's camera pages, validates coordinates and registered image paths, and keeps the packs disjoint.
- Preserves the existing TfL pack's default 250-camera limit while allowing an optional limit up to 1,000. A UK-focused local configuration currently returns 800 TfL + 370 UTMC locations; counts and image availability can change.
- Adds a searchable UK DATA panel with map shortcuts and provider-specific coverage: Environment Agency floods/river levels (England), SEPA gauges (Scotland), Defra UK-AIR station catalogue and last observations, UK airfield METARs, TfL road/rail status, Traffic Wales and TrafficwatchNI road feeds, and nearby OpenStreetMap places.
- Shows original observation/item dates separately from retrieval time, labels old/missing readings and provider outages, preserves a previous retrieval with its original time during short outages, and does not treat missing data as an all-clear. UK-AIR includes historical stations; catalogue presence does not establish operation.
- Fixed upstream routes, bounded requests/caches, rate limits and coalescing; registered UTMC JPEG paths only. The data browser cancels its own requests/timers on close or source change; saved map overlays have an independent lifetime and clear on disable or teardown.
- Sources requiring accounts, licences or provider approval are listed as disconnected official access routes. No restricted CCTV/ANPR access, bundled credentials, or unverified Nuneaton/Northallerton/Peterlee town-centre feeds are claimed.
- Source credits, reuse notes, refresh limits and configuration documented in DATA_SOURCES, CURRENT-STATE, CHANGELOG and .env.example.

### Saved UK map overlays
- Show the 13 registered public feeds together, with a UK overview, individual source switches and a compact map badge.
- Choices persist locally in `gev:uk-map-sources:v1`; closing the data browser retains the overlays. Picking a point opens its source record.
- Three concurrent acquisitions, bounded refresh deadlines, independent cancellation and owned point collections. Unchanged sibling collections remain intact. Hiding the page pauses acquisition; disabling a source or destroying the app clears only owned resources.
- Display limits: 5,000 points per source and 12,000 overall, with duplicates/omissions and records without coordinates reported. Positions are never guessed for list-only records. Nearby places remain a separate opt-in 10 km query.
- Live verification showed 7,808 points from all 13 responding feeds, with 1,794 list-only records lacking coordinates. This is provider-specific public-data coverage, not a complete UK camera or sensor inventory.

### Scope preference
The Scope button persists a local choice. Explicit OFF takes priority over authored ON during restoration; the button can explicitly opt back in. An optional VITE_GEV_SCOPE_DEFAULT_OFF=1 installation setting supports an initially unmasked map. Other installations retain the existing default.

title: Make HUD public-data accurate
feat: Add NOAA Nautical Charts as an Interactive Maritime Layer
body:
### Problem

Problem

God's Eye View brings together real-world data through a unified 3D globe, making it possible to visualize activity across air, land, and sea. However, adding vessel tracking alone does not provide the geographic context needed to meaningfully understand maritime activity.

For anyone interested in maritime operations, AIS vessel positions become much more useful when viewed alongside nautical chart information, including coastlines, navigational hazards, depths, channels, and other features relevant to safe navigation.

NOAA already provides extensive public nautical chart data and chart-display services for U.S. waters. Integrating this data into God's Eye View would connect live maritime activity with the navigational geography surrounding it.



### Proposal

Proposal

Add an optional, toggleable NOAA Nautical Charts layer that overlays official NOAA chart imagery onto the God's Eye View globe.

This would complement the existing vessel-tracking capabilities by allowing users to visualize AIS traffic in the context of the waterways and charted features through which vessels travel.

Suggested Functionality
Chart overlay: Display NOAA nautical chart imagery over applicable U.S. coastal and navigable waters.
AIS integration: Allow the existing vessel layer and nautical chart layer to be displayed simultaneously.
Layer controls: Let users enable or disable nautical charts independently of other map layers.
Zoom-dependent detail: Present appropriate chart detail as users zoom from regional views into harbors, channels, and coastal approaches.
Source attribution: Clearly identify NOAA as the chart-data provider and display relevant source information.
Data freshness: Communicate the source's update status where available, rather than implying that every chart feature is continuously updated.
Graceful fallback: If chart data is unavailable for a location or the service cannot be reached, retain the normal globe and other functioning layers.

### Data source, license, and attribution

NOAA already provides several services that could support this feature:

NOAA Chart Display Service — Provides nautical chart imagery through services including WMS, WMTS, and Esri REST, making it a promising starting point for a visual chart overlay.
NOAA ENC Display Services — Provides chart displays derived from NOAA Electronic Navigational Chart data, including an option using IHO S-52 symbology.
NOAA ENC Direct to GIS — Provides access to ENC data for more advanced geographic visualization and potential future interaction with individual chart features.

Official documentation:

NOAA GIS Data & Services: https://nauticalcharts.noaa.gov/data/gis-data-and-services.html
NOAA ENC Direct: https://nauticalcharts.noaa.gov/learn/encdirect/

### Will you build it?

No, this is a request for someone else

title: test(street-level): settle coverage before reading the ON/OFF pill
body:
## What

Step 6 of the Street Level browser gate ("the header ON/OFF pill switches the layer off and on") read `#sl-status` once, straight after step 5's credit wait. Tiles requested while Cesium paints the credit can flip the pill back to `LOADING` for a moment, so the assertion raced.

It failed CI on #1038, a PR that doesn't touch Street Level ([job log](https://github.com/bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view/actions/runs/38755003677/job/116490979834?pr=1038)):

```
+ 'BUTTON:LOADING:true'
- 'BUTTON:ON:true'
    at scripts/qa-street-level.mjs:1324
```

## Fix

Before the first assertion, `waitForCoverage(page)` and then `settle` until the pill reads `ON`. This matches how the same step already waits after it turns the layer back on. The assertion itself is unchanged, so a pill that really is stuck on `LOADING` still fails the step.

## Verification

- `npm run qa:street-level:fixtures -- --strict` against a production build with the dummy token (same as CI): 36/36, with only the documented Google skips
- `prettier --check` clean

Harness-only change, so no CHANGELOG entry.

title: feat(cameras): speed camera layer from OpenStreetMap via the shared Overpass proxy
body:
## What

Adds an optional **Speed Cameras** layer mapping OpenStreetMap `highway=speed_camera` nodes worldwide — the enforcement-device counterpart to the existing ALPR layer, which only covers the US/CA hourly extract (`surveillance:type=ALPR`).

## How

- `src/layers/speedCameras/`: policy / records / source / model / index. Records parse OSM tags (`maxspeed` incl. mph, `camera:direction` bearings, operator, ref, check_date), validate snapshots strictly, and never let a malformed payload become an authoritative empty map.
- The source POSTs viewport-bounded Overpass QL through the repo's shared `/api/overpass` proxy (caching, abuse guards, rate limiting) — no new server provider, no new keys. DI-injected `fetchImpl` for tests, matching repo convention.
- Lifecycle follows the earthquakes template (CustomDataSource + overlay-host labels) with ALPR-style city-bounded viewports (3°), 0.05° query snapping so pans reuse one accepted snapshot, debounce, and in-flight move handling. Failed queries keep the last accepted records.
- UI: panel entry under Infrastructure; voice manifest entry (queryable fields: maxspeedKph, directionDeg, operator, enforcement, ref); ambient km/h labels via the shared overlay host.
- Registration follows the repo's competing-PR protocol: speed-cameras reserves layer-state token `4` (token `3` was published by `gnss-integrity` after this branch first opened, so the provisional `3` was manually replaced with `4` per `npm run layer-token:check`).

## Data

Community-mapped device locations only — never live detections, enforcement schedules, or exhaustive coverage. Coverage mirrors OSM contributor density (AU: ~1,150 nodes; US: tens of thousands). Attribution rides the existing OpenStreetMap ODbL credit; `DATA_SOURCES.md` documents the layer's semantics next to the ALPR section.

## Validation

- `npm ci && npm test` on the branch rebased onto current `main` (`5b3e852a`): **6877 pass / 0 fail** (4 cancelled = known upstream flakes, 1 skipped = pre-existing)
- `npm run format:check` ✓ (1392 files) · `check:boundaries` ✓ · `npm run layer-token:check -- --base-ref origin/main` ✓ ("29 published, 2 new") · `npm run build` ✓
- Deployed live and exercised through the real proxy: Brisbane viewport returns 31 mapped cameras with correct tags

Related: #1129 (AU bushfire warnings). First CI run from a new account may sit at `action_required` until approved.

- Node 24.22.1/Linux: complete ordinary suite **9,607 passed, zero failed, two platform skips**; all **15 allocation assertions passed** (focus: 1; world overlay: 14). Focused HLS/fMP4/routes/admission suite: **50 passed**.

---

Recover expired live HLS windows and support whole-file fMP4/initialization assets using the existing admission mechanism in main. **No #1267 merge is required.** This updates the existing branch; no duplicate PR.

### Admission and lease scope

- Preserve main's unchanged `admitSameSiteKeyless` for every CCTV route before catalog/upstream work. Reverse-proxy playback works; foreign/opaque Origin, cross-site Fetch Metadata and conflicting forwarding-header cases are refused. The key-bearing Street View fallback retains its forwarding-header refusal.
- Exclude #1267's stricter `/media/` gate, socket-IP ownership and per-peer quota. Forwarded addresses are not used as identity.
- Retain main's demand/session capability model: two global sessions, eight consumer leases per session, active session+lease required for media/init reads, 15-second abandoned expiry, cancellation on last-consumer departure and disconnect cleanup.
- Leases identify decoder demand, not authenticated people. Anyone who learns active tokens can use them. One consumer can occupy both sessions/all leases; these bounds do **not** guarantee session fairness. Socket ownership groups NAT/proxy users and would not solve that scenario.

### Recovery and budgets

- **12 MiB per media file, 256 KiB per init, 24 MiB retained media+inits per session.** In-flight buffers are separately bounded, not a process-RSS promise.
- Start cold/restarted streams at the newest pair. Skip only older expired media 404s once, with discontinuity. Newest-pair/init/access/redirect/origin/TLS/oversize failures retain retries and cleanup.
- Composite media/init identities and initialization generations survive sliding windows, eviction and encoder restarts. Retained segments retain their own init. Encryption, byte ranges, mixed/switching containers remain refused.

title: feat: Integrate Real Estate and Vehicle Listings into the Map, with Listing History and VR Virtual Tours
body:
### Problem

Introduce a new feature in God’s Eye View that allows users to visualize real estate properties available for sale or rent, as well as vehicles listed for sale, directly on the map. Whenever the necessary data is available, the feature should also provide access to listing history and virtual reality (VR) tours.

Motivation

The goal is to make the map a more comprehensive discovery and exploration interface by combining geographic and commercial information into a unified experience.

Instead of relying exclusively on conventional searches across classified websites, users should be able to explore areas of interest visually, discover available properties and vehicles, and access relevant information about each listing without leaving the map experience.

### Proposal

1. Real Estate Listings: For Sale and for Rent

Display properties listed for sale or rent directly on the map.

Allow users to identify property locations and access available listing information.

Display details such as price, property type, images, and a link to the original listing, depending on data availability.

Provide filters for listing categories, including properties for sale and for rent, as well as other relevant characteristics.

2. Vehicles for Sale

Display vehicles listed for sale at their associated geographic locations, whenever this information is available.

Show details such as make, model, year, price, images, and a link to the original listing, depending on the available data.

Allow users to filter and explore vehicle listings directly through the map interface.

3. Listing History

When suitable data sources are available, provide historical information for real estate and vehicle listings.

Allow users to review recorded changes over time, such as price changes, listing updates, and availability status changes.

Clearly distinguish verified historical records from current information and estimates.

4. Virtual Tours and Virtual Reality (VR)

When a listing includes a compatible virtual tour, allow users to access it directly from the God’s Eye View interface.

Explore the possibility of integrating immersive VR experiences for viewing properties and other available environments.

Evaluate ways to display virtual tours within the application when technically feasible, or redirect users to compatible external services when necessary.

5. Map Integration

Associate listings with their corresponding geographic locations.

Allow users to select a listing on the map to view its details.

Evaluate methods for handling large numbers of listings without compromising map performance or usability.

Technical Considerations

Implementation should evaluate the availability of APIs, open data sources, and authorized integrations with listing platforms. Geographic coverage, data freshness, historical information, and access permissions will depend on the available data sources and their respective terms of use.

VR integration should take into account the technologies and devices supported by God’s Eye View.

Expected Benefits

Make geographic exploration more useful for discovering properties and vehicles.

Combine commercial information and geographic context within a single interface.

Make it easier to compare listings and track price changes over time.

Expand immersive exploration capabilities through VR virtual tours.

Initial Acceptance Criteria

Display real estate listings for sale and rent on the map using an available data source.

Display vehicle listings for sale on the map.

Allow users to view listing details and access the original listing source.

Implement basic filters by category and listing type.

Investigate and document viable data sources for listing history.

Investigate and document options for integrating VR virtual tours.

Ensure the feature does not significantly compromise map performance.

### Data source, license, and attribution

Feature concept: Original idea provided by the issue author.

This proposal describes a desired feature. Data availability, integration feasibility, and implementation details should be evaluated by the project's maintainers.

title: feat: Environmental Monitoring Layers for Air Quality, Drinking Water, and Radioactivity
body:
### Problem

Introduce environmental monitoring capabilities in God’s Eye View, allowing users to visualize air quality, drinking water quality, and environmental radioactivity directly on the map.

The goal is to provide an integrated geographic overview of environmental conditions using data from reliable monitoring stations, public agencies, scientific databases, and other authorized sources.

Where data is available, users should be able to explore current conditions, historical measurements, trends over time, and potential environmental risks.

Motivation

Environmental conditions can vary significantly across geographic areas, and relevant information is often scattered across different platforms and monitoring services.

Integrating environmental data into God’s Eye View would allow users to explore these conditions geographically, understand local environmental trends, identify areas requiring further investigation, and access the underlying data sources.

This feature should prioritize transparency, data reliability, geographic coverage, and clear communication of uncertainty.

### Proposal

Proposed Features

1. Air Quality Monitoring

Display air quality information directly on the map using monitoring stations and reliable data sources.

Show available pollutant measurements, including:

Particulate matter (PM2.5 and PM10).

Ground-level ozone (O₃).

Nitrogen dioxide (NO₂).

Sulfur dioxide (SO₂).

Carbon monoxide (CO).

Provide an air quality index (AQI) or equivalent regional indicator when supported by the data source.

Use a geographic overlay or color-coded visualization to represent reported air quality conditions.

Display measurement timestamps, monitoring station locations, data sources, and pollutant concentrations.

Allow users to explore historical measurements and changes in air quality over time.

Clearly distinguish direct measurements from modeled estimates and forecasts.

2. Drinking Water Quality and Potability

Display available drinking water quality data geographically.

Integrate information from public water authorities, environmental agencies, water quality monitoring programs, and other reliable sources.

Where available, display measurements and reported compliance information for relevant parameters, such as:

Microbiological indicators, including E. coli.

Turbidity.

pH.

Nitrate concentrations.

Relevant chemical contaminants and heavy metals.

Other parameters required by applicable drinking water standards.

Display sampling locations, sampling dates, measurement results, applicable standards, and source references.

Allow users to inspect historical measurements and identify documented changes in water quality.

Distinguish between treated public drinking water, surface water, groundwater, and other water sources whenever the underlying data supports that distinction.

Clearly identify whether the available evidence indicates compliance, non-compliance, insufficient data, or an unverified status.

Important: The absence of reported contamination must not be interpreted as proof that water is safe to drink. The interface must not label water as potable without sufficient, relevant evidence and an appropriate assessment against applicable standards.

3. Environmental Radioactivity Monitoring

Display available environmental radiation measurements on the map.

Integrate data from recognized radiation monitoring networks, public authorities, research institutions, and other reliable sources.

Where available, display:

Ambient gamma dose rates.

Measurements reported in nSv/h or µSv/h.

Relevant radionuclide measurements in air, water, soil, or other environmental samples.

Monitoring station locations and measurement timestamps.

Allow users to inspect historical measurements and compare readings over time.

Provide contextual information about measurement units, monitoring methods, and applicable reference levels.

Highlight unusual readings for further investigation when supported by validated data and appropriate thresholds.

Distinguish routine background radiation, verified abnormal measurements, modeled estimates, and unconfirmed reports.

Radiation measurements must be presented with sufficient context to avoid misleading comparisons between different measurement methods, environmental media, or monitoring systems.

4. Historical Data and Trend Analysis

Provide historical environmental measurements wherever reliable archives are available.

Allow users to select a time range and inspect changes in reported conditions.

Support time-series charts and geographic comparisons.

Display data collection dates, reporting dates, source information, and measurement limitations.

Identify missing periods and changes in monitoring coverage.

Avoid presenting interpolated values as direct measurements.

5. Geographic Visualization and Filtering

Provide independent map layers for air quality, drinking water quality, and environmental radioactivity.

Allow users to enable, disable, and combine supported layers.

Support filtering by measurement type, time range, data source, and geographic area.

Use map markers for monitoring stations and geographic overlays where the available data and resolution support them.

Provide a detailed information panel when a user selects a station, sampling location, or mapped area.

Clearly distinguish measured locations from interpolated areas and model-generated estimates.

6. Data Reliability and Transparency

Prioritize official monitoring networks, public environmental agencies, scientific institutions, and documented datasets.

Provide direct references to original data sources whenever possible.

Display timestamps, units, measurement methods, and relevant quality indicators.

Communicate uncertainty, reporting delays, and differences in regional standards.

Avoid generating unsupported safety assessments when data is incomplete, outdated, or unavailable.

Respect source licensing, API restrictions, attribution requirements, and applicable data usage policies.

Technical Considerations

Implementation should evaluate:

Available open datasets and authorized APIs for environmental monitoring.

Geographic coverage, spatial resolution, update frequency, and historical data availability.

Differences between national and international air quality and drinking water standards.

Compatibility with the existing map rendering and layer management architecture.

Efficient handling of large datasets through caching, spatial indexing, aggregation, and appropriate visualization techniques.

Methods for identifying outliers without automatically classifying every unusual reading as a confirmed hazard.

The distinction between measured data, interpolated data, forecasts, and user-reported information.

A modular architecture should be considered so that additional environmental datasets and monitoring categories can be integrated in the future.

Expected Benefits

Provide a unified geographic interface for exploring important environmental conditions.

Help users understand air pollution patterns and historical trends.

Improve access to available drinking water quality information.

Make environmental radiation measurements easier to discover and interpret.

Support environmental research, geographic analysis, and public awareness.

Establish a foundation for future environmental monitoring and alerting capabilities.

Initial Acceptance Criteria

Add an independently configurable map layer for air quality.

Add an independently configurable map layer for drinking water quality.

Add an independently configurable map layer for environmental radioactivity.

Integrate at least one suitable, documented data source for an initial implementation.

Display available measurement values, units, timestamps, and source references.

Distinguish measured data from estimates and areas without sufficient data.

Provide access to historical measurements when supported by the selected data sources.

Avoid unsupported claims that water is safe to drink or that an area is radiation-free.

Document data coverage, update frequency, limitations, and applicable standards.

Ensure that environmental layers can be explored without significantly degrading map performance.

Suggested Implementation Approach

Investigate available datasets and APIs for each environmental category.

Define a common data model for geographic measurements, timestamps, units, provenance, and uncertainty.

Implement one environmental layer as an initial proof of concept.

Extend the architecture to support the remaining layers.

Add historical visualization and geographic filtering.

Document data limitations and establish validation requirements before introducing alerts or risk classifications.

### Data source, license, and attribution

Feature concept: Original idea provided by the issue author.

Writing and structuring: ChatGPT (OpenAI), based on the author's ideas and instructions.

This proposal describes a desired feature. Data availability, integration feasibility, scientific interpretation, and implementation details should be evaluated by the project's maintainers.

### Will you build it?

Yes, I plan to open a PR

title: fix(cctv): serve only live feeds on /media
body:
`/api/cctv/media/:id` exists for live video (HLS, MP4/WebM, MJPEG), but it also accepted still-image cameras and relayed them with an ordinary fetch: it followed redirects to any host, passed through any content type and had no body cap. Still images are already served by `/api/cctv/frame/:id`, which keeps redirects on the registered origin, accepts only `image/*` and caps the body, and no client requests a still through `/media`.

`/media` now answers 404 for anything that is not a live feed, before any upstream request. Video behaviour is unchanged.

Found while reviewing the new camera packs (#595, #607, #640, #644, #645), which all add still-image sources.

**Tests:** `src/data/cctvMediaFeedType.test.mjs` covers a still camera refused on `/media` with no upstream request (the upstream mock redirects to a link-local address and then serves HTML), unknown ids, video and MJPEG still relayed, and stills still served by `/frame`. The refusal test fails on `main`, where the 302 is passed through. Full local gates pass: `npm test`, build, `test:track`.
