title: Proposal: Flat World mode — north-polar azimuthal-equidistant view (follow-up to #96)
body:
Following up on your comment in #96 — I built a working azimuthal-equidistant mode and wanted to ask before sending any code.

**What it is:** a **FLAT WORLD** button that switches to a North-Pole-centred azimuthal-equidistant disc (1892 Gleason layout) in full 3D: terrain, bathymetry, OSM buildings, live aircraft and satellites. **BACK TO GLOBE** returns.

It's presented as a map projection, not a claim about Earth's shape: every real position comes from its true WGS84 coordinates, a route tool compares the flat straight line with the real geodesic, and the procedural ice beyond the South-Pole circle is labelled hypothetical.

**How it's built (upfront):**
- A separate three.js renderer beside the hidden Cesium globe, not Cesium itself. Nothing loads until the button is first pressed; the globe and its layers are untouched.
- New dependencies: `three` and `geographiclib-geodesic`.
- Keyless sources only (Esri, Mapterhorn, NOAA ETOPO, NASA GIBS, OpenFreeMap, Natural Earth), attribution shown, CSP unchanged.
- It's big: roughly 70 files / 26k lines.

**Questions before I open a PR:**
1. Would you take this at all, given it's three.js rather than native Cesium?
2. If yes, behind a flag, or split into smaller PRs (projection + disc first, then live data, then the ice world)?

If you're open to it, I'll rebuild it on current `main` and keep `build`, `npm test` and `test:track` green before opening anything. Happy to share screenshots or a short screen recording.

title: fix(director): land on the requested shot
body:
Go-to-shot sometimes landed on the end of the previous shot. A shot action seeks to the target's `startProgress` (`start / total`). `sceneSeekState` turned that back into seconds, and `(start / total) * total` can round one ulp below `start`, so `targetSec < shotEnd` picked the shot before it. With five 3.9 s shots, going to shots 2, 3 and 5 landed on 1, 2 and 4.

`sceneSeekState` now compares the progress against each shot's `end / total`, the same division the caller used. Exact boundaries still select the next shot. The reported elapsed time is clamped to the selected shot's start too, so `sceneElapsedSec`/`sceneProgress` agree with `shotIndex` instead of sitting one ulp before it.

| go-to-shot seeks (2–12 shots, 0.1–10 s flight, 0–5 s hold) | wrong before | wrong after |
|---|---|---|
| equal shots, 392,700 seeks | 7,316 | 0 |
| every third shot 1.7 s longer, 392,700 seeks | 11,909 | 0 |

**Verified**
- New exhaustive test in `src/director/timeline.test.mjs`. Seeking to every shot's start lands in that shot, at or after its start, and one or two ulps earlier lands in the previous shot. It fails on `main` and against epsilon/tolerance variants, and every check was mutation-tested.
- Driving `SceneDirector` in headless Chrome with the 3.9 s case, all five go-to-shot seeks now land on the requested shot (three were wrong before).
- `npm test`: 7003 pass. `npm run test:track` 109/109, `npm run build`, `format:check`, `check:boundaries` and `scripts/qa-director-timing.mjs` all pass.

I updated `CHANGELOG.md` and `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md`.

title: fix(cctv): keep missing numbers unknown instead of reading them as zero
body:
Number() reads null, blank strings and booleans as 0 (or 1), and /api/cctv/sources sends an unknown number as JSON null. A source-pack camera that left out its pose therefore reached the browser as zeros clamped to each field's floor (north, pitch -2, FOV 20, range 120 m, mount 6 m, ground 0 m) instead of taking the defaults, and a null or blank position put the camera at 0,0.

toFiniteNumber (server) and safeNumber (browser) now return the fallback for absent, blank and boolean values, as validateBox already does for Recent Imagery. The same conversion fixes the per-pack paths: a Tallinn row with a null heading no longer reads as a high-confidence north-facing camera, a Caltrans camera with a blank elevation keeps its 150 m ground prior, and TfL or Catalonia cameras with a null or blank coordinate are dropped instead of kept at 0,0 or on the zero meridian.

title: fix(geo): wrap longitude differences across the antimeridian
body:
The flights ground-floor pipeline and the nearby-sites search subtracted longitudes without wrapping. Two points 0.2° apart either side of 180° (21 km at Fiji) measured about 38,000 km.

- `approxDistanceKm` (the 150 km floor radius, the display-floor check and the held-floor drift bound) and its copy in `meshFloorSampler.js` (the 15 km probe gate). Low and grounded aircraft just across the line from the viewer were never floored or mesh-sampled.
- `corridorFloorCells` walked a segment across 180° the long way round. It filled its cell budget with ground behind the contact and never asked for the cells it was about to cross.
- `stickyFloorCell` lost its hysteresis for a contact on the seam, so the cell flipped every tick.
- SEARCH NEARBY SITES centred its Places search on `(west + east) / 2`. A view across 180° has west > east, so that was longitude 0, the far side of the globe. The radius also ignored the view's width.

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `approxDistanceKm(-16.8, 179.9, -16.8, -179.9)` | 38,343 km | 21.3 km |
| Mesh cells probed, viewer 179.999 / cell -179.999 | 0 of 2 | 2 of 2 |
| Corridor 179.999 → -179.998 | 179.999 … 179.989 (behind), then -179.998 | 179.999, 180, -180, -179.999, -179.998 |
| Sticky cell on the seam | released every tick | held |
| Places search for a 179.7…-179.9 view | lon -0.1, 11 km | lon 179.9, 22 km |

The fix uses the wrap `traffic/footprint.js` already uses. The haversine copies are already safe. I kept the box centre local rather than importing `areaCenter` from `src/tools`, because that import breaks `check:boundaries` (installations-layer would pull in `tools/schema.js`).

Not fixed:
- `vessels/viewArea.js` `viewAreaMovedEnough` has the same bug, but its only effect is an extra request near 180°. I couldn't confirm that the upstream lat/lon/radius_km vessel query wraps across 180°. If it doesn't, that extra refetch is what loads the far side, so I left it alone.
- Other unwrapped flat-earth distances (transit movement and trails, local ADS-B motion, traffic viewport, `featureGeometry`) are left for a follow-up.

**Verified**
- New tests in `recordPolicy.test.mjs`, `meshFloorSampler.test.mjs`, `groundFloor.test.mjs` and `installations/ingestion.test.mjs`. They fail on `main`, and each assertion was mutation-checked.
- `npm test`: 7011 pass.
- `npm run test:track`: 109/109.
- `npm run build`, `format:check` and `check:boundaries` all pass.

I updated `CHANGELOG.md`.

title: fix(sdr): find FM stations after seek wraps the band
body:
Local FM seek never found a station once it wrapped past the end of the band. `seekFm` wraps each spectrum frame's centre back into 87.5–108 MHz, but it kept passing the unwrapped starting frequency to `findDirectionalFmPeak`. After the wrap, every channel in the frame sat on the wrong side of the start and was skipped. So a seek up from the top of the band, or down from the bottom, always ended with "No FM signal found".

The frames either side of the wrap also missed the band edges. Each frame sees about ±0.87 MHz and frames are 1.2 MHz apart, so depending on the starting frequency, 87.5 or 108.0 MHz (and up to 0.3 MHz next to them) fell between two frames. Seeking up from 107.0 never looked at 108.0.

A frame could also be read from the wrong spectrum. The worker keeps posting spectra of samples taken before a retune, and seek read the first one to arrive against the new centre.

| Seek | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Up from 107.5, station at 88.5 | No FM signal found | 88.5 |
| Up from 107.9, station at 87.5 | No FM signal found | 87.5 |
| Down from 87.6, station at 108.0 | No FM signal found | 108.0 |
| Up from 98.5, only station at 98.2 | No FM signal found | 98.2 |

Changes:
- Each frame passes the start frequency shifted by the same lap as the frame.
- The lap is one step longer than the band, with frame centres clamped into it, so both edge channels are always seen. `Math.ceil(lap / step)` = 19 frames cover it.
- `findDirectionalFmPeak` takes a `skipFrequency`, so when a lap comes back to the starting station it moves on to the next one in the same frame.
- `tuneFm` takes a new tag before touching the tuner and sends it to the worker with the reset. The worker echoes the tag, and spectra with any other tag are dropped, including after a retune that fails part-way. A new worker starts the tag again at 0.
- A failed retune stops the seek.

With no other station heard, seek still reports none and returns to where it started.

Not changed: a manual tune during a seek, and audio samples from before a retune (they reach the audio worklet by a separate, untagged path).

**Verified**
- New `controller.test.mjs` cases run on the real `_waitForSpectrum` and worker-message path, with stale spectra delivered on every retune. They cover:
  - the wrap in both directions
  - both edge channels from 16 starting frequencies
  - a full lap
  - passing over the starting station
  - no station found
  - a failed retune
  - a retune that fails part-way
  - a rebuilt worker
- A `spectrum.test.mjs` case covers `skipFrequency` and its 75 kHz boundary.
- The five seek tests fail on `main`, and every assertion was mutation-checked.
- `npm test`: 7013 pass. `npm run build`, `format:check` and `check:boundaries` all pass.

I updated `CHANGELOG.md` and `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md`.

title: Add AlphaEarth Change: where the land changed between two years
body:
Adds **DATA ▸ AlphaEarth Change**, a layer that answers one question for any box up to 100 km a side: **where did the land change between two years?** It reads Google DeepMind's [AlphaEarth Foundations Satellite Embedding](https://deepmind.google/discover/blog/alphaearth-foundations-helps-map-our-planet-in-unprecedented-detail/) dataset from the keyless [Source Cooperative mirror](https://source.coop/tge-labs/aef). It is the first *analytical* earth-observation layer in the app. Every other imagery layer shows a picture. This one compares two years and shows only what changed.

Related: #814 (the "What Changed" RFC) and #303 (Amazon monitoring). It does not implement either. It provides the yearly "where did the ground change" signal both describe. Notes at the end.

## What you see (and what you don't)

**This is a change map, not a before/after photo comparison.** That is the thing most likely to surprise a first-time user, so the panel and docs say it up front.

- AlphaEarth does not ship images. For every 10 m pixel of land, for every year since 2017, it gives a 64-number **embedding**. That is a learned summary of everything the satellites saw there that year: Sentinel-2 optical, Sentinel-1 radar, Landsat, elevation, climate. Similar ground gets similar vectors.
- The layer takes the two years' vectors for each pixel and computes `1 − cosine`. The result is 0 where the place is the same kind of place and grows as it becomes something else. The vectors are unit length, so this is one dot product per pixel.
- The result is draped as a heatmap. Pixels below the threshold are transparent. Above it the colour runs from amber (some change) to magenta (total change), over whatever basemap is showing. Esri imagery underneath gives the context.

Because each embedding summarises a whole year, the layer is **independent of clouds, sensor and season**: a cloudy June does not read as change. It **cannot see single-day events**: a flood that came and went in a week, or a fire scar that greened up the same year. The status line says "annual embeddings, not single-day events".

## What it is good for

- **Construction and urban growth.** New factories, neighbourhoods, roads, airports and solar farms light up clearly. Giga Texas, built 2020–2022, compares at a mean change of 0.185 against 0.036 for a settled Austin neighbourhood next to it. That is the live QA gate below.
- **Deforestation and land clearing** (#303). Forest turned into pasture or cropland is a large change in embedding space. Forest that is the same forest a year later is not.
- **Agricultural conversion.** Pasture to greenhouses, new irrigation, abandoned fields.
- **Mining, quarries, reservoirs and coastline changes.**
- **Triage at a glance.** It answers "where in this 100 km box should I look?" with one map and three numbers instead of scrubbing years of imagery by eye. The panel reports the changed share at the current threshold, the mean change, the 95th percentile and the coverage.

## How to use it

1. DATA ▸ Cameras ▸ **AlphaEarth Change** ▸ ON. Its panel opens on the right rail and takes the rail from an open DISPLAY.
2. **SELECT BOX** and drag on the map, or **USE VIEW** to compare what the camera sees. Boxes larger than 100 km a side are refused with their size, never silently shrunk.
3. Pick **FROM / TO** (2017–2025, as published) and **DETAIL**: Standard, or High, which is slower and about twice as fine.
4. Wait about half a minute the first time a box is read. After that it is cached.
5. Move **THRESHOLD**. It is applied in the browser, so the slider repaints at once and never makes a request. The default is 0.35. Lower values show subtler change, and below about 0.1 normal crop-cycle differences start to show.
6. If almost nothing in the box reaches the threshold, the status says so and names the strongest change found. **SHOW STRONGEST 1%** then sets the threshold that reveals the top 1% of the box. If even that is under 0.05, it says "This place barely changed".

The box, years, detail and threshold travel in **share links** (layer token `5`), so a comparison can be sent to someone else.

## How it works

```
browser                                 server (Vite plugin)                     Source Cooperative
───────                                 ────────────────────                     ──────────────────
box + years ──► /api/alpha-earth/change ──► catalog: which COGs cover the box ──► aef_index.parquet (column + byte-range reads)
                                        ──► cog: overview level that fits budget ──► v1/annual/{year}/{zone}/*.tiff (HTTP ranges)
                                        ──► change: WGS84 grid, 1 − cos, u8
            ◄── { grid (base64 u8), stats, box, m/px } ◄──
threshold + palette on a canvas ─► SingleTileImageryProvider on the current imagery host
```

**Server.** `server/providers/alphaEarth.js` plus `server/providers/alphaEarth/` adds `/api/alpha-earth/{years,change,status}`, registered in `localProviderPlugins()` like the other providers.
- **Catalog.** Reads only the columns it needs from `aef_index.parquet` with `hyparquet` over byte ranges. It never downloads the 800 MB CSV index.
- **COG reads.** Uses `geotiff` with HTTP range requests on the year's UTM COGs (8192², 64 int8 bands, 1024² tiles). It picks the finest overview whose estimated read fits a byte budget: Standard 64 MB, High 256 MB, both years together. It flips the bottom-up rows, de-quantises `sign(v)·(v/127.5)²` and masks `-128` as no data. A transient network error (socket reset, timeout, DNS) reopens the file and retries once. HTTP errors and aborts do not retry.
- **Change grid.** Samples a north-up WGS84 grid (up to 1,024 px a side) across tiles and UTM zones, so boxes that straddle a zone boundary just work. It quantises `1 − cos` to `u8` (0–254, with 255 = no data) and computes `meanChange`, `p95Change` and `validFraction`.
- **Guard rails.** Boxes must be at most 100 km a side, not cross the dateline and lie within ±85°. Two jobs run at once with a 240 s timeout. Identical concurrent requests coalesce. Results are cached for 30 days, 24 in memory and the rest under `.gev-cache/alpha-earth/`. Requests are rate limited per client.

**Client.** `src/layers/alphaEarth/`, structured like `recentImagery/`, with everything injected and tested with `node:test`.
- **Data.** `source.js` validates the grid's encoding and size and turns server error codes into sentences. `model.js` holds the pure pieces: box validation and quantisation, the year pair, grid decoding, the changed share and the quiet-box summary.
- **Drawing.** `rendering.js` colours the grid on one canvas and drapes it on the host that `src/maps/imageryHost.js` resolves: the globe's imagery layers, or the photoreal tileset's while the globe is hidden. It rebuilds when the map stack switches. A newer request aborts an older one, and changing years or detail drops the old map at once.
- **Panel.** `src/ui/alphaEarth.js` builds the panel once and updates it in place, so a notification never steals focus from a select or the slider. SELECT BOX reuses `initImageryBoxTool`. That tool gained an optional `validate` hook so a layer can impose its own limits; Recent Imagery is unchanged.

## Data source and licence

- **Dataset.** AlphaEarth Foundations Satellite Embedding V1, annual, 2017–2025, 10 m. **CC BY 4.0.** Required attribution: *"The AlphaEarth Foundations Satellite Embedding dataset is produced by Google and Google DeepMind."* It is shown in the panel and added to `dataCredits.js` and `DATA_SOURCES.md`.
- **Access.** Source Cooperative mirror at `data.source.coop/tge-labs/aef`. Keyless, CORS `*`, byte ranges. **No API key or account is needed.** Nothing is redistributed: data is read at runtime, and only derived change grids are cached locally.
- **New dependencies**, both MIT and server-only:
  - `geotiff` 3.0.5, for COG range reads.
  - `hyparquet` 1.31.4, a dependency-free Parquet reader for the index.

## Verification

| Gate | Result |
|---|---|
| `npm test` | 7,106 tests, 0 failures |
| `npm run test:track` | 109 passed, 0 failed |
| `npm run build` | ✅ |
| `npm run format:check` | ✅ |
| `npm run check:boundaries` | ✅ (new `alpha-earth-change` and `alpha-earth-source` groups) |
| `npm run layer-token:check -- --base-ref upstream/main` | ✅ 31 published, 1 new (`5`) |
| `node scripts/qa-alpha-earth.mjs` (live, against the real mirror) | **17/17** |

**Unit tests.** They use synthetic COGs and no network:
- Server: index parsing, overview choice, de-quantisation and the bottom-up flip, UTM sampling across zones, the change maths, query validation and the transient-error retry.
- Layer: lifecycle, request supersession, threshold without a request, share-link parameters and host rebinding.
- Panel: first appearance, controls, cleanup of every listener, and the quiet-box message and reveal.

**Live gate `scripts/qa-alpha-earth.mjs`.** Exits 0 with SKIP when the mirror is unreachable. It drives the real app in Puppeteer:
- opens DISPLAY first and checks that the AlphaEarth panel still takes the rail;
- checks the year list;
- compares Giga Texas against a settled Austin neighbourhood for 2018 → 2024 (mean 0.185 vs 0.036, 20.2% changed);
- checks the drape lands on its host;
- moves the threshold and checks that no request is made;
- checks that a 476 km view is refused with its size;
- checks CLEAR and disable;
- checks there are no page errors.

**Manual checks:**
- The Austin and Bogotá savanna greenhouses, at Standard and High.
- A quiet Siberian taiga box, which led to the quiet-box hint.
- Switching between the Esri, OSM and Google 3D maps with a comparison on screen.

## Scope and what's next

Deliberately left out to keep this reviewable. Each would be its own PR:

1. **Before/after imagery.** A swipe between the FROM and TO years' photos under the change map. Esri World Imagery Wayback, keyless, has 197 releases from 2014 to 2026; the swipe would reuse `createImagerySplit`, which Recent Imagery already uses.
2. **MCP / voice tool `get_alpha_earth_change`**, returning the summary and statistics for an area. The voice manifest currently marks the layer `noQuery`.
3. **"Places like this."** Similarity search: click a pixel, and every pixel whose embedding is close lights up. This is the most distinctive thing AlphaEarth can do, and it reuses the same reader with half the bytes.
4. **An RGB view of the embeddings**, for terrain types at a glance.
5. **Finer pixels for small boxes.** The budget would scale with tiles touched instead of area.

**About #814.** The RFC is about a live delta ribbon. AlphaEarth is annual, so it is not a natural live producer. When the ribbon exists, a finished comparison could post one event, such as "AlphaEarth 2018→2024 · 20% changed in box".

title: feat(bikeshare): add Barcelona's Bicing and AMBici
body:
## Summary

Adds Barcelona's two station-based bike-share systems to the Bike Share layer and `get_bike_share`, 780 stations in all:

| System | Area | Source | Stations |
|---|---|---|---|
| Bicing | Barcelona | PBSC (`barcelona.publicbikesystem.net`) | 543 |
| AMBici | Barcelona metropolitan area (e-bikes) | nextbike (`gbfs.nextbike.net`) | 237 |

Both feeds are keyless GBFS 2.3 and are listed in MobilityData's `systems.csv`. These are the layer's first stations in Spain.

## Changes

- **Registry**: two new entries in `src/layers/bikeshare/registry.js`, written longhand like the other PBSC entries. Bicing uses the same `/customer/gbfs/v2/en/station_{information,status}.json` shape as Toronto, Detroit and the Bike Itaú cities.
- **Allowlist**: `gbfs.nextbike.net` joins `GBFS_ALLOWED_HOSTS` as an exact host. It serves only GBFS, so no path prefix is needed. Bicing needs no change, because the `*.publicbikesystem.net` wildcard already covers it.
- **Load radius**: both systems use 40 km. AMBici's farthest station is about 19 km from its centre, so `get_bike_share` over Barcelona searches both systems and nothing farther away. The map layer still uses its 100 km minimum.
- **Attribution**: two rows in `DATA_SOURCES.md`, and both operators are named in the shared `gbfs` credit in `dataCredits.js`:
  - Bicing: the feed publishes no licence. The City's open-data copy of the same station data is CC BY 4.0 but needs a token, so the operator feed is used and attribution goes to Barcelona City Council (B:SM).
  - AMBici: `system_information.license_id` is `CC0-1.0`. No attribution is required, but it is given anyway.
- **Docs**: `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md` and `CHANGELOG.md` are updated.

Out of scope: Barcelona's dockless operators (Bird, Cooltra, Donkey Republic, …) have no fixed stations, so they are not added here.

## Notes

- AMBici stations can report more bikes than their `capacity`, because nextbike lets riders return a bike next to a full station. The layer shows the feed values as they are. Those stations render green and their counts read, for example, `27 avail · 0 docks · 18 cap`.
- MobilityData lists Bicing's v3.0 discovery URL. The v2 feeds are used to match every other PBSC entry; both serve the same stations.

title: ci: add npmscan dependency security check
body:
### What does this PR do?
Integrates `npmscan-action` as a non-blocking supply-chain security check on Pull Requests.

`npmscan` checks incoming PRs for:
- Lockfile overrides that could pull in malicious transitive dependencies
- Unexpected new `postinstall` scripts
- Tarball swaps and checksum mismatches

### Why?
Supply-chain attacks (like the recent ChainDrop and malicious axios typosquats) often sneak in via lockfile updates in otherwise benign PRs. This check helps reviewers spot those anomalies automatically.

### Configuration Notes
- **Non-blocking**: Configured with `mode: warn` and `fail-on-error: false`. It will only post a warning annotation if an issue is found and will **never fail the CI build**, ensuring it doesn't disrupt your workflow.
- **Immutable Action**: The action is pinned to a specific commit SHA (`de14168f65640a4ed1f0e82ad3ad8c80483d360d`) rather than a floating tag, following security best practices.

### Disclosure
I maintain npmscan and npmscan-action. If this isn't a fit for the project, feel free to close; no hard feelings.

title: Proposal: worldwide phone interface with compact navigation and explicit location
body:
### Problem

On a phone, the globe competes with several panels for limited screen space. Common actions such as choosing an area, enabling a layer, inspecting a contact and returning to the map require navigating unrelated controls.

This proposes a worldwide phone interface: the same experience for any chosen place, using whichever existing sources cover that area. Location names, regional presets and source availability come from the application rather than a hard-coded home region. Implementation scope and ownership should be agreed before code is submitted.

### Proposal

A compact phone presentation for worldwide use, using the existing application controls and layer lifecycle, with four navigation entries:

- **Map:** return to the globe and dismiss the current sheet.
- **Nearby:** choose from existing layers and controls relevant to the selected area. Show enabled state, source freshness and unavailable coverage honestly; presence in this menu does not imply coverage everywhere.
- **Location:** use the current map area, search for a place, or explicitly choose **Use my location**.
- **More:** reach every other capability currently available in that deployment, including voice, HUD/display settings, radio, weather, imagery, cameras, scenes and inspection tools. Existing permission and administration restrictions continue to apply.

Only one main sheet takes focus at a time. A visible close button returns space to the map without switching off enabled layers, clearing the chosen area or resetting selection. Selected/tracked context retains a compact, actionable summary. Opening or closing a sheet must preserve existing camera and media ownership rules.

Suggested journey: open the app → choose an area or explicitly use device location → open Nearby → enable Transport → close the sheet → inspect available vehicles on the map. Reopen Nearby to change the layer. The same flow should work with any existing supported area and source.

### Location behavior

- Opening the app or Nearby never requests geolocation or moves the camera.
- **Use my location** requests one browser fix after a user action, with locating, denied, unavailable, timeout and retry states. Manual search and the current map area remain usable.
- Apply navigation through the application's supported handoff. Shared-view restoration, scenes and tracking retain their ownership; a superseded or cancelled location result cannot move the camera later.
- No continuous location watch in the initial version. Device coordinates remain session state and are not silently written to storage, logs, analytics or copied/share links. Any explicit sharing behavior must be documented and tested.
- Distance controls apply only where the existing source supports them; do not imply administrative-boundary filtering or invent missing data.

### Dashboard visibility

Provide a visible, accessible **Hide dashboards / Show dashboards** control. An optional stationary press-and-hold on empty map space may invoke the same action if compatible with existing gestures. Movement, multiple pointers, map picking, controls and active interactions cancel it. The gesture is never the only way to restore controls. Hiding presentation does not change layer, voice, playback or selection state.

### Implementation boundaries

- Install through normal application/UI composition with explicit services and a destroy path. Reuse existing controllers, navigation, layer state and surface ownership.
- No global debug handles or private navigation methods. Remove listeners/timers, abort pending work and release resources/credits on teardown; restoring desktop layout must not leave duplicate controls or bindings.
- Keep attribution and freshness/error feedback visible as appropriate to enabled sources. Automatic refresh must not steal focus or choose a different sheet.
- Respect desktop, embedded, Clean View, cockpit, recording and scene presentation contracts.
- Data providers, regional source packs, native apps, hosting, authentication setup and provider budgets are separate work. This proposal introduces no automatic paid calls or provider activation.

### Acceptance criteria

- At representative 375×667 and 390×844 portrait sizes, and touch landscape, the globe remains usable with no horizontal page overflow or unreachable controls.
- Voice, HUD, radio, weather, imagery, cameras and inspection retain equivalent access; opening one sheet and returning to the map preserves enabled state.
- Touch targets, safe areas, the on-screen keyboard, larger text, focus restoration, keyboard dismissal and VoiceOver labels are verified.
- No location prompt or fly-to occurs on startup. Explicit location, permission denial, cancellation, shared links, scenes and tracking have regression coverage.
- Repeated enable/disable, resize and teardown do not accumulate listeners, timers, requests, credits or map resources.
- Desktop and embedded regressions pass. Any implementation PR includes the repository's required unit/build/tracking checks and relevant browser gates, plus phone screenshots using synthetic data or public demonstration locations. A design proposal is not a claim that these tests have already passed.

### Coordination and delivery

Related work: [mobile request #642](https://github.com/bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view/issues/642), [panel attention #815](https://github.com/bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view/issues/815), [touch/iPad #930](https://github.com/bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view/pull/930), [mobile camera workflows #1069](https://github.com/bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view/pull/1069), [explicit location #238](https://github.com/bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view/pull/238) and [home-screen support #636](https://github.com/bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view/pull/636).

The intent is to agree a shared direction with those contributors and reuse accepted work. Suggested implementation stages: (1) compact navigation and complete control access; (2) Nearby composition and explicit location; (3) optional hold gesture and accessibility refinements. Each stage should be independently reviewable. Maintainer preference for extending an existing proposal is welcome.

### Data source, license, and attribution

None added: this is a UI proposal using existing sources and preserving their attribution.

### Will you build it?

Yes, I plan to open a focused PR after the direction and overlap with existing work are agreed.

title: [Superseded by #1146] test(qa): selected FIRMS action wait
body:
## Closed as duplicate of the original author's work

On current review, **radianx's existing [#1146](https://github.com/bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view/pull/1146) already implements the same bounded selected-action wait**, using the option `selected` and real browser QA. That earlier owner should retain the implementation and merge path; this PR must not compete for it.

The unique contribution here is the three focused tests for delayed selected-state publication, timeout/absence, and default aggregate-count behavior. These were made available with attribution to radianx [on #1146's existing review](https://github.com/bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view/pull/1146#pullrequestreview-5543912872). quanticsoul4772 independently ran them on Windows 11/Node 24.16: 3/3 focused and 7,607 full-suite passes (10 skips) on an integrated local check, but no FIRMS browser gate; thank you for the validation. Prior Hermes-assisted original test work remains credited in [fork #235](https://github.com/kvnloo/gods-eye-view/pull/235).

**Disposition: SUPERSEDED / CLOSED UNMERGED.** No duplicate upstream merge requested; no further action needed on this carrier. If the owner wants the tests, the original evidence remains available. Existing #1146 remains subject to normal maintainer review and tests.

---

## Updated exact-head CI — October 16, 2026

[GitHub Actions run #38932386504](https://github.com/bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view/actions/runs/38932386504) **SUCCESS** for current head [`abe5d81`](https://github.com/kvnloo/gods-eye-view/commit/abe5d81e4a653410f219683f202b9c57936cffe0). Both supported Node jobs (24.14 and 26) completed locked dependency install, doctor, **adopted Prettier formatting, package boundaries, unit tests and production Vite build**. Windows onboarding and the separate Street Level browser/panel gates also passed. The historical statement below that these commands had not run on the transplanted head is superseded.

**Remain DRAFT / LIMITED:** the successful browser job tests Street Level and panel routes, **not a fresh live FIRMS selected-action browser trace**. The motivating FIRMS before/after capture and real-browser proof remain historical donor-branch evidence, not a measured post-port flake reduction. This patch changes only the bounded QA waiter + its three regression tests; no production FIRMS provider change or safety claim. Independent maintainer review and normal branch updating still needed. Original GEV/QA contributors, Hermes donor and GPT-6 port retain credit.

---

## Problem

The FIRMS headless action gate sampled the selected-action proof after a fixed 250 ms sleep. The accessible button may be present before its selected state is published, making a healthy app look broken. The existing `waitForFirmsActionCount` already polls for aggregate buttons, so this fix reuses it with a `selectedOnly` option before sampling selection state.

## Change

- Add `selectedOnly` to the existing bounded action waiter; default still checks aggregate button count.
- Replace the selected-action `sleep(250)` with a wait for exactly one selected FIRMS action.
- Add three focused Node tests for publication delay, bounded absence, and unchanged aggregate mode. Register them in the existing format-scope manifest.
- The application runtime, FIRMS source, layer renderer and provider network behavior do not change.

## Verification and limits

Cleanly applied from the existing [downstream QA carrier #235](https://github.com/kvnloo/gods-eye-view/pull/235) onto **current upstream `main@537e99dfa45a3f7b239ad6230a65be658b3ea29d`**; current branch `abe5d81e4a653410f219683f202b9c57936cffe0`, **3 commits ahead / 0 behind**, exactly three scoped files.

Previous donor source/tests: Node 24.14.0 and Node 26.5.0 **3/3 tests per runtime**, independently verified 11 additional controls per runtime. Earlier real-browser gate **7/8 before → 8/8 candidate** on the motivating captured trace; independent baseline also passed 8/8 twice, so **no measured flake-rate reduction is claimed**. Delayed publication negative control returned 7/8 without the wait and 8/8 with it. Historical source-tree full suites reported ~6,346 passes per Node version.

**Not yet run on the newly transplanted exact head:** full `npm run build`, `npm test`, `npm run test:track` and a fresh whole-browser FIRMS gate. The previous browser/runtime evidence is dated and from the donor branch. Do not infer current-main acceptance from it. There is no mobile/GPU/live-provider benchmark.

## Ownership

Prior donor fix and test methodology from [kvnloo/gods-eye-view #235](https://github.com/kvnloo/gods-eye-view/pull/235), developed and independently checked with Hermes/AI assistance. Original God's Eye View code and QA contracts remain credited to Bilawal Sidhu and contributors. This does not duplicate quanticsoul4772's merged Windows early-exit [#1064](https://github.com/bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view/pull/1064). AI-assisted clean current-main port (GPT-6) and original donor provenance are disclosed.

title: Satellites catalogued since July 2026 never appear: CelesTrak doesn't serve 6-digit catalog numbers as TLE
body:
CelesTrak's usage policy (https://www.celestrak.org/usage-policy.php) says 5-digit catalog numbers ran out on 2026-07-11 and that objects numbered 100000+ are not available in TLE format at all; its TLE output does not use Alpha-5. The satellite layer requests `FORMAT=tle`, so those objects never reach the app, whatever the parser does (#751 / #767 make the parser correct, but the feed never contains them).

Checked 2026-10-16: `GROUP=active&FORMAT=tle` returned 15,927 satellites, none with an Alpha-5 field, highest catalog number 69998.

Reaching newer objects means moving the satellite fetch to one of CelesTrak's OMM formats (JSON or CSV), which carry full catalog numbers. satellite.js can build a satrec from OMM fields (`json2satrec`, present in the installed 6.0.2), so propagation stays the same.

title: fix(sdr): stabilize local playback and integrate seek-wrap fix
body:
Local RTL-SDR could fall behind after several minutes: USB input paused between reads, decoder messages could queue without a limit, and stopping left old worker output alive. This keeps four USB reads pending in order, bounds unacknowledged decoder work, and terminates stopped workers. FM playback uses an 80 ms prebuffer and a 256 ms queue cap; signal display updates are coalesced and spectra are calculated only while seeking.

This also integrates the seek-wrap and fresh-spectrum fixes from #1174 onto current `main`. Thank you to Aditya (@Rohilalala): their runtime changes and regression coverage are retained, with a `Co-authored-by` trailer and release-note credit. #1174 will be closed as superseded after this replacement lands.

### Validation

- Node 24.14.0, keyless isolated checkout, clean environment; setup doctor, formatting and package boundaries pass.
- Final unit suite: 7,121 passed, one skipped; all 15 serialized allocation checks passed. Production build passed.
- The same runtime passed a 10-minute full-app hardware run on a Nooelec NESDR SMArt v5 at 101.3 MHz: 37,547 decoded blocks, zero audio underruns, zero overflow drops and no decoder overload. Pending decoder work peaked at one block. Queue accounting cleared fully on Stop.
- Built-app checks passed for forward/reverse seek, FM → ADS-B → FM, disconnect and reconnect.
- Tracking regression: 109 passed, zero failed/skipped, clean console and no HTTP 5xx responses, using the supported `--url` option on candidate port 4177 (the user's existing server occupies 4173).
- Adjacent Radio browser gate: 106 passed, zero failed/skipped, clean console and no HTTP 5xx responses. It initially passed 105/106 on both candidate and unchanged `main`: the only failure was an optional Google token endpoint returning 404. A separate test-only commit supplies an exact same-origin GET fixture representing no offered token (`200 {}`); it retains the console/error assertions.

### Limits

The historical slowdown trigger was not isolated, and one 10-minute foreground run does not prove hours-long stability or all workloads. This does not change the existing seek peak-selection algorithm, final-retune failure reporting, or USB initialization handling. No dependencies, CI permissions, production network destinations or credential handling change.

title: fix(launches): keep null pad and landing coordinates unknown instead of 0
body:
## Problem

Launch Library pad fields used Number(value), so null, blank and boolean values could become zero. That placed unknown pads at 0°N 0°E and bypassed valid location coordinates. The shared stage helper also turned undisclosed coordinates and flight numbers into zero.

## Change

Reuse finiteCoordinate for both pad fields and the location fallback; retain genuine zero values. The production model remains unchanged from the previously reviewed contribution.

The follow-up adds top-level landing latitude/longitude null to the regression and separates pad, fallback and landing cases so each has its own failure. The changelog entry moves into changelog.d/1186-launch-unknown-coordinates.md with contributor attribution. The runtime reference and this description distinguish the raw-data correction from the visible effects: unknown pads use the fallback or stay off the map, and missing flight numbers no longer show FLIGHT 0. The downrange display already handled zero and unknown alike.

The optional payload amount conversion is outside this coordinate repair. The current-main merge preserves the compatible #1136 assertions.

## Verification

Tested production normalization source on the combined tree: five controlled numeric-owner cases pass; current main's producer fails three with two positive controls passing. This private replay loads the actual unchanged model and local modules, with an explicit angle-only Cesium fixture for policy imports. It does not exercise Cesium rendering or the full rocketLaunches suite.

The committed test file passes Node syntax checking, and changelog:check passes. Full rocketLaunches tests could not load locally because Cesium/satellite dependencies are absent; the failed imports are preserved in the evidence. No dependency install, full build, full formatting/boundary run, browser gate or new hosted CI pass is claimed. Earlier Windows/full-suite results in the discussion belong to the revision named there. Combined-head hosted CI is separate.

title: feat: add MET Norway weather-station webcams as a CCTV pack
body:
## What this changes

MET Norway's own weather-station webcams join the CCTV mesh as an opt-in, keyless pack: the operating cameras on MET's list (on 2026-10-23 the Hurum weather radar, two COAT cameras in Finnmark, and the Arctic stations Bjørnøya, Hopen and Jan Mayen; cameras MET lists as test are skipped). They show under the existing "Norway" picker category beside the Statens vegvesen pack (#929).

- **Catalog.** One request to MET's public webcam list, `obs-view.met.no/obswebcam/`, which MET marks "for free use outside MET's firewall". It is a small HTML page (~7 KB) with each camera's site id, place, position, status and current still, parsed with fixed patterns. Redirects are refused, the body is capped at 512 KB, and the shared 15-minute catalog cache applies. An unavailable list gives an empty pack.
- **Frames.** Stills only. Each camera registers exactly `obs-view.met.no/obswebcam/last/site1_<site>.jpg`; an image link anywhere else, or another camera's frame, drops the row. A camera whose image cell is empty (MET's mark for one that stopped delivering, e.g. Bergebydalen today) is dropped.
- **Heading.** The place text names the facing as a Norwegian compass word ("mot øst", "mot sørvest", and the list's own spelling "søvest"), which becomes an 8-point heading. Cameras without one use the shared id-hash prior at low confidence. The view prior is shallower, wider and longer than the road packs' (pitch −8°, FOV 60°, 400 m), since these cameras look out over terrain and sky.
- **Ground heights.** Positions are 2D, so mainland cameras get their terrain height from Kartverket's keyless point-height API (CC BY 4.0) through the lookup the Statens vegvesen pack uses (#945, now `applyKartverketGroundHeights`): one cache, one backoff and one lookup at a time for both packs, waiting at most 8 s on a cold cache. Kartverket does not cover Svalbard or Jan Mayen; those cameras stand within ~25 m of sea level and keep 0 m.
- **Switches.** The pack is opt-in (`CCTV_MET_ENABLED=1`) until MET confirms the webcam images may be reused; cameras MET lists as `Status:test` are skipped; `CCTV_MET_HEIGHTS=0` skips the height lookup, `CCTV_MET_MAX_SOURCES` caps it (default 100, 1–500), `CCTV_MET_URL` overrides the list.
- **Attribution.** "Data from MET Norway" under NLOD 2.0 and CC BY 4.0 ([MET licensing](https://www.met.no/en/free-meteorological-data/licensing-and-crediting)), plus "camera ground heights © Kartverket (CC BY 4.0)", in the Data attribution popover, DATA_SOURCES.md and CURRENT-STATE.md.

The loader lives in its own module, `server/providers/cctv/met.js`, like Lithuania, and is registered in the package-boundary list. No new layer, so no share-link token or schema change.

## QA

- `npm test`: 7,641 tests, 0 failures (10 new in `src/data/cctvMet.test.mjs`: parsing, pinned frame path, compass headings, dropped rows, loader dedupe and failure paths, height lookup, cache and backoff, both kill switches, catalog wiring).
- `npm run format:check` and `npm run check:boundaries` pass.
- Live against MET: 12 of 13 listed cameras load (Bergebydalen has no current image); all 12 frames answer 200 `image/jpeg`.
- (2026-10-17, before cameras in test were skipped) Live against Kartverket: Haukeliseter 986 m, Reinhaugen 468 m, Trolltinden 434 m, Hurum 347 m, Torvhaugdalen 266 m, Bø 248 m, Snåsa 195 m, Drag 10 m, Buholmsråsa 0 m (sea floor −9.8 m); the full load took ~1.4 s.
- (2026-10-17, before cameras in test were skipped) In the app: `/api/cctv/sources` lists all 12 `no-met-*` cameras; `/api/cctv/frame/no-met-haukeliseter` (and Bjørnøya, Jan Mayen) returns the JPEG through the proxy. Picking "Norway · Haukeliseter (mot sør)" flies to the camera with SNAPSHOT · OK, HDG 180°, FOV 60°, MET Norway as source, and the frame projected into the scene. The MET credit shows in the Data attribution popover.

title: feat(ocean): ocean current field through the wind renderer
body:
Second PR of the split agreed in #100: the surface-current field, served in the wind layer's manifest and `.bin` shape and drawn through the wind renderer. **Stacked on #779** (the GSHHG mask); its five commits are shared history and drop out once #779 merges. Buoys and drift follow in a third PR.

## What it does

- **Server** (`server/providers/oceanCurrents.js`, `server/ocean/*`): `/api/ocean/currents/{manifest,status}?latMin&latMax&lonMin&lonMax` and `/grid/<id>.bin`. The manifest has the wind keys (`schemaVersion`, `cycle`, `grid{nx,ny,lo1,la1,dx,dy}`, `stale`, `unavailable`, `reason`, `gridUrl`) plus `field`, `tier`, `bbox`, `noData: -9999` (finite sentinel in both components), `speed{medianMs,p95Ms,maxMs,validCells,totalCells}` and the old `provenance` block. The body is headerless little-endian Float32 `u` then `v`, row 0 north, exactly like wind.
- **Tiers by view span.** Above 5000 km: one cached 1-degree global lattice (360x181) resampled from HYCOM ESPC-D (CoastWatch blended altimetry when HYCOM is down; the legend says so). 800 to 5000 km: the HYCOM sub-grid on its own axes. Under 800 km: the IOOS HF-radar Barnes analysis composited over the global field. Land is blanked with the bundled GSHHG mask (#779). Responses cache ten minutes on a half-degree box; builds run to completion so a slow cold globe read fills the cache for the next request.
- **Capped streaming reads** for the three fetchers (HYCOM, CoastWatch, HF radar) through `readResponseTextCapped`: an oversized chunked body is refused mid-read and the stream cancelled (tests stream 16 MiB through each fetcher).
- **Renderer** (`src/layers/wind/`): a field spec (`fieldSpec.js`) parameterizes calm cutoff, target median speed, speed ramp and gamma, display height and height fade. The sampler rejects a `noData` corner or a point outside a non-periodic grid; the bake seeds inside the field's `bbox` with a grid-relative step cap; the GPU path gets a per-path `fieldSpeed` instance attribute and a five-stop ramp in the material; the canvas fallback spawns inside the box and scales its advection. The per-field speed scale is the median-based time compression: $s = m_\text{target} / \max(m_\text{field}, 10^{-3})$ with $m_\text{target} = 5.836$ m/s, the median 10 m speed of the GFS 2026-10-16 12Z f010 snapshot through this repo's decoder (65160 cells), so wind runs at $s = 1$.
- **Wind is unchanged**: `WIND_FIELD_SPEC` reproduces the shipped constants (calm 0.15, ramp max 30, five white stops, 12 km lift, 15/60 km fade, 0.75 deg step cap, 1800 s steps) and every pre-existing wind test passes untouched.
- **Streamline density** is set by line coverage, not by a fixed seed count: a box is seeded so that the summed path length divided by the box width lands at `boxLineCoverage` (77 for currents), predicted from the (E1) step and the manifest's valid-cell ratio and corrected once from the realized coverage after the bake, so a coastal box whose paths stop at the shore is reseeded instead of drawn sparse. The globe seeds at `globeSeedScale` (2x) the wind budget. Wind keeps its fixed 7200.
- **Layer** (`src/layers/oceanCurrents/`): `ocean-currents`, refetches on `moveEnd` (450 ms debounce, quarter-degree change gate; a moveEnd whose view span crosses the 5000 km or 800 km tier line refetches at once, with the span formula and both thresholds mirrored from the server and pinned by test), speed overlay, pause, legend from the manifest's p95. `getDiagnostics().timing` reports the last update's `fetchMs` (manifest plus `.bin`), `buildMs` (main-thread bake plus geometry instances), `readyMs` (first frame with every Cesium cell ready) and `totalMs`. Share token `5` from the ledger (no `o`/`n`, #658). Voice aliases, weather panel card, es/ru translations, credits and DATA_SOURCES rows.

## Visible differences from the #100 canvas

- Streamline colour is per path (seed speed), not per vertex.
- The client-side 16 px land gate is gone: land is no-data in the grid.
- The screen-space limb gate is replaced by the wind renderer's occluder test.
- Globe scale draws the 1-degree lattice (about two cells across the Gulf Stream); the regional tier takes over below 5000 km.

## Recording

`scripts/qa-ocean-currents.mjs` drives the app headless through globe, Gulf Stream, Great Australian Bight and Monterey Bay, asserts the manifest tier and valid cells at each stop and that the layer rendered GPU streamlines, prints the update timing per stop (`--budget-build-ms` / `--budget-total-ms` turn it into a check), and records the run. The recording (41 s, 1280 px, warm server cache) and the four screenshots are on the fork's `assets/ocean-currents-pr` branch:

- [ocean-currents.mp4](https://github.com/MarioDanielPanuco/gods-eye-view/raw/assets/ocean-currents-pr/ocean-currents.mp4)
- ![Gulf Stream](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MarioDanielPanuco/gods-eye-view/assets/ocean-currents-pr/gulf-stream.png)
- ![Monterey Bay](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MarioDanielPanuco/gods-eye-view/assets/ocean-currents-pr/monterey-bay.png)
- [globe.png](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MarioDanielPanuco/gods-eye-view/assets/ocean-currents-pr/globe.png), [great-australian-bight.png](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MarioDanielPanuco/gods-eye-view/assets/ocean-currents-pr/great-australian-bight.png)

## Deferred

- A DENSITY control in the layer card (25 to 200% of the coverage constant, rebake without refetch) if people want to tune streamline density themselves. Easy to add on request.
- Fixed-tile regional cache with neighbour prefetch: see the comment below. Kept out so the diff stays the current field.

## Interface text

The layer's strings are marked for translation and the `es`/`ru` catalogs carry entries for them (written by me; corrections welcome).

## Checks

- `npm test`: 8027 tests, 8024 pass, 0 fail, 3 skipped (on upstream `main` 3e5a18f6)
- `npm run check:boundaries`, `npm run format:check`, `npm run changelog:check` (fragment `changelog.d/1188-ocean-currents.md`), `node scripts/check-layer-state-tokens.mjs --base-ref upstream/main` (31 published, 1 new): pass
- `node scripts/qa-ocean-currents.mjs`: all PASS at four stops: globe (7865 GPU paths from 14400 seeds, coverage 89.9; this run's globe is the CoastWatch fallback because the cold HYCOM read timed out, which the legend states), Gulf Stream (1074 paths, coverage 78.6, HYCOM own axes), Great Australian Bight (784, coverage 76.0, a strided regional grid wider than the requested box), Monterey Bay (253, coverage 79.1, HF radar composite, holdout RMSE 0.044 m/s)
- Update timing from the same run, headless chromium on swiftshader (GPU phases run slower than on a real GPU; the fetch numbers are the server's), as `fetch / build / ready / total` in ms. Warm server cache: globe 10 / 215 / 4260 / 4271, Gulf Stream 9 / 53 / 1729 / 1737, Bight 10 / 31 / 931 / 941, Monterey 6 / 10 / 898 / 903. Cold cache, same stops: fetch 58549 (HYCOM global timed out, CoastWatch fallback), 6607, 5985, 11872. The upstream read is the whole cost of a cold box; the bake stays under a quarter of a second everywhere.

title: feat(bikeshare): add nine Spanish city bike systems
body:
## Summary

Adds the station-based public bike systems of seven more Spanish cities, plus Valencia and Seville, to the Bike Share layer and `get_bike_share`. That is 1,841 stations from nine keyless GBFS 2.3 feeds, counted live on 2026-10-17:

| System | City | Platform | Stations |
|---|---|---|---|
| BiciMAD | Madrid | PBSC | 678 |
| Valenbisi | Valencia | JCDecaux | 277 |
| Bizi Zaragoza | Zaragoza | PBSC | 276 |
| Sevici | Seville | JCDecaux | 243 |
| BIKI | Valladolid | PBSC | 104 |
| BiciCoruña | A Coruña | PBSC | 84 |
| Dbizi | Donostia-San Sebastián | PBSC | 70 |
| Bilbao Bizi | Bilbao | PBSC | 67 |
| BicinRivas | Rivas-Vaciamadrid | PBSC | 42 |

It is in four commits, and each can be read on its own.

## Changes

### 1. `fix(gbfs)`: read underscores in station names as word breaks

JCDecaux's Spanish contracts put a `_` in front of every station name, and Valenbisi also uses `_` between words, as in `_PLAZA_MUSICO_LOPEZ_CHAVARRI`. The card and HUD would show the raw identifier. Lillestrøm, also on JCDecaux, does not do this.

The shared parser in `src/sources/gbfsStations.js` now reads a run of underscores, together with the spaces around it, as one word break, and trims the ends. Other spacing stays as the operator published it.

- It applies to `name`, to the `short_name` fallback and to GBFS v3 localized names, so both the layer and `get_bike_share` get it.
- **No registered system changes.** I ran the old and new parsers over all 52 live `station_information` feeds on 2026-10-17: all 13,397 station names came out identical. None of them contains an underscore.
- New cases in `gbfsStations.test.mjs`.

### 2. `fix(gbfs)`: count docks, not PBSC's geofenced area, as station capacity

PBSC adds the bikes a station accepts in the geofenced area around its docks to `capacity`. It reports that part as `geofenced_capacity`, which is not a GBFS field.

- Bilbao Bizi publishes 39 docks as `capacity: 839` with `geofenced_capacity: 800`. Every station therefore read as nearly empty: red, drawn at maximum size, and carded `39 avail · 0 docks · 839 cap`.
- BiciMAD does the same at 671 of its 678 stations, which puts its capacity at about twice its docks. Dbizi does it at 11 of 70.
- The shared parser now reads `capacity − geofenced_capacity` when the extension is present and no larger than the total. The layer, its colour ratio and `get_bike_share` all see the docks.
- **No registered system changes.** None of the 52 publishes a geofenced capacity above 0, and all 13,397 capacities come out identical.

### 3. `feat(bikeshare)`: the nine systems

- **Registry:** nine entries in `src/layers/bikeshare/registry.js`, after AMBici.
  - The PBSC entries are written out in full like Bicing (`/customer/gbfs/v2/en/station_{information,status}.json`).
  - The JCDecaux entries follow Lillestrøm (`api.cyclocity.fr/contracts/<contract>/gbfs/…`).
- **Allowlist:** no change. `*.publicbikesystem.net` and `api.cyclocity.fr` under `/contracts/` already cover every feed.
- **Load radius:** every system uses 40 km. The farthest station is 11.7 km from its centre (BiciMAD).
  - Since #1063, the radius also trims station information. That keeps out what two feeds list away from their city: Sevici's workshop at (0,0) and a lab station in Madrid (399 km), and BiciCoruña's three planned stations with no position yet (0,0).
- **New `spainCitiesSystems.test.mjs`**, modelled on the Barcelona and Bogotá/Santiago tests. It checks that:
  - each feed is registered and passes the proxy host and path checks;
  - the outermost live stations activate their system and sit inside its radius;
  - central Madrid activates both BiciMAD and BicinRivas;
  - the far-away stations are not loaded through the real ingestion path;
  - JCDecaux names arrive without underscores;
  - PBSC capacities reach the layer as docks.

### 4. `docs`: credits and data sources

- **BiciMAD:** Madrid's open-data catalogue (`datos.madrid.es`, dataset `900021-0-bicimad-gbfs`, owner EMT Madrid) publishes this same feed under [EMT's open-data terms](https://mobilitylabs.emtmadrid.es/sip/terms-of-use). They allow commercial and non-commercial reuse, and section 5.2 requires the attribution "Powered by EMT de Madrid". The `gbfs` credit carries it, linked to emtmadrid.es, and the feed has its own `DATA_SOURCES.md` row.
- **The other six PBSC feeds:** they publish no `license_url`, and neither the operators nor the cities publish a licence for them. MobilityData's catalogue lists CC BY 4.0 for them without naming a source. They share one `DATA_SOURCES.md` row with attribution to each operator, like the Bike Itaú row.
- **Valenbisi and Sevici:** each feed's `license_url` is the Licence Ouverte, the same as Lillestrøm. The JCDecaux row and the `jcdecaux-gbfs` credit now name them.
- **`docs/CURRENT-STATE.md`:** the Bikeshare row, and the underscore and geofenced-capacity rules under "GBFS upstream bounds".

Out of scope: nextbike systems in Spain (a follow-up) and dockless operators, which have no fixed stations.

## Notes

- **Overnight closure:** Bilbao Bizi rents from 05:00 to 00:00, with returns until 00:30 ([official FAQ](https://www.bilbao.eus/apps/bilbaobizi/preguntas_frecuentes_es.htm)). At night its feed reports `is_renting: false` at every station, so the layer greys them out and the card reads "Not renting". That matches the service.
- **Placeholder stations:** a few stations are listed but not installed, with capacity 0 or no name (Valenbisi 2, Sevici 4, BiciCoruña 2). They stay grey, the same as Bicing's.
- **JCDecaux `last_reported`:** it is not feed freshness. The median station age is 16–22 h while `last_updated` is under a minute old, and Lillestrøm behaves the same way. Only `get_bike_share` exposes it, and this PR leaves it unchanged.
- **Overflow bikes:** PBSC already counts its overflow bikes (`num_bikes_overflow`) inside `num_bikes_available`. Electric and mechanical bikes are not told apart, as with Bicing.

## Testing

- `npm run format:check`, `npm run check:boundaries`, `npm run build`: pass.
- `npm test` (Node 24): 7,723 passed, 0 failed, 1 skipped.
- `npm run test:track`: 108 passed, 1 failed.
  - The failure is `stale-readout: tracked label carries STALE cue during grace`, in flight tracking. It fails the same way on `main` without this branch.
- Live check through the dev server's `/api/gbfs` (rebased on `main` 1df2a272): all 18 feeds return 200. One run hit a single transient upstream 502, which the next poll recovered.
  - `station_information` comes back with `public, max-age=300` and `station_status` with `no-store`.
  - Every station has a status row: 1,841 of 1,841.
- Tried by hand in the app in all nine cities: names, colours, capacities, the overnight closure in Bilbao and the placeholder stations behave as described above.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: fix(satellites): fetch CelesTrak OMM so six-digit catalog numbers load
body:
Fixes #1182

### What

CelesTrak stopped issuing five-digit catalog numbers on 2026-07-11 and serves objects numbered 100000+ only in OMM formats. The satellite layer requested `FORMAT=tle`, so every newly catalogued object was silently missing, including crewed and cargo vehicles currently at the ISS.

This switches the CelesTrak fetch to OMM JSON, the shape agreed in the triage comment on #1182:

- **Request:** new `celestrakOmmUrl()` next to `celestrakTleUrl()` in `src/data/spaceProviderRequests.js`; the public `./sources/space` export keeps the TLE helper.
- **Proxy:** `server/providers/space/celestrak.js` fetches OMM JSON and treats a body without OMM records as a failure (keeps the cache, serves stale), same as before for TLE.
- **Parser:** new `src/sources/orbitalElements.js` with one parser for both formats. OMM records become `{ name, omm }`, TLE text still parses to `{ name, line1, line2 }`, so `.gev-cache` files written before the switch keep working as stale fallbacks. `satrecFromElements`, `elementsCatalogNumber` and `elementsLaunchYear` hide the format from the callers.
- **Callers:** satellites ingestion, dense catalog, Space Missions lookup (`findSatelliteOrbitTrackInTle`) and the `next_satellite_pass` / overhead tools use the helpers instead of `twoline2satrec` directly.

title: Launch Library 2 (LL2) API Integration: Cache Optimization, User-Agent Header, and API Key Clarification
body:
### What happened

## Launch Library 2 (LL2) API Integration: Cache Optimization, User-Agent Header, and API Key Clarification

Hi team,

I'm one of the developers behind the **Launch Library 2 (LL2) API** (The Space Devs). 

We recently noticed traffic patterns coming from Godseye instances and wanted to reach out regarding a few adjustments. These will help your requests hit our Redis cache, keep our services healthy, and resolve recurring confusion among your users regarding API keys.

---

### 1. Request Optimization: Rounded Timestamps or `/launches/previous/`

Currently, queries fetching past launches (such as the last 30 days) appear to use dynamic timestamps down to the second or millisecond.

* **Issue:** Millisecond/second-level timestamps change on every single execution, completely bypassing our Redis caching layer and forcing our origin database to recompute identical queries repeatedly.
* **Suggested Fixes:**
  * **Option A (Preferred):** Use the dedicated past launch endpoint on v2.3.0: `/launches/previous/`. This endpoint is purpose-built and aggressively cached in Redis on our side.
  * **Option B:** If filtering dynamically by date/time parameters, please **round timestamps to at least the nearest minute** (or hour/day where feasible). That way, requests across your user base can consistently hit cached Redis keys instead of hitting the database directly.

---

### 2. Identifiable `User-Agent` Header

We ask large client integrations to supply an identifiable `User-Agent` header with their HTTP requests:

* **Format:** `<AppName>/<Version> (<Contact/Repo URL>)`  
  *(e.g., `Godseye/1.2.0 (https://github.com/...)`)*

---

### 3. In-App & Documentation Clarification on API Keys

We have had multiple Godseye users join our Discord asking where they can obtain a "free API key":

* **No key is needed:** The public LL2 API works out of the box without any authentication header or token.
* **Keys are paid:** API keys are exclusively tied to paid tiers (via Patreon) for users requiring higher rate limits; there is no free key tier.
* **Request:** Could you update your UI, setup prompts, or docs (e.g., `.env.example`, settings view) to clarify that the API key field should simply be left blank for standard use? Explicitly noting that keys are optional, paid upgrades for higher limits will keep users from getting blocked or visiting our Discord asking for free tokens.



The Space Devs

title: feat(cctv): add opt-in CET-SP São Paulo camera pack
body:
## What

Adds the first Brazilian CCTV source: 14 CET-SP (Companhia de Engenharia de Tráfego) intersection cameras in central São Paulo — Av. Paulista, Faria Lima, Consolação, Ibirapuera and nearby corners.

**Opt-in, like Lithuania.** CET publishes the stills on its public [Câmeras CET](https://www.cetsp.com.br/consultas/cameras-cet.aspx) site for anyone to view, but states no reuse terms. The pack loads only with `CCTV_CETSP_ENABLED=1`. With the flag unset, empty or any other value, no CET camera is registered and the proxy never contacts `cameras.cetsp.com.br`.

## How the source works

- CET's camera page lists its cameras in an inline `gCams` array (folder number, street names, active flag) but publishes **no coordinates or poses**. The curated `config/cctv_sources.cetsp.json` places each camera at the OpenStreetMap node where its two named streets meet. Positions are found with Overpass queries; each is the mean of the shared nodes, within ~40 m. Because of that, the layer shows the shared OSM credit, as it already does for Warendorf. Headings use the existing low-confidence id-hash prior, for calibration with the gizmo.
- Each camera folder holds a ring of 25–50 stills (`/Cams/<folder>/<n>.jpg`). CET overwrites them one at a time, about every 14 s, so no single file is always the newest. The pack registers frame 1, the one CET's own page uses for its thumbnails; it is at most one ring cycle (~12 min) old.
- Two cameras are left out: 16, whose frames have been frozen since November 2024, and 234, which CET marks inactive.
- Only `https://cameras.cetsp.com.br/Cams/<folder>/1.jpg` can be registered. The URL is rebuilt from the folder number, and the id must equal `cetsp-<folder>`. Rows with any other host, path, query, credentials or coordinates outside the municipality are dropped.
- The loader only reads the local file; it makes no catalog request.
- Frames are fetched at request time and never stored. CET takes images offline after serious accidents to protect the people involved, and those disappear here too.

## Changes

- `server/providers/cctv/cetsp.js` (new), with its loader registered as an opt-in pack in `catalog.js` and constants in `constants.js`
- `config/cctv_sources.cetsp.json` (new): the 14 curated cameras
- `src/data/dataCredits.js`: CET-SP credit
- `src/layers/cctv/lifecycle.js`: the OSM credit check now covers `sao-paulo` as well as `warendorf`
- Docs: `DATA_SOURCES.md` (table row + source notes), `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md`, `README.md`, `.env.example`
- `scripts/format-scope.json` and `scripts/package-boundaries.json` list the new module and test

## Verification

- `src/data/cctvCetsp.test.mjs` (new, 10 tests): the curated catalog shape; URL, host, path and coordinate rejection; missing or malformed files; dedupe; the catalog includes the pack only with `CCTV_CETSP_ENABLED=1`, and leaves it out when the flag is unset, empty, `0` or `true`. `sharedOsmDisplays.test.mjs` gains the São Paulo OSM-credit case.
- `npm test`: 7706 pass, 0 fail (1 skipped, the Node-24-calibrated allocation benchmarks, under Node 26)
- `npm run build`: OK. `npm run format:check` and `npm run check:boundaries`: clean.
- `npm run test:track`: 109 passed, 0 failed
- `node scripts/qa-cctv-v2.mjs --url http://localhost:4173` with `CCTV_CETSP_ENABLED=1`: 52 passed, 0 failed, 1 inconclusive. That check is the headless GL geometry-queue drain for N=4000, which the gate itself says needs headful evidence.
- Live check with `CCTV_CETSP_ENABLED=1`: `/api/cctv/sources` serves the 14 `sao-paulo` cameras, and `/api/cctv/frame/cetsp-164` returns a current 480×270 JPEG of Av. Paulista.

I haven't calibrated the headings or checked each camera's placement in the 3D view.

title: feat: allow optional local package boundary additions
body:
Downstream forks and local extensions currently have to edit the shared package-boundary file when they add an owned module or export. This adds an optional `scripts/package-boundaries.local.json`, so those additions can live in a second file.

Arrays append to an existing group's exports, modules and external dependencies; new groups use the same format as the main file. Existing entries and runtimes cannot be replaced. The combined configuration goes through the existing ownership checks, including exactly-once export classification. An absent local file leaves the check unchanged; malformed data and other read errors fail clearly.

The fixed filename keeps the option small and consistent across platforms. If maintainers prefer explicit opt-in, an environment variable naming the overlay would be an alternative.

title: docs: list every npm alias for the qa gates
body:
## Summary

`CONTRIBUTING.md` told contributors that "Only a couple (`qa:map-source-tray`, `qa:transit`) have an `npm run` alias". There are five, and the two that were missing are ones the project's own CI runs through npm.

## Problem

The "Feature regression gates" section lists the `npm run` aliases so a contributor knows when `npm run <gate>` is available versus running `node scripts/<gate>.mjs` directly. The current sentence names two aliases and describes them as "only a couple", so it reads as the complete list. It isn't — `package.json` defines:

```
qa:map-source-tray         => node scripts/qa-map-source-tray.mjs
qa:panel-resize            => node scripts/qa-panel-resize.mjs
qa:street-level            => node scripts/qa-street-level.mjs
qa:street-level:fixtures   => node scripts/qa-street-level.mjs --fixtures
qa:transit                 => node scripts/qa-transit.mjs
```

The two undocumented ones are not incidental. `.github/workflows/ci.yml` invokes both:

- line 105 — `npm run qa:street-level:fixtures -- --strict --url http://localhost:4173`
- line 109 — `npm run qa:panel-resize -- --url http://localhost:4173`

So the guide sends a contributor to `node scripts/qa-panel-resize.mjs` for a gate CI itself runs as `npm run qa:panel-resize`, and tells them the npm form does not exist.

## Change

One sentence in `CONTRIBUTING.md`, listing all five aliases. No code, config or dependency change.

## Validation

Run locally on a clean checkout of `main` (1df2a27):

- `npm run format:check` — passed, "Checked 1423 source files"
- `npm run check:boundaries` — passed
- `npm test` — passed
- `npm run build` — passed, built in 7.25s

Not run: `npm run test:track` and the `qa-*` browser gates. Both need a live dev server and a browser, and this change edits contributor prose only — no runtime behaviour is touched, so there is no gate covering it.

I did not add a `changelog.d/` fragment: that is for user-visible changes, and this only corrects the contributor guide. Happy to add one if you would rather have it.

## Note

This is purely a correction to the documentation of what already exists in `package.json` and `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — no behaviour changes.

title: fix(space): align Launch Library requests with provider guidance
