title: RFC(humanitarian): disaster evidence workspace and accountable relief handoffs
body:
## Summary / scope decision

**Proposal:** make God's Eye View useful as a **provenance-aware, local-first disaster evidence and scenario workspace**, initially for *disaster access*. People should be able to trace what evidence supports or contradicts a route/place assessment, see unknowns and disagreements, compare explicitly hypothetical alternatives, and hand an attributable brief to the real response owner.

**This is a request for maintainer direction, not a monolithic implementation PR or a claim of operational readiness.** If the vertical does not fit GEV, keep the program downstream and contribute only generally useful, small primitives.

The comprehensive downstream [humanitarian roadmap](https://github.com/kvnloo/gods-eye-view/issues/137), [World + Relief Packet RFC](https://github.com/kvnloo/gods-eye-view/issues/11), and [adoption/evaluation plan](https://github.com/kvnloo/gods-eye-view/issues/187) provide deeper implementation and research context. This issue states the proposed upstream product boundary and stop/go gates in one place.

## Why GEV / what problem it would solve

GEV can already juxtapose public hazards, imagery, cameras, maps, and Directions. In a disaster, those signals are **not interchangeable**:

- a routing engine returning geometry is not proof that a bridge is open;
- a warning polygon is not necessarily a burned perimeter or an impassable area;
- historical, stale, simulated, inferred, and current observed data must remain distinguishable;
- a screenshot or an AI summary cannot silently become an authoritative operational claim.

The first useful human workflow is therefore not “automated disaster dispatch.” It is: **“What do we know about this area/route, how do we know it, what changed, what remains unknown, and where should a responsible operator verify next?”**

## End-to-end first use case: historical disaster-access replay

Use the existing Bhote Koshi/Rasuwa reconstruction as a **historical or synthetic exercise**:

1. Select a source-owned disaster/hazard record and inspect linked public imagery, maps, cameras and reports.
2. Collect/compare appropriately licensed, timestamped evidence; display contradictions and gaps.
3. View a candidate OSRM route **without calling it safe or confirmed open**.
4. Assess route segments *only against explicitly associated access observations* and emit a version-bound support receipt: `supported | degraded | unsupported | unknown`.
5. Inject a **clearly simulated** closure of one bridge. Show that the old receipt is no longer current and recompute without mutating the observed record.
6. Export a read-only, source-linked situation brief showing evidence, uncertainties, alternatives, and current limitations for a human decision owner.
7. Compare the workflow against a conventional map + documents exercise with target practitioners.

The [downstream replay](https://github.com/kvnloo/gods-eye-view/issues/137) has demonstrated 16 source-owned context observations and **zero inferred access segments**. The separately supplied synthetic access change is a deterministic proof of the boundary, **not** proof of real route passability or field effectiveness.

## Reuse rather than reinvent (upstream anchors)

- [#797 — selected hazard → existing imagery / cameras](https://github.com/bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view/issues/797): the minimal evidence handoff.
- [#963 — candidate routes + explicit access evidence](https://github.com/bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view/issues/963): narrow disaster route contract.
- [#880 — model-free World Packet](https://github.com/bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view/pull/880): reusable view/state boundary; currently under review, **not merged**.
- [#882 — model-free disaster-access support kernel](https://github.com/bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view/pull/882): data-only support assessment; currently a **draft/unmerged** PR, not a live workflow.
- [#828–#831](https://github.com/bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view/issues/830): relevant optional camera/traffic observation contracts, **not** a substitute for certified road-status evidence.

This RFC adds **no new feed, API key, request loop, or merge request**. Existing work remains in its own review thread. Maintainers can reject or narrow this direction without affecting those independently useful primitives.

## Proposed technical boundary

### World Packet / claim integrity

A small, model-independent, source-owned envelope around coherent observations or derived outputs:

```text
value / schemaVersion
epistemic: observed | declared | derived | simulated | hypothetical
source / license / sourceRevision / observedAt
freshness: current | stale | unavailable | unknown | not-assessed
authority: observation-only | advisory | action-capable
semanticFingerprint / inputEvidenceRefs
```

Invariants:

- `unknown` is not `zero`; `stale-open` is not open; missing records do not become negative evidence.
- Confidence never grants authority. A CCTV/model inference cannot certify a route.
- Derivations cite their input revisions; summaries and compressed packets cannot upgrade their epistemic status.
- Observed Earth and simulated/possible Earth have separate state, visual treatment and serialization.
- Changing a relevant source revision invalidates dependent receipts; a fingerprint does **not** grant permission to take action.
- The fast packet adds no network requests or idle rendering work and preserves existing voice/tool semantics.

### Optional Relief Packet (later, not P0)

Compose the World Packet with **explicitly supplied** crisis need, access, facilities, depot stocks/capacity, and response ownership:

```text
crisis -> source/time/severity/geometry
need -> aggregate indicators/uncertainty
access -> route candidate + independently observed constraints
response -> known facilities + expressly supplied stock/capacity
context -> curated situation reports, source revisions
gaps -> unmet need, unknown/unreachable, conflicts
proposal -> reproducible *candidate* allocations/routes + input receipts
```

For a **historical/synthetic** food or medical-goods delivery benchmark only, compare nearest-first against deterministic capacity-aware routing and one injected outage. Measure travel time, need served/unmet, recomputation, provenance and unknown-state preservation. **No model selects recipients, determines priority policy or authorizes dispatch.** Fairness/priority inputs must be operator-declared; any resulting plans require a responsible human.

## Interoperability, rights and protection

Prefer **linking to existing owners** over cloning their workflows:

- GDACS for public hazard events; HOT/OpenStreetMap for mapped geography; HDX HAPI for aggregate indicators; ReliefWeb for source-linked context; appropriately licensed imagery/cameras; routing engines remain swappable.
- Kobo/ODK, Crisis Cleanup, IFRC/OCHA, local emergency management, and similar tools remain owners of sensitive operations, field forms, authoritative cases and decisions.
- Per-source license, data minimization, freshness, caching/retention, and re-use authority must be checked before any new integration. Publicly accessible does not automatically mean redistributable.
- No face recognition, plate OCR, person/vehicle re-identification, migrant/refugee tracking, or exposure of sensitive shelters/sites by default. Do not track beneficiaries.
- Community-generated/local observations retain explicit local stewardship; remote confidence or reputation must not silently override their authority. Preserve disagreements.
- Read-only deep links / brief exports first. No writes into other response systems without explicit, scoped authority.

## Phased roadmap (separate, independently reviewable work)

| Phase | Smallest evidence of value | Gate |
|---|---|---|
| **0. Scope + rights** | Verify source licensing, data responsibility, claim semantics and real practitioner workflow | Stop if rights, protection or problem ownership fail |
| **1. Core disaster access** | Finish review of existing generic packets/kernel; reproducible Nepal historical replay; source-to-route receipt | No inferred access, stale→unknown and simulated/observed separation; exact-head regression |
| **2. Field proof** | Cheap 2D/Field Lite and offline/intermittent evidence review; source-linked brief | Offline correctness, accessibility, low-resource tests; no unsupported assertions |
| **3. Practitioner falsification** | Two-role/user baseline against conventional map + documents; record mistakes, elapsed verification, comprehension and preference | Pre-register tasks, report sample size/uncertainty; non-inferior correctness and demonstrable usefulness |
| **4. Conditional expansion** | Collaboration/branching; limited humanitarian interoperability; historical deterministic relief-planning benchmark | Explicit permissions/local stewardship, no operational authority leakage, independent validation |
| **5. Long-term only** | Participatory resilience and optional cooperative missions tied to measurable outcomes | Block until prior phases deliver verified benefit and robust safeguards |

Existing granular planning lives in [#137](https://github.com/kvnloo/gods-eye-view/issues/137) (rights, evidence workspace, Field Lite, local stewardship, replay, study, benchmarks) and [#187](https://github.com/kvnloo/gods-eye-view/issues/187) (real-world adoption and source-linked handoffs). **These do not authorize upstream implementations.**

### Acceptance / kill criteria

- Pure, deterministic results replay from a bounded, versioned evidence receipt.
- Injecting stale/missing/contradictory evidence cannot silently produce a supported operational claim.
- Same proposed route + revised explicit bridge evidence invalidates the prior receipt and recomputes deterministically.
- Test on synthetic/historical data first; no “live emergency,” “safe,” “official,” partner-adoption or measured impact claims without the corresponding independently checked evidence.
- If two product iterations do not improve or credibly match the correctness/usability of the existing workflow—or practitioners say this task belongs entirely in their current system—**stop the humanitarian vertical**, keep the genuinely reusable primitives.
- No growing a multi-PR queue off this issue without maintainer acceptance; prioritize feedback on already-open PRs first.

## Non-goals

GEV should **not** become authoritative road status, emergency dispatch, victim/beneficiary selection, case management, field data-collection replacement, government approval, operational safety certification, or a generalized crisis dashboard. And not yet a humanitarian “world game” or automatic agent-driven allocation platform.

## Maintainer decision requested

**Is “spatial evidence + clearly hypothetical scenario reasoning + read-only, attributable handoff” a useful scope for GEV, starting with historical disaster-access review?** If yes, the *next* proposal should be **one small, independently testable slice** building on whatever actually merges from #880/#882; if no, keep this entire vertical in the fork and preserve only generic improvements. No urgency or request to review this ahead of outstanding PRs.

title: fix(launches): report cached fallback missions as stale
body:

Preserve that provenance through ingestion and layer stats so retained mission records read STALE until a genuinely fresh snapshot arrives.

The change keeps `getLaunches()`-only injected sources compatible, preserves cancellation of late responses after disable, and clears provenance on teardown/reinitialization. It includes nine actual source/ingestion/lifecycle regressions and updates CURRENT-STATE.

Validation:
- Final nine regressions against exact base production: four failures reproducing the bug, five healthy controls; all nine pass with the change. Affected native suites: 23 pass.
- Unchanged `npm test`: exit 0, 7,729 pass and one existing skip across ordinary and serialized allocation phases (Node 24.19.0).

title: cctv: color live video cameras apart from stills
body: ## What this is CCTV camera icons now show which cameras have video feed. Cameras with a video feed are violet, stills stay cyan, and the active camera stays amber. With a few thousand cameras on the globe there was no way to tell the DelDOT or Statens vegvesen live feeds from the stills around them without clicking each one. ## How it works One helper, `cameraColorFor(record)` in `rendering.js`, picks the color: active first, then `parts.model.isVideoFeedType(feedType)` (HLS, MP4 or WebM), then the idle cyan. Both places that used to inline the active/idle choice now call it: - `refreshCoverageStyles` when it sets each billboard's color. - `applyCctvFocusDeemphasis` as its `baseColorFor`, so focus de-emphasis fades a violet icon the same way it fades a cyan one, with no extra code. `LIVE_CAMERA_COLOR` (`#b48cff`, alpha 0.88) sits next to the other camera colors in `policy.js`, at the same alpha as the idle cyan so neither reads louder at a distance. ## Docs - `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md`: one sentence in the CCTV v2 foundation paragraph naming the three icon colors. - `changelog.d/1200-cctv-live-icon-color.md`: changelog fragment. ## Validation Environment: native on Arch Linux, Node 24.21.0, system Chromium headless. Branch on `73aec2e`. | Check | Result | | ----- | ------ | | `npm run format:check` | pass, 1,424 files | | `npm run check:boundaries` | pass | | `npm test` | 7,707 tests, 0 failed, 1 skipped | | New tests | src/data/cctv.test.mjs: icon color case. Idle video is violet, idle still is cyan, active video is amber. | | `npm run build` | pass | | `npm run test:track` | 109 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped | | `node scripts/qa-cctv-v2.mjs` | 52 passed, 0 failed, 1 inconclusive (the headless geometry-load drain). The first run, right after a dev server restart, had one failure that did not reproduce on the rerun. | | Manual | Delaware and Norway with CCTV on: DelDOT and Statens vegvesen video cameras show violet among cyan stills, the active camera turns amber, and focus de-emphasis fades violet icons like cyan ones. | ## Not in this PR - A filter or legend for live cameras. The color alone answers "which ones are live" at a glance; a filter is a bigger UI change and its own PR.

title: cctv: draw stills at source aspect
body: ## What this is CCTV stills now keep their shape on the monitor plane. The projection canvas is 16:9 (1920 by 1080) and most DOT cameras publish 4:3 or narrower frames, so every still was stretched sideways to fill it. Stills are now drawn at their source aspect, centered, with the margins filled in. ## How it works The change is in src/layers/cctv/frames.js, with the matte color in policy.js. - `fitToProjection(sourceW, sourceH)` is a contain fit: the smaller of the two scale factors, centered on both axes, so a narrow frame gets pillarboxed and a wide one gets letterboxed. If either dimension is 0 it falls back to the full canvas, which is the old behavior. - In the still path, `clearRect` becomes a fill of `PROJECTION_MATTE_COLOR` (`#01070c`) and `drawImage` uses the fitted rectangle. The placeholder gradient already ends on that color, so both now share the one constant and a pillarboxed still sits on the same dark as the loading state. - The frame signature that skips unchanged frames now includes the fitted size, since the pixel hash is taken at a fixed 64x36 and drops aspect. Identical pixels at the same size still skip the canvas and texture update; a resolution change redraws. ## Docs - `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md`: one sentence in the CCTV v2 foundation paragraph, next to the monitor plane description. - `changelog.d/1201-cctv-stills-aspect.md`: changelog fragment. ## Validation Environment: native on Arch Linux, Node 24.21.0, system Chromium headless. Branch on `73aec2e`. | Check | Result | | ----- | ------ | | `npm run format:check` | pass, 1,424 files | | `npm run check:boundaries` | pass | | `npm test` | 7,710 tests, 0 failed, 1 skipped | | New tests | src/layers/cctv/frames.test.mjs: 4 cases. Pillarbox, letterbox, exact fit, and the zero or missing dimension fallback. | | `npm run build` | pass | | `npm run test:track` | 109 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped | | `node scripts/qa-cctv-v2.mjs` | 52 passed, 0 failed, 1 inconclusive (the headless geometry-load drain). The frame-loop checks pass: plane material and image defined, backend serves the frame, panel and plane share one URL family. | | Manual | 4:3 DOT stills on the monitor plane are pillarboxed instead of stretched. | ## Not in this PR - The live video path in `drawProjectionFrame` still stretches to the canvas. Most live feeds are already 16:9, so it is left alone here. - Ambient card thumbnails (`cards.js`) still stretch. Different surface, separate change.

title: Added KiwiSDR layer for software-defined radio browsing and listening
body:
# Add KiwiSDR layer: map of public receivers with an in-app player

## Summary

This entire app was entirely vibe-coded, though closely tested and requested by a real human. Some further revisions may be necessary for certain edge-cases, but this is beyond "just a concept" and is a fully-realized feature.

Adds a **KiwiSDR** layer to God's Eye View. Every public [KiwiSDR](http://kiwisdr.com) receiver shows up on the globe. Click one to open an in-app player (live audio and a waterfall) with no iframe, so you can listen and browse the radio spectrum without leaving the map.

The layer is off by default and registered `local-only` (no share token). It talks to receivers directly from the browser over `ws://`, so it is meant for local `http://localhost` / LAN use rather than an HTTPS deployment.

## Features

### Map layer
- Station list is fetched at runtime through a server proxy (`/api/kiwisdr`), which uses a fixed upstream, a 10-minute cache (stale up to 6h), an 8 MB cap and no redirects.
- The directory parser is lenient. One malformed row costs one station, not the whole list.
- Dots are coloured by users / max users. Busy and full receivers are clearly dimmed.
- **Colorblind-safe palette:** no red/green pairs. Status text also uses shapes (◌ ● ▲ ✕) and pressed buttons use a fill plus an underline, so nothing relies on colour alone.
- Hover tooltip shows name and load. Far-side points are culled with a horizon occluder.

### In-app player
- Custom KiwiSDR websocket client (audio at 12 kHz plus a 1024-bin waterfall), with Web Audio playback, an S-meter, volume and mute.
- Tuning by typing a frequency, clicking the waterfall, mode chips (AM / AMN / SAM / USB / LSB / CW / NBFM) and quick-tune presets for common bands.
- Visible failure reasons: full receiver, password needed, per-IP limit, maintenance and so on, instead of a silent failure.
- The waterfall canvas uses `willReadFrequently: true`. A GPU-backed canvas stalled the page under software GL.

### Minimize / dock
- A ▾ button docks the player into a slim bar at bottom-left showing the title, frequency, S-meter and mute.
- Audio keeps playing while docked. Waterfall painting pauses.
- Clicking the same receiver on the map expands it again.

### Favorites
- ★ in the player header marks a receiver.
- Favorites get a white ring on the map.
- A "★ Favorites" tray lists them. Clicking one flies to it and opens it. Receivers missing from the current directory are shown disabled.

### Saved frequencies (per receiver)
- "＋ Save this" stores the current frequency and mode for that receiver, as chips with a delete button.
- Favorites and presets are stored in `localStorage` (`gev.kiwisdr.v1`) in `src/layers/kiwisdr/storage.js`. Everything read back is validated, sizes are capped, and a missing, full or corrupt `localStorage` degrades to in-memory instead of throwing.

### Waterfall zoom and precision tuning
- Mouse wheel zooms at the pointer and keeps the frequency under the cursor fixed.
- Drag pans a zoomed view. Hover shows the exact frequency under the pointer.
- Click tuning snaps to the resolution of the current zoom: 1 kHz at full band, down to 10 Hz at max zoom.
- Keyboard: ←/→ tune (Shift ×10), ↑/↓ zoom. There are also ◀ ▶ buttons.
- The zoom label shows the factor and span, for example `×4 · 3.75 MHz`.

## Connection fixes (found with real receivers)

These came from HAR and console captures from Firefox against live receivers.

- **`*.proxy.kiwisdr.com` receivers** are listed on port 80, which only answers a websocket handshake with a `307` to `:8073`. Browsers can't follow redirects on websockets. The client now goes straight to `:8073` for these hosts.
- **Secondary proxy.** Some of them answer with a `307` to `NAME.proxy2.kiwisdr.com`, which also only accepts websockets on `:8073`. The client tries it when the primary refuses.
- **Shared timestamp.** The audio and waterfall sockets were opened with timestamps that could differ by 1 ms. Receivers pair a listener's two sockets by that stamp, so a mismatch looked like two clients. That caused "only one connection per IP" refusals and audio sockets dropped after about 10 s (close code 1005). Both sockets now share one stamp.
- **Diagnostics.** On failure the player shows a small line with the host, port, path tried, close code and elapsed time (also logged with `console.warn`), plus a link to the receiver's own page.

## UI layout

The required map attribution row (`#cesium-credits`, z-index 90) was painting over the lower rows of the player. The player, the docked bar and the favorites tray now share one clearance (`--kiwisdr-dock-clearance`) that sits above the bottom dock and the attribution row.

## Integration

- Module ownership is registered in `scripts/package-boundaries.json` (`application-components` and `application-layer-construction`).
- i18n: new strings go through `t()` / `msg()`, with Spanish and Russian catalogs updated. `npm run i18n` is clean.
- Also touched: the layer panel, layer names (`kiwisdr: msg('KiwiSDR')`), the voice layer manifest, `dataCredits.js` and `DATA_SOURCES.md`.
- The layer catalog test now expects 33 layers.

## Testing

- **Unit tests:** `protocol`, `client`, `audio`, `source` and `storage` for the layer, plus the server provider, the source parser, the catalog and the source composition. The full suite is 7761 tests with only the known failures below.
- **Browser gate:** `scripts/qa-kiwisdr.mjs` runs 30 checks against mock receivers. It covers enabling the layer, hovering and clicking, handshake, live audio and waterfall, tuning, wheel zoom, click and drag, presets, favorites and the map ring, minimize with audio still flowing, reopen persistence, the full-receiver message, and the attribution-overlap regression.
```
  npm run dev   # then:
  PUPPETEER_EXECUTABLE_PATH=/path/to/chrome node scripts/qa-kiwisdr.mjs --url http://localhost:4173
```
- `npm run format:check`, `npm run check:boundaries` and `npm run i18n` pass.
- Checked by hand in Firefox against live receivers, including direct-IP, `ddns` and `*.proxy.kiwisdr.com` hosts.

**Known unrelated failures:** the WSDOT loader test fails on pristine upstream too, and 4 tests cancel under Node 22 (the repo wants Node 24). Neither is touched by this PR.

## Notes for reviewers

- The browser connects to receivers directly. The directory parser rejects non-http(s) origins, credentials, `localhost` / `.local` and non-global IPv4 so a directory entry can't aim the browser at a LAN address.
- `ws://` to arbitrary hosts won't work from an HTTPS page (mixed content), which is why this is local-only.
- Not verified: the layout in browsers other than Firefox and the headless Chromium used by the gate.

## Summary

Adds an **optional, default-disabled Boulder Area camera reference pack** with **36 independently addressable views: 10 City of Boulder HLS streams and 26 Boulder County stills at seven sites**.

- Activate explicitly with `CCTV_SOURCES_FILE=config/cctv_sources.boulder.json`; no default source pack is changed.
- Includes South Boulder Creek and both recovered Coalton views. Poor framing and variable still-image age are disclosed rather than silently excluding functional sources.
- Preserves official master/image URLs, source identity, locality, coordinate provenance, and source credits. No downloaded imagery, footage, credentials, launchers, local paths, or QA artifacts are included.
- Adds City/County acknowledgments to the existing Data attribution registry, explicitly labeled optional/not enabled by default, without implying endorsement or reuse permission. Existing OSM attribution remains.
- Adds bounded HLS rendition fallback needed for variable-size daytime segments: retain working quality; consult only advertised same-origin renditions when a child/segment download fails; preserve existing segment, playlist, memory, timeout, session and lease caps. No temporary child URLs are stored in the catalog.
- Tests cover availability, empty segments, cancellation, private partial-download rejection, and stable published media/discontinuity sequences across rolling eviction.

See [`docs/BOULDER_CAMERAS.md`](docs/BOULDER_CAMERAS.md) for activation, sources, placement limitations, update schedules and rights details.

## Draft status and unresolved items

This is a **draft for review**, not a claim of ready-to-merge acceptance or permission for public redistribution.

1. **Media rights remain unresolved.** Official publication and anonymous access do not establish embedding, proxying, caching or redistribution permission. No blanket media license is claimed; deployment beyond the documented context needs its own rights assessment. The contribution contains URL/metadata references, not bundled media.

The failure requires a real mesh sample absent from the keyless terrain-only scene; five drag checks lack an on-screen gizmo target. Exact named outcomes were compared, and no assertions or security settings were weakened.

Its latest observed status is recorded below. Still-image freshness and South Boulder Creek's downward aim are separate disclosed limitations.

## Validation

Tested upstream base: `93ea088f4556a5a65b3292a2d15142d5a6c562bc`. Runtime: Node 24.21.0; actual browser checks used sandboxed Chrome with NVIDIA D3D11 rendering. Credentials were not included in the contribution or test environment.

title: feat(radio): add configurable priority-country coverage
body:
## Summary

The global popularity catalog can leave some countries poorly represented. Add optional `RADIO_PRIORITY_COUNTRIES` configuration (for example `IN,PL`) to reserve up to 40 eligible stations per country, for up to eight countries, within the existing 750-station cap. No API key or new host is required.

Country seeds precede specialist-tag selection and global popularity fill. Leaving the variable unset preserves that existing global/tag selection. Radio controls and playback are unchanged.

## Reliability and review fixes

- Country query outcomes are advisory and reported in `coverage.priorityCountries`. Failed, malformed or oversized country responses cannot degrade an otherwise healthy global catalog.
- Valid, in-limit country responses with no eligible stations are accepted as empty results and retain the normal 45-minute cache.
- The three-mirror attempt cap and 60-second failed/partial-refresh backoff apply to **all installations**, including when no priority countries are configured. Later fallback mirrors are skipped after three candidates; a cold failure can continue returning 503 during the backoff even if upstream recovers sooner.
- Regression tests cover cold and warm country failures beyond seven days, empty/ineligible/malformed/oversized country responses, cache reuse, and retry recovery both with and without configured countries.
- Updated the Radio Browser source notes, moved the configuration documentation under Radio components, and added the #1206 changelog fragment.

Refs #1020

## Validation after review fixes

- Full test suite: 7,754 passed, 1 skipped, 0 failed.
- Focused radio proxy suite: 30 passed.
- Radio browser gate: 106 passed.
- Tracking browser gate: 109 passed.
- Production build, formatting, package boundaries, changelog check and `git diff --check` passed.

title: fix(street-level): rewrite an untrimmed disk tile once under a slow read
body:
`src/tooling/mapillaryProvider.test.mjs:910` ("concurrent disk hits on an untrimmed tile rewrite it once, keeping its age") fails intermittently on CI with `one rewrite for three hits: 2 !== 1`. Node 26.x hit it on #1210 ([job](https://github.com/bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view/actions/runs/39108523729/job/117619526628)) on a change that touches no Street Level code. The test was right. `fetchTile()` has a real race.

### The race

`server/providers/mapillary/tiles.js` `fetchTile()`: concurrent disk hits each `await readDisk()`.
1. The first to resume trims, starts the rewrite (`writeDisk`, which marks it pending) and puts the tile in memory.
2. The others skip their rewrite because `diskWritePending()` is true.
3. On a slow runner the first rewrite can finish, and stop being pending, before a later hit's read resolves. That hit read the untrimmed file, so it rewrites the tile a second time.

In production that costs only one redundant write, but it makes the suite red for unrelated PRs.

### The change

A later hit also skips the rewrite when the tile is already in memory. The first hit put it there in the same synchronous step that started the rewrite. That is one condition plus a comment. Nothing else changes: the response, `source: 'disk'`, the kept fetch time and the memory LRU behave as before.

### Verified

- **New test, deterministic.** "a disk hit whose read outlasts the first rewrite does not rewrite again" holds the later reads, after they have read the untrimmed file, until the first rewrite has settled. Without the fix it fails 5/5 with the same `2 !== 1` as CI. With the fix it passes 5/5.
- The whole file passes: 52/52, 0 cancelled.
- Node 24, in a container, on `93ea088f`: `format:check`, `check:boundaries`, `npm run i18n -- --check`, `npm test` and `npm run build` are all green.

Changelog: `changelog.d/1211-mapillary-disk-rewrite-race.md`.

title: feat(hud): let a Gemini key drive the AI HUD summary
body:
## What

An install that has a **Gemini API key and no OpenAI key** now gets the AI HUD summary (the five-word `SUMMARY` readout) instead of the deterministic fallback. When `OPENAI_API_KEY` is set nothing changes: the same OpenAI request goes out as before.

## How

- `server/providers/gemini/interactions.js` (new, ~110 lines). A minimal client for the **Interactions API**. Google now recommends it over `generateContent` for new work ([migration guide](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/migrate-to-interactions)). Each call is one stateless turn:
  - `POST /v1beta/interactions` with `store: false`, so nothing is kept for later retrieval.
  - The key goes only in the `x-goog-api-key` header, never in the URL.
  - `redirect: 'error'`.
  - A 5 s timeout, because the HUD drops its own request after 5 s (`src/hud.js`).
  - Only a `completed` interaction counts as an answer. An `incomplete` one can carry a fragment cut off by the output budget, so it falls back like any other failure.
  - The model id is checked before any request, so an env value cannot reshape the URL or body.
- `server/providers/openai/hud-summary.js` picks the provider. With `GEV_HUD_SUMMARY_PROVIDER` unset or `auto`, OpenAI is used if its key is set, otherwise Gemini. `openai` or `gemini` pins one, and **pinning is binding**: a pinned provider without its key gets the existing keyless response, not a quiet switch to the other account.
  - Both providers share the route's per-IP throttle (`GEV_RATELIMIT_OPENAI_PER_MIN`), so switching does not double the budget.
  - Both share the fixed error text. Google's error wording (project ids, quota phrasing) is never relayed.
  - The OpenAI request body is unchanged; it only moved into `requestOpenAiSummary()`.
- The model is `GEMINI_HUD_SUMMARY_MODEL`, defaulting to `gemini-3.5-flash-lite`: stable, Google's fastest and cheapest text model, and it thinks minimally by default. The request sets `thinking_level: minimal` and `thinking_summaries: none`.
- The POWER UP panel gets a **GEMINI** row (`GEMINI_API_KEY`, aistudio.google.com/apikey). es/ru catalogs are updated.
- `.env.example` and the README say plainly that **unpaid Gemini quota may be used by Google to improve its products and read by human reviewers**, and that in the EEA, Switzerland and the UK Google applies its paid data terms even to unpaid quota and requires paid services for apps offered there ([terms](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/terms)). The HUD context is the place and layer names in view.

## Overlap with Gemini Live (#872, now on `main`)

Merged forward onto `main` at `d48b9c4d` (merge `2822dddc`). Gemini Live landed with the same `GEMINI_API_KEY`, the same keySetup id and the same AI Studio URL, so the two now share them as planned:

- **One POWER UP row.** It keeps `main`'s `metered` tier, and its `unlocks` text names both uses: "Gemini Live voice control + AI HUD summary when no OpenAI key is set" (es, ru and zh-CN updated). The "every registry row has its own id and its own env vars" test passes with the single row.
- **One `GEMINI_API_KEY=` line** in `.env.example`. The comment above it covers both uses and keeps the unpaid-quota data terms, then lists `GEMINI_LIVE_MODEL`, `GEV_RATELIMIT_GEMINI_PER_MIN`, `GEMINI_HUD_SUMMARY_MODEL` and `GEV_HUD_SUMMARY_PROVIDER`.
- **README.** This keeps `main`'s provider-chooser text. "does not change the OpenAI-backed AI HUD summary" now reads "does not change which provider drives the AI HUD summary", and the Gemini fallback sentence follows it.
- **Throttle.** The HUD route still uses its own `GEV_RATELIMIT_OPENAI_PER_MIN` route throttle whichever provider answers. `GEV_RATELIMIT_GEMINI_PER_MIN` stays the Live token throttle. Happy to move the summary under the Gemini knob if you prefer.
- `normalizeGeminiTextModel` and Live's `normalizeGeminiModel` use the same id pattern. They can become one helper in `server/providers/gemini/` in a follow-up, which keeps this PR's diff small.
- **#976 (typed agent):** still untouched. The only overlap is a neighbouring row in `keySetupCore.mjs`.

## Evidence

Node 24, in a container. After the merge-forward onto `d48b9c4d`, the full gate passes: doctor, `format:check`, `check:boundaries`, `changelog:check`, build, `i18n --check` (es, ru and zh-CN complete) and `npm test`, with 8,307 passed and 0 failed. The original evidence on `93ea088f`:

- Each commit is green on its own: `format:check`, `check:boundaries`, `npm run i18n -- --check` (es and ru complete), `npm test` and `npm run build`. Results: 7,739 passed and 0 failed after the first commit, 7,748 passed and 0 failed after the second.
- `npm run test:track`: 109/109.
- 15 new tests in `geminiInteractions.test.mjs`, `hudSummaryProvider.test.mjs` and `keySetupCore.test.mjs`. They cover:
  - the request shape and the key travelling only in a header;
  - thought steps (the documented `summary` shape) and the echoed input not counting as answer text;
  - statuses other than `completed` being refused;
  - an HTTP failure keeping its status with no provider text;
  - model-id validation, with no request sent for a bad id;
  - OpenAI-first ordering, with the **whole OpenAI request body pinned** to what `main` sends;
  - binding pins;
  - the keyless path sending no request;
  - the panel and the server reading the same variable;
  - unique registry rows.
- 9 mutations of the new code each turn the suite red: store, status gate, thought filter, redirect, model check, provider table, binding pin, thinking level and a duplicate registry row.
- An independent review found 0 P0/P1. Its P2s are addressed: the README key count, the EEA/UK/Swiss wording against the terms, and the duplicate-row guard. The `[hud-summary]` log lines are byte-identical to `main`.
- **Live check: not yet run.** I don't have a Gemini API key on this machine, so no request has reached the real Interactions API. Everything above is offline: the contract tests pin the documented wire shape. I'm marking this ready so it can be reviewed now. I'll post the live numbers (completed vs incomplete rate, five-word rate, p50/p95 latency) as soon as I have a key. If a reviewer has a key, one `GEMINI_API_KEY` run with `OPENAI_API_KEY` unset shows it end to end.

Changelog: `changelog.d/1212-gemini-hud-summary.md`.

title: feat: query tools for the Air quality and GNSS integrity layers
body:
### Problem

Two recently merged layers can be switched on by voice but cannot be asked anything by an MCP or voice client:

- **Air quality** (#568, ECCC AQHI). The voice layer manifest (`src/voice/layerManifest.js`) can turn it on and count readings. No query tool returns the readings: "what is the air quality in Toronto right now?" has no tool to answer it.
- **GNSS integrity** (#1108). Same gap: the layer classifies half-degree cells by the share of aircraft reporting degraded navigation integrity, but no tool returns the cells, so "is there GPS interference near Kaliningrad?" has no answer outside the globe view.

`docs/TOOLS.md` lists 40 tools. Weather, fires, cyclones, perimeters and quakes each have one; these two layers do not. Nothing under `src/tools/` mentions either of them.

### Proposal

Two small read-only `query` tools, one per domain file, reading only the layers' existing portable sources through `src/tools/services.js`. No new data source, endpoint or dependency.

**`get_air_quality`** (in `src/tools/queries/environment.js`, next to `get_weather`)
- Input: the shared `AREA_SCHEMA` and `LIMIT_SCHEMA`.
- Reads `createEcccAirQualitySource().getSnapshot()` and returns the stations in the area, nearest first: station name, AQHI value, band and health-risk label from `AIR_QUALITY_BANDS`, observed time.
- Uses the model's existing rules, so the tool and the layer agree: readings older than `OBSERVATION_MAX_AGE_MS` are dropped, and `readingsAreStale` is reported.
- Outside the network's coverage (Canada for ECCC) it says so rather than returning an empty list that reads as "clean air".
- Written against `AIR_QUALITY_PROVIDERS`, so a second provider such as #1204 (India CPCB) can join without changing the tool's shape.

**`get_gnss_integrity`** (in `src/tools/queries/aviation.js`)
- Input: `POINT_SCHEMA`, because the proxy reads a 250 nm regional snapshot around an anchor.
- Reads `createAdsbGnssSource().getSnapshot()` through the local `/api/gnss-integrity` route, then reuses the classifier in `src/layers/gnss/records.js` (`accumulateGnssObservations`, `binGnssCells`). It returns the cells with `level`, `aircraft`, `degraded` and `percentDegraded`, plus `GNSS_PROVENANCE`.
- The summary keeps the layer's wording: *suspected* interference, with avionics faults and old transponders named as other causes.

**One open question, on GNSS:** the layer accumulates a 30-minute window of snapshots before it classifies, while a single tool call sees one snapshot. I would report that honestly rather than hold the call open: `window: single snapshot` in the provenance, and the number of aircraft seen, so an area where `binGnssCells` drops every cell for having fewer than `GNSS_MIN_AIRCRAFT` aircraft reads as too few aircraft, not as nominal. If you would rather the tool wait, or read the running layer's window through the panel, say so and I will follow that.

Each tool gets:
- unit tests next to the existing query tests, with fixture snapshots and no network;
- a `docs/TOOLS.md` row;
- a `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md` note;
- a changelog fragment.

They are exposed to MCP and voice like the other environment and aviation queries.

Related: #855 (leopechnicki, open) also works on GNSS interference from ADS-B integrity fields. If it changes the classifier this tool reads, I will build on whichever lands first. #1077 (assigned) is about drawing on the globe and does not overlap. #1167 proposes more environmental layers; this tool would read whatever provider the Air quality layer registers, so it does not compete with that.

### Data source, license, and attribution

None new. Both tools read sources the app already ships, with their existing attribution:
- Air quality: ECCC AQHI via `api.weather.gc.ca`, ECCC Data Servers End-use Licence (attribution required), keyless.
- GNSS integrity: adsb.lol through the existing `/api/gnss-integrity` proxy, ODbL, keyless.

Results carry the same source credits the layers show.

### Will you build it?

Yes, I plan to open a PR

title: feat(layers): introduce ABYSS — deep-sea exploration & intelligence layer
body:
### Description

This PR introduces the **ABYSS — Deep-Sea Exploration & Intelligence** layer to God's Eye View.

The layer integrates global seafloor bathymetry, hydrothermal vent fields, and deep-sea ROV research expeditions into the interactive 3D globe:

1. **GEBCO Bathymetry (WMS):** Drapes global high-resolution seafloor elevation and relief raster imagery directly over the ocean surface (`GEBCO_LATEST_2` colour-shaded bathymetry, `GEBCO_LATEST` shaded relief, and `GEBCO_LATEST_TID` survey-type / source-identification grid). Includes an interactive depth legend running from 0 m down to -11,000 m. Note: As documented, this is high-resolution 2D raster imagery draped onto the reference ellipsoid; it does not claim to displace the Cesium globe's physical terrain into true 3D underwater trenches.
2. **NOAA PMEL Global Hydrothermal Vents:** Displays documented hydrothermal vent fields sourced from the NOAA PMEL Earth-Ocean Interactions program. Markers distinguish active fields (thermal amber-orange), relict/inactive fields (slate-cyan), and unconfirmed/inferred locations (yellow). Selecting a vent opens its scientific detail panel displaying reported depth, coordinates, tectonic setting, spreading rate, and direct links to scientific literature. Served via `/api/abyss/vents` (cached for 24h) with authoritative bundled fallback.
3. **NOAA Ocean Exploration ROV Dives & Tracks:** Integrates documented deep-sea research expeditions conducted by NOAA Ship *Okeanos Explorer* using ROV *Deep Discoverer*. Querying the official NOAA Ocean Exploration ArcGIS FeatureServer populates dive locations. On selection, the vehicle's bottom dive track is fetched on-demand and rendered as a high-visibility subsea polyline with antimeridian-crossing split protection, vessel, year, dive duration, and archival links.
4. **Architecture & Standards:**
   - **Layer Token Reservation:** Allocated `'5'` in `src/data/layerStateTokenReservations.json` and passed `scripts/check-layer-state-tokens.mjs`.
   - **Package Boundaries:** Strictly registered in `scripts/package-boundaries.json` with 0 violations.
   - **Voice Manifest:** Registered in `VOICE_OFF_LAYERS` to preserve existing Realtime action schema hashes and token budgets.
   - **Internationalization (i18n):** Full layer name and control coverage in `src/ui/layerNames.js`, `es.json`, and `ru.json`.
   - **Data Credits & Documentation:** Documented in `src/data/dataCredits.js`, `DATA_SOURCES.md`, `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md`, and `README.md`.

### Validation & Verification
- `npm run format:check` (1,433 files verified, exit code 0)

- `npm run build` (Vite production bundle compiled, exit code 0)
- `node --test src/layers/abyss/*.test.mjs server/providers/abyss.test.mjs` (19/19 tests passed)

title: test(street-level): read the header point and panel box in one page task
body:
The Street Level browser gate fails now and then with `QA_FAIL_ON_RETRY=1 turns this retry into a failure` on changes that touch no panel code:

- #1210 ([job](https://github.com/bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view/actions/runs/39108523729/job/117619526403)): `the press missed the street-level-panel header (on canvas.mapillary-canvas); pre-press hit check passed; stillness held; panel box at hit check 1058,266 330x425 -> at press 1058,266 330x425`
- #794 ([job](https://github.com/bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view/actions/runs/39107974005/job/117617830446)): the same, on the CCTV panel, `1018,266 330x425 -> at press 1018,266 330x425`

The panel did move. The helper read it at the wrong moment.

### The race

`headerTarget()` in `scripts/qa-panelDrag.mjs` made two page calls:

1. `headerPoint()` + `hitAt()`: the title's centre, then what is under it.
2. `panelBox()`: the panel's box.

Right after a dock the rail can still move the panel, for example from `1058,382 330x489` to `1058,266 330x425` when the photo finishes loading. If that move lands between the two calls:
- the point is the old header's;
- the box is already the new one, so it equals the box at pointerdown;
- the press lands on whatever is now at the old point;
- `panelMoved()` sees two equal boxes and calls the miss unexplained.

Both CI failures report the box at exactly that destination, `…,266 330x425`. A local run with a probe caught the same move one step later, between the hit check and the press, and the existing check explained it there: `panel box at hit check 1058,382 330x489 -> at press 1058,266 330x425`.

### The change

- `headerSnapshot()` returns the point, the hit and the box from **one** `page.evaluate`, so all three describe the same layout. A move after it now shows up as a moved box and is retried with the usual `::warning::`.
- A press that misses a header that did not move still fails the run, as before.
- The retry note also prints the checked point (`pre-press hit check passed at 1127,408`), so a future miss can be placed on the screenshot.
- `headerPoint()` and `hitAt()` had no other callers and are folded into `headerSnapshot()`. `qa-panel-resize.mjs` has its own local `headerPoint` and is unaffected.

This only changes the QA harness. No runtime behaviour changes, so there is no `CURRENT-STATE.md` edit or changelog fragment, the same as db790279 when this retry policy was added.

### Verified

- New unit test, `QA_FAIL_ON_RETRY retries a miss when the panel moved right after the hit check`. The fake page moves the panel in the page task after the hit check. On `main`'s helper it fails with the CI error. Here it passes.
- New unit test for the hit check's own wait: it waits for the header, and reports `timedOut` with the element it found when the header never comes.
- Mutations, each red:
  - the old helper;
  - reading the box in a separate call after the snapshot;
  - dropping the point from the note;
  - a hit check that always reports the header;
  - a hit check with no wait loop.

  The `nothing under the point` branch is unchanged from `hitAt()` and still has no test.
- `src/tooling/streetLevelQa.test.mjs`: 29/29.
- Node 24, in a container, on `93ea088f`: `format:check`, `check:boundaries`, `npm run i18n -- --check`, `npm test` and `npm run build` are green.
- Locally, with `QA_FAIL_ON_RETRY=1`, against a fixture build of `main`, `qa-street-level.mjs --fixtures --strict` and `qa-panel-resize.mjs` both passed 4 runs out of 4. Two of those runs hit the same two moves CI saw, and each was retried with a warning and then passed. In both, the move landed after the snapshot, so `main`'s helper would have retried them too. It only fails when the move lands between its hit check and its box read, a window the unit test above opens deterministically.
  - `the press missed the street-level-panel header (on canvas.mapillary-canvas); pre-press hit check passed at 1127,408; stillness held; panel box at hit check 1058,382 330x489 -> at press 1058,266 330x425`
  - `the press missed the cctv-panel header (on img#cctv-frame.); pre-press hit check passed at 1054,349; stillness held; panel box at hit check 1018,323 330x633 -> at press 1018,266 330x425`

title: feat(voice): speak the interface language in cloud voice sessions
body:
## Problem

With the interface in Spanish or Russian (`?lang=es`, `?lang=ru`), the cloud voice still speaks English. Three things are English-only today:

1. **Session instructions** (`server/providers/openai/instructions.js`) never mention a language, and `/api/realtime/token` does not know the interface locale. Captions are transcribed with no `language` hint.
2. **Tool follow-ups.** `RealtimeTurns.flushPendingResponse` sends `response.create` with its own `instructions`, which replace the session's for that response. So even if the session asked for Spanish, every reply after a tool call would lose it.
3. **Progress lines.** `progressLine()` in `src/voice/speech.js` returns English template literals, and `speakProgressLine` asks the model to read them aloud exactly.

The visible voice text (cards, steps, errors) is already translated. Only what is spoken stays English.

## Proposal

The interface language travels with the token request, and the server builds the session from it. Everything else stays as it is.

- **Client:** `requestToken` adds `?lang=<code>` when the locale is a shipped non-English one. English sends nothing, so English URLs are unchanged.
- **Server:** the handler resolves `lang` against `LOCALES`. For a shipped non-English locale it:
  - appends one closing `LANGUAGE:` line to the session instructions;
  - sets `audio.input.transcription.language`;
  - echoes the language in `X-GEV-Voice-Language`, next to `X-GEV-Voice-Tier`.

  Any other value, including a hostile one, resolves to English with byte-identical instructions.
- **The LANGUAGE line** says:
  - speak the interface language unless the user speaks another one;
  - `say` lines and tool result text are English data, voiced without changing facts;
  - numbers, units, callsigns and codes are kept exactly;
  - tool names and arguments stay as defined, so the tool contract does not change.
- **Follow-ups** append the same line. One function produces it for both server and client (`src/voice/voiceLanguage.js`), so the two cannot drift.
- **Progress lines** go through `t()`. That adds 9 catalog entries, translated for es and ru. English output is unchanged.

`realtimeInstructions(annotationGuidance)` keeps its signature; the language is an optional second argument. Voice-bench scripts and existing tests are unaffected.

## Out of scope

- The on-device tier (#843). Its pipeline (Gemma 4, Moonshine, Kokoro) needs a different design for non-English speech.
- Tool `say` lines and other tool results: these stay English data, and the model voices them in the session language. Translating them at the source would change what every tool returns, so it would be a separate change.

## Status

I have this working on a local branch:

- **Tests:** 7 new, covering resolution, instructions, token query, headers and transcription language, follow-ups, progress lines, and the connection passing the locale.
- **Mutation check:** 9 mutations against the new code, 9 killed.
- **Full suite:** node 24, 7740 pass / 0 fail; format, boundaries, i18n and build all pass.

Not yet verified: a live Realtime turn in Spanish or Russian. I'll record one with transcripts before asking for review.

Would you take this as a PR? It touches the voice session setup, so I'd rather check the direction with you first.

title: feat(i18n): add Japanese (ja)
body:
Adds Japanese as a shipped locale, following the six steps in `docs/TRANSLATORS.md` § Adding a language.

## What's in it

- **Catalog:** `src/i18n/locales/ja.json` covers all 2623 messages. `npm run i18n` reports `ja: complete`. Plurals use the single `other` form, with counters such as 機, 隻, 台, 件, か所 and 人.
- **Kept in English:** 95 entries listed under `ja` in `same-as-english.json`. These are codes and readouts that Japanese aviation and broadcast UIs keep in Latin (HDG, ETA, ADS-B, UTC …), product names, and the `$K/M/B` money abbreviations.
- **Registration:** `CATALOGS` and `LOCALES`, the picker name `日本語`, `package-boundaries.json`, the picker test, and the shipped-language lists in `TRANSLATORS.md` and `CURRENT-STATE.md`.
- **Language notes:** `docs/translations/ja.md` covers style (polite です/ます for messages, noun endings for labels and HUD text), punctuation and width rules, units, the counter table, the codes kept in Latin, and a glossary.

## How it was checked

- **Two review passes, as a native speaker would read it:**
  - A full pass over all 2623 entries changed 186 values. Where a string is assembled in code, I checked the call site first: the wind line, ramp and exit directions, the key-guidance `, or ` joins, and FIRMS ages.
  - A second, independent pass over those changes, a random 200-entry sample, and a script check of every entry found nothing wrong in meaning or grammar. I applied 7 of its 8 style suggestions.
- **Screenshots:** `?lang=ja` at 360, 768 and 1440 px, compared with English at the same widths. No page overflow and no JS errors.
  - Text is clipped only where English clips the same text (the long status line).
  - One dock card clipped 「コンテキスト」, so the `CONTEXT` panel title is 「状況」. The glossary records this.
- **Full suite:** node 24, 7760 pass / 0 fail; format, boundaries, `i18n --check` and build all pass.
- **Gates against a dev server:** `npm run test:track` 109 passed / 0 failed. Because Japanese labels change panel widths, I also ran `qa:panel-resize`: all checks pass, with no page or render-loop errors.

## Known limits (code, not catalog)

A few strings are joined in code with ASCII separators or untranslated parts, so the Japanese stays slightly off until the code changes. I'd send these as a separate PR (`t()` whole sentences or `Intl.ListFormat`), not as catalog workarounds:

- `src/ui/applicationShell.js` joins lost-layer names with `', '`.
- `src/layers/firms/model.js` `formatAge` returns `5m` and `<1h` untranslated.
- `src/layers/cctv/presentation.js` passes raw band codes into `{value} CONTEXT`.
- `src/ui/streetLevelPresentation.js` joins requirements with `'; '`.
- `src/voice/resultDisplay.js` joins layer names with `', '`.
- `src/firstRunExperience.js` builds `{detail}` as ` (a, b)`.

#913 by @abiyeenzo was an earlier Japanese translation, stacked on #601, which has since closed. This catalog is a fresh translation against the current key-by-English-text catalogs. Thank you for the earlier work, and reviews from Japanese speakers are very welcome.

Related: #1216 (voice in the interface language). Its 9 progress lines will get Japanese once both land.

title: feat(voice): speak the interface language in cloud voice sessions
body:
Closes #1216.

With the interface in Spanish or Russian, the cloud voice still spoke English. Three places were English-only:
- the session instructions;
- tool follow-ups, whose `response.create` instructions replace the session's;
- the progress lines read aloud verbatim.

## Change

- **`src/voice/voiceLanguage.js`** is one shared source for both server and client:
  - `resolveVoiceLanguage(code)` returns a shipped non-English locale, or `null`;
  - `voiceLanguageInstruction(code)` returns the closing `LANGUAGE:` line, or `''`.
- **Client:**
  - `requestToken` adds `lang=<code>` only for a resolved language, so English token URLs are unchanged.
  - `RealtimeConnection` passes `getLocale()`.
- **Server** (`/api/realtime/token`):
  - Resolves `?lang=`, appends the line through `realtimeInstructions(annotationGuidance, { overpass, language })`, and sets `audio.input.transcription.language`. The Gemini token route resolves `?lang=` the same way.
  - Echoes `X-GEV-Voice-Language`.
  - Unshipped and hostile values resolve to English, and the instructions are then byte-identical to `realtimeInstructions()`.
- **Follow-ups:** `flushPendingResponse` appends the same line to its instructions.
- **Progress lines:** `progressLine()` goes through `t()`, adding 14 catalog entries (every step, including the draw, imagery catalog, image and OpenStreetMap ones). They are translated in all 10 non-English locales; the es, ru and zh-CN lines predate the others, and the rest are machine-assisted and would benefit from a native read. English output is unchanged.
- **Unchanged:** tool names, schemas and results. The model voices English `say` lines in the session language and keeps numbers, units and codes exact.

`realtimeInstructions` keeps its signature (the options object gains `language`), so the voice-bench scripts and existing callers are unaffected. The LANGUAGE line is added there and not in `realtimeDirectives`, so text chat, which reuses the directives, never receives it.

## Tests

9 new tests:
- `src/voice/voiceLanguage.test.mjs` (5):
  - resolution, including hostile input;
  - instructions identical without a language;
  - the token query;
  - the language line riding on top of the Overpass directives and staying out of `realtimeDirectives`;
  - follow-ups in en and es;
  - progress lines in en and es, including the imagery and OpenStreetMap steps.
- `src/tooling/localServices.test.mjs` (1): `?lang=` → instructions, transcription language and header, for es, RU, en, fr, empty and an injected newline.
- `src/voice/realtimeOwners.test.mjs` (1): the session requests its token in the current locale.

**Mutation check:** I ran 12 single-line mutations on the wiring: dropping the line, leaking it into the shared directives, losing `overpass` or `language` in either provider's session or route, ignoring `?lang=`, and leaving each progress step untranslated. The tests caught all 12.

title: feat(maps): add a bundled offline globe fallback
body:
## Problem and change

Closes #1141. Esri's existing fallback is OSM, so losing internet access can leave the globe without a usable basemap. Add **Offline globe** as a final imagery fallback and an explicit Map Source choice.

- Use Cesium's already-bundled Natural Earth II raster tiles (geographic TMS, levels 0–2) with flat ellipsoid terrain. No new imagery download, dependency, key, remote elevation request, or service worker.
- Preserve Esri → OSM; when OSM or Bing construction fails, or either reports two active tile errors, switch to Offline globe. Nested construction errors name the final displayed source rather than an intermediate fallback.
- Show a translated OFFLINE status and tooltip explaining low resolution and the connectivity requirement for live data. Keep the six-source desktop selector in one row and retain keyboard navigation.
- Register the source with voice selection and submarine-cable surface classification; preserve existing tool arguments and comparison recovery behavior.

Select an online source to return to detailed maps after a tile outage. This is a basemap fallback for a locally served app: it does not cache live feeds, make a hosted app shell available without a server, or download Google 3D tiles. A running Google 3D tileset is not automatically switched on network loss; Offline globe is available explicitly in the selector.

Natural Earth raster data is public domain; source/attribution and runtime behavior are documented. The existing Cesium asset-copy step includes the tiles in production builds.

## Validation

Node 24.14.0:

- Full `npm test`, including allocation gates
- `npm run build`, `format:check`, `check:boundaries`, `i18n`, and `layer-token:check -- --base-ref origin/main`
- `node scripts/qa-offline-basemap.mjs --headful`: actual Cesium rendering with remote HTTPS providers blocked; verifies Esri/OSM failure → local tiles, flat terrain, OFFLINE status, manual selection without remote map requests, and teardown
- `node scripts/qa-map-source-controls.mjs`: full-app selection and lifecycle, including the new Offline globe chip and status
- `node scripts/qa-map-source-tray.mjs --headful --keyless`: responsive layout, keyboard focus and selection

The network-blocked gate uses CDP URL blocking after navigation, keeping Cesium module-worker initialization free of Puppeteer request interception.

title: feat(ai-chat): GEV AI text chat via DeepSeek and Xiaomi MiMo
body:
## What

An opt-in **GEV AI text chat** panel that controls the app through the same action tools voice uses, backed by cheap OpenAI-compatible chat-completions providers: **DeepSeek** and **Xiaomi MiMo**. It complements Realtime voice: typed commands, no microphone, and a fraction of a cent per command (provider prompt caching hits ~97% on the tool catalog).

Keyless by default. The panel stays hidden unless `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` or `MIMO_API_KEY` is set, and shows a provider picker when both are.

## How

- **`server/providers/ai-chat.js`**: one provider table (key, base URL, model env vars, extra body per provider), so another OpenAI-compatible provider (OpenRouter, Groq, Ollama…) is one entry.
  - `GET /api/ai/status`: configured providers and models; never the keys.
  - `POST /api/ai/chat` (`{ provider, messages }`): re-wraps `GEV_REALTIME_TOOLS` as chat `function` tools.
- **Security, following the 0.2.1 conventions:**
  - `/api/ai/chat` is `sameSiteGated` and listed in SECURITY.md.
  - It is rate-limited by default with the shared `makeCostRateLimiter`: `GEV_RATELIMIT_AI_CHAT_PER_MIN`, 60/min/IP, `0` disables.
  - Provider error bodies are logged server-side and never relayed.
  - Keys stay server-side.
- **HUD summary fallback:** with no `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `/api/openai/hud-summary` uses the chat provider (`AI_CHAT_PROVIDER` picks which). Provider *thinking* is disabled; with it on, `deepseek-flash` spends the 100-token budget on reasoning and returns empty content.
- `reasoning_content` is stripped from replayed history, so switching provider mid-conversation is safe.
- **Client:**
  - `src/ai/aiChat.js` (panel) and `src/ai/aiChatController.js` (tool-call loop, max 8 rounds) run tools through a `createGevActionRunner` instance.
  - Browser Web Speech gives optional dictation and readback.
  - Panel copy goes through `t()` with ru/es entries.
- **Wiring:** Provider Settings rows, setup doctor, Pinokio env plumbing, `.env.example`, package boundaries, world-overlay/right-rail occluders.

MiMo Token Plan keys (`tp-…`) need their regional base, e.g. `MIMO_API_BASE=https://token-plan-sgp.xiaomimimo.com/v1`; pay-as-you-go keys use the default. MiMo has no OAuth, only keys.

## Validation

- `server/providers/ai-chat.test.mjs`: 7 tests covering:
  - status shape and default provider
  - cross-site 403
  - provider base, auth and extra body forwarding
  - an unknown provider rejected
  - provider error bodies not relayed
  - `reasoning_content` stripping
- `npm test`: the only failures are 5 tests in `src/tooling/localServices`, `src/tooling/previewServing` and `src/tools/localRoute` that return 403 on loopback. They **fail identically on untouched `main`** on this Windows 11 machine, so they're unrelated to this PR and maybe worth a separate look. `streetLevel/meshSampler` was timing-flaky once and passed on rerun.
- `npm run format:check`, `npm run i18n` and `npm run check:boundaries` pass; `npm run build` passes.
- **Live:**
  - Both providers answered "Fly to Warsaw" with `fly_to_location`.
  - The HUD summary returned "Warsaw Poland flights overhead" via DeepSeek.
  - Headless Edge drove the panel: picked MiMo, "Fly to Tokyo", the globe flew, no page errors.
- Not run: `npm run test:track` and the `qa-*` gates; no existing gate covers this panel.

Happy to split this, rename the env vars, or drop the HUD fallback if you'd rather keep the summary OpenAI-only.

title: feat(electron): open the app in a desktop window with npm start
body:
## What

`npm start` now opens God's Eye View in an Electron window instead of a browser tab.

- **`electron/main.js`** (new): the Electron main process. It
  - picks a port: `PORT`, or 4173 by default, falling back to a free port when `npm run dev` already holds it. Keeping 4173 when it is free keeps the page origin stable, so saved settings and layers survive between launches.
  - starts the same Vite dev server as `npm run dev` on `127.0.0.1`, which is loopback only, so Provider Settings keeps its usual admission rules.
  - waits until the server answers, then loads it in a `BrowserWindow` with `contextIsolation`, `sandbox` and no `nodeIntegration`.
  - opens links to other origins (attribution, sources, docs) in the system browser, both for `window.open` and for in-page navigation.
  - grants only `media`, `geolocation`, clipboard and fullscreen, and only to the app's own origin.
  - stops the server when the window closes, and shows an error dialog if the server exits unexpectedly.
- **`package.json`**: `"main": "electron/main.js"`, a `start` script (`electron .`), and `electron@44.9.0` as a pinned devDependency.
- **`Dockerfile`**: sets `ELECTRON_SKIP_BINARY_DOWNLOAD=1`, the same way `PUPPETEER_SKIP_DOWNLOAD` is already set, so `npm ci` in the container doesn't fetch a ~100 MB binary it never uses.
- **`bin/gods-eye-view.js`** + `npm run shortcut` (`npm link`): a `gods-eye-view` command on PATH that opens the same window from any folder. Ctrl+C stops the window and the server.
- **`README.md`**: one paragraph under Path 2 about the desktop window.

## Why

A one-command desktop launch for people who'd rather have a dedicated app window than a browser tab. It changes nothing about how the app itself is served.

## Notes for reviewers

- The server runs under the Node that invoked npm (`npm_node_execpath`), not Electron's bundled Node, because `engines` requires Node ≥ 24.14 and Electron ships an older one. The Vite middleware therefore runs on exactly the runtime it does under `npm run dev`.
- WebUSB (RTL-SDR) has no device chooser in this shell yet. In Electron, that needs a `select-usb-device` handler, which can come in a follow-up.
- This PR doesn't package or sign the app. It is a dev-time desktop shell only.

## Testing

- Ran `npm start` on macOS with Node 26.7.0. The window opened on `http://127.0.0.1:4173/`, the globe and first-run panel rendered, and the console showed no errors (checked over the DevTools protocol).
- Closing Electron also stopped the Vite child process.
- Ran `npm run shortcut`, then `gods-eye-view` from `~`. The window opened, and Ctrl+C stopped Electron and Vite.
- `npm test` passed: 7733 passed, 0 failed, 1 skipped (the allocation microbenchmarks only run under Node 24).
- `npm run format:check` and `npm run check:boundaries` passed.

A changelog fragment follows in a second commit once this PR has a number.

title: feat(gravity): add a Mass Change layer from GRACE/GRACE-FO mascons
body:
## What it adds

A **Mass Change (GRACE)** layer. It shows monthly change in mass at the Earth's surface (groundwater, ice, large lakes) from the UT Center for Space Research's RL06.3 GRACE/GRACE-FO mascon solutions, from 2002 to about five weeks ago. Values are centimetres of equivalent water against the 2004–2009 mean. Northern India's groundwater decline, California's Central Valley and Greenland's ice loss all show clearly.

### Server (`/api/gravity`)

- CSR publishes the whole record as one NetCDF file of about 115 MB. The proxy downloads it at most once a day with a conditional GET, so an unchanged file costs one round trip.
- It reads the file with [h5wasm](https://github.com/usnistgov/h5wasm) (NIST, a new dependency, loaded only while converting).
- It reduces the 0.25° grid to one-degree int16 means on disk, about 34 MB for 260 solutions, then deletes the download. The mascons are about 1° and the missions resolve about 300 km, so the reduction loses nothing real.
- Conversion takes about 3 s, with a peak of about 350 MB RSS.
- Routes:
  - `/index`: solutions, grid, source
  - `/field?id=`: one solution, 130 KB
  - `/cell?lat=&lon=`: one cell's whole record, rate-limited
  - `/landmask`: CSR's static 0.25° land mask, fetched once and run-length packed to about 10 KB
- Every route answers a retryable 503 (`GRAVITY_LOADING` / `GRAVITY_UNAVAILABLE`) while the first download runs. A failed land mask never holds up the record.
- Nothing from CSR is committed; everything is fetched at runtime.

### Layer

- One raised shell at 4 km, below the weather shells.
- Drawn at 0.25°: each pixel blends its four nearest cells, so one-degree steps become gradients. The readout still uses the real cell.
- Red means loss and blue means gain. The scale saturates at ±40 cm so aquifer signals stay visible next to metre-scale ice loss.
- **Land only** is the default and follows CSR's land mask. **Land + ocean** shows every cell. Over the oceans the signal is mostly sea level.
- Share links keep the month, area and opacity, using token `5` from `layer-token:next`.

### MASS CHANGE rail card (`#gravity-panel`)

- Month slider, previous/next, **Latest** and **Play**. Play replays from the first solution and never steps faster than a field arrives; the last 36 fields are cached.
- A click on open ground charts that cell's whole record, broken at the July 2017 to May 2018 gap between the missions. Clicking the chart jumps to that month.

## Verification

- `npm run doctor`, `format:check`, `check:boundaries`, `layer-token:check -- --base-ref origin/main` and `npm run i18n` (es/ru complete) are clean. `npm test`: 7767 tests, 7766 pass, 0 fail. `npm run build` is clean.
- `npm run test:track` against the dev server: 109 passed, 0 failed.
- New gate `scripts/qa-gravity.mjs` against the dev server: 15/15. It covers:
  - live record and land mask
  - previous / Latest / Play / Pause
  - click-to-chart over northern India (−34.5 cm, 8 segments)
  - land and ocean
  - a stubbed `GRAVITY_LOADING` 503
  - a 390×844 phone viewport
  - disable
- End to end on CSR's real file: 260 solutions through Aug 2026. Northern India goes from +66.5 cm in the first solution to −34.5 cm now; the Central Valley from −0.5 to −22.5 cm.
- Unit tests cover:
  - time bounds with overlapping solutions (Oct 2011, Apr 2015)
  - quantisation and no-data
  - block reduction and orientation
  - chunk-aligned conversion
  - proxy caching, conditional refresh, retry backoff and the mask route
  - 0.25° blending and masking
  - month stepping, playback, probe history
  - the card

## Data and attribution

`DATA_SOURCES.md` has the source row and a notes entry (`#gravity`), and the in-app credit names CSR. CSR publishes no licence. It asks users to acknowledge the download and cite Save et al. (2016, doi:10.1002/2016JB013007) and Save (2020, doi:10.15781/cgq9-nh24). Both citations are in the credit and the notes.

`docs/CURRENT-STATE.md` has the layer row and a runtime paragraph. The changelog entry is `changelog.d/1227-gravity-mass-change.md`.

title: fix(opensky): read OPENSKY_CREDENTIALS_FILE in the server and stop sending retired Basic auth
body:
OpenSky's API has accepted only OAuth2 client credentials since 2026-03-18. Its own README says: "basic authentication with username and password is no longer supported". Two parts of our setup lag behind that.

**1. The server now reads `OPENSKY_CREDENTIALS_FILE`.**
- `.env.example` and docs/opensky-auth.md offer it as an alternative to `OPENSKY_CLIENT_ID` and `OPENSKY_CLIENT_SECRET`. It points to the `credentials.json` that OpenSky's account page now hands out.
- Until now only the macOS `dev-fresh.sh` launcher read it. With `npm run dev`, `preview`, Docker or Pinokio, the server silently fell back to anonymous access (400 credits a day instead of 4,000).
- The server now uses the file when the two variables are empty. It accepts `clientId`/`clientSecret` or `client_id`/`client_secret`, expands `~`, and re-reads the file on each token refresh. An unreadable file is warned about once.

**2. Basic auth is no longer sent.** The proxy still sent `OPENSKY_USERNAME`/`OPENSKY_PASSWORD` as a Basic header in `basic` mode, fell back to it in `auto` mode, and retried with it after an OAuth 401. The docs said Basic was "still supported for now". Now:
- `basic` mode requests anonymously (reason `basic_retired`) and warns once with what to set instead. The password is never sent or logged.
- `auto` mode uses OAuth when it's configured, otherwise anonymous (`missing_oauth_creds`). There's no Basic fallback or retry.
- docs/opensky-auth.md, `.env.example` and the setup doctor say Basic is retired, and the client's reason map drops the Basic reasons.
- `scripts/dev-fresh.sh` and `dev-secure.sh` still read a username and password from the Keychain. They only pass environment variables through, and the server now ignores those, so I left the macOS scripts alone.

**Verification**
- `npm test`: 7739 tests, 7729 pass, 0 fail, 10 skipped.
- `format:check`, `check:boundaries`, `i18n` and `changelog:check` pass.
- New tests: `openskyCredentials.test.mjs`, plus two proxy tests. One checks that `basic` mode sends no Authorization header and warns once without the password. The other checks that `auto` mode never retries with Basic after a 401. Both proxy tests fail on main and pass here.
- Live, with only `OPENSKY_CREDENTIALS_FILE` set: `200`, `X-OpenSky-Auth: oauth`, `oauth_ok`, 10,254 aircraft.
- Live, in `basic` mode with a dummy username and password: `200`, `anon`, `basic_retired`, 10,238 aircraft, and one warning.

Update: `npm run doctor` now counts `OPENSKY_CREDENTIALS_FILE` (from the environment or `.env`) as OAuth credentials, instead of reporting keyless anonymous access while the server signs in with the file. `npm test`: 7740 tests, 7730 pass, 0 fail.

title: feat(flights): type and registration for civil aircraft from the Mictronics database
body:
OpenSky state vectors carry no aircraft type or registration. So for civil traffic, area questions get "no type reported", every plane draws as the default airliner until it's clicked, and the adsbdb lookup only covers a few hundred aircraft a session because of its rate limit.

This adds the [Mictronics aircraft database](https://github.com/Mictronics/aircraft-database). It's licensed ODC-By 1.0 per the repository's LICENSE and regenerated weekly, with about 435,000 ICAO addresses carrying a type designator.

**Server: `server/providers/aircraft/types.js`**
- Downloads the 3.4 MB `indexedDB.zip` export when there's no copy or the copy is a week old, keeps it in `.gev-cache/mictronics-aircraft-db.zip`, and indexes it as sorted typed arrays (about 7 MB, against about 40 MB for a Map).
- `POST /api/aircraft-types {ids}` answers up to 20,000 addresses with type designator, type name and registration. Manufacturer names written in capitals read as names, e.g. "Boeing 737-800".
- Never makes a request wait for loading: until a copy is ready it answers `503` with a short `Retry-After`.
- Keeps serving the old copy if a refresh fails, and retries an hour later.

**Client: `src/sources/live/aircraftTypes.js`**
- Fills each flight snapshot's untyped records in batches, asking about each address once. So `aircraft_in_area`, the aircraft classes (a 747 or A380 draws as a four-engine jet, a 787 as a wide-body) and the layer queries all get types without a click.
- Type lookups for a single aircraft (selecting it, `get_aircraft_info`) ask the database first and adsbdb only for addresses it lacks. adsbdb still answers routes, and an adsbdb answer takes precedence.
- Aircraft the database has typed no longer use up adsbdb's lookup budget.
- Aircraft rows gain `type_name`, and `find_aircraft` now searches civil registrations, not only military ones.

**Also included**

title: feat: include existing fire perimeters in Environmental first-run mission
body:
## Problem

The first-run **ENVIRONMENTAL** mission in `src/firstRunExperience.js` enables only `['earthquakes', 'local-firms']`. The app already ships the keyless `fire-perimeters` layer (NIFC/WFIGS), but selecting this mission does not enable it. That means a first-time visitor exploring wildfire/disaster context misses incident perimeters unless they find and enable the layer separately. If their optional FIRMS key is absent, the mission provides only earthquake data.

Relevant current owners:
- [`FIRST_RUN_MISSIONS.environmental`](https://github.com/bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view/blob/main/src/firstRunExperience.js)
- [Existing welcome tile](https://github.com/bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view/blob/main/src/ui/templates/welcome.html)
- [First-run unit/browser QA](https://github.com/bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view/blob/main/src/firstRunExperience.test.mjs) and [`qa-firstrun`](https://github.com/bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view/blob/main/scripts/qa-firstrun.mjs)

## Small proposal

Make the existing Environmental mission enable three **already-shipped** layers, in order:

```js
layerIds: Object.freeze(['earthquakes', 'local-firms', 'fire-perimeters'])
```

Update the tile's functional subcopy/localizations to mention earthquake activity, active-fire detections, and wildfire incident perimeters. Keep the existing mission launcher and layer-state owner; no new UI mode, provider, custom feed, routing service, auto-dispatch workflow, or ongoing requests before the visitor explicitly selects the mission.

## Data source, license, and attribution

No new data integration or redistribution. Reuse the current keyless NIFC/WFIGS Fire Perimeters layer, existing server proxy, provenance/credits, and rights documented in [`DATA_SOURCES.md`](https://github.com/bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view/blob/main/DATA_SOURCES.md). NASA FIRMS remains separately optional/key-gated. This UI change does not turn inferred fire data into verified access or operational safety information.

## Acceptance

- Selecting **ENVIRONMENTAL** enables exactly the three existing layers via the same `origin: 'user'` persistence semantics as current mission choices.
- With FIRMS unavailable, the earthquake and fire-perimeter layers still behave independently; any unavailable state remains visible and honest.
- Manual Explore, share-link skip, session/durable suppression, camera framing, and other missions remain unchanged.
- Update first-run unit assertions and `qa-firstrun`; validate build, i18n, and existing feature gates before a PR.

Downstream source idea: [kvnloo/gods-eye-view#13](https://github.com/kvnloo/gods-eye-view/issues/13). This is deliberately smaller than the separate [humanitarian workspace RFC #1198](https://github.com/bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view/issues/1198) and doesn't depend on that RFC being accepted.

**Implementation:** Happy to send a small test-backed PR if maintainers want this mission behavior; no PR opened yet.
