title: perf: globe draws at 1x on high-DPI screens (stair-stepped lines on Retina) — proposal + numbers
body: ### Problem `createApplicationViewer` (`src/app/viewer.js`) uses Cesium's default `useBrowserRecommendedResolution: true`. Cesium then draws one pixel per CSS pixel, whatever the screen's `devicePixelRatio`: ``` pixelRatio = (useBrowserRecommendedResolution ? 1 : devicePixelRatio) * resolutionScale ``` Cesium also sets `image-rendering: pixelated` on its canvas, so a 2x screen shows a pixel-doubled 1x frame. On every Retina Mac, cable lines, orbit lines, polygon edges and 3D tiles look stair-stepped. MSAA 4 smooths the 1x frame, but the doubling undoes that. ### Proposal Draw in device pixels, with guard rails. I have a working branch and would like to know whether you want this before I open a PR. - `useBrowserRecommendedResolution: false`. A small resolution governor (no timers, no dependencies) sets `resolutionScale` so the drawing ratio is `min(devicePixelRatio, 2)`, within a 3840 × 2160 drawing-buffer budget, and never below today's 1x. - It steps down 0.25 after about 2 s of frames over 20 ms and steps back up after 8 s on time, with back-off on failed step-ups and a 5 s start-up warm-up. It follows DPR changes (a window moved to another screen). - MSAA 2 from ratio 1.5 up (4 below). That keeps at least 4 samples per CSS pixel and costs 17–24% less frame time than MSAA 4 at 2x. - The sharpen, CRT, NVG, FLIR and Anime post stages size their kernels in CSS pixels, so they look the same at 2x. Transit sensor-click mapping uses the same CSS grid (a 2x test case is included). - `?maxPixelRatio=1` restores today's drawing. There is no quality setting in the app today. If you would rather have a DISPLAY control, I can add one. Numbers (Apple M2 Max, Chrome 155, 1200 × 886 CSS viewport). Uncapped frame time, vsync off, mean / p95 ms: | Build | DPR | Drawing | MSAA | Globe | Close (1.2 km) | | --- | ---: | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | main | 1 | 1x | 4 | 3.09 / 5.7 | 3.65 / 6.3 | | branch | 1 | 1x | 4 | 3.56 / 5.9 | 3.16 / 4.7 | | main | 2 | 1x | 4 | 3.17 / 6.0 | 3.80 / 6.1 | | branch | 2 | 2x | 2 | 8.92 / 10.9 | 7.76 / 15.0 | | branch, forced MSAA 4 | 2 | 2x | 4 | 11.70 / 20.9 | 9.32 / 14.6 | - DPR 1 screens: no change (within ±0.5 ms on repeat runs, both directions). - With vsync on: 60 FPS on both builds at DPR 1 and 2. Idle renders are unchanged. - GPU-process memory at DPR 2: 839 → 1,353 MB (1200 × 886 window); 2,181 → 2,887 MB (2560 × 1440 window, held by the 4K budget). That is about 150 bytes per extra drawn pixel. - Governor under load (DPR 3, FLIR, constant motion): 2.25 → 1 in 19 s, then back up to 1.75 once frames were on time. Known limits: frame time cannot tell CPU from GPU cost, so a CPU-heavy scene also steps down, at worst to today's 1x. Cesium label glyphs stay at CSS resolution. Weak GPUs were simulated, not measured on low-end hardware. The branch passes `npm run build`, `npm test`, `npm run test:track` and the `qa-perf` gate. It adds no dependencies, and `npm audit` is unchanged from `main`. ### Data source, license, and attribution none (rendering change only) ### Will you build it? Yes, I plan to open a PR

title: fix(overpass): keyless gate behind a reverse proxy, loopback admission headroom, per-phase arrival budgets
body:
Follow-up to #1264, which merged before gekh's review notes
(https://github.com/bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view/pull/1264#issuecomment-6317249897)
were picked up. Everything in that comment is addressed here.

**P1 — Overpass behind the documented reverse proxy.** `/api/overpass` now uses
`admitSameSiteKeyless`, the gate `/api/terrain/heights` already uses. Forwarding
headers are admitted; a foreign or opaque `Origin` and a non-same-origin
`Sec-Fetch-Site` are still refused, and forwarding headers do not launder either.
SECURITY.md lists the route with terrain, the `localRequestGate.mjs` header no
longer says "four endpoints", and CURRENT-STATE describes the gate.

**P2 — global admission budget.** IPv6 peers are keyed by their /64 and
IPv4-mapped peers fold to IPv4 (`clientNetworkKey`, next to `clientKey`; only
the two Overpass limiters use it), so one rotating host stays in one 300/min
bucket. Loopback has its own 300/min window outside the 900/min global, so LAN
peers can fill the global without locking the owner's browser or the QA
harnesses out. Tests pin the 900 global with loopback still admitted, the /64
and v4-mapped folding, and cache hits spending admission but not the 90/min
upstream budget.

**P2 (unconfirmed) — arrival observation.** Each frame has its own 500 ms
budget: the settle frame measured from the forced moveEnd, the reveal frame
from the settle frame that hid the contact. Either stays inside the 1 s idle
refresh, and a ~300 ms SwiftShader frame fits inside each. The probe also
freshens both layers' rotation passes (moveEnd + one frame) before each attempt
and retries once on a wall-clock timeout, never on a wrong angle: a headless run
here showed a 926 ms first frame that no budget can accept.

**Smaller items.** The dead settings-block check and the stale probe comment in
`query.js` are gone, `[ timeout : N ]` is clamped (test added), and the tests
gekh listed as missing are in. The body read timeout and concurrency cap are
left for a later change: the body is capped at 24 KB and admission is spent
before the read.

Validation on Node 24.21.0, on main at f3bb697e:

- Unit suite: 8,205 tests, zero failed (one skipped), including 21 new or
  updated Overpass admission, rate-limit key and arrival observation tests.
- Format, package boundaries, changelog assembly and the production build pass.
- `test:track` against a dev server: 109 passed, 0 failed; flights settle
  333 ms + reveal 101 ms, military settle 358 ms + reveal 231 ms (589 ms total,
  which the previous single 500 ms deadline would have failed), both on the
  first attempt.
- Live HTTP on a dev server: a proxied same-origin POST reaches validation
  (400), a cross-site POST stays 403, `GET /status` stays 200.

body:
## Summary

Adds an opt-in, keyless NOAA Storm Prediction Center **Severe Weather Outlooks** layer under Weather. Day 1/2 categorical and tornado-probability bands show official colors, UTC issue/validity, a source link, and selected-area details. They are forecasts, **not active NWS warnings**; risk areas are not additive. Significant-tornado hatching is not included.

The browser fetches only `/api/spc-outlooks/{product}`. The server allowlists four products, pins NOAA's origin, rejects redirects and client query strings, and bounds responses, timeouts, cache and stale fallback. Day/type restore through saved state, v2 links and compact shares (new share token `9`, allocated after current `main`'s `5`–`8`). Tornado fills use 70% opacity and risk-ordered edges so nested 5% areas remain visible over desert imagery; categorical fills stay at 35%.

UI screenshots from the original review (before the tornado contrast adjustment); nested-band rendering is covered by the fixture browser gate below:

![Weather outlooks in isolation](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3dec0e5a-1853-4fc6-8f91-4f3ff65fbf79)

## Data and limits

[NOAA SPC FeatureServer](https://mapservices.weather.noaa.gov/vector/rest/services/outlooks/SPC_wx_outlks/FeatureServer); attribution: NOAA/NWS Storm Prediction Center. See `DATA_SOURCES.md` for the observed feed shape and limits. No key, database or new runtime dependency. No active warnings, notifications, or unrelated local changes.

## Validation (Node 24.21.0, based on `7d8b80db`)

- `npm test`: 10,480 passed, 1 skipped, 0 failed; allocation probes also pass.
- `npm run build`, `npm run format:check`, `npm run check:boundaries`, `npm run i18n`, `npm run layer-token:check -- --base-ref origin/main`: pass (35 published tokens, 1 new).
- Fixture browser gate: Esri/OSM ground rendering and map picking, nested 2%/5% tornado bands with an unfilled hole, all selectors, share restoration, and phone/desktop label bounds in English, Spanish and Russian: pass.

title: feat(alpine): add Alpine weather stations from three open networks
body: ## What this changes Adds **Alpine Stations**: about 650 automatic weather stations across the Swiss and Austrian Alps, drawn as markers coloured by a chosen measurement, with the readings, a legend and the nearest stations in view in a WEATHER rail card. This is the fresh branch asked for in #58 ([review](https://github.com/bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view/pull/58#issuecomment-5806188207)), which was closed in favour of it. Nothing is rebased from that branch; the one thing carried across is the normaliser's rule that an absent reading stays `null` rather than becoming zero. Related: #1016. Each point from that review, and where it landed: 1. **One adapter per network, not one Swiss network.** SLF IMIS, MeteoSwiss SwissMetNet and GeoSphere Austria TAWES, in `src/layers/alpineStations/networks/`. Each is a pure function — payload in, canonical records out — so the proxy and the browser share one normalisation and it is tested under `node --test`. Italy, France, Slovenia and Germany are not here: their terms are checked and noted in `docs/ALPINE-STATIONS.md`, and adding one is five steps in "Adding a network". 2. **Proxy under `server/providers/`.** `server/providers/alpine-stations.js` plus `alpine-stations/{upstreams,fetchers}.js`. Fixed upstream URLs with a per-URL read cap through `readResponseTextCapped` / `readResponseJsonCapped`, one in-flight request per upstream via `coalesceProxyRequest`, a failure cooldown, a serve-stale ceiling, a per-client rate limit, and both `configureServer` and `configurePreviewServer`. 3. **Layer under `src/layers/alpineStations/`, in the Weather group**, with a `readout: true` card in the WEATHER rail carrying the readings, a banded legend and the nearest stations in view. 4. **Simple markers, no rebuild, no render hold.** Changing the measurement recolours the existing entities in place (asserted by entity identity, not by count); settling the camera rebuilds no geometry and takes no continuous-render hold. **No imports from the fires layer.** 5. **No share-link token.** Registered `disposition: 'pending-share-token'` — drawable, never serialized — so the namespace stays yours (#658). The layer's enabled state and selected parameter simply do not travel in a share link. Completing it later is one registry move, described in the doc. Some things the networks forced, which are worth a reviewer's eye: - **Per-network capability is explicit, so a network never claims a measurement it cannot make honestly.** SwissMetNet contributes no snow depth (the whole-network VQHA80 file has no snow column; the per-station alternative is ~160 requests a refresh) and GeoSphere no sea-level pressure (`PRED` is only reduced to sea level for low stations — Hohe Warte at 198 m reads P 991.7 against PRED 1016.4, Sonnblick at 3109 m reads 696.7 against 707.7 — and nothing in the payload says which regime a station is in, so shipping it would draw a map of Austrian altitude). - **Three marker states are kept apart**: a reading, reporting-but-not-this-measurement, and offline. Collapsing them would assert readings that do not exist. Coverage is genuinely uneven — only 175 of ~650 stations carry a snow sensor — so in some views most markers are quiet ones by design. - **Staleness follows the reporting network, not one global window.** SLF publishes every 30 minutes and the other two every 10, so an identical reading age is late for one and current for another. - **GeoSphere aligns `data` to a union of timestamps** across every station in the request, with each station carrying a value at only its own index. Reading `data[0]` returns null for almost every station; measured live, 275 of 285 sat at the last index. The index is discovered per station. ## How I verified it - [x] `npm run build` — ✓ built in 7.12s - [x] `npm test` — 8354 + 1 + 14 tests, 0 failures, exit 0 - [ ] `npm run test:track` (dev server running) — not run; see note below - [x] Feature gate for the area I touched: `node scripts/qa-alpine-stations.mjs` — **58/58 checks passed** against the three live upstreams Also green: `npm run format:check`, `npm run i18n` (es and ru complete), `scripts/check-package-boundaries.mjs`, `scripts/check-import-directions.mjs`, `npm run layer-token:check` (31 published, 0 new), `npm run changelog:check`. The browser gate drives the real app and checks the things unit tests cannot see: that `/api/alpine-stations` is actually mounted rather than answered by the SPA fallback, that a measurement change recolours rather than rebuilds, that wind arrows carry real screen rotations and re-aim on camera turn without rebuilding geometry, and that every operator is credited on the globe and in the lightbox. ## New layer checklist **Screenshots** The layer and its WEATHER rail card over the Alps. Snow depth. Coverage is uneven by nature — only 175 of ~650 stations carry a snow sensor — so the quiet markers are stations reporting something else. Temperature, recoloured in place: the same 653 entities, not a rebuild. **Recording** 38 seconds: turn the layer on from the data-layers panel, fly into the Swiss Alps and across to Austria, step through all five measurements, then open a station record from the nearest-stations list (Platthorn, 3345 m). https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e63d4016-df98-411d-afa5-e0da39d75512 **Proposed category** Category: **Weather** It sits with the other atmospheric observation layers, and the card is in the WEATHER rail panel. **Data source and licence** All three are keyless, fetched at runtime, and redistributable; nothing is bundled. | | SLF IMIS | MeteoSwiss SwissMetNet | GeoSphere Austria TAWES | |---|---|---|---| | Provider | WSL Institute for Snow and Avalanche Research SLF | MeteoSwiss (Federal Office of Meteorology and Climatology) | GeoSphere Austria | | Endpoint | `measurement-api.slf.ch/public/api/imis/{stations,measurements}` | `data.geo.admin.ch` (`ogd-smn_meta_stations.csv`, `VQHA80.csv`) | `dataset.api.hub.geosphere.at/v1/station/current/tawes-v1-10min` | | Licence | [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/) | [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/) | [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/) | | Attribution in app | "WSL Institute for Snow and Avalanche Research SLF" | "MeteoSwiss" | "GeoSphere Austria" | | Key | none | none | none | | Publishes | snow, wind, temperature | wind, temperature, precipitation, pressure (QFF) | snow, wind, temperature, precipitation | CC BY requires the credit to be visible where the work is, so the operators are named **on the globe** while the layer is on, not only in the attribution lightbox — SLF in full and linked, as its terms ask. Both are asserted by the browser gate. - [x] Added a row to `DATA_SOURCES.md` - [x] Credit is registered in `src/data/dataCredits.js` - [ ] Share-link token assigned with `npm run layer-token:next`, if the layer is shareable — **deliberately not done**, per point 5 of the review: the namespace is yours to allocate (#658). ## Docs - [x] `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md` updated; the changelog entry is a `changelog.d/` fragment (this repo replaced `CHANGELOG.md` with fragments since #58 was opened) `docs/ALPINE-STATIONS.md` carries the design: the registration points, which modules may load the translation catalogs, the traps each network sets, and how to add a fourth network. --- ### Notes for the reviewer - **`npm run test:track` has not been run.** It needs a dev server and is a tracking-regression gate unrelated to this layer; say the word and I will run it. - **#759 (user-layer discovery) has not landed**, so this registers in the tracked files the current code expects, as the review's fallback assumed. - **The Spanish and Russian strings are machine-written and have not been reviewed by a translator.** 53 new entries. Everything user-facing goes through `t()`/`msg()` and the i18n gate reports both locales complete, but the wording deserves a native eye. - **Snow depth is floored at zero, and it is the one reading that is not relayed as published.** An ultrasonic head ranges to the snow surface from a fixed mount, so a bare station drifts either side of its calibrated ground reference — Dornbirn (TAWES) published −1.0 cm during testing and the card read "Snow depth across the network: −1 to 66 cm". Below zero the sensor is reading its own baseline rather than a snowpack, so `alpineStationRecord` floors it. An absent snow reading is untouched: no sensor is still no sensor, not bare ground. Say the word if you would rather see the raw value.

title: feat(ui): Google Earth-style on-screen navigation control
body:
## What this changes

Adds a Google Earth-style on-screen navigation control at the bottom right of the globe: a compass ring (shows heading, drag to turn, arrow keys turn, Home returns to north, north-up button), a tilt slider with up/down and top-down buttons, zoom in/out with press-and-hold repeat, and a four-way look-around pad. It reuses `readCameraTargetFrame` / `setCameraTargetFrame` and goes through the navigation policy, so it declines while the Cockpit owns the camera and preserves follow ownership.

- Built as a Vue view (`src/ui/views/panels/NavControl.vue`, `NavControlButton.vue`, using the kit's `UiButton` and `UiSlider`) over a Pinia store (`src/ui/stores/navControl.js`). A framework-free owner in `src/ui/navControl/` holds the camera and frame subscriptions and answers the view's actions through the store; it writes no DOM.
- A compass drag asks the navigation policy again on every move. If the policy refuses (for example the Cockpit takes the camera mid-drag), the drag ends and only a new press starts another. This fixes the bypass @kvnloo found in review; the regression test covers an allowed move, a mid-drag refusal and no resume.
- The navigation control is excluded from the side-rail edge wheel handler so scrolling over the compass does not switch panels.
- The exact tilt is read once the camera has been still for 1.5 s, not on every `moveEnd`, so the tilt handle can lag the camera by up to 1.5 s after a move.
- A centre pick outside a plausible surface band (below -1,500 m or above 25,000 m) is not trusted as the orbit target.
- Look-around buttons are disabled while an entity is tracked; the control is hidden in Cockpit, Scene playback, recording and Clean UI.
- UI text goes through `t()` / `msg()`; all 13 locale catalogs are filled in.
- The owner reaches the camera only through the renderer contract: the camera, frame and query ports (`findCamera`, `findFrame`, `findQuery`, `canvasOf`), `followed.js` for what the camera follows, `heightsOf` for the clearance height and `geo` for the orbit maths, the same way `cameraOrientationControls.js` does. It imports nothing from Cesium and passes the `noCesiumOutsideRender`, `viewerAccess` and heights-service guards.

## How I verified it

Head `15693b6a38a6e22d0687c9a6c28b9680d9529a7a`, rebased onto upstream `main` `d9d79ebc4da7379a1359947d23543b72757221bb`. Locale catalogs keep every upstream key and add the navigation keys. The package-boundary list keeps the upstream and navigation entries. The mobile shell keeps the upstream Missions panel and the view switcher. The navigation owner moved onto the renderer ports because upstream now gives the shell its scene object rather than the Cesium viewer. Its behaviour is unchanged, and a new test mounts the control on that scene object. Linux, Node 26.12.1.

- [x] `npm test -- --test-concurrency=4`: 15,988 tests, 15,983 passed, 0 failed, 5 skipped; allocation probes 1/1 and 14/14. Upstream `main` at the same base, same machine: 15,917 tests, 15,912 passed, 0 failed, 5 skipped. An earlier run at this head had one failure, the 400 ms wall-clock budget in `analystEngine.test.mjs` ("ranking 250k rows", 479 ms). This PR does not touch that file. The load average was 36–43 at the time, and the test passed on the rerun.
- [x] Focused tests, all 59 files touching the navigation control, shells, rail, i18n, package boundaries and the six renderer guards (`noCesiumOutsideRender`, `viewerAccess`, `heights`, `inputOwnership`, `internals`, `ui/kit viewControls`): 1,062 passed, 0 failed. Navigation control suite: 28/28.
- [x] `format:check`, `check:boundaries`, `layer-token:check` against the base (39 published, 0 new), `i18n` (13/13 complete), `changelog:check`, `git diff --check` and `build`: passed.
- Feature gate for the area I touched: none applies (no `scripts/qa-*.mjs` covers the navigation control).

**Browser check at this head:** local Vite dev server in headless Chromium with SwiftShader (software GL) at 1280×800, 2026-11-21, near the UT Tower in Austin. Real pointer clicks and drags:
- Zoom in: height went from 193 m to 189 m.
- Tilt up: pitch went from −68.75° to −58.75°, and the slider moved from 20 to 30.
- A quarter-turn drag on the compass ring: heading went from 0° to 270°.
- North: heading back to 0°.
- TOP: pitch −89°, slider 0.
- Page errors: 0.

The crops are 320×240 pixels.

![Navigation control at the start](https://github.com/Byrd-IT/gods-eye-view-upstream/releases/download/pr1312-evidence-15693b6a/pr1312-15693b6a-nav-start-crop.png) ![After the compass-ring drag](https://github.com/Byrd-IT/gods-eye-view-upstream/releases/download/pr1312-evidence-15693b6a/pr1312-15693b6a-nav-rotated-crop.png) ![After TOP](https://github.com/Byrd-IT/gods-eye-view-upstream/releases/download/pr1312-evidence-15693b6a/pr1312-15693b6a-nav-top-down-crop.png)

Full frame after the ring drag: [pr1312-15693b6a-nav-rotated-full.png](https://github.com/Byrd-IT/gods-eye-view-upstream/releases/download/pr1312-evidence-15693b6a/pr1312-15693b6a-nav-rotated-full.png)

**Not tested in this run:** real GPU performance, touch devices, the look-around pad and press-and-hold repeat in the browser (unit tests only), `test:track`, and the orbit target over Google photorealistic 3D tiles.

## Docs

- [x] `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md` has an "On-screen navigation control" section and `changelog.d/1312-navigation-control.md` is added

No server code, no new dependencies, no new network requests. This change was prepared with AI assistance and reviewed before submission.

## What this changes

Clean view (V / Display > Clean UI) left phones with little map: the HUD stayed on top, the EXIT CLEAN VIEW pill took the top centre and the credit line ran off the screen. title: feat(cctv): location-only cameras when no public picture exists
body:
## What this changes

Some published cameras have no public picture (for example a TxDOT district whose images are only on another operator's site); today they show an endless "upstream unavailable" placeholder. The CCTV proxy now learns from real upstream answers which cameras have none and serves them as location-only (`feedType: 'none'`).

- **Per camera:** two consecutive failed frame fetches mark it; any success clears it; a mark expires after 24 h. If the failure that makes the second strike looks temporary (HTTP 5xx, 408, 429, a timeout or a network error), the camera gets only a 10-minute in-memory retry window (never persisted) instead of the 24 h mark: afterwards `/sources` advertises the picture again, and one more failed retry re-opens the window (at most one extra request per window). A 4xx other than 408/429, or a 200 that is not an image, still makes the 24 h mark. Only still-image cameras are learned from: a camera whose feed is HLS, MP4, WebM or MJPEG is never marked, because a failed optional `snapshotUrl` preview says nothing about its live video (kvnloo's review).
- **Per TxDOT district:** up to three evenly spaced cameras are probed one at a time; one all-fail probe only makes the district *suspect* (re-probed after 10 min), a second consecutive all-fail makes it location-only for 6 h.
- State persists in `.gev-cache/cctv-feed-availability.json` (camera ids and timestamps only).
- **Browser:** a location-only camera keeps its icon and position but gets no ambient or hover card, no projection and no frame fetch; its status reads "no public feed".

New: `server/providers/cctv/feedAvailability.js` (pure state + small JSON persistence, no HTTP), wired into `server/providers/cctv.js`; one `isNoFeedType()` check in the CCTV model for cards, hover, presentation and projection.

## How I verified it

Current rebased head `350171e5abe87c5227c7999cb03eed592be817c6` on upstream `cd144ecad595dfe26b4d805323ae98a31835d415`: CCTV-focused tests 622 passed, 0 failed; format, i18n and import-boundary checks passed. The full unit run had 15,159 passes, 6 failures and 4 skips; all six failing test names and error types reproduced on the unchanged upstream base under the same local isolated setup. Configured independent review approved this exact head. GitHub reported no checks at the time of verification, so CI start is unconfirmed.

The following verification results are historical and apply only to the earlier head identified below, not the current head.

Head `c26dcdc9e30e4f23ec2492f5fc0b3ed581f0b4e3`, on upstream `main` 188f0ccd (contributor commits only; 0 commits behind when checked on 2026-11-13). Linux, Node 26.12.1 (a supported engine), scrubbed environment for the screenshot server (no `.env`, no personal keys), headless Chromium with ANGLE/SwiftShader. **That is software WebGL: no GPU was available**, so frame times say nothing about GPU performance.

- [x] `npm run build`: pass
- [x] `npm test` on this head: 12802 tests, 12798 pass, 0 fail, 0 cancelled, 4 skipped. An earlier run of the same head under heavy host load (load average about 60 to 75) had 3 timing failures (isolated KML deadline, tool-string bounds, RTL-SDR card); the re-run on the same head, with nothing changed, passed them.
- [x] `npm run test:track` (dev server, keyless): 111 of 111 pass on this head.
- [ ] Feature gate `node scripts/qa-cctv-v2.mjs` on this head: 45 passed, 3 failed, 5 inconclusive. The same 3 fail identically on unmodified upstream `main` 188f0ccd (45 passed, 3 failed, 5 inconclusive): the terrain-globe DEM height check and two real true-empty canvas-click checks; the 5 inconclusive need a real GPU (east-arrow drag).
- New regression tests for the review fix: `src/data/cctvTransientFrameFailure.test.mjs` has 4 mounted-route cases (HLS, MP4, WebM, MJPEG) in which two 404s on an optional still preview must leave `/sources` and `/stream` reporting the live feed type; on the previous head `a6b17b13` all 4 fail and the other 9 in the file pass; on this head all 13 pass. Together with `feedAvailability.test.mjs` and `frameOutcome.test.mjs` they cover the still-camera, 503, 404, non-image, world-camera and TxDOT behavior, which is unchanged.

Also run on this head: `npm run doctor -- --json`, `format:check`, `check:boundaries`, `layer-token:check -- --base-ref upstream/main` (39 published, 0 new), `npm run i18n` (complete) and `npm run changelog:check`: all exit 0. The hosted CI workflow for this head is `action_required` (waiting for maintainer approval), so there is no hosted CI result.

**Current-head preview** (head `350171e5abe87c5227c7999cb03eed592be817c6`; local keyless preview, headless browser). The camera-source response was intercepted in the browser and Austin camera entries were assigned `feedType: none` to illustrate the location-only UI. The image shows the NO PUBLIC FEED badge and a blank preview, not actual availability at that camera and not a live test of expiration or upstream failures. The panel also displays `Upstream snapshot active`; this screenshot does not validate that separate status text.

![CCTV location-only presentation with browser-provided fixture](https://github.com/Byrd-IT/gods-eye-view-upstream/releases/download/pr1314-evidence-350171e5/pr1314-location-only.png)

## Review follow-up (radianx, #1163 compatibility)

The review found that two HTTP 503 answers were recorded as "no public feed" for 24 h. That is addressed in `433da209` and `1095a93e`, as described under *Per camera* above: a temporary failure is now a 10-minute retry window, not a 24 h mark. Still open: the TxDOT per-district probe is unchanged, and the source-text assertions in `feedAvailability.test.mjs` (`isNoFeedType(` in the client files) have not been reconciled with #1163's `noFeed` wiring, which the review reproduced only in its own local integration. I did not combine this branch with #1163.

title: feat(keys): keep the Cesium ion and Mapillary tokens on the server
body:

title: feat(water): nationwide USGS water levels from the Water Data OGC API
body:
## What this changes

Adds nationwide USGS water levels: three layers in a new **Water** group of the Layers panel show the newest reading at every active USGS stream, lake/reservoir and spring gauge (about 10,100 streams with gage height and discharge, about 720 lakes/reservoirs, about 45 springs; counts from a live run on 2026-10-21). Related to #1072 (a San Antonio-area USGS layer on the same API); this one covers the whole country, refreshes on the server hourly and loads streams by viewport tile. Happy to reconcile in either direction.

- **Server** (`server/providers/usgsWater.js`, routes under `/api/usgs-water/`): once an hour (single flight) it queries the Water Data OGC API `latest-continuous` collection, one site type per request, readings from the last 7 days; serves a manifest, one GeoJSONL file per class and 4-degree stream tiles. A stale hour keeps serving while a background refresh runs; a failed refresh is not retried for 5 minutes; with no data and USGS down the route answers 503 with `Retry-After`. Site names come from `monitoring-locations` and are cached 7 days. Keyless, the server stays under USGS's 50 requests/IP/hour (it uses at most 40); optional `USGS_WATER_API_KEY` raises USGS's limit to 1000 and the server's ceiling to 800 and is sent only as the `X-Api-Key` header.
- **Browser** (`src/layers/usgsWater/`): streams load only the tiles in view and reload when the camera settles; wider than 24 degrees (or over 40 tiles) the layer loads nothing and asks the user to zoom in. `localGeojsonCore.js` gains `reload()`, an optional `cardDetails` hook, `refreshCards()` and a `cacheLoadedFeatures` option (default on; the water layers turn it off so a loader's result is not cached across enables); the loader is called as `loadFeatures({ signal, viewer })`, which is upstream's `loadFeatures({ signal })` contract plus `viewer`. Since upstream made `localGeojsonCore.js` renderer-agnostic, the water layer reads the view through the renderer's camera port (`viewRectangle()`, `on('moveEnd')`) and imports no Cesium; the card hooks sit in upstream's `buildDrawn()`. Existing layers, including the Data Library, are unchanged.
- **Card language**: the gauge card text (reading names, numbers, observation time) follows the app language. The application hands the translator, the formatters and a language-change subscription to the layers as `services.i18n` (`src/app/localGeojsonServices.js`); on a language switch an enabled water layer words its cards again from the gauges it already holds, with no new request. Station names and unit symbols are not translated. The standalone infrastructure package bundles no translator or catalogs; without `services.i18n` the cards are English.
- Share tokens `03` (streams, `local-usgs-water`), `04` (lakes, `local-usgs-lakes`) and `05` (springs, `local-usgs-springs`). Upstream published `9`, `00`, `01` and `02` (Rail) for other layers; preview links using older water tokens need regeneration. Current PR head: `4107980430cd20ac6b4c5ea7e2393646d7544172`. These assignments remain provisional until merge. The coordination proposal in #1592 is under discussion; an updated patch has been offered there.

Current head `4107980430cd20ac6b4c5ea7e2393646d7544172` (2026-11-21) rebases the previous head `dc34de37134c79ebd5fc7e62570cc3b30c94fcbc` onto upstream `main` `e4caf5d3afcb40041cfa6b167b4fda7bb9b393c5`. All 29 PR commits are kept. Locale conflicts in the 13 catalogs keep every upstream translation and add the water strings (collision-checked, 0 collisions); zh-Hant is regenerated with `npm run i18n -- --zh-hant`. Four commits adapt the PR to upstream's renderer-agnostic local layer core: `reload()` drops drawn sets through upstream's `releaseDrawn()`; the water layer uses the camera port and `inputFor` instead of Cesium; test fixtures use the renderer-free `fromDegrees`; the voice schema pin is refreshed. One test-only commit updates upstream's new credit-markup test to this PR's extended USGS credit text. On this head, Linux, Node 26.12.1, isolated `TMPDIR`: the full unit suite (1,334 test files in parallel, then the allocation groups serially) passed 15,959 tests with 0 failures and 5 skipped, plus allocation groups of 1 and 14 tests (all passed); `npm run build`, `format:check`, `check:boundaries`, `i18n -- --check` (13 catalogs, 4,130 messages each), `changelog:check` and `layer-token:check -- --base-ref e4caf5d3` (39 published, 3 new) passed. `qa-layer-panel`, `qa-layer-visibility` and `test:track` were not re-run on this head.

The upstream "GEV Stories" announcement was dismissed in the English and Arabic captures; in the German capture it stayed open in the upper right and does not cover the gauge card.

title: Harden provider response handling and camera source validation
body:
API routes now share the same response protections, provider responses are checked against the format each route expects, and camera sources are pinned by parsed URL.

- Every `/api` response carries `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'; sandbox` and `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, in dev and preview. The headers are applied before the host check and the providers, and matched the way the router mounts paths. The app document keeps its existing policy.
- Camera snapshots and the Street View fallback accept only raster images (JPEG, PNG, GIF, WebP, AVIF). Live camera feeds must match their declared kind (MP4, WebM, MJPEG) before they are relayed, and media redirects stay on the source's own host.
- Camera routes refuse cross-site browser requests and stay reachable behind a reverse proxy. A proxied request is served the placeholder rather than the Street View fallback.
- Camera URL pins (TfL, Caltrans, Tallinn, Tarktee, Warendorf, NSW, Calgary, Hong Kong, King County, WSDOT) compare the parsed origin and normalized path instead of a string prefix, and redirect targets are checked the same way.
- The bike-share proxy returns parsed and re-serialized JSON.

Validation: full unit suite (8,230 passed, 0 failed), build, formatting, package boundaries, setup doctor; header matrix on dev and preview servers, including case, `.`-boundary and absolute-form targets; CCTV browser gate (same result as main).

title: feat(safespot): SafeSpot evaluation lab with honest fleet coverage
body:
## Summary

Adds the **SafeSpotSG Evaluation Lab** layer (corridor diff, pickup simulation, wearable telemetry, HD map, scorecard) with its server providers, training script and QA scripts, and reworks the autonomous fleet coverage engine so "100% of Singapore's road network covered" is earned by driving rather than declared.

### Fleet engine (`server/providers/safespot-fleet-engine.js`)
- The server owns a simulated clock. Each `/api/safespot/fleet-sim?speed=N` call advances every vehicle by wall time × N (wall dt capped at 15 s per call).
- A directed edge counts as covered only once a vehicle has driven it end to end. Nothing is marked at planning time.
- Routes are contiguous and legal: vehicles steer greedily onto uncovered edges; when none is legally reachable from their junction, an edge-state A* honouring turn restrictions, one-way carriageways and the bus no-motorway rule routes them to the nearest free reachable edge (spatial grid picks the aim point).
- Relocations (teleports) happen only for edges unreachable from the network core (about 500 of 228k on the real graph, plus dead ends), are counted in `coverage.relocations`, and charge a 90 s redeploy dwell.
- The instant-100% sweep and the `sweepEdges` / `sweepTo100` parameters are removed. The tray chip is now `⚡ SIM SPEED (Nx)` and only cycles 1x / 10x / 50x / 200x.
- The client animates with the true multiplier and syncs to the server's position on every poll instead of looping over driven edges.
- Four `only_*` turn restrictions whose mandated exit way does not exist at the junction are dropped at load as unsatisfiable data.

## Test plan
- [x] `node --test server/providers/safespot-fleet-engine.test.mjs` (4 new tests: no coverage without sim time, cover-on-drive-through, 100% by driving on the fallback ring, turn restrictions obeyed with relocations reported)
- [x] `node --test src/layers/safespot/index.test.mjs` updated for the new semantics
- [x] `node scripts/qa-safespot-fleet.mjs` on the real Singapore graph: 100% after 17.7 simulated hours (about 5 wall-minutes at 200x), 0 discontinuous or forbidden tracks, 636 counted relocations, mean 245 ms per step
- [x] i18n catalog and package-boundary checks pass
- [x] Layer enabled in the app against a local dev server: polling uses the new `speed` parameter and coverage advances only with elapsed time
- Full `npm test`: two unrelated failures on this Windows machine (a CCTV idle-deadline test that passes in isolation, and a Pinokio launcher temp-dir `ENOTEMPTY` race)

title: feat(cctv): vendor the Bosch MIC PTZ records the Amsterdam register names
body:
## What

Adds three Bosch MIC PTZ datasheet records to `src/layers/cctv/modelSpecs.js`, so the City of Amsterdam camera register's hardware resolves once that pack passes its `model` through (#251):

| Register `model` | Rows | Resolves to |
|---|---|---|
| `Bosch MIC-7522-Z30x` | 93 | MIC-7522-Z30B |
| `Bosch MIC-7502-Z30x` | 5 | MIC-7502-Z30B |
| `Bosch MIC-7130-Px4` | 1 | MIC-7130-PB4 (MIC IP starlight 7000 HD) |

Bosch MIC order codes end in a colour letter (B black, G grey, W white) on one shared datasheet. The G/W siblings, and the `x` the register writes for the colour letter, are aliases of the one vendored record. The register's CSG ANPR units are not in the table and stay unresolved: unknown never implies anything.

The MIC datasheets state FOV ("2.1° to 58.3°") without an axis, so these records add the HUD spec line but no horizontal FOV range. The frustum keeps its estimate, consistent with how the module already treats PTZ hardware.

## Data

Records are verbatim from the [CCTV Camera Database](https://github.com/ch-bas/cctv-camera-database) v2.29.0 model-enrichment extract (CC0-1.0). The 17 records already vendored are unchanged; they still match v2.29.0 exactly. The module header and `DATA_SOURCES.md` now give the current dataset size (29,000+ models, 76% with FOV).

title: perf: draw the globe in device pixels on high-DPI screens
body: Closes #1307 (proposal and numbers discussed there). Also fixes #905, which overlaps open PR #1017 (see below). ## Why `createApplicationViewer` uses Cesium's default `useBrowserRecommendedResolution: true`. Cesium then draws one pixel per CSS pixel (`pixelRatio = (useBrowserRecommendedResolution ? 1 : devicePixelRatio) * resolutionScale`). Cesium also sets `image-rendering: pixelated` on its canvas, so a 2x screen shows a pixel-doubled 1x frame. Cable lines, orbit lines, polygon edges and 3D tiles look stair-stepped on every Retina Mac. ## What changes - **`src/app/resolutionGovernor.js`** (new, no timers, no dependencies) sits above the renderer contract. It reads the quality port's `frame` signals and calls `quality.set({ pixelRatio, msaa })`. `src/app/scene.js` installs it on `renderer.quality`; a renderer without a `pixelRatio` knob draws as before. `useBrowserRecommendedResolution` stays on, as the port expects. - Policy: - Ratio ceiling = `min(devicePixelRatio, 2)`, at most a 3840 × 2160 drawing buffer (on a 0.25 grid), and at most `quality.device().maxTextureSize` on each side. Never below 1, unless the GPU limit cannot hold 1x. **DPR 1 screens draw exactly as before** wherever they rendered before. Every laptop screen gets its full 2x on common GPUs. A full-screen 5K window draws at 1.5. - MSAA 2 from ratio 1.5 up, MSAA 4 below. Ratio² × samples never falls below the old 4 coverage samples per CSS pixel. - Smoothed back-to-back frame interval over 20 ms for 2 s → step down 0.25. 8 s at or under 18 ms → step up. A failed step up doubles the wait (max 64 s). - Only `continuous` frame signals count (a moving camera or a held loop). `demand` frames and the first 5 s are skipped. It never requests a frame. - Under a frame-rate cap below 50 FPS (the lower of the frame and quality ports' `targetFps`) the cap sets the interval, so the budget follows it: 1.2 × the cap interval (40 ms at 30 FPS), on-time threshold scaled the same way. A step up while capped is a probe like any other: a slow one steps back down and doubles the wait. - Follows `devicePixelRatio` changes (other screen, browser zoom) and container resizes on each frame signal. - **`src/render/cesium/drawingBuffer.js`** (new) keeps the Cesium drawing buffer inside the GPU limit, whoever sets `resolutionScale`. It fits the scale in `cesiumWidget.resize()`, before Cesium sizes the canvas, and keeps the scale asked for so a window that shrinks gets it back. It keeps `pixelated` upscaling only at whole-number factors. - **Post stages** (sharpen, CRT, NVG, FLIR, Anime) size kernels, blocks and scanlines in CSS pixels via `czm_pixelRatio`, as Cesium's own blur/edge stages do. Each effect keeps its current look. - **Sensor-click** mapping (`src/input/sensorPick.js`) snaps on the same CSS-pixel grid as those shaders. - `?maxPixelRatio=1` restores the old drawing (1–3 accepted). `__godsEyeView.getResolutionDiagnostics()` reports state. - `scripts/qa-weather-perf.mjs` gains `--dpr` (default 2, as before). Tile detail is unchanged: Cesium divides screen-space error by `frameState.pixelRatio`, so no extra tiles load. ## Relation to #905 and #1017 Drawing at 2x makes Cesium's framebuffer limit easier to reach: a 1200 px window needs 2400 px. Cesium then throws `Width must be less than or equal to the maximum texture size` and stops rendering. So the governor bounds the ratio by the GPU limit, and that bound wins over the 1x floor. The Cesium guard also fits every resize, so a window grown past the limit is in bounds on its first frame. That also fixes #905: a 2560 px window on a 2048-limit GPU now draws at 0.8 instead of crashing. #1017 (VG31OP) fixes #905 by clamping `resolutionScale` and adding `requestedResolutionScale`. Both PRs edit `createApplicationViewer` and own `resolutionScale`, so they conflict. This PR keeps the clamp in the Cesium renderer, under the quality port: one owner for the scale. Whether #1017 is closed as superseded is the maintainers' call once this PR settles. Credit to VG31OP and djabhi31 (#940) for the diagnosis, and to VG31OP for the pre-resize case. Checked in Chrome with WebGL patched to report a 2048 limit: | Build | Window | Result | | --- | --- | --- | | main | 2560 × 1440 @1x | `DeveloperError: Width must be less than or equal to the maximum texture size (2048)`, rendering stops | | this PR | 2560 × 1440 @1x | 2048 × 1152 (ratio 0.8), renders | | this PR | 1200 × 800 @2x | 2048 × 1365 (ratio 1.71), renders | | this PR | 1900 × 1000 grown to 2560 × 1440 @1x after load | 2048 × 1152 (ratio 0.8), keeps rendering | ## Pictures (DPR 2, 1200 × 800 viewport, keyless globe; crops enlarged with nearest-neighbour) Submarine cables near Marseille, the real layer: A 2 px polyline and a Cesium label: Cesium labels and billboards keep CSS-size glyph textures, so Cesium-drawn text gains little. Lines, dots, polygons and tiles gain the most. The world overlay's own labels were already DPR-aware. Sharpen (on by default) at 2x. A 1-device-pixel kernel is visibly weaker than today's default, so the kernel is 1 CSS pixel: CRT keeps its block size: ## Performance (Apple M2 Max, Chrome 155, 1200 × 886 CSS viewport) Matched route (`qa-weather-perf --states off,wind`): every window on both builds at DPR 1 and 2 runs at the 60 Hz vsync ceiling (59.4–60 FPS; one main-DPR 1 window at 43.4 FPS during a wind-data load). Idle renders are identical, so the governor adds no frames. Uncapped frame time (vsync off; median of 3; mean / p95 ms): | Build | DPR | Drawing | MSAA | Globe | Close (1.2 km) | | --- | ---: | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | main | 1 | 1x | 4 | 3.09 / 5.7 | 3.65 / 6.3 | | branch | 1 | 1x | 4 | 3.56 / 5.9 | 3.16 / 4.7 | | branch (repeat) | 1 | 1x | 4 | 3.01 / 5.6 | 2.70 / 4.3 | | main (repeat) | 1 | 1x | 4 | 3.09 / 5.7 | 2.92 / 4.6 | | main | 2 | 1x | 4 | 3.17 / 6.0 | 3.80 / 6.1 | | **branch** | 2 | **2x** | **2** | **8.92 / 10.9** | **7.76 / 15.0** | | branch, forced | 2 | 2x | 4 | 11.70 / 20.9 | 9.32 / 14.6 | | branch, forced | 2 | 1.5x | 2 | 6.24 / 9.3 | 5.34 / 8.7 | DPR 1: within ±0.5 ms between repeats in both directions, so no regression. At 2x, MSAA 2 is 17–24% cheaper than MSAA 4. GPU-process memory (macOS `footprint`): | Build | DPR | CSS viewport | Drawing buffer | MSAA | GPU process | | --- | ---: | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | | main | 2 | 1200 × 886 | 1200 × 886 | 4 | 839 MB | | branch | 2 | 1200 × 886 | 2400 × 1772 | 2 | 1,353 MB | | branch, forced | 2 | 1200 × 886 | 2400 × 1772 | 4 | 1,472 MB | | main | 2 | 2560 × 1440 | 2560 × 1440 | 4 | 2,181 MB | | branch | 2 | 2560 × 1440 | 3840 × 2160 (budget) | 2 | 2,887 MB | About 150 bytes per extra drawn pixel. Without the 4K budget, the 5K window would add about 1.7 GB, not 0.7 GB. Governor under load (DPR 3, `?maxPixelRatio=3`, FLIR, constant motion): 2.25 → 1 in 19 s, held while frames stayed slow, back up to 1.75 once on time; 5 steps down and 3 up in 180 s. Full tables: `docs/PERFORMANCE.md`. ## Review findings Performance - [fixed] 2x with MSAA 4 costs +633 MB GPU memory and 11.7 ms/frame here → MSAA 2 from ratio 1.5 (−119 MB, −17–24% time). - [fixed] Large external displays at 2x would allocate ~150 B per drawn pixel without bound → 3840 × 2160 budget. - [fixed] Start-up loading frames (23–35 ms) could trigger a step down → 5 s warm-up. - [fixed] Short pans never added up to a recovery → windows count sampled frame time, not wall time. - [fixed] A frame time hovering at 20 ms never stepped → 18 ms on-time threshold (hysteresis). - [fixed] Fractional ratios with `image-rendering: pixelated` double uneven rows → `auto` at fractional factors. - [fixed] Style and sharpen shaders shrink to half size at 2x → CSS-pixel sizing via `czm_pixelRatio`. - [fixed] Transit sensor-click mapping assumed drawing-buffer = CSS pixels → CSS grid, plus a 2x test case. - [fixed] 2x could exceed the GPU texture limit and stop rendering (#905 class) → per-side clamp that overrides the floor. - [fixed] A window grown past the limit after load still threw, because the viewport was read in `postRender` → read in `cesiumWidget.resize()` (now `drawingBuffer.js`), with a unit test. - [fixed] The ambient 30 FPS cap in #1422 read as slow frames: 1x by 10 s with 4 steps down (M2 Max, DPR 2, parked camera, Military layer) → the budget follows the cap (40 ms at 30 FPS). The same setup holds 2x at 30 FPS with no steps. - [fixed] Skipping capped frames entirely (reported by quanticsoul4772) left a GPU that cannot hold 30 FPS at 2x stuck there until the camera moved → capped budget above. Blocking steps up while capped was tried and dropped: loading stalls on a parked view then cost resolution until the camera moved. With a 45 ms stall per frame for 10 s, a parked view steps to 1x within 10 s and is back at 2x by 55 s. - [fixed] main's renderer contract now owns `pixelRatio` and `msaa` through the quality port, and the viewer moved to `src/render/cesium/applicationViewer.js` → the governor drives the port and the texture guard sits on the Cesium side. kvnloo's regression test is rewritten as a scene test: a 2x screen must end with `pixelRatio: 2` through the port. - [checked] The new star sky (`src/sky/starrySky.js`) already sizes stars with `czm_pixelRatio`. - [checked] Idle cost: no timers, no render requests; `qa-perf` 24/24, idle renders unchanged at DPR 1 and 2. - [checked] 120 Hz ProMotion with `targetFrameRate = 60`: steady 60 FPS, smoothed peak 16.9 ms, so no false step. - [checked] Screenshots / `preserveDrawingBuffer`: the voice viewport capture already scales by `canvas.width` and downscales to a pixel budget; QA scripts that read pixels use `canvas.width / clientWidth` or run at DPR 1. - [open] Frame time cannot tell CPU from GPU cost: a CPU-bound scene also steps down, at worst to the old 1x. The port's `gpuMs` signal could separate them where the context has a timer; not used yet (not measurable here). - [open] Cesium labels/billboards stay CSS-resolution glyphs (needs per-layer font × 2 / scale 0.5; out of scope). - [open] Weak GPUs were simulated (high ratio, heavy style), not measured on low-end hardware. - [open] Displays at 30 Hz would sit at ratio 1 (the old behaviour); 50 Hz holds. - [open, pre-existing] The world overlay does not re-derive its backing store on a mid-session DPR change. Security - [checked] No new dependencies; `package.json` and lockfile unchanged. `npm audit` identical to main (1 high, `vite ≤ 6.4.3` via `launch-editor`, pre-existing). - [checked] No network calls, `eval`, dynamic `import()` or storage writes. The only input, `?maxPixelRatio`, is parsed as a number and clamped to 1–3. - [checked] `check:boundaries` passes; the new modules are listed in their package boundaries. Scope - [checked] Merged with `main` at 41c79220; no fork-only code. Runtime changes outside the new module are ~55 lines. - [open] Conflicts with open PR #1017 (same function, same `resolutionScale`); needs a maintainer call on which lands first. - [open] No DISPLAY-rail control: the app has no quality/performance setting today, so the cap is a URL flag. ## Validation - `npm run build` ✓ · `npm test` 15904 pass, 0 fail, 6 skip on the merge with 41c79220 - Chrome on the quality-port build: DPR 2 at 1200 × 800 draws 2400 × 1600 (MSAA 2); `?maxPixelRatio=1` draws 1x (MSAA 4); a 2048 limit with the window grown to 2560 × 1440 draws 2048 × 1152 and keeps rendering; a 30 ms stall per frame steps 2x to 1.25x, back to 2x about 26 s after it ends - `npm run test:track` 108/109 on this branch and on `main` 43e8bfd2 alike: the one failure is the existing timing check "arrival moveEnd observation exceeded 500 ms" (branch 554–687 ms, main 785 ms). It passed 109/109 on the earlier base 2da8ced6, so it is not caused by this change. - Feature gate `scripts/qa-perf.mjs` (render governor) 24/24 - `format:check`, `check:boundaries`, `i18n`, `layer-token:check --base-ref origin/main`, `changelog:check` ✓ - `qa-weather-perf --dpr 1|2` on both builds; uncapped frame-time and memory probes as above - Trial merge with #1422: two 60 s runs parked at DPR 2 with the Military layer on hold ratio 2 at 30 FPS, no steps - Allocation microbenchmarks skipped locally (Node 26; they need Node 24). CI runs them. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: chore: remove dead code across the repository
body:
Removes dead code across the repository in one pass. Package exports are unchanged.

## How the candidates were found

Knip was run with every real entry point declared: `src/main.js` (the Vite app), `build/*.js`, `vite.config.js`, `server/standalone/vite.config.js`, `server/mcp/stdio.js`, every `package.json` `exports` target (all 165, whose exports are treated as public API), `scripts/**` and `tools/**` (QA harnesses and builders are run directly), `pinokio/*.js`, the SDR worker, and every `*.test.mjs`. QA harnesses that load modules in the page (`await import('/src/...')`) were checked by the names they destructure. Every finding was then checked by hand with a repository-wide search, including namespace imports that are passed on as service objects. An ESLint `no-unused-vars` scan was repeated until it was stable.

## What was removed

**Files nobody imports (3)**
- `src/ui.js`: a `StyleManager` subclass that pre-selected the standalone catalog. Controls are built through `src/app/controls.js` and `src/standalone/controls.js`.
- `src/standalone/ui.js`: a bare re-export of `StyleManager`.
- `src/data/localLayers.js`: a list of default infrastructure, cable and FIRMS layer instances. The catalog builds these layers itself.

With `src/ui.js` gone, `scripts/check-import-directions.mjs` keeps a single compatibility exception (`server/providers/local.js` → `server/standalone/key-setup.js`), and its test now asserts that a `src/ui.js` importing standalone code is rejected. `docs/CODE-BOUNDARIES.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md`, `README.md`, `scripts/package-boundaries.json`, and `scripts/format-scope.json` are updated to match. Some code comments and test messages elsewhere still mention `ui.js` by name; they don't affect behavior and can be tidied separately.

**Exports nothing imports**
- 176 constants and helpers that are still used in their own module lose only `export`.
- Unused re-exports are removed from barrel modules (flight, military, vessel, CCTV, directions, transit history, local ADS-B, street-level policy, `src/data/radio.js`).
- Declarations nothing uses at all are deleted: `AIS_WATCHDOG_STATUSES`, `applyFilter`, `isRadioCountryCode`, `compactText`, `DENSITY_STOPS`, `GTFS_INCREMENTALITY_DIFFERENTIAL`, `PROJECTION_VERT_ASPECT`, the unused CCTV `SOURCE_ENDPOINT`/`HEALTH_ENDPOINT`, `MAX_VIEWPORT_DEGREES`, KartaView `SINCE_NOTE`, `FLOW_RENDER_RACE_MS`, `SDR_FM_BAND`, `SDR_ADSB_FREQUENCY_HZ`, 20 radio-method aliases in `src/data/radio.js`, and `FIX_HISTORY_MAX`, `DISPLAY_LAG_MIN_MS`, `DISPLAY_LAG_RESET_MS`, `FIX_NOISE_M`, `STOPPED_FIXES` and `courseBetween` in `src/layers/transit/movement.js`.
- Six default exports that nothing imports. The ones in `src/data/earthquakes.js`, `src/data/telegeographySubmarineCables.js`, `src/data/wind.js` and `src/data/bhoteKoshiLocator.js` each built a layer instance at import time that nothing used. The wind and Bhote Koshi modules are in the app graph, so the app no longer builds those two instances when it loads.
- Earlier commits on this branch: `CAMERA_PRESETS` and `flyToPreset`, module-local helpers nothing calls, and unused import specifiers.

**Data and assets (960,345 bytes)**
- `src/data/local_data/dams/dams.geojson` (730,321 bytes) held the same 704 features as `dams.geojsonl`, feature for feature. Only the JSONL file is loaded (`src/sources/infrastructureData.js`).
- `public/models/ship.glb` (230,024 bytes): no module, template, stylesheet or script names it. Its attribution row is removed from `public/models/README.md`.

**Unused local bindings**
- Runtime: the unread result of `enter()`/`exit()` in `src/ui/cockpitInput.js`, the unread entity from `entities.add()` in the launches renderer, and the unread map key in the radio horizon scan. Every call is kept.
- Earlier commit: side-effect-free locals in the flights, military, CCTV, vessel and ALPR modules.
- QA scripts, tools and tests: unused helpers, in-page imports, counters, destructured fields, source files read into variables no assertion uses, and redundant `StyleManager` imports.

**Dependencies:** none. Knip reports no unused dependency, and each one was checked against `src`, `server`, `scripts`, `tools`, `build`, `pinokio` and CI.

## What was kept on purpose
- Every export reachable from a `package.json` `exports` entry.
- `TOMTOM_CREDIT`: the traffic layer reads it from the credits namespace it is given, which static analysis cannot see.
- Exports that QA harnesses read in the page, every script under `scripts/` and `tools/`, and test fixtures.
- `config/cctv_sources.shinjuku.json`: nothing in the repository names it, but it is a source pack that can be selected with `CCTV_SOURCES_FILE`.
- The `_` loop counter in `src/tools/schema.js`, which counts iterations on purpose.
- The `configureWindSource` slot in `src/data/wind.js`, which `configureApplicationSources` still calls.
- The module-level layer in `src/data/bikeshare.js`, whose exported overlay-entry factory and test hooks are still used.

## Size
- 195 files changed, 256 insertions, 773 deletions; 5 files deleted (3 modules, 2 assets); 960,345 bytes of tracked data removed.
- Main bundle `dist/assets/index-*.js`: 3,702.31 kB (gzip 1,168.60 kB) on `main` → 3,701.80 kB (gzip 1,168.43 kB).

## Verification
- `npm run format:check`, `npm run check:boundaries`, `npm run i18n` (and `--prune`, which removes nothing), `npm run build`, `npm run build:panel` and `npm run changelog:check` pass.
- `npm test`: 8,276 of 8,278 pass. The one failure, `a cross-site page cannot fill the cache or spend the visitor quota` in `src/terrainHeightsBounds.test.mjs`, also fails on `main` when the checkout has a local terrain cache (`.gev-cache/terrain-heights.json`) from an earlier run; it passes in a clean checkout.
- `npm run test:track`: 108 passed, 1 failed. The failure is the 500 ms timing check `arrival: moveEnd + first reveal both re-aim before idle refresh`, which also fails on `main` (108/1 there too).
- After the changes, Knip reports no unused files or dependencies, and its only unused export is `TOMTOM_CREDIT` (kept, see above).

title: feat(display): add solar-driven night shading and city lights
body:
## Summary

At globe scale, add an optional night-side tint and city lights that follow Cesium's solar direction. A smooth twilight band follows the scene clock, and the effect fades out as the camera zooms in. The Display panel includes a persisted NIGHT LIGHTS toggle.

- Bundle NASA Black Marble's 2023 annual independent-lights visualization, with a 2016 VIIRS fallback and documented attribution, preparation, and memory budget.
- Apply GPU night shading through guarded Cesium 1.138 native imagery adapters for both the globe and Google 3D Tiles, keeping data imagery above the effect.
- Add regression coverage for twilight masking, dateline sampling, zoom fades, imagery ordering, preferences, and resource cleanup.

The lamp texture is a static annual visualization; the night mask changes with the sun direction. This is separate from the dated Black Marble/JPSS imagery product requested in #850.

## Validation

- `npm run format:check`
- `npm run check:boundaries`
- `npm run changelog:check`
- `npm run build`
- `npm run i18n` and `node --test src/i18n/catalog.test.mjs`: 14 passing
- `node --test src/nightLightsOverlay.test.mjs src/maps/nativeRasterImagery.test.mjs`: 26 passing
- Prior browser verification of the Display toggle, persisted preference, and keyless globe fallback

Local verification limitations:

- `npm test`: 8,304 tests, initially 8,290 passing, 11 skipped, and 3 failing. The missing zh-CN messages were fixed and all 14 catalog tests now pass. The other failures are in unchanged terrain request-count coverage (1 upstream call versus 2 expected) and the sky paint-out test (Windows resolves its asset path as `/C:/.../milkyway_px.webp`).
- `npm run test:track`: initialization, share restoration, voice context, jitter, switching, orphan cleanup, and tracked-plane click checks passed. The harness stopped during age-out checks with `Execution context was destroyed, most likely because of a navigation`; the full gate did not pass.

title: feat: a license gate the person accepts themselves, for data the app can't bundle
body:
### Problem

Hi @bilawalsidhu and @asturksever,

I'm opening this issue before any PR, to get your view on the shape. Our integration of GEV into Mnemosyne OS is still in a testing phase.

Several GEV sources have narrower terms than the MIT license of the code. Three examples:
- TeleGeography's cables (CC BY-NC-SA 3.0) are bundled with a carve-out. `DATA_SOURCES.md` asks commercial users to delete the folder.
- FL511 (#605) stays off behind `CCTV_FLORIDA_ENABLED=1`.
- WiGLE (#11) is waiting for your decision on its terms.

`DATA_SOURCES.md` names others, such as OpenSky and the Bhote Koshi flood path.

### Proposal

**What we built in our fork**

Our fork runs GEV as a Mnemosyne OS app (branch `mnemosyne-os`). We added a license window for the cables. It names the source, the license and the non-commercial use. The browser keeps the choice. If the browser can't read it back, the license counts as refused.

The window covers two paths today:
- the cables button in our bar;
- agents that go through Mnemosyne OS. An agent can't accept on the person's behalf. When it asks for the cables, the window opens and the agent gets a sentence to tell the person. It can always turn the layer off.

GEV's layer panel and its voice assistant still turn the cables on without the window. Our code sits next to GEV and leaves the layer itself untouched. An upstream version should put the gate where the layer turns on.

- The choice: https://github.com/Mnemosyne-OS/gods-eye-view/blob/1f247e8c9af7a9808ba3cee6ddf2b56368651976/src/mnemo/cableLicence.js
- The agent rule: https://github.com/Mnemosyne-OS/gods-eye-view/blob/1f247e8c9af7a9808ba3cee6ddf2b56368651976/src/mnemo/mnemoBridge.js#L290-L295 and https://github.com/Mnemosyne-OS/gods-eye-view/blob/1f247e8c9af7a9808ba3cee6ddf2b56368651976/src/mnemo/mnemoBridge.js#L417-L453

In our fork too, the cables stay in the bundle. The window adds the person's consent. Redistribution stays as it is.

**The same idea in three other modules**

Here we go further. The data stays out of the bundle. The person reads the license, clicks, and their computer downloads from the official source.

- MnemoClio shows historical borders from `historical-basemaps` (A. Ourednik, GPL-3.0). Each map weighs 1 to 3 MB. The person's computer downloads it from GitHub when they look at it. https://github.com/Mnemosyne-OS/MnemoClio/blob/main/src/data/era.ts
- MnemoLaw reads the LOCUS corpus of US local ordinances (UC Berkeley, CC BY-NC 4.0, 1.77 GB on Hugging Face). The person picks their city. Their computer reads only the parts of the file for that city, 35 to 51 MB. https://github.com/Mnemosyne-OS/MnemoLaw/blob/main/src/locus/locusReader.ts
- For our image engine, the person accepts a restricted model's terms on its Hugging Face page, with their own account. The weights come from the publisher's repository.

**What this solves, and what it doesn't**

The "download on click" version solves three things:
- The project stops redistributing data it has no right to redistribute. `CONTRIBUTING.md` already asks for that.
- The person reads the license before seeing the data.
- Consent stays the person's gesture, never an agent's.

It doesn't solve a public deployment. For FL511 and WiGLE, the operator of a hosted instance serves the data to other people, and a user's click changes nothing there. Server configuration stays the right gate. The window serves the local install.

An NC license stays NC after the click. The window tells the person so. It gives them no commercial right.

**What I propose to deliver, in small PRs**

1. A "license pack" contract. It carries an id, the license name, the source and terms URLs, and an accepted or refused state. The browser keeps it. A layer declares the pack it needs.
2. The gate placed where a layer turns on. The panel, the voice assistant, the MCP tools and a shared link then all go through it.
3. One license window for every pack, in the app's languages.
4. The agent rule. An agent that turns on a layer under a pack opens the window and gets an answer meant for the person.
5. Optionally, TeleGeography's cables downloaded on click, from the official address `source.json` already names. On October 23 it answered with 733 cables and 1,928 landing points, updated on October 21. The bundle holds 712 and 1,917, downloaded on May 24. The address sends no CORS header, so GEV's local server would make the request.

If you'd prefer another shape, or only one of these points, say so and I'll adapt.

### Data source, license, and attribution

**The cables license, to confirm with TeleGeography**

While looking for a stable address for the cables, I read what TeleGeography publishes today:
- Its license page puts its maps and screen captures under CC BY-SA 4.0. For the data behind the maps, it points to a paid data license. https://www2.telegeography.com/license-telegeography-map
- That page doesn't name the `api/v3` addresses the GeoJSON comes from. The folder's `source.json` already says it: check TeleGeography's terms.
- I couldn't find where the CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 in `DATA_SOURCES.md` comes from. TeleGeography deleted its old GitHub repository in 2022.

A question to info@telegeography.com would tell which terms cover those addresses. I can send it if you'd like.

**Sources missing from DATA_SOURCES.md, which we read for our climate module**

GDACS is already proposed in #857, so I'm leaving it out.

- NOAA NCEI IBTrACS gives cyclone tracks for the whole globe. The last-three-years file weighs 11.6 MB. It would complement NHC/CPHC, which covers the Atlantic and the eastern and central North Pacific. Its NCEI record has no license field. Downloads are free, and NOAA asks users to cite two references: Gahtan et al. 2024 (doi:10.25921/82ty-9e16) and Knapp et al. 2010. https://www.ncei.noaa.gov/data/international-best-track-archive-for-climate-stewardship-ibtracs/v04r01/access/csv/
- NOAA OISST 2.1, through ERDDAP, gives the daily sea surface temperature anomaly. The final version arrives about two weeks after the preliminary data. The ERDDAP notice allows free use and redistribution. https://coastwatch.pfeg.noaa.gov/erddap/griddap/ncdcOisst21Agg_LonPM180.html
- NASA EONET v3 lists ongoing natural events, with no key. EONET shows no license. NASA's data policy (Earthdata) puts data from NASA missions under CC0, and refers to the source's terms for the rest. 27 of EONET's 33 sources come from elsewhere: JTWC, IRWIN, GDACS, InciWeb… Each event names its source and link in the `sources` field, so attribution can follow the event. https://eonet.gsfc.nasa.gov/api/v3/events
- FEWS NET serves food insecurity IPC phases through an API. Its policy names no license. It allows API use and asks for the attribution given in each dataset's metadata. It forbids implying that FEWS NET endorses your use. Third-party data may need the original provider's consent. Contact: data.policy@fews.net. https://fdw.fews.net/api/ipcphase/

Tony

### Will you build it?

Yes, I plan to open a PR

title: feat(street-level): provider exports and a Mapillary Graph endpoint for hosts
body:
Two small additions that let a host compose Street Level without putting a Mapillary client token in the page.

**1. Export the KartaView and Panoramax providers** as `./layers/street-level/kartaview` and `./layers/street-level/panoramax`, next to the existing Mapillary and Google exports. `createApplicationStreetLevel` takes an explicit `providers` list, but KartaView and Panoramax were reachable only through the default list, which (by design) is empty without a Mapillary source.

**2. Let a Mapillary source name a Graph endpoint.** A source may provide `graphEndpoint`, a Graph API base that adds the token itself (for example a same-origin proxy). When it does, the source's sequence lookups go there through its own transport, and the photo viewer uses MapillaryJS's stock `GraphDataProvider({ endpoint })` with no client token. Without `graphEndpoint`, everything behaves exactly as before (`accessToken: source.token`).

Defaults and existing behavior are unchanged.

**Verification:** new tests import the three non-Mapillary providers through the package exports, and cover the viewer and source with and without `graphEndpoint`. `npm test` (8,299 pass), `npm run format:check`, `npm run check:boundaries`, `npm run changelog:check` and `npm run build` pass. Checked in a browser against the live Mapillary Graph API through a same-origin endpoint: coverage, sequence cones and the photo viewer all load, with no token in any page request.

title: feat(ui): phone layout with a bottom tab bar and one panel sheet at a time
body:
A phone layout for viewports 720px and narrower. Today every panel stacks over the globe on a phone; this keeps the globe full screen and moves the panels behind a bottom tab bar, one sheet at a time.

## What it does
- **Tab bar:** Layers (Data Layers, with Scenes below), Cameras (CCTV and Street Level), Context (Global Context, plus Weather and Recent Imagery when shown), Search (Location) and More (Visual Presets and Map Source above Display).
- **One sheet at a time:** a tab opens its sheet; the same tab, the backdrop or Escape closes it. Focus moves into the sheet and back to its tab, and tabs expose `aria-expanded`.
- **Panels stay where they are in the DOM.** `styles/mobile-shell.css` presents the rails and the dock as the sheet, and the dock's Location and Presets trays render inline.
- **Sheets borrow panels:** opening one expands its panels without persisting them or treating it as the user's choice; share links keep each borrowed panel's earlier state; closing puts back what opening changed, while a panel the user changed inside the sheet stays as they left it.
- **Voice** floats above the tab bar while no sheet is open. **Attribution** (Cesium, Google, data credits) stays visible above the voice control and above any open sheet.
- **Modes:** Cockpit, recording and clean view close the sheet and hide the tab bar. Scene playback keeps both, so STOP in the Scenes panel stays reachable on a phone.
- **Safe areas:** the page draws under the notch and system bars (`viewport-fit=cover`), and the phone chrome uses safe-area insets and dynamic viewport units.
- Wider viewports are unchanged, and crossing to them closes any open sheet.

## Deliberate behavior changes at 720px and narrower
- The right rail no longer hides collapsed siblings, and Cyber's one-panel accordion does not apply, since a sheet (for example Cameras) shows several rail panels at once. `src/ui/panelRails.test.mjs` is updated accordingly: desktop keeps the accordion, and a new test covers phones.
- While a sheet is open, a panel's own Escape collapse and the dock trays' hover auto-close step aside for the sheet.
- The exclusive-surface class list moves to `src/exclusiveSurfaces.js` (re-exported unchanged by `firstRunExperience.js`) so first run and the phone shell share it.

## QA harnesses
`qa-camera-controls`, `qa-scene-controls` and `qa-map-source-tray` open the matching tab before their phone-width checks (from the keyboard where they check focus rings), wait for the shell to follow viewport changes, and run the pin and compact-wing checks at 800px, where the narrow desktop dock still exists.

## Verification
- `npm test` (8,293 pass), `npm run format:check`, `npm run check:boundaries`, `npm run i18n` (es, ru and zh-CN labels added), `npm run changelog:check`, `npm run build`, `npm run build:panel`.
- `npm run test:track`: 109 pass.
- Phone-width QA harnesses compared against `main`: no new failures; `qa-map-source-tray` passes all 82 checks.
- Checked in a mobile-emulated browser at 390×844 and 412×915 (portrait), including Tactical and Cyber HUDs, the Minimal HUD credit, Search, share links while a sheet is open, and Escape.

Adapted from the phone tab-shell proposed in #203 by @blearymoth — thank you for the original approach.

title: perf(terrain): evict from the front of the point cache instead of sorting it
body:
Follow-up to #975 / #686, from @asturksever's review on #975: `evictOverflow` sorted the whole point cache on every write once it was full.

## What

- `server/providers/terrain.js`: the map is kept in fetch-time order, so `evictOverflow()` deletes from the front instead of sorting. The disk load sorts once (`orderByAge()`), because a file written before this change, or a migrated raw-batch cache, is not in age order.
- `src/data/terrainHeightsProxy.js`: the resolver deletes before it sets a refetched point. A plain `set` on an existing key keeps the key's old position in a `Map`, so a refreshed point would otherwise be the first to go.
- Which point gets evicted does not change (oldest fetch first), and a performance changelog fragment records the optimization and `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md` still reads true.

## Tests

- New: `a refetched point counts as new when the cache evicts` (`src/terrainHeightsBounds.test.mjs`). It seeds a cache file in non-age order with one point past the 30-day TTL, refetches it, adds a point, and checks that the oldest fetch was evicted. It uses its own temp `cachePath`, so it never reads the checkout's `.gev-cache`. It is the first commit and passes on `main`'s sort-based code too.
- Mutations: dropping the delete-before-set fails it (the refreshed point is evicted), and so does dropping the sort on load (the newest file entry is evicted).
- Cost, measured on node 24 with 50,000 entries: median 2.46 ms per full-cache write on `main`, 0.9 µs on this branch. Eviction runs once for each request that changes the cache.

## Verification

At `e60cbb42e` on main `224745bd0`: `npm test` 8,277 pass, 0 fail; `doctor`, `format:check`, `check:boundaries`, `changelog:check` and `build` pass.

The second #975 follow-up, moving the last test in `terrainHeightsBounds.test.mjs` to `stubTerrainUpstream(t)`, is not in this PR: #1244 edits the line next to it, so I'll send it after #1244 lands to avoid a conflict there.

title: feat(i18n): add Italian (it)
body:
Adds Italian as a shipped locale, following the six steps in `docs/TRANSLATORS.md` § Adding a language.

## What's in it

- **Catalog:** `src/i18n/locales/it.json` covers all 2681 messages, and `npm run i18n` reports `de: complete`. Plurals use `one`/`many`/`other`. `many`, used for exact millions, puts «di» after the number.
- **Kept in English:** 179 entries are listed under `it` in `same-as-english.json`:
  - HUD and avionics codes (HDG, BRG, CRS, FOV, DEST, ETA, UTC, ADS-B …);
  - keyboard keys;
  - product and dataset names;
  - music genres;
  - placeholder-only strings.
- **Registration:** `CATALOGS` and `LOCALES`, the picker name `Italiano`, `package-boundaries.json`, the picker test, and the shipped-language lists in `TRANSLATORS.md` and `CURRENT-STATE.md`.
- **Language notes:** `docs/translations/it.md` covers:
  - style: the informal «tu» imperative in messages, infinitives or nouns on buttons, sentence case and abbreviations for short labels;
  - units, and the codes kept in Latin;
  - a glossary.

## How it was made and checked

- **Earlier work by @abiyeenzo.** 869 strings come from #912, which was stacked on #601 (now closed), so its per-area modules no longer match `main`'s flat catalogs.
  - I mapped them onto the current keys, and a full review pass changed 204 of them.
  - The changes add the `many` plural form (all 7 plural entries lacked it), restore the `—` separators, align the glossary («inquadratura», «Impostazioni dei provider»), and keep keyboard keys in English («Space», not «Spazio»). They also fix context errors: the route action `CLEAR` had become the weather word «SERENO», and is now «CANCELLA».
  - The commit credits @abiyeenzo as co-author.
- **The other 1812 strings are new translations.** Each chunk went through a script check: placeholders, separators, UPPERCASE, plural forms and still-English text.
- **A whole-catalog consistency pass changed 70 more entries:**
  - The 3D view camera is now «visuale» everywhere, and real cameras stay «telecamera».
  - Map tiles are one word («tile»), timeouts read «Tempo scaduto per…» and Street Level is «Vista stradale» everywhere.
  - FOCUS is translated as «CENTRA», and the COCKPIT chip is shortened to «CABINA».
  - I checked the `{direction}` templates in `src/layers/directions`: each value already carries its preposition, so «Svolta a sinistra» and «Usa la corsia di sinistra» read correctly.
- The HUD codes `SUN`, `ONA` and `ALT` stay English in the HUD line, because the static HUD markup in `src/hud.js` shows `SUN:` before the first update.
- **Full suite:** node 24 in a container, on `d48b9c4d`: doctor, `format:check`, `check:boundaries`, `changelog:check`, build and `i18n --check` all pass, and `npm test` has 8318 passed and 0 failed.

## Known limits (code, not catalog)

As with Japanese (#1217), a few strings are joined in code with ASCII separators or untranslated parts. I'd fix those in a separate PR, not with catalog workarounds:

- `src/ui/applicationShell.js` and `src/voice/resultDisplay.js` join layer names with `', '`;
- `src/layers/firms/model.js` `formatAge` returns `5m`/`<1h` untranslated;
- `src/ui/streetLevelPresentation.js` joins requirements with `'; '`.

Reviews from Italian speakers are very welcome. @abiyeenzo, thank you for #912. If you'd rather carry this forward in your own PR, I'm happy to close this one in its favour.

**Voice:** with #1218, cloud voice sessions speak the interface language through `normalizeLocale`, so Italian voice needs no code beyond this PR. Whichever of the two lands second adds the 9 Italian progress lines (ready).

**Picker order:** if #1217 (ja) or the German PR (#1328) lands first, the expected orders in `localePicker.test.mjs` need a one-line rebase.
