title: feat(layers): EV Charging — OpenStreetMap charging stations, keyless
body:
Adds **EV Charging** (`ev-charging`, 🔌), a keyless Infrastructure layer with the charging stations mapped in OpenStreetMap. Their availability is a basic smart-city question, and the app had no layer for it.

## What it shows

- Points are OpenStreetMap charging stations as OpenFreeMap publishes them in the OpenMapTiles `poi` layer: `class` `fuel`, `subclass` `charging_station`. Petrol stations share that class and are excluded.
  - They are read browser-direct from the same planet tiles that street traffic and installations use.
  - Overpass is never used (public Overpass is off by default).
- **Card:** a click or **SHOW NEAREST** opens a card with:
  - the name as mapped (unnamed stations say so);
  - 5-decimal coordinates;
  - the OpenStreetMap credit.
- **Coverage is honest:**
  - The tiles carry no sockets, power, operator or live availability, and the layer claims none.
  - `getStats().observedAt` is the planet build time named in the tile path, not the fetch time.

## How it loads

- **Zoom 14 only:** OpenMapTiles keeps `poi` features only at z14. On live tiles, z12 and z13 hold 0 charging stations in Oslo, Amsterdam, Ho Chi Minh City and Hanoi, so a coarser read would show a falsely empty map.
- **View box:** like ALPR, a view reads a box around the ground at the screen centre, sized by camera range.
- **Wide views:** a view needing more than 16 tiles shows "Zoom in to load charging stations" before any request, instead of reading a sample.
- **Caching:** decoded tiles are cached, so panning over tiles already read makes no request.
- **Deduplication:** each station belongs to the tile that contains it, never to a neighbour's buffer, so adjacent tiles never draw it twice.
- **Large views:** above 2,000 stations the nearest are kept and the row says coverage is limited.
- **Partial failures:** a failed tile leaves the read `partial`. Errors use the fixed forms `translateFeedError` already handles, and stations already shown stay up as stale.
- **Rendering:** lime points, white when selected, in the installations style. The on-map credit follows the stations shown.
- **Voice:** aliases are "charging stations", "EV chargers", "chargers" and "EV charging stations".

## Outside the layer

- **Share token:** `5`, from `npm run layer-token:next -- ev-charging`.
  - The pinned counts and ledger fixtures moved with it: registry 31 → 32, catalog 32 → 33, ledger digits.
  - The two pinned voice digests (`actionSchemas.test.mjs`, `firstRunExperience.test.mjs`) are re-derived, as the air-quality voice commit did.
- **Source registration:** the source is registered in `src/standalone/layerSources.js` next to ALPR. `reference.js` would have pulled pbf, vector-tile and the military-tile modules into the `reference-sources` boundary group.
- **Coordinate formatter:** `formatCockpitCoordinate` gains an optional `digits` (default 3, so existing callers are unchanged). Three decimals is about 110 m, too coarse to place a charger.
- **README count:** the README sentence above the layer table already undercounted the table ("Twenty… Eighteen" for 23 rows, 21 keyless). It now reads "Twenty-four… Twenty-two", matching the table with this row; the test that pins the sentence is updated.
- **Docs:** `DATA_SOURCES.md` and `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md` describe the layer and its limits.

## Checks

- Full gate in a clean `node:24` container on `6aa49c243` (`npm ci`): doctor, `format:check`, `check:boundaries`, `changelog:check`, build all pass; `i18n --check` reports es, ru and zh-CN at 2692 messages, complete; `npm test` has 8317 passed and 0 failed.
- `npm run layer-token:check -- --base-ref upstream/main`: "Layer tokens valid against upstream/main: 31 published, 1 new."
- Feature gates against a Vite dev server: `scripts/qa-layer-panel.mjs` gives `RESULT: 0 failures`; `scripts/qa-application.mjs` passes startup, data registration, attribution and teardown.

- **Unit tests (25):**
  - decoder (5): fuel/shop exclusion, unnamed stations, the tile buffer, a tile with no `poi` layer, build-time parse;
  - source with injected fetch (8): a zoom-in with 0 requests, exactly 16 tiles, cache, partial, each error form, abort, the 2,000 cap;
  - layer ownership (12): render, stale vs unavailable, late response after disable, superseded read, selection and card, SHOW NEAREST, destroy and re-init.
- **Mutation:** each change below was applied alone and turned its tests red:
  - remove the subclass filter: 2 red;
  - loosen the tile cap: 2 red;
  - never set stale: 1 red;
  - `disable()` not aborting: 1 red;
  - not releasing a vanished selection: 2 red.
- **Real app** (Vite, Chromium, live OpenFreeMap tiles, 1.5 km camera height, 1440×900):

  | View | Stations | Row |
  |---|---|---|
  | Oslo | 117 | `117 nearby` |
  | Amsterdam | 431 | `431 nearby` |
  | Ho Chi Minh City | 2 | `2 nearby` |
  | Hanoi | 6 | `6 nearby` |
  | Oslo from 30 km | 0 | `Zoom in to load charging stations` |

  - The Amsterdam card read "Equans AMS-0053 · EV CHARGING · OSM MAPPED · 52.36986°N 4.89428°E · © OpenStreetMap contributors".
  - The only console error was the keyless `/api/google/tiles-token` 404.
  - That run found one bug, fixed in `6aa49c243`: flying from Amsterdam to Ho Chi Minh City left the Amsterdam card open, because a read without the selected station reset the layer's selection but not the shared one. The new test fails without the fix.
- `test:track`: 108 passed / 1 failed on this branch in each of two runs. The one failure is the arrival-budget case: the `flights` arrival reveal took 500.5 ms and 500.3 ms against its 500 ms budget. Upstream `main` at `d48b9c4df` fails the same family of case in both of two solo runs on the same machine (military moveEnd at 500.2 ms; flights reveal at 500.3 ms), so I read it as a timing flake on `main`, not something this layer adds.

The changelog fragment follows in a second commit, once this PR has a number.

title: feat(cyclones): add optional Taiwan CWA forecasts
body:
## Summary

Adds optional Taiwan Central Weather Administration (CWA) tropical cyclone forecast advisories to the existing Cyclones layer. NOAA advisories remain available without credentials; CWA advisories are added when an operator configures a CWA API key.

## Data sources

| Provider | Coverage | Access |
| --- | --- | --- |
| NOAA National Hurricane Center / Central Pacific Hurricane Center | North Atlantic, Eastern Pacific, and Central Pacific | Public feeds; no key required |
| Taiwan Central Weather Administration (CWA) | Western North Pacific and South China Sea | CWA Open Data API; requires an operator-provided API key |

The CWA provider uses the official [Typhoon Forecast Track dataset](https://opendata.cwa.gov.tw/dataset/forecast/F-A0012-001) and its documented API response.

## How it works

- Adds a server-side CWA provider that requests and normalizes official forecast track data, including forecast positions, valid times, wind radii, and provider attribution.
- Reads the CWA key from server environment configuration and sends it in the provider request. The key is never included in client responses or committed source.
- Keeps NOAA and CWA requests independent, so one provider can remain available when the other is unavailable or misconfigured.
- Integrates CWA storms with the existing cyclone layer, forecast tracks, time controls, query tools, data credits, and localized UI.
- Parses the live CWA response envelope and its forecast-hour/radius fields. The map renders forecast radii supplied by CWA; it does not invent a probability cone when the source does not provide one.

## Geographic coverage

This adds source-backed coverage for Taiwan and nearby western North Pacific / South China Sea waters. The existing NOAA feeds continue to cover their supported basins. Other global basins are not claimed as covered by this change.

## Validation

- Focused cyclone provider, rendering, source, query, and localization checks: 76 passed.
- Formatting checks and production build passed.
- Live local app check with the configured CWA key returned NOAA and CWA providers as available. CWA returned CHAMPI near 24.1°N, 123.2°E with seven forecast points.
- The full suite had 8,231 passing, 2 failing, and 10 skipped tests in the earlier run. The two failures were unrelated existing environment/timing cases: a terrain cross-site fixture expectation and a track arrival-rotation timing threshold. The tracking gate also had 107 passing and 2 timing-threshold failures.

## Limitations and configuration

- CWA data requires each deployment operator to provide their own API key; the key used for local verification is stored only in the ignored local environment file.
- CWA coverage depends on the provider's current published advisories and data availability.
- This change does not claim forecast coverage for basins without an integrated and validated source.

title: feat(agent): add text conversations with ChatGPT Responses over shared actions
body:
## What this changes

Run map conversations in GEV COMMAND without opening a Realtime/Live connection or requesting microphone permission. Preserve ChatGPT sign-in, account-bound model discovery and Responses continuation, alongside the API-key and Ollama transports.

COMMAND is mounted through the Vue view registry and presents its transcript/account controls through Pinia. The original typed core and darrendignam's attribution remain in the ancestry. **No separate merge of #976 is required.**

## Why this complements main's typed commands

Main already accepts typed input through `providerCommands.sendTextCommand`; that path uses the selected provider's connected Realtime/Live session. COMMAND provides an HTTP conversation with model selection, a visible tool transcript and STOP, including a ChatGPT authorization lifecycle independent of Codex credentials and API-key billing.

Both surfaces execute the **same application runner**. `src/app/tools.js` passes `voiceCommands.runner` into COMMAND; the server derives instructions from the voice manual and reuses its tool inventory plus the catalog's HUD caption query. Voice transitions may reset shared pointer/referent/analyst memory, even though COMMAND's transcript and account are separate.

## Server contract and provider privacy

The review against [the closure of #1223](https://github.com/bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view/pull/1223#issuecomment-6587796973) confirmed protections already present:

- Client `system` messages are discarded; instructions/tool schemas are server-owned and returned tool calls are validated.
- History targets 40 messages while preserving tool pairs; content/tool results and client/server byte budgets are bounded. A single oversized exchange can still be rejected deliberately.
- ChatGPT uses explicit authorization, loopback-only admission, protected server-side storage and account bindings. There is no automatic paid API fallback.
- HUD captions retain the app's separately configured summary service. Returned captions may enter the selected conversation provider's tool history.

The new follow-up adds provider-specific disclosure of commands/tool results and map/place context in **all eleven locales**, including OpenRouter's compatible-service override and potentially remote Ollama servers. The existing ChatGPT plan notice and Settings link remain. The notice shares the scrollable header so the input remains reachable with a small keyboard viewport.

OpenRouter requires explicit operator configuration; provider switching remains an explicit user choice. The provider choices and separate conversation view remain product decisions for maintainers to assess.

## Integration and verification

Published head: `f8154e34d08314eca6ad3118e9b451b4a8b842b1`; tree `c3167688af9b3b1b32fb04287662c1dadacb3e0f`. Includes original-repository main `3ad3cc2ab773bb2d694a1e1605cf7ffe5d0dca46` through a history-preserving merge.

Linux / Node 24.22.1:

- **10,369 ordinary tests passed, 7 explicit skips, zero failures** on runtime tree `cd7cdaf5`.
- **561 tests passed, 2 native Windows skips, zero failures** on the final #1308 combination, covering all agent/ChatGPT suites, coexistence, Overpass admission/proxy behavior, request gates/network keys, arrival-observer regressions and HUD caption state.
- Production build, formatting, import/package boundaries, all locale catalogs, changelog and the 34-token ledger passed on the final combination.
- Browser fixtures passed **26 language/size combinations**. Full-application geometry passed **10 en/ar desktop/phone viewports**, including pointer targets, safe areas and simulated keyboard reductions.
- The 15 allocation assertions passed before the final header adjustment; allocation code/tests are unchanged. Full-suite, allocation and browser evidence retains its recorded tree scope; those runs were not repeated solely for the independent #1308 advance.

[Current validation, reproduction commands and limitations](https://github.com/radianx/gods-eye-view/blob/f8154e34d08314eca6ad3118e9b451b4a8b842b1/docs/VUE-COMMAND.md) · [Transport, privacy and history boundaries](https://github.com/radianx/gods-eye-view/blob/f8154e34d08314eca6ad3118e9b451b4a8b842b1/docs/TEXT-AGENT.md) · [Provider notice/account controls screenshot — scripted fixture](https://github.com/radianx/gods-eye-view/blob/f8154e34d08314eca6ad3118e9b451b4a8b842b1/docs/media/command-vue/privacy-en-desktop.png)

**Draft release gates:** real eligible-account OAuth/inference, native Windows credential protection, hosted CI and broad external-feed/tracking validation remain open. Browser requests/account state are fixtures; no real OAuth, microphone or paid inference is claimed.

title: feat: self-hosted personalized intelligence watches → phone notifications
body:
## Problem

I'd like to leave God's Eye View running unattended on a home server and receive **personalized, actionable intelligence notifications on my phone**, without having to keep the globe open or periodically check dashboards.

Inspired by [Bilawal Sidhu's post](https://x.com/bilawalsidhu/status/2113611395069579716). The goal is an **opt-in, local-first personal watch service** over GEV's existing public, attributable signals, not a second intelligence platform.

## Proposed user flow

1. Run GEV on a home server (Docker/Linux). A lightweight **headless watch worker** continues while all browser tabs are closed; no Cesium renderer is needed to evaluate watches.
2. Define a watch from GEV: **where** (saved area/geofence), **what** (supported public-data event/layer), **when/how significant** (threshold, change condition), and **how often** (immediate/digest, quiet hours).
3. On a meaningful new event, receive a phone notification with a concise **why this matched**, event time, confidence/freshness if provided, original source, and a **deep link** to the relevant GEV view.
4. Tap through for context and provenance; pause, snooze, edit or disable the watch at any time.

Example: “Notify me about USGS M4+ earthquakes within 100 km of my saved area,” or “new NASA FIRMS active-fire detections in a saved region.” These are configurable examples, not claims that all live layers currently support server-side watching.

## Narrow MVP

- **Headless + persistent:** one server-side scheduled evaluator and persisted opt-in rules, surviving browser disconnect and process restart.
- **Two initially supported public-data sources** (suggested: USGS earthquakes and NASA FIRMS where terms/availability permit), with source-specific cadence, coverage, stale-data and rate-limit handling. Reuse existing GEV fetch/parsing/provenance boundaries rather than scraping displayed UI state.
- **One mobile delivery path:** an opt-in outbound adapter (e.g., [ntfy](https://ntfy.sh/) for self-hosted Android/iOS notifications); keep a small transport interface for future standards-based Web Push/PWA support. Do not require users to open inbound ports to their home network.
- **Signal quality:** dedupe by stable source/event ID; configurable geographic/severity thresholds, cooldown, quiet hours, rate limits, and optional digest; never treat stale/unavailable feeds as fresh alerts.
- **Safe setup:** delivery test, failure/retry status, disable control. Store credentials server-side, redact logs, keep rules private, and secure any remote configuration/pairing. No public unauthenticated control endpoint.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] On a self-hosted GEV instance, creating an opt-in watch and closing the browser still results in a phone notification for a **new, matching synthetic/test event**.
- [ ] Rules survive restart; duplicate or replayed events do not trigger duplicate pushes.
- [ ] Nonmatching, stale, unavailable and rate-limited-source cases have explicit, tested behavior.
- [ ] Notifications identify the trigger and data source, preserve event timestamp and freshness, and open a relevant GEV context/deep link.
- [ ] Quiet hours, pause/disable, cooldown and delivery failures are covered by tests.
- [ ] No provider secrets or personal watch settings leak into client bundles, notification URLs, or public logs; no browser/GPU/Cesium session is required on the host.

## Scope / related work

This is specifically **durable personal watches + outbound phone delivery**. It should complement, not duplicate, [spatial watch conditions #469](https://github.com/bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view/issues/469), [proximity-alert discussion #136](https://github.com/bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view/issues/136) and the [downstream remote-phone companion proposal](https://github.com/kvnloo/gods-eye-view/issues/109). Prefer existing source adapters and watch/event contracts if/when available. Start with hazard/environmental observations; **no named-person tracking, facial recognition, private surveillance, or autonomous actions**.

Feedback welcome on the smallest upstream-compatible integration seam before implementation.

title: feat: opt-in co-op city-builder mode for comparing park proposals
body:
### Problem

GEV is useful for observing the real world, but a resident or student cannot easily explore **two possible futures for the same block** without confusing a proposal with an observed fact. A small, game-like civic planning view could make the globe more interactive while keeping evidence and official planning authority separate.

### Proposal

Would an **opt-in “World Game / Co-op Planning”** experiment inside the existing GEV Scene/Explore UI fit the roadmap? Please treat the broader civilization-building idea as a direction, **not** a request for a whole game engine.

**Smallest usable pilot:**
1. Start with **one synthetic neighborhood block** and a pinned, read-only baseline. Two people can author **Trees & Shade** versus **Playground & Garden** alternatives as versioned, credited *hypotheses*.
2. Compare the alternatives side-by-side using the **existing Scene dialog/renderer**: visible changes, assumptions, original source revision, and undo/compare. Any marker schematic is clearly synthetic, not surveyed geometry.
3. Show a persistent **HYPOTHETICAL · NOT APPROVED** label. Unknown accessibility, zoning, financial or environmental impacts stay *not evaluated*; a rendered park is not a prediction or government decision.
4. A “Game view / Co-op view” toggle initially changes **presentation only**. Keep single-player working; online rooms, shared cursors, validated municipal models, persistence and city-scale simulation are separate follow-ups only if the first pilot is wanted.

**Acceptance for this initial scope:** original observed layers never change; explicit authorship and revision survive export/import; conflicting or unsupported changes are rejected/visible; keyboard, mobile and reduced-motion paths remain usable; no remote participant location is inferred or broadcast.

### Existing downstream prototype (not production-ready)

- [Collaboration/authority boundary — fork draft #164](https://github.com/kvnloo/gods-eye-view/pull/164): deterministic authored operations; remote edits do not grant action authority.
- [Versioned park alternatives — fork draft #185](https://github.com/kvnloo/gods-eye-view/pull/185): two hypothetical alternatives, pseudonymous recorded authorship and a synthetic footprint.
- [Scene comparison — fork draft #229](https://github.com/kvnloo/gods-eye-view/pull/229): opt-in `?planningPreview=fixture` panel; two synthetic proposals, five markers and local view toggle.

These drafts have **limited isolated source/fixture tests**; #229 had a **stubbed** browser preview, not verified full-app GEV acceptance. **Supported Node 24/26 full gates, real two-browser collaboration and production UX have not been validated.** No code is being requested for upstream merge now.

### Data source, license, and attribution

**Initial pilot: synthetic test data only, keyless.** No real parcels, resident locations or unlicensed city feeds. Any later real map/planning data would need its specific license, attribution, consent and boundary/version checks. Related but separately owned: [#1076 municipal GeoJSON polygons](https://github.com/bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view/issues/1076), proposed by mtmediaai. The [#1198 disaster-evidence workspace](https://github.com/bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view/issues/1198) is adjacent, not the same feature. Existing GEV Scene, Cesium and community contributors retain their original authorship.

### Will you build it?

I've already prepared the three small **downstream drafts** above and can refine an accepted slice, but **no new PR is proposed now**. Mainly seeking a scope/fit decision: is the two-park-comparison pilot useful for GEV, or better kept fork-only?

title: feat: authenticated phone companion with measured local or host-stream presentation
body:
### Problem

On a weak phone, a usable mobile layout does not by itself make a heavy GEV scene responsive. It would be useful to view a GEV session running on a stronger computer, while keeping source credentials and expensive acquisition on that host.

This is distinct from [mobile layout #642](https://github.com/bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view/issues/642) and [phone-interface #1180](https://github.com/bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view/issues/1180), and complements [headless watches #1332](https://github.com/bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view/issues/1332). Existing Scene/Director, layer/source, mobile and voice contributors retain their ownership; the runtime-tier idea is Kevin's, building on Bilawal Sidhu and the GEV contributors' application.

### Proposal

An opt-in, authenticated companion with three presentation choices:

- Lightweight source-linked state/events and narrowly scoped, acknowledged controls, without starting a renderer.
- The actual host GEV canvas streamed to the phone, or the **same existing web frontend** served by the PC and rendered on the phone's GPU. Synchronize camera, enabled layers, time/selection and Director state. Each client uses the PC's authenticated provider APIs; no new per-layer asset packaging or replacement renderer.
- An honest 2D/status fallback when neither interactive path is usable.

Choose from measured client frame time, RTT/jitter/throughput and actual WebRTC encode/decode/transport observations, not GPU model or a low ping alone. Preserve manual override and use hysteresis before automatic switches. Closing/backgrounding a view should release its render/stream resources without stopping watches.

Pairing, expiry/revocation, exact origin checks and server-held provider credentials are required even over a mesh VPN. LAN versus mesh reachability is separate from authentication. Later TV presentation would need a sanitized read-only receiver and explicit local discovery/receiver support; VPN access does not establish Google Cast discovery. Voice should reuse GEV's existing typed action path rather than add another authority or always-on microphone.

### Downstream status and boundaries

The design and ordered implementation contract are in [downstream #109](https://github.com/kvnloo/gods-eye-view/issues/109#issuecomment-6373283228), under [performance program #103](https://github.com/kvnloo/gods-eye-view/issues/103). [Downstream Draft #267](https://github.com/kvnloo/gods-eye-view/pull/267) starts with renderer-free watches and outbound delivery. **These are downstream experiments, not an upstream-ready companion, verified phone stream, verified shared-session local route or working Cast integration.** No new upstream PR or merge is requested.

I found no existing companion/remote-rendering/Cast issue across open and closed searches; the historical recording proposal #1075 and co-op planning #1333 are separate workflows. If this belongs under an existing design, happy to keep the detail there.

### Data source, license, and attribution

No new feed is proposed. Per-client layer requests and streamed media retain existing provider terms, timestamps and attribution. Private watches, provider keys and sensitive media must not reach guest receivers. Existing source/provider modules remain the owners; this is a session and presentation consumer.

### Will you build it?

Downstream implementation and measurement are underway in the linked fork. Is a narrow authenticated companion/host-stream integration a useful direction for GEV, or better kept as an external/downstream consumer? No urgency or request to prioritize it ahead of existing reviews.

title: fix(hud): carry rounded DMS seconds into the minutes
body:
The HUD LAT/LON readout (`#hud-latlon` and the bottom line) formats degrees, minutes and seconds separately and rounds only the seconds with `toFixed(2)`. Any coordinate within 0.005" below a whole minute therefore prints `60.00"` without carrying. Ordinary decimal inputs land there through binary floating point: `122.35 - 122` is `0.34999999999999432`, so a camera at longitude -122.35 reads `122°20'60.00"W`, and 139.7 reads `139°41'60.00"E`. While panning, any position in that ~15 cm band below a minute shows the same thing; at 38.999999 it reads `38°59'60.00"N` instead of `39°00'00.00"N`.

`_toDMS` now rounds once, to hundredths of a second, and splits that integer into degrees, minutes and seconds, so the carry reaches the minutes and degrees. Field widths, zero padding and hemisphere letters are unchanged.

Adds `src/hudDms.test.mjs`: carry into minutes, carry through 59 minutes into degrees (including 180°), unchanged ordinary values, and a live `IntelHUD._updateCameraData()` tick that checks the painted `#hud-latlon` and bottom-line text. It reuses the `mgrs` stub from `hudAltitudeDatum.test.mjs`. Also adds the test to the format scope, a short runtime note to `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md`, and the changelog fragment.

Contributor verification on base `8d454bf` (rebased; first run on `8cdd184` matched), Node 24.22.1:

- New test against unmodified `main`: 3 of 4 fail (`122°20'60.00"W`, `38°59'60.00"N`, and the painted readout `37°45'00.00"N 122°20'60.00"W`). With the fix, 4/4 pass.
- `node --test src/hudDms.test.mjs src/hudAltitudeDatum.test.mjs src/hudA11y.test.mjs src/hudLocality.test.mjs`: 22 pass, 0 fail.
- `npm run build`, `npm run format:check` and `npm run check:boundaries` pass.
- Full `npm test` on unmodified `main` on this machine had 7 timeout failures in launcher, CCTV preset and process-deadline tests (30 s and 2-5 s deadlines on a heavily loaded host). None touch the HUD. I did not get a clean full-suite run locally, so CI is the full-suite check here.
- I did not run `npm run test:track`; this change is limited to the text formatting of the HUD readout.


## Landing follow-up

The HUD regression fixture now supplies the camera move-start event required by current main. The documentation conflict is resolved while preserving current guidance.

## Landing validation

On the combined candidate based on current main `2006c035`: boundaries, doctor, formatting, production build and 8,574 unit tests passed (one skipped); allocation checks passed. The repaired HUD test passes all four cases. Actual-browser overhead and oblique checks show correctly carried DMS readouts without page errors.

Tracking limitation: two unchanged full runs each passed 108/109. The remaining arrival-rotation check timed out waiting for a rendered frame within 500 ms; it did not capture an incorrect rotation. A bounded control restored the exact baseline HUD formatter (the only changed browser-runtime code), verified the old coordinate output, and reproduced the frame timeout under SwiftShader. This is a baseline-runtime control, not a full baseline-checkout run. No test deadline or assertion was changed; no 109/109 or real-GPU claim is made.

title: fix(embed): keep inline panels polling when their host reports them hidden; pause the HUD readout in hidden tabs
body:
## What

Polled layers (flights, quakes, weather, …) keep refreshing while the browser tab is in the background, where nobody sees the result. This pauses those refreshes while the page is hidden and runs **one** catch-up refresh when it is shown again. The HUD's 250 ms camera readout also skips hidden tabs.

## How

- `LayerLifecycle` takes an optional `pageVisibility` service (`{ isHidden(), subscribe(callback) }`), so `src/data/lifecycle.js` stays free of browser globals. `src/app/data.js` passes the `document`-backed one. Without the service, refreshes run exactly as before.
- A refresh that falls due while hidden is marked `updateDue`; on `visibilitychange` back to visible it runs once.
- The seven places that stopped a layer's interval now go through one `_clearUpdateLoop(entry)` helper, which also removes the catch-up listener (disable, cancelled/failed enable, re-arm, destroy).

title: perf(weather): wake a staged frame on a 150 ms timer, not every render
body:
## What

While a staged weather observation waits out its 200 ms quiet interval, its `postRender` listener calls `viewer.scene.requestRender()` on every frame, so the scene renders flat out for that stretch instead of staying under the render governor's frame cap. This arms one 150 ms timer (`READY_WAKE_MS`) that requests a single render to recheck readiness. The timer is cleared when the frame commits, fails or is removed.

It's a small tidy-up found by reading the code. It doesn't change what you see, and `qa-weather-perf`'s scenarios show the same frame rates before and after.

## Contributor verification

- `npm test`: 8,313 pass. The one failure (`skyAssets.paintOut.test.mjs`) also fails on unmodified `main` on Windows, so unrelated.
- `src/layers/weather/weather.test.mjs`: 71 pass, including a new test that a staged frame asks for renders on the timer, not on every frame, and that the timer is cleared.
- `npm run build`: green.

- `qa-weather-swap`: 26 frames across 5 observation times, no blank frames.
