title: feat(layers): add River Flood Gauges from NOAA NWPS
body:
Adds **River Flood Gauges** (`river-gauges`, ≋), a keyless Events layer with the NWS flood category of about 13,000 NOAA National Water Prediction Service (NWPS) river gauges. Rivers in flood are a basic situational question, and the app had no layer for them.

## What it shows

- **Points:** every gauge NWPS lists for the 50 states, Puerto Rico and the U.S. Virgin Islands, coloured by the flood category of its latest observation, with the NWS hydrograph colours for the flood stages:
  - action yellow, minor orange, moderate red, major purple;
  - below flood stage a quiet green, below a low-water threshold brown;
  - no flood stages defined, reading not current and out of service grey and dimmed.
  - Gauges at action stage and above are drawn larger and on top. Points beyond the globe's horizon are hidden on camera change.
- **Card:** a click opens a card with:
  - name, NWS id, state and category;
  - stage, flow and the age of the observation;
  - the current NWPS forecast when one is issued (value, category, when);
  - once the per-gauge record arrives: flood stages (action/minor/moderate/major), the most recent and highest historic crest, and the USGS site id.
  - A click on the card opens the gauge's `water.noaa.gov/gauges/<id>` page. The URL is built from the validated id, never taken from the payload.
- **SHOW MOST SEVERE** selects the worst flooding gauge nearest the camera and flies there. The legend counts gauges per category.
- **Meaning, stated in the docs and the credit:** these are NWS flood categories against each gauge's own flood stages, not flood watches or warnings.
- **Analyst and voice:** the manifest exposes `name`, `state`, `category`, `stageFt`, `flowKcfs`, `observedMs` (stage and flow converted to ft and kcfs whatever unit NWPS sent). Aliases are "flood gauges" and "river flooding".

## Source and terms

- [NWPS API](https://api.water.noaa.gov/nwps/v1/docs/): `/gauges` by bounding box and `/gauges/{lid}`; keyless.
- NWS information is in the public domain and may be used for any lawful purpose provided it is not presented as one's own, as implying NWS endorsement, or, once modified, as official government material ([NWS disclaimer](https://www.weather.gov/disclaimer)). The layer shows NWPS values as published, credits "NOAA/NWS National Water Prediction Service; observations courtesy of USGS and other gauge operators", and links every gauge to its official page.

## How it loads

NWPS has two constraints that shape the server, both measured against the live API:

- **Gateway timeout:** a request that runs past 60 s ends in a 504. A CONUS-wide box does; one request costs about 10 ms per gauge (a 2,714-gauge column took 25.6 s).
- **Rate limit:** the gauge list answers 429 "Rate limit exceeded. Limit: 10 requests / 5 minutes." per client. The per-gauge endpoint was not limited at the same time.

So the browser never calls NWPS, and `server/providers/nwps.js` builds one national snapshot:

- **Seven fixed boxes:** CONUS split at 107°, 94°, 86° and 80°W into five columns of 2,300–2,700 gauges, Alaska, and one 17–23°N strip holding Hawaii, Puerto Rico and the U.S. Virgin Islands. NWPS lists no gauges for Guam, the Northern Marianas or American Samoa.
- **One at a time:** two column reads in parallel both ran past 60 s, and four in parallel all returned 504, so reads are sequential (`NWPS_CONCURRENCY = 1`). The first live build took 83.4 s.
- **Budget:** at most one build per 15 minutes, only while someone requests it. The store counts its own list requests and refuses past 8 per 5 minutes; after a 429 it asks nothing for max(Retry-After, 5 minutes).
- **Failure:** a region that fails keeps its previous gauges and the snapshot reads stale; a rebuild serves the previous snapshot meanwhile (single flight); with no snapshot at all the route answers 503 with `Retry-After: 120`, and a failed build is not retried for 5 minutes.
- **Payload:** each gauge is trimmed to id, name, position, state, forecast office and observed/forecast stage, flow, category and time; NWPS sentinels (`-999`, `-9999`, `0001-01-01`) become null and stage and flow are told apart by unit. Live: 12,941 gauges, 3,647,187 B of JSON, 574,145 B gzip-encoded (sent when the client accepts it); a repeat read is served from memory in about 3 ms.
- **Detail:** `/api/nwps/gauge/<lid>` accepts only `^[A-Z]{4}[0-9]$` (checked before any request, 400 otherwise), returns flood stages, three highest and three most recent crests, USGS id and service state, cached 15 minutes (512 entries) and served stale when a re-read fails. The browser reads it once per selection.
- Both routes are GET/HEAD only and share a per-client rate limit; responses carry the same JSON/CSP headers as the other proxies. The client waits up to 240 s for the first snapshot.

## Outside the layer

- **Share token:** `5`, the next free token on `main` after `recent-imagery`. Another open branch may claim the same next token; whichever merges second takes the following one. The pinned counts and ledger fixtures moved with it (catalog 32 → 33, source composition, ledger digits), and the two pinned voice digests (`actionSchemas.test.mjs`, `firstRunExperience.test.mjs`) are re-derived.
- **Voice prompt ceiling:** `pointAndAsk.test.mjs` pins the assembled prompt below 52,000 characters. `main` is at 51,972; the manifest entry for this layer brings it to 52,132, and even a minimal entry (no aliases, one query field) reaches 52,029. The ceiling is raised to 52,150 with a comment. If you would rather keep 52,000, the entry needs trimming elsewhere in the prompt first.
- **Relation to other work:** the open USGS water draft (#1316) claims the alias "river gauges" and a Water group, so this layer uses the Events group and different aliases; NWPS records carry the USGS site id, so the two can cross-reference. The NWS alerts work (#758, `cap.js`) covers warnings, which this layer deliberately does not show.
- **README count:** the sentence above the layer table reads "Twenty-four… Twenty-two have a keyless path", matching the table with this row; the test that pins the sentence is updated.
- **Boundaries and format scope:** the five new modules are registered in `scripts/package-boundaries.json` and the new tests in `scripts/format-scope.json`.
- **Docs:** `DATA_SOURCES.md` (table row and a section with terms and the request budget) and `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md`.
- **Changelog:** `changelog.d/1346-nwps-river-flood-gauges.md`.

## Checks

- Full gate in a clean `node:24` container on `23f2279e7` (`npm ci`): doctor, `format:check`, `check:boundaries`, `changelog:check`, build all pass; `i18n --check` reports es, ru and zh-CN at 2723 messages, complete; `npm test` has 8547 passed, 0 failed (2 skipped).
- `npm run layer-token:check -- --base-ref upstream/main`: "Layer tokens valid against upstream/main: 31 published, 1 new."
- Feature gates against a Vite dev server: `scripts/qa-layer-panel.mjs` gives `RESULT: 0 failures`; `scripts/qa-ui-disposal.mjs` passes every case.
- **`npm run test:track`**, paired and alternating with upstream main (`d48b9c4df`; this branch is on `9d3548c27`) on the same machine under load:

  | Round | upstream main | this branch |
  |---|---|---|
  | 1 | 108/1 (`military` arrival 500.3 ms) | 109/0 |
  | 2 | 109/0 | 108/1 (`military` arrival 500.4 ms) |

  The only failure is the 500 ms arrival-observation budget, which upstream main also misses.
- **Unit tests (34):**
  - server (15): column split covers the box with no gap; production regions reach every gauge extreme and fit the budget; budget and 429 stop; sentinels and unit split; categories; gauge and detail trimming (from a trimmed real record, `src/data/fixtures/nwps-gauge-aait2.json`); deduplication and gzip; single flight; stale-while-refresh; a failed region kept; 503 and cooldown; gzip/plain/405/404; id validation with 0 upstream calls; stale detail and 502;
  - records (5), source with injected fetch (4), card catalog markers (2);
  - layer ownership (8): one point per gauge with floods on top, horizon culling, card and detail and external link, failed detail retried on reselection, SHOW MOST SEVERE, stale vs unavailable, a response after disable draws nothing, destroy releases the scene.
  - `layerStatusLocale.test.mjs` gains two cases for the row's translated states.
- **Mutation:** each change below was applied alone and turned its test red:
  - drop a failed region's previous gauges: "a failed region keeps its previous gauges and marks the snapshot stale" red;
  - disable the id check in the route and the store: "the detail route validates the id before any upstream call" red;
  - ignore a 429: "list requests stay inside the budget, and a 429 stops all asking" red.
- **Real app** (Vite, Chromium, live NWPS, 1440×900):
  - snapshot: 7/7 regions, 12,941 gauges, built in 83.4 s; the layer drew them 0.1 s after being switched on against the warm snapshot.
  - row: `12,941 gauges · 4 major · 6 moderate · 44 minor · 69 at action`; legend counts below flood stage 7,039, no flood stages 4,087, reading not current 1,006, out of service 615, below low-water 71.
  - major flooding at the time: Devils Lake and Eastern Stump Lake (ND), San Juan River at Farmington (NM), Moenkopi Wash near Tuba City (AZ).
  - the Farmington card read "San Juan River at Farmington · RIVER GAUGE · NWS FRMN5 · NM · Major flooding · Stage 14.07 ft · observed 10 hours ago · Forecast 13.55 ft · Major flooding · in 3 hours · Flood stages (ft): action 7 · minor 8.5 · moderate 10 · major 12 · Recent crest 7.28 ft on Jun 6, 2016 · Highest crest 12.3 ft on Sep 6, 1909 · USGS site 09365000".
  - no console errors other than the keyless Google tiles token 404/403.
  - an earlier design (27 boxes) built 12,744 gauges but the Hawaii and Caribbean boxes hit the 429; a 6-box design with two reads in flight got 504 on every CONUS column. Both shaped the final seven sequential boxes.

## Not in this PR

- A hydrograph (NWPS `stageflow` series) on the card.
- Voice context beyond the analyst fields.
- Tide stations NWPS lists as gauges are shown like any other gauge; their categories are NWPS's own.

title: feat(layers): add US Work Zones from state DOT WZDx feeds
body:
Adds **US Work Zones** (`work-zones`, 🚧), a keyless Movement layer of current work zones and detours read from US state and county DOT feeds in the [Work Zone Data Exchange](https://github.com/usdot-jpo-ode/wzdx) (WZDx) format. The app had no road-works layer for the United States.

This layer is **US-only WZDx**. Related regional road-event layers are open as #1079 (DriveBC Open511, British Columbia), #1090 (Traffic SA, South Australia) and #790 (QLDTraffic, Queensland). This PR does not depend on their code and does not touch Open511 or British Columbia. It follows the design those reviews settled: a server snapshot shared by clients, request coalescing, stale serving, body caps, geometry flattening with Douglas–Peucker simplification and vertex caps, roadworks drawn quieter than closures, colour meaning severity rather than speed, and the share token taken with `npm run layer-token:next`.

## Feeds

Eight feeds, fixed in `server/providers/wzdx.js`. The browser never names a feed or a URL. A feed is on the list only if it needs no key and states CC0 1.0 in its own header (`feed_info.license`), as the WZDx specification asks of public feeds. The URLs are those in the USDOT WZDx Feed Registry (data.transportation.gov `69qe-yiui`). That registry answers 403 to this machine, so I took the URLs from a public snapshot of it and probed each one live.

| Feed | Publisher (header) | WZDx | Licence (header) | Size | Time | Features → kept |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `mn.carsprogram.org/carsapi_v1/api/wzdx` | Minnesota DOT (CARS) | 4.0 | CC0 1.0 | 0.8 MB | 2.2–2.7 s | 405 → 394 |
| `in.carsprogram.org/carsapi_v1/api/wzdx` | Indiana DOT (CARS) | 4.0 | CC0 1.0 | 4.3 MB | 3.8–28.6 s | 1,166 → 1,054 |
| `kscars.kandrive.gov/carsapi_v1/api/wzdx` | Kansas DOT (CARS) | 4.0 | CC0 1.0 | 1.8 MB | 9–11 s | 383 → 358 |
| `travelfiles.dot.nd.gov/geojson_nc/wzdx_geojson.json` | North Dakota DOT | 4.0 | CC0 1.0 | 0.2 MB | 1.7–2.0 s | 71 → 33 |
| `filter.ritis.org/wzdx_v4.1/mdot.geojson` | Maryland DOT SHA | 4.1 | CC0 1.0 | 65 KB | 0.8 s | 59 → 59 |
| `storage.googleapis.com/kytc-its-2020-openrecords/…/kytc_wzdx_v4.1.geojson` | Kentucky Transportation Cabinet | 4.1 | CC0 1.0 | 0.4 MB | 0.4–1.6 s | 233 → 139 |
| `api.mdottraffic.com/prod/v3/data/wzdx` | Mississippi DOT | 4.2 | CC0 1.0 | 0.1 MB | 1.0–1.1 s | 122 → 122 |
| `wzdxapi.aztech.org/construction` | Maricopa County DOT (AZ) | 4.2 | CC0 1.0 | 3.1 MB | 3.2–3.5 s | 2,675 → 1,810 |

Sizes are uncompressed. Times are two curl runs on 24 Oct 2026 from a loaded machine. "Kept" is after dropping ended and far-future events.

**Probed and left out:**
- Keyless and live, but no licence statement in the feed header: Idaho, Arizona (ADOT), Nevada and Alaska (all Arcadis 511), Washington (WSDOT), and New Hampshire/Vermont/Maine (NE Compass).
- Florida: FL511 terms limit use to individual personal use.
- NJIT/TRANSCOM (New Jersey): CC0 and keyless, but a university research host. All 625 records are single points with `all-lanes-open`, and `road_names` holds cross-street text.
- Empty (`features: []`): Pennsylvania, Georgia, Louisiana and Connecticut (511 sites), and Louisiana DOTD.
- Last updated in February 2024 with every event ended: Hawaii (Blyncsy). New Mexico (Blyncsy) answered 503.
- Need a key: Oklahoma, Florida (one.network) and North Carolina. Texas and Ohio (OHGO) were not tried.
- No answer from this machine: Utah, Iowa (Q-Free), Wisconsin and City of Austin (all 403), Missouri (timeout), and Oregon (an empty 200 body).
- The 511NY and Virginia paths tried returned HTML.

## Request budget

- Upstream reads happen only while someone is using the layer. There is one read per feed per snapshot rebuild, and a rebuild runs at most every 5 minutes, so the most is 8 requests every 5 minutes for the whole server, however many clients.
- After a rebuild that leaves no data at all, nothing is read again for 60 s.
- Clients poll the same-origin route every 5 minutes. The route is rate-limited to 30 requests per minute per client.

## Behaviour

- **Server** (`/api/wzdx/events`, GET only, fixed path; anything else is 405 or 404, and query strings are ignored):
  - Each feed read has a 30 s timeout, a 16 MB body cap and `redirect: 'error'`.
  - Concurrent requests share one rebuild. An existing snapshot answers at once while a due rebuild runs behind it, so only the first request waits.
  - A failed feed keeps its last good events for 6 hours, marked `stale`. After that it is `unavailable` and its events go.
  - With no data at all the route answers 503 with `Retry-After`.
  - Per-feed failures leave the server only as fixed codes: `http_<status>`, `timeout`, `network`, `too_large`, `invalid` or `unsupported_version`. Transport text is never passed on.
  - The snapshot is sent gzipped when the client accepts it, with `X-Snapshot-Age`.
- **Normalisation** (`src/layers/workZones/records.js`, shared by the server and its tests):
  - Accepts WZDx 4.0 (`road_event_feed_info`), 4.1 and 4.2 (`feed_info`, or both headers). Any other version is refused, since 3.x has no `core_details`.
  - Drops events whose `end_date` has passed. Kentucky's feed had 94 ended events of 233, Maricopa 593 and North Dakota 37.
  - Drops events starting more than 7 days ahead (Maricopa 272, Indiana about 110). The layer shows what is on the road now and in the coming week.
  - A reused feature id (North Dakota and Kentucky both do this) becomes a second record with `#2`, instead of being lost.
  - Every GeoJSON geometry type is flattened, and every source vertex is validated: one bad vertex rejects the geometry.
  - Lines are Douglas–Peucker simplified at about 11 m and capped at 200 vertices per line, 8 lines and 600 vertices per event, and 60,000 vertices per snapshot. Past the snapshot cap an event keeps only its marker, and the row says so.
  - Text is stripped of tags, control and bidi characters, and bounded.
  - Each record holds id, feed, type, road names, direction, description, start, end, vehicle impact, worker presence, update time, a marker anchor and the lines.
- **Client** (`src/layers/workZones/`):
  - Lines are ground-clamped (`ClassificationType.BOTH`). Markers sit at the line midpoint, or at the first point for MultiPoint events.
  - Markers within 50 km of the camera draw over terrain. Further ones are depth-tested, so a continental view never shows markers through the globe.
  - Colour is lane impact, not speed: road closed red, lanes closed orange, alternating/flagging/temporary signal yellow, open or shifted lanes faint blue, impact not reported faint grey, detours violet and dashed. Open and unreported work is thinner and fainter, so long-running works do not bury the closures.
  - The legend has counts, and its blurb says that colour is not speed.
  - Card fields: road names; kind (WORK ZONE or DETOUR, UPCOMING, direction); impact; start and end through `formatDate`; worker presence when reported; the description wrapped as text, never markup; update age through `formatRelativeTime`; and "Publisher · WZDx".
  - The row reads `PARTIAL` with a feed line when a feed is stale or down ("7 feeds live · feed Kansas unreachable"). It reads `STALE` when no feed is live, or when a refresh fails and earlier events stay up. With nothing shown it reads `UNAVAILABLE`.
  - Errors reach the panel as fixed `translateFeedError` shapes: `WZDx HTTP <status>`, `WZDx rate limited`, `WZDx network error` and `Malformed WZDx response`.
  - Entities of unchanged events are kept across refreshes. A vanished selected event closes its card, and a changed one reopens it.
  - Only the selected event is registered as a context record.
  - Voice-off (`VOICE_OFF_LAYERS`), so the pinned voice schema is unchanged.

## Outside the layer

- **Share token:** `5`, from `npm run layer-token:next -- work-zones`. It is provisional: whichever layer PR merges first keeps `5`. The registry, catalog and ledger counts and digits in the token tests moved with it.
- **Credit:** a static "US work zones (WZDx, CC0 1.0)" entry lists the eight publishers in Data attribution.
- **Layer panel:** `US Work Zones` sits at the end of Movement, and the panel-order test is updated.
- **README:** the layer table gains a row. The sentence above it already undercounted the table, so it now reads "Twenty-four… Twenty-two", matching the table with this row; the test that pins the sentence is updated.
- **Docs:** `DATA_SOURCES.md` (feed row and notes) and `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md` (runtime table row and section) describe the layer.
- **i18n:** es, ru and zh-CN are complete (47 new messages).

## Tests

- **Unit tests (29):**
  - records (9), on trimmed real features from six of the feeds, covering 4.0, 4.1 and 4.2 (`src/layers/workZones/fixtures/`, CC0): 4.0/4.1/4.2 headers and refusal of 3.1 or a missing header, ended and far-future drops, duplicate ids, compact fields, simplification and caps, the per-event vertex budget, vertex validation across every geometry type, and text cleaning;
  - proxy (8, `src/data/wzdxProxy.test.mjs`): fixed keyless feed list; coalescing of three concurrent clients into one read per feed; GET and fixed path only, with a query unable to steer the upstream; a failed feed kept as stale and then expired; 503 with `Retry-After` and the 60 s backoff; fixed failure codes for size cap, version, status and network; gzip; the preview mount;
  - source (3): record re-checks, fixed error shapes translated under `es`, and abort;
  - layer ownership (9): band colours and widths, ground clamp, dashed detours, legend counts, card by marker or line, entity reuse, card reopen and close on refresh, partial, stale and unavailable states, a late response after disable.
- **Mutation:** each change below was applied alone and turned its tests red, then restored:
  - never dropping ended events (`end < now` made unreachable): 2 red;
  - a failed feed not keeping its previous events (`usable = fresh`): 1 red.

## Checks

- Full gate in a clean `node:24` container on `78be0eafb` with the changelog fragment added (`npm ci`): doctor, `format:check`, `check:boundaries`, `changelog:check` and build all pass. `i18n --check` reports es, ru and zh-CN at 2,728 messages, complete. `npm test` has 8,542 tests: 8,540 passed, 0 failed, 2 skipped.
- **`npm run test:track`**, paired and alternating with upstream main (`d48b9c4df`; this branch is on `9d3548c27`) on the same machine under load:

  | Round | upstream main | this branch |
  |---|---|---|
  | 1 | 108/1 (`military` arrival 500.3 ms) | 108/1 (`military` arrival 500.2 ms) |
  | 2 | 109/0 | 109/0 |

  The only failure is the 500 ms arrival-observation budget, and upstream main misses it in the same round.
- `npm run layer-token:check -- --base-ref upstream/main`: "Layer tokens valid against upstream/main: 31 published, 1 new."

## Live run

Vite dev server, real feeds, 24 Oct 2026, Chromium (SwiftShader), 1440×900.

- **Cold snapshot build:** 12.2 s for all eight feeds in parallel. 3,969 events, 22,356 line vertices, no lines dropped, all eight feeds `live`.
- **Payload:** 1,727,076 bytes plain and 249,921 bytes gzipped. A warm request answered in 3 ms.
- **Per feed:** Minnesota 394, Indiana 1,054, Kansas 358, North Dakota 33, Maryland 59, Kentucky 139, Mississippi 122, Maricopa County 1,810.
- **Legend:** road closed 157, lanes closed 453, alternating/flagging/signal 80, open or shifted 17, impact not reported 2,965, detours 297.
- **Route checks:** `POST /api/wzdx/events` gives 405; `/api/wzdx/feeds` gives 404.
- **In the app:** enabling the layer drew all 3,969 events 0.4 s after the request, with the row reading "8 feeds live". The browser received the snapshot gzipped.
- **Cards:**
  - Minneapolis: "I-394 · WORK ZONE · WESTBOUND · All lanes closed · Oct 24, 10:00 AM to Oct 24, 6:00 PM · Closed, Construction Work · Updated 2 days ago · Minnesota DOT · WZDx".
  - Indianapolis: "I-69 · WORK ZONE · SOUTHBOUND · Some lanes closed · Jul 21, 2026 to Jan 4, 2027 · …".
  - Phoenix: a Maricopa County event on N 7th St with workers present.
  - Under `?lang=es` the Minneapolis card read "OBRA VIAL · SENTIDO OESTE · Todos los carriles cerrados", and the row "8 fuentes en vivo".
- **Console:** the only errors were two keyless 404 resource loads not on `/api/wzdx`.

## Not done

- Voice and analyst queries: the layer is voice-off.
- Other states. Each feed left out above is out for a stated reason; a state can be added once it publishes a keyless feed that states CC0 in its header.
- WZDx 3.x is refused, because no configured feed uses it.
- Dates show in the viewer's time zone, not the work zone's.
- Many events carry `vehicle_impact: unknown` (2,965 of 3,969 today, most from Maricopa County and Indiana); they are drawn faint and grey, as reported.
- Not run: a check on Google Photorealistic 3D Tiles (no key on the test machine).

The changelog fragment is `changelog.d/1347-wzdx-work-zones.md`, in a second commit.

title: feat(layers): enrich EV Charging with Open Charge Map when a key is set
body:
Adds **Open Charge Map** (OCM) as an optional, keyed enrichment for the **EV Charging** layer. Stacked on #1329 (`feat/ev-charging-layer`); review that first.

OpenStreetMap tiles give a charging station's position and name, nothing more. OCM has connectors, power, operator and reported status for many of the same sites. It needs an API key, and its licence is set per record, so it comes in server-side and filtered.

## Key handling

- **Env var:** `OPEN_CHARGE_MAP_API_KEY`, server-side only, following the TomTom pattern.
  - The browser reads same-origin `/api/ocm/*` and never sees the key.
  - The proxy sends the key only in the `X-API-Key` header, so it appears in no URL, log line or response.
  - `.env.example` documents the variable.
- **POWER UP:** a new **OPEN CHARGE MAP** row (🟡 free tier). "GET KEY" links to `openchargemap.org/profile/applications`, where OCM's API docs say keys are issued: sign in, **my apps**, register an application.
  - Without a key the chip's "keys waiting" count goes up by one (10 → 11).
- **`server/providers/openChargeMap.js`** mounts `/api/ocm` in dev and preview:
  - `GET /api/ocm/status` returns `{hasKey}`.
  - `GET /api/ocm/poi?south=&west=&north=&east=` without a key returns 503 `{error:'no_key'}` and never calls upstream.
  - The route sits behind the same-site gate (`admitSameSite`), like `/api/tomtom`.
- **Proxy (SECURITY.md):**
  - Requires all four bounds as finite numbers inside the globe, with south < north and west < east.
  - Snaps the box outward to a 0.01° grid and refuses a box wider than 0.5° per side. A 16-tile z14 view is about 0.35°.
  - Builds the only upstream URL itself and forwards no other client parameter: `/v3/poi/?output=json&boundingbox=(N,W),(S,E)&maxresults=500&compact=true&verbose=false&opendata=true`. OCM documents the bounding box as top-left, then bottom-right.

## Licence handling

The filter runs on the server, per record:

- **Kept:** a site whose DataProvider has `IsOpenDataLicensed === true`.
- **Dropped:**
  - providers flagged `false` or `null`;
  - a provider id that `/v3/referencedata` does not list;
  - **Oplaadpalen.nl (provider 26)**: OCM flags it open, but its licence is CC BY-NC-SA 3.0, non-commercial. In the export, 101 of the 115 records around central Amsterdam are from this provider.
- **`opendata=true`:** also sent upstream. In OCM's source (`SearchFilterSettings.cs`, `POIManager.cs`) it filters on the same `IsOpenDataLicensed == true` test, but the server filter does not rely on it.
- **Reference data:** `compact=true` returns ids only. Providers, status types, operators and connector types resolve through `/v3/referencedata`, cached for a day. The provider's licence comes from that table, not from the POI.
- **Not forwarded:**
  - removed listings (status 200/210);
  - user comments, photos and contact details (never requested);
  - placeholder operators: "(Unknown Operator)", "(Business Owner at Location)", "(Private Residence/Individual)";
  - connector type 0 ("Unknown").
  - A charger whose operator is a private individual is shown without its street address.
- **Attribution:**
  - The card names the provider: "© Open Charge Map contributors · CC BY 4.0" for OCM's own records, else "{provider} via Open Charge Map · {licence}".
  - The licence label is shortened only when the text is recognised (CC BY 4.0/3.0, CC0, OGL, Licence Ouverte); otherwise the card shows no licence label.
  - Each provider shown is also registered in the Data attribution popover with OCM's full licence text and a link (`openChargeMapCredit` in `dataCredits.js`).
- **Excluded by id as well:** Mobie.pt (7, "Public Data redistributed by agreement"). The agreement is with OCM and does not pass to this application's users.
- **Kept but worth a look:** ICAEN (25, "General public data"). OCM flags it open, but it names no standard licence. Excluding it is a one-line change to `OCM_EXCLUDED_PROVIDER_IDS`.

## Politeness

OCM publishes no rate limit. Its API description asks callers not to repeat queries and to throttle. The proxy:

- caches each answer for 10 minutes per snapped box;
- shares one in-flight refresh per box (single-flight);
- serves the last answer for that box if a refresh fails;
- makes at most 30 POI requests a minute per process;
- returns at most 500 sites per read, and reports `saturated` when it hits that cap.

Upstream errors become fixed bodies carrying at most the upstream status number:

| Upstream result | Proxy answer |
|---|---|
| 403 | 502 `{error:'upstream', upstreamStatus:403}` |
| 429, or the local ceiling | 429 `{error:'rate_limited'}` |
| Timeout | 504 `{error:'timeout'}` |
| Network failure | 502 `{error:'network'}` |
| Malformed body | 502 `{error:'malformed'}` |

## Behaviour

**Without a key** (or with no `/api/ocm` route, as on a static host):

- Reads, markers, card, row and legend are exactly the keyless ones from #1329. The only addition is one `/api/ocm/status` request per session.
- A definitive "no" (200 `hasKey:false` or 404) is kept for the session. A transient failure is asked again at most once a minute.

**With a key:**

- **Request:** the same read asks `/api/ocm/poi` for the view box, alongside the tiles.
- **Matching (`merge.js`):**
  - An OCM site within 50 m of an OSM station enriches that station. Pairs are taken nearest first, and each station and each site is used at most once.
  - The station keeps its OSM id, name and position.
- **Card:** adds
  - operator;
  - status, with its last update date;
  - connectors grouped by type and power;
  - charge points;
  - cost;
  - the provider credit.
- **Unmatched sites** inside the view become amber stations of their own. Their card is headed "EV CHARGING · OPEN CHARGE MAP", and their context source is Open Charge Map.
- **Row and legend:**
  - The row source reads "OpenStreetMap + Open Charge Map".
  - The legend splits into "Charging stations" and "Open Charge Map only".
- **Status:** OCM status is what contributors or the provider last reported (`DateLastStatusUpdate`), not live occupancy, and the legend says so.

**When OCM fails:** the OSM read is unaffected.

- The stations render, and the row reads DEGRADED with one of the fixed forms `translateFeedError` already handles:
  - `Open Charge Map HTTP <status>`
  - `Open Charge Map rate limited`
  - `Open Charge Map network error`
  - `Malformed Open Charge Map response`
- An OSM failure still fails the read, whatever OCM answers.

## Tests

The fixtures are real records from `openchargemap/ocm-export` at `8e3bedca48ca` (exported 2026-04-22). They are six POIs (Oslo and Amsterdam, providers 1, 19 and 26) plus the matching `referencedata.json` rows. They are trimmed to the fields the proxy reads; user comments, media and contact details were removed. The source is noted in `server/providers/openChargeMapFixture.mjs`.

- **Proxy, `server/providers/openChargeMap.test.mjs` (17):**
  - URL building from the snapped box, with no key in it;
  - strict bbox validation (missing, empty, non-numeric, `Infinity`, inverted, out of range, too wide);
  - keyless status and 503, with no upstream call;
  - cross-site 403, POST 405, unknown paths 404, and a stray `url=` parameter that is not forwarded;
  - the key sent only as a header and absent from every response;
  - the licence filter: 7, 26, `false` (15), `null` (14), an unknown provider and a non-boolean flag, both as a predicate and through the route;
  - no comment, media or contact text in a trimmed site, and placeholder operators, unknown connector types and home addresses dropped;
  - cache per snapped box, single-flight and serve-stale;
  - each failure form, with no upstream text in the body;
  - a reference-data 403;
  - the 30-a-minute ceiling;
  - `saturated`;
  - the plugin mounted once.
- **Client, `src/layers/evCharging/openChargeMap.test.mjs` (11):**
  - merge: inside and outside the threshold, one-to-one with the nearest pair winning, band edges;
  - no key: deep-equal to the plain OSM read for a keyless server, a 404 host, a network failure and a 500;
  - a wide view makes no request;
  - matched and unmatched sites, and sites outside the view filtered out;
  - each OCM failure form keeps the OSM records;
  - an OSM failure still fails the read;
  - a key removed while running;
  - abort;
  - status retry.
- **Layer, `ownership.test.mjs` (+4):**
  - without a key, the layer, row, card, credits and selection are deep-equal between the real source with and without a keyless OCM client;
  - the enriched card, the OCM-only card, colours, credits, legend and row source;
  - a failed OCM read is degraded with the stations kept;
  - OCM-only views keep the OSM credit off.
- **`layerStatusLocale.test.mjs`:** `Open Charge Map rate limited` is translated in es and ru.
- **Mutation:** each change below was applied alone and turned its tests red; the baseline is 52 passing.

  | Mutation | Tests red |
  |---|---|
  | Accept `IsOpenDataLicensed` null | 2 |
  | Drop the provider-26 exclusion | 4 |
  | Skip the server licence filter | 4 |
  | Forward without a key (server) | 1 |
  | Ignore the status answer (client) | 3 |
  | Do not keep a definitive "no" | 3 |
  | Let an OCM error fail the read | 1 |
  | Matching not one-to-one | 1 |
  | Key in the URL | 2 |

## Checks

- **Full gate:** run in a clean `node:24` container on `99d1b63f7`, after merging #1329 with `main` `9d3548c27` (`npm ci`). For that run only, the changelog fragment was renamed to a numbered name.
  - `doctor`, `format:check`, `check:boundaries`, `changelog:check` and `build` all pass.
  - `i18n --check` reports es, ru and zh-CN complete at 2714 messages.
  - `npm test`: 8569 passed, 0 failed (8350 on `7fe10b570` and 8349 on `ef26cd2f4`, before the merges).
  - The two allocation probes each pass (1/1 and 14/14).
- **Feature gates** against a Vite dev server on `ef26cd2f4` (no OCM key, Chromium):
  - `scripts/qa-layer-panel.mjs`: `RESULT: 0 failures`.
  - `scripts/qa-application.mjs`: startup, data registration, annotations and visible attribution pass; teardown releases its owners with no late browser errors.
  - `scripts/qa-attribution-b12.mjs`: 23 passed, 1 failed. The failure is the console check, on a 404 from `/api/google/tiles-token`; this machine has no Google key. Upstream main (`d48b9c4df`, the base of #1329) fails the same check on the same 404, 23/1.

- **`npm run test:track`**, paired and alternating with upstream main (`d48b9c4df`) on the same machine under load:

  | Round | upstream main | this branch |
  |---|---|---|
  | 1 | 108/1 (`military` arrival 500.3 ms) | 108/1 (`flights` arrival 500.2 ms) |
  | 2 | 109/0 | 108/1 (`military` arrival 586.3 ms) |

  The only failures are the 500 ms arrival-observation budget, which upstream main also misses. No other case fails.

## Real app

Both runs used Vite in `node:24`, Chromium (SwiftShader), live OpenFreeMap tiles, a 1.5 km camera height and a 1440×900 viewport.

- **No key (`npx vite`, the dev server that hosts `/api/*`):**
  - `/api/ocm/status` → `{"hasKey":false}`.
  - `/api/ocm/poi` → 503 `{"error":"no_key"}`.
  - A bad box → 400 `invalid_bbox`; a 1° box → 400 `bbox_too_large`.
  - Oslo showed 106 stations ("106 nearby"), and Amsterdam 380.
  - The row read "OpenStreetMap · community mapped" and the card was unchanged ("EV CHARGING · OSM MAPPED · … · © OpenStreetMap contributors").
  - The only OCM request was the one `/api/ocm/status`.
  - POWER UP showed the OPEN CHARGE MAP row with its `OPEN_CHARGE_MAP_API_KEY` field.
- **With a key against a stub upstream:**
  - Setup: the same Vite server with the proxy constructed over a stub `fetchImpl` (its test seam; no user-facing setting). The stub served the ocm-export records for Norway and the Netherlands and ignored `opendata`, so only the server filter decided.
  - Oslo: the stub returned 141 records. The view showed 106 OSM stations (31 enriched) plus 68 Open Charge Map–only sites.
  - Amsterdam: the stub returned 115 records, 101 of them Oplaadpalen.nl. With those dropped, 3 stations were enriched and 6 sites were added.
  - The OCM-only card read: "OnePark Oslo S · EV CHARGING · OPEN CHARGE MAP · Charge & Drive (Fortum - NO) · Jernbanetorget 1, Oslo · Operational · updated 2016-06-22 · 2× Type 2 (Socket Only) 12 kW · 4× … 36 kW · 2× … 7 kW · 8 charge points · … · © Open Charge Map contributors · CC BY 4.0".
  - The popover credited NOBIL, Open Charge Map Contributors and PowerGo with their licence texts.
  - The stub log shows every upstream call carried the key as a header and never in the URL. Repeat reads of a view were served from the proxy cache.

## Not verified

- No live Open Charge Map call was made: there is no key on this machine. The proxy's request shape (`X-API-Key` header, `boundingbox` corner order, `compact=true` field names, `/v3/referencedata` layout) follows OCM's OpenAPI description (`ocm-docs/Model/schema/ocm-openapi-spec.yaml`) and the export records. It has not been confirmed against the live API.
- How many sites carry automated live status (10/20) is unknown; the card treats every status as reported, not live.
- The 50 m matching threshold was checked on the exported Oslo and Amsterdam data only.
- `scripts/setup-doctor.mjs`, `dev-fresh.sh` and the Pinokio environment lists do not name the new key; Vite's `loadEnv` and POWER UP pick it up.

The changelog fragment is `changelog.d/1348-ev-open-charge-map.md`.

title: fix(cyclones): label NHC classification codes by their published meanings
body:
## Summary
The cyclone layer shows `PTC` as "Potential tropical cyclone". NHC uses `PTC` for a **post-tropical** cyclone (remnants) and `PC` for a potential tropical cyclone. So a storm that is falling apart is shown as one that has not formed yet. The map also expects `SS`/`SD` for subtropical systems, but NHC sends `STS`/`STD`, so real subtropical storms and depressions show the bare code.

NHC's [Tropical Cyclone Status JSON File Reference](https://www.nhc.noaa.gov/productexamples/NHC_Tropical_Cyclone_Status_JSON_File_Reference.pdf) lists the `classification` values as `TD`, `STD`, `TS`, `HU`, `STS`, `PTC - Post-tropical Cyclone / Remnants`, `TY` (unused) and `PC - Potential Tropical Cyclone`. The server passes the code through unchanged (`text(raw.classification, 16)` in `server/providers/cyclones.js`), so this map decides what the row and list show. NHC's [live JSON sample](https://www.nhc.noaa.gov/productexamples/NHC_JSON_Sample.json) carries Hilary (`ep092023`) as `PTC` while it was post-tropical over California.

## Change
- `PTC` -> "Post-tropical cyclone", new `PC` -> "Potential tropical cyclone".
- `SS`/`SD` -> `STS`/`STD`, keeping the existing labels.
- Unknown codes still display unchanged.
- Added the one new message to `es`, `ru` and `zh-CN`.

## Test
`src/layers/cyclones/index.test.mjs`, `classification display expands known codes…`, now uses the NHC codes.

On main `9d3548c2`, with the test change applied: the test fails (`PTC` renders " · Potential tropical cyclone · ", `actual: false, expected: true`). On this branch it passes.

- `node scripts/i18n.mjs`: es/ru/zh-CN 2682 messages, complete
- `prettier --check` on the two changed JS files: clean
- `git diff --check`: clean

I couldn't run the full `npm test` / `npm run build` / `npm run test:track` locally (the disk is full, so `npm ci` fails). I ran the cyclone test files with a stand-in Cesium module. The only other failures are two `rendering.test.mjs` cases that need real Cesium, and they fail the same way on main. CI covers the unit suite and build.

title: fix(cyclones): convert NHC movement speed from mph to knots
body:
## Summary
`parseCycloneStatus` stores NHC's `movementSpeed` as `movement.speedKt`. NHC publishes that field in **miles per hour**, while `intensity` is in knots. So every storm's forward speed is about 15% too high under a knots label. The cyclone query tool returns `movement` as-is (`src/tools/queries/environment.js`), so AI and MCP clients get the wrong number.

NHC's [Tropical Cyclone Status JSON File Reference](https://www.nhc.noaa.gov/productexamples/NHC_Tropical_Cyclone_Status_JSON_File_Reference.pdf) defines `"movementSpeed": 9, // Present storm movement speed (miles per hour)` and `"intensity": 125, // Present storm intensity (knots)`. Irma's sample record (`movementDir: 280, movementSpeed: 9`) matches the public advisory of the time: "moving toward the west near 9 mph".

## Change
Convert at parse time with `Math.round(mph * 0.868976)`, so `speedKt` holds whole knots like `windKt`. The existing 0–200 bound still applies to the raw value. A missing or invalid speed is still `null`.

## Test
`src/data/cyclonesProxy.test.mjs`, `status retains official clocks, knots, …`: the fixture's `movementSpeed: 12` (mph) now expects `speedKt: 10`.

On main `9d3548c2`, with only the test change: `actual: { directionDegrees: 255, speedKt: 12 }`, `expected: { … speedKt: 10 }`. On this branch: 13 tests, 0 failures.

`prettier --check` on both files is clean, and `git diff --check` is clean. I couldn't run the full `npm test` / build locally because the disk is full and `npm ci` fails. CI runs both.

title: fix(ais): keep a tracked vessel's motion when static data arrives
body:
## Summary
When a `ShipStaticData` or `StaticDataReport` message arrives for a vessel already on the map, `ingestAisStreamEnvelope` merges the static fields and then falls through into the position path. That path rebuilds the whole row from the static message:
- speed, course and heading become `null`, because static messages carry none of them;
- `last_position_UTC` / `last_position_epoch` move forward to the static message's time, although no new fix arrived.

The fall-through happens because AISStream's `MetaData` repeats the last known position on **every** message. Its [documentation](https://aisstream.io/documentation) says `MetaData` "contains normalized AIS context such as MMSI and last known position". So the "positionless static record" early return never fires. Both static types are in `AISSTREAM_DEFAULT_MESSAGE_TYPES` (`ais-live.js`). Class A ships send static data every 6 minutes, and Class B ships send a position only every 30 s to 3 min. Until the next position report, the vessel card shows no speed or heading and a position time that is really the static message's time.

## Change
After merging the static fields, return early when the vessel already has a live row. A vessel first seen through static data still gets its row as before.

## Test
New case in `src/data/aisStreamSentinels.test.mjs`: a position report (12.4 kn, 86.7°, heading 87) followed five minutes later by `ShipStaticData` with the same MetaData position.

On main `9d3548c2`: `a static data report keeps the motion and fix time of a tracked vessel` fails with `actual: null, expected: 12.4`. On this branch: 6 tests, 0 failures. The destination and IMO from the static report still merge in.

`node --test src/data/aisStream*.test.mjs`: all pass. `prettier --check` on both files is clean, and so is `git diff --check`.

I couldn't run the full `npm test` / build / `test:track` locally because the disk is full and `npm ci` fails. `src/tools/queries/maritime.test.mjs` needs `node_modules`, so it fails to load the same way on main. CI covers the unit suite.

title: fix(cockpit): read a rounded-north destination heading as 000
body:
The destination bearing rounded 359.6° to 360° and printed "360°". The compass tape already wraps that same rounding to 000.

The destination readout now uses the same 000–359 range. 359.6° reads "000°", and 359.4° stays "359°".

`node --test src/cockpitMath.test.mjs`

On main, `Math.round(359.6)` displays `360`. The new case expects `000` and passes after this change.

Maintainer follow-up: documented heading wrapping in `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md`. Validation: full unit suite and build passed; production cockpit DOM checks passed four bearings and invalid-route hiding. Tracking passed 109/109 on an unchanged repeat after one 500.2 ms arrival-timing timeout; unchanged-main control also passed 109/109. The broader cockpit utility checks passed their behavioral assertions but reported a keyless `/api/google/tiles-token` 404, also reproduced on unchanged main.

title: fix(transit): count a 90-second report as one minute
body:
A transit card kept ages in seconds through 89s, then rounded 90 seconds up to two minutes. A report a minute and a half old read "Reported 2 min ago".

Whole minutes now start at 90 seconds, so that card reads "Reported 1 min ago". A report at 120 seconds still reads "Reported 2 min ago", and 89 seconds stays in seconds.

`node --test src/layers/transit/selectionCopy.i18n.test.mjs`

The new case fails on main (`Reported 2 min ago`) and passes after this change.

Maintainer follow-up: documented the rounded-second threshold in `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md`. Validation: full unit suite and build passed; tracking 109/109; 32 rendered report-age cases passed across four locales and two camera angles. The broader transit thermal-sprite coverage check was unexercised (five visible sprites versus six required); that unrelated coverage requirement is not a blocker for this text-formatting change.

title: fix(firms): drop the decimal when fire power rounds to 10 MW
body:
A fire at 9.96 MW was labeled "10.0 MW". The card switches to a whole number at 10 MW, but the cutoff ran before one-decimal rounding, so 9.96 kept a decimal that rounds to 10.

The digit count now follows the rounded value. 9.96 MW reads "10 MW", 9.94 MW stays "9.9 MW", and existing whole values such as 1520 MW and 210 MW are unchanged.

`node --test src/data/firmsLabels.test.mjs`

`formatFrpMw(9.96)` is `10.0` with the previous cutoff and `10` after this change. The card title assertion is in `src/data/firmsCards.test.mjs`.

Maintainer follow-up: documented the display-rounding rule in `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md`. Validation: full unit suite and build passed; tracking 109/109; FIRMS fixture feature gate 8/8 (keyless, software rendering).

title: feat(layers): add the Parking layer from MobiData BW ParkAPI
body:
Adds **Parking** (`parking`, 🅿️), a keyless Infrastructure layer with car parks and garages from MobiData BW's public ParkAPI v3, including live free spaces where the operator reports them. Free parking near a destination is a basic smart-city question, and the app had no layer for it.

## Source and licence

- **ParkAPI v3** at `api.mobidata-bw.de/park-api/api/public/v3`, read browser-direct like EV Charging. It is keyless and answers `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`, so there is no server proxy.
  - `/v3/parking-sites` with a bounding box, `purpose=CAR`, `not_type=ON_STREET`, `limit=500`. ParkAPI merges duplicates by default.
  - `/v3/sources`, read at most twice a day, gives the contributor each source asks to be named (for example "Stadt Karlsruhe"). Most sources name none. If this read fails, sites are shown without a contributor.
- **Licence:** the dataset [Gebündelte Daten Parkplätze und Parkbauten Baden-Württemberg](https://www.mobidata-bw.de/dataset/gebuendelte-parkdaten-bw) is published under Datenlizenz Deutschland – Namensnennung 2.0 (dl-de/by-2-0); I checked the dataset page. The ParkAPI backend is MIT ([mobidata-bw/park-api-v3](https://github.com/mobidata-bw/park-api-v3)).
- **Attribution:**
  - "MobiData BW · ParkAPI (dl-de/by-2-0)" goes into the Data attribution popover once sites show (`PARKING_CREDIT`, registered on demand like the TomTom credit).
  - Every card ends with "MobiData BW · ParkAPI, dl-de/by-2-0", plus the source's contributor where it names one.
- **Coverage:** the sources MobiData BW bundles, mostly Baden-Württemberg (Stuttgart, Karlsruhe, Freiburg, Heidelberg, Mannheim…), plus some truck parking across Germany. Elsewhere the API returns no items, and the row says `No ParkAPI coverage in this view` instead of looking broken.

## What the API looks like (probed before writing)

- `limit` is capped at 1,000 (a larger value is refused with a 400). Without `limit`, a central Freiburg box returned 1,989 CAR sites (1.35 MB), 1,946 of them `ON_STREET` kerbside segments. That is why on-street sites are excluded and every read sets a limit.
- `lat`/`lon` came back as JSON numbers in every sample. The decoder also accepts decimal strings, because the task notes and some ParkAPI versions publish them that way.
- In a Stuttgart city box: 79 CAR sites without on-street, 32 of them live. Karlsruhe: 49 sites, 22 live.
- `has_realtime_data` is ParkAPI's own freshness verdict. With its default `calculate_has_realtime_data`, readings older than 30 minutes (pull sources) or 24 hours (push sources) come back as `false` but keep their old `realtime_*` fields. The layer shows a free count only when the flag is `true`.
- `realtime_data_updated_at` in Stuttgart spread over about six minutes at the time of probing, so the layer polls every five minutes.

## What it shows

- **Points:** coloured by the share of spaces free, read against `realtime_capacity` when published, else `capacity`:
  - green at 30% or more free;
  - amber at 10–30%;
  - red under 10%;
  - grey when there is no live count, so a static capacity never reads as availability.

  Points are sized by capacity (7–13 px) and turn white when selected.
- **Card:** a click or **SHOW NEAREST** opens a card with:
  - the name as published (unnamed sites read "Parking site");
  - the type (underground garage, multi-storey car park, surface car park);
  - free of total, or capacity with "NO LIVE COUNT";
  - the reading's age (`formatCockpitBriefAge`);
  - disabled and charging space counts from `restrictions`;
  - operator, address and the credit line.
- **OPERATOR PAGE** opens the selected site's `public_url` in a new tab. Only `http(s)` links are kept.
- **Selection:** a poll that keeps the selected site refreshes its card in place (`refreshTrackedReadout`). A read without it closes the card, as in the EV Charging fix, and `clearRendered` closes it too.
- **Legend:** four rows with counts. The row reads `121 sites · 33 live`. `getStats().observedAt` is the newest operator reading among the sites shown, not the fetch time.

## How it loads

- **View box:** as in EV Charging, a box around the ground at the screen centre, sized by camera range.
- **Wide views:** a view more than 0.4° across (about 44 km) shows "Zoom in to load parking sites" before any request.
- **Caching:** boxes snap outward to a 0.02° grid, and a read is reused for 60 s, so panning within a cell makes no request.
- **Saturation:** a read that matched more sites than it returned keeps them and says "Coverage limited — zoom in". ParkAPI orders by id, not distance, so the layer does not claim the nearest were kept.
- **Polling:** the layer polls every five minutes itself, with `updateInterval: 0`. With a manager interval, the manager does not tick the row's stats, and the live drive showed the row stuck on the first city's count after the camera moved. ALPR uses the same `updateInterval: 0` pattern.
- **Errors:** the fixed forms `translateFeedError` already handles: `ParkAPI HTTP <status>`, `ParkAPI rate limited`, `ParkAPI network error` (also the 15 s timeout) and `Malformed ParkAPI response`. Sites already shown stay up as stale.
- **Voice:** `parking` joins `SELF_EVIDENT_IDS` (it is the spoken word), so it adds no alias hint. The runner still accepts "car parks", "parking garages" and "parking lots".

## Outside the layer

- **Share token:** `5`, from `npm run layer-token:next -- parking` on `main`.
  - The pinned counts and ledger fixtures moved with it: registry 31 → 32, catalog 32 → 33, ledger digits.
  - EV Charging (#1329), River Flood Gauges (#1346) and US Work Zones (#1347) also hold a provisional `5`. Whichever merges first keeps it; the others rerun the helper.
- **Voice digests:** the two pinned voice digests are re-derived.
- **Prompt budget:** the point-and-ask prompt budget (`pointAndAsk.test.mjs`) moves from 52,000 to 52,100 characters.
  - `main` sits at 51,972. Even with no alias hint, the new id lands in three generated layer enums (30 characters), giving 52,002.
  - The alternative is `context: false`, which saves 10 characters and fits, but drops `parking` from `get_entity_context`'s layer filter. Happy to switch if you prefer to keep the ceiling.
- **Source registration:** in `src/standalone/layerSources.js`, next to ALPR.
- **README count:** the README sentence above the layer table undercounted it ("Twenty… Eighteen" for 23 rows, 21 keyless). It now reads "Twenty-four… Twenty-two" with this row, and the test that pins it follows. #1329, #1346 and #1347 make the same correction for their own rows; each one merged after the first bumps it by one.
- **Docs:** `DATA_SOURCES.md` (table row and request policy) and `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md` describe the layer and its limits.

## Checks

- Full gate in a clean `node:24` container on `a0383f830` (`npm ci`):
  - doctor, `format:check`, `check:boundaries`, `changelog:check` and build pass;
  - `i18n --check` reports es, ru and zh-CN at 2711 messages, complete;
  - `npm test`: 8,548 tests, 8,546 pass, 0 fail, 2 skipped.
- **Unit tests (35)** in `src/layers/parking/`:
  - records (8): live vs outdated counts, string positions, link filtering, occupancy bands, page and contributor decoding;
  - source (10): zoom-in with 0 requests, exact query, grid reuse and TTL, saturation, empty coverage, contributor failure, each error form, timeout, abort;
  - layer ownership (17): colours, empty state, late response after disable, superseded read, zoom-in clears the card, stale vs unavailable, card lines, in-place refresh, vanished selection, another layer's selection, SHOW NEAREST, OPERATOR PAGE, own poll, destroy and re-init.
- **Mutation:** each change below was applied alone and turned its tests red: `disable` leaving the poll timer running (caught after the test re-enables the layer), ignoring `has_realtime_data`, dropping `not_type=ON_STREET`, removing the vanished-selection close, and forcing saturation to false.
- **`npm run test:track`**, paired and alternating with upstream main (`d48b9c4df`; this branch is on `9d3548c27`) on the same machine under load:

  | Round | upstream main | this branch |
  |---|---|---|
  | 1 | 108/1 (`military` arrival 500.3 ms) | 108/1 (`military` arrival 500.3 ms) |
  | 2 | 108/1 (`military` arrival 500.3 ms) | 109/0 |

  The only failure is the 500 ms arrival-observation budget, which upstream main missed in both rounds.
- **Feature gates:** `scripts/qa-layer-panel.mjs` against a Vite dev server: 11 checks pass, 0 failures. `scripts/qa-application.mjs --url <vite>`: both checks pass.
- **Real app** (Vite, Chromium with SwiftShader, live ParkAPI, 3.5 km camera height, 1440×900):

  | View | Sites | Live | Row |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | Stuttgart centre | 121 | 33 | `121 sites · 33 live` |
  | Karlsruhe centre | 61 | 22 | `61 sites · 22 live` (17 green, 3 amber, 2 red) |
  | London | 0 | 0 | `No ParkAPI coverage in this view` |
  | Stuttgart from 60 km | 0 | 0 | `Zoom in to load parking sites`, no request |

  - Clicking Züblin opened "Züblin · PARKING · MULTI-STOREY CAR PARK · 352 FREE OF 376 · LIVE · UPDATED 0M AGO · 11 DISABLED SPACES · 63 CHARGING SPACES · Park Service Hüfner GmbH+Co.KG · Lazarettstraße 5 · MobiData BW · ParkAPI, dl-de/by-2-0", with both chips enabled.
  - The journey made one `/sources` request and one `/parking-sites` request per city.
  - The only failing responses were the keyless `/api/google/tiles-token` 404s.
  - After flying from Stuttgart to Karlsruhe, the tracked overlay source held 0 entries. The old card's pixels stayed on screen until the camera next moved, because the DETECT callout lane replays its last solve while the view is still (`src/data/detection.js`). This looks like existing detection behaviour rather than this layer; I saw it under SwiftShader and did not check it on a GPU.

The changelog fragment is `changelog.d/1355-parking-layer.md`, in a later commit.

title: feat(layers): add the River discharge outlook layer from Open-Meteo Flood (GloFAS)
body:
Adds **River discharge outlook** (`river-discharge`, 🌊), a keyless Weather layer: 187 points on 110 major rivers worldwide, each coloured by the GloFAS 7-day river-discharge forecast against that point's own reanalysis flow. It is the global, modelled complement to gauge-based flood layers: it shows where the model expects a river to run unusually high, not where a river is flooding or a warning is in force.

## Source, licence and terms

- **Open-Meteo Flood API** (`flood-api.open-meteo.com/v1/flood`): keyless, CORS `*`, multi-location; GloFAS v4 (Copernicus Emergency Management Service) at 0.05°.
- **Licence:** Open-Meteo data is [CC BY 4.0](https://open-meteo.com/en/licence) with a linked credit beside displayed data; GloFAS data falls under the [CEMS-FLOODS licence](https://cds.climate.copernicus.eu/licences/cems-floods), which asks for "Contains modified Copernicus Emergency Management Service information [year]" when the data is changed (the percentiles are).
- **Terms:** the free API is **non-commercial**, limited to 600 / 5,000 / 10,000 calls per minute / hour / day ([terms](https://open-meteo.com/en/terms)). DATA_SOURCES carries a note in the style of the Google News one: a commercial deployment needs Open-Meteo's paid API or must remove the layer.
- **Call weight:** Open-Meteo counts a location as max(1, max(v/10, v/10 × days/14)), summed over locations (`calculateQueryWeight` in open-meteo/open-meteo `ForecastApiResult.swift`; it matches the pricing page's 1.5 and 3.0 examples, and a unit test pins it).
- **Natural Earth** 10m `rivers_lake_centerlines` (public domain), pinned by commit and SHA-256 like the other Natural Earth packs.

## The design problem, and what the probe showed

The API gives discharge numbers, not flood thresholds, and point queries only. Two things had to hold before building.

- **Snapping is needed, and a 3×3 neighbourhood is enough on major rivers.** The docs say the API returns "the largest river within 5 km". It does not: on six hand-placed points (Mississippi at Vicksburg, Danube at Vienna, Rhine at Cologne, Amazon at Óbidos, Ganges at Farakka, Elbe at Dresden), the nearest cell averaged 0.4–2.4 m³/s in five cases. The largest mean in the 3×3 block of cell centres found the main stem every time (28,331 / 2,001 / 1,673 / 276,004 / 6,023 / 342 m³/s over Mar–Jul 2022).
- **Full history is not affordable; ten years is.** Data before mid-1997 is null for v4 (the docs say 1984). One daily variable costs 1 call per 140 days per location, so 1984–2022 would be about 100 calls a point, and 1,000 points about 100,000 calls (ten days of the free quota). Ten years (2012-08-01 to 2022-07-31, the end of the v4 reanalysis) cost 26.09 a point, plus 9 for snapping.

## How the points were built

`scripts/build-river-discharge-points.mjs` is run by maintainers, never by the app.

- **Sampling:** named `River` features at scalerank ≤ 5, a point every 800 km and none within 400 km of another: 196 candidates.
- **Snapping:** each candidate's 3×3 cell centres over 140 days (9 calls); the largest mean wins. 9 were dropped because no cell reached 10 m³/s (for example the Amur near its mouth and the Mackenzie and inner Niger deltas). Only 12 of the 187 kept the nearest cell.
- **Climatology:** p50 / p90 / p99, mean and maximum of every day of the ten-year window (NumPy-style percentiles; 90% of days required).
- **Budget:** 6,642 weighted calls in about 75 minutes, paced at ≤ 300 a minute and ≤ 3,500 an hour. Every answer is cached outside the repository, so a run stopped by `--max-weight` or a 429 resumes without repeating calls.
- **Pack:** `src/data/local_data/river_discharge/points.json` (24 KB), with a README stating the parameters, sources and cost.
- **Spot checks** against known rivers look right for the model: lower Mississippi mean 22,379 m³/s, lower Congo 24,550, lower Paraná 21,842, lower Volga 7,434.
  - **Mis-snap:** one Mekong point (12.9°N) averages 106 m³/s, so its 3×3 block missed the main channel.
  - **Model bias:** the Nile below Aswan averages about 11,400 m³/s, about four times what the regulated river carries. GloFAS does not model that dam's operation. The forecast it is compared with carries the same bias, so the colour stays consistent with the model, but the number is not the river's real flow.

## Runtime

- **Proxy:** `/api/river-discharge?south&west&north&east` (`server/providers/riverDischarge.js`) takes exactly four plain decimals and nothing else (400 otherwise).
  - It selects bundled points in the box and reads them at their cell centres: six daily variables, `past_days=1`, `forecast_days=8`, `models=seamless_v4`, in batches of 50.
  - That costs **one weighted call per point**, so refreshing the whole set costs 187.
  - It never forwards a client URL or coordinate (SECURITY.md).
- **Cache:** each point is held for 3 hours (GloFAS publishes daily) and served marked stale for up to 36 hours.
  - Concurrent views share one read per point.
  - A 429 cools the upstream down for its `Retry-After`; a failure cools it for 60 s.
  - An own ceiling of 600 weighted calls an hour applies.
  - If nothing can be shown, the proxy answers 503 with `Retry-After`; a view with no points answers 200 with an empty list.
- **Layer:** it sends the visible rectangle (the whole world when the view leaves the globe). The full set fits one bounded request, so there is no zoom-in state.
  - **Classification:** it takes the highest `river_discharge` day over seven days from the proxy's UTC today. Below p90 is blue, at or above p90 amber, at or above p99 red.
  - **Far side:** points beyond the horizon are hidden by an ellipsoid occluder, because the app usually hides Cesium's globe, as the FIRMS layer notes.
  - **Refresh:** camera moves drive the reads, and the layer's own 30-minute poll refreshes the view. `updateInterval` stays 0, because `DataLayerManager` ticks a row's stats every second only for a layer without an interval; with one, the row's point count stayed on the first view until the next poll.
- **Card:** river name (Natural Earth), forecast peak and day, today's value, the ensemble's middle half and highest member on the peak day (left out when the members do not disagree), the point's 2012–2022 percentiles, the line "Model outlook, not an observed flood or an official warning", and the source.
- **Credit:** the linked "River discharge data by Open-Meteo.com · Contains modified Copernicus Emergency Management Service information 2026" sits on the globe credit line while points are shown, and an entry is added to the Data attribution popover.
- **Errors:** fixed `translateFeedError` forms: `Open-Meteo HTTP <status>`, `Open-Meteo rate limited`, `Open-Meteo network error`, `Malformed Open-Meteo response`. Points already shown stay up as stale.
- **i18n:** complete in es, ru and zh-CN.

## Outside the layer

- **Share token:** `5`, from `npm run layer-token:next -- river-discharge`. Registry, catalog and ledger fixtures moved with it (31 → 32, 32 → 33). `layer-token:check --base-ref upstream/main`: "31 published, 1 new". Other open layer PRs claim the same provisional token, so whichever merges second takes the next one.
- **Voice:** not reachable. The layer is listed in `VOICE_OFF_LAYERS`, because even an alias-free manifest entry put the Realtime prompt at 52,026 characters against the 52,000 ceiling in `src/voice/pointAndAsk.test.mjs` (the base is just under it). The pinned voice digests are therefore unchanged.
- **README count:** the sentence above the layer table undercounted it. With this row the table has 24 layers, 22 keyless, and the sentence and its pin in `transitQa.test.mjs` now say so.
- **Docs:** `DATA_SOURCES.md` (live row, bundled row, note), `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md`, `README.md`.

## Checks

- **Gate:** clean `node:24` container on a detached copy of `27b607ae2` (`npm ci`), with the changelog fragment renamed to a numbered placeholder in the copy only: doctor, `format:check`, `check:boundaries`, `changelog:check` and build pass. `i18n --check` reports es, ru and zh-CN at 2702 messages, complete. `npm test`: 8548 tests, 8546 passed, 0 failed (2 skipped); the two serialized allocation probes pass, 1/1 and 14/14.
- **`npm run test:track`**, paired and alternating with upstream main (`d48b9c4df`; this branch is on `9d3548c27`) on the same machine under load:

  | Round | upstream main | this branch |
  |---|---|---|
  | 1 | 108/1 (`military` arrival 500.3 ms) | 108/1 (`military` arrival 500.1 ms) |
  | 2 | 108/1 (`military` arrival 500.3 ms) | 109/0 |

  The only failure is the 500 ms arrival-observation budget, which upstream main missed in both rounds.
- **Feature gates** against a Vite dev server on `27b607ae2` (Chromium): `scripts/qa-layer-panel.mjs` gives `RESULT: 0 failures`; `scripts/qa-application.mjs` passes startup and teardown; `scripts/qa-ui-disposal.mjs` passes every case.
- **Unit tests (35 new, plus 2 status-text cases):**
  - build helpers (8): cell centres, neighbourhood and wrap, snapping choice, percentiles, coverage, rounding, the weight formula, river sampling;
  - records (6): point validation, antimeridian boxes, series normalisation, level, peak window and today, stale series;
  - proxy (11): box grammar, the upstream URL, batching 120 points as 50/50/20, box selection and freshness, coalescing, stale then gone, 503 with `Retry-After` and 429 cooldown, partial rows, the hourly ceiling, 405/404/400/429;
  - client source (4);
  - layer (6): colours and credit, the card, stale on failure and clean disable, far-side cull, the no-spread card, the poll armed on enable and released on disable with `updateInterval` 0;
  - status texts translated in es/ru: 2 cases added to `layerStatusLocale.test.mjs`.
- **Mutation:** each change below was applied alone, turned its tests red, and was then restored:
  - p99 never reached: 1 records and 2 layer tests red;
  - proxy ignores freshness: 1 red;
  - snapping keeps the nearest cell: 1 red;
  - far-side cull disabled: 1 red;
  - poll not cleared on disable: 1 red;
  - `updateInterval` back to 30 minutes: 1 red.
- **Real app** (Vite dev server in `node:24`, Chromium/SwiftShader, live Open-Meteo, 1440×900, 2026-10-24):
  - Global view: 187 points; 1 above p99, 8 above p90, 178 below.
  - **Negro** (39.7°S 65.4°W), red. Its card: "7-day forecast peak 1,636 m³/s on 2026-10-29 · Today 1,171 m³/s · Ensemble on peak day: middle half 1,555–1,623, highest member 1,737 m³/s · 2012–2022 daily flow: median 506 · 90th 1,032 · 99th 1,555 m³/s".
  - Amber: three Niger points, Neuquén, three Rio Grande points and the lower Colorado.
  - **Danube** (43.9°N 23.4°E), blue: peak 1,953 m³/s today against a median of 5,320.
  - **Calls:** a probe `curl` read 5 points (1 request, 5 weighted calls), then the cold global view read the other 182 in 4 upstream requests (182 calls); later views and two further drives were served from the proxy's cache with 0 upstream calls.
  - **Console errors:** the keyless map's usual 404/403 resource errors only.
- **Calls spent on this work today:** about 105 on probes, 6,642 on the build, 187 at runtime: about 6,935, under the free tier's 10,000 a day.

## Not done

- **Fewer points than first planned:** 187 points, not 1–3k. At 35 calls a point, 1,000 points would need about 35,000 calls, three and a half days of the free quota. The script resumes, so maintainers can grow the set over several days.
- **Percentiles are not return periods:** they come from ten years of daily flow, which is not a 2-, 5- or 20-year return period and not a local flood stage. GloFAS's official return-period thresholds are published on the Copernicus EWDS behind a free account. They would allow a denser set and real return periods, but were not used here.
- **Classification ignores the ensemble:** the level uses the headline series only. The ensemble spread is shown on the card but does not raise the level.
- **Regulated rivers are modelled as unregulated:** GloFAS does not model the Nile's dams and wetland losses. The bundled Nile point below Aswan (26.3°N) has a 2012–2022 mean of 11,394 m³/s, while the release from Aswan is about 55.5 km³ a year (about 1,760 m³/s); the White Nile and Mountain Nile points are also several times their observed flow. The colour compares each point with its own model climatology, so it stays consistent, but the m³/s on such a card is not an observed flow.
- **Mis-snaps not cleaned up:** a 3×3 neighbourhood can still miss braided or deltaic channels (one Mekong point here). A 5×5 search costs 25 calls a point.
- **No voice access:** the prompt budget is full (see above).

The changelog fragment is `changelog.d/1356-river-discharge-outlook.md`.

title: feat(weather): one Temperature layer with land, sea and air modes
body:
Follow-up to #875, as agreed with @Udaydsmls there: one **Temperature** layer with four modes instead of separate overlapping layers.

**Builds on #875.** This branch sits on #875's head (c6af5ed8), so until #875 merges the diff here includes its four commits. Only the last three commits are new. Review #875 first; I'll rebase this once it lands.

## What changes

- **Land surface** (default): #875's MODIS monthly playback, unchanged. It keeps its on-map timeline, and the layer card shows its status under the mode picker.
- **Sea surface** and **Sea anomaly**: daily GHRSST MUR25 from NASA GIBS, with gap-aware dates, exact palette readings at a clicked point and an optional Niño 3.4 box.
- **Air (2 m)**: NOAA GFS 2 m air temperature, served as cached, quantised grids by the local server, readable at a point in °C and °F.

Only the chosen mode's controller runs, so two colour fields never stack. Registration, share state (token `5`), voice aliases and translations move from `surface-temperature` to `temperature`.

## Reuse of #875

- Ocean tile URLs use `src/maps/gibs.js`.
- The ocean palette parser stays separate from `colormap.js`. MUR25 palettes are in °C, with signed and open-ended (`-INF`/`+INF`) intervals, and a sea reading is an exact colour match rather than the nearest stop. I'm happy to merge the two parsers if you'd prefer.

## Testing

- `npm test` (8444 pass), `format:check`, `check:boundaries`, `layer-token:check --base-ref origin/main`, `changelog:check` and `build` all pass.
- Headless Chromium against the dev server: the layer was enabled and each mode chosen in turn. Land loaded its year of frames, and switching away released them. Each other mode drew only its own field. Disabling the layer left only the basemap.
