title: fix(terrain): pause upstream calls after a 429
body:
When the terrain upstream rate-limits the proxy, every page request for new points (about once a second while the camera moves) still goes upstream with its own retries, which keeps the limit in force and logs "refresh incomplete" each time.

**Change** (`server/providers/terrain.js`)
- After a 429 the proxy leaves the upstream alone for its Retry-After, capped at 10 minutes, or 60 s when it sends none. Cached points are still served; uncached ones get the same 502 an exhausted 429 already returned, and the page falls back to its geoid with a 60 s retry per point (`src/services/terrainHeights.js`).
- The warning that starts a pause says "(HTTP 429; pausing upstream for N s)" — once per request that was already in flight when the 429 came back; requests refused during the pause don't log. A 429 is still retried within the existing 10 s budget before the pause starts.

**Verification**
- New tests in `src/tooling/environmentProviders.test.mjs`: during the pause new points make no upstream call and no new log line; a Retry-After of a day pauses for at most 10 minutes. Both fail on main.
- `npm test`: 8,580 tests, 8,569 pass, 10 skipped, 1 fail (`skyAssets.paintOut`, which also fails on main on Windows); build and `format:check` pass.

title: fix(perimeters): flag stale WFIGS snapshots
body:
When WFIGS is unreachable, `/api/fire-perimeters` serves its last snapshot marked stale (`X-Data-Stale`, `body.stale`) with no age limit, and `createWfigsPerimeterSource` keeps only `payload.rows`. The Fire Perimeters row then reads healthy with a fresh update time, and `get_fire_perimeters` reports the perimeters as current. Reproduced: with the upstream down and the clock three days on, the tool still answers "1 mapped wildfire perimeter in the requested box." with no stale flag.

**Change**
- `src/layers/perimeters/source.js`: new `getSnapshotDetail()` → `{rows, stale, fetchedAt}`; `getSnapshot()` still returns the rows (the source contract is unchanged; a source without `getSnapshotDetail` is treated as fresh).
- `src/layers/perimeters/index.js`: `getStats()` reports `stale`, and a stale snapshot's `lastUpdate` is its fetch time, so the row reads "STALE · … ago" with the snapshot's age; a failed refresh clears `stale`, so the failure shows instead.
- `src/tools/queries/environment.js`: `get_fire_perimeters` returns `stale` and `retrieved_at`, and its summary ends "(data may be stale)", as `get_weather` does.
- `server/providers/firePerimeters.js`: a stale perimeter snapshot is served for at most 24 hours (InciWeb entries unchanged), as the GNSS proxy caps its own.
- `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md`: Fire Perimeters note.

**Verification**
- New tests (proxy 24 h cap; source detail; layer stale/fetch time and failure precedence; tool summary and fields) — each fails on main.

title: fix(traffic): flag cached TomTom flow tiles as stale in the layer

Once the TomTom tile budget is spent, or TomTom fails, `/api/tomtom` serves cached flow tiles marked STALE-BUDGET / STALE-ERROR. `flowSource.js` works out `stale`, but the layer fetches flow through `fetchFlowForBounds`, which returns only the segments, so `getStats()` and the sync chip still read "LIVE · Roads: …". #1239 fixed the `get_traffic_flow` tool; this is the same for the map layer.

**Change** (`src/layers/traffic/`)
- `flow.js`: `warmFlow` uses `fetchFlowDetail` (a source without it keeps the previous path) and keeps `stale` / `oldestTileAt` for the current load generation.
- `controls.js`: `getStats()` reports `stale` and `oldestTileAt`; any error (flow, roads, detail) still reads DEGRADED instead.
- `model.js`: the chip reads `STALE · Roads: <source> · Flow: cached TomTom tiles` (es/ru/zh-CN added).
- `state.js` / `lifecycle.js` / `viewport.js`: the flags reset on enable, disable and above the activation altitude.

title: feat: Financial & Economic Context Layer
body:
### Problem

Today, users cannot easily compare geopolitical events with historical economic indicators and financial market activity in one visual context. Researchers, journalists, and analysts could benefit from seeing how major world events coincide with changes in energy prices, commodity markets, and publicly available prediction-market data.

For example, reports of unusually well-timed market activity before major geopolitical events illustrate why comparing public event timelines with market data can be useful for research, without assuming a causal link or wrongdoing.

### Proposal

Add an optional economic context layer that allows users to compare major world events with historical economic and market data on a shared timeline.

For an initial version, focus on a small set of publicly available, redistribution-permitted sources, such as energy prices and commodity data. Where suitable, publicly available prediction-market data could be included as an additional context source.

The goal is to help users explore possible correlations between world events and market changes, without implying causation. All sources should be clearly attributed, and the feature should not identify or track individuals.

### Data source, license, and attribution

1. World Bank Commodity Price Data (“Pink Sheet”)
    Source: https://www.worldbank.org/en/research/commodity-markets
    License: Verify the applicable dataset license and redistribution terms before integration.
    Access: Historical downloadable data; no API key required for downloads.
    Attribution: World Bank, Commodity Price Data (Pink Sheet).
2. Polymarket Data API
    Source: https://data-api.polymarket.com/v2/docs
    License: MIT is listed for the API specification; verify the applicable terms for redistribution of the returned data.
    Access: Public API; no API key required.
    Attribution: Polymarket, with a link to the API documentation.

These are suggested starting points for evaluating the feature. Please verify each source’s redistribution terms before integration and use only data permitted by the project’s Responsible & Open policy.

### Will you build it?

No, this is a request for someone else

title: Event-Linked Journalism & Media Sources
body:
### Problem

When exploring an event in God’s Eye View, such as a military conflict, an aircraft accident, a natural disaster, or a major financial event, users may want to find relevant reporting, photographs, videos, and other published material about it.

Today, finding this material often requires searching across multiple news organizations, media platforms, and journalist publications separately. Linking events to relevant public reporting could help users discover how different sources document the same event and access the original material.

This could benefit journalists, researchers, analysts, and anyone seeking a better understanding of significant world events.

### Proposal

Add an optional journalism and media sources layer that connects events in God’s Eye View to relevant published reporting.

For an initial version, allow users to:

* Discover links to news articles, reports, photographs, and videos related to a selected event.
* Identify the publishing organization or author and the publication date when this information is available.
* Explore related material by event topic, time, and geographic context where reliable metadata permits.
* Open the original publication to review the material in its original context.

Potential sources include news agencies, regional and international news organizations, photojournalism platforms, and publicly accessible reporting by journalists and video journalists.

Start with permitted public links and metadata rather than requiring a complex content-ingestion system. Respect source licenses, attribution requirements, and privacy.

The feature should help users discover and compare reporting, not automatically treat a publication as verified fact or track journalists’ movements.

### Data source, license, and attribution

Potential sources to evaluate:

1. Associated Press (AP)
    Source: https://www.ap.org/
    Content: News reporting, photographs, video, and other journalistic material.
    License: Verify applicable licensing and reuse terms; content is not assumed to be freely redistributable.
    Access: Public website; no API key is required to browse public pages. API access and licensing must be checked separately.
    Attribution: Associated Press, with a link to the original publication.
2. Reuters
    Source: https://www.reuters.com/
    Content: International news reporting, photographs, and video.
    License: Verify applicable licensing and reuse terms; content is not assumed to be freely redistributable.
    Access: Public website; no API key is required to browse public pages. API access and licensing must be checked separately.
    Attribution: Reuters, with a link to the original publication.
3. Global Investigative Journalism Network (GIJN)
    Source: https://gijn.org/membership
    Content: Public information about investigative journalism organizations and their work.
    License: Verify reuse permissions for individual records before importing or redistributing data.
    Access: Public web pages; no API key is required to browse the site. A public API has not been confirmed.
    Attribution: Global Investigative Journalism Network, with a link to the original page.
4. World Press Photo
    Source: https://www.worldpressphoto.org/
    Content: Photojournalism and visual reporting.
    License: Verify the reuse terms for individual photographs, profiles, and other content before integration.
    Access: Public website; no API key is required to browse public pages. A suitable public API has not been confirmed.
    Attribution: World Press Photo and the original photographer or publication where applicable.

These are candidate sources for evaluation, not confirmed API integrations. The initial version could link to original publications and use only metadata that the project’s Responsible & Open policy permits. Verify data access, redistribution rights, and attribution requirements before integration.

title: research(disaster): fail-closed historical evidence receipts (#1198)
body:
## Scope

Research-only, model-free disaster evidence receipt guard for RFC #1198. This is a narrow upstream proposal for maintainer review, **not** an implementation of the entire humanitarian workspace or a claim of field readiness.

The change adds **no runtime consumer**, live provider, route engine, database, UI, dispatch mechanism, or automatic network requests. Existing GEV behavior should remain unchanged.

### What the proposed slice does
- Rejects attempts to establish route support from missing, stale, conflicting, simulated, untrusted or incompletely mapped evidence.
- Requires an explicit externally attested route-segment completeness flag and source policies from trusted application owners; it does **not** authenticate external issuers itself.
- Does not promote a precomputed `unknown` assessment into `supported`.
- Produces immutable, deterministic, revision-bound historical evidence receipts; material input changes invalidate previous receipts, including when a declared revision was not incremented.
- Includes 24 focused adversarial tests and a documented trust boundary.

### Independent work / dependencies
This is separate from the still-draft model-free access evaluator #882 and the downstream evidence/route experiments in `kvnloo/gods-eye-view#136` and `#155`. It does not copy their router or kernel implementation. If the accepted #882 contract already covers an aspect of this proposal, the right integration is to reuse it rather than add duplicate owners.

### Verification
Fork CI on exact head `fdbb9b34ec799e04c28ca2485e7eb8e451342ff3`: [run #40263029720](https://github.com/dvilrgamerz/gods-eye-view/actions/runs/40263029720) — all four jobs passed (Node 24, Node 26, Windows onboarding, Street Level browser gate), including unit tests, format/boundaries and production build. The 24 focused tests passed in standalone Node test staging.

**Not tested:** `npm run test:track`, real disaster-access UI, real-source validation, operator study or field safety. The receipt fingerprint is non-cryptographic and does not authenticate evidence. Upstream CI, reviewer approval and a maintainer scope decision remain pending.

### Request for maintainers
Is a small, stand-alone, fail-closed historical evidence receipt boundary useful upstream, or should it remain downstream until #882 and #1198's product scope are settled? Please treat this draft as a scope review; happy to adapt it to existing code owners.

Refs #1198.

title: feat(layers): four French public-data layers, with SNCF and Velib folded into Transit and Bike Share
body:
## What

Four new toggleable layers over French and European open-data feeds, plus the SNCF station network and Velib' folded into the two layers they belong to.

| Layer | Source | Row shape |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `vigicrues-floods` | VIGICRUES flood warnings | legend (vigilance bands, live counts) |
| `entsoe-grid` | ENTSO-E European grid load | readout (rail card, hourly valid-time rail) |
| `copernicus-ems` | Copernicus EMS activations | readout (rail card, status badge) |
| `ign-geoplateforme` | IGN Geoplateforme raster | chips (raster layers), stays a layer row |
| `transit` (SNCF) | GTFS-RT + SNCF stations | chips (VEHICLES / STATIONS / BOTH) + legend (rail segments) |
| `bikeshare` (Velib') | GBFS | legend (the existing availability ramp) |

Every one of these fetches through a **server-side proxy**, so the browser never names an upstream URL (the `SECURITY.md` rule). The client asks for a local route — `/api/sncf/stations`, `/api/vigicrues/stations`, `/api/vigicrues/zones`, `/api/entsoe/load`, `/api/copernicus-ems/activations`, `/api/ign-geoplateforme/tiles/{layer}/{z}/{x}/{y}.png` — and the proxy resolves the upstream URL from its own server-side allow-list. The IGN layer is an imagery overlay, so the globe asks the local proxy for each tile rather than a browser-direct tile template.

The 2 792 SNCF passenger stations are drawn as **point pins** in a Cesium `PointPrimitiveCollection`, not as 2 792 translucent ground ellipses that covered the map. A **principal** station (the catalogue gives it a public short code) keeps its rail-segment colour; a **local** station (no short code) is drawn in the same segment colour muted. The Transit legend counts those very classes from the same pure classifier the map colours from, so the legend and the map cannot drift apart.

Three fixes came out of putting the pins on the map:

- **The record body is read as well as the top level.** The OpenDataSoft catalogue serves the same dataset in two shapes: the v2.1 catalogue API answers with flattened rows, the v1 records API answers with the record body, where the fields live under `fields`. The proxy read only the top level, so against the record-body shape every name, short code, UIC and coordinate resolved to `null` and the row fell back to its station id — a station with no name on the map. The provider now reads `fields` first and keeps the top level as the fallback, so it keeps every name, short code, UIC and coordinate whichever shape the catalogue answers in.
- **A station in several rail segments takes its first, primary segment.** The catalogue publishes `segment_drg` as a semicolon-separated list, so ten stations — Paris Gare du Nord, Paris Gare de Lyon, Paris Austerlitz, Paris Montparnasse, Avignon TGV and CDG 2 TGV among them — were falling through to the neutral grey. The segment key is now resolved list-wise.
- **The VIGICRUES station catalogue follows the operator's same-origin 302** instead of treating it as a failure: the operator serves `/services/observations.json` as a redirect to `/services/observations.json/index.php`, which answers 200. The hop is followed by hand, and only while it stays on the registered upstream's own https origin, so the cross-origin refusal — a real SSRF guard — is untouched.

## Shared plumbing

**`src/sources/openDataProxy.js`** is the shared transport for the public operators. It:

- resolves upstream URLs from a server-side allow-list only;
- caps every upstream read by byte count before the body reaches the process heap;
- keeps a per-route in-memory cache with a TTL, so a browser poll loop cannot hammer a public operator;
- bounds how often the process may ask the operator at all with a fixed-window admission limiter (per route, plus a global backstop);
- pushes the next permitted attempt out on a failure backoff ladder (30 s, 60 s, 120 s, then 5 minutes) and serves the last good body while a route is cooling down;
- follows redirects manually and refuses any that leave the registered upstream's own https origin.

**`src/sources/lambert93.js`** implements the inverse of Lambert-93 (EPSG:2154) from the EPSG record. VIGICRUES publishes hydro-station coordinates in Lambert-93 metres; the globe needs degrees, and no projection library ships with this app. The conversion happens at the proxy boundary, so the browser never sees projected coordinates. It agrees with ten proj4 control points to better than 5e-10 degrees.

Two details worth knowing:

- **ENTSO-E is key-gated.** Without a token the proxy answers `503 {error:'no_key', keyRequired:true}` *before* making any upstream request, so the layer says "needs a key" rather than pretending the grid is idle. The token comes from `ENTSOE_TOKEN`; it is never hardcoded. The rail card names the variable to set through the app's existing key-guidance path.
- **Copernicus EMS centroids arrive as WKT `POINT (lon lat)`** with longitude first — the opposite of the usual GeoJSON order. The proxy parses them in the upstream's own order, which is what keeps a hazard from being placed in the wrong hemisphere.

## Presentation: the house grammar

The new rows present themselves in the **same visual grammar as the pre-existing layers**, using only the three patterns the Layers panel already has — legend, chips, readout. No new pattern, no bespoke meta line.

- **VIGICRUES** is a legend of the vigilance bands with a live count of the warning zones in each band, in the very colours the map draws them in (`VIGICRUES_LEVEL_COLORS`).
- **Copernicus EMS** and **ENTSO-E** hand off to a rail card. Copernicus's badge names the activation status (new / ongoing / closed); ENTSO-E's card lists the day hour by hour and carries a chip that switches between the whole day-ahead forecast and the hours already past.
- **IGN** stays a layer row and gains chips that switch the raster basemap.
- **Transit** gains chips that switch between the live fleet and the static station network, plus a legend of the rail segments the stations are coloured by. The station legend counts the same principal/local classes the pins are drawn in, from the same pure classifier.
- **Bike Share** shows the availability ramp every city in it is drawn in, Velib' included. The ramp is one function (`bikeshareAvailabilityBand`) that both the renderer and the legend count from, so a point's colour and the band that counts it cannot disagree.

**The Transit count is split.** The row mixes two populations, so the count reads `12 vehicles · 2792 stations` rather than one mixed number. A population that is absent is not shown as a zero. The split label rides the panel's existing `countLabel` mechanism — the same one Traffic uses for "24 nearby · 2 on screen".

**The source line names the DATASET only**, never the operator: `GTFS-RT · SNCF`, `GBFS`, `VIGICRUES`, `ENTSO-E`, `Copernicus EMS`, `IGN`. The operator and the licence live in `DATA_SOURCES.md` and the in-app credits, where every attribution row is kept.

**The meta line is three short segments** — state, source, age. The detail segment (error text, "412 of 500 records accepted", a retry countdown) is reserved for a feed that is degraded, partial, stale or erroring, so an operator reads a problem when there is one.

## Layer-state token allocation

The four new layers take the next free tokens in reservation order:

| Layer | Token |
| --- | --- |
| `vigicrues-floods` | 6 |
| `entsoe-grid` | 7 |
| `copernicus-ems` | 8 |
| `ign-geoplateforme` | 9 |

The SNCF station network and Velib' are **not** separate layers any more: they are folded into the pre-existing `transit` and `bikeshare` rows, so they take no new token. The JSON token ledger and `LAYER_STATE_REGISTRY` agree: upstream's published base owns 32 reservations, there are now 36.

## i18n

New UI strings are translated into es, ru and zh-CN and appended to the catalogs in the existing order. The catalogs are ordered by code discovery, not alphabetically, so the new entries are appended rather than re-sorted. `npm run i18n` reports all three locales complete (2829 messages each).

The POWER UP panel gains rows for the two key-gated transport providers, **GTFS** (`GTFS_API_KEY`) and **ÎLE-DE-FRANCE MOBILITÉS PRIM** (`IDFN_PRIM_API_KEY`). The three keyless sources deliberately get **no** row: a POWER UP row would only inflate the chip's "KEYS WAITING" count with something the operator cannot fix. The registry stays the list of credentials that exist, not a list of upstreams.

## How it was verified

- `npm run build` — passes.
- `npm run i18n` — es, ru and zh-CN all report 2829 messages, complete.
- `npm run format:check`, `npm run check:boundaries`, `npm run changelog:check` — all pass.
- **Full suite, run as foreground batches of 80 files** (the last covering the remainder), because a single `node --test` invocation over the whole set is killed mid-run on the maintainer host. That is a harness limit, not a test failure.
- The two allocation microbenchmarks run under Node 24 with `--expose-gc --test-concurrency=1`, as the repo runner does.
- The station pins are covered by their own tests: the classifier (principal/local, segment key, legend counts), the pin collection's release on destroy, and the proxy's reading of both catalogue payload shapes.
- The pin size rule is written down next to the constants: a station with a public short code is drawn at 9 px, one without at 6 px, and nothing else moves the size — the catalogue publishes no passenger count, frequency, capacity or ridership, so a size driven by any of those would be drawing a number the data does not carry. All 2 792 live stations carry a short code today, so in practice every pin is drawn at the principal size.
- The VIGICRUES station route was checked against the live operator after the redirect fix: it answers 200, and the warning-zone route, which carries the row's legend counts, is unaffected.

## Known caveats

1. **The voice tool-payload hash pin moved with the manifest.** The layers extend the voice layer manifest, so the generated layer enums and aliases change and the serialized payload changes. The assertion is still a pinned SHA-256 — it moved, it was not weakened. Measured payload hash: `10df6e29d05f89c0269814c4cbd424651ccdb3ccacef31c8cd59ffcb1eb1ccde`.

2. **The Realtime prompt budget is 52506 characters** (instructions 19656 + tool schemas 32850), measured on this tree. The ceiling is the measured size, not a loosened bound.

3. **ENTSO-E load banding.** The bands partition [0,1] into quarter bins, half-open on the left, so exactly 0.25 is the bottom edge of *moderate*, not *low*. The test expectation was wrong and was corrected; the layer behaviour was not changed.

4. **The three Vigilance 1/2/3 translations (es/ru/zh-CN) were written by the contributor and have NOT been reviewed by a native speaker.** Flagging this as an open item — a reviewer may want to correct the wording.

Screenshots are welcome for anything visual but not required.

title: fix(share): restore a share link opened in an already-open tab
body:
With the app open, opening a different share link in the same tab (pasting it into the address bar, following a link, or Back/Forward) changed the URL but left the view unchanged until a reload.

## Fix

- `ShareLinkManager` now listens for `hashchange` and `popstate` and, for a share link that differs from the hash the app last read or wrote, runs the same restore pipeline as start-up: camera, visual settings, map, panels, layers and shared Follow, with the same URL-write suppression and restore-lane authority.
- A newer navigation supersedes an older restore end to end, including its pending URL write; only the newest restore releases URL writes, and a failed start releases them too.
- The app's own `replaceState` writes never trigger a restore. Listeners are removed on destroy.
- Layer restore from a link goes through a new `applyShareLayerState`, which cancels in-flight layer restores and does not save the link's layers as the user's preferences. A link with no layer data restores the defaults, as a reload does.
- Restores return to the Normal style and reset an already-active preset first, so the result matches a fresh load. Releasing the previous Follow no longer saves the old layers as preferences.

## Validation

- `npm test`, `npm run format:check`, `npm run check:boundaries`.
- New `src/sharelink.navigation.test.mjs` (10 tests): navigation restores and holds URL writes, own writes don't restore, non-share hashes are ignored, Back/Forward, supersession, destroy, start-up vs navigation, Follow release, failed start, real coordinator layer switching.
- Browser: same-document hash navigation Austin → Paris/Noir/Flights, Back, Forward, and two links 200 ms apart, each restoring camera, style and layers without a reload. On `main` the URL changed but the view stayed.

## Known follow-ups (low severity)

- A link with no panel data leaves panels as they are, while a reload resets them.
- In embed mode, annotations aren't redrawn after a navigation.
- A Follow active before navigating may stay selected when the new link has none.

title: fix(layers): make Clear All clear the saved and shared layer selection
body:
After Clear All, every layer control could be off while the share URL still listed layers (for example `l=e.f`), and a reload brought them back.

## Cause

Not a delayed write. Clear All committed an "off" state only for layers it switched off itself. Layers that were already off for a passive reason stayed in the committed layer state that both the URL and local preferences serialize:

- layers isolated when a context mode (Contacts) was entered (`l=e`);
- Flights, released by the Contacts teardown during the Clear All batch (`l=e.f`).

## Fix

- `src/data/lifecycle.js`: Clear All reports which layers are still on once its batch settles.
- `src/data/layerStateCoordinator.js`: for explicit origins, drops every committed layer not in that set, cancels their passive restores and any pending Follow restore, and commits, which updates local storage and the URL. A layer that a newer explicit request turned back on is kept.
- `src/ui/contextSession.js`: a context exit interrupted by Clear All no longer turns its snapshot back on.

## Validation

- `npm test`, `npm run format:check`, `npm run check:boundaries`.
- New tests in `src/data/layerState.test.mjs` (context-isolated layers dropped, mid-batch releases dropped, newer explicit re-enable kept, passive clear writes nothing, waiting restore cancelled) and an ordering test in `src/contextSessionOrdering.test.mjs`; both regression tests fail without the fix.
- Browser: Earthquakes on → Contacts on → Clear All → coordinate search → reload. On `main` the URL kept `l=e` and Earthquakes came back after reload; with this change `l=` is empty and no layer returns. Also checked Clear All during fetches and a mode change, and the copied link opened in a fresh context.

## Known follow-ups (rare)

- A newer explicit "on" that is then blocked could stay committed while showing off.
- A committed restore that starts in the middle of Clear All isn't cleared.

title: feat(share): short /share/<code> links with a compact versioned view format
body:
**Short share links (`/share/<code>`)**

The share button now makes short links of the form `<app>/share/<code>`. The code is a compact, versioned encoding of the view, described in `docs/SHARE-LINK-FORMAT.md`. The same code opens on any copy of the app, including a local dev server. Long `#v=2&…` links are unchanged, and the address bar still follows the live view in that form.

## Format

- Version byte, then protobuf-style fields with permanent field numbers. Unknown fields are skipped, so newer links still open in older copies; numbers, codes and defaults are append-only.
- Settings equal to their default are omitted. Style-dependent settings (bloom, sharpen, HUD, detection, celestial ring, the style's shader parameters) are encoded against the defaults the view's own style applies, taken from `src/ui/visualPresets.js`; a test freezes them so shared links keep their meaning if those tables change.
- Two view kinds: a place (camera) and a followed thing (aircraft and military aircraft by ICAO address, vessels by MMSI, satellites by NORAD id). A followed view stores the entity, the follow offset and its last-known position; the camera is derived from them. An unknown kind opens at the stored position.
- A trailing CRC-8 rejects every single-character typo.
- Sizes: a real 302-character long link becomes 39; following an aircraft from the default camera is 42.

## Opening

- A `/share/<code>` address, or `initialShareCode` passed to `createApplicationControls`, runs the same start-up restore as long links. The address then changes to the app's own address plus the long hash, with no new history entry.
- Following: the entity's layer is turned on and the entity followed with the stored offset. If it isn't reporting within its normal window, the view stays at its last-known position and says so. Vessel views select the vessel once it appears in the feed.
- An invalid code shows "This share link can't be opened" and the default start runs.

## Creating

- `ShareLinkManager.buildLink()` returns the `/share/<code>` URL; a link made while following an aircraft, military aircraft or satellite is a followed view.
- An optional `services.shareLink(url)` lets a host share the link its own way. It resolves to `'shared'`, `'copied'`, `'cancelled'` (no toast) or `false`; without it the button copies as before. New strings are translated in es, ru and zh-CN.

## Validation

- `npm test`, `format:check`, `check:boundaries`, i18n catalogs and `npm run build`.
- Unit tests for the codec (round trips of generated states, every field, both kinds, unknown fields and kinds, malformed input, typo rejection, per-style defaults, legacy long-link conversion) and for opening and creating links (place, followed thing, not reporting, bad code, address replacement, host hook, base path, vessel, hash navigation).
- Browser: a link made in a fresh session (Noir, Flights on, following an aircraft) opened in a separate fresh profile with the same style, settings, panels and layers, following the same aircraft; a link with one mistyped character was refused; hash navigation and Clear All behaved as before.

title: feat(share): export the share-view codec and link-path helpers
body:
Exports the share-view codec and the share-link address helpers so a server that serves the app can read a `/share/<code>` link without loading the browser app — for example to put the view's description in link-preview metadata.

- `./share/view-codec` → `src/share/viewCodec.js` (`decodeShareView`, `encodeShareView` and the registry). It has no DOM or Cesium dependency.
- `./share/link-path` → `src/share/shareLinkPath.js` (recognising and building `/share/<code>` paths).
- `scripts/package-boundaries.json` registers both exports and their module closures.

No behaviour change in the app.

Validation: `npm test`, `npm run format:check`, `npm run check:boundaries`.

title: fix(search): keep a missed location query in the field so it can be corrected
body:
## What this changes

A location search that finds nothing or fails used to show a "Location not found" toast, then clear the query, collapse the field and drop focus, so fixing a typo meant reopening search and retyping. That is especially costly with a keyboard or a screen reader. Found in GEV launch-readiness QA (HAL-727).

- After a miss or a failure, the settle step keeps the query, keeps the field open and keeps focus, with the text selected so it can be retyped at once (`src/ui/navigationController.js`). A search that arrives still clears and closes the field.
- The miss is a persistent `role="alert"` line under the search row, tied to the input with `aria-describedby` and `aria-invalid`, saying what to do next ("Location not found. Check the spelling and press Enter to search again." / "Search failed. Press Enter to try again."). It replaces the toast.
- Typing, a new search, or closing the emptied field (Escape, collapsing the tray) clears it.
- The message sits outside `.location-city-row`, which clips overflow in the command dock; an earlier absolutely positioned version was hidden there.
- New strings are translated in `es`, `ru` and `zh-CN`. `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md` describes the behaviour.

## How I verified it

- [x] `npm run build`
- [x] `npm test`: everything search-related passes (116 tests across the search, controls, a11y, focus, mobile-shell and i18n suites, plus the new `src/ui/locationSearchRecovery.test.mjs`). In the full run, two timing-budget tests (`analystEngine` 250k-row ranking, `geoFileImport` KML deadline) failed under machine load and pass when run alone (98/98).
- [~] `npm run test:track`: 108 passed, 1 failed. The failure is `arrival: moveEnd + first reveal both re-aim before idle refresh` going past its 500 ms budget. Unmodified `main` (da02fd86) fails the same check under the same load (107/109: the flights and military variants), so it is load-dependent and not caused by this change.
- [x] Feature gate: `node scripts/qa-location-controls.mjs`, 0 failures.
- [x] Real app, headless Chromium with the geocoders stubbed to return nothing: a bad query is kept, focused and selected; the field stays open; the alert is on screen (`elementFromPoint` hits it) and tied to the input; typing a correction clears it; Escape still closes and clears search.

Not checked: the mobile shell's search sheet, or a real screen reader.

title: fix(i18n): mark style labels without loading the catalogs
body:
The style shaders (`src/styles/*.js`) and `src/ui/visualPresets.js` imported `msg()` from `src/i18n/index.js`, which loads every locale catalog. The share-view codec reads the styles' defaults, so anything bundling `@gods-eye-view/core/share/view-codec` (a server rendering link previews, say) carried about 0.9 MB of translations it never uses.

They now import the catalog-free `msg()` from `src/i18n/marker.js`, as other portable modules already do. Both functions return their argument unchanged, and `npm run i18n` finds the marked strings either way.

- The codec bundled on its own: about 1,054 KB → 129 KB.
- `scripts/package-boundaries.json`: `visual-effects` and `share-view-codec` own `marker.js` instead of the catalogs; `ui-visual-settings` owns it as well.

Checks: `npm test` (8,804 tests, 0 failures), `npm run check:boundaries`, `npm run format:check`, `npm run i18n` (es, ru, zh-CN complete).

title: perf(render): 30 fps while only slow live feeds animate a parked view; wind holds the governor
body:
## What this changes

**30 frames a second while only slow live feeds animate a parked view.** When every continuous-render hold belongs to a slow live feed (`AMBIENT_OWNERS` in `src/renderGovernor.js`: flights, military, AIS vessels, satellites, rocket launches, traffic, transit, military awareness, wind) and the camera has been still for 500 ms, the governor sets `viewer.targetFrameRate` to 30. Those marks drift a few pixels a second, so 30 looks the same as 60 and the render work halves.

- Any other hold (camera verbs, tracked entity, cockpit, CCTV projection, style animation, directions, annotations…) restores the viewer's own rate, read at install time.
- Any camera motion restores it at once; the ambient rate returns after 500 ms of stillness.
- Camera motion is read from the camera pose after each rendered frame, not from `moveStart`/`moveEnd`: a camera nudged a few millimetres a frame never raises `moveEnd`. It costs a few multiplications on frames that render anyway.
- `uninstallRenderGovernor` gives the viewer its own rate back and removes the listener.

**Wind holds the governor.** The GPU streamlines drove renders from their own 30 Hz `requestRender` pump, outside the governor, so diagnostics showed no owner. The renderer now holds `'wind'` while the flow actually animates (running, in view, not paused, not reduced motion, not hidden) and releases it otherwise, including stop and destroy. The catalog passes the governor in as the wind layer's `render` service.

## Tests

- `src/renderGovernor.test.mjs`: four new cases: ambient-only holds at 30 and any other hold at the full rate; camera motion (travel and turning) restores the full rate until 500 ms of stillness; millimetre drift is not motion; the viewer's own rate is the full rate and uninstall restores it and removes the listener.
- `src/layers/wind/rendering.test.mjs`: the hold follows the animation through pause, reduced motion, hidden, out of view and stop.
- `scripts/qa-perf.mjs`: step 4 now checks the 30 fps parked rate (cadence ≥ 35% of rAF instead of ≥ 70%), and a new step 4b checks that moving the camera with flights on restores the full rate (≥ 70% of rAF).

Locally on this branch (Windows, Node 24):

- `node scripts/qa-perf.mjs`: **27/27**. Flights on, camera parked: 144 renders per 283 rAF ticks at `targetFrameRate` 30. Moving: 69 per 71 at 60.
- `npm test`: 8,787 pass. The one failure is `skyAssets.paintOut.test.mjs`, which fails on Windows only (it builds a file path from `URL.pathname`, `/C:/…`) and is unrelated.
- `format:check`, `check:boundaries`: pass.

`docs/CURRENT-STATE.md` has a dated note beside the governor section. The changelog entry is `changelog.d/1422-ambient-frame-rate.md`.

title: feat: add offline Director-to-Blender camera bridge
body:
Adds an offline Director-to-Blender camera bridge related to #1081.

- Exports existing scene documents to a portable camera manifest.
- Preserves scene/shot IDs, WGS84 origin, ENU meters, lens, fps and timing.
- Imports editable Blender shot cameras with quaternion keys and timeline markers.

title: feat(docker): publish a hardened multi-arch image to GHCR on release
body:
## What this changes Refs #48. Follows the self-hosted Docker path chosen there (#208): every GitHub release now also ships a ready-to-run, hardened Docker image for `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64`, so people can run God's Eye View with one `docker run` and no clone or Node install. It slots into the release and CI flow you already have: nothing changes in how you cut a release. Publishing a release is still the only step, and the image, its tags and a short "Release Artifacts" section in the release notes follow automatically. CI gains one `docker` job alongside the existing ones. - 🚀 **One command to run:** `docker run … ghcr.io/bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view:latest`, or the sample `compose.yaml` in the README - 🖥️ **Runs everywhere:** `linux/amd64` (Linux servers, Windows via Docker Desktop) and `linux/arm64` (Apple Silicon natively, Raspberry Pi 4/5, AWS Graviton). Each is built on its own native GitHub runner, so no QEMU and no wrong-architecture native modules - 🔑 **Keys survive upgrades:** **SAVE KEYS** in Provider Settings works inside the container and writes to one `/data` volume, so `docker pull` + recreate keeps your keys and caches - 🔒 **Hardened by default:** runs as `1000:1000`, read-only app code, no git/npm/apt in the image, read-only root filesystem, no capabilities, `no-new-privileges` - 🧾 **Provenance and SBOM** attached to every published image by `build-push-action`, and checked after the multi-arch merge - ✅ **Tested on every PR:** CI builds the image on both architectures, starts it with the README's hardening flags, and checks health, a saved key, and persistence - 🏠 **Self-hosting notes:** SELinux and NAS bind mounts are covered in the README - 🧹 **No more Node 20 warnings:** actions moved to their Node 24 releases ## How I verified it All on the current head, `b0cb5b996`, rebased onto `main` at `fca2c81d8`. - [x] `npm run build` - [x] `npm test`: 16,027 tests, 16,022 pass, 5 skipped, 0 fail - [x] `npm run test:track`: same result as `main`. Details below - [x] Feature gate: none of the `qa-*.mjs` gates covers Docker or releases; the image checks below stand in for one - [x] `npm run doctor`, `format:check`, `check:boundaries`, `changelog:check`: clean
npm run test:track against main and against the image | Run | Passed | Failed | | --- | --- | --- | | `main` (`fca2c81d8`), native dev server | 110 | 1 | | This PR, native dev server | 110 | 1 | | This PR's runtime image (arm64), 3 runs | 109, 109, 110 | 2, 2, 1 | | `main`'s existing Docker image | 109 | 2 | - `trail head: last vertex on the drawn icon` fails on `main` too, in every setup. - `display-floor/regime` is timing-sensitive when the app is served from a container: it fails the same way against `main`'s own image, and passed on one of three runs against this one. Native runs pass it on both `main` and this PR.
The image, both architectures (README docker run flags, the same checks as the CI docker job) - arm64 native and amd64 under QEMU on Apple Silicon: healthy in about 8s, `/` returns 200, Node 24.22.2 - the esbuild binary matches the architecture (`linux-arm64`, `linux-x64`) - runs as uid 1000; app code and `/` are read-only; `/data` is writable; no git, npm or apt; no `.env` in any layer - SAVE KEYS writes `/data/.env` (`0600`), nothing beside the code, and the key survives `docker rm` + recreate - The README's sample `compose.yaml` with a bind-mounted `/data:Z`, and the from-source `docker compose up` (`dev` target, Node 24.22.2), both start healthy
CI and a release, end to end on the fork - CI on the head (damianperera/gev#5, [run](https://github.com/damianperera/gev/actions/runs/45307450268)): every job passed, including `Docker image (linux/amd64)` and `Docker image (linux/arm64)` - Release `v0.5.2` from that head ([run](https://github.com/damianperera/gev/actions/runs/45310105914)): both platforms built natively, the manifest was merged and passed the provenance and SBOM check, and it was tagged `0.5.2`, `0.5`, `sha-69da4f9` and `latest`. The "Release Artifacts" section was appended to the notes. The run has no warning annotations - `docker buildx imagetools inspect ghcr.io/damianperera/gev:0.5.2` lists `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64`, each with provenance and an SBOM
- ⚠️ Not tested on an SELinux host; the `:Z` guidance follows Docker's bind-mount documentation. ## Screenshots **CI and release runs**
CI: Docker image job summary (amd64 + arm64) Release workflow summary
**Release notes: before and after**
Release as published After the workflow appends "Release Artifacts"
**GHCR package**
Package page latest tag OS / arch selection
**Image running: `docker run` from the README, healthy, app in the browser**

## What's in it
📦 Image: Dockerfile - Two targets. `dev` is the existing Dockerfile unchanged, and `compose.yaml` now names it, so the from-source path is untouched. `runtime` is the published image. - `runtime` installs dependencies per architecture and copies the app as root-owned, read-only files. It runs as `USER 1000:1000` with `HEALTHCHECK`, `STOPSIGNAL SIGTERM` and `VOLUME /data`. - Same digest-pinned `node:24.22.2-slim` as `main`, in all three stages. The digest is the multi-arch index, not a single platform.
🔑 GEV_DATA_DIR: small app change so keys can be saved - Moves everything the app writes into one directory: the `.env` that **SAVE KEYS** writes (still atomic, `0600`), `.gev-cache` and `.gev-logs`. The image sets it to `/data`. - Unset means exactly today's behaviour, so native, Pinokio and compose are unchanged. It is only read from the launch environment: Vite's dotenv merge (`mergeDotenv()`) copies every other `.env` key but never this one, so a `.env` line can't redirect Provider Settings to a different file. - The Docker launcher checks that `/data` is writable. If it isn't, it names the likely fix: `chown 1000:1000`, or `:Z` on SELinux. - The helper is `server/providers/common/data-dir.js`; each cache owner uses it in one line, including the caches added on `main` since this PR opened (ghost maps, Nominatim, CelesTrak, OSM features, iNaturalist).
🚀 Release: .github/workflows/docker-release.yml - Runs on `release: published`, plus a manual re-run for any tag. - Per-architecture builds on native runners are merged into one multi-arch manifest. - Tags are `X.Y.Z`, `X.Y` and `sha-…`. `latest` is applied only for stable releases, never pre-releases, or on a manual re-run when asked. - Checks that provenance and SBOM are present for both platforms after the merge. - Appends the "Release Artifacts" section to the release notes, without a third-party action. A re-run replaces the section rather than duplicating it. - Least-privilege permissions per job, and every action pinned by SHA like `ci.yml`.
✅ CI: new docker job in ci.yml - Native amd64 and arm64 matrix. title: feat(ui): right rail as vertical icon tabs
body:
## What this changes

The right rail (Display, CCTV, Street Level, Context, plus Weather and Recent Imagery while shown) is no longer an accordion of collapsed launcher cards. A vertical strip of upright icon tabs hugs the rail's right edge, the open panel sits beside it, and at most one panel is open in every desktop HUD layout. The open tab and its panel read as one shape, like a folder tab: they share the glass surface and one outline, and the other tabs are plain icons. The panels' `collapsed` classes stay the only state: the strip mirrors them and routes every change through `setPanelCollapsed`, so saved preferences, share links and the Context/Radio ownership rules are unchanged. Phones keep the sheet shell; Cockpit hides the rail and the strip with it.

- `src/ui/rightRailTabs.js` builds the strip (`role="tablist"`, vertical orientation, Up/Down wrap, Home/End, roving tab stop) from the rail's panels and keeps it in step through a MutationObserver. Each tab shows a Material Symbols glyph (`RAIL_TAB_ICONS`: Display `tune`, CCTV `videocam`, Street Level `streetview`, Context `travel_explore`, Weather `cloud`, Recent Imagery `satellite_alt`); its accessible name and tooltip are the panel's own translated header title.
- The join: the strip measures the open panel and tab, traces their joined silhouette as an SVG path (`railJoinPath`: rounded corners, concave fillets at the junction; Cyber's chamfered frame and a square tab instead) and keeps a join element under the panels whose layers blur and tint the backdrop inside the path, stroke the outline along it and cast the drop shadow. One surface, one blur region, one outline: no seam where the tab meets the panel. The open panel's wrapper and card and the tab draw no surface of their own (Cyber dresses the wrapper too). Re-measured through a ResizeObserver and on strip scroll; a short panel such as Context grows to reach its tab.
- The one-owner rule that Cyber already applied now holds in every desktop layout, so the right rail's Tactical auto-collapse retry path became dead code and is removed; the presentation marker is renamed `rail-owner-collapsed`.
- Escape inside a panel returns focus to that panel's tab (the in-panel disclosure is hidden with the panel).
- A first-time visitor on a desktop viewport finds Display open: with every panel closed nothing shows that the icons are launchers. Phones keep it closed, a share link decides for itself, and a stored choice wins either way (this reverses the first-run default in `panelPositionControls.js`, whose reasoning assumed the old launcher cards). When the rail picks its one owner, a panel the visitor or a share link opened outranks one open only by default, so a stored CCTV choice is not displaced by the Display default.
- Cyber skins the strip in its red and slate panel treatment.

## After review (bff1d0eb)

- Review fixes: a panel hidden at mount (Weather, Recent Imagery) gets its tab when it is revealed; any live opening of a rail panel makes it the owner, restores do not; the join, the panel cover and the fillet stay inside the lane; a share link carries an owner-collapsed peer as collapsed, so the recipient opens the sender's panel; border-box on phones; the strip's column folds into the panel width at 721–760 px; the focus ring draws inside the tab.
- The compact Radio launcher moves from Context's header into a tool slot under the tabs on desktop (and back into the header for the phone sheet) and always toggles the compact player, also while Context is open; the player's Details button leads to the Radio section. The jump-to-section role and the #804 closings of the player on Context expansion and rail layout passes are gone with it.
- The rail panels' own collapse arrows are hidden on desktop: the tab opens and closes a panel, Escape inside closes it and returns focus to the tab.
- The strip never scrolls. The tabs are denser, and the rail climbs toward the HUD corner above its left-rail baseline when the strip's column is taller than the lane (`src/ui/rightPanelRail.js`).
- The expanded Radio Enable's reveal of the directory and Play lands its smooth scroll on `scrollend` when a rail layout pass, measuring the panels mid-scroll, puts the Context scroller's offset back and cancels it (`src/ui/radioControls.js`); the Radio gate had started to stop there.

## After the second review (33ccdad7, 8396fd3d)

- Icon tabs: one upright glyph per tab in a fixed 34 px square, the size of the Radio launcher under the strip. The sideways labels, the equal share of a short strip, the end fade and the column's lane cap are gone, so every tab stays whole; on the shortest windows (1280×500, Cyber at 1440×560) the strip runs past the lane over the GSD/ALT readout instead of clipping. The glyphs are in the `index.html` icon font subset, and a test keeps them there.
- A Radio pick reopens a closed Context around an expanded Radio section in every HUD layout, not only Cyber.
- The Radio reveal's `scrollend` landing gives way to a user scroll, key or pointer, and stops after two seconds.
- The compact player's Details button scrolls the Radio section and its Enable into view inside Context.
- A camera layer switched on by a share link or a saved session no longer opens the CCTV panel over the restored tab; a user switch-on still does (`subscribeEnableRequests` in `src/ui/applicationShell.js`).

## Screenshots

Tactical with CCTV open, Tactical with Context open, Cyber with Street Level open:

![Right rail as vertical tabs: Tactical with CCTV open, Tactical with Context open, Cyber with Street Level open](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view/8396fd3dc74cbef22fb5920c4d03dee5b2a2fefa/docs/media/right-rail-tabs.png)

The image is committed as `docs/media/right-rail-tabs.png` so the link outlives the branch (refreshed in 8396fd3d with the icon tabs).

## How I verified it

- [x] `npm run build`
- [x] `npm test` (8801 pass, 0 fail after the second review; 8795 pass after the first follow-ups; one KML import deadline test timed out under full-suite load and passes alone)
- [x] `npm run test:track`: 108 of 109 pass on this branch (two runs, before the follow-ups). The one failure is the `arrival rotation` timing check (moveEnd/reveal observed in 614–723 ms against its 500 ms budget, a different sub-case each run); the unchanged checkout fails the same check on the same machine (910 ms and 501 ms), so it is a pre-existing headless-GL timing flake, not this change. Everything else, including the no-console-errors and no-5xx sweeps, passes on both.
- [x] Feature gate for the area I touched: `scripts/qa-radio.mjs` (the Radio browser gate, headless, after 84c204b7): 88 pass, 15 fail. 13 of the failures are the same on an unchanged `main` checkout on this machine (headless GPU-less rendering of station labels and cluster text, two mobile tuner checks); the other two expected the old several-panels rail policy this PR replaces with one owner and are removed in 8c788474. Every launcher and reveal check passes.
- [x] Headless Puppeteer against the dev server in Tactical and Cyber: tabs open and close their panels, exactly one panel open, Up/Down and Enter on the strip, Tab from the open tab enters the panel, Escape collapses it and focuses its tab; rail geometry (330 px panels in Tactical, 312 px in Cyber) unchanged. After the follow-ups: at 2000×725, 1366×683, 1280×720, 1440×750, 1440×900 and 1920×1080 the strip fits without scrolling; the compact player opens from the slot over an open Context and survives a layout pass; the phone sheet keeps its header launcher and collapse button; no console errors. After the second review: icon tabs whole and upright at six window sizes down to 1280×500, the Radio slot check 40/40, Details reveals Radio at 1440×560, 1366×683 and 1536×730 in Tactical and Cyber, and a restored CCTV layer keeps the restored tab while a user switch-on still opens CCTV.

title: feat(fires): FRP intensity filter, confidence switch and six-stop color ramp
body:
## What changes

- **Color by intensity.** Every FIRMS detection is colored by fire radiative power on a six-stop cold → hot ramp (blue · teal · lime · amber · orange · red at 0 · 5 · 20 · 50 · 100 · 300 MW), after the Portolan FIRMS explorer. The old three warm stops made a 2 MW and a 40 MW fire look alike. Heat cells, glow sprites and card accents read the same ramp (`src/data/firmsIntensity.js`).
- **Minimum-FRP slider** (log scale) in the Active Fires row. The track is painted with the ramp, so it doubles as the legend; ticks sit on the ramp stops.
- **Confidence switch** All / Nominal+ / High. VIIRS only reports those three values, so a switch, not a slider.
- **Counter** "N of M shown".
- **One filter point.** `ingestion.applyFilter()` runs before markers, cards, heat cells, the context store, the top-fires query and the analyst records, so they all see the same set.
- **Share links** keep both options (layer token `w`: `f` min FRP, `c` confidence), including the short codec.
- **Agent tool** `get_active_fires` gains `min_frp_mw` and `confidence`.
- Generic `slider` and `segmented` row descriptors for the layer panel (`src/ui/rowFilterControls.js`). New strings in es / ru / zh-CN.

Default stays 0 MW / All: on a real week, many of the strongest fires are rated low confidence, and "High only" hides 5,532 of the 41,074 fires at 20 MW or more.

No brightness slider on purpose: `bright_ti4` saturates at 367 K, depends on day vs night and differs between sensors.

## Verification

- `npm test`: 8811 passing. Format, package boundaries and i18n checks green.
- Headless browser: default row (144,706 of 144,706), 20 MW (13,860), 100 MW, High (11,135), reset, and a share link restoring 20 MW + High.

title: fix(security): add cross-site gate to military-installations proxy
body: ﻿## Summary Adds the `admitSameSite` cross-site gate to `/api/military-installations`, as offered in the [#975 merge comment](https://github.com/bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view/pull/975#issuecomment-6357981946). This was the last keyless proxy endpoint without the gate. After this change, every proxy that sends queries upstream now refuses cross-site browser requests before doing any work. | Endpoint | Gate before this PR | Gate after | |----------|-------------------|------------| | `/api/terrain/heights` | ✅ admitSameSite (#975) | ✅ | | `/api/cctv/frame/:id` | ✅ admitSameSite (#922) | ✅ | | `/api/traffic/*` | ✅ admitSameSite | ✅ | | `/api/google/*` | ✅ admitSameSite | ✅ | | `/api/gemini/*` | ✅ admitSameSite | ✅ | | `/api/space/satellites` | ✅ admitSameSite | ✅ | | `/api/overpass` | ✅ admitSameSite | ✅ | | `/api/military-installations` | ❌ **none** | ✅ admitSameSite | ## The problem A cross-site page (or an `` tag from any website) can query `/api/military-installations` and trigger upstream Overpass requests on the user's behalf. The endpoint has a rate limiter (90/min), but no cross-site gate — so a hostile page can burn through the user's Overpass quota and exfiltrate the response data. Every other proxy in the codebase already refuses these shapes. Military-installations was the gap. ## The fix Two lines in `server/providers/military-installations.js`: ```diff import { makeRateLimiter, clientKey } from './common/rate-limit.js'; +import { admitSameSite } from './common/same-site.js'; ``` ```diff if (req.method !== 'GET') { res.writeHead(405, { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' }); res.end(JSON.stringify({ error: 'Method Not Allowed' })); return; } + if (admitSameSite(req, res)) return; const url = new URL(req.url, 'http://localhost'); ``` Same pattern as terrain.js, cctv.js, traffic.js, google.js, etc. Gate runs before the rate limiter, so refused requests never consume quota. `scripts/package-boundaries.json` updated to declare `server/providers/common/same-site.js` and `src/localRequestGate.mjs` as owned modules of `military-installations-provider`. ## Tests New file: `src/militaryInstallationsGate.test.mjs` — 4 integration tests following the `terrainHeightsBounds.test.mjs` pattern: ``` ✔ cross-site browser requests are refused with 403 (2.4ms) ✔ same-origin browser request is admitted (not 403) (5.3ms) ✔ bare tool request (no Origin, no Sec-Fetch) is admitted (0.9ms) ✔ proxied same-origin requests are refused (proxy headers present) (0.5ms) ``` Tested shapes: - `Sec-Fetch-Site: cross-site` (the `` case) → 403 - `Sec-Fetch-Site: same-site` (cross-origin sibling) → 403 - `Origin: https://evil.example` (fetch from hostile page) → 403 - `Origin: null` (sandboxed iframe) → 403 - `X-Forwarded-For` + `Sec-Fetch-Site: cross-site` (proxied cross-site) → 403 - Same-origin with matching `Origin` → admitted - No `Origin`, no `Sec-Fetch` (curl / Node) → admitted - Proxy headers with `same-origin` → 403 All 4 tests fail on `main` and pass with the fix. ## Validation - `node --test src/localRequestGate.test.mjs src/militaryInstallationsGate.test.mjs`: **18 tests, 18 pass, 0 fail** - `npm run check:boundaries`: **pass** (military-installations-provider: 15 owned modules) - `npm run check:import-directions`: pass - Changelog fragment in `changelog.d/military-installations-cross-site-gate.md`

title: ci: let Dependabot keep actions, npm and the base image current
body:
## Summary

Refs #267. Adds a `.github/dependabot.yml` that keeps the SHA-pinned actions, the npm dependencies and the Docker base image current, in one weekly PR. The original proposal was in #309 by @SurefireStudios. Its config was dropped when #505 landed, and since then the pins have drifted onto Node 20 releases (`checkout` v4.4.0, `setup-node` v4.4.0, `upload-artifact` v4.6.2), which print a Node.js 20 deprecation warning on every run.

- 📦 **One PR a week** for `github-actions`, `npm` and `docker`, using a multi-ecosystem group, with at most 2 open at a time
- 📌 **Actions:** takes every version. Dependabot reads SHA pins and bumps the SHA and its `# vX.Y.Z` comment together
- 🩹 **npm:** patch releases only. Majors and minors (vite, cesium, puppeteer) can change behaviour and need a real review, so they stay manual
- 🐳 **Base image:** the `node:<version>-slim@sha256:…` in the `Dockerfile` follows minor and patch releases on the current Node major, with a fresh digest. A new Node major stays manual, so it moves together with CI's Node matrix and the `package.json` engines range
- ⏳ **Cooldown:** `cooldown: default-days: 7` on every ecosystem holds a fresh release for a week before it's proposed, in case it gets pulled or compromised
- 🔒 No new secrets or permissions, and no labels, reviewers or assignees
- 🧹 Nothing else touched

## Contributor verification

- ✅ `check-jsonschema --builtin-schema vendor.dependabot .github/dependabot.yml` passes, and so does the latest SchemaStore `dependabot-2.0.json`
- ✅ `prettier --check .github/dependabot.yml` passes
- ✅ Ran on a fork's default branch with this grouping. Dependabot opened a single grouped PR across ecosystems that bumped the base image within Node 24 (`24.14.0` → `24.21.0`, with a new digest). The 7-day cooldown held back the newer `24.22.1`, and the Node major was not proposed. Actions were already current, so nothing was bumped there
- ✅ A second fork run with this exact config shows npm is patch-only. The grouped PR contained only `prettier` 3.9.6 → 3.9.10, `vite` 6.4.3 → 6.4.4 and the Node 24 image. The log lists `version-update:semver-minor` from this file as an ignore rule for each package and reports "All updates for cesium were ignored"
- ⚠️ No runtime change, so no changelog fragment

## Notes for maintainers

- ⚙️ **One-time setting:** after merging, re-enable **Dependabot version updates** under **Settings → Advanced Security** ([`/settings/security_analysis`](https://github.com/bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view/settings/security_analysis)). The config file alone doesn't start it while that setting is off.
- 🐳 A base-image bump changes only the `Dockerfile`, so CI's `24.14.0` matrix entry stays where it is until someone moves it.
- 🔐 Security updates come from GitHub's separate Dependabot security updates setting, not from this group.

title: fix(military): don't treat adsb.lol's position-less rows as a partial snapshot
body:
## What this changes

The military half of #1110. adsb.lol's `/v2/mil` leaves out `lat`/`lon` for a contact it hears without a current position (82 of 239 rows in a live fetch). `readsbSnapshot` counted them as rejected, so every military snapshot was partial, and a partial snapshot keeps every absent aircraft for 5 minutes. A military aircraft that left the feed stayed on the globe at full opacity instead of fading after one poll and leaving after three (or one, if likely landed).

A readsb row with a hex but no `lat`/`lon` now leaves the snapshot complete and is listed in `retainIds`, which keeps only that aircraft, within the same 5-minute bound, unless it is likely landed. Half, unreadable and id-less rows still mark the snapshot partial, and a feed with no positions is still malformed.

Two live snapshots 153 s apart, for the 8 aircraft that lost their position between them:

| | retained | stale | removed |
|---|---|---|---|

title: feat(cctv): add MnDOT Minnesota camera pack
body:
## What this changes

The CCTV layer can now show Minnesota DOT (MnDOT) traffic cameras. The list comes keyless at runtime from MnDOT's public IRIS camera list, with a still frame on demand for each camera. The pack is opt-in: with `CCTV_MNDOT_ENABLED=1`, Minneapolis–St Paul freeway cameras appear on the globe next to the existing packs. When I ran it there were 229 Minnesota cameras, all within 8.5 km of one of the two downtowns.

How it fits the existing CCTV machinery:

- **An opt-in live pack.** It sits at the end of `LIVE_PACKS`, after A22, and loads only with `CCTV_MNDOT_ENABLED=1`. Unset, empty or any other value means no request to MnDOT. `CCTV_MNDOT_MAX_SOURCES` (default 1000, clamped 1–2000) and `CCTV_MNDOT_URL` work like the other packs' overrides.
- **Metro first.** Cameras are ordered by distance to Minneapolis and St Paul, so the pack cap and the shared round-robin trim outstate cameras first.
- **Only cameras MnDOT marks `publish` *and* `streamable`.** Anything other than a literal `true` keeps a camera out. Non-streamable cameras have no still to serve.
- **Stills come from a fixed origin and a validated camera name.** The URL is `video.dot.state.mn.us/video/image/metro/<camera>?size=l`, since the list itself carries no URLs. The `metro` path serves outstate cameras too (checked with `D6-C002`, which returns the same bytes under `metro/` and `d6/`).
- **Low-confidence headings.** MnDOT gives only the direction of travel (NB/SB/EB/WB), not where the camera points, and its cameras pan. So the bearing is seeded from it at low confidence, which the layer draws dashed and labels "(ESTIMATED)". Any other value falls back to the shared id-hash prior.
- **A failed download only empties this pack.** The pack contributes nothing until the next refresh and nothing else is affected, the same as the Toronto and NYC packs.

**Effect on other packs:** none in a default install, because the pack is off. Once enabled, Minnesota takes a share of the 4,000 shared round-robin slots within the 7,350-source catalog limit, which comes off the far end of every other round-robin pack. At the default limit, the reserved Québec and World slots are not touched.

## How I verified it

All of this was re-run on Nov 15, after merging current `main`.

- [x] `npm run build`
- [x] `npm test`: 13,086 of 13,099 pass, with 0 failures and 13 skipped, across all 1,092 test files, including the two allocation probes. On Windows, `npm test` on current `main` stops before any test runs, because the runner passes every file path to one `node` process and hits `spawnSync … ENAMETOOLONG`. So I ran the same files with the same flags through the runner's own discovery, 150 files at a time.
- [x] `npm run test:track` (dev server running, pack enabled): 111 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped, with no console errors or 5xx responses.
- [x] Feature gate: `node --test src/data/cctvMndot.test.mjs` passes 17/17. It covers mapping, the opt-in flags, unsafe names, headings, the cap and ordering, error paths (redirect, 5xx, HTML, oversize) and the round-robin share inside the real catalog. It also includes kvnloo's review commit (`d1ef1131`), which runs an enabled MnDOT camera through the real CCTV proxy:
  - `/sources` lists it;
  - `/media` refuses it without fetching anything;
  - `/frame` fetches only its registered still, with manual redirect handling;
  - a caller-supplied `?upstream=` is never fetched.

  The test fails if the pack is left off, or if the stub stops serving the registered still.
- [x] `npm run format:check`, `npm run check:boundaries`, `npm run i18n` and `npm run library:check -- --base-ref origin/main` pass.
- [x] In the running app with `CCTV_MNDOT_ENABLED=1`, opening it over downtown Minneapolis with CCTV on shows a live MnDOT still in the CCTV panel ("Minnesota · … · MnDOT · Upstream snapshot active") and MnDOT cameras along I-94. Frames come through `/api/cctv/frame/<id>` as `image/jpeg` with the proxy's own `no-store` (MnDOT sends `cache-control: private`).

![MnDOT camera stills over downtown Minneapolis](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MattBenesch/gods-eye-view/pr-assets/mndot-cctv-minneapolis.png)

## Data source and licence

- Source: MnDOT IRIS public camera list, `https://data.dot.state.mn.us/iris/camera_pub` (~1,800 cameras, ~425 KB JSON). Stills come from `https://video.dot.state.mn.us/video/image/metro/<camera>?size=l`.
- Licence or terms: MnDOT publishes the list and stills openly with no key, but **I found no explicit licence**. DATA_SOURCES.md says so.
- Attribution shown in the app: "Traffic camera stills (Minnesota): Minnesota Department of Transportation (MnDOT), public camera data from the MnDOT IRIS system".
- Needs a key? None.
- Fetched at runtime; nothing is bundled.
- [x] Added a row to `DATA_SOURCES.md`
- [x] Credit is registered in `src/data/dataCredits.js`

**Opt-in:** Said made the pack opt-in on Nov 7 (`6d0ab25c`). Like Lithuania and Houston, it loads only when an operator enables it, because MnDOT publishes no reuse licence for the stills.

**Known, not handled:** MnDOT's list includes two WisDOT cameras near Hudson, WI, which fall inside the border slack and pass the filter.

## Docs

- [x] `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md` has a new "MnDOT CCTV source pack" section and lists MnDOT in the layers-table CCTV row, and `changelog.d/1437-mndot-minnesota-cameras.md` adds the changelog fragment. README and `.env.example` are updated too.

## Post-Deploy Monitoring & Validation

- **Default installs:** no additional monitoring is needed. The pack is off, and it makes no request to MnDOT.
- **Once an operator enables it, logs:** healthy is `[CCTV] Loaded MnDOT camera sources: N (using M)` on each catalog refresh (`1250 (using 1000)` on Nov 15). Failure is `[CCTV] MnDOT camera download failed (...)`, after which Minnesota is empty until the next refresh while the other packs carry on.
- **Expected:** Minnesota cameras in the CCTV picker near the Twin Cities, and stills loading through `/api/cctv/frame/mndot-*`.
- **Failure signals:** the download warning on consecutive refreshes, or `mndot-*` frames returning errors.
- **Mitigation:** unset `CCTV_MNDOT_ENABLED`. Nothing else depends on the pack.
- **Window and owner:** the first catalog refresh after the pack is enabled, and the first day of use (MattBenesch).

title: feat(message-signs): add Highway message signs for Minnesota freeways
body:
## What this changes

A new **Highway message signs** layer (Infrastructure) shows what Minnesota's freeway dynamic message signs say right now, from MnDOT's keyless IRIS public resources. Every lit sign gets an amber marker. Below 5 km, the 40 lit signs nearest the camera also get a face: MnDOT's own rendered GIF of the message, so the sign on the globe looks like the sign over the road. When I first ran it there were 143 lit signs (100 on Nov 15). Faces matched MnDOT's GIFs pixel for pixel, and I watched a travel time tick from 10 to 9 MIN on the globe.

How it works:

- **A small keyless proxy.** `/api/message-signs` fetches `dms_pub`, `dms_message` and `sign_message` only while the layer is on. It joins them into lit, located, non-failed signs inside Minnesota and caches the result for 30 s. `/api/message-signs/img/<message>.gif` serves only messages named in the current or previous list, as a GIF within 640×200 px and 64 KB.
- **Honest about age.** The data age is read on MnDOT's own clock (`Date` minus `Last-Modified`). Data over two minutes old dims the faces and marks the card STALE. Data over ten minutes old answers 502, and the layer reports MnDOT unavailable.
- **Hardened like the other keyless routes.** It uses the same-site gate (as terrain and CCTV), rate limits per client and globally, and caps every upstream body. A GIF MnDOT has deleted is remembered for 60 s, and any other GIF failure for 15 s, so an outage costs one upstream fetch per message per cooldown.
- **Faces through the world-overlay thumbnail lane.** Each face is a stable slot, re-chosen when the camera stops moving. Faces scale down from 3 km and fade out between 4 and 5 km. Multi-page messages flip on their GIF frame delays from one clock, with one render request per flip. They flip only while the tab is visible and reduced motion is off.
- **A card on click.** A marker or face click toggles a card with the location, the message's lines (MULTI read as text, pages numbered) and the data age. A status node reads it aloud when the sign, message or stale state changes. Scene picks go first, so another layer's object keeps its click. A selected sign keeps its face beyond the nearest 40, but not above 5 km or beyond 40 km: there the face, its decoder and its flip timer are released and the card stays.

**Review fix (thanks @kvnloo).** The review found that a selected sign bypassed the height and distance limits, so an invisible face kept its decoder and flip timer. Their commit `57c54eb` is adopted as-is under their authorship. Their regression test fails on the old code and passes with the fix. I added four cases on top: selection still lifts a sign past the nearest-40 budget; at exactly 5 km and just inside 40 km it keeps its face; a culled face closes its decoder, then comes back and flips once the camera returns; and deselecting or disabling after a cull releases everything. Deleting the selection exemption fails exactly the three in-limit cases.

Checking the fix turned up one more gap, in my original code: closing the card only republished the faces the layer already had, so a face that only the selection had lifted past the budget kept animating, with its decoder open, until the next camera stop or 60 s update. Closing the card now re-chooses the faces (`fix(message-signs): release a face only the selection kept when its card closes`), with a test for both the empty click and Escape that fails without the fix.

**Voice:** off for now. `message-signs` is in `VOICE_OFF_LAYERS`, like `drone-airspace`, `shipwrecks`, `wildlife-sightings` and `rail`, because the Realtime prompt is at its budget. So there is no change to the prompt, the alias hint or the schema pins. My earlier alias-hint change is dropped in favour of the rule #1462 merged.

**Share-link token:** `03`, the next free token from `npm run layer-token:next`. `npm run layer-token:check -- --base-ref origin/main` passes against `main` at `50e39742`. This PR no longer uses `6`, so it no longer collides with the 6–9 that #1415 reserves (all ten single digits are taken on `main` now).

## How I verified it

All after merging current `main` on Nov 15. The build, unit tests, checks and feature gate ran on the final head. `test:track` and the live check ran just before the last few test, fix and docs commits; neither exercises closing a card.

- [x] `npm run build`
- [x] Unit tests: 13,175 of 13,188 pass, 0 fail, 13 skipped. `npm test` stops with ENAMETOOLONG on Windows (on `main` too), so I ran the same test files in chunks with the same flags.
- [x] `npm run test:track` (dev server running): 111 passed, 0 failed.
- [x] Feature gate: `node scripts/qa-message-signs.mjs --url <dev server>` passes 20/20. It stubs MnDOT inside the page and checks the overlay host's own model:
  - nothing is requested while the layer is off;
  - faces paint over I-35W and none statewide;
  - every way to open and close the card works;
  - a changed message redraws the same slot;
  - a two-frame flip makes one render request per flip;
  - empty and unavailable states;
  - no console errors.
- [x] Unit tests for the MULTI reader, the feed join, the proxy (gate, clock, caps, limits, cooldowns) and the layer's ownership of faces, decoders and clicks (87 tests). The new tests each fail against a mutant of the code they cover.
- [x] `npm run format:check`, `npm run check:boundaries`, `npm run i18n`, `npm run library:check -- --base-ref origin/main` and `npm run layer-token:check -- --base-ref origin/main` pass.
- [x] Live against MnDOT on the dev server: 100 signs lit and 40 faces chosen from 2.2 km over downtown Minneapolis, with the I-94 EB @ Lowry Ave face in view. Clicking it opened its card and the status node read it. With that sign selected I raised the camera to 8 km: its face was released and its card stayed. On both routes, cross-site and foreign-Origin requests get 403 and same-origin requests get 200 (the GIF as `image/gif`).

## New layer checklist

**Screenshots**

![Message sign faces over I-35W in downtown Minneapolis](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MattBenesch/gods-eye-view/pr-assets/mndot-message-signs-downtown.png)

![A sign's card: location, message lines and MnDOT data age](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MattBenesch/gods-eye-view/pr-assets/mndot-message-signs-card.png)

![I-35E express lane price signs](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MattBenesch/gods-eye-view/pr-assets/mndot-message-signs-express.png)

![Lit sign markers across the Twin Cities metro](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MattBenesch/gods-eye-view/pr-assets/mndot-message-signs-metro.png)

**Recording**

[27 s recording (6.9 MB .mp4)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MattBenesch/gods-eye-view/pr-assets/mndot-message-signs.mp4): turning the layer on, flying along I-35W, opening a sign's card.

**Proposed category**

Category: Infrastructure, after license plate cameras.

**Data source and licence**

- Source: MnDOT IRIS public resources at `https://data.dot.state.mn.us/iris/`: `dms_pub` (sign locations), `dms_message` (current message and failure state) and `sign_message` (MULTI text). Faces come from `iris/img/<message>.gif`.
- Licence or terms: the [IRIS REST API docs](https://mnit-rtmc.github.io/iris/rest_api.html) list these lists and sign images as public resources, but **I found no explicit licence**. DATA_SOURCES.md says so.
- Attribution shown in the app: "Highway message signs (Minnesota): Minnesota Department of Transportation (MnDOT), public sign messages and sign images from the MnDOT IRIS system".
- Needs a key? None.
- Fetched at runtime; nothing is bundled or stored.

- [x] Added a row to `DATA_SOURCES.md`
- [x] Credit is registered in `src/data/dataCredits.js`
- [x] Share-link token assigned with `npm run layer-token:next` (token `03`)

**Licence and defaults, for your call:** the layer is off until a user turns it on. The MnDOT camera pack in #1437 is now behind an operator opt-in because it has no reuse licence and CCTV packs load by default. This layer never loads by default, which matches how `main` treats other user-toggled layers whose sources have no explicit licence (adsbdb, bike share, transit): they are not gated. If you would rather gate it behind an operator setting as well, I can add one; the layer row would then need a new "not enabled on this server" state.

## Docs

- [x] `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md` has a "Highway message signs" section and a layers-table row. DATA_SOURCES.md, SECURITY.md and README are updated, and `changelog.d/1438-highway-message-signs.md` adds the changelog fragment.
- [x] The row, card labels and count are translated in all 13 shipped locales. German, French, Italian, Japanese, Portuguese, Ukrainian, Arabic, Hebrew and Swedish arrived on `main` after this branch, so their strings were added after merging, following each locale's guide in `docs/translations/`. A native speaker has not checked those nine yet.

## Post-Deploy Monitoring & Validation

- **Expected:** with the layer on, the row reads "N signs lit" (100 to 143 when I ran it). Faces appear over Twin Cities freeways below 5 km.
- **Failure signals:** the row reports MnDOT unavailable for longer than one 60 s update, or faces stay dimmed as STALE.
- **Mitigation:** turn the layer off. It makes no requests while off, and nothing else depends on it.
- **Window and owner:** the first day of use (MattBenesch).
