title: build: add a measurement-first production bundle audit
body:
What this changes

Refs #40.

Adds a measurement-first production bundle audit using Vite's manifest and generated HTML.

  • Reports deterministic raw and gzip sizes for initial static JS/CSS, dynamic import chunks, and other deployed assets.

  • Includes copied Cesium assets that Vite's normal chunk reporting omits.

  • Separately identifies resources whose loading time cannot be determined from build metadata.

  • Integrates bundle reporting into existing Linux and Windows CI builds.

  • Documents the largest bundle costs and measurement limitations in docs/BUNDLE-AUDIT.md.

No runtime behavior, dependencies, warning thresholds, or byte budgets change.

Measured baseline

Compared against upstream main at a4d3701c.

Scope | Raw bytes | Gzip bytes -- | -- | -- Initial static JS | 9,719,127 | 2,967,697 Initial static CSS | 377,544 | 64,993 Entire deployed tree | 45,015,180 | 12,786,468 (text assets only)

Windows and native Linux measurements match. All 447 runtime files remain byte-identical to pristine main; only the Vite manifest is added.

These figures do not represent complete browser startup traffic. Dynamic import edges do not necessarily correspond to feature-demand loading.

How I verified it

  • npm run build — passes on Windows and native Ubuntu 24.04 / WSL2.

  • npm test — Linux: 8,842 passed, 0 failed, 2 skipped. Pristine main: 8,837 passed, 0 failed, 2 skipped.

  • npm run test:track -- --url http://127.0.0.1:4173 --offline-imagery — 107 passed, 2 failed on both candidate and pristine main under native Linux.

  • Focused regression tests — all 5 new bundle-audit fixture tests pass on Windows and Linux; combined discovery/audit tests pass 9/9.

  • npm run format:check

  • npm run check:boundaries

  • Setup doctor and published layer-token validation.

  • Build output comparisons confirm that runtime files remain unchanged.

Existing test failures

The following failures were reproduced on untouched main:

  • Linux tracking: Two flights/military arrival-rotation checks exceed the existing 500 ms deadline. Both candidate and pristine main report 107 passing and 2 failing tests.

  • Windows unit tests: The KML subprocess timeout and sky-image URL pathname failure occur on both trees. Candidate: 8,816 passed, 2 failed, 11 skipped. Pristine main: 8,811 passed, 2 failed, 11 skipped.

An earlier Windows analyst ranking timing failure passed in subsequent isolated and full runs. No assertions, timeouts, or thresholds were modified to suppress failures.

No existing browser qa-*.mjs feature gate directly covers this build-only tooling change. The five new fixture tests provide focused regression coverage.

CI status

GitHub Actions currently reports action_required: maintainer approval is needed before the contribution's hosted CI jobs can execute.

Requesting maintainer review with the baseline-equivalent failures disclosed. The tracking gate is not fully green, and this PR does not claim merge readiness. Maintainer acceptance of the existing failures is still required.

Docs

docs/BUNDLE-AUDIT.md documents the audit commands, baseline measurements, largest assets, acquisition limitations, and rationale for deferring byte budgets.

This PR changes build tooling only. No runtime-state documentation, changelog fragment, or data-source attribution update is required.

title: fix(terrain): keep known heights when a terrain request fails
body:
Follow-up to #1402, from Said's review: during a 429 pause, a terrain request that mixes cached and new points gets 502 as a whole, and the page puts the cached points on its geoid as well. The same happens when the upstream answers one point of a chunk with a null height.

**Change**
- The 502 body carries `partial`: the request's real heights (fresh or stale) in request order, null for points without one, and left out when there are none (`src/data/terrainHeightsProxy.js`). It is not named `results`, so no reader takes a failure for a complete answer, and the existing test that a failure body never carries `results` still holds.
- `getHeights` attaches `partial` to the error it throws when its length matches the request (`src/services/requests.js`). The page caches those heights as Re:Earth heights and uses its geoid, with the 60 s retry, only for the points without one (`src/services/terrainHeights.js`).
- `get_terrain_height` still reports the failure as before. CURRENT-STATE's terrain bullet describes `partial`.

**Verification**
- New tests: the proxy lists a cached point and null for an uncached one during a pause; `getHeights` attaches `partial`; the page keeps a real height from a 502 and falls back only for the null and non-numeric points; a `partial` of the wrong length is ignored. The first three fail on main.
- `npm test`: 8,876 tests, 8,865 pass, 10 skipped, 1 fail (`skyAssets.paintOut`, the unrelated failure from #1401); build, `format:check` and `check:boundaries` pass.

title: fix(deps): pin Node 24.22.1 for the October 21, 2026 security release
body:
## What this changes

The Docker image and CI pin Node 24.14.0, which predates the October 21, 2026 [Node.js security release](https://nodejs.org/en/blog/vulnerability/october-2026-security-releases). That release fixes CVE-2026-111497 ("Node2Shell"), an out-of-bounds write in the bundled Brotli decoder that can lead to remote code execution, plus several high-severity DNS, TLS and URL-parsing issues. 24.22.1 is the first patched 24.x release (26.12.1 is the patched 26.x; the CI `26.x` entry already floats to it).

- `Dockerfile`: `node:24.22.1-slim`, digest re-pinned to the multi-arch index (`sha256:be8204d4…`).
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: 24.22.1 in the `verify` matrix and in the other two jobs. `GEV_REQUIRE_ALLOCATION_GATE` compares `matrix.node` as a string, so it now keys on `24.22.1`.
- `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `README.md`, `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md`: setup snippet and dependency baseline name 24.22.1.

Deliberately **not** changed, as a maintainer call: the `engines` floor (`>=24.14.0`), the setup doctor's "24.14 or newer" message and its tests. Raising the floor would stop `npm` accepting 24.14–24.22.0 for anyone not using the pinned image or CI. I haven't found any Brotli decoding in this repo's own code (the two outbound calls that set `Accept-Encoding` ask for gzip only), so exposure comes from Node's own `fetch` and dependencies rather than a call site here.

I searched open and closed PRs and issues for a Node bump first and found none. #1424 reworks the Dockerfile's `FROM` lines and #1428 adds Dependabot; whichever lands second will need a one-line pin update (or Dependabot will raise it).

## How I verified it

- [x] `npm run build`
- [x] `npm test` with `GEV_REQUIRE_ALLOCATION_GATE=1` on Node 24.22.1: 8,875 tests, 0 failures, 1 skipped, plus the 14 allocation microbenchmarks passing on 24.22.1.
- [x] `npm run test:track` (dev server running): 109 passed, 0 failed on one run. Two other runs on this branch each failed one of the `arrival: … exceeded 500 ms` timing assertions (750 ms and 762 ms against a 500 ms budget). The same family of assertion also fails intermittently on unmodified `main` on my machine (651 ms and 505 ms in two of two runs), so this is a pre-existing flake under software-rendered headless Chromium, not something this change touches.
- [x] Feature gate for the area I touched: none applies (Docker base image, CI pins and docs only).
- Also green: `npm run format:check`, `npm run check:boundaries`, `npm run i18n`.
- Not verified locally: I could not build or run the Docker image (no Docker daemon available). I confirmed against the registry that the `24.22.1-slim` tag resolves to the pinned digest, using the same lookup that reproduces the existing 24.14.0 pin.

## Docs

- [x] `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md` updated. A `changelog.d/<pr-number>-<slug>.md` fragment follows in a second commit once this PR has a number.

title: Cut the Google requests the HUD summary makes on its own
body:
## What this changes

The HUD builds place context for its AI summary whenever the camera settles. Each build paid for up to four Google reverse geocodes and a Places Nearby Search. It did this even when no OpenAI key was configured, so the summary could never use the results. The 4-decimal cache key missed on almost every pan, and nothing else limited the calls apart from the 15 s summary tick.

- **No summary, no lookups.** The page asks `GET /api/openai/hud-summary/status` once. With no OpenAI key configured, or after an unconfigured reply, the HUD makes no place lookups for the rest of the page.
- **Two points at most.** It reverse-geocodes the view center and one viewport point, instead of up to four. Nearby Places is still added below 25 km.
- **Look up again only when the view changes.** A lookup is reused until one of these happens:
  - the view center moves a quarter of the visible width, measured from the camera's distance to the center so terrain and tilt scale it;
  - that distance doubles or halves;
  - the camera crosses one of the lookup heights.

  A reused lookup asks again for the same points. Cache hits are free, so only a timeout, failure or empty answer spends.
- **The summary line stays.** When a small pan leaves the context unchanged, the last AI reply is repainted instead of the fallback line, and no new OpenAI request is made.

Voice context lookups are unchanged. A host that passes `basemapContext: { cachedOnly: true }` keeps reading every cached sample.

**Measured.** I ran the same scripted session in the real app before and after: load, 30 pans, then zoom out and in.

| | Google calls | AI summary requests |
|---|---|---|
| Before, OpenAI configured | 29 | 10 |
| After, OpenAI configured | 13 | 2 |
| Before, no OpenAI key | 20 | n/a |
| After, no OpenAI key | 0 | n/a |

## How I verified it

- [x] `npm run build`
- [x] `npm test` (8,895 passing, 1 skipped)
- [x] `npm run test:track` (dev server running): 109 passed, 0 failed
- [x] Feature gate for the area I touched: none applies. New unit tests are in `src/voice/hudPlaceLabels.test.mjs`, `src/hudSummaryGate.test.mjs`, `src/services/requests.test.mjs` and `src/tooling/localServices.test.mjs`. They fail on the previous code.

`npm run check:boundaries`, `npm run format:check` and `npm run doctor -- --json` also pass.

title: feat: export Director cameras for Blender
body:
## What changes

Export a saved Director scene into editable Blender cameras using an offline, camera-only manifest. It preserves scene/shot identity, WGS84 origin, ENU meters, horizontal lens, rational fps and authored seek timing. The importer creates a separate scene with shot cameras, quaternion keys and camera markers, validates inputs and refuses output overwrites.

This complements #1081 without changing Director playback. It transfers no imagery, tiles or geometry and requires no provider credentials.

Capacity testing exposed slow per-sample Blender key insertion. The importer now bulk-writes each animation channel. The projection check also verifies all seven channels, sample frame indices and linear interpolation before and after save/reload. A separate test-only commit fixes the existing Windows sky-fixture URL conversion using `fileURLToPath`, preserving its image assertions and tolerance.

## Validation

Submitted head: `21ac12c105d1f1b5d7c8fd110ba5012ed45adafa`, based on current upstream main `f2c6ff08`.

- **All four CI jobs passed for this exact head:** Linux Node 24.14.0, Linux Node 26.x, Windows onboarding and Street Level browser fixtures. [Full run and logs](https://github.com/UBN606/gods-eye-view/actions/runs/40807908895). This ran on the public contributor fork; the upstream workflow separately awaits maintainer approval.
- **Fresh live camera checks:** Director 12/12; native-browser tracking 109/109. Tracking command: `node scripts/track-regression.mjs --url <isolated-app-url> --offline-imagery --headful`. The browser-tested camera/timeline/QA source bytes are unchanged in this head.
- **Actual Blender 5.2.2 LTS import/save/reload:** three landscape, portrait and integer-valued-input cases; 216 independent Cesium landmark projections before save and 216 after reload. Maximum normalized image error: `2.4742e-7`. New curve-count, frame-index and linear-interpolation checks passed.
- **Maximum supported capacity:** 100,000 frames / 700,000 keys. Import: 1.42 seconds; save: 0.19 seconds; reopen: 0.06 seconds. All seven channel counts/interpolation and first/middle/last camera poses were checked before and after reopening. No rendering.
- **Additional checks:** 12 focused camera/CLI regressions; four Python validation/output-guard tests; production build; formatting; package boundaries; setup doctor; layer-token reservations; i18n. A fresh read-only review of the bulk importer found no actionable issues.

The first software-rendered tracking attempt had 108 passes and one failure: the arrival reveal observation exceeded its 500 ms deadline at 503.9 ms. The documented native-browser mode subsequently passed 109/109 with identical assertions and the unchanged deadline. The software-renderer timing failure is retained, not represented as a pass.

The initial maximum-capacity attempt exceeded its bounded time window before the bulk-write fix. The successful capacity and projection measurements above use the fixed importer.

## Scope

Sampling follows Director seek interpolation. Implicit live `flyTo` paths, runtime layer timing and changing lenses are outside this camera-only format. Blender qualification is 5.2.2 LTS. The bridge does not depend on a video exporter. Changelog fragment `1460-blender-camera-interchange.md` is included.

title: fix(infrastructure): ground-sample only stem bases the camera sees
body:
With Data Centers on over Ashburn, Virginia, on the Esri map, rest frames on main averaged 58 to 997 ms across runs, with slow frames reaching 2 s. The cost comes and goes between windows rather than settling.

**Cause**
`scene.sampleHeight` reads only surface rendered for the current view. For a data-centre or dam base within 75 km that the camera can't see, it reads through the Earth: about -6,344 km at Ashburn. That fails the 9,000 m plausibility check, so the record retries every 2 s indefinitely, each retry a full offscreen render. In a probe at a 20 km, -35° camera over Ashburn, all 222 failing samples were outside the frustum, and all 171 samples inside it succeeded.

**Change** (`src/data/localGeojsonCore.js`)
- `sampleLocalGroundHeight` skips ground the camera can't see, without stamping `lastGroundSampleMs`, so it is sampled on the first walk that sees it. This covers both callers, the walk and `updateLocalStemGeometry`. Unseen ground no longer arms the ground-retry render, so a parked camera goes idle.
- An unsampled base sits on the ellipsoid, which over high terrain can project off screen while the ground above it is in view. So the test uses loaded globe terrain when there is some (Esri). With the globe hidden (Google 3D) it tests the vertical from 0 to 9,000 m, out of view only when both ends are outside the same frustum plane.
- The horizon test uses the ground's height, but not below 0 m: Cesium's ellipsoidal occluder hides ground below the ellipsoid (low-geoid coasts, the Dead Sea) from a camera near it.
- A stem whose base is just off screen keeps its unsampled height until the ground comes into view. CURRENT-STATE's infrastructure paragraph says so.

**Measurement**
Production builds, Intel Arc, `dc-ashburn` camera (20 km, -35°), Data Centers and Dams, 3 windows of 5 s per sample, rest windows. Main (A) against this branch with the in-view test on loaded terrain (C, ecc0ced4), run in the order A1 C1 C2 A2 on each basemap:
- Esri, Data Centers, `sampleHeight` per window: A 222 and 222 calls; C 0 and 0.
- Esri, Data Centers, mean frame (whole tick): A 931.7 and 996.8 ms (p95 2.02 and 1.99 s); C 7.7 and 8.2 ms.
- Esri, Data Centers, main-thread task time: A 700 and 691 ms/s; C 292 and 297 ms/s.
- Esri, Dams, mean frame: A 24.4 and 19.3 ms (2-3 `sampleHeight` calls per window); C 4.6 and 3.8 ms.
- Google 3D: no `sampleHeight` calls in either build; mean frame A 9.4 and 9.4 ms, C 9.3 and 9.1 ms.

The final commit (below-0 m horizon, hidden-globe vertical) was measured afterwards, not interleaved with main: no `sampleHeight` calls in any Esri or Google 3D rest window, and the Ashburn probe again sampled all 171 in-view data centres in the first 5 s with no failures.

**Verification**
- New tests use a real Cesium camera and frustum, and each fails on the code before it: ground outside the frustum or over the horizon is not sampled and arms no retry render; 2,500 m ground in view is sampled with loaded terrain and with a hidden globe although its 0 m point is off screen; ground at -63 m seen from 50 m is sampled; with a hidden globe, ground behind the camera is not.
- `npm test`: 8,904 tests, 1 fail (`skyAssets.paintOut`, Windows-only, fixed in #1461); `format:check`, `check:boundaries` and the build pass.

title: feat(config): load standalone browser credentials at runtime
body:
## What this changes

Built standalone apps currently embed their browser credentials, so changing those values requires rebuilding. This loads the three intentional browser credentials from the existing local server before scene startup, while preserving build-time and keyless fallback.

- `GET /api/runtime-config` returns only the Google Maps browser key, Cesium ion token and Mapillary client token as uncached JSON. Server-only credentials are excluded.
- The same-origin reader refuses redirects, caps responses at 16 KiB and completes within one second, including body consumption. Missing, empty, invalid or unavailable values retain the corresponding build value; cancelled startup cannot construct the scene.
- Resolved values reach scene/search providers and the Mapillary photo viewer. MCP panel builds preserve their separately restricted embedded credentials and exclude the runtime request.
- Existing Host checks and API security headers remain in place. This does not add production hosting support or change provider admission.

## How I verified it

Refreshed onto public base `aaa3ff46cfac5393ab122bb5f50019a2c051d926`, including its updated Vite/Puppeteer dependencies:

- [x] Frontend and MCP panel production builds.
- [x] Node 26: 8,913 ordinary tests passed, two skipped, no failures.
- [x] Node 24: all 15 calibrated allocation checks passed.
- [x] Built Street Level fixture gate: 12/12 passed, zero skips, using a keyless build and synthetic runtime credentials; Mapillary, KartaView and Panoramax requests intercepted.
- [x] Format, import/package boundaries and changelog validation.

On the earlier public base `2bcdca1c`, the candidate also passed the complete Node 24/26 unit suites, real-GPU tracking (109/109), the keyless map-source/keyboard/responsive gate and ten development/preview HTTP checks. The map-source fixture stub now targets the controller used by physical input, preserving its assertions and avoiding an unintended microphone/token request.

Synthetic fixtures only; no real credentials or personal configuration included. Live paid-provider acceptance and hosted CI have not been run for this contribution.

## Docs

- [x] Runtime, contributor and security documentation updated.
- [x] Added `changelog.d/1465-runtime-browser-config.md`; changelog validation passed.

No new data layer, source licence, dependency or UI message is introduced.

title: Rename the Scenes panel to Authoring and lay it out in steps
body: ## What this changes The Scenes panel is renamed **Authoring** and reorganized so it's easier to read and use when building a scene. - **Steps**: controls are grouped under SCENE, SHOTS, PREVIEW and SAVE & SHARE headings. The scene picker gets its own full-width row, and the EDIT DETAILS / SHARE SCENE row moves from below the status line to sit beside EXPORT / IMPORT. - **Readability**: text is larger (shot names 12px, meta and status 10–11px, up from 8–10px), and secondary text has more contrast through a panel token instead of `--text-dim`. Shots are numbered 01, 02…, and a hint explains click-to-select and double-click-to-rename. - **Clearer labels**: NEW → NEW SCENE, DEL → DELETE, CAPTURE SHOT → + CAPTURE SHOT, START → PLAY, EXPORT PRESETS → EXPORT. CAPTURE SHOT and PLAY are highlighted using the theme's `--accent`, including in Cyber. The file row is quieter, and every button in the step rows has a tooltip describing what it actually does (PLAY runs from this scene through the rest of the project; NEXT can move on to the next scene). The restyled buttons keep a hover state. Button sizing (72px minimum, equal growth) and the 360px panel width are unchanged, and the larger type applies only inside this panel. The shot list always keeps two rows visible; on shorter windows the panel scrolls instead. Renaming a shot shows the editor at full width. - **No dead buttons**: outside playback, a button that would do nothing is disabled. That means DELETE and CAPTURE SHOT without a scene, UPDATE SHOT without a selected shot, and PLAY and NEXT when no scene in the project has a shot. Both continue into the following scenes, so an empty selected scene next to scenes with shots keeps them available. During playback the authoring and file actions stay disabled and STOP is enabled, as before. - **Accessibility**: the status line is a polite live region, and the picker's accessible name is "Scene". - **i18n**: every new label and tooltip is translated in all ten shipped languages (de, es, fr, it, ja, pt, ru, uk, zh-CN, zh-Hant), following each language's translator guide, and the retired entries are pruned. The scene's PLAY uses a `scene|PLAY` context, because the radio's PLAY translates as "listen" (ESCUCHAR, OUVIR). Short forms (REPROD., ПУСК, START, СТАРТ) and a tighter file row keep every button to whole words per line in both themes; a headless check measured that for all eight non-English Latin and Cyrillic languages plus Japanese. "Scene" stays the content term, so dialogs, director status, sharing and the voice routing that maps "Scenes" to `scene-panel` are unchanged. Docs that name the panel now say Authoring, and voice also accepts "authoring" as a name for the panel. ## Screenshots | Before (`main`) | After | | --- | --- | | | | | Cyber theme | Spanish (`?lang=es`) | | --- | --- | | | | **Building a scene.** NEW SCENE starts empty, so PLAY, NEXT and UPDATE SHOT are disabled. title: Keep Radio Next and Previous from starting playback before Play
body:
## Summary


Before Play was pressed, clicking Next in the Radio panel picked a station, flipped Play to Pause and started "Buffering broadcaster stream…", although the note beside the controls says audio connects only after Play. `cycleRadio` in `src/ui/radioBindings.js` called `cycleStation` without `autoplay`, which defaults to `true`.

### Next and Previous

In the Context Radio section and Cockpit, Next and Previous pass `autoplay` only while a stream is loading, buffering or playing.

- **Stopped, paused or failed:** they only select. Selecting another station stops a paused or failed stream, so the panel shows Ready and PLAY, Stop is disabled, and Play starts the selected station.
- **Playing:** the stream follows the new station, with the broadcaster fallback as before.
- A silent step arms no fallback, so a later Play cannot jump to a station picked under an earlier filter. Selections now take the fallback as a `playFallback` option instead of callers setting layer state beforehand.

### Tuning dial

The dial follows the same rule. Releasing it plays the chosen station only if a stream was loading, buffering or playing when the drag began. Otherwise it just selects the station, with no stream and no tuning static. Before, every release started playback.

### Voice

- Voice play, next and previous prepare a station silently and start it after the reply. They pass `fallback: true`, so that playback keeps its fallback. If the handoff is cancelled, a later Play from the panel drops the leftover fallback.
- A user step to another station sends a `select` playback control. The realtime voice handoff treats it like Pause and Stop: a prepared voice playback is dropped, so it does not start after the user picked something else.

### Copy

The privacy note now reads "Audio connects directly to the broadcaster when you press play, choose a station on the globe or ask voice to play. Your IP is visible to that broadcaster." It is updated in all eleven locales. Clicking a globe marker still plays straight away, as before.

### Related states found in review

- The transport buttons show Pause while a stream connects, because a click pauses it.
- If the directory changed the station under the tuner needle mid-drag (`station-unavailable`), the stream the drag paused is stopped. The button reads PLAY instead of a RESUME that would have started another station, and a voice handoff is cancelled.

Both were already wrong on `main`.

## Tests

- `src/data/radioNextState.test.mjs` (new, 16 tests) runs the real Radio layer and renders the panel. It covers:
  - Next before Play;
  - Next after a stream error and while paused;
  - a catalog refresh after a paused Next;
  - the fallback for a voice request after a voice pause and for a cancelled voice step;
  - a silent user step and a silent dial release dropping the fallback a voice step left;
  - `select` control emission;
  - a dial release from stopped, paused, connecting and playing streams;
  - the tuner static: a silent release stops its noise source and suspends its audio context, even when the release lands before `resume()` settles, and a second gesture in that window keeps its graph;
  - the `station-unavailable` tuner release;
  - the labels while a stream connects.
- `src/testSupport/radioLayerHarness.mjs` holds the shared Radio layer stand-ins. The tuner fallback test in `src/data/radio.test.mjs` uses it too and now starts from a playing stream, since a release from stopped no longer plays.
- Updated tests:
  - `src/ui/radioControls.test.mjs`: Next and Previous send `autoplay` only while a stream is active.
  - `src/voice/gevRealtime.test.mjs`: a user `select` cancels a pending voice handoff, as Stop does.
  - `src/voice/gevActions.test.mjs`: voice steps pass `fallback: true`.
- `npm test` (merged with current `main`): 9844 pass, 0 fail, 1 skipped.
- Format, `npm run check:boundaries`, `npm run i18n` (all eleven locales complete) and `npm run changelog:check` pass; the build without keys passes.
- Headless browser checks on the Vue UI:
  - the regression scenarios passed on earlier revisions (15/15 for the repro, 72/72 for the broader walk);
  - a dial walk with mouse, keyboard and touch: a release from stopped, paused or error only selects the station and releases the tuner noise; a release from a playing or connecting stream plays the new station;
  - the same dial check on `main` confirms the old behaviour: the first drag starts playback.
- `scripts/qa-radio.mjs`:
  - the Next fallback scenario relied on Next starting a stream from Stop, which this PR removes. It now starts from a playing station and still covers the fallback and the camera rotation;
  - the stopped-release scenario now expects a silent selection, and the channel-12 and failed-tuner-static scenarios start playback first;
  - on this branch and on current `main` it gives the same 86 pass and 8 fail (HUD-off and Tactical lanes, tuner keyboard navigation, filtered-directory center, mobile Context host), then the same click error. Those failures predate this branch.

title: feat: Rio de Janeiro bus and BRT positions in Transit (keyless GTFS-RT, CC BY 4.0)
body:
### Problem

The Transit layer has no city in Latin America. Rio de Janeiro's transport secretariat (SMTR) now publishes keyless GTFS-Realtime VehiclePositions feeds for the city's buses and its BRT, so Rio could be the first. The Mobility Database catalog lists no GTFS-RT feed anywhere in Latin America, which makes these two feeds unusual for the region.

Rio's older JSON position APIs (`/gps/sppo`, `/gps/brt`, `/sppo/conecta/gps` and others) were marked deprecated on 2026-10-07, and their catalog pages say they will be switched off by 30/11/2026 ("será desabilitado até 30/11/2026"). These GTFS-RT feeds are the named replacement, so they are the right ones to build on.

### Proposal

Add two rows to `src/data/transitFeeds.js`, with matching rows in DATA_SOURCES.md and credits in `src/data/dataCredits.js`:

- `smtr-rio-onibus`: https://dados.mobilidade.rio/gtfs/realtime/onibus/vehicle-positions
- `smtr-rio-brt`: https://dados.mobilidade.rio/gtfs/realtime/brt/vehicle-positions

Both are buses (`defaultMode: 'bus'`). A center around -22.91, -43.32 with a 60 km load radius covers the city.

**What I checked** (2026-10-29, about 15:35 BRT): fetched both URLs without any key and decoded them with `decodeVehiclePositions` from `src/data/gtfsRealtime.js`.

- Buses: HTTP 200, `application/x-protobuf`, about 314 KB, 2,491 valid vehicles, median position age about 47 s.
- BRT: HTTP 200, about 26 KB, 202 valid vehicles, median position age about 39 s.

**Things to decide**

1. **Speed unit.** `speed` looks like km/h, not m/s as the spec requires. In one snapshot of 2,510 buses: median 18, p90 42, max 89 (89 m/s would be 320 km/h). BRT max was 62. Options: a per-feed unit or scale option, hiding speed for these feeds, or reporting it upstream (the catalog lists infra.smtr@prefeitura.rio).
2. **Beta status.** Both catalog pages label the feeds [beta]. Whether they ship with `defaultEnabled: true` before that label goes is your call.

**Possible second city: Belo Horizonte (needs a maintainer decision)**

- The PBH open-data portal lists a GTFS-RT dataset under CC BY: https://dados.pbh.gov.br/dataset/gtfs-rt. It is served by Mobilibus, and the published URLs carry an `accesskey` query parameter that the portal itself prints. No registration is needed, but it is a key in the URL, so it may not meet the "no key" admission rule. I have not tested this feed.
- PBH also publishes keyless position files every 20 s (CSV and JSON, CC BY, about 2,580 buses when I checked): https://dados.pbh.gov.br/dataset/tempo_real_onibus_-_coordenada. That is not GTFS-RT, so it would need an adapter plus the dataset's line-code conversion file. The host sits behind a WAF that answered "Acesso Bloqueado" to curl's default User-Agent but served other clients.

Is a key that the publisher prints on its own open-data page acceptable, or should Belo Horizonte wait?

**Other Latin American cities I looked at**

- São Paulo (SPTrans Olho Vivo), Buenos Aires (API Transporte) and Curitiba (URBS): position APIs exist, but each needs a key or registration (401 without one).
- Brasília, Goiânia, Porto Alegre, Fortaleza and Recife: no open real-time positions found.
- Mexico City: the Metrobús RT feed listed on the HDTP hub declares no license and is marked demo-only.

### Data source, license, and attribution

| | Buses (SPPO) | BRT |
|---|---|---|
| URL | https://dados.mobilidade.rio/gtfs/realtime/onibus/vehicle-positions | https://dados.mobilidade.rio/gtfs/realtime/brt/vehicle-positions |
| Catalog page | https://www.data.rio/documents/997bc16cc4344a5cb0e48ab06cbdfd1f | https://www.data.rio/documents/8bb196cc02174d25b77437bb2f6443d4 |
| Publisher | SMTR, Prefeitura da Cidade do Rio de Janeiro | same |
| License | CC BY 4.0 | CC BY 4.0 |
| Key | none | none |

- **License text on both catalog pages:** "This work is licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License".
- **Gateway policy (same pages):** 5 requests per second and 60 per minute, 10 s in-memory cache. Polling every 15 to 30 s stays well inside it.
- **Accuracy note:** SMTR receives the raw tracking from the concessionaires' ITS suppliers and applies its own trip matching (pygtfsrealtime); the pages say accuracy ultimately depends on the suppliers.
- **Suggested attribution:** "SMTR / Prefeitura do Rio de Janeiro, data.rio (CC BY 4.0)".

I can help test, and I can contact SMTR in Portuguese if that helps.

### Will you build it?

Yes, I plan to open a PR

title: feat(transit): add Rio de Janeiro buses and BRT (SMTR GTFS-RT, CC BY 4.0)
body:
## What this changes

Adds Rio de Janeiro to the Transit layer as two keyless GTFS-Realtime feeds published by the city's transport secretariat (SMTR) under CC BY 4.0: municipal buses (SPPO) and the Mobi-Rio BRT. It is the layer's first Latin American region. Closes #1480.

- `src/data/transitFeeds.js`: two registry rows, `smtr-rio-onibus` and `smtr-rio-brt`, with license, catalog links, quoted terms and a note on what the catalog pages say (beta label, gateway limits, the JSON endpoints these replace).
- **Speed unit.** Both feeds put km/h in `Position.speed` instead of m/s. A new optional registry field, `speedUnit: 'kmh'`, is read by `buildTransitSnapshot`, which converts once through `normalizeFeedSpeeds`, so every `speedMps` consumer stays correct. Feeds without the field are untouched.
- Docs: a DATA_SOURCES.md row, the feed count there (eighteen feeds, seventeen regions), and the region lists in README.md and docs/CURRENT-STATE.md.

Through this branch's dev server, `/api/transit/vehicles/<id>` on 2026-10-29:

| Feed | Vehicles | Displayed speed after conversion |
|---|---|---|
| `smtr-rio-onibus` | 2,522 | median 18 km/h, max 81 km/h (would read 292 km/h unconverted) |
| `smtr-rio-brt` | 226 | median 27 km/h, max 62 km/h |

Both are FULL_DATASET and answer with an ETag and Last-Modified. Every vehicle sat within 31 km of the registered center, so the 45 km load radius covers the city from Santa Cruz to the Zona Sul. The attribution panel shows the CC BY 4.0 credit with each catalog link.

The failures were flight and military checks (arrival reveal at 516 to 736 ms against a 500 ms budget, and one stale-label check), and their count changed between runs on this Windows machine; nothing here touches those paths.

The run then failed 21 checks and left 13 unexercised: card-anchor sample counts, the 800 and 3,000 moving-vehicle CPU, frame-interval and allocation budgets (top allocators in `detection.js` and Cesium), one bright-background contrast case, and a detached-frame harness error.
  - This PR changes the registry and the proxy's speed field only, not rendering. I have not run the gate on `main` from this machine for comparison.

- [x] New tests: Rio coverage (Centro, Barra, Santa Cruz in range; Sao Paulo out), the Rio rows' license and `speedUnit`, and km/h conversion applying only to a feed that declares it.

## Data source and licence

Not a new layer, so the layer checklist does not apply; the source details are here for review.

- Source: SMTR, Prefeitura da Cidade do Rio de Janeiro. `https://dados.mobilidade.rio/gtfs/realtime/onibus/vehicle-positions` and `https://dados.mobilidade.rio/gtfs/realtime/brt/vehicle-positions`

## Left for later

title: feat: keyless South American fire detections from INPE's Programa Queimadas (VIIRS 375 m, MODIS, GOES-19)
body:
### Problem

Active Fires is empty without a `FIRMS_MAP_KEY`. #497 adds keyless NOAA GOES ABI detections (about 2 km), and its description notes that keyless VIIRS and MODIS are not available from NASA because LAADS and LP DAAC require an Earthdata Login.

For South America there is a keyless source of exactly those detections. Brazil's National Institute for Space Research (INPE) runs Programa Queimadas and publishes its processed detections every 10 minutes as plain CSV, including VIIRS 375 m (NPP, NOAA-20), MODIS (Aqua) and GOES-19. The South American dry season (Cerrado, Amazon, Pantanal, Chaco) is one of the largest fire regions on Earth, so a keyless VIIRS-resolution source there would matter.

### Proposal

- A server-side reader for the 10-minute files at https://dataserver-coids.inpe.br/queimadas/queimadas/focos/csv/10min/ (`focos_10min_YYYYMMDD_HHMM.csv`; 122 files on 2026-10-29 by 20:10). Each row is `lat,lon,satelite,data`.
- Keep a rolling window (for example the last 24 hours) and feed it into Active Fires as an extra source for South America, labelled by satellite. It could serve only when FIRMS has no key, or run alongside FIRMS with de-duplication; that is your call.
- First version: points only. The 10-minute files carry no FRP or confidence.

**What I checked (2026-10-29).** The newest file (20:10) held 1,936 detections between latitude -39.7 and 11.1 and longitude -74.9 and -37.6: AQUA_M-T 1,070, NOAA-20 767, GOES-19 64, NPP-375 35. No key; a plain HTTPS directory listing.

**Open questions**
- The time zone of the `data` column: the file named 20:10 held detections stamped 18:47.
- Overlap with #497 and #1146: GOES-19 rows appear in both. INPE's VIIRS and MODIS rows are what neither has.

### Data source, license, and attribution

- Source: INPE Programa Queimadas, https://dataserver-coids.inpe.br/queimadas/queimadas/focos/csv/10min/ (portal: https://terrabrasilis.dpi.inpe.br/queimadas/portal/)
- Key: none.
- License: not stated on the files. The Queimadas portal footer reads "Dados Abertos para Uso Público" (open data for public use), and its host site, TerraBrasilis, carries a CC BY-SA 4.0 notice (https://terrabrasilis.dpi.inpe.br/en/about/). I can ask INPE to confirm the terms for the CSV files if that is needed before anything ships.
- Attribution: "Programa Queimadas, INPE".

### Will you build it?

Yes, I plan to open a PR

title: feat: Brazilian aircraft details from ANAC's open registry (RAB), technical fields only
body:
### Problem

For Brazilian-registered aircraft (PP-, PR-, PS-, PT-, PU-), the flight card shows at most the type and registration from adsbdb or, with #1230, the Mictronics database. Brazil's civil aviation agency (ANAC) publishes its full aircraft registry (RAB) as open data, refreshed daily, with details those sources lack: year of manufacture, seats and maximum passengers, certification category, type of operation (private, public, air taxi, airline), and whether the registration is cancelled.

### Proposal

- Download https://sistemas.anac.gov.br/dadosabertos/Aeronaves/RAB/dados_aeronaves.csv (24 MB; its first line read "Atualizado em: 2026-10-29") at most once a day, keep only technical columns, and index them by registration (`MARCAS`, for example `PRJLE`).
- Join on the registration the app already gets from adsbdb (or #1230). RAB carries no Mode S address, so there is no hex join.
- A card line such as "Cessna 188B · built 1972 · 1 seat · private" for matched aircraft.

**Privacy.** `PROPRIETARIOS` and `OPERADORES` hold names and documents. In the 2026-10-29 file, 15,645 owner entries are private individuals: the CPF is partly masked, the name is in full. The file also lists liens (`DS_GRAVAME`), sale dates and sale prices. The proposal drops all of those columns at parse time and never caches, displays or passes them to voice or MCP tools, in line with the project's rule against features that identify individuals. Showing an operator name only for airline and air-taxi certificate holders (62 and 1,093 aircraft) could be a later, separate decision.

**Numbers (2026-10-29).** 35,094 aircraft, of which 8,203 are cancelled; 30,813 carry an ICAO type designator; 26,458 carry a year of manufacture.

### Data source, license, and attribution

- Source: ANAC, Registro Aeronáutico Brasileiro, https://www.anac.gov.br/acesso-a-informacao/dados-abertos/areas-de-atuacao/aeronaves/registro-aeronautico-brasileiro
- Key: none.
- License: the dataset page states none. It is published under ANAC's open-data plan and listed on the federal open data portal. I can ask ANAC to confirm the reuse terms if that is needed before anything ships.
- Attribution: "ANAC, Registro Aeronáutico Brasileiro (RAB)".

Yes, I plan to open a PR

title: perf(cctv): draw only the cameras in view, thinned when zoomed out
body:
## What this changes

The CCTV layer kept every loaded camera live. Every view change touched every icon, every state notification rebuilt every camera's full state, and the picker listed the whole catalog. With large catalogs this cost frame rate while moving the globe, with long stalls. The layer now does work only for the cameras you can see.

- **Only cameras in view are drawn.** Cameras behind the globe or well off-screen are hidden.
- **Fewer icons when zoomed out.** The ground is split into cells sized to the view, and each cell shows one camera, preferring a healthy feed. Cells are anchored to the ground, not the screen, so panning keeps the same cameras and small zooms don't flicker. The active camera always shows.
- **Smooth while moving.**
  - The view pass reruns during camera motion, paced at ten times its own measured cost, and skips tiny moves.
  - It projects with one view-projection matrix per pass instead of a Cesium call per camera.
  - The `BillboardCollection` buffer-usage hint is kept fixed. Before, showing or hiding a few icons flipped it and rewrote the vertex data of every billboard, which caused the longest stalls.
- **Geometry loads only for cameras in view.** Ground placement and coverage are loaded for the cameras in view, the active camera and its coverage neighbours, with at most two attempts per camera and view regime and a cooldown between them.
- **The picker lists what's in view.** It puts the active camera first and closes with a greyed-out "N more cameras outside this view · pan or zoom out" line, translated for every shipped locale. The full camera list in the UI state is built only when something reads it.
- **Lifecycle fixes.** View listeners and the resize observer follow a re-created viewer or canvas, the motion timer stops on disable and destroy, and late ground-height data moves cameras into place.

## How I verified it

- [x] `npm run build`
- [x] `npm test` (9,069 pass, 1 skipped; includes new `cctvViewThinning` and `cctvPicker` tests), `npm run format:check`, `npm run check:boundaries`, `npm run i18n` (all locales complete)
- [ ] `npm run test:track` (dev server running)
- [x] Feature gate for the area I touched: none applies; measured in the browser instead

Frame rate in Chrome (one-tab window), dev server with the default CCTV catalog (4,000 cameras), whole-US view, CCTV on. A stall is a frame over 30 ms.

| | `main` | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| Idle fps | 168–180 | 238–239 |
| Dragging fps | 152–179 | 235–236 |
| Stalls per 4 s drag | 18–24 (worst 112 ms) | 0 (worst 25 ms) |
| Picker entries | 4,000 | 18 + "3,982 more cameras outside this view" |

At street level in Austin the PR runs at 237 fps idle and 232 fps dragging. With a 33,000-camera catalog, dragging went from about 100 fps with 145 ms stalls to about 205 fps with none.

## Docs

- [x] `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md` updated and a `changelog.d/<pr-number>-<slug>.md` fragment added

title: fix(hud): AI summary in the UI language, canonical feed state, partial aggregation
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #602. The AI HUD summary is now written in the UI language. The feed state comes back as a structured, canonical field instead of an English word in the prose, and `partial` no longer disappears when layer states are aggregated.

## Changes

**1. `partial` in the shared feed-state table** (`src/data/layerSnapshot.js`)
- `layerFeedState()` could already return `partial`, but `LAYER_FEED_STATES`, `LAYER_FEED_STATE_LABELS` and `FEED_STATE_SEVERITY` did not list it, so `worstFeedState()` skipped it. One partial layer aggregated to `off`, and partial plus nominal aggregated to `nominal`.
- `partial` now sits between `fallback` and `nominal`. The order of the existing states is unchanged, so every fault still outranks it.
- A partial view is narrated as incomplete coverage rather than as not live.
- Every consumer of `feedProvenanceEnvelope()` is corrected by this:
  - the HUD fallback line and its telemetry tag (`hudTelemetryProvenance`);
  - voice view state (`src/voice/gevActions.js`);
  - analyst provenance (`analyst_query`, `src/data/analystEngine.js`);
  - the `brief` query tool (`src/tools/queries/brief.js`);
  - the agent world packet (`src/agent/worldPacket.js`).

**2. Summary in the UI language**
- `_summaryContext()` sends `locale: getLocale()`. The context is already the dedupe signature (`JSON.stringify(context)`), so the locale is part of it.
- The proxy resolves the locale with `normalizeLocale()` from the supported list, falling back to English. English requests keep the old instructions. For other languages, one sentence naming the language is added to the instructions, and the input starts with `Summary language: <name> (<tag>).`. gpt-5-nano at minimal reasoning often answered in English when the language appeared only in the instructions.

**3. Canonical feed state**
- The request uses Responses structured output (`HUD_SUMMARY_RESPONSE_FORMAT`) with the fields `{summary, feedState}`. `max_output_tokens` goes from 100 to 200: the JSON envelope and a non-Latin summary take more tokens than five English words. `feedState` is one of the snapshot states, or null when `overall` is null (a nullable field rather than a `none` token, which the model wrote into the text). The summary has at most five words: with "exactly five" the model padded a short view with words like «нет данных» or «unavailable» (a live A/B on gpt-5-nano: 2 of 5 English replies before, 0 of 5 after).
- The proxy returns `{summary, feedState, error}`. A reply that does not parse, or has an unknown state, returns `feedState: null`.
- `hudSummaryMatchesProvenance()` compares the model's `feedState` with the HUD's own `feedProvenance.overall`. For a view that is not nominal, a missing or different state falls back to the deterministic line.
- An accepted summary carries the HUD's own translated state, not the model's wording: the state word leads and the layer names trail (`STALE | … | LIVE FLIGHTS`, «УСТАРЕЛ | … | РЕЙСЫ ОНЛАЙН»). The deterministic fallback line uses the same order, so the warning stays visible even in the 280px minimal and 216px cyber layouts; the text and then the layer names may be cut off there.
- The model gets the layer names the user sees: `enabledLayerLabels`, `enabledLayers[].name` and the `feedProvenance` layer names go through `localizeLayerName`. Outside English the narration note and the per-layer state ids are left out (`overall` still carries the state), since a small model copies English words. A non-English reply falls back to the deterministic line (`hudSummaryHasEnglish`) when it carries a feed-state id, a translated layer's English name or id (also written flush against kana or Han; a word written in Han or kana counts anywhere in the reply, since those scripts have no word edges), only Latin letters in a language written in another script, or, with every feed healthy, the UNAVAILABLE word. A state word the locale itself keeps in English (de `FALLBACK`), words of a place label and, in Latin-script locales, one-word layer names (fr `transit`) do not count. The proxy keeps combining marks, in-word apostrophes and name dots (ar vowel signs, fr `d'Orléans`, ja `・`) and normalizes to NFC. Japanese and Chinese requests get a phrase of up to 20 characters, other languages up to 80 characters, cut at a word boundary. The proxy does not count words: the model counts a name like «Rue de Rivoli» as one word, and a five-word cut ended lines mid-name. In Arabic a leading right-to-left mark keeps a reply that opens with a Latin name reading right to left. pt, zh-CN and zh-Hant get explicit language names: Brazilian Portuguese, and for zh-Hant the zh-CN wording in Traditional characters.
- A view with no place, street or nearby-place label does not ask the model; the deterministic line (state and layers) is shown. With an empty input the model answered about it («пусто», «No layer snapshot available none», as on main), and with layers alone it sometimes invented a place.
- Switching language in place (`onLocaleChange` → `_relocalize()`, from b20c80e5 on main) drops the reply received and aborts one in flight, so the next tick asks again in the new language instead of keeping old-language text under the new-language tag. A camera move during typing shows the deterministic line instead of a half-typed reply.
- `get_hud_caption` (`src/tools/queries/brief.js`) checks the reply's `feedState` the same way, returns it as `data.feedState`, and builds the caption as `STATE | text | LAYERS`; a reply naming another state keeps only the place. `provenanceTag` and `hudSummaryMatchesProvenance` live in `src/data/layerSnapshot.js`, so the tools package can use them.
- The unused `{state} {layers}` key is removed from the catalogs.

**4. One partial chip on the analyst card** (`src/voice/resultDisplay.js`)
- When the card's feed state is already `partial`, `result.partial` no longer adds a second "partial" chip. With any other feed state the chip still shows.

`scripts/package-boundaries.json`: `openai-provider` now owns `src/i18n/locale.js`, which `hudSummaryResponse.js` imports.

## Testing

- At 645e13ae: `format:check`, `check:boundaries`, `layer-token:check` and `build` pass. `npm test`: 9623 pass, 1 fails: `radioPanel.test.mjs` › "the RTL-SDR card renders what LocalSdrControls presents", which waits a fixed 40 ms frame and failed only under heavy machine load; it passes on its own, and this branch does not touch `src/ui/`. At 818d2c82 Manjunath's run had 9634 tests and 0 failures.
- Live replies through `handleHudSummary` (gpt-5-nano): the nullable schema is accepted; ru, ar, fr, ja and en replies come back in the requested language and state.
- `hudSummaryLine.test.mjs` covers on a real `IntelHUD`: the localized request, the line order, the English-echo fallback (including Latin flush against CJK and the words that are not an echo), no request without a place label, the per-layer state ids left out for ja, the move during typing, and a language switch with a request in flight.
- New tests:
  - partial alone, partial plus nominal in either order, and partial plus stale;
  - an es request reaching the model with the Spanish instruction and input, and returning the canonical state;
  - a reply without the format or with an unknown state;
  - a localized summary accepted only with a matching state, and fallback on a missing or mismatched one;
  - the locale in the signed context;
  - partial keeps a translated tag in es and ru.
- `hud-caption-feed-state.test.mjs`: `get_hud_caption` keeps the stale state, and keeps only the place on a mismatch.
- Live check against OpenAI through the local proxy. `feedState` came back correct (`stale`, `partial`, and `null` with no layers). Answers were in the requested language, for example ru «Техасский Капитолий …», uk «Аустін Техаський Капітолій …», ja «テキサス州議会 …».

Known limit: gpt-5-nano at minimal reasoning sometimes mixes languages or keeps an English layer label. A stronger model can be set with `OPENAI_HUD_SUMMARY_MODEL`. Raising the reasoning effort ran out of output tokens and came close to the 5 s client timeout.

title: fix: handle route annotation travel modes
body:
## Summary

Fixes route annotation travel modes being silently dropped when saving or restoring a shared view, causing all routes to fall back to walking regardless of the mode requested by the user or a voice action.

Closes [[#1285](https://github.com/bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view/issues/1285)](https://github.com/bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view/issues/1285)

## Root Cause Analysis & Changes

### 1. Alias mismatch at the `annotationOf()` codec boundary

**Root cause:** `annotationOf()` in `src/view/index.js` checked `input.mode` against the three short canonical forms (`walk`, `car`, `bike`). The annotation engine's `normalizeMode()` accepts long-form aliases such as `driving`, `cycling`, `walking`, `foot`, `drive`, `cycle`, and `bicycle`. Any alias that was not an exact match was silently discarded as `undefined`, so the view stored no mode and always restored as walking.

**Fix:**

- Added `ANNOTATION_ROUTE_MODES = ['walk', 'car', 'bike']` as the authoritative list of stored forms.
- Added `ANNOTATION_ROUTE_MODE_MAP` mapping every accepted alias to its canonical short form:
  - `driving`, `drive` → `car`
  - `cycling`, `cycle`, `bicycle` → `bike`
  - `walking`, `foot` → `walk`
- In `annotationOf()`, resolved `input.mode` through the map before storing it, keeping it `undefined` for non-route annotation types and unknown values.

### 2. Missing `mode` field in `VIEW_PROPERTIES` schema

**Root cause:** The `annotations` schema in `VIEW_PROPERTIES` had no `mode` field, so the tools layer could not validate it and callers received no type error when passing an unrecognised mode.

**Fix:**

- Added `mode: { type: 'string', enum: ['walk', 'car', 'bike'] }` to the annotations schema so invalid values are caught at the tool-call boundary rather than silently dropped at encode time.

## Tests Added

**`src/view/index.test.mjs`**

- Verifies that `walk`, `car`, and `bike` pass schema validation and survive a share-link round-trip.
- Verifies that all 7 aliases (`driving`, `drive`, `cycling`, `cycle`, `bicycle`, `walking`, `foot`) canonicalize correctly and survive a share-link round-trip.

title: Let a GNSS integrity source set the layer's evidence window
body:
## What this changes

The GNSS integrity layer keeps cells from visited views for a 30-minute window. The layer already accepted a `windowMs` option, but the catalog never passed one, so a source had no way to set it. A source whose observations arrive less often than every 30 minutes would see its cells expire before the next update.

- **The catalog passes the source's window.** `constructCatalog.js` forwards `sources['gnss-integrity'].windowMs` to the layer.
- **The layer validates it.** Only a positive, finite number is used; a missing, `null`, non-finite, zero, negative or non-number value keeps the 30-minute default. Before, such a value was used as-is and would empty the layer.
- **The row text names the window in use.** It read "over 30 min" regardless of the window; it now takes `{minutes}`, like the legend text already did, translated for every shipped locale.

The bundled source sets no window, so Core's behaviour is unchanged.

## How I verified it

- [x] `npm run build` (then `npm run build:panel`)
- [x] `npm test`: 9,103 of 9,106 pass. The one failure, `a real all-addresses connect failure is recognised as address selection` in `src/data/firmsProxy.test.mjs`, fails the same way on `main` in this environment (it opens real localhost connections). `npm run format:check`, `npm run check:boundaries`, `npm run i18n` (all locales complete) pass.
- [ ] `npm run test:track` (dev server running)
- [x] Feature gate for the area I touched: none applies; a new catalog test checks that a source's 65-minute window reaches the layer's window, row text and legend, and that a missing or invalid window gives 30.

title: test(firms): stop the all-addresses connect test depending on how localhost resolves
body:
## What this changes

The FIRMS test "a real all-addresses connect failure is recognised as address selection" (from #1078) needs `localhost` to resolve to both `::1` and `127.0.0.1`, so that fetch tries both addresses and fails with an all-addresses error. On a host whose `localhost` resolves only to `127.0.0.1`, fetch makes a single attempt, gets a plain `ECONNREFUSED`, and the test fails.

The test now mocks `dns.lookup` for its one request, returning both loopback addresses, so it no longer depends on the host's resolver. It still makes real connections to a closed port on both addresses. It also asserts that fetch resolved through `dns.lookup` once, so a future Node change to that path fails loudly instead of quietly depending on the host again. The existing skip when there is no IPv6 loopback stays. Production code is unchanged.

## How I verified it

- [x] `npm run build`: not affected (test-only change)
- [x] `npm test`: `src/data/firmsProxy.test.mjs` passes 15 of 15 (1 existing skip) on Node 24.14.0, 26.13.0 and 22.21.1, on a host whose `localhost` resolves only to `127.0.0.1`, where it failed before. `npm run format:check` and `npm run check:boundaries` pass.

title: Let a weather source describe its own products
body:
## Summary

A weather source can now describe its own products through an optional `display` object in each product manifest: `source`, `credit`, `units`, `coverage`, `info`, `legend` and `extent`. The weather layer uses each valid field in the row summary, legend, info text, coverage navigation, outside-coverage status, layer stats and imagery credit, and keeps today's built-in value for any field that is absent or invalid.

- Units and legend describe one scale, so they apply only as a valid pair.
- Text is single-line, length-capped, and rejects control, invisible and bidi characters. The credit is escaped as plain text.
- Legend labels must read back exactly as shown; extents must be finite and non-empty (antimeridian-crossing extents are supported).
- Supplied source and units are shown verbatim; built-in values are translated as before.
- A refreshed manifest updates the imagery credit even when the shown frame stays the same.

Manifests without `display`, including the bundled nowCOAST ones, render exactly as before.

## Tests

- `src/layers/weather/display.test.mjs`: validation, fallbacks, pairing, outside-coverage with real extents, source switches, refresh dropping `display`, credit refresh, and hard-coded current output for every product without `display`.
- `npm test`: 9126 passed, 2 skipped, 0 failed. `format:check`, `check:boundaries`, `npm run i18n` pass.

title: fix(traffic): give paired TomTom sides of one street a two-way share of dots
body:
Street Traffic draws twice as many simulated vehicles on many two-way TomTom streets as on the same street drawn from OpenStreetMap. Refs #1455 (point 2, too many vehicles).

**Cause**
TomTom draws some two-way streets as two `one_side` lines on one centreline, one per direction. `flowSegmentsToRoads` gave each a one-way road's full share of dots, so the street got twice the dots of the same street as a single `full` line (two directions at a half share each) or as a two-way OSM road.

**Change** (`src/layers/traffic/roadModes.js`, `src/data/flowMatch.js`)
- A `one_side` line is paired when an opposite-direction `one_side` line runs within 5 m of at least two of three points along it, at a quarter, a half and three quarters of its length. A paired line gets a two-way direction's half share (`densityWeight` 0.5), so two paired sides draw as densely as one `full` line.
- Each line is judged on its own samples. A short side beside the middle of a long one is paired while the long one may not be, so that stretch draws at 1.5× a `full` line rather than 2×.
- A lone side, a divided carriageway (about 20 m apart), same-direction lines, and a line that doubles back beside itself are not paired. `full` lines keep their two-way handling and are not paired.
- Pairing reuses the flow index from `flowMatch.js` (100 m cells). Its pieces now carry their source line, and a `radiusFor` of 0 leaves a piece out, so a line never matches its own pieces.
- CURRENT-STATE's traffic paragraph describes the pairing.

**Measurement**
- On the decoded Austin flow fixture (819 lines, 385 `one_side`), every `one_side` line is paired. Road length weighted by direction share falls from 553 to 417 km.
- Cost: pairing runs on the main thread once per road load (`source.js`). On 16 shifted copies of the Austin tile (13,104 lines) a pass takes 33–50 ms across reruns, against about 1 ms for main's `flowSegmentsToRoads`.

**Verification**
- New tests in `roadModes.test.mjs` cover a pair 1 m apart, a lone side, a divided carriageway, same-direction lines, a `full` line, partners along 30 % and 60 % of the length, and a line that doubles back beside itself. Each fails on the code before it.
- `npm test`: 9,134 tests, 0 fail. `format:check` and `check:boundaries` pass.

title: feat(sky): Sky view, look up at the stars, satellites and planets from any point
body:
## What this changes
A **Sky** button puts the camera at eye height on a chosen point (picked point, browser location, or typed lat/lon or place name) and looks up. Drag, pinch, wheel and arrow keys look around; Back to map restores the previous camera pose, field of view, camera input, collision and globe look.
- Horizon from real terrain (flat ground if none); sky brightness follows the Sun.
- Satellites above you from the existing TLE groups (`/api/celestrak/<group>`, parsed by `src/sources/tle.js`, SGP4 in a module worker), an "Overhead now" panel, next-48 h passes (`src/data/satellitePass.js`) and estimated brightness. No RCS source is wired up, so brightness falls back to the object class; an RCS map can be injected with `createSatSky({ fetchRcs })`.
- 8,920 HYG v4.4 stars to mag 6.5, 88 western constellations with IAU boundaries, Sun, Moon and planets (astronomy-engine), search.
- Point-at-the-sky on phones; true north from the WMM2025 declination (geomagnetism, valid to 2029-11-13, says so outside it). Needs https.
- Time control: live, step, play, reverse, rate, presets Sunset / Twilight end / Midnight / Moonrise / ISS pass, and a shareable `sv` link. Sky stamps the scene time only while it is open (a frame-port `preUpdate` listener after the application's own); closing it drops the listener and the world's time resumes.
- Clear view eye button (also double-tap on the sky or H).

Mounted from `ApplicationShell._initSkyView()` as a separate chunk fetched after shell init. New dependencies: `astronomy-engine` (MIT), `geomagnetism` (Apache-2.0). Star data (HYG) is CC BY-SA 4.0 and constellations (Stellarium) are CC BY-SA; credited in DATA_SOURCES.md, LICENSE, dataCredits.js, src/skyView/NOTICE.md. Strings are in all 13 locale catalogs (machine translated; zh-Hant generated from zh-CN with `npm run i18n -- --zh-hant`).

### Renderer contract
Sky reaches the renderer only through its ports, found from the application's scene object with `src/render/rendererOf.js` (camera, frame, query, input and globe), and asks ground and horizon heights of the height service (`src/queries/heights.js`). No Sky module imports Cesium or the Cesium adapter, and none of the guard allow-lists changed:
- camera input: a counted `camera.controls.suspend('sky-view')` hold instead of `enableInputs`; collision through `camera.controls.collision` (no private Cesium fields);
- picking a point on the map: a pointer claim and the input port's `click` with that lease, instead of Sky's own `ScreenSpaceEventHandler`;
- observer ground height and the horizon profile: one `heightsOf(scene).batch(...)` each;
- the two script-built satellite list buttons use the same `el()` helper as Sky's other buttons;
- field of view: Sky's `fovDeg` spans the longer side of the canvas, as the overlay draws it, and is converted to the camera port's vertical angle (again when the canvas changes shape);
- unit tests run on the stub renderer bound with `createSceneHost` (`src/testSupport/skyTestHost.mjs`).

Two behaviours differ from the earlier Cesium-direct version: the flat horizon hides the globe surface only (3D tiles cannot be hidden through the ports, so Clear view keeps the attribution line), and a camera orbiting a `lookAt` target comes back in the world frame at the same pose.

Not included: the Sky voice tool registration. `src/skyView/skyVoice.js` and its tests are here as a hook (`window.__gevSky.voice`); a follow-up can wire a `control_sky` tool to it.

## How I verified it
Current head `c429fee814ff48dde2b43d440ab16c24508b8c7f`, rebased on upstream `e4caf5d3afcb40041cfa6b167b4fda7bb9b393c5`, Node 26.12.1, headless Chromium with software GL.
- `npm test -- --test-concurrency=4` (the full plan from `scripts/run-unit-tests.mjs`): 16,363 tests, 16,358 pass, 0 fail, 5 skipped; allocation groups 1/1 and 14/14. That includes the renderer guards (`noCesiumOutsideRender`, `viewerAccess`, `internals`, `inputOwnership`, heights, `viewControls`), which pass 61/61 here and failed 6 before this port. An earlier run of the same head on a heavily loaded machine (load average about 40) failed three timing-sensitive tests in other areas (`analystEngine` 250k-row ranking budget, `nominatimGuardLifecycle`, `tool-schema-codepoints`); those files pass alone on this head and on the pre-port head, and the rerun above passed.
- Sky tests alone (`src/skyView/*.test.mjs` and `src/ui/skyMountDiagnostics.test.mjs`): 458/458.
- `npm run build`, `format:check`, `check:boundaries`, `i18n`, `changelog:check` and `layer-token:check -- --base-ref e4caf5d3` pass.
- Upstream `main` has since moved one commit to `d9d79ebc` (#1895, line `breaks`). A local merge of this head with it is clean, and the guard, Sky and that commit's tests pass on the merge (602/602).
- In the browser (vite dev server): the Sky button appears; typing Houston coordinates puts the camera at eye height with the overlay's field of view (70°), camera input and collision off; drag turns the view (heading 180° → 203.8°), arrow keys step it; at night the overlay draws stars, constellations and labels; at 04:00 local on a 412×915 phone viewport with naked-eye filtering off, 92 satellites are drawn (439 overhead) and the list shows 52 rows, and Find "Jupiter" turns to it (az 111.1°, alt 55.6°); Back to map returns the camera to 23,000 km, pitch −90°, field of view 60°, input and collision on. No page or console errors.
- `node scripts/qa-sky-render.mjs` (run on `1162d4ad`, which differs from this head only in a file-header comment): Orion overlay reference diff 0.18% of pixels (tolerance 0.5%); Betelgeuse and Rigel drawn within 0.0001 px of where the camera projects them. One timing row (desktop, 60°, all layers, first run) had p95 12.2 ms over its 8 ms budget under software GL; the other rows passed.

Earlier heads (`0a7468f5`, `1b6e4224f2`, `7d9f1c8b`) were verified on older upstream bases; their results are superseded by the above.

title: Move the application UI to Vue and Pinia
body:
## What this changes Moves the application UI to Vue 3 and Pinia, with no change to how the app looks or behaves except one: on desktop, each side gets an icon rail and keeps one panel open at a time. - **Views and stores.** The panels, command dock, cockpit, dialogs, welcome screen, Provider Settings and the Intel HUD are Vue views in `src/ui/views`, fed from Pinia stores in `src/ui/stores`. The existing controllers publish state to those stores instead of writing the DOM. Reusable pieces live in a small component kit in `src/ui/kit`. - **Pages place views with hosts.** A page puts `

The `build/html` template expansion and its `gev:template` markers are gone. `createApplication` takes `omitViews` for views an application leaves out, and `createApplicationControls` takes `localePicker: false`. - **i18n on vue-i18n.** vue-i18n holds the locale and catalogs; `t()`/`tn()` keep their API and views translate as they render. The language picker now switches language in place without a reload, and code that publishes translated text follows the switch through `onLocaleChange`. - **Panel rails.** Desktop side panels open from icon rails, one per side. The rails hold still when a tall panel opens, and Cyber draws its edge line beside an open panel on both sides. - **Contributor docs.** CONTRIBUTING, `docs/APPLICATION.md` and `docs/VUE-MIGRATION.md` describe views, stores and the kit for new UI. Node tests that import application modules register the component loader with `--import=/build/register-vue`. The changelog fragment lists every host-facing API change, including the removed `persistLocaleAndReload` and `registerUnsavedWork`, `IntelHUD`'s new `publish` option, and map sources whose `unavailableReason` may be a function. ## How I verified it - [x] `npm run build` - [x] `npm test` (9,497 tests, 0 failures) - [ ] `npm run test:track` (dev server running) - [x] Feature gate for the area I touched: checked by hand in the browser. Layers, panels and rails in the default layout and Cyber; language switching ru → en and de in place; flights and vessels loading and selection. Satellites weren't checked because CelesTrak was unreachable at the time. The UI also runs through a downstream host, which mounts the views with `omitViews` and `localePicker: false`, with its own tests and production build passing.

title: Cache compiled components and load them on the test thread
body:
## Summary

Since the move to single-file components, Core's unit tests took about twice as long: every test process compiled each component it imports from scratch, and the component loader ran off-thread (`module.register`), adding a round trip to every module a test imports.

- `build/register-vue` now installs synchronous hooks on the loading thread (`module.registerHooks`, available on every Node version in `engines`).
- Compiled components are cached between test processes, keyed by the file's path and text, the Vue version and the loader's own code. The compiler loads only on a cache miss.
- Cached modules run as code, so the cache directory is used only if it is a real directory owned by the current user and writable by no one else (on POSIX, `<tmpdir>/gev-vue-sfc-<uid>`); on Windows it lives in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\gev-vue-sfc`. Entries are written to a randomly named file and renamed into place. `GEV_VUE_CACHE=0` turns the cache off.

## Results

Full suite pinned to four cores: **441 s → 240 s** from a cold cache, all tests passing.

## Validation

- `npm run format:check`, i18n, boundaries, build and the full unit suite pass locally (Node 24.14).
- New `src/tooling/vueLoader.test.mjs`: caching, key changes, the per-user location, an unwritable directory, and a world-writable or symlinked directory being refused.

- Each rail is placed by its screen-side edge (logical properties), so a widening rail grows toward the middle of the screen and mirrors in right-to-left locales. Collapsed, it sits exactly where it did.
- While the label is on screen the tip is not shown, unless the label is cut short by the pill's width, so the full name can always be read. The button keeps its accessible name and the visible label is `aria-hidden`.

title: feat(cyclones): add GDACS storms outside the NHC/CPHC basins
body:
## What this changes

The Cyclones layer only shows NOAA NHC/CPHC storms, so nothing appears in the North Indian Ocean, the western North Pacific or the Southern Hemisphere. This adds GDACS as a second provider for those basins. GDACS redraws JTWC advisories and publishes per-storm geometry without a key.

- New `server/providers/cyclonesGdacs.js`: event search, episode geometry (track, lead-hour points, cone), and winds from the JTWC timeline GDACS links. Storms inside NHC/CPHC water are left to NOAA.
- `/api/cyclones` merges both providers. Each provider keeps its own last good copy, and the snapshot reports each provider's state, so one outage does not hide the other's storms.
- GDACS storms are labelled as automatic estimates, not official warnings. They name their GDACS episode, link the GDACS report, read as Typhoon (western Pacific) or Cyclone (elsewhere) instead of Hurricane, and may have no cone.
- GDACS is slow (1 to 10 s per request in my tests). Each episode is downloaded once and kept. GDACS gets 8 of the refresh's 12 s, and a download that is still running finishes in the background. While something is pending, the snapshot lives one minute and the layer asks again after 65 s. A cold request took about 4.6 s; winds can arrive a minute later.
- `get_cyclones` returns each storm's provider and the GDACS caveat.

#1330 also changes the cyclone provider (Taiwan CWA). Whichever lands second will need a rebase. Happy to do that on this side.

## How I verified it

Windows 11, Node 24.14.0.

- [x] `npm run build`
- [x] `npm test`: 9588 pass, 11 skipped, 2 fail. The 2 are `ranking 250k rows stays within a budget` and `repeated incomplete KML roots finish within an isolated process deadline`. Both pass when run alone, and both fail the same way on unchanged `main` on this machine.
- [x] `npm run test:track`: 107 pass, 2 fail. Both are the flight `arrival: moveEnd ... re-aim before idle refresh` timing checks (1104 ms and 502.5 ms against 500 ms, software rendering). The cyclone layer is not on in that run. I did not run it on `main` to compare.
- [x] Feature gates: `node scripts/qa-weather-teardown.mjs --headless` passes with no leak. `node scripts/qa-weather-journey.mjs --headless` passes with the cyclone layer at count 1, no error. Its "follow a storm" step looks for storm chips the layer no longer has (`chips: []` on `main` too), so it prints "no active cyclone advisories to follow". That is the same on `main`.
- [x] `npm run format:check`, `npm run check:boundaries`, `npm run i18n` (all 11 locales complete), `npm run doctor -- --json`
- New tests: `src/data/cyclonesGdacs.test.mjs`, plus GDACS cases in the source, layer, proxy and tool tests.
- Live: Tropical Cyclone Murasu (Bay of Bengal, GDACS Red) showed with its track, cone, 12/24/36/48 h points and winds (65 kt now, 25 kt at 48 h).

## Screenshots

Storm view after selecting Murasu from the list:

![Murasu storm view](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kanishka089/gods-eye-view/pr-assets-gdacs-cyclones/storm-view.png)

Regional view:

![Murasu regional view](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kanishka089/gods-eye-view/pr-assets-gdacs-cyclones/storm-regional.png)

## Recording

[gdacs-cyclones.mp4](https://github.com/kanishka089/gods-eye-view/raw/pr-assets-gdacs-cyclones/gdacs-cyclones.mp4) (25 s, 0.4 MB): layer on, storm selected, camera to the storm. Recorded in headless Chrome with software rendering, so it is choppy.

## Category

Weather (existing Cyclone advisories layer; no new layer or share token).

## Data source and licence

- Source: GDACS API, `www.gdacs.org/gdacsapi/api` (`events/geteventlist/SEARCH`, `polygons/getgeometry`, `events/geteventdata`, `export/gettimeline`)
- Licence: © European Union, CC BY 4.0 under the Commission's reuse policy, linked from the [GDACS terms of use](https://www.gdacs.org/About/termofuse.aspx). GDACS says its information is purely indicative; the layer says so for every GDACS storm.
- Attribution in the app: "GDACS (Global Disaster Alert and Coordination System), © European Union, CC BY 4.0; tracks and cones redrawn from its automatic estimates of JTWC advisories, not official warnings"
- Key: none
- Fetched at runtime through `/api/cyclones`; nothing bundled.

- [x] Added a row to `DATA_SOURCES.md`
- [x] Credit is registered in `src/data/dataCredits.js`

body:
## Summary
