- Add 1,120 Québec camera locations: 680 georeferenced MTQ cameras, 426 Montréal OSM cameras, and 14 scenic cameras. MTQ cameras use the official 511 browser player and a separate map preview; no API key or server-side pixel access is required.
- Add Ottawa traffic cameras and 2,396 curated World still feeds: 166 Iceland, 1,176 Oregon, and 1,054 Japan.
- Set the default catalog to 7,516 entries: 4,000 shared slots, 1,120 reserved Québec slots, and 2,396 reserved World slots. Keep World refresh floors at five minutes for Iceland/Oregon and ten minutes for MLIT, with bounded in-memory reuse.
- Recognize the MLIT adjustment image, return the app maintenance card, and report the camera as degraded through the existing health route.
- Document source metadata, attribution, runtime behavior, and contributor workflow. Exclude NZTA feeds whose discovery source conflicts with current automated-scraping terms.

## Screenshots

![Québec camera qc-511-3735: live player and map preview](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f31366fb-6bf2-4005-9a03-e4c07f7567dc)

![World camera world-or-764: TripCheck still projected on the globe](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/25f0e292-5ef3-4f13-827a-7052c6afa52b)

## Validation

- `npm run build`, `npm run format:check`, `npm run i18n`, `npm run check:boundaries`, and `npm run changelog:check` pass.
- Focused CCTV tests passed 70/70 before the final Québec status regression; that new regression passed 1/1.
- `/api/cctv/sources` returned 7,516 sources and included the Québec, Ottawa, and World samples. `world-or-764` returned a real JPEG; an MLIT adjustment sample returned the maintenance SVG and degraded health message.
- The CCTV proof gate reported 45 passed, 3 failed, and 5 inconclusive. The remaining failures are terrain-height and true-empty-canvas assertions; the GL drag checks were inconclusive in headless mode.
- The bounded full-unit run passed 9,624 tests with 12 skipped; its second allocation benchmark did not terminate. The tracking check reported 107 passed and 2 arrival-timing failures over its 500 ms budget.

title: feat(voice): add typed AI chat beside voice
body:
## Summary

Adds a typed AI chat next to the mic in the command dock. Chat replies are silent and never request the microphone. The first message connects with the selected provider and runs the same map actions as voice, through each provider's text API:

- **OpenAI:** `OPENAI_CHAT_MODEL` (default `gpt-4.1-mini`); needs an API key.
- **Gemini:** a text-only `generateContent` request with `GEMINI_CHAT_MODEL` (default `gemini-3.5-flash-lite`); it never starts Live.

Only one mode runs at a time: the mic closes chat, and opening chat stops voice.

Chat is rendered by the voice control presenter (`src/voice/control.js`) and the new `ChatPanel.vue`. Its conversation publishes apart from the rest of the control, like the waveform bars, so a reply revealed frame by frame re-renders only the message list.

- **Chat panel:** recent and quick-command suggestions, Up/Down history, and attachments (up to four map-layer references or UTF-8 TXT/Markdown/CSV/JSON/GeoJSON files, 10 KB each, sent only with the message). Once connected, Stop cancels only the reply in progress, and a failed reply keeps the conversation for the next message, including any map actions it already ran (an action still running when it stopped is recorded as cancelled, and later ones as skipped); a layer is attached with its own button or Enter, not as the picker moves.
- **Placement:** chat and voice panels sit above the dock or dock into the right rail's column (its panels and icon strip), which hides the rail until the panel minimizes or closes, or a rail panel opens. Minimized bars sit centred above the dock, and height animates when one panel replaces the other.
- **Dock trays:** when the pointer reaches the Location or Visual Presets button, a centred panel steps down to its bar and rests above the open tray, without moving keyboard focus. Expanding it while a tray is open docks it right until the trays close; the saved dock choice does not change. Once the trays close and the pointer leaves the wings, a panel that stepped down expands in the centre again and a panel docked for the tray returns to the centre. A pinned tray keeps panels as bars, or docked when expanded.
- **Voice preview:** minimized voice shows the last sentence from each side. The empty Voice Preview suggests things to say until voice starts.
- **Settings from chat:** Settings opened from chat keep chat's frame and show the shared AI provider and the quick-commands option, with Back to chat.
- **Server:** text-chat handlers at `/api/openai/chat` and `/api/gemini/chat` with a same-site Origin check, a 512 KB body cap, a 60 s upstream timeout and their own per-IP throttles, `GEV_RATELIMIT_OPENAI_CHAT_PER_MIN` and `GEV_RATELIMIT_GEMINI_CHAT_PER_MIN`. Unset, each follows that provider's voice throttle (default 30); an explicit value, including 0, wins. `GEV_PREFER_CODEX_OAUTH` turns OpenAI chat off, so a ChatGPT-OAuth-only install never bills the API key through chat. A missing, locked or rejected key and a throttled request each come back with a code the chat turns into its own message, including how long to wait from `Retry-After`. A key or account the provider refuses (401, 403, Gemini's 400 `API_KEY_INVALID`, or OpenAI's out-of-credit 429) cools down for a minute instead of being retried on every message, with a message for each case. SECURITY.md, `.env.example` and the Pinokio launcher cover the variables. Chat offers the same tools as voice, including `osm_query` only when Overpass is configured, and its prompt follows the same switch.

## Behaviour changes to the existing voice UI

These come from fusing the voice and chat panels into one assistant panel in the dock, so they land together with typed chat. Please review them; each changes what voice users see today.

- **Settings gear moved:** the voice Settings gear now sits in the chat header. The voice panel keeps its own Settings tab.
- **Provider choice moved:** the provider choice is now inside Settings as "AI Provider", shared by voice and chat.
- **Preview tab hidden:** the Settings tab toggles back to the preview, and voice Settings show Back to voice. Escape steps back from either Settings view and still closes Voice Preview; in chat it only closes the attach menu.
- **Close turns voice off:** the voice panel's close (×) now turns voice off; before, it only hid the panel. Closing chat ends a typed session.
- **Minimize and dock:** the voice panel can minimize to a bar and dock to the right.
- **Dock size:** the voice control widens to fit the chat button: 11rem idle and 14rem while voice or chat is active (upstream 8.75rem, and 8rem in Cyber). While one is active the wings shrink to 3.25rem. On desktop the Location and Visual Presets wings are 5px narrower; the 900px and 620px breakpoints keep upstream's wing widths.
- **Dock wings:** the wings get a darker gradient and border (Cyber keeps its own wing surface) and new label colours. At 900px and below, where `main` now shows the wings' icons only, the icons are centred in the wings. Hovering or pressing their buttons minimizes a centred assistant panel.
- **Help tray:** the voice help tray now opens when the mic button itself is hovered or focused (and enabled), not when anywhere on the voice control is hovered.
- **Panel styling:** the assistant panels use the same glass surface as the left panels. The dock voice control's own blur moves to a `::before` layer, so the panels inside it can blur the map. The Cyber theme keeps its own surfaces; its dock widths change as above.
- **Mic caption:** unchanged from `main`.
- **Inactivity timeout:** typed chat sessions are exempt from the voice inactivity timeout, so an idle chat stays open; voice sessions time out as before.
- **Border orbit:** the animated border runs only while voice is live or a chat reply is pending, and not on touch screens or with reduced motion.
- **OpenAI key note:** when ChatGPT sign-in is chosen for OpenAI voice, the chat panel says typed chat uses the OpenAI API key.
- **Radio pause during a typed reply:** pausing or turning off the radio cancels that reply and keeps the chat session.

## Verification

Run on Node 24.19, macOS, at this branch merged with `main` a4e1763b.

- `npm run build`: passes.
- `npm test`: 10,326 tests, 0 failures (2 skipped).
- `npm run format:check`, `npm run check:boundaries`, `npm run i18n`: pass; all 11 locales complete.
- `npm run test:track`: 109 of 109. (Earlier runs on this machine missed the two arrival timing checks, which miss on unmodified `main` too.)
- `scripts/qa-voice-auth-focus.mjs`: fails 14 of 14 on unmodified `main` as well; its fixture server can't load `src/keySetup.js`. Unrelated to this change.
- Browser checks at 1440×900 and 375×812: chat open, minimize and close; Settings from chat; both Back buttons; dock and undock; minimized centring; the phone sheet. At 1170 and 801 px: the dock-tray flow (hover, open, expand, close), keyboard focus staying in the chat input, the docked width, and icon-only wings; wing widths at 768 and 600 px match `main`.
- Voice instructions: `realtimeInstructions()` output is byte-identical to `main` at a4e1763b, with default and custom guidance and with Overpass on and off. The only change splits out `realtimeDirectives()` so typed chat can reuse them.
- Voice routing and bench, run on an earlier revision of this branch; the voice instructions and tools have not changed since.
- `scripts/qa-voice-routing.mjs --url …`: every routing check passed (65 of 120 model turns). The behavior layer reports 47 passed and 3 failed, the same three on unmodified `main`: two pointer "this"/"here" checks and fly-to while tracking.
- `scripts/qa-voice-bench.mjs --suite core`:
  - `gpt-realtime-2`: every graded row routed correctly (86 rows, 0 wrong tools). The run stopped early when the account ran out of credits; 49 turns errored without a response.
  - `gemini-3.8-live`: 20 of 20 correct, with correct arguments, before the run's $2 cloud budget was reached.

- Live Gemini typed chat with a real key: "Fly to Tokyo" flew the map to Tokyo, and the follow-up "Now zoom out a bit" zoomed out using the kept conversation (thought signatures included). One upstream 502 on the follow-up was recovered by resending, with the history intact.

Not run: live OpenAI typed chat (the test account is out of credits) and live voice. Not checked on a touch tablet.

## Decisions for the maintainers

- **Close vs Escape:** the panel's × ends voice or chat, while Escape only steps back out of Settings. That split is deliberate: × is the one clear way to end a session from the panel.
- **Session adapters:** `realtimeSession.js` and `geminiSession.js` still wrap the voice controller's push-to-talk `start` and the radio's `isActive`, so a key press ends chat before voice starts. A constructor hook on both controllers would replace that.

## Credit

The text transport is adapted from #976 by Darren Dignam (@darrendignam), credited as co-author on the commit.

## Changelog

Included as `changelog.d/1507-typed-ai-chat.md`.

title: Add Rainfolk Water Wells layer
body:
## What this changes

Adds **Water Wells** to Infrastructure, using Rainfolk's hosted copy of the United States Groundwater Well Database (USGWD). Rainfolk prepares and hosts the map files; the original authors and the contributing state and federal agencies, including USGS, keep source credit.

- Below 50 km camera height, each historical source record in view is drawn as a hollow marker at its own position. Clicking one opens the native tracked card with available well depth, reported capacity, screen dimensions and construction/report years. Overlapping records open a small chooser.
- Above 50 km nothing is loaded and the row reads "Zoom in to see wells". A view wider than 2°, or holding more than 2,000 records, 16 MiB, 256 tiles or 8 states, draws none and the row reads "Too many wells in this view; zoom in closer". Counts are never drawn as clusters.
- Every index and tile file is checked against its SHA-256 before use. The release is pinned (`VITE_RAINFOLK_WELLS_RELEASE` overrides it; a change needs a rebuild).
- The layer draws through the renderer contract: one icon set from `drawOf`, the camera, frame and query ports, the input dispatcher and `heightsOf`. It imports no Cesium and makes no viewer access.
- Wells registers as a pick owner, so a click on a marker's ring does not cancel a tracked flight. A click in the ring's hollow middle still selects the well but picks nothing, so a tracked flight is released as it is for a click on empty map.
- No dependency, bundled dataset or key is added.

The pinned release has **12,452,285 mapped historical records across all 50 states**. Within-state coverage is incomplete. These are source records, not a verified count of distinct wells, current well performance or water conditions.

Against `main` this is 56 files, +3,426 −19. Of that, 764 lines are the per-state source notices and 273 are the 21 strings in 13 locales.

## Shared files touched

Only the standard wiring a new layer needs: catalog and app wrapper (`src/app/layers/usGroundwater.js`), source composition, layer name and panel group, share-link token `03` (News, Shipwrecks and Rail hold `00` to `02`), data credits, voice manifest, translations, `.env.example`, package exports and boundaries, format scope, changelog fragment, one `DATA_SOURCES.md` row, one `README.md` row and a `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md` section.

Two shared files change behaviour or a list:

- `src/data/trackedReadout.js` gains `us-groundwater` in its context layers and honours `verticalOnly: false`.
- `src/render/unboundCamera.test.mjs` lists `./layers/us-groundwater` with the other Cesium-free layer entries.

## How I verified it

Verified at `55565bb5`, synced with `main` at `9523bb18`. Local, Node 24.22.1 on Windows 11. The build, static checks and unit suite were run on that commit. Any later commit on this branch is a GitHub "Update branch" merge of `main` and has not been re-run locally. `test:track`, the browser checks and the screenshots were done on `86c05075`, two merges of `main` earlier. Since then the only wells change is where the Hebrew and Swedish strings sit in their files.

- [x] `npm run build`
- [x] `npm run format:check`, `check:boundaries`, `i18n` (all 13 locales complete), `changelog:check`, `doctor`, and `layer-token:check` and `library:check` against `main`
- [x] Unit suite: 15,588 tests, 15,554 pass, 16 skipped, 18 fail. One is a concurrency test in `tools/mcpPanelKey` that passed three times out of three when run alone. The other 17 are in `inputOwnership`, `heights`, `cesium/internals`, `contract` and `unboundCamera` tests that compare forward-slash paths; the same 17 fail on unmodified `main` on Windows. With paths forced to forward slashes, 13 of them pass on this branch (last checked on `6ab930e8`); the 4 `contract` ones compare a directory name the same way and I did not cover that. `npm test` itself cannot start on Windows (`spawnSync ENAMETOOLONG` with 1,298 test paths on one command line), so I ran the same plan and flags in chunks of 250, allocation probes included (15/15). CI on Linux is the real answer.
- [x] `npm run test:track` (dev server running): 99 passed, 6 failed, 2 skipped. The six are the trail-head check and five "tracked model absent before exit" checks for the 3D aircraft model. The same six fail on unmodified `main` in this headless Chrome, and none involve wells.
- [x] Feature gate for the area I touched: none exists for this layer. These were driven through a real browser against the live public feed, at 1440×900 over Lakeway, Texas, then followed by a hands-on pass:
  - the share link's `l=03` restores the layer and the markers draw
  - a wide view reads "Too many wells in this view; zoom in closer", above 50 km reads "Zoom in to see wells" and the markers hide; zooming back in redraws them
  - clicking a marker opens the tracked card, including markers well away from the screen centre; clicking empty map closes it
  - clicking between two adjacent markers opens the chooser, and "View record" opens that record's card
  - the keyboard record list focuses, moves with the arrow keys and inspects a record (focus events were simulated)
  - turning the layer off removes the markers and the selection
  - no console errors

The 390 px layout renders correctly in an emulated phone viewport (screenshots below); real touch input was not rechecked. The GIF is from an earlier head; the markers, card and chooser look the same.

## New layer checklist

**Screenshots**

[Desktop and 390 px screenshots](https://github.com/bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view/pull/1508#issuecomment-6605206689), taken on `86c05075`.

**Recording**

[Interaction GIF](https://github.com/bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view/pull/1508#issuecomment-6606779118): selecting a well, reading its details and toggling the layer. Recorded on an earlier head.

**Proposed category**

Category: Infrastructure

**Data source and licence**

- Source (provider and endpoint): Rainfolk's hosted copy of USGWD, `https://data.rainfolk.org/usgwd/e6dc61db1500b491671cf094602e2257814c5507e99618d717fbb4f6082d8291/index.json` (public, CORS `*`). Original data: [USGWD — Chung-Yi Lin, Alexandra Miller, Musab Waqar and Landon T. Marston](https://doi.org/10.4211/hs.8b02895f02c14dd1a749bcc5584a5c55). Rainfolk normalizes fields, converts NAD83 to WGS84 and packages the records spatially.
- Licence or terms (link): [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). MIT software terms do not relicense the data.
- Attribution shown in the app: the in-app credit, plus `docs/US_GROUNDWATER_SOURCES.md` with the per-state contributing organizations (Table S1) and the supplied state notices (Table S2).
- Needs a key? (none / optional / required): none
- Fetched at runtime, or bundled in the repo: fetched at runtime

- [x] Added a row to `DATA_SOURCES.md`
- [x] Credit is registered in `src/data/dataCredits.js`
- [x] Share-link token `03` is reserved in the ledger and registry; `layer-token:check` passes against `main`

## Docs

- [x] `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md` updated and a `changelog.d/1508-rainfolk-water-wells.md` fragment added

## History

- **2026-11-19, the layer rebuilt smaller:** one data source and one load path, from 71 files (+6,165) to 55 (+3,343) against the `main` of 2026-11-14. The count-grid download, the in-browser re-derivation of the datum conversion and unused stats fields are gone; card and error text are translated.
- **2026-11-19, synced with `main`:** the layer moved onto the renderer contract, since `main` no longer lets a layer import Cesium or reach through the viewer. The chooser is a `UiDialog` and the record list uses `UiButton`, as `main` now requires. One fix came out of the browser check: a click near a marker missed over high ground, because wells were projected from the ellipsoid while the markers are clamped to the terrain. They are now projected at the terrain height.
- **2026-11-14:** narrowed to the wells layer, from 92 files (+10,152) to 72 (+6,188). The shared `worldOverlay` change, its raised allocation budget, the six-site USGS sample path and wells-only branches in the shared layer panel were removed.

title: fix(routes): report an upstream routing outage as unavailable
body:
When the OSRM routing service is down, the app reports it as a problem with the route. For an error status (5xx, 403, 404) voice `plan_route` hears "No walk route from A to B: no route found" and the Directions layer shows "No route found between A and B". For a timeout, network error or non-JSON body both report "route proxy error".

**Cause**
`/api/route` answered every upstream failure with HTTP 200 `{ok:false}`: a failure status read "no route found" (`routes.js`, `!upstreamRes.ok`), and a timeout, network error or non-JSON body read "route proxy error". Neither client could tell an outage from a request OSRM can't route.

**Change**
- `server/providers/places/routes.js`:
  - These now answer `502 {ok:false, error:'routing service unavailable'}`: a rejected upstream fetch (timeout, network error, refused redirect), any failure status but 400, a non-JSON content type, and a body read that fails or doesn't parse.
  - OSRM's own refusal (a 400 such as NoRoute, or a 200 without a route) still reads "no route found". The 429 handling is unchanged, and an exception in the proxy's own code after the upstream answer is still a 200 "route proxy error".
  - The 12 s timeout still runs from the request's arrival, queue wait included, as on main. If it runs out before the request leaves the outbound queue, the answer is 429 "routing busy" (the proxy's own backlog), not an outage. At today's settings (8 deep, 1 s apart) the queue wait is at most about 7 s, so this applies only if the spacing or depth grows.
- `src/tools/places.js`: `createRouteService` throws "Routing service unavailable (HTTP n)" for a 5xx, before reading the body's `ok:false`. Voice passes only the message on, so this is what the model hears. A 429 keeps its "Routing is rate limited" error.
- `src/layers/directions/source.js`: any 5xx reads "Routing unavailable (HTTP n)", also when the failure page in front of the proxy isn't JSON.
- CURRENT-STATE's routing paragraph is updated.

**Remaining edge case**
A request that waited in the queue gives OSRM only the rest of the 12 s. Wait about 7 s, then have a healthy but slow OSRM take more than about 5 s, and the request still reads as unavailable.

**Other callers**
- `src/search/http.js` `route()` now throws on the 502 where it returned `null`. Its only consumer, the annotation engine's `fetchRoute`, catches and returns `null`, so the result is unchanged: a straight line labelled "direct line (no route)".
- A failure is never cached. Callers sharing one in-flight upstream request all get the 502.

**Verification**
- New tests:
  - the proxy answers 502 for a 503, a 403, a non-JSON content type, an unparseable body, a rejected fetch and an abort;
  - callers sharing one failed upstream call all get the 502, and the next request asks again;
  - a budget spent in the outbound queue answers 429 "routing busy" without calling OSRM;
  - `plan_route` reports an outage as unavailable and throws "Routing service unavailable (HTTP 502)";
  - the Directions layer reads "Routing unavailable" for a JSON and a non-JSON 502.
- Each new test fails on main's code.
- `npm test`: 9,594 tests, 0 fail, 11 skipped. `format:check`, `check:boundaries` and the build pass.
- Not covered: `scripts/qa-directions.mjs` section 6 has no 502 case, so the "Routing unavailable (HTTP 502)" row hasn't been checked in a browser.

title: feat: Improved Radio Station finder
body: ### Problem The Radio stations are very limited, especially when I look at local stations that I personally know of and can't find them. I know you can't do it with ALL stations because there are too many, but at least with most. The global limit of 750 is a bit low in my opinion. In addition, you can't see the song that is playing, nor can you add any favourites. The other thing is that bubbles work relatively badly, you zoom in on 2 stations that are close to each other and can't even properly choose one. ### Proposal - Search radio stations inside the area you look at, so you won't overblow the list. The list also gets cached once loaded, there is a slider you can set for a maximum of 5000 - Implement a song display - The ability to add stations and also song names that you like to your favourites. - Bubbles open a drop-down menu with the stations so no zoom-in is needed, single stations play directly - For stations that have no geocode, there is a fallback that uses the other labels like state, country, or a place name in the station's name/tags. If something doesn't have any of that data, it's in the "approx" field and gets shown in the middle of the state or country, depending on what you look at. My question would be whether opt-in or opt-out is better. I've already coded this with haiku in a prototype running locally. I'd also let it ofc follow your instructions on the contribution.md Before I do any pull requests, I wanted to ask first if there is interest in this. I'd split it up into 4-5 sub-PRs so you can review it better. Apart from that, if you want it in another way, please let me know. I added 2 screenshots so you can see how it already looks like ### Data source, license, and attribution Station directory: Radio Browser (https://www.radio-browser.info/). Directory data is under PDDL 1.0, per DATA_SOURCES.md. Individual broadcaster stream terms still apply. Geocoding: Nominatim (https://nominatim.openstreetmap.org/), operated by the OpenStreetMap Foundation. Data is © OpenStreetMap contributors under ODbL 1.0 (https://www.openstreetmap.org/copyright). Usage policy: https://operations.osmfoundation.org/policies/nominatim/ (max 1 request/s, results must be cached, identifying User-Agent). We use only the returned coordinates and do not redistribute the results. Attribution would be added to DATA_SOURCES.md and the credit line via src/data/dataCredits.js. ### Will you build it? Yes, I plan to open a PR

title: feat(cctv): add NCDOT DriveNC (North Carolina) cameras as a keyless pack
body:
## What this changes

Adds North Carolina's NCDOT DriveNC traffic cameras as a keyless CCTV source pack
(`drivenc`), registered in `LIVE_PACKS` beside DelDOT. ~1,024 cameras statewide; the 400
nearest Raleigh, Charlotte and Greensboro load by default.

- **Catalog (keyless).** One request to the catalog the drivenc.gov map itself loads
  (`https://www.drivenc.gov/map/mapIcons/Cameras`: every camera's id and position, ~73 KB).
  The list is sorted nearest the three anchors (like the DriveBC anchors) and only the cameras
  under the pack cap are looked up on their tooltip page (`/tooltip/Cameras/<id>`, ~4 KB), which
  carries the NCDOT camera code and the still-view id. Lookups run 8 at a time under a 30 s
  sweep deadline (a page answers in ~0.2 s, so 400 cameras resolve in ~10 s cold). Each camera's
  code and view id are remembered for the life of the process, so a 15-minute catalog refresh
  only asks about cameras it has not seen; a camera whose tooltip fails is left out of that
  refresh and retried on the next. Catalog and tooltip fetches refuse redirects and cap the
  bodies they read.
- **Frames.** Built from the validated view id under `https://www.drivenc.gov/map/Cctv/`, never
  read from upstream text. `media.js` pins that directory, so a same-origin redirect cannot leave
  it. Frames are fetched at request time and neither stored nor recorded.
- **Stills only.** DriveNC's HLS streams (`*.services.ncdot.gov:8887/chan-*_l/index.m3u8`) answer
  `401 Basic realm="XEngine"` without credentials the site holds, so no stream is registered.
- **Names and headings.** Codes like `CCTV05-I40-273E_NC54` (division, road, mile marker + side
  of road, cross street) become `I-40 MM 273 E at NC-54`; codes outside the pattern (~1 in 5) are
  kept verbatim, and the code itself is the unselected label. The N/S/E/W letter seeds a
  **low-confidence** heading (it names the carriageway the camera sits beside, not where the PTZ
  head points); codes without one use the id-hash fallback.
- **Optional key.** DriveNC runs the same TravelIQ platform as Ontario 511. With `DRIVENC_API_KEY`
  set, the keyed `api/v2/get/cameras` catalog (Ontario shape) replaces the tooltip sweep in one
  request, with `Direction` as a high-confidence heading. A key the API rejects (400/401/403) is
  reported by name, never by value, and the keyless catalog loads instead. The key never reaches
  a record or a log line.
- **Env.** `CCTV_DRIVENC_ENABLED` (default on), `CCTV_DRIVENC_MAX_SOURCES` (default 400, clamped
  8–1200), `DRIVENC_API_KEY` (optional); all three in `.env.example`.
- **Client.** `staticFrameRefreshMs` gets the `NCDOT DriveNC` cadence (3 min, like the other
  highway packs; DriveNC serves a new still about once a minute).

**Data source and licence**

- Source (provider and endpoint): NCDOT DriveNC, `www.drivenc.gov/map/mapIcons/Cameras` +
  `/tooltip/Cameras/<id>`; frames `www.drivenc.gov/map/Cctv/<viewId>`; optional keyed
  `www.drivenc.gov/api/v2/get/cameras`.
- Licence or terms: public NCDOT traffic camera frames via the [DriveNC map](https://www.drivenc.gov/);
  public availability is not a blanket redistribution licence (noted in `DATA_SOURCES.md`, as for DelDOT).
- Attribution shown in the app: "NCDOT DriveNC" (courtesy), credit key `drivenc-cctv`.
- Needs a key? optional (`DRIVENC_API_KEY`, free developer key at drivenc.gov/developers/doc).
- Fetched at runtime, or bundled: fetched at runtime; nothing bundled.
- [x] Added a row (and a bullet) to `DATA_SOURCES.md`
- [x] Credit is registered in `src/data/dataCredits.js`

## How I verified it

Windows 11, Node 24.22.2.

- [x] `npm run build` — green (9 s)
- [x] `npm test` — 9,635 tests, 0 failures (new `server/providers/cctv/drivenc.test.mjs`: 11 tests
  covering code parsing, tooltip parsing incl. off-directory stills, nearest-first lookup under the
  cap, failed-tooltip retry + cache, redirect refusal / fail-soft, keyed path + key non-leakage for
  400/401/403/503, and the catalog-level kill switch)
- [x] `npm run test:track` (dev server running) — run three times against the running dev server. title: Keep one world clock, with a timeline to move it
body:
## Summary

One world clock that every timed part of the app reads, and a basic timeline to move it.

- **World clock** (`src/time/worldClock.js`): live is the wall clock; away from live the clock holds a cursor, fixed or playing. Layers whose data has a time of its own follow it (the sky, the HUD clock, satellites with launched missions' orbits, launches, and weather through its replay clock). Live feeds such as flights, military, vessels and transit stay live.
- **Timeline** (`WorldTimeline.vue`): a scrubber along the bottom, under the command dock, shown only while a layer with time to show is on. Play and pause, a track over the time those layers cover with a tick per launch or frame, and a way back to live. The dock and the UI above it rise while it shows; clean view, recording and the cockpit hide it.
- **Share links** carry the world time when made away from live (field 28 `worldTime`).
- Cesium's sky (sun, moon, lighting) is drawn at the world time.

No behaviour changes while live.

## Testing

- `npm test`: 9,659 tests, 0 failures. `npm run format:check`, `npm run check:boundaries` and `npm run i18n` are clean.
- In the browser: Space missions shows the track over its launches; scrubbing moves the readout, the HUD clock and the sun; dragging to the end goes live; turning launches off hides the bar; desktop and phone layouts, and clean view.
- Not checked in a browser: satellites (CelesTrak was unreachable from the test machine), covered by unit tests.

title: Move launches with the timeline, choose its speed, and wait for data while it plays
body:
Builds on #1512; the diff below is against that branch. Merge #1512 first.

## Summary

- **Launches follow the timeline.** Away from live, a launch that has yet to lift off at the world time is hidden (marker, label, paths, orbit), so scrubbing or playing brings launches up in the order they flew. The selected mission always stays; live shows every launch as before.
- **Play speed.** A speed menu beside play: 1× (the default), 1 min/s, 1 h/s, 1 d/s, 1 wk/s, applied at once while playing. Play starts from the top of the track when at live and goes live when it reaches now.
- **Smooth play.** The world clock tells its listeners of the time every animation frame while playing (a 250 ms tick where there are no frames), so the handle, the globe and the sky move smoothly instead of in quarter-second steps.
- **Play waits only when it must.** The world clock gains a wait (hold continuous play while a layer loads what the time needs) and a gate (play may not pass a layer's next frame). Weather no longer holds play for the frame it is at: that frame loads as play goes on, and play holds only at the next frame while the one before it still loads, so every frame shows and a frame loaded ahead costs nothing. Weather now loads its next frame ahead during timeline play too. It waits at most 8 s on a frame that never comes. Scrubbing still drops in-flight loads and moves on.
- **A quieter bar.** The long date and the track's end dates are gone; the time rides in a bubble over the handle, with a small spinner beside it while play waits on data. The bar runs left to right in every language.
- **A track that zooms and drags.** With layers of very different reach on (a month of launches, a few hours of lightning), scroll or pinch zooms the track around the handle, `+`/`-` zoom from the keyboard and `0` or a double-click shows it all. The handle drags the time; the track around it drags the zoomed view along (a sideways swipe or shift-wheel too), and a tap goes to the time under it. The same works with a finger: one drags, two pinch, and the handle is larger. A scrub's snap-to-live edge follows the stretch shown.
- **Zoom-out limit.** Cesium set none, so zooming out left the globe a speck. On the globe, zooming out now stops where the globe spans 30% of the screen's height, which follows the screen's shape; a camera already past it stops there instead of jumping in. 2D and Columbus views stay unlimited.

The first commit's message says play runs the whole track in a minute; a later commit replaces that with the speed menu.

## Testing

- `npm test`: 9,888 tests, 0 failures. `npm run format:check`, `npm run check:boundaries` and `npm run i18n` are clean.
- In the browser: launches appear as the time passes them; each speed, and changing it mid-play; at 1 h/s with lightning on, play runs with no hold over 30 ms once frames are cached; the spinner on a slow network; zoom, drag, tap and double-click on the track with a mouse; pinch, one-finger drag and tap at phone width; zooming out stops with the globe in view and zooming back in works.

title: Say which HUD readouts are real camera values and which are styling
body:
The HUD's module and class comments said it "renders authentic reconnaissance metadata". This rewords them to say which readouts are real and which are styling:

- From the live camera: MGRS and lat/lon (the point below the camera), altitude, off-nadir angle.
- Current UTC time: both clocks, so COLL is not a capture time.
- Approximate: sun elevation, estimated from that position and time.
- Styling: the classification banner, generated mission, sensor and orbit identifiers, the BAND/BITS/LVL strip, the REC blink, and the GSD/NIIRS figures scaled from altitude.

Comments only; no runtime change. Follows up on the discussion in #1157.

title: fix(awareness): make the 250 km range ring readable on any ground
body:
## What this changes

The Global Context 250 km range ring was a 1 px Cesium ellipse outline. It disappeared over bright desert and snow and under the FLIR, NVG and CRT styles, and broke into a dotted hairline at wide and close zooms. WebGL ignores larger ellipse outline widths, so it couldn't simply be thickened.

It is now a polyline: a 2 px core in the Context panel's blue inside a 1 px dark halo on each side (`PolylineOutlineMaterialProperty`, 4 px total). The halo gives contrast on both light and dark ground, and it survives the monochrome styles because they keep light and dark. Height (2.5 km) and the 250 m follow threshold are unchanged.

Why this approach:

- A wider ellipse outline has no effect in WebGL.
- A translucent fill tints the whole 250 km disk and competes with contacts.
- A glow line fails bright on bright (desert, snow).
- A dashed line reads as tentative and is less visible.
- A bright core with a dark halo works in both directions and under every post-process style.

Changes:

- `src/layers/awareness/rendering.js`:
  - `awarenessRangeRingPositions()` builds 128 chords using the ellipsoid's radius of curvature along each bearing. Measured within 50 m of 250 km at the equator, mid and high latitudes, the poles and the antimeridian.
  - `renderVisual` draws the polyline and moves it on the same 250 m threshold.
- `src/layers/awareness/policy.js`: `AWARENESS_RANGE_RING_STYLE` holds the colours, widths and segment count.
- `src/layers/awareness/rangeRing.test.mjs`: geometry, core/halo contrast, entity shape and follow behaviour. It fails on `main`.

## How I verified it

- [x] `npm run build`
- [x] `npm test`: 9832 pass, 0 fail, 2 skipped, plus the isolated batches 1/1 and 14/14 (Node 24.19.0)
- [x] `npm run test:track` (dev server running): 107 passed, 2 failed. The same 2 also fail on `main` @ 0e27d69f (107 passed, 2 failed there too). Both are the "arrival: moveEnd + first reveal … exceeded 500 ms" observation budgets.
- [x] Feature gate for the area I touched: `node scripts/qa-context-arrivals.mjs --only contacts`: 6 passed, 3 failed, identical on `main`. The 3 failures are local-environment ones: `/api/vessels` returns 503 without an AIS key, which also trips the console and response checks, and the Fort Cavazos installation lookup returns nothing.

Also checked in the browser, before and after:

- the Sahara at 1,100 km and 3,000 km;
- Greenland at 1,100 km and 450 km;
- the Pacific and the Amazon at 1,100 km;
- FLIR, NVG and CRT over the Sahara.

Before, the ring was near-invisible over desert and invisible under the night styles. After, it reads in every case.

Known limits:

- On touch screens, a tap exactly on the ring stops the expanded contact search, as the old outline did; the band is now a few pixels wider.
- No runtime performance profile was taken. The ring rebuilds on the same 250 m threshold as before, and Cesium keeps the old primitive until the new one is ready, so it doesn't blink.

## Docs

- [x] `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md` updated and a `changelog.d/<pr-number>-<slug>.md` fragment added (`changelog.d/<this PR's number>-range-ring-visibility.md`, in a second commit once the PR had a number)

title: feat(awareness): add calm sonar pulses that flash the range ring and echo contacts
body:
## What this changes

**Stacked on #1518.** Merge that one first. Until it lands, this diff also shows its commit; this PR's own work starts at `e80f583e`. I'll update the branch from `main` once #1518 is in.

This animates the Global Context range ring like a sonar, so the 250 km range reads at a glance, then lets the ring settle back to a steady line.

- **Pulses:** three dim rings grow from the subject to 250 km, one every 3 s, each taking 9 s. Each one fades in, then fades as it travels, so it arrives dim but still visible.
- **Bounded:** the pulses run for 9 s (three ring flashes) after a selection or a camera move you make, fading in and out over 1.2 s, then rest. At rest the ring is steady at full strength, the pulses, gradient and echoes are hidden, and nothing asks for frames, so a parked view is quiet again. Only a camera move within 1.5 s of a pointer, wheel or touch on the map wakes them; a moving subject and the app's own camera moves (tracking, the cockpit view, an orbit, a fly-to) don't. With the camera below the disc's 2.5 km height they rest completely.
- **Ring:** while the pulses run, the 250 km ring dims to 40% and flashes to full strength as each pulse reaches it, then fades over 1.8 s.
- **Gradient:** behind each pulse, a soft band in the same blue fades inward over 35% of the radius.
- **Contact echoes:** as a pulse front crosses a flight, military aircraft or AIS vessel, the detection overlay draws a second bracket around that contact's bracket, spreading outward as it fades over 1.4 s. It is the pulse blue on the default detection style and the style's own line colour under NVG, FLIR and CRT, and never brighter than the contact's own bracket, including under the Cyber sonar sweep. The subject and anything within 5 km never echo. No layer's icon or colour changes; mapped installations have no detection bracket, so they don't echo.
- **Nothing catches a click:** the pulse lines and gradient are drawn by one unpickable disc, and the 250 km ring is an unpickable polyline primitive in the same outline material and width as before, so a click or tap near either reaches the contact underneath. The disc follows the subject by a model-matrix rotation and is rebuilt only every 20 km, and it is hidden while the camera is below its 2.5 km height, where it would sweep across the sky. Terrain or 3D tiles higher than 2.5 km still cut through the disc and the ring, as they did the ring alone.
- **Reduced motion:** no pulses, and the ring stays on screen as in #1518. Turning the setting on or off mid-session rebuilds the ring (with an `addListener` fallback for older Safari). A scene without primitives or `preRender`/`postRender` gets the static ring too.

Code changes:

- **`src/layers/awareness/rendering.js`:** the pulse disc and its shader (lines and band), the bounded wake (`awarenessPulseLevel`, `wakeAwarenessPulses`), the postRender-armed render request on `CYBER_SONAR_RENDER_INTERVAL_MS`, the ring primitive and its flash, the reduced-motion listener, and cleanup.
- **`src/layers/awareness/lifecycle.js`:** a camera move (the existing pose signature) shortly after pointer, wheel or touch input on the canvas wakes the pulses.
- **`src/layers/awareness/policy.js`:** timing and styling in `AWARENESS_RANGE_PULSE`, `AWARENESS_RANGE_ECHO` and `AWARENESS_RANGE_RING_STYLE`.
- **`src/awarenessEcho.js` (new):** a small, policy-free echo field. Awareness publishes it and `src/data/detection.js` reads it, so the overlay never imports awareness internals. Registered in `scripts/package-boundaries.json`.

### Decisions for the owner

1. **Pulses are on by default.** They follow the system reduced-motion setting, but there is no separate OFF control in the app. Each run is bounded to 9 s after a selection or a camera move you make.
2. **The pulse lines are drawn by a shader** on the gradient disc instead of polylines, so they stay out of picking. They match the old 3 px outline look and scale with the pixel ratio.

## How I verified it

On head `a851199f`, Node 24.19.0, macOS:

- [x] `npm run doctor -- --json`: ready
- [x] `npm run format:check`, `npm run check:boundaries`, `node scripts/i18n.mjs`
- [x] `npm run build`
- [x] `npm test`: 9866 tests, 9864 passed, 0 failed, 2 skipped, plus the isolated batches 1/1 and 14/14
- [x] `npm run test:track` (dev server on :4174 via `--url`, on the follow-up tree before its last change, which only removed a keyboard listener): 107 passed, 2 failed. The failures are the "arrival: moveEnd + first reveal … exceeded 500 ms" observation budget; the #1518 head (`8a50705e`) fails the same checks on this machine (1 and 2 failures over two runs)
- [x] Built-in Chromium: after a 12 km move the disc, moved by its model matrix, draws concentric with the moved ring within a pixel
- [x] Parked render count (at `3c6c342b`) in headless Chrome (SwiftShader WebGL2), a request-render Cesium scene with this branch's awareness rendering and lifecycle, frames per 5 s window: idle before selection 0; after selecting a subject 57, 46, then 0, 0, 0; after one camera move 58, 49, then 0, 0
- [x] Built-in Chromium (WebGL2, and WebGL1 via `requestWebgl1`): the pulse shader compiles and draws; a pick exactly on a pulse line or on the ring returns nothing, where the old entity ring returned an `Entity`; the primitive ring renders the same 4 px row as the old entity ring within one colour level; the pulse core measures 2 px at pixel ratio 1 and 4 px at ratio 2

New and updated tests:

- **`rangeRing.test.mjs`:** the pulse curve and calm rate; render requests stop after the bound and stay stopped for a minute, and a burst is capped at 15 s; waking by pointer, wheel, touch and drag but not by keys, app camera moves or stale input; teardown through the layer's `disable()`; a full rest below 2.5 km; the disc following by its model matrix and rebuilt past 20 km; a camera move seen by the lifecycle wakes them for one more bounded run; a frame drawn 67 ms after ours pushes the next request to 80 ms after that frame; reduced motion flipped by event, by a later refresh and through `addListener`; the ring flash never drops below `restOpacity`; the disc (uniforms, rebuild, not rebuilt at rest, hidden below 2.5 km); and no entity, with every primitive unpickable, with and without reduced motion.
- **`src/awarenessEcho.test.mjs`:** echo strength, rim wrap, layer filter, altitude, scaling with the pulse level, no echo within 5 km, and the fade-in near the birth ring.
- **`src/data/detectionAwarenessEcho.test.mjs`:** the echo bracket's band and outward spread, and the colour per detection style, tested through pure helpers.
- **`src/data/detectionHost.test.mjs`:** the echo stroke colour through the real detection paint path for the default style and CRT, NVG and FLIR; the echo's spread and alpha on the canvas; under the Cyber sonar sweep an echo never brighter than its bracket; and with six echo-eligible flights, a resting frame checks the echo level fewer times than there are contacts and paints no echo.

Not measured: GPU frame time on real hardware, the full app with live feeds and a selected subject, Safari and Firefox, phones and battery.

## Docs

- [x] `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md` updated, and `changelog.d/1519-range-ring-sonar-pulses.md` describes the bounded run and the dimmed ring

title: Fix voice camera tilt from a top-down view
body:
### Voice camera tilt

A voice fly-to frames a city top-down, at pitch −90°. The tilt clamp rejected any step that left the pitch below −89°, whatever the direction. So "tilt up" reported success and stopped on its first frame, and "tilt down" was refused: from the view voice lands on, no tilt ever moved the camera. A bare "tilt the camera" also failed, because tilt required a direction. Hosted and standalone share this path (the same tools, run in the browser).

#### What changed

- **Clamp in the direction of travel.** Pitch stays within −89°..−5°, but a −90° view can now tilt up out of it. Tilting further down from top-down is still refused honestly.
- **Pivot about the view centre.** Tilt swings the camera about the ground under the crosshair, so the place stays centred and the heading is kept. With no ground under the crosshair, or beyond 1,000 km of range (where a pivot would swing the camera thousands of km), it tilts in place. Voice releases the follow camera before it moves, so a voice tilt from a tracked view pivots too. Every angle and limit is the camera's own pitch: at regional range the pivot's pitch is up to about 8° shallower (the Earth curves away), so the swing solves for the pivot pitch that gives the camera the angle asked for. A pivot tilt yields when tracking takes the camera.
- **Clearance.** A pivot swing toward the horizon lowers the camera (height above the pivot is range × sin|pitch|), so it stops 150 m above the pivot and the rest of the tilt happens in place. A close view no longer ends inside 3D tiles.
- **Tilt to an angle.** `move_camera` takes an optional `pitchDeg` ("tilt 45 degrees" → −45). A tilt with neither angle nor direction settles at −45° (oblique view), and −89 or −90 from a top-down view is reported unchanged. Blank or non-numeric angles are ignored. `pitchDeg` is an absolute angle, not a step: a `direction` that contradicts it is refused. An angle the camera already holds answers `unchanged` but still takes navigation, so it stops a running motion and releases the follow camera. A tilt left or right is refused.
- **Zoom during a tilt.** A zoom during a pivoting tilt scales the range the tilt holds, as it already did for orbit, instead of being undone on the next frame. A zoom in stops at the range that keeps the 150 m clearance at the current pitch. The zoom limits no longer move a view the wrong way (a zoom in never pushes a view closer than 80 m out, and a zoom out never pulls an orbit beyond 5,000 km in). A tilt's zoom out stops at 1,000 km, where pivoting stops. A zoom that can move no further now answers "not zoomed" instead of success, for orbit as well as tilt, and a tilt's zoom reports `tiltRangeAdjusted` rather than `orbitRadiusAdjusted`.
- **Fly-to and a camera motion in one sentence.** "Fly to London and tilt the camera" or "fly to Paris and orbit it" arrives as two concurrent tool calls. The motion used to cancel the flight, or be replaced by it when the place needed a lookup. A tilt, orbit, pan or rotate now waits for a pending voice flight to land (up to 15 s), then runs where the camera ends up. It moves to a later fly-to as soon as that one begins, whatever the earlier one reports (landed, cancelled, a lookup that lost navigation, or a lookup still pending), and looks past a later lookup that found nothing to the last flight that moved, so it neither drops nor runs early and cancels the newer flight. Malformed calls ("pan" with no direction) are refused before the wait. If the flight never arrives, or the user grabs, touches or scrolls the map during it, the motion is not run and says so. `stop` and `rotate_globe` do not wait. A motion sent before its fly-to runs at once, and the fly-to's result names the motion it stopped (`stoppedMotion`).
- **Schema pins and prompt budget.** The tool schema pins are re-derived for the new argument and wording. To fit `main`'s 55,500-character Realtime ceiling, `pitchDeg` carries no schema range: the runner clamps any angle to −89°..−5° (a positive angle means the same angle below the horizon), and a test pins that. The `pitchDeg` description now says steps use `direction`. The tightest prompt, with Overpass on, measures 55,495, 5 under the ceiling.

#### Verification

At `1c59105a` (merged with `main` at `73c14ac7`), Node 24:

- `npm test`: 10,510 tests, 10,508 pass, 0 fail, 2 skipped. `npm run format:check`, `npm run check:boundaries`, `npm run i18n` and `npm run build` ✓
- `src/cameraTilt.test.mjs` uses a real Cesium camera; 7 of its first 9 tests fail on `main`. The fly-then-tilt tests in `src/voice/gevActions.test.mjs` fail without the second commit, and the fly-then-orbit/pan/rotate tests fail without the third.
- Review follow-ups: each fix has a regression test that fails at `2ac73519`: zoom during a pivot tilt, a drag mid-flight (single and chained fly-tos), clearance on a 250 m top-down view tilted to −5° (it used to end about 22 m up), and `pitchDeg` against a contradicting direction (including at 150 km, where the pivot and camera pitch differ). The P3/P4 follow-ups add tests for a superseding fly-to, the 15 s wait, a stale reply, malformed calls before the wait, a globe-range tilt, and a regional or tracked tilt-up at the pivot limit. The latest round adds a zoom in during a 400 m tilt at −40° (it used to leave the camera about 51 m up) and the "not zoomed" answer at the limit. Sameh's review adds tests that fail at `eeb20d24`: a geocode cancelled by a later fly-to's start, a flight that lands while the next place is looked up, later lookups that find nothing (one or two, in either order, concurrent or one call at a time), a newer lookup cancelling an older one and then finding nothing, an earlier reply's flight never adopted, and `pitchDeg` −89/−90 from top-down. The second review round adds 11 tests that fail at `4c9b27dc`: a tilt to −5° from 100, 400 and 900 km ends with the camera at −5° (it ended at −5.9°, −8.6° and −12.9°), a regional tilt-up nudge and the `pitchDeg`/direction check by camera pitch, a zoom out during a 900 km tilt capped at 1,000 km, an unchanged angle stopping a running motion, tilt left/right refused, a motion following a newer fly-to while its own lookup stalls, and `stoppedMotion`. A zoom in to the clearance asserts the camera takes the range.
- In the dev app, through the voice tool dispatcher: London fly-to (−90°), then `move_camera {motion:'tilt'}` → −45.4°, with the centre (51.49, −0.09) and the north heading unchanged. With keys: a fly-to London and a tilt sent together now end over London at −46° (before: tilted in Austin, or London stayed top-down).
- Spoken in Chrome on the first commit: "Tilt up" (repeated), "Tilt the camera to 80 degrees", "Fly to London" then "Tilt down", "Keep tilting up slowly" then "Stop", and a map drag mid-tilt all work. "Fly to London, then tilt the camera 45 degrees" said as one sentence failed there; the second commit fixes that.
- Third commit, in the dev app with keys, through the voice tool dispatcher (fly-to and motion sent 150 ms apart): "Paris" + orbit waited 4.9 s then orbited over Paris; "Tokyo" + pan left waited 2.3 s; "London" + rotate right waited 2.2 s and ended over London. All three flights landed and each motion ran.
- Not run: `scripts/qa-voice-routing.mjs` (no OpenAI credit available; the `pitchDeg` description changed again), the voice-bench on OpenAI and Gemini, a spoken check of the one-sentence fly-and-tilt, and a spoken or in-app check of the review follow-ups (unit tests only).

#### Notes for reviewers

- A tilt nudge now pivots about the view centre rather than looking up or down in place.
- A tilt, orbit, pan or rotate said while a voice fly-to is still flying now waits for it to land instead of interrupting it. Orbit keeps its own arming for other camera flights.
- The 150 m clearance is measured above the pivot, not above the terrain behind the camera.
- A grab during an earlier, still-pending voice fly-to also drops a motion queued behind a later fly-to, including across replies. It fails safe (the motion is skipped and says why).
- Any press on the map during a voice flight, including a marker click, counts as moving the camera. That also fails safe.
- A zoom in that reaches the clearance during an upward tilt ends the pivot on the next frame, and the rest of the tilt happens in place. A further zoom then moves the camera like any zoom.
- A lookup cancelled by a panel search or share link while a later voice lookup in the same reply is pending is taken as superseded by that voice lookup; if the later one then finds nothing, the motion runs where the camera is. The drag check does not cover a search.
- `resolve_area` with drawing on flies the camera through the annotation engine, which the voice-flight wait does not track (as with `annotate_map`), so "outline Bagmati and tilt the camera" can tilt before that flight. This predates this PR.
- Changelog fragment: `changelog.d/1520-voice-camera-tilt.md`.

title: Name the reporting provider in Contacts and Cockpit counts
body: ## Summary The Layers panel and the Contacts list named the provider each feed reported (`X-Feed-Source` / `X-Flight-Source`). The Cockpit Contact counts ignored it: the template hardcoded OpenSky, adsb.lol, AISStream and OpenStreetMap. Vessels had a second gap. A deployment that serves the same routes from other providers shows the same split for flights and vessels. ### Before / after Same stubbed feeds on both: flights answered by the adsb.lol regional fallback, vessels by a "Datalastic QA" provider. The Layers panel already showed both correctly. | Count | Before (main) | After (this PR) | |---|---|---| | FLT | `OpenSky` — wrong, flights came from adsb.lol | `adsb.lol · FALLBACK` | | AIS | `AISStream` — wrong, vessels came from Datalastic | `Datalastic QA` | MIL (`adsb.lol`) and SITE (`OpenStreetMap`) were already right and are unchanged. ### Changes - **Cohorts** carry `sourceStatus`: `fallback` or `stale`, from the same `layerFeedState` that sets the Layers row's FALLBACK/STALE state. - **`sourceStatusLabel`** (`src/ui/layerNames.js`) presents a provider the way the Layers row names it, plus the state, e.g. `adsb.lol · FALLBACK`. The full text is in the tooltip, since the tile ellipsizes. - **Vessels** `getStats()` reports `source`, as flights and military already do. - `scripts/package-boundaries.json` gives the cockpit and awareness packages the modules they now import. `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md` describes the behaviour. AI tools already report each source's `feedState`, so they are unchanged. ## Tests - `src/ui/cockpitContext.test.mjs`: the counts name the reported provider and its state; the initial card shows `—`. - `src/layers/awareness/queries.test.mjs`: cohorts carry the provider and `fallback` / `stale` / `null`. - `src/layers/awareness/panel.test.mjs` (new): a Contacts row detail reads `adsb.lol · FALLBACK`. - `src/layers/vessels/ownership.test.mjs`: vessel stats name the provider from the last snapshot. - `src/ui/layerNames.test.mjs`: `sourceStatusLabel` in English and Russian. Each new test failed before the fix. ## Verification - `npm test`: 9906 pass, 0 fail, 1 skipped. - Format, boundaries, i18n, layer-token, doctor: clean. - Keyless build passes. - A headless Chrome run on a keyless dev server stubbed the feeds: flights from the adsb.lol regional fallback, military from adsb.lol, vessels from a "Datalastic QA" provider. It enabled Contacts and entered Cockpit on a tracked flight. Cockpit read `adsb.lol · FALLBACK`, `adsb.lol`, `Datalastic QA`, `OpenStreetMap`, and the Contacts rows matched. title: fix: keep the globe on screen when zooming out from a tilted view
body:
## Problem

From a tilted view at ~170 km, scrolling out without moving the cursor slides the globe off the bottom of the screen around 700 km to 2,000 km. After that only stars show, and the camera keeps going (the HUD ended at `ALT: 97679259m`). Zooming out from a top-down view is fine.

Cause: this is stock Cesium `ScreenSpaceCameraController` wheel zoom, and GEV sets no limits on it.
- Below 1,000 km with a shallow pitch (`dot(direction, up) >= -0.5`), Cesium zooms out by backing along the cursor ray, then puts the heading and pitch back after every step (`camera.setView(scratchZoomViewOptions)`).
- The Earth's limb sits `acos(R/(R+h))` below the horizontal: 13° at 170 km, 30° at 1,000 km. A fixed shallow pitch ends up looking above the limb.
- Step size grows with height, and `maximumZoomDistance` was Cesium's default, `Infinity`, so nothing stops the climb.

## Fix

New `src/app/zoomOutGuard.js`, installed in `scene.js` next to `installTrackpadPinchZoom` (same install-and-dispose pattern):

1. **Ceiling:** `maximumZoomDistance = 40,000 km`, a whole-Earth view. This only limits user input. Camera flights, share links and story views can still go further; the largest programmatic altitude in `src` is 22,000 km anyway.
2. **Pitch clamp:** above 300 km, during a user zoom-out, the view is eased each frame (`preRender`) towards at least 8° below the limb (`maxPitchForHeight`). The view tilts towards top-down as you climb, like Google Earth. The clamp only runs when **all** of these hold:
   - there was a wheel, two-finger touch or right-drag on the viewer in the last 500 ms;
   - camera height went up this frame (zooming in is untouched);
   - `enableInputs` is on (cockpit tracking, CCTV gizmo, imagery box and local GeoJSON turn it off);
   - `camera.transform` is identity (no tracked entity or `lookAtTransform`);
   - no `flyTo` is running.

   The tilt toggle cancels its own animation on wheel, so the two never overlap. Oblique browsing below 300 km is left alone.

`docs/CURRENT-STATE.md` describes the new behaviour. The module is registered in `scripts/package-boundaries.json` and `scripts/format-scope.json`.

## Tests

`src/app/zoomOutGuard.test.mjs` (11 tests):
- `maxPitchForHeight`: no limit below 300 km, −38.2° at 1,000 km, −90° at very large heights, and monotonic.
- A wheel zoom-out eases towards the limit and doesn't snap.
- Two-finger touch and right-drag count as zoom input; one finger and left-drag don't.
- The clamp does nothing without recent input, when zooming in, with inputs disabled, with a tracked transform, or during a flight.
- The installer sets the ceiling; the disposer restores it unless someone else changed it since.

`npm test` (9,912 pass, 0 fail), `npm run check:boundaries`, `npm run format:check` and `npm run build` all pass.

## Manual check

Dev server on the keyless Esri globe: Istanbul, 170 km, heading 0°, pitch −25°, wheel zoom-out at screen centre, frames stepped by hand.

| | Before (guard off) | After |
|---|---|---|
| step 50 | 3,770,513 km | 40,000 km, pitch −89°, Earth centred |
| step 200 | 38,852,259,098 km, Earth off-screen | 40,000 km, pitch −89°, Earth centred |

Not covered yet: Google Photorealistic tiles (no key in my local env) and a real touch device. Said's exact path, where the pitch stays fixed on photoreal, is covered by the unit tests but hasn't been checked live. A before/after screen recording on photoreal is still to be attached.

## Out of scope (seen in the same video)

- CCTV labels (Estonia/Finland) drawn past the horizon into space.
- A translucent dark rectangle over the Black Sea.

Changelog: `changelog.d/1522-zoom-out-runaway.md`.

title: fix(tools): wrap whole-degree headings at 360 to 0
body:
The agent and voice query tools round directions to whole degrees without wrapping, so a direction from 359.5° up to 360° comes back as 360: `find_vessel` with course 359.7 and heading 359.6 returns `course_deg: 360`, `heading_deg: 360`.

**Change**
- `course_deg` and `heading_deg` (vessels), `course_deg` (aircraft), `bearing_deg` (transit), `heading_deg` (cameras), and `rise_azimuth_deg` and `azimuth_deg` (satellites) now round through `roundHeadingDegrees` (`src/data/headingDegrees.js`), the helper the layers and UI already use, which wraps into 0–359 (a direction that rounds to 360 reads 0; larger or negative values wrap).
- Null handling is unchanged (a missing value is still null), and other rounding is unchanged.
- CURRENT-STATE notes the 0–359 range for these fields.

**Verification**
- New tests in the five query test files; each fails on main with `360 !== 0`.
- `npm test`: 9,907 tests, 1 fail, 11 skipped. The failure is `nominatimOutlineRoute`'s POSIX 0o700 cache-directory check, which fails on main on Windows too.
- `format:check`, `check:boundaries` and the build pass.
- `npm run test:track` (dev server): 108 passed, 1 failed; a second run 107 passed, 2 failed. The failures are the `arrival: moveEnd + first reveal` timing checks exceeding their 500 ms budget (503–686 ms); on main in the same worktree the same check failed at 503.7 ms, so they are timing variance on this machine, not this change.

title: Add statewide PennDOT camera category and zoom-based camera visibility
body:
## What this changes

Add an opt-in statewide PennDOT / 511PA camera source and adapt CCTV visibility to keep the expanded catalog readable at wide zooms. Its paginated public catalog supplies published WGS84 locations, county/road labels, available views and snapshot URLs. Enabling the pack loads the whole available statewide catalog by default; optional county filters and regional anchors support smaller configured catalogs. Traffic-direction labels are preserved as descriptions rather than presented as PTZ headings.

Add an independent **PennDOT Traffic Cams** row under **Cameras** in the data-layer panel. Statewide 511PA traffic cameras live there; curated and manually configured webcams remain in **Cameras**. Both categories can run independently or together, sharing one viewer and the existing playback limits. Selection, cycling, nearest-camera actions, coverage and detection follow the enabled categories. Turning a category off releases its selected feed. Share token `9` restores PennDOT independently and mirrors the CCTV viewer options; the published drone-airspace token `8` remains unchanged.

511PA video uses fragmented MP4 HLS. Extend the existing bounded relay with initialization-object and MP4-segment support, server-only public-player authorization, required origin headers and rate-limit backoff. Origin checks, session leases, memory limits, idle cleanup and the two-session limit remain enforced. Unavailable or unsupported video retains the snapshot path.

Raise the shared catalog budget from 4,000 to 12,000 (maximum 20,000), enough for the combined shipped pack budgets including statewide Pennsylvania. Smaller explicit budgets keep fair round-robin allocation and trim reporting. Visible-card and live-video concurrency limits do not grow with the metadata catalog.

Camera markers become progressively sparser as the map zooms out: caps are 160 at 25 km viewer altitude, 80 at 100 km, 40 at 500 km and 20 at 2,000 km. Ground-anchored cells retain stable winners during pans; screen-space spacing also removes overlaps in tilted views. The selected camera stays eligible. Ambient thumbnails reduce to eight at 50 km and hide at 100 km, then return on zoom in. Street and city views retain their existing thumbnail budgets.

Camera name callouts use a stricter text-only policy: at most 17 below 5 km viewer altitude, 15 below 15 km, 12 below 30 km, and none at or above 30 km. Anchor spacing grows from 120 to 200 pixels. This camera-only ceiling applies even at maximum detection density and during label fade-out; icons, brackets, other label types and the selected camera's own title keep their existing behavior.

The pack is **off until `CCTV_511PA_ENABLED=1`**.
