title: fix(fires): show a 47.6-hour-old detection as 2d, not 48h
body:
## Problem
`formatAge` and `formatAgeLabel` in `src/layers/firms/model.js` choose the unit on the raw hour count and round afterwards. A detection between 47.5 and 48 hours old therefore reads **48h**, while one exactly 48 hours old reads **2d**, so the label steps from 47h to 48h to 2d in half an hour.

## Change
Round to whole hours first, then pick the unit:
- under 1 h → `<1h` (unchanged);
- 1–47 whole hours → `Nh`;
- otherwise → days, rounded as before.

Ages outside 47.5–48 h read exactly as before.

## Tests
- `src/layers/firms/model.test.mjs` (new): 47.4 h → `47h`; 47.6 h → `2d`; 48 h → `2d`, for both `formatAge` and the translated `formatAgeLabel`.
- `npm test`: 10,201 pass, 1 fail. The failure is `src/tooling/nominatimOutlineRoute.test.mjs`, which checks POSIX `0o700` permissions and also fails on main on Windows.
- `npm run format:check`, `npm run check:boundaries`, `npm run i18n` and `npm run build` pass.

## Overlap
#1426 and #1146 also edit `src/layers/firms/model.js`, in other hunks; neither changes these two formatters.

title: fix(camera): keep the globe in view from orbit
body:
### Keep the globe in view from orbit

From the whole-globe view the camera could end up facing empty space, with only stars on screen. Cesium's free look (Shift+drag) turns the camera in place. From 18,000 km the planet's edge is only about 15° from nadir, so a few drags turned it out of frame (the reported state was at pitch −42°, 48° off nadir, with the camera rolled). The pose was then saved into the share hash, so a reload or a shared link opened on stars too.

#1522 fixed one path to this state: a wheel or pinch zoom-out from a tilted view, now capped at 40,000 km and pitched towards the planet as it climbs. This change covers the other paths, which #1522 does not touch: Shift+drag free look, a drag that Cesium turns into an in-place look, a saved or shared view that already looks away, and voice tilt and turns from orbit.

#### What changed

- **Free look only below 1,000 km.** Shift+drag does nothing above that height. Cesium also turns the camera in place for a drag that starts on the stars below its trackball height (7,500 km by default); that height is lowered to 1,000 km, so such a drag now orbits the globe above it, as it already did higher up. Measured live, a 300 px drag from the stars orbits about 28° at 1,500 km, 55° at 3,000 km and 68° at 5,000 km, against 70° at 8,000 km before the change. A tilt (drag or touch pinch-tilt) there while the screen centre is on the stars now tilts about the planet's edge or does nothing, instead of turning the camera, wherever the gesture starts: Cesium's tilt tests the centre ray, not the start point. Rotation drags that start on the planet, and zoom, are unchanged.
- **A measure of what is on screen.** `src/globeInView.js` casts a 32×18 grid of view rays at the WGS84 ellipsoid to measure how much of the frame shows the planet's surface. While the scope mask is on (the default), only the rays inside its keyhole count, because the mask hides or dims the rest (the keyhole radius is the mask's half-opacity contour at the default feather): surface in the masked corners does not count as in view. With the scope off the whole frame counts. The module is shared by the viewer and the voice camera verbs, and registered in `scripts/package-boundaries.json` (as are `scopeMask.js` and `scopeMaskPolicy.js` for the layer-construction group that owns `cameraVerbs.js`).
- **Recovery when no surface is on screen.** When a camera move ends above 1,000 km with no ray on the surface, the camera turns straight down at the same position and heading. Limb glow and a sliver up to about one grid cell thick (some 50 px on a 900 px tall frame) can count as out of view. #1522's zoom-out guard keeps wheel and pinch zoom-outs in view; this catches the other ways a move can end looking away, such as a saved or shared view that did. Views with more surface than that, such as the oblique orbital Director shots, are left as they are, and so are tracked or locked cameras, a camera flight in progress, a Director scene while it plays (holds included) and the 2D and Columbus modes; a check a flight or scene defers runs once it ends. A Director shot loaded or replayed outside a run is not a playing scene, so a stars-only shot stepped through that way is still turned down. The scope setting is read at every check, so turning the scope on or off takes effect at the next one; a view that loses its surface without a camera move (a resize, or turning the scope on) is left as it is until the next move.
- **A move-end check that does not depend on Cesium's `moveEnd`.** Cesium raises `moveEnd` once its per-frame camera comparison, exact to the last rounding error, has seen no change for half a second. On `main` with #1522, at the reported pose, `moveEnd` stopped arriving at all: the camera's orientation is rewritten by a rounding error every frame, so Cesium never sees it stop (before #1522 the same pose still got `moveEnd`; why #1522 brings the drift was not pinned down). So the recovery also starts its own check on `moveStart`: it samples the pose every 250 ms, treats rounding-size drift as at rest, and runs once the pose has held for half a second after moving. It keeps watching until Cesium raises `moveEnd`, because under that drift Cesium raises no new `moveStart` for a later move, and gives up five minutes after the camera last moved.
- **Honest voice limits from orbit.** Voice tilt and in-place turns of a free 3D globe camera above 1,000 km stop when about a tenth of the visible frame still shows the planet, or about as much as it showed when the turn started if that was less (two grid cells of sampling noise allowed). Whatever the starting point, a voice turn never leaves less than about 1% of the visible frame on the planet, and a view that already shows less only keeps or gains what it has. A turn that cannot go half a degree further without crossing that limit is refused with a reason, as the existing tilt clamp does, instead of being reported as done, and a turn it accepts turns at least that half degree. A turn that keeps or gains surface is not refused, even after the window has been resized, except that near the limit, where the planet's edge crosses the sample grid, sampling wobble can occasionally refuse one (most often above about 15,000 km and on phone or ultrawide frames); nothing then turns away from the planet. A turn that starts where the last voice turn left the camera keeps that turn's limit, or a higher one if the planet now fills more, so repeating the request does not take any more; once anything else has moved or turned the camera, a turn is measured from what is on screen. Tracked or locked cameras and the 2D and Columbus modes are not limited; a request made while the camera is tracked is judged by the pose voice's release of the follow camera will leave, before that release, so a refused turn keeps the tracking.

#### How I verified it

Review follow-ups (`64377db9`, `2f9d13f3`, `29935cc0`, `852e93d0`, and `ef4b319f` for the changelog credit), Node 24.19, at `852e93d0`: `npm test` 10,243 tests, 10,230 pass, 2 skipped, 11 failed: all 11 are deadline or budget tests outside this change that timed out while other work loaded the machine (load average up to 68), and each of their 8 files passes 0-fail when run on its own; doctor, format, boundaries and build ✓; `test:track` 109/109, run back to back with the previous head `d36b28f3` (also 109/109); #1522's zoom-out QA 9/9. These commits follow [Chad Elliott](https://github.com/THEtheChad)'s review: thanks to him, drags from the stars now orbit instead of being recovered afterwards, authored flights and scenes keep their framing, and the drift behind the missing `moveEnd` is traced to its source.

The original change was verified at `99520b52` (one commit on `main` at `1facc09f`, which includes #1522), Node 24.19:

- [x] `npm run build`
- [x] `npm test`: 10,238 tests, 10,236 pass, 0 fail, 2 skipped. `npm run doctor`, `npm run format:check` and `npm run check:boundaries` ✓
- [x] `npm run test:track` (dev server on `be908003`, which differs from this commit only in when the settle check gives up; `--url` on a free port): 109 passed, 0 failed. Its arrival-timing and frame-window checks are load-sensitive on `main` too: on a busy machine during this work both `main` and this branch failed some of them, with the camera ending at the exact pose each time and this branch settling as fast as `main` or faster when they passed; run side by side at similar load, the previous revision passed 109 and `main` 108 (its one failure a console error from a third-party terrain host).
- Feature gate: `QA_BASE_URL=http://localhost:4194 node scripts/qa-zoom-out-guard.mjs` (from #1522) passes all 9 checks at 1200 px and 390 px on `be908003`, so the zoom-out guard and this change work together in the real controller.
- The frame-measure, recovery and voice tests use a real Cesium camera; the free-look and trackball tests use plain fixtures and check the controller settings and their disposal, not drag behaviour, which was checked live. The frame-measure and recovery tests check results against an independent oracle (an 80×45 grid of `camera.getPickRay` rays, optionally limited to the keyhole); the voice tests check the floor with the frame measure and that surface stays on screen (in the keyhole when the scope is on) with the oracle. They cover the reported stuck pose, a limb-only pose, a corner-only pose hidden by the scope, far-orbit tilts run at 60 frames a second across five poses (each must either be refused or really move half a degree, and some must be accepted), a grazing-sliver turn at 18,000 km that used to stop without moving (it must turn at least the half degree its check proved), the same pose reached through a tracked, frame-locked camera that voice releases, a refused turn on a tracked camera (tracking and the locked frame kept, no release), a stuck pose that never gets `moveEnd` (recovered by the settle check on a fake clock, with rounding-size drift between samples), a later move under that drift with no new `moveStart` (recovered again), a half-minute drag that stops at that pose (recovered), a camera that keeps moving for eight minutes (followed and left alone, recovered once it stops, the check giving up five minutes after that), the oblique recipe poses (Global Flights Radar, Omniscience Pullback), a pose below 1,000 km, a locked camera, a tracked camera and Columbus view, with the scope both on and off.
- Mutation checks, each run against this code: putting back a bounding-sphere frame test fails 4 tests; dropping the keyhole from the voice limit or from the recovery in `viewer.js`, the camera-kind guard, the noise allowance, the 1% floor, the cap at what is on screen, the tracked-camera guard on the recovery, the per-motion baseline, the carried baseline between turns, its "same pose" condition, the guaranteed half-degree turn, judging a tracked camera before voice releases it, the recovery's own settle check, its follow of a camera that keeps moving, or its watch for a later move before `moveEnd` each fails its own test. (The `tools.js` install that passes the scope state and `sceneDirector.running` to the recovery is not covered by a test; it was checked live.) Thirteen voice tests in `src/cameraGlobeRotation.test.mjs` fail with `main`'s `cameraVerbs.js` (for the Columbus test, its 3D precondition).
- In the dev app at 1600×900 with the scope on (the default), driving Cesium's real render loop (measured on the revision before the rebase unless noted):
  - The reported pose (18,000 km, heading 180°, pitch −42°, roll 180°), set the way a share link's restore ends, is turned to pitch −90° at heading 180° and the hash is rewritten to `pitch=-90&roll=0`: 554 ms after `moveStart` with the viewer's frame loop running in render-on-demand mode, and 521 ms after it with drawing forced every frame, in both cases by the new check before any `moveEnd`. Re-checked on `be908003` (the only change since moves when the settle check gives up after the camera stops): set the same way with the render loop driven every 30 ms, it was back at pitch −90° after 518 ms, and after 525 ms when set again straight after.
  - Four Shift+drags from the globe view leave the camera at nadir (before the fix they left it 48° off nadir, stars only). Free look still turns the camera at 50 km.
  - The whole "Global Flights Radar" scene (19,000 km at −65°, 8,000 km at −52°, 4,200 km at −46°, 1,700 km at −40°, 12,000 km at −70°) played through with no recovery.
  - Voice from 18,000 km at −80° (51% of the keyhole on the planet): "tilt up" goes to −65° (13%), a second stops at −63.3° (9.4%), and a third is refused with the reason.
  - A continuous voice turn left from an oblique orbit stops with the planet still inside the keyhole: from 5,000 km at −70° it stops at 9.4% of the keyhole, from 3,000 km at −75° at 10.1%. (Measured on the full frame, as before this change, the same turns ended with the planet only in the masked corners.)
  - From 18,000 km at −62° (7.2% of the keyhole), a turn left stops at 6.5%; five more turn-left requests, once and continuous, take no more and the view stays at 6.5%.
  - With the scope off: after "tilt up" stops at its limit (56 of 576 cells) and the window is widened to 3200×900 at the same pose (4 cells on screen), "tilt down" is allowed (190 cells).

#### Notes for reviewers

- The recovery has no pointer-down guard: a user who holds any drag still for more than half a second on a view with no surface can see it fire under the drag. With the trackball change, a drag can no longer turn the camera away from the planet above 1,000 km, so this needs a view that already showed none.

- On a 32:9 super-ultrawide screen, two authored "Global Flights Radar" shots (19,000 km at −65° and 8,000 km at −52°) show no surface at all; a per-pixel raycast finds 0 rows of planet. The recovery leaves a playing scene alone, so they keep their authored framing; that framing gap exists on `main` (the recipes do not fit 32:9). Every other recipe pose above 1,000 km keeps surface inside the keyhole at 1600×900, 1920×1080, 390×844, 844×390, 3440×1440, 1280×1024 and 900×1600.
- A voice turn that the limit stops partway still reports success, as the existing tilt clamp does; only a turn that cannot move half a degree is refused.
- A pose change between voice turns (a wheel notch, an orbit drag, a voice zoom or pan) starts the next turn's limit afresh, so a nudge before each request lets turns step down by about two grid cells each, to the 1% floor. Live, from 7.2% of the keyhole with a 2 m wheel nudge before each request: 6.5, 5.8, 5.1, 4.3, 3.6, 2.9, 2.2, 1.4%.
- Above 1,000 km a voice turn measures the frame twice per animation frame (the current view and the next step, about 0.13 ms each on an idle machine), plus a short bisection on the frame where it reaches its limit.
- This touches the voice tilt tick that #1520 rewrites. Whichever lands second needs a small resolution: #1520's in-place branch `cam.lookUp(limited - from)` becomes `lookWithinFrame(cam, m, delta >= 0 ? 'lookUp' : 'lookDown', Math.abs(delta))` with `delta = limited - from`. Its ground-pivot branch keeps the target centred and needs no limit.
- Changelog fragment: `changelog.d/1532-globe-in-view.md`.

title: Focus quality of life and clutter improvement
body:
## What changes

Clicking a contact currently takes the camera away from the surrounding scene. This change makes a single click select/highlight the object and show its live details while preserving the overview. CCTV continues to open its existing feed panel.

- Double-click or use **Focus** to deliberately move/follow the camera.
- **Restore last view**, available in the details panel and camera toolbar, returns immediately to the exact world position and orientation captured before the latest accepted focus. Each accepted focus replaces the return snapshot; restoring consumes it.
- The right-rail **OBJECT DETAILS** panel refreshes selected telemetry every 500 ms and switches to the next clicked object. Source-supplied values render as plain text.
- Unselected AIS vessels retain their map icons without full name/speed/type cards. Selecting a vessel reveals its details.
- The details panel receives pointer input so Focus, Restore and text clicks cannot pass through to the globe and deselect the contact.

This PR contains the focus/inspection/return behavior and selected-only vessel cards. It adds no data sources or provider credentials. The return snapshot is transient and is not included in share links.

body:
Companion fix for #1426, based on its exact head `dda9a48e5ba7bc4b7f75400c7b496109c3771f14`. This intentionally targets the #1426 branch; it does not bring #1426 or the temporary CONAE integration into main.

When Active Fires is filtered to zero, disabling and reenabling the layer unconditionally shows the cached pre-filter raster while the new snapshot is pending. The counter and query results are empty but the old heat can reappear. Only show retained heat imagery when the current filtered detection set is nonempty.

The regression fails on the unmodified #1426 head (`true !== false`) and passes with the one-line guard; it also verifies that nonempty sets still resume their heat imagery. The test is registered in the format scope and the runtime behavior is documented in CURRENT-STATE.

Validation on the isolated fix (published tree `5d32e0ac77264dd6da050aef6f75c202512933a7`, matching the local validated index):
- 26 focused lifecycle/imagery/raster/intensity tests passed.
- Production build passed (12.99 s); touched-file Prettier, diff, changelog and import-direction checks passed.
- The ordinary `npm test` plan finished with 9,975 passing, 2 skipped and zero failures. Its separate focus allocation probe also passed.
- The complete `npm test` runner did not finish successfully: the 180-second command deadline interrupted `worldOverlayAllocation.test.mjs` (pending promise; no completed probe result). No full-runner or world-overlay allocation pass is claimed. The flight-tracking gate and package-boundary bundling were not run for this isolated patch.

The original validation above left the PR in draft pending those remaining gates. See the follow-up below for the current results and merged status.

This was found while revalidating #1146 against current #1426. It is a general lifecycle issue, independent of CONAE. No raster weights, palette, blur, filter semantics or measurement representation change. The separate temporary joint tree passed 280 focused tests and Chromium mixed-filter, zoom-fade, empty reenable and compact-share checks. Those joint results are not a full-suite claim for this PR.

### Follow-up validation — 2026-11-04

Validated the exact PR head `19e85941e63fad99439e77739137666f686bff45` with Node **24.22.1** and locked dependencies (`npm ci --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund`). Previously documented successful tests and the production build were not repeated.

- **World-overlay allocation: PASS.** Official isolated invocation: `node --import=./build/registerVue.js --expose-gc --test --test-concurrency=1 src/overlays/worldOverlayAllocation.test.mjs`. All **14 tests passed**, zero failures/cancellations/skips, **81,764.44 ms**, exit 0. Default workloads, warmups and allocation budgets were unchanged. The previous whole-command 180-second interruption did not reproduce in isolation; the runner executes this file after the ordinary suite and focus probe, and each world-overlay child has its own 180-second timeout. The earlier interrupted run alone does not establish an allocation regression. This is completion evidence for the remaining allocation file, not a claim that one uninterrupted full `npm test` run passed.

title: Merge DeFlock into the existing mapped ALPR camera feed
body:
## What this changes

The mapped ALPR layer currently reads one community OSM tile feed. Merge DeFlock's primary US/Canada tiles with that existing feed, retaining the existing provider as a fallback and deduplicating shared OSM identities instead of drawing overlapping cameras.

- Prefer newer OSM edits when both publishers provide comparable timestamps; keep node and way identities distinct.
- Support point centroids for OSM ways and refresh build-pinned DeFlock metadata hourly.
- Keep healthy feeds/countries available when another fails; show partial availability and retry.

title: feat(solunar): SOLUNAR card with hunting and fishing windows, sun and moon times and a day rating
body:
## What this changes

Adds a **SOLUNAR** card to the right dock. Click a spot on the map (the default is the middle of the map) and the card lists the next 7 local days for that spot, in the spot's own time zone:

- major windows (moon overhead and underfoot, about 2 h) and minor windows (moonrise and moonset, about 1 h) for hunting and fishing;
- sunrise, sunset, moonrise, moonset, moon overhead and underfoot;
- moon phase and illumination;
- a 1 to 4 star day rating for hunting and for fishing, with the rule printed on the card (new or full moon near the day = 2 points, within 2.5 days = 1; dawn and dusk bands one hour either side of sunrise and sunset; fishing adds a point per band a major window overlaps, hunting a point per band any window overlaps).

Everything is computed in the browser with `astronomy-engine` (MIT) and `tz-lookup` (CC0, a bundled zone table used offline). No outside data feed, no key, nothing fetched. 12 h / 24 h switch is remembered; a gold dot marks the spot on the map.

A day with no moonrise or no moonset shows "none". An event belongs to a local day only when it falls between that day's two local midnights, so the next day's event is never borrowed (a clock-change day is 23 or 25 hours long).

New files are under `src/solunar/`; the card is wired like the Weather and Recent Imagery cards (`ContextView.vue`, `panelRailCatalog.js`, `panelLayoutController.js`, `panelChrome.js` and the rail CSS lists). title: fix(tools): flatten OSM-editable text before it reaches a model (#1262)
body:
Closes #1262. Same three paths the report names, one shared helper.

**What changed**

`textTag()` only trimmed; `cleanText()` capped length but kept newlines; `compactAnalystItem()` copied identity and query fields with no cap at all. A new `src/textSafety.js` exposes `singleLine(value, max)` — control characters, line and paragraph separators flattened to spaces, whitespace runs collapsed, trimmed, capped — and all three sites now use it.

**Two judgement calls**

Control characters become spaces rather than being deleted, so `Town PD\n\nSYSTEM` reads as two words instead of fusing into `Town PDSYSTEM`. And the cap applies *after* flattening, so a tag cannot stay under 120 characters and still spend a character on a newline.

`sanitizeLabel()` already had exactly this rule for scene labels, so it now delegates instead of carrying a second copy. That is the part of the report I most agreed with: the app knew the rule and defended one path.

The ALPR cap is 120 (`SAFE_TAG_MAX`, matching the labels) and tool-output fields cap at 180 (`SAFE_TEXT_MAX`, unchanged from `cleanText`), so nothing that was previously under the limit changes length.

**Tests**

`src/textSafety.test.mjs`: injection shape, tab/NUL/CRLF, U+2028 and U+2029 (not `\s` in every engine), cap-after-flatten, empty and object inputs, numbers, and a 3k-character name.

`src/layers/alpr/records.test.mjs`: the reported injection through `normalizeAlprNode`, every text tag rather than just `operator`, the 255-character OSM maximum, blank tags still reading as missing, and legitimate tags unchanged.

`node --test src/textSafety.test.mjs src/layers/alpr/records.test.mjs` → 13 pass. I could not run `npm test` here: the allocation suites require the calibrated Node 24 runtime and this box has 22, so I ran the two files directly rather than claim a green suite.

**Not done**

`compactAnalystItem` is sanitised but has no test of its own — it is module-private inside `gevActions.js` and reaching it needs the Cesium harness. I did not export it just to test it. Say the word and I will add a harness-level test via `createGevActionRunner` like `src/agent/worldPacket.test.mjs` does.

Changelog fragment and `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md` follow in a second commit, named for this PR's number.

title: feat(layers): opacity slider for Wind, Fire Perimeters, Drone Airspace, Sea Marks and Ski Pistes
body:
## What this changes

Adds an Opacity slider (0–100 %, step 5, double-click resets) under the row of every enabled layer that can be dimmed, so a dense scene can be thinned out without turning layers off. A layer opts in by implementing `setOpacity(fraction)`; layers without it show no slider. This PR wires up five: **Wind** (streamlines, canvas fallback, temperature/pressure field), **Fire Perimeters** and **Drone Airspace** (renderer draw-port fill and outline colours), and the **Sea Marks** and **Ski Pistes** overlays (imagery alpha). The setting is shared as `?lop=<layer-id>:<percent>,…`, a query parameter of its own: the `#v=2` share codec, layer tokens and existing links are unchanged, a link without it means 100 %, and nothing is written for a layer at 100 %.

On the original PR submission, I searched open and merged issues and PRs for opacity, transparency, fade/dim layer and layer slider and found no generic per-layer opacity control. #1084 (cloud strength) and the Weather rows' own controls are untouched.

Design in one paragraph: `LayerOpacity` (`src/ui/layerOpacity.js`, no Vue/Cesium) holds the values, calls each layer's hook, repaints the panel through a subscription and rewrites the address with a debounced `history.replaceState`. The row is a Vue component (`LayerOpacityRow.vue`) on the shared `UiSlider`; `LayerPanel` presents it like its other row parts. `src/data/layerOpacity.js` is the pure `lop` codec. `src/layers/sceneOpacity.js` is a small duck-typed helper (no Cesium import) that scales the constant colours of an entity data source and restores them exactly at 100 %. There is no stack inspection and no patching of scene collections: ownership is explicit through the hook.

**Not covered, on purpose:** every layer without `setOpacity` (flights, vessels, satellites, cameras, traffic, …). The draw-port layers dim their fill and outline colours; textures, time-dynamic colours, primitives, models, world-overlay labels/cards and Wind's inspection marker are drawn as before. Each further layer is a few lines plus a test using the same helper.

`?lop=` reading drops unknown ids and layers without the hook, malformed/duplicate pairs, values outside 0–100, and anything over 2,048 characters or 96 pairs; it never throws (unit tests and a browser run with hostile values). An app embedded inline reads the address but does not rewrite its host page's.

The screenshots show the slider at 100% and 40%; the captured imagery alpha changed from 1 to 0.4 and the address gained `lop=sea-marks:40`. title: perf(cctv): fetch the active camera's pictures only while they can be seen
body:
## What this changes

The CCTV layer already pauses its work for a hidden tab (frame fetch for the plane, panel video) and for cameras outside the view (#1485). Two pictures were still fetched when nobody could see them:

- **The active camera's monitor plane** fetched a new still every 10 s while the plane was panned away or on the far side of the globe (only a hidden tab stopped it). It now skips the fetch while the sphere around the camera mount and the plane is outside the view frustum, or every one of its points is below a horizon computed with the WGS84 ellipsoid shrunk by 200 m. This avoids hiding nearby planes below the reference ellipsoid, while retaining far-side culling. A skipped tick does not use up the refresh interval, so the first tick after the plane returns fetches. Activation and calibration still force a fetch. A 2D or Columbus scene, no viewer and no geometry yet all count as visible, so a missing input never blocks a picture.
- **The panel's still preview** was requested while the tab was hidden or the panel collapsed. It now follows the rule the panel's live video already had (`!document.hidden` and panel not `collapsed`). The panel's existing class observer and `visibilitychange` listener (installed when the panel has its video element, as in the app) render again when the panel is shown, which asks for the current picture.

Nothing else changes: no new strings, no new endpoint, no new setting.

I searched open and merged issues and PRs for CCTV visibility, off-screen, hidden tab and polling. #1485 (view thinning, merged) and #1282 (hidden-tab layer polling, merged) cover the geometry, icons, picker and layer polling; I found nothing for these two pictures. Open #1054, #991 and #671 also edit `src/ui/cctvPresentation.js`, and #1266 edits `src/layers/cctv/frames.test.mjs`, so expect a small textual overlap.

![CCTV panel, empty catalog in the current-head dev preview](https://github.com/Byrd-IT/gods-eye-view-upstream/releases/download/pr1543-evidence-b020a1cd/pr1543-panel-b020a1cd.png)

Screenshot from current head `b020a1cd91a0a265e736586eb9911a02303253c0` at 1440 × 900: the CCTV panel opens, but the preview has no camera catalog or snapshot and does not demonstrate skipped requests. The request-count measurements below are historical.

**Historical measurement (before the current head; exact original head not recorded).** Dev server on `main` and on this branch, the default 4,000-camera catalog, headless Chromium 156 on software GL (SwiftShader), `focusNearest` activates camera 354. I counted `/api/cctv/frame` requests over 65 s after a 3 s settle, twice per build, in four states:

| State | `main` (2 runs) | This PR (2 runs) |
|---|---|---|
| A. panel expanded, camera in view | 20, 21 | 25, 21 |
| B. panel collapsed, camera in view | 13, 13 | 6, 6 |
| C. panel expanded, view on the far side of the globe | 12, 13 | 6, 6 |
| D. panel collapsed, view on the far side | 14, 14 | 0, 0 |

A is the unchanged path (the 25 versus 20 spread is run-to-run variation, not something I looked into). In B the plane's fetches remain, in C the preview's, and in D both are skipped. These are request counts under software GL, not frame rates or a measure of server load; the script is not part of this PR.

**Recording:** none. The change removes requests and has nothing to show on screen, so a clip would add nothing to the table above.

## How I verified it

Current head `b020a1cd91a0a265e736586eb9911a02303253c0` is rebased onto upstream `6e0baacd575435f82668864fcc666c4129596857`. Focused CCTV and renderer tests passed 199/199; `format:check` and `check:boundaries` passed. The complete concurrency-limited suite passed 14,865 tests, 0 failed and 4 skipped; serialized groups passed 1/1 and 14/14. A local dev-server preview opened the CCTV panel, but no camera catalog was available; the screenshot is not evidence of frame-fetch behavior. Build, browser feature gates and `test:track` were not rerun on this head.

On earlier head `43d15c6c61957b6a53796a2da4a38f603b04b520`, rebased onto `main` at `c5cf57917429325b15fd8313e9dee14dacc5bfda`, Node 24.22.2: `npm test` passed 12,930 tests, failed 0 and skipped 4; its additional allocation groups passed 1/1 and 14/14. The targeted CCTV tests passed 114/114. `npm run build`, `npm run format:check`, `npm run check:boundaries` and `npm run changelog:check` exited 0.

Browser checks on headless Chromium 152 / software GL with a keyless dev server: `test:track` passed 111/111; `qa-cctv-v2` reported 45 passed, 3 failed and 5 inconclusive. The unmodified base in the same environment reported the same 45/3/5 and the same failing and inconclusive checks: undefined DEM terrain height, two true-empty canvas clicks, and five east-arrow drag checks inconclusive. `qa-camera-controls` passed 13 checks then timed out at line 312 on both the PR and base. Neither browser feature gate passed; the cause is not established and these comparisons do not rule out a contribution from the PR.

**Earlier head results, not rerun on current head:**

Earlier head `5971cce22c2416a71241a1123674e5ba3f37f1a6` (2026-11-12) is the same code rebased onto `main` at `10a788db78f0657e2eb5f8cdd830e6417aed354d`; only the `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md` paragraph was reworded (it now names the 200 m horizon margin and the phone Cameras sheet rule). This head reported 45 passed, 3 failed and 5 inconclusive in all 6 runs (DEM height undefined; two true-empty click checks; five east-arrow checks inconclusive). `main` reported the same 45 / 3 / 5, with the same failing and inconclusive checks, in 5 runs, and 52 passed / 1 failed (the DEM height check) in 1 run. A separate set of runs of unmodified `main` in the same environment (6 runs, for another branch) failed that same check in 4 of them.
- [x] Feature gate for the area I touched: `node scripts/qa-cctv-v2.mjs --url <dev server>`, see below

Run in a scrubbed environment (`env -i`, no `.env`, no keys) on Node 24.22.2, npm 11.19.1, `npm ci`:

- `npm run doctor -- --json` (ready), `npm run format:check`, `npm run check:boundaries`, `npm run i18n` (no new strings), `npm run layer-token:check -- --base-ref upstream/main` (35 published, 0 new), `npm run changelog:check`: all exit 0.

- New tests: five in `src/layers/cctv/frames.test.mjs` (plane in front, behind, below the horizon, a skipped tick keeps the interval, unjudgeable inputs count as visible; they use the real Cesium frustum, occluder and bounding sphere) and one in `src/ui/cctvPanel.test.mjs` (collapsed panel, hidden tab, shown again). - `qa-cctv-v2`: on this branch in 6 runs the result was 52 passed / 1 failed in 4 runs and 45 / 3 / 5 inconclusive in 2, on unmodified `main` 52 / 1 in 4 runs and 51 / 2 in 1. The failure present in every run of both is `terrain-globe completion uses a real DEM height at the rendered mount without mesh samples` (`terrain=undefined`); I did not look into it. The extra failures are `real true-empty canvas click publishes one active-to-null transition` and its repeat (both builds, intermittent) and, with them in the two branch runs, five east-arrow drag checks reported inconclusive ("no on-screen east-arrow shaft found under this GL stack"). title: Fix the typed AI chat translations
body:
Follow-up to #1507: finishes the translations of the typed AI chat strings in all eleven languages.

## What changes

- **Quick commands were English everywhere.** "Reset to globe view" and "Show earthquakes" reached `t()` through a `.map()` in `src/voice/chatPreferences.js`, so `npm run i18n` never saw them. They are now marked with `msg()`, so the check catches them, and translated in every catalog.
- **Traditional Chinese.** `zh-Hant` is the `zh-CN` text in Traditional characters (`docs/translations/zh-Hant.md`). 40 of the 71 new entries used Taiwan vocabulary instead (資料, 檔案, 訊息, 金鑰, 設定, 供應商…). They are regenerated from `zh-CN` with OpenCC `s2tw`, which reproduces 2787 of 2795 existing entries.
- **Arabic "Dock to the right"** now names the left side: in RTL, `rtl.css` moves that rail to the left (the catalog already renders "Right panels" as «اللوحات اليسرى»).
- **Japanese "What am I looking at?"** read as asking what the assistant is looking at; it now asks what is on screen.
- **Glossary terms** in the new strings: the Provider Settings panel name (es, fr, it, pt, ru, uk, zh-CN, ar), dock (ru, zh-CN, ar), provider (zh-CN 服务商, uk постачальник, it provider), live (it, uk), map (uk карта).
- **Per-language fixes:**
  - German drops the du-form, which its guide forbids, and uses Bereich for panel.
  - Japanese drops the spaces between Japanese and Latin text.
  - French keeps the dock label `CHAT`, since the word must fit a 3rem button.
  - Calques ("too large together", "voice exchange") and status wording are fixed.
  - The example commands now read as something a user would say to the assistant.

## How it was checked

Three independent reviews per language (Codex gpt-6-astra, Fable, Opus), then one fix pass per language that accepted or rejected each finding against that language's guide.

- `npm run i18n`: all 11 catalogs complete.
- `npm test`: 10416 tests, 0 failures.
- `npm run format:check` and `npm run check:boundaries` pass.
- `npm run build` passes with empty keys.

Not changed here: the chat autocomplete matches substrings literally, so Arabic diacritics (shadda) can stop a typed word from matching a suggestion. That is a code change for a separate PR.

title: fix(voice): keep chat's view across a provider switch and clear stale errors
body:
## Summary

Two fixes to the typed chat from #1507, found while testing it on `main`.

- **Switching AI Provider keeps chat's view.** Changing the provider in Settings opened from chat rebuilt the voice control from scratch, so Settings fell back to "Back to voice" and the dock went idle, widening the Location and Visual Presets wings. The switch now carries chat's Settings, in chat's frame, to the new provider, like it already carries the input mode. The conversation still does not carry over, and focus stays on the provider choice.
- **A stale voice error clears when you move on.** After a voice error, the dock stayed red with its status on ERROR even after opening chat or closing the voice panel, because both only stopped a session that was still active. Opening chat or the voice panel's close now also ends a session left in error, which returns the dock to idle. Pressing the mic already did.

- `npm run build`, `npm run format:check`, `npm run check:boundaries`, `npm run i18n`: pass. Voice and panel tests: 1187 pass. In the full `npm test` run, the only failures were timing-sensitive elevation, Overpass route and places tests outside this diff; each passes on its own.

  - `providerCommands.test.mjs`: a provider switch hands it to the new mount.

title: feat: Integrate Mobility Database as the Global Public Transportation Data Catalog
body:
### Problem

We need a centralized and structured database containing information about public transportation systems worldwide, including their operators, geographical coverage, data feeds, datasets, and associated usage licenses.

Mobility Database already provides an extensive catalog of mobility data sources. However, we need to integrate this information into our own infrastructure to enable the registration, discovery, querying, and management of transportation systems through a single database.

Without this integration, operators and their data sources must be discovered and registered manually, making it difficult to maintain, update, and expand the platform's transportation coverage.

We also need to ensure that licensing information, attribution requirements, and usage conditions are preserved individually for each data source.

### Proposal

Implement a complete integration with the official Mobility Database API, using it as the primary source for discovering, registering, and maintaining transportation systems and their associated datasets.

The implementation should:

- Import all available feeds from the catalog, without geographical restrictions.
- Identify and register transportation operators and their respective systems.
- Support GTFS Static, GTFS Realtime, and GBFS standards.
- Store operator information, countries, locations, and geographical coverage.
- Register feed IDs, original source URLs, download URLs, and metadata.
- Retrieve and store the licensing information available for each individual feed.
- Preserve attribution requirements and redistribution and commercial usage restrictions according to each source's license.
- Store datasets and track their versions and updates.
- Retrieve feed availability, reliability, and validation reports.
- Implement automated synchronization to detect new feeds, metadata changes, and unavailable sources.
- Prevent duplicate records and maintain relationships between operators, feeds, and datasets.
- Expose imported information through our own API and database, allowing other application modules to access and reuse the data without repeatedly querying Mobility Database.

Feeds without explicitly declared licensing information should be marked as unknown or unspecified rather than automatically considered unrestricted.

### Data source, license, and attribution

The integration should use the official Mobility Database resources and API documentation:

- Mobility Database: https://mobilitydatabase.org/
- API Documentation (Swagger): https://mobilitydata.github.io/mobility-feed-api/SwaggerUI/index.html
- API Repository: https://github.com/MobilityData/mobility-feed-api
- Mobility Database Catalogs: https://github.com/MobilityData/mobility-database-catalogs
- API Terms and Conditions: https://mobilitydatabase.org/terms-and-conditions
- FAQ: https://mobilitydatabase.org/faq

The API provides access to feed information, datasets, availability, reliability, validation reports, and licensing metadata.

Relevant API resources include:

- "/v1/feeds"
- "/v1/gtfs_feeds"
- "/v1/gtfs_rt_feeds"
- "/v1/gbfs_feeds"
- "/v1/datasets/gtfs/{id}"
- "/v1/licenses"
- "/v1/licenses/{id}"
- "/v1/licenses:match"

Licensing information should be retrieved from the metadata and license resources associated with each feed. Each dataset's original license and attribution requirements must be preserved independently, since different providers may have different licensing conditions.

The Mobility Database catalog metadata license must not be confused with the licenses governing the actual transportation datasets.

### Will you build it?

No, this is a request for someone else

title: feat(tools): query existing air-quality and GNSS observations over MCP (#1213)
body:
## Purpose (partial implementation of #1213)

Expose two **read-only, actually callable MCP queries** backed by data sources God's Eye View already owns, rather than creating another provider or an unused helper:

- `get_air_quality`: ECCC AQHI stations within an area, nearest first, with provider/scale, health-risk band, station observation time, Canada-only coverage and explicit stale/empty-data caveats.
- `get_gnss_integrity`: ADS-B-reported low-navigation-integrity cells around a point, using `accumulateGnssObservations` / `binGnssCells`, a 30-minute observation window, and explicit "not proof of GNSS interference" caveats.

Both tools reuse `createToolServices`, have bounded arguments and results, surface only sanitized station names, and are composed through the normal `coreTools` catalog. There is no new endpoint, provider, UI, automation, or destructive action.

### Scope limit

**MCP first; voice is intentionally gated off.** The existing Realtime prompt has a 52,000-character budget (#1363). Turning on new function schemas would require a separately tested prompt-budget adjustment; this PR does **not** claim to complete the voice half of #1213.

### Tests / review

Includes focused deterministic, network-free tests for service gating, MCP-only availability, area filtering, recency, incomplete coverage, malformed records, GNSS anomaly classification, undersampling, duplicate records, stale input and argument validation. **CI has not yet been verified at the new head; please rely on GitHub checks, not a green claim here.**

Requested review: validate source semantics, prompt-budget isolation, and whether these query contracts are the right first milestone for #1213. Avoid inferring clean air from no ECCC stations or confirmed jamming from degraded ADS-B position quality.

Refs #1213.

title: feat(flights): Brazilian aircraft details from ANAC's open registry (RAB)
body:
## What this changes

Closes #1483.

Brazilian-registered aircraft (PP, PR, PS, PT, PU) gain one line on the tracked aircraft label with their build year, seat count and type of operation, from ANAC's open Registro Aeronáutico Brasileiro (RAB). Tracking the Learjet 45 PS-SLJ over São Paulo, for example, reads "Built 2006 · 11 seats · Air taxi" (in Portuguese, "Fabricado em 2006 · 11 assentos · Táxi aéreo"). When adsbdb has no ICAO type or model name, the RAB fills it in.

### How it works

- `server/providers/aircraft/anacRab.js` parses ANAC's daily CSV (about 24 MB, 35k aircraft). The file is downloaded only on the first Brazilian lookup, then at most once a day with `If-None-Match` / `If-Modified-Since`. Downloads are single-flight, capped at 64 MiB with a 90 s timeout, and back off 30 minutes after a failure while keeping the previous index. The index is cached in `.gev-cache/anac-rab.json` (about 3 MB).
- `/api/adsbdb/type/<hex>` joins on adsbdb's registration. adsbdb does not know most Brazilian general aviation (4 of the 5 small aircraft I sampled over São Paulo), but general aviation flies with its own mark as callsign ("PTTSI"). So the flights layer sends that callsign as `?tail=` when the transponder is in Brazil's ICAO block (E40000-E7FFFF), and the server uses it only when adsbdb has no registration. adsbdb's registration always wins, and a foreign transponder never borrows a Brazilian record. I saw this live: a `PSJSL` callsign on a US transponder (adsbdb: N60JM) correctly gets no RAB line.
- `src/data/aircraftRegistry.js` builds the translated line. The new strings are in all 11 locales, with plural forms.
- `ANAC_RAB_ENABLED=0` turns the lookup off. No key is needed.
- For non-Brazilian transponders the client request is unchanged (same URL, same queue key).

### Privacy and licence

- The same CSV lists owners and operators (names, CPF/CNPJ), liens, sale dates and sale prices. The parser copies only nine technical columns, by position, while it scans each row; every other field is walked over without being sliced out. Personal and financial values are therefore never stored, cached, logged or returned. The test fixture plants such values in every column and asserts that none reach the index or the cache file.
- Cancelled registrations are left out, so a transponder still announcing an old mark shows no details rather than another airframe's.
- Source: `https://sistemas.anac.gov.br/dadosabertos/Aeronaves/RAB/dados_aeronaves.csv`, fetched at runtime, keyless. The dataset page states no explicit licence. The RAB is public by law (Lei 7.565/1986, art. 72: "O Registro Aeronáutico Brasileiro é público, único e centralizado"), and the file is open data of a federal agency (Decreto 8.777/2016, art. 3, IV). ANAC is credited in `DATA_SOURCES.md` and in `src/data/dataCredits.js`.

### Related

- #1230 (Mictronics database) widens type and registration coverage for all transponders; this PR adds Brazilian registry details on top. The two complement each other rather than overlap.

## How I verified it

- [x] `npm run build`
- [x] `npm test`: 10,419 pass, 1 fail. The failure is `the disk cache survives a restart and stays within its bounds` (Nominatim outline cache), a known Windows-only failure (0700 directory mode), unrelated to this change. New tests: `server/providers/aircraft/anacRab.test.mjs`, `src/data/aircraftRegistry.test.mjs`.
- [x] `npm run test:track` (dev server running): 108 pass, 1 fail (`stale-readout: tracked label carries STALE cue during grace`). Unchanged `main` (ac28a11e) fails the same check on this Windows machine.
- [x] Feature gate: `node scripts/qa-enrich-ambient.mjs`: 8 pass, 3 fail (E5, E8 on the `aa0002` quadjet glyph, and E10). Unchanged `main` gives the same three failures on this machine, twice in a row; the synthetic fleet has no Brazilian transponders, so this PR's code path is not reached there.
- [x] `npm run check:boundaries`, `npm run i18n` (2,874 messages, complete), `npm run format:check`.
- [x] Live check with `npm run dev` over São Paulo: PS-SLJ, PS-BRR, PS-JHF, PS-TOY, PS-MGD, PS-PJB and PT-TSI resolve through the callsign, and PT-MUE (a LATAM 777) through adsbdb's registration.

### Screenshots

Tracking PS-VOW (Diamond DA62, transponder `e4a613`) near Campinas, SP, on 2026-11-05 with live data, UI in English.

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: the label shows only callsign, altitude and speed](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/206982b4-53cc-4e3d-b68d-18dc5fb1c37a) | ![After: the label adds "Diamond Aircraft DA 62" and "Built 2018 · 7 seats · Air taxi"](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/78fa631e-e3aa-49a8-ad96-e721729555b8) |

"Before" is this branch with `ANAC_RAB_ENABLED=0`, which behaves like `main` for this aircraft: adsbdb does not know PS-VOW, so the label has no type and no registry line. "After" is this branch with the default settings.

title: Add the Navara globe engine next to Cesium, switchable in place
body:
## What this changes

Adds Navara, an experimental three.js/WASM globe, as a second engine next to Cesium. You pick it under Display → Globe Engine, or with `?engine=navara`. Cesium stays the default.

There are two Navara choices. **Navara** draws at CSS pixels without MSAA, as Cesium does. **Navara HD** (`?engine=navara-hd`) draws at the device pixel ratio with MSAA 4 and needs about 1 GiB more on a Retina screen. Layers and the catalog see both as one Navara engine.

- **One application per page.** Switching engines no longer destroys and rebuilds the app. Catalog, layer models, sources, selection, camera mode and URL state live in the session. Only the parts bound to a globe are attached to the next one: GPU primitives, picks, input and the frame loop. The engine you leave stays parked, so switching back is instant; after three minutes it is released and its WebGL context lost. Only one Navara variant is ever kept: picking the other one rebuilds Navara (about 1.8 s).
- **Layers and UI apart from the planet.** Layers render on both engines through per-engine renderers that share one model and display policy. Annotations, Draw, geo import, scope mask, camera verbs, visual styles, bloom, cockpit clouds and contact sonar work on Navara too.
- **`src/geo`.** Cesium's vector, ellipsoid, transform, Julian date and Simon 1994 maths without the Cesium SDK. Tests compare it with Cesium bit for bit.
- **Cesium only on demand.** The production build loads `/cesium/Cesium.js` and its widget styles only when a Cesium globe starts or a Navara user turns on a feature that still uses Cesium's entity model: traffic, Street Level, the Bhote Koshi event and locator, geo import. A cold Navara start loads neither. `scripts/check-cesium-load-time.mjs` keeps modules from reading Cesium while they load.
- **Strict acceptance harness.** `scripts/qa-all-layer-switches.mjs` runs every layer and switch scenario against a keyless preview:
  - Deny-by-default network policy, with free map tiles served from a disk cache.
  - Per-engine assertion manifests.
  - A trap that fails any read of Cesium before it has loaded.
  - Context-loss, cold-chunk, soak and production-smoke runs.

The engine contract is `src/globe/contract.js`; `src/globe/testing/contractSuite.mjs` runs the same checks on every engine.

## How I verified it

Checked at 60fb8fee:

- [x] `npm run build` (keyless) and `npm run build:panel`
- [x] `npm test`: 12,772 tests, 12,766 pass, 0 failures, 6 skipped (among them the allocation budgets, which are calibrated for Node 24; this run used Node 26)
- [x] `npm run test:track`: 109 of 109
- [x] Feature gates:
  - `check:boundaries`, `format:check`, `check-cesium-load-time`, `i18n` (11 locales) and `layer-token:check` pass.
  - Engine contract suite in headless Chrome: Cesium 87 of 87, Navara 88 of 88.
  - Strict acceptance: 49 of 50 scenarios pass in one run, including `strict-navara-hd` (Navara and Navara HD at a 2x device scale) and `strict-parked-release` (a parked engine is released after its delay and rebuilds cold). `submarine-cables-engine-switch` passed its 7 assertions, but its process did not exit within the 300 s limit, so the runner counted it as failed; rerun on the same build, it passed. Every catalog layer is asserted on both engines, with 0 network violations and no paid keys. The long soak (480 switches) holds JS objects and native memory flat.
  - Run the acceptance in local daylight over the test cities. With an OSM base map Navara lights the globe by the real sun, so at night over Austin or San Francisco the frame is dark and the pixel checks fail. Earlier failures blamed on headless Chrome were this.

**Navara memory** (headless Chrome, 1280×800, Chrome process tree):

| | DPR 1 | DPR 2 |
|---|---|---|
| Navara before | 1,949 MiB | 3,015 MiB |
| Navara | 1,606 MiB | 1,764 MiB |
| Navara HD | 1,811 MiB | 2,722 MiB |
| Cesium | 929 MiB | 1,079 MiB |

- A released Navara stayed alive through three references: the Nepal boundary resolver kept the scene, the abort reason's stack kept the call chain, and postprocessing's shared fullscreen triangle kept the GL context. All three are cut.
- The canvas context no longer asks for its own antialias buffer; Navara renders into its own targets, so frames are identical.
- Cinematic clouds use two 256 px shadow cascades; Navara 0.2.1 replaced the low preset with 512 px and three.
- The tile cache is budgeted as the screen buffers plus 768 MiB instead of Navara's 2 GiB default.

**Fixed since the first version:**
- Native memory no longer grows on engine switches (was about 260 KiB per switch, now under 1). Navara 0.2.1 never frees pick batch ids, and the mover banks rebuilt their instanced meshes on each attach. A per-view pool now hands released ids back out (`src/globe/navara/movers/batchIds.js`). The long soak asserts native growth of at most 32 KiB per switch.
- Turning off drone airspace, air quality, cyclones or infrastructure zones right after a switch back to Navara sometimes left them drawn: Navara 0.2.1 can drop the first `show: false` update on a new vector layer. Polygon displays now hide by deleting their layers (`src/layers/shared/render/navaraPolygons.js`); `open-layers-switch` went from failing about one run in three to 5 of 5.
- `ground-layer-switch` no longer flakes. Navara 0.2.1 keeps feature-change events of deleted vector layers in its queue, so the view never went idle; they are now dropped each frame (`src/globe/navara/featureQueue.js`).

**Cleanup since the first version:**
- Removed the engine-migration notes and one-off QA scripts from the branch history.
- Flights and military tracking share one module (`src/layers/aircraft/tracking.js`).
- Camera verbs drive both engines through the globe contract; the Cesium viewer rig is gone.
- Cesium-only mover and line code paths are optional engine capabilities; shared helpers replace per-layer copies.
- Installation and ALPR labels on Navara read in the UI language, as on Cesium.

**Merged with `main` (up to cd7c5d5a):**
- Main's new layers work on both engines and keep their data across switches: drone airspace, OSM places, sea marks and ski pistes.
- Active Fires: the FRP filter, the confidence switch and the new colour ramp work on both engines, and the far-zoom heatmap drapes on both, with the same hand-off fade to the markers.
- Awareness range pulses and echoes draw on both engines from one pulse clock.
- The zoom-out guard runs on Cesium globes.
- Main's new modules that read Cesium while loading now build those values on first use, so a cold Navara start still loads no Cesium.
- The main-chunk baseline is raised to the merged size: `main` itself grew its main chunk by 93,873 bytes (gzip -9) since the previous merge base.

## What this changes

Cockpit entry no longer needs Contacts or both flight feeds. A civilian aircraft needs Live Flights and a military aircraft Military Flights; Contacts and every other layer can be turned on or off before or during a session, and turning off the ridden layer ends it. title: feat(cockpit): ride the selected vessel from its bridge
body:
## What this changes

With no aircraft tracked, Cockpit can ride the selected AIS vessel from its bridge. Entry needs only Live AIS Vessels and a selected vessel; double-click, `C` and the entry buttons (reading BRIDGE with a ship icon) enter it, while voice stays aircraft-only.

- The vessel layer hides the ridden ship's sprite and card, ignores scene clicks while held, and returns the camera to the vessel's map view on exit. Contact navigation and Live Signals handoffs are refused on the bridge.
- Like an aircraft ride after #1556, riding a vessel while Contacts is on adopts Live AIS Vessels as the user's own layer, so Contacts ending (its own switch, or one of its layers going off) no longer turns that layer off and ends the bridge view.

title: feat(cockpit): ride a tracked satellite in an orbital view
body:
**Stacked on #1558, so please merge that first** (merge order: #1557 → #1558 → #1559 → #1560 → #1580). GitHub also shows the earlier PRs' changes here; this PR's own changes are [satellite-classes → orbital-view](https://github.com/ZloyS/gods-eye-view/compare/denis/gev-satellite-classes...denis/gev-orbital-view).

## What this changes

With a satellite tracked and no aircraft tracked, Cockpit can ride the satellite in an orbital view. Entry needs only the Satellites layer; debris can be tracked but not entered, and voice stays aircraft-only. Double-clicking the tracked satellite or the entry buttons (reading ORBIT) enter it.

- The first commit brings back the satellite owner, operator, COSPAR and TLE-epoch helpers in `classes.js` and the UCS pack's operator and owner fields. #1558 now carries only what the class toggles read, so this groundwork lives here, where the orbital HUD first uses it.
- The camera sits on the satellite's per-frame SGP4 position and looks straight down, turned to the ground track (north-up for a satellite with none, such as GEO).
- The optical zoom steps 1×, 2×, 4× and 8× with a focus pull; the arrows tilt the view up to 45° off nadir and Home or 0 returns to nadir. Off nadir the tilt reads its total angle first and the swath readout is marked approximate.
- While in orbit the map leases flat Esri imagery (Google 3D tiles stay coarse from hundreds of kilometres up), the cockpit cloud pass stays off and the view opens in the optical style.
- The HUD names the satellite with its owner's flag (an SVG from the new `flag-icons` dependency, loaded only for the shown country) or an organisation badge, the operator, class, NORAD and COSPAR ids and TLE epoch with the element lines on request, altitude, orbital speed and the sub-satellite point.
- CURRENTLY OVER names the country and first-level division, or the sea, and from 8× the most prominent populated place nearby, looked up offline from the bundled Natural Earth packs (populated places is a new pack).
- The satellites layer hides the ridden satellite's own marks, dims the other orbit rings and ignores scene clicks and Escape while held. Exit restores the camera's field of view and the satellite's follow camera.
- `C` no longer enters or leaves Cockpit, bridge or orbit: it is left to the app-wide CCTV shortcut (README updated). Escape and the exit button leave first person.

## How I verified it

- [x] `npm run build`, `npm run i18n`, `npm run format:check` and `npm run check:boundaries` on this branch

It passes except tests that also fail on unmodified `main` on this Windows machine (disk-cache restart, 250k-row ranking budget) and three timing-sensitive tests (KML parse deadline, scene-summary typing, a CCTV live-feed idle deadline) that pass when run on their own; no file they cover is changed.

title: feat(cockpit): zoom the orbital view to the imaging sensor's swath
body:
**#1559 is merged, so this is next in the train** (merge order: #1560 → #1580).

## What this changes

An imaging satellite with a known sensor can zoom past 8×, up to 128×, as far as the view stays at least as wide as the sensor's narrowest standard swath at its live altitude. Only swaths confirmed on a cited page open those steps; the top step follows the altitude and the window's shape and steps back when it falls below the zoom shown. Every other satellite keeps 1× to 8×.

- The sensor's swath is drawn to scale along the ground track with a SENSOR SWATH readout (approximate off nadir), and a SENSOR button zooms to exactly that width when it lies in range at nadir.
- From 16×, the imagery tiles the view will need 5 to 20 s ahead along the ground track are pre-loaded at the matching level (every 2 s, at most 12 at a time).
- The mouse wheel steps the zoom one notch at a time; trackpad scrolling is summed to a step.
- The identity line shows how old the TLE is.
- The sensor figures come from a new bundled pack of 46 Earth-observation platforms (`src/data/local_data/imaging_sensors/`), each value cited to its operator's or agency's own pages, with a `DATA_SOURCES.md` entry and a data credit. Values found only on secondary sources are marked unverified and add no steps.
