title: Ignore Arabic short vowels and shadda in chat autocomplete
body:
## What this changes

Chat autocomplete now ignores Arabic short vowels and shadda when it compares the typed text with suggestions. The Arabic catalog writes some of these marks (for example "Show live flights" is «اعرض تتبّع الرحلات المباشر»), but people usually type without them. Before this change, typing «تتبع» showed no suggestion. The marks are removed from both the draft and the candidates only for the comparison, and suggestions still display the catalog text unchanged.

Only Arabic marks (U+064B–U+065F, U+0670) are folded. Marks in other scripts, such as Japanese dakuten, change the letter and still count.

Follow-up to #1545.

## How I verified it

- [x] `npm run build` (with empty keys)
- [x] `npm test`: 10456 tests, 0 failures. The new test in `src/voice/chatPreferences.test.mjs` fails without the fix.
- [x] `npm run test:track` (dev server running): 109 passed, 0 failed
- [x] Feature gate for the area I touched: none applies (chat autocomplete only)

title: feat: search aircraft by flight number from the main search bar
body:
### Problem

The main location search does not offer an obvious way to find aircraft by airline flight number. Users expect the search bar to accept a flight number even when its IATA prefix differs from the broadcast ICAO callsign.

### Proposal

Add aircraft results alongside place results, or a clearly discoverable Flights search mode.

- Accept IATA flight numbers, ICAO callsigns and airline-name-plus-number queries through a deterministic resolver shared with voice.
- Normalize case and spacing and resolve known airline aliases using a documented mapping. For a purely synthetic fixture, an airline with IATA code ZX and ICAO code ZXY would resolve "ZX123", "ZX 123", "ZXY123" and "Example Airline 123" to the same candidate.
- Prefer exact identities. Disambiguate multiple candidates, codeshares and reused flight numbers rather than silently choosing a substring match.
- Show callsign, available aircraft identity, observation time, source and coverage. Keep finding/selecting and following explicit.
- Distinguish no match from disabled layers, unavailable providers, stale data and regional coverage.
- Preserve existing place and coordinate search.

Acceptance: synthetic aliases resolve consistently across typed and spoken input; ambiguous results require selection; failed lookup never claims successful tracking.

### Data source, license, and attribution

Reuse existing aircraft feeds and their authentication, attribution and terms. No new live-data provider or paid subscription is requested. Any airline-code mapping must have a verified redistribution-compatible license and documented attribution before shipping. This concerns aircraft assets only and introduces no passenger or named-person search.

### Will you build it?

No, this is a request for someone else

title: feat: let voice find aircraft beyond already-loaded map layers
body:
### Problem

Voice should be able to look up a named aircraft even when it is absent from the browser's currently loaded layers.

The current src/tools/surfaces.js explicitly excludes find_aircraft from voice although the shared catalog implements it for MCP. track_entity searches enabled layer records without a network lookup fallback. A failed loaded-layer match therefore does not establish that an aircraft is absent from available feeds.

### Proposal

Provide a bounded voice lookup workflow using the existing catalog capability or an equivalent composed action.

1. Resolve flight-number input using deterministic normalization shared with typed search.
2. Query available aircraft feeds independently of current browser layer state and report source, observation time and coverage.
3. Answer lookup-only questions without moving the map.
4. For explicit follow requests, resolve the selected candidate by exact aircraft identifier, enable/refresh the required layer, and follow only after that target is available. Lookup success alone must not be narrated as tracking success.
5. Preserve cancellation, request limits and provider cooldowns. Distinguish ambiguity, unavailable feeds, regional coverage and stale data from genuine no-match results.

Acceptance: a stubbed provider returns an aircraft absent from loaded browser records; voice finds it; following requires exact-identity handoff; cancellation and feed failures cannot produce false success.

### Data source, license, and attribution

Reuse existing aircraft integrations and their authentication, attribution and terms. No general web browser, new paid provider or passenger-identification service is needed for the initial scope. Tool responses should retain provider provenance and freshness.

### Will you build it?

No, this is a request for someone else

title: feat: show provenance and uncertainty for aircraft route enrichment
body:
### Problem

A live aircraft position and callsign do not verify its route for a particular operating date. Callsign-based reference enrichment can retain an old route after schedules change or flight numbers are reused. Showing it as a confirmed current origin/destination can make a correctly selected aircraft appear incorrect.

The current server/providers/aircraft/enrichment.js caches callsign-keyed adsbdb enrichment for 24 hours. That route payload has no operating-date association, so a recent retrieval time does not prove the route itself is current. Client enrichment assigns the route to the aircraft and preserves it across position updates.

### Proposal

- Distinguish live observed position/identity from reference route metadata in aircraft cards and voice/tool results.
- Include route source and retrieval time. Mark undated routes as unverified reference information.
- Do not infer a verified route from callsign, heading or position alone.
- Invalidate/recheck enrichment when callsign or aircraft association changes; do not carry a previous association's route into a new one.
- If a properly licensed dated flight-status provider is configured, associate its route with operating date and available aircraft identity and handle conflicting sources explicitly.
- Keep valid live positions usable when route metadata is missing or conflicting.

Acceptance: synthetic fresh-position/outdated-route fixtures show the position normally while marking the route unverified; callsign changes cannot silently retain the previous route; voice never presents unverified enrichment as confirmed.

### Data source, license, and attribution

The initial provenance improvement reuses existing adsbdb enrichment and aircraft feeds, preserving attribution and applicable terms, with no new paid service. A future dated provider needs separate license, key, cost and attribution documentation. Related: #446 requests AeroAPI support; this request concerns honest route presentation and association regardless of provider.

### Will you build it?

No, this is a request for someone else

title: feat(layers): river levels for Germany, Taiwan, Canada and the Netherlands, with gauge level alerts
body:
## What this changes

Adds **River levels** (Weather group, share-link token `00`): official river gauges for Germany (PEGELONLINE, every federal-waterway gauge), Taiwan (Water Resources Agency), Canada (Water Survey of Canada, ECCC) and the Netherlands (Rijkswaterstaat), about 2,500 to 2,900 gauges reporting depending on the hour. The headline is **per-gauge level alerts** for people who live or work in risk zones beside a river.

### Level alerts

River floods give warning: the water rises over hours, gauge by gauge. Someone in a risk zone selects the gauge nearest to them, picks one of its official levels in the Weather panel, and is told as soon as a fresh reading reaches it. They get a page toast, a system notification if they allow it, and a "Reached" line that stays in the panel. Rising water seen early is time to move people, cars and belongings out of its way, and to heed civil protection before the road out floods.

- The levels offered are the ones that gauge publishes: watch, warning, flood and above record high; for droughts, below normal and lowest on record.
- An alert is said once per crossing and re-arms when the water turns. Late readings and gauges without references change nothing, so stale data never raises or clears an alert.
- Up to 25 alerts persist in this browser only (`localStorage`, ids validated on load). No account, nothing sent anywhere.
- Limits, stated in `DATA_SOURCES.md` and `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md`: the check runs on each 10-minute refresh while the app is open with the layer on, and it complements, never replaces, the operator's and civil protection's own warnings.

| Alert set on Koblenz: toast, card line, panel | The alert controls in the Weather panel |
| --- | --- |
| ![Alert set on the Koblenz gauge](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/IMBrandao/gods-eye-view/640dc84eac407a26ea1cf8cdf25096782217c619/river-levels/1-alert-set.png) | ![River levels readout with the alert chips](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/IMBrandao/gods-eye-view/640dc84eac407a26ea1cf8cdf25096782217c619/river-levels/2-alert-panel.png) |

### The layer

- **Colour from each gauge's own references only.** Gauge zeros are local, so 0.81 m at Bonn and 154 m at a Taiwanese hill station say nothing about each other. The band comes from what the operator publishes for that gauge (lowest on record, below normal, normal, watch, warning, flood, above record high); a gauge without references stays grey. ECCC publishes no flood stages in its open API, so a Canadian gauge with at least five years of HYDAT statistics is referenced by the means of its yearly lowest and highest daily levels (like PEGELONLINE's MNW and MHW): it reads below normal, normal or watch, never flood, and a reading on another datum than the archive gets no references. Rijkswaterstaat publishes no reference levels in its open service, so Dutch gauges stay grey, with level, trend and a 72 h plot but no alert, and their cards read metres above NAP (the national datum) instead of a local gauge zero. Drought shows as clearly as flood: today several Rhine gauges read at or near their lowest on record.
- **From afar:** a dot per gauge with a rising, falling or steady arrow. Dots keep their distance on screen (the most severe wins), grey gauges drop out above 400 km, labels thin with height, and flood and record-high gauges pulse (capped at 24).
- **Rivers on the ground:** each river is drawn in the colour of its nearest gauge on the same river, within 40 km, so a whole river reads at a glance. The lines come from the OpenStreetMap waterways in the OpenFreeMap tiles the app already reads: keyless, no Overpass. A river without a gauge of its own is not drawn.
- **Up close (below 150 km):** the 60 nearest referenced gauges get a slim glass column with the water height on the gauge's own scale and a coloured mark at each of its references.
- **Card:** level, trend, references, a 72 h sparkline, and the "local gauge zero" and "raw data, not quality controlled" caveats.
- **Server:** `/api/river-levels` merges the four networks every 10 minutes and serves the last good snapshot of a network as stale for up to 6 hours; `/api/river-levels/station/…` returns a gauge's series. WRA positions are converted from TWD97 to WGS84 on the server. ECCC is read from its GeoMet OGC API: the active real-time gauges (daily), the last 90 minutes of 5-minute levels (about 2.8 MB in two pages, which also gives most Canadian gauges a trend at once) and the yearly HYDAT extremes since 2006 (weekly), with a page cap. Rijkswaterstaat is read from its DD-API 2.0: the location catalogue (daily) and the newest water height of each non-tidal location in four parallel batches (6 s; one request for all ~560 locations takes about 25 s).

| Germany from afar | The Rhine region |
| --- | --- |
| ![Germany from afar](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/IMBrandao/gods-eye-view/640dc84eac407a26ea1cf8cdf25096782217c619/river-levels/3-germany-far.png) | ![Rhine, Mosel, Main and Lahn coloured by their gauges](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/IMBrandao/gods-eye-view/640dc84eac407a26ea1cf8cdf25096782217c619/river-levels/4-rhine-region.png) |

| Taiwan | Columns at Koblenz |
| --- | --- |
| ![Taiwan gauges and rivers](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/IMBrandao/gods-eye-view/640dc84eac407a26ea1cf8cdf25096782217c619/river-levels/5-taiwan.png) | ![Gauge columns with reference marks at Koblenz](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/IMBrandao/gods-eye-view/640dc84eac407a26ea1cf8cdf25096782217c619/river-levels/6-columns-koblenz.png) |

| Canada | The Netherlands |
| --- | --- |
| ![Canadian gauges coloured by their mean yearly low and high](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/IMBrandao/gods-eye-view/2b55bab65a7e78d3a5fd64516a17057f9b07fbd1/river-levels/four-canada.png) | ![Dutch gauges, grey: Rijkswaterstaat publishes no reference levels](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/IMBrandao/gods-eye-view/2b55bab65a7e78d3a5fd64516a17057f9b07fbd1/river-levels/four-netherlands.png) |

## How I verified it

- [x] `npm run build`
- [x] Unit tests: on this Windows machine `npm test` now stops before running with `ENAMETOOLONG` (the test file list passed on one command line is too long), so I ran the same plan from `scripts/run-unit-tests.mjs` in four batches: 11,172 pass, 1 fail: the `nominatimOutlineRoute` disk-cache test, which fails the same way on unchanged `main` on Windows.
- [ ] `npm run test:track`: not run; on this Windows machine it fails the same way on unchanged `main`.
- [x] Feature gate: none applies. Also ran `npm run check:boundaries`, `npm run i18n` (all 11 locales complete) and `npm run format:check`, plus headless runs of the app: far view, Rhine region, Taiwan, Koblenz columns, Canada from afar and the Ottawa valley, the Netherlands up close, and selecting a gauge and setting an alert (toast, card line, panel lines, stored alert).

## New layer checklist

**Screenshots**

Above.

**Recording**

To follow in a comment.

**Proposed category**

Category: Weather, next to Air quality (it is a Weather-panel readout like it).

**Data source and licence**

- Source (provider and endpoint):
  - PEGELONLINE, German Federal Waterways and Shipping Administration (WSV), REST API v2: `https://www.pegelonline.wsv.de/webservices/rest-api/v2/stations.json` and `…/stations/<uuid>/W/measurements.json` for a selected gauge's series.
  - Water Resources Agency, MOEA (Taiwan), open data API v2: `https://opendata.wra.gov.tw/api/v2/…` (station register, daily, and real-time stage).
  - Rijkswaterstaat (Netherlands), DD-API 2.0 WaterWebservices: `https://ddapi20-waterwebservices.rijkswaterstaat.nl/…` (`OphalenCatalogus`, `OphalenLaatsteWaarnemingen`, `OphalenWaarnemingen`).
  - Environment and Climate Change Canada, MSC GeoMet OGC API: `https://api.weather.gc.ca/collections/hydrometric-stations`, `…/hydrometric-realtime` and `…/hydrometric-annual-statistics` (Water Survey of Canada).
  - River lines: OpenStreetMap waterways in the OpenFreeMap vector tiles the app already uses.
- Licence or terms (link):
  - PEGELONLINE: [Datenlizenz Deutschland – Zero – 2.0](https://www.govdata.de/dl-de/zero-2-0), no conditions.
  - WRA: [Open Government Data License, version 1.0](https://data.gov.tw/license), attribution required.
  - Rijkswaterstaat: **no named open licence found.** The [Verantwoording page of rijkswaterstaatdata.nl](https://rijkswaterstaatdata.nl/vaste-onderdelen/verantwoording/), under "Bronvermelding", allows reuse on two conditions: name the site as the source, and state the date the information was taken. The app names it in the credit with a link, and each card shows when its reading was taken. The Netherlands is in its own commit (`feat(river-levels): add the Netherlands' Rijkswaterstaat gauges`), so it can be dropped alone if this is not enough for the project.

    ![Rijkswaterstaat's reuse conditions (Bronvermelding)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/IMBrandao/gods-eye-view/2b55bab65a7e78d3a5fd64516a17057f9b07fbd1/river-levels/rws-bronvermelding.png)
  - ECCC: [Data Servers End-use Licence](https://eccc-msc.github.io/open-data/licence/readme_en/), attribution required (already listed in `DATA_SOURCES.md` for air quality).
  - OpenStreetMap: ODbL, via OpenFreeMap, already credited in the app.
- Attribution shown in the app: "PEGELONLINE, Wasserstraßen- und Schifffahrtsverwaltung des Bundes (WSV)" (courtesy); "Water level data: Water Resources Agency, Ministry of Economic Affairs (Taiwan), Open Government Data License v1.0"; "Water Survey of Canada, Environment and Climate Change Canada: contains information licensed under the ECCC Data Servers End-use Licence"; "Netherlands: Rijkswaterstaat, rijkswaterstaatdata.nl, taken live every 10 minutes; each card shows when its reading was taken"; "river lines: OpenStreetMap contributors via OpenFreeMap".
- Needs a key? None.
- Fetched at runtime, or bundled in the repo: fetched at runtime.

- [x] Added a row to `DATA_SOURCES.md`
- [x] Credit is registered in `src/data/dataCredits.js`
- [x] Share-link token assigned with `npm run layer-token:next`, if the layer is shareable

## Docs

- [x] `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md` updated and a `changelog.d/<pr-number>-<slug>.md` fragment added, or this PR doesn't change runtime behaviour

Follow-ups, each its own PR: more keyless networks with official references, Brazil's SGB/SACE gauges, and satellite virtual stations for the regions without public gauges.

title: feat: Brazilian scheduled-flight routes and on-time record from ANAC's flight data (VRA)
body:
### Problem

Route enrichment comes from adsbdb's callsign lookup (`server/providers/aircraft/enrichment.js`, `api.adsbdb.com/v0/callsign/…`). For Brazilian domestic flights it often returns nothing, so a tracked LATAM, Azul or GOL flight shows no origin or destination. When it does return a route, the card cannot say where that route came from or how often it is right, which is what #1564 asks for.

Brazil's civil aviation agency (ANAC) publishes every scheduled flight operated in the country, month by month, as open data: the **Voo Regular Ativo (VRA)** dataset. It records the planned and actual departure and arrival of each flight, plus whether it was flown or cancelled.

### Proposal

First version, server side only, no new layer:

- Download the latest monthly VRA file at most once a day (it changes once a month), keep five columns (airline ICAO, flight number, origin ICAO, destination ICAO, scheduled and actual departure), and build an index `airline + flight number → routes seen, with counts`.
- When adsbdb returns no route for a callsign whose prefix is a Brazilian operator in VRA (`TAM`, `AZU`, `GLO`, …), answer with the dominant VRA route for that flight number. When adsbdb does return a route, keep it.
- Show it with its provenance on the card, for example: "GRU → BSB · usual route in ANAC's September 2026 record (28 of 30 flights) · 81% left within 15 min". It is labelled as the usual route, not today's flight plan.
- Airport names for Brazilian ICAO codes can come from ANAC's aerodrome registry (see the aerodromes issue); foreign codes stay as codes.

**Numbers (September 2026 file, "Atualizado em: 2026-10-28").** 85,845 flights in 12 MB of CSV. LATAM Brasil (`TAM`) 25,916, Azul (`AZU`) 24,115, GOL (`GLO`) 22,459. 82,545 flown, 3,300 cancelled. Of 3,974 distinct LATAM/Azul/GOL flight numbers, 3,684 flew a single route all month and 3,715 flew one route at least 80% of the time, so a flight number predicts its route well. Of the 80,045 flown flights with both times, 20.6% left more than 15 minutes late. 8,169 rows are international (one end outside Brazil).

**Privacy.** The file has no personal data: no passenger, crew or aircraft registration columns.

**Out of scope for the first version:** live flight plans, a delay dashboard, and history beyond the latest month.

**Open points to check while building:**
- That live ADS-B callsigns match VRA flight numbers for each airline (e.g. `TAM3456` ↔ `TAM` + `3456`). The PR would include a test fixture from real callsigns.
- Where it belongs: as a fallback inside the existing route lookup, or as its own provider beside `server/providers/aircraft/anacRab.js` (#1554).

Related: #1564 (route provenance and uncertainty), #1562 (search by flight number).

### Data source, license, and attribution

- Source: ANAC, Voo Regular Ativo (VRA), `https://sistemas.anac.gov.br/dadosabertos/Voos e operações aéreas/Voo Regular Ativo (VRA)/<year>/<month>/VRA_<year><month>.csv` (also `.json`), monthly since at least 2021.
- Key: none.
- License: the dataset folder states none. It is published under ANAC's open-data plan, like the RAB in #1483. I can ask ANAC to confirm the reuse terms if needed before anything ships.
- Attribution: "ANAC, Voo Regular Ativo (VRA)".

### Will you build it?

Yes, I plan to open a PR

title: feat: Brazilian aerodromes layer from ANAC's official registry
body:
### Problem

The app has no airport or aerodrome layer. In Brazil much of the low and slow general-aviation traffic flies to and from private airstrips (farms, agriculture, mining), especially in Mato Grosso, Mato Grosso do Sul and Pará. On the map these aircraft seem to start and stop in empty fields, and nothing names the strip they use. Even the main public airports have no label.

ANAC publishes the official list of every registered civil aerodrome, public and private, as open data, with coordinates and runway details.

### Proposal

An off-by-default layer, drawn as small ground markers:

- Download both lists at most once a day and keep only these fields: ICAO code, name, municipality, state, latitude/longitude, elevation, day and night operation (VFR / IFR category), and for private strips the runway designation, length, width and surface.
- Public aerodromes and private strips use two marker styles; interdicted public aerodromes (`Situação = Interditado`) are drawn greyed out.
- Selecting one shows a card such as "SBRB · Plácido de Castro · Rio Branco/AC · 193 m · VFR / IFR CAT I day and night" or "SJ3D · Fazenda Sinimbu · Jaborandi/BA · runway 10/28, 1,500 × 22 m asphalt · VFR day".
- The tracked-aircraft card can name the nearest registered aerodrome when an aircraft is on the ground or below a set height near one.

**Numbers (files read 2026-11-04).**
- Public: 496 aerodromes ("Atualizado em: 2026-11-01"), all with ICAO code and coordinates; 466 registered, 30 interdicted; 67 with IFR operation. Largest states: São Paulo 72, Minas Gerais 67, Rio Grande do Sul 48.
- Private: 3,939 strips ("Atualizado em: 2026-11-04"), all with coordinates, 3,900 with a code. Mato Grosso 995, Mato Grosso do Sul 649, Pará 297, Bahia 292. Main surfaces: dirt 1,245, gravel 1,129, asphalt 705, grass 588. 132 allow night operation.
- About 100 KB and 900 KB of CSV, so the whole layer is a small static snapshot.

**Privacy.** No owner or operator column is used. The registration-ordinance columns (`Portaria de Registro`, `Link Portaria`) are dropped because the linked PDFs can name owners. Private strip names are published by ANAC as they are registered; 2,759 of 3,939 are named after a farm, ranch or similar ("Fazenda …"), and some of those may include a person's name. If you prefer, private strips can show only their code, municipality and runway, without the name.

**Out of scope for the first version:** runways drawn to scale, frequencies, charts, and aerodromes outside Brazil.

### Questions for you

- Would you rather have a Brazil-only layer, or a worldwide airport layer from a global source with ANAC as the authoritative Brazilian part?
- Share-link token, default style and where the layer sits in the menu: your call.

### Data source, license, and attribution

- Public: `https://sistemas.anac.gov.br/dadosabertos/Aerodromos/Aeródromos Públicos/Lista de aeródromos públicos/AerodromosPublicos.csv`
- Private: `https://sistemas.anac.gov.br/dadosabertos/Aerodromos/Aeródromos Privados/Lista de aeródromos privados/Aerodromos Privados/AerodromosPrivados.csv`
- Both are Latin-1 CSV with `;` separators and a first line "Atualizado em: <date>".
- Key: none.
- License: the dataset pages state none. They are published under ANAC's open-data plan, like the RAB in #1483. I can ask ANAC to confirm the reuse terms if needed before anything ships.

title: feat: current airport weather (METAR) for the tracked flight's origin and destination
body:
### Problem

When you follow a flight there is no way to see the weather at its departure or arrival airport. Weather is often what explains a holding pattern, a go-around, a diversion or a long taxi delay. The app has no METAR, TAF or aviation weather anywhere today.

### Proposal

First version, on the tracked-aircraft card only:

- When the route enrichment gives an origin and destination ICAO code, fetch the latest METAR for both through a small keyless server proxy (for example `/api/metar?ids=SBGR,SBBR`).
- Decode it into plain words and keep the raw report one click away, for example: "GRU now: thunderstorm with rain · visibility 2 km · broken clouds at 1,100 ft · wind 250° 10 kt · reported 01:40Z".
- Use the flight category the API already returns (VFR, MVFR, IFR, LIFR) as a small coloured badge.
- Proxy rules: allow only 4-letter ICAO codes, at most a few per request; cache each station for 10 minutes and serve the stale value if the API fails; say "no recent report" when the API returns 204 (no data).
- Translations follow the existing i18n files (`src/i18n/locales/`).

**Numbers (checked 2026-11-04, Brazil night time).** Asking for all 496 public Brazilian aerodromes returned a METAR in the last 3 hours for 69 of them, including the major airports. For example, `SBGR` (São Paulo/Guarulhos) returned a SPECI with heavy thunderstorm and rain, and `SBBR` (Brasília) returned CAVOK. Small aerodromes often have no weather station, so "no report" is a normal answer. The JSON already holds decoded fields (temperature, dew point, wind, visibility, cloud layers, flight category) as well as the raw text.

**Out of scope for the first version:** TAF forecasts, SIGMETs, weather for every airport on the map, and a weather layer.

### Questions for you

- Card only, or also in a future airport layer?
- Is a short line in the card enough, or should it be its own section?

### Data source, license, and attribution

- Source: NOAA / National Weather Service, Aviation Weather Center Data API, `https://aviationweather.gov/api/data/metar?ids=<ICAO>&format=json` (documentation: https://aviationweather.gov/data/api/). Formats: raw, JSON, GeoJSON, CSV, XML, IWXXM.
- Key: none; requests worked without one. Responses carry `Cache-Control: max-age=60`.
- License: US federal government data. I will confirm the usage policy and any rate limits on the API page before opening the PR.
- Attribution: "NOAA / NWS Aviation Weather Center".
- Coverage is worldwide, so this helps every flight, not only Brazilian ones.

### Will you build it?

Yes, I plan to open a PR

title: fix(perimeters): show a 0.25-acre fire as 0.25 ac, not 0 ac

## Summary
The Fire Perimeters incident card rounds the WFIGS `attr_IncidentSize` to whole acres, so every incident under half an acre reads `0 ac`. title: fix(places): don't let the browser cache a refused Google answer
body:
## What this changes

`/api/google/nearby-places`, `/api/google/text-search`, `/api/google/geocode` and `/api/google/reverse-geocode` set `Cache-Control: private, max-age=300` on every upstream reply, including refusals:

- Places: a 403 (key not authorized for the Places API, API not enabled) or a 429 is relayed with its status and `max-age=300`.
- Geocoding: Google reports a denied key or spent quota as **HTTP 200** with `status: "REQUEST_DENIED"` / `"OVER_QUERY_LIMIT"`, which the proxy relays as a cacheable 200.

The browser callers use plain `fetch` (`src/search/defaults.js`, `src/tools/places.js`, `src/layers/installations/source.js`), so a repeated lookup of the same address or the same nearby point is answered from the browser cache with the old refusal for five minutes after the user fixes the key or enables the API. The keyless, rate-limit and bad-request paths in the same file already send `no-store`.

Now a Places reply is cacheable only when `response.ok`, and a geocode reply only when it is ok and its status is `OK` or `ZERO_RESULTS`; everything else is `no-store`. Successful answers keep `private, max-age=300`, and the existing assertion for that still passes. `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md` records the rule next to the other Google route notes.

## How I verified it

- [ ] `npm run build`
- [x] `npm test`: ran the affected file, `node --test src/tooling/placeProviders.test.mjs` → 15/15 pass. I didn't run the full suite or the build.
- [ ] `npm run test:track` (dev server running)
- [x] Feature gate for the area I touched: none applies (server headers only)

New test: `a refused Places or Geocoding answer is not kept by the browser` in `src/tooling/placeProviders.test.mjs`. It covers a 403 on both Places routes, `REQUEST_DENIED` and `OVER_QUERY_LIMIT` on geocode (expects `no-store`), and `OK` / `ZERO_RESULTS` (still `private, max-age=300`). Mutation checks:
- reverting the whole `google.js` change makes it fail;
- reverting only the geocode condition back to `response.ok` makes it fail on `REQUEST_DENIED`.

Prettier check on both changed files passes.

title: feat(firms): keyless South American fires from INPE Programa Queimadas
body:
## What this changes

Closes #1482. Without a `FIRMS_MAP_KEY`, Active Fires is no longer empty: `/api/firms` answers with the near-real-time detections that Brazil's INPE (Programa Queimadas) publishes every 10 minutes for South America, keyless, instead of `503 no_key`. The CSVs come from `https://dataserver-coids.inpe.br/queimadas/queimadas/focos/csv/10min/` and carry VIIRS 375 m (NOAA-20, NOAA-21), MODIS (Aqua, Terra), GOES-19 and a few other sensors. With a key, nothing changes: FIRMS is still the source.

- `server/providers/inpeQueimadas.js` lists the folder, downloads each 10-minute file once, keeps it while it is inside a 30-hour lookback and clamps rows to the trailing 24 h by pass time (GMT). Same single-flight and serve-stale rules as FIRMS. `FIRMS_INPE_ENABLED=0` restores the keyless `503 no_key`.
- `src/data/inpeQueimadasCsv.js` parses the CSV into the FIRMS row shape (satellite and sensor names mapped to the codes the layer already knows).
- INPE publishes **no FRP and no confidence**, so those stay `null`, never `0`: cards read `FIRE` instead of a megawatt figure and skip the confidence, cells skip their maximum, and markers use the middle `flame` stop of the new FRP ramp (unknown heat, not weakest). With the confidence switch or the FRP slider above zero, INPE detections are hidden, since they cannot be shown to pass.
- The layer row credits `INPE Programa Queimadas · SOUTH AMERICA`, the attribution lightbox carries INPE's citation, and `get_active_fires` reports `source`, `coverage` and a South-America-only note.

### How it relates to other open PRs

- **#1552 (drop Suomi NPP, same author):** this branch already merges `fix/firms-drop-snpp`, so `server/providers/firms.js` requests no SNPP here either and the two merge cleanly in either order. If #1552 lands first, its commits simply drop out of this diff.
- **#497 (keyless NOAA GOES ABI, @beneduzi):** complementary rather than duplicate. GOES covers the whole Americas every 10 minutes at ~2 km; INPE adds the finer VIIRS 375 m and MODIS 1 km passes, but only for South America. The code paths are separate (new provider files on both sides), but they meet in two places:
  - Textually, both add `layerState._provider` in `src/layers/firms/ingestion.js` / `state.js` and touch `queries.js`, `dataCredits.js` and `DATA_SOURCES.md`; small conflicts, easy to resolve.
  - Behaviourally, #497 falls back to `/api/goes-fires` only when `/api/firms` answers `503 no_key`. With INPE on, a keyless `/api/firms` answers 200, so GOES would not be reached unless `FIRMS_INPE_ENABLED=0`. Whichever lands second, I am happy to adapt it, for example INPE for South America plus GOES for the rest of the Americas.

## How I verified it

- [x] `npm run build`
- [x] `npm test`: 10 458 pass; the 1 failure is a Windows-only one that also fails on unchanged main on this machine (`nominatimOutlineRoute` disk cache)
- [ ] `npm run test:track` (fails on unchanged main on this machine, so not a useful signal here)
- [x] `node scripts/format.mjs --check`, `npm run check:boundaries`, `npm run i18n`
- [x] Live: with no key, `/api/firms` returned about 29 300 INPE detections for the last 24 h (`provider: 'inpe'`, `coverage: 'south-america'`)

Brazil and its neighbours with no FIRMS key:

![Active fires over South America from INPE, no key](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/IMBrandao/gods-eye-view/pr-assets/inpe-fires/inpe-fires-brazil.jpg)

The layer row credits INPE and shows the new intensity controls:

![Layer row crediting INPE Programa Queimadas](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/IMBrandao/gods-eye-view/pr-assets/inpe-fires/inpe-fires-layer-row.jpg)

## Data source and licence

- Source: INPE Programa Queimadas, 10-minute CSVs at `dataserver-coids.inpe.br/queimadas/queimadas/focos/csv/10min/`
- Terms: the Programa Queimadas FAQ says all data are free to access (FAQ 5) and asks for an ABNT citation (FAQ 36); INPE is a federal body and Decree 8.777/2016 grants reuse of open-format data. Details in `DATA_SOURCES.md`.
- Attribution shown in the app: "INPE Programa Queimadas" in the attribution lightbox and in the layer row while it is the source
- Needs a key? none
- Fetched at runtime, nothing bundled

title: feat(transit): give vehicle icons a readable front, and none without a course
body:
## Why

At the ~20 px the fleet renders at, the bus, tram, metro and unknown transit glyphs were near-symmetric boxes. They rotate along the vehicle's course, but nothing showed which end was the front, so you could not tell which way a bus was going.

## What

- **A front built into the outline** (`src/data/transitIcons.js`): an arrow-like nose for the bus, a pointed cab for the tram, a chamfered cab for the metro, a plain nose for `unknown`. Rail and ferry already had one. Because the front is part of the outline rather than interior ink, it survives the mode tint, the halo and the sensor profiles (mono/thermal/retro), which keep only the outline, at both 48 px and the 96 px selected raster.
- **No implied heading without a course**: a vehicle with no finite `courseDeg` sits at rotation 0, where a pointed glyph would claim it is heading north. Those vehicles, fleet and selected alike, now get a symmetric outline (rail and ferry included) and switch to the pointed one when a course arrives (`syncHeadingIcon` in `src/layers/transit/rendering.js`).
- **Bounded cache**: `transitIcon(kind, px, { heading })` adds the flag to the cache key, so the raster cache is a fixed 72 variants (was 36). The `qa-transit` bound is updated to match.

## Before / after

Rendered by the module itself at the on-screen fleet size (~20 px), tinted with the mode colours and rotated as on the map, then enlarged 6x with nearest-neighbour so the pixels are what a viewer actually gets. Bottom row: the neutral outline used while a vehicle has no course.

![Transit icons before and after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/IMBrandao/gods-eye-view/c013bc3b171d0a779cecb39b6a2882b56709f661/transit-icon-heading/before-after-icons.png)

Live, Boston (MBTA), buses rotated along their streets:

![Boston buses with the new icons](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/IMBrandao/gods-eye-view/c013bc3b171d0a779cecb39b6a2882b56709f661/transit-icon-heading/boston-live.jpg)

## Tests

- New test: at 20 px, each pointed glyph is measurably asymmetric with the narrow end toward -Y, and each neutral glyph is symmetric end to end.
- The existing halo, mono-mask and cache-bound tests now cover both variants.
- `src/data` and `src/layers/transit`: 3082 passing.
- Checked live in Boston (MBTA): buses with a course show their nose along the street; those without one show the neutral outline.

title: feat: 🎅 optional seasonal Easter eggs — winter sleigh and New Year fireworks
body:
### Problem

The 🛸 TR-3B conversion is a lovely touch, and it got me wondering whether the project would welcome a couple of small, seasonal Easter eggs in the same spirit. Before writing any code I'd like to ask whether this fits the project at all — a "no thanks" is completely fine.

Since the app is translated into 11 languages and used worldwide, I've tried to keep both ideas optional, cultural rather than religious, short-lived, and easy to ignore.

### Proposal

**1. Winter sleigh (25 Nov – 25 Dec)**

- During this window, a small 🎅 chip appears next to the existing 🛸 chip in CONTEXT ▸ CONTACTS when a contact is tracked.
- Pressing it turns the tracked aircraft into a sleigh pulled by reindeer; pressing it again restores the real aircraft — exactly like the TR-3B conversion (session-only, nothing persisted, callsign/altitude/speed stay live-feed truth).
- Original art only, drawn in the same 96×96 nose-up sprite pipeline as the TR-3B. No religious symbols, and nothing borrowed from any existing "Santa tracker" (name, look or branding).
- Outside the window the chip is not rendered and nothing is loaded.

**2. New Year fireworks (31 Dec and 1 Jan)**

- On those two days, a short, lightweight fireworks overlay plays once when a session starts, then gets out of the way.
- Dismissable with a click or Esc, never blocks the globe, and does not repeat in the same session.
- Skipped entirely when `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` is set, and in clean-UI / recording mode.

**Shared rules for both**

- Dates come from the viewer's local clock, so each person sees it on their own calendar.
- Zero runtime cost outside the date window (the code can be lazy-loaded only when the date matches).
- One kill switch per egg, similar to `SPLIT_FLAP_ENABLED`, so they can be turned off in one line.
- Happy to drop either one, change the dates, or make them off by default — whatever suits the project.

Would seasonal Easter eggs like these be welcome? If yes, I'd be glad to build them, one small PR each, starting with whichever you prefer.

### Data source, license, and attribution

None — pure UI. All artwork would be original and contributed under the project's license.

### Will you build it?

Yes, I plan to open a PR

title: Say why Transit and Bike Share rows are empty outside coverage
body: ## Problem Over a city that no Transit feed or Bike Share system covers (London, Tokyo, most of the world), both Layers rows read `ON · — · GTFS-RT · never` and `ON · — · GBFS · never`. That looks the same as a feed that never answered, so there is no way to tell "nothing here" from "broken". - **Transit** already worked out the reason (`No feed here yet · 16 regions available`, or `Fly below 2,850 km…` above its gate). It put the text only in `stats.coverage`, which the voice analyst reads but the Layers row does not. The row shows guidance only from `statusMessage`, so it fell through to `{source} · never`. - **Bike Share** reported nothing out of range: `{ count: 0, lastUpdate: null }`. - After flying from a covered city to an uncovered one, `lastUpdate` stayed behind, so a row could read "26s ago" over an empty map. ## Fix - `transit/queries.js`: the out-of-coverage `zoom-in` branch also sets `statusMessage` (the same English note as `coverage`). Above the gate it names the altitude the closed gate opens at, 2,850 km (the enter threshold), as Bike Share does. - `bikeshare/controls.js`: when the layer is on, nothing is loading, no city is in range and none has failed, `getStats()` reports `status: 'zoom-in'` with: - `Fly below 48 km to a covered city` above the altitude gate, or - `No bike share here yet · N systems available` below it. A loading city keeps `syncing N city feeds...`, and a failed one keeps `GBFS fetch error`. - `transit/viewport.js`, `bikeshare/viewport.js`: leaving every feed or system clears `lastUpdate`. When the camera changes coverage (altitude gate, feeds or cities in range, stations loaded), the layer asks the Layers panel to repaint at once instead of waiting for the next 15 s / 60 s tick. Bike Share gets `attachDataManager` for this, like Transit. - `ui/statusText.js`: new `translateStatusMessage()`. It tries the catalog entry, then whole-line coverage notes (their ` · ` is part of one sentence, so they can't be split into pieces), then the piece-by-piece status line. The Layers row's guidance branch and the voice card's empty-note path both use it now. The two Transit patterns move here from `voice/resultDisplay.js` instead of being duplicated. - New strings in all 11 locales: `Fly below {km} km to a covered city` and `No bike share here yet · {n} systems available` (plural). - `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md` describes the new row states. The chip stays `ON`: a guidance status is normal operation, not a fault (`layerFeedState` treats it that way already). "Fly to the nearest covered city" is out of scope here. ## Before / after (headless, keyless dev server, camera over London) At 8 km: | Before | After | | --- | --- | | | | At 2,000 km (above Bike Share's gate, below Transit's): ## Tests - `src/layers/bikeshare/coverageStatus.test.mjs` (new): - The gate prompt and the no-system prompt. - No prompt with a city in range, while loading, with a failed city, or when disabled. - `lastUpdate` is cleared when leaving range, at low and at high altitude. - `src/layers/transit/lifecycle.test.mjs`: Boston → London → 10,000 km reads the coverage prompt with `lastUpdate: null`. - `src/ui/statusText.test.mjs`: English shows as it came, including the singular form. In es / ru / ja the notes translate whole with their numbers kept, and other status messages still translate as before. - `src/layers/transit/gatePrompt.test.mjs` (new): at 2,900 km over Boston the gate stays closed and the prompt says `Fly below 2,850 km`. - `src/layers/promptRepaint.test.mjs` (new): London → Boston (Bike Share) and Boston → London (Transit) ask the panel to repaint. - `src/ui/layerPanel.test.mjs`: both rows read ` · ` with the chip `ON` and the count empty, and are translated in ru. ## Checks - `npm run doctor -- --json`: ready - `npm run format:check`, `npm run check:boundaries`, `npm run i18n` (all 11 locales complete), `npm run changelog:check`: pass - `npm test`: 10,473 pass, 0 fail - `GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY= CESIUM_ION_TOKEN= npm run build`: pass ## How to verify 1. `GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY= CESIUM_ION_TOKEN= npm run dev` 2. Fly to London below 48 km and turn on Transit and Bike Share. The rows read `GTFS-RT · No feed here yet · 16 regions available` and `GBFS · No bike share here yet · 61 systems available`. 3. Zoom out past 50 km. Bike Share reads `Fly below 48 km to a covered city`; past 3,150 km Transit reads `Fly below 2,850 km to a covered region`. 4. Fly to Boston. Both rows show counts and an update time again. 5. Switch the language to Russian or Spanish. The prompts are translated.

title: Hide a vessel's detection callout while its own card paints
body: ## Problem With **Vessels** and **Detection** on, a vessel that has an ambient card on the map also gets its detection callout next to its bracket. The callout lane paints beneath the cards, so the callout text shows through the card's plate and covers the speed and course (`PASSENGER · 5.0KT · 141°` under `QA SHIP 04 5 kn`). Hiding the callout for every vessel whose card the layer *publishes* was tried during #602 and reverted before merge: the shared overlay paints only part of the published cards (shared budget, collisions, UI chrome), so vessels whose card was dropped were left with no text at all. `getOverlayPaintRect` can't answer "is this vessel's card on screen" here either: the detection lane paints first in `paintFrame`, before any card publishes its paint rect for the frame, so inside the lane it always returns `null`. ## Fix - `worldOverlay` exports `getQueuedOverlayEntryAlpha(sourceId, entryId)`: the opacity an entry paints with this frame, or 0 when it is not queued. It reads the paint queue the overlay solves before painting, so it is current while custom lanes paint. The opacity combines source, temporal, distance, altitude and keyhole fades. - Vessel detection objects name their card: `cardSourceId` is the vessel overlay source and `cardEntryId` comes from `vesselOverlayEntryId`, the same id the card is published under. - Each frame the callout lane fades a callout by its own card's opacity: hidden once the card paints at 0.5 or more, fading in below that. A vessel whose card was dropped by the budget, lost a collision, or faded out at the keyhole rim keeps its callout. Callouts that paint at ~0 are left out of `calloutRects` in the detection diagnostics, and the rest report the alpha they paint with. - The index behind the getter adds no allocation on the paint path. Its rows carry a frame stamp, stale rows are pruned every 600 painted frames, and destroy clears it. Trade-offs, kept simple on purpose: - The opacity leaves out only the Cyber sonar fade, which never drops a card below half opacity. An entry hidden by the yield-collision pass reads 0. - The callout fades at paint time. Its slot in the detection label budget is not handed to another contact. ## Before / after Same scene (40 synthetic vessels over San Francisco, 3.2 km, top-down, Detection Dense at 100 %). | Before | After | | --- | --- | | | | ## Tests - `worldOverlay.test.mjs`: a detection lane sees which cards this frame will paint before they publish paint rects. The queued-card index stays bounded while card identities churn. A lane reads zero for a yielding entry the declutter pass hid this frame. - `detectionHost.test.mjs`: - a vessel whose card loses the collision keeps its callout; - the callout fades out while its card fades in, instead of vanishing at once; - the callout stays readable when its card is faded out at the keyhole rim; - the callout stays hidden while its card fades out after leaving the published cohort. - `aisLiveVessels.test.mjs`: vessel detection objects name the card their callout gives way to. ## How to verify 1. Start the app with empty keys: `GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY= CESIUM_ION_TOKEN= npm run dev`. 2. Turn on Vessels and Detection (Dense) over a busy port, or inject vessels through the dev-only `__focusEvidence.setVessels` seam on the `ais-live-vessels` layer. 3. A vessel with a card shows no callout under it. A vessel without a card still has its callout. Headless check I ran: synthetic vessels injected through the dev seam, measured from a paint lane registered above the cards in the same overlay frame. These numbers come from the first version, which hid the callout outright. title: Roll back a Space Missions entry whose mission index fails to load
body: ## What this changes Entering Space Missions when `/api/launches` fails (HTTP 429, timeout, network error or a malformed payload) no longer leaves the workspace in an isolating mode with no missions. **Problem.** The launches layer caught every fetch error inside `update()` and resolved normally, so the data manager treated the failed first load as a successful start. Context then committed `space-missions`: the layers it had cleared stayed off, unrelated enables were refused with "Space Missions isolates replay data. Exit the mode to enable Wind.", the camera stayed at the full-globe view, and the roster read `LOADING 30-DAY MISSION INDEX` indefinitely while the layer reported the error. **Fix.** - Until the first mission index loads, `update()` rethrows the failure (`src/layers/launches/ingestion.js`). The manager already fails an enable closed when its first update throws, and both entry routes (the Data Layers toggle and the Context panel) already roll that back to the pre-entry layers. They now get the failure they need. - A refresh failure after an index has loaded stays non-fatal: records, mode and the error in the layer stats are kept as before. A valid empty index (`results: []`) is still a successful entry. - The camera pose is captured when the layer enables and restored if the layer is turned off before any index loaded, so a failed entry no longer leaves the globe zoomed out (`src/layers/launches/lifecycle.js`). Leaving a mode that did load keeps today's camera behaviour. - The roster shows `30-DAY MISSION INDEX UNAVAILABLE` after a failed first load, and goes back to loading on the next attempt (`src/layers/launches/panel.js`). The new string is translated in every locale. - `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md` documents the entry contract. ## How I verified it - [x] `GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY= CESIUM_ION_TOKEN= npm run build` - [x] `npm test` — 10,460 passed, 0 failed (1 skipped) - [x] `npm run test:track` against a keyless dev server — 109 passed, 0 failed - [x] Feature gate: none covers Space Missions entry; checked headless instead (below) - [x] `npm run format:check`, `npm run check:boundaries`, `npm run i18n`, `npm run changelog:check`, `npm run doctor -- --json` New regression test `src/layers/launches/failedEntry.test.mjs` runs the real `DataLayerManager`, the Context coordinator and the launches ingestion, lifecycle and panel against a local `/api/launches` that answers 429. Before the fix the first three cases fail (`setEnabled` resolves `true` and the mode is entered): - direct entry with 429 resolves `false`, restores the previous layers, does not enter the mode, restores the camera, and an unrelated layer can be enabled afterwards; - Context-panel entry with 429 reports `ok: false` and restores the previous layers; - the roster reports the failed index, then loads on the next attempt; - a valid empty index enters the mode; - a refresh failure after a loaded index keeps the mode and its records. Headless check against a keyless dev server with `/api/launches` intercepted as 429: enable Earthquakes, enable Space Missions, then enable Wind. | | Before | After | |---|---|---| | `setEnabled('rocket-launches')` | `true` | `false` | | Enabled layers after | rocket-launches, satellites | earthquakes, wind | | Context mode | `space-missions` | none | | Camera altitude | 1 km → 21,946 km | 1 km → 1 km | | Roster | `LOADING 30-DAY MISSION INDEX` | `30-DAY MISSION INDEX UNAVAILABLE` | | Wind enable | refused | enabled | Same steps on both builds: Earthquakes on, then Space Missions with the feed returning 429. **Before:** the mode hangs on loading and the camera stays zoomed out. **After:** the entry rolls back to the starting view.

title: Show a recoverable notice when the globe stops drawing
body: ## Problem When the globe stops drawing, the app gives no way back. Cesium stops its render loop after any render error and shows its own "An error occurred while rendering. Rendering has stopped." panel, whose only button dismisses it. A lost WebGL context leaves a page that never draws again. Either way the user is left with a frozen or black globe while the panels, rail and dock keep responding, so it looks like the map is loading or broken in an unexplained way. The only handler in the codebase is the inline conversation panel's (`src/app/globePanelRuntime.js`, `src/app/embed.js`); the main app has none. ## Fix A render failure notice in the scene chrome, built the way the UI guide asks: a framework-free owner publishes to the status store, and a Vue view renders it. - `installRenderFailureNotice()` (`src/ui/renderFailure.js`) listens for Cesium's `scene.renderError` and the canvas' `webglcontextlost`. It logs the error and publishes `{reason, detail, retry, reset}` to the status store (`src/ui/stores/status.js`). - `RenderFailure.vue` renders it as an `alertdialog` with a title, an explanation, the error message and the actions, and moves focus to the first action when it appears. - **Retry** (after a render error) restarts the render loop. The notice stays until a frame starts and ends without a render error: Cesium raises `postRender` after a failed frame too, so a loop that fails again keeps the notice instead of flashing it away. - **Reload** (after a lost context) reloads the page. Cesium cannot draw into a context it has lost, and the address keeps the view. - **Reset view** opens the app's root address (`appRootUrl()`), without the hash or `/share/` path the view was restored from. The query, such as `?lang=`, is kept. - An inline conversation panel never reloads or navigates its host's page. It offers Retry after a render error only, and nothing after a lost context, where the panel runtime's own notice applies. - The application scene creates its viewer with `showRenderLoopErrors: false`, so Cesium's dead-end panel no longer covers the notice. `applicationViewerOptions()` and `createApplicationViewer()` take the option and keep Cesium's panel by default for other callers. New UI strings are translated in every catalog. `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md` describes the behavior. ## Since the first version - Retry keeps the layers' frame listeners. A listener that throws no longer leaves its frame event half-raised: the event is finished as soon as the error surfaces, so a layer turned off and on while the notice is up still updates after Retry. - Retry never starts a second render loop, including a Retry pressed before the next frame and a tab hidden and shown during a failed frame. - Errors thrown out of `render()` or `resize()` show the notice too, including frames drawn by the inline panel's timer, and they no longer reach the host page. - After a successful Retry, focus goes back to where it was before the notice, or to the globe canvas if that element is gone, so Enter still finishes a shape in the draw tool. - The notice sits above the Québec CCTV panel, and its buttons are 44 px tall on touch screens. ## Relation to open work - #1095 recovers from a lost WebGL context: it `preventDefault()`s the event, stops the loop and reloads once with a cooldown. This PR does not overlap with that recovery. It does not `preventDefault()` the context loss or restore the context, it only reports it, and its notice covers every render error, not just context loss. If #1095 lands, its automatic reload runs first; the notice only shows while the page is still on screen, and its Reload button stays a manual fallback once #1095's cooldown stops reloading. - #905 (render error from `maximumTextureSize`) and #1067 (render error on a zero-size drawing buffer) are root causes this PR does not fix. With it, those failures show a notice with Retry and Reset instead of a stopped globe. ## Tests - `src/ui/renderFailure.test.mjs`, 9 tests. A render error shows the notice and survives its own failed frame. Retry restarts the loop, and only a clean frame clears the notice and its per-frame listeners. A loop restarted into the same error keeps one notice, and a new failure after recovery counts as a new appearance. Reset opens the app root without the share path or hash but keeps the query. A lost context offers Reload and no frame clears it. A page that must not reload offers neither Reload nor Reset. Uninstall removes everything. - `src/ui/renderFailureView.test.mjs`, 2 tests. The scene chrome renders the `alertdialog` with its labelled title, description, detail and actions, focuses Retry, and calls the published actions. A lost context shows Reload, and a panel that cannot reload shows no actions. ## How I verified The numbers below are from the first version. Later commits were checked the same way: `npm test`, the notice's own tests, and headless runs with empty keys. A stateful reload (layers, a scene, the cockpit, a coordinate search, then reloading the state URL in the same tab) did not leave a stopped or black globe on `main`: 0 of 30 headless runs. - `npm test`: 10,466 passed, 0 failed, 1 skipped (an existing Node 24-only allocation benchmark). - `npm run doctor -- --json`, `npm run format:check`, `npm run check:boundaries`, `npm run i18n` (all catalogs complete), `npm run changelog:check`, and `npm run build` with empty map keys: all pass. - A headless Chrome run (puppeteer, SwiftShader) against `npm run dev` with empty map keys, opened on a restored view (`#lat=48.8584&lon=2.2945&alt=1500`): 1. The globe draws and no notice shows. 2. A primitive whose `update()` throws stops Cesium's loop. The notice appears focused on Retry, Cesium's panel does not, and no frames draw. 3. Retry while the primitive is still there keeps the notice. 4. After removing the primitive, Retry clears the notice and frames draw again. 5. Reset view navigates to `/` without the hash, and the app starts and draws. 6. `WEBGL_lose_context.loseContext()` shows the notice with Reload, and Reload brings the globe back. There were no unexpected console errors. The notice also fits a 375 px phone viewport in Russian. To try it: open the app, then run in the console: ```js const { viewer } = window.__godsEyeView; viewer.scene.primitives.add({ update() { throw new Error('test'); }, isDestroyed: () => false, destroy() {} }); viewer.scene.requestRender(); ``` ## Screenshot After an injected render error, on a restored view (1440×900, headless Chrome):

title: feat(cockpit): keep the orbital camera on a ground target
body:
**#1560 is merged, so this is the last PR in the train.**

## What this changes

In the orbital view the camera can be held on a mapped site as the satellite passes over it, and the briefing's Live Signals page lists what is around the satellite. Before this, that page showed only TRACK ACQUIRED in orbit.

- **Ground focus.** A click on a Mapped Installations marker, or on a site's Live Signals row, turns the view onto the site and keeps it centred as the satellite moves. The readout gives the single off-nadir angle to it (`OFF-NADIR 23.4°`) and names it (`FOCUS · <site>`). A click elsewhere, the site's row again, NADIR, Home, `0` or an arrow ends it, and the view eases back. It also ends by itself when the site leaves the 45° reach or drops below the horizon, or when the layer is turned off. Turns ease over about 0.75 s and cut under reduced motion. A double-click on a site no longer hands the camera to Cesium's tracking.
- **Live Signals in orbit** (five rows, rebuilt once a second, rows keep their places while they still qualify):
  - TRACK ACQUIRED for the ridden satellite.
  - The nearest sites in reach, with class and off-nadir angle. A row focuses its site, and the focused site's row releases it. With Mapped Installations off, a SITES STANDBY row says why no site is listed.
  - A RETURN row to the satellite ridden before.
  - The nearest shown satellites (debris left out), with bearing and distance. A row rides that satellite without leaving orbit; the camera hops to it over 1.2 s, keeping the zoom.
- **Layer additions:** Mapped Installations gains `getById` and `findByPick`, and the satellites layer gains a bounded `getNearestPositions`.

On phones (760 px and narrower) the briefing is hidden, as it already is for aircraft, so a site can be focused only by tapping its marker.

## How I verified it

The disk-cache restart test also fails on unmodified `main` on this Windows machine. The KML parse deadline and the scene-summary typing test pass when run on their own. No file they cover is changed.

Three independent reviews per language (Codex gpt-6-astra, Fable, Opus). Then one fix pass per language accepted or rejected each finding against that language's guide. Every fix that at least two reviews agreed on is applied.

title: feat(display): switch displayed units between metric and imperial
body:
## What this changes

Display gains a **Units** switch (Metric | Imperial) that chooses how measurements are shown. The page starts in metric; the choice is kept per browser (`gev:units:v1`).

It is display only. Layer data, stored values, tool data fields and `annotate_map` labels stay SI, and share links do not carry the choice. title: feat(layers): add shipwrecks layer (EMODnet + Wikidata)
body:
## What this changes

Adds a **Shipwrecks** layer: about 8,000 wrecks worldwide, each with a placemark and a report card. It follows the air-accidents layer:
- markers grow with the death toll;
- the period picker is the same one, with first and last year;
- the card puts deaths first.

Each card shows the name, vessel type, date sunk, cause, depth, position quality, casualties (counts only), notes and a source link.

Nothing in the repo covered wrecks before. The closest item is #1158, which shows NOAA chart symbols with no cards.

- Markers keep a boat symbol in an era-coloured circle: before 1900, 1900–1945, after 1945, or undated. The eras double as the legend in the panel row.
- A same-origin proxy, `/api/shipwrecks`, fetches both sources. It refreshes daily, and if a source is down it serves the last snapshot for up to 7 days.
- Wikidata ships and their "sinking" event items are folded into one record, so for example Titanic shows once, with its death toll. Dates keep their precision: a month-only date is not shown as day 1.
- Free text that names people is dropped. No personal data is ingested.
- EMODnet rows taken from wrecksite.eu are skipped, because that source is copyrighted.

title: feat(layers): add an Air accidents layer (CENIPA + NTSB + Wikidata)
body:
## What this changes

Adds an **Air accidents** layer in the Events group. It shows Brazilian civil aviation accidents and serious incidents since 2007 from CENIPA open data, US accidents and incidents since 2008 from the NTSB, and notable accidents worldwide from Wikidata. That is about 30,700 markers in total. Each marker is a coloured disc with an aircraft glyph, styled like the shipwrecks markers in #1583 so the two layers read as one family when both are on. Marker size grows with the death toll. Clicking a marker opens a card with the toll, the time and place, flight and route, aircraft, operation, flight phase, damage, what happened, the investigation status and a link to the article, ASN record or CENIPA reports.

The layer row has kind chips (Accident / Serious incident) and a period filter with **From** and **To** year pickers on one line. That period filter is a new generic `range` row control (`RowRange.vue`, `_pickRangeEnd` in `layerPanel.js`) that any layer can use.

`/api/air-accidents` is a Vite middleware proxy. It downloads the three CENIPA CSV tables and runs the Wikidata query at most once a day. For the NTSB, it downloads the full `avall.zip` database once (97 MB, about 565 MB unpacked), reads it with `mdb-reader` (MIT, new dependency) into `.gev-cache/air-accidents/ntsb.json` (gitignored), and then applies only the weekly `upDDMMM.zip` update files (about 1 MB each). The first NTSB build runs in the background, so CENIPA and Wikidata markers show right away and US markers appear on the next refresh. The response leaves out empty fields and is capped at 48 MiB. When a Wikidata item matches a CENIPA accident (same day, within about 50 km), the two are merged into one record.

**No personal data.** Only technical columns are kept: date, place, aircraft type and registration, phase, operation, damage, toll, ICAO category, investigation status and report number. The card never shows names of crew, passengers or owners. From the NTSB database only whitelisted columns of the events and aircraft tables are read; owner, operator-person, address and flight-crew data are never read, and the operator name is kept only for airline (Part 121) flights.

## How I verified it

Two fail only on Windows (nominatim's "disk cache survives a restart" checks Unix file permissions; `mcpPanelKey` concurrent repair). The other two (the CCTV idle deadline and the KML root deadline) pass when their files run alone. On Windows the runner now hits the command-line length limit (`ENAMETOOLONG`), so I ran the same file list in batches.

title: fix(geocode): preserve non-Latin names in keyless search
body:
## What this changes

Keyless search compared place names after stripping everything outside ASCII letters and digits, so a query like `Москва` folded to an empty string. With an empty target, the exact-name guard refused every Cyrillic match, the search retried without the proximity bias, and it could land on the wrong namesake: searching `Москва` near the Tajik village took you to Moscow, Russia.

I switched that comparison to the existing `foldPlaceName()` helper, which keeps non-Latin scripts and still folds Latin accents the same way. The nearby exact match is accepted now.

## How I verified it

The new case fails on `main` with the Russian result and passes with the fix; it runs on a Photon fixture, with no live calls. It also covers Greek, Arabic, CJK, mixed-script names and the existing Latin accent cases.

title: fix(aircraft): disclose undated routes and reject stale callsign enrichment (#1564)
body:
## Summary

Fixes a real failure mode from #1564: undated **adsbdb** route enrichment could be presented as a confirmed operating-day origin/destination, and delayed asynchronous enrichment could attach a previous callsign's route to the current aircraft.

### Integrated behavior changes
- On a nonblank **callsign change**, clear the previous cached route and airline association while preserving the existing sticky-callsign behavior for transient missing fields.
- Bind route fetch completion to **both ICAO24 and the callsign requested**, discarding results after a callsign switch or aircraft eviction. Scope route deduplication by ICAO24 + callsign.
- Include `source: adsbdb`, the server-side cached retrieval timestamp, `operatingDate: null` and `verification: unverified-reference` in successful route API results.
- In the actual tracked-flight readout and voice context, explicitly label any displayed route **unverified reference** rather than a confirmed current flight.
- In `get_aircraft_info`, use unverified reference language and include source/time/verification in the response; the same annotation is included in the flight descriptor.
- Add regression coverage for callsign switches, transient missing callsigns, delayed responses and MCP route wording.

### Limits and non-goals
A retrieved-at time **does not verify the operating date**. Existing route-plausibility filtering is retained but is only a geographic heuristic, not independent evidence. This PR intentionally does not introduce a new provider, speculate about the current route, modify live position fixes or alter tracking behavior. A dated licensed status provider, conflicting-source reconciliation and broader presentation changes remain separate work under #1564.

### Validation
The new tests target `src/layers/flights/enrichment.route.test.mjs`, `src/layers/flights/records.test.mjs`, and `src/tools/queries/aviation.test.mjs`. GitHub CI results on this PR are authoritative; tests are not claimed green until the checks finish.

Closes no open upstream issue automatically; request maintainer review of the limited route-provenance step first.

title: fix(cctv): restrict Street View fallback to catalog cameras and cap requests (#20)
body:
## Fixes #20 — bound paid CCTV Street View fallback

Updated in response to [radianx's reproducible review](https://github.com/bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view/pull/1588#issuecomment-6671472589). This targets the **actual upstream project**; the head branch lives in `dvilrgamerz/gods-eye-view`.

### Security invariant

- Paid Google Street View requests require a catalog-registered camera with finite WGS84 coordinates. All client-supplied location and orientation overrides are ignored.
- Camera pose is normalized from the server catalog. Unknown camera IDs, invalid coordinates, cross-site/forwarded requests and missing API keys degrade to the existing synthetic SVG at **zero Google cost**.
- The registered upstream camera snapshot is always tried **before** cooldown, paid-admission or the synthetic fallback. Live media/HLS handlers remain unchanged.
- Google Street View responses are limited to the existing `CCTV_FRAME_MAX_BODY_BYTES` (16 MiB), time out, reject redirects and require a supported raster media type.

### Shared quota and duplicate handling

The new `processStreetViewAdmission()` singleton is shared by **all CCTV plugin instances in one Node.js process**, correcting the former per-plugin-instance 12/min counter.

| Policy | Default | Environment override |
|---|---:|---|
| Per-client window (socket peer; IPv6 /64) | 16 new attempts/min | `GEV_CCTV_STREETVIEW_PER_CLIENT_PER_MIN` |
| Across one Node.js process | 32 new attempts/min | `GEV_CCTV_STREETVIEW_GLOBAL_PER_MIN` |
| Rolling 24-hour process budget | 512 new attempts | `GEV_CCTV_STREETVIEW_DAILY_MAX` |
| Distinct in-flight Street View requests | 8 | internal bound |
| Cooldown after successful request | none (each new attempt is metered) | internal policy |
| Cooldown after failed request | 120s per camera/pose | internal policy |

An explicit `0` for any quota **disables paid fallback**, not the safety limiter. Invalid values retain the default. A request is charged before the outbound call, including if Google fails; no rejected request spends the key.

Simultaneous requests for the **same canonical camera/pose** share one in-flight Google request. Other cameras have their own cooldown state. These maps and client buckets are bounded; completed images are **not cached** (see [Google's Street View Static API caching policy](https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/streetview/policies)). After Google failure, refreshes in the 120-second cooldown get a synthetic card. Successful frames may be requested again within the independent quota limits; they are never reused from a completed-image cache.

### Verification

- Unit coverage: catalog-only target, invalid and empty coordinates, pose bounds, independent per-client/global/day windows, operator-config fail-closed, simultaneous request coalescing, success/failure cooldown, process singleton.
- Route coverage: unknown-camera refusal, client coordinate/heading override refusal, a burst of 15 registered still cameras, forwarded-request refusal, synthetic cooldown and original response-path compatibility.
- All Google fetches in tests are mocked. No paid Google API key or real billing calls are needed.
- Full GitHub Actions checks must pass for the **latest head** before treating the PR as merge-ready.

### Important limits and coordination

- The 16/32/512 values are **process-local safety defaults, not enforceable spending or billing caps**. Restart, horizontal replicas, key sharing with Places/geocoding, and deployment topology change total exposure. Operators should enforce upstream API restrictions, quotas and billing alerts. IPv4 clients behind one NAT share a per-client window.
- A low-spend no-cache policy means a camera may display synthetic images during its failure cooldown or after quotas run out. Serving the same Google image repeatedly without another paid call would need a separately verified provider-permitted reuse strategy.
- PR #666 independently fixes #20 with a different shared Google limiter and image cache. **Do not merge both implementations unreviewed**; their `cctv.js` changes conflict. PR #1163 has historical integration conflicts outside this narrow route. Maintainers should select or consolidate policy intentionally, preserving the upstream-first behavior and no unverified image-cache permission.

title: feat(search): focus loaded flights by exact ICAO callsign (partial #1562)
body:
## Purpose — bounded first slice of #1562

Make the **existing location search bar** useful for an exact broadcast aircraft callsign, using **only the civil-flight layer's already loaded public observations**. This does not claim to complete all of #1562.

### Changes
- Parse `UAL123`, `UAL 123`, `flight UAL123`, `callsign UAL123` and explicit `icao24: a1b2c3` without sending exact flight-shaped strings to a place geocoder.
- Search **every loaded civil-flight record** (not the first 500 roster rows), require an exact callsign/ICAO24 identity, and distinguish missing, disabled, unloaded, or stale data.
- Reject ambiguous exact callsigns and six-hex tokens rather than selecting the first candidate.
- For one fresh match, fly to its last observed position, **without starting continuous tracking**. Place/coordinate search remains unchanged and cancellation authority is checked just before flying.
- Add tests for parsing, exact matching, duplicate identities, stale/disabled feeds, and camera-handoff cancellation.
- Update `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md` with scope and limitations.

### Explicit limits
- **No IATA-to-ICAO or airline-name alias table.** Issue #1562 requires a documented, redistribution-compatible code source; this PR does not introduce unlicensed guesses.
- No new global lookup endpoint. A no-match does not establish that the flight does not exist outside currently loaded coverage.
- No codeshare resolution, candidate picker, continuous tracking, additional server requests or new third-party provider.
- This is a **functional integrated subset** of #1562, not a standalone unused utility.

### Verification
Unit test and CI results should be taken from GitHub checks on this PR head. `npm run test:track` and other browser-level coverage have **not** been independently verified yet.

Refs #1562.

title: feat(ai): add Claude (Anthropic) as a chat-only AI Provider
body:
## What this changes

Adds **Claude** as a third **AI Provider** next to OpenAI and Gemini, through the typed-chat registry that landed after #375 was closed — one entry in each registry, as invited there ("a small PR adding your provider to its registry is very welcome").

- **Server:** `server/providers/anthropic/chat.js` — `createAnthropicChatHandler` on `createTextChatHandler`, mounted at `/api/anthropic/chat` (Anthropic Messages API). History is validated strictly: `text` / `tool_use` / `tool_result` blocks only, roles alternating from the user, every `tool_use` batch answered by the next user message with matching ids in order, nothing pending at the end.
- **Client:** `textProtocols.anthropic` and `createAnthropicSession` — the first **chat-only** provider. Claude has no realtime voice, so with Claude selected the mic button becomes **Open chat** and a voice start reports an error without requesting the microphone.
- **Shared touch points (two):** `parseUsage` gains an `anthropic` branch (`input_tokens` excludes cache reads/writes and no total is reported, so both are summed); an upstream `529 overloaded_error` is answered as `503`. OpenAI and Gemini paths are unchanged.
- **Keys / env:** `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_CHAT_MODEL` (default `claude-haiku-5-5`), `GEV_RATELIMIT_ANTHROPIC_PER_MIN`, `GEV_RATELIMIT_ANTHROPIC_CHAT_PER_MIN` — in Provider Settings, `.env.example`, `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md`, `README.md`, `SECURITY.md`. All eleven locale catalogs translated.

### Design notes

- `thinking: { type: "disabled" }` is sent: Claude Haiku 5.5 thinks by default and chat history carries only text and tool blocks. Trade-off: models that refuse that setting (Opus 5.5, Fable 5.1) fail with a 400 if set as `ANTHROPIC_CHAT_MODEL` — documented in CURRENT-STATE. Happy to switch to opaque thinking-block pass-through (like Gemini's `thoughtSignature`) if you prefer.
- Reply blocks are rebuilt from allowed keys only (the API adds `citations` to text blocks, which the strict history check would reject next turn); empty text blocks are dropped.
- Only `stop_reason: end_turn` finishes a turn; `pause_turn`, `refusal`, `model_context_window_exceeded` surface as an interrupted reply.

title: fix: coordinate layer token reservations for five pending contributions
body:
## Problem and proposed allocation

#1316, #1565, #1583 and #1584 currently propose token `9` for four different layers. #1143 still proposes `6`, already published for Sea Marks. Merely choosing different higher tokens on independent branches fails the existing contiguous-allocation checker while earlier slots remain free.

Reserve a single contiguous batch first, without adding any runtime registry entries:

| PR | Layer ID | Token |
| --- | --- | --- |
| #1316 | local-usgs-water | `9` |
| #1316 | local-usgs-lakes | `00` |
| #1316 | local-usgs-springs | `01` |
| #1143 | caba-traffic-enforcement | `02` |
| #1565 | river-levels | `03` |
| #1583 | shipwrecks | `04` |
| #1584 | air-accidents | `05` |

All **35 published reservations remain identical**. USGS retains all three current provisional tokens. CABA and the three competing single-layer PRs change one assignment each: the minimum four changes for these conflicts. The next allocation becomes `06`.

This is a coordination proposal requiring maintainer acceptance, not a claim that other authors have agreed. If accepted, land this batch first and retain its complete ledger in each feature PR. Their subsequent order is unrestricted. If main publishes another assignment first, that mapping takes precedence and this proposal must be refreshed. Pre-reservations become permanent even if a feature is withdrawn; the explicit cost is seven namespace slots.

## Compatibility and adoption

No decoder, registry, allocator rule, tool schema or layer feature changes. Active registry remains **35**, application catalog **37**, reservations become **42**. An inactive reserved token still rejects an enabled-layer payload. With only these feature PRs added later, the registry would become 42 and catalog 44; intermediate counts must reflect actual features, not reservations.

Published main share links retain every mapping, including Sea Marks `6`. Branch previews already assign the same v2 tokens to different meanings, so they cannot all remain compatible: regenerate CABA `6` links and IMBrandao `9` previews. USGS `9/00/01` previews retain their mappings. No ambiguous aliases or version change.

The coordination document lists each author's registry/test/documentation updates, count rules, and validation commands. CONTRIBUTING explains existing reservations versus active registry entries. Boundary/race fixtures retain the earlier published ledger independently of the new production pin.

## Validation

Base main: `2470b39f88c6566ff82fc1c1e9d05757df3546e8`.
Exact tested/published tree: `831aa2c76d69f1c48134181473d43972dbf8550d`.

- Official token checker: **35 published, 7 new**, passed against the base above.
- Full format check (1,757 files), import/package boundaries, production build and git diff whitespace check passed. Build retains the existing large-chunk advisory.
- Full unit suite, browser/tracking gates and live source checks were not run for this ledger-only change.
