title: feat(news): News layer with keyless GDELT conflicts and local news
body: ## What this changes Adds the **News** layer (Events ▸ News) and its right-rail **NEWS** panel, and Cockpit Regional News is held to the last 24 hours. - **Panel:** the last 24 hours, narrowed to 12, 6, 3 or 1 hours; a severity floor and a category filter; picture cards and clips; each card links to its publisher and says which service it came through ("via GDELT Project"). Markers are coloured by severity only. A card flies the globe to its report. - **Two sections.** **Conflicts** lists the hotspots' news. **Local**, below 3,000 km, lists the news of the area at the view centre, newest first, names it ("News from Jordan") and outlines it on the globe. A disputed area from the bundled Natural Earth list (11) or a territory without a country code is named as itself and read from no country's outlets. - **Where the news comes from.** Set `GEV_NEWS_ORIGIN` to a news server and the local server forwards the layer's three read routes (`/api/news/hotspots`, `/feed`, `/outline`) there. Unset, Core answers them itself, with no model involved: - **Conflicts, no key:** the last 24 hours of GDELT 2.0 event exports, physical violence only (CAMEO 18–20), one report per story at GDELT's place for it (a town the article names beats a bare country), titled from GDELT's GKG files for the newest 3 hours. GDELT's actor coding is never shown. title: Traffic: name an account's traffic limit instead of a daily budget
body:
When live traffic flow fails, the panel guessed the reason from the status code alone: every 429 read "TomTom daily budget reached" and every 503 "TomTom key unavailable". A hosted deployment that limits traffic per account sends a different reason, so its users saw a daily budget that does not exist, or a missing key when only the usage service was down.

A failed flow tile now carries the server's reason (`code`, or the local proxy's `error`), and the label uses it:

| Server reason | Label |
|---|---|
| `USAGE_LIMIT_REACHED` | Monthly traffic allowance used |
| `RATE_LIMITED` | Traffic rate limit reached |
| 503 with another reason | Traffic service unavailable |
| `no_key`, or no reason (503) | TomTom key unavailable (unchanged) |
| `budget`, or no reason (429) | TomTom daily budget reached (unchanged) |

The local proxy's behaviour and labels are unchanged. The three new labels are translated in all 11 catalogs (`npm run i18n` reports every catalog complete).

Tests: `src/data/traffic.test.mjs` (labels by reason) and `src/layers/traffic/source.test.mjs` (a failed tile carries the reason). Full suite: 10,981 pass, 0 fail.

title: CCTV: record each camera source's terms as data, not only as a free-text string
body:
### What exists today

Every camera source in `server/providers/cctv/sources.js` carries a `license` string, and
`DATA_SOURCES.md` has one prose row per provider. The strings range from a named licence
(`Fintraffic / digitraffic.fi (CC BY 4.0)`, `Contains information licensed under the Open Government Licence – City of Calgary`)
to a description of availability (`Public TxDOT traffic camera data`,
`Public DelDOT traffic camera`, `Public City of Tallinn traffic camera data`).

Several providers are already handled case by case in code and docs, because their terms
are narrower than "public":

| Provider | Terms as documented in `DATA_SOURCES.md` | Handling |
| --- | --- | --- |
| FL511 | individual personal use only; anything else needs written consent | off by default, `CCTV_FLORIDA_ENABLED=1` |
| Houston TranStar | disclaimer prohibits copying, distribution and external framing without written permission | off by default |
| NYC DOT TMC | data-sharing agreement required for the feed | off by default |
| Via Lietuva / Eismoinfo | camera endpoints not covered by the open-data statement | off by default, `CCTV_LITHUANIA_ENABLED=1` |
| DelDOT | "Public availability is not a blanket redistribution license" | on, with a note |

### The gap

The distinction that matters to a deployer is whether the operator may redistribute the
frames, and that distinction lives only in prose. In code it is one of three things: the
free-text `license` string, an env flag on some providers, or nothing. So:

1. A new source can be added with `license: 'Public … camera data'` and no one is asked
   whether that text grants any right to redistribute frames.
2. Nothing can answer "which sources in this build need attribution, which need
   permission, which are personal-use only, and which have unverified terms?" without
   reading every row.
3. The camera card and the Data attribution popover cannot show a different notice for
   a source whose terms are unverified than for one under an open licence.
4. `DATA_SOURCES.md` and the code can disagree, and no check notices.

### Proposal

Add a small, closed descriptor next to `license`, and keep `license` as the human-readable
text:

```js
terms: {
  basis: 'open-licence' | 'public-notice' | 'agreement-required' |
         'personal-use-only' | 'unverified',
  licenceId: 'CC-BY-4.0' | 'OGL-Ontario' | 'NLOD-2.0' | … | null, // SPDX id or null
  termsUrl: 'https://…',            // the page the claim was read from
  attributionRequired: true | false,
  verifiedOn: '2026-11-06',         // date the page was last read
  redistribution: 'permitted' | 'permission-required' | 'not-stated',
}
```

Then:

- a test that every registered camera source has a `terms` object with a valid `basis`,
  a `termsUrl` and a `verifiedOn` date;
- a rule that a source whose `redistribution` is not `permitted` ships off by default
  and cannot be on without an explicit operator setting (today this is per-provider
  convention);
- the Data attribution popover and camera card read `attributionRequired` and `basis`
  instead of re-parsing the `license` string;
- `DATA_SOURCES.md`'s camera rows checked against the descriptors (or generated from
  them), so the two cannot drift.

Existing sources would be filled in from what `DATA_SOURCES.md` already says. Where a
provider's terms have not been read, `basis: 'unverified'`, which is honest and visible
rather than a silent "Public …".

### Contributor-facing rule

Extend the "Add a CCTV source pack" paragraph in `CONTRIBUTING.md`, which today asks for
coordinates, attribution and registered frame URLs: the PR also links the page that states
the terms and records `terms` for the source. No adapter for a new region
merges with `basis: 'unverified'` enabled by default.

### Not proposed

- No change to which sources are on or off today.
- No change to how frames are fetched or proxied.
- No legal claim about any provider; the descriptor records what the linked page says
  and when it was read.

### Open questions

1. Is a closed `basis` list the right granularity, or should this be only
   `attributionRequired` plus `redistribution`?
2. Should `verifiedOn` older than some age (a year?) show as a warning in
   `npm run doctor` or in CI?
3. Is `server/providers/cctv/sources.js` the right home, or should the descriptors live in
   a data file the docs build can also read?

I can open a PR for the descriptor, the test and backfilling the existing rows if the
shape sounds right. I would keep that PR to the schema and the existing sources, with no
new adapters.

title: fix(alpr): treat empty extract tiles (HTTP 404) as empty, not unavailable
body:
## What this changes

Mapped ALPR Cameras showed `UNAVAILABLE · Vector tiles unavailable (HTTP 404)` over Portland, OR and other views north of latitude 41. The extract server at `tiles.dontgetflocked.com` answers HTTP 404 (`Tile not found`) for any tile that holds no cameras. `createVectorTileSource` treated every non-OK response as an error, and `fetchBounds` throws when every tile in a batch fails. For views with `north >= 41` the ALPR source also queries the Canada extract, whose TileJSON bounds reach down to 42.33°N; over Portland all 16 of its tiles are empty, all 404, and that throw took the whole layer down. Austin, LA and SF sit below 41°, so the Canada source is skipped there and the bug never showed.

This adds an opt-in `emptyStatuses` option to `createVectorTileSource`: a tile response with a listed status is treated as an empty tile (decoded from zero bytes, cached under the same TTL, counted as loaded, `partial` stays false). `createAlprTileSource` passes `emptyStatuses: [404]` to both country sources. `traffic/flowSource.js` and `openFreeMap.js` do not pass the option, so their behaviour is unchanged.

Reproduction (same Portland box, `south 45.45, west -122.75, north 45.6, east -122.55`, against the live tile server): `main` throws `Vector tiles unavailable (HTTP 404)`; this branch returns 126 camera records. Verified tile responses: `cameras-us-hourly/12/652/1466.mvt` → 404 while its five neighbours → 200 `application/x-protobuf`.

## How I verified it

- [x] `npm run build` — `✓ built in 33.35s`
- [x] `npm test` — `tests 10988 / pass 10985 / fail 0` (three new tests)
- [x] `npm run test:track` (dev server running) — `RESULT: 107 passed, 2 failed, 0 skipped` on an idle machine. The two failures are flight-tracking checks this change does not touch: `arrival: moveEnd + first reveal both re-aim before idle refresh` (observation 862 ms vs the 500 ms threshold) and `display-floor: a retained-but-hidden tracked model does NOT suppress the floor`. An earlier run under heavy concurrent load gave 99/10 with frame-sampling timeouts. A baseline run of the same harness on the pre-fix commit is in progress; I will post its result in a comment.
- [x] Feature gate: `node scripts/qa-alpr-journey.mjs <url>` ran the full journey against a server bound to 127.0.0.1. Cameras resolved at every stop (neighbourhood 36, pan-east 33, pan-north 28, zoom-out-3km 103, downtown-6km 202, city-30km 957). It reported FAIL on one render-truth check (`3 cameras on screen but no markers rendered` on a 600 m pan) plus `401 (Unauthorized)` console noise. The same gate on the pre-fix commit (same keys, same machine) also reported exactly one render-truth failure at a different stop (`zoom-out-3km: 10 cameras on screen but no markers rendered`) and the same 401 noise, so both look pre-existing; the pre-fix run additionally showed `Coverage limited — zoom in` at downtown-6km, which this fix removes (empty 404 tiles no longer count as partial). Two other attempts of the gate (one per commit) crashed inside the harness recorder with `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'frames')` before the ALPR passes.

Also green: `npm run format:check` (`Checked 1841 source files.`), `npm run check:boundaries`, `npm run layer-token:check -- --base-ref main` (`36 published, 0 new`).

Tests added: `vectorTiles.test.mjs` covers all-tiles-404 with the option (no throw, `partial` false, body cancelled once per tile, `onTile` fires, repeat read hits cache) and without it (still rejects with `Vector tiles unavailable (HTTP 404)`); `alpr/source.test.mjs` covers the Portland box where the US source serves records and the Canada source 404s every tile.

## Docs

- [x] `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md` note and `changelog.d/1597-alpr-empty-tiles.md` fragment (commit 534fe746); `npm run changelog:check` exit 0.

title: fix(cctv): Street View fallback serves catalog cameras only, inside the Google budget
body:
## What this changes

Found in the launch QA pass, rated P2 for security (Google key cost).

- Before this change, the CCTV Street View fallback on `/api/cctv/frame/{id}` built its Google Street View Static request from the `lat`/`lon`/`heading`/`fov`/`pitch` query values for any camera id, including ids not in the catalog, with no rate limit. Any client could use the deployment's Google key as a free Street View image service for a place of its choosing.
- The fallback now answers only for cameras the server lists, always at their catalog position. Coordinates in the query are ignored, and the browser no longer sends them.
- Heading, field of view and pitch still come from the request, the view the browser draws, clamped as before (FOV 20–120°, pitch −40–20°), and fall back to the catalog pose when absent. Position calibration does not reach the fallback.
- A camera the server does not list, such as a bundled seed camera the browser shows when the server catalog is empty, gets the placeholder.
- Each client IP (an IPv6 /64 counts as one client) has its own Street View window on `GEV_RATELIMIT_GOOGLE_PER_MIN` (default 120, `0` disables it), separate from the Places and Geocoding window. Over it, a frame gets the placeholder instead of a `429`. Keyless, forwarded and unknown-id requests spend nothing, and the client is identified before the camera fetch, so a client that drops the connection still pays from its own window.
- `scripts/package-boundaries.json` lists the two shared rate-limit modules inside the `cctv-provider` boundary.

**Steps to reproduce before this change:** with `GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY` set, request `/api/cctv/frame/not-a-camera?lat=48.8584&lon=2.2945&heading=90` from the same site. Expected: the placeholder and no Google call. Actual: a Street View image of that spot, billed to the key, with no limit.

## How it was verified

- `src/data/cctvMediaFeedType.test.mjs`: an unknown id makes no Google call; a catalog camera is framed at its catalog position with the requested heading, FOV and pitch; the per-client budget holds, an IPv6 /64 shares one window, and keyless, forwarded and unknown-id requests spend none of it.
- `src/data/cctvStreetViewDisconnect.test.mjs`: on real sockets, a client that disconnects while the camera fetch is pending stays inside its own budget.
- `src/layers/cctv/source.test.mjs`: frame URLs carry no `lat`/`lon`.

title: Add the Data Library: live regional datasets, tiles and packs
body: ## What this changes Adds the **Data Library**: a second tier of data layers so regional and niche sources stop competing for a place in DATA LAYERS and for the nearly full layer-token ledger. **Browse data library** at the foot of the panel opens a dialog of live entries. Each entry is one JSON manifest in `src/library/entries/` with its licence, coverage and what this instance needs to serve it. **Add** puts the entry under a new Library heading in DATA LAYERS. The authoring guide is `docs/DATA-LIBRARY.md`. - **Nothing is bundled.** Every entry is fetched from its provider (query API, provider-hosted file or tile endpoint), so a self-hosted instance serves the library without hosting data. Sources without CORS go through one allowlisted `/api/library` route. - **Three kinds:** `dataset` (GeoJSON, GeoJSON Lines, CSV, JSON records, paged ArcGIS FeatureServer, partitioned GeoParquet on S3), `tiles` (XYZ, WMS/ArcGIS export via `{bbox-epsg-3857}`, terrarium relief) and `pack` (an operator opt-in for an existing host layer). - **96 entries**, including NASA EONET, Black Marble, Smithsonian volcanoes, NWS alerts, GDACS, EPA Superfund/TRI, FEMA USA Structures and NBI bridges (loaded only for the view once zoomed in), Addresscloud EPC ratings (A–G with live legend counts), 57 aerial layers from the Open Imagery Register, 9 Kartverket maps and Mapterhorn shaded relief. - **Aerial imagery** stays above every other drape, is clipped to its coverage outline, and providers' blank fill no longer whitens the globe. - **Rows:** library rows get Zoom to layer and Remove icon buttons that work while the layer is off. The dialog has stat tiles, search, a theme filter, Zoom, and a two-step Remove all. - **Persistence:** selections are stored locally and travel in share links as `lib=`, separate from the core layer tokens (`src/library/ledger.json`). - **Browse dialog** is a Vue view (`src/ui/views/panels/DataLibraryDialog.vue`, `DataLibraryCard.vue`, placed by `DataLibraryBrowse.vue`) over the `gev-data-library` Pinia store; `src/ui/libraryBrowser.js` is its framework-free owner. - **Validation:** manifests are checked strictly when the catalog loads, so an invalid entry fails the unit suite; `npm run library:check` validates entries and the ledger. This branch was started before the layer panel moved to Vue and is merged with current main. The library's icon/action chips render through `RailChips.vue`, library rows carry `data-library-entry` from `LayerRows.vue`, and the Browse button lives in `LayerPanelsView.vue`. All library strings are translated in the 11 locales. ## Screenshots **Library rows in DATA LAYERS** (Black Marble, Smithsonian volcanoes and NASA EONET added): **Browse data library:** **An aerial entry** (swisstopo SWISSIMAGE) after Zoom to layer, clipped to its coverage and drawn above Black Marble: ## How I verified it - [x] `npm run build` - [x] `npm test`: 12,744 tests, 0 failures - [x] `npm run test:track` (dev server running): 111 passed - [x] Feature gate: `npm run qa:data-library`: 21 passed (fixture-backed: add, share link, a copied `/share` link in a clean browser, share navigation in one tab, reload restore, zoom while off, view-bounded loading, remove, remove all) - [x] `format:check`, `i18n`, `check:boundaries`, `library:check` Not built yet: a nightly probe that flips an entry's status when its upstream breaks, Ask integration, and a `provider` kind. ## Data source and licence Each manifest carries its own provider, endpoint, licence link and attribution, and the generated section in `DATA_SOURCES.md` lists them all. Entries whose terms say "see publisher terms" and the IMF PortWatch and CCTV packs are operator opt-in (`GEV_LIBRARY_ENABLE`), off on a default instance. Excluded on licence or access grounds: non-commercial sources (EOX), vendor-credited imagery (EagleView, Pictometry, Nearmap, WorldView), keyed or authenticated services, and sources that rejected requests during probing. A link check of every manifest on 2026-11-12 removed 11 entries whose licence or provider page returned 404 or whose host did not answer: OpenSeaMap seamarks, EMODnet bathymetry, SEDAC GPW population density, and the PDOK, basemap.at, Geneva SITG, ICGC Catalunya, Luxembourg, Vlaanderen, Minnesota and Bangor aerial photos. Their share tokens were never published, so the ledger was renumbered. Every remaining entry's upstream answered `npm run library:probe`. ## Docs - [x] `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md` updated, `docs/DATA-LIBRARY.md` added, and a `changelog.d/1604-data-library.md` fragment added

title: fix(voice): enter Cockpit without Contacts when an aircraft is ready
body:
## What this changes

Follow-up to #1556. Voice Cockpit entry turned Contacts on before every entry (`setContextMode('flights')` in `src/voice/gevActions.js`). So saying "cockpit" switched off the user's other layers, and the button's "No aircraft layer is on" refusal could not be reached by voice. Cockpit no longer needs Contacts, so voice now enters the way the button does.

- **An aircraft selected or tracked:** voice enters it directly. Contacts stays off and the user's layers stay as they are.
- **Contacts still starts to find an aircraft:** when none is selected or tracked, or when the request names an aircraft class ("cockpit into a helicopter") or another aircraft layer than the one ridden. If entry then fails, Contacts is rolled back as before.
- **The ridden aircraft's layer is off:** voice refuses with the button's reason instead of turning the layer on.

The 5 failures are timing and machine-bound tests that also fail on other branches on this Windows machine: the 250k-row ranking budget, disk-cache restart, KML parse deadline, scene-summary typing and CCTV live-feed idle deadline. None touch voice or Cockpit.
- [x] New tests in `src/voice/gevActions.test.mjs`: a selected aircraft and a tracked aircraft both enter without Contacts (both fail without the fix), and asking for another layer still starts Contacts. title: Check the Nominatim cache privacy modes only where POSIX modes exist
body:
## What this changes

`the disk cache survives a restart and stays within its bounds` in `src/tooling/nominatimOutlineRoute.test.mjs` fails on every Windows checkout: Windows has no POSIX permission bits, so `fs.statSync().mode & 0o777` is `0o666` for the cache directory and its files whatever `chmod` asked for (`438 !== 448`). The two mode checks now run only where POSIX modes exist, with the same `if (process.platform !== 'win32')` guard that `localServices.test.mjs` and `mcpPanelKey.test.mjs` already use. title: feat(ai): add Vertex AI (Express Mode) as a chat-only AI Provider
body:
## What this changes

Adds **Vertex AI** as a fourth **AI Provider**, next to OpenAI, Gemini and Claude (#1590).

**Stacked on #1590** — it reuses the chat-only session adapter introduced there, so this diff shows #1590's commits until that one merges; the Vertex-only changes are commit `ef301146`.

Vertex AI **Express Mode** gives a plain API key (no project, location or OAuth) for the same `generateContent` API the Gemini provider already speaks. So Vertex is Gemini with a different host, key and schema dialect, and no Live API — a chat-only provider.

- **Server:** `createGeminiChatHandler` gains `provider`, `endpoint`, `declareTool` and `thinkingConfig` options with Gemini defaults (its request body is byte-identical — a test asserts it). `server/providers/vertex/chat.js` is a thin layer over it: `https://aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1beta1/publishers/google/models/MODEL:generateContent`, `x-goog-api-key`.
- **Schema dialect:** Vertex's `FunctionDeclaration.parameters` is an OpenAPI-style `Schema` without `additionalProperties`, `$schema`, `const`, `oneOf`…; `toVertexSchema` converts GEV's JSON Schema tools to it (allow-list of the 22 Vertex fields, upper-case types, `nullable` as a flag). The route still validates every call against the full JSON Schema. Argument-less tools declare no `parameters`.
- **Thinking:** Gemini 2.5 and earlier refuse `thinkingLevel`, so Vertex sends none to them; Gemini 3 models get `LOW` like the Gemini provider.
- **Client:** `textProtocols.vertex` spreads `gemini` with its own endpoint and key, accepting both `STOP` and the proto spelling `FINISH_REASON_STOP`. The chat-only adapter from #1590 is generalised into `createTextOnlySession`, used by Claude and Vertex.
- **Keys / env:** `VERTEX_API_KEY`, `VERTEX_CHAT_MODEL` (default `gemini-3-flash-preview` — the 2.5 models listed for Express Mode carry a past retirement date), `GEV_RATELIMIT_VERTEX_PER_MIN`, `GEV_RATELIMIT_VERTEX_CHAT_PER_MIN`. Provider Settings, `.env.example`, `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md`, `README.md`, `SECURITY.md`, all eleven locales.

title: feat(ai): add Amazon Bedrock (Converse API) as a chat-only AI Provider
body:
## What this changes

Adds **Amazon Bedrock** as a fifth **AI Provider**, next to OpenAI, Gemini, Claude (#1590) and Vertex AI (#1607).

**Stacked on #1607** (which is stacked on #1590) — it reuses `createTextOnlySession`; the Bedrock-only changes are the two commits after `a0f88d33`.

A Bedrock **API key** is a bearer token (`AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK`, the same variable the AWS SDKs read), so plain `fetch` reaches the **Converse API** without AWS credentials, SigV4 or an SDK — and Converse is one message format for every model on Bedrock (Claude, Nova, Llama, …). No realtime voice API → chat only.

- **Server:** `server/providers/bedrock/chat.js` mirrors the Claude handler. Content blocks are one-key unions (`text`, `toolUse`, `toolResult` with a `json` payload, `reasoningContent`); roles alternate from the user, each `toolUse` batch is answered by the next user message with matching ids in order, the history ends with the user. Model id (incl. ARNs, URL-encoded) and Region are validated before any call. Tool schemas pass through unchanged as `inputSchema.json`.
- **Reasoning:** Claude Haiku 5.5 on Bedrock thinks by default and binds each reasoning block to the exact conversation before it, while the chat loop shortens earlier tool results — so the route replays only the **current turn's** reasoning blocks (the docs allow removing earlier ones) and never shows them. Nothing model-specific is sent (no `additionalModelRequestFields`), so Nova/Llama ids work too.
- **Errors:** `403 AccessDeniedException` → the shared `ACCESS_DENIED` cooldown (also what a wrong-Region long-term key produces); `429 Throttling/ModelNotReady` → `RATE_LIMITED`; `503` passes through; everything else is the generic failure.
- **Client:** `textProtocols.bedrock`, `createBedrockSession` via `createTextOnlySession`; `parseUsage` gains a `bedrock` branch (`inputTokens = totalTokens − outputTokens`, since Bedrock's total already includes cache reads/writes).
- **Keys / env:** `AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK`, `BEDROCK_REGION` (default `us-east-1`), `BEDROCK_CHAT_MODEL` (default `global.anthropic.claude-haiku-5-5` — the bare Claude ids have no in-Region availability), `GEV_RATELIMIT_BEDROCK_PER_MIN`, `GEV_RATELIMIT_BEDROCK_CHAT_PER_MIN`. title: Street Traffic: Lines and Dots toggles; hosts choose which road modes they offer
body:
Street Traffic now has two separate toggles while live flow is on, and a host can choose which road modes it offers.

**Lines and Dots.** Two chips on the Street Traffic row:
- **Lines** draws every road that has flow as a steady line: green for free flow, amber for slow, red for jam. It reuses the heat-line renderer, takes the dots' style colours, draws at most 1,500 lines, and drapes on 3D tiles in photoreal (terrain otherwise). The old lines stay up until the new ones are ready, so a rebuild doesn't blink.
- **Dots** shows or hides the moving dots.

Defaults are Lines off and Dots on, so the layer looks as it does today. Both are kept in layer state and share links (tokens `l` and `d`). The owner-only `jamViz` behaviour is unchanged while Lines is off.

**Road modes per host.** `createTrafficSource({ roadModes })` lists the modes a host offers (`tomtom`, `osm`, `hybrid`). By default all three are offered, which is today's behaviour. The row shows a chip only for offered modes, and none when there is only one. A mode outside the list is ignored, whether it comes from a chip, a restored state, a share link or `?trafficRoads=`. Without `osm` the layer never draws simulated roads and requests no OpenFreeMap tiles. A load without a key, or without the traffic service, fails with the existing translated reason.

Five new strings are translated in all 11 catalogs (`npm run i18n` reports every catalog complete).

Tests: `src/layers/traffic/hostModes.test.mjs` (new) and `src/layers/traffic/roadStatus.i18n.test.mjs`. Full suite: 11,057 pass, 0 fail. `npm run build`, `format:check` and `check:boundaries` pass.

title: v0.3.0 tracking arrival observer times out without preserving heading evidence
body:
Recording an unresolved qualification result on the v0.3.0 tag (`72eb3fdc739991a1286b7f1251de908e9744bb2a`). The deterministic browser tracking harness completed 108 passed / 1 failed / 0 skipped with Chrome for Testing 152.0.7977.75 on macOS arm64, headless SwiftShader and the documented bundled imagery/synthetic-contact fixtures.

The sole failure was:

`arrival: moveEnd + first reveal both re-aim before idle refresh, flights` — `arrival reveal observation exceeded 500 ms; elapsed=501.7 ms`.

The military sibling passed with settle/reveal rotation error 0.0°/0.0°, settle 344.2 ms + reveal 116.2 ms = 460.4 ms. No tracking-console errors or HTTP 5xx responses were observed.

This receipt establishes an observer timeout, not a measured stale aircraft heading. The frozen `src/tooling/trackArrivalObservation.mjs` checks the combined 500 ms deadline before `read()` and discards measured settle-angle evidence in its timeout result; the script logs no full observation object on failure.

Independent source review found this limitation is already addressed on main by merged #1308: separate phase budgets, preserved measured angle violations and bounded retries of inconclusive timeouts. This issue records the remaining v0.3.0 qualification/evidence gap; it does not request a duplicate implementation or weaken the heading assertions. The failed receipt has been preserved and no unchanged retry was used to turn it into a pass.

Timing comparison does not support attributing the timeout to concurrent local unit/build work: the production build finished before tracking began, and the unit suite overlapped only the first 0.609 seconds of tracking startup, before the much later arrival scenario.

Milestone note: no upstream milestones are listed and the connected account has no triage/administration rights to create or assign one.

### Local resolution and verification — November 6, 2026, EST (UTC−05:00, America/Toronto)

The local v0.3.0 branch now contains the observer repair at `057a9ab6a0234e60a9742af786950a7098357033` (not pushed upstream). Application runtime, package version 0.3.0 and configuration are preserved.

The repair keeps the original **combined 500 ms** measurement, strict **<10°** angle criterion, first-visible-frame capture and one measured attempt. It reads completed frames before classifying lateness, retains measured settle/late-visible angles on timeout, and emits complete observation JSON. Preparation must complete a real frame before tampering. A new strict **<1,000 ms freshness bound from preparation's monotonic origin**, including the setup gap, prevents the idle refresh from masking a broken reset. No per-phase budget extension or retry wrapper was imported.

Verification on the final commit:
- Focused observer regressions: **28 passed / 0 failed / 0 skipped** on Node 24.21.0 and Node 26.13.0. Coverage includes wrong first angles, retained timeout evidence, exact 500 ms/10° boundaries, stale preparation, setup gaps, invalid measurements and cleanup.
- Complete Node 26 ordinary unit plan: **8,814 passed / 0 failed / 2 environment skips** (Docker Compose and native Windows DACL tooling unavailable).
- Production build passed; the generated main application JavaScript is byte-identical to the installed v0.3.0 build.
- One documented native-GPU tracking run: **109 passed / 0 failed / 0 skipped**, Chrome for Testing 152.0.7977.75, observed ANGLE Metal / Apple M5 Pro, on macOS arm64. Window: **21:49:07–21:50:44 EST, November 6**.
- Flights measured **100.8 ms**, military **99.9 ms**, each with **0° settle and first-visible reveal error**. Preparation-origin freshness was 121.4 ms / 108.1 ms, respectively. The 500 ms deadline is unchanged.

An earlier software-renderer attempt on preliminary candidate `4503a3f3` is preserved as **incomplete**: 34 passed / 1 failed among executed assertions, exit 2, aborted before the arrival group with execution-context destruction around tracked-model readiness. Its cause is unresolved; it is not a software-renderer pass and was not retried unchanged. The final native run used the repository's existing `--headful` real-GPU path, with the same assertions and thresholds, after the freshness strengthening.

The local integration was a fast-forward; configuration hashes remain identical and the working tree is clean. The upstream v0.3.0 tag/release and application runtime were not modified. This issue remains open as an upstream release record; the local repair and native-GPU qualification are complete. The existing milestone-permission limitation above remains.

Local diagnostic fix `457adb62645a8aad24c0940cc593e16a058af118` distinguishes genuine Puppeteer `TimeoutError` readiness failures from fatal context/session errors. The latter now retain their original error identity, phase, stack and cause and propagate immediately. All four readiness predicates and their deadlines are unchanged. This fixes lost error classification; it does **not** establish the cause of the historical execution-context destruction.

Controlled cold software-mode results on that candidate:
- Diagnostic run with CDP lifecycle observation: **109 passed / 0 failed / 0 skipped**, exit 0, Chrome for Testing 152.0.7977.75; SwiftShader observed live. Window **10:16:01–10:18:38 EST**.
- Flights arrival **262.7 ms**, preparation **390.8 ms**, preparation-origin freshness **653.7 ms**; military **256.6 ms**, preparation **401.7 ms**, freshness **658.4 ms**. Angle errors were 0 degrees; the original combined 500 ms arrival, strict angle, preparation and freshness bounds remained active.

Fault controls **2/2**: deliberate target closure propagated a fatal error; ordinary controlled navigation completed. No matching crash report or optimizer-reload evidence established an explanation for the historical abort.

The original failed receipt remains preserved. Historical root cause is **unproven**; current software-renderer qualification passes. The v0.3.0 baseline and private configuration are preserved. Separate, explicitly authorized Mini hosting and account OAuth work is tracked in #1621 and #1622; those extensions intentionally change application behavior and have their own validation gate.

A new controlled cold software run on the explicitly extended local candidate `45159ab7e4c5c5e4fec9c2b27b7bb517b0e66556` was **incomplete**: 19 passed / 0 assertion failures / 0 skipped among executed checks, harness exit 2, at the satellite selected-subject evaluation. title: fix(embed): accept comma-separated GEV_EMBED_FRAME_ANCESTORS
body:
## What this changes

`GEV_EMBED_FRAME_ANCESTORS` was written into the CSP header verbatim. CSP separates sources with spaces, so a comma-separated list (the usual shape for env lists, e.g. `http://localhost:4187,https://app.example.com`) produced an invalid `frame-ancestors` directive. Browsers reject it, every embedding page is refused, and the only hint is a console error in the framing page.

`parseFrameAncestors()` in `build/embed-framing.js` now:

- splits sources on commas or whitespace, so both list styles work;
- quotes bare `self` / `none` and collapses duplicates;
- treats `*` as "any page" only when it is the whole value;
- refuses a value containing `;` (it would end the directive and start another) and keeps the default protection;
- drops entries that are not CSP sources (paths, `'unsafe-inline'`, …) with a startup warning instead of writing them into the header. If nothing valid remains, embed documents keep `frame-ancestors 'none'`.

Space-separated values that worked before produce the same header as before. Docs (`docs/TOOLS.md`, `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md`, `.env.example`) and a changelog fragment are updated. I'll rename the fragment to `changelog.d/<pr-number>-embed-frame-ancestors-list.md` once this has a number.

Found while embedding God's Eye View in another app: a comma list silently blocked the frame.

## How I verified it

- [ ] `npm run build`: not run locally (relying on CI)
- [ ] `npm test`: not run locally in full (relying on CI). The new `src/tooling/embedFraming.test.mjs` (5 tests: space/comma/mixed lists, keywords and wildcards, `;` injection and invalid entries, `'none'` precedence, header produced on an embed document) passes with `node --test`.
- [ ] `npm run test:track`: not run; this change does not touch tracking
- [x] Feature gate: none applies (server header only). The existing embed-framing test in `src/tooling/viteBuild.test.mjs` uses single-source and `*` inputs, which parse exactly as before.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: fix(chat): send OpenAI chat tool schemas Chat Completions accepts
body:
## Problem

Typed chat on OpenAI fails for every message. OpenAI answers 400 `invalid_function_parameters`:

```
Invalid schema for function 'resolve_area': '^ne:(?:country|state|county|natural):[\\p{L}\\p{M}\\p{N}]+(?:-[\\p{L}\\p{M}\\p{N}]+)*$' is not a 'regex'.
param: tools[29].function.parameters
```

`resolve_area`'s area-id pattern (`src/voice/areaCandidateContract.js`) uses Unicode property classes. Realtime voice accepts it; Chat Completions does not, and refuses the whole request, so chat shows "Could not connect".

## Fix

`server/providers/openai/chat.js` sends each tool schema through `chatSchema`, which leaves out only `pattern`s that use `\p{…}` / `\P{…}`. Every other rule is kept. The action still checks area ids against its own contract before it runs, so the model loses a hint, not a rule. Voice is unchanged.

## Verification

- Sent the tool list `createOpenAiChatHandler` builds to `https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions` with `gpt-4.1-mini`: 400 before, 200 after.
- `src/textChatServer.test.mjs`: the OpenAI tool body carries no `\p{` pattern, and `chatSchema` drops only those patterns. The test fails without the fix.
- `npm test` and `npm run format:check` pass.

Gemini chat is not changed, and I haven't checked whether Gemini accepts these patterns.

title: feat(cctv): add Iceland (Vegagerðin / IRCA) road cameras as a keyless source pack
body:
## What

Adds Iceland as a keyless CCTV source pack: the Icelandic Road and Coastal Administration (Vegagerðin, IRCA) road cameras.

- Catalog: one JSON list, `https://gagnaveita.vegagerdin.is/api/vefmyndavelar2014_1` (499 camera views at 166 stations on 2026-11-06).
- Frames: JPEG stills in `https://www.vegagerdin.is/vgdata/vefmyndavelar/`. The loader and the media proxy both pin that directory.
- Pack name `iceland`, default on, `CCTV_ICELAND_ENABLED=0` turns it off, `CCTV_ICELAND_MAX_SOURCES` (default 250, min 8, max 600) caps it.

## Licence

IRCA's terms of use (https://www.vegagerdin.is/vegagerdin/gagnasafn/vefthjonustur/terms-and-conditions) publish their data, road camera images included, under CC BY 4.0 (Act 45/2018). They ask that the licensor is acknowledged, that nothing suggests IRCA endorses the user, and they exclude third-party material and IRCA/State logos. Real-time data is provided as is.

- Attribution is in `src/data/dataCredits.js` (`iceland-cctv`) and `DATA_SOURCES.md` (row and bullet, with the terms URL and the no-endorsement condition).
- Every camera carries `license: 'Icelandic Road and Coastal Administration (IRCA) — road camera images, CC BY 4.0'`.
- Frames are fetched at request time and never stored or redistributed.

## Behaviour

- Redirects on the catalog are refused, the body read is capped at 2 MiB, and every rejection path cancels the response body.
- Frame URLs are checked with `pinnedCameraUrl` (scheme, host, no userinfo, no port, no encoded separators, inside the directory) and must be a `.jpg`/`.jpeg` whose file stem is `[a-z0-9_-]`. Coordinates must be numbers inside an Iceland bounding box.
- Ids are `is-vegagerdin-<frame file stem>`, unique per view in the live feed. Repeated frames collapse before the cap.
- Label: the feed's `Skyring` view description, with doubled spaces and repeated words collapsed.
- Heading: an explicit Icelandic facing after `til`, `í` or `séð` ("til vesturs", "í suður", "séð austur") sets a high-confidence heading (264 of 499 views today). A view that states none, or two different ones, keeps the id-hash low-confidence pose. A bare road direction ("Miklabraut austur") or a place name containing a cardinal ("Norðurárdalur") is not read as a facing.
- The feed has no elevation, so cameras carry a flat 60 m prior for the client's ground snap. No change to the precomputed ground-height data.
- The default cap keeps 250 views, ordered by distance to Reykjavík, Akureyri, Egilsstaðir, Ísafjörður and Selfoss, so a cap keeps each region's nearest cameras. This is the one tuning choice worth a look from a reviewer.

## Verification

- `npm run format:check`, `npm run check:boundaries`, `npm test` (11,067 pass, 0 fail, 4 skipped) and `npm run build` in a clean `node:24` container after `npm ci`.
- New `src/data/cctvIceland.test.mjs` (10 tests): row mapping, heading parser table, rejected rows (off-host, http, userinfo, port, traversal, encoded slash, non-JPEG, missing extension, string and null coordinates, out-of-country), redirect/HTTP error/oversize refusals with body cancellation, dedupe and anchored cap, catalog merge and the `CCTV_ICELAND_ENABLED=0` skip. Each mutation of the loader I tried (no `redirect: 'manual'`, no cancel, no pin, no coordinate check, no dedupe, no `séð`, string coordinates, no extension check, ambiguity resolved to the first facing, no anchors) fails at least one test.
- Live check through `fetchCctvImageFromUpstream` against all 499 views on 2026-11-07: 499 returned a JPEG (10–136 KB, median 35 KB), 499 distinct images, `Last-Modified` age p50 8 min, max 19 min, none older than an hour.

## Not in this PR

- No per-provider refresh cadence in `src/data/cctvLod.js`; the 5-minute default fits a source that refreshes every few minutes.
- No change to how other packs are allocated; the shared 4,000 cap and round-robin apply as before.
- A changelog fragment is added once this PR has a number.

title: OAuth account-agent support for ChatGPT and Grok in a private self-hosted deployment
body:
Tracking a local v0.3.0-based integration requested for a private self-hosted installation. Account authentication must use OAuth for ChatGPT and Grok, with no API-key fallback for these account-agent channels.

Planned scope:

- Independently implement OpenAI's published Sign in with ChatGPT flow (PKCE, state, nonce/JWKS validation, dynamic registration and approved direct Responses scope); avoid copying the noncommercial DevKit implementation.
- Integrate the official pinned Grok CLI through OAuth-only ACP, with API-key authentication and unrelated coding-tool permissions disabled.
- Keep credentials on the host with OS-backed encrypted storage; expose only connection status and bounded agent/tool messages to the browser.
- Use the existing canonical GEV action catalog and browser action runner, preserving real tool outcomes, cancellation and provider identity.
- Reachable account/provider controls and text-agent interface on the real application entry point. Accurately distinguish text/tool capability from unimplemented provider realtime audio; no synthetic authentication or live-inference acceptance.
- Preserve the v0.3.0 baseline and existing local configuration; no broad upstream UI/framework upgrade.

The new account service will require authenticated owner admission over direct HTTPS, with connection/revocation restricted to the host. Existing legacy credential/MCP guards will remain intact.

Status: implementation in isolated local lanes; accounts not connected and no live provider inference claimed. Source review, protocol tests, TLS/browser reachability, real OAuth consent, refresh/revocation and live tool execution are separate gates.

Milestone limitation: upstream currently lists no milestones and the connected account has READ rather than triage/administration permission, so it cannot create or assign a milestone.

title: Native HTTPS hosting with existing CA trust distribution and tailnet-owner admission
body:
Tracking a v0.3.0-based private-host deployment with an existing machine CA and a certificate covering its Tailscale DNS name. No new CA or broad public listener is intended.

Implementation scope:

- Native Node HTTPS listener bound only to the host's tailnet address, with exact hostname and Origin admission and real socket client addresses.
- Reuse the existing certificate/key through private runtime paths; never copy private keys into the repository or static assets.
- Serve the exact existing public root certificate and installation instructions for macOS/iOS trust; preserve unrelated services and trust settings.
- Verify owner identity using Tailscale Self/Whois; restrict account administration to the host itself and authenticated account-agent use to the owner.
- Keep existing provider, credential and MCP guards unchanged. Do not strip forwarding headers to make remote requests appear loopback.
- Serve the production browser build and existing Node provider hooks without using Vite's development/preview server as production.
- Prepare reversible per-user hosting configuration outside iCloud working source, retaining configuration and raw TLS/access/browser receipts.

Status: isolated implementation; no persistent listener/autostart installed yet. Targeted TLS/static/access tests and real certificate-chain checks are separate from final hosting and client-device acceptance. No private hostname, IP, key material or account secrets are included here.

title: Add Spain's DGT cameras as a keyless DATEX II pack
body:
## What this changes

Spain's DGT publishes its national road-camera network as one keyless DATEX II
3.7 document (`camaras_datex2_v37.xml`, **1,975 cameras**, licence Creative
Commons Attribution). This adds it as a CCTV pack that is read at runtime —
never bundled, never shipped as a scraped snapshot, which is the shape #660
asked for when the earlier static attempt was closed.

Refs #660.

Details worth reviewing:

- Device blocks are matched by **local name** (`device`, `latitude`,
  `deviceUrl`), so a publisher that changes its namespace prefixes does not
  break the catalog.
- Only `https://etraffic.dgt.es/camarasEtraffic/<id>.jpg` is registered as a
  frame URL; anything else in the document is dropped, so a re-pointed catalog
  cannot turn the frame proxy into an open image proxy.
- Positions come from the published TPEG point location. The document carries
  the carriageway, not the camera bearing, so poses use the shared
  low-confidence prior.
- CC BY credit in the CCTV panel, `DATA_SOURCES.md` and the credits list.
- `CCTV_SPAIN_ENABLED`, `CCTV_SPAIN_MAX_SOURCES` (default 800, bounded 1–2000)
  and `CCTV_SPAIN_URL`.
- Parser and policy tests beside the module (6 cases, including prefix
  variation, non-camera devices, bad frame shapes and entity decoding).

## How I verified it

- [x] `npm run build`
- [x] `npm test` (934 test files, exit 0, no failures)
- [x] `npm run test:track` (dev server running) — 107 passed, 2 failed; both
      failures are the `arrival: moveEnd … 500 ms` budget (589.9 ms / 584.8 ms
      against 500 ms), in the arrival group and unrelated to CCTV
- [x] Feature gate for the area I touched: no `qa-*` gate covers CCTV packs. I
      verified live instead: the server logs `[CCTV] Loaded Spain DGT camera
      sources: 1975 (using 800)` and `/api/cctv/frame/es-dgt-165651` returns
      `200 image/jpeg` (AP-9 km 68.82, A Coruña)

Live sample of the served catalog: 4,000 cameras across 19 packs, Spain taking
its round-robin share of 284.

Screenshots: none yet — I can add a globe capture of the Spain pack on request.

title: test(traffic): load the timing test's Vite server without a file watcher
body:
`src/data/trafficTiming.test.mjs` fails with `ENOSPC` when the host's inotify watch limit is spent, even though the test never reloads anything.

## Cause

The test starts a Vite server in middleware mode to load modules over SSR once. Vite's default file watcher still opens an inotify watch for each directory of the repository, so on a host where `fs.inotify.max_user_watches` is used up, `fs.watch` throws and the test fails:

```
✖ traffic timing pairs real ordering to the scheduling change and guards re-arms
  Error: ENOSPC: System limit for number of file watchers reached, watch '.../src/i18n'
      at createFsWatchInstance (vite/dist/node/chunks/dep-….js)
```

The limit is per user, so it is reached when other watchers share it: dev servers, editors, or containers running Vite on the same host. The other tests that start a Vite server (`src/tooling/allowedHosts.test.mjs`, `src/tools/localRoute.test.mjs`) already pass `watch: null`; this one did not.

## Change

`server: { middlewareMode: true }` becomes `server: { middlewareMode: true, hmr: false, watch: null }`, with a comment saying why. One file, no behaviour change in the test body.

## Verification

Node 24 in a container, native inotify watchers, on a host where the limit was spent:

| | `main` (`52187c91d`) | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `node --test src/data/trafficTiming.test.mjs`, 3 runs | 2 pass / 1 fail every run | 3 pass / 0 fail every run |
| `ENOSPC` in the output | yes | 0 |
| `CHOKIDAR_USEPOLLING=1` (control) | 3 pass | 3 pass |

Full `npm test` on this branch: 11130 pass / 0 fail / 4 skipped, no `ENOSPC` anywhere. `format:check`, `check:boundaries` and `changelog:check` pass.

No changelog fragment: it is a test-only change, like #1493.

title: feat: add a Taiwan Traditional Chinese (zh-TW) locale alongside zh-Hant
body:
### Problem

Thanks for adding Traditional Chinese in #1430. As its description notes, `zh-Hant.json` is the `zh-CN` catalog converted with OpenCC `s2tw`, so only the script changes and the wording stays Mainland Chinese. Users in Taiwan (`zh-TW`, currently mapped to `zh-Hant` in `src/i18n/locale.js`) see terms that read as non-local.

Counts in `src/i18n/locales/zh-Hant.json` at commit 52187c9 (2026-11-08):

| Current (zh-CN wording) | Taiwan usage | Occurrences |
|---|---|---|
| 數據 | 資料 | 138 |
| 加載 | 載入 | 77 |
| 實時 | 即時 | 48 |
| 點擊 | 點選 | 45 |
| 圖標 | 圖示 | 38 |
| 設置 | 設定 | 37 |
| 搜索 | 搜尋 | 20 |
| 信息 | 資訊 | 12 |
| 登錄 | 登入 | 12 |
| 網絡 | 網路 | 10 |

Some terms (e.g. 文件, 項目) are correct in certain contexts, so changes would be reviewed in context rather than applied as global replacements.

Examples:
- `Loading Google 3D Tiles...` → current `正在加載 Google 3D Tiles…`, Taiwan `正在載入 Google 3D Tiles…`
- `Starting live contacts…` → current `正在接入實時目標…`, Taiwan `正在連接即時目標…`
- `Pick a shape, then click the map.` → current `先選擇形狀，再在地圖上點擊。`, Taiwan `先選擇形狀，再點選地圖。`

Quotation marks also follow Mainland style (“ ” instead of 「 」).

### Proposal

Add a separate `zh-TW` locale and keep `zh-Hant` unchanged for Hong Kong and Macau. In `src/i18n/locale.js`, map `zh-TW` to the new locale, and keep `zh-Hant` / `zh-HK` / `zh-MO` on `zh-Hant`.

Two implementation options:

**A. Human-reviewed `zh-TW.json`.**
Start from `zh-Hant.json`, then have a native speaker review every entry for Taiwan terminology and punctuation.

**B. Generated `zh-TW.json` using OpenCC `s2twp` with reviewed overrides (preferred).**
Keep `zh-Hant.json` unchanged. Generate a separate Taiwan-specific catalog from `zh-CN` using OpenCC `s2twp`, then apply context-aware, human-reviewed terminology corrections.

The overrides could be stored in a machine-readable format and documented in `docs/translations/zh-TW.md`, allowing future regeneration without losing Taiwan-specific corrections.

Scope is strictly localization: no changes to CCTV, map layers, LLM/voice, or any other feature.

I'm happy to do the translation and review, keep `npm run i18n` and the existing i18n tests passing (adding a zh-TW mapping test similar to `zh-Hant-display.test.mjs`), and update `docs/TRANSLATORS.md` / `docs/translations/`.

I would appreciate the maintainers' guidance on two points:
1. Would you be open to adding a separate `zh-TW` locale while keeping `zh-Hant` unchanged?
2. If so, would you prefer a fully human-maintained catalog (Option A) or a generated catalog with reviewed overrides (Option B)?

I'm happy to implement the preferred approach and submit a focused PR with tests and documentation.

### Data source, license, and attribution

none (UI translation only)

### Will you build it?

Yes, I plan to open a PR

title: feat(transit): add 34 keyless cities across Europe, Asia, Oceania and North America
body:
## The Transit layer goes global: 34 new live feeds, from Szczecin to Sendai

Until now, live transit in God's Eye View meant North America, the Nordics, the Netherlands, South East Queensland and Rio. This PR adds **34 feeds across 32 regions in 13 countries**: Central and Eastern Europe, Italy, France, the Iberian Peninsula, Japan and Malaysia, plus new cities in the US, Canada and Australia. Every one of them streams vehicle positions live, with no API key.

| | |
|:-:|:-:|
| ![Prague](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/IMBrandao/gods-eye-view/pr-assets/transit-more-cities/wide-1-prague.jpg) | ![Warsaw](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/IMBrandao/gods-eye-view/pr-assets/transit-more-cities/wide-2-warsaw.jpg) |
| **Prague**: 971 vehicles, trams in amber and buses in green | **Warsaw**: 808 buses and trams across the city |
| ![Rome](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/IMBrandao/gods-eye-view/pr-assets/transit-more-cities/wide-3-rome.jpg) | ![Venice](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/IMBrandao/gods-eye-view/pr-assets/transit-more-cities/wide-4-venice.jpg) |
| **Rome**: 600+ buses across the city | **Venice**: buses on the mainland, *vaporetti* (cyan) around the island |
| ![Sendai](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/IMBrandao/gods-eye-view/pr-assets/transit-more-cities/wide-5-sendai.jpg) | |
| **Sendai**: the layer's first city in Asia | |

*Captured on Sunday 8 November, early morning in Europe and mid-afternoon in Japan, so these are quiet-hour numbers.*

### At a glance

- **18 → 52 feeds** in the Transit layer.
- **10 countries new to the layer:** Poland, Czechia, Lithuania, Romania, Italy, France, Portugal, Spain, Japan and Malaysia.
- **5,760 vehicles live** across the new feeds at the quietest hour of the week (Sunday dawn in Europe, night in the Americas). Weekday peaks run far higher: about 1,280 in Warsaw, 1,040 in Rome and 1,000 in Lisbon.
- **Modes from each operator's own route ids:** buses everywhere; trams in Kraków, Bordeaux, Le Havre and Rouen (Métro); Prague's metro, S/R trains, trams, trolleybuses and ferries; and boats in Venice, Bordeaux (BAT³) and Rouen (Calypso).
- **Zero new dependencies.** It's all registry entries, plus one small proxy option for feeds that publish km/h.

### Try it

Open the app with any of these hashes and the Transit layer on:

| City | Hash |
|---|---|

## How it works

Each feed is **one entry in `src/data/transitFeeds.js`**: URL, centre and load radius, licence, attribution, and a terms note that records what the decision to ship rests on. Feeds are polled only when the camera is inside their radius, so 34 more entries cost nothing anywhere else on the globe.

Four small additions make the new feeds look right:

1. **km/h → m/s.** Lisbon (Carris Metropolitana), Montpellier and Toulon publish speed in km/h instead of the m/s the spec requires. Each was measured against real vehicle movement, at about 3.3–3.6× too high. A new `speedUnit: 'km/h'` field has the proxy convert them.
2. **Readable line names.** Route ids become the line a rider sees on the front of the vehicle:

   | Feed | Route id in the feed | Shown as |
   |---|---|---|
   | Prague | `L135` | 135 |
   | Turin | `10NU` | 10N |
   | Venice | `5.1_UN` | 5.1 |
   | Victoria | `95-VIC` | 95 |
   | Lisbon city | `172_1` | 172 |
   | Rouen | `TCAR:93` | 93 |
   | Johor Bahru | `J33CWLMYJB` | J33 |
   | Edmonton, Toulon | `009`, `0002` | 9, 2 |

3. **The right mode for each vehicle:**
   - Modes follow the operators' own route ids: Prague's ranges from PID's routes.txt (metro `L991`–`L993`, trains `L1001`–`L1199`, ferries `L1801`/`L1802`, trolleybuses `L51`–`L59`), Bordeaux's numbered tram ids (`59`–`62`, `163`/`164`) and BAT³ boats (`951`–`953`), Rouen's Métro (`TCAR:90`) and Calypso (`TCAR:99`), and Le Havre's lines A/B.
   - The Kraków tram feed and the Venice waterbus feed default to tram and ferry.
4. **Adelaide's content negotiation.** Adelaide answers any `Accept` that names protobuf with base64 text labelled JSON. Its entry uses the existing per-feed `headers` hook to send `Accept: */*`.

Feeds that carry no bearing (Poznań, Gdańsk, Rzeszów, Málaga, Lisbon city, Johor Bahru) still point the right way: the motion engine already derives heading from the segment between two fixes.

## Licences

- **Read and quoted in the registry:**
  - Szczecin (CC0), Warsaw (City Hall terms; the credit carries the name, the API link and the feed timestamp), Poznań (the credit carries the data's date), Victoria (BC Transit terms) and Halifax (Open Government Licence – Halifax).
  - Prague: PID licenses the data on its own site as CC BY. The realtime feed is served through Golemio, the city's data platform, and the terms note records that.
  - The French feeds (Licence Ouverte 2.0 / ODbL), Sendai (CC BY 4.0) and Gdańsk (CC BY 4.0), quoted from their national catalogue records.
- **Licence page linked but not readable by script:** Edmonton (same municipal template as Mississauga and Burlington) and Venice. Each terms note says so.
- **Denver:** the RTD agreement page is quoted: a revocable click-through that allows redistribution and bars RTD trademarks.
- **No licence stated:** like the Metro Transit and OVapi feeds already in the project (#587), these operators publish a keyless, documented feed without licence text. Each is credited as a courtesy and can be switched off on its own if an operator objects.
- **Worth knowing:**
  - Bordeaux's URL carries `apiKey=opendata-bordeaux-metropole-flux-gtfs-rt`. This is a fixed public string printed in the open-data listing, not a credential.
  - Rouen and Le Havre are read from the operators' own feeds, as listed on transport.data.gouv.fr. Rouen's TAE and TNI networks are separate feeds and are not included.

`DATA_SOURCES.md` has a row for every feed.

## Testing

- **Unit tests:** `node --test src/data/transitFeeds.test.mjs src/data/transitProxy.test.mjs` passes 57/57. The new tests check:
  - that every new feed covers its own city centre;
  - each route-label and mode helper;
  - the exact list of km/h feeds;
  - the Adelaide header;
  - that every no-licence feed names the basis it ships on.
- **Full suite:** passes on top of current `main`, except the Windows-only disk-cache permission test, which is unrelated. On Windows, the new `npm test` runner hits `ENAMETOOLONG`, so the same files were run as globs.
- **Live check:** every new feed was fetched through the dev proxy (`/api/transit/vehicles/<id>`) and decoded with the repo's own decoder; the table's counts come from that run.
- **Visual check:** Prague, Warsaw, Rome, Venice, Sendai and Lisbon were checked in the browser, with detection and the scope vignette off.

title: feat(transit): Porto STCP buses — first feed outside GTFS-Realtime (NGSI v2)
body:
## Summary

Adds **Porto** to the Transit layer: STCP's live bus positions from the Porto Digital Urban Platform, which STCP publishes on dados.gov.pt under **CC0**. It joins Lisbon (#1628) as the layer's second Portuguese city.

It is also the **first transit feed that is not GTFS-Realtime**. STCP publishes through a FIWARE NGSI v2 broker that serves Smart Data Models `Vehicle` entities as JSON. This PR lets a registry entry declare its wire format:

```js
format: 'ngsi-v2', // absent = GTFS-Realtime protobuf, as before
```

![Porto with STCP buses](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/IMBrandao/gods-eye-view/pr-assets/transit-porto-stcp/1-porto-overview.jpg)
![An STCP bus card: route 201, fleet number 3486](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/IMBrandao/gods-eye-view/pr-assets/transit-porto-stcp/2-porto-bus-card.jpg)

## How

- **`src/data/ngsiVehicles.js`** (new, pure) decodes the `/v2/entities` array into the same records `normalizeVehicleEntity` produces (`id`, `lat`, `lon`, `bearing`, `speedMps`, `timestamp`, `routeId`, `directionId`, `label`, …).
  - It reads attributes in both NGSI forms: normalized (`{type, value}`) and `keyValues`.
  - `location` must be a GeoJSON Point.
  - `observationDateTime` must be strict ISO 8601 with a time zone.
  - Route and direction come from the `stcp:route:<line>` and `stcp:sentido:<0|1>` annotations.
- **`transitProxy.js`** gains a small `TRANSIT_FEED_FORMATS` table (`gtfs-rt`, `ngsi-v2`). Each entry names its decoder and its `Accept` header.
  - `buildTransitSnapshot` picks the decoder from the feed. Everything after decoding (timestamp repair, snapshot shape) is shared.
  - An unknown declared format throws instead of being guessed.
- **Every existing proxy rule still applies, unchanged:**
  - only registered URLs are fetched;
  - redirects are validated manually and must stay on the feed's own https origin;
  - the 8 MB body cap is applied before parsing;
  - the entity-count ceiling (`GTFS_MAX_ENTITIES`) applies;
  - the string-length ceiling applies: an over-long id or route drops the whole record instead of truncating it;
  - plausibility checks reject null island and out-of-range coordinates;
  - conditional requests, the 15 s cache, serve-stale, the admission limiter and the backoff ladder all apply.
- **A body that is not JSON, or not an array,** is treated as an upstream outage (serve stale, then back off), not as a shape fault.
- `SECURITY.md`'s transit line now mentions the JSON path and the refusal of unknown formats.

## Data checks (2026-11-07/08)

- **Coverage:** 53 buses at night. Every one had a bearing, a GeoJSON location, an observation time, a fleet number and a route annotation. Median report age was about 30 s.
- **Speed unit, checked against movement:** in two snapshots 60 s apart, reported speeds of 0–15 sat alongside 0–10 m/s of straight-line movement, which rules out km/h. The Smart Data Models unit (m/s) is what arrives, so no conversion is needed. No `speedUnit` is set.
- **Movement in the running app:** every bus present in both of two reads about 70 s apart (49 buses) had moved and carried a newer report time.
- **Caching:** fixes refresh about once a minute. The broker sends no ETag or Last-Modified, so each poll fetches a full body of about 70 KB.
- **Route ids** (`200`, `ZC`, …) are already the number on the bus, so no route table is needed.

## Licence

- The dados.gov.pt dataset page, published by STCP, lists licence id `cc-zero` (Creative Commons CCZero).
- CC0 asks for no credit. STCP and Porto Digital are credited as a courtesy, like the other public feeds.
- `terms.quote` is the CC0 1.0 deed. `terms.note` records the format, the unit check and the caching behaviour.

## Docs

- A `DATA_SOURCES.md` row, plus an update to the transit paragraph (fifty-three feeds, fifty regions).
- The README transit row.
- `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md`: the region count and a note on NGSI. This also fixes the stale "7 keyless regions" table cell.
- A changelog fragment.

## Tests

- **`src/data/ngsiVehicles.test.mjs` (new)** covers:
  - a real STCP entity becoming a record;
  - the keyValues form;
  - bad positions;
  - over-long strings;
  - loose timestamps;
  - negative and non-numeric speeds;
  - newest fix wins on duplicate ids;
  - non-array and non-JSON bodies.
- **`transitProxy.test.mjs`** covers:
  - an NGSI feed decoded through `buildTransitSnapshot` with a JSON `Accept`;
  - a broken body counting as an outage, not a shape error;
  - an unknown format being refused.
- **`transitFeeds.test.mjs`** covers:
  - Porto coverage (Aliados, Gaia, Matosinhos and Maia, but not Lisbon);
  - the CC0 licence, the declared format and the `DATA_SOURCES.md` row.
- **Results:**
  - The transit suites pass, and `node scripts/format.mjs --check` passes.
  - The full unit suite (run with `node --test` over `src`, `server` and `scripts`, because `npm test` hits Windows' command-length limit here) has 11,642 passing after merging main. The one failure, a 5-second KML import deadline, passes when its file runs alone.

## Merged with main after #1628

#1628 has merged, and `main` is merged into this branch. Porto uses the `transitFeed()` helper #1628 introduced. The registry typedef carries `format` alongside `speedUnit`, `refreshMs`, `sourceUrl` and `creditDated`. A feed that sets its own `headers` (Adelaide's `Accept: */*`) still overrides the format's `Accept`. The counts now include #1628's cities.

title: i18n: add Swedish (sv)
body:
## What this changes

Adds Swedish (`sv`) as a shipped UI language: a complete catalog (2,961 messages, nothing missing) registered in the locale list, catalogs, language picker and package boundaries. Browsers set to Swedish get it at once; `?lang=sv` or the language picker choose it elsewhere. Numbers and dates come out Swedish from `Intl`.

- `src/i18n/locales/sv.json`: the catalog, in the same key order as the other locales.
- `docs/translations/sv.md`: style rules (imperative without a pronoun, closed compounds, decimal comma, space before units and %) and the glossary.
- `src/i18n/same-as-english.json`: entries that stay English on purpose (avionics codes such as HDG and FOV, product, place and source names such as iNaturalist and Salish Sea).
- `src/ui/localePicker.test.mjs`: Svenska sorts after Português.
- `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md` and `docs/TRANSLATORS.md` list the new language.

The translation comes from [God's Eye View Sverige](https://github.com/Kajjan7610/Gods-view-sweden), my Swedish fork, where it has been in daily use since early November. I brought it up to date with current `main`, including the wildlife sightings layer, the event age filter and the new traffic styles. Nothing from the fork's own Swedish data layers is included.

## How I verified it

On Windows 11, Node 24.22.2:

- [x] `npm run build`: green.
- [x] `npm test`: 11,126 passed, 2 failed, both unrelated to this change. One is the disk-cache file-mode assertion in `nominatimOutlineRoute.test.mjs` (Windows has no POSIX file modes). The other is the timing budget in `analystEngine.test.mjs`, which passes when run alone (68/68).
- [x] `npm run test:track` (dev server running): 109 passed, 0 failed, no console errors, no HTTP 5xx.
- [x] Feature gate for the area I touched: none applies (i18n only). `npm run i18n` reports `sv: 2961 messages, complete`; package boundaries and import directions pass.

I also loaded `?lang=sv` in the browser. The first-run guide, panels and picker show Swedish, with no console errors.

One note for Windows contributors: on Windows, `scripts/run-unit-tests.mjs` stops with `spawnSync ... ENAMETOOLONG` because the whole file list goes on one command line. I ran the suite with a batched runner for the numbers above. I can send that fix as a separate PR if it's welcome.

I'll add the changelog fragment as `changelog.d/<this PR>-swedish.md` once the PR has a number.

title: bug: npm test fails on Windows with spawnSync ENAMETOOLONG before any test runs
body:
### What happened

On Windows, `npm test` stops before any test runs, with exit code 1:

```
Error: spawnSync C:\Program Files\nodejs\node.exe ENAMETOOLONG
```

I expected the unit suite to run and report its results, as `CONTRIBUTING.md` lists `npm test` as one of the three checks required before a pull request.

`scripts/run-unit-tests.mjs` starts one `node --test` process and passes it every parallel test path as a separate argument: 936 paths at `52187c91`. Together they make a command line longer than the 32,767 characters Windows allows, so Windows refuses to start the process.

CI does not show this. The unit-test job in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs `npm test` on Linux only, and the Windows job runs `node --test` with eight named files, well within the limit.

Other Windows contributors have met the same error and worked around it in their own pull requests, each in a different way (batches or globs): #1565, #1584, #1593, #1628 and #1630.

### Steps to reproduce

1. On Windows, fresh clone and `npm ci`.
2. Run `npm test`.
3. The runner exits at once with `spawnSync ... ENAMETOOLONG`; no test runs.

### How you installed

Terminal (git clone + npm)

### OS, Node version, browser

Subject: Suggestion for Project Name Update & Web Demo Link

Hi everyone,

I hope you’re doing well.

I’d like to share a quick feedback regarding the project name "God's-Eye View". From a cultural and religious perspective, using the phrase "God's Eye" can be seen as sensitive or inappropriate for Muslim users and audiences, as it attributes divine terms to technology.
