title: fix(earthquakes): exclude catalogued blasts from earthquake counts
body:
## What this changes

The shared USGS source now respects `properties.type` when selecting M2.5+ earthquakes. The map, analyst records and `get_earthquakes` follow the same filter. A later poll removes an event if USGS reclassifies it. Snapshots with a missing or null type retain the previous magnitude-only behavior. A malformed non-string type rejects the snapshot so the map keeps its last good data.

I found this while comparing how [LALO’s USGS adapter](https://github.com/ariannamethod/LALO/blob/f79272ae6c2a78acf595a5325fd810d9c12d62d0/src/sources/usgs.js) preserves each event’s source classification. A historical reproduction uses USGS event [uw62216847](https://earthquake.usgs.gov/earthquakes/eventpage/uw62216847), the M2.8 explosion near Benton City, Washington. On `7ee7dc26`, replaying its type, magnitude and location made `get_earthquakes` count it and name it the strongest earthquake. The fix uses the `earthquake` class from the [USGS catalog's event-type selector](https://earthquake.usgs.gov/earthquakes/search/).

## Verification on `d0581b08`

Includes upstream `745c1196` (#1560). All 200 focused tests passed across earthquakes, query tools, the local MCP server, layer state and the orbital view. `git diff --check` passed. All four [upstream CI checks](https://github.com/bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view/actions/runs/42543399051) passed. The Node 24 job passed 11,475 tests, skipped 3 and built the production bundle. All three new earthquake regressions failed on the original upstream revision before the fix.

### Chromium tracking comparison before the #1560 sync

The PR (`77ab27d3`) and its unmodified upstream base (`a274d100`) ran in separate checkouts on the same GitHub runner with the same Chromium, offline imagery and 500 ms limit. Both finished with 107 passed, 2 failed and 0 skipped. Both timed out on the same flight and military arrival observations. [Paired run and logs](https://github.com/ariannamethod/gods-eye-view/actions/runs/42541994323/job/128918736778)

| Revision | Flights | Military |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| PR `77ab27d3` | 558.3 ms | 663.8 ms |
| Upstream `a274d100` | 545.8 ms | 637.1 ms |

Earlier tracking runs recorded the same two timeouts on [`ebc7a28`](https://github.com/ariannamethod/gods-eye-view/actions/runs/42529877848/job/128881492730) and [`8e8e02c5`](https://github.com/ariannamethod/gods-eye-view/actions/runs/42531670198/job/128887003631). An earlier [control on `7ee7dc26`](https://github.com/ariannamethod/gods-eye-view/actions/runs/42530368422) passed all 109 checks.

title: Layer state keeps only layers the application registered
body:
## What this changes

An application that registers fewer layers than Core ships (an embedder with a smaller catalog) could still carry a layer it doesn't have. If a share link or saved state from a full build enabled that layer, the layer was skipped on restore, but its id stayed in the durable layer state. It was then written to local storage and put back into every link that application shared.

`LayerStateCoordinator` now drops enabled-layer ids the application did not register before it normalizes a share, saved state or explicit change. Dependent options (a tracked selection) go with them. Registrations are already final when the coordinator starts (`registrationsFinalized`), so the registered set is complete. An application with every layer registered is unchanged.

## How I verified it

- [x] `npm run build`
- [x] `npm test` (11,180 pass)
- [ ] `npm run test:track`: not run; tracking is unchanged in a full application (the new filter removes nothing there)
- [x] Feature gate for the area I touched: `src/data/layerState.test.mjs`. A new test covers share, explicit change, hash navigation and saved state with a layer left out; it fails without the fix. A second test shows a full application keeps every requested layer.

title: fix(test): batch parallel unit test paths under the Windows argv limit (#1631)
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #1631: `npm test` died on Windows with `spawnSync ... ENAMETOOLONG` before any test ran, because `scripts/run-unit-tests.mjs` passed every parallel test path to a single `node --test` spawn - at this suite's size (~950 paths) that argv is ~33.8k characters, over Windows' 32,767-character command-line limit.

The runner now shards the parallel files into batches whose full spawned command line (executable, shared flags, and per-argument quoting included) stays under a 24,000-character budget, then runs one `node --test` per batch in order. Every batch runs even after a failure and the runner exits with the first non-zero status - the same semantics as the single pre-existing invocation, just under the platform limit. An empty plan spawns nothing, so a bare `node --test` can never fall back to Node's default discovery. Batching is unconditional, so the Windows-safe path is the only path; Linux/macOS runs exercise it too.

`src/unitTestRunner.test.mjs` gains tests that pin the contract: against the real suite, batches flatten back to the full ordered list with nothing lost or duplicated and every batch measures under the budget and under the Windows limit; a fixed synthetic oversized suite (500 fixed-length paths, ~41k characters on any machine, independent of suite size and `process.execPath`) is asserted to need several batches; and degenerate inputs (empty list, single over-budget path) behave.

## How I verified it

- `npm test` (Node 24.14.0): full unit suite green through the sharded path (2 parallel batches, 11,324 tests, 0 failures)
- Runner unit tests: `node --test src/unitTestRunner.test.mjs` - 7/7 pass
- Wall-clock on this Linux machine: `npm test` 621s on main (single spawn) vs 621s on this branch (2 batches) - no measurable difference
- `npm run build` (Node 24.14.0) - built clean
- `npm run test:track` (dev server running) - not run: no runtime behavior changed
- Feature gate for the area I touched: none applies (test tooling only)
- Windows: not run - no Windows machine available. The fix targets the documented 32,767-character limit; the spawned command line is accounted for exactly (executable, flags, separators, per-path quotes) and held under a 24,000-character budget, so the failing spawn cannot get near the limit. A confirmation from a Windows checkout would still be useful.

## Docs

`docs/CURRENT-STATE.md` update not needed (no runtime behavior change); `changelog.d/` fragment added in this PR.

title: Draw rows take an application's own actions
body:
## What

UTILITIES ▸ Draw rows can carry buttons that an application supplies. Pass them as
`createApplicationTools({ drawMarkActions })`. Each action looks like this:

```js
{
  id: 'measure',               // [a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,39}, unique
  icon: 'straighten',          // Material Symbols name
  label: (name) => `Measure ${name}`,
  shapes: ['area', 'line'],    // what it is offered on; pins get nothing
  accepts: (geometry, shape) => geometry.type === 'Polygon',   // optional
  run: ({ id, shape, name, title, geometry }) => '12 km²' | Promise<string>,
}
```

- **Names.** `name` is the name the person typed. `title` is what the row shows, e.g.
  `Line · 950 m`.
- **Geometry.** `geometry` comes from `drawMarkGeometry`. It uses `[lon, lat]` degrees, with
  longitudes wrapped into [-180, 180]:
  - an area is a closed `Polygon`, or a `MultiPolygon` when an area handle has several parts;
  - a line is a `LineString`.
- **No geometry, no actions.** A pin has no geometry. Neither does a shape that crosses the
  antimeridian, or one with a part (a hole, say) that can't be passed whole. None of these is
  offered any action.
- **The row's note.** Whatever `run` returns, or resolves to, becomes a short note under the row
  (`role=status`). A note over 200 characters is cut at a word, with an ellipsis.
- **Busy rows.** The row is busy (`aria-disabled`) until the action settles, and a busy row
  ignores another press.
- **Failures.** If the action throws or rejects, the note is cleared and the error is logged.
  An action should therefore word its own refusals and resolve with them.
- **Removed shapes.** A note is dropped when its shape is removed, so a late answer never lands
  on a removed shape.
- **Bad actions.** Malformed actions and repeated ids are dropped once, at construction.

The standalone shell passes no actions. The open-source build therefore looks and behaves
exactly as before: no new button and no new request.

## Why

An application built on Core can act on a shape the person drew without forking Draw. It can
send the shape to its own service, or run its own analysis on it, and show the result on the
shape's row.

## Tests

- `src/annotations/drawMarks.test.mjs`:
  - the geometry, including wrapping, the antimeridian, and holes that can't be passed whole;
  - the action checks and the offers.
- `src/annotations/drawToolBehaviour.test.mjs`:
  - rows show actions only for the shapes they are for;
  - `run` receives the shape;
  - a throwing label or run is handled;
  - notes, busy state, cutting long notes, and late answers after a removal.
- `src/ui/views/panels/DrawMarkList.test.mjs`:
  - the buttons sit before Fly to;
  - labels, `aria-disabled` and the note.
- Results: `npm test` passed, as did `npm run format:check` and `npm run check:boundaries`.

Docs: `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md`, under UTILITIES ▸ Draw.
Changelog fragment: `changelog.d/<PR>-draw-mark-actions.md`, added once the PR number is known.

title: Orbital cockpit follow-ups: sensor strip through zoom, one owner-flag sheet, place names in the loading status
body:
These are follow-ups to the orbital cockpit stack (#1557, #1558, #1559, #1560, #1580). Each one comes from that stack's review.

- **Sensor strip through a zoom step.** The sensor strip is now measured against the footprint the view is showing. Before, it used the unzoomed footprint, so the strip jumped while a zoom step animated. Switching satellites resets the stored field of view.
- **Owner flags in one generated sheet.** `scripts/build-owner-flags.mjs` rasterises the flag-icons 4x3 SVGs for `OWNER_COUNTRY_CODES` into one 15 KB PNG (`src/data/local_data/owner_flags/owner_flags.png`) and writes `src/ui/ownerFlagSheet.js`. The output is the same byte for byte on every run. The sheet loads at startup. If it fails, the badge falls back to the country code, and the next ride asks for the sheet again. `flag-icons` moves to devDependencies, and the boundary gate's dependency-asset exemption is removed because nothing needs it now.
- **"Place names" in the loading status.** The place-name packs (countries and seas, divisions, populated places) still load lazily on the first lookup. While they load, the status shows "Place names", translated in all 11 locales. A lookup that loads several packs counts as one load, so the status does not show LOAD COMPLETE between packs. A pack that fails ends the load LOAD FAILED. A later load starts with no failures, so a retry that succeeds ends LOAD COMPLETE.
- **Pre-load level test.** The test for the level loaded ahead of the view now checks a worked number instead of recomputing it with the function under test.

Testing: build, `format:check`, `check:boundaries`, `i18n` and `npm test` (11,509 tests, 0 failures) all pass. In the browser, the flag sheet loads at startup, and a Paris lookup showed "LOADING LIVE DATA · PLACE NAMES" and then "LOAD COMPLETE".

title: fix(voice): send OpenAI Realtime tool schemas the API accepts
body:
## Problem

Voice never connects with an OpenAI API key. The mic shows "Realtime connection: Failed to create Realtime token" and the server logs `[realtime-token] upstream HTTP 400` (#1618). The body OpenAI returns:

```
invalid_function_parameters · param=session.tools[29].parameters
Invalid schema for function 'resolve_area': '^ne:(?:country|state|county|natural):[\\p{L}\\p{M}\\p{N}]+(?:-[\\p{L}\\p{M}\\p{N}]+)*$' is not a 'regex'.
```

This is the pattern #1616 fixed for typed chat. #1616 noted that Realtime accepted it at the time. It no longer does: OpenAI rejects the whole session, so no tool works.

## Fix

`server/providers/openai/realtime.js` now builds the session's tools through `realtimeSessionTools()`. That function keeps the existing `offeredTools` selection, then passes each schema through `chatSchema`, the filter from #1616 that drops only `\p{…}`/`\P{…}` patterns. `resolve_area` still checks area ids against its own contract before it runs, so the model loses a hint, not a rule. I also updated the `chatSchema` doc comment, which said Realtime keeps these patterns.

## Verification

- I sent the session GEV builds (`gpt-realtime-2`, 34 tools) to `https://api.openai.com/v1/realtime/client_secrets`: 400 before the fix, 200 after. Bisecting the tools isolates the error to `resolve_area` alone. After the fix, `/api/realtime/token` mints a secret for both the `standard` and `mini` tiers, and voice sessions run with tool calls in Chrome.
- `src/tooling/localServices.test.mjs` has a new test: the Realtime session still offers `resolve_area`, and no schema carries a `\p{` pattern. The test fails without the fix. Four existing assertions compared the session tools to the unfiltered list; they now compare to `realtimeSessionTools(...)`.
- `npm run format:check`, `npm run build` and `npm test` pass.
- `npm run test:track`: 108 passed, 1 failed (`arrival: moveEnd + first reveal both re-aim before idle refresh … exceeded 500 ms`). The same check fails on unmodified `main` (027c961) on the same machine (headless Chrome, Apple M4), so it is a timing issue on this machine, not something this change causes.

Gemini Live voice is unchanged. I haven't checked whether Gemini accepts these patterns.

Fixes #1618

title: fix(flights): read an unreported altitude as unknown, not FL328
body:
An airborne contact whose feed never sent a barometric altitude was stored with the 10 km render default as its aviation altitude. The tracked readout said "FL328", the Cockpit read 32,808 ft, and the voice context said "32,808 ft", for a plane that may be drawn at its 3 km GPS height.

**Flights** (`records.js`, `tracking.js`, `queries.js`)
- The record keeps that altitude `null` and uses 10 km only as the render height.
- The tracked readout says "Alt unknown" (the military layer's wording), and the context altitude is empty.
- `_describeFlight` returns `altitudeM: null`, so the Cockpit shows the altitude as unavailable.
- The follow camera frames by the render height when the altitude is unknown, so a plane drawn at its 3 km GPS height is framed at about 5.8 km instead of the 13.5 km the 10 km default gave.
- Grounded contacts (0 m) and a baro dropout after a report (sticky last value) are unchanged.

**Military** (`queries.js`): `_describeFlight` read `info.altitudeM`, but military records store only `altitudeFt`. So the Cockpit and voice always got the render height instead: a geoid-corrected or GPS height, or the 3,048 m airborne default. It now converts `altitudeFt` to meters, as the layer's analyst records already do, and returns `null` when the altitude is unknown.

**Not changed:** the agent tools' `altitude_m` (`src/tools/queries/aviation.js:75`) still falls back to the GPS (ellipsoid) height when baro is missing. A plane the app labels "Alt unknown" can therefore have a GPS-based altitude in `aircraft_in_area`. I left that alone because the tool reports a measured height and says nothing about flight level.

**Tests**
- New cases in `flights/records.test.mjs`, `ownership.test.mjs` and `queries.test.mjs`, plus a new `military/queries.test.mjs` (adopted in `format-scope.json`).
- Each fails on `main`.
- Full unit suite: 11,516 pass on Windows 11, Node 24.16. `npm test` itself currently fails on Windows with `ENAMETOOLONG`, because the runner passes all 962 test paths in one command, so I ran the same plan in batches.
- `format:check`, `check:boundaries`, `i18n` and `build` pass.

title: fix(hud): show a sun just below the horizon as 0°, not -0°
body:
A sun just below the horizon printed a negative zero in two HUD readouts:
- The summary rounds the elevation with `Math.round`, so −0.3° became `-0` and the summary read `SUN -0°`.
- The corner readout uses `toFixed(1)`, so −0.04° printed `SUN: -0.0° EL`.

Both now add `+ 0` after rounding, which turns −0 into 0 and leaves every other value unchanged. The corner readout keeps `toFixed`'s rounding, so −0.25° still reads `-0.3`.

**Tests:** two live-HUD cases in `src/hudAltitudeDatum.test.mjs`. The summary at −0.3° must read `SUN 0°`; the corner readout at −0.04° must read `0.0`, while −0.3° and −0.25° must still read `-0.3`. Both fail on `main`. The full unit suite passes (11,519, Windows 11, Node 24.16, run in batches until #1635 lands), as do `format:check`, `check:boundaries`, `i18n` and `build`.

title: Applications can take the pointer for their own tool
body:
## What

`createApplicationTools` returns `pointer`, the pointer claim the layers and tools already share (`data/inputOwnership.js`):

- `claim(owner)` takes the pointer as Draw does and returns its lease, or `null` while another tool holds it.
- `release(lease)` gives it back. Only the lease that took it can release it.
- `isFree()` lets the application's own click handlers yield while a tool holds the pointer, as the layers do.

An owner without a name in `pointerOwnerNames.js` is named by its id when another tool reports who holds the pointer.

## Why

An application that adds its own tool on the globe needs clicks to belong to that tool alone: a click on an aircraft is the tool's click, not a selection. Until now only built-in tools could take the claim.

## Changed since the first version

This PR first added `drawShape`, which ran a one-shot session of Draw. That is removed: Draw is unchanged from `main`, and the PR now only exposes the claim.

## Files

- `src/app/tools.js`: returns `pointer`.
- `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`.

## Checks

`node --import=./build/registerVue.js --test src/annotations/*.test.mjs src/app/*.test.mjs src/data/inputOwnership*.test.mjs`: 354 pass. The full suite runs in CI.

title: Keep vehicles off rooftops and bridge decks by reading the 3D-tile surface where each vehicle is
body:
## What this changes

With photoreal 3D tiles on, buses and trains were drawn at rooftop or garage height, or sunk under viaducts and inside bridge decks: about 49 m above Boylston St, 11 m above Haymarket (on the garage deck), 6 m under the Lechmere Viaduct deck and 10–11 m inside the Longfellow Bridge.

**Cause.** The ground floor took one rendered-mesh probe at the centre of each 0.001° cell (about 110 × 80 m), accepted it up to 80 m above the DEM, and kept it for the session. Every vehicle in the cell inherited whatever surface lay under the cell centre: a roof, the river, or the street beside a viaduct.

**Fix.**
- The sampler probes the mesh at the vehicle's own point. A cell with a reading is probed again only at spots at least about 17 m from earlier ones, eight at most. A spot refused only because the cell's DEM prior was cold or evicted is tried again later.
- The floor keeps each reading that passes the gate at the point it was taken (two within about 5 m keep the lower; sixteen at most per cell) and answers a read from the reading nearest the asked point, so a viaduct and the street beside it in one cell keep their own heights.
- Transit offers the sampler the latest point of each vehicle's path in a cell, and the newest fix in the vehicle's own cell (it used to offer the oldest). The grounded-flight display clamp reads at the aircraft's own position, held inside its sticky cell.

## How I verified it

- [x] `npm run build`
- [x] `npm test`: 11573 pass, 0 fail; `check:boundaries` and `format:check` pass
- [x] `npm run test:track` (`--offline-imagery`): 109/0 on main and on this branch
- [x] Feature gate: `node scripts/qa-transit.mjs`, without a Google key on both builds: the same checks fail on main and on the branch (frame and allocation budgets at 800/3000 vehicles, style colour tolerances, Google 3D checks that need the key); none is new. A lone branch rerun passed all 7 mouse-click selections.

**Fixed markers on photoreal**, height above the surface directly under the point (the intended lift is 1.5 m):

| Site | main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| Haymarket street (2 points) | +11.8 / +11.4 | +1.5 / +1.5 |
| Lechmere Viaduct deck (2) | −6.4 / −6.6 | +1.5 / +1.5 |
| O'Brien Hwy beside the viaduct | +1.8 | +1.5 |
| Longfellow Bridge deck (2) | −10.5 / −11.3 | +1.5 / +1.5 |
| Boylston St (cell centre on a roof) | +49.2 | +1.5 |
| Open street (control) | −0.5 | +1.5 |

**Live MBTA vehicles downtown**, 19 shown on each build: 9 of 19 within 0–3 m of the surface on main (worst +75.8 m and −47 m), 16 of 19 on this branch.

**Cost**, 150 s windows, same view, alternating builds: about 35% more probes and about 50% more probe time (about 1.6 ms per second), still bounded by the existing 40-probe-per-poll budget.

**Limits**
- A vehicle whose reported position falls on a building lower than the 80 m gate is drawn on that roof (one bus downtown, reported about 20 m inside the building).
- A vertical probe can still hit a deck or overhang above the road.
- The floor steps when the nearest reading changes; the flight clamp has no smoothing between readings.
- A cell whose eight probe spots were all refused can be left with a single reading; a cell with sixteen readings stores no new spots.

## Docs

- [x] `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md` updated and a `changelog.d/<pr-number>-<slug>.md` fragment added

title: .env Reorg: Keep API keys in .env.local and settings in .env
body:
## What this changes

Keys and settings shared one `.env`, so anything that touched a setting
touched every key too: sharing a config, pasting it into an issue, backing it
up, or letting a coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, Copilot …) open the file to
change a port. Every one of those is a way for a key to leak.

This gives keys their own file, `.env.local`, and leaves `.env` for settings,
so the keys file can be locked down without getting in the way of ordinary
configuration:

- `npm run env:init` and Provider Settings create it owner-only (`0600`, on
  Linux and macOS).
- An AI agent can be kept out of it entirely (a deny rule in the agent's own
  settings, or running the agent as a user with no read access to that one
  file) while it still reads and edits `.env` and the code. This PR was built
  that way: the agent that wrote the code was blocked from `.env.local` by a
  rule in its settings.
- The template's SECRETS banner tells users, scripts and AI assistants never
  to read, print, log or commit those values.

Vite already loads the whole dotenv ladder (`.env`, then `.env.local` over
it), so the app needs no new loader: this splits the template, the writers and
the docs along that line.

- `.env.example` opens with a contents list, a **SECRETS** section (every
  key, each with a "Get one:" link; now including `GITHUB_TOKEN` and
  `TFL_APP_KEY`) and a **SETTINGS** section, which also gains seven settings
  the server reads but the template never listed.
- `src/secretEnv.mjs` holds the one list of secret names; a test keeps the
  template, the setup doctor and Provider Settings to it.
- `npm run env:init` creates `.env.local` (owner-only) and `.env` from the
  template when missing, and moves every key line it finds in `.env` into
  `.env.local`, into that key's placeholder line. Names only are printed;
  `--dry-run` previews; a rerun is a no-op.
- Provider Settings saves keys to `.env.local` and removes them from `.env`.
- The setup doctor names the file each key came from and warns while a key
  is still in `.env`.
- The `tools/` scripts read the Google key through the dotenv ladder; the
  launchers stop passing OpenSky's retired username/password; the Pinokio
  `ENVIRONMENT` template gets the same two sections.
- Docs and server comments: `.env.local` for keys, `.env` for settings.

**Existing installs keep working.** Keys left in `.env` still load, the
doctor warns about them, and `npm run env:init` moves them. Per key name, the
line with a value is the one kept:

| `.env` | `.env.local` | result |
|---|---|---|
| value | blank placeholder / absent | the line takes the placeholder's place (appended if none) |
| blank | value | value kept; blank line leaves `.env` |
| blank | blank | placeholder stays; line leaves `.env` |
| value | same value | line leaves `.env` |
| value | different value | `.env.local` stays live (it already wins today); the `.env` value is kept beneath it as a comment and the run says CHECK |
| value set more than once | — | the **last** value is the live one (what dotenv loads today); earlier values are kept in `.env.local` as comments and the run lists the name |

Thanks @kvnloo for catching the repeated-key case in review (a7449f5).

**For PRs that add a variable** (several open ones touch `.env.example` —
#625 and #1571 add keys): a key goes in SECTION 1 and its name in
`SECRET_ENV_NAMES` (`src/secretEnv.mjs`); a setting goes in SECTION 2. A
key-shaped name left in SETTINGS fails a test whose message says exactly that.

Not in this PR:
- (pre-existing, separate fix) `scripts/dev-secure.sh` exports the OpenSky
  OAuth variables empty when unset, which shadows values from the dotenv files.
- (possible follow-up) The repo has no `AGENTS.md`, so coding agents only meet
  the "keys live in `.env.local`; never read or print them" rule if they open
  `.env.example`. A few lines there, or in your existing agent docs, would
  cover it — happy to send that separately if you want it.

## How I verified it

Debian 13 LXC, Node 24.22.2, npm 11.19.1, on head `d5d461c` (merged with
`main` at `41c7922`).

- [x] `npm run build` — success
- [x] `npm test` — 15,919 tests, 0 failures
- [x] `npm run test:track` (dev server running) — 110 passed, 1 failed
  (Debian Chromium 156 via `PUPPETEER_EXECUTABLE_PATH`, against a
  `localhost` dev server). The one failure, "trail head: last vertex on the
  drawn icon", fails the same way on `main` at `41c7922` (110 passed,
  1 failed), so it does not come from this PR.
- [x] The full CI workflow on my fork (both Node jobs, Windows onboarding,
  Street Level browser gate) — green:
  https://github.com/BeerMan81/gods-eye-view/actions/runs/44803734412
  (the Street Level gate on its second attempt; the first failed one Cesium
  check, `globe.imagery.video`, "early in the segment", which passes on `main`)
- [x] Feature gate: none covers key setup; ran the CI checks
  `format:check`, `check:boundaries`, `layer-token:check --base-ref
  origin/main`, plus `env:init` end to end with fake keys in a throwaway
  root: an upgrade from the old single-file template, and every row of the
  table above (incl. `export` and commented lines, CRLF, multi-line values),
  the doctor before and after, a key repeated in `.env`, and a rerun.
  Mutation checks: disabling the in-place fill, the blank rule or the
  conflict rule each fails the tests.

Changelog fragment: `changelog.d/1644-secrets-env-local.md`.

title: perf(traffic): build road lines one set at a time
body:
With Lines on, every progressive paint of a loading city rebuilt all road lines: up to three ground-line primitives for as many as 1,500 roads, built asynchronously. Builds started faster than they finished, and each kept the set it replaced in the scene until it was ready, so sets piled up.

Now one set builds at a time. A rebuild asked for while lines are building replaces the one waiting, and the newest starts when the build finishes. Lines replaced by a finished build are removed before the next one starts. Turning Lines off removes the lines at once and drops the waiting rebuild.

## Measured

Traffic fixtures in headless Chromium, a 15 s pan with Lines on (all ground primitives counted):

| | Primitives added | Most in the scene | Most building at once |
|---|---|---|---|
| `main` | 87 | 44 | 21 |
| This change | 10 | 3 | 2 |

Both end with the same 83 lines.

## Tests

- New `src/layers/traffic/lineRebuild.test.mjs`: rebuilds asked for during a build are coalesced, the newest request wins, Lines off is immediate, and no replaced set stays in the scene. Six of its seven tests fail on `main`.
- Feature gates run: `scripts/qa-traffic.mjs --fixtures` (11 pass, 1 inconclusive: the quota check, which fixtures cannot exercise) and `npm run test:track` (109 passed).
- `npm test` (11,594 pass), `npm run build`, `npm run format:check`, `npm run check:boundaries`, `npm run layer-token:check` and `npm run doctor` pass.

Not checked on a real GPU or against live flow for a 1,500-road city; the fixtures give about 90 lines.

`docs/CURRENT-STATE.md` is updated.

title: bug: keyless search sends "Heathrow" to Florida
body:
### What happened

With no Google key, searching "Heathrow" puts the camera on Heathrow, Florida, a locality near Orlando. I expected London's airport.

### Steps to reproduce

1. No Google key configured, so search goes through Photon.
2. Search "Heathrow".
3. The camera lands in Florida, wherever it started from.

I first saw this in the app on 2026-10-19. For this report I measured it by asking Photon directly, with the URL `photonSearchUrl` builds, and by reading `src/keylessGeocoder.js` at the commit below.

### Measured cause

Photon returns Heathrow, Florida first for `q=Heathrow`: with no position, with a position over Austin, and with a position over Paris.

```text
q=Heathrow&limit=5
  Heathrow | place=locality | Florida, United States
  Heathrow | place=locality | Florida, United States
  Heathrow Terminal 5 | railway=station | London Borough of Hillingdon, United Kingdom

q=Heathrow&limit=5&lat=48.85&lon=2.35
```

title: Show the tracked aircraft's Planespotters photo in Contacts
body:
## What this changes

Tracking a civil flight now shows a photo of that aircraft. The browser asks [Planespotters](https://www.planespotters.net/photo/api) for it directly, once per aircraft, and the CONTEXT panel's CONTACTS view shows it under the flight's name.

- **Attribution.** The thumbnail is hotlinked from the URL the API gives. The photographer is named in visible text ("Photo © {photographer}"), and the photo and credit are a plain link to the photo's Planespotters page (`rel="noopener"`, never `nofollow`).
- **Only Planespotters.** `src/data/planespottersPhoto.js` accepts an image only on `https://*.plnspttrs.net` and a page only on `https://www.planespotters.net`, with a named photographer. Anything else is dropped.
- **Who gets one.** The tracked civil flight only. Vessels, installations, military aircraft and a converted TR-3B show none, and military aircraft and TR-3B are never looked up.
- **No key, no proxy.** The API answers cross-origin, so the standalone source calls it from the browser with an 8-second timeout.

It also hardens the flights layer's lookups (type, route, photo):

- A lookup whose source failed temporarily (an outage, a timeout, a rate limit, an authorization refusal that may clear) is asked again after a 60-second cool-down. Until now one failure meant no answer for the rest of the session. An answer, found or not, and a permanent refusal such as a 404 stay final.
- The tracked aircraft re-asks on each snapshot, so a failed lookup recovers without re-selecting it.
- A route belongs to the callsign it was looked up for. A callsign change drops the old route and airline, and a late answer for the old callsign is ignored.

`parsePlanespottersPhoto` is exported as `gods-eye-view/sources/planespotters`. It reads the API's answer, and also the same answer after a server has cached it, so a deployment that proxies the lookup can reuse the checks.

Browser QA scripts that track a flight now answer the photo lookup themselves (`scripts/qa-photo-stub.mjs`), so QA never calls the third party.

## How I verified it

- [x] `npm run build`
- [x] `npm test` (11,621 pass, 0 fail)
- [x] `npm run test:track` (dev server running): 106 pass, 3 fail. All three are the "no console errors" checks, and each reports only a 403 from Google's 3D Tiles for the Maps key in my local `.env`. No tracking, trail or photo check fails.
- [x] `npm run format:check`, `npm run check:boundaries`, `npm run i18n` (all 11 locales complete)
- [x] In Chrome on a live feed: tracked airliners show the photo, credit and link in CONTACTS; an aircraft with no Planespotters photo shows none. A direct request from the page to `api.planespotters.net` returned 200 with CORS headers.

title: feat(search): find a loaded aircraft by flight number (#1562)
body:
## What this changes

Typing a flight number into the location search now follows the aircraft flying it, when that aircraft is already on the map. Closes #1562.

- `src/data/flightNumber.js` parses IATA flight numbers (`BA 123`, `a3-602`, `U2 1234`) and ICAO callsigns (`BAW123`) into exact callsigns.
- IATA airline codes resolve through the existing adsbdb proxy, which gains `/api/adsbdb/airline/<code>` (validated, cached 24 h like the route and type lookups). A reassigned code yields one callsign per airline; only an aircraft actually broadcasting one of them decides.
- Only the enabled Flights and Military layers are searched, and only an exact callsign matches (`BAW12` never answers for `BAW123`).
  - One match: followed with origin `user`, toast "Tracking UAL100 (UA 100)".
  - Several matches: the field lists their callsigns and follows none.
  - No match: the text falls through to place search, so a road such as "A10" still works. Only when no place answers does the field say why: Flights layer off, unknown airline code, code lookup unavailable, or no aircraft on the map.
- Following starts after the lookup reports `found`, because a user track supersedes pending location work and would otherwise cancel the search that started it.
- No new provider, key or bundled data: aircraft come from the existing OpenSky / adsb.lol layers and airline codes from adsbdb, already listed in `DATA_SOURCES.md` (row updated).

Not in this PR: voice does not use the resolver yet; airline-name queries ("British Airways 123") are not supported because adsbdb has no name search; callsigns that do not follow the flight number (`EZY12AB`) are found by callsign only; aircraft outside the loaded snapshot are #1563.

title: fix(firms): label a snapshot that ends at a set time with that time, not LIVE
body:
A FIRMS source may answer the 24 hours to a set time instead of the trailing 24 hours to now, naming the end of those 24 hours as `at` (epoch ms) in the payload. Until now such a snapshot still read as live.

- `ingestion.js` keeps `at` (a printable epoch-ms time) from the payload; `state.js`/`lifecycle.js` reset it, and a keyless answer clears it.
- `getStats()` reports `at`, labels the row "24 h to MM-DD HH:MM UTC" (day via `formatUtcDayMonth`, per locale) and names the source `NASA FIRMS`, so the catalog's `NASA FIRMS · LIVE` no longer leads the row: it reads `NASA FIRMS · 24 h to 10-21 15:00 UTC`. Loading, KEY REQUIRED, STALE and errors still take precedence.
- `get_active_fires` says "in the 24 hours to" that time and reports it as `window_end`.
- A snapshot without `at` (the trailing 24 hours to now, as the dev proxy serves) is unchanged.
- The new string is translated in all 11 catalogs (`npm run i18n` complete); `server/providers/firms.js` and `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md` document the field; changelog fragment added.

Tests: `src/layers/firms/windowLabel.test.mjs` (labels in English and German, `at`, source, LIVE returning without `at`) and `src/tools/queries/hazards.test.mjs` (summary and `window_end`); the FIRMS layer, i18n, tool and layer-panel suites pass.

title: feat: Singapore traffic cameras from data.gov.sg (keyless)
body:
### Problem

Singapore has no camera source. The government's real-time traffic images API is keyless and returns JPEG stills with coordinates.

### Proposal

A keyless source pack modelled on the Calgary pack:

- Catalog: `https://api.data.gov.sg/v1/transport/traffic-images`, one JSON request per refresh, capped and redirect-pinned like the other loaders.
- Frames pinned to `https://images.data.gov.sg/api/traffic-images/`.
- Stable ids from `camera_id` (`singapore-2701`), names from a short table with the evidence for each one.
- On by default (`CCTV_SINGAPORE_ENABLED=0` turns it off).

Three things I measured that shape the design:

1. **The feed shrank.** With `date_time`, it returned 90 cameras on 2026-06-15 and 8 on 2026-07-01 and every date I checked since: 3 at Woodlands (2701, 2702, 2704), 3 at Tuas (4703, 4712, 4713) and 2 near Sentosa Gateway (4798, 4799). The full expressway set is on LTA DataMall behind an AccountKey. I'd keep this PR keyless and do DataMall as a separate opt-in pack, if you want it.
2. **Frames come back as `application/octet-stream`**, not `image/jpeg`, so the still-frame fetch in `server/providers/cctv/media.js` rejects them today and the panel would show the fallback image. My plan is a check for this one origin only: accept `octet-stream` from `images.data.gov.sg` when the body starts with the JPEG signature (`FF D8 FF`). Is that the approach you'd want, or would you handle it another way?
3. **The image URL changes with every snapshot** (about every 1 to 2 minutes), while the catalog refreshes every 15 minutes. Old links keep working (a 27-day-old one still returned 200), so frames would be up to 15 minutes stale. I'd resolve the current link per camera at frame time with a short single-flight cache, like Ottawa's 60-second floor.

### Data source, license, and attribution

- Publisher: Land Transport Authority, through data.gov.sg.
- License: Singapore Open Data Licence v1.0 (https://data.gov.sg/open-data-licence). It allows commercial and non-commercial use and redistribution, with a notice and a link to the licence.
- Attribution: "Contains information from Traffic Images accessed on {date} from data.gov.sg which is made available under the terms of the Singapore Open Data Licence version 1.0".
- Keyless. No rate limit is documented; the pack makes one catalog request per refresh.

### Will you build it?

Yes. I'll follow `docs/CCTV_INTEGRATION.md`, with tests under `src/data/` and the `DATA_SOURCES.md` entry.

title: feat(flights): trails split at gaps and follow the aircraft; a lost aircraft coasts, then reads SIGNAL LOST
body:
## What this changes

A tracked flight's trail used to join its whole day of history into one line, so it drew straight lines across oceans and back to earlier legs, cut corners through turns, and kept a lost aircraft frozen in mid-air with no cue. Now:

**Gaps break the line.** Between two trail points the pen lifts when time does not move forward, the gap is over 48 minutes, the implied speed is over 1,500 kt, or either point has no altitude. A pair under 3 hours apart and within 0.1 nm (a parked aircraft) stays joined. Every history point is kept, each leg drawn as its own segment, and nothing is drawn across a break. A history point without altitude is never given an invented one (the old 10 km fallback is gone). The rules live in `src/data/trailContinuity.js` and apply to flights and military alike.

**The live end follows the aircraft.** The trail records the path the icon is actually drawn along, thinned to its shape (30 m off the line, at most one point per 10 km on a straight), so it no longer cuts a chord across a turn. A report that arrives late, or one that is not the same flight as the previous report under the speed rule, trims what was drawn after it, so there is no spur or V. The head to the aircraft is not drawn across a break or from more than 150 km away.

**Cheap to draw.** Old segments are frozen in 128-point chunks (`src/data/trailRenderer.js`); only the newest chunk and the head change per frame. At the 2,000-point limit a frame costs about 0.1 ms instead of about 3 ms.

**A lost aircraft says so.** A tracked aircraft that misses an update (including a feed re-sending the same old fix) shows STALE and is dimmed. It keeps flying on its last speed and heading for five minutes, at most 1,500 kt, then stops, dimmed, with its label reading `SIGNAL LOST · <n> min` counted from its last report (new i18n key, all 12 locales). It is kept for ten minutes after that report so the camera keeps its target, then removed. Aircraft on or within 150 m of known ground hold at their last report instead of coasting, and never coast below the ground. Untracked aircraft keep their existing removal timing.

`scripts/qa-trail-freeze.mjs` checks that frozen chunks stay frozen while tracking.

## How I verified it

- [x] `npm run build`
- [x] `npm test`: 11,743 tests, 11,738 pass, 0 fail (5 skipped)
- [x] `npm run format:check`, `npm run check:boundaries`, `npm run i18n` (all 12 locales complete)
- [x] `npm run test:track` (dev server running): 111 pass, 0 fail. M3 now checks that the tracked aircraft stays tracked through three missed polls, then is released in place once the page clock passes ten minutes after its newest fix
- [x] On a live feed in a browser: airliners turning onto approach, a helicopter at 175 ft, and a cruise flight tracked for several minutes each. The trail stayed on the aircraft (its end 60–320 m behind the icon at that zoom), with no chords across turns and no lines across feed gaps. An aircraft dropped from the feed went STALE and dimmed, kept moving for five minutes, stopped as `SIGNAL LOST · 5 min`, stayed tracked to nine minutes, and was gone at ten.

title: fix(flights): a long flight keeps its route up to 15% of its length off the great circle
body:
## What this changes

A flight's route (origin and destination) is hidden when the aircraft's position does not fit it, so a wrong leg looked up by callsign is never shown. The check allowed at most 200 km off the great circle between the airports. That is too tight for long flights: airways and winds routinely take a coast-to-coast flight several hundred kilometres off it, so a real JFK→SFO flight over Kansas, 384 km south of the great circle, lost its route.

The tolerance is now **200 km or 15% of the route's length, whichever is larger** (`src/data/routePlausible.js`). JFK–SFO (4,152 km) allows 623 km; SFO–LAX (543 km) still allows 200 km. The 130 km endpoint rule, the along-track extension and the vertical-trend check are unchanged.

## How I verified it

title: perf: bound layer memory and sharpen aircraft rendering
body:
## What this changes

Dense maps retained offscreen native objects, decoded media and repeated per-frame work. Bound that work while preserving complete logical contact populations, search, tracking and existing update cadence, with Standard mode continuing to target 60 FPS.

- Aircraft use viewport-bounded native residents plus a shared full-display-resolution GPU surface, keeping silhouettes crisp without scaling globe framebuffers. Bound asynchronous model loading, reject cancelled late results, and flush pending native references on final-resident removal.
- Surface teardown releases current and cached native collections on disable and public clear. Reset/source deletion invalidate previously painted pixels while other fleets remain visible.
- Grounded aircraft offer Show / Dim / Hide, defaulting to Dim, with tracked/cockpit exceptions and saved/shared settings. New controls are translated in every shipped language.
- Transit has one native marker ownership path for admission, migration, viewport release, ingestion eviction and disable. Per-collection counts eliminate repeated Cesium compaction while retaining global records and histories.
- Detection reuses exact projections/bracket paths and bounded raster caches. One cleanup path replaces duplicate clearing; aircraft eviction immediately removes cached detection objects, replacing threshold-triggered cleanup scans. Remove unused model-preload fields, assignments and teardown.
- Dispose inactive CCTV projection buffers/materials, trim paused weather decoding, compact infrastructure records and materialize native infrastructure/cable geometry in the viewport. Trim unused map/Google 3D tiles while retaining Standard detail settings.
- Reuse traffic detection contacts and settled positions; share satellite rotation calculations and localized labels. Low resource mode remains optional at 30 FPS.

## Plane resolution and resource use

The separate aircraft layer renders 2D planes at full display resolution while the globe uses a smaller framebuffer.

| Before: native Cesium aircraft | After: full-resolution aircraft layer |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: softer aircraft silhouettes](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/piersonmarks/gods-eye-view/88686503f7e50b05483b6b8cfc50164a189e9cd2/aircraft-before.png) | ![After: crisp full-resolution aircraft silhouettes](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/piersonmarks/gods-eye-view/88686503f7e50b05483b6b8cfc50164a189e9cd2/aircraft-after.png) |

Open the images at full resolution to see the edge detail. These historical captures use the same synthetic 200-plane scene at 1440 × 860 CSS pixels, DPR 2. The browser gate switches from native Cesium at 1.5× to the aircraft surface at 2× with the map at 1×; this is a renderer-path comparison within the candidate, not two upstream checkouts.

Separately measured paired production runs on the baseline M2 Pro/16 GiB laptop, same 10,000 visible aircraft:

| Measurement | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Total browser physical footprint | 1,570 MiB | 1,298 MiB (**17% lower**) |
| Sampled main-thread CPU | 74.7% | 57.6% (**23% lower**) |
| Frame rate | 54.8 FPS | 59.8 FPS |

These are five-second warmed observations, not universal guarantees; CPU is main-thread task time, not total system CPU. Screenshots show sharpness, while the separate workload measurements establish resource use. Full methodology and limits are in `docs/PERFORMANCE.md`. Screenshot assets are hosted separately from the code PR.

## Measurements

The methodology, scenarios, commands and limits are in `docs/PERFORMANCE.md`. Historical baseline-laptop workloads include:

| Scenario | Before → after |
| --- | --- |
| CCTV + models + weather footprint | 2507 → 1791 MiB (~29% lower) |
| Cable workload footprint | 3312 → 2202 MiB (~34% lower) |
| 10,000-aircraft footprint | 1570 → 1298 MiB (~17% lower) |
| 10,000-aircraft frame rate | 54.8 → 59.8 FPS |
| Combined traffic + satellites median main-thread task CPU | 41.7% → 35.8% (~14% lower), around 60 FPS |

Additional ownership measurements against `2d544996`:

- Real Cesium 10,000-contact retention fixture, three paired runs: retained native residents fall **10,000 → 0** after hide or clear. Hide preserves all 10,000 logical contacts and re-enable readmits them. Median retained heap falls **61,365,704 → 47,837,440 bytes** for hide and **54,316,368 → 40,548,096 bytes** for clear (roughly 13 MiB each).
- Real Cesium 8,192-marker ownership benchmark, median of five runs: release **165.292 → 2.543 ms**, migration **187.853 → 17.289 ms**. Length reads fall **8,192 → 0** and compaction traversals **33,558,528 slots → 0**; final pending references remain zero.
- The 3,000-vehicle browser fixture retains every analyst record, passes offscreen search/tracking/re-entry, and measures city samples **56.8/58.1/59.0 FPS**, street samples **60.0/60.0/60.0 FPS**.
- The unchanged 5,000-moving-contact allocation probe passes: median **209,338 B/frame**, versus **333,921 B/frame** on upstream before this ownership follow-up, with all brackets and 56 selected labels retained.

These are separate workloads, not additive savings or a demonstrated app-wide 75% reduction. The ownership benchmarks isolate native JS retention and CPU operations without WebGL; their gains are not whole-browser RAM/GPU or CPU percentages. title: Hide street-vehicle brackets and labels behind buildings and terrain
body:
## What this changes

Street Traffic marks its contacts `depthTested`, and the detection overlay now hides a depth-tested contact's bracket and callout while the scene drew a surface in front of it: a building, 3D tile, hill or tunnel roof. Before, only the Earth's curve hid a contact, so "VEH-nnnn" callouts were painted over facades and rooftops while the vehicle's own dot was correctly hidden. Other layers are unchanged; their markers draw over the scene on purpose.

The test runs on the GPU and never waits for it: one occlusion query per contact against the frame's pick depth, answers collected a frame or two later (0.3–0.5 ms a frame with ~500 contacts in view). A surface counts as in front once it stands more than 2 m above the vehicle on its line of sight (at least 3 m, at most 2% of the range). Contacts are retested every 100–200 ms (at most 256 a frame, slower when more are in view), hide at once, return 600 ms after the last "hidden", and a contact new to the view, or back in it, waits for its first answer. With no pick depth (2D, Columbus view, depth picking off) or a failed self-check, nothing is hidden. The renderer internals used are read in `readSceneDepthSource`, with the engine version they were checked against.

## How I verified it

- [x] `npm run build`
- [x] `npm test`
- [x] `npm run test:track` (dev server running)
- [x] Feature gate for the area I touched: photoreal downtown Boston, every contact's decision compared with `scene.pickPosition`; frame time compared with main (within about 2 ms at equal load, probe 0.3–0.5 ms a frame).

title: feat(live): flights, military and vessels follow the world clock; vessels keyed by source id; share a selected vessel
body:
## What this changes

Three changes to Flights, Military Flights and AIS Vessels, in two commits.

**Layers follow the world clock.** A live source may declare a timeline (`source.timeline`: `coverage()`, `stepMs` and an optional `subscribe`), read by `readSnapshotTimeline` from `gods-eye-view/sources/live`.
- Away from live, the layer shows the source's snapshot at the clock's time and moves on with it as it plays. Back at live it polls as before.
- `timeline.subscribe` lets a source say it has a better answer for a time it has already answered. While paused, the layer loads the time it shows again.
- A source with no timeline stays live, unchanged.

**Vessels are keyed by their source's stable id, not by MMSI.** An MMSI can be shared, spoofed, reused or left at a default such as 0, and a number can move to another hull.
- Two vessels with one MMSI are now two vessels, each selected, followed and carded on its own.
- `mmsi` is an attribute, shown when known. Looking a vessel up or selecting it by MMSI (an older link, say) still finds it.
- `vesselSnapshot` takes `idFor(row)`. Tool and voice results carry the vessel's id beside its MMSI, and `get_vessel_track` also takes an `id`.
- AISStream has only MMSIs, so nothing changes there.

**A share link made while a vessel is selected opens that vessel.**
- The link names the vessel, opens with the camera where it was, and selects the vessel once the feed has it.
- A UUID vessel id travels as its 16 bytes in a new thing field (13), documented in `docs/SHARE-LINK-FORMAT.md`. Existing links and ids are unchanged.
- A shared flight, military flight, vessel or satellite that isn't reporting now says so in a sentence per kind. Its id goes on a second line: ICAO, NORAD, MMSI or vessel UUID. The id used to open the sentence.

title: feat(weather): a host can supply decoded frames to the weather layers
body:
## Summary

A weather feed may now also be a frame source. Both methods are optional; a feed without them reads the image and tile routes exactly as before.

- `getFrameImage({ product, time, size, bbox, signal })`: the layers take whole-extent images, detail windows and the global mosaic from it.
- `getFrameTile({ product, time, z, x, y, size, signal })`: regional tiles and their prefetch come from it; `null` is a transparent tile.

Pixels may be an `ImageBitmap`, `ImageData`, canvas or `VideoFrame` of exactly the requested size. The layer draws each once and closes it. Cancellation reaches the source through `signal`.

This lets an application decode weather frames itself (for example in a worker, from its own archive format) instead of serving pre-rendered images.

## Changes

- `src/layers/weather/source.js`: the optional frame source on the feed (`weatherFrameSource`).
- `src/layers/weather/rasterTiles.js`: `createFrameTileProvider`, a Cesium imagery provider over `getFrameTile`.
- `src/layers/weather/infraredImage.js`, `rendering.js`, `shellRendering.js`, `index.js`: images and tiles from the source when it has them.
- `docs/APPLICATION.md`: the feed contract.

## Tests

`node --test src/layers/weather/*.test.mjs`: 196 pass. New cases cover frames from the source for images, detail windows and tiles, null tiles, size checks, closing drawn frames, cancellation, and the unchanged route path for feeds without the methods.

title: self-hosting: a keyless install contacts four third-party hosts on load, and none can be redirected
body:
### Summary

With no keys and default configuration, opening the app and moving the globe makes the browser
contact four third-party hosts. The server makes no outbound request at all in that run. None of the
four can be pointed at an operator's own server or turned off through configuration today:

| Host | What triggers it | Where it is fixed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `services.arcgisonline.com` | Keyless basemap (Esri World Imagery), every pan and zoom | `src/maps/imagery.js:16` |
| `terrain.reearth.land` | Keyless terrain mesh, every pan and zoom | `src/maps/terrain.js:6` |
| `fonts.googleapis.com` | Font stylesheets linked from `index.html` | `index.html:22-29` |
| `fonts.gstatic.com` | Font files referenced by those stylesheets | (via the above) |

Setting `GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY` or `CESIUM_ION_TOKEN` swaps the basemap to another hosted service.
It does not offer a local one. For self-hosters who want the globe to work on an isolated network,
or who do not want every viewport sent to a third party, this is the gap that remains after
`OVERPASS_UPSTREAMS`, `NOMINATIM_URL` and `PHOTON_URL` made the other public services optional.

The same terrain host is also used server-side by the `/api/terrain/heights` proxy
(`src/data/terrainHeightsProxy.js:134`, `server/providers/terrain.js`) when a layer samples ground
heights.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Check out `upstream/main` (measured at `9bca22834`), `npm ci` on Node 24, no `.env`.
2. Start the dev server with a clean environment and a preload that logs every outgoing request
   the Node process makes. Nothing in the repository is edited.

   ```js
   // egress-hook.mjs
   import dc from 'node:diagnostics_channel';
   import fs from 'node:fs';
   const log = (kind, url) => fs.appendFileSync(process.env.EGRESS_LOG, JSON.stringify({ kind, url }) + '\n');
   dc.subscribe('undici:request:create', ({ request }) => log('fetch', request.origin + request.path));
   dc.subscribe('http.client.request.start', ({ request }) => log('http', `${request.protocol}//${request.host}${request.path}`));
   ```

   ```sh
   env -i HOME="$HOME" PATH="$PATH" EGRESS_LOG="$PWD/server-egress.jsonl" \
     NODE_OPTIONS="--import=$PWD/egress-hook.mjs" \
     node node_modules/vite/bin/vite.js --port 4391 --strictPort --host 127.0.0.1
   ```

3. Open the app in headless Chrome (Puppeteer), enable `Network` over CDP, record every
   `Network.requestWillBeSent` URL, wait 20 s, then call `viewer.camera.setView` on
   `window.__godsEyeView.viewer` for Paris (1.5 km altitude), Tokyo (6 km), New York (3 km),
   Sydney (40 km) and a whole-globe view, waiting 25 s at each.
4. Group the recorded URLs by host, excluding `127.0.0.1`, `data:` and `blob:`.

### Measured output

No layer was enabled at boot. The globe rendered Esri imagery at each stop (screenshots kept).

```
browser requests to third-party hosts, by host (boot + 5 camera stops)
  609 services.arcgisonline.com   boot, paris, tokyo, newyork, sydney, global
  295 terrain.reearth.land        boot, paris, tokyo, newyork, sydney, global
    3 fonts.gstatic.com           boot
    2 fonts.googleapis.com        boot

server outbound requests: 0
```

A second pass that also enabled every data layer reached 59 third-party hosts in total. Layer
providers are out of scope here because they only run when a user turns a layer on, and turning
the layer off stops them. The four hosts above are the ones a viewer cannot avoid.

### Proposed direction

Each host needs one optional setting, with today's behavior when unset:

1. A basemap URL template (XYZ or WMTS) used in place of Esri for the keyless default, for example
   `GEV_BASEMAP_URL`, with an attribution string next to it.
2. A terrain URL for the quantized-mesh provider and the heights proxy, for example
   `GEV_TERRAIN_URL`. Unset keeps Re:Earth. A value of `none` selects the flat ellipsoid that the
   code already falls back to when Re:Earth is unreachable (`createKeylessTerrain` in
   `src/maps/terrain.js`).
3. Self-hosted fonts. Bundling the woff2 files under `public/` and dropping the two
   `fonts.googleapis.com` links removes the request for everyone. The icon font request already
   names the glyphs it uses (`icon_names=` at `index.html:29`), so a bundled subset stays small.

Browser-side values must be `https` or same-origin because `connect-src` allows no plain-`http`
origin (`build/vite.js:77`). The variables would be read on the server and handed to the client,
the way `PHOTON_URL` is today.

### Related

- #1221 (open PR) adds a bundled, low-resolution Natural Earth "Offline globe" as a manual choice
  and last fallback, with flat terrain. It covers the connection-lost case. It does not let an
  operator serve their own detailed imagery or terrain, and it does not touch fonts.
- #1141 (closed): request for a local map layer, answered by #1221.
- #177 (closed, unmerged) proposed a script to vendor Google Fonts for offline builds.
- The vector tile endpoint, which only some layers use, is filed separately.

### Environment

- `upstream/main` at `9bca22834`, clean worktree, `npm ci`, no `.env`, `env -i` shell.
- Node 24.20.0, npm 11.19.0. `npm run doctor` reports `Ready.`
- Headless Chrome for Testing via Puppeteer 25.16.0, SwiftShader WebGL.

## A working implementation

A pull request linked below implements the direction above as three independent commits, one per host group, so any of them can be taken or dropped on its own.

- `GEV_BASEMAP_URL` (an https XYZ template with `{z}`, `{x}`, `{y}`) and an optional `GEV_BASEMAP_ATTRIBUTION`. They replace Esri in the existing `esri-imagery` slot, so share links keep working. When the setting is on, nothing falls back to a public host.
- `GEV_TERRAIN_URL`, which takes an https quantized-mesh URL or `none`. `none` uses the flat ellipsoid. Once the variable is set, `/api/terrain/heights` contacts no upstream and heights come from the bundled geoid. Point heights from a self-hosted mesh would need a separate setting in a follow-up.
- Fonts are bundled under `public/fonts/` with their OFL and Apache texts, regenerated by a script from the same Google requests `index.html` makes today. #177 was closed for bugs in its script, not for the idea.

Both variables accept absolute https values only. An invalid value stops the server instead of falling back. Operator tile and terrain servers must send `Access-Control-Allow-Origin`. The MCP panel's fixed origin allowlist is not covered.

Measured with the three changes and a local tile mirror: default boot and five camera stops made 1777 browser requests, with 0 to third-party hosts, and the server made 0. With nothing set, behaviour is unchanged apart from the font hosts.

title: self-hosting: the OpenFreeMap vector tile endpoint has no configuration path
RFC: shared append files block most open pull requests from merging cleanly
body:
## Measurement

On 2026-11-11 I ran `git merge-tree --write-tree upstream/main pull/<n>/head` for every open pull request. That covered 286 pull requests from 135 authors.

- 59 merge cleanly.
- 227 conflict.
- 34 of the 227 conflict only in the ten files listed below. Their own code merges cleanly.
- 18 of the 227 are mine, so the remaining 209 come from other authors.

These files appear most often among the conflicting files. Each count is the number of pull requests that conflict in that file:

| File | Pull requests |
|---|---|
| `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md` | 113 |
| `src/i18n/locales/*.json` (any locale) | 87 |
| `scripts/package-boundaries.json` | 77 |
| `src/data/layerState.test.mjs` | 71 |
| `src/app/constructCatalog.test.mjs` | 64 |
| `src/data/layerStateTokenLedger.test.mjs` | 57 |
| `DATA_SOURCES.md` | 56 |
| `src/app/sourceComposition.test.mjs` | 50 |
| `scripts/format-scope.json` | 43 |
| `CHANGELOG.md` | 41 |

<details><summary>Measurement script</summary>

```sh
gh pr list -R bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view --state open --limit 500 --json number --jq '.[].number' |
while read -r n; do
  git fetch -q upstream "pull/$n/head:refs/hotspot/$n" || continue
  if files=$(git merge-tree --write-tree --name-only upstream/main "refs/hotspot/$n"); then
    echo "$n CLEAN"
  else
    echo "$n CONFLICT $(printf '%s\n' "$files" | sed -n '2,/^$/p' | paste -sd, -)"
  fi
done
```

</details>

## Why these files conflict

Every pull request appends to the same lines of these files:

- A behavior change adds a paragraph at the top of `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md`. CONTRIBUTING step 3 asks for that.
- A new string adds keys at the end of each locale catalog.
- A new module adds an entry to `package-boundaries.json` and `format-scope.json`.
- A new layer bumps a hard-coded count in `constructCatalog.test.mjs` and `sourceComposition.test.mjs`, and adds a row to the layer-state tests.

Git cannot merge two insertions at the same position. Each pull request is correct on its own, but every merge to `main` puts the others back into conflict. Authors then rebase, the next merge breaks them again, and reviewers re-check diffs that only moved.

`CHANGELOG.md` had the same problem (#781). `changelog.d/` fragments fixed it for new pull requests (#787). The 41 that still conflict there were opened before that change.

## Options

1. **`docs/CURRENT-STATE.md` fragments.** Add `docs/current-state.d/<pr>-<slug>.md` and assemble it with the existing changelog script. The constraint is that CONTRIBUTING lets regression tests assert against `CURRENT-STATE.md`. Those tests would read the assembled text, or a fragment would be folded in when its pull request merges. This file accounts for the largest share, 113 pull requests.
2. **Derive counts instead of pinning them.** Layer-count tests would compare against the catalog they test, for example `Object.keys(catalog).length`, rather than a literal. A layer pull request would no longer need to touch them.
3. **Sorted keys for the JSON lists.** Keep locale catalogs, `package-boundaries.json` and `format-scope.json` sorted, and enforce it in `format:check`. Insertions would then spread across the file instead of piling up at the end. Two pull requests would conflict only when their keys sort next to each other. This option needs a one-time reorder commit.

These options are independent of each other. Option 1 would unblock the most pull requests. Option 2 is the smallest change.

I can open a pull request for any of them in the same shape as #787. I'd like a maintainer to say which, if any, fits the project before I write it.

title: self-hosting: optional basemap and terrain endpoints, bundled fonts
body:
## What this changes

Closes #1667.

A keyless install makes every viewer's browser contact four third-party hosts: Esri for the basemap, Re:Earth for terrain, and Google Fonts on two hosts. No setting points any of them at a server the operator runs. This PR adds one optional setting per host group, as three independent commits. Any commit can be taken or dropped on its own. A last commit merges their changelog entries into the single `changelog.d/1670-*.md` fragment the check allows. If a commit is dropped, its bullet comes out of that file. When nothing is set, behaviour is unchanged, apart from fonts no longer coming from Google.

- **`GEV_BASEMAP_URL`** takes an https XYZ template (`{z}`, `{x}`, `{y}` or `{reverseY}`). **`GEV_BASEMAP_ATTRIBUTION`** is an optional plain-text credit.
  - The template replaces Esri World Imagery in the existing `esri-imagery` slot, so share links keep working.
  - The slot has no OSM fallback, so a failing operator server never hands the viewport to a public host.
- **`GEV_TERRAIN_URL`** takes an https quantized-mesh URL, or `none` for the flat ellipsoid that `createKeylessTerrain` already falls back to.
  - Once it is set, `/api/terrain/heights` answers 503 without contacting an upstream, and placement uses the bundled geoid.
  - Point heights are a Re:Earth API, not part of quantized mesh, so heights from a self-hosted mesh would be a follow-up.
- **Fonts** (Inter, JetBrains Mono, Noto Sans Arabic and Hebrew, and the Material Symbols subset) are served from `public/fonts/`.
  - Their OFL and Apache 2.0 texts sit beside them, and `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` is updated.
  - `scripts/vendor-fonts.mjs` regenerates the files from the same requests `index.html` made. #177 was closed for bugs in its script, not for the idea.
  - The CSP and the MCP panel allowlist drop both Google Fonts hosts.

Both variables accept absolute https values only. An invalid value stops the server instead of falling back. Tile and terrain servers must send `Access-Control-Allow-Origin`.

## How I verified it

- [x] `npm run build`
- [x] `npm test`: 12108 tests, 0 failures, on top of `0ceee8df4`. The run also passed layer-token, format, boundaries, changelog and i18n checks.
- [ ] `npm run test:track`
- [x] Feature gate: `src/maps/selfHostedSources.test.mjs` covers validation, the share-link id, the no-fallback rule and the heights proxy. `src/materialSymbolsSubset.test.mjs` checks the bundled icon subset.

The egress was measured as #1667 describes: headless Chrome over CDP, plus a Node preload logging outgoing requests. The run covered boot and five camera stops, with all three settings pointed at a local tile mirror.

| | Browser requests | To third-party hosts | Server outbound |
|---|---|---|---|
| `upstream/main`, nothing set | (see #1667) | 909 to 4 hosts | 0 |
| This PR, settings set | 1777 | 0 | 0 |

title: self-hosting: OPENFREEMAP_TILEJSON_URL points the vector tile sources at your own server
body:
## What this changes

Closes #1668.

Street Traffic, Mapped Installations and the voice outline source read road and military geometry from `tiles.openfreemap.org`. Today a self-hoster with their own OpenFreeMap-compatible tile server can only redirect them by editing source. #935 already made `createVectorTileSource` derive `allowedOrigin` from `tileJsonUrl`. This PR adds the missing wiring, one optional variable read the way `PHOTON_URL` is.

- **The variable.** `OPENFREEMAP_TILEJSON_URL` is validated in `build/vite.js` and defined for the page only when set. Unset or empty keeps `https://tiles.openfreemap.org/planet` exactly.
- **Accepted values.** An absolute `https` URL, or a path on the app's own origin (resolved against the page origin). Credentials, query, fragment, `//host` and plain `http` are refused.
- **Invalid values.** An invalid value stops `dev`, `build` and `preview` with an error that names the variable and does not echo the value. This is stricter than `PHOTON_URL`, which is silently disabled when invalid. Here a silent fallback would send the viewport back to the public host without telling the operator who set it.
- **Call sites.** Traffic, installations, voice outlines and the standalone catalog pass it as `tileJsonUrl`. `createOpenFreeMapSource` now treats an explicit `undefined` as the default instead of blanking the host.
- **Origin check.** Unchanged. `tiles[0]` must share the TileJSON's origin, so a mirror serves its own TileJSON, not upstream's verbatim (case C in #1668).
- **Docs.** `.env.example`, `DATA_SOURCES.md` and `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md`, with the note that the page's `connect-src` allows `https:` but not plain `http:` on another origin.

## How I verified it

- [x] `npm run build`. With `OPENFREEMAP_TILEJSON_URL=https://tiles.example.test/planet` the bundle carries that address. With `http://x.test/planet` the build fails with the variable named.
- [x] `npm test`: 12106 tests, 12102 pass, 0 fail, on top of `0ceee8df4`. The run also passed layer-token, format, boundaries, changelog and i18n checks.
- [ ] `npm run test:track`
- [ ] Feature gate: not run. The traffic and installations `qa-*.mjs` gates need a dev server and a browser.

The new tests in `src/tooling/viteBuild.test.mjs` and `src/sources/openFreeMap.test.mjs` cover three areas:
- **Wiring.** They load the real traffic, installations, outline and standalone sources through `vite.createServer().ssrLoadModule` with the build's actual `define`. For each source they assert the first TileJSON request it makes, in three cases: unset, an https URL, and a site path.
- **Validation.** Eleven invalid values are rejected, and the error never echoes credentials.
- **Mutation check.** Ten deliberate breaks of the wiring, the validator, the define and the default each turned at least one test red.

title: test: derive layer counts and token fixtures instead of pinning them
body:
## What this changes

Part of #1669 (Option 2: derive counts instead of pinning them).

Every pull request that adds a layer edits the same lines in four test files, because the tests pin the layer count and the token ledger as literals. Once one layer merges, every other open layer PR conflicts in those files. On the open PRs, 64, 50, 71 and 57 conflict in `constructCatalog.test.mjs`, `sourceComposition.test.mjs`, `layerState.test.mjs` and `layerStateTokenLedger.test.mjs`.

This is a test-only change. Each pin either restated the catalog's size or guarded a real invariant. Size restatements are now derived from the catalog. Invariants are asserted structurally.

- **Catalog tests.** Layer ids must be unique and must equal the exported `APPLICATION_LAYER_METADATA` ids. A catalog with a source omitted must hold the same ids as one built from every source. This replaces `layers.length, 40`.
- **Layer-state tests.** Ids and tokens must be unique, and the next token must be free and a valid next allocation. The allocation-rule cases use a synthetic ledger (legacy tokens plus every digit), which does not change when the production ledger grows.
- **Ledger tests.**
  - Fixtures are built from the legacy and single-digit rows instead of excluding layers by name.
  - Published tokens are still immutable. A frozen snapshot of them is checked against the production ledger with `validateLayerStateAllocations`, and every published layer must stay registered.

Behaviour, source files and the checker script are unchanged. A layer inserted inside an ordered run, for example `traffic..directions`, still edits that order assertion, because the order is a real contract.

## How I verified it

- [x] `npm run build`
- [x] `npm test`: 12101 tests, 12097 pass, 0 fail, on top of `0ceee8df4`. The run also passed layer-token, format, boundaries, changelog and i18n checks.
- [ ] `npm run test:track`
- [x] Feature gate: none applies (test-only).

Further checks:
- **Mutation checks**, each restored afterwards. Each of these faults fails the rewritten tests:
  - a layer dropped from the catalog;
  - a missing registry row;
  - a duplicate id;
  - a duplicate token;
  - a changed published token;
  - a skipped token;
  - a dropped ledger row;
  - a broken `nextLayerStateToken`.
- **Forward test.** A synthetic layer (registry row, ledger row `02`, catalog instance) passes these four files with no test edits. The current tests fail 8 times on the same tree.
- **Merged history.** Seven merged layer PRs (#1583, #1593, #1591, #1086, #114, #1297, #568) changed 825 lines in these files. About 689 of those were pin edits this change makes unnecessary. The rest were new tests for the layer.

## Limits

- **No existing PR is unblocked by this alone.** All 74 open PRs that conflict in these four files also conflict elsewhere.
- **Existing PRs conflict once more.** Open PRs that already edit the old pinned lines conflict with the rewritten lines once (220 to 221 conflicting PRs). Rebasing then means dropping those hunks. The payoff is for every future layer PR.
- **Other pins are untouched.** The tool-schema length and hash in `src/firstRunExperience.test.mjs` (38 PRs) and `src/voice/actionSchemas.test.mjs` (36 PRs) are intentional drift detectors and would need a different design.

title: Add Moscow outdoor cameras and native public-stream playback
body:
## Changes

Adds an opt-in Moscow pack of 100 outdoor cameras (97 HLS streams and 3 refreshing street-camera JPEG feeds), with short English labels, attribution and approximate positions. Enable with `CCTV_SOURCES_FILE=config/cctv_sources.moscow.json`; the default catalog is unchanged.

Extends existing native on-map playback with clear fMP4 HLS and bounded, camera-pinned resolvers for public Exdesign, anonymous Ivideon and unrestricted RTSP.ME/RTSP.RU streams. Deleted, password-protected and domain-restricted players are rejected. No separate player UI is introduced. Downloads remain capped at 16 MiB per segment and retained data at 24 MiB per session, with two sessions and no disk cache.

## Review follow-up: init.m4s

Retains @kvnloo's original commit `7cc99c50385e54591e5e4daaeabbd42f470194c4` and authorship. A same-origin `#EXT-X-MAP:URI="init.m4s"` now works through the parser, puller and existing browser playback path. Same-origin validation, redirect refusal and byte caps remain enforced.

Merged upstream main `41c792208e73f2ded123844cfce41fe88fd6d4f3` in `237770d3c`, resolving the CCTV integration conflicts. Supported public-player endpoints now share the HLS eligibility check for media and frame fallback, preserving stream health on fallback/capacity refusal while still marking real upstream failures degraded. Added a regression test. Windows-only audit and TypeScript-contract test path comparisons are normalized without weakening their assertions.

## Validation (21 November 2026, Windows, Node 24.22.1)

- Demonstrated RED/GREEN for the reported bug: temporarily restoring the `.mp4`-only guard makes the focused `fMP4 HLS accepts a same-origin .m4s initialization segment` test fail with `Unsupported HLS initialization segment`; restoring the fix passes.
- `node --test src/data/cctvHlsStream.test.mjs`: 15 passed.
- `node --import=./build/registerVue.js --test server/providers/cctv/player.test.mjs src/data/cctvHlsStream.test.mjs src/data/cctvHlsMiddleware.test.mjs`: 30 passed, including fallback health, capacity, origin validation, download limits and lease cleanup.
- Actual headless Edge decoding through shipped `attachCctvVideo`, hls.js and the CCTV proxy: an FFmpeg-generated H.264 fMP4 HLS fixture with upstream `init.m4s` decoded four 160x90 frames; canvas readback succeeded, no page errors, and disposal issued the lease-release DELETE. This proves the affected playback path rather than only checking HTTP status.
- `npm run build`: passed.
- `node scripts/format.mjs --check`: passed.
- Import-direction and package-boundary checks: passed.
- Setup doctor, layer-token check and Data Library check against upstream/main: passed; no new layer tokens.
- The complete unit discovery (1,330 ordinary test files plus both serialized allocation probes) was executed in Windows batches using the standard runner's discovery, flags and allocation plan. The single-command runner exceeds Windows' command-line length limit. Windows path-comparison failures were reproduced and corrected; affected tests were rerun successfully. This is local execution evidence, not a claim that the exact `npm test` invocation succeeds on Windows.

### Remaining general browser-gate failures

`node scripts/track-regression.mjs --url http://127.0.0.1:44173 --offline-imagery` completed with **109 passed, 2 failed** under headless Edge/SwiftShader: `trail head` (39/40 frames outside the asserted bound) and `display-floor/regime` (a tracked grounded model still rendered at the zoom-out probe). The tracking implementation and harness are unchanged from upstream main. A separate upstream-provider control attempt timed out at application boot, so it does not establish a base-pass/head-fail or base-fail/head-fail comparison. These failures remain unresolved; this PR does **not** claim the full contribution gate is green. Hosted GitHub CI status must be checked separately; local results do not replace any maintainer approval required for fork workflows.

## Camera data and docs

Historical media checks from 10 November 2026 are retained in `config/moscow-verification.json`; this follow-up does not claim a fresh browser audit of all 100 cameras. Coverage and positions remain approximate. Attribution and source/usage notes: `DATA_SOURCES.md`, `docs/MOSCOW_100_CAMERAS.md`, `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md` and `changelog.d/1673-moscow-outdoor-cameras.md`.

Personal Pinokio modifications and discovery archives are excluded.

title: fix(server): discard an OpenSky OAuth token the snapshot rejects
body:
## What this changes

When OpenSky answers the global snapshot with **401** for a cached OAuth token, the proxy now discards that token, so the next poll requests a fresh one.

Before this, the token was only cleared when the token request itself failed. A token that OpenSky rejected (revoked, or issued before a client secret was rotated) was replayed on every poll until it expired, so `/api/flights` kept answering `401 oauth_invalid_credentials` for up to ~29 minutes even though valid credentials were in place.

The change is 12 lines in `server/providers/aircraft/opensky.js`:

- Only a 401 on a request that actually sent the OAuth token clears it. 403, 429 and 5xx are unchanged.
- The token is cleared only if it is still the cached one, so a token installed by a concurrent refresh (the track route shares the cache) is left alone.

One behavior to be aware of: if OpenSky keeps issuing tokens that its API then rejects, each poll now makes one token request plus one snapshot request, instead of one snapshot request. I kept it simple and did not add a backoff; happy to add one if you prefer.

## How I verified it

- [x] `npm run build`
- [x] `npm test` (12,107 passed, 0 failed, Node 24.22.2)
- [x] `npm run test:track` (dev server running): 111 passed, 0 failed
- [x] Feature gate for the area I touched: none applies (server-only change)

Also `npm run format:check` passes.

New regression test in `src/tooling/liveProviders.test.mjs`: "OpenSky discards an OAuth token the snapshot rejects, so the next poll signs in again". It fails on `main` (second poll answers 401) and passes with the fix.

Docs updated in the same PR: `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md` (Proxy/Security Baseline) and `docs/opensky-auth.md` (Troubleshooting).
