title: fix(hud): show a 999.6 m camera height as 1.0 km, not 1000 m
body:
The HUD summary's ALT tag and the spoken view state compared the raw camera height against 1000 before rounding it. A height of 999.5 to 999.9 m therefore read "1000M" and "Camera 1000 m up.", where 1000 m itself reads "1.0KM" and "Camera 1 km up."

**Changes**
- `src/hud.js`: the ALT tag rounds to the meter before choosing the unit. The branch moves into `hudLocalityFormat.js` as `hudAltitude()` so it can be tested under Node; output formats are otherwise unchanged.
- `src/voice/speech.js` (`getCurrentViewState`): the same rounding before the km/m choice.
- `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md`: one sentence on the rounding.

**Tests**
- New cases in `hudLocality.test.mjs` and `voice/speech.test.mjs` cover 999.4 m, 999.6 m, 1000 m and a multi-kilometer height. The 999.6 m cases fail on `main`.
- Full unit suite: 1,009 test files pass on Windows 11, Node 24.16. `npm test` itself fails on Windows with `ENAMETOOLONG` (#1631), so I ran the same plan in batches.
- `format:check`, `check:boundaries`, `i18n` and `build` pass.

title: feat(news): the News layer reads its time from the world clock
body:
The News layer already takes a `now` option. Every time rule reads it: report ages, the 24-hour window, "today", fading, and the pressing and card rules. The catalog never set it, so the layer always counted from the wall clock. A host that follows the world clock for `news` and serves a past time's reports therefore had them all dropped as older than 24 hours.

The catalog now passes `worldClock.timeFor('news')`. Nothing changes in Core, since it never follows the clock for the layer: `timeFor` returns the wall clock unless a host follows the layer, so Core keeps reading `Date.now()`.

- `src/app/constructCatalog.js`: `createApplicationNews({ source, now: worldClock.timeFor(NEWS_LAYER_ID) })`.
- `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md`: a **Time** entry under News.
- `changelog.d/1677-news-world-clock.md`.

No new test. `layer.test.mjs` already covers the layer reading its times from `now`. The catalog builds the layer through a static import, so there is nothing to observe there without enabling the layer on a viewer.

Checks run:
- Format check, import directions, package boundaries.
- Catalog, source composition, news layer, world clock and docs-claim tests: 200 of 200 pass.
- The full suite, run by glob on Windows because `run-unit-tests.mjs` exceeds the Windows command-line length there: 12,262 pass, 0 fail, 14 skipped.

title: ci(windows): run the Nominatim cache test in the Windows job
body:
Since #1547, `src/tooling/nominatimOutlineRoute.test.mjs` skips its POSIX file-mode checks on Windows, where the cache keeps the checkout's ACLs. No CI job runs that file on Windows, so nothing would catch the skip regressing and the test failing there again.

**Change:** `.github/workflows/ci.yml` adds the file to the Windows job's "Run focused onboarding tests" step, as #997 did for other files.

**Why it fits that step:** the test needs no Vue loader, network or environment, so it runs under the step's plain `node --test`.

**Checked:** the step's exact command passes 140/140 on Windows 11 with Node 24.16. The Nominatim file alone passes 31/31, and `format:check` passes. No runtime behavior changes, so there is no changelog fragment.

title: feat(layers): Eclipse Paths, solar and lunar eclipses from 1583 to 3000
body:
## What this changes

Adds **Eclipse Paths**, a layer in the Events group that shows every solar and lunar eclipse from 1583 to 3000 on the globe, driven by the world clock. The next big one is the total solar eclipse of 2 August 2027 (Spain, North Africa, Egypt).

![Total solar eclipse of 2 August 2027: the path, the Moon's shadow and the sky view in totality](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/IMBrandao/gods-eye-view/pr-assets/eclipse-paths/1-total-2027.jpg)

**Solar eclipses**

- The path of totality or annularity as a band with its central line, UTC time marks along it, and the point of greatest eclipse with its duration.
- The Moon's shadow at the world time, drawn by a post-process stage at true scale: the penumbra as a shaded disc and the umbra as its dark core. Move the clock or press Play and it crosses the Earth.
- A dashed limit round the area where at least a partial eclipse is seen.

**Lunar eclipses**

- The half of the Earth with the Moon in its sky is tinted while the eclipse runs.
- Lines mark where the Moon sits on the horizon as the penumbral (dashed) and umbral (solid) phases begin and end.

**Sky view**

- A small picture, bottom right, of the eclipse as seen from a flag on the globe. The flag starts where the eclipse peaks; a click on the globe moves it.
- It shows the Moon's bite out of the Sun, the corona in totality, or the Moon under the Earth's shadow, with the share covered. A cross closes it.

![The same eclipse earlier: 43% of the Sun covered in the sky view](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/IMBrandao/gods-eye-view/pr-assets/eclipse-paths/2-partial-sky-view.jpg)
![Total lunar eclipse of 7 September 2025: horizon lines and the Moon entering the umbra](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/IMBrandao/gods-eye-view/pr-assets/eclipse-paths/3-lunar-2025.jpg)

**Row controls**

- Earlier / Later, −100 / +100 years, a year slider over one century, and a list of the eclipses around the chosen one (☀️ or 🌙 in front of each).
- Play runs the clock through the eclipse at 480×. Follow shadow (on by default, solar only) keeps the camera over the shadow along the central line: it waits at the line's start and stops at its end.
- An All / Solar / Lunar switch.

## How

- `src/layers/eclipses/besselian.js` computes everything for solar eclipses from the Besselian elements against the WGS84 ellipsoid, with the ΔT correction: shadow axis and cones, central line, the band's edges (the envelope of the umbra's rim, with rounded ends), local circumstances.
- `lunar.js` works from the catalogue's own figures (gamma, magnitudes, phase durations, sub-lunar point).
- `shadow.js` is the Cesium `PostProcessStage`; `visibility.js` contours the partial-eclipse limit; `skyView.js` and `skyPanel.js` work out and paint the sky view.
- Nothing is fetched at runtime. `elements.json` (about 1 MB) and `lunar.json` (about 260 KB) are loaded only when the layer is first enabled; `scripts/build-eclipse-elements.mjs` and `scripts/build-lunar-eclipses.mjs` rebuild them from NASA's files.
- Share-link token `03`, assigned with `npm run layer-token:next` (`02` went to Rail on `main`). The layer is `enabled-only`: the chosen eclipse is not stored in links.
- The layer is off for voice (`VOICE_OFF_LAYERS`).

**One small change outside the layer:** a chip in `RailChips.vue` may carry `breakBefore`, which starts a new line of chips (a zero-height flex item, styled in `radio.css`). The row uses it to group its chips. Rows that don't set it render exactly as before.

**Left in the code but turned off:** a "Look at the Sun / Moon" mode that turns the real camera to the sky (the layer's `sunView` option, false by default). Happy to delete it if you would rather not carry it.

## How I verified it

- [x] `npm run build`
- [x] `npm test`, run in batches (the single command hits `ENAMETOOLONG` on Windows): 12,840 passed after merging the latest `main`
- [ ] `npm run test:track` (not run)
- [x] `npm run i18n` (13 locales complete), `npm run format:check`, `npm run check:boundaries`, `npm run layer-token:check -- --base-ref origin/main`
- [x] Feature gate: none applies
- Checked against the catalogue: for each solar eclipse the build script compares the gamma computed from the elements with the published one, and the path width at greatest eclipse for 2 August 2027 comes out at the catalogue's 258 km.
- Checked in the running app: path, shadow, limit and sky view for 2 August 2027; the lunar eclipse of 7 September 2025; Play with Follow shadow; closing the sky view from its cross.

## New layer checklist

**Screenshots**

Above.

**Recording**

To follow in a comment on this PR.

**Proposed category**

Category: Events

**Data source and licence**

- Source (provider and endpoint): NASA's GSFC, Five Millennium Canon of Solar Eclipses (`eclipse.gsfc.nasa.gov/eclipse_besselian_from_mysqldump2.csv`) and Five Millennium Canon of Lunar Eclipses (`eclipse.gsfc.nasa.gov/LEcat5/LE<years>.html`), by Fred Espenak and Jean Meeus.
- Licence or terms (link): reproduction freely granted with acknowledgment. [5MCSE](https://eclipse.gsfc.nasa.gov/SEpubs/5MCSE.html), [lunar catalogue](https://eclipse.gsfc.nasa.gov/LEcat5/LEcatalog.html).
- Attribution shown in the app: "Eclipse predictions: Five Millennium Canons of Solar and Lunar Eclipses by Fred Espenak and Jean Meeus (NASA's GSFC)"
- Needs a key? (none / optional / required): none
- Fetched at runtime, or bundled in the repo: bundled

- [x] Added a row to `DATA_SOURCES.md`
- [x] Credit is registered in `src/data/dataCredits.js`
- [x] Share-link token assigned with `npm run layer-token:next`, if the layer is shareable

## Docs

title: feat(news): an application may draw the News picture cards itself
body:
## What this changes

An application built on Core can now draw the News layer's picture cards in its own way (for example as HTML cards) instead of the layer's canvas cards.

- `createNewsLayer({ pictureCards })` takes an optional function. With it, the layer paints no picture cards of its own and calls `pictureCards(cards, { selectedId })` on every redraw:
  - `cards`: one per event on the map that has a picture, single source or not, most severe then newest first: `{ id, title, lat, lon, publishedAt, severity, color, image, video, credit }`, at the report's marker.
  - `selectedId`: the selected report's id, or `null`. Its own text card still stands at its marker, so the application can keep clear of it.
  - When the layer turns off it is called with no cards.
- Anything other than a function throws `TypeError`.
- `createApplicationCatalog({ newsOptions })` passes options through to the News layer.
- A click on an application-drawn card can select the report with `layer.setParams({ reportId, focus: true })`, as the News panel does.

Without the option nothing changes.

## How I verified it

- [x] `npm run build`
- [x] `npm test` (12,266 pass, 4 skipped)
- [ ] `npm run test:track`: not run
- [x] Feature gate: `node --test src/layers/news/layer.test.mjs` (24/24), including two new tests: the handed cards (one per event, ranking, picture and clip, position, the selected id, empty on disable) and the non-function `TypeError`.

title: fix: keyless search for Heathrow lands on Florida (#1646)
body:

title: feat(air-accidents): worldwide air accidents layer from Wikidata
body:
## Summary

Adds an **Air accidents** layer to the Events group: about 2,500 notable aviation accidents worldwide, from Wikidata only (CC0, keyless). This replaces #1584, which mixed in two national agencies (CENIPA and NTSB); those are regional and are better suited to the Data Library (#1604).

- **Coverage:** about 1,900 accidents with their own coordinate, plus about 580 without one that are placed at their location item (an airport, a mountain, a town) and marked approximate. By continent: Europe ~530, North America ~470, Asia ~380, South America and Africa ~110 each, Oceania ~40, and ~390 at sea.
- **Card:** death toll, injuries, and survivors first, then date, place and country, flight number and route, aircraft (with the registration when there is a single aircraft), and operator. For a placed accident, the card says where it was placed. Clicking the card opens the English Wikipedia article, else the Aviation Safety Network record, else the Wikidata item.
- **Markers:** a red disc with an aircraft, 16 to 36 px by fatalities (the Shipwrecks scale). Accidents that fall on the same point, such as several placed at one airport, are laid on a small spiral about 3 km apart, so each one can be clicked.
- **Period filter:** start-year and end-year pickers under the row, reusing the Shipwrecks range control.
- **Privacy:** only the event's own properties are queried. No property that points at people (crew, passengers, victims) is read, and a test asserts that.

### Server

`/api/air-accidents` runs two SPARQL queries in parallel, at most once a day. One query for both would exceed the query service's 60 s limit.

- **Placed query fails:** the accidents with their own coordinate are still served, and the row says the placed ones are missing.
- **Query exceeds the 60 s limit:** the service returns a cut-off 200 that the edge cache keeps for five minutes. The proxy retries once with a different URL, so the retry reaches the query service instead of the cached failure.
- **Refresh fails:** the last good snapshot is served as stale for up to seven days.
- **Limits:** 32 MiB response cap, rate limiting, and no new dependencies.

### Share link

Token `02`, the next free one (`npm run layer-token:check` passes). #1679 (eclipse paths) also takes `02`; whichever merges second moves to the next free token.

title: feat(cctv): add the Singapore traffic camera pack from data.gov.sg
body:
## What this changes

Adds Singapore traffic cameras from the Land Transport Authority (LTA), through data.gov.sg, as a keyless CCTV pack. Closes #1653.

- **Catalog.** One keyless JSON request to `api.data.gov.sg/v1/transport/traffic-images` per catalog refresh, with a 15 s deadline, a 1 MiB body cap and redirects refused, as the Calgary pack does.
- **Validation.** Ids must be digits only (`singapore-<camera_id>`). Coordinates must pass `isLikelySingaporeCoordinate`. Frame links are pinned to `images.data.gov.sg/api/traffic-images/` with `pinnedCameraUrl` and must end in `.jpg`.
- **Frame type.** data.gov.sg sends frames as `application/octet-stream`, so the raster-type rule refuses them. `media.js` now reads that type as JPEG only for the pinned Singapore directory, and only when the body starts with `FF D8 FF`. It then sends `image/jpeg`. Every other origin keeps the raster-type rule.
- **Frame links.** Each frame link changes every 1 to 2 minutes, which is shorter than the 15 min catalog cache. The frame proxy looks up the current link at frame time: 1 shared lookup at most once a minute, with concurrent requests sharing it. The lookup has a 3 s deadline, and the frame fetch gets what is left of the normal 8 s frame deadline. If the lookup fails, the proxy uses the catalog link and does not retry for 60 s.
- **Names.** The 8 cameras in the feed today get LTA's "View from ..." captions from the OneMotoring traffic-camera page (Woodlands, Tuas, Sentosa Gateway). Other ids get "Singapore camera <id>".
- **Attribution.** Each record carries the Singapore Open Data Licence v1.0 notice. The Data attribution popover has a `singapore-cctv` credit. `DATA_SOURCES.md` lists the source, licence and attribution. Frames are fetched at runtime; nothing is bundled.
- **Settings.** `CCTV_SINGAPORE_ENABLED=0` turns the pack off. `CCTV_SINGAPORE_MAX_SOURCES` sets the cap (default 100, clamped to 8 to 200).

The feed listed 90 cameras on 2026-06-15 and 8 cameras from 2026-07-01 (checked again on 2026-11-11). The default cap leaves room if the full list comes back.

## How I verified it

- [x] `npm run build`: built in 10.40 s, only the existing chunk-size warning
- [x] `npm test`: 12,107 tests, 12,104 passed, 0 failed, 3 skipped; allocation probes 1 of 1 and 14 of 14
- [x] `npm run test:track` (dev server running): 111 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped (run before the rebase onto 9bca228; the 3 new `main` commits touch no CCTV file)
- [x] Feature gate: `src/data/cctvSingapore.test.mjs` 21 of 21. Removing the signature check, the origin check or the shared lookup, one at a time, makes tests fail. `npm run format:check`, `npm run check:boundaries` and `npm run changelog:check` exit 0.

Live check on a local dev server (2026-11-11):

- `/api/cctv/sources` served all 8 Singapore cameras with names and the licence notice.
- `/api/cctv/frame/singapore-2701`, `-4703` and `-4799` each returned 200, `Content-Type: image/jpeg`, `X-CCTV-Source: upstream-image`, with a 1920 x 1080 JPEG body. The first frame took 0.93 s (it includes the link lookup); the next two took 0.05 to 0.08 s.
- `/api/cctv/health` reported `ok`.

This is not a new layer: the cameras join the existing CCTV layer.

title: feat(cockpit): application cockpit subjects
body:
## What this changes

An application can register its own Cockpit subjects through `services.cockpitSubjects`. GEV itself registers none, so the Cockpit still offers aircraft, satellites and vessels.

- **Provider API.** Providers are checked once; their frames and HUD views are checked on every update. Provider methods are synchronous and called on the provider, `hold` answers `true` or `false`, and a provider that fails ends its view.
- **Camera options for a provider's frame:** ground clamp off, an exact anchor, a per-frame update, and floor clearance that eases in. A frame with no known height keeps the last good one, or waits for the ground.
- **A generic HUD:** kicker, cards, always-visible source rows, a banner, a veil (off under reduced motion), and a bottom progress line. The text comes from the provider, in the page's language (`getLocale` and `onLocaleChange` from the `./i18n` entry).
- **Rail and Transit read and hold APIs,** so an application can ride a selected train or vehicle; a held one hides its marker, 3D model and card. Plus a `./layers/rail/paths` export. These APIs and the new export are marked experimental.
- **Docs:** `docs/APPLICATION.md` has a "Cockpit subjects" section with a minimal provider.

**Entry:** the built-in views keep their entry order (aircraft, satellite, vessel) exactly as on `main`. An application's subject takes entry when it was selected after every built-in subject present. Nothing changes on screen without providers.

title: feat(overlay): draw selected and tracked map cards as a Vue component, without the accent bar
body:
## What this changes

Map cards no longer carry a coloured bar down their left edge, and the selected and tracked cards are now drawn by a Vue component instead of on the overlay canvas.

- **No left bar:** removed from detail cards, selected cards and annotation callouts. An annotation callout is outlined in its mark's colour instead.
- **`WorldOverlayCards` component:** draws the plate and text of selected and tracked cards. The world overlay still solves where each card goes, handles hit testing and paints the leader line. It publishes the card list to the `gev-world-overlay-cards` store when content changes and writes each frame's position straight to the elements, so a camera move re-renders nothing.
- **Tokens:** the component uses the overlay's own style tokens, so element cards and canvas cards match.
- **Flags:** `?overlayCards=all` also draws ambient detail cards as elements; `?overlayCards=off` paints every card on the canvas.
- **Fallback:** a composition that does not pass `subscribeWorldOverlayCards` keeps every card on the canvas.

Left as they are: tactical cards, camera thumbnails, labels and tracks stay on the canvas. Detection callouts keep their tier bar, which an existing test records as a deliberate choice.

title: fix(transit): keep terrain heights per point so rereads stop freezing the page
body:
## What this changes

Fixes the page freezing for seconds at a time with Transit on over a terrain globe (the keyless Esri stack), most visibly while zooming over a large fleet. Chrome showed "Page Unresponsive" over Boston with about 650 MBTA vehicles.

**Cause.** `requestHeight` in `src/layers/transit/height.js` called `globe.getHeight()` for every trail fix of every vehicle in view, twice per reread pass, on each 15-second poll and up to six more passes after it. In Cesium 1.138 that call is a ray cast against the drawn tile's mesh, not a cache lookup. Over Boston that was about 150,000 reads per 10 seconds for about 8,000 distinct points, and a single pass blocked the page for up to 19 seconds while zooming.

**Fix.**
- Heights read from the loaded terrain are kept per point (1e-5°, about a metre).
- While the camera moves or tiles load, a kept height is read again after 2 s. A height read once both have been still for 5 s is kept until either changes.
- Reads are budgeted at 16 ms per 200 ms window, 12 ms of it for re-reads, longest-kept first so no point starves.
- Requests are ranked: a vehicle's own position is always read; the path its marker is drawn along comes next; the undrawn trail history of unselected vehicles may use a quarter of each budget.
- Past the budget a kept point keeps its last height, and a new point takes the last height read in its ~111 m floor cell or waits. The reread cycle continues until none waits.
- A flat (ellipsoid) globe answers without reading terrain.

The 3D Tiles path is untouched; it never took this branch.

## Measurements

Boston, MBTA, keyless terrain globe, Apple M3 Max (Metal), headless Chrome against `vite` dev servers.

Scripted repro: Transit on, detection DENSE, one vehicle selected, six zoom-in/zoom-out cycles.

| | `main` | This branch |
|---|---|---|
| Longest main-thread block | 19.0 s | 0.46 s (during initial load) |
| Long tasks (>50 ms) | 77 | 4 |
| CPU time in terrain intersection | 191 s | 0.2 s |

Terrain reads per 10-second window with the camera still, eight consecutive windows from page load:

| | `main` | This branch |
|---|---|---|
| Range | 2,100 to 150,900 | 0 to 3,500 |
| Total over 80 s | 452,400 | 12,000 |

On `main` the count grows as trails lengthen; the last two windows were 150,900 and 108,000.

Marker height against the exact terrain height under each visible marker:

| | `main` | This branch |
|---|---|---|
| Camera still, 48 km, about 700 markers | 0 m | 0 m |
| Camera still, 6 km, 155 markers | 0 m | 0 m |
| After a zoom from 48 km to 6 km | up to 4.7 m off for about 4 s, then 0 m | up to 6.3 m off for about 6 s, then 0 m |

Both builds show stale heights for a few seconds after a zoom while finer tiles load; this branch settles about two seconds later.

## How I verified it

- [x] `npm run build`
- [x] `npm test` (12,651 passed, 0 failed, 3 skipped), including 13 new tests in `src/layers/transit/height.test.mjs`
- [x] `npm run test:track` (111 passed, 0 failed)
- [x] `npm run test:perf` (2 passed)
- [x] `npm run format:check`, `npm run check:boundaries`
- [ ] Feature gate for the area I touched: `npm run qa:transit` does not pass, on `main` or here

`qa:transit` detail, one run on `main` and two on this branch:

| Check | `main` | Branch run 1 | Branch run 2 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Totals | 197 pass, 5 fail | 199 pass, 5 fail | 198 pass, 4 fail |
| Boston bright/white-hot readable | fail | fail | fail |
| Boston dark/black-hot readable | fail | fail | fail |
| Brackets carry the mode colour | fail | fail | pass |
| 800 moving vehicles within budgets | fail | pass | fail |
| 3000 moving vehicles within budgets | fail | pass | pass |
| Boston dark/nvg readable | pass | fail | fail |
| Boston fixture: same vehicles drawn 30 s later | pass | fail | pass |

- The dark/nvg check failed on one sprite per run, a different one each time, at centre brightness 0.589 and 0.580 against a 0.594 limit; on `main` the lowest sprite passed at 0.600. Sprite screen positions are identical to `main` to within 0.02 px, so I read this as noise at the threshold, not placement.
- The fixture check failed once and passed on the rerun. Reproducing that step alone (jump to 600 m, load the 16-vehicle fixture) showed all 16 vehicles at once on both builds, three rounds each.

Not verified:

title: perf(terrain): one shared, cached terrain height reader for Transit, Rail, Bike Share and local data
body:
## What this changes

Moves the terrain-height cache from #1688 into a shared service and uses it in the other layers that read the terrain globe directly. Three of them had measurable stalls.

**Stacked on #1688.** This branch contains that PR's two commits; review only the last commit here, or merge #1688 first.

`globe.getHeight` is a ray cast against the drawn tile's mesh and `scene.sampleHeight` is a GPU depth render. Several layers called them uncached and unbudgeted, each with its own approach.

- **`src/services/terrainSurface.js`** (new): the per-point cache, settle-aware refresh and 16 ms per 200 ms read budget from #1688, unchanged in behaviour, plus `observe(viewer)` for callers that ask nothing while tiles load. The ground service exposes one instance as `groundFloor.terrainSurface`, so every layer shares one cache and one budget. A layer built without it creates its own.
- **Transit**: uses the shared instance. No behaviour change from #1688.
- **Rail**: read each train's terrain height every frame. It now asks on a grid about 4 m apart, as a marker, so a moving train reads a few times a second and a standing one not at all.
- **Local data layers** (Data Centers, Dams): terrain floors go through the shared reader, and depth samples stop once a frame has spent 8 ms and continue on the following frames.
- **Bike Share**: sampled a depth render per station while creating a city's stations. Stations are now drawn at once at the fallback height and moved onto the ground afterwards in 4 ms steps, from the terrain reader on a terrain globe and from depth samples where the globe is hidden.

Not changed: Street Traffic already has its own height cache and profiled clean. ALPR cameras already budget their samples; no data loads without a key, so I could not profile them.

## Measurements

Keyless Esri terrain globe, Apple M3 Max (Metal), headless Chrome against `vite` dev servers. Each run: 25 s load, 20 s still, about 21 s of zoom in and out, 15 s settle.

**Data Centers** (4.4K sites, northern Virginia, 15 km)

| | `main` | This branch |
|---|---|---|
| Longest main-thread block on load | 2,748 ms | 229 ms (app start-up, also on `main`) |
| Depth samples on load | 168 calls in one task | 168 calls, one per frame |
| Terrain reads while zooming | 17,733 calls, 1,304 ms | 2,518 calls, 218 ms |
| Long tasks while zooming | 10, longest 347 ms | 1, 77 ms |

The same 168 sites were grounded at identical heights in one run of each build.

**Bike Share** (618 stations, Boston, 12 km)

| | `main` | This branch |
|---|---|---|
| Depth samples on load | 618 calls, 857 ms | 0 |
| Longest main-thread block on load | 862 ms | none |

**Rail** (about 125 trains, Boston, 48 km)

| Terrain reads | `main` | This branch |
|---|---|---|
| Still, 20 s | 4,985 | 212 |
| Zooming, 21 s | 16,238 | 1,738 |
| Settling, 15 s | 34,797 | 2,797 |
| CPU in the layer's terrain reads | 1,612 ms | 270 ms |

Train height against exact terrain: at rest `main` 0 m, this branch p90 0.1 m, max 0.25 m. Six seconds after a zoom: `main` p90 0 m with 3 trains over 3 m, this branch p90 0.1 m with 4 over 3 m.

**Transit** (same repro as #1688): 2 long tasks, longest 540 ms during initial load.

## How I verified it

- [x] `npm run build`
- [x] `npm test` (12,668 passed, 0 failed, 3 skipped), including new tests for the service, Bike Share height refinement and local-data sampling
- [x] `npm run test:track` (111 passed, 0 failed)
- [x] `npm run format:check`, `npm run check:boundaries`, `npm run i18n`
- [ ] Feature gate for the area I touched: `npm run qa:transit` not rerun on this branch; see #1688 for its state on `main`

Behaviour differences:
- **Bike Share on a terrain globe with a building tileset on top:** stations now sit on the terrain, where the old depth sample could land on a roof. Not tested.
- **Bike Share stations with no depth sample:** 122 of Boston's 618 stations got no answer from `scene.sampleHeight` but do from the terrain reader, so they now stand on the ground. I infer they sat at the 2 m fallback before; not confirmed on `main`.
- **Local data:** a refined terrain floor is picked up as much as 2 s later than before.
- **Rail:** a train can stand up to about 0.25 m off the surface because of the 4 m grid.

Not verified:
- Photorealistic 3D Tiles for any of these layers; unit tests only. Bike Share there settles over about 3 to 4 seconds for a 618-station city without blocking.
- Dams, and any city steeper than Boston.
- One of eleven Data Centers runs during development took no depth samples in 25 s and grounded nothing; it did not recur and was not diagnosed.

title: feat(satellites): ISS 3D model with moving parts, command panel and NASA live video
body:
## What

- **3D model.** Within 1,500 km of the camera the ISS is drawn as NASA's own 3D model of the current station (Nauka, Prichal, Bishop, the roll-out arrays) instead of the red dot; farther out the dot stays as it is. The model and the dots (ambient and tracked) split the distance range, so exactly one of them draws.
- **Moving parts.** The solar arrays and radiators turn with the Sun, the two Ku-band dishes aim at relay satellites, and the robotic arms sway. All of it is computed in the app; none of it is telemetry (see "What is computed and what is illustrative").
- **Command panel.** Selecting the ISS shows a collapsed "ISS · Command panel" bottom left: a zoom button, **Automatic** (the default) and **Manual**, which opens controls for the Sun's position, the arrays, the radiators, the dishes and Canadarm2.
- **Live video.** Selecting the ISS also opens a small panel with NASA's official live stream from the station ("Live High-Definition Views from the International Space Station", channel @NASA). The tracked card itself is unchanged.

## Prior work checked

- No open or closed PR or issue adds a 3D model for the ISS (#628 asked for Tiangong and is closed; #1497 Sky view is a different feature).
- #285 (closed) had "NASA ISS" among 17 channels in a live-news dock. It was closed because it resolved live video ids by **scraping YouTube pages**, which goes against YouTube's terms. This PR does not read any YouTube page. It embeds one fixed video through YouTube's own embedded player (`youtube-nocookie.com`, already in the page's `frame-src`), which is the use YouTube's terms allow. The trade-off is that the id is a constant to update if NASA restarts the broadcast.
- #1162 (open) adds YouTube players to the CCTV layer. There is no overlap in files or behaviour beyond `frame-src`, which this PR does not change.

## The model

- **Source:** NASA Johnson Space Center, Integrated Graphics, Operations and Analysis Laboratory: ["International Space Station (ISS) (D) (IGOAL)"](https://science.nasa.gov/3d-resources/international-space-station-iss-d-igoal/) on NASA 3D Resources. NASA media is not subject to US copyright; the credit follows NASA's usage guidelines (no endorsement implied, no insignia). Credited in `public/models/README.md`, `DATA_SOURCES.md` and the Data attribution popover.
- **Reduction:** the original is 96 MB and 2.7 M triangles. `public/models/iss.glb` is 3 MB and 314 k triangles: handrails left out (3 cm tubes, under a pixel at the closest view); geometry simplified within 15 cm of the original surface for structure and 40 cm for small details; normals rebuilt; normal maps dropped; textures at 512 px WebP; Draco. The file is fetched only once the camera nears the model's range, so a globe-wide view of the layer never downloads it.
- **Two corrections to NASA's file:** it is a mirror image of the station (port and starboard swapped), which is undone; and 15 materials are marked as blended, which draws those parts see-through in Cesium, so they are made opaque. Both are recorded in `public/models/README.md`.
- **Joints:** parts that move stay separate nodes at the joints NASA names in the file. The two Ku-band dishes and three of the four power-module radiators are welded into the truss meshes in NASA's file, so the build cuts them out by position.
- **Identity, scale, attitude, position:** NORAD 25544 by number, never by name; real size (109 m truss) with a 72 px floor; the usual "+XVV" attitude from the station's own SGP4 state each frame; on the follow camera's sample while tracked.

## What is computed and what is illustrative

| Part | Rule | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| Solar arrays (2 alpha joints, 8 beta joints) | Face the Sun; in the Earth's shadow, feather along the flight direction | Computed from the Sun's position and a cylindrical shadow |
| Truss radiators (2 joints) | Stay edge-on to the Sun | Computed from the Sun's position |
| Ku-band dishes (2) | Aim at the two highest relay satellites above the station's horizon plane | Computed from the TDRS fleet's nominal slots (41°W, 171°W, 85°E). Which satellite the station is using at a given moment is not public in real time |
| Canadarm2, Dextre's arms, the Japanese arm | Sway a few degrees about the pose in NASA's file | **Illustrative only.** No public source gives their real pose |
| European arm | Does not move | NASA's file has no joints for it |

Joints turn at most 12°/s of wall time, so day/night changes glide. The command panel's Automatic mode says this in one line ("Computed, not live telemetry") and shows whether the station is in sunlight or in the Earth's shadow.

## The command panel

- **Zoom to the ISS:** offered only when the camera is more than 1 km away; eases the follow camera to 260 m, where the whole station fills the view, then goes away. It comes back on zooming out.
- **Manual:** replace the Sun with a chosen position or a 40 s orbit, to watch each joint move without waiting for the real orbit; fold and extend the arrays and the radiators; aim the dishes; pose Canadarm2 joint by joint. Folding is labelled as a demonstration: the real arrays stay extended, and the real radiators can fold but stay extended.
- **Back to Automatic**, a new selection, the Cockpit or turning the layer off hands every joint back to its rule.
- Translated in all 13 locales; follows a language change without a reload (the live panel now does too, without restarting the player).

## Other changes

- **Docked objects.** Nauka, a Progress or a Dragon have dots of their own at the station's position; near the model they are part of it. Whether an object is docked is now read from both orbits at one instant: dots are moved at different moments, and at 7.6 km/s a fraction of a second put a docked object's dot outside the radius, which brought its mark back beside the model.
- **Tracked card.** Up close the card keeps clear of the model instead of sitting on it.

## Limits

- The arrays' and radiators' angles are the app's geometry, not NASA's flight rules: the real station also biases its arrays for power, drag and loads.
- The fold is a squash along the mast (the file has rigid, deployed panels), not a pleat-by-pleat fold.
- The arms' joint axes are taken from the orientation NASA stored on each joint node.
- The live stream id is a constant (`ISS_LIVE_VIDEO_ID`): one line to change if NASA restarts the broadcast.
- Render cost was measured on one machine: 3.3 ms per frame at 260 m against 3.8 ms at 726 km (CPU side of `viewer.render()`).

## Tests

- `issModel.test.mjs`: visibility rules, the 109 m scale and centre against the shipped asset, flight axes along a propagated orbit, the embed URL.
- `issArticulation.test.mjs`: every array faces the Sun for a spread of Sun directions; radiators edge-on; feathering in shadow; joints keep the nearer of two equivalent answers; dish aim and relay directions; the arm sway stays small; every joint the code names exists in the model file.
- `issCommand.test.mjs`: when the panel shows; the zoom eases in and never overshoots; when the zoom is offered; the fast orbit; the status line.
- `npm test`, `npm run check:boundaries`, `npm run i18n`, `npm run format:check`, `npm run build`.
- In the app: arrays measured facing the Sun in daylight and feathered in shadow; panel collapsed on selection, Automatic by default, Manual controls, back to Automatic; zoom from 726 km to 265 m; phone-size viewport; Arabic (right-to-left).

## Screenshots

**ISS selected: the model, the collapsed command panel and the live video**

![ISS selected](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/IMBrandao/gods-eye-view/pr-assets/iss-3d-model/1-selected-far.jpg)

**After "Zoom to the ISS", Automatic mode, station in sunlight**

![Close, Automatic](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/IMBrandao/gods-eye-view/pr-assets/iss-3d-model/2-close-automatic.jpg)

**Manual mode, Sun set to "Overhead"**

![Manual controls](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/IMBrandao/gods-eye-view/pr-assets/iss-3d-model/3-manual-controls.jpg)

title: fix(shortcuts): a shortcut key held with Cmd, Ctrl or Alt runs no shortcut
body:
## Problem

The application shortcuts are bare keys read from every `keydown` that reaches the document: 1-6 pick a style, H the HUD, O orbit, V clean view, F the layers panel, D detection, C the CCTV layer. The listener skips form controls but never looks at the modifier keys, so a browser or system chord on the same key runs the shortcut as well:

- **Cmd+C / Ctrl+C (copy) turns the CCTV layer on and opens the camera nearest the view.** Where the catalog has no camera nearby, that camera is in another region or country.
- Cmd+F opens the layers panel, Cmd+H toggles the HUD, Cmd+D cycles detection, Cmd+O toggles orbit, Cmd+V clean view, Cmd+1 to 6 change the visual style.

To reproduce: open the app with CCTV off, click the globe so no field has focus, press Cmd+C. CCTV turns on and a camera opens.

## Change

`bindApplicationShortcuts` returns early when `metaKey`, `ctrlKey` or `altKey` is held. Unchanged:

- Shift is not treated as a chord, so `Shift+C` is still `C`.
- A held key still repeats its shortcut.
- Escape dismisses search with or without a modifier.
- Form controls keep native typing.

## A test pin changed

`visualInput.test.mjs` had `shortcut extraction does not change repeat or modifier policy`, which asserted that `Ctrl+H` (held, repeating) toggles the HUD. It pinned the behaviour across the extraction refactor. The repeat half is kept in a new test; the modifier half is the bug, so it is replaced by a test that no chord on any shortcut key runs a shortcut.

## Validation

- `npm run format:check`
- `npm test`: 12,624 pass, 0 fail
- `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md` updated ("Application shortcuts and shader parameter controls")
- Not run: `npm run test:track` and the `qa-*` browser gates. `npm run build` could not run in my checkout (Core's own `node_modules` is not installed there); a dependent application builds against this commit.

title: fix(cctv): a new camera's frame shows the moment it is decoded, without a fade
body: ## What this changes Clicking to another camera left the CCTV preview on an empty box for a moment. The preview settled as soon as the image had **loaded**, so the panel's `` took the src while it was still decoding, and then faded in over 180 ms. Now the preview settles once the frame is **decoded**, and the fade is gone. A decode that rejects still shows the loaded frame, as before. A decode that never settles (a hidden tab can hold it) shows the frame after one second. A failed refresh still keeps the settled pixels, and a camera change still never shows the old camera's frame. ## How I verified it - [x] `npm run build` - [x] `npm test` (two new tests in `src/ui/cctvControls.test.mjs`: decode settle and stale decode; rejected and never-settling decode) - [x] `npm run test:track` against the dev server: 98 checks passed. Two failed in areas this PR does not touch (`voice-context`: a satellite subject slot; `H1`: the tracked flight model's pick id), and the run then stopped when the dev server reloaded the page. - [x] Feature gate: switched cameras with NEXT/PREV in the running app and sampled the preview each frame. The only blank time left is the frame's own fetch.

title: fix(cctv): on a globe map the camera plane ends where the view meets the ground
body:
## What this changes

On a globe map (Esri imagery, for example), the active camera's monitor plane often stood at the camera's full range: about a kilometre wide and hundreds of metres up, filling the middle of the screen.

The activation probe raycasts with `scene.pickFromRay`, which picks primitives (the photoreal tiles) but never the globe. On a globe map the ray missed, or ran on through the Earth and met a primitive about 1,869 km away. Either way the range was never clamped.

Now:
- A hit at or beyond the camera's range counts as none.
- On a globe map the plane also clamps short of the globe's terrain along the axis (`globe.pick`). While that terrain is still loading or is met beyond the range, flat ground at the mount's own ground stands in. Whichever is nearer wins.
- The photoreal path, the user's range slider override, and the once-per-activation rule are unchanged.

## How I verified it

- [x] `npm run build`
- [x] `npm test` (new: `flatGroundAxisDistance` and the clamp it gives)
- [x] `npm run test:track` against the dev server: 98 checks passed. Two failed in areas this PR does not touch (`voice-context`: a satellite subject slot; `H1`: the tracked flight model's pick id), and the run then stopped when the dev server reloaded the page.
- [x] Feature gate: in the running app on the Esri imagery map, activated Oregon TripCheck cameras near Newport over repeated headless runs and read back the plane entity. Before, the plane was 1055 x 593 m about 260-300 m up. After, it is 118-145 m wide just in front of the camera, for each camera tried.

title: feat(vessels): a selected vessel shows its Open Vessel Photos photo and MMSI

Selecting a vessel now shows its photo from [Open Vessel Photos](https://openvesselphotos.org), a free, keyless photo API by MMSI with CORS open, under the vessel's name and MMSI in the CONTEXT panel's CONTACTS view.

- **Lookups:** once per MMSI, an 8-second timeout, a miss final for the session, and a failure asked again after five minutes (`src/layers/vessels/photos.js`).
- **Checks:** only an image on Open Vessel Photos' own https host is shown, and an answer about another MMSI counts as no photo (`src/data/openVesselPhoto.js`).
- **Source:** the vessel source exposes the lookup as `getEnrichment({kind: 'photo'})`. `fetchOpenVesselPhoto` is exported from `gods-eye-view/sources/live` for applications with their own vessel source.

## How I verified it

- [x] `npm run build`

title: feat(i18n): an ./i18n entry for an application with its own language choice
body:
## What

A new package entry, `./i18n` (`src/i18n/page.js`), for an application that composes Core and offers the interface language somewhere other than the globe picker (an account or settings menu), with `localePicker: false`:

- `startPageLocale(document)` starts the page in its language (`?lang=`, the stored choice, the browser's languages, English), sets `<html lang>`/`<html dir>` and translates the page's static `data-i18n` markup. Call it before any view renders.
- `followPageLocale(document)` keeps `<html lang>`/`dir` and the `data-i18n` markup in step with each switch; it returns the function that stops it.
- `switchLocale(code)` does what a picker choice does: switches in place and keeps the choice for the next visit (in `?lang` when storage is blocked). It returns `'unchanged'` for the active language.
- Re-exported for building a menu: `LOCALES`, `LOCALE_NAMES`, `DEFAULT_LOCALE`, `getLocale`, `onLocaleChange`, `isRtlLocale`, `applyDocumentTranslations`.

The standalone application now starts and follows its language with these, so the behaviour is the same in both.

Until now `localePicker: false` was documented as being for a host that does not initialize Core's locale; such a host had no supported way to start the stored language or switch it.

## Checks

- `src/i18n/page.test.mjs`: start order (`?lang=` over the stored choice), `lang`/`dir`, markup translated at start, a switch stored with `?lang` dropped and the hash kept, following and stopping, unchanged for the active language.
- `npm test`: 12,768 passed, 0 failed. `npm run check:boundaries` (new `i18n` group: 1 export, 16 modules, no externals), `npm run format:check` and `npm run i18n` pass.
- Checked in a browser: an application with its own language menu switches Core's panels, dock and `<html lang>` in place, and the choice is stored.

Docs: `docs/I18N.md` (new section), `docs/APPLICATION.md`, `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md`.

title: docs(performance): slowdown audit — 17 findings, their causes and the fix for each
body:
## What this is

A sweep of `main` for bugs that freeze the page or hold the frame rate down. This pull request adds `docs/PERFORMANCE-AUDIT-2026-11.md`, which records each finding, how it was measured, why it happens and how to fix it. It changes no code.

Each fix is its own pull request, listed below; this description is the index. Three findings (6, 10 and 17) were measured again while being fixed and turned out not to need one; the document says why.

## Findings and their fixes

Worst first. Measured on a keyless dev server in headless Chrome (Apple silicon, Metal), unless marked "read in code".

| # | Where | What happens | Fix |
| ---: | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Bike Share, local data, Transit, Rail | 18 s freeze switching Bike Share on over New York; 2.7 s on Data Centers; multi-second freezes with Transit | #1688, #1689 |
| 2 | Shipwrecks | 3–5 s freeze when markers are built over loaded terrain | #1703 |
| 3 | Camera | Rendering stops until reload after pan then wheel zoom at a whole-globe, straight-down view | #1704 |
| 4 | Street Traffic | Zooming over Manhattan: 25 long tasks in 24 s, longest 746 ms | #1705 |
| 5 | ALPR cameras | Depth samples inside the overlay paint, repeated on every re-enable (~1 s across eight toggles) | #1706 |
| 6 | Wind | Re-measured twice: Wind's two shader programs link during load in under 20 ms; the links seen on zoom are Cesium's own globe shaders, with Wind on or off. The ~30 renders/s is the animation at its 30 Hz cap | none needed |
| 7 | Submarine cables | ~2 s of long tasks on load, heap briefly 1 GB | #1707 (first step), #1722 (batched primitives, stacked on #1707) |
| 8 | Live Flights, whole globe, detection labels | 8 fps at 4x CPU throttle | #1708 (fleet pass), #1719 (detection overlay) |
| 9 | Radio | 7–10 long tasks on directory load, longest 447 ms | #1709 |
| 10 | Pointer pick | Not reproduced when re-measured: picks take 3–30 ms; the slow one is a one-off first pick per page load | none needed |
| 11 | CCTV | A still-image camera holds continuous rendering | #1710 |
| 12 | `/api/firms` (read in code) | Whole fire set serialised uncompressed per request | #1711 |
| 13 | AIS store (read in code) | Whole vessel map pruned per message | #1712 |
| 14 | Satellite clouds on 3D Tiles (read in code) | 90–180 ms CPU pixel pass per image | #1713 (canvas path), #1721 (shader, stacked on #1713) |
| 15 | NVG and FLIR styles | 100+ texture reads per pixel, and 60 renders/s while the style is on | #1718 |
| 16 | Wind server | GRIB decode on the event loop: 68 ms blocked per refresh, ~400 ms when all six keys refresh together | #1717 |
| 17 | Per-feature ground clamps, imported geo files | Measured afterwards: 20,000 imported points finish in ~1.5 s, longest task ~0.5 s; already batched | none needed |

The cause and the proposed fix for each are in the document.

## Limits

- Nothing was run on Google Photorealistic 3D Tiles, on a PC GPU, or with keyed feeds (AISStream, FIRMS, TomTom).
- Four profiling sessions shared one machine, so absolute timings carry noise.

title: i18n: review and fix the strings added since the last translation review
body:
Follow-up to the 27 pull requests merged since the last translation review (among them News, the Data Library, Wildlife Sightings, Shipwrecks, Rail, and the vessel and orbital cockpits): fixes the translations of their 474 new strings in all twelve languages, and most findings earlier reviews left open.

## What changes

- **Traditional Chinese.** `zh-Hant` is the `zh-CN` text in Traditional characters (`docs/translations/zh-Hant.md`). 133 of the new entries were translated separately with Taiwan vocabulary (影片, 伺服器, 載入, 加薩, 葉門…). The catalog is converted from `zh-CN` again with OpenCC `s2tw`. The guide lists two more characters OpenCC picks wrongly: 控制檯 → 控制台, and 周 → 週 where it means a week.
- **Placeholders that take a neutral value.** "Reported by {side} sources" read «Сообщают источники Международные», «fontes de Internacional», «Quellen aus Unabhängig». It now reads "sources: {side}" in de, es, fr, it, pt, ru, uk, he, ja and zh-CN. The Street View titles "{source} at {place}" got the same fix where {place} is "this point" or "the view centre" (de, fr, it, pt, he).
- **Counts without plural forms.** `{count} sightings in view`, `Showing {shown} of {total}`, the News time window (`Last {hours} h`, which offers 1 h) and the GhostMaps event age (which offers 1 day) are plain `t()` strings, so they read "1 Sichtungen", "1 dias", "últimas 1 horas". They are reworded so any number fits.
- **Shared-link notices.** "The shared flight / vessel / satellite isn't reporting now — … at {time}" said "common" or "joint" flight in ru, uk and zh-CN (共享航班 also reads as codeshare). In es, fr, it, pt and he, "at {time}" assumed a clock time, but `{time}` carries a date once the fix is over a day old.
- **Terms.** The wording now follows each glossary and the reviewed catalog: cockpit (it, zh-CN), site (ja, zh-CN, de), "Mapped installations" named as the layer is (ru, uk, es, zh-CN), course over ground, feed, Wikidata kept in Latin script (ar, he), "Live" in es, "OPT-IN" as enabled by the operator, not "optional".
- **Meaning.**
  - ar "Casualties" said "injuries".
  - ru and uk "Independently reported" said "confirmed".
  - de "Karte anklicken" on the shipwreck card read as "click the map".
  - ja "Before 1900" and "After 1945" overlapped the 1900–1945 chip.
  - pt "editor" named an editor instead of the publisher.
- **Typography.** The rules each language guide sets:
  - fr: narrow no-break space before `:` and `;`, straight apostrophes;
  - ja: full-width colons and brackets, no spaces between Japanese and Latin text;
  - zh-CN: spaces between Chinese and Latin text or numbers;
  - space before units (`{days} d`);
  - Ukrainian apostrophe ʼ.
- **Open findings from earlier reviews.** 61 of them are applied, among them the CCTV "pan or zoom out" hint, the GNSS regional-sample text, scene PLAY in es, and ru «ЖУРНАЛ ТАЙМИНГОВ». The rest stay as they are.

Not fixable in the catalogs, left for a code change:
- the plural-less counts above want `tn()`;
- `{range} NM` and `RINGS {spacing} NM` take fractional values;
- `{place}` receives the English "the view centre" from `src/voice/gevActions.js`;
- `Latest`, `FOCUS`, `CONFIRMED` and `{label} · COURSE {heading}°` are each one key shown in two places that need different wording.

## How I verified it

Three independent reviews per language, then a merge pass that checked each finding against the code (where and with which values the string is shown) and the language guide, and kept only the confirmed ones.

- [x] `npm run build` (empty keys)
- [x] `npm test`: 12,770 pass. Three tests expected the old German and Spanish wording and now expect the new.
- [ ] `npm run test:track`: not run, no runtime code changes
- [x] Feature gate: none applies. `npm run i18n` shows all 13 catalogs complete, and `npm run format:check`, `npm run check:boundaries` and `npm run layer-token:check` pass.

No native speaker has checked the new wording, and the UI was not opened in a browser, so the width of a few longer labels (for example «ВКЛЮЧАЕТ ОПЕРАТОР», «ATIV. PELO OPERADOR») is not checked.

## Docs

- [x] `changelog.d/<pr-number>-<slug>.md` fragment added; no `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md` change, translations only

title: i18n: generate zh-Hant from zh-CN
body:
## What this changes

`zh-Hant` is the `zh-CN` text in Traditional characters (`docs/translations/zh-Hant.md`), but nothing enforced it. `npm test` requires every catalog to be complete, so contributors filled `zh-Hant` by hand from `npm run i18n -- --missing zh-Hant`. A model asked for Traditional Chinese writes Taiwan vocabulary (影片, 伺服器, 載入, 圖示…), and #1698 had to regenerate 133 such entries. This PR makes the catalog generated:

- **`npm run i18n -- --zh-hant`** rewrites `src/i18n/locales/zh-Hant.json` from `zh-CN.json`: same keys in the same order, indent 2, trailing newline. It converts with OpenCC `s2tw` through [`opencc-js`](https://github.com/nk2028/opencc-js) (new devDependency, pinned to 1.4.2; `cn` → `tw` changes characters only, unlike `twp`), then applies the fixed list of characters OpenCC picks wrongly: 年曆史 → 年歷史, 下遊 → 下游, 並道 → 併道 (only in entries whose English key says merge), 發佈 → 發布, 公佈 → 公布, 宣佈 → 宣布, 控制檯 → 控制台, 箇中 → 個中 (全部 {n} 個中), and ` 周/秒` → ` 週/秒`. The list is `ZH_HANT_CORRECTIONS` in `scripts/i18n.mjs`, next to the conversion.
- **The check.** `npm run i18n` and `npm test` (`src/i18n/catalog.test.mjs`) fail when `zh-Hant` differs from the conversion of `zh-CN`. Each error names the key, e.g. `"Video" is "影片", not zh-CN converted ("視頻"). zh-Hant is generated: edit zh-CN, then run npm run i18n -- --zh-hant`. A missing or extra key, or a key out of `zh-CN` order, fails too. A key `zh-CN` already has is reported once, with `run npm run i18n -- --zh-hant`. Without `node_modules`, the zh-Hant check says to run `npm ci` and the other checks still run.
- **`--missing zh-Hant`** no longer prints a template. It says to add the entries to `zh-CN` and run the command, and exits 1.
- **Docs.** One line each in `docs/TRANSLATORS.md` and `docs/I18N.md`. `docs/translations/zh-Hant.md` now says not to translate the catalog and describes the command. The i18n gate in `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md` mentions it.

**The conversion matched the catalog, then main moved on.** When the PR was opened, converting `zh-CN` reproduced all 3346 entries of `zh-Hant` on main exactly, and the only change was 25 keys moving into `zh-CN` order. Since then main has added zh-Hant entries by hand, again in Taiwan wording (搜尋, 資料, 即時, 儲存, 「」 for 搜索, 數據, 實時, 保存, “”). After merging main (624c229bc), 91 of the 3818 entries are not `zh-CN` converted, and the last commit regenerates them; keys and order stay. Two of those entries showed characters OpenCC picks wrongly, now in the list: 箇中 → 個中 and 宣佈 → 宣布. #1700, merged after that, edits `zh-Hant` in line with the conversion: on a merge with it, `--zh-hant` changes nothing. Open branches that add `zh-Hant` entries by hand will fail the check until they run `npm run i18n -- --zh-hant`. One correction, 控制檯 → 控制台, never fires with this dictionary version (1.4.2 already writes 控制台). It stays in the list in case a later version changes that.

`opencc-js` is loaded on first use, so code that only extracts messages never loads the dictionaries. `src/i18n/stale-index.test.mjs` copies the script into a folder without `node_modules`, and it still passes. The package is not in the app bundle.

Not changed: `src/i18n/same-as-english.json` still has its own `zh-Hant` list (identical to the `zh-CN` one). An entry `zh-CN` keeps in English needs the same line under `zh-Hant`, and the zh-Hant guide says so.

## How I verified it

- [x] `npm run build` (empty keys): passes. `dist` has no `opencc-js` code and no Google key.
- [x] `npm test` after merging main: 14,427 pass, 3 skipped. Two Cesium camera tests (`cameraGoldens`, `cameraPort`) fail on my Mac, on plain main too; main's CI passes them. New tests cover the real catalogs, the conversion (視頻, not 影片; the corrections), each error, and the command line in a throwaway repo (`src/i18n/zh-hant-cli.test.mjs`).
- [ ] `npm run test:track`: not run, no runtime code changes
- [x] Feature gate: `npm run i18n` shows all 13 catalogs complete. `npm run format:check` and `npm run check:boundaries` pass. I also changed one `zh-Hant` entry by hand: the check failed and named the key, and `--zh-hant` restored the file byte for byte. Adding then pruning a stale `zh-CN` entry pruned both catalogs.

## Docs

- [x] `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md` updated and a `changelog.d/<pr-number>-<slug>.md` fragment added

title: i18n: plural forms and contexts the catalogs could only work around
body:
## What this changes

Follow-up to #1698. That translation review found problems it could only reword around in the catalogs. They are fixed in the code now, and the catalogs go back to natural wording in all twelve languages.

- **Counts with plain `t()` are `tn()` plurals.** The wildlife count (`{count} sightings in view`), the Data Library `Showing {shown} of {total}`, the News time window (`Last {hours} h` and the three News strings around it; the window offers 1 h) and the GhostMaps event age (which offers 1 day). The English keys stay, so only the catalog entries change, from strings to plural forms:
  - es «Última 1 h» / «Últimas 24 h», de «1 Tag» / «7 Tage», it «1 giorno» / «7 giorni»;
  - ru «Новости за последний 1 час» / «за последние 12 часов», «1 наблюдение» / «5 наблюдений в кадре»;
  - he «השעה האחרונה (1)», «מוצג 1» / «מוצגים 3», following `LAST {count} DAYS`;
  - ar «آخر ساعة (1)», «آخر 3 ساعات», «آخر 12 ساعة».

  Languages whose wording already fit any number (ru/uk «дн.», fr «j», sv «h», ja, zh) keep it in every form.
- **The bridge radar range and ring spacing are `tn()` plurals.** The spacing is a fraction at the short ranges (0.75 and 1.5 NM), and `Intl.PluralRules` gives fractions a form of their own. `Intl.NumberFormat` has no nautical-mile unit, so this goes through the plural rules:
  - ru «3 МОР. МИЛИ», «12 МОР. МИЛЬ», «КОЛЬЦА 0,75 МОР. МИЛИ» (uk the same), replacing the earlier «МОР. МИЛ.»;
  - ar gets proper noun forms;
  - every other language keeps its symbol (NM, SM, MN, 海里) in all forms.
- **Street level no longer passes a phrase as `{place}`.** With no place to name, the voice plan step passed "the view centre" or "this spot" into `{source} at {place}` and `Street level at {place}`. Those phrases now have messages of their own (`{source} at the view centre`, `Street level at this spot` …), so `{place}` only receives a name. The step also reads its arguments the way `show_street_level` does: a pointed or numbered thing has no place yet, and "this spot" needs both coordinates. The on-screen progress line had the same leak and showed the English phrase («Bilder werden geöffnet: the view centre»). An empty search at the view centre already shows the Street Level layer's own translated text, so it needs no new message.
- **Keys shared by two places are split with a context.**
  - `Latest`: the News heading, now plural like the news under it (fr «Dernières»; es, it, pt and he too). Its other user, the timeline button, has since left main, so plain `Latest` is pruned.
  - `FOCUS`: the orbital site status, now the word the FOCUS card above it uses (es «ENFOQUE», fr «CENTRÉ», it «PUNTAMENTO», pt «FOCO», he «מוקד»). The FOCUS command keeps its verb.
  - `CONFIRMED`: the Wildlife chip, which names the sightings: sv «BEKRÄFTADE», plus the plural in es «CONFIRMADOS», it «CONFERMATI», fr, pt, he and ar. A launch landing keeps «BEKRÄFTAD».
  - `{label} · COURSE {heading}°`: a ship's course (pt «RUMO»). An aircraft's is now «CURSO», as the pt glossary has it.
- **Checked against the other two #1698 notes.**
  - `CURRENTLY OVER` is followed by a country name in the nominative. In uk, de, it and pt the label ended in a preposition that needs another case or an article («над Україною», «über den Vereinigten Staaten», «sopra gli Stati Uniti»). There it is now the noun for an overflight, which a bare name can follow: uk «ПРОЛІТ», de «ÜBERFLUG», it «SORVOLO», pt «SOBREVOO». Each is shorter than the old label, so a place name keeps its room on a phone. In the other languages the current wording works.
  - `CONFIRM · REMOVE ALL {count}` already works: it «TUTTE LE {count}» refers to *voci*, whose article doesn't change with the number, and he avoids the article.

`docs/I18N.md` gains the two rules behind these fixes. The language guides record the new terms: the nautical mile (ru, uk), the FOCUS status, the CONFIRMED chip, CURRENTLY OVER, and pt «rumo» for a ship's course. zh-Hant is converted from zh-CN with OpenCC `s2tw` plus the guide's corrections; the conversion reproduces the existing catalog apart from the documented 週 exception.

## How I verified it

- [x] `npm run build` (empty keys)
- [x] `npm test` on the branch merged with main: 14,418 of 14,423 pass (3 skipped). The two that fail, the Cesium camera traces in `cameraGoldens` and `cameraPort`, fail the same way on main on macOS and pass in main's CI. New tests at each call site:
  - plural forms for the wildlife count, the News window (es, ru), the Data Library status (he), the GhostMaps age (de, es) and the radar range and rings (ru, all four ranges);
  - the street-level plan step for the view centre, this spot, a pointed and a numbered thing (de, en);
  - each context split (sv chip and landing, es site status, card and command, pt aircraft and ship, fr News heading).
- [x] `npm run test:track` against a keyless dev server: 111 passed
- [x] Feature gate: `npm run i18n` shows all 13 catalogs complete; `npm run format:check`, `npm run check:boundaries` and `npm run layer-token:check -- --base-ref origin/main` pass. `scripts/qa-data-library.mjs` 21/21 and `scripts/qa-street-level.mjs` pass. `scripts/qa-ghostmaps.mjs` passes its event-age checks but fails its live-data checks: it expects the product `kinetic-30d`, which the live S2 repository no longer publishes (unrelated to this change).
- Headless check against `npm run dev` and `npm run preview` with empty keys: all 13 locales boot from `?lang=` without page errors, and every changed message renders as expected with the browser's `Intl.PluralRules` (the same forms Node picks). Walked through at 1440 and 375 px: the News window and empty states (es, ru, fr, he, ar), the Data Library line with 0, 1 and 2 entries (he, fr, it), the Wildlife chip and count (sv, es), the GhostMaps age (de, es), and the orbital view's CURRENTLY OVER line and site rows (uk, de, es, fr, it). The bridge radar and a ship's course need an AIS key, so their strings were checked through the page's i18n module.
- A full review (bugs, security, text, the project's review policy, and the frontend in a headless browser) found nothing blocking. Its eleven minor findings are fixed in the second commit.

No native speaker has checked the new wording.

## Docs

- [x] `changelog.d/<pr-number>-<slug>.md` fragment added; no `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md` change, wording only

title: Recent Imagery: drape the next ranked day when the automatic day is empty
body: ## What this changes When the automatic Recent Imagery day probes empty, the layer hands over to the next ranked day. That day was probed and came back present, but it never reached the map. Two ways to hit it: - VIIRS only, SHOW EMPTY DAYS on, and today's overview is empty. Follow moves to yesterday, but focus stays on today's empty card. Yesterday probes present, the map stays empty, and yesterday's card shows LOADING for good. - HLS and VIIRS, with a strip of V21, S18, V15. The automatic day S18 probes empty and follow moves to V21. Focus moves to the nearest card instead, and a tie goes to the older day, so it lands on V15. V21 probes present and is never draped. The cause: the thumbnail subscriber previews a followed day only while it is focused (`_followKey === _focusKey`). `autoPreview()` sets focus only when there is none, and `reconcileFocus()` moves focus off a hidden card to its nearest neighbour, not to the next ranked day. After the hand-over, follow and focus point at different days. The fix: `pruneEmpty()` passes the empty automatic day to `autoPreview()`, and focus still on that day moves to the successor. If the user moved focus elsewhere, it stays where it is. The subscriber is unchanged. ## How I verified it - Two new layer tests in `src/layers/recentImagery/index.test.mjs`, one per case above. Both fail on main (`preview.key` is null instead of the successor) and pass with the fix. - Recent Imagery suites: 92/92 pass. - `npm test`: 12,775 tests, 12,772 pass, 0 fail, 3 skipped; both allocation probes pass (1/1 and 14/14). - `npm run format:check` and `npm run check:boundaries` pass. - Headless Chrome against the dev server with no keys, first case: VIIRS only, SHOW EMPTY DAYS on, today's probe answered empty, yesterday's probe from the live network. All 14 checks pass: follow and focus move to yesterday, yesterday probes present, previews and drapes, and nothing stays pending. With the fix taken out of the served file, the same run reproduces the bug: focus stays on today, the preview stays empty and yesterday stays pending. - `node scripts/qa-recent-imagery.mjs`, headless and without keys: 107 checks, 5 failures, 11 skipped (the Google 3D branch). Main fails the same 5 checks in the same run: B preview by arrows, the oversized USE VIEW notice, the collapsed header, and the collapsed-panel layout at 900 and 700 px. - Not run: `npm run build` and `npm run test:track`. ## Before / after Base `346269f50` (where the branch leaves main) and head `06dccdb00`, captured the same way on both sides: keyless headless Chrome, English UI, 1440 × 900, software rendering, a fixed clock (September 21 UTC) and the same camera over central Italy. Both sides get the same catalog entries, probe replies and raster bytes in the same order. These are fixtures: a bundled Natural Earth II raster stands in for the dated imagery, so the map shots show whether a day is draped, not real imagery. **VIIRS only, SHOW EMPTY DAYS on, today's overview empty.** Before, focus stays on the empty September 21 card and September 20 says LOADING. After, September 20 has focus and PREVIEW. 31.6% of pixels differ. Before, the grayscale basemap shows through. After, September 20 is draped. 100% of pixels differ. **HLS and VIIRS, the automatic HLS day September 18 empty.** Before, focus lands on the older September 15 card and September 21 stays LOADING. After, September 21 has focus and PREVIEW. 31.59% of pixels differ. Before, the grayscale basemap shows through. After, September 21 is draped. 100% of pixels differ. **A day picked while the automatic day is still being probed.** September 15 keeps focus on both sides. After the change it reaches PREVIEW, and September 21 no longer waits in LOADING. 31.0% of pixels differ. ## Docs `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md` now says that focus moves with the hand-over and the successor drapes once present. Changelog fragment: `changelog.d/1701-recent-imagery-auto-successor.md`.

title: Keep an explicit CCTV pick of the camera a move re-opened
body: ## Problem Turn on CCTV, then move the view somewhere else, for example to London. Until someone picks a camera, CCTV follows the view: when the move settles, it switches to the camera nearest the view (here Charing Cross Rd / Cambridge Circus). Now press NEAREST. The nearest camera is the same one, so the pick looks done. It does not stick. When NEAREST's own flight lands, CCTV switches to Shaftesbury Ave / Macclesfield St. A pan to Trafalgar Square then switches it to the Trafalgar Square camera. The panel shows a camera the user did not pick, while the view shows the one they did. FOCUS on the shown camera, and a scene or voice command that selects it, have the same problem. ## Cause `setActiveCamera` ends the opening pick by clearing `_openingCameraProvisional`. For a camera that is already active and activated, it returns `UNCHANGED` early, so re-selecting it does not flash the monitor plane. That early return skips the line that clears the flag. A settled move re-opens CCTV through `reopenNearestCamera`. It activates the nearest camera and sets the flag back to true, because this is still the opening pick. So an explicit pick of that same camera takes the early return, the flag stays set, and every later settled move picks the nearest camera again. ## Fix - `src/layers/cctv/selection.js`: a pick clears the flag on the `UNCHANGED` path too. This covers NEAREST (`focusNearest`), FOCUS and scenes (`setParams({ selectedCameraId })`), `selectCamera` and `focusNearestToPoint`. Re-selecting the active camera still skips the activation work. - `src/layers/cctv/navigation.js`: `reopenNearestCamera` calls `setActiveCamera(nearest, { opening: true })`, so the camera it opens stays the opening pick. - The camera list cannot pick the camera it already shows: a native select sends no `change` for the option it shows. To keep that camera, press FOCUS, or NEAREST when it is the nearest. Closing the list without a choice keeps automatic selection. `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md` now says when automatic selection ends. ## Tests - `src/data/cctvExplicitPickEndsOpening.test.mjs`: a settled move re-opens the layer on a second camera. Picking that camera with NEAREST, `selectCamera`, `setParams({ selectedCameraId })` or `focusNearestToPoint` keeps it through the next settled move. A control case checks that without a pick the next settled move still follows the view. - `src/ui/cctvPickerOpening.test.mjs`: the CCTV panel on the real layer. The shown camera is its own visible option, listed once. FOCUS on it keeps it after a pan. Opening and closing the list without a choice lets it follow the pan. - `src/layers/cctv/selection.test.mjs`: the `UNCHANGED` path ends the opening pick without notifying snapshot feeds. Without the `selection.js` change, the four pick cases, the selection case and the FOCUS case fail. ## Checks - `npm test` on `ab33ac533` (main merged at `ba0d92650`): 15,574 tests, 15,571 pass, 0 fail, 3 skipped. - CCTV, voice and scene tests: 731 of 731 pass. - `npm run format:check`, `npm run check:boundaries` and a build without map keys: pass. - `scripts/qa-camera-controls.mjs` against a preview without map keys, before the main merge: 20 of 21 pass. "Contacts isolation keeps the open CCTV panel and restores its camera" fails on main too. - Browser, dev server without map keys, headless: no hidden option in the list; closing the list without a choice lets the camera follow a pan; after FOCUS the camera stays through its own landing and a pan (6 of 6). ## Before and after Before is main at `ba0d92650`, after is this branch at `ab33ac533`. Both run headless at 1440 × 900 with the same clock and seed, without map keys and without Google 3D Tiles. The map is an offline street schematic with fixture camera poses and feed frames; coverage and projection are off. NEAREST and FOCUS run their normal flights. Red frames mark what differs. **NEAREST on the camera already shown.** Before, the panel switches to Shaftesbury Ave / Macclesfield St when the flight lands. After, it keeps Charing Cross Rd / Cambridge Circus. **Pan to Trafalgar Square after NEAREST.** Before, the panel switches to Trafalgar Square. After, it keeps Charing Cross Rd / Cambridge Circus. **FOCUS on the camera already shown.** Before, the panel switches to Shaftesbury Ave / Macclesfield St when the flight lands. After, it keeps Charing Cross Rd / Cambridge Circus. **Pan to Trafalgar Square after FOCUS.** Before, the panel switches to Trafalgar Square. After, it keeps Charing Cross Rd / Cambridge Circus. **Pan to Trafalgar Square without a pick.** Identical on both sides: CCTV still follows the view.

title: perf(shipwrecks): place markers without a terrain height read each
body:
## What was slow and how to see it

Open `/?welcome=0`, let the globe load, then switch Shipwrecks on. The page freezes for about three seconds (up to five in other runs) while the 7,958 markers are built.

## Cause

`rebuild()` in `src/layers/shipwrecks/index.js` added every billboard with `heightReference: CLAMP_TO_GROUND`. A ground-clamped billboard reads the terrain height as it is created (`Billboard._updateClamping` → a ray against the terrain mesh), and all of those reads ran in one task. The cost is only paid when terrain is loaded at the time the markers are built.

## What changed

The markers are placed on the ellipsoid with no height reference. Wrecks lie at sea, the depth test is already off, and the card already sits at that position, so the marker shows in the same place.

## Before and after

Keyless dev server, headless Chrome at 1440 x 900 (Apple silicon, Metal), same script on `main` (`188f0ccd9`) and on this branch. Two runs each, switching the layer on after the globe has loaded.

| | `main` | this branch |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Long tasks | 1 | 0 |
| Longest task | 2,943 / 3,038 ms | none |
| `getHeight` calls | 7,958 (2,881 / 2,990 ms) | 0 |
| Markers built / shown | 7,958 / 7,222 | 7,958 / 7,222 |

A screenshot of the layer is pixel-identical on both, and clicking a marker opens its card on both.

## Tests

- A new unit test fails on the unfixed file (the billboard still carries a height reference).
- Unit suite, `format:check`, `check:boundaries` and `build` pass locally.

## Not tested

- An oblique close-up of a wreck in an inland lake above the ellipsoid: the marker now sits on the ellipsoid rather than the lake surface (the depth test is off, so it still draws).
- Google Photorealistic 3D Tiles.

title: fix(camera): a wheel zoom at the screen centre no longer stops rendering
body:
## What was broken and how to see it

From a whole-globe view looking straight down, one wheel notch with the pointer on the centre pixel of the canvas can stop rendering for good. Cesium shows "An error occurred while rendering. Rendering has stopped. DeveloperError: normalized result is not a number" and nothing draws again until the page is reloaded. No layer needs to be on.

Repro on `main` (keyless dev server, 1440×900 window so the centre pixel is 720,450):

1. Open `/?welcome=0#lat=30&lon=-30&alt=22000000&pitch=-90&v=2`.
2. Put the camera straight down, 22,000 km above lat −13.37, lon −41.11 (also lat 27.78, lon 72.34 and lat −40.75, lon −117.25).
3. Move the pointer to the centre of the canvas and scroll in one notch.

It was first seen as "pan the globe, then wheel-zoom": the pan only moves the camera onto a pose where the rounding below goes the wrong way.

## Cause

Pure Cesium; `src/app/zoomOutGuard.js` is not involved (it only reads input and eases pitch after the frame).

Above 1,000 km, `handleZoom` in `ScreenSpaceCameraController` turns the globe from the point under the screen centre towards the point under the pointer. It normalizes both points, takes their dot product, and when that is between 0 and 1 rotates the camera about their cross product. With the pointer on the centre pixel the two points are the same. A unit vector's dot product with itself often rounds to 0.9999999999999999, so the check passes while the cross product is exactly the zero vector. `Camera.rotate` normalizes it and throws.

The throw comes from `Scene.initializeFrame`, which runs outside the scene's error handling, so `scene.renderError` never fires. Cesium's render loop catches it, turns itself off and shows the panel.

## What changed

- `src/app/renderRecovery.js` (new), installed in `createApplicationViewer`:
  - `guardDegenerateRotation(camera)`: `camera.rotate` returns without rotating when the axis is zero or not finite, or the angle is not finite. The zoom then carries on and moves the camera in. Ordinary rotations are passed through unchanged.
  - `installRenderRecovery(viewer)`: when an error stops the render loop, put the camera back on the last pose a frame drew with, drop the input that was being applied, and turn the loop back on. At most 3 restarts in 10 s; after that Cesium's panel is shown as before. It hooks the widget's `showErrorPanel`, because that is the only place both kinds of stop (during frame preparation, and during render) pass through.
- `scripts/package-boundaries.json`: the new module is listed beside `atmosphereCompat.js` in the two packages that own `viewer.js`.

## Before and after

Same script on both (fresh page per run, the three poses above in turn, one wheel notch at the centre), headless Chrome, keyless:

| | Runs | Rendering stopped | Zoomed in normally |
|---|---|---|---|
| `main` (188f0ccd9) | 10 | 10 | 0 |
| This branch | 10 | 0 | 10 |

The original "drag the globe 8 times, then wheel-zoom" repro stopped rendering in 4 of 8 runs on `main` across two sessions, and 0 of 3 on this branch.

## Tested

- `src/app/renderRecovery.test.mjs` (9 tests): the zoom's own arithmetic produces a zero axis and unguarded `Camera.rotate` throws on it; the guarded camera does not move; ordinary rotations match Cesium exactly; a stopped loop restarts from the last drawn pose; a pose from a broken camera is not kept; the restart limit and its window; a panel shown while the loop runs is left alone; disposal.
- In the app, with the rotate guard removed in the page so the Cesium error still happens: the loop restarted once, no panel, 60 frames in the next second.
- `node scripts/run-unit-tests.mjs`, `npm run format:check`, `npm run check:boundaries`, `npm run build`.

## Not tested

- The restart limit (3 in 10 s) in the app; unit tests only.
- A production build's behaviour on `main`. If the bundled Cesium has its debug checks stripped, the same input would write NaN into the camera instead of throwing; the rotate guard covers that too, but I did not reproduce it.
- Touch pinch. The same code path applies when the pinch centre lands on the canvas centre.
- The embedded panel's own stalled-frame watchdog (`src/app/embed.js`) still marks itself failed on `scene.renderError`; not changed here.
