title: Draw airport ground vehicles by callsign and ground stations as a radio mast
body:
## What this changes

Airport ground vehicles and ground stations now draw as what they are instead of the generic plane.

- **Airport vehicles (type `ZVEH`)** pick a model by callsign (`aircraft_callsign` rules in `types.json`, upper case, spaces ignored, first match wins): `FIRE…` fire truck, `PUSH…`/`TUG…` pushback tug, `DEICER…`/`SQUID…`/`SQB…` van, anything else a car.
- **Ground stations (type `GRND`)** draw a new 11.8 m radio mast (`public/models/fleet/other/radio_mast.glb`, 940 tris; set is now 122 models).
- These vehicles and the mast (catalog category `other`) are drawn at their built size, and a contact with no altitude whose model is one of them stands on the ground instead of at the 10 km airborne default. Such contacts keep the feed's own type, since no airframe lookup knows `ZVEH`/`GRND`.
- `resolveAircraft` / `aircraftModelSpec` take the callsign (new `aircraftCallsignRule` export); a matched rule outranks a type's class model. The layer spec cache keys these types by the rule matched, so it holds at most one entry per rule. Local ADS-B passes the callsign too.
- `civil-flight-records` in `scripts/package-boundaries.json` now owns `src/data/fleetModels.js` and `src/data/fleetTrailAnchors.js`, which `records.js` imports to decide whether a contact is a ground model.

**Why:** feeds carry many such contacts, and they were drawn as generic planes, some hovering at 10 km over the airport.

## How I verified it

- [x] `npm run build`
- [x] `npm test` (12,938 tests, 0 failures), including new cases in `src/data/fleetModels.test.mjs`, `src/data/modelScale.test.mjs` and `src/layers/flights/records.test.mjs`
- [x] `npm run format:check`, `npm run check:boundaries`, `npm run doctor -- --json`, `npm run layer-token:check -- --base-ref origin/main`, `npm run library:check -- --base-ref origin/main`
- [ ] `npm run test:track` (not run)
- [ ] Feature gate: none applies

## Docs

- [x] `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md` updated; `changelog.d/1729-fleet-ground-vehicles.md` added

title: Rebuild the airport vehicle models with real shapes
body:
Airport ground vehicles (type `ZVEH`) were drawn as stacked boxes: the car read as a small pickup, and close up every one looked broken.

- **car**: an operations SUV, 4.6 × 1.85 × 1.84 m, with a rounded body, a glass house with sloped windscreen and hatch, a roof light bar, a grille, lamps and mirrors
- **van**: a high-roof panel van, 5.5 × 2.0 × 2.56 m, with a short bonnet, a steep windscreen, cab windows, a rub strip and a beacon
- **fire_truck**: an airport crash tender, 11 m long and 3.6 m to the turret, with a forward cab, a locker body with stripe and shutters, roof and bumper turrets and three axles
- **pushback**: a low chamfered tug with a glazed cab, a hitch and bumpers

All four stand within 3 cm of the ground at their built size; these `other` models are not scaled. Their trail anchors are measured again (`scripts/measure-fleet-trail-anchors.mjs`). The set grows by about 18 KB.

Tests: `node --test src/data/fleetModels.test.mjs src/data/modelScale.test.mjs` passes.

title: Draw aircraft models in their own mesh colours
body:
Aircraft models (Flights, Military Flights, Local ADS-B) mixed 94% of a flat class colour over the mesh (`MODEL_COLOR_BLEND_AMOUNT = 0.94`, MIX), so every airliner drew as a white silhouette and every military aircraft as amber, whatever the model's paint.

- Models now blend with `HIGHLIGHT` (`aircraftModelBlend` in `src/data/aircraftModelLighting.js`). White leaves the mesh's colours as built; the tracked (cyan / amber) and emergency (red) colours multiply into the mesh, so the paint still shows.
- Ordinary contacts draw white (the mesh as built), including military ones and Local ADS-B. Billboards keep their colours.
- The IR boost is unchanged: flat white, MIX at 1, unlit.
- The dynamic environment map stays off.
- `MODEL_COLOR_BLEND_AMOUNT` and the specs' `blendAmount` are removed.

Tests: `npm test`, with the tint and Local ADS-B assertions updated. Checked over SFO with 3D models set to all: liveries (tail colours, grey bellies) show, and models are not darkened.

title: fix(flights): an aircraft with no ground track faces its true heading, not north
body:
## What this changes

readsb rows often send no `track` for an aircraft on the ground, only `true_heading`. The track then read as missing and the aircraft was drawn facing north, so a plane taxiing south looked like it was moving backwards. The adsb.lol fallback (`src/data/adsbLolFallback.js`), the readsb source (`src/sources/live/aircraft.js`) and the local dump1090 receiver (`src/sources/adsbRecords.js`) now fall back to `true_heading` when there is no track. They never use the magnetic heading.

## How I verified it

- [ ] `npm run build` (not run locally; left to CI)
- [ ] `npm test` (not run in full locally; left to CI)
- [ ] `npm run test:track` (not run)
- [x] Feature gate for the area I touched: `node --test src/sources/adsbRecords.test.mjs src/sources/live/contract.test.mjs src/data/adsbLolFallback.test.mjs` (38 pass). Each of the three normalizers has a new test: the track wins over the heading, `true_heading` is used when there is no track, `mag_heading` alone gives none, and an empty row gives none. The readsb test fails without the fix.

Seen live: a 737 taxiing at SFO with no track in its adsb.lol rows was drawn nose-north while moving south-south-west.

title: Draw aids to navigation as buoys
body:
Buoys, beacons, RACONs, lights and IALA marks in the vessel feed were drawn as ships. Core ships 24 buoy models, but nothing chose them.

- `isAidToNavigation` (`src/data/vesselTypes.js`): a record is an aid when its type names one of the 32 aid kinds (cardinal N/E/S/W, port or starboard hand, safe water, isolated danger, special mark, RACON, lights, …), or when its MMSI is an aid station's (`99MIDxxxx`). Buoy tenders and buoy layers stay ships.
- `vesselModelSpec` draws an aid as the buoy model of its mark, at its built size, and flags it fixed: it faces north and does not turn to a heading. A type that names no mark gets the red can.
- Icons: an aid is a bone-white disc, not a chevron. Its card, selected card and HUD show its kind, with no speed or heading.
- AISStream subscribes to `AidsToNavigationReport` by default. Aid type codes 0–31 are stored as their kind, and the name extension is joined to the name.
- Aids never take ships' places: `aisStreamRows` lists every vessel ahead of every aid. `vessels_in_area` (and the brief built on it) counts ships only.

Tests: `npm test` (12,936 pass, 4 skipped), `format:check`, `check:boundaries`, `changelog:check`, `i18n`. Checked in the browser near Fort Point: every mark draws as its own buoy, a container ship beside them is unchanged, and zoomed out the aids show as discs.

title: Draw transit vehicles as trolleybuses, cable cars, funiculars, gondolas and monorails
body:
The transit layer knew five modes (bus, tram, subway, rail, ferry). A trolleybus therefore drew as a bus, a funicular as a train, and a coach as a city bus, even though `types.json` already maps every GTFS route type to a fleet model.

- **New modes:** trolleybus, `cable_tram`, monorail, funicular and `aerial_lift`. Each has heading and neutral icons, a colour, a detection tier in every theme, a card word in all 13 locales, a voice name, a speed ceiling and a fleet model.
- **`routeType`:** a vehicle record may carry its route's GTFS `route_type`.
  - It settles the mode after the feed's fleet hint (so a bus on a tram route stays a bus) and before its route hint.
  - It picks the finer model when the type is a kind of the vehicle's mode, for example a coach for 200 and a high-speed set for 101.
- **Trails:** retained history classifies epochs with `transitModeFor`, so trails join the live vehicle.
- **Route hints and corrections:**
  - Hints from each operator's routes.txt: Prague's trolleybus lines and Petřín funicular, and the trams, trolleybuses and metro of Bucharest, Cluj-Napoca and Turin.
  - A feed may also name route corrections that outrank the route type. Le Havre's routes.txt types its funicular (`8-FUNI`) as a bus, so it is corrected.

**Checks:** `npm test` (12,963 pass), `format:check`, `check:boundaries`, `changelog:check` and `i18n` all pass. Checked in the browser on the Prague feed: 25 vehicles classed as trolleybuses, and line 53 drew with the trolleybus model.

title: Side rails: Visual on the left rail, edge mode and edge scrolling
body:
Side rails and the screen edge, by @manjunath22466 and @samehkhamis.

## What

- **Visual moves to the left rail**, as the last left panel after Data Layers, Utilities and Authoring. Context leads the right column. An open Context or CCTV panel takes the column's full height; the other right panels keep the content-sized layout.
- **Rails:** with nothing open, a rail's icons and names show as two glass pieces side by side; once a panel opens, the icons stay put and a highlight slides to the open one.
- **Edge switch** in each panel header (`UiPanelEdge.vue`, `src/ui/panelEdge.js`): moves that side's panels over their rail to the screen edge, with the rail as a row of icons above the open panel. Per side, kept in `localStorage`, desktop shell only.
- **Edge scrolling** (`src/ui/railEdgeScroll.js`): the wheel at a screen edge steps that side's rail to the next or previous panel instead of zooming the globe. One gesture is one step, at least half a second apart. Panels, controls, dialogs and the world timeline keep their own wheel; off on phones, touch screens, and while the rails are hidden (clean view, recording); follows the rails' sides in right-to-left languages.
- Minimal HUD shows its coordinates once, and the side rails line up.

The phone keeps its sheets: Visual is in More with Visual Presets, as before. The dock keeps Location and Visual Presets.

## Verified

- `npm run build`, `npm test` (12,973 tests), `npm run test:track` (111 passed), `npm run format:check`, `npm run i18n`.
- New `src/ui/railEdgeScroll.test.mjs` (9 tests); the right-rail hysteresis tests now use a content-sized panel, plus a test for the full-height rule.
- In Chrome: rails, Visual from the left rail, wheel steps, edge mode, right-to-left (Arabic layout), the phone's More sheet, and the Cyber HUD.

title: Fix scrubs to live on long tracks, fire ages in a past window, and gaps between hourly cloud frames
body:
Three time readings on the world timeline went wrong once a layer's time reached far from now.

- **Scrubbing near now on a long track.** A scrub counted as live within 0.5% of the track. With a layer whose source covers years, the unzoomed track is about 14 years, so any time within about 25 days of now snapped to live. The window is now at most two minutes, with the 5 s floor kept; tracks under about 6.7 hours keep the window they had. Dragging the hand to the end, End, and Back to live still go live. (`src/ui/stores/worldTime.js`)
- **Fire ages in a window that ends at a set time.** When the fire snapshot covers the 24 hours to a set time (the `at` its stats report as "24 h to MM-DD HH:MM UTC"), card and detail ages were counted from now, so a fire three hours old at the time shown read "new 105d". Ages now count back from the end of the window shown, and from now while live. The cached-data age in the stats still counts from now. (`src/layers/firms/model.js` `ageReferenceMs`, `cards.js`, `selection.js`)
- **Gaps between frames of a feed with sparse frames.** Regional satellite clouds hold a frame for 30 minutes and read late after 20, so a feed whose frames come an hour apart drew nothing for the second half of every hour while scrubbing, and its latest frame read late from 20 minutes on. A product's max gap and late delay are now at least 1.5 times its feed's median frame spacing. Feeds with frames minutes apart keep their values; an hourly feed draws continuously. (`src/layers/weather/clock.js` `frameSpacingMs` / `atLeastFrameSpacing`, `index.js`)

**Tests:** each fix has a regression test that fails without it (`WorldTimeline.test.mjs`, `firms/windowLabel.test.mjs`, `weather/clock.test.mjs`, `weather/weather.test.mjs`). `npm test`, `format:check`, `check:boundaries`, `changelog:check` and `i18n` pass. `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md` describes the new behaviour.

title: Let a host application place live contacts
body:
An application can decide where its live contacts are drawn, with no change to how Core draws them by default.

- `createApplicationCatalog({ placement })` takes an optional placement provider (`src/data/placementProvider.js`). Its `layer(kind)` gives Flights, Military Flights, AIS Vessels, Transit and Rail a `place(id, wallMs)`, and optionally `observe(id, fix)` and `forget(id)`.
- While live, each of those layers tells the provider every fix it accepts, and draws a contact where the provider places it: position, height (the layer's own when none is given), course and speed.
- A null answer, a provider that throws, a kind it leaves out, or no provider at all keeps the layer's own motion unchanged. While following the world clock, the layers never ask it.
- Contacts are forgotten when removed, when the layer is reset or turned off, and when the clock jumps.
- A transit vehicle or train the provider holds still lets the render loop idle and is asked again each second. Vessels ask for frames only while the provider places one, and stop when the layer turns off.

**Tests:** the layers draw and reconcile exactly as before without a provider and with one that places nothing, draw where a provider places them, and idle while it holds them still (`placementProvider.test.mjs`, `flights/motion.test.mjs`, `flights/clockFollow.test.mjs`, `transit/lifecycle.test.mjs`, `transit/movement.test.mjs`, `rail/cockpitSubject.test.mjs`, `vessels/placement.test.mjs`, `vessels/renderGovernor.test.mjs`). `npm test`, `format:check`, `check:boundaries` and `changelog:check` pass.

title: Visual panel: scope opacity, a reset, and grouped controls
body:
The Visual panel gets a Scope opacity slider and a Reset, and its controls are regrouped.

- **Visual panel.** It is titled VISUAL and its controls are grouped as Look, Map source, Overlay and Effects, with Reset at the bottom. The presets appear in the panel and also stay in the dock tray. In the phone's More sheet the panel has no presets.
- **Scope opacity.** Sets how strongly the scope mask darkens the scene, from 50% to 100%; the floor keeps a faint mask from looking like Scope is off. Share links carry it as `sco` (compact field 30), but only when it is below 100, so existing links are unchanged. Saved scenes don't store it.
- **Reset.** Restores the look, effects and overlay defaults and keeps the current HUD layout, so Cyber stays Cyber. A reset done inside Contacts becomes the detection setting that is restored when you leave Contacts.
- **Shadows.** The HUD gets backplates when Scope is off.
- **Cyber.** Under the Cyber HUD the panel keeps Cyber's own skin. The toggle buttons expose their state through `aria-pressed`, and the pills are hidden from screen readers.

All 13 locales are translated. Unit, track-regression, layer-token and library checks pass, and the change was checked in Chrome.

Work by @manjunath22466, with fixes and review by @samehkhamis.

title: Cockpit side panels: the main page's rails and panels in first person

The rail buttons are disclosures (`aria-expanded`, `aria-controls`) and go through a single `toggleCockpitUtility` action. Closing a panel returns focus to the rail.

title: Data Layers: a finder and a section index
body:
The Data Layers panel gets a search and filter in its header and a section index down its side.

- **Search.** Matches each layer's name as shown on screen as well as its English name, so it works in every language. Escape closes the search and leaves the panel open, both on the main page and in the cockpit.
- **Filter.** A small popover with two groups. Status offers All layers, On and Off, based on whether each layer is enabled. Category lists the list's groups, stored by key so a choice survives a language change. It is a disclosure of toggle buttons: opening it moves focus inside, the arrow keys, Home and End move between options, and Escape closes it and returns focus to its button. It stays within the panel.
- **Feedback.** Chips under the header show the active filters and clear them. "No layers match" appears when nothing is left. Neither the search nor the filter is saved or included in share links.
- **Section index.** One tick per group still shown, down the list's inline end. Hovering or focusing a tick names its group on whichever side has room; clicking scrolls the list there. It re-reads the list only when a group changes, not on every live count update. Phones don't show it.
- **Voice.** A voice request for a layer the finder is hiding clears the finder first.

All 13 locales are translated, and the three new glyphs are added to the icon font subset. New tests are in `src/ui/layerFinder.test.mjs`. Unit and track-regression checks pass, and the change was checked in Chrome.

Work by @manjunath22466, with fixes and review by @samehkhamis.

title: feat(i18n): an application uses Core's translator and words Core's messages its own way
body:
## What this changes

An application that composes Core can now use Core's translator and word Core's messages its own way, without Core changing its strings.

- The `./i18n` entry exports `t`, `tn`, `msg`, `translateKnown`, `formatNumber`, `formatDate` and `formatRelativeTime`, so the application's own text follows the same language as Core's.
- `setMessageOverrides({ en: {…}, de: {…} })` replaces any catalog entry by its key: the English text, `context|text`, or the English plural for `tn` with `{one, other, …}` forms.
  - An overridden message shows the application's text in the active locale, else its English, else Core's translation.
  - Plural forms follow the rules of the locale they are worded in.
  - An entry of the wrong kind is ignored.
  - Each call replaces the previous set, and `{}` removes it.

Core's own text and catalogs are unchanged. Usage and limits are in docs/I18N.md, including that a view already drawn keeps its text until it next renders.

## How I verified it

- [x] `npm run build`
- [x] `npm test` (12,998 tests, 0 failures)
- [ ] `npm run test:track` (dev server running): not run; no rendering or tracking code changed

title: Bundle Wikidata cities for offline place lookups
body:
Bundles a pack of the world's cities from Wikidata, so place names can be looked up without calling a geocoder. This is the first part of Manjunath's Context work; the Context panel, its first reader, follows in the next PR.

**What ships**
- `src/data/local_data/wikidata_cities/cities.json`: 31,827 settlements of 15,000 people or more (1.6 MB, CC0), with name, position, population, ISO country code and Wikidata id.
- `src/data/wikidataCities.js` reads the pack on the first lookup:
  - `nearestCity`: the largest city within 12 km, else the nearest within 60 km;
  - `citiesAround`;
  - `findPlace`: "Paris, France" keeps only cities in France, otherwise the nearest namesake near the view wins, else the largest one;
  - `countryName`.
- Names match without case or accents, including ł, ø, đ, ı and ß ("lodz" finds Łódź).
- The app never calls Wikidata. Credit: "City, town and village names from Wikidata (CC0)".

**Build (`scripts/build-wikidata-cities.mjs`)**
- Groupings of settlements are left out: items stated as a metropolitan area, conurbation and so on, even when they are also typed as a megacity. A city that is only a narrower grouping kind stays (Istanbul is a "metropolitan municipality in Turkey").
- Places that no longer stand are left out (former entities, ghost towns, archaeological sites).
- A unit dissolved where no other place within 15 km names the spot stays. This keeps the Vietnamese provincial cities that ended as units in 2025, such as Nha Trang and Quy Nhon.
- A missing country is filled from the area the place lies in, one level up at a time.
- Retries network errors, splits a population band the service cannot answer in time, stops on a malformed query, and picks coordinates and countries the same way on every build.
- Fails if well-known cities are missing or a known grouping gets in.

**Tests:** `src/data/wikidataCities.test.mjs` covers name folding, the cell lookup (antimeridian and poles), the country qualifier and the nearest namesake.

**Docs:** `DATA_SOURCES.md` (table row and section), the folder README, `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md`.

**Checks run:** format:check, check:boundaries, i18n, layer-token and library checks, the full unit suite (13,023 tests, 0 failures), build.

Co-authored by @manjunath22466 and @samehkhamis.

title: A weather source can name its provider for each product
body:
The Rain radar, Lightning density and Satellite clouds rows say "NOAA nowCOAST" until a manifest's `display.source` names the provider, whatever the weather source actually reads. An application whose source is not nowCOAST has no way to name it before the first manifest arrives, or while the layer is off.

- A `weather` source may supply an optional `sourceName(kind)`, where `kind` is `'radar'`, `'lightning'` or `'satellite'` (`src/layers/weather/index.js`).
- The layer's `source` and its `getStats().source` (marked verbatim) use that name until a manifest names its own. The manifest still wins once loaded.
- The name is read once, when the layer is built. It is held to the same rule as a manifest's `display.source`, through `weatherSourceName` in `src/layers/weather/display.js`: 60 characters, no control or invisible characters, refused rather than cut.
- A source with no names, or whose name is refused or throws, keeps "NOAA nowCOAST" as before. A throw is logged and does not stop the catalog being built.
- `docs/APPLICATION.md` documents it, and notes that the map credit still comes from each manifest's `display.credit`.

Tests: a new case in `src/layers/weather/weather.test.mjs`. `node --test src/layers/weather/weather.test.mjs src/layers/weather/display.test.mjs` passes, 101 tests.

title: One time control; the timeline marks launches and strong earthquakes, with labels
body:
The world clock already decides what time every layer shows; this makes the main timeline the only thing that moves it, and makes the timeline mark only events worth stopping at.

## One time control
- The Weather panel's own slider, step buttons, Latest and Play are removed. The panel shows the frame time only: the newest frame and its age while live, the timeline time alone at a past time (it still shows under reduced motion, on a hidden page or without an imagery host).
- The weather clock's own replay (a frame every two seconds, wrapping from the last frame to the first) is removed, along with `setTarget`, `step`, `latest`, `play`, `pause` and `togglePlay`, and it no longer drives the world clock. **Breaking** for code calling those methods on the catalog's `weatherClock` (`gods-eye-view/application/layers`).
- Weather still follows the world clock, registers its coverage span, and holds the world's play at each next frame until it loads.
- A weather layer built without a clock builds one on the world clock when first enabled; there is no second replay path.
- A weather row's `play`, `latest` and `step` params move the world clock: play at the timeline's chosen speed (the world clock now keeps its rate while paused and live), latest goes live, step goes to the previous or next weather frame. Play does nothing while the row is suspended for reduced motion.

## Marks that matter
- Weather frames no longer put a tick on the timeline (they came every few minutes and filled the track).
- Launches stay marks; earthquakes of magnitude 6 and up become marks while their layer is on. The map still draws every M2.5+ quake.
- Marks may carry `{ time, label?, id?, kind? }`. `worldClock.coverage()` keeps `marks` as numbers and adds `markDetails`. Labels are cut to 60 characters.
- Hovering within 6 px of a tick shows its label; a tap there goes exactly to the mark. A tap elsewhere and a drag work as before.

## Checks
`npm test` (13,013 tests, 0 failed), `npm run build`, `format:check`, `check:boundaries`, `i18n`, `changelog:check`, `library:check` and `layer-token:check` against main all pass. Hover and tap were also checked in a browser against live launch data.

title: Move satellites every frame between SGP4 samples
body:
Satellite points were propagated once a second and held still in between. While the world clock plays faster than real time they jump: at 1 min/s, about 45 px once a second at globe scale.

## What changes

- Each SGP4 call keeps a **sample**: the satellite's inertial position, velocity, gravity and its rate of change (`src/layers/satellites/motion.js`).
- **Every frame**, each shown point is reckoned from its sample to the world time and rotated into the Earth-fixed frame by the sidereal angle. Points glide at any play speed.
- **Core satellites** still take a fresh sample every second. They also take one at once when the world time is 30 s from the sample (fast play, a seek). That keeps every point within about 10 m of SGP4.
- **Starlink extras** take their first sample as they load. After that they are resampled round-robin, more per frame the faster time plays, up to 2,000 a frame. A point more than two minutes from its sample waits for the next one.
- **Hidden points** are moved when they are shown again.
- **The tracked satellite** keeps its own per-frame SGP4 path.

## Measured (Chrome, globe scale)

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| 1 min/s: frames a point moves on | 1 a second | every frame |
| 1 min/s: step | ~45 px | 0.4 px median, 1.4 px max |
| 11,880 satellites (Starlink on) | | 60 fps, 16.7 ms median frame, 19.7 ms p95 |
| Reckoning cost | | 0.02 ms a frame for 1,342 points, 0.15 ms for 10,000 |

Reckoning error against SGP4 for the ISS: 0.7 m at 10 s and 6.7 m at 30 s from the sample (`motion.test.mjs`).

## Tests

- `npm test`: all pass.
- New `motion.test.mjs`: the reckoned track against SGP4, forwards and back.
- New `reckon.test.mjs`: shown, hidden and tracked points; a pause; the horizon resample and a seek; the dense limit; and the dense slice growing with play speed.

title: Move vessels every frame and ask for frames as they move
body:
Vessels between two fixes, and live vessels a host placement places, were redrawn at most every 250 ms. A frame was asked for only once a second. With nothing else asking for frames, the scene drew vessels at about 1 to 2 fps live. While the world clock played at 1×, it drew none at all.

## What changes

- **Every frame:** vessels are redrawn on every frame the scene draws, moved in place without new allocations.
- **Next frame on demand:** after each pass, the layer works out how far the fastest drawn vessel moved on screen. It asks for the next frame for when that vessel will have moved another half pixel.
- **At least once a second** while any drawn vessel moves. A frame already asked for later is brought forward when a vessel speeds up.

A vessel crossing the view close up glides, and one far away lets the scene idle.

## Tests

- `npm test`: all pass.
- New case in `renderGovernor.test.mjs`: a vessel moving about 11 m a frame, 20 km away, asks for its next frame within the frame. One moving about 1 cm a frame asks once a second.

title: Global clouds drawn from a feed's tiles to the level it names
body:
## What

A weather feed that supplies its own tiles (`getFrameTile`) can now say, for each product, the deepest level of the geographic tiling its tiles hold detail at: `frameMaximumLevel(product)`, an integer from 0 to 12.

- **Global infrared (`clouds`):** drawn from the feed's tiles down to that level. Each tile gets the same display transfer as a regional infrared tile. Before, it was always one 2048×1024 image cut to level 3.
- **Other tiled products:** they take the named level in place of 6.
- **No usable level:** a feed that names none (null, a non-integer, out of range, or a throw) keeps the layer's own detail, so global clouds stay on the one image.

## Why

Global clouds topped out at level 3, about 8 km a pixel, even when the feed's own tiles held much more detail.

## Tests

`src/layers/weather/weather.test.mjs` and `source.test.mjs` cover:
- the named level for clouds and radar;
- every unusable answer, for radar and for clouds;
- the infrared transfer on clouds tiles;
- prefetch asking for tiles and never the image;
- `frameMaximumLevel` passed through by `weatherFrameSource`.

`npm test` and `check:boundaries` pass.

title: Contacts move back as smoothly as they move on
body:
## What

A snapshot timeline can now declare `spanMs`. Each record of a snapshot at a time then carries `fixes`: `{ atMs, lat, lon, altitudeM? }` in time order, its own track from `spanMs` before the time to `spanMs` after it (`src/time/timelineFixes.js`, documented in `src/sources/live/contract.js`).

While following the clock, flights, military flights and vessels are placed on those fixes at the clock's time:
- **Seek or move back within the loaded fixes:** this is no jump. Nothing is cleared, play does not wait, and contacts move to the time smoothly.
- **The step there:** it is asked for once, quietly, and then stands in for every contact. It brings back those that left after it, and those it has keep their place.
- **Paused near the end of the fixes after the newest:** the snapshot there is asked for.
- **Before a contact's first fix:** it is not drawn more than a minute before it.
- **Fixes kept:** merged across snapshots, at least 20 s apart and at most 240 per contact.
- **Paused vessel visibility:** vessels get a visibility pass when the time drawn changes while paused.

A source without `spanMs` behaves exactly as before.

## Notes

- Merged on top of #1747. The vessel clock pass keeps its drawn-only, once-per-world-time rule and now also moves vessels that carry fixes.
- A timed vessel load now replaces a load in progress, since the timeline asks for one time at a time.
- `scripts/package-boundaries.json` lists the two new modules for the packages that use them.

## Known limit

A move back loads the step at or before the time, as a seek always has. A contact first seen between that step and the time shown is not drawn until the next step loads.

## Tests

New and updated tests:
- `timelineFixes`: merging and thinning, and runs a step apart reaching back over every step;
- `timelineHistory`;
- `snapshotTimeline`: a quiet replace on a move back, play not held, retry after a failure or a dropped load;
- vessel `records`, `motion` and the render governor.

`npm test` and `check:boundaries` pass locally.

title: Search reads degrees-minutes-seconds, UTM, MGRS and plus codes
body:
The search box flew to decimal coordinates and geo URIs only. Coordinates written the other common ways went to the geocoders, which matched them to some place by name, or found nothing.

## What

Search now reads, without any geocoder or key:

- **Degrees, minutes and seconds:** `40°26'46"N 79°58'56"W` or `40°26.8' N, 79°58.9' W`. Each part is marked by its symbol (`°`, `'` or `′`, `"` or `″`). The rules are the same as for decimal degrees: a sign or a hemisphere letter, never both. Minutes and seconds are below 60. Only the last number may have a decimal part.
- **UTM:** `18T 585628 4511322` (zone, latitude band, easting, northing).
- **MGRS:** `18T WL 85650 11369`, `18TWL8565011369`, or anything from 3 to 5 digits per axis (100 m to 1 m). The result is the centre of the square the digits name, or its corner for a 1 m reference.
- **Full plus codes:** `849VCWC8+R9`, decoded as the Open Location Code specification gives.

Like the decimal parser, each one is strict: a query either reads exactly or is declined and goes to the geocoders as before.

- MGRS needs at least 3 digits per axis. Coarser references (`18T WL 85 11`) decline, because written that way `1 JAN 2023`, `3 USA 12` or `20 KPH 1000` would read as grid squares.
- Three letters that spell a month decline (`1 JAN 2023 1200`). A date is far likelier than one of those few squares.
- The square must lie within its zone's longitudes, with the widened zones of southwest Norway and Svalbard.
- MGRS letters must be capitals, as references are printed, unless the reference is written unspaced (`18twl856113`).
- The polar UPS bands (A, B, Y, Z) decline, as do the zones Svalbard does not use (32X, 34X, 36X).
- A UTM `N` or `S` is read as the latitude band when the northing falls in it. Otherwise it is the hemisphere, as UTM is also written (`33N 500000 4500000`).
- Unmarked runs (`40 26 46 N`) and short plus codes (`CWC8+R9 Mountain View`) still go to the geocoders.

## Where

- `src/search/gridReference.js`: UTM and MGRS. The inverse transverse Mercator uses Krüger's series to the sixth order.
- `src/search/plusCode.js`: full plus codes.
- `src/search/coordinateParser.js`: degrees, minutes and seconds, and the fallback to the two new modules.

## Tests

`src/search/gridReference.test.mjs` checks UTM and MGRS against pyproj and the `mgrs` package to within 1 m, and plus codes against the specification's own test data. It also covers the declines: dates and short words in either case (`1 JAN 2023`, `1 JAN 2023 1200`, `3 USA 12`), squares outside their zone, the non-existent zones, the polar bands, and digit runs of unequal length. A probe of every `D MON YYYY`, `D MON YY` and `D MON YYYY HHMM` date from 1990 to 2030, in capitals, finds none read as a grid reference. `coordinateParser.test.mjs` covers degrees, minutes and seconds. All unit tests pass, along with the format and boundary checks.

title: GNSS Integrity on H3 resolution-4 hexagons, as gpsjam.org
body:
## What

GNSS Integrity now follows gpsjam.org's published method in its cells:

- **Grid:** aircraft are binned into H3 resolution-4 cells (`latLngToCell`, h3-js 4.4.0, Apache-2.0) and drawn as their hexagons (`PolygonGeometry` in one ground primitive), instead of 0.5° squares.
- **No minimum count:** every hexagon with an aircraft is shown. The three-aircraft minimum is gone; gpsjam.org has none. Discounting one bad aircraft, `100 · max(0, bad − 1) / total`, stays the only small-sample guard.
- **Bands:** unchanged at < 2 %, 2–10 % and > 10 %.
- **Rolling window:** still 30 minutes over visited views.
- **Cells:** keyed by their H3 index, carrying their centre and boundary. Antimeridian rings are unwrapped (`gnssCellRing`); pentagons and polar cells draw correctly.
- **Provenance:** records the grid under the gpsjam.org part (`grid: 'h3'`, `h3Resolution: 4`).
- **Text:** the legend's minimum-aircraft sentence is gone, and the info text says blank areas had no reporting aircraft (all 13 locales).

## Size

h3-js adds about 85 KB gzipped to the startup bundle, since the layer is imported statically.

## Tests

- GNSS tests (50) cover: a known point's res-4 cell; antimeridian, pentagon and polar cells; unchanged bands; one- and two-aircraft cells now shown.
- `npm test`, `check:boundaries` and `npm run i18n` pass.

title: Draw at the display's refresh rate while anything moves
body:
The globe was capped at 60 FPS (`viewer.targetFrameRate = 60`). On a 240 Hz display an empty globe measured 239 FPS without the cap, against 60 with it.

## What changes
- **No fixed cap while anything moves.** The render governor sets `targetFrameRate` to `undefined` in continuous mode, so layers in motion, the camera and a followed contact draw at the display's refresh rate.
- **A parked scene still ticks at most 60 times a second** (`IDLE_FRAME_RATE`). Cesium runs the clock, data sources and every pre/post-update listener on each animation frame even when `requestRenderMode` skips the draw, so an uncapped idle scene would do 4x the update work on a 240 Hz display. The viewer starts at this cap until the governor is installed, so startup loading does not compete with drawing.
- **The camera holds continuous render** from `moveStart` to `moveEnd`. Cesium never raises `moveEnd` for a camera that drifts by rounding errors, so between those events the governor samples the pose every 250 ms with a tolerance. Half a second at rest releases the hold, and a later move takes it again. This mirrors `installGlobeInViewRecovery`.
- **Waits that counted frames now count drawn time** (`src/time/frameWait.js`, at most 100 ms per frame, so a background tab does not use them up):
  - a tracked contact's first position (`trackedCamera`, 2 s);
  - the shared follow view (`shareFollow`, 2 s);
  - a trail chunk's temporary copy (`trailRenderer`, 10 s).
  At 240 Hz the first two would have shrunk to 0.5 s.

## Checked and left alone
- `DENSE_REFRESH_FRAMES`: the per-frame cost is unchanged.
- `QUEUED_ITEM_PRUNE_FRAMES` and `PROBE_MAX_PENDING_FRAMES`: GPU queries answer within a few frames either way.
- The detection paint skip: it only fires above 22 ms paints.
- Animation already scaled by elapsed time is unaffected.
- `zoomOutGuard`'s per-frame pitch ease settles faster in real time at high refresh rates; that is harmless.

## Tests
- New: `frameWait.test.mjs`, a trail test of the 10 s wait at 240 Hz, and governor tests for the idle cap, the camera hold and a drifting camera.
- Full suite: 13,065 pass. The changelog fragment is renamed to this PR's number in a follow-up commit.

title: An aircraft with no track or true heading faces the way it moved
body:
Follow-up to fd06272e. An aircraft whose row carries neither a ground track nor a true heading still faced north (`true_track` fell back to 0), so one taxiing south was drawn moving backwards or sideways.

## What changes
- `FlightRecords.receive` (`src/layers/flights/records.js`) now picks the course in this order:
  1. the reported track (or true heading);
  2. the course from the last fix to this one, when they are at least 30 m apart (`courseFromFixes`);
  3. the last known course;
  4. 0.
- Fixes closer than 30 m are treated as position noise on a stopped aircraft, so it keeps its course.

## Tests
- `records.test.mjs`: a southbound taxi with no course reads 180; a stop keeps 180; a reported course always wins.
- `courseFromFixes`: rejects noise and missing values, and reads east as 90.
- The full suite passes; the only failure was the changelog fragment's name, fixed by renaming it to this PR's number.

title: Vessels following the clock: draw at the display's rate, move drawn vessels on a half-pixel step
body:
## Why

A Chrome profile of about 9,000 vessels following a playing world clock (1 min/s) ran at 26–31 FPS. The main thread was busy the whole time:

| Per rendered frame | Cost |
|---|---|
| `followClockPositions`: the loop over every record | ~3.3 ms |
| `vesselPositionAt` (great circle, built arrays) | ~3.3 ms |
| moving each drawn vessel (3 × `fromDegrees` + normal) | ~5 ms |
| `billboard.position` set | ~1.5 ms |
| BillboardCollection re-upload of the moved billboards | ~4 ms |

Every drawn vessel was moved every frame, typically by a few hundredths of a pixel. Playback also stayed under the parked scene's 60 FPS cap, because the world clock only requested frames and never held continuous render.

## What

- **Playback draws at the display's rate.** `followWorldTime` reports when the clock starts and stops playing away from live (not stepped by a driver, not waiting for data). `scene.js` holds continuous render meanwhile.
- **Drawn vessels move on a step.** While following the clock, drawn vessels move again once the fastest would have moved half a pixel on screen. Each vessel's speed is measured from the world time it was last drawn at. They also move at least once a second, and at once when the camera moves or changes height by a tenth of its height, or the view zooms. A pass that holds them back asks for a frame, so a paused clock settles on the exact time.
- **Hidden vessels move a share each pass.** Each still moves within 250 ms, but they no longer all move in one frame every 250 ms. The visibility pass moves a vessel coming into view to the clock pass's time before showing it.
- **Cheaper position writes.** Positions are written from one surface point and normal, using Cesium's own `fromRadians` formula, instead of three `fromDegrees` calls. The unused `visual.normal` is gone. `greatCircleAt` no longer builds arrays.

## Measurements

Node benchmark of the clock pass alone, which leaves out Cesium's billboard re-upload: 9,000 vessels, 3,000 of them drawn, frames at 240 Hz, the clock at 1 min/s, the camera at 60 km.

| | mean | p50 | p90 | p99 | max |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| main | 4.63 ms | 4.20 | 6.97 | 10.9 | 16.5 |
| this branch | 0.37 ms | 0.12 | 0.22 | 6.7 | 20.4 |

About one frame in 22 runs a full pass over the drawn vessels (7–9 ms). Frames in between move nothing drawn, so Cesium has no billboards to re-upload.

## Tests

- New tests in `src/layers/vessels/renderGovernor.test.mjs`. They cover:
  - the half-pixel step;
  - the one-second limit;
  - camera height, pan and zoom;
  - a vessel drawn afresh between passes;
  - a pause after a held-back pass;
  - the hidden share;
  - a vessel shown before its turn;
  - positions matching `Cesium.Cartesian3.fromDegrees`.
- New `src/time/viewerClock.test.mjs`.
- `npm test`: 13,082 pass. `format:check` and `check:boundaries` pass.

title: Revert #1755: vessel playback change is not faster in the browser
body:
Reverts #1755.

Measured in the browser at 1 min/s with about 8,900 vessels in view, the change was not faster than before, and it showed intermittent multi-second stalls inside the vessel clock pass. The benchmark used to justify it left out Cesium's billboard costs and drew a third as many vessels. Reverting until a version is measured faster in the browser.

title: vessels: cheaper label pass and fix merge during playback
body:
Two costs left in vessel playback after #1755: the label pass and the merge of each vessel's kept fixes at every snapshot.

**Labels.** The label pass projects every vessel in view each time it runs, and asked `Cesium.SceneTransforms.worldToWindowCoordinates` for each one, which reads the camera and allocates per point. `createWindowProjector` (`src/data/windowProjection.js`) reads the camera's matrices and the canvas size once and runs the same arithmetic in the same order, so the window positions are the same numbers. A test compares them bit for bit with Cesium across pitches and heights, including points behind the camera. Outside a 3D perspective view, at the eye itself, or with no position, it asks Cesium as before. Grid cells are keyed by number, a cell's candidate object is made only once, and whether a name is worth a card is kept per vessel until its name, MMSI or id changes.

**Merge.** `mergeTimelineRuns` read an entry's time again on every comparison, and the vessel layer passed a new arrow for every vessel. Times are now read once, and the leading older entries the loop would keep one by one are sliced in one step. The output is unchanged: a test checks 3,000 random merges against the previous algorithm (unsorted runs, NaN times, shared entries, random limits), and a separate review ran 60,000 more.

### Measured in the browser

Perf harness with real Cesium, 9,000 vessels, 1 min/s, same machine, runs alternated:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| Label pass | 33 ms | 11 ms |
| Forced visibility pass | 42 ms | 27 ms |
| Merge per snapshot (240 kept fixes each, one implementation per page, 5 pairs) | 65–87 ms | 57–61 ms |

### Tests

`npm test`: 13,086 pass, 0 fail. `format:check`, `check:boundaries`, `library:check` pass.

title: Grounded aircraft turn 3D as soon as the tiles settle
body:
Grounded aircraft turn 3D as soon as the tiles settle

A grounded aircraft is drawn as a 3D model only after a terrain height sample places it on the ground. While the 3D tiles were still streaming, the ground snap counted that as a failed sample. Each such frame doubled the aircraft's retry delay, from 2 s up to 30 s. After a pan, models replaced icons late and in batches, up to half a minute after the view had settled.

Streaming tiles now return the last measured ground for that aircraft, if it has one, and leave the retry delay alone (`src/services/groundSnap.js`). The first frame after the tiles settle samples and hands over. Only a sample that finds no ground still backs off. The rest is unchanged: no model is placed without a measurement, there is still one visual owner, and the at-most-four-samples-per-250-ms cap stays.

Tests:
- `src/services/groundSnap.test.mjs`:
  - streaming tiles earn no backoff;
  - a held measurement answers while tiles stream;
  - a sample that finds no ground still backs off;
  - streaming after a real miss leaves that miss's backoff as it was.
- `src/data/trackedModelRegime.test.mjs`: the two handoff tests now expect the handover on the first settled frame.

Three of these fail without the fix.

title: Revert #1757 (vessel label pass and fix merge): no gain in the app
body:
Reverts #1757.

The test page showed faster label, visibility and merge passes, but the app itself did not get faster. Measured in the same browser, back to back, Rotterdam with about 9,000 vessels at 1 min/s, 30 s of frames after 15 s of play:

| Build | fps | p50 frame | frames 40–500 ms |
|---|---|---|---|
| Without #1757 | 43.5, 48.1 | 19.5, 16.4 ms | 109, 79 |
| With #1757 | 42.3, 37.6, 44.0 | 20.2, 23.3, 18.4 ms | 133, 144, 110 |

No better, slightly worse if anything, so it comes out. #1758 on top of it is untouched; this only undoes the #1757 merge.

title: Renderer ports: layers draw, pick and move the camera through a renderer contract
body:
Layers no longer call Cesium directly. They draw through draw sets (icons, points, models, shapes, lines), take clicks through an input port, read and move the camera through a camera port, and ask globe and query ports for heights, occlusion and settled tiles. `src/render/cesium` implements these ports; `docs/RENDERER-CONTRACT.md` describes them.

User-visible changes:
- When two tools want the globe's clicks, the newest takes them and the older one turns itself off.
- The Display panel no longer has a Weather group.
- The globe opens at planet level.
- Double-clicking no longer follows or zooms.
- Data-pack and Directions labels use the shared label overlay.
- Turning CONTACTS on with a vessel selected keeps that vessel as the subject instead of following the nearest flight.

title: feat(aircraft): name the operator and country of the selected aircraft
body:
## Why

When you select an aircraft, the card should say who is flying it and where it is registered, not just what type it is. This fills the card's `operator` and `country` fields, which shipped as reserved `null` placeholders. A live contact already carries an ICAO 24-bit address and a callsign; from those two the card now names the operator airline and the state of registry.

Stacks on #1720 (the selected-aircraft hologram and type card). The two commits of this change are the compare range https://github.com/daikaginza/gods-eye-view/compare/feat/aircraft-type-card-hologram...feat/aircraft-card-operator-country; everything below #1720's head belongs to that PR and drops off this one once #1720 merges.

## What

- **Bundled country library** (`src/data/countries/`): every ISO 3166-1 country, each with its flag (computed from the ISO code), aircraft registration prefixes, and the ICAO 24-bit Mode-S address blocks allocated to it. `countryForIcao24(hex)` names the state of registry behind a contact's address with a binary search over the sorted blocks.
- **Bundled airline registry** (`src/data/airlines/`): the OpenFlights airline database (5,774 carriers with a 3-letter ICAO designator), deduplicated by designator. `airlineForCallsign('SWR100')` takes the callsign's leading letter run (`SWR`) and names the operator. A registration-style callsign (`N123AB`) resolves to nothing.
- **Card fill** (`src/layers/flights/typeCard.js`): the resolver now returns `operator {name, icao, iata, callsign, tailColor}` and `country {iso2, name, flag}`, each null on no match. The card (Vue) shows the operator name with its tail colour when one is curated, and the country flag with its name, both only when present.
- **i18n** for the two new labels across the shipped locales.
- **Provenance**: `DATA_SOURCES.md` rows and Data-popover credits for the ICAO 24-bit allocation, ISO 3166-1, and OpenFlights.

## Licensing

The ICAO 24-bit allocation and the ISO 3166-1 list are facts (ICAO Annex 10 Vol III via the dump1090-fa table, BSD). The airline registry is the OpenFlights database under the **Open Database License (ODbL 1.0)**, attributed in `DATA_SOURCES.md` and the Data popover, matching how the repo already bundles other ODbL datasets.

## Verification

- `npm run build`, the targeted resolver/card/library tests, `npm test`, `npm run i18n`, `npm run format:check` and `npm run check:boundaries` pass.
- The builders are idempotent: a re-run with a warm cache produces a byte-identical catalog.
- The card was rendered on a real GPU: a civil contact (`SWR100`/`4B1814`) names Swiss International Air Lines with its tail colour and Switzerland; a military contact (`RCH871`/`AE01D2`) names Air Mobility Command and the United States.

## Notes for review

- `src/data/airlines/catalog.json` is about 989 KB (5,774 rows), bundled and statically imported by the flights layer, so it adds roughly 1 MB to that bundle. If you would rather load it on demand, say so and I will split it.
- OpenFlights is ODbL (share-alike). It is disclosed; the choice to bundle it is yours.
- A few newer states (South Sudan, Timor-Leste, Taiwan and others) have no block in the dump1090 allocation table, so those contacts show no country until a second allocation source is added. 70 OpenFlights rows have no country because the source row is column-shifted.
- Non-English translations for the two new labels are best-effort; native review is welcome.

title: Vessel playback moves icons on the renderer's clock
body:
## What this changes

During timeline playback, the AIS vessel layer moved every vessel icon on the CPU every frame: in a profile at 1 min/s about half the frame went to per-vessel moves and icon writes (the icon book's `put`, `followRecord`, slerp, `fromDegreesInto`). Vessel icons now move on the renderer's clock as motion segments, the way aircraft icons already do (`motionSegments`). The layer writes an icon again only when its segment runs out or time moves back before it.

- **Segments** (`src/layers/vessels/rendering.js`, `planMotion`): the stretch between the two fixes around the world time (`vesselSpanAt`, new in `motion.js`), cut into straight pieces of at most 10 km on the great circle. A 10 km chord stays within 2 m of the track. Course is the same `vesselCourseDeg` as before. Before the first fix and after the last, the icon holds.
- **What still reads positions every frame:** vessels with a card, the selected one, ship models and the vessel the bridge camera rides. Cards are anchored on those positions. The rest are caught up in a rotation within `HIDDEN_FOLLOW_MS`, as before.
- **Position queries:** `getAllPositions`, `getNearby` and the focus pass read the icon's segment at the world time (one lerp, no CPU move). Single-vessel reads and the detection overlay bring the vessel to the world time first.
- **Unchanged:**
  - Live mode (host placement) and renderers without `motionSegments`.
  - Trails: they are built from the feed's fixes, never from the per-frame position.
  - Vessels are still never camera-followed.

### Behaviour kept, with a test each (`src/layers/vessels/motionSegments.test.mjs`)

- An icon moves along its fixes with no writes until its segment runs out, then is written once. Past the last fix it holds with no further writes.
- A seek back before the drawn segment redraws the one the time is in.
- A long stretch is drawn a 10 km piece at a time. A time exactly on a piece's end (including when float rounding puts it in the piece before) draws the next piece.
- A vessel shows `TIMELINE_UNSEEN_MS` before its first fix and hides again when the time moves back before that.
- Bulk positions, single lookups and the detection overlay return where the icon is drawn at the world time.
- Going live, every icon holds where its segment last drew it. One a live update has drawn since stays where that update put it.
- A renderer without `motionSegments` gets the previous behaviour.

Each of these tests fails with its fix removed. An independent review also walked selection, the bridge camera, model handoff, snapshot refreshes mid-playback, the geoid re-lift, picking, focus emphasis and trails, and found no change in behaviour.

### Measured in the browser

Real Cesium in Chrome, same page and machine, tab in front, 1 min/s playback from 3 h back over Rotterdam at 60 km, AIS vessels on, 20 s window after 12 s of warm-up. Builds were swapped on the same server and the page reloaded between runs.

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| **Final code** | | |
| Frames per second | 11.7 | 113.3 |
| Frame gap p50 / p90 | 66.1 / 104.8 ms | 6.1 / 8.8 ms |
| `scene.render` p50 / p90 (includes the layer's preRender work) | 57.6 / 65.0 ms | 3.6 / 5.0 ms |
| **Earlier pair, before the review fixes, machine less loaded** | | |
| Frames per second | 46.3 | 195.9 |
| `scene.render` p50 / p90 | 21.7 / 27.9 ms | 2.6 / 3.2 ms |

The machine's load moved between the two pairs (the idle frame rate dropped from about 235 to about 150), so compare within a pair, not across.

## How I verified it

- [x] `npm run build`
- [x] `npm test`: 14,233 pass, 0 fail
- [ ] `npm run test:track`: not run; it checks aircraft tracking and serves vessels zero rows, so it does not reach this change
- [x] Feature gate for the area I touched: `format:check`, `check:boundaries`, `library:check` pass

Vessels move along the rivers in the browser during playback, stay on the water, and their cards move with them.

title: fix(ghostmaps): stop polling GitHub when nobody is watching
body:
## What this changes

The S2 GhostMaps watcher stops polling GitHub once no browser has the layer open and no request has come for `GHOSTMAPS_IDLE_MS` (10 min by default); the next request starts it again.

## How I verified it

- [x] `npm run build`
- [x] `npm test`
- [x] `npm run test:track` (dev server running; same result as unmodified `main`, details below)
- [ ] Feature gate for the area I touched: `scripts/qa-ghostmaps.mjs` not run; the change is server-side and covered by unit tests

## Docs

- [x] `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md` updated and a `changelog.d/<pr-number>-<slug>.md` fragment added

## Details
### Problem

`server/providers/ghostMaps.js` starts its watcher with the first `/api/ghostmaps` request (good: an install that never enables the layer never contacts GitHub). After that it reads the branch head every `GHOSTMAPS_POLL_SECONDS` (15 s) **until the server stops**, even when every browser turned the layer off hours ago. For an always-on install (a wall display, a home server) that is about 5,800 requests a day to GitHub for a layer nobody is looking at.

### Change

- The watcher stops once **no browser holds the event stream** and **no request has come for `GHOSTMAPS_IDLE_MS`** (10 min by default).
- The next request starts it again and checks at once (the existing `start()` path), so a viewer who comes back sees a fresh catalog.
- The idle window restarts on every request and when the last event-stream subscriber leaves.
- `GHOSTMAPS_IDLE_MS=0` keeps today's behaviour (poll until the server stops). Empty or invalid values fall back to the default.
- Docs: the GhostMaps updates section of `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md` and the `DATA_SOURCES.md` row say so.

No new dependency, host or route; the polling, backoff and caching code is unchanged.

### Tests

`server/providers/ghostMapsIdle.test.mjs` (3 tests, fake GitHub, injected clock): polling stops after the idle window and a request restarts it; a held event stream keeps it polling and the window starts when the last viewer leaves; env parsing. The existing `ghostMaps.test.mjs` passes unchanged.

### Validation (on `main` da81cf7, 2026-11-16)

Node 24.22.1 in a Linux container without network:

- `npm run format:check`, `npm run check:boundaries`, `npm run i18n`: clean.
- `npm run build`: clean.
- `npm test`: 14,224 tests, 14,218 pass, 4 skipped. The 2 that failed (`src/render/noCesiumOutsideRender.test.mjs`, `src/render/viewerAccess.test.mjs`) run `git merge-base HEAD origin/main`, which my container could not resolve; re-run with the repository history visible, both pass (14/14).
- `npm run test:track` (both changes together, Chrome on Windows, dev server): 97 passed, 6 failed, 4 skipped Ã¢â‚¬â€^] exactly the same result and the same six `display-floor` failures as unmodified `da81cf7` on the same machine.

Also seen on a downstream always-on install running the same change: after the last viewer closed the page, the server kept one short GitHub connection every 15-30 s for 9 min 55 s, then none at all for the next 6 minutes of sampling.

`scripts/qa-ghostmaps.mjs` was not run (it needs a dev server and a browser); the change is server-side only and covered by the unit tests above.

title: Question: would you want an unattended “TV mode” (a live, self-directing camera), built in or as a plugin?
body:
Before writing a PR I'd like to know whether you want this at all, and in what shape.

**What it is.** A mode for a screen nobody is driving (a wall display, a TV, a lobby): GEV directs its own camera through a rotation of live shots and keeps going for hours. It is not the scene Director: the Director plays scenes someone authored; this picks its subjects from what the live layers show right now.

What I have running in a downstream build:

- **Shot kinds:** follow a live aircraft; a landing (wide shot of the approach, a slow push-in, then the cockpit view to touchdown); a working vessel; a landmark or a mountain (a slow orbit); a street-level ride-along on a route; Earth from orbit.
- **Transitions:** the last frame of a shot is held and dissolved into the next one, so there is no black frame and no flight through half-loaded tiles in between.
- **Push-ins wait for the 3D tiles:** the camera only moves in as fast as the photorealistic tiles arrive, so a shot never lands on a blurry or empty city.
- **A weighted shot picker:** each kind has a base weight and a length range, with cooldowns (the same landmark not again for 3 hours, landings at least 7 minutes apart, nothing within 1.5 km of a recent shot for 20 minutes) and target airtime shares per kind and per region, so the rotation stays varied.
- **Places are data:** the landmark list is a table (name, one-line caption, lat/lon, target height, wide and close range, pitch, first heading, region, kind). In the version I'd contribute, every region, place and airport lives in that data, not in the code.
- **Built on existing actions:** it drives the camera and picks subjects through the existing typed voice actions (`move_camera`, `analyst_query` and friends), and follows only airline-style callsigns and working vessels.

**Questions**

1. Is an unattended mode like this something you'd want in GEV?
2. If yes, which shape?
   - **(a) Built in:** a Display option or `?mode=tv`, using `src/director/camera.js` for the moves and the existing typed actions for subjects; places ship as a small JSON file per region (a short world list by default).
   - **(b) A plugin:** it stays outside the repo and needs one documented seam (a way to register a "show" that receives the viewer, the layer queries and the camera helpers). The new host-application seams could carry most of it: application cockpit subjects (#1686), the placement provider (#1737) and the renderer contract (#1760); user layers (#759) would cover the rest.
3. Anything it must respect that I should design for from the start (performance budgets on low-end screens, privacy rules for which aircraft or vessels may be followed, kiosk or accessibility concerns)?

I'll open a PR only in the shape you pick, and keep it small: the shot picker and the places format first, then shot kinds one at a time.

title: Add Kubernetes base, Dockerfile.prod and GHCR image workflow
body:
## Summary

Adds a generic Kubernetes deployment base, a production Dockerfile, and a GitHub Actions workflow that publishes the image to GitHub Container Registry.

- `k8s/base/`: one-replica Deployment (`Recreate`) and a ClusterIP Service. The image is a placeholder that an overlay must set.
- `k8s/base/kustomization.yaml`: `images:` entry as the single override point.
- `k8s/README.md`: build, overlay, Secret, deploy, and known limitations.
- `Dockerfile.prod`: production image for shared deployments.
- `.github/workflows/docker-publish.yml`: builds `Dockerfile.prod` and pushes to `ghcr.io/<owner>/<repo>` on pushes to `main` and `v*` tags, using the built-in `GITHUB_TOKEN`.

Provider keys are read from an optional Secret (`gev-provider-keys`) that is created outside kustomize, so redeploys never reset it.

## Notes for reviewers

- No overlay or environment-specific config is included.
- The app refuses requests carrying reverse-proxy forwarding headers on the realtime token, typed chat, and Provider Settings routes. Ingress or gateway layers add those headers, so voice and chat need the headers stripped at the mesh or the gate changed. The README documents this; I did not change the gate here.
- The workflow has not been run in this repository yet.

title: ISS and Tiangong as 3D models with moving parts, STATION and LIVE sections, ISS live telemetry
body:
## Summary

Closes #1690 by carrying it: this branch is @IMBrandao's `feat/iss-3d-model` as of his last push, with his commits unchanged underneath, brought onto main's renderer contract and extended with a second station, live telemetry and the Cockpit views. Most of the work on the model, its moving parts and the renderer contract is his; the sections below say what he built and what was added on top.

## What @IMBrandao built (PR #1690)

- **The ISS model.** NASA JSC IGOAL's current-configuration station, reduced from 96 MB and 2.7 M triangles to 3 MB and 314 k: handrails left out, geometry simplified within 15 cm of the original surface, normals rebuilt, textures at 512 px WebP, Draco. Two corrections to NASA's file (it is mirrored, and 15 materials were blended and drew see-through), both recorded in `public/models/README.md`. The joints are kept as named nodes; the two Ku-band dishes and three radiators, welded into the truss meshes in NASA's file, are cut out by position so they can move.
- **The moving parts.** `issArticulation.js`: the alpha and beta joints face the arrays to the Sun and feather them in the Earth's shadow (a cylinder), the radiators stay edge-on, the two dishes aim at the highest TDRS slots above the station's horizon plane, and Canadarm2, Dextre and the Japanese arm sway a few degrees as an illustration. Joints glide at 12°/s. Every rule, its basis and what is illustrative are documented.
- **The renderer contract's `nodes`.** `ModelItem.nodes`: a model item poses its named glTF nodes by column-major matrices, applied by the Cesium renderer once the model is ready, changed ones only, with a dropped name going back to the authored pose. This is what lets a layer articulate a model without reaching Cesium. (Here it gains a `modelNodes` capability and the conformance check `draw.models.nodes`; see below.)
- **Placing the station.** Identity by NORAD number, real scale with a pixel floor, the "+XVV" attitude from the station's own SGP4 state each frame, the model and the dots splitting the distance range so exactly one draws, and the inverse of the contract's heading/pitch/roll placement worked out for the station's flight axes.
- **Docked objects.** Nauka, a Progress or a Dragon are judged docked by comparing both orbits at one instant rather than by their dots' spacing, which at 7.6 km/s put a docked object's mark back beside the model.
- **The command panel and the live video,** as a floating panel and a floating player: Zoom to the ISS, Automatic with a lit/shadow line, Manual with Sun positions, array and radiator folding, dish aim and Canadarm2 sliders; NASA's live stream through YouTube's embedded player. Both survive here as the STATION and LIVE sections of Context (below).
- **Attribution and docs:** `DATA_SOURCES.md`, the model README, the attribution popover, `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md`, 13 locales.

@kvnloo contributed a test covering the live panel's ownership during his review; it is replaced here by `livePanel.test.mjs` because the panel it tested no longer exists (see "For reviewers").

## Added on top

- **Onto main's renderer seam.** No satellites file reaches Cesium. The station models are items of a `models` set on the draw port, posed by heading, pitch and roll (`geo/frames.js`), their joints through the item's `nodes`; the camera, canvas and clicks come from the renderer's ports. One `stationModel.js` factory serves both stations.
- **ISS live telemetry.** The arrays, radiators and one dish take their real angles from NASA's public ISSLive feed. Off by default: `ISS_TELEMETRY_ENABLED=1` makes the server relay the feed over one connection, open only while a model is on screen. Without signal the joints keep the computed rules, and the STATION section says which it is and how old the last reading is.
- **STATION section.** The command panel moved from a floating window into a section of Context, shown while a station is selected: Automatic says where the angles come from, Manual pauses telemetry and offers the controls. Another station plugs in with a description of its own.
- **LIVE section.** The live video moved into a section of Context: two NASA streams stepped with arrows, an ON AIR dot, an offline card with Try again. Nothing loads on selection: the screen is a poster with Play under the line that YouTube sees the viewer's IP address, as SECURITY.md asks of third-party media. The player goes when the section collapses, Context collapses or closes, the Cockpit leaves its LIVE page, or the Cockpit is entered or left. In the Cockpit the same stream is the briefing's LIVE page.
- **Cockpit station views.** The ISS is ridden from mounts on its model (Nauka, Zarya, Poisk, the Cupola, Kibo, the docked vehicle) instead of the straight-down picture; the readout describes the module each view is from. Tiangong has four (Tianhe, Wentian, Mengtian, the docked vehicle). Leaving a station view selects the station's home entry.
- **Tiangong.** An original model of the T configuration (built from primitives; sources in the model README), its wings following the Sun, its antenna aimed at the Tianlian relays, its arms swaying for illustration. Computed only: China publishes no telemetry.
- **Docked entries.** A click on the station's dot that lands on Nauka or a docked vehicle keeps the model centred and offers the STATION and LIVE sections; such an entry shows the station's ring rather than a second ring of its own.
- **Installations.** A click on a mapped installation's label box selects the site, as a click on its dot does. The label takes a click through a click claim, as CCTV counts do, only where nothing another layer draws is under it: an aircraft or vessel under a base's label stays selectable, and another layer's card above the label keeps its click.
- **Renderer contract.** `nodes` sits behind a `modelNodes` capability, which the Cesium port lists; a renderer without it draws the model as authored. The conformance check `draw.models.nodes` moves the harness model's node off the screen's centre and back (Cesium: 144 passed, 0 failed); the stub poses its one-node models too.
- **ISS telemetry relay** (`ISS_TELEMETRY_ENABLED=1`): one shared socket, frames capped at 64 KB on the socket, a 10 s handshake timeout, a retry ladder that only a minute-long session resets, IPv6 clients rate-limited by /64; listed in SECURITY.md. @kvnloo's reconnect fix is in (old joint values never count as live after a reconnect).

## For reviewers

- The joint driver writes node matrices into a per-station pose map that is the item's `nodes`; the Cesium renderer applies them (@IMBrandao's `poseNodes`). Nothing in the layer touches a Cesium model.
- The station's dots stand until the renderer reports the model ready, and stay if the load fails. The model's draw set is released on layer-off and after a minute undrawn.
- The unused `issCommand` helpers were removed: nothing called them once the panel moved.
- The test suite passes except a set of tests that also fail on a pristine `main` checkout on Windows (path and renderer-factory tests); none are touched by this branch.

## Tests and gates

`npm test` (satellites, render, UI and server suites), `check:boundaries`, `i18n`, `format:check`, `build`, `npm run qa:conformance` (Cesium: 144 passed, 0 failed, 1 expected skip), `node scripts/qa-cockpit-utility.mjs` (no regression against `main`: the same checks fail on both on the same machine) and `node scripts/qa-perf.mjs` (23 of 24, the same as `main`: both fail only "animated style takes the style-anim hold"). In the app: ISS and Tiangong models up close, articulation computed and live, STATION and LIVE sections, Cockpit views on both stations, telemetry relay against the live feed.
