title: feat: Saved Views / Bookmarks for globe configurations
body:
### Problem

Users who regularly explore the same regions or layer configurations have no convenient built-in way to organize and revisit their favorite globe views.

While Share Links already capture much of the globe state, repeatedly generating and managing URLs is inconvenient for everyday use.

A lightweight bookmarking mechanism would make recurring exploration faster and more intuitive, without introducing a new scene-management system.

### Proposal

Introduce a lightweight **Saved Views / Bookmarks** feature that lets users save and restore their current globe configuration with a single click.

**Suggested MVP:**
- Save the current view with a custom name.
- Restore camera position, zoom, orientation, active layers, and visual style.
- List, rename, and delete saved bookmarks.
- Store bookmarks locally, without requiring accounts or backend changes.
- Reuse existing Share Link serialization/restoration logic where possible.
- Avoid new dependencies and preserve existing Director scenes and Share Links.

**Example bookmarks:**
- European Aviation — aircraft activity over Europe.
- Persian Gulf Maritime — vessels around the Persian Gulf.
- Global Weather — worldwide weather overlays.

**Questions for maintainers:**

Would this feature fit the project's roadmap? Is there already a similar capability planned or in development?

If the direction is welcome, I'd be happy to contribute a small, focused PR implementing the MVP.

### Data source, license, and attribution

none

### Will you build it?

Yes, I plan to open a PR

title: fix(vessels): back at live, drop a snapshot still loading at a time so the live poll goes out at once
body:
## What

Select a vessel during playback, then press **Live**: the map could show no vessels until the next refresh, up to a minute later.

## Why

Going live cancels the timed snapshot load and starts the live poll right away. But the vessel feed still marked the timed load as in flight, so `loadPositions` returned early and no live request went out. Live polling only retried on its 60 s refresh.

## Change

- `src/layers/vessels/ingestion.js`: the feed records whether its in-flight load is for a time (`loadingAtTime`). `loadLivePositions` drops a timed load still in flight before polling. `loadAt` uses the same `dropLoad` helper.
- `src/layers/vessels/clockFollow.test.mjs`: a test where a timed load is still pending when the clock goes live. It expects the live query to go out at once and its rows to be applied. The test fails without the change.

A live load already in flight is left alone, so live polling behaves as before.

## Checks

- `npm test`: 14,238 pass, 0 fail
- `format:check` and `check:boundaries` pass

title: Vessel tracks end at the vessel
body:
The selected vessel's track drew every fix it held. Following the world clock, it ran ahead of the icon to the vessel's newest fix; live, it stopped at the last fix while the icon moved on from it. A change of time restarted it from a single point until the track at the new time arrived, so it went blank at every step.

- The track draws the fixes at or before the time the vessel is drawn at; live, every fix.
- Each frame a head joins its last drawn fix to the icon where it is drawn (`drawnPositionNow`, so the renderer's position while it moves the icons), as flight tracks do; none past `TRAIL_HEAD_MAX_M` (20 km), where the clock has moved beyond the fixes the track holds.
- A change of time keeps the track, drawn up to the new time, until the track at that time replaces it.

Checked: the vessel layer's tests (three new ones in `tracking.test.mjs`), the full suite, format and boundary checks; and in the browser, live and playing at 1 min/s, the track ends at the icon.

title: Idle frame rate in the app, timed line batching, KEY REQUIRED status
body:
Three fixes to how the globe draws and reports loading.

**The idle frame rate is the app's rule.** The Cesium frame port capped the loop at `IDLE_FRAME_RATE` whenever nothing held it, so the rule lived inside the renderer. The render governor now sets the rate: the display's own while the loop is held, `IDLE_FRAME_RATE` while not. The frame port gains `onHeldChange(cb)`, which says when its first hold is taken and its last released (animated visual styles included), so the governor hears every hold. The quality setting's frame-rate cap is kept apart from the governor's rate, and the loop draws at the lower of the two, so neither overwrites the other.

**Line batching is timed.** A line set waited 30 drawn frames before its unchanged lines settled into a static batch (300 for the long wait), so the batch built twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz, and took seconds at the idle rate. It now waits `SETTLE_MS` (500 ms) and `LONG_SETTLE_MS` (5 s), and moved shapes go back into their batches on the same timing.

**KEY REQUIRED.** A layer that cannot load without a provider key ended the global status chip LOAD FAILED. The chip now has a KEY REQUIRED outcome, ranked below a real failure: a layer whose stats say `keyRequired` ends KEY REQUIRED, any other failure still ends LOAD FAILED. Vessels report a missing AISStream key as `keyRequired` and name the key in the panel; a later outage clears it, as it is no longer the key that is missing.

Checked: the full suite (new tests for `onHeldChange`, the quality cap against the governor's rate, timed settling, and the chip with and without a key), format, boundaries, build, the stub renderer boot and the Cesium conformance run; in the browser, the idle and held frame rates; and the first-run check now asserts that with no keys set the chip never says LOAD FAILED.

title: Stories: GEV scenes as stories on the live globe (#1724 with review fixes)
body:
# Stories: GEV scenes as stories on the live globe

This carries #1724 by @manjunath22466 unchanged (all of its commits, same hashes), plus review fixes on top, because #1724's fork branch does not accept maintainer edits. Merging this marks #1724 merged.

## What Stories adds (from #1724)

An Explore feed and a player for GEV scenes on the live globe: a timeline, chapters, key moments and source context. **Open in GEV** selects the current shot in Authoring, where a scene can get a thumbnail and tags, be saved to Stories, or be deleted. Back restores the globe view after playback; Explore and player links reopen where they were shared. Stories opens from its button, by saying "Open Stories", or through typed AI; entering it turns off active voice.

## Review fixes

**Playback**
- Play goes on from the exact paused, sought or linked moment instead of restarting the current shot (`startScene` takes `fromProgress`). In a flight the camera continues along the rest of its path; in a hold the layers continue from that moment (the Nepal evidence reveal carries on from where the seek left it). A clip cannot be joined partway, so a resumed clip starts again and the timeline waits at the shot's end until it finishes.
- A tap on the globe pauses a story again after a camera move stopped on the press (Stories reads the playing state in the capture phase).
- If closing a story times out waiting for the scene's cleanup, that run loses its authority to change layers, including cleanup it reaches later, so it cannot undo the restored view.

**Authoring**
- The scene picker lists every scene again, and the first scene and shot are selected on load (after shot-pack upgrades), after a delete and after an import, so PLAY and NEXT work after a reload.
- SAVE TO STORIES and tags roll back and show the error when the project cannot be saved.
- An import treats appended packs as built in, as drafts do.

**Links and history**
- Going Back or Forward into the entry of a deleted story removes `?story=` and `storyTime` from the address in any mode.
- `restore()` reports false when the hash is not a share state.

**Cleanup**
- Removed the Mute button (scene media plays muted; it controlled nothing), the Live chip and filter, and other prototype paths no GEV story can reach.
- The Stories button lines up with the ACTIVE STYLE readout and any element marked `data-stories-corner`.
- The Stories document fields are accepted from version 6, as #1724 intended.

## How it was verified

- `npm test` on the branch with current main merged in: 14,381 passed, 0 failed, 4 skipped.
- `npm run build`
- `npm run qa:stories`: all 6 checks, including Play on a paused link carrying on from its time.
- Each fix has a test that fails without it.

title: Context panel: one card for what is picked, the view when nothing is
body:
Context leads with one card for whatever is picked, and describes the view when nothing is. This is the Context part of Manjunath's context UI prototype. The card previews (route globe, 3D model, cockpit view) follow in the next PR.

**The card** (`src/ui/views/panels/EntityCard.vue`, `src/ui/stores/entityCard.js`)
- A click on anything a layer can identify opens its card: facts from the record, a route with progress for a flight, an altitude graph, and transit motion and fleet.
- It shows the weather, local time and news where the item is, plus flights, vessels, hazards and warnings within the panel's radius (25 to 2,500 km).
- Aircraft and satellites offer Enter Cockpit and Enter orbital view. A camera's card shows its latest frame.
- The card says Following only while the camera follows the card's own item, read from the follow's key (`src/data/followed.js`). Closing the card lets go of the camera.

**The view** (`src/ui/views/panels/ViewContext.vue`)
- With nothing picked, the panel describes the view: the place and nearby towns from the Wikidata cities pack (#1743), the height, solar time and daylight, and what is in view per layer, with live counts and breakdowns.
- A header search narrows every list.
- Expanded, Context becomes a full-height column (on the left edge in right-to-left languages), and the credits stop short of it.

**What stays**
- Contacts (nearby sites search, TR-3B, the Awareness list), Space Missions (roster and launch replay) and Radio stay in the main tab.
- When Contacts follows the aircraft the card shows, its list sits inside the card.
- Turning Radio or Launches on opens Context.
- The Properties tab holds the Labels and 3D aircraft settings while a layer they act on is on.

**Seams and cost**
- Clicks come from the input dispatcher, and the camera from the camera port. Nothing reaches Cesium or the viewer.
- Closed, the panel mounts neither the card nor the view summary, so it reads and fetches nothing.
- The weather and news brief goes through the regional service. Satellite fire hits are read only while FIRMS is on.

**Checks**
- format, boundaries, i18n (13 locales complete), layer-token, library and build all pass.
- Unit tests: 14,255 pass, 0 fail.
- Track regression: 97 passed, 6 failed, 4 skipped. The same 6 display-floor checks fail on main.
- Checked in Chrome:
  - the closed panel makes no data requests;
  - opening it reads the brief;
  - picking DAL1989 shows Following and the share link tracks it;
  - closing the card stops tracking;
  - Properties shows 3D aircraft, and Contacts and Space Missions show in the main tab.

title: Preview a flight's photo, route, model and cockpit view in its Context card
body:
The Context card's top tile now previews what is picked. This is the card-preview part of Manjunath's context UI prototype, following #1773. It also adds vessel photos.

**What it shows** (`src/ui/views/panels/EntityCard.vue`)
- A flight shows:
  - its Planespotters photo, once the flights layer has looked one up for the plane it tracks;
  - its route on a small globe: origin to destination, the flown part solid and the rest dashed, with the plane on the arc;
  - its fleet model turning, with callouts of what can be worked out about the flight (phase, flight level, Mach, squawk, signal age);
  - the view ahead from its cockpit, with speed and altitude tapes.
- The model and the cockpit view take turns, and a switch picks one and holds it. Under reduced motion nothing swaps by itself.
- A vessel shows its Open Vessel Photos photo, with its credit.
- A satellite shows the ground beneath it (Esri World Imagery) and graphs its altitude and speed.

**Seams and cost**
- The route globe, model and cockpit view are the renderer's. The Cesium plugin hands them over as a new `cardPreviews` application hook (`src/render/cesium/cardPreviews.js`, typed in `contract/renderer.d.ts`). The card's tiles keep only the words, figures and HUD over them, so nothing in the UI reaches Cesium.
- Each preview draws in a small scene of its own. It stops drawing while hidden and frees its graphics context as it closes, so flicking through cards never pushes out the globe's.
- The model is the fleet model the globe draws for that type, built from the set loaded at startup, so opening a card fetches no model. The flights layer's record now carries the type code and emitter category that pick it.
- The photo comes from the item's own layer, not from Contacts.
- The prototype's NASA satellite models are not included.

**Checks**
- format, boundaries, i18n (13 locales complete), layer-token, library and build all pass.
- Unit tests pass (14,401).
- Checked in Chrome:
  - picking EJM848 (a G550) turns the T-tail business jet model, not an airliner;
  - DAL841 shows its photo with "Photo © OMGcat", then 3D and Cockpit view; the cockpit view draws with its tapes;
  - the route globe, driven through the hook with JFK to LHR, draws both codes, the flown and dashed arcs, and the plane.
- Not checked live: the satellite ground view and vessel photos. The satellite and AIS feeds error on a local dev server, so these are covered only by unit tests.

**Review fixes**
- A route globe that cannot draw tells the card, which shows another view.
- A card opened before the model set has loaded waits for that load instead of dropping the model.
- The model turns at the same rate on any display, and holds still under reduced motion.
- A hidden cockpit view stops drawing.
- The route plane keeps the craft's latest position through the fly-in.
- Metric altitude graphs keep main's 0.5% change threshold.

title: Base map through the globe port
body:
Cesium switches the map stacks through its globe port, as any renderer
does, rather than through a map engine of its own. Every route keeps its
behaviour:

- Google 3D turned off is kept hidden, and shown again without loading it
  anew; the key route's tiles take clamped marks, as the token routes' do.
- Esri goes to its deepest level (23); its "Map data not yet available"

- Keyless terrain that does not answer is the flat ellipsoid, tried again
  behind it; world terrain asks ion first, as before.
- window.__godsEyeView.tileset is the Cesium photoreal tileset.

title: Voice: an app can supply what open_stories does
body:
`open_stories`, spoken or typed, always opened the Stories page: `createApplicationTools` set `openStories` after spreading the `voice` options, so an app could not choose what the action does.

Now an app can pass `voice.openStories({ isCurrent })`. It is used for the action when given, and answers true when it opened, `'already-open'`, or false. Without it, the action opens the Stories page exactly as before. The default moved into `storiesOpener` in `src/stories/boot.js`.

- `src/stories/boot.test.mjs`: a supplied `openStories` is called with `{ isCurrent }` and the Stories page is not opened; the default opens the page when Stories is closed, answers `'already-open'` when open, and is null where Stories is not offered.
- `npm test`: 14,418 passed, 0 failed, 4 skipped. `npm run build` passes.
- `docs/APPLICATION.md` documents the option.

title: Running God's Eye View on Android with Termux (works)
body:
I got this running on my Android 15 phone (arm64) through Termux. Steps:

1. pkg update && pkg upgrade -y
2. pkg install nodejs-lts npm git
3. termux-wake-lock
4. git clone https://github.com/bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view && cd gods-eye-view
5. PUPPETEER_SKIP_DOWNLOAD=1 npm ci --force
6. npm run dev
7. Open localhost:4173 in Chrome

Notes: --force is needed because one dependency (eccodes-wasm) blocks the "android" platform. Puppeteer's download fails on Termux, so it's skipped. The first load is slow and it needs internet the whole time, since all the data is live. It runs fine on my phone.

title: Launches and satellites leave the world clock when destroyed
body:
The launches and satellites layers register their time coverage with the page's world clock when they are created, and never unregister it. When a page destroys its application and starts a new one, each old layer stays reachable through the clock, and with it that application's scene and loaded tiles.

Both layers now keep the function `register` returns, call it on destroy, and register again on init, as the earthquakes layer already does.

Test: destroying the satellites layer removes its registration, and init puts it back (`src/layers/satellites/stale.test.mjs`).

title: feat: source-linked ports and terminals layer using NGA World Port Index
body:
## Problem

Vessel tracking shows movements, but users researching maritime trade and infrastructure also need selectable port profiles with facility information and attributable commercial facts. I could not find a dedicated World Port Index layer in the current core catalog or Data Library.

## Proposal

Add an opt-in Ports & terminals layer under Infrastructure (or the Data Library if preferred by maintainers), using NGA's World Port Index (WPI/Pub 150) for global port locations and facility attributes. Keep the first version a reference-data display, with users conducting their own analysis.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Toggleable, clickable port markers using stable WPI identifiers; display port name, country and UN/LOCODE when supplied.
- [ ] Country filter and container / solid-bulk / oil-terminal / LNG-terminal filters. Match affirmative facility flags only; unknown must remain unknown, not be inferred as absent or operational.
- [ ] Selected profile includes operator, ownership, annual throughput, handling capacity, operational status and expansion fields. Explicitly display unavailable values rather than inventing information or implying comprehensive commercial coverage.
- [ ] Throughput and capacity remain separate, with units, reporting period and geographic scope. Proposed future capacity must not be shown as current capacity.
- [ ] Supplemental commercial facts come from dated official port-authority/operator sources, matched to stable identifiers, with field-level links and review dates. Port-wide figures must not silently be assigned to individual terminals.
- [ ] Source attribution and metadata distinguish mirror last-edit time, retrieval time and individual fact dates. Listing in WPI is not proof of live operational status.
- [ ] Bounded, ordered pagination with response-size limits, cancellation and explicit failure/partial-data reporting; disabling/destroying the layer must prevent late responses from redrawing it.
- [ ] Tests for source validation/pagination, positive/unknown facility filtering, clickable selection, lifecycle cleanup, and the visible panel; project-required build/unit/tracking checks and visual evidence before review.
- [ ] Update CURRENT-STATE.md, DATA_SOURCES.md, credits and changelog; register any share token under the existing allocation rules. Describe whether filters are shared or session-local.

## Data source, license, and attribution

**Primary dataset:** National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency, World Port Index (Pub 150).

- Provider reference: https://msi.nga.mil/Publications/WPI
- NGA's official repository describes the dataset and its fields: https://github.com/ngageoint/marlin/blob/main/data/World%20Port%20Index.md
- NGA public-information policy: https://www.nga.mil/resources/Privacy_Policy.html — public information may be copied/distributed unless otherwise specified; appropriate credits requested.
- Working government-hosted mirror tested on 2026-11-17: https://arcgis.netl.doe.gov/server/rest/services/Hosted/CCS_EJ_SJ_Data/FeatureServer/17
- Query path: `/query` with WGS84 GeoJSON, `orderByFields=objectid`, `resultOffset` and `resultRecordCount`. Two downloaded pages contained 3,824 features. The mirror metadata last-edit timestamp is 1776674191094 (2026-04-20 UTC), so it must be described as a mirror snapshot, not guaranteed to be NGA's latest monthly publication. NGA's direct endpoints were unavailable during this check.
- NETL disclaimer: https://netl.doe.gov/home/disclaimer
- No key required. Fetch global port data at runtime; preserve NGA / DOE NETL attribution and do not imply government endorsement.

**Commercial enrichment:** WPI does not provide a complete global ownership/throughput/expansion dataset. Initial limited factual supplements can use official sources such as:

- DP World, Jebel Ali: https://www.dpworld.com/en/news/releases/uae/dp-world-records-highest-cargo-volumes-at-jebel-ali-port-since-2015 (2024 throughput and reported handling capacity, with separate periods).
- Port of Los Angeles: https://portoflosangeles.org/about and https://portoflosangeles.org/business/statistics/container-statistics (municipal landlord structure and dated annual throughput; the statistics page requests attribution).
- Singapore MPA terminals: https://www.mpa.gov.sg/port-marine-ops/operations/port-infrastructure/terminals (operators; avoid treating all Singapore terminals as one WPI point).

Use only independently transcribed factual values and short descriptions with source links; do not copy articles, imagery or bulk proprietary datasets or claim that website content is MIT licensed. Leave unsupported fields explicitly unavailable.

## Will you build it?

Yes, I plan to open a PR. Source research and an initial implementation have started; the implementation is not yet fully validated or submitted for review.

title: feat(voice): lookup-only aircraft feed resolution via track_entity (#1563)
body:
Fixes #1563.

## What

Adds an opt-in lookup-only aircraft resolution to `track_entity` (`lookupOnly: true`). Given an aircraft flight number or ICAO identifier it queries the live feeds independently of loaded layers and reports source, observation time, and coverage without moving the map or starting a track. Non-aircraft kinds fail closed with a refusal and a redirect to `analyst_query`. The follow/enable path refreshes the required layer and verifies the exact ICAO twice: after the refresh and immediately before tracking.

## Changes

- `src/voice/aircraftLookup.js`: lookup-only resolution path with feed querying, staleness/refusal handling, and the double ICAO verification.
- `src/voice/gevActions.js`, `src/voice/actionSchemas.js`, `src/standalone/toolCatalog.js`, `src/tools/queries/aviation.js`, `server/providers/openai/toolDescriptions.js`: action wiring, schema, and tool description.
- `src/data/contactMatch.js`, `src/data/flightIdentity.js`: shared matching helpers. **Contract note:** this widens the contactMatch matching contract - exact-tier callsign matching now deterministically normalizes known flight-number aliases and zero-padding via `flightIdentity`. It never guesses unknown airline codes.
- `src/voice/aircraftLookup.test.mjs`: coverage for the new path, including the non-aircraft fail-closed refusal.
- `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md`: behavior recorded (repo policy for runtime changes).
- `changelog.d/1780-voice-aircraft-lookup.md`: changelog fragment.

## Adjacency to #1649

This branch shares no files with #1649 (checked against its full diff: 26 files, zero overlap) and does not depend on its outcome. Where behavior on main is still settling, the docs here record what this branch's code does today.

## Verification

- Targeted tests: 429/429 pass (`aircraftLookup.test.mjs` and the related voice suites).
- Repo prompt-size gate (integrationContract.test.mjs, instructions + tool schemas <= 56,500 chars in both configs): 55,725 default / 56,480 with Overpass, both pass.
- i18n key check: 13/13.
- `npm run format:check`: clean on the full branch tree (2,322 files).
- `test:track`: aborted with a browser navigation failure (LifecycleWatcher 601); cause unknown, not established to be memory-related.
- Inconclusive here: full `npm test` did not finish within the sandbox time limit; `build` and `check:boundaries` exceed sandbox memory. CI should decide those gates.
- No live-voice (realtime API) verification was performed; behavior was verified through the deterministic action-runner tests only.

## AI assistance

This change was drafted with AI assistance (OpenAI Codex CLI) under my direction; the diff was independently reviewed and the tests above were run before opening this PR.

title: fix(earthquakes): make quakes clickable, with card click arbitration
body: ## What this changes Earthquake discs and magnitude labels now respond to clicks. A disc selects the quake and shows its magnitude, USGS class, depth band, place, UTC time and source. The card opens the USGS event page when an event ID is available; clicking empty map clears it. Magnitude labels also select and fly to the quake through the existing world-focus route, and remain keyboard-accessible. - Selection participates in the shared context store. Feed refresh updates the card without retaking selection or restarting animation. - Quake discs are deliberately not registered as pick owners, like drone airspace and fire perimeters, so other layers read a click over a disc as empty space. The quake handler yields to another layer's card or label painted on top, and to another layer's registered object under its own card or label when that layer acts on it. - World-overlay hit rectangles now stay what is painted on screen until the next paint, instead of clearing whenever any source changes. Every click subscriber therefore sees the overlay the user clicked, even after an earlier subscriber publishes its selection card in the same click, so the outcome no longer depends on listener order. - Only the topmost painted card acts on a click. Vessel, FIRMS, wildlife, news, CCTV, perimeter, ghost-map and shipwreck card handlers read the unfiltered top entry, so a covered card neither acts nor clears its selection. Drone airspace, fire perimeters, submarine cables and rocket launches stand aside when another layer's card or label is on top. A top news or wildlife card still acts over another layer's scene item. - Flight trails and the directions route line and markers become passive pick owners (`registerPickOwner(…, { passive })`): still not empty space, but they no longer make quake, fire, vessel or CCTV cards dead clicks. Directions still acts on its maneuver steps. - Layers whose shapes stand aside for a card (drone zones, fire perimeters, quake discs, cables, launch markers) register them with `registerCardBackground`. A live top CCTV card acts over any of them; previously its click was dead over cables, launch markers and quake discs. Unknown identified objects and registered owners still block it. - Coarse-pointer taps distinguish an exact scene hit from a nearby contact. Owners whose clicks select nearby contacts register as `expanded` (flights, military, vessels, radio, Street Level). An exact-only FIRMS or CCTV item reached only as a nearby contact no longer swallows a quake card or label tap, or a tap on a vessel's own card, and the Context panel does not name that item under the card (`cardKeepsClick`). Aircraft and vessel touch selection keep priority, and an exact hit or an open-map near miss is unchanged. Radio and Street Level also pick through their own windows (17 and 9 px); an item found only through that window yields to another layer's card or label painted over it, and Street Level now also takes its own touch contact beyond its 9 px window. Under a card, Context leaves an item whose owner does not act on that hit (a passive route, or a near-missed fire or camera) to the card. Fire and CCTV cards in turn yield to a touch contact whose layer acts on it. The aircraft a layer already tracks and Street Level's position marker count as passive picks, since a click on either does nothing. The pick registry records which layers act on a click's hit when the click first reads it, so an aircraft that starts tracking during a click does not also hand that click to a quake, fire, CCTV or vessel card, or to Context. - The selected disc gains a fading radial gradient and contour animation bounded to three cycles (about 14 seconds), then rests. Reduced motion is read live, and off-screen animation does not request frames. - Application services remain injected into the earthquake package. New class/depth and navigation strings cover all 13 locales. - Two separate test-only commits: camera traces are compared within platform roundoff (structure, counters and viewport stay exact; the golden file and production camera code are unchanged), and the tracking regression follows the shared 3D toggle and draw-port trails. Review follow-ups (after the first review round): - Pick owners can declare the clicks they ignore (`registerPickOwner(…, { declinesClick })`). Flights and military decline a tap that drifts past the click travel or comes in cockpit mode, and CCTV declines any click that is not clean, so a fire, quake, vessel or CCTV card beside them, and the Context panel, keep that tap instead of deferring to a layer that will not act. - The selected quake's gradient and contours sit on the ground the disc is draped on, read through the heights service and re-read while they paint (a label's fly-to starts before that ground loads). A label's fly-to frames the whole disc for large quakes. - A quake that ages out of the feed clears its selection as evicted; id-less quakes are named by their content rather than their row. - The Bhote Koshi trigger-record callout opens its source on a click, as its keyboard action does, yielding to drags and to layers that act under it. - The card's place line is cut to 48 code points, its link hint shows only with an opener, its accessible name carries depth, place, time and source, and a link-less card's click and keyboard action fly to the quake. - Camera trace comparison scales its tolerance with the value and wraps heading and roll. Known limits: the gradient and contours use the 2D world overlay, so terrain and 3D tiles do not occlude them, and they use the existing fixed depth palette. The tangent-plane projection is approximate for very large events at grazing angles. Ground height is re-read only while painting, at most twice a second; a late terrain update may wait for the next repaint, particularly with reduced motion. ## How I verified it - [x] `npm run format:check`, `npm run check:boundaries`, `npm run i18n` (13/13 locales) and `npm run build` pass on commit `731228081`. The build reports the existing bundle-size warning. - [x] `npm test`: 14,502 passed, 4 expected skips, 0 failures, plus 15 allocation-test passes. - [x] Hardware tracking regression (`npm run test:track -- --headful --offline-imagery`): 111 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped on the final commit. An earlier keyless run returned 109/2/0 when the public terrain provider rate-limited requests and tripped both console checks; its unchanged retry passed. - [x] Fail-first coverage, each test failing without its production change: buried cards; news/wildlife cards over trails; quake card and labels over trails and the directions route; fire, CCTV and vessel cards over a passive pick; cable and launch yields; card-background registration per layer; a CCTV card over a quake disc, cable and launch marker; the five `expanded` registrations, the tracked aircraft and the Street Level position marker as passive picks; coarse FIRMS near misses under a quake label or card through the real dispatcher and FIRMS handler; fire and CCTV cards yielding to an acting touch contact and keeping a non-acting one; radio and Street Level window-only items yielding to a card, and keeping their own touch contact under it; Street Level's touch-contact fallback; Context leaving a near-missed fire or an exact route to the card through the real bridge; a vessel card keeping a near-miss tap; quake, fire, CCTV, vessel and Context checks reading the acting owners recorded for the click while an aircraft starts tracking in it. - [x] Fresh production-build checks on `731228081`, Apple M5/Metal with desktop Chrome touch emulation and real scene picks: an out-and-back touch gesture (40 px total travel) beside an aircraft opens the quake source once without tracking; a clean tap with the aircraft handler first starts tracking once without opening the source; a quake label beside Radio selects and plays the station once. Focused regression tests: 152 passed, 0 failed. Physical-device testing was not performed. - [x] Prior production-build touch checks on `54fd3d3be` on Apple M5/Metal with desktop Chrome touch emulation: a tap on the quake card beside an untracked aircraft starts tracking once and leaves the USGS link closed in both listener orders. The aircraft-first FIRMS card overlap also starts tracking once and leaves the fire unselected. Exact and nearby shared-dispatch regression tests confirm the card opens once on a later tap over an already tracked aircraft. Physical-device testing was not performed. - [x] Earlier built-app touch checks on `99bd0443c`: a quake label beside a Radio station selects the station once with Context initially open or closed. A quake card beside an untracked aircraft still starts tracking once when the aircraft handler runs first. These cases use desktop Chrome touch emulation and real scene picks. - [x] Prior built-app checks included quake and vessel cards beside FIRMS and a quake label beside radio with Context initially open and closed. Earlier checks also covered a quake label and card over an actual route; news card over a route and flight trail; CCTV over quake-disc and cable-reference geometry with exactly one activation. Prior cable-overlay QA 8/8 and synthetic vessel-card checks passed; these are fixture results. - [ ] CCTV QA (`scripts/qa-cctv-v2.mjs`), head and base run back to back against the same live catalog and the same active camera (`deldot-scam083`): base `624c229b` 46 passed / 2 failed / 5 inconclusive, published head `fde5f95b` 47 / 1 / 5. This comparison predates `731228081` and is not a passing aggregate gate. The remaining failure (the panel `` and plane share one frame-URL family, `panelSrc=null`) fails on base too; the five inconclusives are the same drag-target skips on both. - [ ] FIRMS fixture QA: 7 passed, 1 failed on both an earlier committed branch revision and its matched base; not rerun on the repaired candidate (a manually assigned native `viewer.trackedEntity` sentinel at the flight boundary). - Directions QA is not run: its inherited observer reads legacy Entity geometry while the renderer uses draw-port geometry on both main and this branch. Route-overlap behavior is covered by focused tests and the built-app checks above. A review identified a possible dead tap when Radio or Street Level's own pick window and the shared touch contact name different items from the same layer under a quake overlay. Under another layer's card, both layers now act on their own touch contact in that case (covered by regression tests). Tested Radio layouts did not produce differing first picks, so the case has unit-test coverage but no reproduced in-browser instance. Separate inherited limits remain: clicking any card while an aircraft is tracked also releases the tracking (the aircraft layers' empty-space branch does not hit-test the overlay); some top perimeter/ghost-map/shipwreck link cards over registered scene contacts can co-act; a stale CCTV card over bare map keeps the existing deselection behavior; a card over a trail lying on a local ADS-B aircraft can co-act because that layer drills through trails. Native-speaker wording review has not been performed. ## Docs - [x] `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md` updated. - [x] Numbered changelog fragment `changelog.d/1781-earthquake-click-details.md` added. The branch is 151 commits behind upstream `main@4f1a4a3f2`. A local merge-tree check is conflict-free; these results cover the branch tree, not a merge with newer main.

title: feat: add source-linked NGA WPI ports and terminals layer
body:
## What this changes

Closes #1779.

**Draft validation status:** the ports-specific fixture/live browser gates, unit suite and production build pass. The required stock tracking harness is not green in this software-rendered workspace: both the feature and unchanged upstream base reproduce the same six grounded-aircraft failures. The comparison is recorded below.

Adds an opt-in **Ports & terminals** Infrastructure layer with stable WPI markers, clickable selection, country and affirmative-only container/solid-bulk/oil/LNG filters, and a Vue/Pinia profile panel. Unknown facilities stay unknown. Unsupported operator/ownership/throughput/capacity/status/expansion fields explicitly say **Not provided by source**.

The DOE NETL adapter validates metadata and ordered object IDs, advances offsets by received page length, caps requests at six pages / 4 MiB each, and supports cancellation and timeouts. The live mirror returns **3,824 records → 3,820 valid unique ports**; two non-integer WPI IDs and two duplicate IDs are excluded with a visible partial-data warning and count. Failed refreshes retain prior data with an error; disable/destroy prevents late redraws and releases input/render resources.

Small official-source supplements are matched to Jebel Ali (48276), Los Angeles (16080), and Keppel (50000). Facts carry field-level links, period, scope and review dates, with publication dates for dated releases. Throughput and capacity remain separate; Tuas future capacity is only a related expansion, never Keppel's current capacity. Commercial facts never populate WPI facility flags. WPI inclusion is not evidence of live operational status.

Mirror last edit, retrieval time and individual fact dates are distinct. The floating panel stays above the context dock with a nearly opaque background for readable profiles. Share token **03** is registered; only enabled state is shared, while filters remain session-local. No new voice/MCP query tool is introduced.

## How I verified it

- [x] `npm test`: 14,435 passes including both allocation gates; four existing skips. Node 24.22.1, bounded CPU affinity for the full suite.
- [x] `npm run build` (also rerun after the final panel CSS fix)
- [x] Focused source/lifecycle and Vue panel tests after the readability fix: 12 passes
- [x] `npm run format:check`, `npm run check:boundaries`, `npm run i18n`
- [x] `npm run layer-token:check -- --base-ref upstream/main` (upstream main still 624c229)
- [x] `node scripts/qa-ports.mjs` and `--record`: fixture filtering, source-linked profile, real rendered marker click, panel stacking, 390px layout, disable and recording cleanup
- [x] `node scripts/qa-ports.mjs --live`: real DOE mirror, exactly 3,820 ports / two invalid + two duplicate exclusions, filters and selection, phone layout and disable
- [ ] `npm run test:track -- --offline-imagery`: **97 passed, 6 failed, 4 skipped** (exit 1). Five failures report `tracked exit model identity changed` in grounded-aircraft floor/model controls; one loading-regime failure reports undefined model state / NaN floor. The run reports no console errors and no HTTP 5xx responses. A clean upstream `624c229` worktree reproduced **the exact same 97/6/4 result and identical six failure details** with no ports layer installed. [Full comparison](https://github.com/anishPSU/gods-eye-view/blob/feat/ports-wpi-1779/docs/media/ports/tracking-comparison.md). Full Chrome cannot start because the workspace blocks its Unix singleton socket; these results use Chrome Headless Shell 156.0.8078.47 with SwiftShader. This gate remains unresolved and the PR remains draft.

The tested implementation tree was published as **0873415 before browser QA**. Final panel/QA fixes and evidence were published as **6748841**. Shell Git had no write credentials, so publication used the connected GitHub Git-data API; remote tree hashes were checked against the tested local Git trees.

## New layer checklist

**Screenshots (live DOE data and real imagery)**

![Global ports and explicit partial-data count](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anishPSU/gods-eye-view/feat/ports-wpi-1779/docs/media/ports/live-globe.jpg)

![Jebel Ali facts, separate metrics and source dates](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anishPSU/gods-eye-view/feat/ports-wpi-1779/docs/media/ports/live-facts.jpg)

![390px profile layout](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anishPSU/gods-eye-view/feat/ports-wpi-1779/docs/media/ports/live-phone.jpg)

**Recording:** [25-second accelerated fixture walkthrough](https://github.com/anishPSU/gods-eye-view/raw/refs/heads/feat/ports-wpi-1779/docs/media/ports/ports-demo.mp4). This recording uses four WPI-shaped fixtures and fixture imagery; the screenshots above use the live mirror. [Evidence notes](https://github.com/anishPSU/gods-eye-view/blob/feat/ports-wpi-1779/docs/media/ports/README.md).

**Category:** Infrastructure (off by default).

**Data source and licence**

- NGA World Port Index (Pub 150), fetched at runtime from the [DOE NETL ArcGIS mirror](https://arcgis.netl.doe.gov/server/rest/services/Hosted/CCS_EJ_SJ_Data/FeatureServer/17), with WGS84 GeoJSON and ordered pagination. No key needed; no global port dataset is bundled.
- [NGA WPI reference](https://msi.nga.mil/Publications/WPI), [NGA public-information policy](https://www.nga.mil/resources/Privacy_Policy.html) and [NETL disclaimer](https://netl.doe.gov/home/disclaimer). Public-information reuse remains subject to stated exceptions; no government endorsement is implied.
- Common data credits and the Ports panel attribute NGA WPI / DOE NETL and the named commercial fact providers.
- Supplements use independently transcribed factual values from DP World, Port of Los Angeles and Singapore MPA, linked per field. No articles, logos, imagery or bulk proprietary datasets are copied, no runtime scraping is added, and the providers' websites are not claimed to be MIT licensed.

title: feat(library): 15 Data Library entries for Germany, European seas and Earth observation
body:
## What this changes

Adds 15 Data Library entries: manifests only, no JavaScript, every source keyless, CORS-enabled and hosted by its provider.

- **Germany:** PEGELONLINE waterway gauges, DWD weather warnings, DWD radar composite, DWD lightning density, the BfS gamma dose rate network, LGB's Brandenburg and Berlin DOP20 aerial photos, and the 22 Hamburg traffic-camera positions the city publishes as open data (locations only, no image).
- **European seas:** EMODnet offshore wind farms (areas and point-only sites), oil and gas installations and 2023 vessel density; Digitraffic AIS vessel positions in the northern Baltic.
- **Worldwide:** GEBCO 2026 shaded relief, NASA GIBS IMERG half-hourly precipitation and MUR sea surface temperature.

See also #1294 (BfS radiation observations): this only adds the network's latest one-hour values, no station history.

## How I verified it

- [x] `npm run build`
- [x] `npm test` (0 failed)
- [ ] `npm run test:track`: **not green in my sandbox.** 85 passed, 16 failed, 6 skipped, and the same 16 fail there on unchanged `main` (624c229): basemap and terrain hosts are blocked and rendering is SwiftShader. It needs a run on an open network.
- [x] Feature gate: `npm run qa:data-library` (21 passed), `library:check -- --base-ref origin/main`, `library:probe` (all new entries `ok`; the existing entries' hosts are not reachable from my sandbox), `format:check`, `check:boundaries`, `i18n`.

Each entry was also added in the real app in headless Chromium: datasets drew with their counts (the 22 Hamburg cameras as labelled points), tiles read DRAPED, no library error logged.

## Data sources and licences

All fetched at runtime, none bundled, no key. Licence and attribution per entry are in the generated `DATA_SOURCES.md` rows of this diff.

- Stated in the service itself: Hamburg (WFS `AccessConstraints`: dl-de/by-2-0, no access restrictions), Brandenburg (WMS `AccessConstraints`), EMODnet (its catalogue records, CC BY 4.0), GEBCO (citation form in the WMS abstract), DWD (`AccessConstraints`, `EC_LICENSE`).
- BfS: `odlinfo_odl_1h_latest` has no catalogue record of its own; the BfS catalogue licenses its sister ODL open-data products under dl-de/by-2-0. A maintainer may prefer `operatorOptIn`.
- The licence pages on `dwd.de`, `govdata.de`, `gebco.net`, `digitraffic.fi` and `earthdata.nasa.gov` are blocked in my sandbox, so please check those links.

## Known limits

- **Tile layers do not reload.** Radar, lightning and precipitation show the time step current when each tile was fetched, with no time shown; switching the layer off and on reloads. The descriptions say so.
- **DWD warnings:** an empty answer in calm weather reads as `FAIL` in `library:probe`; a Germany-wide view draws only part of a large set (the dataset feature budget); severity uses the status palette, not the DWD's own styles.
- **Digitraffic:** a manifest cannot send the `Digitraffic-User` header the core feeds send, so requests count as unidentified. Positions can be up to a day old.
- **Hamburg cameras:** locations and the junction name only — the service publishes no image URLs, so there is no live picture.
- **Legends:** none for lightning (the DWD's SLD labels do not match the integer raster it draws) or GEBCO; the radar legend has 16 items (validator limit; the guide says 12).
- **PEGELONLINE:** 46 of 738 gauges have no coordinates and are not drawn; cards show value and unit, not the time.

## Docs

- [x] `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md` updated and a `changelog.d/1784-…` fragment added.

title: 3D models only within 3 km of the camera, at true size
body:
## What this changes

**3D models only within 3 km, at true size.** An aircraft (civil or military), vessel, transit vehicle or train now draws as its 3D model only when it is within 3 km of the camera, measured from the eye to the vehicle. Farther away it draws as its icon. A model already drawn is kept out to 3.6 km, so a vehicle sitting on the edge does not flicker between the two. Models are drawn at their true size: the minimum pixel size that inflated distant models into blobs is gone.

Proximity and All now use the same 3 km distance and differ only by how many models they allow (150 and 350). Before, Proximity reached 150 km (kept to 185 km) and All 400 km (kept to 450 km), with a 24 px minimum size.

The camera altitude above which no model is considered at all was 800 km. It is now the highest aircraft the layers draw (30 km) plus the 3.6 km, so a camera high above the ground still gets a model for an aircraft close to it, and the distance alone decides below that.

The cockpit view's aircraft silhouettes (icons shown out to 150 km in Proximity and 400 km in All, dots beyond) used the same distances as the models. They keep their old distances, since they are icons and not models.

**Deselecting a plane no longer flashes its icon.** When a selected plane was drawn as a model, deselecting it showed its icon for about a second before the model came back. The selected plane is drawn by its own model, and the plane's ordinary model was dropped once that one drew. On deselect the icon showed at once while a new ordinary model loaded. Now the ordinary model stays loaded but hidden while the plane is selected, placed where the plane is. On deselect the plane goes straight back to it in the same frame, and the icon shows only when there is no loaded model. Military aircraft share this code and get the same fix. Vessels, transit and rail vehicles keep their model when selected, so they never had this flash.

## How I verified it

- [x] `npm run build`
- [x] `npm test`: 14,418 passed, 0 failed (plus the allocation and performance runs, all passing)
- [x] `npm run test:track` (dev server running): 98 passed, 6 failed, 3 skipped. The same 6 fail on `main` (96 passed, 7 failed, 4 skipped there): the arrival timing check and five display-floor checks that stop at "tracked exit model identity changed". The harness's tracked-model checks now zoom the follow camera to within 2 km of the plane, and its grounded-model check parks the camera 2 km above the planes instead of 8 km, since models draw only within 3 km.
- [x] `npm run format:check` and `npm run check:boundaries`
- [ ] Feature gate for the area I touched: none runs. `scripts/qa-sprites-b5.mjs` covers model scale but does not parse on `main` (a quote in a test name).

New and changed tests:

- `src/data/aircraftModelLayer.test.mjs`: models within 3 km and icons beyond, in both modes; a model kept to 3.5 km and released at 3.7 km, and not taken again until back within 3 km; a camera 2 km above an aircraft at 30 km still models it; no minimum pixel size; the selected plane keeps a loaded, hidden model that takes it back on deselect. The fixture now uses the flights layer's own model settings.
- `src/data/fleetModelInstances.test.mjs`: the same 3 km and 3.6 km distances for vessels, transit and rail in both modes, and no minimum pixel size.
- `src/data/trackedModelForm.test.mjs`, for both aircraft layers: the ordinary model is kept, loaded and hidden, once the selected model draws; deselecting hands the plane back to it in the same frame with its icon hidden; the icon shows when there is no model, when the model has not loaded yet, and when 3D was turned off meanwhile.
- `src/data/cockpitModels.test.mjs`: both modes share the 3 km and 3.6 km distances; the cockpit silhouettes keep their own.
- `src/layers/localAdsb/index.test.mjs`: its model tests put the camera 2 km from the aircraft instead of 50 km.

## Docs

- [x] `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md` updated and a `changelog.d/<pr-number>-<slug>.md` fragment added. The README's 3D fleet line now says 3 km.

title: Fix application Cockpit rides on Rail trains and Transit vehicles
body:
## What this changes

Follow-up to #1686. These are five fixes for riding a Rail train or Transit vehicle that an application adds as a Cockpit subject (`services.cockpitSubjects`). GEV itself registers no such provider, so the stock app never reaches these paths.

- **Held Transit icon stayed drawn.** Hiding a vehicle with a direct `marker.show = false` left its icon under the rider’s eye with the depth test off. The renderer ports only flush dirty entries. A hold now places the vehicle through `placeSample` and flushes the icon set immediately with `flushMarkers()`. Moving or ending the hold takes the vehicle out of play until a visibility sweep finds it in view. If that first sweep finds it visible, it keeps the clock that advanced during the hold, even if the feed’s target lag grew (`src/layers/transit/cockpitSubject.js`, `src/layers/transit/rendering.js`).
- **A hold outlived the layer.** `disable()` now clears the held key, so after Transit is turned off and on the vehicle shows again (`src/layers/transit/lifecycle.js`).
- **Transit height on the ellipsoid.** Above 60 km on a cold floor, the marker stands on the ellipsoid and the snapshot reported −1.5 m as known ground. It now reports no height until both segment floors are known, so the view waits for the ground (`src/layers/transit/cockpitSubject.js`).
- **Rail height on an unknown floor.** `railHeightM` is now null when the drawn position has no floor (`drawn.q === 0`) (`src/layers/rail/cockpitSubject.js`).
- **A standing train turned around.** GPS jitter flipped `binding.direction` and swung the ride’s heading between 5° and 185°. On both reports and playback segments, `steer()` now advances its reference point after 15 m (`DIRECTION_MIN_M`) of movement along the line. Small steps can add up to a reversal, while jitter under 15 m on either side of the reference point preserves direction. After a position correction, playback moves its reference point to where it resumes: the start of a segment that begins at a break, or of the first segment it draws in a new playback epoch, which a clock correction starts. The jump itself is not a move. Once playback owns direction (`directionPlayed`), the train turns when playback reaches the reversal. Until movement establishes direction, the snapshot uses the operator’s last reported bearing, even across reports that omit it (`src/layers/rail/pathBinding.js`, `src/layers/rail/cockpitSubject.js`). The follow check compares directly with `DIRECTION_MIN_M` (`src/layers/rail/policy.js`). Only the ride snapshot reads `binding.direction`.

Of the 16 new top-level tests, 12 fail on main at `6b05cd58b` because of the bugs above, and all 16 pass here. The other four cover a known rail floor at sea level and three regressions from earlier commits of this PR: a corrected playback position, an omitted bearing, and a clock correction that playback joins past its break. The last one fails on main only because main has no `directionPlayed`.

Four existing tests changed. The selected-train snapshot uses a known 12 m floor, and the stopped-train binding test steps back 10 m. The uneven-ground transit test checks the drawn height mid-segment, where interpolating the endpoints would give about 54 m instead of the 10 m floor it crosses. The held-vehicle test for an unknown floor uses the shared one-bus fixture.

## How I verified it

- [x] `npm run build` (keyless) passed.
- [x] `npm test` ran 14,432 tests. 14,427 passed, 2 failed and 3 were skipped. The failures in `src/render/cesium/cameraGoldens.test.mjs` and `src/render/cesium/cameraPort.test.mjs` also occur on main at `6b05cd58b`.
- [x] `npm run test:track` (keyless dev server, at `58afb169d`): 93 passed, 8 failed and 6 were skipped. All 8 failures are flights and military checks outside this diff. Six of them also fail on main at `6b05cd58b`; the other two fail at the merge base `624c229bc` and are fixed on main.
- [ ] `npm run qa:transit`: not run. It opens a visible browser (`headless: false`), and the hold scenarios need an embedding application’s Cockpit subject provider.
- [ ] Feature gate: none applies. An embedding application supplies the Cockpit subject provider.

All 174 Rail tests and 153 Transit tests passed. The hold-release test covers transferring and ending a hold. `npm run format:check`, `npm run check:boundaries`, `npm run changelog:check` and `git diff --check` passed.
