- [x] `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md` updated and a `changelog.d/1786-cockpit-ride-transit-rail.md` fragment added.

title: Keep an application's Cockpit subject steady in the camera and HUD
body:
## What this changes

Follow-up to #1686. These are five fixes in the Cockpit camera and HUD for a subject that an application adds (`services.cockpitSubjects`). GEV itself registers no such provider, so the stock app never reaches these paths.

- **The view closed on a cold floor.** `enterSubject` reset `subjectHeightM` to null. A height that the entry frame gave was then lost while later frames gave none and the floor was cold, so the view ended. It now starts from the entry frame's height (`src/ui/cockpitTrackingController.js`).
- **The camera fell behind at low frame rates.** Each camera step was capped at the update interval plus 0.1 s. At 5 frames a second the camera fell 700 m behind a 30 m/s subject in a minute. The cap is now the interval plus 1 s, and a hidden tab still counts as one late update (`src/cockpitMath.js`).
- **Live Signals lost a warning.** A provider's rows were logged as new entries, so a changing ETA filled the five-row list. A warning that was still listed and fell off never came back, because its signature stayed. Provider rows now change in place by key and come back after being pushed off. The aircraft, ISS and vessel log is unchanged (`src/ui/cockpitSignals.js`, `src/ui/cockpitInstruments.js`, `src/ui/cockpitController.js`).
- **CJK progress labels were too narrow.** The width estimate counted every character as 6.4 px. Full-width glyphs (CJK, kana, Hangul, full-width forms) now count 10.6 px (`src/cockpitProgress.js`).
- **Provider words broke after a failed read.** `refusal()` now keeps the `entryFace`, `labels` and `look` it checked, and the kept provider starts from them. A getter that fails on a later read no longer leaves empty words or throws on entry (`src/cockpitSubjectProviders.js`).

Text fixes:
- the JSDoc names `'inertial'` as the default anchor for a frame with a valid speed;
- `docs/APPLICATION.md` says an entry face's `icon` must be one of the loaded Material Symbols;
- the unreleased #1686 release note no longer says the veil is off under reduced motion;
- the vessel double-click test now projects through `SceneTransforms` and has a control.

Tests: eight new tests fail on main and pass here. Two existing step tests follow the new cap.

## How I verified it

- [x] `npm run build` (keyless)
- [x] `npm test`: 14 419 tests, 14 414 pass, 3 skipped, 2 fail. Both failures, `src/render/cesium/cameraGoldens.test.mjs` and `src/render/cesium/cameraPort.test.mjs`, fail the same way locally on main.
- [ ] `npm run test:track`: not run, because the stock app has no path to these views.
- [ ] Feature gate: none applies, because without a provider the browser cannot reach these views. Unit tests cover all five fixes.

`npm run format:check`, `npm run check:boundaries`, `npm run doctor -- --json` and `npm run changelog:check` also pass.

## Docs

- [x] `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md` updated and a `changelog.d/<pr-number>-<slug>.md` fragment added

title: Sprites for helicopters, ground vehicles, stations and vessel types; history to live without an empty map; model parts in Cesium
body:
## What changes

**Sprites by kind**
- Aircraft icons are one size. Size by class is gone, and the 3D models show true scale up close.
- Helicopters get a rotor sprite, three frames turning at about 10 fps, each with its own phase. The rotor turns only while airborne or moving above 1 m/s on the ground, the same rule the 3D rotor follows.
- Ground vehicles (ADS-B emitter category C1/C2, OpenSky 16/17, or type ZVEH) get one vehicle sprite in amber `#FF8F1F`. They are recognised from the first report where the feed carries the category or type.
- Ground stations and obstacles (C3–C5, OpenSky 18–20, GRND) get one upright mast sprite, labelled "Ground station / obstacle".
- `category` may now be a string such as `"C1"`, as well as the OpenSky number. The new classes are `vehicle` and `station`.
- Vessels get a hull sprite by type, plus one upright buoy sprite for aids to navigation, with no halo. New colours: sailing `#b49cff`, pleasure `#ff6f61`, military/law enforcement `#a9bccb`, high-speed `#c6ff3d`.

**History to live**
- Going back to live keeps the contacts on screen until the first live answer, then replaces them by id. A contact present in both keeps its icon and model, and eases to its live position when under 5 km away. The map is cleared only if the live request fails.
- Tracked and selected contacts and their trails survive the switch. A contact absent from a partial answer goes through the usual retention rules, judged by its last position report rather than when it was loaded.
- Before: going live from 10 minutes back dropped every aircraft, then redrew them. After: the drawn count never fell below the history count (about 470 → 13,000, 583 frames measured).

**Smoother fast playback**
- Play holds one minute before where 90% of the loaded positions reach, not at the next step.
- It prefetches 4 s of real time ahead at the current rate.
- It merges only newer positions into each aircraft.
- At 1 min/s over 20 s: the clock advanced exactly 20 min, never buffered, with no long tasks and a slowest frame of 36 ms.

**Model parts in Cesium**
- Implements the optional model part state from the renderer contract (`./render/modelParts`): rotors, propellers, gear and doors move on Cesium models. A new conformance check is `draw.models.parts`.

## Tests

- `npm test`: 14,528 run, 14,524 pass, 0 fail, 0 cancelled.
- `npm run check:boundaries` and `npm run format:check` are clean.
- New tests:
  - glyph rasterisation (every sprite the same size);
  - rotor frames;
  - vessel sprites;
  - the history-to-live handover for flights, military and vessels (through the real retention path);
  - the ease;
  - playback hold and prefetch.
- Conformance runs under a software GL renderer with a 300 px canvas, where the globe never settles. Under it, the full suite fails the same 55 checks as `main`, plus the new `draw.models.parts`, which fails on the same settle timeout. With the settle wait lifted, the model and icon checks pass: 8/8 here against 7/7 on `main`.

## Overlap

This touches some of the same files as #1785 (models within 3 km at true size): flights and military policy and motion, and vessel and rail rendering. Whichever merges second gets rebased onto the other.

title: Multi-part fleet models: rotors, propellers, gear and doors as named parts
body:
Replaces the fleet models in `public/models/fleet/` with multi-part versions. Same files, same names, same sizes on screen.

- Every aircraft, helicopter, vessel, ground vehicle and transit model now has named parts: rotors, propellers, landing gear, doors. A renderer that supports the optional model part state (#1788) can spin, pose or highlight them; one that doesn't draws the model as before.
- Stowed gear and closed doors are built in place and hidden, so a model with no part state looks as it did.
- `types.json` gains rocket type rules (real launchers by vehicle name, plus generic small, medium and heavy) for later use; nothing reads them yet.
- 122 models, 2.5 MB in total; the fleet grows about 9%.

Tests: the fleet model, model scale, tracked form, records, transit, rail, Local ADS-B and conformance scene tests pass (233/233).

title: Vessels turn on and off again when their feed fails
body:
#1788 made the vessel layer's live load return the poll's answer, and `enable()` passes that on. With no AIS key the poll answers `false`, so `setEnabled` reported the layer as not turned on and the Street Level browser gate failed (`ais-live-vessels failed to turn on or off`).

The live load resolves with nothing again; going back to live reads the answer through a separate internal poll. A new test turns vessels on and off with a failing feed and fails without the fix. Vessels, time and AIS suites pass (265/265).

title: feat(turbulence): add a keyless Turbulence layer from NOAA AWC
body: ## What this changes Adds a keyless **Turbulence** layer to the Weather group, built from the NOAA Aviation Weather Center Data API: - **G-AIRMET turbulence forecasts:** contiguous US, TURB-HI and TURB-LO, five snapshots 3 h apart. Drawn as translucent 3D volumes from each area's floor to its top, coloured by severity. - **SIGMETs for turbulence and mountain waves:** worldwide, drawn as volumes for the period they are in force. - **Pilot reports of light or stronger turbulence:** from the 3 hours before the time shown, drawn as points at their flight level. The layer follows the world timeline. It shows the forecast snapshot nearest the time shown, the SIGMETs in force at that time, and the recent reports. Clicking the map inside a volume, or clicking a report, opens a card. The card ends "Informational only · not for flight planning". It also fixes the Cesium draw adapter. Absolute (non-clamped) shapes in a `pickable: false` set were still built pickable. As a result, the translucent volumes blocked clicks on aircraft, satellites and other layers' items under them. That fix is its own commit, with a test. There is no existing issue for turbulence. #1568 notes that the app has no aviation weather yet. ## How I verified it - [x] `npm run build` - [x] `npm test`: 14,509 tests in 1,221 files (run in batches, see the note below). 14,460 pass, and none of the failures is new. The 35 that fail are the same 35 that fail on unmodified upstream `main` on this Windows machine, before any of these changes: - `pinokioUpdatePreview` ×18 - `render/unboundCamera` ×10 - `render/contract` ×4 - `render/cesium/internals`, `queries/heights` and `data/inputOwnership`, one each None of them is in a file this PR touches. - [x] `npm run test:track` (dev server running): 92 passed, 9 failed, 6 skipped. That is **identical** to unmodified upstream `main` run the same way on this machine (a separate worktree and dev server): the same 9 failures, all in flight tracking (`H1` model pick id, the two `arrival` timings at about 505–535 ms against 500 ms, and the six `display-floor` checks). None of them involves turbulence. - [x] Feature gate for the area I touched: - `node scripts/qa-layer-panel.mjs`: 0 failures. - `node scripts/qa-weather-journey.mjs`: completes all 19 steps, exit 0. Its `!! chip … missing` notes are about Wind, Radar and Satellite chips, which this PR doesn't change. - `node scripts/qa-weather-teardown.mjs` (with `weather-turbulence` added to its `WEATHER` list): the only difference after teardown is `primitives` 1 → 4. On unmodified `main` the same script gives 0 → 3, so it fails there too, with the same three leftover primitives. Turbulence disposes every draw set when turned off (`fix(turbulence): leave no draw set behind…`, with a test); before that commit it added two more. Also passing: `npm run format:check`, `npm run check:boundaries`, `npm run i18n` (all 13 locales; zh-Hant generated with `--zh-hant`), `npm run layer-token:check -- --base-ref origin/main`, `npm run library:check -- --base-ref origin/main`, `npm run changelog:check` and `npm run doctor -- --json`. Checked by hand against live NOAA data: - `/api/turbulence` returned 34 forecast areas across five forecast hours, 47 SIGMETs and about 260 pilot reports. - The layer turns on from the panel and from a share link (`l=03`). - A click inside a volume opens its card. - Scrubbing to +6 h swaps the forecast hour without rebuilding draw sets. - Report dots stay whole when zoomed far out. - There were no console errors. **Note on Windows:** `npm test` fails before any test runs there (`spawnSync … ENAMETOOLONG`). It passes all ~1,200 test files to one `node` process, which exceeds Windows' 32,767-character command-line limit. I ran the same plan in batches of 150: the same `discoverUnitTestFiles` and `buildUnitTestPlan`, the same flags, and the allocation probes on their own. Happy to open a separate issue or PR for the runner. ## New layer checklist **Screenshots** **Proposed category** Category: **Weather**. It sits after Cyclone advisories, and its card is in the Weather panel. **Data source and licence** - **Source (provider and endpoint):** the NOAA/NWS Aviation Weather Center Data API, all GeoJSON: - `https://aviationweather.gov/api/data/gairmet` (`product=tango`, `fore` 0, 3, 6, 9 and 12) - `/api/data/sigmet` - `/api/data/pirep` (worldwide box, `age=3`, `inten=lgt`) - **Licence or terms:** U.S. government work; [NWS public-data terms](https://www.weather.gov/disclaimer). No endorsement is implied. - **Attribution shown in the app:** "Turbulence: NOAA/NWS Aviation Weather Center · G-AIRMETs (US), SIGMETs and pilot reports. Informational only, not for flight planning." - **Needs a key?** None. - **Fetched at runtime, or bundled in the repo:** fetched at runtime through `/api/turbulence`. Only trimmed test fixtures are bundled (`src/layers/turbulence/awc.fixture.mjs`, public domain). - [x] Added a row to `DATA_SOURCES.md`, plus a "Weather: Turbulence (NOAA AWC)" subsection - [x] Credit is registered in `src/data/dataCredits.js` - [x] Share-link token assigned with `npm run layer-token:next`, if the layer is shareable (`03`, `enabled-only`) ## Docs - [x] `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md` updated and a `changelog.d/-.md` fragment added, or this PR doesn't change runtime behaviour. The fragment is `changelog.d/1791-turbulence-layer.md`. `SECURITY.md` (the proxy and the keyless route) and `README.md` (layer table and keyless list) are updated too. I left README's "Twenty-three layers" sentence as it is, because `transitQa.test.mjs` pins it. ## Notes for reviewers **Proxy.** `/api/turbulence` takes no parameters. It sends seven fixed requests, one after another, at most once every 10 minutes for all viewers together, well inside AWC's 100 a minute. It caps every body and normalizes records server-side (`records.js`, shared with the client). Each feed falls back to its last good copy, marked stale, for up to 6 hours, and the response flags `partial` or `unavailable`. A cold refresh takes about 20 s. The client source waits 45 s. **Rendering.** - Each forecast hour is its own `draw.shapes` set, built once per refresh. Every extruded item is a synchronous Cesium Primitive, so a scrub only flips `set.show`. - Warnings are rebuilt only when the set in force changes. - Volumes are `pickable: false`. A surface click is tested against the polygons (`pointInPolygon`, holes skipped, longitudes unwrapped across the antimeridian). - Report points are drawn over depth and culled at the horizon, like cyclone and fire points. - Every draw set is made when it first has something to draw and disposed when the layer is turned off. - Surface floors are buried 300 m below the ellipsoid, so they don't hover over coastal 3D tiles. **Time.** The layer `hold`s the world clock and registers coverage; it adds no marks. A cheap selection key (binary searches) means a playing timeline redraws only when what is shown changes. **Scope choices.** - Voice is off (`VOICE_OFF_LAYERS`), because the Realtime prompt is at its budget. - Filters stay local; the share link records only whether the layer is on. - There is no context-panel record; the layer has its own click card. **Known limits.** - Forecasts cover the contiguous US only. - A volume is hidden while the camera is inside it (closed geometry culls back faces). - This is not the gridded WAFS EDR forecast, which needs an aviation account. **AI assistance:** written with Claude (Anthropic). The commits carry a `Co-Authored-By` line. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: draw.models.parts: wait for frames while a part spins
body: The parts check added in #1788 waited for a settled scene while a part was spinning. A spinning part asks for frames for as long as it spins, so the wait timed out (`settled (redraw): expected "settled", got "timeout"`) and failed the Street Level browser gate on main. The spin step now waits for three drawn frames instead; the next step stops the spin and waits for the scene to settle as before.

title: Panels show the reported ground speed while a placement waits
body: A placed aircraft can wait in place while its next report catches up, so its placement speed is 0. `displayedKinematics` preferred the placement speed, so the flights and military panels showed 0 m/s for an aircraft flying at speed. With `derivedFromPlacement` it now prefers the reported ground speed and falls back to the placement's only when nothing is reported; motion and dead reckoning still use the placement. A new civil and military test has a placement waiting at 0 while the panel reads 100 m/s. Flights, military, vessels, time and data suites pass.

title: Tracked and emergency aircraft models keep their paint instead of turning black
body:
Aircraft models multiplied their tint into the lit paint (`colorBlend` 'highlight'). The tracked tint is pure cyan, with no red, so a red helicopter followed in cyan drew black (about 0, 0.09, 0.1) and a white Cessna flat cyan. Cesium applies the model colour after lighting, so no light could bring it back.

Tracked and emergency tints now mix in at 30% (`AIRCRAFT_MODEL_TINT_MIX`) instead of multiplying. White still draws the model's own colours, and the IR boost stays flat white. A red model followed in cyan reads grey-brown rather than red.

Night alone was not the cause: an untinted red EC145 with the sun at −32° draws dark red under the default ambient light, and the multi-part models and the part shader render the same pixels as before.

Tests: a new conformance check, `draw.models.paint`, renders a red vertex-painted model under a fixed sun (221,42,42 by day, 139,15,15 at night) and fails with red 0 when a cyan tint multiplies. New unit tests keep every paint under every tracked and emergency tint. The unit suite (14,537), the 8 model conformance checks, boundaries and format checks pass.

title: The followed aircraft's trail runs to where the aircraft is drawn
body:
When an application places live contacts itself (the placement interface added in 6f830a2e7), the followed aircraft is drawn at the placement's time, but its trail was still cut at the flights layer's own delayed clock (now minus `displayDelayMs`). That clock can run minutes behind, so:

- the trail body ended tens of kilometres behind the drawn aircraft, joined to it by nothing or by a long straight line;
- for the whole delay after a contact was first seen, the warm-up gate dropped the trail's head, leaving only an old segment far behind.

Now, when the tracked aircraft is placed, the trail reads the aircraft's time off its own reports at the drawn position (`trailTimeAt`, `src/data/trailContinuity.js`) and uses it for the body cut, the head curve and the warm-up gate, in Flights and Military Flights. Without a placement nothing changes.

Tests: new cases in `src/layers/flights/trail.test.mjs` and `src/layers/military/trail.test.mjs` (time between, on, after and before reports, never across a break; a placed aircraft ahead of the layer's delay gets a body plus a head to the aircraft during warm-up; a placed aircraft behind the delay gets no trail ahead of it). Full unit suite passes.

title: Civil aircraft take their class and model from the feed's type on the first fix
body:
State-vector snapshots carry no aircraft type, so every civil contact drew as an airliner until its per-aircraft type lookup returned, and the lookups run under a small budget: most helicopters, light aircraft and business jets kept the airliner icon and model for as long as they were in view.

A snapshot may now send `typeByIcao` (`{hex: 'EC45'}`) next to its state vectors, as it already sends `emergencyByIcao`. The flights layer classifies and picks the model from that type on the first fix; a looked-up type replaces it from then on, and the lookup still runs to fill the type name and registration. Surface categories still accept only ZVEH and GRND from a feed. The adsb.lol fallback sends `typeByIcao` too.

Tests: a helicopter type in the feed classes as a helicopter from the first fix, and a lookup overrides it. Flights, military, data and sources suites, boundaries and format checks pass.

title: Selecting a contact never recolours it
body:
Selecting or tracking a contact no longer recolours it. It keeps the colour it has unselected, and selection shows through the brackets, the label and card, the tracked billboard's larger size, the selected trail and (for satellites) the orbit ring.

- **Flights / Military Flights 3D models:** the tracked aircraft's model no longer mixes cyan or amber into its mesh; it draws its own paint, or emergency red (`src/layers/flights/rendering.js`, `src/layers/military/rendering.js`).
- **Flights / Military Flights icons:** the tracked icon keeps the contact's fleet colour (white, emergency red, airport-vehicle orange, military amber); only its alpha changes while stale or while its model draws it (`trackedIconColor`, `src/data/trackedAircraftIcon.js`, one frozen array per colour and alpha).
- **Vessels and aids to navigation:** a selected one keeps its type colour instead of turning white.
- **Satellites:** the tracked dot takes the satellite's own colour instead of always yellow; it keeps its size, outline and depth.
- A tracked aircraft in an emergency now stays red (tracking used to override it).

Docs (`docs/CURRENT-STATE.md`) and tests updated: the tracked model and icon colours match the fleet's, a selected vessel keeps its colour, the tracked satellite dot keeps its class colour. `npm test`, `format:check`, `check:boundaries`, `changelog:check` and `vite build` pass.

title: Pin the clock in the weather panel's identical-updates test
body: The panel shows each frame's age in whole minutes from the wall clock. When the test's two identical updates fell on either side of a minute (more likely on a loaded machine), six age lines were rightly rewritten and `f.writes()` read 6, not 0. The test now pins `Date` as the other tests in the file do. Checked: with the clock moved one minute between the updates the panel writes exactly 6 lines; with it pinned, 0. Test-only change.

title: Airport vehicles and ground stations must behave as such
body:
A feed's ground types were trusted whatever the contact did. Seen in one live snapshot: two ZVEH contacts on the ground at 77 and 85 m/s drew as cars driving at airliner speed, a ZVEH at 762 m (a drone) drew as a car in the air, and a GRND station reporting 11,880 m drew as a radio mast in the sky.

- `ZVEH` now holds only for a contact that drives: reported on the ground (or with no altitude) and no faster than 40 m/s (`VEHICLE_MAX_SPEED_MPS`). Otherwise the contact is classed as any other aircraft.
- A `GRND` station is fixed: its reported heights are ignored, so it stands on the ground.

Tests cover the fast vehicle, the airborne one and the high station; the vehicle fixtures now report themselves on the ground at a vehicle's speed (the shared fixture defaults to 1,000 m at 120 m/s). Flights, local ADS-B, data and sources suites (3,935), boundaries and format checks pass.

title: Hand the host's live placement the ground under each aircraft
body:
A host's live placement judges a landing by height above the ground, and the drawn height alone does not give it at a high airport (Denver's runways are at about 1,656 m).

The flights records now keep `groundM`: the ground the warm cache already reads, in the render height's reference: the surface a grounded contact stands on, and the floor under a low airborne contact (below `GROUND_FLOOR_WARM_MAX_ALT_M`) near the view or tracked. `observeLiveAircraft` passes it as `groundM`, NaN where the layer does not know it. No new reads or fetches: it is the value the floor clamp already used.

Tests: a low contact near the view carries its ground, one at cruise or away from the view carries none, and the placement is told it (NaN when unknown). Flights, military and data suites (3,767), boundaries and format checks pass.

title: The title logo goes back to live at the starting view
body:
The logo in the title was only a picture: clicking it did nothing, and there was no one-click way back to live time and the opening view.

- The logo is now a button, "Back to live at the starting view". The world clock goes live and the camera flies to the view the app started from, letting go of whatever it follows as Reset Globe does (`returnToStart()` on the shell, answered through the globe actions store).
- `createApplicationControls` takes `homeView`, where the logo goes; it is the start view unless given, for an application whose `startView` only carries a view across a rebuild. `START_VIEW` is exported from `./application/controls`.
- `flyToGlobeView` and `resetToGlobeView` take an optional view to fly to instead of zooming out over the current spot; called as before they behave as before.
- The title heading keeps "GOD'S EYE VIEW" as its name beside the button. The new message is in every locale.

Checked in headless Chromium against a dev server: from 13.41, 103.81 at 32 km, three hours in the past, a click on the logo ended at 35, −82.5, 23,000 km, live. The full unit suite passes.

title: Bike Share marks its covered cities on the globe
body:
Above the height stations draw at, Bike Share only said "Fly below 48 km to a covered city": nothing showed which cities those are.

- Every system in the registry now has a marker there: a green, white-ringed dot over its city, 5 km up so terrain never hides it while the globe still hides the ones behind it. The markers show only while the layer is on and stations are not drawn, and belong to the layer for picking.
- Clicking a marker flies straight down into its city from 20 km, as an explicit camera action through the shell's `runNavigation` (`attachShellServices`), like News and the weather layers.

Tests cover the markers' show and hide across the activation height and the layer's on/off, pick ownership, and the click's flight. Checked in headless Chromium against a dev server: at 6,000 km over the US east coast with Bike Share on, a click on Boston's marker (picked through the scene) flew to 42.3601, −71.0589 at 20 km, where the layer starts loading Boston's stations. The bike share suite (62) passes.

title: Go to a shot by clicking it; move shots up and down
body:
The shot list's LOAD button is removed: going to a shot is what clicking it does.

- **Click to go:** clicking anywhere on a shot row (its title or its summary line) selects the shot and moves the view to it (its look, layers and camera), as LOAD did. The title is focusable (`role="button"`), so Enter or Space does the same. Double-click still renames.
- **Move up / move down:** in LOAD's place, two compact buttons swap the shot with its neighbour (disabled at the ends). `director.moveShot(sceneId, shotId, index)` keeps the index in range, refuses while the scene plays, saves, and publishes `shot-moved`. The row's other buttons never trigger the move.
- Locales: new "Move up", "Move down", the title's label and the panel hint in all 13 catalogs; the unused "LOAD" and old hint are removed. `arrow_upward` / `arrow_downward` added to the Material Symbols subset.

Tests in `src/scenes/director.test.mjs` and `src/ui/sceneControls.test.mjs`; `npm test`, `format:check`, `check:boundaries` and `i18n` pass. Docs: `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md`.

title: Export route steps from sources/places
body:
The Directions layer asks `/api/route` for turn-by-turn steps (`steps=1`). Core's dev server projects them with `normalizeOsrmSteps`, but that function is not part of any package entry, so a route proxy built on `gods-eye-view/sources/places` can serve the route line but not its steps.

- `sources/places` re-exports `normalizeOsrmSteps` (`src/data/routeSteps.js`).
- The boundary entry lists `routeSteps.js` and `distanceFormat.js`; neither imports Node.
- Test: the entry's export is the same function the dev proxy uses.
- Docs: CODE-BOUNDARIES; changelog fragment.

title: Name the world timeline's real-time speed Real-time
body:
The world timeline's speed control labelled its real-time speed `1×`, beside `1 min/s`, `1 h/s`, `1 d/s` and `1 wk/s`. It now reads **Real-time** (`t('Real-time')`, `src/ui/views/panels/WorldTimeline.vue`), translated in every catalog (zh-Hant generated from zh-CN).

`npm test`, `format:check` and `npm run i18n` pass.

title: Hand the application the renderer's own engine
body:
An application sometimes needs to draw with a renderer's own engine beside the contract (effects the contract has no port for). Until now the only way to reach Cesium's viewer was the QA scripts' handle.

`ApplicationHooks` gains `engine`: the renderer's own engine, whose `kind` names it. Cesium's plugin hands `{kind: 'cesium', viewer}`. An application draws only with engines whose kind it knows, and what it draws there is its own to add, update and remove. Nothing changes for a renderer without it, and the contract itself is unchanged.

Documented in `src/render/applicationHooks.js`, `contract/renderer.d.ts` and `docs/RENDERER-CONTRACT.md`; `appRenderer.test.mjs` checks the hook. Render tests, boundaries and format pass.

title: Serve the Data Library from any server, and let a server shape it
body:
## What

- **The library proxy as a fetch handler.** `createLibraryHandler` (`src/library/proxy.js`, exported as `sources/library`) answers `/catalog`, `/data/<id>`, `/tile/<id>/<z>/<x>/<y>` and `/index/<id>` as a `Request` in, `Response` out, so any server can mount it. The dev server's `libraryProxy` now wraps it behind the same same-site gates and rate limits; its behaviour is unchanged apart from cache headers.
- **A server can hide catalog entries or route them through its proxy.** `listed(entry)` false marks an entry `listed: false` in `/catalog`; Browse leaves it out entirely and no route serves it. `proxied(entry)` true marks a browser-direct entry `fetch: "proxied"`, and the browser then asks the server for its tiles and data.
- **View-bounded entries through the proxy.** A routed view-bounded entry asks `/data/<id>?bbox=…` for the camera's box snapped out to a power-of-two grid (`libraryViewBox`), so nearby views share one answer; any other box is refused (`parseLibraryViewBox`). ArcGIS queries the box; partitioned GeoParquet is read on the server with the browser's own reader.
- **Cacheable answers.** Tile, data and complete index answers carry `public, max-age=<cacheSeconds>` (`private` for a keyed entry). `keep: false` keeps nothing in process memory, for a server with a shared cache in front.
- **An application's own fetches.** `createApplicationTools({ library: { fetchTile, fetchData } })`: `fetchTile` becomes the library imagery spec's `fetchTile` (told which entry asks), `fetchData` answers proxied dataset URLs, so an application can keep library tiles and datasets in its own cache.
- **Fail closed when asked.** `createApplicationTools({ library: { requireCatalog: true } })` makes the server's `/catalog` an allowlist: only what it names is offered, and while it does not answer (an error status, 429, a timeout, a page that is not the catalog) nothing is offered and nothing is loaded from a publisher. The controller asks again after 30 s, doubling up to 10 min, and restores the viewer's saved entries once it answers.
- **One spelling per resource.** Tile paths need integer z/x/y without leading zeros, `x`/`y` below `2^z`, `z` within the entry's zoom range; empty segments and trailing slashes are refused; a view box is accepted only in `libraryViewBox`'s exact spelling. A shared cache keyed on the path holds each answer once.
- **Bounded partitioned reads.** `partitionCache` lets a host cap decoded GeoParquet partitions per process (four); `fetchIndex` reads a partition index from the handler's own (cacheable) `/index/<id>`, and a `/data` request never builds one (503 `index_unavailable` without it); `subrequestLimit` refuses a request with 503 `subrequest_limit` before it would pass a host's per-request upstream limit.
- `createLibrarySource` no longer reads `localStorage` itself; the controller passes the page's storage, which keeps `sources/library` free of browser globals.

## Checks

- Library and application tests (`src/library`, `src/app`): 249 passed, 0 failed; the full `npm test` passed (14,590) before this round.
- `npm run check:boundaries` (new `library-proxy` group) and `npm run format:check` pass; `npm run library:check` passes.
- New tests: `src/library/proxy.test.mjs` (hidden entries, routing, view boxes, tile path spelling, index and subrequest limits), `src/library/source.test.mjs`, and controller tests for hidden entries and a required catalog that fails then answers; the existing `server/providers/library.test.mjs` passes unchanged.

title: CCTV clustering
body: ## What this changes Zoomed out, the CCTV layer keeps one camera per ground cell (#1485) and drew that camera as an ordinary icon. Nothing showed whether 2 or 1,200 other cameras sat behind it, so you could not see where coverage is or where to zoom. A cell with two or more cameras is now one round marker with a small camera icon and the count inside. - **No zoom threshold.** The existing cell hierarchy is the hierarchy: each halving of the distance splits a cell into four, from one number per region at globe scale down to individual cameras below about 1.2 km. - **Stable counts.** The count covers the whole cell, not only its on-screen part, so a number does not change while the cell crosses the screen edge. Cameras beyond the horizon are not counted. - **No overlap, no lost cameras.** Markers that would overlap on screen merge into one that carries their sum. A lone camera whose icon would sit within 4 px of a marker is counted in that marker instead of poking out beside it. - **Click zooms in.** Clicking a marker frames its group until it splits. It does not choose a camera: an explicit pick stays active, and the opening camera keeps following the view as after any other move. - **Says what it counts, and how much.** The marker grows with the count, from 40 px for two cameras to 58 px for several thousand. Thousands print as `1.7K` or `12K` in every UI language. The camera layer is green: count markers and idle single cameras share the colour, the active camera stays gold and live-video cameras violet. - **Sharp on high-density displays.** Markers are painted on the world overlay canvas, at the same resolution and in the same typeface as the camera callouts. The scene itself renders at CSS resolution, so a sprite there looked coarse next to them. - Single cameras and the active camera keep their icons. Ambient cards and coverage attach only to cameras drawn as icons. The camera picker keeps one representative per visible cell, as before. - No new UI strings. Europe from 4,000 km: London from 25 km: ## Look of the marker: how it was decided The pictures are in the order they were made; under each one is what we chose. Steps 1, 5, 8, 9, 10 and 11 are real captures, the rest are mockups. **1. First version: a bare count in the layer's cyan.** Europe from 4,000 km, London from 25 km. Outcome: this was the first pushed version. A bare number does not say what is being counted, and cyan is shared with labels, HUD chrome and the ALPR layer. The marker should also grow with the count. **2. Where a camera glyph sits.** Four placements. Chosen: **A**, the glyph inside the marker above the number. The marker grows by about 12 px to hold it and scales with the count, 40 to 58 px. **3. Layer colour.** Five options. Chosen: **the fourth, green `#5dff8f`**. Single idle cameras take the same green; the active camera stays gold and live-video cameras stay violet. **4. Which glyph.** Five treatments of the Data Layers list icon and two drawn pictograms. Chosen: first **5**, the flat green silhouette; built, it read as a blob at marker size. Then **7**, the icon a single camera has on the map, so a group reads as many of the same thing. **5. As built after step 4** (an intermediate build, never pushed): the single-camera icon in green, 12 to 16 px tall, 2 px above the number. Outcome: the icon is too large and sits tight against the number. Steps 6 and 7 fix that. **6. Icon size and place.** Five sizes, from half size (6 to 8 px tall) to full size (12 to 16 px), each in two placements: A, centred in the space above the number; B, near the top of the circle. Chosen: **B2**, the icon 7.5 to 10 px tall near the top of the circle. **7. Number position.** With the icon fixed at B2, five heights for the number: from the exact centre of the circle (1) down to where it is now, 40% of the inner radius below the centre (5). The gap is the clear distance between the icon and the number. Chosen: **3**, the middle of the digits 20% of the inner radius below the centre. **8. As built after steps 6 and 7** (pushed): the icon 7.5 to 10 px tall under the top of the ring, the number just below the centre. Small markers are now true circles, because the small icon no longer forces extra width. Outcome: pushed; the two screenshots at the top show it in full. **9. A lone camera beside a count marker.** A cell with one camera always drew its icon, so at some zooms a camera poked out from under a count marker with its own callout. Now an icon closer than 4 px to a marker joins that marker and the count grows by one. Two lone cameras with no count beside them stay two icons, and the active camera always keeps its own icon. Outcome: pushed. **10. A marker over cameras with stale heights.** Reported at OR140 at the Nevada state line: the "2" drifted across the map while zooming, and a click flew the view into the ground. Cause: a marker stood at its cameras' mean height, and cameras behind a marker never enter the view, so when the terrain height service is rate-limited they keep the catalog height (4 m there, with the terrain at 1,872 m). Now, on a globe map, a marker takes its height from the drawn terrain and a click frames that ground. Outcome: pushed together with step 11. It fixed the marker only; the cameras themselves still held the stale height, which step 11 deals with. **11. Cameras with stale heights, and cameras on one mount.** A second recording at the same place showed five things: the count vanished in a tilted view; a click on it opened nothing; zoomed in by hand there was one icon with two callouts; and the icons drifted with every tilt and pan. Four of them had one cause: the two cameras held a height of 4 m under terrain at 1,872 m (the height service answered 429, which leaves a geoid fallback), and the view pass decided "is it on screen" and "how far is it" from that point. Now a camera the height batch never answered for takes the terrain the globe draws under it, once it is near the screen; a later batch answer replaces it. The fifth: cameras on one mount draw side by side, 30 px apart, each with its own callout. Outcome: pushed. Still open: on the photoreal map stack terrain is not the surface, so cameras there are not corrected this way; and the height batch itself still loses chunks to the rate limit. ## Related: #1530 #1530 also changes how CCTV icons thin out at wide zooms. This PR does not build on it, for three reasons: - **It hides cameras without saying so.** It makes icons sparser with altitude and caps them (160 at 25 km, down to 20 at 2,000 km). An icon past the cap is dropped, so the map shows less coverage than there is. The aim here is the opposite: every camera stays accounted for, in a number. - **Its overlap pass drops; this one merges.** #1530 removes an icon that sits too close to another on screen. With counts, an overlapping marker has to merge into its neighbour and carry the sum, or cameras go missing from the totals. - **The thinning cannot be taken on its own.** It ships together with a statewide PennDOT source, fragmented-MP4 relay support, a catalog budget raised from 4,000 to 12,000, and a new layer row with its share token (76 files), and it currently conflicts with `main`. Both change the same view pass in `src/layers/cctv/rendering.js`. If #1530 lands after this one, its icon cap and overlap pass will need to merge cells instead of dropping them. ## How I verified it - [x] `npm run build`, keyless - [x] `npm test` at head b322ac1df (fresh `main` merged in): 15,472 pass, 0 fail, 3 skipped. Keyless build, `format:check`, `check:boundaries` and `layer-token:check` pass. - [ ] `npm run test:track` (not run) - [x] CCTV and world overlay tests, including the allocation budgets: 731 pass. - [x] `npm run format:check`, `npm run check:boundaries` - [x] Headless Chrome at device pixel ratio 2, keyless, against the live catalog (7,350 cameras): globe, continent, city and tilted views, English and Russian UI. No page errors. Clicking a 250-camera marker from 4,000 km lands at 25 km with the group split. - [x] The same headless run at OR140 at the Nevada state line while the terrain height service answered 429: the two cameras stand on the drawn terrain (1,872 m) instead of at 4 m, a tilted view keeps the "2" on its ground point, and a click opens both cameras 30 px apart with a callout each. No page errors. - [x] After the review fixes (head 81fe7f88c), the same OR140 run again: the "2" keeps its ground point in a tilted view, a click opens both cameras 30 px apart with a callout each, the icons stay apart after the view settles, and the marker draws the same as before. No page errors. - [x] After merging the fresh `main` (head 2b7a6b0c6): the same OR140 run gives the same result, with no page errors. - [x] After the second round of review fixes (head f6982dc93): the OR140 run again, including the click on the "2": both cameras open 30 px apart, no page errors. - Feature gate: none applies.

title: Let an application ask the library catalog with its own fetch
body:
createApplicationTools({ library }) took tile and dataset fetches but not the fetch the library source uses for its catalog, so an application whose server wants its own credentials on library routes had its catalog refused, and with requireCatalog nothing was offered.

- library.fetchImpl is passed through createDataLibrary to createLibrarySource; without it the page's fetch is used as before.
- Test: the catalog is asked through the given fetch and its entries are offered.

title: fix(vessels): vessels on lakes and rivers sit on the water, not at sea level
body:
## What this changes

AIS vessels were always drawn at sea level (the EGM96 geoid). On lakes, rivers and locked docks that puts them under the visible water by the water's own height: about 27 m under the Seine in Paris, 75 m under Lake Ontario, 176 m under Lake Michigan. Below sea level (the Caspian) they float. This is the same on Google 3D tiles and on terrain, since both draw the real water height. Ship models there were hidden under the surface at every camera angle, and their icons were hidden too while the model "owned" the visual.

Vessels now sit on the water they are on:

- **Water level from the terrain service.** A new `src/layers/vessels/waterSurface.js` reads the terrain cache (Re:Earth via `/api/terrain/heights`) for each vessel's 0.001° cell. The vessel's own cell comes first. The eight cells around it are fetched only when that cell is 4.5 m or more from sea level, since at sea they cannot change the answer.
- **The rule.** The level is the lowest height another cell confirms within 1 m: the terrain flattens water, so a lone low cell (a lock chamber, a hole in the data) is not the water. It is used when it is at least 4.5 m above sea level, as the service gives it (its own `elevation`, which avoids the bundled geoid's ±1–2 m difference from the service's). It is used below sea level only when the vessel's own cell is too, three cells agree, and it is no lower than −450 m. Otherwise the vessel stays on the geoid, so the sea is unchanged.
- **Calibration.** The threshold was checked against 495 live AIS positions and 60 placed points. Open and tidal water around ports reads −3…+4 m. The lowest raised water seen, the Seattle ship canal and Liverpool's impounded docks, reads 4.8–5 m. Lakes and rivers come out at their published levels: Superior 183.5 m, Huron 176.3, Ontario 74.6–75.5, the Seine in Paris 26.8, the Rhine at Duisburg 22.8–25, the Caspian −28, the Dead Sea −432.
- **When terrain is fetched.** After each poll, while the camera is at most 60 km up, for up to 120 vessels nearest the view. Each vessel contributes where it is reported, where it is drawn, and two minutes ahead on its course. That is at most 512 cells a poll and 768 a minute (twelve proxy requests a minute, against the proxy's 90 per client). Batches of up to 256 cells, four proxy requests, run one at a time. A cell the service did not answer rests a minute. Leaving a view drops its queued cells; turning the layer off cancels everything.
- **Everything that draws a vessel follows.** Icons, ship-model waterlines, the selected trail and the Cockpit bridge's `markHeightM` move onto a level as it arrives. A vessel drawn over cells not fetched yet keeps the level last read for it, within 5 km. The trail asks for up to 128 of its samples' cells, spread along it, and a vertex not known yet takes the nearest known one's water.
- **Flat globe.** When the shown globe is the bare ellipsoid, because terrain did not load or an install has none, every vessel is drawn at height 0, where that globe draws the sea. It used to sit at the geoid, up to tens of metres above or below. This uses the same detection the Transit layer uses. The photoreal stack hides the globe and is never treated as flat.
- **Cockpit bridge.** Its floor (`seaSurfaceHeightM`) is the geoid, or the water the ship is drawn on where that lies lower (a flat globe, the Caspian). Raised water above it the bridge still reads off the scene itself, as before.
- **Terrain heights service.** `terrainHeights` now keeps the service's `elevation` with each real entry and exposes `cachedRealOrthometricGround`. The resolver's answers and every other consumer are unchanged.

## How I verified it

- [x] `npm run build`
- [x] `npm test`: everything passes except 17 renderer-contract tests (`unboundCamera`, `contract`, `internals`, `heights`, `inputOwnership`) that fail the same way on a clean `main` checkout on Windows. On Windows `npm test` itself hits ENAMETOOLONG, so I ran the same files with `node --import=./build/registerVue.js --test "src/**/*.test.mjs" "server/**/*.test.mjs"`.
- [x] `npm run test:track` (dev server running): same result as a clean `main` checkout on the same machine. Both fail the same seven checks: two arrival timings just over 500 ms, and five `display-floor` checks ("tracked exit model identity changed").
- [x] `format:check`, `check:boundaries`
- [x] In the app, live AIS on Google 3D tiles and on Esri imagery with terrain. Vessel waterline against the drawn surface:
  - Seine (Paris): 27 m under → within about 1 m
  - Lake Union (Seattle): 4.4 m under → within about 1 m
  - Lake Ontario (Toronto): 75 m under → within about 1 m
  - Lake Michigan (Chicago): 176 m under → at lake level, including vessels 17 km out in a tilted view
  - Rotterdam: unchanged
  - Moving Rhine barges stay on the river between polls
  - Terrain swapped for the bare ellipsoid: every vessel at 0 + 3 m within a second, and back when terrain returned

New tests cover the level rule on real cases, the two-stage fetch, list replacement and cancellation, the per-poll and per-minute budgets, failed cells, the stand-in, the trail fill, the flat-globe switch, the app wiring, and a layer-level poll that moves a lake vessel onto the lake.

## Known limits and follow-ups

- **Under Google 3D tiles a river can be drawn a few metres off the terrain's level.** On the Rhine at Duisburg vessels sit 1.5–3 m above the photographed water. Each source captured the river at a different stage. Tidal harbours (Hamburg) are the same against the geoid. A follow-up can read the drawn water around vessels whose 3D model is drawn, from tiles already loaded.
- Narrow canals and quays beside sea berths can read a few metres high, since the terrain's ~100 m cells do not resolve them.
- The terrain must be the water's surface, as Re:Earth's is. A source with sea-floor depths could sink vessels over a flat harbour floor.
- The flat-globe check repeats the Transit layer's; a shared helper next to `heightsOf` would serve both. Vessels also keep their own request budget beside the other layers' ground floors, so one shared budget in `terrainHeights` would be the cleaner home.

## Docs

- [x] `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md` updated and a `changelog.d/<pr-number>-<slug>.md` fragment added

title: Add Proxmox LXC installer and trusted key-setup hosts for headless servers
body:
## What this changes

Adds scripts/proxmox-lxc.sh, which installs God's Eye View headless in an unprivileged Debian container on Proxmox VE: Node 24 from NodeSource, the app running as a non-root gods-eye-view systemd service on port 4173, service settings kept in /etc/gods-eye-view/service.env outside the checkout, and a gev-update command. docs/PROXMOX.md covers installing, browsing by name, keys, updates and removal.

On a headless server, Provider Settings (POWER UP) had no way to work. The gate requires a local Host (localhost, 127.0.0.1, ::1), and a container has no browser of its own: the operator's device always browses to the server by its LAN name or address. GEV_KEY_SETUP_TRUSTED_PEERS admits the device's address, but its Host is still refused with not-local-host.

This PR adds GEV_KEY_SETUP_TRUSTED_HOSTS, a list of exact names or addresses that count as local only for a request from a GEV_KEY_SETUP_TRUSTED_PEERS address:

Loopback requests are unchanged. They accept only the stock local names, whatever the list holds, so tunnel and DNS-rebinding traffic over loopback gains nothing.
Unlisted peers are refused before the list is read.
Suffix (.lan) and wildcard (*) entries are dropped, as in GEV_ALLOWED_HOSTS.
The sharing, proxy-header, exact-Origin and JSON Content-Type checks are unchanged. The Origin must equal the listed Host exactly.
Unset, behaviour is identical to today.

The panel cannot write the new variable (it is not in KEY_SETUP_KEYS).

Docs: docs/PROXMOX.md (new), a pointer in the README's "Running on Linux, a NAS, or behind a reverse proxy" section, a SECURITY.md threat-model bullet with the limits, .env.example, docs/CURRENT-STATE.md, and a changelog fragment.

How I verified it
[ ] npm run build: not run locally (no Node 24 available); CI runs it.
[ ] npm test: full suite not run locally; CI runs it. Run on Node 22 with no node_modules: src/keySetupCore.test.mjs (24/24), src/keySetupHardening.test.mjs (16 pass, 0 fail), src/dockerTrustedPeers.test.mjs (4/4), src/tooling/changelogFragments.test.mjs (17/17) and the other doc tests that read the edited files. Three doc tests could not load without vue/pinia installed; they fail the same way without this change.
[ ] npm run test:track: not run. This PR does not touch flight tracking or the client.
[x] Feature gate for the area I touched: no qa-*.mjs gate covers Provider Settings; the gate is covered by src/keySetupCore.test.mjs.

New assertions in src/keySetupCore.test.mjs cover: a listed peer on a listed name or IP is admitted; a listed peer on an unlisted name is refused (not-local-host); a listed host does not admit an unlisted peer (not-loopback); listed hosts never widen a loopback socket; the Origin must still match exactly; proxied requests and sharing still refuse; suffix and wildcard entries are ignored. Disabling the new code makes the suite fail.

scripts/proxmox-lxc.sh passes shellcheck -S warning. An earlier version of the same script has been run on a Proxmox VE cluster, together with an equivalent local gate patch, and Provider Settings worked from a listed iPad on the LAN.

Docs
[x] docs/CURRENT-STATE.md updated and a changelog.d/<pr-number>-<slug>.md fragment added (changelog.d/0000-proxmox-lxc-installer.md, to be renamed to this PR's number)

title: feat(cctv): opt-in BayernInfo (Bavaria) road webcam pack
body:
## What this changes

Adds an **opt-in, off-by-default** CCTV source pack for BayernInfo (VIZ-BY), the Bavarian Road Administration's traffic webcams: 432 Bavarian road cameras, each projected into the 3D scene like the other camera packs, with its real viewing bearing.

The pack makes **no request unless an operator sets `CCTV_BAYERN_ENABLED=1`**. BayernInfo publishes no reuse licence for the webcam images and documents the feed only through the Mobilithek (registration), so the reuse terms are unconfirmed — the same handling the repo already uses for Lithuania, NYC, Florida and Houston.

- **Catalog:** the public web-map list `map.bayerninfo.de/cam/listOfWebcamsV3.json` (keyless, one request, nested categories → roads → cameras).
- **Frames:** stills under `map.bayerninfo.de/cam/bi/`, refreshed about once a minute, fetched on demand and never stored.
- **Austria excluded:** the same list carries 552 Austrian ASFINAG cameras under `.../cam/asfinag/`; the loader keeps only the 432 Bavarian cameras (`.../cam/bi/`), and only that directory is registered as a frame origin.

## Why opt-in / off by default

The documented, licensed route for these images is the Mobilithek, which needs registration and (for most feeds) a data-usage agreement. The public web-map JSON is keyless but carries no stated reuse licence (the config's attribution field is empty), and the operator is the Bavarian Road Administration / Autobahn GmbH. Per `docs/CCTV_INTEGRATION.md` ("If access terms require an agreement or remain unconfirmed, make the pack opt-in and ensure it makes no request by default"), the pack is off until an operator confirms the terms and sets the flag. The cameras show traffic only — BayernInfo states they do not show faces or licence plates.

## Security (per CCTV_INTEGRATION.md / SECURITY.md)

- Frame URLs are pinned to `map.bayerninfo.de/cam/bi/` via `pinnedCameraUrl`; ASFINAG paths, `../` traversal, protocol-relative, absolute, root-absolute and `%2f`-encoded URLs are all rejected (unit-tested).
- Redirects are refused on the catalog fetch and, on the frame host, followed only within the pinned `cam/bi/` directory (unit-tested with `fetchWithinHost`).
- Catalog body capped (`BAYERN_MAX_CATALOG_BYTES`), request deadline set, coordinates validated, ids validated, duplicates deduped, pack capped (`DEFAULT_BAYERN_MAX_SOURCES`, 500). Partial/offline/oversized upstreams return `[]` rather than failing the merged catalog.
- Headings use the feed's numeric bearing at **low** confidence (corrected with the in-app gizmo); cameras without a usable bearing fall back to the shared id-hash heading.

## How I verified it

- [x] `npm run build`, `npm run format:check`, `npm run check:boundaries` all pass.
- [x] Focused gate `src/data/cctvBayern.test.mjs` (10 tests): normalisation, the real bearing, ASFINAG/traversal/off-origin rejection, bad id/coords, nested-group walk + dedupe, cap + sort, error/redirect/offline → `[]`, off-by-default (no request), `CCTV_BAYERN_ENABLED=1` wiring, and the frame-host redirect pin. Plus `cctvCatalogCap` and `cctvProxy` shared gates.
- [x] Runtime check with `CCTV_BAYERN_ENABLED=1`: `/api/cctv/sources` lists 432 Bavaria cameras, and `/api/cctv/frame/de-bayern-1434` returns `image/jpeg` with `X-CCTV-Source: upstream-image` (a real upstream frame, not a fallback).
- [x] Live loader run: 432 Bavarian cameras, every frame URL under `cam/bi/`, no ASFINAG, all with a real bearing.
- [ ] `npm test`: 7 pre-existing failures in `src/i18n/catalog.test.mjs` (the zh-Hant OpenCC `s2tw` conversion) that **also fail on unmodified `main`** in my sandbox and are unrelated to this change (it touches no i18n files); everything else passes.
- [ ] `npm run test:track`: not green in my sandbox (basemap/terrain hosts blocked; the same failures occur on unchanged `main`). Needs a run on an open network.

## Data source and licence

Fetched at runtime, nothing bundled, no key. Documented in `DATA_SOURCES.md` and `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md`, credited in `src/data/dataCredits.js`, flag in `.env.example`.

- Provider: BayernInfo / Bayerische Straßenbauverwaltung (VIZ-BY), `map.bayerninfo.de`.
- Licence: **no reuse licence published for the images**; documented route is the Mobilithek (registration). Pack off by default; enable only after confirming terms with the operator.
- Attribution shown: "Verkehrskameras: BayernInfo (Bayerische Straßenbauverwaltung)".

## Docs

title: An estimated aircraft position stands in on the trail only until the next received one
body:
Some aircraft feeds estimate positions out of receiver range: they carry the aircraft forward on its last course, then the next received position lands well off that line. Drawn into the tracked aircraft's trail, every such stretch became a straight run and a sharp jump back, a staircase across oceans.

A feed can now say which positions were estimated:
- a state-vector snapshot names those aircraft in `estimatedByIcao` (alongside `typeByIcao` and `emergencyByIcao`);
- a readsb-style row carries `estimated: true`.

Such a record is marked `estimated`. It still places the aircraft as before. On the tracked trail an estimated report stands in only until the next received report, which takes every estimated report out of the trail (`insertTrailFix` in `src/data/trailContinuity.js`), so the line runs between received positions. A received report that arrives late, older than the estimates, takes them out too. Feeds that send neither field behave exactly as before.

Tests: `src/data/trailReports.test.mjs` (an estimated report stands in only until the next received one, including a late received report) and `src/sources/live/contract.test.mjs` (only named aircraft are marked).

title: Make the fleet models, their handover and the vessel sprites a public entry point
Add a metric / imperial units switch (°C/°F, km/mi, m/ft, km/h/mph)
body:
What this changes

Adds a units switch to the bottom-right corner row, beside the language picker. It shows the system in use as °C or °F; one press switches the page, and the choice is kept for the next visit (gev:units:v1). Metric is the default, and metric text reads exactly as it did before: every converted site keeps its existing metric code path, and the full suite passes unchanged.

How it works

src/units.js holds the choice (getUnitSystem, setUnitSystem, onUnitSystemChange) and the conversion constants. It follows the locale's pattern: a plain value until src/ui/unitSystem.js binds it to a Vue ref in createUiRuntime, so any view that formats a quantity while rendering re-renders on a switch with no listener.
src/ui/unitLabels.js gains formatTemperature, formatDistance, formatRoadSpeed, formatHeight and formatPrecipitation, plus mi, mm and a context-keyed in label (unit of length|in, so it never collides with the preposition).
distanceParts / formatDistanceText (src/data/distanceFormat.js) give feet below 1,000 ft, then miles (one decimal below 10 mi), in the imperial system, so directions, awareness, annotation measurements and route steps follow it. A new largeOnly option keeps km/mi below one unit. system can be passed explicitly.
formatFact (src/data/entityContext.js) takes a system option.
UnitSystemToggle.vue wears the language button's HUD frame (same CSS rules, plus the cyber theme list). On phones it drops the ruler icon and keeps °C/°F.

What converts in imperial: weather in the context panel (temperature, feels-like, wind, visibility, rain, distances, radius); the wind layer's temperature legend and readings (°F), and its speed unit (mph) until a units chip is chosen; entity-card and view-context distances; entity facts (orbital altitude, road speed, depth, …Km and …M fields); HUD corner altitude, summary altitude, view window and locality distance; camera and satellite altitude graphs; satellite card altitude; cockpit contact distance, context radius, vessel eye height, briefing temperature and wind; voice result-card distances.

What deliberately does not: aviation and marine units (feet and knots for aircraft, knots and hPa for storms, NM on the cockpit radar, ft/min); imagery resolution in metres; readings written for AI tools (wind readings stay °C in data); share-link parameters. Text built outside Vue (cockpit briefing, a measurement label already drawn) picks up the new system the next time it is drawn.

Translations: the 10 new strings are translated in all 13 locales; zh-Hant is regenerated with npm run i18n -- --zh-hant, and unit labels identical to English are listed in same-as-english.json. npm run i18n reports every catalog complete.

src/data/distanceFormat.test.mjs: imperial feet/miles cut-offs and rounding, largeOnly, and metric output identical with system: 'metric'.

title: Let typed chat use a model server of your own (Ollama, LM Studio, vLLM)
body:
What this changes

Typed chat already speaks OpenAI's Chat Completions API with tool calls, which Ollama, LM Studio, vLLM and llama.cpp's server all answer too; the endpoint was hard-coded to api.openai.com. This adds two optional settings so an operator can keep typed chat on their own hardware:

OPENAI_CHAT_BASE_URL: an OpenAI-compatible base such as http://ollama.lan:11434/v1; chat posts to <base>/chat/completions. Only a plain http(s) URL without credentials, query or fragment is accepted. Anything else answers 503 and nothing is sent.
OPENAI_CHAT_API_KEY: a key for that server, if it wants one.

When a base URL is set:

OPENAI_API_KEY is never sent to it. It gets OPENAI_CHAT_API_KEY or the placeholder local. Without a base URL, OPENAI_CHAT_API_KEY can also give OpenAI chat a key of its own, and otherwise chat uses OPENAI_API_KEY as before.
GEV_PREFER_CODEX_OAUTH does not refuse it, since it bills nothing.
The request timeout is two minutes instead of one (createTextChatHandler now accepts a function for timeoutMs).
max_tokens is sent beside max_completion_tokens for servers that read only the older name.
A leading <think>…</think> block, which some local servers leave in thinking models' replies, is removed before the reply is shown or kept in history.

Neither setting is in Provider Settings' writable key list, so only whoever runs the server decides where chat goes. Voice and the HUD summary are unchanged: voice needs a realtime speech service these servers do not offer, and the HUD summary keeps OpenAI or its keyless fallback.

With no new settings, behaviour is identical: same endpoint, same key, same body, same 60-second timeout.

Docs: new docs/LOCAL-CHAT.md (settings, model choice: tool calling, Ollama's context length, GPU memory; reaching Ollama on another machine; troubleshooting), .env.example, README.md, docs/CURRENT-STATE.md, and a changelog fragment.

How I verified it
[x] npm run build
[x] npm test: 14,615 pass, 0 fail on Node 22 (the repo asks for 24, which CI uses). 42 tests in server/providers/news/keyed.test.mjs are cancelled under Node 22 with "Promise resolution is still pending"; the same 42 are cancelled on unmodified main, so they are unrelated.
[ ] npm run test:track: not run (needs Puppeteer's Chromium). This PR touches only the typed-chat server route.
[x] Feature gate for the area I touched: src/textChatServer.test.mjs (41 pass), plus npm run format:check and npm run i18n (no new UI strings).

New assertions in src/textChatServer.test.mjs:

chatEndpoint: the OpenAI default, trailing-slash and whitespace handling, and refusal of a bare host, file:, credentials, query and fragment.
chatApiKey: OpenAI keeps OPENAI_API_KEY or OPENAI_CHAT_API_KEY; a local server never receives OPENAI_API_KEY.
End to end against a stand-in Ollama /v1/chat/completions server: the request reaches /v1/chat/completions with the placeholder key, the configured model, max_tokens and the tools; the <think> block is stripped; the ChatGPT OAuth lock does not apply.
A malformed base URL answers 503 without any upstream request.

The existing OpenAI and Gemini chat tests pass unchanged.

title: Renderer contract: decoded imagery, finished tile images handed over by the application
body:
## What

A renderer can now draw timed imagery whose tiles the application makes itself and hands over as finished images.

- **Contract.** `TimedSource` gains `{ kind: 'decoded', slotAt, prefetch?, tile }` behind the new capability `imageryDecoded`. Its slots are times (epoch ms):
  - `slotAt(time)` names the slot a time shows, or `null` to show nothing;
  - `prefetch(time)` names the slots to hold ahead of it, nearest first;
  - `tile({ tile, slot, signal, urgency })` answers one tile of one slot with `{ image: ImageBitmap }`, `{ missing: true }` or `{ defer: true }`.
  It is set with `setFrames`, as frames and video are, and `frameReady` names the slot shown once it is drawn.
- **Cesium.** Each held slot is a Cesium imagery layer of its own, as a frame is (`src/render/cesium/imageryFrames.js`, `imagery.js`).
  - The `prefetch` option caps how many of the source's slots load unseen.
  - A deferred tile is asked again on a later frame; a missing one draws its parent's.
  - A slot let go aborts the tiles it still waits on and closes an image that arrives after.
- **Stub.** It shows the slot `slotAt` names.
- **Docs.** `docs/RENDERER-CONTRACT.md` describes it.

## Tests

- The conformance check `globe.imagery.decoded` covers it: slot colours read back from the drawn pixels, shown and prefetch asks, the prefetch cap, deferred tiles and a time with no slot. It runs on the stub and on Cesium (`npm run qa:conformance -- --only globe.imagery.decoded` passes). The check fails if the prefetch cap is broken.
- Unit tests in `src/render/cesium/imageryFrames.test.mjs`.
- `npm test`, `npm run format:check` and `npm run check:boundaries` pass.

title: Icons drawn over depth no longer flicker
body:
An icon drawn over depth (aircraft, vessels and every other icon set that ignores depth) set its log depth to exactly the near plane, `v_depthFromNearPlusOne = 1.0`. Interpolated across the quad, that value can arrive a rounding step or two under `czm_writeLogDepth`'s `0.9999999` cut, which discards the fragment. A moving icon then vanished for a frame now and then, most visibly far away in dense clusters (busy ports, approach corridors).

It now sits 1e-4 m past the near plane (`1.0001`), which is still in front of everything the scene draws.

Measured in a live view with aircraft and vessels on, counting icons that vanish and come back within three frames over the same 300 frames: 504 with `1.0`, 19 with `1.0001`, 345 again after switching back.

title: Hold the clock still in the delayed-live aircraft icon test
body: `an aircraft layer draws its contacts as one GPU icon set moving on the delayed live clock` (`src/render/cesium/draw.test.mjs`) compares where the icon is drawn with where the layer reads it, and each side reads `Date.now()` separately. The test contact covers about half a metre per millisecond against a 0.5 m tolerance, so on a busy machine the two readings landed far enough apart to fail `same place`. The comparison now runs with `Date.now` held still.

title: Keep the panel rails clear of an obstacle across the middle of a short window
body:
This follows up a review finding on the panel rails.

**The problem.** In windows shorter than about 520px, both rails ignored an obstacle that crosses the middle of the window, such as the World Timeline, the voice control or a card. A rail's panels could then be laid out over it.

**The fix.**
- Obstacles wholly above or wholly below the middle are handled as before.
- An obstacle across the middle is now checked after the others. The panels go on whichever side of it has more room, or above it on a tie, so the band always ends before the obstacle starts.
- When nothing fits, the existing fallbacks stay: the right rail gives a zero-height band, and the left rail keeps its minimum lane.

Code:
- Right rail: `src/ui/panelRailGeometry.js`.
- Left rail: `src/ui/leftPanelRail.js`.

**Tests.** New tests in `src/cockpitMath.test.mjs` and `src/ui/panelRails.test.mjs` fail without the fix.

title: Prefer a nearby small place over a far namesake, and bound the place tiles a lookup reads
body:
This follows up review findings on #1816, nearby places.

**A small place in view now comes before a far bigger namesake.**
- Before, the detail tiles were read only when no city had the typed name, so "villages near Paris" while looking at a village called Paris went to Paris, France.
- Now the nearest place of the name within 150 km of the view wins, small places included.
- With nothing of that name near the view, the largest city of the name still wins, and a country in the request still decides.
- Code: `findPlace` in `src/data/wikidataCities.js`.

**A whole-globe view no longer reads every detail tile.**
- Small places are now looked for within 500 km at most (`PLACE_TILE_KM`), so a view of the whole globe reads only the tiles around its centre.
- Cities still count to the full radius.

**Rebuilding the pack is safer.**
- `scripts/build-wikidata-cities.mjs` now writes all the new files before it removes tiles from an earlier build, so a build that stops part way never leaves an index naming a removed tile.
- `meta.built` keeps its earlier date when nothing else in the file changed, so rebuilding unchanged data leaves the files as they were.

**Tests:**
- `src/data/wikidataCities.test.mjs`: a small place in view comes before its namesake, and a whole-globe view reads exactly six tiles around Austin.
- `src/tooling/wikidataPlaceTiles.test.mjs`: the build date is kept when nothing changed.

**Docs:** `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md` and both pack READMEs.

Co-authored-by: Manjunath Paparaju <manjunath@halfpixel.ai>
Co-authored-by: Sameh Khamis <sameh@halfpixel.ai>

title: Vue kit: the kit's classes carry Core's standard looks
body:
First step toward building all Core UI from the Vue kit in `src/ui/kit/`.

**The problem.** The kit components carried behaviour only. `.ui-button`, `.ui-chip`, `.ui-badge`, `.ui-empty` and `.ui-segmented` had no CSS, so every feature restyled its own controls. As a result most controls are hand-written: 231 `<button>`s against 70 `UiButton`s. Moving them onto the kit needs the kit to carry Core's standard looks first.

**The change.** Each kit class now shares one selector list with the Core skin it stands for, so no rule is copied:

| Kit | Look | Rules |
|---|---|---|
| `UiButton` default `ghost` | unchanged: no styles, the caller styles it | — |
| `UiButton variant="action"` (+ `tone="danger"`, `size="compact"`) | the `.gev-action-button` surface | `action-button.css` |
| `UiButton variant="primary"` | the action surface with the accent of the scene panel's primary buttons | `action-button.css` |
| `UiButton variant="icon"` | the `.panel-collapse-btn` 22px glyph button | `controls.css` |
| `UiChip` | the `.news-chip` pill | new `chip.css` |
| `UiEmpty` | the news readout's dim one-line empty state | new `empty-state.css` |
| `UiBadge`, `UiSegmented` | already wore `gev-status-badge` / `gev-segmented`; the kit classes now share those rules | `status-badge.css`, `segmented-control.css` |

The skins load early, so feature stylesheets still override them. Nothing in the app changes look:
- The command dock's two pin buttons had `variant="icon"` without ever wearing the icon look, so they are now plain ghost buttons.
- Three feature rules that relied on inherited type keep inheriting it.

**Checked in Chrome.** I compared this build with main:
- The computed styles of all 201 kit and shared-skin controls on the start screen were identical.
- With News and Recent Imagery on, every readout, chip, empty and status element was identical.

**Tests:**
- `src/ui/kit/kitStyles.test.mjs` pins that each kit class has rules and that `ghost` stays unstyled.
- `UiButton.test.mjs` covers the variant classes and the pressed state.

**Docs:** the kit section of `docs/VUE-MIGRATION.md`.

Co-authored-by: Manjunath Paparaju <manjunath@halfpixel.ai>
Co-authored-by: Sameh Khamis <sameh@halfpixel.ai>

title: Vue kit: UiCloseButton for every close button in the views
body:
Builds on #1839: the second step of the Vue kit.

**What changes**
- New `UiCloseButton` (`src/ui/kit/UiCloseButton.vue`). It is a `UiButton` with a fixed glyph and a required accessible name. `glyph` is `times` (×) or `icon` (the Material `close` symbol).
- Its look lives in `src/ui/styles/close-button.css`: a bare glyph with no padding, border or background, and a pointer cursor. That rule shares one selector list with the guide's close, so nothing is copied.
  - The rule loads before the feature stylesheets, so each site's own class still sets its size, colour, hover and any surface.
  - `bare` turns the kit look off for a skin that sets its own padding and border (Street Level, space missions).
- 16 hand-written close, dismiss and clear buttons in the views now use it:
  - chat, Data Library and key setup
  - Context search clear and the Inspector's turn-off
  - entity card and CCTV popup
  - voice card and voice panel
  - wildlife sighting and Bhote Koshi
  - Street Level and mission deselect
  - Recent Imagery unpin, the rail chip clear and draw-mark remove

Every site keeps its id, classes, `data-*` hooks, title, label and handler.
- `src/ui/kit/closeButtons.test.mjs` fails if a view writes a close button by hand again.
- `kitStyles.test.mjs` pins the stylesheet load order.

**Checked in Chrome** against main, computed styles side by side. These are identical: chat close, Data Library close, Context search clear, the Inspector's turn-off, voice card and voice panel close, Street Level close, Recent Imagery unpin, the rail chip clear, and mission deselect.
- Clicking the Context search clear still empties the field and refocuses it.
- The Data Library close still closes its dialog.

Reviewed by Claude and Codex. Neither found a defect; the two wording and test nits are fixed.

The close buttons built in script (credits, Quebec CCTV overlay, guide) move with their SFC conversions in a later step.
