title: Vue kit: UiSearchField for the Context and Layer Finder searches
body:
Builds on #1840: the next step of the Vue kit.

**What changes**
- New `UiSearchField` (`src/ui/kit/UiSearchField.vue`): the Material `search` glyph and a search input in a flex row.
  - Props: `v-model`, a required `label` (the input's accessible name), `placeholder`, and `tag` (`div` or `label`, so each site keeps its frame element).
  - The input takes its own `inputId`, `inputClass`, `autocomplete` and `spellcheck`. Other attributes and classes go on the frame.
  - Optional clear: with `clearLabel`, a `UiCloseButton` shows while text is typed. It empties the field and focuses the input again.
  - Escape stops at the input and is emitted with its event. `focus()` focuses the input.
- Kit look, `src/ui/styles/search-field.css`: the declarations both search skins had in common, moved out of them rather than copied. That is the frame's flex row, and an input with no border or background that is free to shrink.
  - It loads before the feature sheets, which still set each frame's size, surface, focus ring and the input's type and outline.
  - Chrome's built-in clear (×) in search inputs is left to each skin: Context hides it, the Layer Finder shows it.
- Converted: the Context panel search and the Layer Finder search.
  - The locale picker's combobox, the Omnibar's location field and the Data Library's labelled search are different controls, so they are not converted.

**Checked in Chrome** against the parent build, side by side.
- Computed styles are identical at rest and focused, for both fields' frame, glyph, input and Context's clear button. Input attributes are identical too.
- Escape closes each search exactly as before: Context's is stopped, the Layer Finder's is stopped and prevented.
- The Layer Finder's filtered list is identical for every query tried.

Reviewed by Claude and Codex. Neither found a defect. The review's small items are fixed: a parent-reset test, a doc gap, the line wrap and a comment.

Co-authored-by: Manjunath Paparaju <manjunath@halfpixel.ai>
Co-authored-by: Sameh Khamis <sameh@halfpixel.ai>

title: Vue kit: UiCheckbox for the Visual, voice, Data Library and welcome checkboxes
body:
Builds on #1841: the next step of the Vue kit.

**What changes**
- New `UiCheckbox` (`src/ui/kit/UiCheckbox.vue`): a `<label>` around a native checkbox and its content.
  - `v-model` (`modelValue`, a Boolean): leave it unset and the box is the browser's own, never rewritten by a re-render.
  - `trailing` puts the box after the content.
  - `inputId` and `inputAttrs` reach the input. Other attributes and classes go on the label.
  - `restore` puts the box back to its value after a change the owner did not take. This keeps the voice settings' refused-change behaviour that the removed `v-checked` directive gave.
- Kit look, `src/ui/styles/checkbox.css`: `.ui-checkbox`'s flex row. It is moved out of the two skins that only label a checkbox, not copied.
  - Nothing is shared on the box itself. Its accent colour differs per skin, and the Data Library box keeps the browser's default.
- Converted:
  - the Visual panel's Scope, sky and application-group toggles
  - the two voice settings (quick chat, Voice Preview)
  - the Data Library's "available only" box
  - the welcome screen's "Don't show this again"
- `src/ui/kit/checkboxes.test.mjs` fails if a view writes a checkbox by hand. The Explore screen's filters are the one exception, and convert later in the sweep.
- Core has no switch control, so there is no `UiSwitch`.

**Checked in Chrome** against the parent build, side by side.
- Computed styles are identical for every converted label, box and text: the Visual panel, the Data Library, the welcome screen and the voice settings.
- Clicking the welcome box, and clicking its words, behave the same.
- Turning quick chat off and on again behaves the same.
- One difference you can't see: the voice boxes now carry a `checked` attribute as well as the property, as every `:checked` binding in Vue does. No stylesheet, form reset or `defaultChecked` reads it.

Reviewed by Claude and Codex. Neither found a defect. The review's nits are fixed:
- the QA mutation for the welcome box is sharper
- one comment is corrected
- the welcome box's attributes are hoisted into a constant

Co-authored-by: Manjunath Paparaju <manjunath@halfpixel.ai>
Co-authored-by: Sameh Khamis <sameh@halfpixel.ai>

title: Vue kit: UiDialog for the Data Library and scene sharing dialogs
body:
Builds on #1842: the last new component of the Vue kit's second step.

**What changes**
- New `UiDialog` (`src/ui/kit/UiDialog.vue`): the native modal `<dialog>`, opened and closed by its `open` prop.
  - It opens with `showModal()` once its content has rendered, opens on mount when `open`, and closes on unmount.
  - Events:
    - `opened` and `closed`
    - `dismiss`: the person asked to leave. Escape's cancel is prevented so the owner decides, and with `backdropDismiss` a click on the backdrop counts too.
    - `browserClose`: the browser closed it on its own while it was meant to be open.
  - `element` is exposed. Attributes, classes, styles and listeners go on the `<dialog>`, and the content is the default slot.
  - No kit look: the two dialogs share no declarations.
- Converted: the Data Library dialog, and the scene sharing dialog.
- `src/ui/kit/dialogs.test.mjs` fails if a view writes a `<dialog>` by hand.
- The `role="dialog"` panels are different controls and are not converted: key setup, the welcome launcher, the CCTV popup, the credits and the render failure.

**Behaviour changes**, each with a test that fails without it:
- The Data Library dialog is also closed if it is removed while open.
- A `close` event the browser queued from an earlier close no longer shuts a dialog that has been opened again since. The old Data Library code had this race.
- When Chrome closes the scene sharing dialog on its own (a repeated Escape whose cancel the page cannot stop), the dialog now cancels through its owner. Before, it stayed mounted but closed, which blocked the next share.

**Checked in Chrome** against the parent build, side by side.
- Data Library:
  - Same as before: it opens as a modal with focus in its search field, with identical computed styles.
  - Escape, a backdrop click and its close button each close it and return focus to Browse. Clicks inside leave it open.
- Scene sharing: it opens as a modal with focus on Cancel, at the same size and colours, and Escape removes it.

Reviewed by Claude and Codex.
- Neither found a defect introduced here.
- The two older races above are fixed.
- The open-timing test now changes its content in the same update that opens the dialog, so it fails if `opened` comes early.

Co-authored-by: Manjunath Paparaju <manjunath@halfpixel.ai>
Co-authored-by: Sameh Khamis <sameh@halfpixel.ai>

title: Vue: the credits line and its Data attribution list are a single-file component
body:
Builds on #1843. The Vue kit's third step converts the views still built in script; this is the first of the three.

**What changes**
- The attribution line and its "Data attribution" list are now single-file components, `src/ui/credits/CreditsView.vue` and `CreditItem.vue`.
- `src/ui/creditsView.js` keeps `mountCreditsView(viewer, { root })` and every decision:
  - which credits show, and whether the list is open;
  - focus, clicks and Escape.
- It renders the view synchronously, which teleports the line and the list to the end of `root`. They stay direct children of the body, as the Stories rule needs.
- The list's close button is the kit's `UiCloseButton`.
- Link safety is unchanged: text is text, and links and logos pass `safeUrl` with the same schemes.
- `docs/VUE-MIGRATION.md` gains a note: `t()` is not reactive, so words in a kit component's slot do not follow a locale change by themselves.

**One small behaviour change**: list items are keyed by credit. A focused link that stays in the list now keeps focus when the list redraws, where a redraw used to move focus to the close button. A test pins it.

**Checked**
- A test render of the old and new code gives byte-identical HTML, except the close button's added kit classes.
- Core mounts this view only for a renderer without its own credit display. On the stub renderer, booted headless by `npm run qa:stub-boot`, both builds show the same line, "Powered by Esri · Data attribution", and the list opens with the same 115 credits.

Reviewed by Claude and Codex. Neither found a defect. The review's additions are in: the focus test, the comment on why the locale prop exists, and the doc note.

Co-authored-by: Manjunath Paparaju <manjunath@halfpixel.ai>
Co-authored-by: Sameh Khamis <sameh@halfpixel.ai>

title: Vue: the Quebec CCTV overlay is a single-file component
body:
Builds on #1843. The second of the Vue kit's script-view conversions.

**What changes**

- `src/ui/quebecCctvOverlay.js` stays the owner. `cctvControls.js` calls `createQuebecCctvOverlay(viewer)`, `setCamera` and `dispose` as before.

- The window's fixed labels are now worded when it renders, so a locale change shows at the next update. Before, they kept the language they were created in.

**Checked in Chrome** against the parent build, on the dev server with a live Québec 511 camera picked from the CCTV panel.
- The window's 13 elements have identical computed styles.
- The close button hides it.
- The marker shows with the same class and name.

Reviewed by Claude and Codex. Neither found a defect. They checked:
- node identity across re-renders, so no reset of a playing video
- listeners across repeated `setCamera` calls
- dispose order
- Escape, drag and focus
- specificity against the kit classes

The two small review notes are applied: dispose marks the overlay disposed before unmounting, and a doc line is re-wrapped.

title: Vue: the Omnibar's guided walk is a single-file component
body:
The third of the Vue kit's script-view conversions.

**What changes**
- The Omnibar's guided walk (the spotlight ring and its callout) is now a single-file component, `src/ui/views/panels/OmnibarGuide.vue`.
- `startGuide()` in `src/ui/omnibarGuide.js` keeps its signature and stays the owner:
  - it works out every step's words and settings;
  - it renders the view synchronously;
  - it keeps the parts the template never binds: the fade-in, the callout's place and side, the rings' boxes, focus, Escape and click tracking.
- The walk finds its elements in the rendered tree, not through template refs. Refs are filled after a render returns, and later still when a walk starts inside one of Vue's own post-render updates. There the walk would have failed with its listeners already in place.
- Close is the kit's `UiCloseButton`, which drops the old `<span aria-hidden>` around the ×; Skip, the offer and Next are `UiButton`s. No stylesheet styles their kit classes, so their look is unchanged.

**New tests** in `src/ui/omnibarGuide.test.mjs`:
- the walk's place, aria and focus;
- the status line changes once per step;
- each step gets new progress dots;
- a new walk ends the one in progress;
- a walk started from a component's `onMounted` starts and ends. This one fails on the first commit and passes on the fix.

**Checked in Chrome** against the parent build, with "how to measure distance" + Enter in the Omnibar:
- All 25 elements of the walk have identical computed styles. The close button differs only by the dropped wrapper; its box is the same.
- Skipping steps gives the same count, text, status line, progress dots, ring and side at every step, and "Finish" on the last.
- Escape and the close button end the walk.
- Pressing the highlighted Utilities moves the walk on to the Draw step.
  - In one of four runs on each build, a scripted click right after the walk opened did not advance it. This is the same on the parent build.

Reviewed by Claude and Codex:
- Codex found nothing.
- Claude found the post-render start defect, which is fixed here. Nothing else.

Co-authored-by: Manjunath Paparaju <manjunath@halfpixel.ai>
Co-authored-by: Sameh Khamis <sameh@halfpixel.ai>

title: Vue kit: the Omnibar's mic, strip chips and glyphs are kit controls
body:
The first surface of the Vue kit sweep: the Omnibar's hand-written controls are the kit's.

**What changes** in `src/ui/views/panels/Omnibar.vue`:
- **The mic** is a ghost `UiButton`. It is a pressed toggle with `active` as its pressed class, and its `aria-label`, `title`, `aria-pressed` and `disabled` are the same as before.
- **The suggestion strip's chips** are ghost `UiButton`s. They keep `role="option"`, `aria-selected`, `aria-current`, `tabindex="-1"` and their mousedown guard, and gain no `aria-pressed`.
- **The search glyph, the row glyphs and the chip glyphs** are `UiIcon`s with `:size="null"`, so the Omnibar's own rules still size them.
- **Left as they are:**
  - the mic's glyph and the chat row's bubble stay inline SVG, since no Material symbol the page loads draws them;
  - the field stays its own combobox rather than a `UiSearchField`.
- **New guard test,** `src/ui/kit/omnibarControls.test.mjs`. It pins:
  - no hand-written `<button>` and no hand-written Material span;
  - the kit counts and `:size="null"` on every glyph;
  - the two remaining SVGs.
- `docs/VUE-MIGRATION.md` describes the Omnibar.

**Checked in Chrome** against main, with the Omnibar idle and with "paris", "layers" and "flights" typed, and arrow keys onto the strip:
- **Every element** matches in box and computed style, except two properties on the converted glyphs. They gain `.ui-icon`'s `font-variation-settings`, which are the values the font is loaded with, and its `user-select: none`.
- **The glyphs draw the same:** compared pixel by pixel, the largest difference is 3 out of 255, from the translucent backdrop behind them.
- **The only behaviour change:** select-all no longer copies the glyph names as text.

**Reviewed by Claude and Codex:**
- Claude found no defects.
- Codex noted that the guard test did not pin `:size="null"`, although the docs said it did. The test now pins it, and fails when it is removed.

**Checked in Chrome** against main on the dev server, with live flights over SFO and the same aircraft (FDX1874) opened through CONTACTS on both:

title: Hands: steer the globe with webcam hand gestures (UTILITIES ▸ Hands)
body:
## What this changes

Adds **UTILITIES ▸ Hands**: steer the globe with hand gestures seen by the webcam. MediaPipe Hand Landmarker (`@mediapipe/tasks-vision` 1.2.2, pinned) runs in the browser. The app serves the model and the WASM, and loads them only when the toggle is first turned on. No frame leaves the machine. Turning it off (or hiding the tab) stops the camera stream and closes the model.

| Gesture | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| Pinch, right hand | drag; nearer/farther zooms; turning the wrist rotates |
| Pinch, left hand | tilt, like the middle mouse button |
| Pinch, both hands | spread = zoom, up/down = tilt, turn = rotate (locks until both let go) |
| Let go of a moving drag | the map coasts to a stop |
| ✊ fist | stops everything (drag, flight, orbit, globe spin, voice camera motions) |
| 👉 "pilot" (index + thumb out), held | slow straight flight; lean the index to turn, bring the hand nearer to speed up |
| 👍 sideways, held | slow orbit about the centre (`move_camera` orbit) |
| ☝️ index only | reticle; a quick pinch from it clicks there; held, it is a grab (and drags the before/after split line when on it) |
| ✌️ held still / swiped | pin at the centre (annotations) / next or previous shot of the selected scene |
| ✋ swiped left/right | previous/next view (hand-control history); above 2,500 km spins the globe |
| ✋✋ both open and still | north up |
| 🤌 all fingertips together | fly to the start view |
| 👉👉 two-hand frame | PNG screenshot |
| 🤙 held | microphone toggle, the same claim/release path as holding Space |

How it fits the current architecture:
- `src/handControl/gestures.js` is pure (no DOM, renderer or MediaPipe), with 27 unit tests. It uses One Euro smoothing, hysteresis and hold-to-fire latches.
- `cameraDriver.js` works only through the camera port (`cameraOf`), `findQuery().pickEllipsoid`, `findFrame` and `moveCamera`/`interruptCameraMotion`. It never imports Cesium.
- The panel publishes `{active}` to the display store and answers `toggleHands` through `connect`, as the Draw tool does. `HandControls.vue` is the toggle.
- `RealtimeInput.claimPushToTalk()` is the existing Space-hold body, extracted unchanged. `toggleGestureTalk()` and `voice/gestureTalk.js` reuse it, with 4 tests.
- A pinch counts only when the thumb is seen touching the index: MediaPipe's depth rejects a thumb tucked behind it. Calibration (3 × ~3 s) stores per-hand thresholds in `localStorage`, and there is a left-handed switch.
- Strings are translated in all 13 locales; the zh-Hant file is generated.
- The model is bundled under Apache 2.0; it has a row in `DATA_SOURCES.md` and a provenance README with its SHA-256.

## How I verified it

- [x] `npm run build`
- [x] `npm test`: 15,390 pass and 4 fail. Two timing tests (`ranking 250k rows…`, `tool string bounds…`) failed under load and pass when run alone. Two ratchets (`the allow-list only shrinks`, `the record only shrinks`) need an `origin/main` ref, which my clone names differently; they pass with that ref.
- [x] `npm run format:check`, `npm run check:boundaries`, `npm run doctor`, `layer-token:check` and `library:check` pass.
- [x] `npm run test:track`: same result as an untouched `main` on this machine. Both show the same 9 FAILs (trail head, STALE cue, arrival nose, display-floor ×5). My headless Chromium renders at about 1 fps, so I read those as environment and not this change. I'd appreciate a run on a normal machine.
- [x] Browser, dev server, synthetic intents through the QA handle `window.__gevHandControl`:
  - drag, tilt, pilot flight (moves north at the expected speed, then stops on a fist), north up, history back, orbit (heading advances), coast, pin, start view;
  - the toggle in UTILITIES opens the panel top-right, and turning it off releases the camera;
  - no console errors.
- [ ] Not yet tested with a real hand in front of a webcam. The thresholds are a first tuning, and the built-in Calibrate step is there to adapt them.

## Docs

- [x] `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md` updated (new "Hands — webcam gesture control" section; Utilities lists Hands) and a `changelog.d/1853-hand-gesture-control.md` fragment added.

title: fix(render): wheel zoom no longer stalls with an icon under the canvas centre
body:
## What

With the camera below 150 km and an aircraft or vessel icon under the exact centre of the canvas, wheel and trackpad zoom froze: zooming in did nothing and zooming out moved by centimetres. Panning the icon off the centre, or starting above 150 km, made zoom work again. Seen with Live Flights over a busy airport and with a selected vessel the view had centred on.

## Why

1. Below `minimumPickingTerrainHeight` (150 km) Cesium's `zoom3D()` sizes a zoom step from the depth it picks at the canvas centre.
2. Icons drawn over depth (`disableDepthTest: Infinity`, which aircraft and vessels use everywhere) sit on the near plane and write depth.
3. #1835 moved their log depth from `1.0` to `1.0001` so `czm_writeLogDepth` would stop discarding fragments (the flicker fix). `1.0` gives a depth of 0, which the depth pick ignores; `1.0001` gives a small positive depth, which the pick accepts as a surface a near plane's distance from the camera.
4. With that distance `handleZoom()` returns early on zoom in (already at `minimumZoomDistance`) and clamps zoom out to a rate well under a metre per notch.

A plain revert of #1835 would bring the flicker back, and `1.0` interpolated across the quad could still land a rounding step above 1.0.

## Fix

Over-depth rows now write `gl_FragDepth = 0.0` in the fragment shader themselves (flagged by a new `v_overDepth` varying) and no longer go through `czm_writeLogDepth`:

- depth exactly 0 is never discarded, so the #1835 flicker fix holds;
- Cesium's pick depth copy only takes a scene depth strictly between 0 and the globe's, so it keeps the depth of the ground under the icon and the zoom step is the same as over bare ground.

Rows that test depth are unchanged. No camera controller settings are touched.

## Verification

New real-browser script `scripts/qa-zoom-under-icon.mjs` (one always-over-depth icon through the draw port, camera 15 km above it looking straight down, no live data). On macOS, ANGLE Metal, log depth on, keyless globe:

| | depth pick at centre | wheel in from 15,000 m | wheel out from 15,000 m |
|---|---|---|---|
| no icon (control) | 15,665 m | 3,285 m | 47,889 m |
| icon, `main` | **0.100 m** | **15,000 m** | **15,006 m** |
| icon, this branch | 14,942 m | 3,267 m | 56,497 m |

(The settled heights vary a little from run to run with the zoom easing; the control shows the same spread.)

The script fails on `main` and passes here; it also checks that the icon still picks by click. A source-level unit test in `iconSetPrimitive.test.mjs` pins the shader path, since shaders do not compile under `npm test`.

- `npm run format:check`, `npm run check:boundaries`, `npm run build`: pass
- `npm test`: passes locally except `src/i18n/zh-hant-cli.test.mjs`, which could not find `opencc-js` in my local install (unrelated to this change; CI installs it)

## Not verified

- Google Photorealistic tiles (no key on the machine used): tested on the keyless globe only.
- WebGL 1 and `logarithmicDepthBuffer = false`: the `LOG_DEPTH` block is skipped there and depth comes from `gl_Position.z = -w` as before; not exercised.
- Dense moving clusters were not watched by eye for flicker; depth 0 cannot be discarded by construction, and two over-depth icons on one pixel order as they did before #1835.
- No before/after recording attached yet.

Other custom primitives were checked for the same pattern (`gl_Position.z = -gl_Position.w` with depth writes): only `iconSetPrimitive.js` has it.

title: Wheel zoom no longer stops over an icon drawn over depth
body:
#1835 moved icons drawn over depth (aircraft, vessels and every icon set that ignores depth) 1e-4 m past the near plane, so their fragments wrote a depth just above zero. Cesium's \`pickPosition\` accepts any depth above zero, and the camera controller measures the distance to whatever is under the screen centre below 150 km. An icon there read as a surface 0.1 m in front of the camera: zoom-in was refused and zoom-out moved a few metres a notch, until the icon left the centre pixel.

Over-depth fragments now write a depth of exactly zero, the depth a billboard over depth writes, and skip \`czm_writeLogDepth\`, whose near-plane discard was the flicker #1835 fixed. \`pickPosition\` skips a depth of zero, so zoom measures to the surface behind the icon, and the icon is still never discarded. On WebGL1 without \`EXT_frag_depth\` nothing changes.

Measured in headless Chromium on the plain globe, camera straight down at 60 km, one stationary vessel, pointer off the icon, six wheel notches in and then six out:

| Build | Distance picked at centre | After zoom in | After zoom out |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| Before, vessel at centre | 0.1 m | 60,000 m | 60,010 m |
| After, vessel at centre | 59,963 m | 4,040 m | 47,455 m |
| After, vessel off centre | 59,963 m | 3,901 m | 46,531 m |

The vessel is still drawn at the centre after the change. A test pins the zero depth write.

title: A bare address starts with the default layers
body:
Layer choices are saved to local storage (`gev:layer-state:v2`) and were restored at start-up whenever the address carried no link. The address writes the view into its hash as you use the app, so a reload keeps working from the hash. But clearing the address and loading the bare URL brought the last session's layers (flights, radar, wind and so on) back every time: there was no way back to a reset view.

`ShareRestoration` now starts the layer-state coordinator with `allowLocalState: false`. A link still restores everything its hash carries; a bare address starts with the default layers and options. The camera was never stored, so it already started at the default view.

Checked in headless Chromium with one browser profile: switching Earthquakes on saves it; the bare address then opens with no layers on; the full link from before opens with Earthquakes on. The layer-state, share-link and share-restoration unit tests pass.

Layer choices are still written to local storage, and nothing reads them back at start-up now. Panel collapsed state is unchanged.

title: Vue kit: Bhote Koshi's buttons and media cards are kit controls and a view
body:
The second Vue kit sweep, seventh surface: the Bhote Koshi panel uses the kit's controls, and its embedded media cards are a Vue view rather than script-built markup.

**What changes:**
- **`BhoteKoshiPanel.vue`:** every hand-written button (Close, ‹ ›, PLAY, CINEMATIC, FULL STORY, OPEN ORIGINAL, LOWER GORGE, the field reports, OPEN PUBLIC MAP) is a ghost `UiButton`. Each keeps its `data-action`, title, `aria-label`, hidden, disabled and click handler. ‹ and › are text characters and stay text.
- **CINEMATIC's pressed state** is Vue state now.
  - The event layer (`src/data/bhoteKoshiEvent.js`) sets `pressed` on the button's record instead of writing `aria-pressed`, and the button is `UiButton :pressed`.
  - `bhote-koshi.css` still styles it by `[aria-pressed='true']`.
  - The named exception for it is gone from `viewControls.test.mjs` and `docs/VUE-MIGRATION.md`.
- **Media cards:** the new `src/ui/bhoteKoshi/BhoteKoshiMediaCards.vue` draws each card (leader line, YouTube frame, title, status, original link) and the hidden YouTube warm-up frame.

  - Classes, `data-provider`, the root's id and attributes, listeners, placement after each frame, timers, provider loading and cleanup are kept.
  - Cards are keyed by id, so a redraw never recreates a frame or reloads a video.
- **Left in script, and why:**
  - **Facebook player node:** it is created hidden as a warm-up before its card exists, then moved, already loaded, into the card. A template would rebuild it and reload the player.
  - **X post:** X's own script builds it inside the card's empty player box.
  - **Plumbing:** the provider script tags, the preconnect links and the overlay root.
  - **Video and canvas in the event layer:** offscreen textures drawn on the globe, not page UI.
- **Tests:**
  - New guard test `src/ui/kit/bhoteKoshiControls.test.mjs`. It pins:
    - no hand-written button in the panel or cards;
    - no hand-written `aria-pressed` in any form;
    - the one `:pressed`, with no `pressed-class`;
    - no `innerHTML` or script-built card in the media module;
    - the layer never writing `aria-pressed`.
  - Each check was confirmed to fail when its violation is put back.
  - The media module's tests now run on a real page.
  - The event layer's tests check that CINEMATIC is pressed while it owns the camera and unpressed once released.
- **Docs:** `docs/VUE-MIGRATION.md` gains a Bhote Koshi paragraph.

**What a user could notice:**
- The panel buttons gain the kit's classes, which have no CSS rules.
- The card overlay gains Vue's invisible empty text and comment nodes.

**Checked in Chrome** against main, with the `bhote-koshi-2026` layer on.
- All 16 panel controls match in box, computed style and aria.
- CINEMATIC goes from `◉ CINEMATIC`/false to `■ RELEASE CAMERA`/true and back, the same as main.
- I stepped progress through nine evidence points, seven YouTube and one Facebook among them. Each card matches main in classes, provider, frame source, child structure and position, and the overlay root's attributes match.
- On the Facebook card, the section and its player frame stay the same elements across redraws, so nothing reloads.

**Reviewed by Claude and Codex.**
- Codex found nothing.
- Claude found no defect. It confirmed:

title: A phone no longer zooms the page when a text field gets focus
body:
iPhone Safari zooms the page in whenever a text field with a font size under 16 px gets focus, and it stays zoomed after the keyboard closes. Every text field in the app is under 16 px (32 of them at phone width; the search box is 13 px), so tapping the search box on an iPhone left the page zoomed in, with buttons and panels cut off.

The viewport now sets `maximum-scale=1`, as map pages usually do. The map already handles pinch zoom itself, so a page-level zoom only scales the controls. Safari keeps the page at scale 1 when a field gets focus but still lets a pinch zoom the page for people who need it; Android Chrome no longer zooms the page itself, while pinching the map still zooms the map.

The alternative was 16 px text in every field on touch screens, which keeps page zoom available but needs layout changes in compact panels.

title: A host names the layers a bare address starts with
body:
A bare address (one that carries no link) starts with no layers on, and an application had no way to choose otherwise.

`createApplicationControls` now takes `startLayers`, the layer ids a bare address starts with; none by default, so the standalone app is unchanged. A host may pass, for example, `['flights', 'satellites']`.

- The layers restore through the passive start-up path (`LayerStateCoordinator.start({ startLayerIds })`), so they are never written to local storage as the user's own choice.
- A link's own layers always win: a share with a layer payload restores exactly that, and a link without one keeps the legacy defaults.
- The address writes them like any other layer (`l=f.s`), so a reload keeps them.

Checked in headless Chromium with the standalone app temporarily passing `['flights', 'satellites']`: the bare address starts with both on, `l=f.s` in the hash and nothing stored; a link naming only wind starts with only wind. Two unit tests cover the start path and a share winning over it.

title: Vue kit: Street Level's photo viewer is a Vue view
body:
The second Vue kit sweep, eighth surface: Street Level's photo viewer (KartaView and Panoramax, flat and 360° photos) is a Vue view instead of markup built in script.

**What changes:**
- **The layer** (`src/layers/streetLevel/photoViewer.js`) no longer creates or writes any element.
  - It publishes the viewer's state through a new optional `ViewerAdapter.subscribeView()`: kind, image, FIT/FILL, canvas key, dragging, and the step buttons' labels and disabled states.
  - The view hands back the root, picture, canvas and buttons, so the layer still measures, checks fullscreen, moves focus and draws the panorama.
  - `mount()` resolves once the view has drawn.
- **Wiring:**
  - `src/layers/streetLevel/photoViewers.js` picks which mounted viewer is shown: the latest mount wins, and an older one still presenting is closed.
  - `index.js` exposes it as `subscribePhotoViewer()`. `applicationShell.js` publishes it to the new store `src/ui/stores/streetLevelPhoto.js`, the same way it handles the launches replay overlay.
- **The view** is `src/ui/views/panels/StreetLevelPhotoViewer.vue`, beside `StreetLevelPanel` in `LayerPanelsView.vue`.
  - It teleports into the viewer host with the same `.sl-photo-*` markup, data attributes, tabindex, role and labels.
  - ‹ and › are ghost `UiButton`s; their glyphs are text characters.
  - Each mount gets its own root, picture, canvas and buttons, and a lost WebGL context gets a fresh canvas.
- **`street-level-layer` still has no Vue dependency.** Like the other layers with UI, it needs the application's view to draw.
  - Without one, mounting a KartaView or Panoramax viewer throws.
  - `docs/VUE-MIGRATION.md` and `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md` say so.
- **Left in script:** the globe panel page's "lost its 3D graphics" notice (`src/app/globePanelRuntime.js`). That file is sent as source text and runs before the app loads, so it can import nothing; the doc names it. The other `createElement('div')` sites left are mount hosts and containers.
- **Tests:**
  - New real-page tests in `StreetLevelPhotoViewer.test.mjs` cover:
    - markup, attributes and FIT/FILL;
    - stepping by click and keys, with clicks kept from reaching the globe;
    - close, and focus moving to the viewer when a focused step button disables;
    - panorama drag, wheel and context loss, and Esc;
    - a provider switch in one tick getting fresh elements;
    - a mount overtaken before it is drawn closing and never showing later.
  - `photoViewers.test.mjs` covers which viewer is shown.
  - The layer-side tests stay DOM-free through a fake view that batches and reuses elements as Vue does.
  - New guard test `src/ui/kit/streetLevelPhotoControls.test.mjs`. It pins:
    - no hand-written button, field or Material span;
    - the two ghost step buttons, and no `aria-pressed`;
    - the keyed canvas;
    - no DOM creation or writes in the layer;
    - no Vue in `street-level-layer`.
  - Each check was confirmed to fail when its violation is put back.

**What a user could notice:**
- ‹ and › gain the kit's classes, which have no CSS rules, and their `title` and `aria-label` are written in the other order.
- Updates land one microtask later, before the next frame.
- A panorama image now waits for the view to draw its canvas before it uploads.

**Checked in Chrome** against main, on Panoramax in Paris (the browser talks to Panoramax directly).
- **Flat photo:** the viewer, picture, canvas and both step buttons match in box, computed style and attributes. › and ← step through the sequence, and focus stays in the viewer.
- **360° photo:** it matches when opened, after a drag, wheel and keys, after a lost WebGL context (the canvas is replaced, and one canvas remains), and after reopening.
- **Fast switching:** five quick opens alternating Panoramax and KartaView end with one viewer showing the 360° photo on its canvas, not the flat fallback.

**Reviewed by Claude and Codex.**
- Both found that switching KartaView↔Panoramax in one tick could hand the new viewer the old viewer's dead canvas, so 360° photos fell back to flat. Every mount now gets fresh elements.
- Claude also found three more problems, all fixed:
  - Two overlapping opens could leave a stale, empty viewer to show later. An overtaken mount now closes.
  - The test fake drew synchronously, which hid the dead-canvas bug. It now batches like Vue.
  - The guard test's check for DOM writes was too narrow.
- Codex re-reviewed the fixes and found nothing.

Co-authored-by: Manjunath Paparaju <manjunath@halfpixel.ai>
Co-authored-by: Sameh Khamis <sameh@halfpixel.ai>

title: Vue kit: the view scan forbids any hand-written button, glyph, checkbox or range
Find a selected vessel or aircraft again from its card
body:
## What changes

A selected vessel or aircraft used to vanish from the map while its card stayed open as "Out of feed · last reading". That happened whenever it left its layer's feed, either because the clock moved to a time the feed lacks it or because the view moved away from it. Now, while the selected item is off screen, behind the globe or out of its feed, the card's header shows **Find it**, a bullseye button:

- **Still in its feed:** clicking Find it flies the camera to the item; an aircraft is also followed.
- **Out of its feed:** clicking Find it looks the item up on its own track at the layer's time (the world clock's time while the layer follows the clock). The card moves to that reading and says how old it is ("Last reading · 4 min ago"), and the camera flies there. Once the feed has the item again, its layer selects it again.
- **No reading at or before that time:** the card says "No reading at this time" and the camera stays where it is.

This works the same for vessels, flights and military aircraft. Each layer gets a `locate(id, {reference, signal})` method, built on `locateOnTrack` in `src/data/locate.js` over the source's `getTrack`. The card keeps the item's track reference from when it was selected, so the item can still be looked up after its record is gone.

A followed item is never counted as off screen: the camera follows it where it is drawn, which can be ahead of its last reading.

One fix along the way: a vessel announced by its layer through `gev:entity-selected` is now named by its own id, as a click names it, not by the context store's `ais-` id.

## Testing

- `npm test`: 15,509 pass, 0 fail.
- New tests:
  - `src/data/locate.test.mjs`: the reading at a time, the track lookup, and the on-screen and horizon test.
  - `src/ui/stores/entityCardLocate.test.mjs`: found, not found, off screen while still in the feed, a followed item, and a lookup still running when the item comes back.
  - A bridge test for the vessel id.
- In a browser with live flights:
  - Select a flight and pan to Europe: Find it appears, and clicking it brings the camera back and follows the flight.
  - With the card out of its feed: Find it asked for that flight's track, flew to its newest point (18 s old), and the follow resumed once the flight was back in its feed.

title: Street Level photo viewer: settle every open and mount, one viewer drawn, a stated contract
body:
A follow-up to #1868, the move of Street Level's photo viewer to a Vue view. A second review of that PR's fixes found five edge cases, and this fixes all of them. None of them showed in the app.

**What changes:**
1. **A panorama open could wait forever** when a view draws immediately inside its listener, or when the last view unsubscribes mid-open.
   - The viewer now counts the view's canvas hand-backs and waits for the count to rise, so a draw made immediately is seen.
   - When the last view leaves, anything waiting is released. `ViewerAdapter.subscribeView` documents that a view may draw at once or later.
2. **With two subscribers, the second briefly saw no viewer** between the earlier and the later mount. `photoViewers.js` now closes the overtaken mount on a microtask, after the later one has reached every subscriber.
3. **The picker's contract is now documented and safe.**
   - `mountKey` and `actions.supersede` are described on `ViewerAdapter.subscribeView` (`registry.js`) and in the store's comment.
   - A presentation without a `mountKey` counts as the latest mount.
   - One without `actions` or `supersede` is drawn or passed over without throwing.
4. **The guard test now also refuses** `.width=`, `.height=`, `.ariaLabel=`, `.id=` and `.value=` in `photoViewer.js`, and `.src=` everywhere except on the off-page `Image` that `loadImage` creates.
   - Sizing the panorama's drawing buffer in `panorama.js` is drawing work, not page markup, so it stays outside the guard, as the test notes.
5. **The test fake view now uses the app's picker,** so layer and provider tests see the same one-viewer rule the app does.

**Tests:** each new test was confirmed to fail without its fix:
- a view drawing immediately, and a view leaving mid-open;
- subscribers never seeing a gap;
- a missing `mountKey`, and missing `actions`;
- each new guard pattern;
- the shared fake drawing only the later mount.

**What a user could notice:** nothing. In the app the view draws on Vue's microtask as before. The only differences are edge cases: an overtaken mount closes one microtask later, and an open now finishes instead of hanging when the view is torn down.

**Checked in Chrome** against main, on Panoramax in Paris.
- **Flat photo:** it matches when opened, while stepping and with focus.
- **360° photo:** it matches when opened, after a drag, wheel and keys, after a lost WebGL context and after reopening.
- **Fast switching:** five quick opens alternating Panoramax and KartaView end with one viewer showing the 360° photo on its canvas.

**Further review rounds** on this branch (Codex and Claude each round) found more edge cases, all in paths the app never takes. They are fixed in the later commits, each with a test that fails without its fix:
- A presentation without a `mountKey` is ranked by when it began presenting, on the same counter as mount keys (`nextViewKey()`), however often the picker is made again.
- An overtaken mount unmounts only its own presentation.
- A mount whose view re-subscribes in the same tick still draws.
- A mount its view unmounts in the first draw fails as closed.
- A canvas moving while an open waits goes on with that open. A canvas moved off is taken back once one view is left, so the next open never waits forever.
- The guard also refuses compound, destructuring, bracket, `Object.assign`, `Reflect` and `defineProperty` writes.
- The fake view resets between tests.

**Reviewed by Claude and Codex.** The final round found nothing reachable in the app. Codex found nothing in the last fix.

Co-authored-by: Manjunath Paparaju <manjunath@halfpixel.ai>
Co-authored-by: Sameh Khamis <sameh@halfpixel.ai>

title: Centre the phone Omnibar when no language picker sits beside it
body:
## What changes

On a phone (`body.mobile-shell`) the Omnibar always kept 60px clear on its right, for the language picker in the corner actions. A host that turns the picker off (`localePicker: false`) gets that space empty, so the field sat left of centre: 16px on the left, 60px on the right.

The field now keeps 16px on either side, and reserves the picker's room (`16px 60px`) only when `#locale-picker` is on the page.

## Testing

- Measured at 430×932 and 375×667, as a phone:
  - With the picker, unchanged: the field still keeps 16px and 60px, and the picker at x 385–418 is clear of it.
  - Without the picker: 16px on each side.
- `src/ui/omnibarRows.test.mjs`, `omnibarGuide`, `omnibarIntent` and `kit/omnibarControls`: 200 pass.

title: Read the weather texture limit and reveal time in the body, not a parameter default
body:
## What changes

Satellite clouds showed "Weather imagery unavailable" in a built app, on every frame, while every test passed.

The weather shell read its texture limit in a parameter default: `maxTextureSize = rendererOf(viewer)?.quality?.device?.().maxTextureSize ?? 0`. For browsers whose optional chaining it lowers (Chrome and Edge before 91, which Vite's default build target still includes), esbuild compiles an optional call of an optional property read from a property or a call (`a.b?.c?.()`, `f()?.g?.()`) in a parameter default into nested arrow functions, and the inner `.call(...)` reads a variable declared in a sibling function. The built shell threw `ReferenceError: b is not defined` on every `setFrame`, and the layer's catch turned that into the message. Under `node:test` the source runs unbuilt, so nothing failed.

- `createWeatherShell` (`src/layers/weather/shellRendering.js`) reads the limit in its body when none is passed.
- `leaderRevealProgress` and `tacticalCardRevealAlpha` (`src/overlays/worldOverlayDraw.js`) took their default time the same way (`globalThis.performance?.now?.()`); they read it in the body too.
- `src/parameterDefaults.test.mjs` parses every module the build compiles under `src/` (`.js`, `.mjs` and the script blocks of `.vue` components) and fails on an optional call of a member reached through an optional chain in any parameter default, destructured or not, outside nested functions. That is a little stricter than what breaks (`a?.b?.()` and `a?.b.c?.()` compile correctly but are refused too), as such a value is as easily read in the body. `a?.b()` and `a.b?.()` are allowed.

A value passed explicitly is used as before; only an omitted one is read in the body.

## Testing

- esbuild 0.28.2 at `--target=chrome87`: the old default compiles to `(u=>(u=(r=>…)())==null?void 0:u.call(r)…)()`, with `r` out of scope; at `es2020`, Firefox 78 or later Chrome it is left as written.
- The new test fails on the three lines before this change and passes after; a probe `.vue` script block and `.mjs` module with the form are refused at their own lines.
- `src/layers/weather/*.test.mjs`, `src/overlays/worldOverlayDraw.test.mjs`, `src/parameterDefaults.test.mjs`, `src/browserModuleBoundary.test.mjs`: 219 pass.

title: globe.imagery.video: paint the test video red before recording starts
body:
## What changes

`globe.imagery.video` records two seconds of a canvas, red then blue, as the video it plays. The canvas was first painted on a 20 ms interval tick, after `recorder.start()`, so the recording could open on blank frames; on a loaded runner the pixel read 300 ms into the segment came out dark. `main` failed this way once after #1872 (Cesium, `early in the segment: (28, 54)`), with the runs before and after it passing.

The canvas is now painted red before recording starts, and on every tick after.

## Testing

- Conformance-check change only; the Street Level browser gate on this PR runs it on Cesium.

title: Weather imagery and shells say what they show
body:
## What changes

- `ImagerySpec` (`src/render/contract/globe.d.ts`) and the `rasterShell` field (`src/render/contract/draw.d.ts`) take an optional `shows` string, such as `'clouds'` or `'radar'`. Drawing never depends on it; a renderer may use it to tell such a layer apart, for example to fade a flat cloud picture where it draws clouds of its own.
- The weather layer sets it on its globe imagery (`src/layers/weather/rendering.js`) and its shells (`shellRendering.js`) from `WEATHER_IMAGERY_SHOWS` (`imageryOrder.js`): `'clouds'` for both cloud products, the product's name for the rest.

Optional and ignored by the Cesium renderer, so nothing draws differently.

## Testing

- `src/layers/weather/*.test.mjs`, `src/render/stub/stub.test.mjs`: 209 pass; the satellite mosaic's imagery spec carries `shows: 'clouds'`.

title: The search dock sits above the World Timeline on desktop
body:
On desktop the World Timeline sat above the search dock. Now the timeline takes the dock's floor and the dock, with the search field, sits above it, rising by the timeline's height while it shows, the same order the dock has outside the search layout.

- `src/ui/styles/omnibar-dock.css`: the timeline sits at `--omnibar-dock-bottom`. The dock, the search field, the results' height budget and the narrow-screen corners are placed from `--omnibar-dock-raised`, which is that floor plus `--world-timeline-lift`. The layout no longer zeroes `--world-timeline-lift`, so toasts and the panels that clear the dock rise with it, as they do elsewhere. The timeline no longer hides while search results or the chat and voice panels are open: they open upward from the dock and no longer cover it.
- Tests: `creditAttribution.test.mjs` measures the credit clearance from the dock's floor (the timeline, or the dock itself when no timeline shows) and pins how the dock rises from it. `hudSonarStyle.test.mjs` pins the new order.
- `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md` describes the order.

Checked: `creditAttribution`, `hudSonarStyle` and `mobileShell` tests pass, and `format:check` passes. A 1600×1000 headless screenshot shows the search dock at 804–860 px and the timeline at 884–926 px; before this change the timeline was at 818–860 px, above the dock at 870–926 px.

title: Keep a landed aircraft on the ground, not at its approach height
body:
## What was wrong

A plane that landed and was then reported on the ground with no altitude (readsb's `alt_baro: "ground"`) fell back to its stored altitude. That value carries over between reports, so straight after a landing it is still the approach height.

- **Military:** the icon stayed at the approach height (one live case: 1,539 m at an airfield about 320 m up) for as long as the plane was on the ground. The grounded floor (`floorAltitudeM` = max(height, ground)) only ever raises a height. The 3D model is ground-snapped separately, so the plane dropped when the model took over, and the cockpit view switched between the two heights.
- **Civil:** the same thing happened until the ground cell under the plane warmed. A contact more than 150 km from the viewer never has its cell queued, so it stayed at the approach height indefinitely.
- **Labels:** for a parked plane, the flight-level label and the tracked readout still showed the approach altitude (e.g. FL050, "5049 ft").

## What changes

- `military/records.js`: a new `groundAltitudeM`. It is set only by a grounded report that carries an altitude, held while the plane stays grounded, and cleared on takeoff. A grounded report with no altitude uses it, else 0 m, and the existing floor then lifts it onto the ground.
- `flights/records.js`:
  - Only a height the plane held while already on the ground is kept as its prior. An airborne height is no longer carried into a landing.
  - A landing with a cold cell falls to the geoid surface, or 0 m before the geoid loads.
  - A parked plane whose cell goes cold still keeps its ground height, as before.
- Labels:
  - A grounded plane shows no flight level, and its tracked readout reads "On the ground". This is an existing translated string.
  - The follow distance for a grounded plane is sized for the ground.
  - The military analyst record reports only a ground altitude for a grounded plane.

**Behaviour change:** the test `ground transitions preserve last render height while a surface cell is cold` kept the approach height through a landing. It is replaced by tests that put the landing on the geoid (or at 0 m) on every grounded poll.

## Testing

- New military and civil record tests for a landing with no altitude, on every grounded poll after it, with and without a model owning the visual. They also cover holding a ground altitude and dropping it on takeoff. The civil landing tests fail without the change.
- The full suite passes: 15,559 tests.

title: feat: bring your own AIS-catcher into a separate Local AIS vessels layer (#714)
body:
## Summary

Adds an opt-in **Local AIS** layer for vessels heard on your own AIS-catcher receiver, next to Local ADS-B.

- A server proxy reads `ships.json` (or `/api/ships.json`) from the receivers in `LOCAL_AIS_FEEDS`. Local and private hosts only, no AISStream key, at most four feeds. It serves validated vessels at `/api/local-receivers/vessels`, through the same pinned local-receiver transport Local ADS-B uses.
- The layer draws one marker per vessel with a card (MMSI, name, speed, course, and a note for approximate or not-yet-validated positions), polls every five seconds only while enabled, and is local-only (not in share links).
- Unknown values stay unknown. A 0,0 position, a position the receiver rejected, a bad MMSI and readings older than ten minutes are refused and counted. Ship type 0 ("not available") is kept as unknown, not refused. Type-27 positions are kept and marked approximate.
- Classes above 8 that are not beacons are not drawn: SAR aircraft (9, 10) and base stations and aids to navigation (11, 12). They are counted per feed as `filtered` in the route payload and they date the receiver's last activity, so a receiver that hears only these reads as alive but quiet (STALE with an age), not as silence. Drawing SAR aircraft is a possible follow-up.
- **Distress and test beacons.** AIS-SART, man-overboard (MOB) and EPIRB-AIS transmitters (by MMSI prefix 970, 972 or 974 only: AIS-catcher gives class 13 to every MMSI from 970000000 to 980000000, so class 13 under any other prefix is filtered, not drawn) are drawn with their own orange marker and card, never as vessels. The card says it is a distress or test beacon heard by your receiver, that test transmissions are common, and that active or test status is unknown (the receiver's vessel list does not carry it). GEV never says an emergency is verified. A beacon follows the vessel rules for age, refused positions, 0,0 and the validated and approximate flags, counts as heard in the row (`1 feed live · 1 beacon heard`, never "no recent messages"), and voice reads it like any other Local AIS record (its kind is a `beaconType` query field; a flagged beacon has no coordinates). A beacon is its own kind: it is not in the vessel lists (nearby, search, ship-type counts) and the view summary leaves it out, its Context card says "beacon" even when its fix is withheld, and voice is told a pointed pick is a `beacon`, not a vessel (the record is looked up with no 2000 cap, so a beacon heard after 2000 or more vessels is still a beacon, and a pick the layer cannot find is a neutral `feature`), and a Local AIS count is worded "results", never "ships". The caveat (heard by your receiver, test transmissions are common, not a verified emergency, active or test unknown) is a note on the **Context card only**: the voice model is not given it.
- The row never reads healthy by accident. An empty or silent receiver is STALE with the age of its newest message, an unreachable receiver or one that reports an error is an error, a misconfigured feed is named apart from an unreachable one, and a receiver that is also sending rows the layer rejects as invalid reads as `rejected`, not as silence. A refused row counts as rejected only while its `last_signal` is 600 s or less or unknown, and any refused row dates the receiver by its `last_signal`, so a quiet receiver whose list holds only a 50-minute-old refused row reads STALE with that age, not "never". Filtered classes never count as rejected. The row is nominal only while at least one vessel or beacon is held. Each feed also reports the time of its newest row, and the browser shows a feed whose newest row has aged past the ten-minute window by the time the snapshot is read as stale, so "2 feeds live" is not said while one of them has nothing left. Feed state changes are logged with an error code, never the address.
- The layer is in the Layers panel (Movement group), has its own status strings in all 13 locales (including zh-Hant), and is in the voice layer manifest like Local ADS-B.
- Docs: `docs/LOCAL-RECEIVERS.md`. Changelog entry added.

## Validation

All run on Node 24 at the final head:

- `format:check`, `check:boundaries`, `npm run i18n` (4130 strings, 13 locales, complete), `changelog:check`, `layer-token:check --base-ref upstream/main` and `build`: exit 0.
- The PR's own test files (13, run with `--import=./build/registerVue.js`): 274 of 274 pass. They cover the proxy, the normaliser, the layer, its status and card, the Layers panel order, the voice catalog and manifest, the status-text translations in all 13 locales, the real `analyst_query` path (a flagged fix reaches the model with no position, for vessels and beacons, and only a boolean `true` validates: `1` and `"true"` do not), the pointer (the real pointer picker and gesture item, and the real `get_entity_context` pointer scope, with a flagged vessel or beacon), the beacon classification, marker, card and status, and the error a withheld vessel gets (position withheld, not "nothing under the pointer").
- Full `npm test`: 16,036 tests, 16,031 pass, 0 fail, 5 skipped (skips are upstream's).
- Mutation checks on the new code (shiptype 0, 0,0, the validated flag, dropped rows, the stale-versus-live rule, the manifest id, the position guard in the voice payload, the pointer guard in the picker and in `get_entity_context`, the strict `approx === false` check, the 600 s limit on rejected rows, filtered rows dating the receiver, the aged-feed rule, the strict boolean validated check, refused rows dating the receiver, the beacon classification (the prefix-only rule, the any-97 and class-13-fallback mutants, the real AIS-catcher class-13 shape), the exact 600 s edges, the withheld camera and view-centre paths, the vessel-count and beacon-count translations) each fail a test when broken.
- Runtime checks: with the proxy, layer and panel wired together, a 5 s and a 590 s old vessel read nominal; a 605 s old one, an empty list and an all-rejected list do not; an unreachable receiver or HTTP 500 reads unavailable. The vessel count in the row (beacons counted apart) reads as ships in es, fr and zh-CN.

## Privacy

The proxy and layer keep receiver data in memory only. Three paths can still send vessel data out, and each is stopped by a different step:

- **Voice (when on).** Because Local AIS is in the voice manifest, the analyst tools send the vessels and beacons they query (MMSI, name, speed, course, beacon kind and, for a validated exact fix only, the position) to the model provider. The voice payload carries only the manifest fields, so the `validated` and `approx` flags do **not** reach the model. Instead the text tools are default-deny: the only fix that sends a position is `validated === true && approx === false`. Any other (unvalidated, approximate (type 27), or flags that cannot be read) is given to the analyst with `lat` and `lon` null. The same rule holds on the pointer text paths: when you point at one, the pointer context and `get_entity_context` send its id (`local-ais:<MMSI>`) and, for a validated exact fix only, the cursor's ground point; for a flagged one the id is sent and the `ground` and `pointer` coordinates are withheld, and a tool that needs a place for it says its position is withheld because it is not validated or is approximate (only for a withheld Local AIS fix, never for an item that merely has no position, such as an aircraft picked against the sky). For a withheld pointer target, `get_entity_context` also drops the view centre, the viewport samples and their place names, and the camera latitude and longitude (its height stays), because the marker may be at the centre. Flagged vessels also leave the omnibar search and the nearby lists, and their Context card shows only the id and kind (and, for a beacon, the beacon type and caveat), with no position.
  **What this does not do.** The text tools do not hand a flagged fix to the model as coordinates, but flagged vessels and beacons are still **drawn on the map**, so map paths can locate them: a screenshot sent for a voice turn shows the marker, the pointer's screen position can be turned into coordinates by `annotate_map`'s pixel resolution, a cursor next to the marker (or over its card) sends the nearby ground point, and the view's camera position, if you centre a flagged vessel (`get_current_view_state` always sends it, as it does for every layer; that is existing behaviour and unchanged). `get_entity_context` also still sends coordinates, including for a withheld target: its default scope (no pointer) sends the camera latitude and longitude, the view-centre point and the text "view centered near ...", and in pointer scope the nearby visible items are listed by distance from the screen centre with their coordinates, and this list is also sent when the pointed target is withheld (a vessel close to a withheld beacon can come first). So centring the view on a flagged fix can reveal roughly where it is. These paths are not closed, and the docs say so. Voice can run on Codex OAuth, so unsetting `OPENAI_API_KEY` does not by itself stop it.
- **HUD (voice on or off).** The HUD summary (layer name, record count (vessels and beacons), data age and error text, but no positions) goes to OpenAI whenever `OPENAI_API_KEY` is set.
- **MCP.** `panel_request` can reach `/api/local-receivers/vessels` whenever `LOCAL_AIS_FEEDS` is set, even with the layer off, so a connected MCP client can read the vessel snapshot.
- Liveness trusts the receiver's own `last_signal`: a receiver serving a frozen `ships.json` would read live.

What each step stops: voice off stops the voice reads and screenshots; disabling the layer stops the voice and HUD vessel data but not the MCP route; unsetting `OPENAI_API_KEY` stops the HUD summary but not voice on Codex OAuth; unsetting `LOCAL_AIS_FEEDS` stops the route and the layer. The docs say the same.

## Voice prompt budget

The manifest entry is trimmed to keep the voice prompt inside its ceiling: the alias is `local ais`, only speed, course, name, MMSI and beacon kind are exposed, and there is no destination. The two voice schema pins were re-derived with a comment, as the Local ADS-B change did. This PR adds no prompt text, and headroom against the 56,500-character ceiling is 4 characters with Overpass on (759 without). The next voice-prompt change will need to make room.

## Machine-translated strings

Every Local AIS string in all 13 non-English locales (zh-Hant included) was machine translated and needs a native check, most of all the vessel nouns and plural forms:

- `{count} vessels heard` (plural forms per locale)
- `feeds {names} rejected` (plural forms per locale)
- `Validated` and `Beacon type` (labels on the entity card), `Note` and the beacon caveat sentence (`Heard by your receiver. Test transmissions are common, this is not a verified emergency, and whether it is active or a test is unknown.`)
- `Local AIS`, `Local AIS receiver unavailable`, `not configured`, `no recent messages`
- `Position approximate (AIS type 27)`, `Position not yet validated by the receiver`
- Beacons: `AIS-SART beacon`, `Man-overboard (MOB) beacon`, `EPIRB beacon`, `AIS distress beacon`, `Distress or test beacon heard by your receiver`, `Test transmissions are common. This is not a verified emergency.`, `Active or test status: unknown`, `{count} beacons heard` (plural forms per locale) and `beacon`. The wording of the safety lines in particular needs a native check. The es, fr, ru, it, pt and uk card titles are capitalised; Arabic uses a transmitter word (مرسل), not the lighthouse word, for a beacon, and Italian uses "radioboa" (a distress radio buoy, feminine, so "ricevuta" in the receiver line), not "radiofaro" (a navigation light); those terms and the agreement in particular need a native check.

zh-Hant is generated from zh-CN with `npm run i18n -- --zh-hant`.

## Out of scope

- A map layer for AISStream or any hosted AIS service (this is local receivers only).
- Showing SAR aircraft (classes 9 and 10): they stay filtered.
- Closing the map-based paths for a flagged fix (screenshots, the pointer's screen position, a cursor beside the marker, the view's camera position). The guarantee is reworded instead.
- Multi-receiver deduplication beyond keeping the newest row per MMSI.
- Reading AIS-catcher over anything but its `ships.json` endpoints (no NMEA, no sockets, no radio samples).
- Changing how Local ADS-B or the shared local-receiver transport behave.
- Trimming the voice prompt elsewhere to regain headroom.

## Screenshots

All data shown is synthetic, from a local test feed (fake MMSIs 200000001 to 200000010, one test AIS-SART 970000001, placed around an open-ocean test point). No real vessel or place.

1. Local AIS layer on the globe, with its status row in the Layers panel ("1 feed live · 10 vessels heard · 1 beacon heard"):
   <!-- drag 01-local-ais-layer-globe.png here -->
2. A vessel card (TEST VESSEL 4), with the Context panel:
   <!-- drag 02-vessel-card.png here -->
3. The AIS-SART beacon card, showing the caveat "Test transmissions are common. This is not a verified emergency.":
   <!-- drag 03-sart-beacon-card.png here -->
4. The layer is off by default (Layers panel, before it is turned on):
   <!-- drag 00-layer-off-default.png here -->

## Recording

About 28 s, 1.6x speed, no audio. The layer goes on, the view zooms to the test area, a vessel card opens, then the beacon card opens. All data is synthetic, from a local test feed.

## What this changes

Adds an opt-in **Ports & terminals** layer (Infrastructure group): a global reference map of the NGA World Port Index (Pub 150), served through a fixed-origin server proxy to the US DOE NETL government-hosted ArcGIS mirror. Implements the reference-data phase of #1779. Field-by-field sourced commercial enrichment (operator, ownership, throughput, capacity) is a separate follow-up: #1904.

- Markers use stable `wpi:<number>` IDs. Selecting one opens a source-linked card with name, country, UN/LOCODE and container / solid bulk / oil / LNG flags shown as Yes, No or Unknown.
- Country filter and affirmative-only facility filter in the data-layer panel. Unknown never becomes No. Filters are session-local.

- The server bounds, caches (24 h, 7 d max stale) and labels complete, partial, stale and unavailable states. The browser cannot choose the upstream URL.
- Share token `03` carries the layer on/off state only.
- A bad source row never sinks the snapshot, except an invalid or out-of-order `objectid` (a system-managed field), which still returns 502. The live NETL layer has 3,824 rows: 3,820 are served and 4 are skipped and counted (2 repeated WPI numbers, 400 and 49460, where the first row in source order is kept and fields are never merged; 2 fractional WPI numbers, 49454.5 and 9510.1). title: fix(traffic): fall back to TomTom Orbis flow tiles when the key is refused
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #1809. TomTom keys are assigned products, and the traffic proxy only called the TomTom Maps flow tile endpoint (`traffic/map/4/tile/flow/relative`). A valid key that is not assigned that product gets HTTP 403 there, so live traffic never loaded and the layer reported "TomTom upstream unreachable".

- **Proxy fallback** (`server/providers/traffic.js`): the TomTom Maps endpoint is still asked first. On 403 the proxy asks the TomTom Orbis Maps one (`maps/orbis/traffic/flow/vector/tile/{z}/{x}/{y}?apiVersion=2`) and keeps whichever answered until the key changes or the process restarts. Keys that work today see no change.
- **Decoder** (`src/layers/traffic/flowDecode.js`): Orbis tiles keep the `Traffic flow` layer but rename properties. `relative_speed` is read as `traffic_level`, and `road_category` (with `_link` ramps) is mapped onto the `road_type` names the layer classifies roads by. Service roads and tracks are dropped. Nothing downstream changes.
- **Rejected key**: when both endpoints answer 403, tiles answer `403 {error:'key_rejected'}`, the panel shows "TomTom key rejected" (13 locales), `/api/tomtom/status` reports `keyRejected: true`, and upstream is left alone for five minutes. Before, every tile was retried and counted against the daily tile budget.

### Not verified

- The Orbis path has not run against a real TomTom key. The request shape and tile schema come from TomTom's [Orbis v2 vector flow tiles reference](https://docs.tomtom.com/traffic-api/documentation/tomtom-orbis-maps/v2/traffic-flow/vector-flow-tiles) and [migration guide](https://docs.tomtom.com/traffic-api/documentation/tomtom-orbis-maps/v2/product-information/migration-guide). Without a key, the Orbis v2 URL answers 401, and 403 `InvalidApiVersion` when `apiVersion` is missing.
- Every Orbis line is treated as one travel direction (`coverage: 'one_side'`), from the docs' description of `part_of_two_way_road`. If Orbis sends one line for both directions, vehicle density on those roads would be halved. This needs a look at a real tile.
- No Orbis fixture tile is committed; the decoder tests build tiles in the Orbis schema by hand.

`npm run doctor` still reports "live TomTom flow" whenever a key is present; that is left for a follow-up.

## How I verified it

- [x] `npm run build`
- [x] `npm test` (15,846 pass, 0 fail)
- [ ] `npm run test:track` (dev server running)
- [ ] Feature gate for the area I touched: `node scripts/qa-traffic.mjs` not run

Also `npm run format:check`, `npm run i18n` (all locales complete) and `npm run check:boundaries`.

New tests: `src/layers/traffic/flowDecode.test.mjs` (both schemas), three proxy tests in `src/tooling/environmentProviders.test.mjs` (fallback and endpoint memory, rejected key and its expiry, ordinary upstream failure stays on one endpoint), and the `key_rejected` reason in `src/data/traffic.test.mjs`.

## Docs

- [x] `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md` updated and a `changelog.d/<pr-number>-<slug>.md` fragment added, or this PR doesn't change runtime behaviour

title: Space stations: follow-ups from the #1767 review
body:
Follow-ups from the review of #1767 (items 3 to 10), plus three related bugs found while checking them. Each fix comes with a test that fails on main.

**Tracking and rings**
- **Docking is judged again while tracked:** every second, and after each catalog update. Once docked, an object stays so until 15 km apart, so a pair whose elements swing about the 5 km radius does not flip. The station model's own docked set, which the Cockpit's mount reads, holds the same way. A vehicle that undocks while tracked gets its own ring back, and drops the ISS ring and the STATION and LIVE sections. One that docks hands its ring to the ISS's. A panel left in Manual goes back to Automatic when the station drops.
- **A catalog update keeps the tracked ring.** The 5-minute rebuild cleared every ring and rebuilt only the ISS's, so any other tracked satellite lost its ring and its dot was shown again under the tracked one. The dense load after it does the same.
- **Every orbit ring is built by the Orbits setting.** Rings already followed it on toggle, re-enable and Cockpit release, but were created shown whatever it said. The station close-up's restore follows it too.
- **A ring baked again keeps whether it shows, and its alpha.** The 30-minute rebake brought back a class-hidden ISS ring and a ring hidden by the close-up or the Cockpit.

**Station model**
- **A joint set by hand before the model is posed takes its angle once it is,** on the ISS and on Tiangong's arms.
- **A station whose orbit will not propagate gives back every dot it stood in for** (its own, the docked ones and the ring), as an unloaded model does. In range the model is kept until the orbit propagates again.
- **`hideInCockpit` is removed.** No station set it, and the comments in `cockpitSubject.js` describe today's behaviour.

**Telemetry**
- **A live relay short of an array or radiator joint reads "Telemetry incomplete · computed values"** (amber), not "unavailable". A whole pose is kept for its 20 s across partial answers and relay reconnects. "No signal since" shows the last live answer.
- **The relay admits 240 requests a minute per address (about 20 tabs) and 12,000 in all.** Before, it was 60 and 1,200, so behind a reverse proxy or the Docker bridge, where every browser shares one address, an instance fit five tabs. The relay counts in one-second buckets of its own (a clock stepped back starts a fresh minute), and the shared limiter is unchanged. A refusal is a 429 with `Retry-After`. The items' JSON is encoded again only when a value changes.
- **The client reads a 429 as busy:** it waits for `Retry-After` plus jitter and shows "Connecting to telemetry…", not "unavailable".
- **The STATION view is built only when something it shows changes,** not every frame. 600 frames used to give 600 builds for 9 changes.

The new string is translated in every locale; zh-Hant is generated from zh-CN.

**Checks:** `npm test` passes, except the tests that also fail on a pristine `main` checkout on Windows. `check:boundaries`, `i18n`, `format:check` and `build` pass.

title: fix(satellites): stop requesting the CelesTrak sar group, which does not exist
body:
## What

The Satellites layer row reads **DEGRADED** with "1 CelesTrak group unavailable" (GEV Hosted product review, item 7).

## Cause

Since #1558 the core catalog asks CelesTrak for `GROUP=sar` on every five-minute update. CelesTrak has no `sar` group: its Weather and Earth Resources section lists Weather, Earth Resources, Search & Rescue (`sarsat`), Disaster Monitoring, TDRSS, ARGOS, Planet and Spire. The proxy gets no TLE lines back, answers 502, the layer counts one failed group and `getStats()` returns `status: 'degraded'`. It never clears, because the group fails again on the next update. Each failed read also puts the whole TLE feed into a 60 s cooldown.

## Change

Remove `sar` from `CATALOG_GROUPS`, the client group allowlist, the proxy's `coreGroups` and the group-to-class table, and update the tests and `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md`. Ten groups load instead of eleven.

## Checks

- `node --test src/layers/satellites/*.test.mjs src/tooling/space*.test.mjs src/data/satellite*.test.mjs`: 245 pass.
- `npm run format:check` and `npm run i18n` pass.
- **Not checked live.** The session that wrote this could not reach celestrak.org, so the missing group is established from CelesTrak's published group list, not from a request. Before merging, open `https://celestrak.org/NORAD/elements/gp.php?GROUP=sar&FORMAT=tle` (expect an "Invalid query" answer), or look for `[Data:Satellites] Groups failed or empty: sar` in the browser console on main.
- Build, `npm run test:track` and a browser check are left to a maintainer.

## Note

Radar imaging satellites that CelesTrak files only under `active` (not under `resource`) are not in the core catalog. That was already the case, since the `sar` read never returned anything.

title: Releasing a tracked satellite clears its focus dimming
body:
## What this changes

Releasing a tracked satellite could leave its focus dimming behind. Every icon inside a rectangle at the centre of the screen (planes make it obvious) stayed at 25% opacity once the camera zoomed out past the old follow distance, until something else was selected, Satellites was turned off, or the page reloaded.

`_clearTracking` (`src/layers/satellites/tracking.js`) cleared the focus rectangle, then told the camera to stop following, and only after that marked the satellite released. The Cockpit entry button listens for follow changes and reads the tracked satellite's position at once; with the satellite still marked tracked, that read published the rectangle again, and nothing cleared it afterwards. This started when the orbital view (#1559) made the entry button read the satellite's position.

The satellite is now marked released before the camera hears of it, so a listener reading mid-release gets nothing and publishes nothing. The release steps before that point use the saved id. Planes, military aircraft and ships were not affected and are unchanged.

title: Voice Cockpit entry no longer switches Contacts on
body:
## What this changes

Voice "enter cockpit" no longer switches Contacts on. Before, every voice entry switched Contacts on first (four layers plus dense detection), and leaving Cockpit never switched it off, so a person who only asked for Cockpit was left with Contacts' layers, range rings and detection boxes, at about three times the frame work. Cockpit does not need Contacts; the COCKPIT button never used it.

- Plain voice entry goes through the same path as the COCKPIT button and changes no layer, Context mode or detection.
- Targeted entry ("cockpit in a military helicopter") used Contacts' next-contact navigation to find its aircraft. It now searches that layer's own aircraft near the followed aircraft (or the ground under the camera), respecting the person's filters, and follows the nearest match; an aircraft already followed that matches is kept.
- If the request names a military class and Military Flights is off, it is switched on as a plain layer, entry waits for its first data, and if entry then fails the layer is switched off again. A layer the person already had on stays on.
- The class filter is now one shared function used by this search and by Contacts navigation.

## How I verified it

- [x] `npm test` (no failures). New tests: entry, successful or not, changes no Context mode or layer; a military entry waits for a just-switched-on layer's first data; a failed entry switches off only the layer it switched on; the search never asks for hidden aircraft; class search cases.

title: Show JTWC cyclones: western Pacific, Indian Ocean and Southern Hemisphere
body:
## What this changes

The cyclone layer only knew the US National Hurricane Center and Central Pacific Hurricane Center, which cover the Atlantic and the eastern and central North Pacific. Storms in the western Pacific, the Indian Ocean and the Southern Hemisphere (for example a South Pacific cyclone near Fiji) never appeared, and an empty layer read as "no cyclones anywhere".

This adds the Joint Typhoon Warning Center (JTWC), whose warnings are US government work and need no key:

- `server/providers/jtwc.js` reads JTWC's warnings feed and, per storm, its warning data and Google Earth overlay. `/api/cyclones` merges them with NHC's; a storm both centres list shows NHC's advisory.
- JTWC is read under its own deadline and never fails, delays or stales the NHC answer; a JTWC outage keeps its last good storms. One unreadable storm is skipped, not the whole feed.
- JTWC publishes no cone. Its 34-knot wind swath is drawn as its own "34-knot wind danger area", dashed and labelled for the selected storm; the cone is optional.
- JTWC storm cards say that the regional centre's warning is the official one, and that JTWC winds are 1-minute averages, higher than many regional services quote.
- Each storm now ages out on its own (12 h for NHC, 13 h for JTWC) instead of one old advisory staling every storm.
- Danger areas that cross 180° are wrapped, not dropped.
- Source and coverage wording names both centres, in every locale. Formation alerts are not included.

## How I verified it

- [x] `npm run build`
- [x] `npm test` (no failures). New tests cover the JTWC parsers against real warning products, the merge (NHC wins), per-storm ageing, a hanging or failing JTWC leaving NHC unchanged, a bad storm skipped, a ring crossing 180°, the danger area drawing and the card note.

title: Lines can fade with the age of their points, drawn by the renderer on the GPU
body:
Lines can fade with the age of their points, drawn by the renderer on the GPU, so a moving trail is not re-sent each frame.

## What

- `LineItem.ageFade` (`LineAgeFade` in `src/render/contract/draw.d.ts`), behind a new capability `lineAgeFade`:
  - `times`: one epoch-ms time per position, on the scene clock (`frame.setTime`)
  - `windowMs`: the age a point fades over
  - `alphaFloor`: alpha × `mix(alphaFloor, 1, smoothstep(0, 1, recency))`
  - `squaredAlphaFloor` (optional): alpha × `mix(squaredAlphaFloor, 1, recency²)` as well
  - `widthFloor` (optional): width × `mix(widthFloor, 1, recency)`
  - recency is `1 - clamp((now - time) / windowMs, 0, 1)`, running evenly between positions
- Time passing changes the drawing, not the line: a line whose points stay put is never sent again. New times with new positions are an ordinary update. A renderer without the capability draws the line unfaded.

## Cesium

- Listed where the context has floating-point textures.
- An aged line's material wraps its style's: it reads the points' times from a small RGBA float texture (each texel a point's place along the line and its time) and the scene's time from a uniform set once a frame, and fades per fragment. Draped lines look up by length (binary search), others by vertex index. Width narrowing is drawn by discarding outside the narrowed half-width.
- Undraped aged lines stay in their polyline collection and move and recolour in place; segment-coloured lines, depth-fail and draped lines carry the fade on each of their primitives.
- Old materials and textures are released with their primitives.

## Tests

- `src/render/cesium/drawLineAges.test.mjs`: texel data, the scene clock moving `ageNow` over 120 frames with the same polyline and material, in-place moves and recolours, segment pieces, draped lines, material release, capability off and invalid fades refused.
- Conformance check `draw.lines.ageFade` (draped, undraped and narrowed lines read back for pixels as time moves on and back). `npm run qa:conformance`: 145 passed, 0 failed, 1 skipped (`query.heights`, as before).
- `npm test`: 15905 tests, 0 failed. `format:check`, `check:boundaries`, `library:check` pass.

The tab now only presents the Context panel, which shows the tracked aircraft's card as on desktop. The tab bar's open callback had no other use and is removed.
