title: A line can show only the part of it within a time span of the scene clock
body:
A line can show only the part of it within a time span of the scene clock, so a moving trail can be sent once as its whole track and cut by the renderer as time runs.

## What

- `LineAgeFade.showMs` (`src/render/contract/draw.d.ts`), behind a new capability `lineTimeWindow`:
  - only the part of the line whose time (interpolated along it, as the fade's is) lies in `[now - showMs, now]` is drawn; parts after the scene clock, or older than `showMs`, are not drawn nor picked
  - the cut runs along the line, not at a position, and follows `frame.setTime` without the line being sent again
  - `Infinity` cuts at now alone; `showMs` must be positive
- Without `showMs` the fade from #1892 is unchanged. A renderer without the capability ignores `showMs` and draws the whole line.

## Cesium

- Listed with `lineAgeFade` (where the context has floating-point textures).
- The aged line material discards a fragment by its interpolated time against the scene time it already reads each frame (one more uniform, `ageShow`), draped or not. A new span is a new look; time passing touches only the uniform.

## Tests

- `src/render/cesium/drawLineAges.test.mjs`: the span's uniform (seconds, endless, none, port without the capability), a windowed line over 120 frames keeping the same polyline, material and positions, the capability off drawing it whole, and bad spans refused.
- Conformance check `draw.lines.timeWindow` (draped and undraped lines read back for pixels: drawn within the span, not after now, not before it, as time moves on and back, never sent again). `npm run qa:conformance`: 146 passed, 0 failed, 1 skipped (`query.heights`, as before).
- `npm test`: 15905 tests, 1 failed: `src/dockerTrustedPeers.test.mjs` ("Compose resolves shell and project dotenv policy"), which fails the same on `main` in this environment. `format:check`, `check:boundaries`, `library:check` pass.

title: A line can be drawn as several runs (`breaks`)
body:
A line can be drawn as several runs, so many lines that share one style can be sent as one item: thousands of moving objects' trails as one line, say, which the renderer then handles as one item instead of thousands.

## What

- `LineItem.breaks?: number[] | Uint32Array` (`LineBreaks`, `src/render/contract/draw.d.ts`), behind a new capability `lineBreaks`:
  - each break is the index `i` of a position that starts a new run, sorted, `0 < i < positions.length`
  - the segment from position `i - 1` to `i` is not drawn nor picked, and the line does not join across it: each run has two ends of its own, capped and joined as a line of its own would be
  - `segmentColors` and `segmentShow` stay one a pair of positions (`j`: from position `j` to `j + 1`); the entry of a pair across a break is ignored
  - `ageFade.times` stays one a position; `revealFraction` runs along all the runs, in order, as one length (the gaps have none)
- It is an optimisation, in the optional list of `docs/RENDERER-CONTRACT.md`: a renderer without it is never sent `breaks`, and is sent the same lines as an item a run instead, drawing the same picture.

## Cesium

- Listed always. A line in runs draws a piece a run: undraped, a polyline each in the set's own polyline collection; draped, a ground polyline each; with a depth-fail style or in the sky's frame, a primitive each. Each piece takes its own points' times (age fade and time window), its share of the reveal, its segment colours and an arrow head at its end, and is picked as the line.
- A draped solid line with segment colours stays one ground instance a segment, none across a break. A segmented line of any other kind is a piece a segment, none across a break.
- Where the scene cannot drape, each run is drawn over the surface and hidden past the horizon, as a line of one run is.
- Colours and shows change in place; new positions, times, reveal or breaks draw the line anew. Bad breaks (not whole, not increasing, out of range) are refused before anything changes.
- Each run is cut by time (`ageFade.showMs`) by its own points' times, whatever order the runs' times come in.
- The stub honours `breaks` in its picks and reveal.
- Fixed on the way: a plain line drawn in a polyline collection after an aged one was the page's first material of its style's type stopped the frame (`material._uniforms[uniform] is not a function`). Cesium keeps a material type's uniform names from the first material of it, and a part of a composite material has them renumbered; a part's type is now made on its own first.

## Tests

- `src/render/cesium/drawLineBreaks.test.mjs`: a polyline a run (packed positions and `Uint32Array` breaks too), arrow heads on each run, segment colours and shows per pair with nothing across a break and recoloured in place, each run's own age times, the reveal along the runs, draped runs and draped segment instances, a draped line whose first run is later than its second (each run timed by its own points), the overlay where the scene cannot drape (culled past the horizon), breaks changed or not, the capability off, and bad breaks refused.
- `src/render/cesium/drawLineAges.test.mjs`: an aged line made first leaves its style's type named as a plain one is, and a plain line beside it draws.
- Conformance check `draw.lines.breaks.timeWindow`: 3D and draped lines in runs whose first run is later than their second, each run drawn and cut by its own times as the clock moves, nothing between them.
- Conformance check `draw.lines.breaks`: 3D and draped lines, with segment colours and without, read back for pixels and picks: each run drawn in its colour and picked, nothing drawn or picked between them (it fails with the breaks ignored). `npm run qa:conformance`: 148 passed, 0 failed, 1 skipped (`query.heights`, as before).
- `npm test`: 15917 tests, 0 failed. `format:check`, `check:boundaries`, `library:check` pass.

title: Context UI: Remove the fallback flight when Cameras turns on
body:
## What this changes

If you deselected a camera while Cameras was turning on, the shell could select another camera when enabling finished and fly there if the view was free. This removes that fallback and its debug logging. Normally, Cameras still picks a provisional opening camera and updates that choice as the view settles, until you pick a camera yourself.

## How to review

1. Press **C** to turn on Cameras. The layer chooses an opening camera while the globe stays put.
2. Turn Cameras on while following an aircraft. The same aircraft stays followed.
3. Before picking a camera, pan toward another one. The opening selection updates after the view settles. Click **FOCUS** to try the separate camera flight.

## How I verified it

- [x] The eight focused suites below passed 293/293 on Node 24.22.3. A focused test holds layer enabling open, clears the camera selection, and verifies that the shell neither reselects nor flies when enabling settles. That test fails on main.

- [x] In a local browser test with two synthetic cameras and one synthetic aircraft, normal enabling held the view and preserved aircraft follow on both main and the earlier revision. Panning updated the provisional camera. Clicking **FOCUS** flew to that camera and kept it selected.
- [x] `npm run build` and `npm test` passed on the pushed tree. The full suite passed 15,924 checks, with five skips and no failures or cancellations.
- [ ] The supplemental `node scripts/qa-camera-controls.mjs` run passed 13 checks on main and on the earlier revision. Both runs then timed out waiting for the second camera's decoded frame.

```sh
node --import=./build/registerVue.js --test \
```

title: Context UI: A click on a camera's projected image opens that camera's card
body:
## What this changes

Clicking a camera's projected image or view ray now opens that camera's Context card. Previously Context looked up the geometry's ID instead of the camera's ID, so it showed the layer name and stayed on “Acquiring frame…”. Now the card shows the camera's name and its frame when available.

- Camera cards for loaded records carry the camera's name and position, including cards opened from the camera icon. The card uses that position for **Fly to** and passes it to **Ask GEV**.
- With Cameras on and the camera loaded, the existing entity-targeted voice `fly_to_location` and Ask's `describeTargetEntity` can use the camera catalog lookup. I verified those paths by reading the callers. The browser checks below exercised the camera card and frame.
- Clicking a camera icon still activates that camera in the CCTV panel. The optional `recordIdForPick` hook leaves other layers' pick handling unchanged.
- If a layer's pick mapper throws, Context still looks up the original pick ID and keeps its name and coordinates when it resolves.

## How to review

| Read first | What to check |
| --- | --- |
| `src/layers/cctv/pickIds.js`, `src/layers/cctv/lifecycle.js` | The pick owner and camera mapper use the same geometry ID pattern. |
| `src/layers/cctv/controls.js`, `src/data/pickedContext.js` | Once the layer resolves a geometry ID, Context uses the camera ID for the lookup and the card. |

Turn on Cameras and select one with a projected image on the globe. Click the image and then a visible view ray. Both should open the named camera card and show its frame when available.

## How I verified it

The build, full suite, tracking, and projected-image and view-ray browser checks ran on this tree. The camera-icon check ran on an earlier revision.

- [x] `npm run build` passed.
- [x] `npm test` on Node 24.22.3 for the final candidate. 15,935 passed, 4 skipped, with zero failures or cancellations across 15,939 tests.
- [x] `npm run test:track` passed all 111 stock assertions in native Chrome with bundled imagery and the repository's terrain fixture.
- [x] In a local browser test with two synthetic cameras and no provider keys, the projected image and a view ray opened the matching named card and frame. The adjacent camera-icon check passed on the earlier revision.

The resolver regression in `src/data/pickedContext.test.mjs` uses the real CCTV controls and the same pick ownership rule that the layer registers. On main, the resolver returns the raw projection ID. A separate case exercises a mapper that throws. `src/layers/cctv/pickIds.test.mjs` covers helper roles, plain IDs, IDs with dashes, unknown cameras and roles, and gizmo IDs.

## Known gaps

## Docs

title: Quantized-mesh terrain can supply its tiles through `fetchTile`, like imagery
body:
`xyz` imagery can already fetch its own tiles through `fetchTile`. This gives
`quantizedMesh` terrain the same option.

- `TerrainSpec` (`src/render/contract/globe.d.ts`): `quantizedMesh` takes an
  optional `fetchTile({ tile, url, signal })`. It returns a `TileFetch`, the
  same type imagery uses. `tile` is in the terrain's own tiling scheme, rows
  counted from the north. `url` is the tile's URL as Cesium resolved it. The
  `bytes` are the uncompressed tile.
- Cesium still does the rest:
  - it reads `layer.json` at the spec's `url`, with the retry policy as before;
  - it decides which tiles a frame needs;
  - it schedules and cancels their requests through its `RequestScheduler`;
  - it decodes the meshes.

  Only the bytes of each tile come from `fetchTile`
  (`src/render/cesium/terrainTiles.js`). The resource handed to
  `CesiumTerrainProvider.fromUrl` keeps that kind through Cesium's clones, so
  every tile resource derived from it goes through `fetchTile`.
- Each kind of answer:
  - `missing` fails the tile, so Cesium draws the parent's terrain there.
  - `defer` asks again after 250 ms.
  - A cancelled request aborts the `signal`.
- Without `fetchTile`, terrain loads exactly as before.

Tests:

- `src/render/cesium/terrainTiles.test.mjs` drives a real `CesiumTerrainProvider`
  over a served `layer.json` and a one-triangle mesh. It covers:
  - the tile and URL handed to `fetchTile`, including the tms row flip;
  - requests made without a `Request`;
  - missing, deferred and cancelled tiles;
  - resources that are not tiles fetching as before.
- `globe.test.mjs` checks `setTerrain` wiring and that a `fetchTile` that is
  not a function is refused.
- `npm test`: 15924 tests, all pass after the follow-up that moved off a private
  Cesium field. `check:boundaries` and `format:check` are clean.

title: feat(aircraft): draw far-away aircraft as shaded sprites seen from the camera's angle
body:
## Why

Far-away aircraft were flat, top-down silhouettes turned along their course. From above that is fine; from an oblique camera they read as paper cut-outs lying on the ground.

## Before and after

The same grid of synthetic contacts (a class a row, eight courses across) in Flights, camera tilted 55° from straight down.

| Before: flat glyphs | After: view sprites |
|---|---|
| ![Flat glyphs, camera tilted 55 degrees](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view/mazeyar/pr-1903-media/pr-1903/before-tilt.jpg) | ![View sprites, camera tilted 55 degrees](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view/mazeyar/pr-1903-media/pr-1903/after-tilt.jpg) |

Tilted 75°, close to the horizon:

| Before | After |
|---|---|
| ![Flat glyphs, camera tilted 75 degrees](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view/mazeyar/pr-1903-media/pr-1903/before-low.jpg) | ![View sprites, camera tilted 75 degrees](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view/mazeyar/pr-1903-media/pr-1903/after-low.jpg) |

The camera swinging round the grid, 3° a frame. Each sprite is one rendered view, tilted until the next view is the nearer:

![The camera orbiting the grid of view sprites](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view/mazeyar/pr-1903-media/pr-1903/orbit.gif)

| From straight above | From below, looking up | Military Flights (amber tint) |
|---|---|---|
| ![View sprites from straight above](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view/mazeyar/pr-1903-media/pr-1903/after-above.jpg) | ![View sprites seen from below against the sky](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view/mazeyar/pr-1903-media/pr-1903/after-below.jpg) | ![Military contacts as view sprites, camera tilted](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view/mazeyar/pr-1903-media/pr-1903/after-military.jpg) |

## Change

Aircraft are now shaded sprites that show the aircraft from where the camera is.

- **Sheet.** Each aircraft class, and each helicopter rotor frame, is rendered in Blender from a sphere of directions into one image, `public/sprites/aircraft-views.webp`: 302 views a class, 7.5° apart from straight above to 30° below the horizon, 12 blocks, 4096×3648, lossless, 3.1 MB. Sprites are neutral grey with shading, dark glass and a dark edge, so the fleet, tracked and military tints still multiply them.
- **Drawing.** The renderer lays a contact flat on the ground along its course, works out where the eye is in that frame and draws the nearest view, mirrored for the port side. The view is a card standing at the contact, square to the direction it was rendered from, so between views the sprite is tilted (foreshortened and turned) as the aircraft would be. Views are not blended.
- **Contract.** A new `viewSheets` capability, `DrawPort.views(id, sheet)`, and an icon image `{views, first, fallback}`. `src/data/viewSheet.js` holds the layout and the maths in JS and GLSL.
- **Fallback.** A view row draws its flat `fallback` glyph along its course until the sheet has loaded, and for good if it cannot load (a 404, a blocked request, a sheet larger than the context's textures).
- **Where it applies.** Flights, Military Flights (fleet and tracked contact) and Local ADS-B. The TR-3B, airport vehicles, ground stations and Cockpit's far pips stay flat. View sheets are offered on WebGL 2 only; on WebGL 1 the icon shader is unchanged and everything stays flat, as on any renderer without the capability.
- **Tools.** `npm run build:aircraft-views` bakes the sheet from the repo's own fleet models (about 7 minutes, needs Blender). `scripts/qa-aircraft-view-sheet.mjs` writes contact sheets of a bake. `scripts/qa-aircraft-views.mjs` photographs a grid of every class in the app from above, tilted, from below and round an orbit.

## Cost

| | New sprites | Flat glyphs |
|---|---|---|
| Frame, 5,000 contacts (M3 Max, 1500×1000, two runs each) | 5.9–6.1 ms | 5.9 ms |
| GPU memory for the images | about 37 MB (the sheet, luminance + alpha, one mip level) | a share of the icon atlas |
| Download | 3.1 MB, once | none |

Not measured: phones and integrated GPUs, and the one-off decode and upload of the sheet.

## Verified

- `npm test`, `npm run check:boundaries`, `npm run format:check`, `npm run build`, `npm run changelog:check` and `npm run layer-token:check` pass.
- In the app (`scripts/qa-aircraft-views.mjs`, synthetic contacts): every class at eight courses, from straight above, three tilts, three sides and from below, plus a 90° orbit in 1.5° steps; and the same grid with the sheet's request blocked, which draws the flat glyphs.
- The shipped sheet is checked by a test: its size, every pixel grey, and a clear 2 px edge on every cell.

## Known limits

- A helicopter is baked for one side and mirrored for the other, so its tail rotor swaps sides and its rotor appears to turn the other way from the port side.
- The views stop 30° below the horizon; a camera passing straight underneath a contact makes its sprite jump.
- The tracked contact draws the same 64 px cell as the fleet, with no sharper close-up image.
- The sheet's texture is kept for the life of the WebGL context.

title: Ports & terminals: per-field sourced commercial enrichment
body:
Follow-up to #1779 and the World Port Index layer (#1879).

## Context

The WPI layer shows operator, ownership, annual throughput, handling capacity, operational status and expansion as **Unavailable**. NGA WPI does not provide verified, current values for these, and the layer must not guess them or copy a port-wide figure onto a terminal.

## Goal

Add an optional enrichment set that fills those fields only where a reviewed, authoritative, dated record exists.

## Requirements

Each enriched fact must carry:

- the WPI ID it applies to (explicit match, no fuzzy name matching);
- the source URL and publisher, with its licence or reuse terms;
- unit, reporting period and geographic scope (port-wide vs terminal);
- publication date and review date;
- a clear Proposed / Operating distinction, so reported proposed capacity never reads as current.

Facts without all of the above stay Unavailable. Source terms must permit redistribution, or the data is fetched at runtime instead of bundled.

## Out of scope

Routing, navigational advice, live terminal status.

## Acceptance

- A reviewed data file or runtime source with the fields above, validated against WPI IDs.
- The card shows each enriched value with its source, period and date, and still shows Unavailable for the rest.
- Tests cover ID mismatch, missing period or date, proposed capacity and port-wide vs terminal scope.
- `DATA_SOURCES.md` and `src/data/dataCredits.js` list every new source.

Assisted by AI tooling.

title: fix(server): meter OpenSky track backfill and give /tracks its own cooldown (#259)
body:
Fixes #259. Carries #685 by `daikaginza` onto current `main`, with three review fixes on top.

## The issue is real on `main`

`/api/flights/track` (the renamed `/api/opensky-track`) in `server/providers/aircraft/tracks.js` has no limiter and no cooldown on `main` at d9d79ebc4. Its only throttle is a 60-second cache keyed by `icao24`, so every distinct six-hex value is a live `/tracks/all` call at 4 OpenSky credits. `/api/military/track` (the renamed `/api/adsblol/trace`) no longer calls an upstream; it answers a fixed 503, so that half of the issue is already closed.

## What this branch contains

1. **#685 as written** (merge commit 2eef8cd90, all of the contributor's commits kept): an always-on limiter of 30/min per client and 90/min overall on `/api/flights/track`, and a cooldown for the `/tracks/*` credit bucket that a 429 from OpenSky arms. #685 conflicted with `main` only in `scripts/format-scope.json`; the resolution keeps `main`'s list and adds the one new test file.
2. **Review fixes** (7ba53f6d0):
   - The limiter is charged only when the upstream is about to be called. A cached answer or a malformed `icao24` costs OpenSky nothing, and before this change 30 of either in a minute locked a real operator out of backfill.
   - During a cooldown only a cached track (status 200) is replayed past its 60-second window. An old cached 404 or 502 was being served as if current.
   - The 429 that arms the cooldown is no longer cached. It and its repeats now carry `Retry-After` with the time left, the same as every other key.
   - No OAuth token is requested unless the upstream is called.

## Verification

Node 24, on this head:

- `node --test src/openSkyTrackGovernor.test.mjs`: 10 pass, 0 fail (7 from #685, 3 new: cached and malformed requests are free; the arming 429 and its repeat carry the cooldown; a stale cached error is not replayed).
- `GEV_REQUIRE_ALLOCATION_GATE=1 npm test`: 15,927 tests, 15,924 pass, 0 fail, 3 skipped; both allocation groups pass (1 and 14).
- `npm run format:check`, `npm run check:boundaries`, `npm run changelog:check`: pass.

Not run: `npm run test:track` and the browser gates. Nothing here was exercised against live OpenSky.

## Known limit

The limiter caps calls per minute, not per day. At the overall ceiling (90 calls, 360 credits a minute) the daily `/tracks` budget is still reachable before OpenSky answers 429; the cooldown is what stops the spend after that. A daily ceiling would need the bucket's real size, which this PR does not assume.

## Relationship to #685

Same change plus the fixes above. If #685 is updated instead, the fixes are one commit to cherry-pick (7ba53f6d0); close whichever is not used.

title: fix(adsbdb): rate-limit /api/adsbdb and cap its caches (#261)
body:
Fixes #261. Carries #689 by `daikaginza` onto current `main`.

## The issue is real on `main`

`server/providers/aircraft/enrichment.js` on `main` at d9d79ebc4:

- `/api/adsbdb` has no rate limiter. A caller cycling callsigns (`[A-Z0-9]{2,8}`) or hex codes forces one live request to api.adsbdb.com per distinct key.
- `cache.routes` and `cache.aircraft` are plain objects that are only ever added to. The 24-hour TTL decides whether an entry is served, but an expired entry is never removed, and every 404 is stored too. The whole object is written to `.gev-cache/adsbdb.json` every 15 seconds and read back at start.

## What this branch contains

#689 as written (merge commit 48ef645d6, all of the contributor's commits kept), with no further code changes:

- A per-client limiter on `/api/adsbdb`, 720/min by default (`GEV_RATELIMIT_ADSBDB_PER_MIN`; `0` disables, an unreadable value takes the default), checked before the cache, the disk or the upstream is touched.
- Both stores hold at most 20,000 entries, dropping the least recently written first; expired entries are dropped on load; a cache file above 16 MiB is ignored at start.
- The Flights and Local ADS-B enrichment queues treat a 429 as "ask later" rather than as an answer, so a refused aircraft is not left without metadata for the session.

#689 conflicted with `main` only in `scripts/format-scope.json`; the resolution keeps `main`'s list and adds the two new test files.

## Verification

Node 24, on this head:

- `node --test src/adsbdbCacheGovernor.test.mjs src/layers/enrichmentRateLimitRetry.test.mjs src/proxyErrorResponses.test.mjs`: 29 pass, 0 fail.
- `GEV_REQUIRE_ALLOCATION_GATE=1 npm test`: 15,926 tests, 15,923 pass, 0 fail, 3 skipped; both allocation groups pass (1 and 14).
- `npm run format:check`, `npm run check:boundaries`, `npm run changelog:check`: pass.

Not run: `npm run test:track` and the browser gates. Nothing here was exercised against live adsbdb.

## Notes for review

- 720/min per client is sized to two browser enrichment queues at five lookups a second. It bounds an enumerating caller at 720 upstream requests a minute per address (2,160 overall), which is a ceiling, not a small number.
- An entry that expires while the server is running stays in memory until it is overwritten, evicted by the 20,000 ceiling, or dropped at the next start. Memory is bounded either way.

## Relationship to #689

Same change, brought up to date with `main`. Close whichever is not used.

title: feat(vessels): draw vessels as shaded sprites seen from the camera's angle
body:
Stacked on #1903 (it uses that PR's view-sheet renderer). Review and merge #1903 first; this PR's diff is only the vessel work.

## Why

Vessels were flat, top-down hulls turned along their course, like the aircraft before #1903: from an oblique camera they read as cut-outs lying on the water. They were also drawn at one size at every range, so from far out they were larger than aircraft, and a ship at the horizon was as large as one close by.

## Before and after

The same grid of synthetic vessels (a hull shape a row, eight courses across), camera tilted 55° from straight down.

| Before: flat hulls | After: view sprites |
|---|---|
| ![Flat hulls, camera tilted 55 degrees](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view/mazeyar/pr-1907-media/pr-1907/before-tilt.jpg) | ![View sprites, camera tilted 55 degrees](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view/mazeyar/pr-1907-media/pr-1907/after-tilt.jpg) |

Tilted 75°, close to the horizon:

| Before | After |
|---|---|
| ![Flat hulls, camera tilted 75 degrees](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view/mazeyar/pr-1907-media/pr-1907/before-low.jpg) | ![View sprites, camera tilted 75 degrees](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view/mazeyar/pr-1907-media/pr-1907/after-low.jpg) |

Size by range. The whole globe, vessels (blue) and aircraft (white) alternating over the Atlantic:

| Before: vessels larger than aircraft | After |
|---|---|
| ![Whole globe, vessels drawn larger than aircraft](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view/mazeyar/pr-1907-media/pr-1907/before-globe.jpg) | ![Whole globe, vessels drawn smaller than aircraft](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view/mazeyar/pr-1907-media/pr-1907/after-globe.jpg) |

A line of ships from 8 km out to the horizon, camera 5 km up:

| Before: one size out to the horizon | After: shrinking and fading toward it |
|---|---|
| ![Ships out to the horizon, all one size](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view/mazeyar/pr-1907-media/pr-1907/before-horizon.jpg) | ![Ships out to the horizon, shrinking and fading](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view/mazeyar/pr-1907-media/pr-1907/after-horizon.jpg) |

| From straight above | Up close, beside aircraft |
|---|---|
| ![Vessel view sprites from straight above](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view/mazeyar/pr-1907-media/pr-1907/after-above.jpg) | ![Vessels and aircraft up close](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view/mazeyar/pr-1907-media/pr-1907/after-close.jpg) |

## Change

- **Sheet.** Twelve hull shapes (the ten vessel kinds, a dredger and a pilot boat) rendered in Blender into `public/sprites/vessel-views.webp`: 208 views a shape, 7.5° apart from straight above down to the horizon, 4096×2496, lossless, 2.2 MB. Hulls are cut at the waterline and neutral grey, so the kind colours still tint them.
- **Layer.** On a renderer with `viewSheets` a vessel is the view of its hull from where the eye is, with the flat hull as its fallback while the sheet loads or if it cannot load. Aids to navigation keep their upright buoy. A renderer without view sheets draws the flat hulls as before.
- **AIS coverage.** Every ship type code 0–99 maps to a shape in the sheet (`vesselShape`), pinned by a test. Type text such as "Search & Rescue" and "Anti Pollution" is now recognised, which also gives those vessels their right kind colour.
- **Size.** A vessel's icon follows its range from the eye over the range aircraft icons use, and the vessel set recedes toward the horizon with the renderer's defaults, as the aircraft sets do.

  | Range | Before | After | An aircraft |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | 8,000 km and out | 19–25 px | 7–9 px | 10 px |
  | About 2,000 km | 19–25 px | 16–21 px | 31 px |
  | A few km | 19–25 px | 28–36 px | 55–60 px |

- **Tools.** The bake script handles both sheets (`scripts/bake-view-sheet.py`; `npm run build:aircraft-views`, `npm run build:vessel-views`) and refuses a partial bake over a shipped sheet. `scripts/qa-view-sheet.mjs` writes contact sheets of a bake, and `scripts/qa-aircraft-views.mjs` takes `--layer vessels`. The aircraft sheet is byte-for-byte unchanged.

## Verified

- `npm test`, `npm run check:boundaries`, `npm run format:check`, `npm run build`, `npm run changelog:check` and `npm run layer-token:check` pass.
- In the app with synthetic vessels: every shape at eight courses from straight above, three tilts, three sides and at the horizon; the same grid with the sheet's request blocked, which draws the flat hulls; and vessels beside aircraft from the whole globe, 2,000 km, up close and out to the horizon.
- In the app with live AIS around Rotterdam (about 12,000 vessels in the feed), before the size change.
- The shipped sheet is checked by a test: its size, every pixel grey, and a clear 2 px edge on every cell.

Not measured: frame time with the vessel sheet. It draws through the same path as the aircraft sheet (#1903: no measurable change at 5,000 contacts) and adds about 26 MB of GPU memory for its texture (luminance + alpha, one mip level).

## Known limits

- The sailboat and the dredger are not symmetric (the sail, the drag arm). A shape is baked for one side and mirrored for the other, so that detail swaps sides as the camera crosses the centre line.
- The views stop at the horizon, a ship never being seen from below.
- The sheet's texture is kept for the life of the WebGL context.

title: Context UI: Show nearby items and suggested layers in Context
body:
## What this changes

When nothing is selected, Context describes the center of the view and groups nearby items by layer. Zoom in for the local time and weather. Zoom out for loaded counts and nearby items on the visible hemisphere. With all layers off, Context can show the latest counts available in provider caches.

The Inspector and selected cards share a 25–1,000 km radius. An existing 2,500 km setting reads as 1,000 km. Opening **Suggested Layers** focuses the filter in Data Layers and keeps each layer's current setting. On a phone, Layers replaces Context until you switch sheets.

The Inspector shows the actual centre coordinates. City names are identified as nearby when the centre is elsewhere. The clock uses the new point’s own time zone. While it waits, the clock shows UTC and a loading hint. A failed read leaves plain UTC and becomes eligible to retry after one minute. Globe view keeps UTC and daylight without the sundial. The local daylight estimate is fixed for the date, using the point’s civil date when its time zone is known. A Recent Imagery field shows loading while a new catalog search is pending. Recent Imagery separates provider outages from successful empty searches and preserves valid readings during a partial outage. VIIRS previews are labeled as area evidence when coverage at the inspected point is unknown.

## Changed components

- [Inspector](https://github.com/manjunath22466/gods-eye-view/blob/dad544cf53360ad5d8bab46505626c0651bc8ac2/src/ui/views/panels/ViewContext.vue) shows the clock, feed state and counts. [Weather owner](https://github.com/manjunath22466/gods-eye-view/blob/dad544cf53360ad5d8bab46505626c0651bc8ac2/src/ui/viewWeather.js) handles deadlines, retries and cancellation. [Context tests](https://github.com/manjunath22466/gods-eye-view/blob/dad544cf53360ad5d8bab46505626c0651bc8ac2/src/ui/contextPanel.test.mjs) cover the first render after resuming, while [weather tests](https://github.com/manjunath22466/gods-eye-view/blob/dad544cf53360ad5d8bab46505626c0651bc8ac2/src/ui/viewWeather.test.mjs) cover two points in one coarse weather cell and an incomplete host response. [Weather Effects](https://github.com/manjunath22466/gods-eye-view/blob/dad544cf53360ad5d8bab46505626c0651bc8ac2/server/providers/regional/weather-effects.js) keeps exact-point reads in a separate bounded cache so they cannot evict coarse Cockpit readings.
- [Spatial results](https://github.com/manjunath22466/gods-eye-view/blob/dad544cf53360ad5d8bab46505626c0651bc8ac2/src/data/entityContext.js) filters before limiting Nearby rows and matches visible cable and GeoJSON segments even when their vertices are outside the viewport. [Geometry tests](https://github.com/manjunath22466/gods-eye-view/blob/dad544cf53360ad5d8bab46505626c0651bc8ac2/src/layers/submarineCables/records.test.mjs) cover a line crossing the date line and independent cable sections. [Local GeoJSON tests](https://github.com/manjunath22466/gods-eye-view/blob/dad544cf53360ad5d8bab46505626c0651bc8ac2/src/data/localGeojson.analyst.test.mjs) cover a drawn part ID that collides with another feature’s source ID.
- [Cached counts](https://github.com/manjunath22466/gods-eye-view/blob/dad544cf53360ad5d8bab46505626c0651bc8ac2/server/providers/common/layerCounts.js) serves existing provider snapshots. Provider tests cover withheld counts, source timestamps, shared reads during simultaneous satellite count requests, and the trailing 24-hour fire total. [Finder](https://github.com/manjunath22466/gods-eye-view/blob/dad544cf53360ad5d8bab46505626c0651bc8ac2/src/ui/views/panels/LayerFinder.vue) owns the Suggested search and keyboard focus. Its filters also hide rows when an embedder mounts the panel in its own container.
- [Selection and point readings](https://github.com/manjunath22466/gods-eye-view/blob/dad544cf53360ad5d8bab46505626c0651bc8ac2/src/data/entityContext.js) keep distinct source vessels separate when they share an MMSI, retain viewing guidance for Acartia sightings, mark obscured wildlife distances and chat coordinates as approximate, and leave Bhote Koshi drawing height out of geographic facts. [GNSS point readings](https://github.com/manjunath22466/gods-eye-view/blob/dad544cf53360ad5d8bab46505626c0651bc8ac2/src/layers/gnss/index.js) report the selected cell's observation time.
- [Intel HUD](https://github.com/manjunath22466/gods-eye-view/blob/dad544cf53360ad5d8bab46505626c0651bc8ac2/src/ui/stores/hud.js) keeps compatibility with host-supplied HUDs whose visibility callback is optional. The original Bhote Koshi reconstruction stays in its dedicated panel, with its controls visible even when it takes over from expanded Context.

## Try it

1. At globe scale with layers off, open Context. If provider counts are cached, their age appears beside the count. Choose **Open** beside Suggested Layers. Keyboard focus should land on **Suggested**, and none of the suggested layers should switch on.
2. Choose **Show all layers**, then turn on Data Centers and zoom into Paris. Reduce the radius and check the count and Nearby rows. With Street Traffic on, the nearby count is road segments and the globe count is loaded traffic dots.
3. Zoom in somewhere with weather coverage. Pan to a different point and check the clock. It should show UTC and the loading hint until that point's weather and zone are available. No provider key is needed for the bundled Data Centers exercise.

Nearby can use mapped GeoJSON lines, including a dam crest inside the radius when the representative point is farther away. On a remount, worldwide counts keep their cooldown only for the same configured source. Stock search and Suggested Layers use the Finder that owns the displayed list.

A settled pan uses exact viewport and radius inputs. GeoJSON cards keep their source identity through a refresh, including when a numeric and string ID share the same spelling. Anonymous cards keep the same feature where the feed provides enough information to identify it, including when the Data Library reorders two records at the same coordinates. Contacts and the underlying subject exclude each other from their own Nearby results. Viewport and globe results rank a line by its closest visible drawn point, and Recent Imagery includes both edges of the date line in point readings.

Line cards take their website from the selected source feature. Radius results use the same distance cutoff for points and line segments, including near the poles. If a host layer temporarily fails to provide records, other layers remain available and the Inspector retries the failed layer while the view stays still. The Omnibar keeps its ordinary viewport results when an optional point snapshot fails. If the optimized layer snapshot fails, the Inspector starts over with ordinary loaded records when they are readable, including when a lazy snapshot fails mid-read and shows **Unavailable** when neither read succeeds. A successful search can still show zero. Local and globe search list unavailable layers alongside any successful matches. Local field tiles distinguish failed reads, loading and a successful empty result. Traffic cards show translated labels for known flow sources and drop a cleared live reading immediately. Ask shows its referenced item in the composer and the conversation. A retry keeps that reference until the draft is edited or sent.

## How I verified it

- [x] 331 focused tests on the current merge cover the Context Inspector and bridge, refresh cancellation and Fire Perimeters records, rendering and selection.
- [x] `npm run build`. Each of the two Cesium runtime paths matches all 390 installed runtime files byte for byte.
- [x] `npm test` on Node 24 (16,420 passed, four skipped, zero failed or cancelled on retry). The first run hit an unchanged Cesium wall-clock assertion. The test passed on main and this branch in isolation, and passed in the full retry.
- [x] Stock native tracking via `npm run test:track` in headed Chrome with measured Austin terrain and bundled imagery fixtures (111/111 on main and the release candidate).
- [x] Desktop and phone Context, Suggested Layers and pending, resolved and failed local clocks in the production build. On phone, Layers replaces the Context sheet. Context search showed matches and an empty result, then restored the dashboard on clear.
- [x] Both CCTV projection paths played the fixture video and showed the registered camera still in the production build.
- [x] Format, import and package boundaries, changelog, 13 locale catalogs and layer tokens.


- [x] Matched offline browser performance in both orders with three aircraft and two satellites. Animation-frame p95 was 16.7–16.8 ms on both builds in the matched scenarios. Twenty Context open/close cycles produced no net change in page-wide nodes, documents or listeners on either build. Globe count tiles have no equivalent on main.

## Verification limits

The headless offline setup reproduced trail-head and first-frame model-to-billboard failures on upstream and the earlier candidate. Both checks passed in the matched headed terrain run. Browser mode and terrain inputs changed together, so that comparison cannot isolate the cause.

On an earlier candidate, Gemini passed a synthetic text check for asking about the selected vessel. A read-only cable-count question attempted to turn on the layer in one Gemini run. The repeat declined the count. The fixture executed no map changes. OpenAI live routing and spoken “Open Contacts” remain unverified on this PR.

## Existing behavior on main

- A fixed-time Active Fires snapshot can show a Live status in Context without its 24-hour window end.
- The Bhote Koshi locator can show a Live status in Context when its boundary is unavailable.
- At Live, Weather-row Play starts at the beginning of covered weather time. Play in the World Timeline stays live.
- CCTV camera activation requires a short tap. A stationary long press on a camera marker does not activate it.
- Two rapid presses of the Cameras shortcut can land while the first toggle is pending.
- Aircraft Cockpit entry can continue if the card changes while its tracking request is pending.
- Fire Perimeters can keep the prior draw order when an update only reorders existing pieces. Custom source IDs containing line breaks can share one draw key.
- Using Find it and immediately starting a new place search can briefly move the camera to the earlier target before the newer search completes.

## Covered by the Context card follow-up

- An aging-out wildlife sighting can become out of feed while its Nearby card is open. The Context card slice retains the selected record.
- The same slice separately covers the elevation assertion, single count-request watcher, and duplicate selected-card weather and radius controls.

## Docs

- [x] Updated [Current state](https://github.com/manjunath22466/gods-eye-view/blob/dad544cf53360ad5d8bab46505626c0651bc8ac2/docs/CURRENT-STATE.md), [Data sources](https://github.com/manjunath22466/gods-eye-view/blob/dad544cf53360ad5d8bab46505626c0651bc8ac2/DATA_SOURCES.md) and the [release fragment](https://github.com/manjunath22466/gods-eye-view/blob/dad544cf53360ad5d8bab46505626c0651bc8ac2/changelog.d/1908-context-nearby.md).

title: The app opens with the logo turning into the globe over your country
body: ## What this changes The app used to open by fading the loading screen out over a fixed planet view centred on the eastern United States. Now the loading screen's logo turns into the globe: 1. The words fade and the logo glides to the centre of the screen. 2. The eye's arcs grow and fade, as if flying at the viewer. The background clears. 3. The real globe is already drawn behind the pupil at the same size and in the same place, so the drawn planet fades straight into it. 4. The globe spins west to east, growing and slowing, and stops with the whole planet in view over the visitor's country. It does not zoom in to a city. 5. The welcome launcher appears after that, as before. All of it takes about 5 s after the world has loaded. - **Country from the time zone.** The browser's time zone gives the country, or a language's region for UTC. No request is made and nothing leaves the browser. `scripts/build-home-countries.mjs` writes the table (`src/data/homeCountries.js`, 437 zones, 247 countries) from tzdata's `zone.tab`, including the older names ICU still reports (`Asia/Calcutta`), and the Natural Earth countries pack already in the repository. A country stops over the centroid of its largest part (the contiguous United States, mainland France). An unknown zone keeps the current start view. - **Home goes there too.** The title's logo ("Back to live at the starting view") goes back to the same view over the country. - **When it does not play.** A share link, a Stories link, reduced motion and `?intro=0` open with the plain fade, as before. With reduced motion the camera starts over the country without the spin. - **Taking over.** A click, a key or the wheel skips to the end view at once. Any other camera move (a search, a voice command) stops it where it is. - **Globe-in-view recovery waits.** At the far start the globe is about 20 px across, which the recovery took for a camera looking away from the planet; it turned the camera back and cut the opening short. It now waits while the opening plays. - No new UI strings. Berlin time zone, 0 to 5.5 s: The end view for Chicago, São Paulo, Tokyo and Sydney, and the reduced-motion fade (first two frames): ## How I verified it - [ ] `npm run build` - [x] `npm test`: 15,992 pass, 0 fail - [ ] `npm run test:track` (dev server running) - [x] Feature gate for the area I touched: none applies. Checked in headless Chrome on a keyless dev server (no Google 3D tile requests): frames of the whole opening, the end view in five time zones, reduced motion, `?intro=0`, and a click mid-flight landing at the end view (altitude 276,881 km → 23,000 km). `npm run format:check` and `npm run check:boundaries` pass.

title: Colour Fire Perimeters by how recently each area burned
body: ## What this changes Fire Perimeters now shows how recently each burned area was mapped instead of colouring by containment. The layer draws a snapshot of fires and the pieces of their burned area. Each piece is coloured by its age at the snapshot's moment: under 6 h yellow, 6–24 h orange, 1–3 days red, older or unknown dark red. Containment stays on the card. **Source contract.** A perimeter source has one method, `getSnapshot({ signal })`, returning: ```js { at, // the moment shown; null = now fetchedAt, stale, revision, // changes when anything drawn changes note, // the source's line under the legend fires: [{ id, name, acres, containedPct, discoveredTime, updatedTime, lastGrowthTime, anchor: { lon, lat }, … }], pieces: [{ fireId, born, polygons, outline }], } ``` `getSnapshotDetail` is removed. A fire may have no pieces, and a piece whose `fireId` is not in `fires` is dropped. When to read again (a timeline, the camera) is the host's call through the manager's `refreshLayer`, and a host that cancels that read leaves the picture as it was. **WFIGS.** The proxy also requests `poly_PolygonDateTime`; its response format is otherwise unchanged. Each polygon becomes one piece, outlined by all its rings, and is born at `poly_PolygonDateTime`, else at `poly_DateCurrent`. On today's service some perimeters have no `poly_PolygonDateTime`. The fallback moves with any edit to the record, so such a fire can look newly grown after an attribute edit; `DATA_SOURCES.md` and `docs/TOOLS.md` say so. A time up to 10 minutes ahead of the browser clock counts as now; further ahead counts as unknown. **Drawing.** Outlines are drawn apart from fills, so a piece cut from a larger area has no line along the cut. The layer redraws only on a new `revision` or when a piece moves to another age band. A failed read keeps the last picture and the row shows the error. **Card and legend.** Clicking a piece selects its fire, and the card stays while the fire is listed, with or without pieces. The card counts ages from `at` and adds "last growth … ago". The legend has the four age bands, counted by each fire's `lastGrowthTime`, with the source's note below them. **InciWeb.** `createApplicationCatalog({ perimeterOptions: { inciweb: false } })` creates no InciWeb sources, so no InciWeb requests are made, even when the host passes its own. The default is unchanged. For a snapshot with a past `at`, a card links only to an InciWeb incident that began by then: of several same-name incidents, the one that began nearest the fire's discovery, else the fire's complex. A page that fails to load is skipped and the next candidate checked. **Other consumers.** `get_fire_perimeters` filters by pieces, places each fire at its anchor and returns `last_growth`; for a past `at` it also returns `snapshot_at` and treats later times as unknown, as `analyst_query` does. Context's hazard list measures distance to the anchor. Voice queries on the layer return `lastGrowthTime` next to `time`; this changes the pinned voice tool schema, so its two pins are re-derived. ## How I verified it - [x] `npm run build` (without keys) - [x] `npm test`: 15,995 tests, 15,992 pass, 0 fail - [x] `npm run test:track` (dev server running): 109 passed, 2 failed (`trail head`; `arrival · flights`), the same two that fail on `main` - [x] Feature gate: `node scripts/qa-gnss.mjs` (its PICK section clicks a fire perimeter under GNSS cells): 27 passed, 1 failed (`VIEWPORT`, fails the same way on `main`) - [x] `npm run format:check`, `npm run check:boundaries`, `npm run i18n` In headless Chromium on Cesium, without keys: - **Live WFIGS:** 51 fires in 2,070 pieces, drawn near and far; legend 0 / 0 / 4 / 47, which matches a count of the proxy's answer. - **Test source:** one fire in four adjacent pieces, born 2, 10, 30 and 100 hours before a past `at`. They draw yellow, orange, red and dark red, with no line along the cuts. Moving `at` forward recolours them and moves the legend with them. - **States:** a 502 keeps the picture and the row reads `DEGRADED`; a stale proxy answer reads `STALE`; an empty answer draws nothing. The row fits a 390 px viewport in Russian. InciWeb links were not checked live: InciWeb answers 403 to the proxy today, so the catalog route returns 502 and cards carry no link. This happens on `main` too. Links were checked with stub sources instead. ## Docs - [x] `README.md`, `DATA_SOURCES.md`, `docs/TOOLS.md` and `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md` updated, and a `changelog.d/1910-perimeters-growth-age.md` fragment added

title: Page state is kept in classes on the page root; the HUD rests while not displayed
body:
Page state the stylesheets depend on is kept in classes on `<html>` instead of being found with `body:has(...)`, and the Intel HUD does no work while it is not displayed.

## Why

Chrome checks a `:has()` anchored on `body` again after every node added or removed anywhere in the page, and when it does it restyles the whole page (about 640 elements, 6–11 ms each time). Replacing a text node counts, so any readout or counter updated every frame restyled everything every frame. The HUD's readouts did that on every camera move, even while `#intel-hud` was hidden.

## What

- Every `body…:has(X)` rule is now `body…:is(.flag *, X)`. The flag is a class on `<html>` held by the component that owns that state (`src/ui/rail/rootClass.js`: the `v-root-class` directive, and `followRootClass` / `followSelectorRootClass` for the loading screen, the first-run launcher and the left panel stack, which are followed through the DOM so they clear however the element goes). `:is()` takes the specificity of its heaviest argument, so every rule keeps its place in the cascade.
  - Flags: `has-omnibar`, `dock-has-voice`, `omnibar-focus-within`, `omnibar-has-results`, `assistant-voice-mode`, `hud-minimal-active`, `left-panel-open`, `launcher-shown`, `loading-screen-shown`, `has-world-timeline`, `has-locale-picker`.
  - `src/ui/pageRootClasses.test.mjs` fails if a stylesheet anchors a `:has()` on `body`, `html`, `:root` or `&` again, or if an `:is(.flag *, X)` disagrees with the flag map.
- The Intel HUD (`src/hud.js`, `src/ui/stores/hud.js`, `src/ui/views/IntelHudView.vue`) rests while `#intel-hud` is not displayed (a ResizeObserver on it): its timers are cleared, the summary typewriter stops and an in-flight summary is dropped, and readouts are not published. As soon as it is displayed again it publishes the current readouts and starts its timers. `active`, `variant` and `colors` still publish, because other rules and layout code read them.
- Changing readouts update their text nodes in place (`v-text-data`, `src/ui/rail/textData.js`) instead of replacing them.

## Checks

- The built CSS: 4,162 rules identical; the 128 that differ differ only in selector, each `:has(X)` → `:is(.flag *, X)` with equal specificity.
- In Chromium, every flag was compared with the browser's own `body.matches(':has(X)')` on every frame and after every change, across page loads and the loading screen being removed, added, shown, hidden and renamed: 593 checks, 0 mismatches.
- With `#intel-hud` given `display: none`, the HUD made 0 DOM writes in 3 s (6 in 2 s while shown); shown again, its clock read the current time within 300 ms.
- `npm test`, `npm run build` and `npm run format:check` pass. `npm run test:track` fails the same 2 checks as `main` (trail head; display-floor/regime, which depends on timing).

title: Add Hiking Trails and Cycling Routes overlays, and on-screen zoom buttons
body:
## What this changes

Adds two raster overlay layers under Infrastructure, built the same way as Sea Marks and Ski Pistes (#114): one descriptor each in `OSM_OVERLAYS`.

- **Hiking Trails** 🥾: every waymarked hiking route in OpenStreetMap, worldwide (the European long-distance E-paths, national trails, local loops), from Waymarked Trails.
- **Cycling Routes** 🚲: every signed cycle route in OpenStreetMap (EuroVelo, national and regional networks), from Waymarked Trails.

It also adds **+/− zoom buttons** in the bottom-right corner. They run the same `adjust_camera_zoom` action that the omnibar ("zoom in") and voice already use, so zooming inside an orbit or tilt behaves the same way as it does there. Scroll zoom is unreliable on some touchpads, in remote-desktop sessions and in TV browsers; these buttons give those users a way to zoom.

## How I verified it

- [x] `npm run build`
- [x] `npm test` (see note below)
- [ ] `npm run test:track`: not run
- [x] Feature gate: none applies. Checked by hand in the running app on the globe.

Pinned values updated:
- layer registry count, token ledger and its fixtures
- overlay list and catalog counts
- Omnibar `UiButton` count
- voice tool-schema length and digests

Translations for the two names were added in all 12 catalogs, and `npm run i18n -- --zh-hant` was run.

Voice prompt: 56,449 of 56,500 with Overpass, 55,694 without (main: 56,411 / 55,656). To fit, the layer ids are the plain words `hiking` and `cycling` and sit in `SELF_EVIDENT_IDS`, so they add no alias-hint line.

## New layer checklist

**Screenshots**

![Hiking Trails and Cycling Routes on the globe](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ralfjj/gev-trails/main/docs/trails.jpg)

**Recording**

None yet. I can add one if you'd like.

**Proposed category**

Category: Infrastructure, next to Ski Pistes and Sea Marks. These are the same kind of OpenStreetMap-derived raster overlay.

**Data source and licence**

- Source: Waymarked Trails (Sarah Hoffmann), `https://tile.waymarkedtrails.org/hiking/{z}/{x}/{y}.png` and `https://tile.waymarkedtrails.org/cycling/{z}/{x}/{y}.png`
- Licence or terms: route data © OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL.
  - I couldn't find a published tile-usage page for Waymarked Trails; the old `/help/legal` path returns 404.
  - The tiles send `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`.
  - The layers request tiles on demand only: no prefetch, no bulk download, no server-side caching. This is the same as Ski Pistes.
  - If you'd rather have written permission first, I'm happy to ask the maintainer.
- Attribution shown in the app: "Hiking routes © waymarkedtrails.org (Sarah Hoffmann) · Data © OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL)", and the same wording for cycling routes.
- Needs a key? None
- Fetched at runtime, or bundled in the repo: fetched at runtime

- [x] Added a row to `DATA_SOURCES.md`
- [x] Credit is registered in `src/data/dataCredits.js`
- [x] Share-link tokens assigned with `npm run layer-token:next`: `03` hiking, `04` cycling. `beforeLastDigitRows` and the fixture registry now leave both out, as they already do for News, Shipwrecks and Rail.

title: Use case for registerable layers: community add-on packs (Estonia pack, trails pack)
body:
In #1058 you closed the add-on request as not planned and asked for a concrete use case. Here is one, from two packs I've built and published:

- **gev-estonia** (https://github.com/ralfjj/gev-estonia):
  - the Estonian Land Board's national orthophotos as a map stack
  - Tallinn's live buses and trams in Transit
  - Estonian weather stations
  - speed cameras, road conditions and drone zones
  - five historical map overlays (Soviet, interwar, 1944, Tsarist, 1990s aerial), reprojected server-side from Estonia's national grid
- **gev-trails** (https://github.com/ralfjj/gev-trails): hiking and cycling route overlays and zoom buttons. The general part is offered upstream in #1913.

Both are distributed as patches with an install script, pinned to one upstream commit. That works, but it shows what it costs to add a layer from outside:

- **One point layer touches about 11 core files.**
  - The files: `constructCatalog.js`, `sourceComposition.js`, `sources/reference.js`, `layerState.js`, the token ledger, `layerNames.js`, `layerPanel.js`, `weatherPanel.js`, `contextLayerTabs.js`, `entityContext.js` and `voice/layerManifest.js`.
  - It also needs a provider registered in `server/providers/local.js`.
  - A map stack touches 7 more.
- **Two packs collide on shared lines.** Both insert into the same alphabetical registries, so I had to tune the patch context to make them install in either order.
- **Share tokens are a permanent public namespace.** The Estonia pack holds `03`, `06`–`0d`. The trails PR takes `03`/`04` upstream, so the pack and main already disagree on what `03` means in a link.
- **Every upstream commit can break a pack.** Main moves daily, so packs have to pin a commit.
- **The voice prompt has a hard ceiling, and add-ons spend it.**
  - Main sits at 56,411 of 56,500 characters with Overpass.
  - Each layer id appears twice in the Realtime tool JSON, and each map stack once more.
  - The Estonia weather layer had to drop its analyst query fields to fit.
  - The pack's eight newer layers are left out of the voice manifest entirely.
  - An add-on mechanism would need either a separate budget for add-on layers, or a way to leave them out of the model-facing enums. The browser runner could still resolve them by alias.

**A minimal shape that would cover this** (not the n8n-style sandbox #1058 described):

1. **A build-time list of extra layer modules**, along the lines of the virtual-module idea in #138 (`GEV_EXTRA_LAYERS=…`).
   - Each module exports one layer object with the existing interface, plus a small manifest: id, panel group, display name, credit, optional voice aliases and query fields.
   - It can optionally export a server middleware for its `/api/<id>/*` proxy.
2. **The registries read those manifests** instead of needing hand-edits: the panel, names, credits and voice manifest.
3. **A reserved token prefix for add-ons** (for example `x` + an id hash), so add-ons never take tokens from the published ledger.
4. **Map stacks and transit feeds stay core-only for now.** Overlays and point layers cover most add-ons.

Add-ons would be trusted code you choose to install, the same as editing the repo today. There is no sandbox and no remote loading.

If this fits where you want GEV to go, I'm glad to build it as a PR in whatever shape you prefer. If not, the patch packs keep working and I'll keep them pinned.

title: Add local SDR support for ATC audio
body:
**Depends on #1898 (HackRF One WebUSB).** Please merge that PR first. This draft currently includes its commits in the diff against `main`. The [ATC-only comparison](https://github.com/musithang/gods-eye-view/pull/1/files) is available in my fork.

## What this changes

Add receive-only VHF ATC audio to **Radio → Local SDR** on RTL-SDR and HackRF One. The ATC AM mode accepts 25 kHz and 8.33 kHz channel designators and uses the existing browser audio pipeline.

The aircraft card opens the receiver in ATC mode. The bottom of the SDR card offers Tower and Approach presets for airports on the selected aircraft's route, or for a nearby airport when route information is unavailable. A preset retunes an open receiver or prepares the channel for the next connection.

## How I verified it

- [x] `npm run build`
- [ ] `npm test` (full suite)
- [ ] `npm run test:track` (dev server running)
- [ ] Radio feature gate (`node scripts/qa-radio.mjs`)
- [x] SDR tests recovered a known tone from synthetic AM IQ and covered channel validation and switching between AM, FM, and ADS-B.
- [x] Targeted Radio and aircraft-card tests, plus the locale catalog check, passed.
- [x] Chromium with a real HackRF One received live IQ in ATC mode, started audio output, retuned, switched back to ADS-B, and released USB. Intelligible live ATC speech and physical RTL-SDR hardware remain unverified. One retune produced a brief meter reading above 0 dBFS.
- [x] A Chromium check with a synthetic aircraft near JFK verified that the aircraft shortcut opens Radio, the preset list appears at the bottom in ATC mode, and choosing Tower sets the tuner.

## Data source and licence

Airport presets are bundled from the [OurAirports public-domain catalog](https://github.com/davidmegginson/ourairports-data/blob/main/LICENSE). OurAirports is credited in the presets and in Data attribution. The catalog can be incomplete or stale. For Budapest, the app links to the official channel reference. No key is needed.

## Docs

- [x] Updated `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md`, `docs/LOCAL-RECEIVERS.md`, and `DATA_SOURCES.md`.
- [x] Added `changelog.d/1916-local-sdr-atc-audio.md`.

title: Icons keep their glyph under a page-wide .ui-icon rule
body:
The kit's icons are font ligatures under the class `ui-icon`, which is also jQuery UI's sprite-icon class. A stylesheet that brings jQuery UI's rule into the page (some browser extensions inject it into every site) sets `text-indent: -99999px`, `overflow: hidden`, a 16 px box and a sprite background, and every icon button shows empty.

`kit.css` now resets exactly those properties under `.ui-icon.ui-icon`, which outranks the single-class rule wherever it is loaded. The kit never sets them elsewhere, so nothing changes without such a stylesheet.

Checked in a browser with such an extension: the toolbar, rails, search and timeline icons, empty before, draw again.

title: Satellite class pills show their colour and count
body:
## What this changes

The Satellites row in Data Layers showed each satellite class twice: a toggle chip, and under it a separate list of coloured dots with counts. That list is gone. Each class now has one pill:

- **On:** the class's colour (the same colour its satellites draw in), its name, and how many are loaded, e.g. `● IMAGING 424`.
- **Off:** only its name, in a plain pill.

The pills keep the chips' existing font, size and colours, so several still fit on a line.

Clicking a pill, keyboard use (each pill is a toggle button with `aria-pressed`; Space and Enter toggle it and focus stays put) and the saved and shared class choice all work as before.
