title: Moving layers redraw as fast as they move on screen, 3 to 30 times a second
body:
## What this changes

Moving layers no longer hold the globe at the display's refresh rate. Satellites, flights, military flights and vessels drew 100–170 frames a second while they were on, even when nothing on screen moved. Each one now draws as often as its fastest mark in view moves on screen, about half a pixel a draw:

- **Range:** never fewer than 3 draws a second, so animated marks keep moving, and never more than 30, leaving room in the frame for the rest of the scene.
- **Following and steering:** following a contact draws at 30 a second. Steering the camera with a drag, a pinch or the wheel still draws at the display's rate.

Placed flights (positioned through `placeAt`) also get cheaper and smoother:

- **Replans:** each flight's plan now ends at a different time, so the whole fleet no longer replans in the same pass. Far or off-screen flights replan about every 4 s instead of every second.
- **Atlas look-ups:** finding a row's icon in the atlas no longer builds a key from the icon's data URL.
- **Corrections:** a new report that moves a flight eases it there from where it is drawn. Between plans, each one goes on from where the last is drawn.

The trail head of a tracked aircraft now ends where the aircraft is drawn in that frame, not where it was in the frame before.

### Code

- `src/renderPace.js` (new) picks the rate from on-screen speed. `src/renderGovernor.js` takes a rate for each hold (`holdContinuousRender(owner, { maxFps })`), and the loop draws at the highest rate its holders ask for.
- Renderer contract: a draw set's motion clock may say `frames: 'owner'`. That set then asks for no frames for its moving rows or rows written in place, because its owner's pace does. This is in `src/render/contract/draw.d.ts` and `frame.d.ts` (`onHoldsChange`, behind the `holdChanges` capability), the Cesium renderer, the stub renderer and a new conformance check.
- Placed flights: `src/data/aircraftIconLayer.js` and `src/data/aircraftModelLayer.js`. Icon atlas: `src/data/iconAtlas.js`.
- Trail head: `src/layers/flights/motion.js` and `src/layers/military/motion.js`.

### Measured

These are draws a second in Chrome on a still camera:

| View | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Satellites, whole globe | 162 | 6 |
| Satellites, 1,500 km | 114 | 30 |
| Flights, whole globe | 132 | 10 |
| Flights, Europe | 53 | 5 |
| Flights, London | 114 | 9 |

- **Planes:** none moved more than 0.6 px between draws.
- **Placed flights, about 9,500:** icon rows rewritten a second fell from about 1,730 to 69, and the periodic task's CPU time from 40–116 ms to 10–41 ms.
- **London at 200 km:** 30 draws a second, median gap between frames 37 ms, worst frame 38 ms, no jumps.

## How I verified it

- [x] `npm run build`
- [x] `npm test`: 16,042 pass and 1 fails. The failure is in `src/data/firmsProxy.test.mjs`, a network test this branch doesn't touch, and it passes when run alone (3 of 3).
- [x] `npm run check:boundaries`: passes. `src/renderPace.js` is added to the groups whose modules import it.
- [x] Prettier: passes on every changed file except `src/data/detectionRenderDemand.test.mjs` and `src/layers/satellites/classes.test.mjs`, which already fail it on `main`. I didn't reformat them.
- [x] `npm run test:track`, against the dev server on `localhost:4173`, headless SwiftShader:
  - **`main`, 3 runs:** 109–110 pass. Every run fails "trail head: last vertex on the drawn icon", with the worst frame 83–1,414 m off. 2 of the 3 runs also fail "display-floor/regime: the TRACKED grounded contact is floored exactly when the billboard is the visual".
  - **This branch, 5 runs:** 107–110 pass. The same two checks fail as on `main`: the trail head in every run (worst frame 220–950 m off), the display-floor regime in 2.
  - **Unconfirmed:** three other checks each failed once on this branch and never in the 3 `main` runs. They are "display-floor/gate", "display-floor/placement" and "arrival: the drawn nose is right on the settle frame and the first reveal, flights", which timed out at 783 ms against a 500 ms budget.
  - **Trail-head readings:** the check reads the head in its own after-frame callback, so the head it sees is a frame behind in every run. Software-rendered frames there are 250–300 ms apart, with stalls of 2–6 s on both `main` and this branch, so how far off the head reads depends on whether a stall lands inside its 40-frame sample.
- [x] Unit tests are added for each change, and each was checked to fail without its fix.
- [x] Each change was reviewed in rounds, and the whole branch was then reviewed again. That review found that the speed read fell near the end of each plan, which is fixed here.
- Feature gate: none applies beyond `test:track`.

## Docs

- [x] `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md` updated, and a `changelog.d/1919-moving-layers-redraw-pace.md` fragment added.

title: fix(test): batch parallel unit test paths under the Windows argv limit
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #1631. On Windows, `npm test` stopped with `spawnSync ... ENAMETOOLONG` before any test ran, so the unit suite (one of the three pre-PR checks in `CONTRIBUTING.md`) could not run there at all.

Why:

1. `scripts/run-unit-tests.mjs` `runUnitTests()` passes every parallel test path to a single `node --test` spawn.
2. At `1f105a68` that is 1,335 paths. With a quoted `C:\Program Files\nodejs\node.exe` the command line is 47,742 characters, over Windows' 32,767-character `CreateProcess` limit, so Windows refuses to start the process.
3. CI does not show this: the unit-test job runs `npm test` on Linux only, and the Windows job runs `node --test` on a few named files.

The fix:

- New `batchUnitTestFiles(files, budget)` splits the parallel paths, in order, into batches whose spawned command line stays under a 24,000-character budget. The count covers the quoted executable, the shared flags, one space per argument and two quote characters per path.
- `runParallelTestBatches` runs every batch, even after a failure, and returns the first non-zero status. A red run still lists every failing file, as the single spawn did.
- An empty plan spawns nothing, so a bare `node --test` never falls back to default discovery.
- Batching is unconditional, so Linux and macOS run the same path Windows does. On this suite that is 3 batches of 22,698, 22,713 and 2,477 characters.

## Credit

This re-lands @hakarrr's #1635, rebased on current main, with @hakarrr kept as commit author. That PR was closed by its author while it waited for review, after review rounds with @daikaginza. Changes from its last head (`9f920c3b`):

- The overhead also counts the two quotes around the executable path.
- The comments give the current suite size.
- The tests measure a real quoted command line through one helper, instead of repeating the function's own arithmetic.

Thanks also to @Badisheng for the precise #1631 report.

## How I verified it

- [x] `npm run build`: exit 0
- [x] `npm test`: exit 0 on macOS arm64, Node 26.13.1. 3 parallel batches (7,324 + 7,366 + 1,333 tests, 0 failures, 4 skipped) plus both allocation probes (1 + 14 pass). Also exit 0 from a checkout whose path contains a space.
- [ ] `npm run test:track` (dev server running): ran twice against this branch's dev server: 108/111 and 107/111 passed. The failing checks differed between the two runs (trail-head frame tolerance, the 500 ms arrival budget, display-floor regime), on a heavily loaded host. This PR changes only the unit-test runner and its test, which the app never loads, so the served app is byte-identical to main. I'd ask for one re-run on a quiet machine rather than claim green.
- [x] Feature gate for the area I touched: none applies (test tooling only)

Focused test, `node --import=./build/registerVue.js --test src/unitTestRunner.test.mjs`:

| tree | result |
|---|---|
| main + new tests | fails: `run-unit-tests.mjs` does not export `UNIT_TEST_ARGV_CHAR_BUDGET` |
| this branch | 8/8 pass |
| this branch with batching disabled (`batchUnitTestFiles` returns one batch) | 4 fail, the four #1631 tests |

Windows itself is not run here; I have no Windows machine. The evidence is the measured command line: 47,742 characters on main, at most 22,713 per batch on this branch. A Windows confirmation would still be welcome.

## Docs

- [x] `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md` updated and a `changelog.d/1920-windows-unit-test-argv.md` fragment added, or this PR doesn't change runtime behaviour. No runtime behaviour changes (test tooling only); `changelog.d/1920-windows-unit-test-argv.md` is added for the contributor-facing fix.

Prepared with an AI coding agent; reviewed before submission.

title: feat(air-quality): worldwide stations and a computed US AQI
body:
Closes #1291
Closes #1204

This brings together the two community air-quality PRs — worldwide OpenAQ and South Africa from @khanmjk (#1291) and India's CPCB from @m3ayush (#1204), both reviewed by @kvnloo — on current main, and builds one global air-quality layer on top. Their commits are kept as they were, so authorship stays with them.

### What changes

- **One station set.** OpenAQ, India's CPCB and South Africa's SAAQIS are read together and drawn on one map. Where two networks report the same site (within 150 m), the direct national feed wins over OpenAQ's copy, and a rated reading wins over an unrated one.
- **One index worldwide.** The default view is a US AQI that GEV computes per station from its concentrations with the US EPA's breakpoints (it is not an official reading; values above 500 show as 500+). Canada's AQHI is retired, as it covered Canada only; Canadian stations now come through OpenAQ like every other country's. No network's own index is requested or shown.
- **One view per pollutant.** PM2.5, PM10, O₃, NO₂, SO₂ and CO, each on the European Air Quality Index bands (CO on WHO-based bands). One colour scale per view, for stations, clusters, legend and ranking.
- **Clustering at far zoom.** Stations that would overlap draw as one bubble coloured by the mean of its members; a click zooms in, or selects the worst station when they cannot be separated.
- **A slim card in the Weather panel.** Index and pollutant tiles with the band in words, a Stations switch, a one-line "highest in view" list, and the selected station at the top.
- **A model field from the host.** A host can supply a gridded forecast (the contract is in `src/layers/airQuality/field.js`); it draws under the stations, fades as the camera comes close, and puts its forecast on the timeline. Stand-alone Core can read one from a local folder (`AIR_QUALITY_FIELD_DIR`) for development.

### Keys and defaults

- OpenAQ and data.gov.in keys go in Provider Settings. Without keys the layer still turns on, its Layers row says KEY REQUIRED, and the card names the keys to add.
- South Africa is off by default and needs `SAAQIS_ENABLED=1`, since no reuse licence is established for the portal's session API.
- India's values are shown unrated until the units and averaging period of the OGD feed are confirmed.

### For hosts

- Installs with keys and hosts with their own providers are unaffected. A host that relies on the reference source needs the `/api/air-quality` routes or its own providers (or should withhold the layer), since Canada's readings no longer come from the browser directly.
- `createEcccAirQualitySource` and the AQHI helpers are removed; the changelog lists them. A layer's `requiresKeyId` may now be an array.
- Older share links that turned on Air quality now open the US AQI view. Air-quality dots now own their clicks over CCTV count markers, like other owned layers.

### Verification

- Unit tests for every part (merge, US AQI table against the EPA document, clustering, field sampling and blending, the card, keys and failures); the full suite passes apart from main's known Windows-only failures.
- Browser QA scripts: `qa-air-quality`, `qa-openaq`, `qa-south-africa-air-quality`, `qa-india-air-quality`, run with keys unset.
- format, i18n (13 locales), package boundaries, build and changelog checks pass.

The new strings were translated without a native speaker; corrections are welcome.

title: Fire Perimeters: redraw only the pieces that changed
body:
## What

Fire Perimeters redraws only the pieces that changed since the last read, instead of every fill and fire line at once.

- **`pieces[].id`** (optional) joins the snapshot contract: a string, unique among its fire's pieces, that stays the same while the piece's geometry does. The WFIGS source fills it with the record's version (`poly_DateCurrent`, else a hash of the mapping time and outline) and the polygon's place in the perimeter.
- **Diff against the last draw.** With an id on every piece, a read adds new pieces (`upsert`), removes pieces that are gone (`remove`), and upserts pieces whose age band changed with their new colours, in the sets they are already in. A set that loses and gains pieces in one read gets one `set`. A read with nothing changed writes nothing, with or without a `revision`.
- **Small sets, oldest first.** Pieces go into the newest draw set of each kind until it is full (fills: 8,000 polygons, lines: 2,000), then a new set starts. Only the newest set takes new pieces, so a step rebuilds small sets only. Fills are written before lines, and a new fill set re-makes the existing line sets after it, so every fire line is still drawn over every fill, as before. The overlap order of fills matches a full redraw of the snapshot, whatever reads came before.
- **Item ids from piece ids:** `fire-perimeter:<fire>:<piece>:<n>` and `…:<piece>:line:<n>` (piece URI-encoded). Each item carries its fire in `meta.fireId`, so a pick finds the fire even for a piece still drawn after a version change.
- **Recovery.** Layer state changes only once the renderer writes succeed; a failed write or an interrupted read is repaired by the next read, and enable/disable work after one.
- **Without ids** (any piece missing one, duplicate ids, or an id with a lone UTF-16 surrogate), the layer draws everything into one fill set and one line set with the old counter ids, as before.
- `scripts/qa-perimeters-perf.mjs` and `scripts/fixtures/perimeterPeak.mjs`: a synthetic peak day and a headless benchmark of hourly steps on Cesium.

## Two small host-facing additions

- **`./layers/perimeters/records`** joins the package exports: `perimeterAnchorDegrees`, `firePerimeterSnapshot` and `normalizeFirePerimeterSnapshot`, with nothing but the i18n marker behind them (`scripts/package-boundaries.json`: 2 modules). A server or worker can now stand an incident card where the map does without importing the layer and its rendering code.
- **`refreshLayer(layerId, { supersede: true })`** cancels a refresh still in flight instead of waiting for it: its update's signal aborts (`AbortError`), it settles `false`, and the new update starts at once. Every update now receives an `AbortSignal` that also carries the caller's cancellation. It used to receive `null` when the caller gave none. Without `supersede`, a refresh still waits, and waits again if another one starts meanwhile. Three new tests in `src/data/manager.test.mjs`.

## Why not one set per age band

That was the first plan: colour per set, and a piece that ages moves from one band's set to the next. Measuring the peak day ruled it out:

- An hourly step adds ~14 pieces and moves ~42 into the next band (5.4% of ~1,000). That touches all four bands on every step, and the 1–3 day band holds two-thirds of the polygons.
- On Cesium, removing a fill from a set, or adding one, rebuilds the whole set (`draw.js` `remove`/`upsert`). Per-band sets would still rebuild about three-quarters of the geometry each step.
- Recolouring a drawn ground fill doesn't rebuild anything: `patchShapes` writes the instance colour in place. So colour stays per item, and a piece stays in the set it was first drawn in.

Set size is a trade-off. Each fill set costs its own ground batches every frame, ~8–10 at this density, because a batch takes only fills whose rectangles don't overlap. Fill sets are large. Line sets cost one ground polyline primitive each, so they are small: an aged piece's lines rebuild only their own small set.

## Numbers

Synthetic peak (`perimeterPeak`): 1,000 pieces of 160 fires, 47,000 polygons, 0.8 M fill vertices, each piece a growth ring of its fire cut into 47 sectors, born over 3 days. 12 hourly steps, one run each way. Headless Chrome 152, ANGLE Metal, Apple Silicon, keyless dev server, 60 Hz frames. The benchmark runs `update()` in a page task, so its own long task counts.

| per hourly step | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| longest task | 939–1143 ms, median 1060 ms | 61–169 ms, median 107 ms; 225–274 ms on the step that opens a new fill set |
| draw commands of a frame at rest | 84–92 | 308–354 |
| frame time at rest | ~1 ms | ~1 ms |

A new fill set opens about every 8,000 polygons of new pieces, every ~12 hours of timeline at this rate. Without piece ids the numbers match "before".

**Known limitation.** On the step that opens a new fill set, the layer re-makes every line set so fire lines stay above the new fills. Cesium builds ground lines asynchronously, so fire lines blank for ~2.7 s, and the step stays above 200 ms. Live WFIGS (~1,800 pieces) fits in one fill set and never gets there. Fixing it needs ground ordering in the draw contract (`drawOrder` for ground sets), left for a follow-up.

Where the time went before (CPU profile, one step): about 0.9 s in `update()`, mostly building the two sets again, 1.5 s in `GroundPrimitive.update` building vertex arrays over the next frames, and 1 s of GC.

## Verification

- `npm test` is green, including `src/render/conformance`. Renderers are unchanged.
- New `src/layers/perimeters/incremental.test.mjs` on the stub renderer covers: a read with no changes writes nothing; a band change upserts only the piece's items in its two sets; a new piece is only upserted and a gone piece only removed; remove and add in one set become one `set`; a full set is left alone; line sets are re-made after a new fill set; a snapshot without ids is drawn whole; a click resolves through the stub's own pick to the right fire after recolours and additions. Further tests cover id encoding, staged state after failed writes, overlap order over random read histories, picks during a version swap and an interrupted read followed by enable/disable.
- Existing layer tests (`ownership`, `cards`, `records`, `source`, i18n) pass. `records.test.mjs` checks WFIGS piece ids.
- Screenshot of the busiest synthetic fire at 45 km after three steps, before vs after: 1,576 of 1.24 M pixels differ. These are the HUD clock, 1 px seams between sectors (the fills batch differently) and a few triangles at the frame edge. Colours, fire lines over fills and newer over older are unchanged.

Not in scope: geometry simplification, host changes.

title: fix(flights): settle cancelled military handoff refreshes
body:
## What this changes

When the Military layer deactivates while Flights is enabled, `_onMilitaryActiveChange(false)` triggers a fire-and-forget `flightsLayer.update(flightState._viewer)` refresh. If Flights is disabled or torn down (for example during context restoration) before that refresh settles, `_abortActiveUpdates()` rejects the in-flight promise with an `AbortError`, which previously surfaced as an unhandled promise rejection.

This wraps the handoff refresh in `Promise.resolve(...).catch(...)` so `AbortError` cancellations settle cleanly while unexpected background errors are logged with `console.warn`, and adds regression unit tests for both paths in `src/layers/flights/tracking.test.mjs`.

title: Aurora layer: NOAA OVATION oval and live space weather
body:
## What this changes

Adds a default-off **Aurora** layer in the Weather group. NOAA SWPC's OVATION aurora forecast (the chance of aurora overhead, about 30–90 minutes ahead) is drawn as one world `rasterShell` field 110 km up, roughly where the green oxygen line glows. Faint chances stay a thin wisp, the core of the oval reads as a glow, and displays above 30% shift toward red. The layer row shows the planetary Kp index, today's NOAA G/R/S scales, solar wind speed and Bz, how far toward the equator the ≥10% oval reaches in the north, and the forecast's valid time; the legend counts nodes at ≥10/30/50%.

- `src/layers/aurora/records.js`: pure parsing (OVATION grid, Kp, scales, solar wind), the 360×180 equirectangular image, band counts and reach.
- `src/layers/aurora/source.js`: browser fetches of five keyless SWPC products. Only OVATION is required; a failed optional product leaves its readout out.
- `src/layers/aurora/index.js`: the layer. Refreshes every 5 minutes, updates the one shell's image in place, keeps the last forecast drawn on a failed refresh with the error in the row, and goes stale after 30 minutes without a new run. A permanent refusal with nothing drawn fails the enable.

Voice control doesn't name the layer yet (listed in `VOICE_OFF_LAYERS` for the prompt budget, like Shipwrecks).

title: Tracked aircraft stop drawing as model and icon at once when the camera leaves model range
body:
## What this changes

When the camera leaves model range of a tracked aircraft, one frame drew it twice: as its 3D model and as its icon, already lifted onto the display floor. From the next frame on only the icon drew.

**Why:** the tracked model's visibility is set at the start of the frame (`_updateTrackedModel`, preUpdate) from whether the aircraft may draw as a model, as the previous fleet pass decided. The fleet pass (`_fleetTick`, preRender) clears that later in the same frame. From that point the icon owns the visual and is floored, but the model stays shown until the next frame's preUpdate.

**Fix:** the fleet pass now sets eligibility through `_setTrackedModelEligible`, which hides the tracked model and its fleet model as soon as eligibility turns off. The frame that loses the model regime draws only the icon. The flights and military layers share this code.

With fast frames the extra frame passes unseen. With slow ones (headless SwiftShader, 300–900 ms a frame) the tracking regression catches exactly that frame, and its grounded model to billboard transition check fails. The bug predates #1919.

## Checks

- New unit test in `aircraftModelLayer.test.mjs`: a tracked contact the camera leaves behind has its model hidden in the same frame. It fails without the fix.
- `npm test`: 0 failures.
- `npm run test:track`: the display-floor/regime check passes (`OUT @ 10 km: 0 model(s) rendering`).

title: Tracking regression measures the trail head against the icon the frame drew
body:
## What this changes

The tracking regression's trail head check (`npm run test:track`) compared the trail's head to the wrong position and failed by about one frame's travel.

**Why:** the probe reads the followed contact in postRender. `position()` dead-reckons once per rendered frame, keyed on the frame counter, but the counter has already moved on by postRender. So `position()` dead-reckons anew, a frame interval ahead of the icon just drawn. It also caches that result, which the next frame then draws from: the probe changed what it measured. Since #1919, flights draw at 3–30 Hz instead of every display refresh, so a frame interval is long enough for the gap to exceed the check's tolerance.

**Fix:** both reads (on a frame and between frames) take `displayPosition()`, the cache the frame drew from. They fall back to `position()` for a contact without it. The app is unchanged.

## Checks

- `npm run test:track`: trail head alignment is 0.0 m both on a frame and between frames. It now passes on current main and on main before #1919.

- Each event is a glowing marker where it was brightest, drawn at that altitude when JPL reports one (otherwise on the ground), always over depth and hidden past the horizon.

title: Weather Balloons layer: live SondeHub radiosondes
body:
## What this changes

Adds a default-off **Weather Balloons** layer (`radiosondes`) in the Weather group: radiosondes that volunteer receiving stations hear, from SondeHub.

- Each sonde is drawn at its reported altitude (on the ground without one), over depth and culled past the horizon, coloured **rising** (≥ 1 m/s), **falling** (≤ −1 m/s) or **not heard for 15+ min**, with counts in the legend.
- Selecting one shows a card: altitude, climb or descent rate, drift speed, temperature, humidity, pressure, model and frequency, last-heard time and predicted landing time. SondeHub's forecast is drawn as a 3D path from the balloon to a landing cross. Activating the card opens the sonde on the SondeHub tracker.
- `getAnalystRecords` gives Context each sonde by serial with altitude, vertical rate and last-heard time.

**How it reads SondeHub.** Their API docs ask clients not to poll repeatedly: read the current state once, then follow the live feed, and mirror it for your users rather than have every browser connect. So the browser only reads the local mirror, and `server/providers/sondehub.js` is that mirror:
- `GET /api/sondehub/latest`: on the first request of a session, one `GET /sondes?last=10800`, then the live `batch` topic over MQTT-over-WebSocket (`wss://ws-reader.v2.sondehub.org/`), keeping the newest frame per serial and pruning frames over three hours old. It disconnects ten minutes after the last browser request and reconnects with 5 s → 5 min backoff if the feed drops.
- `server/providers/sondehubMqtt.js` is a subscribe-only MQTT 3.1.1 client on Node's built-in WebSocket (CONNECT, SUBSCRIBE at QoS 0, PUBLISH in, PINGREQ), so no new dependency.
- `GET /api/sondehub/prediction?serial=…`: SondeHub's `/predictions?vehicles=<serial>`, cached for two minutes, only for a selected sonde.
- Receiver callsigns, station positions and antennas are dropped on arrival; they describe the hobbyists who heard the balloon.

Voice control doesn't name the layer yet (listed in `VOICE_OFF_LAYERS` for the prompt budget).

title: On macOS, Command+drag tilts and rotates the globe like Ctrl+drag
body:
On macOS, Ctrl+click is a right click, so the Ctrl+drag camera tilt/rotate is awkward there. With this change, Command+drag on the globe tilts and rotates the camera just as Ctrl+drag does.

- Applies only on macOS. Windows and Linux behave as before.

- Ctrl+wheel is unchanged and stays the trackpad pinch. Wheel events are never remapped.
- When Command is held without Ctrl, pointer and mouse events on the globe canvas, plus the moves and releases of a press that began there, report Ctrl to Cesium's camera controller. This happens in `src/render/cesium/commandDrag.js`, which the camera controls install and remove.

title: Tracking regression's arrival check counts frames, not milliseconds
body:
## What this changes

The arrival check in `npm run test:track` failed on slow machines even though the angles it measures were correct. It now counts frames instead of milliseconds.

**Why it failed:** the check required the settle frame (the first frame after a forced `moveEnd`) and the reveal frame (the first frame that draws the aircraft again) to land within 500 ms each. Under headless SwiftShader on a busy machine, frames are 650–950 ms apart, so both attempts timed out with 0.0° error. Results varied from run to run with machine load.

**Why the budget is no longer needed:** it was set so a one-second idle rotation refresh could not repair a wrong nose before the check read it. The aircraft layers no longer have that refresh; icons turn along their course on the GPU every frame. So the nose a frame draws does not depend on how long the frame took.

**Now:**
- The settle frame is always the first frame after `moveEnd`, whatever its duration.
- The reveal must be drawn on the next frame, or the one after it if the next was already in flight. It is counted from the last frame that drew the aircraft hidden.
- A 10 s wall-clock wait remains only for a renderer that stopped drawing.
- A stall, or a reveal that misses its frames after a correct settle frame, is retried once, as before. A measured wrong angle still fails without retry.

`docs/CURRENT-STATE.md` describes the check accordingly. The app is unchanged.

## Checks

- `src/tooling/trackArrivalObservation.test.mjs`: 19 tests pass, including 700 ms frames passing, a reveal two frames late failing, an unmarked hidden frame, and stall and retry cases.
- `npm run test:track` (keyless dev server, headless SwiftShader, loaded machine): 111 passed, 0 failed. The flights settle frame took 913 ms, which the old 500 ms budget would have failed. Log line: `settle-err=0.0° reveal-err=0.0° flipFrame=3 revealFrame=1 settle=913.4 ms`.
- `npm run format:check`: pass.

title: GNSS Integrity: cells draw as a flat overlay instead of streaking through 3D tiles
body:
## What was wrong

GNSS Integrity cells were drawn as ground primitives clamped to both terrain and 3D tiles. Over photorealistic 3D tiles, a ground primitive is a classification volume. Zoomed out to globe scale, a cell hundreds of kilometres wide is a volume that cuts through the tiles. The cells showed up as green streaks across the globe, for example over the mid-Pacific near the date line from about 8,750 km up.

## What changes

- **New `clampTo` value: `'overlay'`.** Clamped flat fills, their outlines and draped lines of such a set are drawn as a flat layer on the ellipsoid, over everything. Neither 3D tiles nor terrain hide them. Only the ellipsoid does: whatever lies past its horizon from the eye is not drawn, so cells on the far side of the globe never show through it. Edges follow the curve. Icons, points and models clamp to `'overlay'` as they do to `'both'`. The contract type (`src/render/contract/draw.d.ts`) and `docs/RENDERER-CONTRACT.md` describe it.
- **Cesium renderer (`src/render/cesium/draw.js`):**
  - Overlay fills are one `Primitive` on the ellipsoid, cut every tenth of a degree.
  - They draw in the translucent pass with no depth test and no depth writes, so they draw after the opaque tiles and over them.
  - The fragment shader drops each fragment past the ellipsoid's horizon. In the ellipsoid's unit sphere, a fragment stays only while the eye is on its side of the tangent plane. This works per fragment, so a cell that straddles the limb is cut exactly there.
  - Outlines and draped lines are drawn the way draped lines already are where the scene cannot drape: over the surface, and hidden once all of a line is past the horizon.
  - An image fill on an overlay shape is refused.
- **GNSS Integrity (`src/layers/gnss/index.js`)** draws its cells with `clampTo: 'overlay'`.

Why not keep draping, or float the cells at a height? Draping onto tiles is exactly what streaks. Cells raised off the ground float visibly. Cells draped on the globe alone are hidden under photoreal tiles.

## Tests

- `src/render/cesium/draw.test.mjs`:
  - the GNSS cells are one overlay primitive (no ground primitive), with the depth test off, the horizon discard in the shader, on the ellipsoid and finely cut;
  - a draped overlay line draws over the surface and hides past the horizon while the scene can drape;
  - an overlay shape's fill and outline;
  - an image fill is refused.
- `src/layers/gnss/ownership.test.mjs`: the layer's set is `clampTo: 'overlay'`.
- New conformance check `draw.shapes.overlay`: with the globe hidden, an overlay rectangle is drawn and picked; the one at its antipode, straight behind it, is not.

`npm test`, `npm run format:check` and `npm run check:boundaries` all pass.

title: Phones get the desktop search dock; the unused location and preset trays go
body:
Phones had three search entry points that desktop does not: the Omnibar pinned at the top of the screen, a separate voice card (mic, chat, carousel) above the timeline, and the old location tray ("Search any location…" with city pills) as a Search tab in the bottom bar. The More tab stacked the old Visual Presets tray on top of the Visual panel, filling the screen and riding up under the header.

Phones now get the desktop dock itself.

- `[mic] [Omnibar] [chat]` in one row above the World Timeline and the tab bar, results opening upward, the voice waveform in the field, as on desktop.
- 44px touch targets, a 16px field (iOS does not zoom on focus), safe-area insets; the dock rises above the on-screen keyboard and steps aside while a sheet is open.
- No top Omnibar, no voice card, no Search tab. More shows the Visual panel alone (presets and every map source), as the left rail does on desktop.

The trays no layout showed any more are deleted: `#location-bar`, `#control-panel`, the tray parts of `LocationControls`, `locationStatus.js`, hover/pin disclosure, tray metrics, their CSS and 15 strings in every language (~8,300 lines). Landmark keys (Q-W-E-R-T), city and landmark fly-to, and place and coordinate search keep working through the Omnibar, whose landmark chips replace the pills. Voice names for presets and map sources open Visual. Share-link panel numbers 0 and 1 stay reserved, so old links still decode.

Public exports changed: `./ui/location` (no `locationStatus`), `./ui/input` (`bindApplicationShortcuts` loses `searchInput` / `dismissSearch`), `./ui/panels` (no `createHoverDisclosure`).

Checked in Chrome at 390×844 (phone: one search at the bottom, results upward, Layers / Cameras / Context / More sheets) and 1440×900 (desktop unchanged). Full unit suite (16,063), `format:check`, `check:boundaries`, `i18n` and `build` pass.

title: Phones and low-memory devices cache 384 MiB of photorealistic 3D tiles
body:
On a phone the photorealistic 3D tileset kept Cesium's desktop cache: 1.5 GiB plus 1 GiB of overflow. Emulating an iPhone (390×844, DPR 3), flying to a new city added ~150 MB each: 668 MB after 4 cities, 1,291 MB after 8, flat at 1,536 MB. iOS Safari closes a tab well before that (reports range ~0.5–1.5 GB for the whole tab), so a few fly-tos were enough to lose the page.

Touch-only devices (coarse pointer, no fine pointer) and devices reporting `navigator.deviceMemory <= 4` now cache 384 MiB plus 128 MiB of overflow. Everything else keeps 1536/1024 MiB.

- `photorealCacheBudget({ touchOnly, deviceMemory })` in `src/render/cesium/google3d.js` decides it; `browserMemoryClass()` reads the inputs with the same touch-only test as `quality.js`.
- The key, token and ion routes all take the budget (the key route passes it into `createGooglePhotorealistic3DTileset`, which keeps given values).
- An iPad with a trackpad or mouse reports a fine pointer and keeps the desktop cache unless it reports 4 GB or less.

Measured with 256 MiB + 128 MiB set at runtime on the same 8-city sweep: tiles stayed at ~255 MB and a street-level city view still drew at full detail; going back to a city re-downloads what was dropped. Docs: `docs/CURRENT-STATE.md` ("Google 3D tile memory on phones"), `docs/PERFORMANCE.md`.

Checked: unit tests for the budget and all three routes; headless Chromium on the dev server read 384/128 MiB from the tileset as an iPhone and 1536/1024 MiB at 1440×900. Full suite passes except two timing tests that fail only under full-suite load (`analystEngine`, `tool-schema-codepoints`) and pass on their own; `format:check` and `check:boundaries` pass.
